title: FDA Seeks Public Input to Advance Development of Botanical Drug Products
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced a request for information (RFI) to gather public input on opportunities to advance the development of botanical drug products. Botanical drug products include products derived from plant materials, algae, macroscopic fungi, or combinations of these materials. The FDA is committed to modernizing regulatory frameworks to ensure the evaluation of promising, natural health options through rigorous science. The agency is seeking feedback on topics including challenges in botanical research and development, innovative approaches to support development, and potential updates to FDA guidance and resources. The public will have 60 days to submit comments to the docket, with the comment period closing on November 3, 2026.

title: FDA Approves First Drug of Its Kind for Polycythemia Vera, a Rare Blood Disorder
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Mimrylo (rusfertide), a new treatment for adults with polycythemia vera, a rare blood disorder. Mimrylo mimics hepcidin, a hormone that regulates iron in the body, to reduce red blood cell overproduction and keep levels under control. This approach offers a new option for patients who have not achieved adequate control with existing therapies. The approval was granted based on the VERIFY trial, a phase 3 study of 293 adults with polycythemia vera, in which Mimrylo showed efficacy in reducing the need for phlebotomies. The safety and efficacy of Mimrylo were evaluated, with the most common adverse reactions being injection site reactions and anemia. The approval was granted to Takeda Pharmaceuticals America, Inc.

title: FDA Approves First Oral Drug Indicated to Treat Dermatomyositis in Adults
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Lisraya (brepocitinib) tablets for the treatment of dermatomyositis in adults. This approval provides an important new alternative for managing symptoms. Nikolay Nikolov, M.D., Director of the Office of Immunology and Inflammation, described the approval as a "meaningful step forward" for patients with this rare and debilitating disease. Dermatomyositis is a condition in which the immune system attacks the muscles and skin, causing chronic inflammation and progressive muscle weakness. Lisraya, a once-daily oral tablet, works as a Janus kinase (JAK/TYK2) inhibitor. In a phase 3 study, participants treated with Lisraya 30 mg showed a higher average Total Improvement Score at week 52 compared to those given a placebo. The study also found improvements in physical function and skin disease activity. Common adverse reactions to Lisraya included upper respiratory tract infection, headache, and fatigue. The FDA granted Lisraya Orphan Drug and Priority Review designations.

title: FDA Issues Emergency Use Authorization for Generic Drug to Prevent New World Screwworm in Cattle
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for Bimectin (ivermectin) injection for the prevention of New World screwworm (NWS) infestations in cattle when administered within 24 hours of birth, at the time of castration, or at the appearance of a wound. The authorization reflects the FDA's commitment to expanding generic drug options against NWS and ensures producers aren't dependent on a single manufacturer or product. Bimectin injection is available over the counter and is a generic version of Ivomec, which was previously authorized for the prevention of NWS myiasis in cattle. The EUA will be effective until it is revoked or the HHS Secretary terminates the declaration justifying the emergency use authorization.

title: FDA Approves First in Class Targeted Therapy for Metastatic Pancreatic Cancer
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Rasonque (daraxonrasib), a RAS inhibitor, for the most common form of pancreatic cancer, 6.5 months before the user fee deadline. Rasonque targets multiple forms of a protein called RAS, a key driver of tumor growth in most patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The approval is for adults with metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma who have received at least one prior systemic therapy or are not candidates for multiagent systemic therapy. Rasonque improved median overall survival to 13.2 months compared to 6.7 months for standard chemotherapy in a randomized, open-label, multicenter clinical trial involving 500 adults. The FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy and Orphan Drug designations and Priority Review for this indication. Revolution Medicines, Inc. will manufacture and distribute the drug.

title: FDA Authorizes First Wearable Device That Continuously Monitors Both Ketone Levels and Blood Sugar
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the Libre Duo 10 Day Continuous Dual Glucose Ketone Monitoring System for people aged 2 years and older living with diabetes. This wearable device continuously monitors ketone levels and glucose levels together in a single device. The FDA Director, Michelle Tarver, M.D., Ph.D., stated that this authorization is a breakthrough for the safety of children and adults living with diabetes. The device was approved based on data from six clinical studies that enrolled over 600 participants to evaluate its accuracy. The Libre Duo 10 Day was granted Breakthrough Device designation and De Novo premarket review pathway, and the FDA is establishing special controls to ensure safety and effectiveness.

title: FDA Approves First Therapy for Patients aged 8 years and older with Glycogen Storage Disease Type Ia
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an accelerated approval for Genglycos (pariglasgene brecaparvovec-opnr) to reduce daily cornstarch intake in adults and pediatric patients 8 years of age and older with glycogen storage disease type Ia (GSDIa). This is the first approved treatment for GSDIa. The accelerated approval pathway was used due to the treatment's effect on a surrogate endpoint, with a 31% mean reduction in daily cornstarch intake in patients treated with Genglycos. The treatment aims to restore the deficient enzyme glucose-6-phosphatase to improve stable blood sugar levels. Clinical trials have shown that Genglycos has a numerical increase in the percentage of glucose values in the hypoglycemic range and a higher rate of hypertriglyceridemia. The FDA granted accelerated approval to Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical, Inc.

title: FDA Authorizes First-Of-Its-Kind Robotic Blood Draw Device
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has authorized the Aletta, a standalone robotic device, for use in drawing blood from adults in outpatient settings. The device, which can operate without human intervention, must be supervised by a trained phlebotomist. One phlebotomist can oversee up to three Aletta devices simultaneously, addressing the current phlebotomist shortage in the U.S. The FDA's Director, Michelle Tarver, M.D., Ph.D., stated that the authorization reflects the agency's commitment to innovative medical devices that meet public health needs while ensuring safety and effectiveness. The Aletta autonomously handles each step of the blood draw, with a trained phlebotomist initiating each session and responding to any issues. The device was granted marketing authorization to Vitestro through the De Novo pathway, with the FDA establishing special controls to ensure safety and effectiveness.

title: FDA Seeks Public Feedback to Inform Regulatory Approach for Generative AI-Enabled Medical Devices
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued a discussion paper on the regulation of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI)-enabled medical devices, seeking feedback from interested parties on risk assessment, premarket evaluation, postmarket monitoring, and other topics. The effort aligns with the Trump Administration's priority to harness AI to accelerate the delivery of innovative medical products. Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas said "Artificial intelligence is transforming medicine, and the United States must lead in shaping how this technology is developed and used safely and responsibly." The Digital Health Center of Excellence is leading the discussion paper, which supports the FDA's Public Health Pillar on Innovation and Global Leadership. The FDA Center for Devices and Radiological Health Director Michelle Tarver, M.D., Ph.D., said "Patients and clinicians deserve a regulatory approach that keeps pace with the rapid innovation of digital health technologies." The discussion paper proposes a two-axis framework for risk assessment and discusses premarket evaluation and postmarket monitoring approaches. The FDA encourages feedback from device manufacturers, clinicians, consumers, researchers, and the public, with a deadline for submission under the docket FDA-2026-N-7874 on Regulations.gov by October 19, 2026.

title: FDA Issues Emergency Use Authorization for Drug to Treat New World Screwworm in Dogs and Puppies
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for Simparica TRIO to treat New World screwworm (NWS) infestations in dogs and puppies. The EUA allows veterinarians to prescribe Simparica TRIO to dogs that have traveled to or returned from areas with NWS infestations, or live in areas with a high risk of exposure. The FDA has concluded that Simparica TRIO may be effective in treating NWS myiasis when used as authorized. The product was approved for heartworm, flea, and tick-related indications in 2020 and is available only by prescription from a licensed veterinarian. The EUA is effective until it is revoked or terminated by the HHS Secretary, and is sponsored by Zoetis Inc.

title: FDA Issues Emergency Use Authorization for Drug to Prevent New World Screwworm in Multiple Species, Including Sheep, Cattle, Goats, and Swine
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued an Emergency Use Authorization for CLiK Extra (dicyclanil topical suspension) wound spray to prevent New World screwworm (NWS) infestations in sheep, cattle, goats, swine, camelids, and certain captive and captured wildlife species. The authorization allows for the use of CLiK Extra wound spray on or around wounds for the prevention of NWS myiasis. The FDA has concluded that the known benefits of the product outweigh its known and potential risks. The EUA will be effective until it is revoked or the HHS Secretary terminates the declaration justifying the emergency use authorization. CLiK Extra wound spray is available over the counter for topical use on or around wounds, and its detailed product information can be found in the Fact Sheet for Emergency Use Authorization of CLiK Extra.

title: FDA Approves New Engineered Viral Immunotherapy for Patients with Treatment-Resistant Advanced Melanoma
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has granted accelerated approval to Tudriqev, a genetically modified oncolytic viral therapy, for the treatment of advanced, refractory melanoma. The therapy is indicated in combination with nivolumab for adult patients with unresectable advanced cutaneous melanoma. One in four patients responded to treatment, with responses lasting a median of nearly 14 months. The approval was supported by data from a clinical trial and considered input from clinical experts and patient advocates. Tudriqev is an oncolytic viral therapy based on a modified herpes simplex virus type 1 that selectively targets and destroys cancer cells. The therapy is injected directly into tumors once every two weeks for eight consecutive doses, combined with nivolumab. The safety and effectiveness of Tudriqev were evaluated in a clinical trial enrolling 140 adult patients, with 24% achieving an objective response. The FDA convened a Cellular, Tissue, and Gene Therapies Advisory Committee Meeting to discuss the application, which was granted Breakthrough Therapy and Priority Review designations. The approval was granted to Replimune, Inc. under the FDA's accelerated approval pathway based on objective response rate and duration of response.

title: FDA Approves First Drug to Treat the Full Range of Narcolepsy Type 1 Symptoms
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Orzeyful tablets for the treatment of narcolepsy type 1 in adults. Orzeyful is the first medicine approved to address the full range of symptoms of narcolepsy type 1, targeting the loss of orexin signaling. The approval was granted to Takeda Pharmaceuticals America, Inc. The medicine directly activates the brain receptor that orexin would normally stimulate, restoring the missing signal. The effectiveness and safety of Orzeyful were evaluated in two randomized studies enrolling 273 adults. Patients taking Orzeyful showed improvements in staying awake during the day, reduced daytime sleepiness, and a full spectrum of narcolepsy symptoms. The most common side effects included insomnia, increased urinary frequency, and increased saliva production.

title: Executive Order 14417—Establishing the President's Military Spouse Commission
body_summary: President Donald J. Trump orders the establishment of the President's Military Spouse Commission to prioritize the quality of life of military spouses and families. The Commission will advise and assist the President on policies affecting military spouses, including monitoring implementation, developing policies, and recommending actions to improve their well-being. The Commission will consist of the spouse of the Secretary of War as Chair and senior military leaders' spouses, with members serving contingent on their spouse's duration in service. The Commission will terminate two years from the date of the order, unless extended by the President.

title: FDA Licenses First-Ever Freeze-Dried Plasma Product in the U.S.
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has licensed Ezplaz Freeze Dried Plasma (FDP), making it the first freeze-dried plasma product licensed for use in the United States. Ezplaz is intended for transfusion in adult patients who need plasma and for whom other plasma products are not available. This product was developed for patients experiencing life-threatening bleeding in austere environments, where conventional frozen plasma is unavailable. Ezplaz is a freeze-dried plasma product derived from a single unit of fresh frozen plasma collected from FDA-licensed blood establishments. It can be stored at room temperature, is stable after exposure to temperature fluctuations, and is rapidly reconstituted. The FDA expects this product to be compatible with austere environments, including combat zones, remote areas, and disaster response settings. Ezplaz is indicated for transfusion in adults when plasma is required and other plasma products are not available, including bleeding patients and patients needing massive transfusion.

title: FDA Announces First Participant Selected for TEMPO for Digital Health Devices Pilot
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has selected Dexcom, Inc. as the first manufacturer for the Technology-Enabled Meaningful Patient Outcomes (TEMPO) for Digital Health Devices Pilot. The pilot aims to improve health outcomes for Americans managing certain chronic diseases, particularly those related to diabetes. The FDA will evaluate the Dexcom Glucose Health Program, which enables patients to monitor metabolic and nutritional status, receive tailored guidance, and access real-time data for informed decision-making. The pilot will help the FDA and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) understand how digital health technologies perform in real-world settings. The FDA plans to select up to ten TEMPO pilot participants in each of four clinical use areas, with the goal of promoting patient access, safeguarding patient safety, and generating meaningful data. The pilot began in July 2026 and will continue to select participants with no specified deadline.

title: FDA Takes Further Steps to Remove Outdated Authorizations for Color Additives in Food
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is issuing a final order revoking the use of Orange B as a color additive in food and proposing to revoke the use of Citrus Red No. 2 as a color additive in food. The agency is taking these actions as part of its efforts to modernize food safety regulations and eliminate outdated authorizations. The proposed revocation of Citrus Red No. 2 is based on the conclusion that its use has been abandoned by industry. The FDA is accepting public comments on the proposed revocation for 30 days, with a deadline for submission by August 24, 2026.

title: FDA Approves First Oral PCSK9 Inhibitor to Lower LDL Cholesterol in Adults with High Cholesterol
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Lipfendra, the first oral inhibitor of proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9), to reduce low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) in adults with hypercholesterolemia, including those with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH). Lipfendra is administered as a once-daily oral tablet and provides an additional treatment option for adults who require further LDL-C reduction despite existing therapies.

The approval was granted based on results from two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trials involving 3,207 adults with hypercholesterolemia, including patients with and without HeFH. Treatment with Lipfendra resulted in significant reductions in LDL-C, with an average 56% reduction in the first trial and 59% reduction in the second trial.

The FDA's Acting Director, Michael Davis, M.D., Ph.D., stated that the approval provides an additional treatment option for adults with hypercholesterolemia and reflects the FDA's commitment to supporting meaningful advances in patient access and tackling chronic diseases.

Lipfendra was received Priority Review, and the approval was granted to Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC, following review under the Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher (CNPV) pilot program.

title: FDA Issues Emergency Use Authorization for Drug for Short-Term Prevention of New World Screwworm in Horses
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for Ivermectin Liquid for Horses to prevent New World screwworm (NWS) infestations in horses. The EUA is authorized for use within 24 hours of birth or at the time of initial wound care. The product is only available for use in horses and can be administered as an oral drench or via a tube.

The authorization is part of the Trump administration's efforts to safeguard American agriculture. The FDA has concluded that Ivermectin Liquid for Horses may be effective in the short-term prevention of NWS myiasis in horses when used as authorized. However, the product is not intended for treatment of existing infestations, and owners and veterinarians should be aware of the limitations.

Ivermectin Liquid for Horses is sponsored by Alberta Vet Labs Ltd. based in Canada, and is available only by prescription from a licensed veterinarian. The EUA will be effective until it is revoked or the HHS Secretary terminates the declaration that justifies the emergency use authorization.

title: FDA Proposes Rule to Modernize Drug Manufacturing Registration
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has proposed a rule to create a streamlined registration pathway for distributed manufacturing establishments operating as a single "hub-and-spoke" model. If finalized, the rule would allow these establishments to register as a single entity, simplifying the registration process. The proposed rule would also clarify registration requirements for foreign drug manufacturing establishments, particularly those manufacturing active pharmaceutical ingredients. This action aims to strengthen domestic pharmaceutical manufacturing, ensure regulatory frameworks keep pace with innovation, and increase supply chain transparency. The proposed rule is expected to reduce registration costs and generate long-term efficiencies for industry and the agency.

title: The President's News Conference in Ankara, Turkey
body_summary: The US President attended a successful NATO summit in Turkey, thanking President Erdoğan for his leadership and Secretary General Mark Rutte for their efforts. The US has led a historic defense spending increase, exceeding 5% of GDP, and investing $1 trillion in its Armed Forces. The President believes other NATO members will meet the 5% target, and the US will receive over $1 trillion. The US aims to increase production of defensive equipment, aiming for a 2-week wait instead of a 1-year wait, expected to create thousands of jobs and boost American manufacturing.

title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapy for Young Children with Sickle Cell Disease
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a supplemental approval for Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel) for patients aged 2 years and older with either sickle cell disease (SCD) or transfusion-dependent β thalassemia (TDT). This is the first gene therapy approved for patients aged 2 years and older with SCD. Casgevy has been previously approved for patients aged 12 years and older with SCD. The FDA granted this approval through expedited review programs, including the CNPV Pilot Program. 

Casgevy is a gene therapy consisting of the patient's own hematopoietic stem cells, edited using CRISPR/Cas9, and administered as a one-time single dose for intravenous infusion. It increases a type of hemoglobin (HbF) in patients with severe SCD and total hemoglobin levels in patients with TDT, thereby eliminating VOCs and dependence on regular RBC transfusions. 

The safety and effectiveness of Casgevy in patients aged 5 years to less than 12 years with SCD and TDT were evaluated in clinical trials. Eight patients with SCD achieved the primary efficacy outcome of no protocol-defined severe VOCs for at least 12 consecutive months within the first 24 months after infusion with Casgevy. Eight of the nine efficacy evaluable patients with TDT achieved transfusion independence for 12 consecutive months. 

The FDA granted Casgevy Orphan Drug, regenerative medicine advanced therapy, and Fast Track designations. The approval decision was granted 53 days after filing, representing the eighth approval selected for the CNPV Pilot Program.

title: FDA Approves New Treatment That Uses Donor Immune Cells to Prevent Serious Complications in Blood Cancer Patients
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Tregzi, the first regulatory T cell-based immunotherapy, for improving chronic graft-versus-host disease-free survival in adult patients with blood cancers undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. Tregzi uses stem cells and immune cells collected from a closely matched donor to fight cancer while reducing the risk of chronic GVHD. Patients receive the treatment after undergoing chemotherapy. The treatment was approved based on the results of a clinical trial, PRECISION-T, in which 187 adult patients were randomly assigned to receive Tregzi or a standard stem cell transplant. Patients who received Tregzi achieved significantly higher rates of chronic GVHD-free survival, with 78% of patients achieving this outcome at one year, compared to 38.4% of patients who received a standard transplant. The FDA determined that the benefits of Tregzi outweigh its risks.

title: FDA Selects Seven Participants for PreCheck Pilot Program to Advance U.S. Drug Manufacturing
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has selected seven companies to participate in the FDA PreCheck Pilot Program, a new initiative to boost American global competitiveness, strengthen domestic drug manufacturing, and improve the US drug supply chain. The program was launched on February 1, 2026, in response to Executive Order 14293 signed by President Trump in May 2025. The selected companies are Amneal Pharmaceutical, Cellares Corp., Eli Lilly and Company, FUJIFILM Biotechnologies, Kriya Therapeutics, Inc., Kyowa Kirin, Inc., and Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. These companies will engage with the FDA under the two-phase PreCheck model, receiving early technical guidance and enhanced engagement to support expedited facility evaluation and inspections. The program aims to support the development of new US pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities, improve access to critical medicines, and create high-quality American jobs.

title: FDA Proposes Rule That Would Help Hold Foreign Tobacco Product Manufacturers Accountable, Protect Public Health
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has proposed a rule to strengthen its ability to identify and take action against illegal foreign tobacco products, including youth-appealing e-cigarettes. The proposed regulation, if finalized, would require foreign tobacco product manufacturers to register their establishments and list their products with the FDA, closing a regulatory gap. The rule, titled "Establishment Registration and Product Listing for Tobacco Products," would prescribe format, content, and procedures for establishment registration and tobacco product listing. This would include both foreign and domestic establishments that manufacture tobacco products. The FDA would prescribe the format, content, and procedures for establishment registration and tobacco product listing. The proposed rule would significantly expand the agency's knowledge of tobacco products manufactured abroad for import into the U.S. and allow the agency to be more proactive in identifying and acting against illegal foreign tobacco products.

title: FDA Approves First Single-Dose Generic Treatment for Influenza
body_summary: The US FDA approved the first generic version of Xofluza (baloxavir marboxil) tablets, a single-dose treatment for acute uncomplicated influenza in patients 5 years of age and older. This approval is part of the Trump Administration's commitment to increasing generic drug availability. The FDA Director of the Office of Generic Drugs, Iilun Murphy, noted that expanding patient access to drugs and improving their ease of use are critical public health imperatives. The generic baloxavir marboxil tablets are approved for treatment and post-exposure prophylaxis, but contraindicated in patients with a history of hypersensitivity reactions. The FDA has also highlighted the importance of increasing generic drug availability to create competition, making treatment more affordable and increasing access to healthcare.

title: FDA Broadens Access to Over-the-Counter Naloxone Nasal Spray for Opioid Overdose
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved an over-the-counter (OTC) intranasal naloxone product, Rextovy, a 4 milligram (mg) naloxone hydrochloride nasal spray for emergency treatment of opioid overdose. Consumers can purchase this product without a prescription in pharmacies, convenience stores, and online. This approval aligns with President Trump's Great American Recovery Initiative to address the U.S.'s addiction crisis. The FDA approved Rextovy to broaden access and offer an additional option for consumers, with naloxone being a medication that rapidly reverses opioid overdose effects. The number of overdose deaths has decreased since the first FDA approval of an OTC naloxone nasal spray in 2023, but remains a major public health issue. The FDA remains committed to ensuring nonprescription options are widely available, and the product's packaging includes pictorial directions for safe use.

title: FDA Approves New Indication for Tzield (teplizumab) for Certain Pediatric Patients with Recently Diagnosed Stage 3 Type 1 Diabetes
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted accelerated approval to Tzield (teplizumab) on June 12, 2026, for a new indication to delay the decline of insulin production in pediatric patients aged 8 through 17 years with recently diagnosed Stage 3 type 1 diabetes. The approval is based on robust evidence of safety and effectiveness from an adequate clinical trial. Acting Associate Director Mahtab Niyyati M.D. stated that this accelerated approval provides a chance for pediatric patients to alter the course of their disease. A required postapproval study is ongoing to verify clinical benefit. The approved labeling includes a boxed warning regarding serious viral reactivation cases. Common side effects of Tzield include vomiting, rash, liver enzyme elevation, and reduction in white blood cells.

title: FDA Clears First Over-the-Counter Continuous Glucose Monitor for Children
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has cleared for marketing the first over-the-counter continuous glucose monitor (CGM) for children, Dexcom Inc.'s Stelo Glucose Biosensor System, for use by children two years of age and older who do not use insulin. This clearance reflects the FDA's commitment to fostering innovation for pediatric patients and supporting the safe and effective use of medical devices. The device is indicated for children with diabetes who receive oral medication to manage their condition and for people who want to understand how diet, exercise, and other lifestyle changes affect their glucose levels. The Stelo Glucose Biosensor System uses a wearable sensor and an application to continuously measure and display glucose values. The device is cleared for use under the supervision of an adult caregiver and is not suitable for individuals with problematic hypoglycemia or those on dialysis. The FDA used real-world evidence to support regulatory decision-making.

title: FDA Issues Emergency Use Authorization for Generic Over-the-Counter Drug to Treat New World Screwworm in Dogs and Cats
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for generic Nitenpyram Tablets for the treatment of New World screwworm (NWS) infestations in dogs, puppies, cats, and kittens weighing at least two pounds and are at least four weeks old. The FDA has concluded that Nitenpyram Tablets may be effective in treating NWS myiasis in certain animals and found that the known benefits outweigh the risks. The authorization is the first generic animal drug approved for use against NWS. The U.S. government has taken an aggressive approach to stop the spread and eradicate the pest, with the FDA issuing ten EUAs and three conditional approvals for drugs to combat the threat since August 2025.

title: FDA Expands Sunscreen Options for the First Time in 20 Years
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration added bemotrizinol to the list of permitted sunscreen active ingredients, marking the first new ingredient added to the over-the-counter sunscreen monograph since the late 1990s. Bemotrizinol has been used safely in Europe for decades and provides protection against both ultraviolet A and B rays. The FDA finalized this action within seven months of issuing the proposed order, which was issued on December 12, 2025, and received public comments until January 26, 2026. The new ingredient aligns with the FDA's Make America Healthy Again Strategy Report priority to promote innovation in the sunscreen market. Bemotrizinol has low levels of absorption through the skin and is considered generally recognized as safe and effective for use in sunscreens by adults and children 6 months of age and older.

title: FDA Issues Draft Guidance to Help Accelerate Cell and Gene Therapies for Patients
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a draft guidance to help developers bring promising gene therapies to patients more efficiently by leveraging existing scientific and regulatory knowledge. The guidance aims to streamline regulatory submissions for human gene therapy products that use genome editing in human somatic cells. The FDA encourages sponsors to use publicly available information and established platform knowledge to build on existing nonclinical, clinical, and manufacturing data. The guidance complements the agency's Plausible Mechanism Framework and the recently issued draft guidance on Safety Assessment of Genome Editing in Human Gene Therapy Products Using Next-Generation Sequencing. Sponsors should provide a scientific rationale for the applicability of the data being leveraged to their specific product and development context. The draft guidance is available for public comment, and comments must be submitted within 90 days.

title: FDA Issues Draft Guidance to Cut Unnecessary Animal Testing for Cancer Drugs
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a draft guidance to reduce unnecessary animal testing in nonclinical safety assessments for certain cancer drugs. The guidance aims to support the FDA's commitment to expedite regulatory pathways for meaningful treatments and reduce animal testing. According to FDA's Oncology Center of Excellence Director Angelo de Claro, the guidance will provide recommendations for eliminating unnecessary animal testing, using a single relevant species instead of two, or replacing animal studies with evidence-based approaches. The guidance will be finalized after considering public comments by July 30, 2026.

title: Executive Order 14407—Realigning United States Core Childhood Vaccine Recommendations With Best Practices From Peer, Developed Countries
body_summary: President Donald J. Trump orders that the core childhood vaccine schedule should be aligned with scientific evidence and best practices from peer, developed countries, while preserving access to vaccines currently available to Americans. The Department of Health and Human Services completed a scientific assessment comparing United States childhood immunization recommendations with those of peer nations. The assessment found that the United States recommends more childhood vaccines than any peer nation and identified a set of consensus vaccines recommended in all peer countries. The CDC and ACIP shall review the assessment and update the United States childhood and adolescent vaccine schedule, considering flexibility for parents and doctors. The executive departments and agencies shall ensure all actions align with the updated schedule, including providing coverage without cost sharing for private insurance and Medicaid.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Chronic Hepatitis Delta Virus (HDV) Infection
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Hepcludex (bulevirtide-gmod) injection to treat chronic hepatitis delta virus infection in adults without cirrhosis or with compensated cirrhosis. Bulevirtide is the first FDA-approved treatment for chronic HDV infection, a serious condition that can cause rapid liver damage and death. The efficacy of Hepcludex was demonstrated in a phase 3 trial, showing a combined response of 48% at week 48, with undetectable HDV RNA levels increasing to 36% at week 96. The FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation and Orphan-Drug Designation, and approved the treatment under the Accelerated Approval pathway for Gilead Sciences, Inc.

title: FDA Warns Retailers Selling Illegal Tobacco Products That Look Like Everyday Products
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued warning letters to eight retailers for selling unauthorized tobacco products, including nicotine pouches and dissolvable tobacco products. The products in question have labeling, advertising, and design features that resemble candy, breath strips, and cough drops. The FDA is committed to enforcing its regulations to stop such products from reaching the market, particularly those that appeal to children. The agency has already issued over 800 warning letters to firms and more than 1,000 to retailers for selling unauthorized tobacco products. The FDA maintains a list of approved tobacco products and offers free educational materials to retailers to support their compliance with the law.

title: FDA Finalizes Food Chemical Safety Post-Market Assessment Program, Launches Reassessment of BHT, ADA
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has reopened the comment period for the Request for Information (RFI) on butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) in human food and as a food contact substance for 30 days, with a new deadline of August 31, 2026. Electronic comments can be submitted to Regulations.gov using docket number FDA-2026-N-2526, while written comments should be submitted to the Dockets Management Staff at Food and Drug Administration, 5630 Fishers Lane, Room 1061, Rockville, MD 20852.

The FDA has finalized its new proactive food chemical safety post-market assessment program and launched reassessments of BHT and azodicarbonamide (ADA), chemical additives commonly used in food products. The agency is also revising its annual food chemical post-market assessment plan, which will guide its monitoring and prioritization of chemicals in the food supply.

The public comment period for the BHT and ADA RFIs will close on July 13, 2026. The FDA encourages food manufacturers, researchers, and consumers to submit relevant data and information. The agency will provide regular updates on the progress of ongoing assessments through the FDA's List of Select Chemicals in the Food Supply Under FDA Review.

title: FDA Advances Drug Repurposing to Address Unmet Medical Needs
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is soliciting input on drug repurposing efforts to address unmet medical needs across various diseases and conditions. The agency aims to accelerate the availability of treatments by repurposing FDA-approved drugs to identify new indications or populations. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary stated that "too many patients lack effective treatment options, even when promising science exists." The FDA is seeking information from patients, clinicians, researchers, and other stakeholders on priority disease areas and potential candidates for drug repurposing, particularly in areas with significant unmet medical need. The agency is requesting input on candidates with promising preliminary data, innovative approaches to identifying repurposing opportunities, and barriers to developing repurposed drugs.

title: FDA Grants Seventh Approval under the National Priority Voucher Pilot Program
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Bizengri (zenocutuzumab-zbco), a drug treating NRG1fusion-positive cholangiocarcinoma. This is the seventh approval under the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) pilot program. Bizengri showed an overall response rate of 36.8% in a single-arm trial of 19 patients. The drug has Breakthrough Therapy and Orphan Drug designations. Serious side effects include infusion-related reactions, interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis, and left ventricular dysfunction. The FDA granted approval to Partner Therapeutics, Inc. A public meeting will be held on June 4, 2026, to solicit feedback on the CNPV pilot program.

title: FDA Issues Guidance to Improve Collection of Pregnancy Safety Data for Drugs and Biologics
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a final guidance for industry on postapproval pregnancy safety studies. The guidance recommends various methodologies for collecting safety information after approval to better understand potential risks to pregnant patients and developing fetuses. The FDA aims to provide clear and reliable information for healthcare providers to make informed treatment decisions. The guidance describes several methods, including pregnancy registries and complementary studies, and recommends leveraging post-marketing data to generate information for drug labeling. The FDA encourages the use of this guidance in combination with established scientific standards and other relevant guidances. The final guidance is available on the FDA website.

title: FDA Expands AI Capabilities and Completes Data Platform Consolidation
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced major steps in its initiative to modernize the agency, launching Elsa 4.0, a significant upgrade to its internal AI tool, and consolidating over 40 disparate application and submission data sources into a new platform called HALO. The agency began integrating HALO and Elsa, enabling FDA staff to query data and build workflows without manual uploads. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary stated that the new capabilities empower staff, making their work streams more efficient. Jeremy Walsh, Chief AI Officer, noted that integrating AI into workflows will allow the FDA to rapidly advance regulatory science and deliver more treatments to patients faster. Elsa 4.0 features include custom agents, document generation, and enhanced search capabilities, built within a secure Google Cloud Platform environment.

title: FDA Launches One-Day Inspectional Assessments to Strengthen and Expand Oversight
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is piloting one-day inspectional assessments as part of a broader initiative to make its inspectional resources more targeted and efficient. The pilot, launched in April 2024, conducts shorter, focused screening assessments to complement standard FDA inspections. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary and Associate Commissioner Elizabeth Miller will analyze the operational and compliance data from these assessments. As of late April 2026, the FDA has completed approximately 46 one-day assessments, with most successfully confirming compliance. The pilot aims to enhance the agency's overall effectiveness, provide timely feedback to industry, and support the development of more robust risk models. The assessments will continue through fiscal year 2026 and will be evaluated using metrics such as inspection duration and the utility of findings in informing risk-based decision-making.

title: FDA Expands Market Access, Authorizes New ENDS Products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of four Glas electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS) pods containing 50mg/ml of tobacco-derived nicotine. This marks the FDA's first authorization of non-tobacco and non-menthol ENDS products. The products include Classic Menthol, Fresh Menthol, Gold, and Sapphire. Under President Trump's leadership, the FDA has authorized 11 ENDS products from American companies, which have been found to mitigate youth access with age-verification technology. The authorized products are designed for adults 21 and older and will be marketed with restrictions on advertising to adults only. The FDA has also authorized 45 ENDS products for marketing in the US, and the agency continues to enforce laws against unauthorized products targeting youth.

title: FDA Permits Expanded Access for Investigational Pancreatic Cancer Drug
body_summary: The US FDA has issued a "safe to proceed" letter to Revolution Medicines, allowing the sponsor to initiate an expanded access treatment protocol (EAP) for its experimental pancreatic cancer drug, daraxonrasib. The EAP is for patients with previously treated metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). The FDA received the expanded access request on April 28 and signed it on April 30. Commissioner Marty Makary stated that the action reflects the FDA's commitment to facilitate early access to therapies for serious conditions, including pancreatic cancer. Daraxonrasib is a RAS inhibitor designed to inhibit a protein mutated in most pancreatic cancer tumors. The company intends to submit a new drug application for daraxonrasib under the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher pilot program, to which the FDA granted a voucher in October 2025.

title: FDA Approves First Non-Antipsychotic Drug to Treat Agitation Associated with Dementia
body_summary: The US FDA has approved Auvelity, a treatment for agitation associated with dementia due to Alzheimer's disease, to treat adults. This approval is the first non-antipsychotic treatment for this condition. The drug was initially approved in 2022 to treat major depressive disorder. Agitation is a common symptom in patients with Alzheimer's disease, characterized by excessive motor activity or verbal/physical aggression. Two randomized trials found Auvelity to be efficacious in treating agitation in Alzheimer's disease. The FDA granted breakthrough therapy designation and priority review designation for this action, and approval was granted to Axsome Therapeutics.

title: FDA Proposes to Exclude Semaglutide, Tirzepatide, and Liraglutide on 503B Bulks List
body_summary: The US FDA has proposed excluding semaglutide, tirzepatide, and liraglutide from the 503B bulks list, finding no clinical need for outsourcing facilities to compound these drugs from bulk substances. The 503B list identifies bulk drug substances that outsourcing facilities can use in compounding. The FDA has evaluated nominations for these substances and did not identify a clinical need for compounding them from bulk drug substances. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary has stated that outsourcing facilities cannot lawfully compound using bulk drug substances unless there is a clear clinical need. The FDA is now inviting interested parties to submit comments on the proposal by June 29, 2026, before making a final determination.

title: Executive Order 14402—Promoting Efficiency, Accountability, and Performance in Federal Contracting
body_summary:
The President orders that the US Government should adopt best business practices to protect taxpayer dollars and achieve returns on investment. The current cost-reimbursement model is deemed inadequate and should be replaced by a fixed-price contracting model, which encourages contractors to control costs and meet deliverables to maximize profits.

The default and preferred method of procurement should be fixed-price contracts with performance-based considerations. Executive branch departments and agencies should utilize these contracts to advance cost predictability, budget discipline, and contractor accountability.

The use of non-fixed-price contracts must be justified in writing by the contracting officer to the agency head, except for contracts valued at $100 million or more, which require agency head approval. Agency heads may delegate approval to non-career employees.

The order applies to all agencies and requires semi-annual reporting on non-fixed-price contracts approved under the order. The Director of the Office of Management and Budget will issue guidance to agencies to ensure consistent implementation of the order.

The order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations. It does not create any right or benefit enforceable at law or in equity against the US Government or its entities.

title: FDA Releases Results from Largest-Ever Testing of Infant Formula in the U.S.
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has announced results from the largest and most rigorous examination of chemical contaminants in infant formula available on the US market. Most infant formula products meet a high safety standard, but even small exposures matter for newborns. The FDA tested over 300 samples, representing products sold at retail, and found most samples had undetectable or very low levels of contaminants. The agency will continue to advance formula innovation and safety, and follow up with additional testing as part of its ongoing monitoring efforts.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a solid pace. Job gains have remained low, on average, and the unemployment rate has been little changed in recent months. Inflation is elevated, in part reflecting the recent increase in global energy prices. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. Developments in the Middle East are contributing to a high level of uncertainty about the economic outlook. The Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate. In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3â1/2 to 3â3/4 percent. In considering the extent and timing of additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. The Committee is strongly committed to supporting maximum employment and returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Philip N. Jefferson; Anna Paulson; and Christopher J. Waller. Voting against this action were Stephen I. Miran, who preferred to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting; and Beth M. Hammack, Neel Kashkari, and Lorie K. Logan, who supported maintaining the target range for the federal funds rate but did not support inclusion of an easing bias in the statement at this time.

title: Implementation Note issued April 29, 2026
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on April 29, 2026: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 3.65 percent, effective April 30, 2026. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective April 30, 2026, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations at a rate of 3.75 percent. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 3.5 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Increase the System Open Market Account holdings of securities through purchases of Treasury bills and, if needed, other Treasury securities with remaining maturities of 3 years or less to maintain an ample level of reserves. Roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities. Reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency securities into Treasury bills." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 3.75 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: FDA Announces Major Steps to Implement Real-Time Clinical Trials
body_summary: The FDA has announced two major steps as part of an initiative to advance real-time clinical trials (RTCT). The agency has initiated two proof-of-concept clinical trials with AstraZeneca and Amgen, which will report endpoints and data signals to the agency in real time. The trials are part of a proposed pilot program for RTCT, which the agency will announce a Request for Information (RFI) regarding. The RFI seeks input on potential pilot program design and implementation, as well as evaluation metrics and success criteria. The FDA aims to build on these proofs-of-concept with a broader pilot program, which will enable "continuous" trials and facilitate faster drug development.

title: FDA Accelerates Action on Treatments for Serious Mental Illness Following Executive Order
body_summary: President Trump issued an Executive Order on April 18 directing the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services to accelerate access to treatments for patients with serious mental illness. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced a series of regulatory actions to support the development of serotonin-2A agonists, a class of perception-altering psychedelic medications. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. and FDA Commissioner Marty Makary stated that these medications have the potential to address the nation's mental health crisis, including conditions like treatment-resistant depression, alcoholism, and PTSD. The FDA issued national priority vouchers to companies studying Psilocybin for treatment-resistant depression, Psilocybin for major depressive disorder, and Methylone for PTSD. The agency also allowed an early phase clinical study of noribogaine hydrochloride to proceed, investigating it as a potential treatment for alcohol use disorder.

title: FDA Approves First-Ever Gene Therapy for Treatment of Genetic Hearing Loss Under National Priority Voucher Program
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Otarmeni, the first dual adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector-based gene therapy, for the treatment of pediatric and adult patients with severe-to-profound and profound sensorineural hearing loss associated with molecularly confirmed biallelic variants in the OTOF gene. The approval was issued 61 days after the Biologics License Application (BLA) filing, marking the sixth approval under the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) pilot program. Otarmeni is indicated for patients with preserved outer hair cell function and no prior cochlear implant in the same ear. The therapy delivered a functional copy of the OTOF gene to inner hair cells to restore otoferlin production and auditory signaling. Results from a single clinical trial showed 80% of evaluable patients experienced improved hearing. Common side effects included middle ear infection, nausea, dizziness, and procedural pain. The FDA granted accelerated approval to Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. and will host a public meeting on June 4, 2026, to solicit feedback on the CNPV pilot program's eligibility criteria and other aspects.

title: CMS and FDA Announce RAPID Coverage Pathway to Accelerate Patient Access to Life-Changing Medical Devices
body_summary: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) have announced the Regulatory Alignment for Predictable and Immediate Device (RAPID) coverage pathway. This pathway will expedite access to certain FDA-designated Class II and Class III Breakthrough Devices for people with Medicare. The pathway was announced by CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz and FDA Commissioner Marty Makary, who stated that aligning regulatory and coverage expectations earlier will significantly reduce delays and help beneficiaries access new, life-changing health technologies faster. The RAPID pathway allows for early engagement between the FDA, device innovators, and CMS experts, and will link manufacturers to CMS experts to understand clinical outcomes most relevant for Medicare beneficiaries. The pathway is available for certain Class II devices participating in the FDA Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program (TAP) and Class III devices regardless of participation in TAP.

title: FDA Achieves Year 1 Goals in Reducing Animal Testing in Drug Development
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has achieved its first-year goals under its April 2025 Roadmap to Reducing Animal Testing in Preclinical Safety Studies. Commissioner Marty Makary announced the achievement, stating that the agency aims to replace animal testing with more precise ways of predicting drug safety in humans. The FDA has made progress in reducing research and development costs, which will lower drug prices for Americans. To address the limitations of animal testing, the agency is advancing the use of new approach methodologies, including advanced in vitro systems, computational modeling, and human-derived platforms. The FDA has released a follow-up report outlining its progress and next steps. Since issuing the roadmap, the agency has released draft guidance on reducing or eliminating nonhuman primate testing, updated guidance on endotoxin testing, and launched a searchable database clarifying alternative methods. The FDA has also deployed key infrastructure, including a permanent pathway for qualifying innovative drug development tools and a formal partnership with the National Institutes of Health.

title: Executive Order 14401—Accelerating Medical Treatments for Serious Mental Illness
body_summary:
The President orders a policy to address the burden of suicide and serious mental illness in America. The President states that over 14 million American adults have a serious mental illness and 8 million are on prescription medication for these conditions. Suicide rates increased by 37 percent from 2000 to 2018, but decreased by 5 percent from 2018 to 2020.

The President believes that psychedelic drugs, including ibogaine compounds, show potential in clinical studies to address serious mental illnesses. The President orders the FDA to provide Commissioner's National Priority Vouchers to appropriate psychedelic drugs and to facilitate access to these drugs for eligible patients under the Right to Try Act.

The President also allocates $50 million to support state governments' programs to advance psychedelic drugs for serious mental illnesses and collaborates with the Department of Veterans Affairs and the private sector to increase clinical trial participation and data sharing.

The President initiates review of products containing Schedule I substances that have successfully completed Phase 3 clinical trials for serious mental health disorders.

title: FDA Takes Step Forward on Testosterone Therapy for Men
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is encouraging sponsors of approved testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) products to contact the agency for information on pursuing a potential new indication for low libido in men with idiopathic hypogonadism. This step follows a preliminary review of emerging evidence from published clinical literature, which suggests that TRT may be safe and effective for certain men experiencing low libido related to idiopathic hypogonadism. The agency's preliminary assessment focused on published literature of rigorous, well-controlled clinical trials. FDA is now encouraging holders of approved TRT new drug applications to contact the agency by April 30 to discuss submission of a supplemental NDA, including data needed to support an approval. Approval would require demonstration of substantial evidence of effectiveness and that the benefits outweigh the risks for the intended population.

title: FDA Issues Draft Guidance on Genome Editing Safety Standards to Advance Gene Therapy Development
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a draft guidance for sponsors seeking approval of human gene therapy products involving genome editing technologies. The guidance aims to provide standardized methods for comprehensively assessing the safety of genome editing therapies. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary and Chief Medical and Scientific Officer Vinay Prasad have emphasized the potential of genome editing to treat previously incurable genetic diseases. The draft guidance focuses on next-generation sequencing-based methods to evaluate potential safety risks associated with off-target editing and loss of genome integrity. The recommendations are intended for nonclinical studies submitted with IND applications and BLAs, and apply to both ex vivo and in vivo products. The guidance is available for public comment, with a 90-day submission period.

title: FDA Reminds More Than 2,200 Sponsors and Researchers to Disclose Trial Results
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has reminded over 2,200 medical product companies and researchers of their requirement to submit clinical trial results information to ClinicalTrials.gov. The agency aims to reduce gaps in the public record and publication bias, which obscure the true landscape of drug development outcomes. According to an internal analysis, 29.6% of studies subject to mandatory reporting requirements have no results information submitted. The FDA Commissioner, Marty Makary, emphasized the ethical obligation to make results public, and Acting Director of the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, Tracy Beth Hoeg, supported the initiative to increase the prompt publication of results information. The FDA sent messages to companies and researchers on March 30, 2026, seeking voluntary compliance, and may send Pre-Notices of Noncompliance and Notices of Noncompliance as part of risk-based compliance efforts.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on March 17-18, 2026. They discussed market developments, including concerns about AI disruptions and the conflict in the Middle East, which led to shifts in policy rate expectations and Treasury yields rising while equity prices fell. Total PCE price inflation was 2.8% in February, with core PCE inflation at 3.0%. The committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent, with one member voting against and preferring a decrease. They also approved minutes from January 27-28, 2026, and updates to the Program for Security of FOMC Information.

title: Proclamation 11020—Adjusting Imports of Pharmaceuticals and Pharmaceutical Ingredients Into the United States
body_summary: The President of the United States, Donald J. Trump, has issued a proclamation stating that pharmaceuticals and associated active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) pose a national security threat due to the US's heavy reliance on imports. The Secretary of Commerce found that disruptions to the global supply chain could threaten access to life-saving medications. The President has decided to direct negotiations with foreign governments to address this threat, imposing tariffs on patented pharmaceuticals and ingredients produced overseas. A 100% ad valorem duty rate applies to patented pharmaceuticals, while a 20% rate applies to companies committing to onshore production. Tariffs will take effect on July 31, 2026, for some companies and September 29, 2026, for others.

title: FDA Approves First New Molecular Entity Under National Priority Voucher Program
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Foundayo (orforglipron), a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, under the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher pilot program. The approval, issued 50 days after filing, represents a historic milestone as the first new molecular entity (NME) approved under the program. Foundayo is approved for adults with obesity or overweight with at least one weight-related comorbid condition, to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction long-term. The approval is the fastest since 2002 and demonstrates the agency's ability to complete national priority reviews with outstanding efficiency. The program aims to expedite approval of applications addressing critical national health priorities, with a target decision timeline of two months.

title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapy for Severe Leukocyte Adhesion Deficiency Type I
body_summary: The US FDA has approved Kresladi (marnetegragene autotemcel), the first gene therapy for severe Leukocyte Adhesion Deficiency Type I (LAD-I). Kresladi is indicated for pediatric patients with severe LAD-I due to biallelic variants in ITGB2 without an HLA-matched sibling donor. The approval is based on a single open-label, single-arm, multicenter study showing increases in neutrophil CD18 and CD11a cell surface expression at month 12 with sustained effect through month 24 post-infusion. The most common side effects included anemia, low platelet and white blood cell counts, mouth sores, and viral infections. The FDA granted accelerated approval to Rocket Pharmaceuticals, Inc. as a condition of accelerated approval, requiring post-approval studies to verify and describe the clinical benefit of Kresladi.

title: FDA Approves Drug to Treat Neurologic Manifestations of Hunter Syndrome
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Avlayah, a treatment for certain individuals with Hunter syndrome, a rare inherited disorder affecting about 500 people in the US. The FDA Commissioner, Marty Makary, stated that the approval demonstrates the agency's ability to exercise regulatory flexibility and comply with its obligation to approve drugs based on substantial evidence of effectiveness. Avlayah, an IV infusion given once weekly, is approved for treating neurologic manifestations of Hunter syndrome in pediatric patients weighing at least 5 kg. The approval was based on a surrogate endpoint: reduction of cerebrospinal fluid heparan sulfate, which the review team determined was reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit. The drug's application holder, Denali Therapeutics, is conducting a randomized clinical trial to evaluate the clinical benefit of Avlayah, with over 95% of patients enrolled.

title: FDA Schedules Public Meeting on the Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher Pilot Program
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration published a Federal Register Notice seeking public comment on the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher pilot program. A public hearing on June 4 will allow stakeholders to present information and views about the program. The program, established in June 2025, aims to address critical public health needs by providing an ultra-fast review pathway for drugs and biological products of strategic national importance. The FDA has awarded vouchers for 18 products and granted four approvals, including two for oncology drugs delivered 44 and 55 days after filing. Companies that receive a national priority voucher must align with one or more national health priorities and are issued a nontransferable voucher entitling them to expedited FDA review. The program features expedited pre-filing, enhanced pre-submission engagement, and a multidisciplinary review approach. The FDA is soliciting written comments until June 29 and requests public feedback on the program's eligibility criteria, voucher selection processes, and other aspects of implementation.

title: FDA Approves Fourth Product Under National Priority Voucher Program, Higher Dose Semaglutide
body_summary: The US FDA approved a new higher dose (7.2 mg) of Wegovy (semaglutide) injection for weight loss and long-term weight maintenance in certain adult patients. This is the fourth approval under the Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher pilot program, granted just 54 days after filing. Wegovy HD is a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist indicated to reduce excess body weight and maintain weight reduction in adults with obesity or overweight with at least one weight-related condition. The approval was supported by clinical data showing additional average weight reduction with a safety profile consistent with known side effects. Common adverse reactions include gastrointestinal issues and altered skin sensation, which occurred more frequently at the higher dose. The FDA granted the approval to Novo Nordisk, which will benefit from the Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher pilot program, which aims to expedite approval of applications addressing critical national health priorities.
