title: FDA Releases Draft Guidance on Alternatives to Animal Testing in Drug Development
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a draft guidance to help drug developers validate new approach methodologies (NAMs) to replace animal testing in drug development. The guidance aims to bring safe and effective drugs to market sooner using human-centric data. The FDA's commitment to reducing animal testing is reflected in the draft guidance, which describes general recommendations for validating NAMs. 

HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. stated that the draft guidance advances the FDA's commitment to replace animal testing with human-relevant methods. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary emphasized the need for modern alternatives to animal testing, citing technological advances that can move beyond animal testing. 

Examples of NAMs include in vitro studies, three-dimensional models, and computer simulations. The draft guidance establishes four core validation principles for NAMs: Context of Use, Human Biological Relevance, Technical Characterization, and Fit-for-Purpose. The FDA encourages drug developers to consult with the appropriate review division when considering NAMs.

title: Executive Order 14395—Establishing the Task Force To Eliminate Fraud
body_summary: The President has ordered a national strategy to stop fraud, waste, and abuse in Federal benefit programs. A Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, led by the Vice President, has been established to improve eligibility verification, prevent improper payments, and disrupt fraud networks. The Task Force aims to facilitate information sharing, evaluate fraud indicators, and investigate mechanisms of fraud. The President will receive frequent updates from the Task Force, and agencies must submit transactions and processes susceptible to fraud for review within 30 days.

title: FDA Launches New Adverse Event Look-Up Tool
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has launched a new unified platform for analyzing adverse event reports called the FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS). The system represents a major achievement in the agency's mission to modernize and provide transparency into the safety of regulated products. The new platform will display adverse event reports for drugs, biologics, vaccines, cosmetics, and animal food in a single streamlined dashboard. The FDA expects to save approximately $120 million over the next five years by adopting AEMS. The system will replace legacy systems such as FAERS, VAERS, AERS, MAUDE, HFCS, and CTPAE, which will be decommissioned. The new system will be fully operational by the end of May 2026, and will contain real-time adverse event reports for all FDA-regulated products.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Patients with Cerebral Folate Transport Deficiency
body_summary: The US FDA approved expanded use of Wellcovorin (leucovorin calcium) tablets for treating cerebral folate deficiency in adult and pediatric patients with a confirmed variant in the folate receptor 1 gene. This action reflects the agency's commitment to accelerating cures and expanding treatment options for patients with serious and unmet needs. The approval was based on a systematic review of published literature, including case reports and mechanistic data. Cerebral folate deficiency is a neurological condition affecting folate transport into the brain, often causing severe developmental delays, movement disorders, seizures, and other neurological complications. The FDA collaborated with GSK on updating the labeling to include essential scientific information for the safe and effective use of the drug. The approval demonstrates the FDA's commitment to rapidly identifying effective treatments for ultra-rare diseases while maintaining evidentiary standards. Possible side effects of leucovorin include itching, rash, hives, dyspnea, rigors, and impaired thermoregulation, with anaphylaxis requiring immediate medical attention.

title: FDA Takes Further Steps to Streamline Biosimilar Development and Make Medicines More Affordable
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced new draft guidance to streamline the development of biosimilar medicines. The agency recommends streamlining unnecessary clinical pharmacokinetic testing when scientifically justified, which could save biosimilar developers up to 50% of their PK study costs, or approximately $20 million, and help lower drug costs. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary stated that streamlining biosimilar development reflects the agency's commitment to lowering drug costs for everyday Americans.

The new draft guidance builds on a prior FDA effort in October, where Commissioner Makary announced another draft guidance reducing certain unnecessary comparative efficacy studies. The guidance aims to inform prospective applicants and facilitate the development of proposed biosimilars and proposed interchangeable biosimilars.

The FDA has approved 82 biosimilars to date, providing Americans with additional affordable treatment options for conditions such as cancer, rheumatoid arthritis, diabetes, Crohn’s disease, and osteoporosis.

title: FDA Holds Meeting with States on Importation of Lower Cost Drugs
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration held a meeting with several states to discuss the Section 804 importation program, which allows states and Indian tribes to import certain prescription drugs from Canada to reduce costs. The meeting aimed to make it easier for interested states to obtain authorization without compromising safety or quality. Representatives from HHS and the National Academy for State Health Policy participated. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary stated that the agency is committed to lowering prescription drug prices for Americans. The FDA has been offering states and tribes the opportunity to submit draft SIP proposals for pre-review and providing assistance with cost savings analysis and quality assurance. A quality assurance tool was launched in January 2026 to help sponsors prepare compliant SIP proposals. Presentations from the meeting are available for download.

title: FDA Grants Third Approval Under the National Priority Voucher Program
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved teclistamab in combination with daratumumab hyaluronidase-fihj (Tec-Dara) for adult patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma who have received at least one prior line of therapy. This decision marks the third approval under the Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher (CNPV) pilot program, issued 55 days after filing. The FDA awarded a voucher for the drug combination on December 15, 2025, after a Phase 3 clinical trial study showed significant improvements over the standard of care. The study demonstrated a 83% reduction in disease progression or death compared to the standard of care control arm. The CNPV program aims to expedite approval of applications addressing critical national health priorities. The FDA also approved the drug combination for patients with relapsed refractory multiple myeloma, confirming existing indication of teclistamab-cqyv used as monotherapy. The approval was granted to Janssen Biotech, Inc.

title: FDA to Address Unused Opioids in American Homes
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a Request for Information (RFI) to gather public comment on potential new standards for in-home opioid disposal products. The agency is considering requiring opioid sponsors to make available in-home disposal systems to combat the opioid crisis. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary has stated that unused opioids at home can pose a significant risk to those struggling with opioids.

Currently, the FDA recommends dropping off unused opioids at a drug take-back location or mailing them back using a pre-paid envelope. A 2017 study found that flushing unused opioids presents a negligible eco-toxicological risk. The RFI seeks input from industry, healthcare providers, and advocates on appropriate criteria for in-home disposal kits. Responses to the RFI are due by April 6, 2026, and interested parties are invited to submit comments.

title: FDA Warns 30 Telehealth Companies Against Illegal Marketing of Compounded GLP-1s
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued 30 warning letters to telehealth companies for making false or misleading claims about compounded GLP-1 products offered on their websites. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary stated that the agency is taking swift action against misleading claims being made by telehealth and pharma companies. The letters address primary violations including claims implying sameness with FDA-approved products and obscuring product sourcing. Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved, meaning the agency does not review their safety, effectiveness, or quality before marketing.

title: FDA Grants Second Approval under the National Priority Voucher Pilot Program
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the lung cancer drug Hernexeos (zongertinib) as part of the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) pilot program. The application was filed on January 13, 2026, and a final decision was rendered 44 days later. Hernexeos targets molecular alterations in non-small cell lung cancers (NSCLC) and has been approved for adults with unresectable or metastatic non-squamous NSCLC whose tumors have HER2 (ERBB2) tyrosine kinase domain activating mutations. The CNPV pilot program seeks to expedite approval of applications addressing critical national health priorities. Hernexeos was granted Breakthrough Therapy and Priority Review designations and was proactively granted a national priority voucher by the FDA on November 6, 2025.

title: FDA Launches Framework for Accelerating Development of Individualized Therapies for Ultra-Rare Diseases
body_summary: The US FDA has issued draft guidance for sponsors seeking approval for targeted individualized therapies, focusing on genome editing and RNA-based therapies for ultra-rare diseases. The draft guidance, developed by the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research and Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, outlines a "Plausible Mechanism Framework" for therapies that target a specific genetic, cellular, or molecular abnormality. Key criteria include identifying the disease-causing abnormality, demonstrating the therapy targets the root cause, and relying on well-characterized natural history data. The guidance aims to remove barriers and exercise regulatory flexibility to encourage scientific advances and deliver more cures and meaningful treatments for patients suffering from rare diseases. The draft guidance is open for public comment, with a submission deadline of 60 days.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A joint meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) and the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System was held on January 27-28, 2026. The FOMC selected Jerome H. Powell as Chair, John C. Williams as Vice Chair, and Joshua Gallin as Secretary. They also approved various policies and reaffirmed existing ones. The Committee expected the Federal Reserve's balance sheet to increase until early April due to reserve management purchases, then drop sharply as tax revenues flow into the Treasury General Account. Real GDP continued to expand in 2025, labor market conditions stabilized, and consumer price inflation remained elevated. The January Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey on Bank Lending Practices suggested a slight easing in lending standards for commercial real estate and consumer loans. Credit performance was stable but weaker than pre-pandemic levels. The staff assessed the US financial system's stability, noting vulnerabilities due to asset valuation pressures, corporate debt growth, and leverage in the financial sector. The Committee voted to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent.

title: FDA Approves Labeling Changes to Menopausal Hormone Therapy Products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved labeling changes for six menopausal hormone therapy products to clarify risk considerations. The changes include removing risk statements related to cardiovascular disease, breast cancer, and probable dementia from the "boxed warning." This decision reflects the agency's commitment to follow the science and provide accurate information to women. The FDA initiated the removal of these warnings in November 2025, following a comprehensive review of the scientific literature. The labeling changes will help women make well-informed medical decisions about their treatment plan for menopause symptoms.

title: FDA Approves First-of-Its-Kind Device to Treat Pancreatic Cancer
body_summary: The US FDA has approved a first-of-its-kind device for treating adult patients with locally advanced pancreatic cancer. Optune Pax, developed by Novocure, is a portable, non-invasive device that delivers alternating electrical fields to the abdomen, targeting rapidly dividing cancer cells. The device, which works by physically disrupting cancer cell growth, was approved through the premarket approval pathway. The FDA Commissioner, Marty Makary, and the Center for Devices and Radiological Health Director, Michelle Tarver, have stated that this approval provides a novel, non-invasive approach for expanding access to cancer care. The therapy is administered through adhesive patches placed on the patient's skin and connected to an electric field generator, and the device was approved based on data from a pivotal clinical study that showed improved Overall Survival by approximately two months compared to standard of care chemotherapies.

title: FDA Launches Assessment of BHA, a Common Food Chemical Preservative
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has launched a comprehensive re-assessment of butylated hydroxyanisole (BHA), a chemical preservative used in food. The review considers BHA's safety under its current conditions of use. The FDA has issued a Request for Information on the use and safety of BHA as part of its broader efforts to proactively review chemical additives. BHA was previously listed as Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS) in 1958 and approved as a food additive in 1961. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. stated that the reassessment marks the end of the "trust us" era in food safety. The FDA plans to remove BHA from the food supply if it cannot meet today's gold-standard science for its current uses.

title: Joint Statement by the United States and Bangladesh on Reaching an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade
body_summary:
The United States and Bangladesh have agreed to an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade to strengthen their bilateral economic relationship. The Agreement will provide unprecedented access to each other's markets. 

Bangladesh commits to provide significant preferential market access for U.S. industrial and agricultural goods, including chemicals, medical devices, machinery, and energy products. The United States will reduce tariff rates on certain goods from Bangladesh. 

The United States and Bangladesh commit to addressing non-tariff barriers, such as accepting vehicles built to U.S. Federal motor vehicle safety and emissions standards, and removing import restrictions on U.S. remanufactured goods. 

Bangladesh commits to protecting internationally recognized labor rights, adopting and implementing high levels of environmental protection, and strengthening intellectual property protection. 

The Agreement also includes provisions on geographical indications and strengthening economic and national security alignment to enhance supply chain resilience and innovation.

title: FDA Intends to Take Action Against Non-FDA-Approved GLP-1 Drugs
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is taking steps to restrict GLP-1 active pharmaceutical ingredients in non-FDA-approved compounded drugs being mass-marketed by companies like Hims & Hers. The FDA aims to safeguard consumers from drugs with unverified quality, safety, and efficacy. The agency is also cracking down on misleading direct-to-consumer advertising and marketing. Companies must avoid claiming non-FDA-approved compounded products are generic or the same as FDA-approved drugs, or stating they use the same active ingredient or are clinically proven. The FDA will use compliance and enforcement tools to address unsubstantiated claims and associated public health concerns.

title: FDA Takes New Approach to "No Artificial Colors" Claims
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has taken steps to support the transition of the nation's food supply from artificial petroleum-based colors to alternatives derived from natural sources. Companies can now claim products contain 'no artificial colors' even if they don't contain petroleum-based colors. The agency approved beetroot red and expanded the use of spirulina extract, a natural color additive. This brings the total number of new food color options approved under the current administration to six. The FDA is working to phase out the use of petroleum-based colors from the nation's food supply, with ongoing progress being tracked by the agency.

title: FDA Launches PreCheck Pilot Program to Strengthen Domestic Pharmaceutical Manufacturing
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) began accepting requests to participate in the FDA PreCheck pilot program, designed to strengthen the domestic pharmaceutical supply chain. The program aims to increase regulatory predictability, facilitate manufacturing site construction, and streamline assessments. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary stated that the program is one of several incentives to make the U.S. pharmaceutical manufacturing sector more resilient and competitive. The agency will select an initial cohort of new facilities based on alignment with national priorities, including products to be manufactured, timeline, and innovation. The program consists of two phases: a Facility Readiness Phase and an Application Submission Phase, with the first cohort to begin conducting PreCheck activities in 2026.

title: Executive Order 14379—Addressing Addiction Through the Great American Recovery Initiative
body_summary: President Donald J. Trump has ordered a national effort to prioritize addiction treatment and recovery. The White House Great American Recovery Initiative will be co-chaired by the Secretary of Health and Human Services and the Senior Advisor for Addiction Recovery. The initiative aims to create stronger coordination across government, the healthcare sector, faith communities, and the private sector to save lives, restore families, and strengthen communities. The initiative will consist of various officials, including the Attorney General, the Secretary of Education, and the Director of National Drug Control Policy. The President has established the initiative to address the disease of addiction, a crisis that touches families in every community and neighborhood in the United States.

title: Implementation Note issued January 28, 2026
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on January 28, 2026: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 3.65 percent, effective January 29, 2026. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective January 29, 2026, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations at a rate of 3.75 percent. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 3.5 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Increase the System Open Market Account holdings of securities through purchases of Treasury bills and, if needed, other Treasury securities with remaining maturities of 3 years or less to maintain an ample level of reserves. Roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities. Reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency securities into Treasury bills." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 3.75 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Available indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a solid pace. Job gains have remained low, and the unemployment rate has shown some signs of stabilization. Inflation remains somewhat elevated. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. Uncertainty about the economic outlook remains elevated. The Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate. In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3â1/2 to 3â3/4 percent. In considering the extent and timing of additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. The Committee is strongly committed to supporting maximum employment and returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Beth M. Hammack; Philip N. Jefferson; Neel Kashkari; Lorie K. Logan; and Anna Paulson. Voting against this action were Stephen I. Miran and Christopher J. Waller, who preferred to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.

title: FDA ImportShield Program Delivers Impressive Results in Strengthening FDA Oversight at U.S. Ports of Entry
body_summary: The US FDA has announced its initial review of the effectiveness of the FDA ImportShield Program, which was launched in August 2025 to modernize the review of imported products. In four months, FISP increased processing speed by 66%, boosted monthly volume capacity by 33%, and reduced staff hours by 20%. The program, which streamlines the FDA's import review process, provides consistent oversight across all US ports of entry. The FDA Commissioner, Marty Makary, and Associate Commissioner, Elizabeth Miller, have praised the program for improving efficiency and accountability in import decision-making. The FDA is also pursuing comprehensive technology modernization, including an advanced review platform system, to tackle the growing import review workload.

title: FDA Takes Steps to Improve Gluten Ingredient Disclosure in Foods
body_summary: The Food and Drug Administration is extending the comment period on a Request for Information regarding labeling and preventing cross-contact of gluten in packaged food. Comments must be submitted electronically or in writing by April 22, 2026.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Children With Menkes Disease
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Zycubo (copper histidinate) injection as the first treatment for Menkes disease in pediatric patients. Children with Menkes disease will have an FDA-approved treatment option and the potential to live longer. The FDA evaluated Zycubo in two open-label clinical trials in pediatric patients treated for up to three years. Overall survival was assessed, with children who began treatment within four weeks of birth having a 78% reduction in the risk of death compared to untreated patients. Nearly half of early-treated patients survived beyond six years, and some survived more than 12 years. Zycubo is a copper replacement therapy given by subcutaneous injection and was approved for Sentynl Therapeutics.

title: FDA Issues Guidance on Modernizing Statistical Methods for Clinical Trials
body_summary: The US FDA has published a draft guidance to facilitate the use of Bayesian methodologies in clinical trials of drugs and biologics. The guidance aims to help drug developers make better use of available data, conduct more efficient clinical trials, and deliver safe and effective treatments to patients sooner. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary stated that Bayesian methodologies can help address high costs and long timelines in drug development. The guidance provides recommendations on the appropriate use of Bayesian methods, with an emphasis on supporting primary inference. The publication is intended to satisfy the FDA's commitment in the Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) VII. The FDA is seeking public comment on the draft guidance.

title: FDA Increases Flexibility on Requirements for Cell and Gene Therapies to Advance Innovation
body_summary: The FDA is sharing information about its flexible approach to overseeing chemistry, manufacturing, and control (CMC) requirements for cell and gene therapies (CGT). Commissioner Marty Makary, M.D., M.P.H., and Vinay Prasad, M.D., M.P.H., stated that regulatory flexibility is necessary for CGTs. The FDA's Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER) has approved around 50 CGTs in the last decade. CBER has implemented regulatory flexibilities to accommodate the unique characteristics of CGTs, while maintaining quality standards. The agency aims to expedite product development across the CGT field. In June, the FDA hosted a Cell and Gene Therapy Roundtable to discuss advancing the field.

title: The President's News Conference in Palm Beach, Florida
body_summary: US President announced a successful military operation in Venezuela, capturing and indicting dictator Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores for their campaign of deadly narcoterrorism. The operation resulted in the death of Maduro and the extraction of the Maduro pair with no US loss of life. Over 150 aircraft were involved. Maduro had been indicted in the US and was a fugitive with a $50 million bounty. The US aims to rebuild the oil infrastructure, pay billions in oil company profits, and ensure proper governance.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary:
Here is the final summary of the source document:

The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on December 9-10, 2025. The committee discussed market developments and inflation risks, with participants generally judging that risks remained tilted to the upside but noting decreased upside risks. They emphasized maintaining well-anchored longer-run inflation expectations to return inflation to 2% in a timely manner. The labor market showed signs of softening, with some indicators pointing to continued weakening, while others suggested stability. Most participants viewed risks to employment as tilted to the downside. In response to rising downside risks to employment since mid-2025, the committee lowered the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent, with nine members voting in favor and three against.

title: FDA Finds Insufficient Data to Determine Safety of PFAS in Cosmetic Products
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) released a congressionally mandated report on the use of perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in cosmetic products. The report, under the Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022, evaluates available scientific evidence on potential safety concerns. The FDA found that toxicological data for most PFAS are incomplete or unavailable, leaving significant uncertainty about consumer safety. The agency evaluated 25 of the most frequently used PFAS, representing 96% of PFAS added to cosmetic products, and found that five PFAS appeared to present low safety concerns. However, the safety of most PFAS could not be definitively established, and one PFAS was identified as having a potential safety concern with significant remaining uncertainty. The FDA will continue to monitor emerging scientific data and devote additional resources to address data gaps.

title: FDA Grants Two National Priority Vouchers
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has awarded national priority vouchers to two investigational products: Enlicitide decanoate, an oral PCSK9 inhibitor, and Sacituzumab Tirumotecan, a TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugate. The vouchers aim to increase access to these products through affordability for American patients. This is the 18th product to receive a voucher under the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher pilot program, established in June 2025. The program aims to address key national priorities, including improving access and affordability of healthcare. Voucher recipients receive enhanced communications with review staff and review decisions are targeted for completion within 1-2 months.

title: FDA Explores New Contracting Approach to Advance Public Health Innovation
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a Request for Information (RFI) to gather input from venture capital firms on a new contracting approach to strengthen collaboration between the agency and innovative companies. The FDA aims to harness the talent of American innovators, rather than relying on middlemen and D.C. insiders. The proposed contract model creates direct relationships with qualified venture capital firms, enabling companies with an approved firm's portfolio to compete for and receive task orders. The RFI requests feedback on qualification criteria, financial and administrative considerations, intellectual property protections, and regulatory compliance frameworks. Responses to the RFI are due by 2 p.m. EST on Jan 18, 2026, and are open to all interested parties, with a focus on venture capital firms.

title: Executive Order 14370—Increasing Medical Marijuana and Cannabidiol Research
body_summary:
By the authority vested in me as President, it is hereby ordered: Americans deserve access to the best medical treatments and research infrastructure in the world. In 2023, the FDA found scientific support for marijuana's use to treat anorexia, nausea and vomiting, and pain. Chronic pain affects nearly 1 in 4 United States adults and more than 1 in 3 United States seniors.

In 2023, the Department of Health and Human Services recommended to the Drug Enforcement Agency that marijuana be controlled under Schedule III of the CSA. The recommendation included a determination that medical marijuana has a currently accepted medical use, based on over 30,000 licensed healthcare practitioners and credible scientific support.

The National Institute on Drug Abuse concurred with the FDA's recommendation. In May 2024, the Department of Justice issued a proposed rule to reschedule marijuana to Schedule III. The Federal Government's long delay in recognizing the medical use of marijuana has impeded research and limited access to patients and doctors.

It is the policy of my Administration to increase medical marijuana and CBD research to better inform patients and doctors. I direct the Attorney General to complete the rulemaking process related to rescheduling marijuana to Schedule III of the CSA. I also instruct the Assistant to the President and Deputy Chief of Staff for Legislative, Political, and Public Affairs to work with Congress to update the statutory definition of hemp-derived cannabinoid products.

This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations. The costs for publication of this order shall be borne by the Department of Health and Human Services.

title: FDA Takes Action to Improve Recall Effectiveness Following Infant Botulism Outbreak Investigation Linked to ByHeart Infant Formula
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration reminded industry of its legal responsibilities under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act regarding food recalls. The FDA called for industry to increase adoption of best practices in recall implementation, especially for recalls involving foods for vulnerable populations. Last week, the FDA sent warning letters to several major retailers for failing to remove recalled ByHeart infant formula from store shelves. The FDA investigated recalls and found that recalled infant formula continued to be found on store shelves in over 175 locations across 36 states for over three weeks. The FDA Commissioner, Marty Makary, stated that food safety is a shared responsibility and that retailers must play a crucial role in removing unsafe products from store shelves. The FDA asked retailers to respond to the warning letters within 15 days stating the specific steps they have taken to address any violations and prevent recurrence.

title: FDA Eliminates Major Barrier to Using Real-World Evidence in Drug and Device Application Reviews
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has removed a key limitation on the use of real-world evidence (RWE) in drug and device applications reviews. The agency will now accept RWE without requiring identifiable individual patient data, allowing consideration of strong RWE on an application-by-application basis. This change responds to the position of sponsors and data scientists that meaningful information can be extracted from large databases without private individual information. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary stated that this reform will unlock access to vast databases, including cancer and cystic fibrosis registries, to get life-changing treatments to patients faster.

title: FDA Proactively Awards National Priority Voucher Based on Strong Phase 3 Study Results
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has awarded a national priority voucher to teclistamab in combination with daratumumab for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma. This is the 16th product to receive an award under the Commissioner's National Priority Voucher pilot program. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary announced that the agency aims to deliver more cures and meaningful treatments to the American people. After reviewing Phase 3 clinical trial data released on November 24, the FDA swiftly contacted the company to discuss the national priority voucher. The trial data showed significant improvements over the standard of care in progression-free survival and overall survival among patients with one to three prior lines of therapy. Over 80% of recipients remained free of progression at three years. The CNPV pilot program accelerates the review of products addressing key national priorities, including public health crises, innovative cures, and affordability.

title: FDA Approves Two Oral Therapies to Treat Gonorrhea
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved two new oral medicines to treat gonorrhea. Nuzolvence (zoliflodacin) granules, approved for adults and children 12 years and older weighing at least 77 pounds, and Blujepa (gepotidacin) oral tablets, approved for patients 12 years and older weighing at least 99 pounds, were approved to treat uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhea. The medicines were tested in clinical studies and showed comparable effectiveness to the standard treatment. The FDA granted Fast Track, Qualified Infectious Disease Product, and Priority Review designations for both medicines. The approval marks a significant milestone for treatment options for patients with uncomplicated urogenital gonorrhea, caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

title: FDA Proposes Expanding Sunscreen Active Ingredient List
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is proposing to add bemotrizinol as a permitted active ingredient for use in sunscreens. Bemotrizinol provides protection against both ultraviolet A and B rays, has low levels of absorption, and rarely causes skin irritation. If finalized, bemotrizinol will be an additional sunscreen active ingredient generally recognized as safe and effective for use by adults and children 6 months of age and older, expanding consumer choice. The FDA is seeking public comments on this proposed order.

title: Implementation Note issued December 10, 2025
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on December 10, 2025: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to lower the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 3.65 percent, effective December 11, 2025. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective December 11, 2025, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations at a rate of 3.75 percent. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 3.5 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Increase the System Open Market Account holdings of securities through purchases of Treasury bills and, if needed, other Treasury securities with remaining maturities of 3 years or less to maintain an ample level of reserves. Roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities. Reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency securities into Treasury bills." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve a 1/4 percentage point decrease in the primary credit rate to 3.75 percent, effective December 11, 2025. In taking this action, the Board approved requests to establish that rate submitted by the Boards of Directors of the Federal Reserve Banks of New York, Philadelphia, St. Louis, and San Francisco. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Available indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace. Job gains have slowed this year, and the unemployment rate has edged up through September. More recent indicators are consistent with these developments. Inflation has moved up since earlier in the year and remains somewhat elevated. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. Uncertainty about the economic outlook remains elevated. The Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate and judges that downside risks to employment rose in recent months. In support of its goals and in light of the shift in the balance of risks, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-1/2 to 3â3/4 percent. In considering the extent and timing of additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. The Committee is strongly committed to supporting maximum employment and returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. The Committee judges that reserve balances have declined to ample levels and will initiate purchases of shorter-term Treasury securities as needed to maintain an ample supply of reserves on an ongoing basis. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Susan M. Collins; Lisa D. Cook; Philip N. Jefferson; Alberto G. Musalem; and Christopher J. Waller. Voting against this action were Stephen I.
