Schmid, who preferred no change to the target range for the federal funds rate at this meeting.

title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapy Treatment for Wiskott-Aldrich Syndrome
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Waskyra (etuvetigene autotemcel), the first cell-based gene therapy, for the treatment of Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome (WAS) in pediatric patients six months and older and adults with the condition. The approval is based on substantial and sustained clinical benefit in 27 patients with severe WAS, with significant reductions in severe infections and bleeding events. The treatment, which uses the patient's own genetically corrected hematopoietic stem cells, restores functional WAS protein expression in affected cells. The most common side effects include rash, respiratory tract infection, and liver injury. The FDA has granted Orphan Drug, Rare Pediatric Disease, and Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy designations to Fondazione Telethon ETS, a non-profit applicant, for the approval of Waskyra.

title: First Approval in Commissioner's National Priority Voucher Pilot Program Strengthens Domestic Antibiotic Manufacturing Capacity
body_summary: The document was updated on December 10, 2025, to include the name of the sponsor.

title: FDA Approves First Cellular Therapy to Treat Patients with Severe Aplastic Anemia
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Omisirge (omidubicel-onlv), the first hematopoietic stem cell transplant therapy to treat patients with severe aplastic anemia (SAA). Omisirge is indicated for adults and pediatric patients six years and older with SAA following reduced intensity conditioning and for whom a compatible donor is not available. The approval is based on an ongoing, open-label, prospective, single arm study evaluating use of Omisirge in patients six years and older with severe aplastic anemia. The study showed that Omisirge provided early and sustained neutrophil engraftment in 12 of 14 patients, with a median time to neutrophil recovery of 11 days. The most common side effects associated with Omisirge include febrile neutropenia, viral and bacterial infections, hyperglycemia, and pneumonia. The FDA granted approval of Omisirge to Gamida Cell Ltd.

title: FDA Launches TEMPO: A First-of-Its-Kind Digital Health Pilot to Expand Access to Chronic Disease Technologies
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced the Technology-Enabled Meaningful Patient Outcomes (TEMPO) for Digital Health Devices Pilot, a voluntary pilot to promote access to certain digital health devices while safeguarding patient safety. The pilot will evaluate a risk-based enforcement approach for digital health devices intended to improve patient outcomes in cardio-kidney-metabolic, musculoskeletal, and behavioral health conditions.

The pilot is in collaboration with the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Innovation Center and will help the FDA and CMS better understand how digital health technologies perform in real-life settings. Participating manufacturers will offer devices for an intended use, collecting and reporting real-world performance data.

The pilot supports CMS's ACCESS Model, which aims to increase beneficiary access to technology-enabled, integrated care. The FDA plans to select up to 40 manufacturers in four clinical use areas to participate in the pilot, with the first applications for participation due in January 2026.

The TEMPO pilot aligns with the rapid and iterative nature of digital health development and aims to expand patient access to innovative technologies. Devices included in the pilot may be intended for conditions such as prediabetes, back strain, and depression. The pilot is a key component of the FDA's Home as a Health Care Hub initiative, which seeks to improve outcomes and reduce the burden of chronic disease.

title: FDA Approves First CAR T-Cell Therapy for Marginal Zone Lymphoma In the US
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Breyanzi (Lisocabtagene maraleucel) as the first Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy in the U.S. for treatment of adults with marginal zone lymphoma (MZL) who have failed treatment with or relapsed after two or more prior lines of therapy. The approval represents a major advancement in precision medicine, according to Vinay Prasad, M.D., M.P.H. Chief Medical and Scientific Officer and Director of the FDA’s Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research. The therapy, which genetically engineers a patient’s own T-cells to target and kill cancer cells, showed a high and durable response rate in patients with MZL, with almost half experiencing progression within two years of diagnosis. The safety and effectiveness of Breyanzi were evaluated in a single-arm trial, which found 95.5% of patients experienced a response to treatment. The most common adverse reactions were cytokine release syndrome, diarrhea, fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, and headache. Breyanzi was granted Priority Review and Orphan Drug designation for this application, and traditional approval was granted to Juno Therapeutics, Inc.

title: FDA Conditionally Approves Topical Drug for Cattle for New World Screwworm and Cattle Fever Tick
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has conditionally approved Exzolt Cattle-CA1 (fluralaner) topical solution for preventing and treating New World screwworm (NWS) larval infestations and treating cattle fever tick in beef cattle 2 months of age and older and replacement dairy heifers less than 20 months of age. This approval was granted due to the product's safety and effectiveness for its intended use. The sponsor, Intervet, Inc., has 5 years to generate additional effectiveness data to support a full FDA approval. The FDA has also established a 98-day slaughter withdrawal period to ensure human food safety.

title: FDA Approves Nerve Scaffold for the Treatment of Sensory Nerve Discontinuity
body_summary: The US FDA has approved Avance, an acellular nerve allograft, for surgical implantation. Avance is approved for sensory nerve discontinuities of ≤25mm in adults and pediatric patients over one month old, and also for larger sensory nerve discontinuities, motor and mixed nerve discontinuities under the Accelerated Approval pathway. Avance was studied in patients with sensory nerve discontinuities and additional investigations of mixed and motor nerve discontinuities. The approval is based on the study's results, which showed Avance's statistical non-inferiority to comparator nerve cuffs in restoring sensory function. Common adverse reactions reported include procedural pain and increased sensitivity to sensory stimuli. FDA approval was granted to Axogen Corporation, subject to the requirement of confirmatory clinical trials.

title: FDA Announces Leadership Appointments at Center for Drug Evaluation and Research
body_summary: The FDA appointed Tracy Beth Høeg, M.D., Ph.D., as acting director of the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER). Dr. Høeg, a physician and epidemiologist, previously served as Senior Advisor for Clinical Sciences at the FDA. She has a background in medicine and public health, having completed her education at the Medical College of Wisconsin, University of Copenhagen, and University of California, Davis. Dr. Høeg has co-authored 45 peer-reviewed publications. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary, M.D., M.P.H., praised Dr. Høeg, stating she is "the right scientist" to modernize CDER. Dr. Høeg committed to transparency, honesty, and science-based decisions. The FDA also announced the appointment of Karen Murry, M.D., as director of the Office of Nonprescription Drugs, with the goal of delivering affordable over-the-counter options to the public.

title: FDA Releases Draft Guidance on Reducing Testing on Non-Human Primates for Monoclonal Antibodies
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued draft guidance outlining specific product types for which six-month non-human primate toxicity testing can be eliminated or reduced. The guidance reflects the FDA's progress in modernizing nonclinical drug evaluation to make it more efficient and reduce animal testing. The FDA will incorporate risk assessments that integrate human-relevant models into regulatory decision-making. The guidance aims to accelerate cures and meaningful treatments for Americans, reduce research and development costs, and lower drug prices. The FDA will continue to collaborate with other agencies and partners to validate and expand the use of new approach methodologies to reduce or replace animal testing. The guidance is part of the agency's roadmap to reducing animal testing in nonclinical safety studies for certain monoclonal antibodies, which was outlined in May 2012.

title: FDA Seizes 7-OH Opioids to Protect American Consumers
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, in coordination with the U.S. Department of Justice, has seized approximately 73,000 units of 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) products valued at roughly $1 million from three firms in Missouri. The seizure focused on foods and dietary supplement products containing concentrated 7-OH, which is increasingly recognized as having potential for abuse. The FDA has not approved 7-OH for medical use and considers these products adulterated. The agency worked closely with the Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services and has taken steps to protect Americans from the dangers of concentrated 7-OH products, including recommending scheduling and issuing warning letters.

title: FDA Expands Artificial Intelligence Capabilities with Agentic AI Deployment
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has deployed agentic AI capabilities for all agency employees. Agentic AI enables the creation of complex AI workflows to assist with multi-step tasks. The tool, which is optional for FDA staff, aims to improve the agency's ability to accelerate cures and meaningful treatments. The FDA has previously deployed an LLM-based tool, Elsa, voluntarily used by over 70% of staff. The new deployment will enable staff to advance the use of AI for tasks such as meeting management, pre-market reviews, and inspections. The agency is launching a two-month Agentic AI Challenge for staff to build solutions and demonstrate them at the FDA Scientific Computing Day in January 2026. The deployment is part of the agency's plan to embed AI more deeply into workflows, achieving operational efficiency.

title: FDA Approves Gene Therapy for Treatment of Spinal Muscular Atrophy
body_summary: The US FDA has approved Itvisma (onasemnogene abeparvovec-brve) for treating spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) in patients 2 years old and older with confirmed SMN1 gene mutations. Itvisma is a gene therapy using an adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector. The approval is based on substantial evidence of effectiveness from a Phase 3 study and confirmatory data on the product's mechanism of action. The active ingredient is identical to Zolgensma but formulated at a different concentration. Itvisma is administered directly to the central nervous system via a single intrathecal injection, providing a treatment with rapid onset and direct targeting of the genetic root cause of SMA. The FDA granted Fast Track, Breakthrough Therapy, and Priority Review designations, as well as Orphan Drug designation.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on October 28-29, 2025. The manager discussed market developments and corporate bond spreads increased. Investors tracked credit markets and money market conditions indicated reserve levels approaching ample. The manager recommended stopping balance sheet runoff soon to avoid intensifying money market volatility. The Committee reviewed SOMA portfolio composition, considering market functioning, macroeconomic implications, and interactions with Treasury's management of federal debt. Participants agreed to end balance sheet runoff and reinvest principal payments received on agency securities holdings into Treasury bills. Financial markets were generally strong, with foreign equity indexes moderately higher and technology stocks outperforming. Yields declined in most major advanced economies due to weak economic data. The broad dollar index increased modestly driven by US economic data. Reserve balances moved closer to ample levels. Corporate bond yields edged down, while commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) yields rose modestly. Labor market conditions were discussed, citing slower job gains and rising unemployment rate. Participants assessed downside risks to employment and favored or supported a federal funds rate reduction. The Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent.

title: FDA Pilots Faster Clarifications to Meeting Minutes
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced a pilot program to streamline communications with sponsors following formal meetings. The program provides a "Meeting Minute Clarification Opportunity" for sponsors to obtain quick clarification on responses from a single discipline. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary stated that this will spare drug developers months of guesswork and allow them to focus on delivering innovative treatments. The pilot has been in operation since October and has already provided helpful clarifications to sponsors. Agency staff aim to respond to questions via email within three business days. The program is part of the FDA's broader initiative to streamline the drug development process and improve agency interactions with sponsors.

title: FDA Approves New Safety Warning and Revised Indication that Limits Use for Elevidys Following Reports of Fatal Liver Injury
body_summary: The FDA has approved substantial labeling revisions for Elevidys, a gene therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, following reports of fatal acute liver failure in non-ambulatory patients. The revised labeling includes a Boxed Warning, limits the indication to ambulatory patients aged 4 years and older with confirmed DMD gene mutations, and adds a Limitations of Use statement. The FDA has also required the manufacturer to conduct a postmarketing observational study to assess the risk of serious liver injury. Key safety information includes weekly liver function tests, prompt medical attention for yellowing of the skin, and monitoring for cardiac injury.

title: Joint Statement by the United States, Switzerland, and Liechtenstein on Reaching a Framework for an Agreement on Fair, Balanced, and Reciprocal Trade
body_summary: The United States, Switzerland, and Liechtenstein agree to negotiate an Agreement on Fair, Balanced, and Reciprocal Trade, aiming to create a dynamic and balanced trading relationship by the first quarter of 2026. The United States and Switzerland will negotiate trade-related environmental measures, including good regulatory practices, as well as cooperation on procurement markets, digital trade, and economic security. They intend to facilitate trusted data flows, address data localization, and promote interoperability in privacy frameworks, with a focus on strengthening economic security, including review of inbound investment and supply chain resilience.

title: Joint Statement by President Trump and President Javier Gerardo Milei of Argentina on Reaching a Framework for an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade and Investment
body_summary:
President Donald J. Trump and President Javier Milei have reaffirmed the strategic alliance between the United States and Argentina, grounded in shared democratic values and a common vision for free enterprise. The two countries have agreed to a Framework to deepen bilateral trade and investment cooperation, aiming to drive long-term growth and expand opportunity. Key elements of the deal include:

Tariffs: The countries will open their markets to each other on key products, with Argentina providing preferential market access for U.S. goods exports and the U.S. removing reciprocal tariffs on certain unavailable natural resources.

Elimination of Non-Tariff Barriers: Argentina has dismantled many non-tariff barriers, including import licensing, and committed not to require consular formalities for U.S. exports.

Standards and Conformity Assessment: Argentina will align with international standards in sectors to facilitate trade, allowing U.S. goods to enter Argentina without additional conformity assessment requirements.

Intellectual Property: Argentina has taken action against counterfeit goods and committed to address structural challenges, including patentability criteria and geographical indications.

Agricultural Market Access: Argentina has opened its market to U.S. live cattle, committed to allow market access for U.S. poultry, and agreed not to restrict market access for certain cheese and meat terms.

Labor: Argentina has reaffirmed its commitment to protect internationally recognized labor rights and adopted a prohibition on the importation of goods produced by forced or compulsory labor.

Environment: Argentina has committed to take measures to combat illegal logging, encourage a more resource-efficient economy, and fully implement WTO obligations.

Economic Security Alignment: Argentina will enhance cooperation with the U.S. to combat non-market policies and practices of other countries.

Commercial Considerations and Opportunities: The two countries wil

title: Longtime FDA Innovator Appointed as Director of Center for Drug Evaluation and Research
body_summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced that Richard Pazdur, M.D., has been appointed director of the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER). Pazdur is a 26-year veteran of the FDA and a renowned regulatory innovator. He previously led initiatives such as Project Orbis, Project Facilitate, and Project Renewal, which streamlined oncology drug approvals, access, and labeling. Dr. Pazdur holds a medical degree from Loyola Stritch School of Medicine and has published over 800 articles. He will continue to serve as director of the Oncology Center of Excellence until a successor is named.

title: HHS Advances Women’s Health, Removes Misleading FDA Warnings on Hormone Replacement Therapy
body_summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services has announced the removal of broad "black box" warnings from hormone replacement therapy (HRT) products for menopause. This action follows a comprehensive review of scientific literature and a public comment period. The FDA is working with companies to update product labeling to remove references to risks of cardiovascular disease, breast cancer, and probable dementia. Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and FDA Commissioner Marty Makary made the announcement. Women have used HRT products for decades, but their use plummeted after the FDA applied boxed warnings following a Women's Health Initiative study. The FDA is not seeking to remove the boxed warning for endometrial cancer for systemic estrogen-alone products. The agency is also approving a generic version of Premarin and a non-hormonal treatment for moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms.

title: FDA Awards Second Batch of National Priority Vouchers
body_summary: The US FDA announced six additional awardees under its Commissioner's National Priority Voucher pilot program, bringing the total number of voucher recipients to 15. Commissioner Marty Makary said the program aims to accelerate review of products addressing key national priorities. Voucher holders will receive a decision within months, contingent on additional requirements. The accelerated timeline is based on a one-day "tumor board style" meeting. The selected products include Zongertinib for HER2 lung cancer, Bedaquiline for drug-resistant tuberculosis, Dostarlimab for rectal cancer, Casgevy for sickle cell disease, Orforglipron for obesity and related health conditions, and Wegovy for obesity and related health conditions.

title: FDA Warns Companies Over Illegal Marketing of Botox and Related Products
body_summary: The US FDA has issued 18 warning letters to website owners illegally marketing unapproved and misbranded botulinum toxin products, commonly known as Botox. The agency is aware of adverse events associated with these products, including botulism symptoms. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary has stated that unapproved and misbranded Botox products carry serious health risks. These products, which are injectable drugs, are used for cosmetic purposes and to treat medical conditions such as chronic migraines and muscle stiffness. Patients should only receive these products from authorized sources, licensed healthcare professionals, and ensure they are obtained from trusted providers.

title: FDA Acts to Protect Children from Unapproved Fluoride Drug Products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has announced actions to restrict the sale of unapproved ingestible fluoride prescription drug products for children. The agency intends to take enforcement action against four companies marketing these products for use in children under 3 or those at low or moderate risk for tooth decay. The FDA's intention is driven by outdated science and a desire to protect children from associated risks. The agency has published a scientific evaluation of the current use of these products, concluding that they should not be used in children under 3 or by older children not at high risk of tooth decay. The FDA has not reviewed or approved these products, despite their use since the 1940s.

title: FDA Moves to Accelerate Biosimilar Development and Lower Drug Costs
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced significant actions to make it faster and less costly to develop biosimilar medicines, which are lower-cost alternatives to biologic drugs. The agency proposes major updates to simplify biosimilarity studies and reduce unnecessary clinical testing. This effort aims to help patients and pharmacists choose lower-cost options more easily.

The FDA plans to make it easier for biosimilars to be developed as interchangeable with brand-name biologics, helping to drive market competition, expand patient options, and advance the mission to "Make America Healthy Again."

The agency has approved 76 biosimilars since 2015, but the market share remains below 20%. The FDA expects only about 10% of biologic drugs expected to lose patent protection in the next decade to currently have a biosimilar in development.

The FDA's new draft guidance aims to streamline the biosimilar development process, reduce costs, and promote efficient and effective development, while ensuring safety and effectiveness.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Available indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace. Job gains have slowed this year, and the unemployment rate has edged up but remained low through August; more recent indicators are consistent with these developments. Inflation has moved up since earlier in the year and remains somewhat elevated. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. Uncertainty about the economic outlook remains elevated. The Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate and judges that downside risks to employment rose in recent months. In support of its goals and in light of the shift in the balance of risks, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent. In considering additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. The Committee decided to conclude the reduction of its aggregate securities holdings on December 1. The Committee is strongly committed to supporting maximum employment and returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Susan M. Collins; Lisa D. Cook; Austan D. Goolsbee; Philip N. Jefferson; Alberto G. Musalem; and Christopher J. Waller. Voting against this action were Stephen I. Miran, who preferred to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point at this meeting, and Jeffrey R. Schmid, who preferred no change to the target range for the federal funds rate at this meeting.

title: Implementation Note issued October 29, 2025
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on October 29, 2025: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to lower the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 3.90 percent, effective October 30, 2025. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective October 30, 2025, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 3-3/4 to 4 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 4.0 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 3.75 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in October and November that exceeds a cap of $5 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Beginning on December 1, roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities. Reinvest the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) received in October and November that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month into Treasury securities to roughly match the maturity composition of Treasury securities outstanding. Beginning on December 1, reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency securities into Treasury bills. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve a 1/4 percentage point decrease in the primary credit rate to 4.0 percent, effective October 30, 2025. In taking this action, the Board approved requests to establish that rate submitted by the Boards of Directors of the Federal Reserve Banks of Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Richmond, Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas, and San Francisco. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Joint Statement by President Trump and Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul of Thailand on a Framework for a United States-Thailand Agreement on Reciprocal Trade
body_summary:
The United States and Thailand have agreed to a Framework for an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade to strengthen their bilateral economic relationship. The Agreement will provide both countries' exporters unprecedented access to each other's markets. Key terms include:

Thailand eliminating tariff barriers on approximately 99% of U.S. industrial and food and agricultural products. The U.S. will maintain reciprocal tariffs at 19% on originating goods of Thailand.

The U.S. and Thailand will work together to address non-tariff barriers affecting bilateral trade, including Thailand's commitment to address barriers to U.S. exports in areas such as vehicles, medical devices, and food products.

The U.S. and Thailand will finalize commitments on protecting internationally recognized labor rights, environmental protection, intellectual property, digital trade, services, and investment.

The U.S. and Thailand will also finalize commitments on addressing distortionary behaviors of state-owned enterprises and strengthening economic and national security cooperation.

Commercial deals between U.S. and Thai companies include purchases of agriculture products, energy products, and aircraft worth an estimated $2.6 billion, $5.4 billion, and $18.8 billion, respectively. Negotiations and finalization of the Agreement on Reciprocal Trade are expected to be completed in the coming weeks.

title: FDA Issues Emergency Use Authorization for New World Screwworm Drug for Dogs
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for Credelio chewable tablets to treat New World screwworm (NWS) infestations in dogs and puppies. The FDA concluded that Credelio may be effective in treating NWS and that its benefits outweigh its risks. This is the first time the FDA has issued an EUA for an animal drug. The EUA was granted after the Secretary of Health and Human Services determined that NWS presents a significant potential for a public health emergency. Credelio was originally approved in 2018 for flea and tick-related indications, but its active ingredient, lotilaner, has been associated with neurologic adverse reactions. Pet owners should consult with a veterinarian to determine whether Credelio is appropriate for their pet. The EUA will be effective until it is revoked or terminated.

title: FDA Publishes Filing Checklists to Prevent Submission Delays
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has made public filing checklists used by the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) to determine if a submitted application is complete and reviewable. The agency aims to increase transparency into FDA filing procedures and reduce the prevalence of filing deficiencies. The checklists were published in the latest update of CDER's MAPP 6025.4 Good Review Practices: Refuse to File. The move is expected to increase efficiency by eliminating preventable Refuse to File (RTF) actions. More than 200 applications to CDER have resulted in RTF notifications over the last ten years, with applications involving a new molecular entity experiencing an average delay of 426 days before re-submittal. The checklists were released by FDA Commissioner Marty Makary and Director of CDER George Tidmarsh, with the goal of ensuring transparent and accurate communication between the FDA and sponsors.

title: FDA Awards First-Ever National Priority Vouchers to Nine Sponsors
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced nine voucher recipients under the new Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) pilot program. The recipients are selected based on products addressing major national priorities such as meeting unmet medical needs, reducing healthcare utilization, or increasing medication affordability. Voucher recipients can expect a decision within 1-2 months after filing a complete application. President Trump has celebrated the FDA awarding a voucher to the infertility product Pergoveris, citing its potential to reduce costs significantly. The new CNPV process accelerates the standard review timeline by convening a multidisciplinary team to review applications concurrently. The selected products include Pergoveris for infertility, Teplizumab for Type I diabetes, and Cytisinicline for nicotine vaping addiction. The agency expects to announce more recipients in the coming months.

title: Executive Order 14356—Ensuring Continued Accountability in Federal Hiring
body_summary:
The President, by authority vested in me, hereby orders that federal hiring shall be subject to the following policies and procedures.

Within 30 days, each agency head shall establish a Strategic Hiring Committee to approve the creation or filling of vacancies, ensuring agency hiring is consistent with the national interest, needs, and the President's Administration priorities. Agencies shall submit written notice of approved hires to OPM.

Agencies shall prepare an Annual Staffing Plan within 60 days, outlining new career appointments in highest-need areas, operational efficiency improvements, and recruitment initiatives. Agencies shall submit final plans to OPM and OMB, and update plans quarterly, starting with the second quarter of the 2026 fiscal year.

The order applies to all executive departments and agencies, except for non-career positions requiring Presidential appointment, Senior Executive Service, and certain other exceptions. The Director of OPM may grant exemptions, and exemptions previously granted shall remain in effect unless withdrawn.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A Federal Open Market Committee meeting took place on September 16-17, 2025, discussing financial market developments and open market operations. The committee discussed softening labor market conditions, modest GDP growth, and elevated inflation. Participants expected inflation to remain elevated in the near term but return to 2% thereafter. They projected slower job gains and a slightly higher unemployment rate. The majority of participants supported reducing the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point, citing increased downside risks to employment and diminishing upside risks to inflation. The Committee lowered its target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 4-4.25% in response to moderation in economic growth and job gains slowing down.

title: FDA Conditionally Approves First Drug for Prevention and Treatment of New World Screwworm Infestations in Cattle
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has conditionally approved Dectomax-CA1 (doramectin injection) injectable solution for the prevention and treatment of New World screwworm larval infestations and prevention of reinfestation in cattle for 21 days. Dectomax-CA1 is eligible for conditional approval because it is intended to prevent and treat a serious disease in cattle and addresses an unmet animal health need. The FDA has determined the drug is safe and has a reasonable expectation of effectiveness. Dectomax-CA1 contains the same active ingredient as Dectomax, which is already fully approved for treatment and control of certain nematode and arthropod parasites in cattle and swine. The withdrawal period for cattle is 35 days. Dectomax-CA1 is sponsored by Zoetis.

title: A Statement From FDA Commissioner Marty Makary, M.D., M.P.H.: Encouraging Retailers to Stop Selling Illegal Vapes
body_summary: The FDA is launching an initiative to increase voluntary compliance from retailers selling vaping products in American communities. The goal is to stop the sale of illegal vaping products, mainly imported from China, that are marketed to young people with fruit or candy flavors. The FDA has identified 54% of vaping products sold nationally as illegal, containing chemicals such as formaldehyde, lead, and acrolein. The initiative will provide retailers with a list of 39 authorized e-cigarettes and 20 nicotine pouch products, access to an online database of over 17,000 tobacco products, and retailer education materials. Mailings with these resources will begin this fall.

title: FDA Authorizes Marketing of First Eyeglass Lenses to Slow Progression of Pediatric Myopia
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has authorized marketing of the Essilor Stellest eyeglass lenses to treat myopia in children aged 6 to 12, and slow its progression in this age group. The lenses have been shown to reduce myopia progression by 71% at 24 months and 53% in eye elongation, with no serious adverse events reported. The FDA granted Breakthrough Device designation in April 2021 and marketing authorization via the De Novo premarket review pathway to Essilor of America Inc. The lenses are a lower risk alternative to contact lenses, with no adverse events and a clear design.

title: FDA Removes Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS) for Caprelsa (vandetanib)
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has removed the Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS) program for Caprelsa (vandetanib), a thyroid cancer medication manufactured by Sanofi, after over a decade of oversight. The REMS program was initially required to ensure proper heart rhythm monitoring and safe use of the medication. Recent assessments reported no cases of Torsades de pointes or unexplained sudden deaths among US patients taking Caprelsa, and clinical data showed no concerning patterns of heart rhythm problems. According to Richard Pazdur, M.D., FDA Oncology Center of Excellence Director, cancer specialists now have adequate knowledge about managing heart rhythm-related risks, making the formal requirements unnecessary. Caprelsa will remain available with the same prescribing information, and healthcare providers will no longer need special certification or extra monitoring beyond standard clinical care.

title: FDA Takes Action to Make a Treatment Available for Autism Symptoms
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has initiated the approval of leucovorin calcium tablets for patients with cerebral folate deficiency (CFD), a neurological condition affecting folate transport into the brain. The FDA has conducted a systematic analysis of literature between 2009-2024 and determined that leucovorin calcium can help individuals with CFD. Commissioner Marty Makary stated that a four-fold increase in autism over two decades is tragic and that children deserve access to potential treatments. The FDA is working with GSK, the innovator of Wellcovorin, on a process to include essential scientific information for safe and effective use in adults and pediatric patients with CFD.

title: FDA Responds to Evidence of Possible Association Between Autism and Acetaminophen Use During Pregnancy
body_summary: The US FDA initiated a label change for acetaminophen to reflect evidence suggesting a possible increased risk of neurological conditions such as autism and ADHD in children when used by pregnant women. The FDA also issued a nationwide letter alerting physicians. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary stated that the precautionary principle may lead parents and doctors to avoid using acetaminophen during pregnancy, especially for low-grade fevers. However, pregnant women may still use acetaminophen in certain scenarios. Multiple large-scale cohort studies, including the Nurses' Health Study II and the Boston Birth Cohort, have found a correlation between acetaminophen use during pregnancy and subsequent diagnosis of conditions like autism and ADHD.

title: FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to First Treatment for Barth Syndrome
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted accelerated approval to Forzinity (elamipretide) injection as the first treatment for Barth syndrome, in patients weighing at least 30 kg. The FDA granted this approval based on improved strength of the muscle used to straighten the leg at the knee, which is considered reasonably likely to predict patient benefit. The approval is conditioned on a post-approval randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial to confirm patient benefit. Forzinity is administered subcutaneously once daily, and the most common side effects identified in clinical trials were mild-to-moderate injection site reactions. Stealth Biotherapeutics Inc. was granted a rare pediatric disease designation and a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that growth of economic activity moderated in the first half of the year. Job gains have slowed, and the unemployment rate has edged up but remains low. Inflation has moved up and remains somewhat elevated. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. Uncertainty about the economic outlook remains elevated. The Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate and judges that downside risks to employment have risen. In support of its goals and in light of the shift in the balance of risks, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 4 to 4â1/4 percent. In considering additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. The Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgageâbacked securities. The Committee is strongly committed to supporting maximum employment and returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Susan M. Collins; Lisa D. Cook; Austan D. Goolsbee; Philip N. Jefferson; Alberto G. Musalem; Jeffrey R. Schmid; and Christopher J. Waller. Voting against this action was Stephen I. Miran, who preferred to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point at this meeting.

title: Implementation Note issued September 17, 2025
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on September 17, 2025: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted to lower the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 4.15 percent, effective September 18, 2025. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective September 18, 2025, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 4 to 4-1/4 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 4.25 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 4 percent and with a perâcounterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $5 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: FDA Launches Real-Time Adverse Event Reporting Dashboard for Cosmetic Products
body_summary: The FDA is implementing an initiative to integrate adverse event reporting systems for medical products, devices, tobacco, food, cosmetics, and veterinary medicines into a unified system, the FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS), to improve data quality and enhance pharmacovigilance capabilities. The FDA launched the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) Public Dashboard for Cosmetic Products, an interactive tool allowing users to query real-time adverse event data on cosmetic products. The dashboard was launched on September 12, 2025, and follows the agency's modernization strategy, which includes radical transparency. The dashboard contains reports of cosmetic product adverse events, including serious adverse event reports submitted by responsible persons and healthcare professionals. Users can search, filter, and sort results by various criteria. Reports in the dashboard have not been verified by the FDA, and the data is not an indicator of the safety profile of the cosmetic product.

title: FDA Issues New Guidance to Expand Non-Opioid Options for Chronic Pain, Curb Misuse
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued draft guidance titled "Development of Non-Opioid Analgesics for Chronic Pain" to accelerate safe and effective non-opioid treatments for chronic pain. The guidance emphasizes efficient drug development approaches, focusing on trial design, patient populations, and meaningful outcomes. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary emphasized the need for alternative treatments for patients with chronic pain. The guidance outlines regulatory considerations, including establishing indications, designing clinical trials, and evaluating the effectiveness of non-opioid drugs. This guidance fulfills a mandate under the SUPPORT Act and is part of the FDA's broader strategy to address the opioid crisis, which includes requiring safety labeling changes and facilitating the development of non-opioid alternatives.

title: HHS, CBP Seize $86.5 Million Worth of Illegal E-Cigarettes in Largest-Ever Operation
body_summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, FDA, and CBP seized 4.7 million units of unauthorized e-cigarette products with an estimated retail value of $86.5 million, the largest-ever seizure of this kind. The seizures were part of a joint federal operation in Chicago to examine incoming shipments and prevent illegal e-cigarettes from entering the country. Almost all the illegal shipments originated in China. The operation was led by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. and FDA Commissioner Marty Makary, M.D., M.P.H. The FDA has authorized 39 e-cigarette products and devices that can be legally marketed and sold in the U.S. In total, the FDA and CBP have stopped over 6 million unauthorized e-cigarettes worth over $120 million from entering the country this year.

title: Memorandum on Addressing Misleading Direct-to-Consumer Prescription Drug Advertisements
body_summary: The memorandum instructs the Secretary of Health and Human Services and the Commissioner of Food and Drugs to ensure transparency and accuracy in direct-to-consumer prescription drug advertising. The FDA is tasked with enforcing the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act's prescription drug advertising provisions to provide fair, balanced, and complete information for American consumers. The action includes increasing the amount of information regarding any risks associated with the use of prescription drugs in advertisements, to the extent permitted by applicable law.

title: FDA Launches Crackdown on Deceptive Drug Advertising
body_summary:
The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and the Food and Drug Administration have announced sweeping reforms to regulate misleading direct-to-consumer pharmaceutical advertisements. The FDA is sending thousands of letters warning pharmaceutical companies to remove misleading ads and issuing approximately 100 cease-and-desist letters to companies with deceptive ads. The FDA is also initiating rulemaking to close the "adequate provision" loophole created in 1997, which has been used by drug companies to conceal critical safety risks in ads.

Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. stated that "Pharmaceutical ads hooked this country on prescription drugs" and that the agency will shut down the "pipeline of deception" and require drug companies to disclose all critical safety facts in their advertising.

The FDA is concerned that patients are not seeing a fair balance of information about drug products, and Commissioner Marty Makary, M.D., M.P.H., said that "For far too long, the FDA has permitted misleading drug advertisements, distorting the doctor-patient relationship and creating increased demand for medications regardless of clinical appropriateness."

The agency plans to use AI and other tech-enabled tools to proactively surveil and review drug ads, and will aggressively deploy its available enforcement tools to protect patients and safeguard public health.

title: FDA Launches Green List to Protect Americans from Illegal Imported GLP-1 Drug Ingredients
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has established a "green list" import alert to stop potentially dangerous GLP-1 active pharmaceutical ingredients from unverified foreign sources entering the US market. The FDA is taking steps to protect consumers from illegal GLP-1 drugs, including compounded versions of approved drugs like semaglutide and tirzepatide. The FDA has identified serious concerns with these compounded drugs, including dosing errors and adverse events. The FDA will continue to monitor the market and take enforcement actions as necessary to prevent unsafe or fraudulent GLP-1 drugs from reaching US consumers. The FDA Commissioner, Marty Makary, and the Director of the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, George Tidmarsh, have emphasized the importance of protecting public health and ensuring that all active ingredients used in GLP-1 drugs are obtained from compliant manufacturers.

title: FDA Approves Expanded Use of Vonvendi for von Willebrand Disease, Including for Certain Uses for Children
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Vonvendi, a recombinant von Willebrand factor product, for routine preventative use in adults and treatment of bleeding episodes and perioperative use in children with von Willebrand disease (VWD). The approval is based on clinical study data showing efficacy in controlling bleeding episodes and perioperative management in patients of all ages. The product also showed success in preventing bleeding episodes in adults with VWD. This is the first recombinant VWF product approved for pediatric patients in the US. The approval was granted to Takeda and demonstrates the FDA's flexibility in evaluating applications for rare diseases.

title: FDA Announces Real-Time Release of Complete Response Letters, Posts Previously Unpublished Batch of 89
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced it will release future complete response letters (CRLs) promptly after issuance, starting immediately. This change follows the publication of 89 previously unpublished CRLs issued from 2024 to the present, detailing safety and effectiveness deficiencies. FDA Commissioner Dr. Marty Makary stated that embracing transparency will provide valuable insights to speed therapies and cures to market, while restoring public trust. Going forward, the agency will release newly issued CRLs and publish batches of previously issued CRLs associated with withdrawn or abandoned applications. All CRLs will be redacted to remove confidential information, but will contain company names. This change complies with the President's Executive Order No. 14303, which requires agencies to release data and conclusions associated with scientific information that affects public policies or private sector decisions.

title: FDA Advances Rare Disease Drug Development with New Evidence Principles
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration introduced the Rare Disease Evidence Principles (RDEP) to provide speed and predictability in reviewing therapies for rare diseases with small patient populations and significant unmet medical need. Sponsors will receive clearer guidance on the types of evidence that can be used to demonstrate substantial evidence of effectiveness. The RDEP addresses the challenges of rare disease drug development by allowing reviews to encompass additional supportive data. Sponsors can apply to the process prior to the launch of a pivotal trial and must specifically address a genetic defect and target a rare disease population of fewer than 1,000 patients in the US. The FDA will work closely with sponsors to define the evidence needed for approval, with patient and expert input encouraged.

title: FDA Urges Nicotine Pouch Manufacturers To Use Child-Resistant Packaging Following Increasing Reports of Accidental Exposure
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is calling on nicotine pouch manufacturers to use child-resistant packaging to protect American children from accidental exposure. From April 1, 2022, to March 31, 2025, reported nicotine pouch exposure cases to US Poison Centers increased, with 72% occurring in children under 5 years of age. The FDA is issuing guidelines for consumers on how to properly store nicotine pouches and prevent accidental exposure to children. Parents and caregivers are advised to store all nicotine products, including pouches, in secure locations away from children and seek immediate medical attention if accidental ingestion occurs. Manufacturers with pending premarket applications can contact the FDA through their assigned Regulatory Health Project Manager or at AskCTP@fda.hhs.gov or 877-CTP-1373.

title: FDA Begins Real-Time Reporting of Adverse Event Data
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration began publishing daily adverse event data from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS). This move aims to modernize the agency's safety monitoring infrastructure and ensure rapid transparency. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary stated that fast, seamless, and transparent adverse event reporting is crucial. FAERS is the FDA's primary database for collecting and analyzing adverse event reports. The shift is part of the FDA's data modernization strategy to streamline adverse event reporting and identify safety signals faster. The public can access the latest data on the FAERS Public Dashboard.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary:
Here is a factual, neutral summary of the source document within the 10,000 character limit:

The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on July 29-30, 2025, discussing monetary policy strategy, tools, and communication practices. The committee observed progress towards revising its statement on longer-run goals and monetary policy strategy. Maximum economic momentum slowed in Q2 due to reduced investment growth offset by faster PCE growth, while net exports made a large positive contribution and real imports of goods and services declined sharply. Exports of goods and services showed mixed results. Foreign economic growth slowed, with Canada's GDP contracting and China's continuing moderate expansion. The staff's real GDP growth projection for 2027 remained similar to the June meeting's forecast, reflecting offsetting revisions. The labor market was expected to weaken, with the unemployment rate projected above its natural rate through 2027. Inflation was projected to decline to 2% by 2027, but uncertainty around the projection remained elevated due to policy changes and their effects. Participants discussed risks to inflation and employment, noting upside risk to inflation due to tariff uncertainty and potential for inflation expectations becoming unanchored. They also mentioned downside risk to employment from possible financial condition tightening, housing market deterioration, and AI-induced job displacement. The Committee agreed to maintain the federal funds rate at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent, with a few members preferring a 25 basis point decrease due to concerns about labor market weakness and potential tariff effects on inflation.

title: HHS Allows FDA Emergency Use of Animal Drugs to Combat New World Screwworm, Protect U.S. Food Supply
body_summary: The US Department of Health and Human Services issued a declaration allowing the FDA to issue Emergency Use Authorizations for animal drugs to treat or prevent infestations caused by the New World Screwworm. The declaration applies only to drugs for animals, which currently have no FDA-approved treatments in the US. The move aims to safeguard the nation's food supply from the emerging threat posed by NWS, which has been detected approaching the US-Mexico border. The FDA can now authorize the flexible use of certain animal drug products for other purposes or available in other countries to protect pets, livestock, and the food supply.

title: Proclamation 10964—90th Anniversary of the Social Security Act
body_summary: President Donald J. Trump has signed a proclamation declaring August 14, 2025, as the 90th Anniversary of the Social Security Act. He recommitting to defending Social Security, rewarding workers, and taking care of citizens. The Social Security Act, signed into law by President Franklin D. Roosevelt on August 14, 1935, protects seniors, uplifts citizens, and sustains hardworking Americans. The Administration is rooting out fraud, waste, and abuse, making the Social Security Administration more efficient, and restoring strong border security policies.

title: FDA Approves First Immunotherapy for Recurrent Respiratory Papillomatosis
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Papzimeos, a non-replicating adenoviral vector-based immunotherapy, for the treatment of adult patients with recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP). RRP is a rare disease caused by persistent human papillomavirus 6 or 11 infection. The therapy, administered via subcutaneous injection, is designed to stimulate an immune response against HPV types 6 and 11. The approval is based on results from a single-arm, open-label trial, where 51.4% of patients achieved a complete response after treatment. The product received Orphan Drug designation and Breakthrough Therapy designation, and was granted to Precigen, Inc.

title: Executive Order 14336—Ensuring American Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Resilience by Filling the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve
body_summary: President Donald J. Trump orders the filling of the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve (SAPIR) within 30 days. The goal is to stockpile APIs for 26 critical medicines, which will be developed in consultation with agencies and experts. The reserve will be ready to receive and maintain APIs within 120 days. The order also requires a plan to store and maintain a 6-month supply of APIs for essential medicines, including a proposal for opening a second SAPIR repository within 1 year.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Marty Makary, M.D., M.P.H., on Florida Restriction of 7-OH Opioid Products
body_summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier has filed an emergency rule to classify certain concentrated forms of 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) as a Schedule I controlled substance in Florida, effective immediately. The rule makes it illegal to sell, possess, or distribute these potent opioids, particularly in fruit-flavored products appealing to children and teenagers. The FDA has recommended a federal scheduling action to control concentrated 7-OH products, and the Drug Enforcement Administration is reviewing the recommendation, which requires a public comment period.

title: FDA Commissioner Makary, USDA Secretary Rollins Celebrate Proposed Modernization of Orange Juice Regulations to Benefit American Growers
body_summary: U.S. Food and Drug Administration Commissioner Dr. Marty Makary and U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke L. Rollins have announced plans to update the standard of identity for pasteurized orange juice to support American citrus growers. The proposed rule change would reduce the minimum required Brix level from 10.5% to 10%, making it easier for domestic farmers to meet the regulation. The change is estimated to save orange juice manufacturers over $50 million per year and reduce reliance on imported oranges. The FDA expects this change to have no effect on the taste of pasteurized orange juice. The rule change is part of the FDA's broader effort to review over 250 standards of identity, with public comments accepted through November 4, 2025.

title: A Statement from FDA Commissioner Marty Makary, M.D., M.P.H.: Announcing Resolution of the IV Saline Solutions Shortage
body_summary: The nationwide shortage of sodium chloride 0.9% injection products has ended. This marks a significant milestone for public health, following close collaboration between the FDA, the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response, and industry partners who expanded manufacturing capacity and restored supply chain stability. The FDA used regulatory tools to facilitate temporary imports and expedited reviews to increase manufacturing capacities. The shortage has been resolved, and these products will be removed from the FDA list of Current Shortages. The FDA recommends hospitals use FDA-approved IV fluids when available and will continue to monitor supply to ensure patients have access to needed medicines.

title: FDA Announces New FDA PreCheck Program to Boost U.S. Drug Manufacturing
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced FDA PreCheck, a program to strengthen the domestic pharmaceutical supply chain. The program aims to increase regulatory predictability and facilitate the construction of manufacturing sites in the US. Over half of pharmaceuticals distributed in the US are manufactured overseas, and only 11% are produced by US manufacturers. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary stated that the program is one of many steps to reverse the US's reliance on foreign drug manufacturing and ensure a resilient and domestic drug supply. The program introduces a two-phase approach, with the Facility Readiness Phase providing more frequent FDA communication and the Application Submission Phase streamlining the development of the Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls section of the application. An upcoming public meeting on September 30, 2025, will feature a presentation of the FDA PreCheck draft framework and discussions on framework strengths and opportunities.

title: FDA Names Top HHS Lawyer as Chief Counsel
body_summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced the appointment of Sean Keveney as Chief Counsel at the FDA. Keveney previously served as Acting General Counsel of HHS, leading the Department's legal team under the Trump Administration. During his tenure, HHS successfully cracked down on discrimination, including settlements with Columbia and Brown universities. Keveney, a career public servant, has a background in the Department of Justice's Civil Rights Division and has clerked for Judge William Garwood. Robert Foster will assume Keveney's role at HHS, while Foster will remain FDA Chief Counsel for Food, Research, and Drugs.

title: FDA Requires Major Changes to Opioid Pain Medication Labeling to Emphasize Risks
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration is requiring safety labeling changes to all opioid pain medications to better emphasize and explain the risks associated with their long-term use. This change follows a public advisory committee meeting in May that reviewed data showing serious risks for patients who use opioids over long periods. 

FDA Commissioner Marty Makary, M.D., M.P.H., stated that the opioid epidemic's impact, including almost one million American deaths, was a public health failure. The updated labeling change reflects robust data from two large observational studies, which showed that long-term opioid use can lead to serious side effects. 

The FDA has also required an additional clinical trial to directly examine the benefits and risks of long-term opioid use. The labeling changes will include updates on clearer risk information, dosing warnings, use limits, treatment guidance, safe discontinuation, overdose reversal agents, drug interactions, and more risks with overdose.

title: Executive Order 14327—President's Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition, and the Reestablishment of the Presidential Fitness Test
body_summary: The President revokes and amends two executive orders, reestablishing the Presidential Fitness Test and the President's Council on Sports, Fitness, and Nutrition. The Council will advise the President on progress and recommend actions to promote youth sports, fitness, and nutrition. A 3-year plan is established to host major sporting events, encourage children's participation in youth sports, and address childhood obesity. The Council's order terminates in 2 years, unless extended by the President. Executive Order 12345 is revoked, and a new section 6 is added to clarify the Council's authority.
