title: FDA Takes Steps to Restrict 7-OH Opioid Products Threatening American Consumers
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is recommending a scheduling action to control certain 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) products under the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). The FDA is targeting 7-OH, a concentrated byproduct of the kratom plant, which is recognized for its potential for abuse due to its ability to bind to opioid receptors. This recommendation follows a thorough medical and scientific analysis by the FDA and is part of efforts to address concerns around the growing availability and use of 7-OH opioid products. The FDA has already issued warning letters to seven companies for illegally distributing products containing 7-OH and is publishing educational materials for consumers. The recommendation is expected to be reviewed by the Drug Enforcement Administration, which has the final authority on scheduling.

title: FDA Recommends Removal of Voluntary Hold for Elevidys for Ambulatory Patients
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration recommends removing the voluntary hold for ambulatory patients to receive Elevidys, a Sarepta Therapeutics gene therapy for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD), after concluding that the death of an 8-year-old boy is unrelated to the product. The FDA will continue to work with the sponsor on non-ambulatory patients, who are still subject to a voluntary hold following two deaths. Elevidys is a single intravenous dose administered using an adeno-associated virus vector-based gene therapy platform.

title: FDA Investigating Death of 8-Year-Old Boy Who Received Elevidys
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is investigating the death of an 8-year-old boy who received Elevidys, a gene therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, on June 7, 2025. The FDA has requested a voluntary suspension of product distribution as it investigates safety concerns. Elevidys is a gene therapy using Sarepta Therapeutics' AAVrh74 Platform Technology. Duchenne muscular dystrophy is a rare genetic condition characterized by progressive muscular weakness, caused by a defective gene.

title: HHS, FDA and USDA Address the Health Risks of Ultra-Processed Foods
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration and U.S. Department of Agriculture are announcing a joint Request for Information to gather information and data to establish a federally recognized uniform definition for ultra-processed foods. Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, and Secretary Brooke L. Rollins of the U.S. Department of Agriculture, are leading this effort. A uniform definition is crucial to provide transparency to consumers about the foods they eat. The goal is to address the growing concerns around ultra-processed foods and the current epidemic of diet-related chronic disease in America. Approximately 70% of packaged products in the U.S. food supply are foods often considered ultra-processed, and this effort aims to help address overconsumption of these foods. The Request for Information will be publicly available in the federal register on July 24.

title: Joint Statement by President Trump and President Prabowo Subianto Djojohadikusumo of Indonesia on Framework for United States-Indonesia Agreement on Reciprocal Trade
body_summary: The United States and Indonesia have agreed to a Framework for negotiating an Agreement on Reciprocal Trade to strengthen their bilateral economic relationship. Key terms of the Agreement will include Indonesia eliminating 99% of tariff barriers for U.S. industrial and food products, while the U.S. will reduce reciprocal tariffs to 19%. The U.S. and Indonesia will also work together to address non-tariff barriers, including intellectual property issues, conformity assessment procedures, and labor rights. Additionally, the U.S. and Indonesia have committed to addressing barriers to digital trade, services, and investment, and to strengthen economic and national security cooperation. Forthcoming commercial deals between U.S. and Indonesian companies include procurement of aircraft valued at $3.2 billion, purchases of energy products estimated at $15 billion, and agriculture products worth $4.5 billion.

title: HHS, FDA Praise Consumer Brands Association’s Vow to Remove Artificial Colors from America’s Food Supply
body_summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services leadership praised the Consumer Brands Association for its pledge to remove certified Food, Drug & Cosmetic (FD&C) petroleum-based colors from America's food supply. With support from the Trump Administration, this pledge urges member companies to stop manufacturing with FD&C colors by December 31, 2027. President Trump, Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., and U.S. Food and Drug Administration Commissioner Dr. Marty Makary have made the removal of artificial colors a priority. The Consumer Brands Association has committed to eliminating the use of six specific FD&C colors, including Blue No. 1, Blue No. 2, Green No. 3, Red No. 40, Yellow No. 5, and Yellow No. 6, from their product portfolios starting from the 2026-2027 school year.

title: Stanford faculty member George Tidmarsh, M.D., Ph.D. named Director of Center for Drug Evaluation and Research
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has appointed George Francis Tidmarsh, M.D., Ph.D., as Director of the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER). Dr. Tidmarsh will lead efforts to ensure safe, effective, and high-quality drugs are available to the American people. Dr. Tidmarsh earned his M.D. and Ph.D. from Stanford University and brings over 30 years of experience in biotechnology, clinical medicine, and regulatory science. He has authored 143 scientific publications and patents, and was the founding co-director of Stanford's Master of Translational Research and Applied Medicine (M-TRAM) program. Dr. Tidmarsh has led the successful clinical development of seven FDA-approved drugs and has served on advisory boards across academia, government, and industry.

title: FDA Requests Sarepta Therapeutics Suspend Distribution of Elevidys and Places Clinical Trials on Hold for Multiple Gene Therapy Products Following 3 Deaths
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has placed Sarepta Therapeutics' investigational gene therapy clinical trials for limb girdle muscular dystrophy on hold following three deaths potentially related to the products, due to new safety concerns. The FDA has also revoked Sarepta's platform technology designation and requested the company to voluntarily stop all shipments of Elevidys, which the company refused to do. The FDA Commissioner, Marty Makary, stated that the agency takes swift action when patient safety is at risk. Director of the FDA's Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, Vinay Prasad, said that the agency will not allow products with harms greater than benefits. Elevidys is an adeno-associated virus vector-based gene therapy for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, and the FDA has revoked the platform technology designation due to insufficient evidence of its safety.

title: FDA to Revoke 52 Obsolete Standards of Identity for Food Products
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is revoking or proposing to revoke 52 food standards, including those for canned fruits and vegetables, dairy products, baked goods, and macaroni products. This decision is part of the agency's ongoing analysis to ensure that food standards are useful, relevant, and serve consumers in the best possible way. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. stated that eliminating outdated food regulations will cut through bureaucratic red tape and increase transparency. The FDA will publish a direct final rule revoking standards for 11 types of canned fruits and vegetables, and proposed rules for 18 types of dairy products and 23 other food products. The decision aligns with the broader effort to reduce regulatory burdens and increase transparency, as supported by President Trump's Executive Order 14192.

title: FDA Issues Warning Letters to Firms Marketing Products Containing 7-Hydroxymitragynine
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has announced seven warning letters to companies for illegally marketing products containing 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH). The Agency is concerned about novel potent opioid products being marketed to US consumers, particularly concentrated 7-OH products such as tablets, gummies, and shots. The warning letters focus on products containing 7-OH as an added ingredient or enhanced levels of 7-OH. The FDA has issued letters to Shaman Botanicals, LLC, My Smoke Wholesale, Relax Relief Rejuvenate Trading, LLC, Thang Botanicals, Inc., Royal Diamond Imports, Inc., Hydroxie, LLC, and 7Tabz Retail, LLC, requesting they respond within 15 business days.

title: FDA Approves Gardenia (Genipin) Blue Color Additive While Encouraging Faster Phase-Out of FD&C Red No. 3
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Gardenia Blue Interest Group's color additive petition to use the color gardenia blue in various foods, consistent with good manufacturing practice. This is the fourth color derived from natural sources approved in the last two months. The FDA's action aligns with Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr.'s priority to phase out synthetic, petroleum-based dyes from the nation's food supply. About 40% of the food industry has committed to a voluntary phase-out of such dyes since Secretary Kennedy announced measures in April. The FDA has approved the color additive for use in sports drinks, flavored water, fruit drinks, and candies. The approval was expedited and aims to make it easier for food manufacturers to end their use of petroleum-based dyes. The FDA also sent a letter to manufacturers encouraging them to accelerate the phase-out of FD&C Red No. 3 in foods.

title: A Statement from FDA Commissioner Marty Makary, M.D., M.P.H:  100 Days of Embracing Gold-Standard Science, Transparency and Common Sense
body_summary: The FDA has marked its 100th day in office by launching initiatives to address significant issues, including food safety, childhood diseases, and chronic health concerns. Under the leadership of Commissioner Dr. Marty Makary, the agency has phased out petroleum-based food dyes, improved infant formula, and reviewed chemicals in the food supply. The FDA has also reformulated GRAS submissions, revised broken dietary guidelines, and defined ultra-processed foods. Additionally, the agency has introduced a new approach to Covid-19 booster approvals, removed restrictions on gene therapies, and cleared the first in vitro diagnostic device for Alzheimer's disease. The FDA has expanded unannounced foreign inspections, initiated a review of foreign inspections policies, and implemented AI-assisted reviews and a generative AI tool. The agency has also consolidated adverse event reporting databases and modernized its operations, with Commissioner Makary committing to transparent communication with the public through regular unscripted conversations.

title: FDA Embraces Radical Transparency by Publishing Complete Response Letters
body_summary: The US FDA has published over 200 complete response letters (CRLs) for drugs and biological products submitted between 2020 and 2024. The CRLs provide insight into the FDA's decision-making process and common deficiencies cited for application approval. Commissioner Marty Makary stated that the goal is to deliver predictability to drug developers, bringing cures and treatments to patients faster. The FDA has made CRLs publicly available, with some redactions for trade secrets, to increase transparency. The Agency is publishing more CRLs from its archives and exploring ways to provide greater transparency.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors to review monetary policy strategy, tools, and communications on June 17-18, 2025. The committee discussed assessing risks and uncertainty related to economic outlook and potential implications for monetary policy, as well as ways to enhance communication tools and practices. SOMA securities holdings had fallen by almost $2-1/4 trillion since balance sheet runoff commenced in June 2022, with a corresponding drain in Federal Reserve liabilities largely coming out of balances at the ON RRP facility. Respondents expected runoff to end in February next year with an expected size of the SOMA portfolio of $6.2 trillion or about 20% of GDP. Credit conditions were solid in May and early June, with private credit broadly available and bank credit growth moderating. The Federal Reserve kept the target range for the federal funds rate at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent, considering recent data suggesting economic growth remained solid despite uncertainty about tariffs and policy changes.

title: FDA Encourages Industry Leaders to Streamline, Enhance Product Recall Communications to Safeguard Foods for Infants and Children
body_summary: The US FDA is calling on industry leaders in infant formula, baby food, and child food manufacturing to improve product recall communication. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary is urging industry leaders to adopt "radical transparency" to ensure the safety and well-being of infants and children. Makary stated that protecting vulnerable children is not just a moral duty but a responsibility. The FDA will create a centralized webpage on FDA.gov to provide easy access to recall information for parents and caregivers. The agency is also increasing collaboration with industry leaders and public-private partnerships to enhance recall communication and protect children's health.

title: Memorandum on Ensuring Accountability and Prioritizing Public Safety in Federal Hiring
body_summary: By the authority vested in me as President, a policy shall govern the hiring of Federal civilian employees within the Executive Branch through October 15, 2025: no vacant position may be filled, and no new position may be created, except as provided for in this memorandum or required by applicable law. This policy applies to all executive departments and agencies, except military personnel and positions related to immigration enforcement, national security, or public safety. The Director of OPM may grant exemptions from this policy where necessary. Hires approved by the executive department or independent establishment head, chief of staff, or President-appointed officer may proceed one business day after official notification to OPM. Contracting outside the Federal Government is prohibited. This policy encourages efficient use of existing personnel and funds to improve public services, allowing staff reallocations and reassignments to meet priority needs and protect national security, homeland security, and public safety.

title: Memorandum on Reissuance of and Amendments to National Security Presidential Memorandum 5 on Strengthening the Policy of the United States Toward Cuba
body_summary: The US President's National Security Presidential Memorandum/NSPM-5 aims to strengthen US policy towards Cuba by promoting a stable, prosperous, and free country for its people, while channelling funds away from the communist regime. Key actions include restricting financial transactions, travel, and tourism, as well as supporting free markets, free enterprise, and democracy in Cuba. The memo outlines specific regulations, including a 30-day timeline for implementation, which includes a list of prohibited entities. The new US government policy, replacing previous directives, aims to enhance engagement with the Cuban people and ensure compliance with relevant laws and regulations.

title: FDA Eliminates Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS) for Autologous Chimeric Antigen Receptor CAR T cell Immunotherapies
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has eliminated the Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS) for currently approved BCMA- and CD19-directed autologous chimeric antigen receptor CAR T cell immunotherapies. The FDA determined that the approved REMS for products such as Abecma, Breyanzi, Carvykti, Kymriah, Tecartus, and Yescarta are no longer necessary to ensure the benefits outweigh the risks. The REMS elimination expedites the delivery of potentially curative treatments to patients and reduces burden on providers. The information regarding the risks for these CAR T cell immunotherapies can be conveyed adequately via the current product labeling, which includes boxed warnings and medication guides.

title: Implementation Note issued June 18, 2025
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on June 18, 2025: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 4.4 percent, effective June 20, 2025. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective June 20, 2025, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 4-1/4 to 4â1/2 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 4.5 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Although swings in net exports have affected the data, recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace. The unemployment rate remains low, and labor market conditions remain solid. Inflation remains somewhat elevated. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. Uncertainty about the economic outlook has diminished but remains elevated. The Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate. In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent. In considering the extent and timing of additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. The Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgageâbacked securities. The Committee is strongly committed to supporting maximum employment and returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Susan M. Collins; Lisa D. Cook; Austan D. Goolsbee; Philip N. Jefferson; Adriana D. Kugler; Alberto G. Musalem; Jeffrey R. Schmid; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: FDA Halts New Clinical Trials That Export Americans’ Cells to Foreign Labs in Hostile Countries for Genetic Engineering
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced an immediate review of new clinical trials involving sending American citizens' living cells to China and other hostile countries for genetic engineering. The review follows mounting evidence that some trials failed to inform participants about the international transfer and manipulation of their biological material, potentially exposing sensitive genetic data to misuse by foreign governments. The review is a response to a data security rule finalized under the Biden Administration in December 2024, which allowed US companies to send trial participants' biological samples for processing overseas. FDA Commissioner Dr. Marty Makary stated that the agency is taking action to protect patients, restore public trust, and safeguard US biomedical leadership. The FDA will require companies to demonstrate full transparency, ethical consent, and domestic handling of sensitive biological materials, and will not permit new trials that cannot meet these standards.

title: FDA to Issue New Commissioner’s National Priority Vouchers to Companies Supporting U.S. National Interests
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced its Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher (CNPV) program to enhance the health interests of Americans. The new voucher allows drug developers to participate in a priority program that shortens its review time from 10-12 months to 1-2 months. The program convenes experts from FDA offices for a team-based review, with clinical information reviewed by a multidisciplinary team. The FDA plans to give a limited number of vouchers to companies aligned with U.S. national priorities in the first year, with the goal of bringing more cures and meaningful treatments to the American public. To qualify, sponsors must submit specific components of the application at least 60 days before submitting the final application, and be available for ongoing communication with the FDA. The program aims to accelerate the drug review process while maintaining the FDA's rigorous standards for safety, efficacy, and quality.

title: Memorandum on Eliminating Waste, Fraud, and Abuse in Medicaid
body_summary: The memorandum states that the administration will take action to eliminate waste, fraud, and abuse in Medicaid. This decision was made to protect and improve the Medicare and Medicaid programs, which were designed to provide compassionate care to vulnerable Americans. The programs were originally capped at the same level as Medicare payments to healthcare providers, with the State and Federal Governments sharing the cost burden. However, under the Biden Administration, States and healthcare providers were allowed to game the system, leading to a significant increase in payments. The memorandum pledges to ensure that Medicaid payments rates are not higher than Medicare rates, where permitted by law, to prevent further waste, fraud, and abuse.

title: FDA Launches Agency-Wide AI Tool to Optimize Performance for the American People
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has launched Elsa, a generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tool designed to help employees work more efficiently. The tool was built within a high-security environment and is being used to accelerate clinical protocol reviews, shorten scientific evaluation times, and identify high-priority inspection targets. The rollout of Elsa is ahead of schedule and under budget, thanks to collaboration between in-house experts. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary and Chief AI Officer Jeremy Walsh are optimistic about the tool's potential to enhance employee performance and support the agency's mission. The introduction of Elsa marks the beginning of the FDA's AI journey, with plans to integrate more AI in different processes in the future.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary:
Here is a summary of the source document:

A Federal Open Market Committee meeting was held on May 6-7, 2025, where participants reaffirmed their commitment to a 2% longer-run inflation objective and emphasized the importance of anchored long-term inflation expectations. They assessed significant uncertainty about their economic outlooks due to changes in fiscal, regulatory, and immigration policies. Participants noted solid economic expansion, low unemployment rate, and stable labor market conditions, but also observed increased uncertainty and downside risks to employment and economic activity. The median modal path for the federal funds rate indicated two or three rate cuts this year.

title: FDA Takes Action to Address Data Integrity Concerns with Two Chinese Third-Party Testing Firms
body_summary: The US FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH) issued General Correspondence Letters to two Chinese testing companies, Mid-Link Technology Testing Co., Ltd. and Sanitation & Environment Technology Institute of Soochow University Ltd., for falsified or invalid data. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary stated that the agency will respond to data integrity issues accordingly. CDRH Director Michelle Tarver said the FDA is committed to protecting public health and will reject testing facilities' data if it cannot be ensured to be reliable and valid. The letters were sent in response to laboratory oversight failures and animal care violations, and the FDA has previously alerted the medical device industry to concerns about data quality and integrity from third-party testing labs in China.

title: FDA and CBP Seize Nearly $34 Million Worth of Illegal E-Cigarettes During Joint Operation
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has seized nearly two million units of unauthorized e-cigarette products in Chicago, valued at $33.8 million. The seizures were part of a joint federal operation with US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to prevent illegal e-cigarettes from entering the country. The team found shipments of various illegal e-cigarette products, mostly from China, and determined that many contained vague product descriptions with incorrect values. The FDA Commissioner, Marty Makary, stated that the seizures will keep unauthorized products out of the US and away from youth. The operation was part of a coordinated effort to curb the distribution and sale of illegal e-cigarettes, and the FDA has also sent import informational letters to 24 tobacco importers, advising them to ensure their import entries contain complete and accurate information. This is the latest in a series of joint FDA-CBP actions, including seizures of over $77 million worth of illegal e-cigarettes in Chicago in 2024, and the FDA has issued over 750 warning letters to firms and more than 800 to retailers for selling unauthorized products.

title: FDA takes steps to enhance state importation programs to help lower prescription drug prices
body_summary: The US FDA is enhancing the pathway for state importation programs to import prescription drugs from Canada, as part of its efforts to implement Executive OrderLowering Drug Prices by Once Again Putting Americans First. FDA Commissioner Marty Makary has stated that this will support the ability to import drugs at lower prices while maintaining high quality and safety. The agency will offer individual states and tribes the opportunity to submit draft proposals for pre-review, meet with the agency for initial feedback, and develop a user-friendly tool to assist states in developing proposals. The goal is to clarify requirements, enhance proposal quality, and streamline the review process. The agency anticipates meeting with interested states this fall to gather feedback and provide a forum for exchanging information that protects public safety.

title: FDA Clears First Blood Test Used in Diagnosing Alzheimer’s Disease
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared for marketing the Lumipulse G pTau217/ß-Amyloid 1-42 Plasma Ratio, a first-in-vitro diagnostic device that tests blood to aid in diagnosing Alzheimer's disease. The test is for adults aged 55 years and older with signs and symptoms of the disease. The test measures two proteins, pTau217 and β-amyloid 1-42, found in human plasma, and calculates their numerical ratio, correlating it to the presence or absence of amyloid plaques in the brain. The test is less invasive than previous methods, requiring only a simple blood draw. The FDA evaluated data from a multi-center clinical study of 499 individual plasma samples and found that 91.7% of individuals with positive results had amyloid plaques, and 97.3% of individuals with negative results had a negative result. The test is intended for patients presenting at a specialized care setting and must be interpreted in conjunction with other patient clinical information. The FDA granted Breakthrough Device designation to Fujirebio Diagnostics, Inc., which was cleared for marketing.

title: FDA to Host Inaugural, Independent, Scientific Expert Panel Open to Public
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration's Commissioner Martin A. Makary, M.D., M.P.H., is leading a roundtable discussion of an independent panel of scientific experts to discuss the safety and necessity of talc as an additive in food, drug, and cosmetic products on May 20, 2025. The public roundtable will review the latest scientific evidence, evaluate potential health risks, and explore safer alternatives. The panel, comprising world-renowned experts, will be convened due to growing concerns about potential health effects, especially with asbestos contamination and prolonged consumption. The discussion aims to assess the available evidence and consider whether talc's continued use is necessary given modern alternatives. The decision follows a recent call from public health leaders for a systematic reevaluation of talc's use in consumer products, including a recent commentary by global talc experts that underscored this need. The roundtable will take place at the FDA's White Oak Campus in Silver Spring, Maryland, and will be livestreamed.

title: FDA Advances Robust, Transparent Post-Market Chemical Review Program to Keep Food Supply Safe and Healthy
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is launching a stronger review process for food chemicals, prioritizing transparency and safety. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. said, "No parent should ever worry about what's in their child's food." The FDA will modernize its review process, release a draft for public comment, and implement a final systematic post-market review process. This effort will include a new prioritization scheme, an updated list of chemicals under review, and expedited review of certain chemicals like phthalates and propylparaben. The FDA will also share information about the review process on its website. The agency is taking proactive, science-based steps to improve food chemical oversight, part of a larger initiative to phase out petroleum-based synthetic dyes and eliminate the GRAS process.

title: FDA Begins Action To Remove Ingestible Fluoride Prescription Drug Products for Children from the Market
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is initiating action to remove concentrated ingestible fluoride prescription drug products for children from the market. These products have never been approved by the FDA and have been shown to alter the gut microbiome, potentially leading to thyroid disorders, weight gain, and decreased IQ. The FDA Commissioner, Marty Makary, has stated that the best way to prevent cavities is through good dental hygiene, not altering a child's microbiome. The agency aims to complete a safety review and public comment period by October 31 and has set a goal to disseminate best practices for dental hygiene in children. The US Department of Health and Human Services plans to provide best practices that do not alter gut health. The move aligns with the Secretary's Make American Healthy Again effort and is consistent with the removal of fluoride from drinking water in several European countries.

title: HHS, FDA Initiate Comprehensive Review of Nutrients in Infant Formula
body_summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced the next steps in Operation Stork Speed, a comprehensive initiative to ensure the safety, reliability, and nutritional adequacy of infant formula. The FDA issued a Request for Information (RFI) to begin the nutrient review process, seeking public input on whether existing requirements should be revised based on the latest scientific data. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., said "Operation Stork Speed brings radical transparency to ingredients in infant formula and puts science front and center." The FDA will convene a publicly accessible expert panel in June and increase testing for heavy metals and other contaminants in infant formula. Commenters will have 120 days to submit responses to the RFI.

title: HHS, FDA Issue RFI on Deregulatory Plan to Lower Costs and Empower Providers
body_summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) have launched a public Request for Information (RFI) to identify and eliminate outdated or unnecessary regulations. This initiative is part of a broader federal effort to reduce regulatory burdens and increase transparency, in line with President Trump's Executive Order 14192, "Unleashing Prosperity Through Deregulation." HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. has committed the Department to a "10-to-1" deregulatory policy, where for every new regulation proposed, at least ten existing regulatory actions will be rescinded. The effort aims to lower the cost of living, remove bureaucratic barriers, and allow health care providers to devote more time and resources to patient care. The 60-day public comment period opens today, and stakeholders are encouraged to submit their ideas for deregulatory actions through Regulations.gov or the newly launched online portal.

title: Executive Order 14297—Delivering Most-Favored-Nation Prescription Drug Pricing to American Patients
body_summary: The President orders an end to the United States' contribution to global pharmaceutical profits by forcing drug manufacturers to sell their products in the US at the most-favored-nation price, similar to those in other developed nations. The US has less than 5% of the world's population yet funds around 3/4 of global pharmaceutical profits. This abuse must end, and Americans should no longer be forced to pay almost three times more for the same medicines. The Administration will take immediate steps to end global freeloading and take additional action if drug manufacturers fail to comply.

title: FDA and NIH Announce Innovative Joint Nutrition Regulatory Science Program
body_summary: The US FDA and NIH announced a joint innovative research initiative to address the rising diet-related chronic diseases. Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. committed to Make America Healthy Again, and the initiative aims to provide critical information for effective food and nutrition policy actions. The FDA and NIH will implement a comprehensive nutrition research agenda to answer questions about ultra-processed foods, food additives, and maternal and infant dietary exposures. The initiative brings together experts in various disciplines to advance gold standard nutrition and food science. The FDA will provide regulatory science expertise, while NIH will provide scientific research infrastructure. The joint effort is to tackle the chronic disease crisis head-on, ensuring fair, independent, and conflict-free research.

title: Executive Order 14296—Keeping Promises to Veterans and Establishing a National Center for Warrior Independence
body_summary: The President orders the establishment of the National Center for Warrior Independence at the West Los Angeles VA Medical Center, with the goal of providing care, benefits, and services to homeless veterans. The center will be designated by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs and will work to restore self-sufficiency and the warrior ethos among homeless veterans. The Secretary of Housing and Urban Development will use vouchers to support homeless veterans in the Los Angeles metropolitan area and around the Nation. The President also directs the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to take steps to restore accountability and excellence at the Department of Veterans Affairs, including investigating and addressing misconduct and improving care, benefits, and services for veterans.

title: FDA Approves Three Food Colors from Natural Sources
body_summary: The US FDA has granted three new color additive petitions to expand the palette of available colors from natural sources for food manufacturers. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and FDA Commissioner Martin A. Makary announced the approval, aiming to phase out petroleum-based dyes. Three new colors have been approved: Galdieria extract blue for use in various beverages, Butterfly pea flower extract for a range of colors in foods, and Calcium phosphate for use in ready-to-eat chicken products. The approval expands the options for manufacturers, with more committing to remove petroleum-based dyes from their products.

title: FDA Announces Completion of First AI-Assisted Scientific Review Pilot and Aggressive Agency-Wide AI Rollout Timeline
body_summary:
FDA Commissioner Martin A. Makary announced an aggressive timeline to scale the use of artificial intelligence internally across all FDA centers by June 30, 2025. Makary stated that the agency-wide deployment of AI capabilities holds tremendous promise in accelerating review times for new therapies. The goal is to deploy AI tools across all centers immediately, with the objective of full integration by the end of June.

The FDA plans to expand generative AI capabilities across all centers using a secure, unified platform. Future enhancements will focus on improving usability, expanding document integration, and tailoring outputs to center-specific needs. The initiative is being coordinated by Jeremy Walsh, the FDA's newly appointed Chief AI Officer, and Sridhar Mantha.
