title: FDA Announces Expanded Use of Unannounced Inspections at Foreign Manufacturing Facilities
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration plans to expand its use of unannounced inspections at foreign manufacturing facilities that produce foods, medicines, and other medical products for American consumers. This change aims to ensure equal regulatory oversight and scrutiny for foreign companies as domestic ones. The FDA's Office of Inspection and Investigations Foreign Unannounced Inspection Pilot program in India and China will be expanded. The agency will evaluate its policies and practices to improve the foreign inspection program. Unannounced inspections will help expose bad actors who falsify records or conceal violations before they can put American lives at risk. The FDA will also refuse travel accommodations from regulated industry to maintain oversight integrity. This shift ensures every product entering the US is safe and legitimate. The FDA is authorized to take regulatory action against firms that delay or deny inspections.

title: Executive Order 14292—Improving the Safety and Security of Biological Research
body_summary: The President has ordered an end to dangerous gain-of-function research conducted by foreign entities in countries of concern, effective immediately. A new set of guidelines for federal funding of life-science research will be established to ensure compliance with U.S. oversight standards and policies. Grant recipients are required to certify that they do not fund or participate in "dangerous gain-of-function research" that could cause significant societal consequences or national security risks. Violating this order may result in revocation of funding and a 5-year ineligibility for life-sciences grant funds.

title: Executive Order 14293—Regulatory Relief To Promote Domestic Production of Critical Medicines
body_summary: The President of the United States has ordered the elimination of regulatory barriers to the domestic production of pharmaceutical products, aiming to make the United States the most competitive nation in the world for the manufacture of safe and effective pharmaceutical products. The order, issued on May 5, 2025, sets a 180-day timeline for the FDA Commissioner to streamline the review process for domestic pharmaceutical manufacturing, including reducing duplicative requirements and maximizing timeliness and predictability. The order also establishes a new framework for inspections of foreign manufacturing facilities involved in the supply of US medicines, with the FDA Commissioner to publicly disclose annual inspection numbers by country and manufacturer.

title: HHS, FDA to Phase Out Petroleum-Based Synthetic Dyes in Nation’s Food Supply
body_summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and FDA announced new measures to phase out all petroleum-based synthetic dyes from the nation's food supply. The FDA will establish a national standard and timeline for the food industry to transition to natural alternatives. Two synthetic food colorings, Citrus Red No. 2 and Orange B, will be revoked within the coming months. Six synthetic dyes will be eliminated by the end of next year, and four new natural color additives will be authorized in the coming weeks. The FDA is partnering with the NIH to conduct research on the impact of food additives on children's health and development. The agency is also requesting food companies to remove FD&C Red No. 3 sooner than previously required.

title: FDA Commissioner Makary Announces New Policy on Individuals Serving on FDA Advisory Committees
body_summary: FDA Commissioner Martin A. Makary, M.D., M.P.H., has announced a policy directive to limit individuals employed at companies regulated by the FDA from serving as official members on FDA advisory committees. This effort aims to mitigate perceived industry influence and conflicts of interests, prioritizing patients and caregivers' voices. Commissioner Makary emphasized the need for independent scientific evaluation and public trust in the healthcare-industrial complex. Exceptions can be made in rare circumstances where scientific expertise is only available from an FDA-regulated company employee, provided they comply with ethics requirements.

title: Memorandum on Extension of Hiring Freeze
body_summary: The President has extended the hiring freeze for Federal civilian employees within the executive branch through July 15, 2025. The freeze, initially directed on January 20, 2025, prohibits filling vacant positions and creating new ones, except as otherwise provided in the memorandum or required by law. The freeze applies to all executive departments and agencies, except for military personnel, immigration enforcement, national security, and public safety positions. Exemptions can be granted by the Director of OPM, and the heads of agencies are allowed to make reallocations and reassignments to meet priority needs.

title: Executive Order 14273—Lowering Drug Prices by Once Again Putting Americans First
body_summary: The President of the United States orders the establishment of a new payment mechanism to prevent pharmaceutical manufacturers from charging significantly higher prices in the US compared to abroad. This move aims to improve transparency, prioritize high-cost prescription drugs, and minimize negative impacts on innovation. The administration also directs various actions to promote competition, efficiency, and lower drug prices for Americans. The Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy, in coordination with the Secretary, OMB Director, and Assistant to the President for Economic Policy, must provide recommendations within 90 days. The Secretary must issue reports within 180 days on accelerating competition, improving prescription drug importation, and reducing costly care for seniors.

title: Memorandum on Preventing Illegal Aliens From Obtaining Social Security Act Benefits
body_summary:
President Donald J. Trump directs the Secretary of Labor, Secretary of Health and Human Services, Commissioner of Social Security, and Secretary of Homeland Security to take measures to ensure ineligible aliens do not receive Social Security Act benefits.

The Secretary of Labor, Secretary of Health and Human Services, and Commissioner of Social Security shall take all reasonable measures to verify eligibility and prevent abuse, including promulgating guidance and regulations. The Attorney General and Commissioner of Social Security will cooperate to expand fraud-prosecutor programs in at least 65 US Attorney Offices by October 1, 2025.

The Commissioner of Social Security must implement the Inspector General's audit recommendations and refer reports of earnings from individuals age 100 or older with missing death information to the Inspector General. The Inspector General will investigate and refer matters to the Department of Justice and other agencies as warranted.

The memo also states that nothing in it impairs or affects existing authority or functions, and it is implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to appropriations. The Commissioner of Social Security is authorized to publish the memo in the Federal Register.

title: FDA Honored to Welcome HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. to FDA Campus
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration welcomed HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. to its headquarters in Silver Spring, Maryland. The visit included remarks to FDA employees, meetings with agency leadership, and a tour of medical device innovation laboratories on the FDA's White Oak campus. Secretary Kennedy charged employees with responding to the chronic health care crisis in children and noted the importance of a public health workforce. Commissioner Martin A. Makary thanked Secretary Kennedy for the confidence placed in him and pledged to build on the agency's history, applying the gold standard of scientific research to find new cures and end the epidemic of chronic illness. The tour visited several laboratories, including those focusing on 3-D printing and cardiovascular device performance simulation.

title: FDA Announces Plan to Phase Out Animal Testing Requirement for Monoclonal Antibodies and Other Drugs
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is replacing animal testing in the development of monoclonal antibody therapies and other drugs with more effective, human-relevant methods. The new approach aims to improve drug safety, accelerate the evaluation process, and reduce animal experimentation, research and development costs, and drug prices. Implementation will begin immediately for investigational new drug (IND) applications, with inclusion of AI-based computational models of toxicity and cell lines and organoid toxicity testing encouraged. The FDA will use pre-existing, real-world safety data from other countries to make determinations of efficacy. Key benefits include advanced computer simulations, human-based lab models, and regulatory incentives. The roadmap is designed to reduce the need for animal trials, promote streamlined review, and incentivize investment in modernized testing platforms. The FDA aims to accelerate the validation and adoption of innovative methods through partnerships with federal agencies.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting on March 18-19, 2025, reviewing their monetary policy framework and focusing on labor market dynamics and maximum employment goals. They discussed conceptual benchmarks for evaluating labor market position and presented model-based analysis of simple monetary policy rules. The committee maintained the target range for the federal funds rate at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent, citing elevated inflation but solid labor market conditions. Some participants expressed caution due to high uncertainty around government policies' impact on the economic outlook. The committee also decided to slow the pace of decline in securities holdings by reducing the monthly redemption cap on Treasury securities from $25 billion to $5 billion, starting in April.

title: Executive Order 14257—Regulating Imports With a Reciprocal Tariff To Rectify Trade Practices That Contribute to Large and Persistent Annual United States Goods Trade Deficits
body_summary: US President Donald J. Trump declares a national emergency due to large and persistent US goods trade deficits, totaling $1.2 trillion in 2024, driven by non-reciprocal trade differences and non-tariff barriers. On April 2, 2025, President Trump imposes ad valorem duties of 30-37% on goods from Algeria, Angola, and China, effective upon entry. He also imposes 10% additional ad valorem duty on all imports, except for specific goods, from April 5, 2025, to mitigate domestic manufacturing capacity loss and national security concerns. The US lists various classes of organic compounds, including petroleum products, inorganic bases, monohydric alcohols, acids, and other chemical substances with specific names, numbers, and notes.

title: Martin A. Makary, M.D., M.P.H., Sworn in as FDA Commissioner
body_summary: Martin A. Makary, M.D., M.P.H., took office as the 27th Commissioner of Food and Drugs after being confirmed by a bipartisan U.S. Senate vote. He was welcomed by HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., who praised Dr. Makary's credentials and qualifications for leading the FDA. Dr. Makary has authored over 300 peer-reviewed articles and founded the Johns Hopkins Center for Surgical Trials and Outcomes Research. He is the co-developer of the Surgery Checklist used in operating rooms worldwide. Dr. Makary is a member of the National Academy of Medicine and has held visiting professorships at 25 medical schools. He assumes the role at the FDA under President Trump and Secretary Kennedy, aiming to advance the agency's public health mission and uphold the agency's commitment to trusted science, transparency, and common sense.

title: FDA Grants Marketing Authorization of First Home Test for Chlamydia, Gonorrhea and Trichomoniasis
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted marketing authorization to Visby Medical for its Women’s Sexual Health Test, the first diagnostic test for chlamydia, gonorrhea, and trichomoniasis that can be purchased without a prescription and performed at home. The test is intended for females with or without symptoms and delivers results in approximately 30 minutes. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, more than 2.2 million cases of chlamydia and gonorrhea were diagnosed in the U.S. in 2023. The test correctly identified 98.8% of negative and 97.2% of positive Chlamydia trachomatosis samples, 99.1% of negative and 100% of positive Neisseria gonorrhoeae samples, and 98.5% of negative and 97.8% of positive Trichomonas vaginalis samples. The test is a single-use, at-home test that includes a collection kit and a powered testing device. The FDA reviewed this test under the De Novo remarket review pathway and is establishing special controls to ensure safety and effectiveness.

title: FDA Approves Novel Treatment for Hemophilia A or B, with or without Factor Inhibitors
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Qfitlia (fitusiran) for routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce bleeding episodes in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with hemophilia A or hemophilia B. Tanya Wroblewski, M.D., stated that Qfitlia is significant for patients with hemophilia as it can be administered less frequently than existing options. Qfitlia reduces the amount of antithrombin, leading to an increase in thrombin, an enzyme critical for blood clotting. The FDA granted clearance of the INNOVANCE Antithrombin test to monitor and adjust dosing and frequency of injections. Two multicenter, randomized clinical trials enrolled 177 patients, assessing Qfitlia's efficacy and safety. Qfitlia's efficacy was established in a long-term extension study, showing a 73% reduction in estimated annualized bleeding rate in participants with inhibitors, and a 71% reduction in participants without inhibitors. Qfitlia has warnings for thrombotic events, gallbladder disease, liver toxicity, and common side effects such as viral infection and cold symptoms. The FDA granted Qfitlia Orphan Drug and Fast Track designations, and approved it for Sanofi.

title: FDA Roundup: March 28, 2025
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has published two new videos as part of its Learning and Education to ADvance and Empower Rare Disease Drug Developers initiative. The videos provide an overview of considerations for selecting endpoints in clinical trials and leveraging natural history study data. The FDA has also issued a Blue Box update to a Safety Alert on contaminated Korean oysters, adding additional recalled products. On the same day, the FDA approved Exelixis, Inc.'s Cabometyx for treating certain types of pancreatic and extra-pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. Additionally, the FDA published a Consumer Update on Pulse Oximeter Basics and an update on its ongoing evaluation of Essure. The FDA also celebrated 15 years since the passage of the Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act and marked the 10th anniversary since the approval of the first biosimilar in the United States.

title: Executive Order 14251—Exclusions From Federal Labor-Management Relations Programs
body_summary: US President Donald J. Trump issued an executive order (EO 12171, as amended) that delegates authority to certain government officials to issue orders suspending the application of labor laws to certain subdivisions of the departments they supervise, including the Secretaries of Defense and Veterans Affairs, and the Secretary of Transportation.

title: FDA Roundup: March 21, 2025
body_summary: The US FDA approved Fabhalta (iptacopan) for treating adults with C3G to reduce proteinuria. C3G causes inflammation and damage to kidney glomeruli. The FDA also issued a medical device early alert for Calyxo CVAC Aspiration Systems due to updated instructions for use. Additionally, the FDA authorized marketing for the CORIS System, the first automated endoscope channel cleaner for colonovideoscopes used in colonoscopy.

title: HHS, FDA Announce Chemical Contaminants Transparency Tool for Foods
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) unveiled the Chemical Contaminants Transparency Tool (CCT Tool), an online searchable database, under the leadership of Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. The database provides a consolidated list of contaminant levels used to evaluate potential health risks of contaminants in human foods. The FDA establishes or utilizes tolerances, action levels, and guidance levels for some contaminants in food to protect public health. The CCT Tool, launched as part of the FDA's initiative to modernize food chemical safety, includes contaminant levels in one location for easy searching. The consolidated list can be filtered by contaminant type, and the FDA will continue to monitor the food supply through testing programs.

title: Executive Order 14241—Immediate Measures To Increase American Mineral Production
body_summary: The President has ordered the immediate facilitation of domestic mineral production to maximize national security and economic benefits. The order defines critical minerals, mineral production, and processing, and establishes a National Energy Dominance Council to oversee the process. It prioritizes mineral production projects, identifies suitable Federal lands for leasing, and waives certain regulations to accelerate private and public capital investment in domestic mineral production. The order, issued under the Defense Production Act, also delegates authority to the US International Development Finance Corporation's CEO to provide loans and investments to domestic mineral producers, aiming to advance national security and secure vital mineral supply chains.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace. The unemployment rate has stabilized at a low level in recent months, and labor market conditions remain solid. Inflation remains somewhat elevated. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. Uncertainty around the economic outlook has increased. The Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate. In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent. In considering the extent and timing of additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. The Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgageâbacked securities. Beginning in April, the Committee will slow the pace of decline of its securities holdings by reducing the monthly redemption cap on Treasury securities from $25 billion to $5 billion. The Committee will maintain the monthly redemption cap on agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities at $35 billion. The Committee is strongly committed to supporting maximum employment and returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Susan M. Collins; Lisa D. Cook; Austan D. Goolsbee; Philip N. Jefferson; Adriana D. Kugler; Alberto G. Musalem; and Jeffrey R. Schmid. Voting against this action was Christopher J. Waller, who supported no change for the federal funds target range but preferred to continue the current pace of decline in securities holdings.

title: Implementation Note issued March 19, 2025
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on March 19, 2025: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 4.4 percent, effective March 20, 2025. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective March 20, 2025, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 4.5 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 4.25 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in March that exceeds a cap of $25 billion per month. Beginning on April 1, roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $5 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to these monthly caps and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly caps. Reinvest the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month into Treasury securities to roughly match the maturity composition of Treasury securities outstanding. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 4.5 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: HHS, FDA Announce Operation Stork Speed to Expand Options for Safe, Reliable, and Nutritious Infant Formula for American Families
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, under Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., is taking steps to enhance the quality, safety, and nutritional adequacy of the domestic infant formula supply. The FDA will use all resources to ensure infant formula products are safe and wholesome for families and children. The agency is beginning the nutrient review process, increasing testing for heavy metals and contaminants, and encouraging companies to develop new formulas and improve labeling. The FDA also aims to communicate regularly with consumers and industry stakeholders, collaborating with the National Institutes of Health on scientific research gaps.

title: FDA Roundup: March 18, 2025
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has taken action against Totally Cool, Inc., a Maryland-based ice cream manufacturer, and its CEO Michael J. Uhlfelder. The FDA suspended the company's food facility registration on July 8, 2024, after an inspection revealed contamination and manufacturing failures. A consent decree was entered, prohibiting Totally Cool and Mr. Uhlfelder from handling food until they meet certain requirements. The FDA is also aware of disruptions in hemodialysis bloodline supplies, which are expected to last through early fall 2025, and has recommended health care providers conserve use and report problems. The FDA has announced the conditional approval of Felycin-CA1, a medication for managing ventricular hypertrophy in cats with subclinical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Additionally, the FDA has issued a safety alert warning consumers against inhaling or recreationally using nitrous oxide products due to serious health risks.

title: FDA Educational Efforts Prevented Nearly 450,000 Youth from Starting E-Cigarette Use in One Year
body_summary: A study co-authored by U.S. Food and Drug Administration scientists found that the agency's youth e-cigarette prevention campaign, "The Real Cost," successfully reduced e-cigarette use among youth. The campaign, launched in 2018, prevented an estimated 444,252 American youth from starting to use e-cigarettes between 2023 and 2024. Since 2019, the number of U.S. middle and high school students using e-cigarettes has declined from 5.38 million to 1.63 million. Acting FDA Commissioner Sara Brenner said, "This includes taking evidence-based actions to prevent youth tobacco product use." The survey collected information on how frequently youth were exposed to "The Real Cost" campaign and showed that viewing ads lowered chances that youth who had never used an e-cigarette would later initiate use. The FDA's Center for Tobacco Products director, Brian King, said, "Youth tobacco prevention campaigns not only work, but they are also a cost-effective approach to protecting young people from a lifetime of nicotine addiction." The campaign also saved $180 for every dollar spent, totaling more than $53 billion in reduced smoking-related costs.

title: Executive Order 14236—Additional Rescissions of Harmful Executive Orders and Actions
body_summary:
The President has issued an Executive Order rescinding 78 Presidential orders and memoranda issued by then-President Biden, as part of a broader effort to "restore common sense to the Federal Government and unleash the potential of American citizens." The rescissions include Executive Orders 13994, 14026, and 14112, among others, and are intended to advance the policy of the United States.

Important actions include the revocation of Executive Order 13994, National Security Memorandum 3, and Presidential Memorandum of February 4, 2021, among others. The order also includes provisions for the implementation of the rescissions, including consistent implementation with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.

The order was signed by President Donald J. Trump on March 14, 2025.

title: FDA Roundup: March 14, 2025
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration posted information on the flu vaccine composition for the 2025-2026 U.S. flu season on Thursday. The agency reviewed available data with federal partners and recommended updated vaccine production to manufacturers. This decision does not impact vaccine supply or timing of availability. The FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) published two case studies and a user guide on rare disease drug development as part of the Accelerating Rare Disease Cures (ARC) Program's LEADER 3D initiative. The American Society of Addiction Medicine (ASAM) issued the final guideline "The Joint Clinical Practice Guideline on Benzodiazepine Tapering" on Wednesday, focusing on safe tapering strategies for clinicians. The FDA also issued a Safety Alert on Tuesday advising against serving or selling certain frozen oysters potentially contaminated with norovirus.

title: FDA Roundup: March 11, 2025
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a General Correspondence Letter to Mid-Link Technology Testing Co., Ltd., stating that the firm has submitted unreliable testing data, including copied or falsified results, which will be rejected. The FDA is vigilant in ensuring data submitted to the agency can be relied upon to assess device effectiveness and safety. The agency is also taking action against companies introducing unapproved fat dissolving injectable drug products into interstate commerce, including Amazon.com, Inc., Fox Pharma LLC, Filler Lux dba Filler Lux USA, Hyaluron Pen Store, LLC dba Glow Nest Beauty, Julian Naya Beauty LLC, and Vivid-Scientific LLC. Additionally, the FDA has approved Omlyclo (omalizumab-igec) injection for subcutaneous use to treat certain allergic, inflammatory, and autoimmune conditions, marking the first interchangeable biosimilar to Xolair (omalizumab).

title: FDA Roundup: March 7, 2025
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Encelto (revakinagene taroretcel-lwey), an allogeneic encapsulated cell-based gene therapy, for the treatment of adults with idiopathic macular telangiectasia type 2 (MacTel). Encelto is administered during a single surgical procedure and works by expressing recombinant human ciliary neurotrophic factor to promote the survival and maintenance of macular photoreceptors. The FDA also expanded the indication for neffy (epinephrine nasal spray) to include children four years of age and older who weigh 15 to less than 30 kg, allowing for treatment of anaphylaxis.

title: FDA Roundup: March 4, 2025
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved several drugs on Friday. The FDA informed sponsors of testosterone products of new labeling changes due to results from the TRAVERSE clinical trial. The changes include a new warning about increased blood pressure. The FDA also approved TNKase to treat acute ischemic stroke in adults, with the most common adverse reaction being bleeding. Additionally, the FDA approved the first generics of Xarelto, a 2.5mg tablet, to reduce cardiovascular risks in patients with CAD and PAD.

title: FDA Roundup: February 28, 2025
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Odactra for individuals 5-11 years old to treat allergic rhinitis, expanding its approved age range. The FDA also updated an outbreak advisory on Listeria monocytogenes and cleared Tandem Diabetes Care's Control-IQ+ technology for type 1 and type 2 diabetes management. Additionally, the FDA approved a software update for Medtronic's Activa, Percept, and SenSight Deep Brain Stimulation Therapy System, providing an option for adaptive deep brain stimulation for Parkinson's Disease.

title: The President's News Conference With Prime Minister Keir Starmer of the United Kingdom
body_summary: President Trump welcomed Prime Minister Starmer to the White House for a historic second state visit, thanking him for the visit. The two leaders discussed a breakthrough agreement to provide the US with reimbursement for loans sent to Ukraine, and the US will become a major partner in Ukraine's minerals and rare earths development. They agreed to work together to deliver a "tough and fair" deal, backed by strength to stop Putin coming back for more. The UK will give more military aid to Ukraine than ever, while the US will work on a peace agreement. President Trump also expressed concern over the BBC's reporting on the Gaza coverage. The two leaders discussed a potential deal with Russia, with Prime Minister Starmer stating it could be "really terrific" for both countries, and President Trump saying he would end the war and secure a great trade deal.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Cerebrotendinous Xanthomatosis, a Rare Lipid Storage Disease
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Ctexli (chenodiol) for the treatment of cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis (CTX) in adults. The FDA's Office of Rare Diseases director, Janet Maynard, M.D., M.H.S., stated that the approval provides a safe and effective treatment option for CTX. CTEX is a genetic metabolic disorder caused by a mutation in the CYP27A1 gene, resulting in a deficiency of the enzyme that breaks down fats. The efficacy of Ctexli was evaluated in a 24-week trial, which demonstrated significant reduction in plasma cholestanol and urine 23S-pentol compared to placebo. Ctexli works by replacing deficient levels of bile acids, reducing abnormal cholesterol deposits. The prescribing information includes a warning for liver toxicity, and patients should obtain liver blood tests before and annually while on treatment. The recommended dosage is 250 milligrams, taken orally three times a day. The FDA granted Ctexli Priority Review, Fast Track, and Orphan Drug designations.

title: Executive Order 14217—Commencing the Reduction of the Federal Bureaucracy
body_summary: The President has ordered a dramatic reduction in the size of the Federal Government, aiming to minimize Government waste and abuse, reduce inflation, and promote American freedom and innovation. The order commences a reduction in non-statutory components and functions of certain governmental entities. The following entities will be eliminated: the Presidio Trust, the Inter-American Foundation, the United States African Development Foundation, and the United States Institute of Peace. Heads of executive departments and agencies must submit reports confirming compliance within 14 days. Funding requests for these entities will be rejected if inconsistent with the order.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on January 28-29, 2025. The committee selected John C. Williams as chair and Jerome H. Powell as vice chair, reaffirming its FOMC Authorizations and Continuing Directives for Open Market Operations without revision. The committee emphasized its firm commitment to achieving maximum employment and 2% inflation. Participants expected framework review discussions to continue at upcoming meetings, with a goal of wrapping up by late summer. Financial market developments were reviewed, noting moderate declines in equity prices, tight credit spreads, and a slight rise in the dollar value. The modal policy rate path implied no significant change, consistent with a single quarter-point lowering of the federal funds rate in 2025. Employment-to-population ratio increased slightly, while African American and Hispanic unemployment rates decreased but remained higher than those for Asians and Whites. Average hourly earnings rose 3.9% over the year. Real GDP grew at a solid pace, private domestic final purchases rising faster. Foreign economic growth slowed in some regions, with Chinese growth picking up due to policy stimulus. Inflation abroad eased, except in Brazil where it continued to rise. CRE property prices declined, but flat in Q3. Business debt leverage was elevated, while household balance sheets remained solid. The staff's economic outlook projection showed a narrowing output gap and low unemployment rate. Inflation projections were unchanged, with 2% expected by 2027. Participants viewed the uncertainty around the baseline projection as similar to the average over the past 20 years. The Committee maintained the target range for the federal funds rate at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent, agreeing to continue reducing securities holdings.

title: FDA Approves First Rapid-Acting Insulin Biosimilar Product for Treatment of Diabetes
body_summary: The US FDA approved Merilog, a biosimilar to Novolog, for improving glycemic control in adults and pediatric patients with diabetes. Merilog is a rapid-acting human insulin analog, helping to lower mealtime blood sugar spikes. It is the first rapid-acting insulin biosimilar product approved by the FDA and is available in a 3mL single-patient-use prefilled pen and a 10mL multiple-dose vial. This approval joins two long-acting insulin biosimilar products approved in 2021. The FDA has approved a total of 65 biosimilar products. Approximately 8.4 million Americans rely on insulin therapy, and having a biosimilar option can increase access to life-saving medications. Merilog should be administered subcutaneously before meals, and dosing should be individualized.

title: Executive Order 14212—Establishing the President's Make America Healthy Again Commission
body_summary: The President issued an order to combat alarming health challenges, particularly in children, and established the Make America Healthy Again Commission to advise on addressing the childhood chronic disease crisis. The Commission aims to study the crisis, advise the public, and provide policy recommendations. On February 13, 2025, President Trump issued an executive order requiring the Commission to develop a "Make Our Children Healthy Again Strategy" within 180 days. The strategy will restructure the Federal Government's response and add new solutions to address childhood chronic diseases.

title: The President's News Conference With Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba of Japan
body_summary: US President Trump welcomed Japanese Prime Minister Ishiba Shigeru to the White House, reaffirming the US commitment to Japan's security, including increased defense spending and military cooperation. Japan is set to double its defense spending by 2027. The US and Japan also agreed to strengthen the Japan-US alliance to achieve a free and open Indo-Pacific, with the US to defend Japan. The two leaders discussed economic cooperation, with Japan aiming to invest $1 trillion in the US. They also talked about North Korea's nuclear program and denuclearization. The US President expressed a desire for a strong education system, citing the example of states like Norway and Denmark, which have no debt and operate well. Trump announced a reciprocal deal with U.S. Steel, allowing for investments rather than purchases, and the US will resume importing LNG to Japan.

title: FDA Alerts Patients of Potential to Miss Critical Safety Alerts Due to Phone Settings When Using Smartphone-Compatible Diabetes Devices
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is alerting patients to a safety concern with diabetes devices that rely on a smartphone to deliver critical safety alerts. Users of these devices can configure alert settings, but if not configured correctly, it may lead to serious harm. The FDA has identified software configuration issues, hardware changes, and smartphone operating system updates that can interrupt critical device operation. Users are advised to carefully follow manufacturer instructions, turn off automatic OS updates, and regularly check their alert settings. The FDA is working with manufacturers to evaluate smartphone alert configurations and ensure settings are tested and communicated clearly to users.

title: FDA Approves Novel Non-Opioid Treatment for Moderate to Severe Acute Pain
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Journavx (suzetrigine) 50 milligram oral tablets, a first-in-class non-opioid analgesic, to treat moderate to severe acute pain in adults. The drug reduces pain by targeting a pain-signaling pathway involving sodium channels in the peripheral nervous system. The approval follows two randomized, double-blind, placebo- and active-controlled trials demonstrating a statistically significant superior reduction in pain with Journavx compared to placebo. Journavx is contraindicated for concomitant use with strong CYP3A inhibitors and patients should avoid food or drink containing grapefruit when taking Journavx. The FDA granted approval of Journavx to Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated.

title: Implementation Note issued January 29, 2025
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on January 29, 2025: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 4.4 percent, effective January 30, 2025. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective January 30, 2025, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 4-1/4 to 4â1/2 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 4.5 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 4.25 percent and with a perâcounterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $25 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency mortgageâbacked securities (MBS) received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month into Treasury securities to roughly match the maturity composition of Treasury securities outstanding. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 4.5 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace. The unemployment rate has stabilized at a low level in recent months, and labor market conditions remain solid. Inflation remains somewhat elevated. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are roughly in balance. The economic outlook is uncertain, and the Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate. In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent. In considering the extent and timing of additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. The Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgageâbacked securities. The Committee is strongly committed to supporting maximum employment and returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Susan M. Collins; Lisa D. Cook; Austan D. Goolsbee; Philip N. Jefferson; Adriana D. Kugler; Alberto G. Musalem; Jeffrey R. Schmid; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: Executive Order 14187—Protecting Children From Chemical and Surgical Mutilation
body_summary: President Donald J. Trump signed an order on January 28, 2025, ordering an end to the practice of "chemical and surgical mutilation" of children, which includes puberty blockers, hormone treatments, and surgical procedures aimed at altering a child's physical appearance to align with their gender identity. The order prohibits federal funding, promotion, or support for these procedures and requires a review of existing literature on best practices for promoting the health of minors with gender dysphoria. The order also directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to rescind or amend policies that rely on "Standards of Care Version 8" by WPATH and to increase the quality of data to guide practices.

title: Memorandum From the Acting Director, Office of Management and Budget on Temporary Pause of Agency Grant, Loan, and Other Financial Assistance Programs
body_summary:
The Executive Office of the President has issued a memorandum requiring heads of executive departments and agencies to temporarily pause all activities related to obligation or disbursement of Federal financial assistance programs, including grants, loans, and other assistance, effective January 28, 2025. The pause is intended to allow the Administration to review agency programs and determine the best uses of funding consistent with the law and the President's priorities.

This pause is in response to the President's policies and requirements, which aim to advance Administration priorities such as increasing the impact of every federal taxpayer dollar, eliminating the financial burden of inflation, and promoting efficiency in government. The pause applies to all Federal financial assistance programs, including those related to foreign aid, nongovernmental organizations, and social engineering policies.

Each agency must immediately identify any legally mandated actions or deadlines for assistance programs arising during the pause and report this information to the Office of Management and Budget. No later than February 10, 2025, agencies must submit detailed information on programs, projects, or activities subject to the pause.

title: Executive Order 14154—Unleashing American Energy
body_summary: The President issued an executive order to promote America's energy resources, restoring economic prosperity and national security. Key actions include reviewing and revising agency actions impeding energy development, eliminating burdensome regulations, and redirecting resources from the American Climate Corps. The order terminates all American Climate Corps activities, effective immediately, and revokes Executive Order 11991. It also requires expedited permitting approvals, prioritizing efficiency and certainty over activist group objectives, and restarts reviews of liquefied natural gas export projects to assess public interest.

title: Executive Order 14148—Initial Rescissions of Harmful Executive Orders and Actions
body_summary: The President has ordered the revocation of 32 executive actions, including those related to climate change, immigration, and diversity, equity, and inclusion. Executive Order 14143, signed by President Donald J. Trump on January 16, 2025, was the first to be issued. The order revoked National Security Presidential Memorandum 5 and directed agencies to end Federal implementation of DEI ideology. The Director of the Domestic Policy Council and National Economic Council will review Federal Government actions and submit a list of orders to be rescinded or replaced within 45 days.

title: Memorandum on Hiring Freeze
body_summary: The President orders a hiring freeze for all Federal civilian employees in the executive branch, to be applied throughout the branch, except for certain exceptions such as military personnel, immigration enforcement, national security, and public safety positions. The freeze applies to all executive departments and agencies unless otherwise provided for in this memorandum or applicable law. The Director of the Office of Personnel Management may grant exemptions where necessary. A plan to reduce the size of the Federal Government's workforce must be submitted within 90 days. The memorandum expires for all agencies except the Internal Revenue Service, which remains under the freeze until lifted by the Secretary of the Treasury.

title: Statement on Medicare Prescription Drug Price Negotiations
body_summary: The administration has selected 15 new drugs for Medicare drug price negotiation. The selected drugs treat conditions such as diabetes and cancer. This brings the total to 25 drugs, representing about a third of Medicare Part D spending on prescription drugs. The Inflation Reduction Act delivered dramatic savings, slashing prices by 40 to 80 percent. The administration completed the first round of price negotiation last year.

title: FDA Roundup: January 17, 2025
body_summary: The FDA released updates and approvals in 2023. The agency released a prevention strategy for berry contamination, held a public workshop on cellular therapies, and created an IT operating plan for Fiscal Years 2024-2027. The FDA also hosted a workshop on optimizing pregnancy registries and issued an early alert on the Ivenix Infusion System. In addition, the FDA approved sotorasib 960 mg/panitumumab for patients with previously untreated mantle cell lymphoma, and granted traditional approval for acalabrutinib as a single agent for adults with previously treated MCL.

title: Memorandum on Orderly Implementation of the Air Toxics Standards for Ethylene Oxide Commercial Sterilizers
body_summary: The President ordered the Administrator of the EPA and the Secretary of Health and Human Services to implement a new rule reducing emissions of ethylene oxide from commercial sterilizers, aimed at protecting public health. The rule applies to facilities sterilizing medical products and establishes a process for considering requests for Presidential exemptions, which must be submitted 12-24 months before the compliance deadline. The Administrator will review requests with the Secretary, providing public notification and receiving necessary information within specified timeframes. The process ensures consideration of exceptional circumstances where a facility cannot meet the standards before the deadline.

title: Executive Order 14144—Strengthening and Promoting Innovation in the Nation's Cybersecurity
body_summary: The US President orders additional actions to improve the nation's cybersecurity. The Secretary of Homeland Security is required to develop a concept of operations to identify novel cyber threats and vulnerabilities across the Federal civilian enterprise. Working groups for EDR solutions and endpoint security must be established, with endpoints enrolled in the CISA Persistent Access Capability program within 180 days. The Director of NIST must publish updated guidance on deploying BGP security methods and emerging technologies for Internet routing security and resilience. Agencies must develop and issue mobile driver's licenses, remote digital identity verification guidance, and research AI for cyber defense within 180, 270, and 150 days, respectively. Agencies must also implement minimum cybersecurity practices within 240 days, with contractors following these practices under agency contracts. This order targets cyber-enabled attacks, including ransomware, and is built on Executive Order 14028, which sets standards for security controls, including "key establishment", "least privilege", and "zero trust architecture".

title: FDA Authorizes Marketing of 20 ZYN Nicotine Pouch Products after Extensive Scientific Review
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has authorized the marketing of 20 ZYN nicotine pouch products through the premarket tobacco product application (PMTA) pathway. The agency determined that these products met the public health standard, considering risks and benefits to the population as a whole. The authorized products have substantially lower amounts of harmful constituents than cigarettes and most smokeless tobacco products, posing lower risk of cancer and other serious health conditions. The FDA also found that these products have the potential to provide a benefit to adults who smoke cigarettes and/or use other smokeless tobacco products, outweighing the risks. The authorizations impose stringent marketing restrictions, including measures to ensure ads are targeted to adults ages 21 and older. The products are not "FDA approved" and there is no safe tobacco product. The agency will closely monitor the marketing and use of these products.

title: Memorandum on Orderly Implementation of the Air Toxics Standards for Ethylene Oxide Commercial Sterilizers
body_summary: The President ordered the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency and the Secretary of Health and Human Services to implement the Air Toxics Standards for Ethylene Oxide Commercial Sterilizers, aiming to reduce emissions of toxic air pollutant EtO from sterilizing facilities. A process for considering Presidential exemptions will be established, allowing facilities to request exemptions if they cannot install necessary technology before compliance deadlines. Facilities can request an exemption, which involves submitting a request to the Chairman of the Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ) within 30 days. CEQ advises the President on the request, usually within 45 days, and the President grants or denies the exemption, with the Administrator notifying the applicant within 10 days. If granted, the Administrator makes the information publicly available within 60 days and submits a report to Congress, while providing technical assistance to facilities with exemptions to ensure compliance with the EtO Rule.

title: FDA Proposes Significant Step Toward Reducing Nicotine to Minimally or Nonaddictive Level in Cigarettes and Certain Other Combusted Tobacco Products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has proposed a rule to make cigarettes and certain other combustible tobacco products minimally or non-addictive by limiting the level of nicotine in those products. If finalized, this would be the first country to take such a bold action. The FDA first announced its intent to propose this rule in 2018 and is now seeking input from the public, including through public comment and the FDA's Tobacco Products Scientific Advisory Committee. The proposed nicotine level for cigarettes would be 0.7 milligrams per gram of tobacco, significantly lower than the average concentration in these products on the market today. The proposed rule would apply to cigarettes, cigar tobacco, roll-your-own tobacco, most cigars, and pipe tobacco. The FDA estimates that this rule could prevent approximately 48 million U.S. youth and young adults from starting smoking, and 12.9 million people who smoke cigarettes would stop doing so within one year of the rule becoming effective. The estimated benefits of the proposed rule are over $1.1 trillion per year over the first four decades.

title: FDA Proposes Requiring At-a-Glance Nutrition Information on the Front of Packaged Foods
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is proposing to require afront-of-package (FOP) nutrition label for most packaged foods. The proposed label, called the "Nutrition Info box," would display information on saturated fat, sodium, and added sugars content, helping consumers make informed choices. The FDA aims to address the nation's chronic disease crisis, which affects 60% of Americans and costs $4.5 trillion annually. The proposal is part of the White House National Strategy on Hunger, Nutrition and Health to reduce diet-related diseases by 2030. The FDA Commissioner, Robert M. Califf, and Deputy Commissioner, Jim Jones, support the initiative, which has been informed by research and consumer focus groups. The proposed rule would require food manufacturers to add the Nutrition Info box to most packaged products three years after the final rule's effective date for businesses with $10 million or more in annual food sales, and four years for those with less. Comments on the proposed rule can be submitted electronically by May 16, 2025.

title: FDA Roundup: January 14, 2025
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration issued a Request for Information on industry practices related to poppy seeds to better understand the presence of opiate alkaloids. The FDA also issued a Dear Veterinarian letter warning practitioners about burns associated with Megadyne grounding pads. Commissioner Robert M. Califf wrote a personal reflection on COVID vaccines in the FDA Voices blog. The FDA published a blog on global efforts to address substandard and falsified medical products through informal markets. The FDA, US Homeland Security Investigations, and US Customs and Border Protection seized over 628,000 unauthorized e-cigarette products valued at more than $7 million from a warehouse in Miami.

title: FDA Roundup: January 10, 2025
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration released a Long-Term National Strategy to Increase the Resiliency of the U.S. Infant Formula Market, focusing on achieving a more robust and nimble infant formula supply. The strategy builds on the 2023 Immediate National Strategy and a study by the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering and Medicine. Consumers can expect increased confidence in the safety and nutrition of infant formula, according to Jim Jones, FDA Deputy Commissioner for Human Foods. The FDA also published reports on drug approvals, including a first-in-class drug for schizophrenia, and issued a Request For Comments on the National Antimicrobial Resistance Monitoring System. Additionally, the FDA updated an outbreak advisory for Salmonella Typhimurium infections linked to cucumbers, and published a Consumer Update on keeping a medication list.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary:
Here is a summary of the source document:

The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting on December 17-18, 2024. The committee judged risks to achieving maximum employment and price stability roughly in balance, with upside risks to inflation increasing due to stronger-than-expected readings on inflation and potential changes in trade and immigration policy. Real GDP posted a solid gain in the third quarter, while exports rose briskly and imports fell more than exports. Nominal Treasury yields rose slightly, then reversed those increases, ending little changed. The committee viewed uncertainty around the baseline projection as within normal range, with balanced risks for employment and real GDP growth, but tilted upside for inflation. Inflation was forecasted to decline from 2024's 2% rate to 1% by 2027. The staff set a target range for the federal funds rate at 4¼ to 4½ percent, lowering it by 25 basis points to achieve maximum employment and price stability.

title: FDA Roundup: January 7, 2025
body_summary: The US FDA has issued several draft and final guidances on various topics, including medical devices, optical imaging, food safety, animal food ingredients, and human cells, tissues, and cellular and tissue-based products. The FDA has also announced its participation in the NIH Rare Disease Day 2025 meeting, scheduled for February 27 and 28, 2025.

title: FDA Proposes Updated Recommendations to Help Improve Performance of Pulse Oximeters Across Skin Tones
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has published a new draft guidance to improve the accuracy and performance of pulse oximeters, which estimate blood oxygen levels, across a range of skin pigmentation. The FDA aims to address concerns about accuracy differences in pulse oximeter performance between individuals with lighter and darker skin pigmentation. The draft guidance proposes recommendations for manufacturers to gather clinical data, increase study participant numbers, and use standardized methods to evaluate device performance. The FDA expects some marketed pulse oximeters to meet the updated performance criteria without modifications. The guidance applies to pulse oximeters intended for medical purposes, primarily used in hospital settings, and does not apply to general wellness or sporting/aviation products. The FDA will review comments on the draft guidance within 60 days of publication.

title: FDA Proposes Framework to Advance Credibility of AI Models Used for Drug and Biological Product Submissions
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has issued draft guidance on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to support regulatory decision-making for drug and biological products. This is the first guidance on the use of AI in the development of medical products. The FDA aims to provide an agile, risk-based framework that promotes innovation and ensures robust scientific and regulatory standards are met. 

The FDA has substantial experience reviewing submissions with AI components since 2016. AI can be used to predict patient outcomes, improve understanding of disease progression, and analyze large datasets. To ensure model credibility, the FDA provides a risk-based framework for sponsors to assess and establish the credibility of an AI model. The agency encourages early engagement with AI credibility assessment or the use of AI in human and animal drug development.

The FDA's human and animal medical product centers, along with the Office of Inspections and Investigations, worked collaboratively on this draft guidance. The agency recognizes that AI management requires a risk-based regulatory framework built on robust principles, standards, and best practices. The FDA is seeking public comment on the draft guidance within 90 days, seeking feedback on how well the guidance aligns with industry experience and whether the options for engagement are sufficient.

title: FDA Issues Draft Guidance on Including Tissue Biopsies in Clinical Trials
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a draft guidance with the Office for Human Research Protections to provide recommendations for including tissue biopsies as part of clinical trials. The draft guidance, intended to assist industry, clinical investigators, institutions, and institutional review boards, aims to improve participant safety and further clinical research. Richard Pazdur, M.D., director of the FDA's Oncology Center of Excellence, stated that tissue biopsies are often needed to determine eligibility or understand the effect of the medical product being studied. The guidance focuses on considerations for when a tissue biopsy is included in a clinical trial protocol, including risk and benefit considerations specific to children. The agency emphasizes the importance of obtaining informed consent from participants, including parental permission for children and, when appropriate, assent from children. Comments on the draft guidance must be submitted within 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.

title: FDA Issues Comprehensive Draft Guidance for Developers of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Medical Devices
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued draft guidance to support the development and marketing of safe and effective AI-enabled devices throughout their total product life cycle. The guidance, if finalized, would be the first to provide comprehensive recommendations for AI-enabled devices from design to maintenance and documentation. The FDA is encouraging sponsors to engage with the agency early and often to use the guidance to guide their activities throughout the life cycle of the device. The draft guidance includes recommendations for transparency and bias in AI-enabled devices, as well as strategies to address these risks. The FDA is requesting public comment on the draft guidance by April 7, 2025, and will hold a webinar on February 18, 2025, to discuss the guidance.

title: FDA Roundup: January 3, 2025
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has issued several notices, including:
The FDA determined that 35 food contact notifications related to per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are no longer effective due to abandoned uses. 
A safety alert was issued for restaurants, retailers, and consumers in Oregon and Washington regarding the consumption of shellstock oysters harvested from December 2 to December 17, 2024, due to a norovirus outbreak. 
The FDA issued a medical device early alert for solution sets, fluid delivery sets, and single-use blood circuits as part of the Center for Devices and Radiological Health's communications pilot to enhance the medical device recall program.
A virtual public meeting will be held on January 30, 2025, to share updates on the Center for Devices and Radiological Health's Real-World Evidence program.
The FDA unveiled an Idea Lab, part of the Home as a Health Care Hub initiative, to reimagine the home as an integral part of the health care system, including a virtual reality prototype called Lilypad.

title: Statement on Prescription Drug Costs Under Medicare
body_summary: The President believes that healthcare should be a right, not a privilege. Throughout their Presidency, they have advanced this goal. The new $2,000 cap on prescription drug costs under the Inflation Reduction Act is now fully in effect. Before the cap, people with Medicare faced a crushing burden, paying $10,000 a year or more in copays. The cap has saved people with Medicare $1 billion in cost sharing in the first 6 months of 2024. Starting January 1, 2025, the cap will fully phase in, saving an estimated 19 million people an average of $400 each.

title: FDA Roundup: December 27, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has announced several updates and approvals. On Thursday, the FDA recommended changes to labeling for transmucosal buprenorphine products to encourage the submission of supplemental new drug applications. On Monday, the FDA issued a final rule establishing requirements for a nonprescription drug product with an additional condition for nonprescription use. Director Patrizia Cavazzoni stated that the action aims to broaden the types of nonprescription drugs available to consumers. The FDA shared findings from an independent review of publication studies on contaminants in tampons, concluding that the findings did not identify safety concerns. On Friday, December 20, the FDA approved Alhemo for routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce bleeding episodes in patients with hemophilia A or B. The FDA also approved the alfapump System, an implanted pump for removing excess peritoneal fluid in patients with liver cirrhosis.

title: FDA Proposes Rule to Require Standardized Testing Methods for Detecting and Identifying Asbestos in Talc-Containing Cosmetic Products
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced a proposed rule to establish standardized testing methods for detecting and identifying asbestos in talc-containing cosmetic products. The proposed rule aims to protect consumers from harmful exposure to asbestos, a known human carcinogen, found in contaminated talc-containing cosmetic products. The FDA will require manufacturers to test for asbestos using specific techniques, including Polarized Light Microscopy and Transmission Electron Microscopy, and to keep records to demonstrate compliance. The proposed rule is part of the FDA's work to fulfill the requirements of the Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022. The comment period for the proposed rule will end 90 days after publication in the Federal Register, and the FDA will review and consider comments as it develops the final rule.

title: FDA Approves First Generic of Once-Daily GLP-1 Injection to Lower Blood Sugar in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes
body_summary: The US FDA has approved the first generic version of Victoza (liraglutide injection), a GLP-1 receptor agonist, for improving glycemic control in adults and pediatric patients over 10 years old with type 2 diabetes. The FDA prioritizes the assessment of generic drug applications for drugs in shortage, including GLP-1 medications that are currently in short supply. The approval of this generic version is part of the FDA's efforts to increase access to needed medications. The generic liraglutide injection has a Boxed Warning to advise health care professionals and patients about the increased risk of thyroid C-cell tumors. The prescribing information also includes warnings about pancreatitis, hypoglycemia, and hypersensitivity reactions. The FDA approved this generic version for Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc.

title: FDA Approves First Medication for Obstructive Sleep Apnea
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Zepbound (tirzepatide) for treating moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in adults with obesity, to be used in combination with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity. Zepbound works by reducing appetite and food intake through the activation of hormones, and also improves OSA by reducing body weight. Two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies involving 469 adults without type 2 diabetes showed a statistically significant and clinically meaningful reduction in apnea and hypopnea events with Zepbound. The primary measure of efficacy was the change from baseline in the apnea hypopnea index (AHI) at week 52. Zepbound can cause side effects and has warnings for pancreatitis, gallbladder problems, hypoglycemia, and other conditions. The FDA granted approval to Eli Lilly and Co.

title: FDA Roundup: December 20, 2024
body_summary: The FDA has updated its guidance on clinical decision support software, authorized AI/ML-enabled medical devices, and provided approvals for various medical products. The agency approved an over-the-counter HIV test for adolescents, resolved a tirzepatide shortage, and cleared new medications for rare genetic disorders and cancer treatment. The FDA has also closed the E. coli outbreak linked to organic whole and baby carrots, which it confirmed occurred between 2023 and 2024. In 2013, the FDA and USDA signed a charter to clarify jurisdiction on animal biologicals, and a new one was announced to help resolve unclear cases, with a specific date not mentioned.

title: FDA Approves First Acellular Tissue Engineered Vessel to Treat Vascular Trauma in Extremities
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Symvess, a sterile, acellular tissue-engineered vessel, for use in adults as a vascular conduit for extremity arterial injury. This approval provides an important treatment option for individuals with vascular trauma, particularly when urgent revascularization is needed to avoid imminent limb loss. Symvess is manufactured using a tissue engineering process utilizing human vascular smooth muscle cells derived from human aortic tissue. The product was assessed in a prospective, single-arm, multicenter study involving 54 patients, with 67% retaining primary patency and 72% retaining secondary patency 30 days after implantation. The most common adverse reactions include thrombosis, fever, pain, and anastomotic stenosis. The FDA granted approval to Humacyte Global, Inc., following Priority Review, Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy (RMAT) designation, and designation as a Priority Product by the US Department of Defense.

title: FDA Updates “Healthy” Claim, Providing a Refreshed Tool for Consumers
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced a final rule to update the definition of the nutrient content claim "healthy." The updated definition will help ensure that consumers have access to more complete and accurate nutrition information on food labels, which is part of the FDA's whole-of-government approach to address the growing crisis of preventable diet-related chronic diseases in the U.S. 

The updated "healthy" claim will be used on food packages by manufacturers who meet the new definition, which requires foods to contain a certain amount of a food from at least one of the food groups or subgroups outlined by the Dietary Guidelines for Americans. The definition also includes limits on saturated fat, sodium, and added sugars. 

The FDA Commissioner, Robert M. Califf, M.D., stated that improving access to nutrition information is an important public health effort to help people build healthy eating patterns. The agency has already partnered with Instacart to make it easier for consumers to find products with the "healthy" claim through online grocery shopping filters and a virtual storefront. 

The FDA is also developing a "healthy" symbol that manufacturers could use to indicate their food meets the criteria of "healthy," which may be helpful for those who are less familiar with nutrition information.

title: FDA Approves First Mesenchymal Stromal Cell Therapy to Treat Steroid-refractory Acute Graft-versus-host Disease
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Ryoncil, an allogeneic bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cell therapy, for the treatment of steroid-refractory acute graft-versus-host disease in pediatric patients 2 months of age and older. Ryoncil contains MSCs isolated from healthy adult human donors and was evaluated in a multicenter study with 54 participants. Study participants who received Ryoncil twice weekly for four consecutive weeks showed an effectiveness based on the rate and duration of response to treatment 28 days after initiating Ryoncil. Sixteen participants had a complete response, while 22 had a partial response. The most common adverse reactions were infections, fever, and hypertension. The FDA granted approval to Mesoblast, Inc.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace. Since earlier in the year, labor market conditions have generally eased, and the unemployment rate has moved up but remains low. Inflation has made progress toward the Committee's 2 percent objective but remains somewhat elevated. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are roughly in balance. The economic outlook is uncertain, and the Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate. In support of its goals, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent. title: Implementation Note issued December 18, 2024
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on December 18, 2024: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to lower the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 4.4 percent, effective December 19, 2024. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective December 19, 2024, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 4.5 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 4.25 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Setting this rate at the bottom of the target range for the federal funds rate is intended to support effective monetary policy implementation and the smooth functioning of shortâterm funding markets. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In taking this action, the Board approved requests to establish that rate submitted by the Boards of Directors of the Federal Reserve Banks of Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Chicago, and San Francisco. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: FDA Roundup: December 17, 2024
body_summary:
The FDA posted four warning letters to companies for introducing unapproved GLP-1s into interstate commerce, including semaglutide, tirzepatide, and/or retatrutide products. The letters were sent to Xcel Peptides, Swisschems, Summit Research, and Prime Peptides. 

The FDA also announced new EU requirements for importing honey and other apiculture products, effective November 29, 2024, requiring establishments to register in the EU's Trade Control and Expert System. 

The FDA issued a letter to veterinarians regarding the evaluation of adverse events reported in dogs treated with Librela. 

The FDA issued a safety communication about the potential need for early device replacement of Boston Scientific Accolade pacemaker devices. 

The FDA announced the continuation of their webinar series exploring food safety culture. 

The FDA Office of Inspections and Investigations published a feature story about the identification of a doctor who poisoned patients with tainted IV bags. 

The FDA updated a prior Drug Safety Communication with the addition of a Boxed Warning for Veozah. 

The FDA approved Unloxcyt for adults with metastatic cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. 

The FDA approved Crenessity to control androgen levels in adults and pediatric patients. 

The FDA Office of Criminal Investigations was involved in a Justice Department announcement regarding the resolution of a criminal and civil investigation into McKinsey's advice to Purdue Pharma.

title: FDA Roundup: December 13, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing an update on recent announcements. The FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER) launched the Center for Real-World Evidence Innovation (CCRI) to coordinate and promote the use of real-world data and evidence in regulatory decision-making.
