FDA Commissioner Dr. Robert Califf and CDER deputy center director Dr. Marta Sokolowska authored an op-ed about the FDA's Prescribe with Confidence campaign, which aims to inform and support prescribers in treating opioid use disorder. The FDA also issued a letter to retailers and distributors of cookware products, warning them that certain imported products may contain lead and should not be sold in the U.S. market. Additionally, the FDA updated guidance on the registration and listing of cosmetic product facilities and products, with new FAQs open for public comment until January 13, 2025. A joint public meeting of the Drug Safety and Risk Management Advisory Committee and the Anesthetic and Analgesic Drug Products Advisory Committee will be held on February 5, 2025, to discuss epidemiological studies on opioid overdose.

title: FDA Approves New Treatment for Congenital Adrenal Hyperplasia
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Crenessity (crinecerfont) for adults and pediatric patients 4 years of age and older with classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH). The approval allows Crenessity to be used with glucocorticoids to control androgen levels. The FDA's Director of the Division of General Endocrinology, Theresa Kehoe, stated that the approval provides an important advance for patients with classic CAH. Crenessity's approval is based on two randomized trials involving 182 adults and 103 children with classic CAH. The primary measure of efficacy showed that patients who received Crenessity reduced their daily glucocorticoid dose by 27% compared to 10% for those who received placebo. Crenessity has a warning for acute adrenal insufficiency and should not be taken by patients with hypersensitivity to its active ingredient.

title: FDA Roundup: December 10, 2024
body_summary: The US FDA announced that on January 1, 2025, the Voluntary Qualified Importer Program (VQIP) application portal for fiscal year 2026 will open. The portal will be open until September 1, 2025. The FDA is also updating the outbreak advisory for Salmonella Typhimurium infections linked to cucumbers with additional retailer recall information. Additionally, the FDA's Office of Global Policy and Strategy published a conversation with Dr. Hilary Marston and Ann Meeker-O'Connell about the FDA's role in revising the Declaration of Helsinki.

title: FDA Roundup: December 6, 2024
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration is publishing an at-a-glance summary of recent news. 

The FDA published the draft guidance "Expedited Program for Serious Conditions — Accelerated Approval of Drugs and Biologics" proposing updates to agency policies and procedures for accelerated approval. 

The FDA updated the outbreak advisory on Salmonella: Cucumbers (November 2024) to include additional downstream recalls. 

A report on Risks and Benefits to Health of Non-Device Software Functions – December 2024 highlights findings on software functions excluded from the device definition by the 21st Century Cures Act. 

The FDA published a report stating youth tobacco product use continues to decline as FDA actions build momentum, according to Dr. Brian King, Director of FDA’s Center for Tobacco Products. 

The FDA granted accelerated approval to Bizengri (zenocutuzumab-zbco, Merus N.V.) for adults with specific types of cancer. 

The FDA approved Imfinzi (durvalumab, AstraZeneca) for adults with limited-stage small cell lung cancer. 

The FDA added empty intravenous (IV) containers to the Medical Device Shortages List due to a shortage expected to last through March 2025. 

The FDA approved the AeroPace System, a temporary diaphragm activation system, to improve ventilator weaning success in patients 18 years or older.

title: Statement on a Congressional Budget Office Report on Health Insurance Coverage
body_summary: The administration believes health care should be a right, not a privilege, and aims to make quality affordable coverage accessible to every American. The plan is working, with lower premiums, stronger Medicare and Medicaid, lower prescription drug costs for seniors, and more Americans with health insurance than ever. A Congressional Budget Office report supports this legislation, citing its role in reducing health care costs. The report highlights the impact of expanded premium tax credits, which benefit millions, and warns that removing these credits would lead to a spike in premiums and an estimated 3.8 million people becoming uninsured. The administration will continue to call on Congress to protect affordable health insurance for millions of Americans.

title: FDA Roundup: December 3, 2024
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has posted final guidance on Marketing Submission Recommendations for a Predetermined Change Control Plan for Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Device Software Functions. The guidance aims to promote the development of safe and effective AI-enabled devices. On January 14, 2025, a webinar will be hosted to discuss the final guidance.

The FDA has also issued draft guidance on notifying the agency of a permanent discontinuance or interruption of infant formula manufacture, and the 2024 edition of the Voluntary National Retail Food Regulatory Program Standards.

The FDA has updated its outbreak advisory for Salmonella Typhimurium infections linked to cucumbers, with 68 reported cases as of November 26, 2024. SunFed Produce, LLC, Baloian Farms of Arizona Co., Inc., and Russ Davis Wholesale have initiated voluntary recalls of American/slicer cucumbers.

The FDA is working with recalling firms to determine if additional downstream customer recalls are necessary. The agency's investigation is ongoing.

The Office of Global Policy and Strategy published a blog, "A rising tide that lifts all boats can help ensure a secure, resilient, and high-quality medical product supply chain," and the FDA published a Spotlight on CDER Science exploring the use of concise summary of risk information for drug safety.

title: USDA-FDA Seek Information About Food Date Labeling, Aim is to Provide Further Clarity, Transparency and Cost Savings for U.S. Consumers
body_summary:
USDA FSIS and the FDA have extended the comment period for their joint Request for Information (RFI) on date labeling until March 5, 2025, from its original end date of January 3, 2025. The RFI seeks information on industry practices and preferences for date labeling, consumer perceptions, and the impact of date labeling on food waste and grocery costs. 

The RFI also explores how consumers interpret date label information and whether it affects decisions about food purchasing and disposal. The USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) and the FDA jointly oversee the U.S. food supply and aim to inform future policy decisions using the collected information. 

The FDA Deputy Commissioner for Human Foods, Jim Jones, stated that the information collected will help consumers understand terms like 'Sell By,' 'Use By,' and 'Best By.' 

USDA Under Secretary for Food Safety, Dr. Emilio Esteban, hopes to learn more about how date labels are determined and whether they confuse consumers and lead to food waste. 

The joint RFI is part of the National Strategy for Reducing Food Loss and Waste and Recycling Organics, which aims to reduce food loss and waste by 50% by 2030.

title: Proclamation 10867—World AIDS Day, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States issues a proclamation on World AIDS Day, honoring the memory of those who have lost their lives to HIV and renewing the nation's commitment to accelerating efforts to end the HIV/AIDS epidemic by 2030. The Administration has made historic progress, including reestablishing the White House Office of National AIDS Policy and launching a new National HIV/AIDS Strategy. Funding has been committed to ensure low-income individuals have access to medication and quality care, and initiatives have been implemented to increase access to HIV interventions like PrEP and self-tests. The Administration has also decreased HIV incidence by 21 percent in participating jurisdictions and worked to fight stigma surrounding HIV. The President calls on the American people to join in activities to remember those who have lost their lives to AIDS and to provide support to people with HIV.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: Federal Open Market Committee meetings were held on November 6-7, 2024, and the committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 4-1/2 to 4-3/4 percent. The committee agreed that economic activity had continued to expand at a solid pace, with inflation making progress toward its 2 percent objective. The unemployment rate edged down slightly since August and was 4.1 percent in October, while average hourly earnings for all employees rose 4 percent over the 12 months ending in October. Net exports were a drag on third-quarter real GDP growth, but credit quality of nonfinancial firms borrowing remained stable, with delinquency rates on small business loans modestly increasing. House prices remained elevated, and regulatory capital ratios in the banking sector were high.

title: Statement by President-elect Donald J. Trump Announcing the Nomination of Jim O'Neill as Deputy Secretary of Health and Human Services
body_summary: Jim O'Neill is nominated to serve as the Deputy Secretary of Health and Human Services, working alongside Robert F. Kennedy Jr. He will oversee operations and improve Management, Transparency, and Accountability. Jim previously served as Principal Associate Deputy Secretary of HHS, leading reforms at FDA, including the FDA Amendments Act, which improved Drug and Medical Device Safety. He also helped design and launch the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response. After HHS, Jim became Managing Director of Clarium Capital and CEO of the Thiel Foundation, funding Innovative Nonprofits and co-founding the Thiel Fellowship. He later served as CEO of SENS Research Foundation, leading efforts to research and develop Regenerative Medicine Solutions for age-related diseases.

title: FDA Roundup: November 26, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a guidance on transitional enforcement policy for Class III devices in response to changes in ethylene oxide sterilization activities. The guidance aims to prevent or mitigate medical device supply chain disruptions. The FDA has also approved Attruby to treat adults with cardiomyopathy caused by a rare disease affecting the heart muscle. Additionally, the FDA has updated its advisory on an E. coli outbreak linked to whole and baby organic carrots from Grimmway Farms, expanding the recall to include additional bag sizes for certain organic carrot products.

title: Statement on Efforts To Promote Manufacturing Industry Private-Sector Investment
body_summary: The speaker's "Investing in America" agenda has attracted over $1 trillion in private-sector investments, following the passage of the bipartisan infrastructure law, the CHIPS and Science Act, and the Inflation Reduction Act. The agenda has helped create over 1.6 million construction and manufacturing jobs, making America a leader in clean energy and semiconductor technologies.

title: FDA Roundup: November 22, 2024
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is reminding owners and consignees of certain imported foods that, starting December 1, 2024, mycotoxin analyses must be conducted by accredited laboratories under the Laboratory Accreditation for Analysis of Foods (LAAF) program. 

The FDA has announced a communications pilot to enhance the medical device recall program, aiming to improve timeliness of communications about corrective actions being taken by companies, particularly those likely to be the most serious type of recalls. 

The FDA has updated the outbreak advisory for E. coli O21:H19 infections linked to organic whole and baby carrots supplied by Grimmway Farms. 

The FDA has granted accelerated approval to Jazz Pharmaceuticals Inc.’s Ziihera for previously treated, unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive biliary tract cancer. 

The FDA has issued a final guidance on the 510(k) Third Party Review Program and Third Party Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) Review. 

The FDA published a report titled "From Our Perspective: OMUFA – Past, Current, and Future" discussing the OTC Monograph drug user fee program. 

A recent OCI investigation led to the conviction of a Dallas anesthesiologist on four counts of tampering with consumer products resulting in serious bodily injury.

title: Proclamation 10864—National Family Week, 2024
body_summary: By the President of the United States of America, a proclamation is issued. My Dad taught me that family is the beginning, the middle, and the end. During National Family Week, we celebrate the love shared by millions of American families, and we recommit to uplifting them. Since I came into office, I have been determined to give hardworking families a little more breathing room and a fair shot at achieving their dreams. This work began with building an economy that would strengthen our middle class. My American Rescue Plan kept millions of families afloat during the pandemic. It also delivered the largest-ever Child Tax Credit, which helped tens of millions of working families. My Bipartisan Infrastructure Law created jobs rebuilding our Nation's infrastructure. My CHIPS and Science Act revitalized American manufacturing. My Inflation Reduction Act made healthcare more affordable for families, saving millions of them an average of $800 per year. I signed the Respect for Marriage Act, the Respect for Marriage Act, and an Executive Order to make high-quality child care and long-term care more accessible. I also took historic actions to prevent children from being placed into foster care and separated from their families. Furthermore, I signed the most comprehensive gun reform bill in nearly three decades. I hereby proclaim November 24 through November 30, 2024, as National Family Week.

title: Statement by President-elect Donald J. Trump Announcing the Nomination of Marty Makary as Commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration (FDA)
body_summary: The nominee for FDA Commissioner is Marty Makary MD, MPH, FACS. The FDA needs Dr. Makary to course-correct and refocus the agency to properly evaluate harmful chemicals in food supply, drugs, and biologics affecting children. Dr. Makary, a Johns Hopkins surgical oncologist and health policy expert, has a strong background in improving medical quality and reducing costs. He has authored over 300 scientific articles and three New York Times bestselling books on healthcare. Dr. Makary is a member of the National Academy of Medicine and a leading advocate for healthcare transparency.

title: Proclamation 10863—National Rural Health Day, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States of America has issued a proclamation declaring November 21, 2024, as National Rural Health Day. The proclamation recognizes the importance of ensuring that rural communities have access to affordable, quality health care. Since 2010, over 150 rural hospitals have closed down or stopped providing in-patient care. The President has committed to investing in rural America, including rural hospitals and health care. The Administration has delivered $8.5 billion to rural healthcare providers, launched a Rural Emergency Hospital designation, and provided tens of millions of dollars to expand health services. The President has also launched programs to train health care professionals, support the training of nurse midwives and nurse practitioners, and tackle health challenges impacting rural communities.

title: FDA Roundup: November 19, 2024
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a request for information (RFI) on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in seafood. The FDA is seeking data and information from the seafood industry, academia, and other entities on PFAS concentrations in seafood and the surrounding environment. 

The FDA has also posted a new Consumer Update on safe use of antibiotics and has approved PropofolVet Multidose, the first generic propofol injectable emulsion for dogs. 

The FDA has issued advisories for outbreaks of E. coli O121:H19 infections linked to organic whole and baby carrots supplied by Grimmway Farms, and Investigation of Illnesses: Diamond Shruumz-Brand Chocolate Bars, Cones, & Gummies. 

The FDA has also approved Revuforj, a menin inhibitor, for relapsed or refractory acute leukemia, and cleared the Ultromics Limited, EchoGo Amyloidosis 1.0, an automated machine learning-based decision support system for screening cardiac amyloidosis.

title: Statement by President-elect Donald J. Trump Announcing the Nomination of Dr. Mehmet Oz as Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator
body_summary: Dr. Mehmet Oz is nominated to serve as the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator. America faces a Healthcare Crisis, and Dr. Oz, a renowned Physician, Heart Surgeon, Inventor, and Communicator, is believed to be qualified to address it. Dr. Oz will work with Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to tackle the "illness industrial complex" and promote disease prevention. He will also aim to reduce waste and fraud in the CMS, a third of the nation's Healthcare spend and a quarter of the national budget. Dr. Oz holds a degree from Harvard College and the University of Pennsylvania, and has received numerous patents, awards, and publications. He co-founded HealthCorps with his wife Lisa, which has improved millions of lives nationwide over two decades.

title: Proclamation 10862—National Child's Day, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States renews his commitment to building a future worthy of America's young people on National Child's Day. The Administration has secured $130 billion in funding for K-12 schools through the American Rescue Plan, expanding access to high-speed internet, providing free, healthy school meals, and investing in child care and early childhood education. The President has also signed several laws to address gun safety, mental health, and climate change, including the most significant gun safety law in nearly 30 years and a historic investment in climate change. On November 20, 2024, the President declares National Child's Day, calling on all Americans to observe the day with appropriate programs and activities.

title: Proclamation 10861—International Conservation Day, 2024
body_summary:
The President of the United States, Joseph R. Biden Jr., has proclaimed November 17, 2024, as the first International Conservation Day. The President aims to safeguard natural treasures and combat climate change by working with partners across the Nation and globally. The Administration has made significant progress in conservation, including conserving over 45 million acres of lands and waters, establishing national monuments, and launching initiatives to protect forests, wetlands, and oceans.

The President has delivered an ambitious land and water conservation agenda, aiming to protect at least 30 percent of the Nation's lands and waters by 2030. The Administration has also made record climate financing to support developing countries' efforts to preserve and protect ecosystems. The President has surpassed the pledge to deliver $11 billion per year in climate financing by 2024 and has provided over $100 million to the Amazon Fund.

The President is working with international partners to launch initiatives such as the Brazil Restoration and Bioeconomy Finance Coalition and the Tropical Forest Forever Facility. The President believes that forests like the Amazon represent the heart and soul of the world and must be protected to ensure their continued existence.

title: Proclamation 10860—National Apprenticeship Week, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States announces National Apprenticeship Week from November 17 to November 23, 2024. The President reiterates support for Registered Apprenticeship programs, which have produced skilled workers for generations. The programs allow workers to earn while learning and connect them to good-paying jobs. Since taking office, the Administration has invested over $730 million in expanding Registered Apprenticeships, leading to the hiring of over one million apprentices. The Administration has also committed over $80 billion to strengthen and expand workforce programs, including Registered Apprenticeships.

title: FDA Roundup: November 15, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing an at-a-glance summary of news from around the agency. The World Health Organization's Member State Mechanism on Substandard and Falsified Medical Products will hold its 13th meeting in Geneva, Switzerland next week. Ahead of the meeting, FDA Associate Commissioner Mark Abdoo published a blog on November 7 on how to make the Mechanism more effective. The FDA issued a letter to health care providers about safety concerns with Getinge/Maquet VasoView HemoPro Endoscopic Vessel Harvesting (EVH) Systems, and a supply concern for EVH devices. Getinge/Maquet announced a voluntary recall for removal of all unused VasoView HemoPro 1.5 devices due to the risk of silicone detaching from the jaws of the harvesting tool. The FDA has updated its medical device shortage list to include EVH devices. The FDA released updated guidance for the Voluntary Qualified Importer Program (VQIP), part of the FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA), to streamline processes and improve program efficiency. The FDA also posted a new video in the "FDA In Your Day" series and updated the outbreak advisory for E. coli O157:H7 infections linked to onions sold at McDonald's restaurants. Additionally, the FDA granted marketing authorization for the Steris VERIFY RESI-TEST SLIDE-THRU Cleaning Process Protein Indicator.

title: Proclamation 10859—American Education Week, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States of America proclaims American Education Week, celebrating the power and promise of the Nation's public education system, which empowers students to realize their full potential regardless of their zip code. The President shows gratitude for educators and staff who ensure schools are filled with hope and possibilities. The President recommitts to ensuring each student, educator, and school has the resources and opportunities needed to thrive. The President's Administration secured historic funding for K-12 schools, including $130 billion, and invested in mental health and substance use programs, providing critical funding to increase mental health providers in schools. The Bipartisan Safer Communities Act made important steps toward ending gun violence and included $2 billion in funding to create safe learning environments. The Administration also made it easier for schools to bill Medicaid and is working to make preschool universal for every 3- and 4-year-old in America.

title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapy for Treatment of Aromatic L-amino Acid Decarboxylase Deficiency
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Kebilidi (eladocagene exuparvovec-tneq), a gene therapy for adult and pediatric patients with aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC) deficiency, the first FDA-approved gene therapy for this condition. The approval is based on evidence of effectiveness from an open-label, single-arm clinical study in 13 pediatric patients, which demonstrated gross motor function improvement in 8 of 12 treated patients. Kebilidi is administered via four infusions in one surgical session and is contraindicated in patients who have not achieved skull maturity. Common adverse reactions include dyskinesia, fever, and low blood pressure. The approval was granted using the Accelerated Approval pathway, and a confirmatory clinical trial is ongoing to verify Kebilidi's clinical benefit.

title: Proclamation 10858—America Recycles Day, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States recognizes the importance of recycling in securing a sustainable future and recommitting to addressing climate change. The administration has made significant investments in recycling infrastructure, including the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which has launched hundreds of new projects to support manufacturing, improve waste management, and educate people about recycling. The President has also released a comprehensive strategy to limit plastic pollution and announced a goal to end single-use plastics in the Federal Government by 2035. The administration aims to reach net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050 and calls on manufacturers to ensure their products are reusable and recyclable. The President proclaims November 15, 2024, as America Recycles Day and encourages Americans to continue their environmental efforts by recycling throughout the year.

title: FDA Roundup: November 8, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued a final rule to amend color additive regulations, increasing fees for certification services, including a $0.10 per pound increase for straight colors including lakes. The final rule will be effective 30 days after its publication in the Federal Register on November 8, 2024. The FDA also issued a renewal of modified risk granted orders to Swedish Match USA, Inc. for eight General Snus products, allowing them to continue marketing with a specific modified risk claim. Additionally, the FDA requested public input on its export certification process for human food products to gather insights from stakeholders on how to improve the program. The FDA also updated its Breakthrough Device designations data and reported 1,041 Breakthrough Device designations and 128 authorized devices for marketing.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace. Since earlier in the year, labor market conditions have generally eased, and the unemployment rate has moved up but remains low. Inflation has made progress toward the Committee's 2 percent objective but remains somewhat elevated. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are roughly in balance. The economic outlook is uncertain, and the Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate. In support of its goals, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 4-1/2 to 4-3/4 percent. In considering additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. The Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgageâbacked securities. The Committee is strongly committed to supporting maximum employment and returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Michael S. Barr; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Mary C. Daly; Beth M. Hammack; Philip N. Jefferson; Adriana D. Kugler; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: Implementation Note issued November 7, 2024
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on November 7, 2024: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to lower the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 4.65 percent, effective November 8, 2024. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective November 8, 2024, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 4-1/2 to 4â3/4 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 4.75 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 4.55 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $25 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency mortgageâbacked securities (MBS) received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month into Treasury securities to roughly match the maturity composition of Treasury securities outstanding. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve a 1/4 percentage point decrease in the primary credit rate to 4.75 percent, effective November 8, 2024. In taking this action, the Board approved requests to establish that rate submitted by the Boards of Directors of the Federal Reserve Banks of Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Chicago, Minneapolis, Dallas, and San Francisco. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: FDA Proposes Ending Use of Oral Phenylephrine as OTC Monograph Nasal Decongestant Active Ingredient After Extensive Review
body_summary: The US FDA has proposed removing oral phenylephrine as an active ingredient in over-the-counter (OTC) monograph drug products for temporary nasal congestion relief due to concerns over its effectiveness. The agency conducted a comprehensive review of available data and consulted with an advisory committee, which unanimously concluded that the current scientific data do not support the recommended dosage of oral phenylephrine for nasal decongestant use. The FDA will seek public comments on this proposed order and, if approved, will issue a final order removing oral phenylephrine from the OTC monograph, allowing manufacturers to reformulate or remove such drugs from the market.

title: FDA Roundup: November 5, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has published a blog by Commissioner Robert M. Califf discussing One Health and the FDA's mission to promote human and animal health. The FDA Center for Veterinary Medicine is hosting a Symposium on One Health. The FDA has published a Supplement to the 2022 Food Code, which updates the code with recommendations from stakeholders. The FDA has also registered the first antimicrobial treatment for pathogen reduction in pre-harvest agricultural water. Additionally, the FDA authorized the marketing of LumiThera, Inc.'s Valeda Light Delivery System for treating dry age-related macular degeneration. The FDA Office of Criminal Investigations has arrested a Massachusetts spa owner for allegedly performing thousands of illegal injections of counterfeit Botox and other products.

title: Statement on Health Insurance Enrollment Under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: The first day of open enrollment for health insurance in the Affordable Care Act marketplace has begun, giving millions of Americans access to quality healthcare. The Affordable Care Act has lowered costs by $800 per person per year and eliminated red tape. As a result, 9 million more Americans have gained coverage. Vice President Harris and the author have worked to make the ACA more accessible. However, prominent Republicans in Congress have threatened to undo this progress, which would affect 45 million Americans, 100 million with preexisting conditions, and erode Medicaid coverage for millions of children, pregnant women, and people with disabilities. The author and Vice President Harris will continue to fight to make healthcare and prescription drugs more affordable for all Americans.

title: FDA Roundup: November 1, 2024
body_summary: The FDA published a final Compliance Policy Guide on the adulteration of fish and fishery products with Scombrotoxin (histamine). The CPG aims to increase consumer protections related to scombrotoxin (histamine) fish poisoning by lowering the levels of histamine in fish at which the FDA may take action. The FDA will host a public meeting on November 20, 2024, to discuss recommendations for reauthorization of the OTC Monograph Drug User Fee Program (OMUFA). The FDA approved a modification to the Opioid Analgesic Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (OA REMS), requiring companies participating in the program to provide pre-paid drug mail-back envelopes to outpatient pharmacies by March 31, 2025. The FDA released its 2025 Priority Deliverables for the Human Foods Program, highlighting activities to focus on during its first year following a reorganization. The FDA updated the outbreak advisory for E. coli O157:H7 infections linked to slivered onions served on McDonald's Quarter Pounders. The FDA issued warning letters to nine online retailers and one manufacturer for selling unauthorized disposable e-cigarettes.

title: Proclamation 10853—National Native American Heritage Month, 2024
body_summary: President Joseph R. Biden Jr. issued a proclamation declaring November 2024 as National Native American Heritage Month. He honored the history, rich cultures, and contributions of Native peoples, celebrating the hundreds of Tribal Nations ushering in a new era in Nation-to-Nation relationships. The President re-committed to respecting Tribal sovereignty and self-determination, working in partnership with Tribal Nations to bring new prosperity and security to Native peoples. He acknowledged the Nation's failed policies of the past, which subjected Native peoples to cruelty, violence, and intimidation, and recognized their strength, survival, and commitment to their heritage and ways of life. The President made record investments in Tribal Nations, including $8 billion in Federal contracts with Native American-owned companies and historic funding to Tribal communities to fight the behavioral health crisis. He also signed an Executive Order to improve the Federal response to the epidemic of missing and murdered Indigenous peoples and provided advance funding for the Indian Health Service. The proclamation also urged all Americans to observe the month with appropriate programs, ceremonies, and activities, and to celebrate November 29, 2024, as Native American Heritage Day.

title: Proclamation 10852—National Lung Cancer Awareness Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States of America has proclaimed November 2024 as National Lung Cancer Awareness Month. The proclamation honors those living with lung cancer and their loved ones, and recommitting to ending cancer as known it. The Administration aims to cut the cancer death rate by at least 50 percent over the next 25 years. The Biden Cancer Moonshot and $4 billion in bipartisan funding support research and innovation. The Administration also works to make cancer treatments more affordable and the treatment process more manageable for families. The Inflation Reduction Act caps out-of-pocket prescription drug costs for Medicare beneficiaries at $2,000 per year.

title: Proclamation 10849—National Diabetes Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States, Joseph R. Biden Jr., hereby proclaims November 2024 as National Diabetes Month to raise awareness about diabetes and promote prevention, treatment, and management strategies. Over 38 million Americans, or 1 in 10 people, have diabetes, a condition that takes a physical and financial toll on the nation. The President reiterates the commitment to making treatment more affordable and accessible, and to finding cures. To address this issue, the Inflation Reduction Act was signed, capping the cost of insulin at $35 for people on Medicare and empowering Medicare to negotiate lower drug prices. The law also requires drug companies to pay Medicare back the difference if they raise prices faster than inflation. The President has secured $4 billion for the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health to advance research on preventing, detecting, and treating diabetes.

title: Proclamation 10851—National Family Caregivers Month, 2024
body_summary:
The President of the United States has signed a proclamation to honor family caregivers, who make tremendous sacrifices for their loved ones. The proclamation reiterates the commitment to providing support to these caregivers, who often struggle to afford care and pay for their own jobs. 

The American Rescue Plan has delivered historic support to over 225,000 child care programs, serving 10 million children, and expanded the Child Tax Credit to nearly cut child poverty in half. The Administration has also increased funding for child care by nearly 50 percent and finalized new rules to strengthen staffing standards in nursing homes. 

The National Family Caregiver Support Program has received $145 million, and a National Strategy to Support Family Caregivers has been released. The President has also signed an Executive Order to increase access to high-quality child care and long-term care, as well as support for caregivers. 

The President pledges to get every family caregiver the same kind of relief, respect, and support, and has proclaimed November 2024 as National Family Caregivers Month.

title: Proclamation 10848—National Alzheimer's Disease Awareness Month, 2024
body_summary: By the President of the United States, a proclamation is issued during National Alzheimer's Disease Awareness Month to honor the courage and resilience of those facing this devastating disease. The President recommitts to supporting caregivers and strengthening the resolve to prevent, treat, and eliminate Alzheimer's. Currently, over six million Americans have Alzheimer's disease, disproportionately impacting African Americans and Latino Americans. The President's Administration has taken steps to drive new breakthroughs, securing $4 billion for the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health. The National Institutes of Health is funding new clinical trials, and the President signed the reauthorization of the National Alzheimer's Project Act and the Alzheimer's Accountability and Investment Act. The President also signed an Executive Order to improve care for caregivers and launched the GUIDE Model to offer respite services and support. National Alzheimer's Disease Awareness Month is hereby proclaimed for November 2024.

title: Proclamation 10850—National Entrepreneurship Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States, Joseph R. Biden Jr., proclaims November 2024 as National Entrepreneurship Month to celebrate the spirit of entrepreneurs who drive innovation, create jobs, and uplift communities. To support entrepreneurs, especially small business owners, the Biden-Harris Administration has invested billions of dollars in capital and research, and has made significant strides in providing loans to small businesses, particularly those from underrepresented communities. This month is also marked by a record number of new business applications filed, with a focus on Black, Latino, and women entrepreneurs. The President calls on Americans to commemorate National Entrepreneurship Month with programs and activities and to celebrate November 19, 2024, as National Entrepreneurs' Day.

title: Proclamation 10846—Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States has proclaimed November 2024 as Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience Month. This proclamation recommitting to strengthening the country's critical infrastructure comes as the President updates the policy for the first time in a decade to secure and enhance the resilience of the United States' critical infrastructure. The President has also announced investments in the Nation's infrastructure, including the American Rescue Plan, Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, Inflation Reduction Act, and CHIPS and Science Act, totaling billions of dollars to secure and bolster the infrastructure. These investments include improving the electric grid, elevating roads and bridges, and funding community resilience programs. The President has also collaborated with Canada and Finland on producing polar icebreakers, and announced a United States Port Security Initiative to reverse dependence on foreign manufactured port equipment.

title: FDA Roundup: October 29, 2024
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has responded to objections on its final rule removing phthalates from authorized food contact uses, concluding that objections did not provide a basis for modification. The FDA is working on an updated safety assessment of remaining authorized uses, including phthalates on the list of select chemicals under review. 

A hybrid meeting, In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD) Roundtable, will be held on November 12, 2024, at 10 a.m. ET, to facilitate communication between the FDA and the IVD industry. The FDA has also shared information on medical device cybersecurity, emphasizing the need to drive and refine medical device cybersecurity policy. 

The FDA has issued safety communications, including one about BioZorb Markers, and granted marketing authorization for the Dexter L6 System, an electromechanical surgical system. Additionally, three individuals in London were sentenced for their role in the international importation and distribution of unapproved drugs, with the operation seizing over £1M ($1.3M) and 1 million illicit pills.

title: FDA Roundup: October 25, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has updated the advisory for the outbreak of E. coli O157:H7. A specific ingredient has not been confirmed as the source of the outbreak, but most sick people report eating McDonald's Quarter Pounder burgers. McDonald's has temporarily stopped using Quarter Pounder slivered onions and beef patties in affected states. As of October 24, 75 people infected with the outbreak strain of E. coli O157:H7 have been reported from 13 states. The FDA is working closely with the US Department of Agriculture, the Food Safety and Inspection Service, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and state partners to determine the likely source of contamination. The FDA has also issued guidance to help tattoo ink manufacturers and distributors recognize situations in which tattoo ink may become contaminated with microorganisms. Additionally, the FDA has finalized Guidance for Industry #293: FDA Enforcement Policy for AAFCO-Defined Animal Feed Ingredients and will continue to accept comments until December 9, 2024.

title: $76 Million in Illegal E-Cigarettes Seized in Joint Federal Operation
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, in collaboration with U.S. Customs and Border Protection, announced the administrative seizure of approximately three million units of unauthorized e-cigarette products with an estimated retail value of $76 million. The seizures were part of a July joint operation to examine incoming shipments and prevent illegal e-cigarettes from entering the country. The FDA and the Department of Justice had announced a joint federal task force in June to curb the distribution and sale of illegal e-cigarettes. The joint team worked for several months to review shipping invoices and identify potentially violative shipments, which included various brands of illegal e-cigarettes originating from China. The operation resulted in the seizure of products that were intentionally mis-declared to evade duties and detection. The FDA and CBP will continue to focus on actions to stop the illegal importation and distribution of unauthorized e-cigarette products in the United States.

title: Statement on Efforts To Expand Contraception Coverage Under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: The Biden administration is taking a major step to expand contraception coverage under the Affordable Care Act. Republican elected officials have made clear they want to ban or restrict birth control and defund Federal programs that help women access contraception. The administration has worked to protect and build on the Affordable Care Act, lowering costs for marketplace coverage by an average of $800 per year. Vice President Harris has been a key partner in this effort. The administration believes that women in every State must have the freedom to make deeply personal health care decisions, including the right to decide if and when to start or grow their family.

title: FDA Roundup: October 18, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has facilitated the temporary importation of 23 IV and PD fluids to aid recovery from Hurricane Helene-related damage. The agency has also approved Vyloy, a treatment for certain types of cancer, and a companion diagnostic test. Additionally, the FDA approved Novocure GmbH's Optune Lua, a portable device producing tumor treating fields, to treat adults with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer alongside concurrent drug treatments. The CDC reported a decline in tobacco product use among youth, with at least half a million fewer students using tobacco products in the past year.

title: Proclamation 10843—National Forest Products Week, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States of America issues a proclamation to recognize National Forest Products Week, which begins on the third Sunday in October. The proclamation acknowledges the importance of conserving forests, which support livelihoods, sustain the health of the environment and communities, and provide essential resources. The President highlights the efforts to conserve at least 30 percent of the nation's lands and waters by 2030 through local, voluntary efforts. The proclamation also notes the President's Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and Inflation Reduction Act, which invest in forest management, wildfire prevention, and sustainable practices. The President encourages Americans to join in recognizing the importance of forest stewardship and calls upon the people of the United States to support the nation's forest products.

title: Proclamation 10841—Minority Enterprise Development Week, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States of America has proclaimed October 20 through October 26, 2024, as Minority Enterprise Development Week. The proclamation celebrates the talent and ingenuity of minority-owned businesses and their contributions to the economy. Since 2020, the Small Business Administration (SBA) has lent tens of billions of dollars to small businesses, with significant increases for Asian American, Black, and Latino-owned businesses. The American Rescue Plan invested $10 billion to launch and expand programs providing access to capital for small businesses. The Administration has also taken steps to ensure minority-owned businesses get a fair shot at success, including increasing the share of Federal contracts to 15 percent by 2025.

title: FDA Roundup: October 15, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has released the 2024Accelerating Rare Disease Cures (ARC) ProgramAnnual Report. Since its launch in 2022, the ARC Program has become a key resource for the rare disease community and a driver of innovation in rare disease drug treatments. The FDA has announced a free public webinar, Informed Consent – More than Just Another Document to Sign?, to be held on Friday, November 8, 2024, from 2-3 p.m. ET. The webinar will discuss expectations around informed consent and how informed consent materials can be improved.

title: FDA Roundup: October 11, 2024
body_summary: The US FDA has issued several key updates. The agency has added three new drug products to the Drug Shortages Database due to Hurricane Helene's impact on Baxter International's North Cove facility. The FDA is working to address shortages of certain parenteral drugs, including IV solutions. Additionally, the FDA has published its 2023 Summary Report on Antimicrobials Sold or Distributed for Use in Food-Producing Animals, showing a 2% decrease in US sales and distribution of medically important antimicrobial drugs. The agency has also proposed new guidances for fiscal year 2025 and approved Itovebi (inavolisib with palbociclib and fulvestrant) for adults with endocrine-resistant breast cancer.

title: Proclamation 10839—Indigenous Peoples' Day, 2024
body_summary:
By the President of the United States of America, a proclamation is issued On Indigenous Peoples' Day. Indigenous peoples' strength, courage, and resilience are honored. The vast contributions of Indigenous communities to the world are celebrated. Tribal sovereignty and self-determination are recommitments. The history of America's Indigenous peoples is marked by perseverance, survival, and a deep commitment to their heritage, right to self-governance, and ways of life. Since time immemorial, Indigenous peoples have built and sustained powerful Tribal Nations, cultivated rich cultures, and established vibrant communities.

Generations of Native peoples have faced cruelty, violence, and intimidation due to the Nation's failed policies. Despite trauma and turmoil, Indigenous peoples have persisted and survived. Today, Indigenous peoples lead, share their histories, and strengthen their communities. They are stewards of lands and waters, growing our shared prosperity.

The President remains committed to writing a new chapter in history. Honoring solemn promises and working together to rebuild Tribal economies and institutions is key. Indigenous voices have been included in the Federal Government. Deb Haaland, America's first Native American Cabinet secretary, has been appointed. The White House Council on Native American Affairs has been re-established to coordinate policy.

Historic steps have been taken to improve the consultation process between Federal agencies and Tribal Nations. An Executive Order has been signed to respect Tribal Nations' autonomy. The Buy Indian Act has been strengthened to grow Tribal economies while respecting Tribal sovereignty.

The Federal Government has made record investments in Tribal Nations. The American Rescue Plan, Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, and Inflation Reduction Act have provided significant investments in Tribal roads, bridges, water, high-speed internet, and environmental cleanup.

Increased resources have been provided to

title: FDA Approves New Treatment for Hemophilia A or B
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Hympavzi (marstacimab-hncq) for routine prophylaxis to prevent or reduce bleeding episodes in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older with hemophilia A or B without inhibitors. Ann Farrell, M.D., Director of the Division of Non-Malignant Hematology, stated that Hympavzi provides patients with hemophilia a new treatment option. The drug works by reducing the activity of the anticoagulation protein tissue factor pathway inhibitor, increasing thrombin generation, and reducing bleeding episodes. An open-label, multi-center study in 116 patients showed that Hympavzi was superior to on-demand factor replacement in reducing bleeding rates. Hympavzi's approval is based on a 12-month study period, with estimated annualized bleeding rates of 3.2 and 5.08. The drug comes with warnings and precautions, including thromboembolic events, hypersensitivity, and embryofetal toxicity. The most common side effects are injection site reactions, headache, and itching. Hympavzi is granted to Pfizer Inc.

title: Statement on the Death of Former Senator Timothy P. Johnson
body_summary: Tim Johnson served the people of South Dakota with distinction in the United States Senate for over a decade. He prioritized South Dakotans and worked to bring clean drinking water to Americans, investing in Indian Country and South Dakota's development and infrastructure. As a Senator, Tim improved access to health care, including a critical vote on the Affordable Care Act, veterans health care funding, and expanding Medicaid in South Dakota. He also established the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau to defend the economy. Tim Johnson's legacy is honored by Barb, his children, grandchildren, and the people of South Dakota, whose lives he touched.

title: Proclamation 10836—International Day of the Girl, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States proclaims October 11, 2024, as International Day of the Girl. The proclamation honors the lives and contributions of girls worldwide, celebrating their limitless potential and recommitting to opening doors of opportunity so girls everywhere can realize their dreams. The Administration has taken steps to provide girls with support to thrive, including expanding the Child Tax Credit, investing in education, and strengthening protections against violence and abuse. The proclamation calls on the people of the United States to observe the day with programs, ceremonies, and policies that advance equity and opportunity for girls everywhere.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary:
Here is the final summary:

A joint Federal Open Market Committee and Board of Governors meeting took place on September 17-18, 2024. Real GDP rose solidly through the first half of the year, with real private domestic final purchases growth stronger than GDP. Economic growth was expected to continue at a solid pace in the third quarter. Average hourly earnings for all employees rose 3.8% over the 12 months ending in August. The Committee assessed risks to achieving dual-mandate goals as roughly in balance and decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point to 4-3/4 to 5 percent.

title: Federal Court Enters Consent Decree Against Rizo Lopez Foods Inc. Following Multistate Outbreak of Listeriosis Linked to Queso Fresco and Cotija Cheese Products
body_summary: The U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of California has entered a consent decree of permanent injunction against Rizo Lopez Foods Inc. and its co-owners, Edwin Rizo and Tomas Rizo. The decree prohibits the company from manufacturing and selling certain food products until it complies with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention investigated a multi-year, multistate outbreak of Listeria monocytogenes infections linked to queso fresco and cotija cheeses manufactured by Rizo Lopez Foods. The outbreak, which occurred across 11 states, resulted in 26 illnesses, 23 hospitalizations, and two deaths. The company voluntarily recalled its entire inventory of dairy products in February 2024. The consent decree requires the defendants to make corrective actions and receive FDA approval before they may resume operations.

title: FDA Authorizes Marketing of First Home Flu and COVID-19 Combination Test Outside of Emergency Use Authorities
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration granted marketing authorization for the Healgen Rapid Check COVID-19/Flu A&B Antigen Test, allowing it to be used without a prescription for individuals experiencing respiratory symptoms. The test detects COVID-19 and influenza A and B using a nasal swab sample and provides results in approximately 15 minutes. The test was authorized under a traditional premarket review pathway, making it the first over-the-counter test to do so for influenza detection. The FDA reviewed data from a study showing the test's high accuracy and effectiveness, and it will establish special controls to ensure safety and effectiveness. The test is available for use by individuals 14 years or older, or 2 years and older with a sample taken and tested by an adult.

title: Proclamation 10830—Fire Prevention Week, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States has proclaimed October 6-12, 2024, as Fire Prevention Week. The President encourages all Americans to learn about fire safety and recommit to preventing fires before they occur and supporting families affected by fires. The President thanks firefighters and first responders for their bravery and sacrifices. The Administration has made significant investments to fight climate change and keep people safe, including billions of dollars for wildfire detection programs, green manufacturing, and clean energy. The President has also increased funding for firefighters, including a $350 billion investment from the American Rescue Plan, and launched new programs to recruit, retain, and train Federal firefighters. The President urges Americans to install smoke alarms, test them monthly, and replace them every 10 years to ensure public safety.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Report on the Employment Situation in September
body_summary: The US government has released a report showing 250,000 new jobs in September, bringing the total to 16 million jobs created under the current administration. Unemployment remains at 4.1 percent, and wages are growing faster than prices. This marks a record 19 million new businesses created. The administration plans for Congress to pass a bill building millions of new homes, expanding prescription drug price caps, empowering workers and protecting collective bargaining rights, and cutting taxes for hard-working families. In contrast, Congressional Republicans propose a different plan that includes giant tax cuts for billionaires and big corporations, ending the Affordable Care Act, and imposing a national sales tax that would raise costs by nearly $4,000 per year.

title: Proclamation 10833—Child Health Day, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States has issued a proclamation on Child Health Day, recommitting to supporting families and children to lead healthy lives. The proclamation aims to provide resources and support for families to care for their children without worrying about financial burdens. Key initiatives include expanding the Child Tax Credit, investing in child care, and reducing health insurance costs. The President has also strengthened the Maternal, Infant, and Early Childhood Home Visiting Program, launched the National Maternal Mental Health Hotline, and modernized the Thrifty Food Plan. Additionally, the President has taken steps to secure free and healthy school meals for every child, invest in mental health care, and tackle the climate crisis. The proclamation also highlights the importance of gun safety and calls for action to reduce violence and ensure a safe community for children.

title: FDA Roundup: October 4, 2024
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) provided an update on various news items. On October 7, the FDA's Science Board will convene to receive an update from the New Alternative Methods subcommittee and hear about the FDA's reorganization. 

The FDA's Office of Women's Health (OWH) released its updated Women's Health Research Roadmap, which provides a science-based framework to address women's health research questions. 

The FDA approved Opdivo (nivolumab) with platinum-doublet chemotherapy as a neoadjuvant treatment and single-agent nivolumab after surgery as adjuvant treatment for adults with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). 

The FDA updated its outbreak advisory for Diamond Shruumz-Brand Chocolate Bars, Cones, & Gummies and published a list of unsafe imported radiation-emitting products. 

The FDA announced a new, streamlined approach for processing complaints and published a list of known radiation-emitting electronic products that have failed safety testing. 

The FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH) announced that breakthrough designated devices are eligible to enroll in the Total Product Life Cycle (TPLC) Advisory Program (TAP) Pilot. 

The FDA approved its 60th biosimilar since the start of the biosimilars program.

title: FDA Roundup: October 1, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced seven new clinical trial grants awarded in fiscal year 2024 under the Orphan Products Grants Program, totaling approximately $17.2 million over four years. Newly funded projects include treatments for Cushing’s syndrome, blood disorders, cancer, lymphatic malformations, and an inherited eye disease. The FDA has also awarded three new natural history study grants, providing approximately $4.7 million over four years, to advance understanding of rare diseases progression. In FY 2024, the FDA provided over $5.4 million in funding to support clinical research under the Rare Neurodegenerative Disease (RNDD) Grants Program. The FDA has committed to supporting medical product development for all rare neurodegenerative diseases.

title: FDA’s Unified Human Foods Program, New Model for Field Operations, and Other Modernization Efforts Go into Effect
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is marking a new chapter with the implementation of the unified Human Foods Program, the single largest reorganization in the agency's modern history, affecting over 8,000 employees. This new model is designed to improve the agency's field operations and modernization efforts. The FDA is confident that the Human Foods Program will better protect consumers, promote wellness, and prevent disease. An important part of this reorganization includes restructuring and renaming the Office of Inspections and Investigations to focus on inspections, investigations, and imports. A new online consumer complaint form will also be piloted to improve the consumer experience and internally handle complaints more efficiently. The FDA aims to build a stronger, more integrated, and modernized agency, which includes laboratories, food safety and nutrition, medical products, tobacco products, and cosmetics.

title: Proclamation 10823—National Clean Energy Action Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States announces that October 2024 will be National Clean Energy Action Month. Since day one of his Administration, he has committed to building a clean energy economy that creates good-paying and union jobs for American workers. The President's Investing in America agenda has made the most significant investment in climate and clean energy in history, attracting over $426 billion in private sector investment commitments and creating over 330,000 new jobs. The Inflation Reduction Act is delivering on his commitment to be the most pro-worker, pro-union President in history, with provisions that incentivize companies to pay clean energy workers a prevailing wage and employ registered apprentices. The Administration is also launching the American Climate Corps to train the next generation of clean energy, conservation, and resilience workers.

title: Proclamation 10822—National Breast Cancer Awareness Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States declares October 2024 as National Breast Cancer Awareness Month, honoring the memories of those lost to breast cancer and giving strength and support to survivors and their families. The Administration has made significant efforts to combat breast cancer, including reiterating the Cancer Moonshot to cut the cancer death rate by at least 50 percent over 25 years. The President has also taken steps to make cancer treatment more affordable, strengthening Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act, and introducing measures to cap out-of-pocket costs for prescription drugs. The Administration has also ensured access to patient navigation services and expanded screening and early detection services, particularly for underserved communities.

title: Proclamation 10827—National Youth Justice Action Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States has proclaimed October 2024 as National Youth Justice Action Month. The proclamation recommitting to ensuring safe and supportive communities for young people and developing a juvenile justice system that reflects America's values of equality, fairness, and opportunity is reaffirmed. The number of young people in the juvenile justice system has declined significantly since 2000, but young people of color and those with disabilities are still disproportionately represented. The Administration has made historic investments in evidence-based diversion programs, access to lawyers, and programs helping youth find housing, education, and job training upon release.

title: Statement on Efforts To Reduce Prescription Drug Prices
body_summary: The Inflation Reduction Act requires companies that increase prescription drug prices faster than inflation to provide a rebate to Medicare. Starting in October, Medicare beneficiaries will pay less for 54 Part B prescription drugs, with some seniors saving more than $3,800 per day. In 2025, out-of-pocket costs for prescription drugs will be capped at $2,000 for Medicare beneficiaries. The law passed with the leadership of Democrats in Congress and Vice President Harris' tie-breaking vote in the Senate, although Republicans aim to repeal it.

title: Proclamation 10819—National Hunting and Fishing Day, 2024
body_summary: By the President of the United States, A Proclamation, Generations of Americans have enjoyed hunting and fishing, cherishing traditions that bring us closer to America's natural wonders and embody the nation's spirit of resourcefulness and adventure. The President's Administration has set a goal to conserve at least 30 percent of all Nation's lands and waters by 2030, as part of the "America the Beautiful" initiative. The Department of Agriculture and the Department of the Interior are working to improve hunters' and anglers' access to public lands and waters. The President has also launched the Federal Interagency Council on Outdoor Recreation to create more safe, affordable, and equitable opportunities for outdoor recreation. The Inflation Reduction Act has made the largest investment in addressing the climate crisis, harnessing nature as a climate solution. Now, Therefore, the President, Joseph R. Biden Jr., by virtue of the authority vested in him, does hereby proclaim September 28, 2024, as National Hunting and Fishing Day.

title: Proclamation 10820—National Public Lands Day, 2024
body_summary: President Joe R. Biden Jr. has proclaimed September 28, 2024, as National Public Lands Day. This day honors America's natural wonders and renews the nation's commitment to preserving its public lands and waters. Since taking office, the President has taken historic steps to conserve the nation's natural treasures, including conserving over 42 million acres of land and water, establishing and expanding eight national monuments, and protecting waters across the country. The President's "America the Beautiful" initiative supports voluntary conservation efforts, while the Inflation Reduction Act and Bipartisan Infrastructure Law provide historic investments to combat climate change and promote outdoor recreation opportunities.

title: FDA Roundup: September 27, 2024
body_summary: The US FDA updated its Mycotoxins in Domestic and Imported Human Foods Compliance Program to include monitoring of T-2/HT-2 toxins and zearalenone. The FDA approved Motiva USA's SmoothSilk Round and Round Ergonomix Silicone Gel-Filled Breast Implants for breast augmentation, with conditions for post-approval studies. The agency also announced a virtual town hall on sterilization, a digital health and AI glossary, and reorganization of its Office of New Animal Drug Evaluation. In 2024-2027, the FDA updated its Information Technology strategy to modernize and enhance its technological capabilities, with a focus on global collaboration. The agency led an indictment in the District of Puerto Rico, charging 27 individuals with conspiracy and selling diverted prescription drugs, resulting in estimated revenue loss of $13 million and cost to Medicare and Medicaid of $7.6 million.

title: FDA Approves Drug with New Mechanism of Action for Treatment of Schizophrenia
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Cobenfy (xanomeline and trospium chloride) capsules for the treatment of schizophrenia in adults. Schizophrenia is a severe, chronic mental illness that affects about 1% of Americans and is one of the 15 leading causes of disability worldwide. Cobenfy targets cholinergic receptors instead of dopamine receptors, offering a new alternative to existing antipsychotic medications. Its effectiveness was evaluated in two 5-week studies, which showed a meaningful reduction in symptoms in participants who received Cobenfy compared to the placebo group. The primary efficacy measure was the change from baseline in the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) total score at week 5. Cobenfy's prescribing information includes warnings for potential side effects, such as urinary retention and liver damage. The approval was granted to Bristol-Myers Squibb Company.

title: Statement on a Department of the Treasury Report on Small Business Health Insurance Coverage Under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: The President of the United States is proud of the Affordable Care Act's success in allowing more Americans to start small businesses and have access to health insurance. Under the President's and Vice President Harris's efforts, more Americans have signed up for health care coverage through the Affordable Care Act marketplace. Specifically, 618,590 small-business owners in Florida, 450,010 in California, 423,790 in Texas, and 168,070 in Georgia have benefited from this coverage.

title: FDA Approves New Drug to Treat Niemann-Pick Disease, Type C
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Aqneursa (levacetylleucine) for the treatment of neurological symptoms associated with Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 15 kilograms. The approval is the second treatment for NPC within a week. The safety and efficacy of Aqneursa were evaluated in a study that enrolled 60 patients. The primary efficacy outcome showed that participants treated with Aqneursa for 12 weeks showed a better outcome in the functional Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (fSARA) score compared to placebo. The FDA granted Aqneursa Priority Review, Fast Track, Orphan Drug, and Rare Pediatric Disease designations.

title: FDA Roundup: September 24, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration held a ribbon-cutting ceremony for the completion of a 64,000 square foot expansion and renovation of the National Forensic Chemistry Center in Cincinnati, Ohio. The revitalization effort aims to improve the agency's mission readiness nationally and attract highly qualified employees. The FDA issued safety advisories for pet owners, warning them not to feed their pets products from Answers Pet Food and Darwin's Natural Pet Products, which tested positive for Salmonella and Listeria monocytogenes. The FDA also approved the use of atuximab-irfc (Sarclisa) for adults with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma.

title: Joint Statement by President Biden and Prime Minister Narendra Modi of India—Roadmap for U.S.-India Initiative To Build Safe and Secure Global Clean Energy Supply Chains
body_summary:
The United States and India commit to deepening their collaboration on shared national and economic security issues, focusing on clean energy transition. They aim to expand complementary U.S. and Indian manufacturing capacity for clean energy technologies and components, and lay the groundwork for enhanced cooperation in third countries, with a focus on partnerships in Africa.

The effort builds on existing clean energy cooperation, including the Strategic Clean Energy Partnership launched in 2023. The United States and India intend to unlock USD$1 billion in new multilateral finance through the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) for projects that include catalyzing India's domestic clean energy supply chain buildout.

The partnership will focus on specific clean energy components, including solar wafers, wind turbine nacelle components, energy storage components, and high-efficiency air conditioners and ceiling fan components. The U.S. and Indian governments pledge to work with industry leaders to identify near-term investment opportunities and collaborate with the private sector to scope eligible opportunities.

The effort will also build on private sector partnerships facilitated by the U.S. Development Finance Corporation across the solar, wind, battery, and critical minerals sectors. The United States and India aim to mobilize additional financing into priority clean energy manufacturing sectors and establish a shared, resilient, and cutting-edge techno-industrial base centered on innovative clean energy manufacturing techniques.

title: FDA Roundup: September 20, 2024
body_summary: The FDA and NIH announced a joint public meeting to advance innovation in smoking cessation products for adults and youth. The meeting will be held on October 21, 2024. Additionally, the FDA approved Zenrelia for dogs with allergic dermatitis and approved Rybrevant for adult patients with non-small cell lung cancer. The FDA also supported a collaborative agreement with the Reagan-Udall Foundation to conduct a SWOT analysis of the animal health and veterinary industries. Four Animal and Veterinary Innovation Centers were established to advance regulatory science and innovative products for animal health. The FDA updated an outbreak advisory and approved Kisqali and Keytruda for various cancer treatments.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Niemann-Pick Disease, Type C
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Miplyffa (arimoclomol), an oral medication, for the treatment of Niemann-Pick disease, type C (NPC), in adults and children 2 years of age and older. Miplyffa, in combination with miglustat, is approved to treat neurological symptoms associated with NPC. The FDA is the first agency to approve a drug for NPC. NPC is a rare genetic disease that results in progressive neurological symptoms and organ dysfunction. The approval of Miplyffa was based on a 12-month trial in patients with a molecularly confirmed diagnosis of NPC, which showed a slower disease progression. The FDA granted Miplyffa priority review, orphan drug, rare pediatric disease, fast track, and breakthrough therapy designations.

title: FDA Approves Nasal Spray Influenza Vaccine for Self- or Caregiver-Administration
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved FluMist for self- or caregiver-administration to prevent influenza disease in individuals 2 through 49 years of age. FluMist, a nasal spray vaccine, was initially approved in 2003 for use in individuals 5 through 49 years old, and in 2007, the FDA expanded its use to include children 2 through 5 years old. The vaccine has been safely and effectively used for many years, and its approval provides a new option for receiving a seasonal influenza vaccine with greater convenience, flexibility, and accessibility. The flu can cause mild to severe illness and serious complications, including hospitalization and death. The vaccine manufacturer plans to make FluMist available through a third-party online pharmacy, and caregivers should administer the vaccine to individuals 2 through 17 years old.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace. Job gains have slowed, and the unemployment rate has moved up but remains low. Inflation has made further progress toward the Committee's 2 percent objective but remains somewhat elevated. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. The Committee has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent, and judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are roughly in balance. The economic outlook is uncertain, and the Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate. In light of the progress on inflation and the balance of risks, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point to 4-3/4 to 5 percent. In considering additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. The Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgageâbacked securities. The Committee is strongly committed to supporting maximum employment and returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Michael S. Barr; Raphael W. Bostic; Lisa D. Cook; Mary C. Daly; Beth M. Hammack; Philip N. Jefferson; Adriana D. Kugler; and Christopher J. Waller. Voting against this action was Michelle W. Bowman, who preferred to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.

title: Implementation Note issued September 18, 2024
