body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on September 18, 2024: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to lower the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 4.9 percent, effective September 19, 2024. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective September 19, 2024, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 4â3/4 to 5 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 5 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 4.8 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $25 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency mortgageâbacked securities (MBS) received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month into Treasury securities to roughly match the maturity composition of Treasury securities outstanding. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve a 1/2 percentage point decrease in the primary credit rate to 5 percent, effective September 19, 2024. In taking this action, the Board approved requests to establish that rate submitted by the Board of Directors of the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: FDA Roundup: September 17, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued three draft guidances: one on integrating randomized controlled trials into routine clinical practice, and two on clinical trials with decentralized elements and generative AI-enabled medical devices. The FDA also announced a Digital Health Advisory Committee meeting on November 20-21, 2024, to discuss total product lifecycle considerations for generative AI-enabled medical devices. Additionally, the FDA cleared for marketing Apple's Sleep Apnea Notification Feature, an over-the-counter software application that analyzes Apple Watch sensor data to identify patterns of breathing disturbances. The FDA issued six warning letters to manufacturers and retailers for selling unauthorized e-cigarette products.

title: FDA Issues Draft Guidance on Conducting Multiregional Clinical Trials in Oncology
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a draft guidance for industry on conducting multiregional clinical trials in support of cancer drug applications. The guidance aims to provide recommendations for sponsors to ensure the generalizability and applicability of results from these trials to the US population and US medical practice. The guidance will support the FDA's review of data from multiregional clinical trials and help improve the planning, design, conduct, and analysis of future trials. The guidance is expected to expand on current principles for multiregional clinical trials and will provide additional recommendations to aid sponsors in planning multiregional clinical development programs. Comments on the draft guidance must be submitted within 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.

title: Presidential Determination on Major Drug Transit or Major Illicit Drug Producing Countries for Fiscal Year 2025
body_summary: The US President has designated 21 countries, including Afghanistan, Mexico, and Venezuela, as major drug transit or production countries, citing geographic, commercial, and economic factors. This determination affects countries that fail to adhere to international counternarcotic agreements. The US, in collaboration with Colombia, Peru, and the PRC, is working to address global drug trafficking issues. Colombia has seen a 10% increase in cocaine interdictions in 2023, with the Colombian National Police seizing over 841 metric tons of pure cocaine. The US-PRC Counternarcotics Working Group aims to share law enforcement information and tackle illicit financing. The US welcomes Colombia's 10-year drug strategy and urges adequate funding and implementation. Bolivia's efforts to address coca cultivation are noted, with more work needed. Opium poppy cultivation in Afghanistan requires global attention, and the PRC has taken steps to reduce precursor chemical flows to illicit drug producers.

title: FDA Roundup: September 13, 2024
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has published news from around the agency. The FDA will hold the first National Hispanic/Latino Family Cancer Awareness Week from September 20-26, 2024, to increase cancer awareness within the Hispanic/Latino population. The week will feature a virtual conversation on cancer and a social media campaign using the hashtag #LatinoCancer.

The FDA has also released a Drug Safety Communication warning about Veozah (fezolinetant), a medicine used to treat hot flashes due to menopause, which can cause rare but serious liver injury. Patients should stop taking Veozah immediately and seek medical attention if they experience signs and symptoms that suggest liver problems.

Additionally, the FDA has approved Tecentriq Hybreza for all adult indications, including non-small cell lung cancer, small cell lung cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, melanoma, and alveolar soft part sarcoma.

The FDA has also recognized additional consensus standards for medical device sterilization processes, including ISO 11737-3:2023, ISO 11140-1:2014, and ISO 13004:2022. These standards aim to facilitate the adoption of sterilization techniques, enhance quality, and advance international harmonization.

The FDA has also announced the final rule for updated mammography regulations, which went into effect on September 10, 2024. The final rule established federal standards to categorize breast tissue density, enhance communication to patients, and raise the bar for accreditation and facilities.

title: Proclamation 10809—National Hispanic Heritage Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States of America has issued a proclamation declaring September 15 through October 15, 2024, as National Hispanic Heritage Month. The proclamation honors and celebrates the culture, history, and contributions of the Latino community, recognizing their achievements and impact on the Nation. The President acknowledges the dedication of Latino leaders, including Secretary of Health and Human Services Xavier Becerra, Secretary of Homeland Security Alejandro Mayorkas, and others. The administration has made efforts to promote the American Dream, including creating nearly 16 million jobs, doubling Small Business Administration loans to Latino-owned businesses, and investing in Hispanic-serving colleges and universities. The President also emphasizes the importance of immigration reform, including a pathway to citizenship for Dreamers, and has taken action to protect and support these individuals.

title: FDA Authorizes First Over-the-Counter Hearing Aid Software
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has authorized the first over-the-counter hearing aid software device, Hearing Aid Feature, intended for use with compatible versions of Apple AirPods Pro headphones. The device enables the AirPods Pro to serve as an over-the-counter hearing aid for individuals 18 years or older with perceived mild to moderate hearing impairment. 

The FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health acting director, Michelle Tarver, M.D., Ph.D., stated that this marketing authorization advances the availability, accessibility, and acceptability of hearing support for adults with mild to moderate hearing loss. 

More than 30 million American adults report some degree of hearing loss, which can be caused by aging, exposure to loud noises, and other factors. 

The FDA's OTC hearing aid regulation, established in October 2022, enables consumers to purchase hearing aids directly from stores or online retailers without a medical exam, prescription, or seeing an audiologist. 

The Hearing Aid Feature is a software-only mobile medical application that uses a self-fitting strategy, allowing users to adjust it to meet their hearing needs without assistance. 

A clinical study with 118 subjects demonstrated that subjects who used the HAF self-fitting strategy achieved similar perceived benefit as subjects who received professional fitting. 

The FDA granted marketing authorization of the Hearing Aid Feature to Apple Inc.

title: FDA Issues Warning Letters to Two Chinese Firms Regarding Data Quality and Integrity Concerns, Violative Lab Practices
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued warning letters to Mid-Link Testing Company Ltd. in Tianjin, China, and Sanitation & Environmental Technology Institute of Soochow University Ltd. in Suzhou, China, citing laboratory oversight failures and animal care violations. The FDA will not authorize premarket device submissions with unreliable data. The agency inspected the firms earlier this year and found pervasive failures with data management, quality assurance, and staff training. Owen Faris, Ph.D., acting director of the Office of Product Evaluation and Quality, stated that the FDA will take action to protect patients and the medical device supply chain from quality failures. The FDA has requested that the firms notify the agency of their corrective actions within 15 working days.

title: FDA Roundup: September 10, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued warning letters to Root Bioscience Brands LLC for selling unapproved CBD products for human and pet use, making unproven claims about treating various diseases. The FDA has also commissioned an independent literature review and initiated an internal study to evaluate metals in tampons. Additionally, the FDA has issued an advisory for the Outbreak Investigation of Salmonella: Eggs, with 65 reported cases from nine states. The agency has also updated its list of medical devices that incorporate Augment Reality (AR) and Virtual Reality (VR), authorizing 69 devices.

title: Statement on a Department of the Treasury Report on Health Insurance Enrollment Under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: Nearly 50 million people have had coverage in the Affordable Care Act marketplace over the past decade. The Affordable Care Act is more popular than ever, and coverage is more affordable than ever. Vice President Harris and the speaker have worked to protect and build on the ACA, lowering costs by an average of $800 per year and investing in outreach and in-person assistance. As a result, more Americans have signed up for health care coverage through the marketplace than ever before. Congressional Republicans have voted over 50 times to repeal the ACA, which would take health care away from tens of millions of Americans and threaten coverage for over 100 million with preexisting conditions.

title: Statement on the United States Census Bureau Reports on Income, Poverty, and Health Insurance Coverage
body_summary: Reports show progress in growing the middle class, with incomes increasing by more than $3,000 last year and since taking office, adjusted for inflation. Health insurance coverage reached record highs under the administration, thanks to building on the Affordable Care Act and lowering healthcare costs. The expanded child tax credit, which cut child poverty nearly in half in 2021, must be restored and a plan to build millions of homes and make rent more affordable must be passed. These policies, blocked by congressional Republicans, will continue to be pursued to lower poverty and build the middle class by lowering taxes on families.

title: Proclamation 10806—World Suicide Prevention Day, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States issues a proclamation on World Suicide Prevention Day, honoring those lost to suicide, supporting loved ones, and recognizing mental health professionals. Nearly 50,000 Americans died by suicide last year, and 10 million seriously considered it in 2022. The President aims to connect more Americans to affordable, quality mental health care and strengthen the mental health care system. The Administration has issued a rule requiring insurers to cover mental health care, provided over $12 billion for mental health services, and expanded access to treatment for veterans and first responders. The President also launched the 988 National Suicide and Crisis Lifeline and the National Maternal Mental Health Hotline.

title: Executive Order 14126—Investing in America and Investing in American Workers
body_summary: The US government has issued an order to prioritize and invest in projects that promote good jobs, economic security, and equitable workforce development. The Investing in America agenda focuses on rebuilding American infrastructure, reviving manufacturing, and fostering a clean energy economy. The policy aims to create well-paying jobs, especially union jobs, and support workers' free and fair choice to join a union. Key priorities include transparency measures, fair pay practices, paid leave, healthcare, and retirement benefits, as well as access to high-quality training and portable credentials. The order also establishes an Investing in Good Jobs Task Force, co-chaired by the Secretary of Labor and the Assistant to the President for Economic Policy, to coordinate policy development and support implementation.

title: Proclamation 10805—National Grandparents Day, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States, Joseph R. Biden Jr., proclaims September 8, 2024, as National Grandparents Day. The proclamation recognizes the contributions of grandparents to American families and the country, thanking them for their love, guidance, and care. The President notes that grandparents are primary caregivers for over 2.7 million grandchildren, providing stability and warmth to their homes. The Administration is working to support grandparents by ensuring they have access to healthcare, including lowering prescription drug costs through the Inflation Reduction Act. Additionally, the President announces the National Strategy to Support Family Caregivers, which includes the AmeriCorps Seniors Foster Grandparent Program, to provide resources and opportunities for seniors to mentor young people.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Report on the Employment Situation in August
body_summary: Unemployment fell to 4.2 percent, with 142,000 jobs created last month. Nearly 16 million new jobs have been created, and wages and incomes are rising faster than prices. The Vice President and the author are working to expand opportunity and grow the middle class, focusing on sustaining historic gains for American workers. They aim to support American workers and businesses, lower housing and healthcare costs, and prevent a return to failed trickle-down economics.

title: FDA Roundup: September 6, 2024
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is hosting a virtual Medical Device Sterilization Town Hall: Sterility Master Files and Effective Use in Premarket Submissions on September 11 from 1-2 p.m. ET. The agency also issued a draft guidance on incorporating voluntary patient preference information into decision-making processes. The guidance aims to provide recommendations on collecting and sharing patient preference information and designing studies for reliable scientific evidence.

The FDA will also host a webinar on October 15, 2024, to discuss the draft guidance. Comments on the guidance can be submitted by December 5, 2024, at www.regulations.gov.

The agency updated an advisory on the Investigation of Illnesses: Diamond Shrumz-Brand Chocolate Bars, Cones, & Gummies, and issued a Constituent Update on food traceability efforts. Deputy Commissioner Jim Jones highlighted online resources and roundtables to aid industry implementation of the Food Traceability Rule.

The FDA is accepting site proposals for the Experiential Learning Program (ELP) for the Fall 2025 cycle until October 7, 2024. It also released tips on protecting public health during emergencies and disasters, and a Pesticide Residue Monitoring Program Report for Fiscal Year 2022.

Additionally, the FDA issued a Dear Veterinarian letter on federal requirements for veterinarians dispensing prescription animal drugs, and posted a new video in the "FDA In Your Day" series featuring Chief Medical Officer Dr. Hilary Marston discussing hurricane preparedness.

title: Youth E-Cigarette Use Drops to Lowest Level in a Decade
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) released new data from the National Youth Tobacco Survey (NYTS) showing a significant drop in e-cigarette use among US youth, with 2.13 million youth reporting current use in 2023 compared to 1.63 million in 2024. The decline was largely driven by reduced e-cigarette use among high schoolers. The number of youth who used e-cigarettes in 2024 is approximately one-third of its peak in 2019. The survey found that 26.3% of youth who used e-cigarettes used them daily, and the most common flavors were fruit, candy, and mint. Disposable e-cigarette products were the most common product type used, with Elf Bar being the most popular brand. The FDA has been enforcing compliance and enforcement actions against unauthorized products, including more than 1,000 warning letters and 240 civil money penalties.

title: Proclamation 10797—National Preparedness Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States issues a proclamation during National Preparedness Month to honor first responders and recommit to equipping Americans with resources to overcome the climate crisis and extreme weather events. The proclamation notes that historic heat waves, flooding, and fires have claimed many lives and impacted communities severely. The Administration has invested over $50 billion in climate resilience, including elevating roads and bridges, upgrading buildings, and planting trees. The Federal Emergency Management Agency has expanded benefits for disaster survivors and simplified the disaster assistance application process. The Administration has also expanded the Affordable Care Act, lowered healthcare costs, and created new jobs. The President proclaims September 2024 as National Preparedness Month, encouraging all Americans to recognize the importance of preparedness and work together to enhance resilience and readiness.

title: FDA Authorizes Updated Novavax COVID-19 Vaccine to Better Protect Against Currently Circulating Variants
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted emergency use authorization for an updated version of the Novavax COVID-19 vaccine, which more closely targets currently circulating variants, to provide better protection against serious consequences of COVID-19. The updated vaccine is authorized for use in individuals 12 years of age and older and includes a monovalent component that corresponds to the Omicron variant JN.1 strain of SARS-CoV-2. The vaccine follows recent approvals and authorizations of updated mRNA COVID-19 vaccines for 2024-2025 manufactured by ModernaTX Inc. and Pfizer Inc. Individuals 12 years of age and older who have never been vaccinated with any COVID-19 vaccine are eligible to receive two doses of the updated vaccine, 3 weeks apart. The FDA assessed manufacturing and nonclinical data to support the change to the 2024-2025 formula, and the vaccine has met the statutory criteria for issuance of an EUA.

title: La FDA autoriza la vacuna contra el COVID-19 de Novavax actualizada para brindar una mejor protección contra las variantes que circulan actualmente
body_summary: La Administración de Alimentos y Medicamentos de los Estados Unidos (FDA) ha otorgado una autorización de uso de emergencia para una versión actualizada de la vacuna contra el COVID-19 de Novavax que ataca más de cerca a las variantes circulantes para brindar una mejor protección contra las consecuencias graves del COVID-19. La vacuna actualizada está autorizada para su uso en personas de 12 años o mayores y incluye un componente monovalente que corresponde a la cepa JN.1 de la variante ómicron del SARS-CoV-2. La vacuna se fabrica mediante un proceso similar al de las fórmulas anteriores y las personas que reciben esta vacuna pueden experimentar efectos secundarios similares a los informados por las personas que recibieron fórmulas anteriores. La FDA ha determinado que la vacuna actualizada contra el COVID-19 de Novavax ha cumplido con los criterios legales para la emisión de una EUA y ha otorgado la autorización de uso de emergencia a Novavax Inc.

title: FDA Roundup: August 30, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved a new indication for ACAM2000 to include the prevention of mpox disease in individuals at high risk. ACAM2000 has also been approved for the prevention of smallpox disease. A Medication Guide is required for safe use of the vaccine. The FDA has granted marketing authorization for Renata Medical's Minima Stent System for the treatment of pulmonary artery stenoses and aortic coarctation in neonates, infants, and children. The FDA has posted warning letters to firms selling medical devices for cleaning, disinfecting, or sanitizing continuous positive airway pressure machines and accessories without authorization. The FDA has also announced a Patient Engagement Advisory Committee meeting on October 30, 2024, to discuss patient-centered informed consent in clinical studies. The FDA has authorized Germitec's Chronos for the high-level disinfection of certain ultrasound probes.

title: Proclamation 10798—National Prostate Cancer Awareness Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States announces National Prostate Cancer Awareness Month. Nearly 300,000 American men are diagnosed with prostate cancer each year, and over 35,000 die from it. The President honors those who have lost loved ones to the disease and acknowledges the resilience of those living with it. Despite progress, challenges persist, including disparities in diagnosis and treatment for Black and Hispanic men. The President reiterates the goal of cutting cancer death rates by 50% over 25 years and announces investments in research, clinical studies, and cancer navigation resources. The President also highlights efforts to expand access to healthcare, including free cancer screenings and primary care visits, and to reduce prescription drug costs.

title: Proclamation 10796—National Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month, 2024
body_summary: President Biden declares September 2024 as National Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month, honoring the memories of women lost to the disease. Nearly 20,000 women will be diagnosed this year. The Administration reaffirms support for women with ovarian cancer and their families, and recognizes the importance of research and awareness. The Biden Cancer Moonshot aims to reduce cancer deaths by 50% over 25 years. The Administration has secured $4 billion in funding for cancer research and established patient navigation services to guide patients and families through the cancer diagnosis process. This year, the Administration has also expanded health care coverage to millions of Americans, including those with ovarian cancer. President Biden encourages citizens to discuss risk factors with their doctors and remain vigilant against symptoms.

title: Proclamation 10800—National Sickle Cell Awareness Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States of America has issued a proclamation declaring September 2024 as National Sickle Cell Awareness Month. Every person in the country deserves to live a healthy and fulfilling life, but approximately 100,000 Americans suffer from Sickle Cell Disease, a painful genetic blood disorder that causes life-threatening complications. The Administration is working to deliver for people with Sickle Cell Disease and their families, including following the science to find new treatments. Last year, the Food and Drug Administration approved the first gene therapies and new drug therapies to treat SCD. The National Institutes of Health is also working to improve the quality of life for people with SCD. The Administration is working to make treatment more accessible and affordable, empowering people with SCD on Medicare and Medicaid to have greater access to cell and gene therapy treatments. The Health Resources and Services Administration is expanding access to quality care through community-based organizations, while the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is expanding data collection efforts to better target resources.

title: Proclamation 10802—Labor Day, 2024
body_summary: Every year on Labor Day, the President of the United States celebrates the dignity of America's workers and labor unions. President Joe Biden honored pioneers who fought for workers' rights, paid tribute to the American workforce, and recognized the enduring movement that powers the economy and strengthens the Nation. The President promised to be pro-labor and pro-union, ensuring unions have the support they need to fight for workers. Since taking office, nearly 16 million new jobs have been created, including 800,000 manufacturing jobs and 900,000 construction jobs. The Administration has invested in construction projects, reduced inflation, and positioned American workers to lead the world in innovation. The President signed the Inflation Reduction Act and the CHIPS and Science Act, attracting nearly $900 billion in private-sector commitments to invest in manufacturing and clean energy. The Administration has also strengthened Davis-Bacon requirements and enacted the Butch Lewis Act to protect union retirement security. The President is working to crack down on noncompete agreements and ensure workers' safety and security on the job.

title: Proclamation 10795—National Childhood Cancer Awareness Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States honors the courage of children facing cancer, survivors, and families who care for them. The President renews the commitment to end cancer, ensuring every child can live a healthy, fulfilling life. The Biden Administration accelerates cancer research and improves treatment options, securing $4 billion in bipartisan funding and launching initiatives such as the Childhood Cancer-Data Integration for Research, Education, Care, and Clinical Trials. The President also strengthens Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act, increasing funding for childhood cancer research and ensuring cancer navigation services are paid for. The President proclaims September 2024 as National Childhood Cancer Awareness Month, encouraging citizens to support the fight against childhood cancer and connect with support services.

title: FDA Issues Final Rule Increasing the Minimum Age for Certain Restrictions on Tobacco Sales
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced a final rule raising the minimum age for certain restrictions on tobacco product sales. The rule, which aligns with legislation signed in December 2019, immediately raises the federal minimum age of sale of tobacco products in the United States from 18 to 21 years of age. Beginning Sept. 30, retailers must verify the age of anyone under 30 with photo identification, while sales via vending machine are prohibited in facilities where individuals under 21 are present or permitted to enter at any time. The goal of these changes is to maximize the public health impact of the original legislation, which aims to protect the nation's youth from tobacco product health risks.

title: Statement on the Price of Anti-Obesity Medications
body_summary: The US pays two to three times more for prescription drugs than other countries. Vice President Harris and I have allowed Medicare to negotiate drug prices for the first time. We've capped insulin at $35/month and required drug companies to pay rebates if they raise prices faster than inflation. Last month, Senator Sanders and I called on drug manufacturers to lower prices on popular obesity and diabetes drugs. Eli Lilly has taken steps to lower prices by offering a direct-to-consumer version of their medication for less than half the original price. The Vice President and I will continue to fight to make all Americans access necessary medications.

title: FDA Roundup: August 27, 2024
body_summary: The US FDA has revised the Emergency Use Authorization for Pemgarda (pemivibart) to limit its use to when the combined national frequency of variants with substantially reduced susceptibility is less than or equal to 90%. The FDA has also opened registration for a September 6 public meeting on advancing treatments for PTSD, featuring a panel discussion on psychedelic drug development and opportunities for public comment. A new video featuring Dr. Hilary Marston discussing Lyme disease was posted in the "FDA In Your Day" series. A webinar on the Final Guidance: Remanufacturing of Medical Devices is scheduled for September 10, 2024, 1-2 p.m. ET, to clarify the difference between remanufacturing and servicing.

title: FDA Clears First Device to Enable Automated Insulin Dosing for Individuals with Type 2 Diabetes
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has expanded the indications of the Insulet SmartAdjust technology to also include the management of type 2 diabetes in individuals 18 years and older. The technology, an interoperable automated glycemic controller, automatically adjusts insulin delivery by connecting to an alternate controller-enabled insulin pump and integrated continuous glucose monitor. The FDA's action helps expand access to this important diabetes management tool to millions of adults living in the U.S. with type 2 diabetes. The technology was previously only available for people with type 1 diabetes. A clinical study of 289 individuals 18 years and older with type 2 diabetes on insulin used the Insulet SmartAdjust technology for 13 weeks, showing improved blood sugar control across all demographic groups. The FDA reviewed the SmartAdjust technology software through the 510(k) premarket clearance pathway, and no serious adverse events were reported during the study.

title: FDA Roundup: August 23, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued a Small Entity Compliance Guide to help small entities comply with the 2023 MQSA Rule, which amends regulations issued under the Mammography Quality Standards Act of 1992. The rule becomes effective September 10, 2024. The FDA also updated an advisory on a Salmonella outbreak linked to cucumbers, which is now over with 551 illnesses in 34 states and the District of Columbia. The FDA issued a draft guidance on Predetermined Change Control Plans for Medical Devices, which proposes a policy for predetermined change control plans. The FDA will host a webinar on September 3, 2024, about the guidance. The agency also updated an advisory on Diamond Shruumz-brand chocolate bars and announced a new funding opportunity for the FDA Rare Neurodegenerative Disease Grant Program to fund clinical trials of products evaluating efficacy and/or safety for rare neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Proclamation 10794—Women's Equality Day, 2024
body_summary: President Biden proclaims August 26, 2024, as Women's Equality Day, recognizing the 104th anniversary of the ratification of the 19th Amendment, which granted American women the right to vote. The proclamation honors the courage of generations of women's rights activists and acknowledges the ongoing struggle for equality and women's rights in the US. The President's Administration has taken actions to promote women's empowerment, including expanding reproductive freedom, advancing pay equity, and increasing access to healthcare and education. The proclamation also calls on Americans to celebrate and continue to build on progress toward gender equality and to defend the right to vote.

title: FDA Approves and Authorizes Updated mRNA COVID-19 Vaccines to Better Protect Against Currently Circulating Variants
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved and granted emergency use authorization for updated mRNA COVID-19 vaccines with a monovalent component targeting the Omicron variant KP.2 strain of SARS-CoV-2. The updated vaccines, including Comirnaty and Spikevax, are approved for individuals 12 years of age and older, and the Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine and Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine are authorized for emergency use for individuals 6 months through 11 years of age. The agency advised manufacturers to update the vaccines to more closely target currently circulating variants and provide better protection against serious consequences of COVID-19. The FDA assessed manufacturing and nonclinical data to support the change, and the updated vaccines are expected to provide protection against COVID-19 caused by the currently circulating variants.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A Federal Open Market Committee meeting was held July 30-31, 2024, to review financial markets and open market operations. Financial conditions eased modestly, with nominal Treasury yields declining and inflation expectations falling. The policy rate path predictions pointed to a first rate cut at the September FOMC meeting, with further easing expected in 2025. China lowered key policy rates amid property-sector woes and weak consumer sentiment. Market-implied federal funds rate path shifted downward, with nominal Treasury yields declining. Broad stock price indexes rose slightly, while yield spreads on corporate bonds remained near historical lows. Credit conditions were mixed, with some sectors tightening standards. The staff assessed the US financial system's stability, noting elevated asset valuation pressures and moderate vulnerabilities in business and household debt. The Committee maintained its target federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent, citing recent progress on inflation but needing more data before adjusting policy.

title: FDA Roundup: August 20, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Lazcluze (lazertinib) in combination with amivantamab for treating adult patients with specific non-small cell lung cancer mutations. The approval was announced on Monday, with full prescribing information to be posted on the Drugs@FDA website. A joint NIH-FDA Nutrition Regulatory Science Workshop is scheduled for December 17 and 18, 2024, to discuss topics such as ultra-processed foods, regulatory actions, and emerging technological innovations in nutrition science.

title: FDA Marketing Authorization Enables Increased Access to First Step of Syphilis Diagnosis
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted marketing authorization to NOWDiagnostics for the First To Know Syphilis Test, the first at-home, over-the-counter test to detect syphilis antibodies in human blood. The test, which provides results in approximately 15 minutes, allows individuals to better inform next steps with a healthcare provider. This authorization aims to increase initial screening for syphilis, particularly among those who may be reluctant to see a healthcare provider. The test will contribute to the goals of the Department of Health and Human Services' STI National Strategic Plan, which seeks to reverse the recent dramatic rise of STIs in the US. The test should be followed by additional laboratory testing through a healthcare provider to confirm a diagnosis of syphilis, and results should not be used to start, stop, or change treatments without a healthcare provider.

title: FDA Roundup: August 16, 2024
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration issued notices on several topics. A warning letter was sent to Austrofood, a manufacturer of apple cinnamon fruit puree pouches, due to elevated levels of lead and chromium. The FDA approved Imfinzi (durvalumab, AstraZeneca) for treating adults with resectable non-small cell lung cancer. 

The FDA updated its advisory for a Salmonella outbreak linked to cucumbers, with samples from Bedner Growers and Thomas Produce Company likely sources of illnesses. 

The FDA advised consumers not to use antibacterial soaps, as there's no evidence they are more effective than plain soap and water. It also approved Niktimvo (axatilimab-csfr, Incyte Corporation) for treating chronic graft-versus-host disease. 

The FDA released the results of a second retail sampling survey testing dairy products for avian influenza A (H5N1), finding no viable virus in the samples. It updated its advisory for Diamond Shruumz-brand chocolate bars and cones, and granted a marketing authorization to SoClean Inc. for a bacterial reduction device for CPAP accessories.

title: Statement on the Second Anniversary of the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022
body_summary: The President signed the Inflation Reduction Act two years ago, investing in climate and lowering prescription drug costs. The law is lowering health care costs, strengthening energy security, and creating over 330,000 clean energy jobs. It has also generated $265 billion in private sector clean energy and manufacturing investments since taking office. The administration announced lower prescription drug prices for 10 negotiated drugs by Medicare, cutting prices by nearly 40-80% and saving taxpayers $6 billion. Republicans want to repeal the law, which would increase prescription drug costs, but the President and Vice President Harris will continue to fight for investing in America and giving families more breathing room.

title: FDA Announces Milestone in Sodium Reduction Efforts, Issues Draft Guidance with Lower Target Levels for Certain Foods
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued draft guidance for Phase II of its voluntary sodium reduction targets, aiming to reduce average individual sodium intake to approximately 2,750 milligrams per day. The initial Phase I targets, set in October 2021, encouraged the food industry to reduce sodium levels in processed, packaged, and prepared foods. Preliminary data shows that about 40% of the initial Phase I targets have been reached, indicating early success. The Phase II targets will focus on commercially processed, packaged, and prepared foods, with the goal of reducing sodium intake by approximately 20% compared to pre-2021 levels. The FDA's sodium reduction initiative is part of the White House National Strategy on Hunger, Nutrition and Health to reduce diet-related diseases by 2030. The agency has also taken additional actions, including proposing a rule to amend the standards of identity to permit the use of salt substitutes and guidance on the use of "potassium salt" instead of "potassium chloride". The FDA will issue regular evaluations of sodium levels in foods every three years and consider future phases of sodium reduction targets as part of its evaluation and monitoring.

title: FDA Issues Warning Letter to Austrofood and Continues Robust Activities to Ensure Safety of Cinnamon Products Sold in U.S.
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) initiated an investigation into apple cinnamon fruit puree pouches found to be contaminated with harmful levels of lead and chromium. The pouches, manufactured by Austrofood, were recalled after being found to contain elevated levels of lead. The FDA's leading hypothesis is that the contamination was an act of economically motivated adulteration. The agency has issued a warning letter to Austrofood, citing violations of the Current Good Manufacturing Practice, Hazard Analysis, and Risk-Based Preventive Controls for Human Food rule. The warning letter states that Austrofood failed to conduct a hazard analysis to identify lead as a hazard requiring a preventive control. The FDA is taking additional efforts to prevent future lead-related incidents, including sampling and testing of cinnamon and other spices in the food supply.

title: Statement on Prescription Drug Cost Reduction Efforts
body_summary: The US administration is announcing that Medicare has reached agreements on new, lower prices with the manufacturers of 10 selected drugs. These lower prices will result in $1.5 billion in savings for people on Medicare and $6 billion in savings for Medicare in the first year. This milestone is possible due to the Inflation Reduction Act, which passed with the leadership of Democrats in Congress and Vice President Harris' tie-breaking vote. The administration is continuing to fight to make all Americans pay less for prescription drugs and give more breathing room for families.

title: Statement on Clean Energy Job Creation
body_summary: The President claims that since signing the Inflation Reduction Act into law, over 330,000 new clean energy jobs have been announced, many of which are good-paying and union jobs requiring no college degree. These jobs are driving a manufacturing boom and lowering utility bills for families, thanks to the administration's policies. House Republicans have voted to repeal these policies, despite jobs being created in their districts. The President will continue to fight for American families, aiming to lower utility bills and increase access to good-paying, union jobs.

title: FDA Roundup: August 13, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued two warning letters to BullyKamp Products LLC and Top Dog Pet Store LLC dba The Bulldog Cartel for marketing unapproved animal drugs intended for dogs. The FDA will hold a public meeting on October 16, 2024, to discuss the establishment of a Rare Disease Innovation Hub. The FDA has also approved Yorvipath (palopegteriparatide) injection for adults with hypoparathyroidism. The FDA has updated its advisory on Diamond Shruumz-brand products, including additional testing results.

title: FDA Approves First Nasal Spray for Treatment of Anaphylaxis
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved neffy (epinephrine nasal spray) for the emergency treatment of allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, in adult and pediatric patients weighing at least 30 kilograms. The approval is based on four studies involving 175 healthy adults, which showed comparable epinephrine blood concentrations and similar increases in blood pressure and heart rate between neffy and approved epinephrine injection products. Neffy is a single dose nasal spray administered into one nostril, and a second dose may be given if symptoms worsen. The FDA granted neffyFast Track designation and approved it to ARS Pharmaceuticals.

title: FDA Roundup: August 9, 2024
body_summary:
The US FDA invites the public to a public meeting on September 25, 2024, from 12:30-4:30 p.m. ET, to share information on its enhanced systematic process for post-market assessment of chemicals in food. The meeting will include open public comment. The project is part of a larger enhanced approach for food chemical safety. 

The FDA has released documents regarding the transition phase after its Memorandum of Understanding with the Association of American Feed Control Officials (AAFCO) expires on October 1, 2024. These documents include draft guidance for industry #293, #294, and a request for public comment. The FDA is accepting public comments until September 9, 2024, and December 9, 2024. 

The FDA has released its updated 2024 Language Access Plan, aiming to address language barriers and strengthen language access to health information and services. The plan supports the FDA's ongoing work to help individuals make informed decisions about their health.

The FDA has granted an emergency use authorization to Octapharma Pharmazeutika Produktionsges.m.b.H. for emergency use of octaplasLG Powder for U.S. military forces. 

The FDA has updated the list of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI/ML)-Enabled Medical Devices, authorizing 950 devices. 

The FDA has published a blog titled FDA India Office Addresses Herbal and Ayurvedic Products, discussing regulatory issues surrounding India's Ayurvedic and Herbal exports.

title: FDA Approves First Nalmefene Hydrochloride Auto-Injector to Reverse Opioid Overdose
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Zurnai, a nalmefene hydrochloride auto-injector, for the emergency treatment of known or suspected opioid overdose in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. The approval follows a May 2023 approval of the first nasal spray formulation of nalmefene. The FDA has worked to increase availability and accessibility of nalmefene and naloxone to encourage harm reduction. The agency granted Fast Track and Priority Review designations to support the development and review of the product. Nalmefene is an opioid receptor antagonist used to treat acute opioid overdose, and the newly approved product delivers 1.5 milligrams of nalmefene under the skin or into muscle. The approval is supported by safety and pharmacokinetic studies.

title: FDA Roundup: August 6, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing a summary of recent news. On Monday, the FDA issued a Safety Alert advising restaurants and retailers not to serve or sell certain oysters from Lewis Bay, Massachusetts, due to potential contamination with Campylobacter jejuni. The Center for Devices and Radiological Health released a Discussion Paper on Health Equity For Medical Devices to obtain feedback on ways to ensure timely access to safe and effective medical devices. The paper requests comments under docket number FDA-2024-N-3616 by October 4, 2024. The Digital Health Center of Excellence published its summer edition newsletter, exploring digital health advancements to protect and promote public health. The Office of Regulatory Affairs partnered with NASDA and NC State to create a new course on public health food inspections, offering students a comprehensive understanding of the federal regulatory food inspections and enforcement system.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Report on the Employment Situation in July
body_summary: The US economy has created nearly 16 million jobs since Vice President Harris and the speaker took office, with lower unemployment rates than any administration in 50 years. Incomes have risen faster than prices. The report shows employment growth slowing, but business investment remains strong thanks to the "Investing in America" agenda. Prices are still too high and efforts to lower costs will continue, including tackling price gouging and capping prescription drug costs. Congressional Republicans are supporting tax cuts for billionaires and big corporations while threatening Social Security and Medicare, prompting a continued fight for the middle class.

title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapy to Treat Adults with Metastatic Synovial Sarcoma
body_summary: The US FDA has approved Tecelra (afamitresgene autoleucel), a gene therapy, for the treatment of adults with unresectable or metastatic synovial sarcoma who have received prior chemotherapy. The approval is based on an accelerated approval pathway, which allows earlier approval for serious or life-threatening diseases with unmet medical need. Tecelra is an autologous T cell immunotherapy that targets the MAGE-A4 antigen expressed by cancer cells in synovial sarcoma. The product was administered as a single intravenous dose and showed a 43.2% overall response rate and a median duration of response of six months in a multicenter clinical trial. The most common adverse reactions were nausea, vomiting, fatigue, and infections. The FDA granted Orphan Drug, Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy, and Priority Review designations for this indication and approved the product to Adaptimmune, LLC.

title: FDA Roundup: August 2, 2024
body_summary: The US FDA has published several news items. Representatives attended a community discussion on clinical trial diversity for sexual and gender minority communities. The FDA approved Jemperli for adult patients with primary advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. The FDA established a Digital Health Advisory Committee to advise on digital health technologies. The FDA introduced online resources on reprocessing single-use medical devices. The FDA announced executive career opportunities related to its reorganization of the Human Foods Program. The FDA issued warning letters to five online retailers for selling unauthorized disposable e-cigarette products. The FDA published a Spotlight on CDER Science describing a method to identify patient populations who will benefit from drug therapies. The FDA published a summary of adverse event reports related to Purina pet food. The FDA issued medical device user fees and annual establishment registration fees for Fiscal Year 2025. The FDA issued a letter to healthcare providers about the safe use of Mega 2000 and Mega Soft Patient Return Electrodes. The FDA announced fiscal year 2025 fee rates and payment procedures under the Animal Drug User Fee Amendments. The FDA approved Darzalex Faspro for patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma.

title: Proclamation 10789—National Health Center Week, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States of America has issued a proclamation to recognize the importance of federally funded community health centers, which provide affordable access to quality medical, dental, and behavioral health services to over 30 million Americans. The proclamation expresses gratitude to dedicated health center staff and renews the commitment to ensuring every American has access to good-quality, affordable health care. The proclamation also honors the significant role health centers play in addressing health disparities and promoting health equity, particularly in Tribal, rural, and underserved communities.

title: Implementation Note issued July 31, 2024
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on July 31, 2024: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 5.4 percent, effective August 1, 2024. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective August 1, 2024, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 5-1/4 to 5â1/2 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 5.5 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 5.3 percent and with a perâcounterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $25 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency mortgageâbacked securities (MBS) received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month into Treasury securities to roughly match the maturity composition of Treasury securities outstanding. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 5.5 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace. Job gains have moderated, and the unemployment rate has moved up but remains low. Inflation has eased over the past year but remains somewhat elevated. In recent months, there has been some further progress toward the Committee's 2 percent inflation objective. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals continue to move into better balance. The economic outlook is uncertain, and the Committee is attentive to the risks to both sides of its dual mandate. In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent. In considering any adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. The Committee does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgageâbacked securities. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Michael S. Barr; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Mary C. Daly; Austan D. Goolsbee; Philip N. Jefferson; Adriana D. Kugler; and Christopher J. Waller. Austan D. Goolsbee voted as an alternate member at this meeting.

title: FDA Roundup: July 30, 2024
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration announced fiscal year 2025 user fee rates for importers and accreditation bodies participating in the Voluntary Qualified Importer Program and the Accredited Third-Party Certification Program. The user fee rates are authorized by the FDA Food Safety Modernization Act and will cover the agency's costs of administering these programs.

The FDA issued a public health alert advising consumers to discard and not buy nine ground cinnamon products due to elevated levels of lead. This alert is part of previous alerts issued on March 6, 2024, and July 25, 2024, for ground cinnamon products previously recommended for recall.

Deputy Commissioner for Human Foods Jim Jones said reducing dietary exposure to lead and other heavy metals among babies and young children is a top priority of the human foods program.

The FDA officially opened the CDRH Center Director vacancy following the retirement of former CDRH Director Jeff Shuren. The position will remain open until August 27 as the agency conducts a national search for the next director.

The FDA approved the Guardant Health, Inc. Shield, a test intended to screen for colorectal cancer (CRC) using blood collected in the Guardant Shield Blood Collection Kit. The test is used for CRC screening in individuals at average risk for the disease who are 45 years of age or older.

title: FDA Roundup: July 26, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Palforzia, a peanut allergen powder, for individuals ages 1-3 years with peanut allergy to mitigate allergic reactions. The FDA also released findings on the prevalence of Cyclospora cayetanensis, Salmonella spp., and Shiga toxin-producing Escherichia coli in fresh basil, cilantro, and parsley. The agency issued warnings to retailers selling unauthorized e-cigarette products and a public health alert about a ground cinnamon product containing elevated levels of lead. Additionally, the FDA advised restaurants and consumers not to eat certain oysters from Maine potentially contaminated with Campylobacter and published a blog on AI-enabled healthcare. The agency also announced a virtual Medical Device Sterilization Town Hall and updated the advisory for illnesses linked to Diamond Shruumz-brand chocolate bars.

title: Proclamation 10787—Anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States of America has proclaimed July 26, 2024, as the Anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), a landmark civil rights law protecting people with disabilities from discrimination. The ADA enshrines the idea that all Americans deserve opportunity, inclusion, respect, and dignity. The President has co-sponsored this legislation and is proud of its legacy. Despite progress, disabled Americans often face obstacles, including lower wages and voting barriers. To address this, the President has signed an Executive Order ensuring equal employment opportunities, including in Federal workplaces. The Department of Labor and Office of Personnel Management are working to make Federal workplaces accessible. The President has also taken action to improve access to healthcare, education, and digital infrastructure for people with disabilities. The Administration is investing in programs to hire disabled Americans, provide rigorous education, and create accessible public spaces.

title: FDA Roundup: July 23, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Femlyv, the first orally disintegrating tablet for pregnancy prevention, on Monday. The drug, containing norethindrone acetate and ethinyl estradiol, offers an alternative treatment option for individuals who have difficulty swallowing traditional pills. The FDA also published updates on laboratory-developed tests, influenza diagnostic tests, and e-cigarette products. Additionally, FDA Commissioner Dr. Robert M. Califf discussed the decline in US life expectancy due to common chronic diseases. The agency has issued a draft guidance for industry on pediatric inflammatory bowel disease treatment and will host a virtual public meeting on July 25 to discuss its "Home as a Health Care Hub" initiative.

title: Proclamation 10786—Made in America Week, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States is proclaiming Made in America Week from July 21 to July 27, 2024. American workers are bringing new jobs, businesses, and hope to their communities after a once-in-a-century pandemic. Since the President's administration, the economy has created over 15 million jobs, including nearly 800,000 manufacturing jobs. The unemployment rate fell to its lowest level in half a century. Companies have invested over $700 billion in American manufacturing, and the Federal Government is using its purchasing power to bring manufacturing back home. The Buy American Act has been strengthened, with a 65% domestic content threshold set for 2024 and plans to raise it to 75% in 2029. The Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and Inflation Reduction Act are driving manufacturing jobs and investments in clean energy. The President is calling on all Americans to observe Made in America Week and support American workers and domestic businesses.

title: FDA, FTC Continue Joint Effort to Protect Consumers Against Companies Illegally Selling Copycat Delta-8 THC Food Products
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) have issued warning letters to five companies for selling copycat food products containing delta-8 THC, a psychoactive compound found in cannabis, in violation of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act). The companies are Hippy Mood, Earthly Hemps, Shamrockshrooms.com, Mary Janes Bakery Co. LLC, and Life Leaf Medical CBD Center. In July 2023, the agencies also warned six other companies for similar violations, and all six companies have removed such products from stock.

The FDA has received over 300 adverse event reports involving children and adults who consumed delta-8 THC products, including hospitalizations and emergency department visits, since January 1, 2021. The FDA is concerned about the ease of purchasing delta-8 THC products, particularly for youth, and the potential for harm from impurities or variations in composition.

The FTC's Bureau of Consumer Protection has stated that companies that market and sell edible THC products that are easily mistaken for snacks and candy are putting the health of young children at risk and may face legal action. The FDA has requested written responses from the companies within 15 working days stating how they will address these violations and prevent their recurrence.

title: FDA Roundup: July 16, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced several key developments. The FDA revised its final guidance on Application User Fees for Combination Products, clarifying how user fees are applied for single and separate applications. The agency authorized the marketing of DiaSorin Molecular LLC's Simplexa C. auris Direct, a test for detecting Candida auris DNA, to help prevent and control infections in healthcare settings. The FDA also announced organizational changes within the Center for Devices and Radiological Health to strengthen the center and improve efficiencies. Additionally, the FDA issued a guidance on Drugs for the Treatment of Partial Onset Seizures, which provides recommendations on extrapolating efficacy from adult to pediatric patients.

title: FDA Roundup: July 12, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is providing an update on recent news and actions. On Wednesday, the FDA notified healthcare providers about disruptions in the supply of BD BACTEC blood culture media bottles due to supplier issues, adding them to the medical device shortage list. The FDA recommends conserving the use of these bottles for patients at highest risk. A webinar on In Vitro Diagnostic Products (IVDs) - MDR Requirements, Correction and Removal Reporting Requirements, and Quality System Complaint Requirements will be held on August 22, 2024. The FDA has also issued a final guidance on Clinical Considerations for Studies of Devices Intended to Treat Opioid Use Disorder. Additionally, the FDA announced the approval of Felanorm, a generic methimazole oral solution for the treatment of hyperthyroidism in cats. The FDA has also updated advisories for illnesses linked to Diamond Shruumz-brand products and bulk organic walnuts, which have been linked to a multistate outbreak of E. coli O157:H7 infections.

title: FDA Updates Guidance to Further Empower Companies to Address the Spread of Misinformation
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is providing updated recommendations to industry to address misinformation about FDA-regulated medical products. FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf has stated that regulated industry plays a critical role in ensuring consumers have accurate information. The revised draft guidance, Addressing Misinformation About Medical Devices and Prescription Drugs Questions and Answers, supports companies that issue "tailored responsive communications" to address internet-based misinformation created by independent third parties. The guidance is open for public comment for 60 days and aims to help companies address misinformation and provide factual, accurate, and scientifically sound information to the public.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Report on the Employment Situation in June
body_summary: The administration reported 206,000 jobs created last month, totaling 15.7 million jobs created during the administration. This marks the highest share of working-age Americans in the workforce in over 20 years. The administration aims to address rising living costs by tackling corporate price gouging, capping insulin and prescription drug costs, and pushing for rent reduction through new home construction. In contrast, Congressional Republicans propose a different vision, which includes high consumer tariffs, a giant tax cut for the wealthy, repealing the Affordable Care Act, and allowing corporate price increases.

title: FDA Roundup: July 5, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has updated an advisory for two separate outbreak investigations: one linked to Salmonella illnesses from cucumbers and another from Diamond Shruumz-brand products. The FDA and CDC are investigating 449 illnesses in 31 states and the District of Columbia, with cucumbers from Bedner Growers, Inc. identified as a likely source. A public workshop on developing clinical outcome assessments for implanted brain-computer interfaces will be held on September 19-20, 2024. The FDA has also warned consumers not to eat, sell, or serve any flavor of Diamond Shruumz-brand Chocolate Bars, Cones, or Gummies, due to a total of 48 reported illnesses in 24 states.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A joint meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee and the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System was held on June 11-12, 2024. Financial conditions eased modestly due to higher equity prices, nominal Treasury yields declined moderately, and inflation compensation fell at shorter horizons. The path of the federal funds rate implied by futures prices shifted slightly lower, indicating one and one-half 25 basis point cuts by year-end. Nominal Treasury yields fell moderately, driven by real yield declines. Inflation compensation decreased, while market-based interest rate uncertainty remained elevated. Broad stock indexes increased amid positive outlook on corporate profits. The dollar depreciated against most currencies, but the broad dollar index slightly increased. Participants judged inflation remained elevated but saw modest progress toward the 2 percent goal, aided by lower services price inflation and reduced pricing power among firms. Jerome H. Powell and nine others voted in favor of maintaining the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent, aiming for inflation to reach 2 percent sustainably.

title: FDA Roundup: July 2, 2024
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration approved Kisunla(donanemab-azbt) injection for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease. The trial data demonstrated that Kisunla reduces the rate of cognitive and functional decline in patients with mild cognitive impairment and mild dementia stages of Alzheimer's disease. The approval is evidence of the FDA's commitment to helping more safe and effective drugs to treat Alzheimer's disease become available.

The FDA is revoking the regulation authorizing the use of brominated vegetable oil (BVO) in food, effective August 2, due to potential adverse health effects found in studies conducted with the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

The FDA is expanding its Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program to spur faster development of high-quality, safe, effective, and innovative medical devices. Two webinars are available for stakeholders interested in FDA regulation of intentional genomic alterations in animals.

The FDA updated its advisory for the Investigation of Illnesses: Diamond Shruumz-Brand Chocolate Bars, Cones, & Gummies, to include information about the Prophet Premium Blends, LLC, recall, which was initiated on June 27, 2024, for all flavors of Diamond Shruumz-brand products.

title: FDA Roundup: June 28, 2024
body_summary: The FDA has announced several updates and recalls, including a recall of Diamond Shruumz-brand Chocolate Bars, Cones, and Gummies due to potential health risks, and the removal of a national shortage for the cancer drug cisplatin. The agency has also partnered with the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation to develop breath-based diagnostic devices for infectious disease detection. Additionally, the FDA granted accelerated approval to Epkoritamab-bysp for adult patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma.

title: FDA Permits Marketing of First Point-of-Care Hepatitis C RNA Test
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted marketing authorization to Cepheid for the Xpert HCV test and GeneXpert Xpress System, the first hepatitis C virus test for point-of-care settings. The test can detect HCV RNA in about an hour using a blood sample from the fingertip. This authorization enables a test-and-treat approach, where a person can be tested for HCV, linked to care, and potentially receive treatment during the same healthcare visit. The test is indicated for adults with signs or symptoms of, or at risk for hepatitis C. The proposed fiscal year 2025 budget includes a five-year program to eliminate hepatitis C in the US, aiming to significantly expand testing, treatment, and prevention. Validation data was gathered through the Independent Test Assessment Program (ITAP), a National Institutes of Health (NIH) Rapid Acceleration of Diagnostics (RADx) Tech program. The test is available for use in settings operating under a CLIA Certificate of Waiver, such as substance use disorder treatment facilities, correctional facilities, and doctor's offices.

title: FDA Roundup: June 25, 2024
body_summary: The US FDA issued a Small Entity Compliance Guideto assist small entities with FDA regulations on in vitro diagnostic (IVD) products. The LDT Final Rule was published on May 6, 2024, and includes a phase-out of general enforcement discretion for LDTs over four years. The FDA also issued a report on the New Drugs Regulatory Program Modernization, which provides a look at strategic objectives and impact progress. Additionally, the FDA converted Sirturo to traditional approval, granted accelerated approval to Krazati, and approved Vyvgart Hytrulo for CIDP treatment.

title: FDA Roundup: June 21, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration published final guidance on Circumstances that Constitute Delaying, Denying, Limiting, or Refusing a Drug or Device Inspection. The guidance defines the types of behaviors that FDA considers to constitute delaying, denying, or limiting inspection. The FDA also issued final Guidance for Industry #278, Human User Safety in New and Abbreviated New Animal Drug Applications, to clarify the current approaches and the FDA’s recommendations for Human User Safety assessment. On Thursday, the FDA approved an application for Trimeprazine with Prednisolone Tablets, the first generic of the animal drug Temaril-P. The FDA announced a recall related to unauthorized plastic syringes, initiated by Cardinal Health. A new web page and virtual public meeting were also announced for the Home as a Health Care Hub initiative, with a virtual meeting scheduled for July 25, 2024. The FDA updated the advisory for the investigation of illnesses linked to Diamond Shruumz-brand Chocolate Bars, Cones, & Gummies, with 26 reported illnesses as of June 17, 2024.

title: FDA Authorizes Marketing of Four Menthol-Flavored E-Cigarette Products After Extensive Scientific Review
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of four e-cigarette products through the premarket tobacco product application (PMTA) pathway. The FDA granted marketing orders to NJOY LLC for four menthol-flavored e-cigarette products: NJOY ACE Pod Menthol 2.4%, NJOY ACE Pod Menthol 5%, NJOY DAILY Menthol 4.5%, and NJOY DAILY EXTRA Menthol 6%. The authorizations mark the first non-tobacco flavored e-cigarette products to be authorized by the FDA. The authorizations are specific to these four products only and do not apply to any other menthol-flavored e-cigarette products. The FDA evaluated the applications based on a public health standard that considers the risks and benefits of the product to the population as a whole. The agency determined that there was sufficient evidence to demonstrate that permitting marketing of the products would be appropriate for the protection of the public health.

title: FDA Expands Approval of Gene Therapy for Patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has expanded the approval of Elevidys, a gene therapy, to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in ambulatory and non-ambulatory individuals aged 4 years and older, with a confirmed mutation in the DMD gene. A randomized clinical trial for Elevidys has raised concerns about safety, with reported side effects including vomiting, nausea, liver injury, fever, and low platelet count. The FDA approved Elevidys for Sarepta Therapeutics Inc. and requires monitoring for potential heart problems and muscle inflammation.

title: FDA Roundup: June 18, 2024
body_summary:
The FDA announced a request for input on patient safety associated with certain medical software functions excluded from the medical device definition. This input will help develop the 2024 report on the risks and benefits to health of non-device software functions. Comments must be submitted by July 18, 2024, under docket number FDA-2018-N-1910 at www.regulations.gov. 

The FDA issued a warning letter to Dollar Tree Inc. due to the company's failure to adequately remove recalled WanaBana apple cinnamon fruit puree pouches from store shelves. The company must respond within 15 days with specific steps to address any violations. 

The FDA approved the vaccine Capvaxive for the prevention of invasive disease caused by 22 different serotypes of Streptococcus pneumoniae and pneumonia caused by 21 different serotypes of Streptococcus pneumoniae for individuals 18 years of age and older. 

The FDA announced the first of a series of five public meetings to provide educational sessions for stakeholders interested in the new animal drug approval process. The first meeting will be held on July 17, 2024, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. ET. 

The FDA published a new blog on the promise of artificial intelligence for improving healthcare. 

The American Society of Addiction Medicine issued a draft clinical practice guideline on benzodiazepine tapering, available for public comment. 

The FDA approved pembrolizumab (Keytruda, Merck) with carboplatin and paclitaxel, followed by single-agent pembrolizumab, for adult patients with primary advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma. 

The FDA issued a proposed administrative order to amend over-the-counter monograph M013: Internal Analgesic, Antipyretic, and Antirheumatic Drug Products for Over-the-Counter Human Use. 

The FDA published a summary of patient listening sessions held in March 2024 on Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). 

The FDA approved durvalumab (Imfinzi, AstraZeneca UK Limited) with carboplatin plus paclitaxel f

title: Statement on the 12th Anniversary of the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) Program
body_summary: President Obama and I announced the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) program 12 years ago, allowing over 800,000 "Dreamers" to live and work lawfully. I am proud of Dreamers' contributions and committed to providing support for their success. I directed the Department of Homeland Security to preserve and fortify DACA and will continue to defend it in court. The Department of Health and Human Services expanded access to affordable health coverage for DACA recipients through the Affordable Care Act. I sent a comprehensive immigration reform plan to Congress on day one of my administration to protect Dreamers and their families. Only Congress can provide permanent and lasting stability for them.

title: FDA Roundup: June 14, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued a proposed exemption for certain cottage cheese products from the Food Traceability Rule, exempting Grade “A” cottage cheese on the Interstate Milk Shippers List from requirements. The FDA also announced a recall initiated by Merit Medical Systems, Inc. due to unauthorized plastic syringes. The agency issued warning letters to six online retailers for selling unauthorized e-liquid products, including those from the Bad Drip brand. The FDA granted accelerated approval to repotrectinib (AUGTYRO) for adult and pediatric patients with solid tumors having a neurotrophic tyrosine receptor kinase gene fusion. The FDA posted a CDER Conversation with Robert Ball, discussing the Emerging Drug Safety Technology Meeting program and the application of artificial intelligence in pharmacovigilance. The agency updated its advice to manufacturers of COVID-19 vaccines (2024-2025 Formula) to use the KP.2 strain, if feasible, to ensure the vaccines more closely match circulating SARS-CoV-2 strains. The FDA announced the Transparency for Machine Learning-Enabled Medical Devices: Guiding Principles, published jointly with Health Canada and the UK's Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency. The FDA granted traditional approval to selpercatinib (Retevmo) for adult and pediatric patients with advanced or metastatic RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer. The FDA posted warning letters to four companies marketing the unapproved animal drug toltrazuril. The agency approved phenylpropanolamine hydrochloride chewable tablets for the control of urinary incontinence in dogs.

title: Joint Statement by Group of Seven (G-7) Nation Leaders—G7 Apulia Leaders' Communiqué
