body_summary: Leaders of the Group of Seven (G7) gathered in Apulia to reaffirm their commitment to global challenges, democratic principles, and free societies, agreeing to provide approximately USD 50 billion to support Ukraine's fight for freedom and reconstruction. The US condemned Russia's "blatant breach of international law" and its nuclear rhetoric, supporting Ukraine's right of self-defense. The EU welcomed Israel's proposal acceptance and urged rapid humanitarian relief for civilians in Gaza, while criticizing Iran's nuclear program escalation. The G7 reaffirmed its commitment to promoting sustainable development, food security, and resilient infrastructure in Africa, addressing global challenges such as terrorism, climate change, and poverty. They also committed to cutting methane emissions from fossil fuels by 2030 and reducing global methane emissions by 75% by 2035, as well as strengthening international climate finance and halting biodiversity loss by 2030. The G7 will coordinate with other stakeholders to advance AI governance, promote job quality, and address migration as a global phenomenon.

title: Proclamation 10776—World Elder Abuse Awareness Day, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States of America issues a proclamation to recommit to standing with elder abuse survivors and creating a world in which no older person has to live in fear of violence, abuse, or neglect. The proclamation was issued on World Elder Abuse Awareness Day. The President's Administration has dedicated over $430 million to Adult Protective Services and proposes a $30 million investment to sustain and strengthen these resources. The Administration is also working to protect older Americans' savings from scams, ensuring access to quality care, and supporting caregivers. Globally, the Administration is working to combat elder abuse through partnerships with nations abroad, training foreign counterparts in best practices, and implementing strategies to prevent and respond to gender-based violence.

title: Proclamation 10777—Father's Day, 2024
body_summary: By the President of the United States of America A Proclamation Every Father's Day, we pay tribute to the fathers and father figures in our lives who shower us with unconditional love and support. On June 16, 2024, the President of the United States, Joseph R. Biden Jr., hereby proclaims this day as Father's Day, in accordance with a joint resolution of the Congress approved April 24, 1972. The President recalls his own father, Joseph Robinette Biden Sr., and the values he taught him, including the importance of dignity and respect. The President's Administration is creating jobs, rebuilding American infrastructure, and lowering healthcare costs to support families. The President also recognizes the sacrifices of fathers who have lost loved ones and recommit to safeguarding their legacies.

title: Statement on the United States Supreme Court Decision in Food and Drug Administration v. Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine
body_summary: The fight for reproductive freedom continues despite today's decision. The Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade 2 years ago, but medication abortion, approved by the FDA over 20 years ago, remains available. Republican elected officials' extreme agenda to ban abortion nationwide is being implemented, with extreme abortion bans in 21 States, including zero exceptions for rape or incest. Women are facing barriers to care, with doctors and nurses threatened with jail time for providing necessary healthcare. Vice President Harris and the author stand with the vast majority of Americans who support a woman's right to make personal health care decisions, committing to continue the fight for reproductive freedom.

title: Biden-Harris Administration Announces National Strategy to Reduce Food Loss and Waste and Recycle Organics
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) have announced a "National Strategy for Reducing Food Loss and Waste and Recycling Organics" as part of President Biden's whole-of-government approach to address climate change and promote a circular economy. The strategy aims to reduce food loss and waste by 50% by 2030. Key objectives include preventing food loss, preventing food waste, increasing organic waste recycling, and supporting policies that incentivize food loss and waste prevention. The strategy highlights actions such as adminstering a mandatory pre-market review program, updating food packaging, and promoting food donation practices. Resources have been made available to guide stakeholders in meeting the National Strategy's goals.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace. Job gains have remained strong, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation has eased over the past year but remains elevated. In recent months, there has been modest further progress toward the Committee's 2 percent inflation objective. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals have moved toward better balance over the past year. The economic outlook is uncertain, and the Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks. In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent. In considering any adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. The Committee does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgageâbacked securities. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Michael S. Barr; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Mary C. Daly; Philip N. Jefferson; Adriana D. Kugler; Loretta J. Mester; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: Implementation Note issued June 12, 2024
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on June 12, 2024: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 5.4 percent, effective June 13, 2024. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective June 13, 2024, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 5.5 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 5.3 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $25 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month into Treasury securities to roughly match the maturity composition of Treasury securities outstanding. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 5.5 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: FDA Roundup: June 11, 2024
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued an advisory warning consumers and retailers not to eat, sell, or serve Diamond Shruumz-Brand Chocolate Bars, Cones, and Gummies due to a series of illnesses associated with eating these products. As of June 10, 2024, 12 illnesses have been reported from eight states, with 10 people hospitalized. The FDA is investigating the cause of these illnesses and considering next steps.

The FDA also updated its Artificial Intelligence Program, launched the Emerging Drug Safety Technology Program, and created a federal multi-agency task force to combat the illegal distribution and sale of e-cigarettes.

Additionally, the FDA approved Iqirvo (elafibranor) oral tablets for the treatment of primary biliary cholangitis, and Arexvy, a Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine, Adjuvanted, for the prevention of lower respiratory tract disease caused by respiratory syncytial virus.

title: Justice Department and FDA Announce Federal Multi-Agency Task Force to Curb the Distribution and Sale of Illegal E-Cigarettes
body_summary: The US Department of Justice and the US Food and Drug Administration have created a federal multi-agency task force to combat the illegal distribution and sale of e-cigarettes. The task force, which includes multiple law enforcement partners, will coordinate and streamline efforts to bring criminal and civil tools to bear against the sale and distribution of e-cigarettes. Acting Associate Attorney General Benjamin C. Mizer stated that unauthorized e-cigarettes pose a significant health risk to Americans, particularly children and adolescents. The task force will focus on investigating and prosecuting cases under the PACT Act, the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, and other authorities. The Justice Department has authorized the sale of 23 specific tobacco-flavored e-cigarette products and devices, and has issued over 1,100 warning letters to manufacturers and retailers for illegally selling and/or distributing unauthorized products.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Report on the Employment Situation in May
body_summary: The great American comeback continues, with 15.6 million more Americans having the dignity and respect that comes with a job. Unemployment has been at or below 4 percent for 30 months, the longest stretch in 50 years. The president will continue to fight for lower costs for families, including lowering grocery prices, making rent more affordable by building 2 million new homes, and lowering the cost of health care and prescription drugs. In contrast, the Republican plan would repeal the Affordable Care Act, raise utility bills, and increase inflation by slashing taxes for billionaires.

title: FDA Roundup: June 7, 2024
body_summary: The FDA has advised vaccine manufacturers to produce monovalent (single-strain) JN.1 vaccines to match circulating SARS-CoV-2 viruses. The FDA has updated the Manufacturer and User Facility Device Experience (MAUDE) database to provide additional information to the public, with updated search results displaying supplement report dates. The FDA has approved imetelstat for adults with certain blood disorders. The FDA has rescinded marketing denial orders for JUUL Labs, Inc., pending review of their premarket tobacco product applications. The FDA has issued safety alerts and guidance documents on various topics, including bioresearch monitoring and tobacco products. The FDA has also announced the closing date of a public comment period for Swedish Match U.S.A., Inc.'s modified risk tobacco product renewal application.

title: FDA Roundup: June 4, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has published an interview with European Medicines Agency's Emer Cooke, part of its blog series "From a Global Perspective." This follows FDA Commissioner Robert Califf's trip to the European Medicines Agency in February and April's FDA-EU Bilateral in Washington. The FDA has also initiated additional recalls of plastic syringes made in China by Medline Industries LP, including bulk unauthorized syringes and those with performance testing failures. The FDA will continue to evaluate problems with syringes made in China and inform the public as new information becomes available. Additionally, the FDA has published "10 things to know about CDER's pharmaceutical quality functions" and issued a safety alert warning parents and caregivers about Cronobacter contamination in Crecelac Infant Powdered Goat Milk Infant Formula, which was initially recalled on May 24, 2024, due to non-compliance with FDA regulations.

title: Proclamation 10770—National Ocean Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States issues a proclamation declaring June 2024 as National Ocean Month. The proclamation celebrates the ocean's wonder and power, highlighting its importance to millions of jobs, food supply chains, and recreation. The ocean faces unprecedented threats, including record-breaking temperatures, pollution, and ocean acidification, which threaten marine life and ecosystems. The President's Administration is taking aggressive action to address the climate crisis, launching the Nation's first Ocean Climate Action Plan and protecting and restoring key coastal habitats. The plan aims to protect communities, reduce natural disasters, and protect biodiversity. The President also announces historic investments in offshore wind projects, infrastructure modernization, and sustainable fisheries, and takes executive action to designate over 700,000 square miles of the Pacific Ocean as a National Marine Sanctuary.

title: FDA Roundup: May 31, 2024
body_summary: The US FDA approved three new drugs: mRESVIA for individuals 60+ years to prevent lower respiratory tract disease caused by RSV, Breyanzi for adult patients with relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma, and Retevmo for pediatric patients under 12 with RET alterations. Retevmo was also approved for advanced or metastatic medullary thyroid cancer, solid tumors with a RET gene fusion, and certain cases of thyroid cancer. Common adverse reactions include musculoskeletal pain, diarrhea, and nausea. The FDA also approved the first generics of Entresto, a medication to treat heart failure, and announced a co-sponsored public webcast workshop on using patient-generated health data in medical device development.

title: Proclamation 10769—National Homeownership Month, 2024
body_summary:
The President of the United States has issued a proclamation declaring June 2024 as National Homeownership Month. The President reiterates the importance of homeownership as a pathway to the middle class and a means to build community and pass down wealth. The Administration has made significant efforts to promote homeownership, including:

- Lowering mortgage costs for approximately 850,000 homeowners
- Providing financial assistance for homeowners to repair and upgrade their homes
- Lowering utility costs through the Inflation Reduction Act
- Offering tax credits and financial assistance to new and first-generation homebuyers
- Increasing the supply of affordable housing through the creation of the Neighborhood Homes Tax Credit
- Cutting red tape to facilitate Federal financing for new construction projects

The President calls upon Americans to ensure that everyone has access to an affordable home in a community of their choice, safeguarding the American Dream.

title: Proclamation 10772—Immigrant Heritage Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States of America A Proclamation announces that June 2024 will be National Immigrant Heritage Month. The proclamation honors the contributions and celebrates the remarkable courage of the Nation's immigrants, who have helped found the country and continue to push it forward today. The President mentions that immigrants come from various backgrounds, including those who came freely, chained by force, fleeing persecution, or chasing dreams, and that they contribute significantly to the economy, healthcare, and education systems. The President also mentions that the Administration has worked to strengthen the legal immigration system and support those who are here, including rebuilding the Refugee Admissions Program and defending the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) policy. The proclamation urges Americans to learn about the history of immigrant communities and observe the month with programs and activities that promote diversity, equity, and inclusion.

title: FDA, USDA, EPA enhance efforts to reduce food loss and waste, welcome USAID to interagency collaborative
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has signed a formal agreement with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to renew their Federal Interagency Collaboration to Reduce Food Loss and Waste (FIFLAW). The U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) has also joined the collaboration. The agreement was signed by Secretary of Agriculture Tom Vilsack, EPA Administrator Michael S. Regan, FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf, and USAID Administrator Samantha Power. The goal of the collaboration is to achieve a 50% reduction of food loss and waste by 2030. The FDA Commissioner stated that consumers can play a role in helping to reach the national goal by using the FDA's resources. The collaboration will continue to produce educational materials, conduct outreach, research, and community investments, and work with external partners to drive national and global change. The agreement builds on the current work of the Federal Interagency Collaboration, which was first formed in 2018 and has published a draft National Strategy to Reduce Food Loss and Waste. The strategy aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, save households and businesses money, and build cleaner communities.

title: FDA’s Reorganization Approved for Establishing Unified Human Foods Program, New Model for Field Operations and Other Modernization Efforts
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved its reorganization, creating a unified Human Foods Program (HFP), adopting a new model for field operations, and implementing other modernization efforts. The reorganization is set to be implemented on October 1, 2024, aiming to enhance the agency's ability to oversee and protect the human food supply. The creation of a unified HFP will enable the FDA to be more efficient, nimble, and prepared for the ever-changing industries it regulates. Commissioner Robert M. Califf stated that this reorganization is a "distinctive moment" for the FDA, and it will allow the agency to better meet its public health mandate. The reorganization will also position the FDA to regulate innovative food and agricultural products more effectively and strengthen local, state, and international partnerships.

title: FDA Roundup: May 28, 2024
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is providing an update on recent news. The FDA has opened a new period for applications for grants to support the development of new animal drugs for treating uncommon diseases in major and minor species. The maximum individual award amount is $250,000 per year, with a total of $500,000 for routine studies and $750,000 for toxicology studies. Eligible applicants are animal drug sponsors with Designated MUMS animal drugs or their research partners.

The FDA has also posted a new video in the "FDA In Your Day" series, featuring Principal Deputy Commissioner Dr. Namandjé Bumpus discussing clinical trials, a webinar on The Real Cost campaign, and sun safety tips.

Additionally, the FDA has provided clearance for a labeling modification for Intuitive Surgical's da Vinci Xi and X Surgical Systems, which includes real-world evidence used to support the use of the device in radical prostatectomy. The evidence was collected and analyzed by the National Evaluation System for health Technology (NEST) and its partners.

title: FDA Approves First Interchangeable Biosimilar for Two Rare Diseases
body_summary: The US FDA approved Bkemv (eculizumab-aeeb) as the first interchangeable biosimilar to Soliris (eculizumab) for treating rare diseases such as paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH) and atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS). Bkemv is approved for patients with PNH to reduce hemolysis and aHUS to inhibit complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy. The FDA has approved 13 interchangeable biosimilars, including Bkemv, which is available only through a restricted program to ensure safe use.

title: FDA Roundup: May 24, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced news on several fronts. Medline Industries, LP, and Jiangsu Shenli Medical Production Co. Ltd, both initiated recalls to stop using unauthorized plastic syringes made in China. The FDA recommends continuing its efforts to evaluate problems with syringes made in China and inform the public of new information. The agency published a new campaign by Dr. Robert M. Califf, Commissioner of Food and Drugs, called "Prescribe with Confidence" to raise awareness about opioid use disorder. The FDA cleared a mobile app, CamAPS FX, for use in people with type 1 diabetes. The agency also issued a supplemental approval for Safe-Guard (fenbendazole) for treating gastrointestinal worms in wild quail. Additionally, the FDA made new user-friendly updates to the Searchable Tobacco Products Database.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on April 30-May 1, 2024, discussing financial markets and open market operations. Domestic data pointed to persistent inflation and a resilient economy, shifting policy expectations towards fewer rate cuts by year-end. Treasury yields rose, equity prices fell, and the dollar strengthened, tightening financial conditions. The committee maintained the target federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent and slowed the pace of decline of securities holdings.

title: FDA Roundup: May 21, 2024
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced several initiatives. Registration is open for the "FDA's Fifth Online Controlled Substances Summit," a two-day virtual public meeting to identify innovative solutions to reduce the illegal availability of controlled substances online. The summit will be held in partnership with the Reagan-Udall Foundation for the FDA.

The FDA has extended the comment period for the proposed rule "Labeling Requirements for Approved or Conditionally Approved New Animal Drugs" by 60 days, until August 9, 2024. The agency has also approved two interchangeable biosimilars to Eylea.

The FDA has published an article, "FDA Promotes Clinical Trial Innovation," highlighting the progress made in advancing clinical trial innovation. A public workshop, "Evaluating Immunosuppressive Effects of In Utero Exposure to Drug and Biologic Products," has been announced for July 11 and 12.

The FDA Oncology Center of Excellence has formed the OCE Equity Program, expanding efforts to improve access to clinical trials for underrepresented populations. The FDA has also launched the precisionFDA Phase 1 of the Digitally-Derived Endpoints for Freezing-of-Gait Detection Challenge, inviting participants to submit AI models by August 2, 2024.

title: FDA Roundup: May 17, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has granted accelerated approval to several new drugs and medical devices. Tarlatamab-dlle (Imdelltra, Amgen, Inc.) was approved for extensive stage small cell lung cancer with disease progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy. Lisocabtagene maraleucel (Breyanzi, Juno Therapeutics, Inc.) was approved for adults with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma. The FDA has also qualified a patient-reported outcome instrument for ocular symptoms after receiving bilateral intraocular lens implants. Additionally, the FDA has issued an import alert for two Chinese manufacturers of plastic syringes and updated recommendations to prevent their use. The FDA has also posted a determination that tara flour is not a Generally Recognized As Safe (GRAS) standard and granted accelerated approval for a new drug.

title: Proclamation 10763—National Hepatitis Testing Day, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States has issued a proclamation declaring May 19, 2024, as National Hepatitis Testing Day. The proclamation aims to encourage Americans to get tested for viral hepatitis, particularly hepatitis C, which can be cured or managed with the right treatment. Hepatitis C is spread through contact with infected blood and can lead to serious health complications if left untreated. The President has proposed a comprehensive plan to speed up testing, increase access to life-saving medication, and boost research into a vaccine. The plan includes simplifying testing, expanding access to medication for uninsured individuals, and investing in health centers and training more healthcare professionals. The President also encourages Americans to get vaccinated for hepatitis B and to take steps to protect their own health.

title: Joint Statement by President Biden and Prime Minister Justin P.J. Trudeau of Canada
body_summary: Canada and the United States have renewed their bilateral Canada-U.S. Energy Transformation Task Force (ETTF) for an additional year. In August 2022, President Biden signed the Inflation Reduction Act into law, creating over 170,000 clean energy jobs. Canada has implemented a C$93 billion suite of economic investment tax credits for a clean economy. The ETTF aims to accelerate cooperation on critical clean energy opportunities and supply chains. The inaugural ETTF meeting took place in May 2023. Jointly, Canada and the United States have advanced shared priorities, including deploying clean energy solutions, supporting critical mineral and civil nuclear supply chains, and promoting environmental, social, and governance standards. The ETTF has accelerated several accomplishments, including co-investments targeting the development of strategic critical mineral deposits in Canada. The U.S. Department of Defense has announced US$14.8 million in awards to two Canadian companies, while the Canadian Department of Natural Resources has announced complementary funding. Canada has also issued a 10-year, C$4 billion green bond to support nuclear energy. The United States and Canada will work together to leverage historic investments and strengthen ties between their industries.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index Report for April
body_summary: My top economic priority is fighting inflation and lowering costs. Inflation has fallen over 60% from its peak, but prices are still too high. My agenda includes building 2 million new homes to lower housing costs, taking on Big Pharma to lower prescription drug prices, and calling on grocery chains to lower grocery prices. Congressional Republicans want to increase costs by slashing taxes for the ultrawealthy and big corporations, while protecting special interests and undermining workers and seniors. They plan to slash Social Security and Medicare, which would send inflation skyrocketing. My vision is to take on special interests to lower costs and give the middle class a fair shot.

title: FDA Roundup: May 14, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has launched an improved online Regulatory Science Tool (RST) Catalog to enhance search and browse capability. The catalog is now organized by research program and device type and provides peer-reviewed resources for medical device companies and innovators. The FDA has also announced a virtualMedical Device Sterilization Town Hall on May 23, 2024, to discuss sterilization method selection. Additionally, the FDA has issued a safety communication warning patients not to use Cue Health's COVID-19 Tests due to increased risk of false results. The agency has added 191 AI/ML-enabled devices to its list of authorized medical devices, bringing the total to 882. The FDA has also posted a new video featuring Principal Deputy Commissioner Dr. Namandjé Bumpus discussing various topics, including biosimilars and high blood pressure education month.

title: Proclamation 10756—Women's Health Week, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States announces National Women's Health Week, to be observed from May 12 to May 18, 2024. The President commits to investing in women's health, closing the research gap, and providing access to affordable, quality healthcare. The White House Initiative on Women's Health Research was launched last year, with an initial investment of $200 million. The President calls on Congress to deliver an additional $12 billion to accelerate research on women's health conditions. The Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health invests $100 million in its "Sprint for Women's Health" to accelerate discoveries. The Administration boosts funding for breast and cervical cancer early detection, heart disease research, and enacts a national strategy to promote healthier food and exercise. The President also reinforces the Affordable Care Act, cracking down on junk insurance and securing Medicare's ability to negotiate lower prescription drug prices.

title: FDA Roundup: May 10, 2024
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is providing an update on recent news from around the agency. 

The FDA has announced a webinar on June 27, 2024, to provide guidance on Remanufacturing of Medical Devices, which clarifies regulatory requirements for remanufacturing and servicing activities. 

The agency has also initiated a recall of unauthorized plastic syringes made in China and has advised consumers to use broad-spectrum sunscreens with an SPF of at least 15 to protect themselves from skin cancer and early skin aging. 

Additionally, the FDA's Center for Tobacco Products has announced a webinar on June 11, 2024, to commemorate the 10th anniversary of the "The Real Cost" youth tobacco prevention campaign. 

The agency has also issued a warning about Getinge/Maquet/Datascope Cardiosave Hybrid and Rescue Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump (IABP) devices and recommends that healthcare providers and facilities transition away from these devices. 

Registration has opened for a public workshop on June 27, 2024, to explore the use of ketamine for emerging areas of therapeutic interest. 

The FDA has also taken a risk-based decision regarding the approval of PrecisePRP Equine, a product for intra-articular use in horses. 

The FDA will also be discussing the renewal of a risk modification order for loose snus and portioned snus products at a meeting of the Tobacco Products Scientific Advisory Committee on June 26, 2024.

title: Proclamation 10757—Mother's Day, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States issues a proclamation declaring May 12, 2024, as Mother's Day. He expresses gratitude to mothers and mother-figures for their unwavering love and dedication to their children. The President shares personal stories about his mother, Catherine Eugenia "Jean" Finnegan, and his wife, First Lady Jill Biden, highlighting their selfless sacrifices and leadership. The proclamation acknowledges the crucial role mothers play in driving innovation, strengthening the economy, and making history. It also recognizes the Administration's efforts to support working mothers, including expanding child care and ensuring job security for pregnant and nursing mothers.

title: Proclamation 10754—National Defense Transportation Day and National Transportation Week, 2024
body_summary:
By the President of the United States, a proclamation:

The President recommitting to an infrastructure decade, the stronger and safer the Nation is, has signed the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law—a once-in-a-generation investment in American infrastructure. Over 51,000 new projects are transforming communities, including modernizing rail infrastructure and ports, fixing roads and bridges, and bringing public transportation to more communities. The investments will make the Nation safer, facilitate quicker responses from emergency responders, and ensure commerce flows more freely.

title: FDA Issues Final Guidance to Clarify “Remanufacturing” of Devices that Need Maintenance or Repair
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued final guidance to provide clarity on the definition of "remanufacturing" for reusable medical devices. The guidance aims to ensure consistency in defining remanufacturing activities and promote a better understanding of applicable federal law and regulations. The FDA director, Jeff Shuren, stated that the guidance provides important clarity on defining remanufacturing and helps remove perceived barriers to obtaining repair or maintenance of a device.

Remanufacturing involves processing, conditioning, or renovating a finished device that significantly changes its performance, safety specifications, or intended use. Servicing, on the other hand, is the repair and/or preventive maintenance of parts in a finished device to return it to the safety and performance specifications established by the original equipment manufacturer.

The FDA has determined that remanufacturing is when a significant alteration is made to a device's performance, safety specifications, or intended use, changing the device from what was legally marketed as approved, cleared, or authorized by the FDA. The guidance sets forth guiding principles, a flowchart to help determine whether activities may be remanufacturing, and examples that may be helpful to industry.

The FDA recommends including instructions for preventive maintenance and repair in the labeling of reusable medical devices and provides examples of activities that constitute remanufacturing. The agency recognizes the importance of stakeholders' perspectives regarding proper servicing and the availability of timely, cost-effective, quality maintenance and repair of medical devices.

title: EPA, FDA, and USDA Issue Joint Regulatory Plan for Biotechnology
body_summary: The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Food and Drug Administration (FDA), and Department of Agriculture (USDA) have developed a plan to update, streamline, and clarify their regulations and oversight mechanisms for biotechnology products. This plan aims to improve transparency, predictability, coordination, and efficiency in the regulation of biotechnology products. The plan focuses on five major areas: modified plants, modified animals, modified microorganisms, human drugs, biologics, and medical devices. The agencies will implement joint efforts to clarify and streamline regulatory oversight for genetically engineered (GE) products, update information sharing through a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU), and explore the feasibility of a web-based tool to inform developers about regulatory agency oversight. The plan builds on the 1986 Coordinated Framework for the Regulation of Biotechnology, which describes the comprehensive federal regulatory policy for ensuring the safety of biotechnology products.

title: FDA Roundup: May 7, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is announcing several upcoming meetings and announcements. The Psychopharmacologic Drugs Advisory Committee will meet on June 4 to discuss a new drug application for midomafetamine capsules for the treatment of post-traumatic stress disorder. The Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee will meet on June 10 to discuss a biologics license application for donanemab for the treatment of early symptomatic Alzheimer’s disease. The Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee meeting on May 16, 2024, has been rescheduled to June 5, 2024, to allow for additional time to obtain surveillance data. The FDA is also seeking public comments on a proposed glossary of clinical research terminology, with a 45-day public comment period.

title: Statement on the Social Security and Medicare Trustees Reports
body_summary: The President is committed to strengthening Medicare and Social Security. As long as they are President, they will protect these programs from Republicans' attempts to cut benefits. Since taking office, their economic plan has extended Medicare solvency by 5 years. The President's plan would extend Medicare solvency permanently by asking the wealthy to pay more and lowering prescription drug costs. They also plan to extend Social Security solvency by asking the highest income Americans to pay more without cutting benefits. Republicans in Congress propose $1.5 trillion in cuts to Social Security, increasing the retirement age, raising prescription drug costs, and transitioning Medicare to a premium-raising system. The President will fight to prevent these changes, particularly for America's seniors.

title: Statement on the Department of Health and Human Services Final Rule To Expand Health Insurance Coverage for Recipients of the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) Program
body_summary: The administration is expanding affordable, quality health care coverage to Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) recipients. The program, announced nearly 12 years ago, has provided over 800,000 Dreamers with the ability to work lawfully and contribute to their communities. The President has directed the Department of Homeland Security to preserve and fortify DACA, and is now taking steps to ensure DACA recipients have access to health care through the Affordable Care Act. The President has previously sent a comprehensive immigration reform plan to Congress to protect Dreamers and their families, and is urging Congress to take action to provide permanent status and a pathway to citizenship.

title: FDA Roundup: May 3, 2024
body_summary: The US FDA announced various news items. The agency is accepting public comments on draft guidance for veterinary drug products. A public meeting on evaluating the negative symptoms of schizophrenia in clinical trials will be held on August 16, 2024. The FDA revised pre-harvest agricultural water provisions for covered produce in the Produce Safety Rule. The agency announced the 2024 Regulatory Education for Industry Annual Conference on May 29-30, 2024. The Office of Translational Sciences published its 2023 annual report, highlighting achievements in drug development and regulatory review. The FDA issued warning letters to 14 online retailers for selling unauthorized e-cigarette products. A new tool to assess atrial fibrillation burden estimates was qualified under the Medical Device Development Tools program. The FDA released updated guidance documents on intentional genomic alterations in animals. A memorandum of understanding was established with the US Department of Agriculture to clarify roles and responsibilities for regulation of IGAs in animals. The Center for Drug Evaluation and Research published its 2023 Office of New Drugs Annual Report. An outbreak advisory was issued for a multistate outbreak of E. coli O157:H7 infections linked to organic walnuts. The FDA released the latest episode of the Health Equity Forum Podcast on Asian American, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander Heritage Month.

title: FDA Clarifies Approach to Genomic Alterations in Animals
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken steps to modernize its regulatory process for intentional genomic alterations (IGAs) in animals. The FDA has updated guidance documents to increase regulatory flexibility, predictability, and efficiency. The agency has also established a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) to clarify roles and responsibilities for regulating IGAs in animals. Tracey Forfa, director of the FDA's Center for Veterinary Medicine, stated that the agency aims to facilitate innovation while ensuring product safety. The FDA has released two guidance documents: GFI #187A, which outlines the agency's risk-based approach to regulating IGAs, and draft GFI #187B, which describes the approval process for these products. The FDA is requesting public comment on draft GFI #187B, which is due by July 31, 2024.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace. Job gains have remained strong, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation has eased over the past year but remains elevated. In recent months, there has been a lack of further progress toward the Committee's 2 percent inflation objective. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals have moved toward better balance over the past year. The economic outlook is uncertain, and the Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks. In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent. In considering any adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. The Committee does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgageâbacked securities. Beginning in June, the Committee will slow the pace of decline of its securities holdings by reducing the monthly redemption cap on Treasury securities from $60 billion to $25 billion. The Committee will maintain the monthly redemption cap on agency debt and agency mortgageâbacked securities at $35 billion and will reinvest any principal payments in excess of this cap into Treasury securities. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Michael S. Barr; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Mary C. Daly; Philip N. Jefferson; Adriana D. Kugler; Loretta J. Mester; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: Implementation Note issued May 1, 2024
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on May 1, 2024: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 5.4 percent, effective May 2, 2024. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective May 2, 2024, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 5.5 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 5.3 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in May that exceeds a cap of $60 billion per month. Beginning on June 1, roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $25 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to these monthly caps and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly caps. Reinvest into agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in May that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month. Beginning on June 1, reinvest the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month into Treasury securities to roughly match the maturity composition of Treasury securities outstanding. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 5.5 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: FDA Roundup: April 30, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced that the US Marshals Service seized unauthorized e-cigarette products valued at over $700,000 in a warehouse in Alhambra, CA. The FDA also authorized the marketing of the Eversense AP CGM System, a fully implantable sensor with an anti-inflammatory drug, for people with diabetes 18 years of age and older. Additionally, the FDA granted traditional approval to tisotumab vedotin-tftv for recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer. The FDA will host a virtual public meeting on June 13, 2024, to discuss the composition of advisory committees. On Friday, the FDA approved the Espirt BTK Everolimus Eluting Resorbable Scaffold System for treating patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia.

title: Proclamation 10739—National Mental Health Awareness Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States recognizes the bravery and resilience of Americans living with mental health conditions and expresses gratitude to dedicated mental health professionals and loved ones. Mental health care is essential to living a full and healthy life, but many Americans face barriers to accessing care. The President has taken steps to expand access to mental health care, including signing the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act, investing $1 billion in schools, and launching the 988 crisis lifeline. The administration is also working to ensure full mental health parity, invest in mental health programs, and address social media's impact on youth mental health. The President calls on citizens and organizations to join in activities to strengthen mental health and urges Americans to reach out to one another to support those struggling with mental health issues.

title: Proclamation 10741—Older Americans Month, 2024
body_summary: President Joe R. Biden Jr. has proclaimed May 2024 as Older Americans Month, celebrating the contributions of older Americans who have worked their whole lives to achieve the American Dream. Sixty years ago, a third of older Americans lived in poverty, but programs like Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid have helped transform lives. The President proposes strengthening Social Security by asking high-income Americans to pay their fair share and extending Medicare Hospital Insurance Trust Fund indefinitely. He also aims to cut junk fees on retirement savings, reduce health insurance and prescription drug costs, and expand Medicare services, including dental, mental health, and nutritional health services. Additionally, the President is making historic investments in home care, hearing aids, and cancer research. The proclamation calls on Americans to celebrate older adults' contributions, support their independence, and recognize their value to the Nation.

title: FDA Takes Action Aimed at Helping to Ensure the Safety and Effectiveness of Laboratory Developed Tests
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken action to ensure the safety and effectiveness of laboratory developed tests (LDTs), which are used in various healthcare decisions. LDTs are in vitro diagnostic products that can play an important role in healthcare, but concerns have been raised about their accuracy and reliability. The FDA has announced a final rule to amend its regulations to make IVDs devices under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, and has issued a policy to phase out its general enforcement discretion approach for LDTs over four years. This phaseout will help assure the safety and effectiveness of LDTs, while avoiding undue disruption to patient care. The FDA will also exercise enforcement discretion with regard to certain requirements, such as premarket review and quality system requirements, for IVDs manufactured by laboratories. This will help promote access to critical tests while ensuring their accuracy and reliability. The FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf, M.D., and Jeff Shuren, M.D., J.D., director of the FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health, have emphasized the importance of this action in ensuring patient safety and confidence in IVDs.

title: FDA to Hold Listening Session as Part of Broader Work to Optimize Use of, and Processes for, Advisory Committees
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) will host a virtual public meeting in June to gather feedback on optimizing advisory committees' role in the agency's decision-making process. The meeting aims to improve the experience for committee members, ensure public awareness and understanding of the role of advisory committees, and incorporate diverse perspectives and experiences. The FDA seeks input on streamlining administrative burdens, improving public understanding, and clarifying misconceptions about advisory committee votes. The listening session will take place on June 13 from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. ET and can be registered for on the FDA's website.

title: Proclamation 10733—National Small Business Week, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States of America is proclaiming April 28 through May 4, 2024, as National Small Business Week. During this week, the President celebrates the grit and strength of every entrepreneur who has chased a dream and put in the hard work to see their business and the Nation thrive. The President's Administration has reformed the Paycheck Protection Program, provided $450 billion in relief to 6 million small businesses, and signed the American Rescue Plan to support 100,000 restaurants and 225,000 child care centers. Three years later, America is experiencing a historic small business boom, with 17 million new business applications, a doubling of Black-owned businesses, and a growing Latino business ownership. The President is relying on America's Main Street entrepreneurs to help rebuild the Nation's infrastructure, expand access to affordable internet, and create good-paying jobs.

title: Proclamation 10734—Workers Memorial Day, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States of America has proclaimed April 28, 2024, as Workers Memorial Day. The proclamation honors workers who lost their lives or were injured on the job and recommit to making sure every worker is safe on the job. The President has been a strong advocate for workers' rights and has taken various actions to improve workplace safety and conditions. These include investing $200 million in keeping workers safe during the pandemic, delivering personal protective equipment, and vaccinating 230 million Americans. The Administration has also finalized rules requiring Project Labor Agreements for large-scale Federal construction projects and signed the Butch Lewis Act to protect pensions. The President has also expanded coverage through the Affordable Care Act, slashed prescription drug prices, and made it easier for whistleblowers to report unsafe working conditions.

title: FDA Roundup: April 26, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the 50th biosimilar, expanding the availability of biosimilar products for treating various chronic and severe illnesses. Biosimilars are now approved for 15 different reference biologics and treat illnesses like rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, and psoriasis. The FDA has also updated its Biosimilars Action Plan to further expand biosimilar product availability and utilization. Additionally, the FDA finalized guidance on the Veterinary Feed Directive Regulation Questions and Answers, provided guidance on the requirements of the veterinary feed regulations, and approved the first generic pimobendan for the management of congestive heart failure in dogs. The FDA issued a warning letter to Cardinal Health for violating quality system regulations related to syringe products. The agency also approved lutetium Lu 177 dotatate for pediatric patients with somatostatin receptor-positive gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, and granted accelerated approval to tovorafenib for patients with relapsed or refractory pediatric low-grade glioma harboring a BRAF fusion or rearrangement.

title: FDA Approves New Treatment for Uncomplicated Urinary Tract Infections
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Pivya tablets for female adults with uncomplicated urinary tract infections (UTIs) caused by susceptible isolates of Escherichia coli, Proteus mirabilis, and Staphylococcus saprophyticus. Pivya is an additional treatment option for uncomplicated UTIs, which are bacterial infections of the bladder in females with no structural abnormalities of their urinary tract. The efficacy of Pivya was assessed in three controlled clinical trials, showing a composite response rate of 62%, 72%, and 66% in the trials comparing Pivya to placebo, another oral antibacterial drug, and ibuprofen, respectively. The most common side effects of Pivya included nausea and diarrhea. Pivya is not recommended for patients with a known history of severe hypersensitivity or primary/secondary carnitine deficiency. The FDA granted Priority Review and Qualified Infectious Disease Product designations for this indication. Pivya was granted approval to UTILITY therapeutics Ltd.

title: FDA Roundup: April 23, 2024
body_summary:
The FDA announced a new initiative, "TheHome as a Health Care Hub," aimed at integrating medical devices, healthcare, and prevention into people's lives. The initiative is part of the FDA's commitment to advancing health equity. 

The FDA published "Reflections on Travel to Europe – Part Three" by Robert M. Califf, M.D., Commissioner of Food and Drugs, describing key events and issues from his trip to the European Union. 

On Monday, the FDA approved no gapendekin alfa in bakicept-pmln (Anktiva) with Bacillus Calmette-Guérin for adult patients with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer. 

The FDA also approved Rezenopy, a 10-milligram naloxone hydrochloride intranasal spray indicated to treat opioid overdose. 

A safety communication was issued to encourage the public to follow established anti-choking protocols. 

An outbreak advisory was updated to include Infinite Herbs, LLC, recall and expanded recall of Salmonella Typhimurium infections linked to fresh organic basil.

title: Proclamation 10732—Earth Day, 2024
body_summary: President Biden announces Earth Day, urging Americans to protect the planet and combat climate and biodiversity crises. He highlights the progress made in building a greener, more sustainable nation, including investments in clean energy, infrastructure, and conservation. The President notes that climate change is the existential crisis of our time, with devastating impacts on communities, ecosystems, and human health. He emphasizes the importance of international cooperation and action, rejoining the Paris Climate Accord and pledging $3 billion to the Green Climate Fund. The President calls on Americans to do their part to protect the planet, grow the economy, and work towards a healthier, safer, more equitable future.

title: FDA Roundup: April 19, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has required labeling changes for genetically modified autologous CAR-T cell immunotherapies to include new safety information on the serious risk of T cell malignancies. The FDA also approved Alecensa for adjuvant treatment following tumor resection in patients with ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer. The agency shared updates on Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) in the food supply and released reports on medical device safety and innovation. The FDA issued an outbreak advisory for a multistate outbreak of Salmonella Typhimurium infections linked to Infinite Herbs-brand organic basil. The agency approved Lumicell Inc.’s Direct Visualization System for detecting cancerous tissue during breast conserving surgery. The FDA also approved Lumisight for adults with breast cancer. A new webpage was launched to educate the public about the relative risks of tobacco products, and a post-incident response webpage was launched about elevated lead levels in cinnamon. Marketing denial orders were issued to Shenzhen Yibo Technology Co. Ltd. for 65 disposable e-cigarettes.

title: FDA Roundup: April 16, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced the unveiling of a new public dataset to help analytical chemistry labs ensure the robustness of chemical characterization methods used to assess the biocompatibility of medical devices. This dataset allows labs to determine their ability to detect a broad range of potential chemicals. The FDA also announced the next Medical Device Sterilization Town Hall, which will be held on April 29, 2024, and features topics and formats discussions. Additionally, the FDA published a blog by Commissioner Robert M. Califf, M.D., on his recent trip to Europe, and launched the CDER Center for Clinical Trial Innovation (C3TI) to promote clinical trial innovation activities.

title: FDA Roundup: April 12, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is reopening the comment period for 60 days for the draft guidance on collecting representative samples for food testing used as evidence for release of certain fish and fishery products. The FDA has also taken several actions to better understand the safety and effectiveness of surgical mesh mini-slings for treating female stress urinary incontinence, and has announced an update on its evaluation of quality and performance issues related to plastic syringes made in China. The FDA has approved Pradalex (pradofloxacin injection) solution for certain respiratory diseases in cattle and swine, and has authorized marketing of the Rho software application, which uses machine learning to pre-screen patients for low bone mineral density. The FDA Office of Minority Health and Health Equity is hosting a virtual panel discussion on April 17th to discuss strategies for increasing clinical trial participation for diverse communities.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary:
Here is a summary of the source document:

The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on March 19-20, 2024, reviewing financial market developments and discussing policy rate cuts, balance sheet runoff, and market indicators. The committee noted stable conditions in US short-term funding markets and revised upwards its economic projection due to higher population growth. They projected inflation to edge down to around 2-1/2 percent by 2024 and maintained the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent, citing solid economic activity and low unemployment.

title: Joint Statement by President Biden and Prime Minister Fumio Kishida of Japan—Global Partners for the Future
body_summary: US President Joe Biden and Japanese Prime Minister Fumio Kishida announced a new era of strategic cooperation, pledging to strengthen their alliance and address global challenges. They co-led the Forum on Defense Industrial Cooperation, Acquisition and Sustainment, identifying priority areas for partnering industries. Plans were announced to deepen cooperation on space exploration, AI, and cybersecurity, as well as strengthen bilateral economic ties. The US and Japan launched a dialogue on clean energy, with Japan's participation in the US Floating Offshore Wind Shot. The two nations reaffirmed their commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific, promoting regional security, countering North Korea's nuclear threats, and supporting international law. They also commit to a world without nuclear weapons, a new $12 million STEM program, and expanding scholarship and exchange programs.

title: Proclamation 10727—Black Maternal Health Week, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States reiterates his commitment to ending the maternal health crisis, which claims the lives of far too many mothers, particularly Black women. Since taking office, Vice President Kamala Harris has been a key leader on maternal health. The Administration has taken several steps to address the crisis, including expanding postpartum coverage for Medicaid recipients, making coverage under the Affordable Care Act more affordable, and releasing a blueprint for addressing maternal health. The Administration has also launched a Maternal Mental Health Hotline, created a "Birthing-Friendly" hospital designation, and partnered with community-based organizations to provide services for pregnant women and new mothers. The President has signed legislation to ensure employers make reasonable accommodations for pregnant and nursing mothers and has committed to addressing long-standing inequities affecting Black communities. He declares April 11-17, 2024, as Black Maternal Health Week, urging Americans to raise awareness of the issue and commit to building a world where Black women can live safely and with dignity.

title: FDA Roundup: April 9, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) authorized the marketing of MMI North America, Inc.'s Symani Surgical System, indicated for use in certain microsurgical procedures on small blood vessels and lymphatic ducts in adults. The system includes a motion scaling function. The FDA also granted accelerated approval to fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki (Enhertu) for adult patients with unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive solid tumors who have received prior systemic treatment and have no satisfactory alternative treatment options.

title: Federal Court Enters Consent Decree Against Philips Respironics Following Recall of Certain Sleep Therapy Machines
body_summary: The US District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania has entered a consent decree against Philips Respironics, its subsidiaries, and individual defendants, including CEO Roy Jakobs. The decree restricts the production and sale of CPAP and BiPAP machines at certain facilities until requirements are met. Philips Respironics must implement a Recall Remediation Plan, which includes providing patients with new or reworked devices, refunds, or replacement parts, and is subject to FDA review. The FDA requires the company to submit a plan to address testing gaps and ensure regulatory compliance. An independent expert will inspect other Sleep and Respiratory Care facilities to identify and correct compliance issues. The FDA continues to prioritize patients affected by the June 2021 recall, encouraging those with unregistered devices to register and ensuring up-to-date contact information.

title: FDA Roundup: April 5, 2024
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued several emergency use authorizations (EUA) and taken actions related to device quality and postmarket surveillance. 

On Wednesday, the FDA issued EUAs for CorDx TyFast Flu A/B & COVID-19 At Home Multiplex Rapid Test and OSANG QuickFinder COVID-19/Flu Antigen Self Test. The FDA also announced the availability of a draft guidance for industry on new dietary ingredient notifications for dietary supplements. 

The FDA issued an import alert for Jiangsu Caina Medical Co. Ltd. for not meeting device quality system requirements. The agency will continue to work on the evaluation of quality and performance issues related to plastic syringes made in China. 

On Tuesday, the FDA granted authorization for Prenosis, Inc.'s Sepsis ImmunoScore, an Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning-Based Software that identifies patients at risk for having or developing sepsis. The device will be subject to specific premarket and postmarket requirements, including software validation and clinical performance testing. 

The FDA also published a CDER Conversation highlighting the system of postmarket surveillance and risk assessment programs to identify and evaluate adverse drug reactions and medication errors.

title: FDA Approves New Antibiotic for Three Different Uses
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Zevtera (ceftobiprole medocaril sodium for injection) for the treatment of adults with Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections, acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections, and community-acquired bacterial pneumonia, including pediatric patients three months to less than 18 years old. Zevtera was evaluated in three randomized, controlled, double-blind trials, demonstrating efficacy in treating Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia, acute bacterial skin and skin structure infections, and community-acquired bacterial pneumonia. The primary measure of efficacy was overall success, with 69.8% of subjects who received Zevtera achieving overall success compared to 68.7% of subjects who received the comparator. Zevtera's efficacy in treating pediatric patients with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia was supported by evidence from the adult trial. The most common side effects of Zevtera included anemia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and increased levels of certain liver tests.

title: FDA Roundup: April 2, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is releasing scientific review policy memoranda on the premarket tobacco review process. This follows the 2022 Reagan-Udall Foundation's evaluation of the Center for Tobacco Products. The FDA also published a Consumer Update, "Is Food Safe if it Has Chemicals?", to help people navigate food chemical safety. On April 17th, the FDA Office of Minority Health and Health Equity will host a panel discussion on increasing clinical trial participation for diverse communities. The FDA has updated stakeholders and veterinarians on the mandatory "Approved by FDA" statement on labeling components for approved animal drugs, and cleared Rejoyn, a prescription digital therapeutic smartphone app for Major Depressive Disorder, and the Abbott Point of Care i-STAT TBI cartridge for evaluating patients with suspected mild traumatic brain injury. The FDA has also issued an import alert for unauthorized plastic syringes made in China and cleared the i-STAT TBI cartridge.

title: Proclamation 10725—World Autism Awareness Day, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States has issued a proclamation establishing April 2, 2024, as World Autism Awareness Day. The proclamation aims to promote equal rights and dignity for individuals with autism, who make significant contributions to American society. The administration is committed to providing resources and tools to support autistic individuals, including early diagnosis, access to healthcare, education, and employment opportunities. The President has also taken steps to increase awareness and understanding of autism, including launching research initiatives and promoting inclusive policies. The proclamation calls on Americans to learn more about autism, support autistic individuals, and build welcoming communities.

title: Proclamation 10717—National Cancer Prevention and Early Detection Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States has issued a proclamation declaring April 2024 as National Cancer Prevention and Early Detection Month. The goal is to cut the cancer death rate by at least 50 percent in the next 25 years through prevention and early detection methods. The Administration has re-ignited the Cancer Moonshot, a goal that was established during the previous administration. The President has also established the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health to secure $4 billion in bipartisan funding to improve the prevention, detection, and treatment of cancers. The Administration is working to increase access to cancer screenings, expand health coverage, and provide resources to help Americans get and stay healthy. Additionally, the President has signed the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law to clean up toxic sites and reduce Americans' exposure to environmental toxins that can lead to cancer.

title: Proclamation 10715—Care Workers Recognition Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States has proclaimed April 2024 as Care Workers Recognition Month. The Administration is committed to getting care workers the resources and respect they deserve. In 2021, over $60 billion was invested in the care economy, helping keep child care centers open during the COVID-19 pandemic. My Budget includes proposals in care infrastructure, including investments in caregiving for military families and child care to increase accessibility and affordability. An Executive Order signed last year includes actions to increase access to high-quality care and support for caregivers. The Department of Health and Human Services has released a proposed rule to raise Head Start teacher wages by over $10,000 on average. The President also directed the Department of Veterans Affairs to give veterans more flexibility to pick their own caregivers.

title: Proclamation 10722—National Public Health Week, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States declares April 1-7, 2024, as National Public Health Week to celebrate the life-saving care of public health professionals. The President recognizes their courage and dedication in promoting the country's health, safety, and well-being. The President has made significant investments in public health, including expanding health care coverage, reducing prescription drug costs, and funding scientific research. The President also launched initiatives to combat the maternal health crisis, improve mental health, and address substance use disorder. Additionally, the President has made investments to combat climate change, including replacing lead pipes and promoting clean energy. The President calls on citizens, government agencies, and private businesses to take action to improve the health of the Nation.

title: Proclamation 10719—National Donate Life Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States, Joseph R. Biden Jr., proclaims April 2024 as National Donate Life Month. The President highlights the importance of organ donors, who have saved countless lives through their generosity and courage. The current waiting list for organs has over 100,000 people, including nearly 2,000 children, with 17 Americans dying each day while waiting for a transplant. The Administration is working to improve the organ donation process, including implementing a bipartisan law to increase competition in the contracts process and establishing an independent board of directors. The law also aims to bring more transparency to the system and spearhead needed reforms. Additionally, the President has taken action to extend Medicare coverage of vital drugs for kidney transplant patients and ensure high-quality care for transplants.

title: FDA Roundup: March 29, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has made several updates and announcements. On Thursday, the FDA updated the Mammography Quality Standards Act and Program section on its website, enhancing user experience and providing current information. The FDA also launched the Searchable Tobacco Products Database, a new list of tobacco products including e-cigarettes, designed to serve the public and retailers. Additionally, on Wednesday, the FDA authorized the marketing of the Medline Autologous Regeneration of Tissue (ART) Skin Harvesting System, a handheld device for obtaining skin tissue. On Tuesday, the FDA updated its advisory for the E. coli O157:H7 outbreak, recommending not to eat, sell, or serve certain types of raw cheese. The FDA and CDC will continue to monitor for additional illnesses. A public workshop on Natural History Studies and Registries in Rare Disease Treatments will be held on May 13, 2024, hosted by the FDA, NIH, and the Reagan-Udall Foundation.

title: FDA Roundup: March 26, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has proposed a ban on electrical stimulation devices intended to reduce or stop self-injurious or aggressive behavior due to an unreasonable and substantial risk of illness or injury. The agency has determined this is the second time it has proposed such a ban. The Center for Drug Evaluation and Research's new Quantitative Medicine Center of Excellence aims to facilitate the continuous evolution of Quantitative Medicine across CDER. A public workshop on QM will be held on April 25. The FDA has also advised consumers in a guidance document that allergies can cause persistent sniffles and sneezes, and recommended reading and following directions when giving medicine to children. On March 22, the FDA approved Elahere for adult patients with specific types of cancer who have received one to three prior systemic treatment regimens.

title: FDA Warns Consumers to Avoid Certain Topical Pain Relief Products Due to Potential for Dangerous Health Effects
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is warning consumers not to use certain over-the-counter analgesic products marketed for topical use before, during, or after cosmetic procedures. Six companies have been issued warning letters for marketing these products in violation of federal law. The products, which contain high concentrations of lidocaine, can lead to serious injuries such as irregular heartbeat, seizures, and breathing difficulties if applied before or during cosmetic procedures. The FDA is committed to stopping the sale of these products and has asked the companies to respond within 15 days. The FDA recommends consumers not to use OTC pain relief products with more than 4% lidocaine, and to avoid applying them to large areas of skin or to irritated or broken skin.

title: FDA Roundup: March 22, 2024
body_summary: The FDA issued an emergency use authorization for Pemgarda (pemivibart) for COVID-19 pre-exposure prophylaxis in certain adults and adolescents. Pemgarda is authorized for individuals with moderate-to-severe immune compromise due to a medical condition or immunosuppressive medications. The FDA also updated the Breakthrough Devices Program webpage, granting 933 designations and authorizing 95 devices for marketing. Additionally, the FDA approved safety labeling changes for fluorouracil injection products and issued a final rule on food contact notifications. The agency notified stakeholders of a new report on seafood and child growth, and issued an import alert for food products with human-made chemical contaminants. The FDA granted accelerated approval to ponatinib for adult patients with Philadelphia chromosome-positive acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and approved the cobas Malaria test for screening blood donors for Plasmodium DNA and RNA.

title: FDA Approves Nonsteroidal Treatment for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Duvyzat (givinostat) as an oral medication for treating Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) in patients six years of age and older. DMD is a rare neurological disorder that causes progressive muscle weakness, and Duvyzat works by targeting pathogenic processes to reduce inflammation and loss of muscle. The FDA's approval provides another treatment option to help reduce the burden of DMD, with efficacy demonstrated in a 18-month phase 3 study. Duvyzat's primary endpoint showed a statistically significant reduction in the decline of muscle function, with patients receiving the treatment taking 1.25 seconds longer to climb four stairs compared to those receiving placebo. The most common side effects include diarrhea, abdominal pain, decreased platelets, nausea, vomiting, increased triglycerides, and fever.

title: Implementation Note issued March 20, 2024
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on March 20, 2024: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 5.4 percent, effective March 21, 2024.
