As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective March 21, 2024, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 5.5 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 5.3 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $60 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest into agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 5.5 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a solid pace. Job gains have remained strong, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation has eased over the past year but remains elevated. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are moving into better balance. The economic outlook is uncertain, and the Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks. In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent. In considering any adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. The Committee does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in its previously announced plans. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Michael S. Barr; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Mary C. Daly; Philip N. Jefferson; Adriana D. Kugler; Loretta J. Mester; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: FDA Roundup: March 19, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued warning letters to three entities for selling unauthorized plastic syringes made in China, and will take additional steps as needed to address quality and performance issues. The FDA expects these entities to fully address the violations and will keep the public informed as new information becomes available. The agency has also launched a new portal for reporting potential drug shortages, expanding access to its NextGen system. Furthermore, the FDA has approved DuOtic, a new otic gel for treating yeast-only otitis externa in dogs, which is the first otic drug without an antibiotic.

title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapy for Children with Metachromatic Leukodystrophy
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Lenmeldy (atidarsagene autotemcel), the first FDA-approved gene therapy for treating children with metachromatic leukodystrophy (MLD). MLD is a rare genetic disease caused by a deficiency of the enzyme arylsulfatase A (ARSA), leading to damage in the central and peripheral nervous system. Lenmeldy is a one-time, individualized single-dose infusion made from the patient's own hematopoietic stem cells, genetically modified to include functional copies of the ARSA gene. The treatment has been shown to significantly reduce the risk of severe motor impairment or death in children with pre-symptomatic late infantile MLD. Side effects include fever, low white blood cell count, and risk of delayed platelet engraftment. Patients should undergo lifelong monitoring for hematologic malignancies. Lenmeldy was granted Priority Review, Orphan Drug, Rare Pediatric Disease, and Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy designations, and was approved by the FDA for Orchard Therapeutics.

title: Proclamation 10712—National Agriculture Day, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States declares March 19, 2024, as National Agriculture Day to celebrate generations of American farmers, farmworkers, fishers, ranchers, and foresters who work to put food on America's tables and steward the Nation's lands. The proclamation acknowledges the challenges faced by rural America, including failed trickle-down economic policies, consolidation, and weakening of small businesses and bargaining power. The President has signed historic legislation to create new opportunities for farmers and ranchers, investing in rural America, strengthening farm supply chains, and addressing the climate crisis.

title: FDA Roundup: March 15, 2024
body_summary: The FDA published a new paper, "Artificial Intelligence and Medical Products: How CBER, CDER, CDRH, and OCP are Working Together," outlining focus areas for AI development and use across the medical product lifecycle. Commissioner Robert M. Califf discusses the agency's work on AI, including 300+ submissions for AI components in drugs and 700+ submissions for AI-enabled devices since 1995. The agency is exploring AI for internal operations and regulatory processes. The FDA also revoked frozen cherry pie standards, revoked norovirus-contaminated oyster standards, and announced a Medical Device Sterilization Town Hall. The FDA issued updated draft guidance for Medical Device Submissions: The Q-Submission Program and approved Breyanzi, a cell-based gene therapy for adult patients with relapsed or refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Patients with Liver Scarring Due to Fatty Liver Disease
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Rezdiffra (resmetirom) for the treatment of adults with noncirrhotic non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) with moderate to advanced liver scarring, to be used along with diet and exercise. The approval was granted under the accelerated approval pathway. Rezdiffra is a partial activator of a thyroid hormone receptor that reduces liver fat accumulation. A 54-month, randomized, double-blind placebo-controlled trial evaluated the safety and efficacy of Rezdiffra, showing that a greater proportion of subjects who received Rezdiffra achieved NASH resolution or an improvement in liver scarring compared to those who received the placebo. The trial found that 26-27% of subjects who received 80 milligrams of Rezdiffra experienced NASH resolution, and 23-28% experienced an improvement in liver scarring. The most common side effects of Rezdiffra included diarrhea and nausea. The FDA also warned of potential drug interactions with Rezdiffra and advised patients with decompensated cirrhosis to avoid using the medication.

title: FDA Roundup: March 12, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued several updates. The FDA has proposed updated recommendations for quality system considerations in device premarket submissions for cyber devices, and will accept comments on the draft guidance until May 13, 2024. The agency will host a webinar on April 30, 2024, to provide information on the guidance. The FDA also advised consumers to check if their medications can cause side effects that may affect safe driving. The agency's Center for Devices and Radiological Health held the 25th Session of the International Forum, with nearly 1,200 attendees from 62 countries. The FDA has also issued a Safety Alert, advising restaurants and retailers not to serve or sell certain mussels from Newfoundland, Canada, due to potential contamination.

title: Proclamation 10710—National Equal Pay Day, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States has proclaimed March 12, 2024, as National Equal Pay Day. This day marks how far into the year women have to work to earn what men made last year, highlighting the injustice of gender wage gaps. Women working full-time and year-round are paid an average of 84 cents for every dollar paid to men. Despite progress in labor force participation and the gender pay gap, the fight for equal pay continues. The President's Administration has made efforts to address pay inequities, including finalizing a rule to eliminate pay inequities and proposing regulations to advance pay equity and transparency. The Administration calls on Congress to pass the Paycheck Fairness Act to increase pay transparency and give workers more tools to fight sex-based pay discrimination.

title: FDA Seeks $7.2 Billion to Enhance Food Safety and Nutrition, Advance Medical Product Safety, and Strengthen Public Health
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is requesting $7.2 billion as part of the President's fiscal year 2025 proposed budget. The funding will enhance food safety and nutrition, advance medical product safety, support supply chain resiliency, strengthen public health and mission-support capacity, and modernize the FDA's infrastructure and facilities. The request includes a 7.4% increase above the FY 2023 funding level.

The FDA's priorities include enhancing food safety and nutrition, addressing shortages and supply chain disruptions, bolstering modernization efforts and mission support, and improving data infrastructure. The funding will also support the implementation of expanded cosmetics regulation, protect and promote a safe and nutritious U.S. food supply, and modernize the agency's infrastructure and facilities.

The FY 2025 request covers the period from October 1, 2024, to September 30, 2025. The highlights of the agency's request include $15 million for food safety and nutrition, $12.3 million for shortages and supply chain, $114.8 million for modernization efforts and mission support, and $8.3 million for data infrastructure.

title: FDA Roundup: March 8, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing an at-a-glance summary of news from around the agency. The FDA announced proposed new regulations to provide animal drug sponsors with predictable requirements for the labeling of prescription and over-the-counter new animal drugs. The proposed rule would also benefit veterinarians, animal owners, and animal producers by providing a more consistent presentation of information on the safe and effective use of these new animal drugs. The FDA is accepting public comments on the proposed rule for 90 days from the date of publication in the Federal Register. The public can submit comments by June 10, 2024.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment to Reduce Risk of Serious Heart Problems Specifically in Adults with Obesity or Overweight
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Wegovy (semaglutide) injection to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death, heart attack, and stroke in adults with cardiovascular disease and either obesity or overweight. Wegovy should be used in addition to a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity. The approval is based on a multi-national, multi-center trial involving over 17,600 participants, which showed Wegovy significantly reduced the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events. The prescribing information contains warnings about risks such as thyroid C-cell tumors, pancreatitis, and low blood sugar. Wegovy is now the first weight loss medication to also be approved to prevent life-threatening cardiovascular events.

title: FDA Takes Steps to Ensure Safety of Cinnamon Products Sold in the US
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is taking additional steps to address concerns over elevated lead levels in cinnamon following a recent incident associated with cinnamon apple sauce pouches that resulted in lead poisoning in young children. The agency is reminding all cinnamon manufacturers, processors, distributors, and facility operators in the US to implement controls to prevent contamination from potential chemical hazards. The FDA is also recommending the voluntary recall of certain ground cinnamon products sold by several brands at six different retail chains that were found to contain elevated levels of lead. The agency has notified distributors and manufacturers of products found to contain elevated lead levels and recommended that they voluntarily recall these products due to prolonged exposure risks.

title: FDA Roundup: March 5, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has announced the availability of a final guidance for industry on Dietary Supplements: New Dietary Ingredient Notification Procedures and Timeframes: Guidance for Industry. The FDA has also approved the first interchangeable biosimilar to Prolia (denosumab) and Xgeva (denosumab), Jubbonti (denosumab-bbdz) and Wyost (denosumab-bbdz), for the treatment of osteoporosis and bone complications from cancer. The most common side effects of Jubbonti and Wyost are similar to those of Prolia and Xgeva. The FDA has also updated its list of select chemicals under review to provide more insight into the agency's post-market assessments of chemicals in the food supply. Additionally, the FDA has approved amivantamab-vmjw (Rybrevant) for the first-line treatment of locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations.

title: FDA Clears First Over-the-Counter Continuous Glucose Monitor
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has cleared the Dexcom Stelo Glucose Biosensor System for over-the-counter marketing. The device is an integrated continuous glucose monitor (iCGM) intended for individuals 18 years and older with diabetes who use oral medications or want to track blood sugar levels due to diet and exercise. The system is not for individuals with problematic hypoglycemia. According to Jeff Shuren, director of the FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health, the clearance expands access to CGMs without healthcare provider involvement, promoting health equity. The device uses a wearable sensor paired with a smartphone app to continuously measure and display glucose values. Users can wear the sensor for up to 15 days before replacing it. A clinical study showed the device performed similarly to other iCGMs, with reported adverse events including local infection, skin irritation, and pain. The FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health aims to advance health equity by supporting innovation in home care and wellness.

title: Statement on Medicare Prescription Drug Price Negotiations
body_summary: The US administration is announcing that all manufacturers of ten selected prescription drugs will continue to participate in drug price negotiations with Medicare. This follows the submission of counteroffers by manufacturers, which is an important milestone in the administration's fight to lower health care costs and make prescription drugs more affordable for all Americans. The decision comes after a court challenge by Big Pharma and Republican efforts to repeal the Inflation Reduction Act, which would benefit seniors on Medicare. The administration will further discuss its efforts to lower health care costs in a State of the Union Address this week.

title: Statement on Food and Drug Administration Certification of Major Retail Pharmacies To Dispense Mifepristone
body_summary: The Food and Drug Administration has approved mifepristone for safe and effective use for over 20 years. Major retail pharmacy chains are now certified to dispense medication abortion, allowing women to pick up their prescription at a local, certified pharmacy like any other medication. The Vice President and the author will continue to fight to ensure women's access to healthcare, defend the FDA's independent approval and regulation of mifepristone, and restore protections of Roe v. Wade in federal law.

title: Proclamation 10707—National Consumer Protection Week, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States issues a proclamation declaring March 3-9, 2024, as National Consumer Protection Week. The Administration reiterates its commitment to protecting consumers from fraud, cybercrimes, and unfair business practices. Since taking office, the Administration has created nearly 15 million jobs, driven stable economic growth, and brought down inflation by two-thirds. The Department of Justice and the Federal Trade Commission have taken action to address powerful corporations' use of market dominance to inflate prices and limit job mobility. The FTC has proposed rules to end noncompete agreements, require upfront pricing, and ban hidden junk fees. The Administration has also seen progress in reducing overdraft fees, credit card late fees, and junk fees in banking and healthcare. The President encourages Americans to visit consumer.ftc.gov for information on consumer rights and report suspected fraud or issues.

title: FDA Roundup: March 1, 2024
body_summary: The FDA issued a letter of enforcement discretion for yogurt-related health claims, allowed the use of certain conditions. The agency also published guidance on informed consent and a draft guidance on key information and facilitating understanding in informed consent. The FDA reminded consumers about the dangers of measles and the importance of vaccination. The agency issued an EUA for the OSOM Flu SARS-CoV-2 Combo Home Test and approved the Boston Scientific Corporation's premarket approval application for a Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Catheter. The FDA alerted patients to a higher risk of device failure with the Hintermann Series H3 Total Ankle Replacement system. The agency updated an advisory on cinnamon applesauce pouches with lead and chromium levels and announced the end of sales for grease-proofing substances containing PFAS. The FDA granted marketing authorization for the Technozym ADAMTS13 Activity enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. The FDA also announced a virtual public workshop on April 17 to discuss expanding its Accreditation Scheme for Conformity Assessment (ASCA) program.

title: Proclamation 10705—National Colorectal Cancer Awareness Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States announces National Colorectal Cancer Awareness Month. Colorectal cancer is the second leading cause of cancer death in the US, affecting approximately 150,000 Americans this year. The President reiterates the goal of ending cancer and commends progress made over the past decades. Despite advancements, more Americans under 50 are diagnosed with cancer each year. The President reignites the Cancer Moonshot, aiming to cut cancer death rates by half in 25 years and improve patient outcomes. $2.5 billion is secured in bipartisan funding for the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H) to create innovative cancer treatments. The Administration works to make cancer treatments more affordable, expanding Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act. The President encourages regular screenings starting at age 45 and supports awareness and prevention efforts nationwide.

title: Proclamation 10706—Women's History Month, 2024
body_summary: The President of the United States declares March 2024 as Women's History Month. The Administration celebrates the courageous women who have strengthened the Nation and opened doors of opportunity for all. Women have made significant contributions in various fields, including science, art, public service, and the Armed Forces. Despite progress, barriers remain, and the Administration continues to advance women's rights and opportunities. The President's Administration has implemented various initiatives, including the White House Gender Policy Council, the National Gender Strategy, and the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, to ensure women's access to economic opportunities, health care, and education. The Administration also champions equal pay, child care, and reproductive rights, while protecting women's physical security. The President has signed legislation providing protections for pregnant and postpartum workers and has launched initiatives to combat maternal mortality and promote women's health research.

title: FDA, Industry Actions End Sales of PFAS Used in US Food Packaging
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is announcing that grease-proofing materials containing per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are no longer being sold for use in food packaging in the U.S. This marks the fulfillment of a voluntary commitment by manufacturers to not sell food contact substances containing certain PFAS intended for use as grease-proofing agents. The FDA led this effort, with cooperation from industry, and research conducted by FDA scientists played a key role in obtaining these commitments. The announcement is the result of a post-market safety assessment conducted in 2020, and the FDA will continue to conduct research and update evaluations using the most up-to-date science to ensure the risk determinations remain accurate.

title: FDA Roundup: February 27, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced that on May 16, 2024, the Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee will meet to discuss and make recommendations on selecting strains for the 2024-2025 COVID-19 vaccine formula. The FDA anticipates changes to the vaccine composition based on circulating virus strains. If recommended, changes may be made annually, similar to the seasonal influenza vaccine. The FDA expects updated vaccines to be available in advance of the fall/winter respiratory virus season.

title: FDA Roundup: February 23, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced its final decision to withdraw approval of Pepaxto (melphalan flufenamide), a treatment for multiple myeloma, due to a lack of clinical benefit and safety concerns. The decision was made by Director Peter Marks, M.D., Ph.D., as the Commissioner's designee. The agency also approved or tentatively approved 956 generic drug applications, including 90 first generics, in 2023. The FDA continued to advance its Diagnostic Data Program, harmonizing diagnostic data and creating analytics tools to optimize data use. The agency issued guidance on genome-edited plants, allowing developers to voluntarily inform the FDA of safety measures. The FDA also warned consumers about risks associated with smartwatches or smart rings claiming to measure blood glucose levels. Additionally, the agency updated its Ingredient Directory and issued guidance on assessing COVID-19-related symptoms in clinical trials. The FDA recalled Listeria monocytogenes linked to Cotija and Queso Fresco Cheese and updated its advisory for the outbreak. The agency also presented its 6th annual Conversations on Cancer program, highlighting the under-representation of African Americans in medical oncology.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary:
Here is the final summary:

Jerome H. Powell was selected as Chair and John C. Williams as Vice Chair of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) in a joint meeting with the Board of Governors held January 30-31, 2024. Roberto Perli and Julie Ann Remache were chosen to manage the System Open Market Account (SOMA). The FOMC approved four policies: Investment and Trading, Information Security, External Communications, and Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy. Real GDP rose in Q4 driven by private domestic final purchases and real exports. The staff's economic forecast showed slightly stronger growth in 2023 and slower output growth in 2024 and 2025 due to monetary policy actions. Total PCE price inflation was projected to step down before returning close to 2% by 2026. The FOMC maintained its target interest rate range of 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent and reduced securities holdings.

title: FDA Roundup: February 20, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is reminding device study sponsors and manufacturers to evaluate third-party test labs and verify testing results before submitting data. The FDA has seen an increase in unreliable data from China and India, which has hindered substantial equivalence determinations or marketing authorizations for medical devices. The FDA is pursuing actions to identify data integrity violations and is calling on the industry to ensure data integrity. The agency published an Outbreak Advisory for E. coli O157:H7 linked to raw cheddar cheese, recommending its removal from the market. The FDA also approved osimertinib for patients with non-small cell lung cancer. Additionally, Jonathan Nyce was sentenced to 97 months in prison for wire fraud and interstate shipment of misbranded animal drugs.

title: FDA Approves First Medication to Help Reduce Allergic Reactions to Multiple Foods After Accidental Exposure
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Xolair injection for immunoglobulin E-mediated food allergy in certain adults and children over 1 year old to reduce allergic reactions and anaphylaxis risk. Xolair reduces IgE binding to receptors, but patients must still avoid foods they're allergic to. The drug was originally approved in 2003 for asthma and is now approved for food allergy treatment. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention state that 6% of US people in 2021 had a food allergy, and there's currently no cure. Xolair's safety and efficacy were established in a study of 168 subjects with peanut and multiple other food allergies. The primary measure showed 68% of Xolair recipients could eat peanut without severe symptoms, compared to 6% of placebo recipients. Common side effects include injection site reactions and fever. Xolair comes with warnings and precautions, including anaphylaxis, malignancy, and abnormal laboratory tests. The drug should be used in healthcare settings equipped to manage anaphylaxis, and patients with a history of severe hypersensitivity should not receive it.

title: FDA Roundup: February 16, 2024
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is providing updates on various news around the agency. The FDA reminded consumers to adjust or change medications as they age due to physical changes that can affect medication handling and effectiveness. The FDA issued its CDER Drug Safety Priorities report for Fiscal Year 2023, highlighting key safety milestones and accomplishments. The report focuses on programs and initiatives aimed at improving public health and drug safety. 

The FDA converted tepotinib's approval to traditional approval for adult patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer, based on an additional 161 patients and 28 months of follow-up time. The FDA cleared the PBC Separator with Selux Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing System from Selux Diagnostics, Inc. to be marketed in the US. This system is intended for use with positive blood culture samples for quantitative in vitro antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

The FDA approved irinotecan liposome with oxaliplatin, fluorouracil, and leucovorin for the first-line treatment of metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The FDA cleared the eQUANT System from Avails Medical, Inc. to be marketed in the US, an automated lab inoculation preparation system for direct antimicrobial susceptibility testing. The FDA is also updating the announcement of a Listeria monocytogenes outbreak linked to Cotija and Queso Fresco cheeses.

title: FDA Approves First Cellular Therapy to Treat Patients with Unresectable or Metastatic Melanoma
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Amtagvi (lifileucel), a tumor-derived autologous T cell immunotherapy, for the treatment of adult patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma. This approval represents a novel T cell immunotherapy for patients with limited treatment options. Amtagvi was evaluated in a global, multicenter, multicohort clinical study, which showed an objective response rate of 31.5% among 73 patients treated with the recommended dose. The treatment's effectiveness was established based on objective response rate to treatment and duration of response. A confirmatory trial is ongoing to verify Amtagvi's clinical benefit. Patients treated with Amtagvi may experience severe low blood count, severe infection, cardiac disorder, or develop worsened respiratory or renal function, and a Boxed Warning is included in the label to inform about these risks.

title: FDA Approves First Medication to Treat Severe Frostbite
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Aurlumyn (iloprost) injection to treat severe frostbite in adults to reduce the risk of finger or toe amputation. Norman Stockbridge, M.D., Ph.D., director of the Division of Cardiology and Nephrology, stated that this approval provides patients with a new treatment option. Iloprost, a vasodilator, prevents blood clotting and was primarily established in an open-label, controlled trial that randomized 47 adults with severe frostbite. The trial showed that patients receiving iloprost had a lower incidence of needing amputation compared to those not receiving it. Aurlumyn's most common side effects include headache, flushing, and dizziness. The approval was granted to Eicos Sciences Inc.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index Report for January
body_summary: Wage growth has been the strongest in 50 years, with inflation declining by two-thirds from its peak. The speaker is fighting to lower costs for middle class families, including insulin and prescription drugs, junk fees, and calling on corporations to pass savings on to consumers. They will continue to oppose congressional Republicans' efforts to cut taxes for the wealthy, raise costs for middle class families, and cut Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid.

title: FDA Roundup: February 13, 2024
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has posted warning letters to US Chem Labs and Synthetix Inc. doing business as Helix Chemical Supply for introducing unapproved and misbranded semaglutide and tirzepatide products into interstate commerce. 

US Chem Labs offers semaglutide and tirzepatide "for research purposes," accompanied by claims such as weight loss and reducing the risk of stroke, heart attack, or heart disease. Helix Chemical Supply also offers these products for "research purposes," but with claims related to treatment of Alzheimer's disease and lowering blood sugar. 

Covetrus North America LLC, based in Dublin, Ohio, has pleaded guilty to causing the introduction and delivery of misbranded veterinary prescription drugs into interstate commerce. As part of the agreement, Covetrus will pay over $23 million in criminal fines and forfeitures.

title: FDA Roundup: February 9, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration issued a draft guidance for collecting representative samples for seafood products subject to Detention Without Physical Examination due to adulteration caused by pathogens, animal drugs, and decomposition. The agency also updated an outbreak advisory for Listeria monocytogenes: Queso Fresco and Cotija Cheese, adding three new recalls from Rizo Lopez Foods, Inc. The FDA published a CDER From Our Perspective article discussing the implementation of the Parallel Scientific Advice pilot program with the European Medicines Agency. The agency authorized a software-only mobile medical application, the Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd.'s Sleep Apnea Feature, for detecting signs of obstructive sleep apnea in adults 22 years old and older.

title: FDA Roundup: February 6, 2024
body_summary: The US FDA has issued an outbreak advisory for consumers not to eat, sell, or serve recalled dairy products from Rizo Lopez Foods, Inc., due to a multi-year, multistate outbreak of Listeria monocytogenes infections linked to queso fresco and cotija cheeses. There are 26 reported illnesses with 23 hospitalizations in 11 states. The FDA is investigating and will update the advisory as information becomes available. Additionally, the FDA has issued marketing denial orders to Fontem US LLC for four blu Disposable and one myblu brand e-cigarette products.

title: FDA Roundup: February 2, 2024
body_summary: The US FDA issued a safety communication warning consumers, healthcare providers, and facilities not to use certain syringes due to dimensional changes that may cause performance issues. The agency announced a public workshop on March 19-20 to discuss innovative clinical trial approaches. The FDA updated the medical device shortages list and approved the Edwards EVOQUE Tricuspid Valve Replacement System. Additionally, the agency authorized marketing of the Hologic Genius Digital Diagnostics System. The FDA granted Breakthrough Device designation to the FARAPULSE PFA system, which uses electrical pulses to ablate cardiac tissue, offering an alternative treatment for Afib with potentially reduced risks. The FDA released draft guidance on collecting and reporting race and ethnicity data in clinical trials and studies.

title: Statement on Medicare Prescription Drug Price Negotiations
body_summary: Medicare is making offers on the fair price for ten of the most widely used and expensive drugs. For the first time in history, Medicare is no longer taking whatever prices that pharmaceutical companies demand. The Inflation Reduction Act, signed by the President, aims to negotiate lower prices on drugs to treat various diseases, including diabetes, Crohn's disease, arthritis, heart disease, and cancer. Through this act, seniors are already saving $800 per year on health insurance costs, and insulin costs have been cut to $35. Starting next year, seniors' out-of-pocket drug costs will be capped at $2,000. The administration plans to continue protecting programs like Medicare and Social Security, and deliver lower costs for seniors and families, despite Republican efforts to repeal the Inflation Reduction Act and cut Medicare and Social Security benefits.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a solid pace. Job gains have moderated since early last year but remain strong, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation has eased over the past year but remains elevated. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are moving into better balance. The economic outlook is uncertain, and the Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks. In support of its goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent. In considering any adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks. The Committee does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in its previously announced plans. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Michael S. Barr; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Mary C. Daly; Philip N. Jefferson; Adriana D. Kugler; Loretta J. Mester; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: Proclamation 10698—American Heart Month, 2024
body_summary: By the President of the United States of America, a proclamation: This American Heart Month, we recommit to promoting heart-healthy lifestyles, expanding access to quality health care, and breaking new bounds in heart disease research and treatment. Each year, heart disease takes the lives of nearly 700,000 Americans. The President's Administration is committed to giving families the tools they need to stay healthy. In 2022, we hosted the first White House Conference on Hunger, Nutrition, and Health and released a national strategy to end hunger and reduce diet-related diseases by 2030. The strategy includes improving food access and affordability. In 2022, the President signed the Inflation Reduction Act, which will cap the total out-of-pocket drug costs for seniors at $2,000 per year. The President has also improved access to dental services for people with Medicare who need certain cardiac procedures. We are working to advance new breakthroughs on a range of diseases. It is also important for every American to be aware of individual actions they can take to keep their hearts healthy. The President encourages every American to raise awareness about heart health by wearing red on National Wear Red Day, this Friday, February 2nd. Now, Therefore, we proclaim February 2024 as American Heart Month, and invite all Americans to participate in National Wear Red Day on February 2, 2024.

title: Proclamation 10699—National Black History Month, 2024
body_summary:
President Joseph R. Biden Jr. proclaims February 2024 as National Black History Month, recognizing the vast contributions of Black Americans to the country and acknowledging that Black history is American history. The President notes that Black Americans have never given up on the promise of America, despite facing moral stains and vestiges of slavery. Throughout history, Black Americans have held a mirror up to the Nation, confronting hard truths about who America is and pushing for a more equitable nation.

The President has taken steps to continue this legacy, including signing Executive Orders on Advancing Racial Equity and Support for Underserved Communities. Since taking office, the Vice President and President have created over 14 million jobs, reduced Black unemployment, improved health care access, and addressed historic health inequities.

The President's Administration is also working to close racial gaps in education and economic opportunity, including delivering funding for Historically Black Colleges and Universities and expanding access to home-ownership. By 2025, 15 percent of Federal contracting dollars will go to small disadvantaged businesses, including Black-owned small businesses.

The President has also taken action to address systemic racism, including banning chokeholds, restricting no knock warrants, and promoting community policing. The Administration continues to call on Congress to pass the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and the Freedom to Vote Act to secure the right to vote for every American.

The President concludes that America's progress depends on acknowledging the good, the bad, and the full truth of its history, and recognizes that our only way forward is by marching together.

title: Implementation Note issued January 31, 2024
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on January 31, 2024: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 5.4 percent, effective February 1, 2024. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: FDA Roundup: January 30, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) published news on World Cancer Day 2024, announcing collaborations and updates. The FDA and European Medicines Agency will host a virtual public discussion on February 1 to spotlight innovative cancer treatment advances for patients with CML, multiple myeloma, and melanoma. The discussion aims to introduce new therapeutic classes and regulatory programs that expedite access to patients. On the same day, the FDA will host a panel discussion from 9:30 to 11 am ET. The FDA also issued a Safety Alert on toxic yellow oleander products and revised the EUA for Paxlovid to transition from government to Pfizer distribution.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Economic Analysis Advance Estimate of Gross Domestic Product for the Fourth Quarter of 2023
body_summary: The U.S. economy grew 3.1 percent over the past year, adding 2.7 million jobs, with core inflation moving back towards pre-pandemic levels. As a result, wages, wealth, and employment have increased, benefiting American families and workers. The President attributes this growth to a three-year effort to grow the economy from the middle and bottom up. To further support the economy, the President plans to implement legislation to lower prescription drug costs, health insurance premiums, and clean energy costs, as well as take on hidden junk fees and call on large corporations to pass on savings to consumers. The President vows to prevent extreme Republicans from giving massive giveaways to the wealthy and large corporations while raising costs and cutting Social Security, Medicare, and Medicaid.

title: Statement on Health Insurance Enrollment Under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: The US President announced a record 21.3 million Americans have signed up for health coverage through Affordable Care Act marketplaces. Since taking office, 9 million more people gained coverage under the law, with the President's actions to protect and strengthen the law making a significant difference. However, Republicans in Congress have proposed a budget that would get rid of improvements signed into law, raising costs for millions. Repealing the Affordable Care Act would throw 21 million people off coverage and end Medicaid coverage for millions more, causing widespread health care costs to skyrocket or coverage to be lost.

title: FDA Roundup: January 23, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced several news updates. The FDA will hold a Medical Device Sterilization Town Hall on Jan. 26 from 12-1 p.m. ET to discuss reducing reliance on ethylene oxide. The agency has also issued a marketing denial order to Bidi Vapor LLC for its Bidi Stick – Classic e-cigarette due to insufficient evidence demonstrating its safety. The FDA and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention have closed an investigation into a Salmonella outbreak linked to recalled cantaloupe. The FDA has approved erdafitinib for adult patients with certain types of cancer. Additionally, the FDA has issued safety labeling change notifications for licensed CAR T cell immunotherapies due to the risk of T cell malignancies.

title: FDA Roundup: January 19, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued marketing denial orders to Shenzhen Youme Information Technology Co. Ltd. for two Suorin brand e-cigarette products and to Fontem US, LLC for blu PLUS+ brand e-cigarette products, requiring them not to market or distribute these products in the United States. The FDA and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) reiterated mutual support for laboratory developed test (LDT) oversight. The FDA also issued safety communications about recalled ResMed Ltd masks and advised users to check if their mask is one of the recalled products. Additionally, the FDA issued safety alerts about potentially contaminated oysters from Baja California, Mexico, and notified restaurants and retailers not to serve or sell them. The FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH) issued its 2023 Annual Report, highlighting the authorization of the highest number of novel medical devices on record.

title: FDA Roundup: January 16, 2024
body_summary:
The FDA has announced an open period for applications to support the development, implementation, and evaluation of a human abuse potential (HAP) study on the use of botanical kratom. The agency is prioritizing kratom due to the lack of published literature and clinical evaluations despite its increased human use. 

The FDA has approved Casgevy, a cell-based gene therapy, for patients 12 years of age and older with transfusion-dependent beta-thalassemia. Casgevy uses CRISPR/Cas9 technology to modify patients' hematopoietic stem cells, increasing fetal hemoglobin production and decreasing anemia. 

Casgevy received Fast Track and Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy designations. The product was also recently approved for the treatment of sickle cell disease in patients 12 years and older.

The FDA has authorized the DermaSensor device, a prescription device for evaluating skin lesions suggestive of melanoma, basal cell carcinoma, and/or squamous cell carcinoma. 

The FDA approved pembrolizumab (Keytruda) with chemoradiotherapy for patients with FIGO 2014 Stage III-IVA cervical cancer. 

The FDA issued a safety alert advising restaurants and retailers not to serve or sell certain oysters from Bahia Salina in Sonora, Mexico potentially contaminated with Norovirus. 

The FDA authorized Fibresolve, a software-only device that analyzes lung computed tomography images to aid in the referral of patients with suspected findings related to scarring of the lungs. 

The FDA granted marketing authorization of Fibresolve to Imvaria, Inc.

title: FDA Roundup: January 12, 2024
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued a safety alert regarding whole, live scallops from a prohibited area in Massachusetts, distributed by Intershell International Corp. The FDA also announced the winners of the Veterans Cardiac Health and AI Model Predictions (V-CHAMPS) Challenge, which aims to develop AI models to predict heart failure-related outcomes. The FDA published a blog on digital health collaboration and invited comments by January 31, 2024. Additionally, the FDA approved 55 new drugs in 2023, which have not been previously FDA-approved, and made some prescription drugs available over-the-counter.

title: Statement on Health Insurance Enrollment Under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: The Affordable Care Act has reached a record-breaking 20 million Americans enrolled in health care coverage. With 6 days left to sign up, 8 million more Americans have joined the ACA coverage than when the current administration took office. The ACA is more popular and affordable than ever, with millions saving hundreds or thousands on health insurance premiums. However, extreme Republicans want to repeal the law, which would raise costs for millions, especially older Americans and small-business owners, and strip 20 million of their coverage. The president will continue fighting to bring down health care and prescription drug costs, encouraging Americans to sign up for health coverage at healthcare.gov before January 16.

title: FDA Roundup: January 9, 2024
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing an update on recent news from around the agency. On January 10, the OCE will host a discussion on oncology drug approvals in 2023 at 2:00 pm. The discussion will highlight transformative approvals and showcase the agency's commitment to protecting and advancing patient care. 

The FDA has issued a letter to healthcare providers about the potential exposure to chemicals from General Electric HealthCare accessory components. The agency has also updated its final guidance on submission and review of sterility information in premarket notifications for devices labeled as sterile. 

A town hall on medical device sterilization will be held on January 10, 2024, at 2:00 p.m. ET, discussing takeaways from the 2019 Advisory Committee meeting and the current medical device sterilization landscape. 

The FDA's Coordinated Outbreak Response & Evaluation (CORE) Network has released its first annual report, summarizing investigations of outbreaks and adverse events linked to FDA-regulated human foods for the 2022 calendar year. 

The FDA has published its report on new drug approvals in 2023, featuring novel approvals and notable approvals for new and expanded uses. 

An investigation into elevated lead levels in cinnamon apple puree pouches has found chromium in the recalled products, but the form of chromium is not definitively known.

title: FDA Facilitates Broader Adoption of Vaporized Hydrogen Peroxide for Medical Device Sterilization
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is announcing that it considers vaporized hydrogen peroxide (VH2O2) as an established method of sterilization for medical devices. The FDA has revised its final guidance to list VH2O2 as an example of an Established Category A method of sterilization. This update aims to facilitate the broader adoption of VH2O2 as a sterilization method for the medical device industry. VH2O2's long history of safety and effectiveness has led to its recognition as an Established Category A method. The FDA's goal is to reduce the use of ethylene oxide (EtO) and advance medical device supply chain resiliency. VH2O2 will strengthen industry's capacity to adopt alternative sterilization processes that pose less potential risk to the environment.

title: FDA Authorizes Florida’s Drug Importation Program
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has authorized Florida's Agency for Health Care Administration's drug importation program under section 804 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. This is the first step towards Florida facilitating the importation of certain prescription drugs from Canada. President Biden's Executive Order on Promoting Competition in the American Economy directed the FDA to work with states and Indian tribes on these plans. Florida's SIP is authorized for two years from the date the FDA is notified of the first shipment of drugs to be imported. The FDA requires Florida to submit additional information for review and approval, ensure drugs meet FDA standards, and relabel them. Florida must also submit a quarterly report to the FDA on imported drugs, cost savings, and potential safety and quality issues. The FDA will exercise oversight to ensure the authorized proposal is followed and that Florida's program meets requirements.

title: FDA Roundup: January 5, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is issuing a safety communication to inform health care providers not to use the Total Hip System, including resurfacing implants, manufactured by Synovo Production, Inc. The FDA is also warning about certain tejocote root supplements substituted with toxic yellow oleander. The Reagan-Udall Foundation will hold a virtual public workshop on January 31 and February 1 to discuss scientific issues in psychedelic clinical trials and drug development. The workshop aims to explore considerations for psychedelic clinical trial designs, understand the experiences of scientists working with psychedelics, and explore perspectives and current research in psychedelic clinical trials.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A Federal Open Market Committee joint meeting was held on December 12-13, 2023, with Jerome H. Powell as Chair. Financial conditions eased due to declining interest rates, increasing equity prices, and a depreciating dollar. Treasury yields declined sharply over the intermeeting period, driven by reduced term premiums and policy rate expectations. The FOMC's Survey of Primary Dealers and Survey of Market Participants indicated that many respondents believed the peak federal funds rate had been reached. Inflation compensation decreased amid softer data releases. Stock prices increased, and bond spreads narrowed. The Committee maintained the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent, citing continued progress toward its 2 percent inflation objective and better labor market balance.

title: FDA Roundup: January 2, 2024
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) provided updates on various actions and announcements on December 27, 2023. The FDA issued guidance to help drug manufacturers limit benzene exposure in certain drug products. Additionally, the FDA revised a draft guidance for topical ophthalmic drug products, including new information on product sterility and preservative use. The agency also issued a letter to clinical laboratory staff and healthcare providers about false reactive results in herpes simplex virus type 2 serological tests. Furthermore, the FDA provided safety alerts regarding contaminated oysters from British Columbia, Canada, and a voluntary recall of Nutramigen Hypoallergenic Infant Formula Powder products due to possible Cronobacter sakazakii contamination.

title: Proclamation 10689—50th Anniversary of the Endangered Species Act, 2023
body_summary: The President of the United States of America has issued a proclamation commemorating the 50th anniversary of the Endangered Species Act. The law, passed by Congress 50 years ago, has prevented 99 percent of fish, wildlife, and plants under its protection from going extinct. The law has safeguarded biodiversity, supported species recovery, and conserved habitats. The President's Administration has reaffirmed its commitment to conserving America's flora and fauna, building on the legacy of the Endangered Species Act. This includes proposing two rules to restore critical parts of the law, investing billions of dollars in conservation efforts, and designating new national marine sanctuaries. The President has also taken steps to conserve natural treasures, including the establishment of a National Conservation Goal and the protection of over 13 million acres of lands in the Western Arctic. The proclamation also calls upon Americans to work together to conserve the Nation's biodiversity, with the goal of conserving at least 30 percent of lands and waters by 2030.

title: FDA Roundup: December 22, 2023
body_summary: The FDA is not issuing a new Roundup product during the week of Dec 25 and plans to resume issuance on Jan 2, 2024. The agency advises consumers not to use counterfeit Ozempic (semaglutide) and reminds people to take precautions against fall respiratory illnesses. The FDA has issued a guidance for industry on rare diseases, and has warned against counterfeit Ozempic. The agency has also published guidance on real-world evidence and new animal drugs for minor uses. Additionally, the FDA has issued warning letters to online retailers for selling unauthorized e-cigarettes and is revising its 510(k) Third Party Review program.

title: Statement on Health Insurance Enrollment Under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: The Affordable Care Act has broken all previous records with over 19 million people signing up for coverage, a growth of over 7 million since the speaker took office. Thanks to policies signed into law, millions of Americans are saving hundreds or thousands of dollars on health insurance premiums. Currently, four out of five Americans who sign up for health insurance through the Affordable Care Act can find coverage for $10 a month or less. The speaker's administration will continue to fight to expand health coverage and lower prescription drug costs for all, as every family deserves dignity and peace of mind with health insurance. The speaker encourages Americans to visit healthcare.gov before January 16, 2024, to sign up for health coverage for the coming year.

title: FDA Roundup: December 19, 2023
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the first test that uses DNA to assess the risk of developing opioid use disorder. The AutoGenomics Inc. AvertD test is intended for patients 18 years and older who have no prior use of oral opioid analgesics and will be used prior to first exposure to oral opioid pain medications. 

The FDA has refreshed its Know Your Treatment Options for COVID-19 Consumer Update and reminded consumers of several treatment options to prevent hospitalization and serious complications. The agency has approved drug treatments for COVID-19 and authorized others for emergency use, with more therapies being tested in clinical trials.

The FDA released joint Q&A documents with the European Medicines Agency on generating quality and manufacturing information for products in the breakthrough therapy designation program and PRIME scheme. 

The FDA launched its Cosmetics Direct electronic submission portal for registration of cosmetic product facilities and listing of cosmetic products, as mandated by the Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022 (MoCRA). 

The Center for Tobacco Products (CTP) Director Brian King published a statement on the release of the center's comprehensive strategic plan. 

The FDA expanded in-person face-to-face industry meetings for Prescription Drug User Fee Act, Biosimilar User Fee Act, and Over-The-Counter Monograph Drug User Fee Program (OMUFA) meeting types. 

The FDA issued a draft guidance on the use of real-world evidence to support regulatory decision-making for medical devices. 

The FDA updated the CDRH's Customer Collaboration Portal to improve the user experience. 

The FDA updated its advisory on the Investigation of Elevated Lead Levels in Cinnamon Applesauce Pouches. 

The FDA granted marketing authorization to the Body Temperature Software (BTS) App for measuring body temperature in people of all ages, excluding premature infants. 

The FDA approved enfortumab vedotin-ejfv (Padcev) in co

title: FDA Roundup: December 15, 2023
body_summary: The FDA has updated its web page on breast implants to share the latest information on risks and complications, labeling for approved implants, and reports of squamous cell carcinoma, various lymphomas, and mesenchymal tumors. The agency issued draft guidance to expedite the development and review of Priority Zoonotic Animal Drug (PZAD) designations for new animal drugs. Belzutifan (Welireg) was approved for patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma. The FDA also approved the PulseSelect PFA system for cardiac electrophysiological mapping and treatment of atrial fibrillation. Additionally, the FDA issued warning letters to manufacturers and distributors of unapproved antimicrobial drugs, updated a public health advisory on Listeria monocytogenes linked to peaches, plums, and nectarines, and announced the opening of the Voluntary Qualified Importer Program application portal for fiscal year 2025. The FDA approved deflornithine (IWILFIN) to reduce the risk of relapse in patients with high-risk neuroblastoma.

title: FDA Warns Nine Manufacturers, Distributors of Unapproved Antimicrobials for Animals
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued nine warning letters to manufacturers and distributors of unapproved and misbranded antimicrobial animal drugs for violating federal law. The FDA is concerned about the misuse of antimicrobials that are also used in human medicine, contributing to antimicrobial resistance. The products, marketed for minor species such as aquarium fish and pet birds, contain important antimicrobials like amoxicillin and erythromycin, and are being sold over the counter without FDA verification. The FDA's director, Tracey Forfa, warns that unapproved animal drugs pose a two-fold risk to public health due to their potential safety and effectiveness issues and the risk of antimicrobial resistance. The FDA encourages consumers, veterinarians, and health care providers to report adverse events associated with these products. The companies receiving warning letters must respond within 15 days to address the violations, or face potential legal action, including product seizure and a court order to stop manufacturing and distributing unapproved products.

title: Joint Federal Operation Results in Seizure of More Than $18 Million in Illegal E-Cigarettes
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) seized approximately 1.4 million units of unauthorized e-cigarette products, including Elf Bar, during a three-day joint operation. The estimated retail value of the seized products is more than $18 million. The FDA Commissioner, Robert M. Califf, stated that the agency will continue to stop the flow of illegal e-cigarettes into the United States. The operation was conducted at Los Angeles International Airport, where the team examined incoming shipments for potentially violative items. The seized products were found to be flavored disposable e-cigarettes, with fruit flavors being the most popular. The FDA has authorized 23 tobacco-flavored e-cigarette products and has issued over 650 warning letters to firms for manufacturing, selling, and distributing new tobacco products without marketing authorization.

title: Federal Court Enters Consent Decree Against Pharmasol for Distributing Adulterated Drugs
body_summary: The U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts has ordered Pharmasol Corporation, a Massachusetts-based company, and President Marc L. Badia to stop distributing drugs until they comply with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic (FD&C) Act. The company was found to have unlawfully distributed adulterated drugs, meaning they do not meet manufacturing quality requirements. Pharmasol manufactures and distributes over-the-counter and prescription drugs, including topical corticosteroids and inhalant anesthetics. The company was under contract with multiple pharmaceutical companies. The consent decree prohibits the company and Badia from manufacturing, preparing, or distributing any drug unless they meet certain requirements to ensure compliance with the FD&C Act and regulations. This decision was made after repeated warnings from the FDA, which cited customer complaints of product leakage and the company's failure to investigate. The decree was filed along with a complaint by the U.S. Department of Justice.

title: FDA Advances Reorganization Proposal for Unified Human Foods Program, Field Operations and Additional Modernization Efforts
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is updating its efforts to create a unified Human Foods Program and a new Office of Regulatory Affairs model. The proposed changes aim to strengthen the agency's ability to oversee and protect the human food supply and other products. The FDA's reorganization package is now under review at the US Department of Health and Human Services, with a timeline for implementation expected in 2024. The proposed changes include: making the Human Foods Program solely responsible for consumer complaints, renaming the Office of Regulatory Affairs as the Office of Inspections and Investigations, and establishing an Office of the Chief Medical Officer. The FDA has also merged the Office of Counterterrorism and Emerging Threats and the Office of Regulatory Science and Innovation, and created an Office of Enterprise Transformation.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that growth of economic activity has slowed from its strong pace in the third quarter. Job gains have moderated since earlier in the year but remain strong, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation has eased over the past year but remains elevated. The U.S. banking system is sound and resilient. Tighter financial and credit conditions for households and businesses are likely to weigh on economic activity, hiring, and inflation. The extent of these effects remains uncertain. The Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent. The Committee will continue to assess additional information and its implications for monetary policy. In determining the extent of any additional policy firming that may be appropriate to return inflation to 2 percent over time, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in its previously announced plans. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Austan D. Goolsbee; Patrick Harker; Philip N. Jefferson; Neel Kashkari; Adriana D. Kugler; Lorie K. Logan; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: FDA Creates New Advisory Committee for Evaluation of Genetic Metabolic Disease Treatments
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has created a new advisory committee to provide independent, knowledgeable advice and recommendations on potential treatments for genetic metabolic diseases. The committee, known as the Genetic Metabolic Diseases Advisory Committee, will consist of nine voting members, including a consumer representative and an industry representative. Committee members will evaluate evidence on key issues and offer recommendations for FDA consideration. The committee will be comprised of experts in metabolic genetics, management of inborn errors of metabolism, small population trial design, translational science, pediatrics, epidemiology, or statistics, and related specialties. The advisory committee has been established to advise the agency on products used for the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of genetic metabolic diseases under the Division of Rare Diseases and Medical Genetics.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index Report for November
body_summary: The report demonstrates progress in lowering inflation to 3.1 percent, down from its peak, while maintaining low unemployment below 4 percent for 50 years. Workers' wages and household wealth have increased due to the decline in inflation. Prices for various products have fallen over the last year, including cars, gas, TVs, toys, appliances, eggs, and milk. The President is fighting to reduce insulin, prescription drug, health insurance premium, and utility bill costs, as well as eliminate hidden fees. Congressional Republicans do not have a plan to lower costs for families, instead focusing on benefits for the wealthy and big corporations. The President will continue to fight to bring down costs and promote economic growth with a strong middle class.

title: Statement on Food and Drug Administration Approval of Gene Therapies To Treat Sickle-Cell Disease
body_summary: The U.S. Government has made a major breakthrough in treating sickle-cell disease, a condition affecting 100,000 Americans. This announcement represents the power of medical innovation to improve lives and holds promise for developing additional lifesaving treatments. The administration will continue to accelerate the development of cures for rare diseases and support medical research and innovation that achieved this breakthrough.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Report on the Employment Situation in November
body_summary: The economy created 199,000 jobs in November, bringing the total to over 14 million jobs since the president took office. The unemployment rate has remained below 4 percent for 22 months, and inflation has fallen by two-thirds. Workers' paychecks and household wealth are higher now than before the pandemic, after adjusting for inflation. The president's top economic priority is to lower costs for hard-working Americans. The president is taking steps to bring down prescription drug costs, health insurance premiums, and utility bills. They are also calling on large corporations to pass along the savings to consumers. In contrast, Congressional Republicans are fighting to raise prescription drug costs, lower taxes for the wealthy, and cut Medicare and Social Security.

title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapies to Treat Patients with Sickle Cell Disease
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved two cell-based gene therapies, Casgevy and Lyfgenia, for the treatment of sickle cell disease (SCD) in patients 12 years and older. Casgevy is the first FDA-approved therapy utilizing CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing technology. Both therapies use a patient's own blood stem cells, which are modified, and are given as a one-time, single-dose infusion as part of a hematopoietic stem cell transplant. Casgevy was approved for patients with recurrent vaso-occlusive crises, while Lyfgenia was approved for patients with a history of vaso-occlusive events. The therapies have shown promising results, with 93.5% of patients achieving freedom from severe vaso-occlusive episodes with Casgevy and 88% of patients achieving complete resolution of vaso-occlusive events with Lyfgenia. The FDA has granted Priority Review, Orphan Drug, Fast Track, and Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy designations to both applications.

title: FDA Roundup: December 8, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced that STARis is now available for voluntary use for certain PMA Submissions. STARis an interactive PDF form that guides applicants through the medical device submission process, aiming to enhance submission quality and ensure comprehensive data for premarket review. The updated STAR Template includes a guide following the cybersecurity recommendations for medical devices, promoting consistency and efficient review. Additionally, the FDA initiated an onsite inspection at the Austrofoods facility in Ecuador due to elevated lead levels in cinnamon applesauce pouches, and updated adverse event report numbers and CDC case counts.

title: FDA Roundup: December 5, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing an at-a-glance summary of news from around the agency. Registration opened for the FDA's virtual Rare Disease Day on Friday, March 1, 2024, which is dedicated to patients and health care professionals. The FDA also published an article titled "The Importance of Clinical Trial Transparency and FDA Oversight" by Robert M. Califf, M.D., Commissioner of Food and Drugs. The agency granted accelerated approval to pirtobrutinib (Jaypirca, Eli Lilly and Company) for adults with chronic lymphocytic leukemia or small lymphocytic lymphoma who have received at least two prior lines of therapy. A virtual public workshop is scheduled for December 12-13, 2023, to discuss adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) diagnosis, treatment, and implications for drug development.

title: FDA, USDA and EPA Propose National Strategy to Reduce U.S. Food Loss and Waste
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, U.S. Department of Agriculture, and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency released a national strategy to reduce food loss and waste in the U.S. by 50% by 2030. The strategy is a continuation of the agencies' efforts to build a more sustainable future. In the U.S., food waste is a significant issue, with 100 million tons of municipal waste being organic waste and 66 million tons of that being food. The strategy identifies opportunities to reduce food loss and waste across the entire supply chain. FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf expressed support for the mission, encouraging the public to comment on practical ways to reduce food waste. The strategy features four objectives, including preventing food loss and waste, increasing organic waste recycling, and supporting policies that incentivize prevention and recycling. The draft strategy highlights actions that the agencies can take, such as contributing to a national consumer education campaign and working with the food industry to adopt digital tracing technologies. The public comment period begins on December 5 and will remain open for 30 days.

title: FDA Roundup: December 1, 2023
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has rolled out new tools and FAQs to inform stakeholders about the Food Traceability Rule and help covered entities come into compliance. The rule aims to facilitate faster identification and removal of potentially contaminated food from the market, resulting in fewer foodborne illnesses and deaths. The FDA is also evaluating the potential for device failures with syringes manufactured in China, particularly those made of plastic, and plans to work with manufacturers to ensure adequate corrective actions are taken.

The agency has also updated its advisory on the Investigation of Elevated Lead Levels in Cinnamon Apple Puree Pouches, which was linked to a root cause investigation conducted by Wanabana USA and Austrofood. The investigation suggests that the cinnamon used to manufacture the recalled products was supplied by Negocios Asociados Mayoristas S.A., a third-party distribution company in Ecuador. The FDA is continuing to work with Ecuadorian authorities to investigate the source of the contamination.

Additionally, the FDA has proposed to classify certain unclassified, wound dressings and liquid wound washes containing antimicrobials or other chemicals into three separate classification regulations. The proposed classification is intended to subject these devices to special controls and premarket notification requirements, with different timelines for class II and class III devices.

title: Proclamation 10681—International Day of Persons With Disabilities, 2023
body_summary: The President of the United States of America has recommitted to building a world where disabled people are treated with dignity and respect, and afforded equal opportunities. Since the beginning of his career, he has worked hard to change the laws that discriminated against disabled people, co-sponsoring the Rehabilitation Act and the Americans with Disabilities Act. Over 180 nations have passed similar laws, but there is still more to do at home and abroad. The President's Administration has taken action to improve access to healthcare, invest in accessibility, and promote disability rights worldwide. He has launched initiatives to promote labor rights, increase infrastructure accessibility, and integrate disability rights into foreign policy. The President has proclaimed December 3, 2023, as International Day of Persons with Disabilities, calling on Americans to observe the day with ceremonies, activities, and programs.

title: Statement on North Carolina's Medicaid Expansion Under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: The United States is moving closer to providing high-quality, affordable health care to all Americans. North Carolina, the 40th state to expand Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act, is now covering 600,000 residents, including 300,000 immediately. This expansion, thanks to Governor Roy Cooper's leadership, will help keep rural hospitals open. The Affordable Care Act, which covers 40 million people, is under threat from MAGA Republicans who want to repeal it. Repealing the law would put care at risk, especially in states like North Carolina. The speaker proposes strengthening the Affordable Care Act to reduce healthcare and prescription drug costs, while expanding Medicaid in the remaining 10 states.

title: FDA Cautions Public of Safety Issue with Philips’ DreamStation 2 CPAP Machines
body_summary: The US FDA is alerting patients and healthcare providers about an emerging safety issue with Philips Respironics' DreamStation 2 Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) machines, which can cause thermal issues, including fires, smoke, burns, and other signs of overheating. The agency has received over 270 reports of thermal issues between Aug. 1, 2023, and Nov. 15, 2023, and is in discussions with the company to mitigate the risk to patients. The FDA recommends users to carefully monitor machines for signs of overheating, follow the manufacturer's instructions, and inspect the machine for unusual smells or changes before and after each use. The agency will continue to analyze and address this issue and provide updates as necessary.

title: FDA Roundup: November 28, 2023
body_summary: The FDA is issuing a drug safety communication warning that antiseizure medicines levetiracetam (Keppra, Keppra XR, Elepsia XR, Spritam) and clobazam (Onfi, Sympazan) can cause a rare but serious reaction that can be life-threatening if not diagnosed and treated quickly.
