The FDA is also investigating reports of T-cell malignancies in patients who received treatment with BCMA- or CD19-directed autologous CAR T cell immunotherapies. The agency is requiring warnings about this risk to be added to the prescribing information and patientMedication Guides for these medicines. The FDA has been implementing the Drug Supply Chain Security Act since 2013, and it has published a Small Entity Compliance Guide to help small entities comply with recent changes made to the final rule for Milk and Cream Products and Yogurt Products. The FDA has withdrawn as a member of the Global Harmonization Working Party, but will continue to work with the International Medical Device Regulators Forum. The agency has approved nirogacestat (Ogsiveo) for adult patients with progressing desmoid tumors. The FDA has issued updates to the Outbreak Advisory for Listeria monocytogenes linked to peaches, plums, and nectarines, and has issued guidance on COVID-19: Developing Drugs and Biological Products for Treatment or Prevention.

title: FDA Approves First Therapy for Rare Type of Non-Cancerous Tumors
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Ogsiveo tablets for adult patients with progressing desmoid tumors. Ogsiveo is the first drug approved for the treatment of desmoid tumors, a rare subtype of soft tissue sarcomas. Desmoid tumors are non-cancerous but can be locally aggressive. The FDA evaluated the effectiveness of Ogsiveo in an international, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 142 adult patients. The trial demonstrated that Ogsiveo provided clinically meaningful and statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival compared to placebo. Ogsiveo was granted Priority Review, Fast Track, and Breakthrough Therapy designations, as well as Orphan-Drug designation for the treatment of desmoid tumors. The approval was granted to SpringWorks Therapeutics Inc.

title: FDA Roundup: November 21, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued several safety communications and alerts regarding various products. The FDA issued a warning to consumers not to purchase or use Neptune's Fix products due to reports of seizures and loss of consciousness. The agency also issued a recall for SoClean2 and SoClean3 equipment used in CPAP devices and accessories. The FDA will host a virtual public meeting on January 23-24, 2024, to discuss advancing drug development for the prevention of preterm birth. Additionally, the agency published a final rule on direct-to-consumer prescription drug advertisements, established standards for presenting major side effects and contraindications in a clear and conspicuous manner. The FDA has also issued alerts to health care providers about the use of certain syringe types and to consumers about an outbreak of Listeria monocytogenes linked to stone fruit and Salmonella Sundsvall in cantaloupes.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary:
Here is the final summary:

A joint Federal Open Market Committee and Board of Governors meeting was held on October 31-November 1, 2023. The manager reviewed financial market developments, noting tighter conditions driven by higher Treasury yields, lower equity prices, and a stronger dollar. The Federal Reserve's balance sheet runoff continued smoothly, with reduced holdings of Treasury securities, agency debt, and agency mortgage-backed securities. Interest rates on loans, credit cards, and fixed-income securities rose, with corporate bond yields increasing more than Treasury yields. The Committee maintained its target range for the federal funds rate at 5¼ to 5½ percent, citing strong economic activity and moderate job gains. Inflation remained elevated, and participants agreed to continue reducing Federal Reserve's securities holdings to achieve maximum employment and inflation at 2 percent over time.

title: FDA Roundup: November 17, 2023
body_summary: The US FDA marked its 15th anniversary by publishing an interview with former FDA chief of staff Susan Winckler. The agency also announced initiatives to improve pulse oximeter accuracy and approved new drugs, including enzalutamide for prostate cancer and capivasertib for breast cancer. The FDA investigated elevated lead levels in cinnamon applesauce pouches and issued warning letters to online retailers selling unauthorized e-cigarettes. Additionally, the FDA released a guidance on in silico methods for device development and premarket evaluation, set to be discussed during a webinar on January 11, 2024.

title: Proclamation 10675—National Family Week, 2023
body_summary: President Joseph R. Biden Jr. has proclaimed November 19-25, 2023, as National Family Week. He celebrates the importance of family, which he believes is the beginning, middle, and end of everything. The President has made significant investments in American families, including the American Rescue Plan, Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, and the Inflation Reduction Act, which have helped millions of families keep their homes, food on the table, and people on the job. The President has also taken action to revitalize American manufacturing, expand access to clean drinking water, and connect every home to high-speed internet.

title: Proclamation 10676—National Child's Day, 2023
body_summary: The President of the United States, Joseph R. Biden Jr., has proclaimed November 20, 2023, as National Child's Day. The proclamation recognizes the importance of the nation's children, who are the dreamers and doers of the future. The President's Administration has invested billions of dollars in America's schools, prioritizing teacher recruitment, tutoring programs, and infrastructure improvements. The Administration has also expanded access to reliable high-speed internet, lowered healthcare costs, and promoted healthy school meals. Additionally, the President has signed significant gun safety legislation and addressed the youth mental health crisis, including measures to increase school psychologists and counselors. The proclamation also emphasizes the need to protect children's health and safety online and to tackle climate change, as evidenced by the Inflation Reduction Act.

title: Federal Judge Enters Consent Decrees Against Utah-Based Dietary Supplement Distributor and Manufacturer of Balance of Nature Products
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has ordered two companies, Evig LLC and Premium Production LLC, and their executives, Douglas Lex Howard and Ryan Petersen, to stop producing and selling their dietary supplement products until they come into compliance with federal regulations. The companies, which market products as dietary supplements, have been found to violate current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) requirements and have made unapproved claims about their products. The FDA has not approved Balance of Nature products for any use, despite the company's claims that they can diagnose, cure, or treat diseases. The companies have been warned multiple times about their violations, but failed to address them. The FDA is taking action to prevent products that potentially put people's health at risk.

title: Federal Court Enters Consent Decree Against Arizona-based Company for Distribution of Unapproved Contraceptive Drugs
body_summary: The U.S. District Court for the District of Arizona has entered a consent decree ordering Smart Women's Choice, Inc. and its CEO, Jennifer A. Richard, to stop distributing drugs until they comply with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. Smart Women's Choice and Richard unlawfully distributed unapproved new drugs in the US marketplace. The FDA has not approved the company's drug, a vaginal cream marketed as a contraceptive, despite a 2021 warning letter advising against its distribution. The consent decree prohibits the company, Richard, and those in active concert with them from manufacturing, preparing, and distributing drugs unless they meet specific requirements and receive written notice from the FDA that they are in compliance.

title: Proclamation 10674—National Rural Health Day, 2023
body_summary: The President of the United States of America issues a proclamation on National Rural Health Day. America's rural communities are crucial to the nation's economy and future. The President renews commitment to investing in rural communities, delivering affordable quality healthcare, and addressing healthcare disparities. Since 2010, over 150 rural hospitals have closed, affecting local economies. The American Rescue Plan provided $8.5 billion to rural providers, and scholarships and student loan assistance have been offered to rural clinicians and nurses. The President has invested in rural broadband, telehealth, and mental health services. The Administration's Blueprint for Addressing the Maternal Health Crisis and Unity Agenda aim to improve maternal health and address mental health and substance use disorder services. The President has also released a national strategy to end hunger and reduce diet-related diseases in America by 2030.

title: Proclamation 10673—America Recycles Day, 2023
body_summary: The President of the United States recognizes the critical role recycling plays in addressing climate change and caring for the environment. The President reiterates the importance of recycling and reducing waste to secure a greener future. The Administration has invested in recycling through the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, and a National Recycling Strategy was released to promote best practices in recycling and waste management. The President calls upon manufacturers, businesses, and Americans to adopt sustainable practices, such as reducing single-use plastics and increasing recycling awareness. The President also proclaims November 15, 2023, as America Recycles Day, encouraging programs and activities to promote environmental efforts.

title: Memorandum on the White House Initiative on Women's Health Research
body_summary: By the authority vested in me as President, I hereby direct the establishment of a White House Initiative on Women's Health Research, which will advance women's health research in the United States. The Initiative will be led by a Chair designated by the President and will consist of the heads of 21 executive departments and agencies, as well as offices. The mission of the Initiative is to advance women's health research, and its functions include assessing the Federal research landscape, setting priorities, improving coordination, and developing policy recommendations. The Initiative will also engage the scientific and research communities, identify opportunities for public-private partnerships, and assess opportunities to recruit and train women in health and biomedical research careers. The Initiative will provide recommendations to the President within 45 days of its establishment, and agencies and offices participating in the Initiative will bear their own expenses.

title: Joint Statement by President Biden and President Joko "Jokowi" Widodo of Indonesia
body_summary: US President Biden and Indonesian President Joko Widodo welcome each other, marking a new phase of bilateral cooperation and friendship between the two democracies. The US and Indonesia aim to elevate their relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, committing to cooperation on good governance, human rights, and sustainable development. They pledge to work together on promoting inclusive economic growth, reducing supply chain dependencies, and supporting sustainable development and critical minerals. The two leaders plan to strengthen health, energy, and economic ties through collaborations on infectious disease prevention, climate change mitigation, and clean energy development. They also agree on ASEAN centrality, Indo-Pacific cooperation, freedom of navigation in the South China Sea, and a two-state solution in the Middle East.

title: Proclamation 10672—National Apprenticeship Week, 2023
body_summary: The President of the United States of America has issued a proclamation to recommit to supporting Registered Apprenticeship programs. The programs offer workers direct pathways to good-paying jobs with dignity and respect. The administration has invested more in Registered Apprenticeships and career technology education programs than any previous administration in American history. Over 4,000 new Registered Apprenticeship programs have been developed, and more than one million new apprentices have been hired. The administration has also launched initiatives to strengthen and diversify Registered Apprenticeships across industries, including creating clean energy apprenticeships and jobs in communities that have suffered legacy pollution. The President has urged Congress, state and local governments, educational institutions, industry and labor leaders, apprentices, and all Americans to support Registered Apprenticeship programs. The proclamation also declares November 12 through November 18, 2023, as National Apprenticeship Week.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Patients with Rare Inherited Blood Clotting Disorder
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Adzynma, a recombinant protein product, for prophylactic or on-demand enzyme replacement therapy in adult and pediatric patients with congenital thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (cTTP), a rare and life-threatening blood clotting disorder. The approval was granted based on the efficacy of Adzynma in reducing thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) events and manifestations. The product was administered intravenously once every other week for prophylactic therapy and once daily for on-demand therapy. The safety and effectiveness of Adzynma were demonstrated in a global study, with the most common side effects including headache, diarrhea, and abdominal pain. The FDA approved Adzynma for patients with cTTP, estimated to affect fewer than 1,000 people in the US, and granted the application Priority Review, Fast Track, and Orphan drug designations. The product is expected to provide a much-needed treatment option for patients with this life-threatening disorder.

title: FDA Clears First COVID-19 Home Antigen Test
body_summary: The US FDA has cleared the ACON Laboratories' Flowflex COVID-19 Antigen Home Test for marketing as an over-the-counter antigen test for COVID-19. The test is the first to be cleared for home use by symptomatic individuals within six days of symptom onset, and is intended for individuals aged 14 years or older testing themselves or adults testing individuals aged two years or older. The test correctly identified 89.8% of positive and 99.3% of negative samples in individuals with signs and symptoms of upper respiratory infection. The test was reviewed through the 510(k) premarket review pathway, and its clearance follows that of an earlier molecular home test.

title: FDA Approves First Vaccine to Prevent Disease Caused by Chikungunya Virus
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Ixchiq, the first chikungunya vaccine, for individuals 18 years of age and older at increased risk of exposure to the virus. The vaccine is administered as a single dose by injection into the muscle and is approved for use in tropical and subtropical regions of Africa, Southeast Asia, and parts of the Americas where chikungunya virus-carrying mosquitos are endemic. The most common symptoms of chikungunya include fever, joint pain, and a rash. The safety of Ixchiq was evaluated in two clinical studies, which showed that the most commonly reported side effects were headache, fatigue, and muscle pain. In addition, severe chikungunya-like adverse reactions occurred in 1.6% of Ixchiq recipients and two recipients were hospitalized. The vaccine is expected to prevent severe disease and prolonged health problems, particularly for older adults and individuals with underlying medical conditions.

title: FDA Approves New Medication for Chronic Weight Management
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Zepbound (tirzepatide) injection for chronic weight management in adults with obesity or overweight, with at least one weight-related condition. Tirzepatide, the active ingredient, is already approved for type 2 diabetes treatment. The approval addresses an unmet medical need for obesity and overweight in the US, where approximately 70% of American adults have obesity or overweight. Zepbound is administered once weekly and has been shown to reduce body weight by 5-10% in patients with obesity or overweight. The maximum approved dosage is 15 mg once weekly. Zepbound has been associated with side effects such as nausea and injection site reactions. It is contraindicated in patients with certain medical conditions, including medullary thyroid cancer and pancreatitis. The FDA granted Eli Lilly and Co. Priority Review and Fast Track designations for this indication.

title: FDA Roundup: November 7, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is issuing a safety communication warning consumers, healthcare providers, and healthcare facilities not to use recalled saline and sterile water medical products manufactured by Nurse Assist, LLC, due to potential sterility issues. The recalled products were sold under multiple brands and were available in various sizes and formats. The FDA has also recognized a key consensus standard to support device sponsors in addressing cybersecurity concerns. Additionally, the FDA has issued advisories regarding elevated lead levels linked to certain apple cinnamon pouches and cleared the Control-IQ Technology for marketing, which can automatically manage type 1 diabetes in children over 2 years old.

title: FDA Roundup: November 3, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is seeking public input on advancing health equity and facilitating access to digital health technologies for detecting prediabetes and type 2 diabetes, particularly in racial and ethnic minorities. The FDA has proposed to revoke the regulation authorizing the use of brominated vegetable oil (BVO) in food due to adverse health effects in animals at levels more closely approximating real-world human exposure. The FDA has issued a guidance on enforcement policy for certain supplements, revised the Emergency Use Authorization for Paxlovid, and released a summary of a recent article on cannabis research and drug development. Additionally, the FDA approved pembrolizumab for use in biliary tract cancer, and issued a Safety Alert regarding oysters harvested from Canada.

title: National Survey Shows Drop in E-Cigarette Use Among High School Students
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) released data from the 2023 National Youth Tobacco Survey (NYTS), showing that 10% of U.S. middle and high school students (2.8 million youth) reported current use of any tobacco product in 2023. Among high school students, current overall tobacco product use declined from 16.5% to 12.6%, primarily due to reduced e-cigarette use. E-cigarettes remained the most commonly used tobacco product among both high school and middle school students for the 10th year in a row. The FDA is taking enforcement action against retailers selling unauthorized e-cigarettes with youth appeal, including 22 civil money penalty actions in September and 20 additional actions announced today.

title: FDA Proposes to Ban Food Additive, Continues Assessments of Additional Chemicals
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration proposed to revoke the regulation authorizing the use of brominated vegetable oil (BVO) in food due to studies conducted in collaboration with the National Institutes of Health finding potential adverse health effects in humans. BVO is a vegetable oil modified with bromine, previously used in small amounts in beverages. The FDA no longer considers BVO "Generally Recognized as Safe" and is reviewing its use under food additive regulations. This action prioritizes risk, science, and regulatory authority, following recent toxicology studies and California's ban on BVO in that state. The FDA is also reviewing color additive regulations and plans to enhance its review of food chemical safety through the proposed Human Foods Program.

title: Statement on Health Insurance Enrollment Under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: The US government is making healthcare a right, not a privilege, for all Americans. As the open enrollment period begins on healthcare.gov, Americans can sign up for quality, affordable health coverage from January 15, 2024, to next year. Over 16 million people signed up for health insurance through the Affordable Care Act last year. Thanks to the Inflation Reduction Act, coverage is more affordable and accessible, with consumers saving $800 on premiums annually. Four in five customers can find quality coverage for less than $10 a month. If not through an employer, various affordable coverage options are available. The government has made progress in expanding coverage and lowering healthcare costs, saving families money and providing peace of mind.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity expanded at a strong pace in the third quarter. Job gains have moderated since earlier in the year but remain strong, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation remains elevated. The U.S. banking system is sound and resilient. Tighter financial and credit conditions for households and businesses are likely to weigh on economic activity, hiring, and inflation. The extent of these effects remains uncertain. The Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent. The Committee will continue to assess additional information and its implications for monetary policy. In determining the extent of additional policy firming that may be appropriate to return inflation to 2 percent over time, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in its previously announced plans. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Austan D. Goolsbee; Patrick Harker; Philip N. Jefferson; Neel Kashkari; Adriana D. Kugler; Lorie K. Logan; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: Implementation Note issued November 1, 2023
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on November 1, 2023: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 5.4 percent, effective November 2, 2023. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective November 2, 2023, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 5.5 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 5.3 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $60 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest into agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 5.5 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Proclamation 10660—Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience Month, 2023
body_summary: President Joe R. Biden Jr. issues a proclamation declaring November 2023 as Critical Infrastructure Security and Resilience Month. He reiterates the importance of protecting America's critical infrastructure from natural disasters, cyber threats, and other hazards that strain its supply chains and threaten national security. The President is committed to bolstering the nation's infrastructure through investments from various sources, including the American Rescue Plan, Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, Inflation Reduction Act, and CHIPS and Science Act. He highlights the need to improve cybersecurity and has appointed senior officials to address cyber threats. The President also announces international partnerships to develop sustainable infrastructure around the globe, including the Trans-African Corridor with the European Union.

title: FDA Approves Interchangeable Biosimilar for Multiple Inflammatory Diseases
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Wezlana (ustekinumab-auub) as a biosimilar to Stelara (ustekinumab) for multiple inflammatory diseases. Wezlana is approved to treat moderate to severe plaque psoriasis, active psoriatic arthritis, moderately to severely active Crohn’s disease, and moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis in adults and pediatric patients 6 years of age and older. The approval is based on a comprehensive review of scientific evidence showing Wezlana is highly similar to Stelara, with no clinically meaningful differences in safety and effectiveness. Wezlana is an interchangeable biosimilar, allowing for pharmacy-level substitution without consulting the prescriber. The FDA’s approval aims to increase access to safe and effective treatment options for patients with inflammatory diseases.

title: FDA Roundup: October 31, 2023
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is providing an update on news from around the agency. On Monday, the FDA posted interim results from a postmarket surveillance study on Essure, a permanently implanted birth control device for women. The study, which has completed three years of follow-up, will continue for another five years. Final analyses will be performed when the study concludes. The FDA remains committed to collecting and providing updates on the long-term safety and effectiveness of Essure. 

On Friday, the FDA accepted a master file for the Radiation Sterilization Master File Pilot Program, a voluntary program to help sterilize medical devices using new or improved modalities. The master file was submitted by Steris Corporation. 

The FDA also approved toripalimab-tpzi (LOQTORZ, Coherus BioSciences, Inc.) for the treatment of adults with metastatic or recurrent nasopharyngeal carcinoma. This approval demonstrates an improvement in overall survival and delaying disease progression when combined with chemotherapy. 

Additionally, the FDA announced that the outbreak of Listeria monocytogenes infections linked to recalled dairy and non-dairy products has ended, and the investigation is complete. The Ice Cream House and Real Kosher Ice Cream have voluntarily recalled all affected products.

title: Proclamation 10662—National Alzheimer's Disease Awareness Month, 2023
body_summary: The President of the United States declares November 2023 as National Alzheimer's Disease Awareness Month. Over six million Americans live with Alzheimer's, a devastating disease that deprives people of their memories, thoughts, and identity. The Administration has taken actions to help treat and prevent the disease, including securing $2.5 billion in funding for the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health and approving a prescription drug for some people. The Administration has also signed an Executive Order on Increasing Access to High-Quality Care and Supporting Caregivers, and the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services have announced a model offering comprehensive care management and coordination for people living with Alzheimer's. The President calls on the American people to honor and support those living with Alzheimer's and encourages them to visit www.Alzheimers.gov for evidence-based resources.

title: Executive Order 14110—Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
body_summary: US President Joseph R. Biden Jr. orders a Federal Government-wide approach to governing AI development and use safely and responsibly. The Federal Government will ensure the collection, use, and retention of data is lawful, secure, and mitigates privacy and confidentiality risks using privacy-enhancing technologies. Guidelines and standards for safe, secure, and trustworthy AI systems, including generative AI, are established within 270 days. The US Secretary of Commerce defines and updates technical conditions for models and computing clusters, and authorizes exemptions for IaaS providers. An AI safety board is established, and plans for AI pilot projects and a framework to mitigate biosecurity risks are developed. Immigration policies are reviewed and updated to attract experts in AI and other critical technologies. The Secretary of HHS prioritizes grantmaking for responsible AI development and use, and the US government promotes employee well-being, advances equity in the criminal justice system, and issues a directive to address AI use in various sectors.

title: FDA Roundup: October 27, 2023
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a summary of recent news from around the agency. Director Brian King of the FDA Center for Tobacco Products has published a statement summarizing the center's efforts to address an independent expert panel's evaluation. 

The FDA has cleared the first over-the-counter test for fentanyl detection, which can be used with a urine sample. The test provides preliminary results, and a more specific alternative method is required to obtain a confirmed result. 

Jeff Shuren, M.D., J.D., Director of the FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health, stated that this test is an example of the FDA's commitment to authorize tools that can reduce deaths associated with overdoses. 

The FDA has also approved a new oral corticosteroid for the treatment of Duchenne muscular dystrophy in patients 2 years of age and older. 

Commissioner Robert M. Califf recently traveled to India and published an article on the FDA Voices website. 

The FDA has issued a draft guidance on remote interactive evaluations of drug manufacturing and bioresearch monitoring facilities. 

The FDA has issued an Outbreak Advisory for Salmonella Thompson infections linked to fresh diced onions from Gills Onions of Oxnard, California. 

The FDA has approved Tibsovo for adult patients with relapsed or refractory myelodysplastic syndromes. 

The FDA, Health Canada, and the United Kingdom's Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency have jointly issued a Predetermined Change Control Plan for Machine Learning-Enabled Medical Devices.

title: FDA Raises Concerns About Probiotic Products Sold for Use in Hospitalized Preterm Infants
body_summary: The US FDA is warning healthcare providers and the public about the potential risks of using products containing live bacteria or yeast (probiotics) in preterm infants in hospital settings. The agency has issued two warning letters to companies for illegally selling their products for treating or preventing certain diseases in preterm infants. Probiotic products have been associated with invasive, potentially fatal disease, infection, and adverse events, including one infant death in 2023 and over two dozen reported adverse events in the US since 2018. The FDA has not approved any probiotic product for use as a drug or biological product in infants of any age. The agency requires approval of a Biologics License Application for these products to ensure they have been appropriately evaluated and meet rigorous manufacturing and testing standards. Healthcare providers who administer unapproved probiotic products must submit an Investigational New Drug application to the agency.

title: FDA Roundup: October 24, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Medtronic's Aurora EV-ICD System for treating patients with life-threatening abnormally fast heart rhythms. The FDA also granted accelerated approval to entrectinib (Rozlytrek, Genentech Inc.) for pediatric patients with solid tumors and a specific gene mutation. Additionally, the FDA approved a new oral pellet formulation for entrectinib and issued a Safety Alert advising consumers not to eat oysters from Future Seafoods, Inc. due to possible contamination. The FDA's Office of Women's Health will host a free public webinar on November 8, 2023, to discuss decentralized clinical trials and other strategies for bringing clinical research to patients.

title: FDA Approves New Therapy for Rare Form of Blood Cancers Called Myelodysplastic Syndromes
body_summary: The US FDA approved Tibsovo for treating adult patients with relapsed or refractory myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) with an IDH1 mutation. This is the first targeted therapy approved for this indication. The FDA also approved the Abbott RealTime IDH1 Assay as a companion diagnostic. Tibsovo was previously approved for certain adults with Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML) and locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma. The approval was based on an open-label, single-arm, multicenter study of 18 adult patients with relapsed or refractory MDS with an IDH1 mutation. The study showed a 39% complete remission rate, and six out of nine patients who required transfusions no longer needed them after treatment. The most common side effects were similar to those seen with ivosidenib monotherapy. Tibsovo may cause QTc prolongation and differentiation syndrome, which can be fatal if not treated. The FDA granted Priority Review, Breakthrough Therapy, and Orphan Drug designations for the indication. Approval was granted to Servier Pharmaceuticals LLC for Tibsovo and Abbott Laboratories for the Abbott RealTime IDH1 Assay.

title: FDA Roundup: October 20, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced fiscal year 2024 fee rates and payment procedures for animal drugs subject to user fees under the Animal Drug and Animal Generic Drug User Fee Amendments of 2023. The Animal Drug User Fee Act (ADUFA) and Animal Generic Drug User Fee Act (AGDUFA) authorize the FDA to collect fees for certain animal drug applications and products. ADUFA V and AGDUFA IV reauthorize the FDA to collect user fees through FY 2028. The FDA has also authorized an extension for the shelf life of Gohibic (vilobelimab) for specific lots, from 24 months to 30 months. The FDA has removed certain ventilation-related products from the medical device shortage list and added 171 AI/ML-enabled devices to the list of legally marketed devices in the United States.

title: Joint Statement by President Biden, President Charles Yvon Michel of the European Council, and President Ursula von der Leyen of the European Commission
body_summary: The US and EU reaffirm their commitment to a transatlantic partnership to secure peace, stability, and prosperity globally. They aim to promote security, stability, and prosperity in North Africa and the Indo-Pacific, supporting ASEAN centrality and unity. The US and EU call on China to engage on global challenges and build constructive relations, pushing for a level playing field in economic relations and addressing human rights concerns. They also aim to strengthen their partnership by intensifying climate action, promoting renewable energy, and investing in research collaboration, including reducing methane emissions and promoting a climate-neutral economy. Furthermore, the US and EU plan to build a more secure cyberspace, promote high cybersecurity standards, and support partner countries in countering foreign information manipulation and interference, with increased transatlantic people-to-people exchanges and cooperation on modern-day trade challenges.

title: FDA Deputy Commissioner for Human Foods Commits to Fulfilling Vision of Proposed Program
body_summary:
US Food and Drug Administration Commissioner Robert M. Califf has proposed a unified Human Foods Program (HFP) to transform the agency's human foods enterprise. The proposed program aims to protect and promote the health and wellness of all US consumers by focusing on three priority areas: preventing foodborne illness, decreasing diet-related chronic disease through improved nutrition, and safeguarding the food supply through the safe use of chemicals and dietary supplements.

As the first Deputy Commissioner for Human Foods, the author is committed to executing the proposed framework and upholding the principle of protecting and promoting consumer health. The proposed HFP includes creating an Office of Critical Foods to manage the regulation of infant formula and medical foods, and a Nutrition Center of Excellence to focus on nutrition policies and initiatives.

The author plans to work with industry, federal partners, and other stakeholders to prevent foodborne illness outbreaks, reduce diet-related chronic disease, and ensure the safe use of chemicals and dietary supplements. The proposed program also includes creating an Office of Food Chemical Safety, Dietary Supplements, and Innovation to leverage scientific expertise and facilitate the safe use of innovative ingredients.

The FDA has already made significant progress in reducing diet-related chronic disease, such as reducing sodium across the food supply and updating labels to make them more accessible. The author looks forward to sharing further details about the proposed program and its goals in the coming months.

title: FDA Roundup: October 17, 2023
body_summary: The US FDA is soliciting public comments on the state of innovation in clinical trial design and conduct, with a public workshop planned for March 19-20, 2024. The FDA also published a new draft guidance for the development of antibacterial drugs for Diabetic Foot Infections. Additionally, the agency approved pembrolizumab for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer, and announced a webinar on its proposed rule regarding laboratory developed tests. The FDA also approved nivolumab for the adjuvant treatment of completely resected Stage IIB/C melanoma in patients 12 years and older.

title: Statement on the Open Enrollment Period for Medicare
body_summary: The main action is that Medicare open enrollment has started, and seniors and their families can see the progress made in lowering healthcare costs. Starting January 1, 2024, due to the Inflation Reduction Act, prescription drug costs will be more affordable. Key changes include: high-drug spending seniors having out-of-pocket costs capped at about $3,500 in 2024 and all enrollees at $2,000 in 2025, low-income seniors and disabled people getting extra help with premiums and cost-sharing, and the cap on insulin price at $35 per month, with recommended vaccines becoming free. The speaker is proud of the cost savings delivered for millions of seniors and families, while Republicans voted to keep healthcare costs high.

title: FDA Roundup: October 13, 2023
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is hosting a public panel discussion on October 19, 2023, with the European Medicines Agency, to address the experience of living with metastatic breast cancer. The panel will feature international speakers with varying perspectives on breast cancer. Richard Pazdur, director of the FDA's Oncology Center of Excellence, stated that the collaboration aims to highlight the global experiences of patients living with metastatic breast cancer.

The FDA also approved encorafenib (Braftovi) with binimetinib for adult patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer with a BRAF V600E mutation. Companion diagnostics, FoundationOne CDx and FoundationOne Liquid CDx, were approved as well. The most common adverse reactions were fatigue, nausea, and diarrhea.

The FDA posted a list of guidance documents it intends to publish in Fiscal Year 2024. The public is invited to submit comments on the guidance documents at www.Regulations.gov. The FDA authorized marketing of the HistoSonics Inc. Edison System for non-invasive destruction of liver tumors using focused ultrasound.

title: FDA Denies Marketing of Six Flavored Vuse Alto E-Cigarette Products Following Determination They Do Not Meet Public Health Standard
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued marketing denial orders to R.J. Reynolds Vapor Company for six flavored e-cigarette products under its Vuse Alto brand. The products include three menthol-flavored and three mixed berry-flavored products with three nicotine strengths each. The company must not market or distribute these products in the US, risking FDA enforcement. The FDA evaluated premarket tobacco product applications and determined that the applications lacked sufficient evidence to demonstrate the products' benefits outweighing their risks to public health. This decision was based on a lack of evidence showing the flavored products provided an added benefit for adult smokers compared to tobacco-flavored products. The products are subject to the 2009 Family Smoking Prevention and Tobacco Control Act, which requires a public health standard for tobacco product marketing.

title: FDA Establishes New Advisory Committee on Digital Health Technologies
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced the creation of a new Digital Health Advisory Committee to explore the complex scientific and technical issues related to digital health technologies. The committee will advise the FDA on issues related to digital health technologies, providing relevant expertise and perspective. The committee should be fully operational in 2024. The committee will consist of a core of nine voting members and will solicit views from individuals with technical and scientific expertise from diverse disciplines and backgrounds. The FDA aims to advance health equity by expanding access to digital health technologies, bringing prevention, wellness, and healthcare to all people. The committee's goal is to ensure digital health medical devices are designed and targeted to meet the needs of diverse populations.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A Federal Open Market Committee joint meeting with the Board of Governors was held on September 19-20, 2023. The manager reviewed developments in financial markets over the intermeeting period, noting a higher expected trajectory for the policy rate at longer horizons and higher term premiums. Participants noted solid business activity despite higher interest rates and softer conditions, with housing demand resilient but price sensitive households becoming more prominent. Labor market remained tight, with job gains slowing and supply-demand balance improving. Inflation had moderated, but remained above 2% objective. The Committee maintained the target federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent, continued reducing securities holdings, and reaffirmed commitment to returning inflation to 2 percent over time.

title: FDA Roundup: October 6, 2023
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has updated its infant formula compliance program to comprehensively outline its approach for inspections, sample collection, and compliance activities. The FDA remains committed to strengthening the safety and oversight of the infant formula industry. 

The agency provided an update on the recalled Philips ventilators, BiPAP machines, and CPAP machines associated with the breakdown of PE-PUR foam, and continues to monitor the company's recall progress. The FDA remains unsatisfied with the status of this recall and is taking steps to protect patient health and safety. 

A new resource section on FDA.gov was published, including a comprehensive timeline of FDA activities related to the June 2021 recall, to provide timely and accurate information. The FDA authorized the marketing of Marizyme, Inc.'s DuraGraft Vascular Conduit Solution for flushing and short-term storage of saphenous vein grafts. 

The FDA signed a partnership agreement with the Pennsylvania Department of Agriculture to focus on inventory reconciliation, reducing foodborne illness risk, and minimizing duplication of work. The FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research is hosting its 2023 NanoDay Symposium: Continuous Manufacturing of Nanomaterials on October 11.

title: FDA Takes Steps to Advance the Development of Novel Therapies for Stimulant Use Disorders
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration published a new draft guidance to assist sponsors in developing treatments for stimulant use disorders. The guidance aims to provide the FDA's current thinking on the overall development program and clinical trial design for drugs and biologics to support treatment of moderate to severe cocaine use disorder, methamphetamine use disorder, and prescription stimulant use disorder. Marta Sokolowska, Ph.D., deputy center director for Substance Use and Behavioral Health in FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, stated that the guidance will support the development of novel therapies critically needed to address treatment gaps. The draft guidance contains recommendations on clinical trial design, trial conduct, data collection, and new drug application requirements. The agency has previously taken action to promote safe use and appropriate prescribing of prescription stimulants and has funded research projects to inform prevention of prescription stimulant misuse, addiction, and overdose. Comments on the draft guidance are requested within 60 days.

title: FDA Authorizes Updated Novavax COVID-19 Vaccine Formulated to Better Protect Against Currently Circulating Variants
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) amended the emergency use authorization (EUA) of the Novavax COVID-19 Vaccine, Adjuvanted for use in individuals 12 years of age and older, adding the 2023-2024 formula. The updated vaccine addresses circulating variants and provides better protection against serious COVID-19 consequences. Eligible individuals receive one dose, while unvaccinated individuals receive two doses. The vaccine has been updated to include the spike protein from the SARS-CoV-2 omicron variant lineage XBB.1.5. The authorization follows recent approvals of updated mRNA COVID-19 vaccines for 2023-2024, manufactured by ModernaTX Inc. and Pfizer Inc. Peter Marks, M.D., Ph.D., director of the FDA’s Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, stated that the vaccines have saved lives and provided better protection. The FDA evaluated manufacturing and non-clinical immune response data, as well as clinical trial and postmarketing data, to support the change to the 2023-2024 formula. The agency granted the emergency use authorization to Novavax Inc. of Gaithersburg, Maryland.

title: FDA Roundup: October 3, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced a public workshop titled "Defining 'Candy-Like' Nonprescription Drug Products" in partnership with the University of Maryland Center of Excellence in Regulatory Science and Innovation. The workshop will take place on October 30 from 8:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. ET. The FDA also issued minor updates to the final guidance for Electronic Submissions Template for Medical Devices 510(k) Submissions, requiring all 510(k) submissions to be electronic submissions starting October 1, 2023. Additionally, the FDA approved Rivfloza, indicated for lowering urinary oxalate levels in children and adults with a rare genetic disorder, and Tofidence, a biosimilar product for treating rheumatoid arthritis. The FDA also granted marketing authorization for Procise IFX and Procise ADLassays, two in vitro diagnostic tests for measuring medication levels used to treat inflammatory bowel diseases.

title: FDA Launches Pilot Program to Help Further Accelerate Development of Rare Disease Therapies
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is launching a pilot program, the Support for Clinical Trials Advancing Rare Disease Therapeutics (START) Pilot Program, to accelerate the development of novel drug and biological products for rare diseases. The program aims to facilitate more efficient development of potentially life-saving therapies with rare disease indications. Selected sponsors will be able to obtain frequent advice and regular communication with FDA staff to address product-specific development issues.

The program is open to sponsors of products currently in clinical trials under an active Investigational New Drug application, regulated by the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER) and/or the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER). Eligibility criteria differ between CBER and CDER-regulated products.

The FDA will accept applications for the program between January 2, 2024, and March 1, 2024, and will select up to three participants for each center. Pilot participants will be selected based on application readiness. The agency may consider a second iteration of the program based on feedback from selected sponsors.

The FDA has also undertaken additional efforts to enhance and expedite the availability of therapies intended to treat rare diseases. These include publishing a Request for Information and an adocet for stakeholder feedback, as well as publishing draft guidance documents on cell and gene therapy.

title: FDA Grants First Marketing Authorization for a DNA Test to Assess Predisposition for Dozens of Cancer Types
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration granted de novo marketing authorization for the Invitae Common Hereditary Cancers Panel, an in vitro diagnostic test that can help detect hundreds of genetic variants associated with an elevated risk of developing certain cancers. The test evaluates DNA from a blood sample to identify variants in 47 genes linked to an increased cancer risk. The test's director, Jeff Shuren, said it provides a public health tool that offers individuals more information about their health and can help guide physicians to provide appropriate monitoring and therapy. The test is not intended to identify all known genes associated with cancer predisposition, and patients should discuss their personal/family history with a healthcare professional. The FDA reviewed the test under its De Novo premarket review pathway, and Invitae tested over 9,000 clinical samples, achieving ≥99.0% accuracy. The test's performance is validated, and the FDA is establishing special controls to mitigate risks, including false positive and false negative test results.

title: FDA Roundup: September 29, 2023
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has released a video titled "Importing FDA-Regulated Products: Human Foods" providing basic information for importers, foreign suppliers/exporters, and customs brokers on importing safe and compliant food into the US.

The FDA has awarded 10 new clinical trial studies, funded by Congress through the Orphan Products Grants Program, to support the development of medical products for rare diseases. These grants will provide over $27 million of funding to clinical researchers over the next four years.

The FDA has also awarded over $16.9 million in funding over the next four years to support research through its Rare Neurodegenerative Disease Grant Program, including studies for amyotrophic lateral disease (ALS) and other rare neurodegenerative diseases.

The FDA has released two guidance documents for sprout operations, and issued a Warning Letter to Infinant Health, Inc. for its product Evivo with MCT Oil, which is an unapproved new drug and unlicensed biological product.

The FDA has issued a Dear Healthcare Provider Letter to provide important safety information to healthcare providers on the use of products containing live bacteria or yeast in preterm infants.

The FDA's Center for Veterinary Medicine has released its FY 2024-2028 plan for supporting antimicrobial stewardship in veterinary settings, which kicks off on October 1, 2023.

The FDA has approved bosutinib (Bosulif, Pfizer) for pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with chronic phase (CP) Ph+ chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML).

The FDA has announced a public workshop "Advancing the Development of Pediatric Therapeutics (ADEPT 8) on Drug Dosing in Pediatric Patients with Renal Impairment," which will be held on November 30 and December 1.

title: FDA Proposes Rule Aimed at Helping to Ensure Safety and Effectiveness of Laboratory Developed Tests
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced a proposed rule to help ensure the safety and effectiveness of laboratory-developed tests (LDTs), which play a significant role in healthcare. The rule aims to amend the FDA's regulations to make LDTs devices under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, including when the manufacturer is a laboratory. The FDA intends to provide greater oversight of LDTs through a phaseout of its general enforcement discretion approach. The proposed phaseout would help protect public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of IVDs offered as LDTs. The FDA believes this proposal would advance responsible innovation by better assuring the safety and effectiveness of IVDs offered as LDTs and removing a disincentive for non-laboratory manufacturers to develop novel tests.

title: FDA Seeks Fines Against 22 Retailers for Selling Illegal Youth-Appealing E-Cigarettes
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued complaints for civil money penalties (CMPs) against 22 retailers for the illegal sale of Elf Bar/EB Design e-cigarettes. The FDA had previously warned each retailer to stop selling unauthorized tobacco products, but they failed to correct the violations. The agency is seeking a maximum civil money penalty of $19,192 for each retailer. The FDA has also issued 168 additional warning letters to brick-and-mortar retailers selling Elf Bar/EB Design products. Retailers have 30 days to respond with steps to correct the violations. The FDA has issued over 400 warning letters to retailers and more than 600 warning letters to firms for manufacturing and distributing illegal tobacco products.

title: FDA Draft Guidance Could Result in Safer Food Options for People with Allergies to Sesame, Other Food Allergens
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has released updated draft guidance to help food facilities comply with current good manufacturing practices (CGMPs) and preventive controls for human food, particularly regarding protection from major food allergen cross-contact and proper labeling. The new guidance chapter on food allergens outlines ways to minimize or prevent cross-contact and ensure proper labeling of products containing major food allergens. Millions of Americans have food allergies, and the FDA aims to help consumers with food allergies find safe food options. The guidance encourages industry to follow best practices to minimize or prevent allergen cross-contact, rather than intentionally adding allergens to comply with the law.

title: Statement on North Carolina's Medicaid Expansion Under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: The 40th State, North Carolina, has expanded Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act, thanks to Governor Cooper and bipartisan elected officials. This move will provide affordable, quality coverage to 600,000 North Carolinians, many for the first time in their lives. The expansion will also benefit rural hospitals and invest in mental health resources. Governor Cooper is commended for his leadership in achieving this milestone. The President supports this effort, urging other states to join the expansion.

title: FDA Roundup: September 22, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a revised draft guidance on formal meetings between the FDA and sponsors or applicants of PDUFA products. The draft guidance replaces a 2017 version and outlines recommendations for industry on formal meetings. The FDA has also provided an update on its strategy to prevent Cronobacter sakazakii illnesses associated with powdered infant formula. The agency announced that its Accreditation Scheme for Conformity Assessment (ASCA) program is converting to a permanent program, authorized by the Medical Device User Fee Amendments of 2022. The FDA has issued a draft international harmonization strategic plan for the Center for Devices and Radiological Health, which aims to encourage harmonization among medical device regulatory authorities. The FDA Office of Women's Health will host a free public workshop on October 11, 2023, to discuss the impact of menopause on clinical pharmacology and opportunities for future research.

title: Executive Order 14108—Ensuring the People of East Palestine Are Protected Now and in the Future
body_summary: A Norfolk Southern Railway Company train carrying hazardous materials derailed in East Palestine, Ohio, on February 3, 2023, releasing substances into local waterways. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) deployed a team to support emergency and environmental response efforts. A Unilateral Administrative Order was issued on February 21, 2023, directing cleanup efforts under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA). As of February 2023, over 115,000 tons of contaminated soil and 33 million gallons of contaminated liquid had been removed. The EPA is required to direct removal of contaminated soils and wastewater from the site within 30 days, and will submit reports to the President on cleanup efforts and compliance with the UAO within 30 and 60 days.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a solid pace. Job gains have slowed in recent months but remain strong, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation remains elevated. The U.S. banking system is sound and resilient. Tighter credit conditions for households and businesses are likely to weigh on economic activity, hiring, and inflation. The extent of these effects remains uncertain. The Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent. The Committee will continue to assess additional information and its implications for monetary policy. In determining the extent of additional policy firming that may be appropriate to return inflation to 2 percent over time, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in its previously announced plans. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Austan D. Goolsbee; Patrick Harker; Philip N. Jefferson; Neel Kashkari; Adriana D. Kugler; Lorie K. Logan; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: Implementation Note issued September 20, 2023
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on September 20, 2023: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 5.4 percent, effective September 21, 2023. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective September 21, 2023, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 5.5 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 5.3 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $60 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest into agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 5.5 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: FDA Roundup: September 19, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued several updates on its regulatory actions and announcements. The agency regulates certain tests and treatments for prostate cancer to ensure they are safe and effective. African American men are more likely to get prostate cancer and die from the disease than men of other races. The FDA has released a new IT strategy, which is a shared vision that unites the agency's IT portfolio and will foster innovation, enhance public health outcomes, and lead the FDA into a new era of scientific and technological advancement. The agency has also issued draft guidance on demonstrating substantial evidence of effectiveness based on one adequate and well-controlled clinical investigation and confirmatory evidence. Additionally, the FDA has issued draft guidance on regulatory considerations for prescription drug use-related software, a call for comment on its electronic submission portal, and approved a new medication for the treatment of intermediate or high-risk myelofibrosis.

title: Statement on International Day of Democracy
body_summary: The President of the United States believes that democracies can deliver for their people in a rapidly changing world and has taken action to prove it. Over the last 2½ years, the President has signed several laws, including the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, the Inflation Reduction Act, and the CHIPS and Science Act, to tackle challenges at home. The President has also taken steps to protect democracy abroad, including helping to rally the world to stand with Ukraine against Russia's assault, revitalizing the G-7's commitment to inclusive economic growth, and launching the Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment. The President has identified corruption as a threat to national security and launched a new strategy to counter it. The President has also mobilized efforts to counter the proliferation of commercial spyware and has dedicated more resources to digital and physical security training for journalists. The President reiterates the importance of democracy and human rights protection, committing to preserving democracy for generations to come.

title: FDA Supports Innovation in Animal Biotechnology, Veterinary Products, Food for Animals Through New Comprehensive Agenda
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced a new agenda to modernize its approach to evaluating and supporting innovative animal and veterinary products. The agenda lists four objectives and supporting actions to increase regulatory flexibility, predictability, and efficiency. The agency aims to foster product development and implement smart, risk-based approaches to regulating modern animal and veterinary products, including novel food ingredients and animal biotechnology products. The agenda applies to products like cell-cultured animal food ingredients and intentional genomic alterations in animals.

FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf has stated that the agency is committed to helping developers bring products that enhance public health, animal health, and food production to market while providing consumers with confidence that they meet the FDA's high standards. The agency plans to reassess its animal and veterinary product review programs and processes, adjusting them where appropriate, to account for the diversity of products developed using innovative technologies.

CVM Director Tracey Forfa has said that the new agenda will lead to modernizing approaches in ways that support and spur innovation, while protecting public health and ensuring consumer confidence. The agency is expanding the Veterinary Innovation Program to include additional features for developers of animal biotechnology products, and plans to provide advanced computational tools for analyzing complex genomic data.

title: FDA Roundup: September 15, 2023
body_summary: The US FDA took enforcement actions against several entities, including online retailers and manufacturers selling unauthorized e-cigarette products, and warned them to cease sales. The agency also reminded consumers to get vaccinated against the flu. The FDA updated its guidance on the Breakthrough Devices Program and issued a warning letter to a company selling LittleOak infant formula without a premarket notification. Furthermore, the FDA supported the seizure of bulk dry food products at Gold Coast Distributors, Inc. in California, due to insanitary conditions, with a scheduled on-site meeting on November 9.

title: FDA Issues Warning Letters to Firms Marketing Unapproved Eye Products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued warning letters to eight companies for manufacturing or marketing unapproved ophthalmic drug products in violation of federal law. These warning letters aim to protect Americans from potentially harmful ophthalmic products. The FDA is concerned that these products pose a heightened risk of harm due to bypassing the body's natural defenses. The agency is committed to ensuring the safety and quality of medicines Americans take. Eight companies have received warning letters: Boiron Inc., CVS Health, DR Vitamin Solutions, Natural Ophthalmics, Inc., OcluMed LLC, Similasan AG/Similasan USA, TRP Company, Inc., and Walgreens Boots Alliance, Inc. Consumers using these products should speak to their healthcare professional. The FDA encourages reporting of adverse reactions to its MedWatch program. The companies must respond within 15 days, stating how they will correct the violations. Failure to correct may result in regulatory or enforcement actions, including product seizure and court orders.

title: Statement on Food and Drug Administration and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Actions on Updated COVID-19 Vaccines
body_summary: The Food and Drug Administration and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention have authorized, approved, and recommended that everyone 6 months and older get an updated COVID-19 vaccine to protect against serious illness this fall and winter. This announcement also includes immunizations for all three major seasonal respiratory viruses: COVID-19, flu, and RSV. The administration has made historic progress in managing COVID-19 since entering office, and now has a strong position with safe and effective vaccines, widely available at-home tests, and effective treatments. Vaccination against COVID-19 remains the most important protection against hospitalization, long-term health complications, and death.

title: FDA Takes Action on Updated mRNA COVID-19 Vaccines to Better Protect Against Currently Circulating Variants
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration approved and authorized updated COVID-19 vaccines for emergency use, formulated to target currently circulating variants and provide better protection against serious consequences of COVID-19. The vaccines, manufactured by ModernaTX Inc. and Pfizer Inc., include a monovalent component against the Omicron variant XBB.1.5. 

Individuals 5 years of age and older can receive a single dose of the updated vaccine, while those 6 months through 4 years of age who have previously been vaccinated can receive one or two doses. Unvaccinated individuals 6 months through 4 years of age can receive three doses of the updated Pfizer-BioNTech or Moderna COVID-19 vaccine.

The FDA is confident in the safety and effectiveness of the updated vaccines and believes their benefits outweigh the risks. The vaccines are expected to provide good protection against COVID-19 from currently circulating variants. The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention will meet on September 12 to discuss clinical recommendations for who should receive the updated vaccine.

title: FDA Roundup: September 8 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration published a report on device safety, a final guidance on biocompatibility, and granted marketing authorization for a new medical device. The FDA also awarded grants to five non-profit consortia for pediatric medical device development, totaling $6.75 million. In addition, the FDA issued draft guidances to strengthen and modernize the 510(k) Program, announced a public workshop on Positron Emission Tomography product quality, and authorized the marketing of a disinfection system. The FDA also updated the advisory on the Listeria monocytogenes outbreak and recalled dairy and non-dairy frozen dessert products.

title: FDA Roundup: September 1, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has cleared for marketing an updated 23andMe Personal Genome Service Genetic Health Risk Report for BRCA1/BRCA2 (Selected Variants). This direct-to-consumer test analyzes DNA from saliva samples and reports selected genetic variants associated with increased cancer risks. The test was updated to include 41 additional BRCA1/BRCA2 variants. The FDA is promoting safe and effective genetic testing to aid patients in informed conversations with healthcare providers.

title: FDA Issues Warning Letters to Three Infant Formula Manufacturers
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued warning letters to three infant formula manufacturers: ByHeart Inc., Mead Johnson Nutrition (Reckitt), and Perrigo Wisconsin, LLC. The letters reflect findings from FDA inspections over the last several months, highlighting violations of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and the FDA's Infant Formula regulations.

The FDA inspected the facilities of these companies in December 2022, February 2023, and March 2023, and issued inspectional observations and exercised oversight of each firm during the recalls of potentially contaminated product in the same months. The FDA does not advise parents and caregivers to discard or avoid purchasing any particular infant formula at this time.

The companies must conduct root cause investigations and perform subsequent cleaning and sanitation activities. They must also evaluate their cleaning and sanitation practices, schedules, and procedures before releasing product. Each company has 15 working days to respond to the FDA to explain the corrective actions they are taking.

The FDA is committed to identifying and acting on issues early to prevent any firms from reaching the level of concern that prompted last year's large-scale recall and contributed to the infant formula shortage. The agency has increased oversight of powdered infant formula facilities and will continue to conduct annual inspections and engage with industry to enhance infant formula safety.

In November 2022, the FDA released an outline of a prevention strategy to prevent Cronobacter sakazakii illnesses associated with consumption of powdered infant formula. The agency has also strengthened regulatory tools and increased funding to oversee the infant formula industry and has worked closely with the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to support the addition of invasive Cronobacter infections among infants under one year of age to the Nationally Notifiable Conditions List.

title: La FDA emite cartas de advertencia a tres fabricantes de fórmula infantil
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued warning letters to three infant formula manufacturers, ByHeart Inc., Mead Johnson Nutrition (Reckitt), and Perrigo Wisconsin, LLC, for violating federal regulations and guidelines for infant formula production. The FDA has identified areas for improvement after conducting inspections at these facilities in recent months. The warning letters require the manufacturers to take corrective actions, including recalling products potentially contaminated with Cronobacter sakazii. The FDA emphasizes that no contaminated products have been confirmed, and parents and caregivers should not discard or avoid purchasing any specific formula. The agency will continue to monitor the industry, conduct regular inspections, and implement a national strategy to increase the resilience of the US infant formula market.

title: Statement on Prescription Drug Cost Reduction Efforts
body_summary: The US administration has announced the selection of 10 Medicare Part D drugs for price negotiation, the first time ever. These drugs are among the most common and costly prescriptions for conditions like heart failure, blood clots, and diabetes. The selection is part of the Inflation Reduction Act, which reduced insulin costs to $35 a month for seniors on Medicare. The plan will decrease prices for up to 9 million seniors who currently pay up to $6,497 in out-of-pocket costs per year. The Congressional Budget Office estimates this will save taxpayers $160 billion. The plan is a key part of the administration's economic vision, known as Bidenomics, which aims to grow the economy from the middle out. Despite opposition from Big Pharma, the administration is committed to continuing the fight to lower healthcare costs.

title: FDA Roundup: August 25, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced several actions. The agency signed a first-of-its-kind Regulatory Partnership Arrangement with Ecuador's seafood regulatory authority to enhance shrimp safety. The FDA also issued a proposed rule to revise canned tuna standards, responding to a citizen petition from Bumble Bee Foods, LLC, and others. Additionally, the FDA updated information for consumers on the treatment of molluscum, a common skin condition, which can only be treated with FDA-approved Ycanth (cantharidin). The FDA issued warning letters to 15 online retailers for selling unauthorized e-cigarette products. The agency also updated resources for Hurricane Season: Be Prepared, raising awareness about the need for preparedness during National Preparedness Month.

title: FDA Approves First Biosimilar to Treat Multiple Sclerosis
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Tyruko (natalizumab-sztn), the first biosimilar to Tysabri (natalizumab), for the treatment of adults with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) and moderately to severely active Crohn’s Disease. The approval was based on evidence showing no clinically meaningful differences between Tyruko and Tysabri in terms of safety, purity, and potency. The biosimilar is approved for treating clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease. The FDA's approval aims to increase access to safe and effective medications for patients with MS, who are often at risk of progressive disability.

title: FDA Names First Deputy Commissioner for Proposed, Unified Human Foods Program
