body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has selected James "Jim" Jones as the first Deputy Commissioner for Human Foods, effective September 24. Jones will lead the proposed unified Human Foods Program, which aims to improve food safety, chemical safety, and innovative food products to bolster the U.S. food supply in the face of climate change and globalization. Jones has over 30 years of experience in the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, managing teams and providing strategic planning on chemical safety and sustainability. He was a principal architect of the 2016 overhaul of the Toxic Substances Control Act and led several national sustainability programs. Jones holds a master's degree in economics from the University of California at Santa Barbara and a bachelor's degree in economics from the University of Maryland. The Deputy Commissioner for Human Foods will report directly to the FDA Commissioner and will exercise decision-making authority over the program.

title: FDA Approves First Vaccine for Pregnant Individuals to Prevent RSV in Infants
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Abrysvo, the first vaccine approved for use in pregnant individuals to prevent lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) and severe LRTD caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in infants from birth through 6 months of age. The vaccine is approved for use at 32 through 36 weeks gestational age. Abrysvo is administered as a single dose injection into the muscle. 

RSV is a highly contagious virus that causes respiratory infections in individuals of all age groups. The virus is especially common in children, and most individuals can be expected to be infected with RSV by the time they reach two years of age. 

A clinical study evaluated the effectiveness of Abrysvo to prevent LRTD and severe LRTD caused by RSV in infants born to individuals who were vaccinated during pregnancy. Among approximately 3,500 pregnant individuals who received Abrysvo, compared to approximately 3,500 pregnant individuals who received placebo, Abrysvo reduced the risk of severe LRTD by 81.8% within 90 days after birth. 

The safety of Abrysvo was evaluated in two studies. The most commonly reported side effects by pregnant individuals who received Abrysvo were pain at the injection site, headache, muscle pain and nausea. A dangerous hypertensive disorder, known as pre-eclampsia, occurred in 1.8% of pregnant individuals who received Abrysvo compared to 1.4% of pregnant individuals who received placebo.

title: FDA Roundup: August 18, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing an update on news from around the agency. On Thursday, the FDA updated the list of ultraviolet wand products that may present a risk of injury due to exposure to unsafe levels of ultraviolet-C radiation. The FDA authorized marketing for BlueWind Medical's Revi System, a Tibial Neuromodulation System, for the treatment of patients with symptoms of urgency incontinence. The FDA approved Sohonos, the first treatment for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva, which reduces extra-skeletal bone formation in adults and children with the rare disease. The FDA also issued an advisory warning pet owners not to feed their pets certain lots of Darwin's Natural Pet Products raw cat and dog food due to contamination with Salmonella.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A Federal Open Market Committee meeting was held on July 25-26, 2023. The committee reviewed financial markets, noting a robust economy with easing inflation pressures. Survey respondents expected real interest rates to increase through 2024 and remain above neutral levels for several years. Term interest rates in AFEs increased modestly, tempered by inflation and PMI surprises. Risk sentiment improved, with foreign equity indexes increasing and bond spreads narrowing. The Federal Reserve Committee raised the target range for the federal funds rate to 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent, citing concerns about inflation and economic activity. Total PCE price inflation is expected to ease further over 2024, reaching 2.2% by 2025.

title: FDA Roundup: August 15, 2023
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced a request for information on a citizen petition asking to amend the standard of identity for pasteurized orange juice by lowering the minimum soluble solids content. Comments are due by October 16, 2023.

The FDA has approved HEPZATO KIT (melphalan for Injection/Hepatic Delivery System) for liver-directed treatment of adult patients with uveal melanoma. The FDA has also approved elranatamab-bcmm for adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Additionally, the FDA has approved the fixed dose combination of niraparib and abiraterone acetate for adult patients with deleterious or suspected deleterious BRCA-mutated castration-resistant prostate cancer.

The FDA has warned consumers and patients to not use certain tests manufactured by Universal Meditech Inc., as their performance could not be confirmed, raising concerns about their safety and effectiveness.

title: FDA Roundup: August 11, 2023
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued an Outbreak Advisory for an investigation of Listeria monocytogenes potentially linked to ice cream. The FDA advises consumers, restaurants, and retailers not to eat, sell, or serve recalled Real Kosher Ice Cream Soft Serve On The Go ice cream cups. 

The FDA has granted accelerated approval to talquetamab-tgvs for adults with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Pralsetinib has also been approved for adult patients with metastatic rearranged during transfection fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer. 

The FDA has cleared the V-PRO maX 2 Low Temperature Sterilization System for the sterilization of 3D printed devices in health care facilities.

title: FDA Roundup: August 8, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is issuing a direct final rule to complete administrative actions related to partially hydrogenated oils (PHOs) in foods. This rule addresses outdated references to PHOs in regulations, which were highlighted in the 2015 final determination that PHOs are no longer Generally Recognized as Safe (GRAS). The FDA will not completely remove PHOs from the food supply due to their natural occurrence in meat and dairy products. Additionally, the FDA has issued a draft guidance on incorporating QTc interval prolongation-related information into the labeling of non-antiarrhythmic human prescription drug and biological products. Comments on the guidance must be submitted by October 7, 2023, for review before finalization.

title: FDA Issues Draft Guidance for Registration and Listing of Cosmetic Product Facilities and Products
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a draft guidance to assist cosmetics companies in registering and listing their product facilities and products. This requirement is a result of the Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022, which mandates submission of information about existing cosmetic product facilities and products by December 29. The guidance outlines the exemptions for small businesses and provides information on the frequency of updates, including facility registration, product listing, and product ingredient changes. The FDA aims to strengthen its oversight on cosmetic safety, using registration and listing information to identify potential safety issues, facilitate product recalls, and conduct testing and surveillance programs.

title: FDA Approves First Oral Treatment for Postpartum Depression
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Zurzuvae (zuranolone), the first oral medication indicated to treat postpartum depression (PPD) in adults. PPD is a major depressive episode occurring after childbirth or later stages of pregnancy, characterized by sadness, loss of interest in activities, and decreased ability to feel pleasure. The efficacy of Zurzuvae was demonstrated in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter studies, showing significant improvement in depressive symptoms compared to placebo. Patients should take 50mg of Zurzuvae once daily in the evening for 14 days, and should not drive or operate heavy machinery for at least 12 hours after taking the medication. Side effects include drowsiness, dizziness, diarrhea, fatigue, and suicidal thoughts. The FDA granted this application Priority Review and Fast Track designation to Sage Therapeutics, Inc.

title: FDA Roundup: August 1, 2023
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is providing an update on its ongoing actions to resolve prescription stimulant medication shortages. Beginning October 1, 2023, the Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program (TAP) Pilot will expand to include the Office of Neurological and Physical Medicine Devices (OHT5). The TAP Pilot aims to promote early communications between the FDA and medical device sponsors to ensure patients have access to high-quality medical devices.

The FDA has also approved dostarlimab-gxly (Jemperli, GlaxoSmithKline) for primary advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer that is mismatch repair deficient or microsatellite instability-high. However, immune-mediated adverse reactions occurred with dostarlimab-gxly, including pneumonitis, colitis, and skin adverse reactions.

Additionally, the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of California entered a consent decree in United States v. Organic Pastures Dairy Co., LLC, et al., Case No. 08-cv-1786 (E.D. Cal.). The FDA moved for contempt in March 2023, alleging that Organic Pastures distributed an unapproved new drug and failed to affix required statements on its invoices and packaging slips.

The FDA has also cleared the DEKA ACE Pump System for marketing, which is a prescription-only device for single patient use and can be used with an interoperable Automated Glycemic Controller (iAGC) to form an automated insulin dosing system.

title: FDA Roundup: July 28, 2023
body_summary: The US FDA approved Ervebo, a vaccine for Ebola virus disease, for individuals 12-17 years old, in addition to those 18 years and older, who have been eligible since December 2019. The FDA entered into a Mutual Recognition Agreement with Switzerland, allowing both countries to rely on each other's inspection findings. The FDA published an update on sesame allergen labeling on food packages by Dr. Robert M. Califf, highlighting the addition of sesame as the ninth major food allergen. The agency announced FY2024 user fee rates for importers and accreditation bodies participating in the Voluntary Qualified Importer Program. The FDA's CDER issued final guidance on recognizing voluntary consensus standards for pharmaceutical quality and launched a portal for submitting standards.

title: FDA Approves Second Over-the-Counter Naloxone Nasal Spray Product
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved RiVive, a 3 milligram naloxone hydrochloride nasal spray, for over-the-counter use to treat known or suspected opioid overdose. This is the second nonprescription naloxone product approved by the agency. The approval was supported by data showing similar levels of RiVive reach the bloodstream as an approved prescription naloxone product. The approval was granted to Harm Reduction Therapeutics, and the timeline for availability and price will be determined by the manufacturer. The FDA has taken steps to facilitate access to opioid overdose reversal products and reduce unnecessary opioid exposure. In the 12-month period ending in February 2023, more than 105,000 reported fatal overdoses occurred in the US.

title: FDA Takes Steps to Facilitate Innovation for Devices Intended to Treat Opioid Use Disorder
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced new steps to facilitate innovation in devices intended to treat opioid use disorder (OUD). The FDA's draft guidance, "Clinical Considerations for Studies of Devices Intended to Treat Opioid Use Disorder," aims to aid sponsors in designing clinical studies for devices intended to treat OUD. The guidance recommends that pivotal OUD device studies should have a well-defined study population, appropriately monitor drug use, control for bias, and include an appropriate follow-up period. The FDA Commissioner, Robert M. Califf, M.D., stated that the agency is committed to helping industry develop solutions that are proven to be effective in addressing the overdose crisis. The draft guidance provides critical recommendations for bringing safe and effective devices intended to treat OUD to market. The FDA will review feedback from stakeholders before finalizing the guidance. The Overdose Prevention Framework, introduced in August 2022, outlines the agency's priorities, including supporting primary prevention, encouraging harm reduction, and advancing evidence-based treatments for substance use disorders.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace. Job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation remains elevated. The U.S. banking system is sound and resilient. Tighter credit conditions for households and businesses are likely to weigh on economic activity, hiring, and inflation. The extent of these effects remains uncertain. The Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent. The Committee will continue to assess additional information and its implications for monetary policy. In determining the extent of additional policy firming that may be appropriate to return inflation to 2 percent over time, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in its previously announced plans. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Austan D. Goolsbee; Patrick Harker; Philip N. Jefferson; Neel Kashkari; Lorie K. Logan; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: Implementation Note issued July 26, 2023
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on July 26, 2023: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 5.4 percent, effective July 27, 2023. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective July 27, 2023, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 5.5 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 5.3 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $60 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest into agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve a 1/4 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate to 5.5 percent, effective July 27, 2023. In taking this action, the Board approved requests to establish that rate submitted by the Boards of Directors of the Federal Reserve Banks of Boston, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Richmond, Chicago, St. Louis. Minneapolis, Kansas City, Dallas, and San Francisco. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: FDA Roundup: July 25, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has reopened the comment period for the "Quantitative Research on Front of Package Labeling on Packaged Foods" study, with a new deadline of July 26, 2023. The agency has also recognized several sterilization standards and Technical Information Reports to advance innovation in medical device sterilization processes, including ISO 22441:2022 and AAMI TIR104:2022. The FDA denied a petition requesting a ban on the use of eight ortho-phthalates and revocation of the prior sanctioned uses for five ortho-phthalates in food based on alleged safety concerns. On Friday, the FDA approved the Cordis Palmaz Mullins XD Pulmonary Stent for pediatric patients receiving treatment for pulmonary artery stenosis, a serious form of congenital heart disease.

title: Statement on the Appointment of Shuwanza R. Goff as White House Director of Legislative Affairs
body_summary: The President announces that Shuwanza Goff, a day 1 member of their team, will serve as the new Director of Legislative Affairs. Shuwanza is a proven leader and trusted voice on both sides of the aisle, with over a decade of experience on Capitol Hill. She previously worked as Deputy Director of Legislative Affairs and helped pass landmark legislation such as the American Rescue Plan, bipartisan infrastructure bill, Chips and Science Act, and Inflation Reduction Act.

title: FDA Roundup: July 21, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is hosting a virtual listening session on August 22, 2023, to gather feedback on a new 5-year strategic plan for the Center for Tobacco Products. Registration is open for public comment, and the proposed strategic goals are available on the event webpage. The FDA also published a CDER Conversation featuring William (Bill) Chong, M.D., director of the Office of Safety and Clinical Evaluation, who discusses the office's work on evaluating generic drug safety. The FDA recently approved two vaccines: Cyfendus for anthrax and quizartinib for acute myeloid leukemia. Additionally, the FDA approved an expansion of indications for the ThermoCool SmartTouch Catheter for symptomatic persistent atrial fibrillation. The FDA is also accepting meeting requests for its Complex Innovative Trial Design (CID) Paired Meeting Program until September 30, 2023.

title: FDA Provides Update Regarding Storm Damage at Pfizer Facility in North Carolina
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is working closely with Pfizer to assess the impact of damage at Pfizer's Rocky Mount, North Carolina facility. The FDA expects no immediate significant impacts on supply, but is monitoring the situation closely. Pfizer's facility produces 25% of its total product for the U.S. market and supplies 8% of U.S. consumption, but the FDA has identified less than 10 drugs for which the facility is the sole source for the U.S. market. The FDA has initiated mitigation steps, including looking for additional sources and asking other manufacturers to prepare to ramp up production. Pfizer has put the inventory of many products on strict allocation, which could lead to localized supply disruptions. The FDA will work with partners in government, industry, and the health care system to minimize impact on patient care.

title: FDA Roundup: July 18, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration announced findings from a voluntary pilot program evaluating alignment of private third-party food safety audit standards with FDA regulations. The FDA published a laboratory study on mixing an oral antacid with different foods, confirming that a laboratory assessment can detect the effect of the food vehicle on drug performance. The FDA also warned consumers not to use ultrasound medical devices manufactured by RoyalVibe Health, CellQuicken, and Well-Being Reality. Additionally, the FDA granted marketing authorization for the Ruthless Spine RJB device, an intraoperative surgical angle measurement guide. The FDA updated the Medical Device Shortages List, removing product codes for certain devices and supplies.

title: FDA Approves New Drug to Prevent RSV in Babies and Toddlers
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Beyfortus (nirsevimab-alip) for the prevention of Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract disease in neonates and infants, and in children up to 24 months of age. The approval was based on the results of three clinical trials, which showed a significant reduction in the risk of severe RSV disease. The trials involved preterm infants, term and late preterm infants, and infants with chronic lung disease of prematurity or congenital heart disease. The FDA has also warned about possible side effects, including rash and injection site reactions, and advised caution in infants and children with bleeding disorders.

title: Statement on the Resignation of White House Director of Legislative Affairs Louisa M. Terrell
body_summary: As a U.S. Senator for 36 years, the President developed a deep respect for the United States Congress and its role in democracy. Elected President, they knew Louisa Terrell, a longtime friend and former colleague, was the best partner to help deliver legislation to the American people. Louisa has provided wise counsel, reflected values, and delivered key priorities over the past 2½ years. She played a crucial role in historic legislation, including the American Rescue Plan, Inflation Reduction Act, CHIPS and Science bill, bipartisan infrastructure bill, Bipartisan Safer Communities Act, and bipartisan budget agreement. Louisa's perseverance helped secure the confirmation of Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson to the Supreme Court, appointing a historic number of diverse judges. The President expresses gratitude to Louisa for her years of service, as well as her family, who shared her with the administration.

title: FDA Roundup: July 14, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has re-issued two temporary guidances for regulatory requirements involving onsite visits abroad under the Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA). The FDA will participate in the 2023 Pain in Animals Workshop on September 26-27, 2023. The agency has made the 120-Day Food and Agriculture Interim Risk Review available, which reviews critical and emergent risks to the U.S. Food and Agriculture sector. The FDA has released a public inventory of food ingredients with unsafe uses and a conversation with experts on post-market assessments. The agency has updated the Breakthrough Devices website with data on 32 devices granted Breakthrough designation from January 1 to March 31, 2023. The FDA has also published a Spotlight on CDER Science on patient-reported outcomes for frailty in patients with multiple myeloma.

title: FDA Approves First Nonprescription Daily Oral Contraceptive
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Opill (norgestrel) tablet for nonprescription use to prevent pregnancy, making it the first daily oral contraceptive approved for use without a prescription in the US. The approval allows consumers to purchase oral contraceptive medicine at drug stores, convenience stores, and grocery stores, as well as online. Director of the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, Patrizia Cavazzoni, stated that daily oral contraception is safe and expected to be more effective than currently available nonprescription methods in preventing unintended pregnancy. The approval may reduce barriers to access, particularly for women who may not have had access to healthcare. Opill's efficacy was established with its original approval in 1973. To approve the product for nonprescription use, the FDA required that the manufacturer demonstrate its safety and effectiveness for consumers using only the product's labeling. Studies showed that consumers understood the label instructions well, supporting the product's availability as an over-the-counter product.

title: FDA Roundup: July 11, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is detailing its efforts to stop illicit xylazine from entering the United States. The Center for Veterinary Medicine is working in partnership with other offices across the FDA and Department of Health and Human Services as part of a whole-of-government response to this issue. In February, CVM restricted the entry of xylazine active pharmaceutical ingredients and finished dosage form drug products into the country. The FDA also assigned a Confidentiality Commitment with the Fish Quarantine and Inspection Agency of Indonesia to prepare the country to participate in a program ensuring shrimp safety for U.S. export. Additionally, the FDA authorized the marketing of Better Therapeutics' BT-001, a prescription-only digital therapeutic device for type 2 diabetes patients. The FDA Grand Rounds lecture series will discuss "The Plasmid Puzzle: Finding Solutions in Salmonella" on July 13, 2023.

title: FDA Roundup: July 7, 2023
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing an at-a-glance summary of news from around the agency. 

The U.S. Embassy & Consulates in India published a news release highlighting "Operation Broader Sword," a multi-agency enforcement operation with the Government of India identifying illicit pharmaceuticals, devices, or precursor chemicals shipped using the international mail system. The operation, taking place in June 2023, stopped over 500 shipments of illicit, and potentially dangerous, unapproved prescription drugs, combination medical devices, and synthetic drug precursors from reaching American consumers.

The FDA updated its webpage on Dermal Fillers (Soft Tissue Fillers) to reflect information from reports of delayed onset inflammation such as swelling or redness that can develop near the dermal filler injection site following viral or bacterial illnesses or infections, vaccinations, or dental procedures.

The FDA issued a Safety Alert advising consumers not to purchase or eat certain Everest Garam Masala, Everest Sambhar Masala, and Maggi Masala ae Magic spices because they have the potential to be contaminated with Salmonella.

The FDA, Office of the Chief Scientist,Office of Regulatory Science & Innovation, announced several renewal awards and one new award for theCenters of Excellence in Regulatory Science & Innovation (CERSI)Program. The institutions in the CERSI program promote innovation in regulatory science through cutting-edge scientific research that supports FDA's regulatory science needs. The institutions received awards up to $50M for 5 years.

title: FDA Converts Novel Alzheimer’s Disease Treatment to Traditional Approval
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has converted Leqembi, an antibody to treat adult patients with Alzheimer's disease, to traditional approval after a confirmatory trial verified clinical benefit. Leqembi works by reducing amyloid plaques in the brain, a feature of the disease. The drug was approved in January under the Accelerated Approval pathway, which allows the FDA to approve drugs for serious conditions based on clinical data. A confirmatory trial, Study 301, verified the clinical benefit of Leqembi, which demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in decline from baseline to 18 months on the Clinical Dementia Rating Scale Sum of Boxes score compared to placebo. The FDA convened a Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee on June 9 to discuss the study's results, and all committee members voted affirmatively that the results verified the clinical benefit of Leqembi. The drug's most common side effects include headache, infusion-related reactions, and amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA).

title: FDA, FTC Warn Six Companies for Illegally Selling Copycat Food Products Containing Delta-8 THC
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration and the Federal Trade Commission have issued warning letters to six companies for selling copycat food products containing delta-8 tetrahydrocannabinol (delta-8 THC). The FDA is concerned that these products can be mistaken for traditional foods and may be ingested by children or taken in higher doses than intended. The warning letters were sent to Delta Munchies, Dr. Smoke LLC, Exclusive Hemp Farms/Oshipt, Nikte’s Wholesale LLC, North Carolina Hemp Exchange LLC, and The Haunted Vapor Room. The FDA and FTC are concerned that these products are marketed in a way that could be appealing to children and may result in serious consequences, including hallucinations, vomiting, and loss of consciousness. The FDA has received reports of serious adverse events associated with these products and has issued warnings to consumers and companies before.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A joint meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee and the Board of Governors was held on June 13-14, 2023. The manager reviewed financial market developments, including increased policy-sensitive rates, higher Treasury yields, and improved investor sentiment about the banking sector. Respondents expected no rate change at this meeting but saw a clear probability of additional tightening at coming meetings. Market participants expect a roughly flat federal funds rate for the rest of 2023, with a year-end rate about 70 basis points higher than before the May FOMC meeting. Nominal Treasury yields rose, driven by an increase in real yields as measures of inflation compensation remained little changed. The S&P 500 stock price index increased, while bank equity prices moved up. Longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored, but participants emphasized the need for monetary policy firming to support a return to the Committee's 2% goal.

title: Statement on National Wildland Firefighter Day
body_summary: Today, the President joins Americans in expressing gratitude to wildland firefighters and support personnel for their protection of communities and natural resources from wildfires. National Wildland Firefighter Day, celebrated from June 30 to July 6, commemorates the lives of firefighters who made the ultimate sacrifice, such as the 19 Granite Mountain Hotshot firefighters who died in the 2013 Yarnell Hill Fire in Arizona. The President has deployed 1,300 Federal and State firefighters to Canada to battle the historically difficult wildfire season. The administration has included $7 billion in funding for wildland firefighter support in the bipartisan infrastructure law and the Inflation Reduction Act, benefiting over 100 at-risk communities in 22 States and seven Tribes. The President has directed his administration to invest in pay, benefits, and health investments for wildland firefighters, technological innovations, and community resilience.

title: FDA Roundup: June 30, 2023
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has accepted the first master file for participation in the 510(k) Ethylene Oxide (EO) Sterility Change Master File Pilot Program. This will allow 510(k) holders of devices labeled as sterile to reference the master file rather than submitting a new 510(k) for the sterilization change. 

The FDA granted marketing authorization for Renalytix AI, Inc.’s KidneyIntelX.dkd, an in vitro diagnostic intended to aid in the assessment of risk of progressive kidney function decline in adult patients with Type 2 diabetes and existing chronic kidney disease. 

The FDA approved the AAV5 DetectCDx, a companion diagnostic test, to aid in identifying patients who may benefit from receiving gene therapy with ROCTAVIAN to treat an inherited bleeding disorder in which the blood does not clot properly due to a very low level of a certain coagulation factor. 

The FDA also provided an update to information and recommendations for NuVasive Specialized Orthopedics’ Precice Intra-medullary Limb Lengthening (IMLL) system, including recommendations for health care providers and actions to evaluate potential biocompatibility concerns with all Precice devices.

title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapy for Adults with Severe Hemophilia A
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Roctavian, a gene therapy for adults with severe hemophilia A without pre-existing antibodies to adeno-associated virus serotype 5. The approval allows for the treatment of a potentially serious bleeding disorder that can cause life-threatening health issues. The disorder is caused by a mutation in the gene producing factor VIII, a protein essential for blood clotting. 

The therapy involves a single dose of Roctavian, a viral vector carrying a gene for clotting factor VIII, administered by intravenous infusion. The safety and effectiveness were evaluated in a multinational study of 112 patients followed up for at least 3 years. Results showed a significant decrease in bleeding episodes, from 5.4 bleeds per year to 2.6 bleeds per year. 

The most common adverse reactions associated with Roctavian include mild changes in liver function and infusion-related reactions. Close monitoring is advised. The therapy was granted Orphan, Breakthrough Therapy, Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy, and Priority Review designations. Roctavian is approved by BioMarin Pharmaceutical Inc. and is accompanied by a companion diagnostic test, AAV5 DetectCDx, to identify patients who may benefit from the treatment.

title: FDA Approves First Cellular Therapy to Treat Patients with Type 1 Diabetes
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Lantidra, the first allogeneic pancreatic islet cellular therapy, for the treatment of adults with type 1 diabetes who experience severe hypoglycemia despite intensive management. Lantidra is administered as a single infusion into the hepatic portal vein and aims to provide insulin production by infused allogeneic islet beta cells. The therapy was evaluated in two single-arm studies with 30 participants, who showed varying degrees of insulin independence, with 21 participants not needing insulin for a year or more. Adverse reactions included nausea, fatigue, anemia, diarrhea, and abdominal pain, and serious adverse reactions required discontinuation of immunosuppressive medications. The FDA granted approval to CellTrans Inc.

title: FDA Roundup: June 27, 2023
body_summary: The US FDA published new frequently asked questions and tools about the Food Traceability Rule to facilitate faster identification and removal of contaminated food from the market. The FDA also published a document on the Oncology Quality, Characterization, and Assessment of Real-World Data (QCARD) Initiative, which aims to facilitate effective communication between study sponsors and protocol reviewers in the cancer drug development community. The FDA issued a draft guidance on patient-matched guides to orthopedic implants, which provides recommendations for manufacturers to include in regulatory submissions and design processes. Additionally, the FDA finalized a guidance on presenting quantitative efficacy and risk information in direct-to-consumer promotional labeling and advertisements. The FDA approved Rystiggo for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis in adult patients.

title: FDA Provides Update on Proposal for Unified Human Foods Program, including New Model for the Office of Regulatory Affairs
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration is proposing a unified Human Foods Program (HFP) and a new model for the Office of Regulatory Affairs (ORA). This update aims to enhance coordination, prevention, and response activities across the FDA to better support its public health mission. 

FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf announced earlier this year that the agency must build a stronger Human Foods Program and ORA. The new model will unify field work with priorities of program offices and Centers. 

The proposed changes include: 
- Establishing ORA's core mission as conducting investigations, inspections, and imports for all FDA-regulated products 
- Merging compliance functions into the HFP and product Centers' existing compliance functions 
- Realigning ORA's laboratories into the HFP 
- Transitioning certain functions to ORA 
- Reviewing support functions and realigning resources and personnel 

The proposed changes aim to align with the Reagan-Udall Foundation's recommendations and empower the Deputy Commissioner for Human Foods to have full authority over all foods-related resources. The agency is also considering a renaming effort for the Office of Regulatory Affairs.

title: Statement on the First Anniversary of the United States Supreme Court Decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization
body_summary: The Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade one year ago, denying women the right to choose, effective nearly half a century of law. States have imposed extreme abortion bans, forcing women to travel for care and threatening doctors' rights. Congressional Republicans aim to ban abortion nationwide, removing FDA-approved termination medication and restricting contraception access. The administration will continue to protect reproductive health care and call on Congress to restore Roe v. Wade protections in federal law.

title: Executive Order 14101—Strengthening Access to Affordable, High-Quality Contraception and Family Planning Services
body_summary: The President orders that women should have access to healthcare, including contraception and family planning services. In response to the Supreme Court's Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization decision, the President directs the Administration to protect access to reproductive healthcare services. The Secretary of Health and Human Services is tasked with encouraging health centers to offer family planning services, supporting Title X program participants, and providing guidance on contraception-related obligations. The Secretary of Labor and Education are also directed to identify best practices for making affordable contraception available to health plan enrollees and convene institutions of higher education to raise awareness about options for accessing contraception.

title: FDA Issues First Draft Guidance on Clinical Trials with Psychedelic Drugs
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has published a new draft guidance to highlight fundamental considerations for researchers investigating the use of psychedelic drugs for potential treatment of medical conditions. The guidance aims to provide information on how to address unique challenges in designing clinical studies for psychedelic drugs. Dr. Tiffany Farchione, director of the Division of Psychiatry, emphasized the need for careful consideration of psychedelic drugs' unique characteristics when designing clinical studies. The draft guidance covers trial conduct, data collection, subject safety, and new drug application requirements, including the potential for abuse and regulatory requirements for Schedule I controlled substances. The FDA encourages public comments on the draft guidance within 60 days.

title: FDA Roundup: June 23, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued an updated consumer update reminding parents about the dangers of accidental exposure to nicotine-containing e-liquids, which can cause injury and death in children. The FDA is also open to applications for the development of evidence-based guidelines for managing acute low back pain and acute postoperative pain in patients undergoing laparoscopic abdominal surgeries. The FDA has approved Pfizer's talazoparib with enzalutamide for the treatment of adult patients with homologous recombination repair gene-mutated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, based on a 55% reduction in radiographic progression-free survival. The FDA Oncology Center of Excellence is hosting a patient-focused workshop on June 27 to discuss the use of patient-reported outcome measures in cancer clinical trials.

title: Joint Statement by President Biden and Prime Minister Narendra Modi of India
body_summary: US President Biden and Indian Prime Minister Modi reaffirmed a strong bilateral partnership, aiming to advance democracy, freedom, and human rights. They reaffirmed a US-India partnership on AI, defense, and clean energy, as well as their commitment to a free, open, and prosperous Indo-Pacific region. The US and India called for the release of arbitrarily detained people in Myanmar and condemned North Korea's ballistic missile launches. They also discussed Afghanistan, human rights, and cybersecurity, while reaffirming their commitment to denuclearization and counter-terrorism. The leaders agreed to enhance cooperation on critical minerals, nuclear energy, and climate change, and pledged to work together on strengthening the multilateral system and reforming the UN Security Council. A new dedicated pool of funds at the World Bank and enhanced crisis response support were also announced.

title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapy for Treatment of Certain Patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Elevidys, the first gene therapy for pediatric patients 4 through 5 years of age with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), with a confirmed mutation in the DMD gene and no pre-existing medical reasons preventing treatment. The approval addresses an urgent unmet medical need and is an important advancement in the treatment of DMD. Elevidys is a recombinant gene therapy designed to deliver a gene that leads to production of Elevidys micro-dystrophin, a shortened protein that contains selected domains of the dystrophin protein. The product is administered as a single intravenous dose. The FDA approved Elevidys through the Accelerated Approval pathway, which provides patients earlier access to promising new drugs while the company conducts clinical trials to verify the predicted clinical benefit. The accelerated approval was based on data from a randomized clinical trial that established that Elevidys increased the expression of the Elevidys micro-dystrophin protein in individuals with DMD.

title: FDA Inspection Blitz Leads to More Than 180 Warning Letters to Retailers for the Illegal Sale of Youth-Appealing Elf Bar and Esco Bars E-Cigarettes
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued warning letters to 189 retailers for selling unauthorized tobacco products, including Elf Bar and Esco Bars disposable e-cigarettes, which are popular among youth. The FDA Commissioner, Robert M. Califf, stated that the agency is committed to a multipronged approach to protect the nation's youth. The warning letters were the result of a nationwide retailer inspection blitz, which led to concerns over the products' appeal and risks to young people. Two studies published in the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Morbidity & Mortality Weekly Report reinforce concerns about the risks of Elf Bar products among young people. The FDA has also issued import alerts for all products under the Elf Bar and Esco Bars brands and has authorized 23 tobacco-flavored e-cigarette products and devices. As of June 16, the FDA has issued over 570 warning letters to firms for manufacturing, selling, and distributing illegal tobacco products.

title: FDA Approves New Class of Medicines to Treat Pediatric Type 2 Diabetes
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Jardiance (empagliflozin) and Synjardy (empagliflozin and metformin hydrochloride) as treatments for type 2 diabetes in children aged 10 years and older. The approvals provide a new class of medicines taken by mouth to treat pediatric type 2 diabetes. The approvals are based on a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of 157 patients aged 10 to 17 years with inadequately controlled type 2 diabetes. The trial found that treatment with empagliflozin was superior in reducing hemoglobin A1c, a measure of average blood sugar, compared to placebo. The FDA granted the approvals to Boehringer Ingelheim and are expected to help increase treatment options for children with type 2 diabetes.

title: FDA Launches Pilot Program to Help Reduce Risks Associated with Using Laboratory Developed Tests to Identify Cancer Biomarkers
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has launched a new voluntary pilot program to help clinicians select appropriate cancer treatments for patients. The pilot aims to address safety risks posed by poorly performing laboratory developed tests. The program will provide transparent performance recommendations for diagnostic tests used to select certain oncology drug treatments. The FDA will request performance information from drug manufacturers and post minimum performance characteristics recommended for similar tests on its website. This transparency aims to facilitate better and more consistent performance of these tests, resulting in better drug selection and improved care for patients. The initial phase of the pilot program will last up to one year and will evaluate up to nine drug sponsors.

title: FDA Roundup: June 20, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has released a report on foodborne illness risk factors in fast food and full-service restaurants, based on 2017-2018 data. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, more than half of foodborne illness outbreaks occur in restaurants. The FDA's 10-year study (2013-2022) summarizes findings on food safety behaviors and practices in food service facilities. The agency has also authorized marketing of the Invictus Medical, Neoasis, a prescription medical device for neonatal intensive care units (NICUs), to reduce noise levels and allow infants to hear caregiver voices through a speaker.

title: FDA Roundup: June 16, 2023
body_summary: The FDA posted information on its website regarding the formula for COVID-19 vaccines for the 2023-2024 fall and winter seasons, recommending that manufacturers develop vaccines with a monovalent XBB.1.5 composition. The FDA granted accelerated approval to glofitamab-gxbm (Columvi) for relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The FDA released findings from a sampling assignment that collected and tested refrigerated, multi-commodity ready-to-eat dips and spreads for Salmonella spp. and Listeria monocytogenes. The FDA approved the Premia Spine, Inc. TOPS System as an alternative to spinal fusion for certain patients with degenerative spondylolisthesis. The FDA extended the comment period for the Draft Guidance for Industry entitled “Questions and Answers About Dietary Guidance Statements in Food Labeling” until September 25, 2023. The FDA announced a 30-day procedural notice for a study on front-of-package labeling on packaged foods. The FDA issued a public health alert regarding potential contamination of raw oysters from Dai One Food Co., Ltd. The FDA issued the final guidance on Content of Premarket Submissions for Device Software Functions, replacing an earlier guidance issued in 2005.

title: Statement on the Appointment of Mandy Krauthamer Cohen as Director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
body_summary: Dr. Cohen, a top physician and health leader, led North Carolina's Department of Health and Human Services, developing innovative programs that improved health and lives. Her leadership during the COVID-19 crisis drew bipartisan praise. She transformed North Carolina's Medicaid program and played a pivotal role in the bipartisan passage of Medicaid expansion. Prior to North Carolina, Dr. Cohen held senior roles at the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, implementing Affordable Care Act programs. Dr. Cohen has been recognized for her ability to find common ground and put complex policy into action.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a modest pace. Job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation remains elevated. The U.S. banking system is sound and resilient. Tighter credit conditions for households and businesses are likely to weigh on economic activity, hiring, and inflation. The extent of these effects remains uncertain. The Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5 to 5-1/4 percent. Holding the target range steady at this meeting allows the Committee to assess additional information and its implications for monetary policy. In determining the extent of additional policy firming that may be appropriate to return inflation to 2 percent over time, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in its previously announced plans. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Austan D. Goolsbee; Patrick Harker; Philip N. Jefferson; Neel Kashkari; Lorie K. Logan; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: Implementation Note issued June 14, 2023
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on June 14, 2023: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 5.15 percent, effective June 15, 2023. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective June 15, 2023, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 5 to 5-1/4 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 5.25 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 5.05 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $60 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest into agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 5.25 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: FDA Roundup: June 13, 2023
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration published a summary of recent news from around the agency, including the announcement of the FDA Voices article "Accelerating Rare Disease Cures (ARC) Program Emerges as a Conduit for Empowering Rare Disease Stakeholders." The ARC Program aims to increase treatments for rare diseases through innovative scientific design, regulatory policy understanding, and engagement with patients and stakeholders. 

The FDA fully implemented Guidance for Industry (GFI) #263, requiring animal drug sponsors to change the approved marketing status of certain antimicrobial drugs for animals from over-the-counter (OTC) to prescription (Rx) or withdraw approval of their affected OTC animal drug applications. As a result, products affected by GFI #263 will now have prescription labels, while animal owners and caretakers can access appropriate antimicrobials through licensed veterinarians. 

The FDA authorized the marketing of Eroxon (MED3000) by Future Medical Developments Limited, a non-medicated hydro-alcoholic gel for the treatment of erectile dysfunction in adult males aged 22 years and over. 

The FDA hosted its fourth Online Controlled Substances Summit, "Reducing the Availability of Controlled Substances Online," to address the illegal availability of opioids and other controlled substances online. The summit aimed to develop strategic and effective solutions to prevent these products from reaching the American public. 

On Thursday, June 15, at 2:30 pm ET, the FDA Oncology Center of Excellence will host an online public panel discussion, Conversations on Cancer - National Black Family Cancer Awareness Week, Engaging the Generations, to increase cancer awareness, equity, and reduce morbidity and mortality.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index Report for May
body_summary: The report shows continued progress in tackling inflation, with annual inflation at its lowest level since March 2021 and less than half of what it was last June. Unemployment remains at historic lows, below 4 percent for over 50 years, supporting wage gains despite inflation. A bipartisan agreement was reached earlier this month to protect historic economic progress and reduce deficits by nearly $1 trillion over the next decade. The "Investing in America" agenda aims to rebuild infrastructure, manufacturing, and supply chains, creating good-paying jobs. Under this administration, private sector companies have invested over $470 billion in manufacturing, and America is leading in critical industries such as semiconductors and clean energy.

title: FDA Provides Draft Recommendations to Help Reduce Microbial Contamination in Tattoo Inks
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a draft guidance to help manufacturers and distributors recognize situations that will prevent microbial contamination in tattoo inks. The FDA Chief Scientist, Namandjé Bumpus, stated that it's imperative to ensure tattoo inks are free of contamination, as pathogens in these inks can cause infections and serious injuries. The FDA has received reports of illness caused by infected tattoo inks and has found many sealed tattoo inks with microbial contamination. The agency is issuing this guidance to help tattoo ink manufacturers and distributors take steps to protect public health. The draft guidance includes recommended steps such as testing ink and components for microbial contamination, ensuring the manufacturing process does not introduce microbial contamination, and taking corrective measures to prevent the release of contaminated tattoo inks.

title: FDA Roundup: June 9, 2023
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing a summary of news from around the agency. The FDA issued a letter to healthcare providers and facilities about a recall notice for Quadrox Oxygenators, and provided recommendations for healthcare providers and facilities, actions the FDA is taking, and how to contact the FDA if issues arise.

The FDA also approved an expanded indication for the Inspire Medical Systems’ Inspire Upper Airway Stimulation (UAS) System, which includes an updated apnea hypopnea index (AHI) and body mass index (BMI) threshold for adult patients with moderate to severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA).

Additionally, the FDA updated the Medical Device Shortages List, removed some devices from the list, and added new devices with changes to estimated shortage duration. The FDA also cleared for marketing the Elecsys Total-Tau Cerebral Spinal Fluid (CSF) and Elecsys ß-Amyloid (1-42) CSF II tests for the detection of amyloid plaques in patients aged 55 years and older being evaluated for Alzheimer’s disease.

The FDA sent its tenth annual report to Congress, summarizing major actions taken to prevent or mitigate drug shortages in the United States. The agency helped prevent or mitigate 222 potential shortages in CY 2022.

The FDA will host the 2023 Science Forum, a virtual event featuring talks from FDA science experts, including a keynote speech by Dr. Murray Lumpkin, Deputy Director of Integrated Development, Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.

title: Joint Statement—The Atlantic Declaration: A Framework for a Twenty-First Century United States-United Kingdom Economic Partnership
body_summary: The US and UK announce the Atlantic Declaration, a 21st-century economic partnership aimed at building resilient and diversified supply chains, reducing strategic dependencies, and harnessing innovation to drive growth. The partnership will focus on critical and emerging technologies, including semiconductors, quantum technologies, and artificial intelligence, and will lead on key areas such as export controls, economic security, and technology protection. The US and UK plan to launch joint research and development initiatives, enhance information-sharing, and promote private investment to address fundamental research questions in quantum science and advance cutting-edge telecoms, synthetic biology, and AI. They also commit to accelerating cooperation on AI, promoting safe and responsible development, and deepening collaboration on key areas such as privacy enhancing technologies, clean energy, and space. The partnership aims to strengthen global norms against the misuse of biology and prohibitions on biological weapons, and will increase collaboration to tackle emerging infectious disease threats and promote biosafety and biosecurity.

title: FDA Roundup: June 6, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued several recommendations and approvals. On Monday, the FDA advised health care providers to implement conservation strategies for non-sterile, single-use pneumatic tourniquet cuffs, providing a list of best practices and instructions for cleaning and sterilization/disinfection. The FDA approved Advanced Medical Solutions Limited's LIQUIFIX Hernia Mesh Fixation (HMF) Devices, which include the FIX8 Laparoscopic HMF Device and Precision Open HMF Device, for the fixation of prosthetic mesh in laparoscopic and open surgical repair of femoral and inguinal hernias. The HMF Devices utilize an acrylic glue for securement. The FDA also authorized the marketing of Tristel Solutions Limited's Duo UL, a high-level disinfectant foam for reprocessing ultrasound probes. Additionally, the Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee will meet virtually on June 9th to discuss a confirmatory study for the supplemental biologics license application for Leqembi solution, which was previously approved for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease in January 2023.

title: FDA Announces Additional Steps to Modernize Clinical Trials
body_summary: The US FDA is announcing the availability of a draft guidance on updated good clinical practices (GCPs) aimed at modernizing the design and conduct of clinical trials. The updates, adopted from the International Council for Harmonisation's (ICH) E6(R3) draft guideline, aim to make clinical trials more agile without compromising data integrity or participant protections. The draft guidance proposes a risk-based approach to data collection, monitoring, and quality management, and encourages sponsors to be proactive in trial quality considerations. The FDA Commissioner, Robert M. Califf, and M. Khair ElZarrad, director of the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research's Office of Medical Policy, emphasized the importance of building quality into trial design and conduct. The draft guidance will be open for public comment for 60 days, with the ICH Expert Working Group reviewing and considering comments before finalizing the ICH guideline.

title: FDA Permits Marketing of First COVID-19 At-Home Test Using Traditional Premarket Review Process
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted marketing authorization for the Cue COVID-19 Molecular Test, a molecular nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT) for detecting SARS-CoV-2 virus in nasal swabs. The test is the first at-home over-the-counter (OTC) test to be granted marketing authorization using a traditional premarket review pathway and the first for any respiratory illness. Jeff Shuren, M.D., J.D., director of the FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health, stated that this authorization represents a new era of consumer access to diagnostic tests. The test has a 98.7% accuracy rate for negative and 92.9% for positive samples. The FDA is also establishing special controls to define labeling and performance testing requirements, creating a new regulatory classification for subsequent devices of the same type. The marketing authorization was granted to Cue Health Inc.

title: FDA Roundup: June 2, 2023
body_summary: The US FDA is providing an update on news from around the agency. The FDA has received over 105,000 medical device reports, including 385 reports of death, related to the breakdown or suspected breakdown of the polyester-based polyurethane (PE-PUR) foam used in ventilators, BiPAP machines, and CPAP machines. The FDA is making minor updates to the Requests for Feedback and Meetings for Medical Device Submissions: Q-Submission Program final guidance, including information on when informal communication is appropriate instead of a Pre-Sub. The FDA has also revoked the emergency use authorization (EUA) of the Janssen COVID-19 Vaccine, announced the availability of a final guidance for industry on Action Level for Inorganic Arsenic in Apple Juice, and approved Abrysvo, the second respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine approved for use in the US. Additionally, the FDA has concluded that exposure to certain PFAS in the general food supply is not a health concern for young children or the general population, and has approved Abrysvo for the prevention of lower respiratory tract disease caused by RSV in individuals 60 years of age and older.

title: FDA Conducts Retailer Inspection Blitz, Cracks Down on Illegal Sales of Popular Disposable E-cigarettes
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued warning letters to 30 retailers and one distributor for illegally selling unauthorized tobacco products, specifically Puff and Hyde brand disposable e-cigarettes, popular among youth. The action underscores the agency's commitment to addressing the public health issue of youth e-cigarette use. The FDA Commissioner, Robert M. Califf, stated that protecting the nation's youth from tobacco products is a top priority. The warning letters are a result of a nationwide investigation, which included hundreds of retailers and distributors, and is part of the FDA's efforts to crack down on the sale of unauthorized e-cigarettes. The FDA has authorized 23 tobacco-flavored e-cigarette products and devices, and has issued over 560 warning letters since January 2021.

title: FDA Proposes New, Easy-to-Read Medication Guide for Patients, Patient Medication Information
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration proposes to require a new type of Medication Guide called Patient Medication Information for prescription drugs and certain biological products. The aim is to provide clear, concise, and accessible written information to help patients use their medications safely and effectively. The new Patient Medication Information would be delivered in a consistent and easy-to-understand format, including drug name, indications, safety information, common side effects, and directions for use. The information would be given to patients with their prescription drugs and also be available online. This proposal is part of the FDA's effort to reduce health misinformation and disinformation, and is considered a practical step towards improving public health.

title: FDA Roundup: May 30, 2023
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued the Adjusting for Covariates in Randomized Clinical Trials for Drugs and Biological Products Final Guidance for Industry. This guidance describes the agency's recommendations for adjusting for covariates in the statistical analysis of randomized clinical trials in drug and biological product development programs. 

The FDA also published an article titled "How FDA's New Approach to Reviewing Chemicals Added to Food Will Strengthen Food Safety" by Robert M. Califf, M.D., Commissioner of Food and Drugs, and Susan Mayne, Ph.D., Director of the Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition. The article outlines the FDA's enhanced approach to regulating food chemical safety, including a new framework for systematic post-market review.

title: FDA Roundup: May 26, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration issued warning letters to firms responsible for two flavored e-cigarette products, Shenzen Innokin Technology Co. Ltd. and Breeze Smoke LLC, for making, distributing, or importing tobacco products without authorization. The FDA is committed to protecting youth from tobacco product harms and will take enforcement action against violators. The agency also issued a draft guidance for industry on efficacy endpoints for clinical trials investigating antidiabetic drugs and biological products, providing a 15-year update. Lisa Yanoff, M.D., deputy director of the Office of Cardiology, Hematology, Endocrinology, and Nephrology, stated that the draft guidance demonstrates the FDA's commitment to providing industry with up-to-date recommendations. The draft guidance outlines the FDA's general recommendations on evaluating the efficacy of antidiabetic drugs. The FDA is also announcing a new grants application period for funding of studies on animal drugs for uncommon diseases and is requesting feedback on factors to consider when reviewing proposed modifications to risk evaluation and mitigation strategies.

title: FDA Approves First Oral Antiviral for Treatment of COVID-19 in Adults
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Paxlovid, an oral antiviral pill, for the treatment of mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in adults at high risk of progression to severe disease. Paxlovid is the fourth drug approved by the FDA to treat COVID-19 in adults. The approval was based on substantial evidence of effectiveness and safety, primarily supported by the EPIC-HR clinical trial. The trial showed that Paxlovid significantly reduced hospitalization or death from COVID-19 by 86% compared to placebo among patients treated within five days of symptom onset. The FDA also approved Paxlovid for treatment of eligible children ages 12-18 who are not covered by the current approval. The approved label and authorized Fact Sheet for Health Care Providers come with a boxed warning and instructions for prescribers to assess for potential drug-drug interactions.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary:
Here is the final summary:

The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting on May 2-3, 2023, with Jerome H. Powell as Chair and John C. Williams as Vice Chair. Asset prices became less volatile, financial market conditions eased, and nominal Treasury yields declined. Equity prices appreciated, credit spreads tightened, and the trade-weighted value of the dollar depreciated. Policy-sensitive rates fluctuated due to economic data and risk perceptions. The Committee raised the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5% to 5-1/4%, and reduced Treasury securities and agency debt holdings.

title: FDA Approves New Buprenorphine Treatment Option for Opioid Use Disorder
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Brixadi, a buprenorphine extended-release injection, for treating moderate to severe opioid use disorder (OUD). Brixadi is available in two formulations: a weekly injection and a monthly version. The FDA Commissioner, Robert M. Califf, M.D., stated that the approval expands dosing options and provides people with OUD a greater opportunity for long-term recovery. Buprenorphine is a safe and effective medication for OUD, and patients receiving medication for OUD have a reduced risk of death from all causes. The FDA has implemented a comprehensive approach to increase options to treat OUD, including a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program. Brixadi will be available in various doses, including lower doses for those who do not tolerate higher doses. The most common adverse reactions with Brixadi include injection-site pain, headache, and constipation.

title: FDA Roundup: May 23, 2023
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is announcing a new collaboration with the Veterans Health Administration to jointly develop emergency preparedness and response tools and protocols. The goal is to increase medical product manufacturing capacity and flexibility, and improve resilience of domestic supply chains during emergencies, shortages, and pandemics. A new Memorandum of Understanding will facilitate the development of requirements for trusted networks needed to enable the use of distributed manufacturing and digital stockpiles.

The FDA has also published two Guidance Snapshots and accompanying podcasts to promote diversity in clinical trials. This is part of the agency's commitment to increase awareness of its 2020 guidance, Enhancing the Diversity of Clinical Trial Populations—Eligibility Criteria, Enrollment Practices, and Trial Designs.

Additionally, the FDA has approved Artivion, Inc.'s PerClot Polysaccharide Hemostatic System, intended to control bleeding during surgical procedures. The PerClot system consists of an applicator tip and absorbable polysaccharide granules that rapidly absorb water to form a gelled adhesive matrix.

title: FDA Approves New Treatment for Pneumonia Caused by Certain Difficult-to-Treat Bacteria
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Xacduro, a new treatment for hospital-acquired bacterial pneumonia and ventilator-associated bacterial pneumonia caused by susceptible strains of Acinetobacter baumannii-calcoaceticus complex, for patients 18 years of age and older. The approval was granted due to the high level of need for additional treatment options amid growing global resistance to antimicrobial medicines. Xacduro consists of sulbactam and durlobactam, which work together to kill A. baumannii and protect sulbactam from degradation. The efficacy of Xacduro was established in a clinical trial of 177 hospitalized adults with carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii, where Xacduro was shown to be noninferior to colistin. The most common adverse reaction with Xacduro was liver function test abnormalities. The FDA granted Xacduro Fast Track and Priority Review designations and approved it for use by Entasis Therapeutics.

title: FDA Approves Prescription Nasal Spray to Reverse Opioid Overdose
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Opvee, the first nalmefene hydrochloride nasal spray, for emergency treatment of known or suspected opioid overdose in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. This is the first FDA approval of nalmefene hydrochloride nasal spray for health care and community use. The approval was supported by safety and pharmacokinetic studies, as well as a study in people who use opioids recreationally. The product delivers 2.7 milligrams of nalmefene into the nasal cavity and is intended for use in health care and community settings. The FDA granted this application Priority Review designation to expedite the development and review of the drug. The approval of Opvee was announced by FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf, M.D.

title: The President's News Conference in Hiroshima, Japan
body_summary: The US President recently addressed budget negotiations, stating that a bipartisan deal is unlikely due to extreme proposals. He refused to agree to protecting oil industry tax breaks, pharmaceutical industry excess payments, or wealthy tax cheats while cutting programs for Americans. The President emphasized unity among G-7 leaders on addressing global challenges, including strengthening global health security, climate action, and building a resilient economy. A new tranche of military aid to Ukraine, including artillery and F-16 fighter jets, was announced, with the US beginning to train Ukrainian pilots and strengthening the Ukrainian Air Force. The President also discussed strengthening US alliances with Japan, South Korea, and other nations to counter China's growing military presence, while reaffirming the "one China" policy. The US Government plans to cut spending by 22-35% next year, sparking controversy, with some proposals being accepted and others rejected. Sanctions on China's Defense Minister are being reconsidered, and the President assured world leaders that the US will not default on its debt, citing the 14th Amendment.

title: Joint Statement—Australia-United States Climate, Critical Minerals, and Clean Energy Transformation Compact
body_summary: The United States and Australia agree to strengthen bilateral cooperation under a Climate, Critical Minerals and Clean Energy Transformation Compact, aiming to advance ambitious climate and clean energy action. They commit to establishing a dedicated Clean Energy Industrial Transformation forum to coordinate clean energy supply chain strategies, identifying concrete actions within 12 months to meet Compact objectives, and deepening bilateral collaboration on critical minerals and materials vital to clean energy and defence supply chains. The agreement also includes promoting responsible critical minerals supply, reducing the cost of clean energy technologies, and expanding renewable energy generation. Furthermore, the US and Australia pledge to deepen climate security cooperation, including information sharing and dialogue on defence, diplomacy, and development, with a focus on limiting global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees Celsius and supporting adaptation and resilience in the Indo-Pacific region.

title: Joint Statement—Group of Seven (G-7) Nations Hiroshima Leaders' Communiqué
body_summary: G7 leaders met in Hiroshima from May 19-21, 2023, to discuss global challenges. They reaffirmed support for Ukraine and a commitment to a world without nuclear weapons. The G7 also vowed to promote a free and open Indo-Pacific, strengthen economic resilience, and accelerate the transition to clean energy. The G20 called on MDBs to mobilize up to $600 billion by 2027 through the G7 Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment. G7 nations committed to accelerating climate finance, implementing net-zero transitions, and halting biodiversity loss by 2030. They also aim to end unabated coal-fired power generation globally by 2050. The G7 renewed its commitment to achieving Universal Health Coverage by 2030 and promoting quality job creation, universal social protection, and gender equality.

title: FDA Roundup: May 19, 2023
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration announced that the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine will conduct an independent study on infant formula supply, market competition, and regulation in the United States. The FDA will use the study's findings to develop a long-term national strategy. 

The FDA approved Rinvoq for adults with moderately to severely active Crohn’s disease who have had an inadequate response or intolerance to one or more tumor necrosis factor blockers. The most common side effects of Rinvoq include upper respiratory tract infections, anemia, fever, acne, herpes zoster, and headache. 

The FDA issued marketing denial orders to Mothers Milk WTA for over 250 flavored and tobacco-flavored e-liquids, and published a Small Entity Compliance Guide for the Food Safety Modernization Act Food Traceability Rule.
