The FDA published a Spotlight on CDER Science focused on the role of disclosures in helping consumers understand oncology clinical trial endpoints in direct-to-consumer television advertisements for prescription drugs. 

The FDA granted marketing authorization of the B·R·A·H·M·S sFlt-1/ PlGF KRYPTOR Test System to aid in the risk assessment of certain pregnant women hospitalized for hypertensive disorders. 

The FDA issued draft guidances for industry on Pediatric Drug Development: Regulatory Considerations – Complying with PREA and Qualifying for Pediatric Exclusivity Under the BPCA. 

The FDA issued an import alert for the disposable e-cigarette brand Elf Bar to prevent their illegal tobacco products from entering the U.S. marketplace.

title: FDA Clears New Insulin Pump and Algorithm-Based Software to Support Enhanced Automatic Insulin Delivery
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) cleared the Beta Bionics iLet ACE Pump and the iLet Dosing Decision Software for people six years of age and older with type 1 diabetes. These devices, along with a compatible FDA-cleared integrated continuous glucose monitor (iCGM), form a new system called the iLet Bionic Pancreas. The iLet Bionic Pancreas uses an algorithm to determine and command insulin delivery. The FDA's Director, Jeff Shuren, stated that this action will provide the type 1 diabetes community with additional options and flexibilities for diabetes management. The iLet Bionic Pancreas is an adaptive closed-loop algorithm that requires no additional insulin dosing parameters. The FDA reviewed the devices through the 510(k) premarket clearance pathway and granted clearance to Beta Bionics Inc. The iLet system also simplifies use at mealtime by replacing conventional carb counting with a new meal announcement feature. The clearance applies to people with type 1 diabetes, with more than 11% of Americans diagnosed with the condition.

title: FDA Approves First Topical Gene Therapy for Treatment of Wounds in Patients with Dystrophic Epidermolysis Bullosa
body_summary: The US FDA has approved Vyjuvek, a gene therapy for the treatment of dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa (DEB) in patients 6 months of age and older, as a result of a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled study. Peter Marks, director of the FDA’s Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, described the approval as a commitment to new treatments for rare diseases. Vyjuvek is a genetically modified herpes-simplex virus used to deliver normal copies of the COL7A1 gene to wounds, improving wound healing. A total of 31 subjects with DEB participated in the study, with 60% of Vyjuvek-treated wounds closing completely compared to 26% of placebo-treated wounds. Common adverse reactions included itching, chills, and rash. Vyjuvek was granted to Krystal Biotech, Inc., following Orphan Drug, Fast Track, Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy, and Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review designations.

title: FDA Roundup: May 16, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) updated its newRumor Control page to inform the public on how growing rumors about science, medicine, and the FDA are putting patients at risk. The FDA approved the Globus Medical REFLECT Scoliosis Correction System for treating progressive idiopathic scoliosis in pediatric patients. Idiopathic scoliosis is a common spinal deformity in children, often diagnosed between ages 10 to 18. The FDA issued marketing denial orders to 10 companies manufacturing and marketing approximately 6,500 flavored e-liquid and e-cigarette products, which are now banned from marketing and distribution in the US.

title: FDA Roundup: May 12, 2023
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has updated information on medical device shortages on its website, reflecting the end of the COVID-19 public health emergency. The FDA will continue to monitor the supply chain and update device shortage and discontinuance lists as new information becomes available.

The FDA has also issued updates to standardize prescribing information for amphetamine and methylphenidate products, a class of stimulant medications used to treat ADHD and other disorders.

The FDA has published two discussion papers on the use of artificial intelligence and machine learning in drug development and manufacturing, aiming to spur a discussion with the medical products development community.

The FDA and the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) have issued a joint letter clarifying buprenorphine prescribing recommendations and affirming a commitment to addressing the overdose crisis.

The FDA has announced a joint project with the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop tools for identifying unintended effects of genome editing in animals.

The FDA has authorized the marketing of Swing Therapeutics' Stanza, a smartphone-based prescription digital therapeutic for treating fibromyalgia symptoms in adult patients.

The FDA has approved Librela (bedinvetmab injection) for the control of pain associated with osteoarthritis in dogs, marking the first monoclonal antibody approved for use in dogs.

title: FDA Approves Novel Drug to Treat Moderate to Severe Hot Flashes Caused by Menopause
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Veozah (fezolinetant), an oral medication for treating moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms, or hot flashes, caused by menopause. Veozah is the first neurokinin 3 (NK3) receptor antagonist approved to treat moderate to severe hot flashes from menopause. The medication works by blocking the NK3 receptor, which plays a role in the brain's regulation of body temperature. Menopause, a natural change in a woman's life, occurs between ages 45 and 55, when the body produces less estrogen and progesterone. Veozah targets neural activity causing hot flashes during menopause and is taken orally once a day. The FDA demonstrated Veozah's effectiveness in two phase 3 clinical trials, with a 40-week extension study for safety. The medication has a warning for elevated liver transaminase and should not be used with certain medications or in patients with liver damage or kidney disease.

title: FDA Approves First Drug to Treat Agitation Symptoms Associated with Dementia due to Alzheimer’s Disease
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is announcing the supplemental approval of Rexulti (brexpiprazole) oral tablets for the treatment of agitation associated with dementia due to Alzheimer's disease. This is the first FDA-approved treatment option for this indication. The approval was granted based on two 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies that showed patients who received 2 mg or 3 mg of Rexulti showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in agitation symptoms compared to patients in the placebo group. The recommended starting dosage is 0.5 mg taken once daily, with the target dose of 2 mg once daily. The most common side effects include headache, dizziness, urinary tract infection, and sleep disturbances. The FDA granted this application Fast Track designation, a process designed to facilitate the development and expedite the review of drugs to treat serious conditions and fill an unmet medical need.

title: FDA Finalizes Move to Recommend Individual Risk Assessment to Determine Eligibility for Blood Donations
body_summary: The US FDA finalized recommendations for assessing blood donor eligibility using individual risk-based questions to reduce the risk of transfusion-transmitted HIV. The questions will be the same for every donor, regardless of sexual orientation, sex or gender. Blood establishments can implement these recommendations by revising their donor history questionnaires and procedures. The policy is based on the best available scientific evidence and aims to expand the number of people eligible to donate blood while maintaining safeguards to protect the safety of the blood supply. All prospective donors will answer a series of individual, risk-based questions to determine eligibility. Those with new or recent HIV infection, or taking HIV medications, will be deferred. The FDA worked diligently to review comments and finalize these recommendations as quickly as possible, with support from data from countries with similar policies.

title: FDA Roundup: May 09, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has granted marketing authorization for the VITROS Immunodiagnostic Products Anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG Reagent Pack, which can be used to detect IgG antibodies to SARS-CoV-2 in human serum and plasma samples. This test is intended for prescription use only and is meant to aid in identifying individuals who have an adaptive immune response to SARS-CoV-2 from a recent or prior infection. The test is one of the first serology COVID-19 tests to receive marketing authorization through a traditional premarket review process. The FDA has also authorized over 449 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 302 molecular tests and 83 antibody tests.

title: Executive Order 14099—Moving Beyond COVID-19 Vaccination Requirements for Federal Workers
body_summary: President Joseph R. Biden Jr. has issued an executive order revoking vaccination requirements for Federal employees and federally specified safety protocols for Federal contractors. The order follows the end of the acute phase of the COVID-19 pandemic and the decline of COVID-19 deaths and hospitalizations since September 2021. The Administration has implemented the largest adult vaccination program in U.S. history, with over 270 million Americans receiving at least one dose of the COVID-19 vaccine. The order is effective at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on May 12, 2023, and does not create any right or benefit enforceable at law.

title: FDA Roundup: May 05, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued safety communications to warn consumers and healthcare providers about certain recalled SD Biosensor, Inc. Pilot COVID-19 At-Home Tests distributed by Roche Diagnostics due to bacterial contamination concerns. On the same day, FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf published a statement on Cronobacter, a naturally occurring bacteria found in environments, and actions the FDA is taking to keep the food supply safe. The FDA also seized nearly 250,000 bottles of kratom products worth over $3 million after allegations of inadequate information and adulteration. Additionally, the FDA posted 33 deemed final orders for 32 monograph therapeutic categories and one for non-monograph conditions as part of over-the-counter monograph reform. As of today, 447 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 300 molecular tests and 83 antibody and other immune response tests.

title: Statement on the Appointment of Neera N. Tanden as Domestic Policy Council Director and Stefanie G. Feldman as White House Staff Secretary
body_summary: The President is pleased to announce that Neera Tanden will continue to drive the formulation and implementation of his domestic policy agenda. Neera, as Senior Advisor and Staff Secretary, has 25 years of experience in public policy, having served three Presidents and led one of the largest think tanks in the country. She was a key architect of the Affordable Care Act and helped drive key domestic policies, including clean energy subsidies and sensible gun reform. The President looks forward to continuing to work closely with Neera in her new role.

title: FDA Approves First Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Vaccine
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Arexvy, the first respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine, for the prevention of lower respiratory tract disease caused by RSV in individuals 60 years of age and older. The vaccine was approved based on the results of an ongoing, randomized, placebo-controlled clinical study conducted in the US and internationally. The study showed that Arexvy significantly reduced the risk of developing RSV-associated LRTD by 82.6% and severe RSV-associated LRTD by 94.1%. The vaccine's safety was also evaluated, with most common side effects reported at the injection site, including pain, fatigue, and muscle pain. However, the FDA has required the company to conduct a postmarketing study to assess potential serious risks, including Guillain-Barré syndrome and acute disseminated encephalomyelitis. The approval was granted to GlaxoSmithKline Biologicals and was granted Priority Review designation.

title: Implementation Note issued May 3, 2023
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on May 3, 2023: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 5.15 percent, effective May 4, 2023. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective May 4, 2023, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 5 to 5â1/4 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 5.25 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 5.05 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $60 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest into agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve a 1/4 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate to 5.25 percent, effective May 4, 2023. In taking this action, the Board approved requests to establish that rate submitted by the Boards of Directors of the Federal Reserve Banks of Boston, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Chicago, St. Louis, Minneapolis, Kansas City, Dallas, and San Francisco. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Economic activity expanded at a modest pace in the first quarter. Job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation remains elevated. The U.S. banking system is sound and resilient. Tighter credit conditions for households and businesses are likely to weigh on economic activity, hiring, and inflation. The extent of these effects remains uncertain. The Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 5 to 5-1/4 percent. The Committee will closely monitor incoming information and assess the implications for monetary policy. In determining the extent to which additional policy firming may be appropriate to return inflation to 2 percent over time, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in its previously announced plans. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Austan D. Goolsbee; Patrick Harker; Philip N. Jefferson; Neel Kashkari; Lorie K. Logan; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: FDA Roundup: May 2, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has published a Conversations with Experts QA discussing its engagement with international organizations to support the global food safety system. On Monday, the FDA warned consumers not to purchase or use Nose Slap and Soul Slap products, which are unapproved drugs marketed to promote alertness and boost energy. The FDA also released its third video on cybersecurity for medical devices, featuring Dr. Mark Jarrett, Chief Quality Officer from Northwell Health. On April 24, the FDA approved the xT CDx, a next-generation sequencing-based companion diagnostic that detects certain mutations in RAS genes in tumor samples of colorectal cancer patients. The FDA published Consumer Updates warning consumers about incidents of serious adverse events associated with the use of Apetamin and SARMs. On Monday, April 24, the FDA issued an emergency use authorization for the Status COVID-19 Antigen Rapid Test for Home Use. As of today, 446 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations.

title: FDA Takes Additional Steps to Advance Decentralized Clinical Trials
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is releasing a new draft guidance on decentralized clinical trials. The guidance provides recommendations for sponsors, investigators, and stakeholders on implementing decentralized trials, which involve trial-related activities at locations other than traditional clinical trial sites. The FDA aims to increase the breadth and diversity of participants in clinical trials and improve accessibility for those with rare diseases or mobility challenges. The new guidance builds on 2020 agency recommendations and is expected to facilitate the development of drugs in areas of medical need. The FDA Commissioner, Robert M. Califf, M.D., stated that decentralized clinical trials may enhance convenience for trial participants, reduce the burden on caregivers, and expand access to more diverse populations. The guidance covers topics such as design considerations, remote clinical trial visits, and roles and responsibilities of the sponsor and investigators.

title: FDA Conditionally Approves First Drug for Anemia in Cats with Chronic Kidney Disease
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has conditionally approved Varenzin-CA1 (molidustat oral suspension), the first drug for treating nonregenerative anemia associated with chronic kidney disease (CKD) in cats. Nonregenerative anemia is a fatal condition that can occur in cats with CKD, resulting from the kidneys' inability to produce enough red blood cells. Varenzin-CA1 works by increasing production of the hormone erythropoietin, which stimulates the bone marrow to produce red blood cells. The drug was approved under expanded conditional approval, a pathway for innovative treatments, and is available only by prescription from a licensed veterinarian. The initial approval is valid for one year with the potential for four annual renewals, and the drug's safety and effectiveness were evaluated in a study of 23 cats.

title: FDA Roundup: April 28, 2023
body_summary: The FDA issued several key guidance documents and approvals, including finalizing guidance for nicotine replacement therapy drug products to assist with smoking cessation and related indications. The agency also authorized additional doses of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine, Bivalent, for individuals with certain types of immunocompromise, and approved modifications to the Medtronic MiniMed 770G System for over-the-air firmware updates. Additionally, the FDA approved the vaccine Prevnar 20 for the prevention of invasive disease and otitis media caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae. The FDA has also authorized various COVID-19 tests and sample collection devices, including 446 EUAs for tests and devices, with 47 antigen tests and 7 molecular tests for serial screening programs.

title: The President's News Conference With President Yoon Suk Yeol of South Korea
body_summary: US President Biden and South Korean President Yoon discussed strengthening the US-ROK alliance amid an unprecedented global crisis. They agreed on significant steps, including extending deterrence against North Korea's nuclear threats, enhancing economic security, and promoting cooperation in emerging technologies. The two leaders reaffirmed their commitment to democracy, peace, and stability in the Indo-Pacific region. They also agreed on joint research and development, cyber, space, and defense cooperation, aiming to strengthen the alliance through a Strategic Cybersecurity Cooperation Framework. The US plans to invest $60 million to support 2,023 youths' exchanges, including the largest Fulbright program. President Biden confirmed Korea's participation in the Nuclear Consultative Group, sharing information and acting jointly to strengthen extended deterrence against North Korea's nuclear threat.

title: FDA Approves First Orally Administered Fecal Microbiota Product for the Prevention of Recurrence of Clostridioides difficile Infection
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Vowst, the first fecal microbiota product taken orally, for the prevention of recurrence of Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile) infection in individuals 18 years of age and older, following antibacterial treatment for recurrent CDI. The approval was granted with Priority Review, Breakthrough Therapy, and Orphan designations. Vowst contains live bacteria manufactured from human fecal matter and is taken orally in four capsules once a day for three consecutive days. The safety of Vowst was evaluated in clinical studies, which showed the product had a lower CDI recurrence rate compared to placebo in a randomized, placebo-controlled clinical study. Common side effects of Vowst included abdominal bloating, fatigue, constipation, chills, and diarrhea.

title: Joint Statement by President Biden and President Yoon Suk Yeol of South Korea Commemorating the 70th Anniversary of the Alliance Between the United States and South Korea
body_summary: US President Biden and ROK President Yoon Suk Yeol met in Washington to commemorate the 70th anniversary of the US-ROK Alliance, reaffirming their commitment to a secure and brighter future for the American and Korean people. They condemned Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine and reiterated their support for diplomacy with the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. The two leaders committed to strengthening regional partnerships and cooperation on supply chain resilience, as well as U.S.-ROK-Japan trilateral cooperation and shared values. They emphasized the importance of preserving peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait and opposing unilateral attempts to change the status quo in the Indo-Pacific. The US and ROK pledged to deepen their ties, investing in critical technologies, combating climate change, and accelerating the clean energy transition, with a focus on power sector decarbonization and clean energy technologies.

title: Statement on the Resignation of Domestic Policy Council Director Susan E. Rice
body_summary: The main action is that the President named Ambassador Susan Rice as their Domestic Policy Advisor. Susan Rice is a capable and determined leader who has led the Domestic Policy Council for over 2 years. Thanks to her efforts, several important initiatives have been implemented, including expanding and strengthening the Affordable Care Act, releasing a national mental health strategy, and enabling Medicare to negotiate lower prescription drug prices. The President has also taken historic actions to reduce gun violence, advance police reform, and address failed approaches to marijuana. Additionally, the President has committed to a national strategy to end hunger and reduce diet-related disease by 2030. The President thanks Susan Rice for her service, counsel, and friendship, and expresses gratitude to her husband Ian and children Jake and Maris for sharing her with the team.

title: FDA Roundup: April 21, 2023
body_summary: The US FDA has approved the MiniMed 780G System for continuous delivery of basal insulin and insulin boluses, and has reopened the comment period for the draft guidance on labeling of plant-based milk alternatives. The FDA has also authorized the Bateman Bottle Breast Implant Removal System, new educational material on genetically modified organisms, and the Selux AST System for antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Additionally, the FDA has authorized over 445 emergency use authorizations for COVID-19 tests and sample collection devices, including molecular tests and antigen tests for serial screening programs.

title: Statement on the Supreme Court's Decision in Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine v. U.S. Food and Drug Administration
body_summary: The Supreme Court granted the Department of Justice's emergency stay application in Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine v. FDA, preventing a lower court decision that would have undermined FDA's medical judgment and put women's health at risk. As a result, mifepristone remains available and approved for safe and effective use. The FDA's evidence-based approval of mifepristone is being defended by the administration, which will continue to defend FDA's independent authority to review, approve, and regulate prescription drugs. The administration will fight politically driven attacks on women's health, emphasizing the need for the American people to use their vote to elect a Congress that will pass a law restoring protections under Roe v. Wade.

title: Executive Order 14096—Revitalizing Our Nation's Commitment to Environmental Justice for All
body_summary: The US government has established a government-wide approach to environmental justice, requiring each agency to incorporate it into its mission. Agencies must analyze and address disproportionate health and environmental effects, provide opportunities for public engagement, and collaborate with Tribal governments. To advance environmental justice, the government plans to require agencies to submit Environmental Justice Strategic Plans and Assessments every 4 years, set goals and metrics, and evaluate their effectiveness. The plan also establishes an Environmental Justice Science, Data, and Research Plan to analyze gaps in data and research. The US government requires agencies to provide recommendations to the Chair of CEQ on data sources for the Climate and Economic Justice Screening Tool and develop research and data on environmental justice. Executive Order 14008 has been amended to add sections related to the Interagency Council, public meetings, and a clearinghouse. A new White House Office of Environmental Justice has been established, headed by a Federal Chief Environmental Justice Officer.

title: FDA Roundup: April 18, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has granted marketing authorization to the NTX100 Tonic Motor Activation (NTX100 ToMAc) System, a non-invasive device that provides high-frequency, low-level electrical stimulation to treat primary moderate-severe Restless Legs Syndrome. The system, which includes two separate therapy units and electrode patches, can be adjusted by the patient and calibrated by the prescribing clinician using a Clinician App. The device received Breakthrough Device designation in 2020. The FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research has also released updates on COVID-19 testing, with 446 tests and sample collection devices authorized under emergency use authorizations, including 300 molecular tests, 84 antibody tests, 61 antigen tests, and one diagnostic breath test.

title: Executive Order 14095—Increasing Access to High-Quality Care and Supporting Caregivers
body_summary: The US government aims to improve access to high-quality early care and education, as well as long-term care, by addressing the persistent gap between costs and prices. The President directs agencies to enhance jobs and support for caregivers, increase affordable care access, and provide more care options for families. The Secretary of Health and Human Services will consider actions to promote adequate nursing home staffing, including guidance and technical assistance. The government plans to issue regulations to reduce child care costs, expand employee access to child care services, and enhance recruitment and retention of child development program workers. Additionally, the government is enabling individuals to start and operate care businesses locally, reviewing policies to increase community care capacity, and designing a pilot program for Co-Employer Option in veteran home health services.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Changes to Simplify Use of Bivalent mRNA COVID-19 Vaccines
body_summary: The US FDA amended the emergency use authorizations for Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 bivalent mRNA vaccines to simplify the vaccination schedule for individuals 6 months of age and older. The vaccines are now authorized for use in all doses. This change follows a unanimous vote by the FDA's Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee (VRBPAC) on January 26. The updated vaccines have new fact sheets, consolidating information for healthcare providers and recipients.

title: FDA Approves Cell Therapy for Patients with Blood Cancers to Reduce Risk of Infection Following Stem Cell Transplantation
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Omisirge (omidubicel-onlv), a cell therapy to quicken the recovery of neutrophils in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older with blood cancers after umbilical cord blood transplantation. The product is intended to reduce the risk of infection. Director of the FDA's Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, Peter Marks, stated that the approval is an important advance in cell therapy treatment for patients with blood cancers. The safety and effectiveness of Omisirge were supported by a randomized, multicenter study involving 125 subjects with confirmed blood cancers. The study found that 87% of Omisirge recipients achieved neutrophil recovery within 12 days, compared to 83% of umbilical cord blood transplantation recipients. The FDA has granted regular approval of Omisirge to Gamida Cell Ltd.

title: FDA Roundup: April 14, 2023
body_summary: The US FDA issued an emergency use authorization for the Azure Fastep COVID-19 Antigen Pen Home Test, allowing it for serial testing of symptomatic and asymptomatic individuals. The test provides results in 15 minutes and requires retesting if a negative result is obtained. As of the latest update, the FDA has authorized 446 tests and devices under emergency use, including 300 molecular tests, 84 antibody tests, 61 antigen tests, and one diagnostic breath test.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary:
Here is the final summary:

The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on March 21-22, 2023, discussing recent banking sector developments, including Silicon Valley Bank, Signature Bank, and Credit Suisse. The Vice Chair for Supervision noted the U.S. banking system's soundness but will lead a review to strengthen supervisory and regulatory practices. The Committee continued monitoring market developments and inflation expectations, with forward-looking measures showing little change in longer-term expectations but shorter-horizon expectations rising. Market-based policy expectations suggested a peak federal funds rate in May 2023 before declining. Borrowing costs increased due to policy rate expectations and Treasury yields, while lending volumes remained solid. The Committee projects total and core PCE price inflation to step down significantly this year, with near-2% rates expected for 2024 and 2025. The FOMC voted to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 4-3/4 to 5 percent and will closely monitor incoming information, anticipating potential additional tightening.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index Report for March
body_summary: The 12-month inflation rate has fallen to its lowest level since May 2021, following a historically strong job market. Inflation has declined by 45% from its summer peak, with gas prices dropping over $1.40 and grocery prices falling in March for the first time since September 2020. This progress gives hard-working Americans "more breathing room," with wages now higher than 9 months ago after adjusting for inflation. The administration will continue to fight to lower costs, including historic action to lower prescription drug costs for seniors. The "Investing in America" agenda aims to grow the economy, lower costs, create jobs, and reduce the deficit.

title: FDA Roundup: April 11, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has authorized the marketing of the MISHA Knee System, an implant placed alongside the knee joint to reduce load on the joint, for patients with certain types of osteoarthritis. The FDA also announced a virtual public meeting on May 10-11, in partnership with SAMHSA and the Reagan-Udall Foundation, to discuss buprenorphine initiation and maintenance care. Additionally, the FDA has authorized 446 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody tests, antigen tests, and diagnostic breath tests.

title: Statement on the United States District Court for the Northern District of Texas Decision in Alliance for Hippocratic Medicine v. U.S. Food and Drug Administration
body_summary: A single Federal district judge in Texas ruled that a prescription medication approved by the FDA for over 22 years should no longer be approved in the US. The medication, used for medication abortion, accounts for over half of abortions in America. The court substituted its judgment for the FDA, potentially affecting women's access to the medication nationwide. The Department of Justice has filed an appeal and will seek an immediate stay of the decision. The administration will fight this ruling, and Vice President Harris and the president will continue to lead the fight to protect a woman's right to an abortion.

title: FDA Commissioner and Chief Scientist Announce Decision to Withdraw Approval of Makena
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has announced the final decision to withdraw approval of Makena, a drug approved to reduce the risk of preterm birth in women pregnant with one baby. The decision was issued jointly by the FDA Commissioner and Chief Scientist. Effective today, Makena and its generics are no longer approved and cannot be distributed in interstate commerce. The decision was made after a post-marketing confirmatory study failed to verify clinical benefit, and the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research had proposed withdrawing the drug's approval in 2020. FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf and Chief Scientist Namandjé Bumpus recognized the need to develop treatments to reduce the serious risks associated with preterm birth, stating that the decision will help galvanize further research.

title: FDA Roundup: April 4, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued draft Guidance for Industry #278 to clarify approaches and recommendations for Human User Safety assessment and submission of information to support safety of proposed new animal drugs. The FDA has also published a Spotlight on CDER Science examining pharmacodynamic biomarkers in biosimilar product development. Additionally, the FDA provided an update on the ongoing postmarket evaluation of Essure, a permanently implanted birth control device, and has authorized 446 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 300 molecular tests and 84 antibody tests.

title: FDA Moves Forward with Mail-back Envelopes for Opioid Analgesics Dispensed in Outpatient Settings
body_summary: The US FDA requires manufacturers of opioid analgesics dispensed in outpatient settings to make prepaid mail-back envelopes available to pharmacies and other dispensers as an opioid disposal option for patients. This requirement aims to increase convenient disposal options and reduce opportunities for nonmedical use, accidental exposure, and overdose. The FDA anticipates approval of the modified Opioid Analgesic Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (OA REMS) in 2024. The agency also plans to explore in-home disposal options and has issued a Federal Register notice to seek public comments. The FDA's implementation of the Overdose Prevention Framework aims to prevent drug overdoses and reduce deaths through impactful actions.

title: FDA Roundup: March 31, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved several new products, including three generic animal drugs, a opioid monitoring system, an infant sleep system, and a metal alloy screw for surgical fixation. The FDA also released new content on its website, issued a guidance on cybersecurity, and informed consumers about the safety of certain naloxone products. The agency authorized 446 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations. Additionally, the FDA announced a public-private partnership to address scientific hurdles in lupus clinical trial success.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Economic Analysis Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index Report for February
body_summary: The administration is making progress in the fight against inflation, with annual inflation down by nearly 30 percent from this summer. The administration is working to give families more breathing room, taking historic action to lower prescription drug costs for seniors, capping insulin at $35 and allowing Medicare to negotiate lower prices. In February, food inflation hit its lowest level in nearly 2 years. The administration is also investing in America through its Investing in America agenda, creating good-paying jobs for the long term, and rebuilding the country with modern infrastructure and supply chains. The administration is committed to investing from the middle out and the bottom up, rather than turning back to trickle-down economics and cutting critical programs.

title: FDA Approves First Over-the-Counter Naloxone Nasal Spray
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Narcan, 4 milligram naloxone hydrochloride nasal spray, for over-the-counter (OTC) use, making it the first naloxone product approved for use without a prescription. The approval paves the way for the life-saving medication to be sold directly to consumers in stores and online. The timeline for availability and price is determined by the manufacturer. Other formulations and dosages of naloxone will remain available by prescription only. The FDA has used its regulatory authority to facilitate greater access to naloxone, and Commissioner Robert M. Califf said the approval will help improve access to naloxone, reduce opioid overdose deaths, and make the product available at an affordable price. The manufacturer, Emergent BioSolutions, was granted the OTC approval.

title: FDA Outlines Immediate National Strategy to Further Increase the Resiliency of the U.S. Infant Formula Market
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has released a national strategy to ensure access to safe and nutritious infant formula, strengthen the market, and increase resiliency. The strategy is in response to the 2022 infant formula shortage and aims to advance long-term stability and mitigate future shortages. Key elements include: 

- Ensuring industry develops and implements redundancy risk management plans to identify and mitigate supply chain disruptions. 
- Enhancing inspections of infant formula manufacturers by expanding infant formula training for investigators. 
- Expediting review of premarket submissions for new infant formula products to prevent shortages. 
- Continuing to monitor the infant formula supply and developing a forecasting model to prepare for future disruptions. 
- Engaging with U.S. government partners to mitigate factors influencing the supply, such as tariffs and market concentration. 
- Supporting the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) through the U.S. Department of Agriculture. 
- Advancing efforts to prevent Cronobacter sakazakii illnesses and improving consumer education materials. 

The strategy follows the Food and Drug Omnibus Reform Act of 2022 and is expected to be followed by a long-term national strategy, also called for in the same act, to be issued in early 2024.

title: FDA Roundup: March 28, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has released an Immediate National Strategy to Increase the Resiliency of the U.S. Infant Formula Market. The strategy follows a months-long infant formula shortage sparked by unsanitary conditions at an infant formula facility. The FDA took immediate actions to address the shortage and has detailed plans to improve the infant formula supply. The strategy also notes multiple issues beyond the FDA's purview. Additionally, the FDA has stopped accepting and processing submissions to the Voluntary Cosmetic Registration Program (VCRP) due to the Modernization of Cosmetics Regulation Act of 2022 (MoCRA). MoCRA gives the FDA new authorities to regulate cosmetics, including facility registration and product listing. The FDA has also published a webpage about MoCRA and its implementation.

title: FDA Takes Additional Steps to Improve Nutrition, Reduce Disease with Expanded Use of Salt Substitutes to Help Lower Sodium Intake
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration proposed changes to the standards of identity for foods that include salt to permit the use of safe and suitable salt substitutes. This would help support a healthier food supply by providing flexibility for industry innovation to reduce sodium content in standardized foods. The proposed rule would affect 80 SOIs that specify salt as a required or optional ingredient, impacting 140 of the 250 existing SOIs. The rule defines salt substitutes as safe and suitable ingredients that can replace some or all of the salt in standardized foods. The FDA aims to reduce sodium intake and lower the risk of hypertension, a leading cause of heart disease and stroke, as part of the Biden-Harris Administration's National Strategy on Hunger, Nutrition, and Health.

title: FDA Works to Further Improve Nutrition, Reduce Diet-Related Chronic Disease with Dietary Guidance Statements on Food Labels
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a draft guidance on how to use Dietary Guidance Statements on food labels to promote good nutrition and consistency in labeling. The guidance is part of the FDA's goal to reduce the burden of chronic disease and advance health equity. The FDA Commissioner, Robert M. Califf, stated that diet-related chronic diseases are leading causes of death and disability in the US, disproportionately affecting communities of color and rural areas.

The guidance recommends that products contain a meaningful amount of the food or category of foods subject to the statement, and not exceed certain amounts of saturated fat, sodium, and added sugars. The aim is to enhance consistency in the use of such statements, consumer understanding, and facilitate industry innovation towards healthier foods.

The FDA's nutrition initiatives include empowering consumers with more informative labeling and education, and complementing the Biden-Harris Administration's National Strategy on Hunger, Nutrition, and Health, which aims to end hunger and reduce diet-related diseases by 2030. The agency has also issued a proposed rule to update the definition of "healthy" on food labels and is exploring a "front-of-pack" labeling initiative.

title: FDA Issues Draft Guidance Aimed at Improving Oncology Clinical Trials for Accelerated Approval
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued draft guidance on Clinical Trial Considerations to Support Accelerated Approval of Oncology Therapeutics. The guidance provides recommendations to sponsors for designing clinical trials to support accelerated approval. Director Richard Pazdur, MD, stated that the FDA's accelerated approval program has provided patients with cancer earlier access to novel treatments.

The draft guidance discusses the design of clinical trials, the use of randomized clinical trials versus single-arm studies, and the conduct of postmarketing confirmatory studies. It highlights the potential advantage of using a single trial for both accelerated approval and verification of clinical benefit.

The Oncology Center of Excellence has launched Project Confirm, a transparency initiative that promotes discussion and research on the accelerated approval program. The project developed a searchable database of oncology accelerated approvals, which has been adopted by the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research.

title: FDA Roundup: March 24, 2023
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration finalized two guidances: one for medical devices issued during the COVID-19 public health emergency and another for devices issued emergency use authorizations related to COVID-19. The guidances outline the FDA's general recommendations for transitioning to normal operations. The transition period for impacted devices is 180 days, and the FDA encourages stakeholders to plan for the transition process.

The FDA also issued a press release announcing the expanded use of salt substitutes to help lower sodium intake, as part of the Biden-Harris Administration's National Strategy on Hunger, Nutrition, and Health. Additionally, the FDA released a draft guidance on Dietary Guidance Statements on food labels to promote good nutrition and consistency in labeling.

The FDA announced rates for over-the-counter monograph drug user fees for fiscal year 2023 and released a framework for the use of digital health technologies in drug and biological product development.

The FDA released a report on the comprehensive approach to ensuring that imported seafood meets food safety requirements and standards of domestically produced seafood. New educational materials were also released to educate patients about biosimilars, including materials specifically for patients with diabetes.

As of today, 445 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody and other immune response tests, antigen tests, and diagnostic breath tests.

title: Joint Statement by President Biden and Prime Minister Justin P.J. Trudeau of Canada
body_summary: The US and Canada reaffirmed their historic alliance, committing to a renewed partnership focusing on clean energy, critical mineral supply chains, and protecting shared waters and the Arctic. Key initiatives include catalyzing clean energy, creating good jobs, and launching an Energy Transformation Task Force. The US welcomed Canada's investment of CAD $420 million for the Great Lakes, while the US Bipartisan Infrastructure Law provided USD $1 billion for cleanup and restoration activities. The two countries aim to modernize their treaty regime, focusing on flood risk management, power generation, and environmental benefits. Additionally, they are expanding cooperation on fentanyl and precursor chemicals, as well as joining a global coalition against synthetic drugs, and remain committed partners on migration and protection issues, including welcoming 15,000 migrant arrivals on a humanitarian basis.

title: The President's News Conference With Prime Minister Justin P.J. Trudeau of Canada in Ottawa, Canada
body_summary: US President Biden welcomed Canadian Prime Minister Trudeau to the White House, marking progress on the February 2021 Roadmap for a Renewed U.S.-Canada Partnership. The two leaders discussed priorities such as growing the middle class, strengthening the economy, and protecting the environment. Canada will invest $420 million to protect the Great Lakes and $1 billion in semiconductors with IBM. The US and Canada agreed to secure critical mineral supply chains, including semiconductors, and strengthen their economic and security partnerships. President Biden praised Canada's support for Ukraine and expressed gratitude for Canadian companies' investment in semiconductor packaging. The two leaders also discussed security measures, social media, and Haiti, agreeing that the international community must take action to stabilize the country.

title: Implementation Note issued March 22, 2023
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on March 22, 2023: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 4.9 percent, effective March 23, 2023. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective March 23, 2023, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 4-3/4 to 5 percent. Conduct standing overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 5 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion. Conduct standing overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 4.8 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $60 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest into agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve a 1/4 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate to 5 percent, effective March 23, 2023. In taking this action, the Board approved requests to establish that rate submitted by the Boards of Directors of the Federal Reserve Banks of Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Richmond, Atlanta, Kansas City, Dallas, and San Francisco. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators point to modest growth in spending and production. Job gains have picked up in recent months and are running at a robust pace; the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation remains elevated. The U.S. banking system is sound and resilient. Recent developments are likely to result in tighter credit conditions for households and businesses and to weigh on economic activity, hiring, and inflation. The extent of these effects is uncertain. The Committee remains highly attentive to inflation risks. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 4-3/4 to 5 percent. The Committee will closely monitor incoming information and assess the implications for monetary policy. The Committee anticipates that some additional policy firming may be appropriate in order to attain a stance of monetary policy that is sufficiently restrictive to return inflation to 2 percent over time. In determining the extent of future increases in the target range, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in its previously announced plans. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Austan D. Goolsbee; Patrick Harker; Philip N. Jefferson; Neel Kashkari; Lorie K. Logan; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: FDA Roundup: March 21, 2023
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has completed its second pre-market consultation for a human food made from cultured animal cells. The firm will use animal cell culture technology to produce the food. The consultation is not an approval process, and the FDA has no further questions about the firm's safety conclusion. Before entering the U.S. market, the food must meet federal requirements.

The FDA posted a warning letter to www.ivermectin4covid.com for offering drugs for sale in the U.S. that are intended to mitigate, prevent, treat, diagnose, or cure COVID-19. Consumers should consult with their healthcare provider.

The FDA approved an expanded indication for the Inspire Medical Systems, Inc., Inspire II Upper Airway Stimulator (UAS) system to add certain pediatric patients between 13 and 18 years of age with Down syndrome and severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).

As of today, 445 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 300 molecular tests and sample collection devices, 84 antibody and other immune response tests, 60 antigen tests, and one diagnostic breath test.

title: FDA Denies Marketing of Two Vuse Solo Menthol E-Cigarette Products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued marketing denial orders for two menthol e-cigarette products, Vuse Replacement Cartridge Menthol 4.8% G1 and Vuse Replacement Cartridge Menthol 4.8% G2, currently marketed by R.J. Reynolds Vapor Company. The products must not be marketed or distributed in the US or risk FDA enforcement action. The company can resubmit applications to address deficiencies. The FDA evaluated the products' premarket tobacco product applications and determined they lacked sufficient evidence to demonstrate the products' benefits for public health. The FDA's decision is guided by science and will always guide its decision-making on tobacco product applications. Existing evidence shows non-tobacco-flavored e-cigarettes, including menthol-flavored e-cigarettes, have a known risk with regard to youth appeal, while tobacco-flavored e-cigarettes do not pose the same risk.

title: FDA Roundup: March 17, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued an emergency use authorization for the Cue Mpox (Monkeypox) Molecular Test for use in a point-of-care setting. The FDA has also updated its webpage on medical device shortages, added several medical devices to the device discontinuance list, and issued a warning letter to Olympus Medical Systems Corporation for compliance issues related to the reprocessing of endoscopes. Additionally, the FDA has announced a final guidance on definitions of suspect and illegitimate products for verification obligations under the Drug Supply Chain Security Act, and has issued draft guidance on developing local anesthetic drug products with prolonged duration of effect. As of today, 445 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations.

title: FDA Authorizes Copenhagen Classic Snuff to be Marketed as a Modified Risk Tobacco Product
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has authorized the marketing of U.S. Smokeless Tobacco Company's Copenhagen Classic Snuff as a modified risk tobacco product. The product's claim suggests that switching from cigarettes to this snuff reduces the risk of lung cancer. The FDA's review of available evidence, including recommendations from the Tobacco Products Scientific Advisory Committee, found the claim to be scientifically accurate. The company is required to conduct postmarket surveillance and studies to assess product users' behavior and impact on population health. The modified risk granted order will expire in five years and the company must request and receive FDA authorization to continue marketing the product.

title: Statement on Insulin Price Reductions
body_summary: The three leading insulin producers in America have agreed to substantially reduce their prices, following the President's calls to expand the $35 cap for seniors to all Americans. Sanofi has recognized that charging hundreds of dollars for insulin that costs $10 to produce is unjust. The President's administration continues to work on bringing relief to working people and families. Congress should pass legislation to ensure affordable insulin for all, a Junk Fee Prevention Act, and childcare affordability. Repealing the Inflation Reduction Act, which would cut Medicare benefits and increase prescription drug costs, is not supported. The President is optimistic about America's future, citing strong job growth and progress against global inflation.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Bivalent Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine as Booster Dose for Certain Children 6 Months through 4 Years of Age
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) amended the emergency use authorization (EUA) of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine, Bivalent, to provide a single booster dose for children 6 months through 4 years of age at least 2 months after completion of primary vaccination with three doses of the monovalent vaccine. This authorization was based on data from a clinical study of 60 children in this age group who received a booster dose of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine, Bivalent. The study showed an immune response to both the original SARS-CoV-2 virus strain and the omicron BA.4/BA.5 lineages. The authorization is also supported by previous analyses of the effectiveness of primary vaccination with the monovalent Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine in individuals 16 years of age and older and individuals 6 months through 4 years of age. Peter Marks, M.D., Ph.D., director of the FDA's Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, stated that the authorization provides an opportunity for parents and caregivers to update their children's protection with the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine, Bivalent.

title: FDA Roundup: March 14, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has revised its Fact Sheets for Healthcare Providers Administering Vaccine (Vaccination Providers) and Recipients and Caregivers for the Janssen COVID-19 Vaccine to include warnings about increased risks of myocarditis and pericarditis, particularly within 0-7 days following vaccination. The scope of authorization for a booster dose has also been revised. Additionally, the FDA has approved Daybue (trofinetide) oral solution as the first treatment for Rett syndrome in adults and children 2 years of age and older. The FDA has authorized 444 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 299 molecular tests and 84 antibody and other immune response tests.

title: Joint Statement by President Biden and President Ursula von der Leyen of the European Commission
body_summary: The US and EU are deepening their economic partnership to build clean energy economies and address climate change, national security challenges, and economic security. They are launching initiatives to boost clean energy, electric vehicle batteries, and clean hydrogen, with ambitious outcomes in the Global Arrangement on Sustainable Steel and Aluminum negotiations by October 2023. The US and EU are also working together to support Ukraine's energy security and impose swift sanctions to reduce Russia's revenue, addressing the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Additionally, the US and EU will strengthen economic security and national security through transatlantic cooperation, diversifying supply chains and increasing collective preparedness to address non-market policies and economic coercion.

title: FDA Roundup: March 10, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a notice addressing COVID-19-related guidance documents, including those that will no longer be in effect after the expiration of the COVID-19 public health emergency on May 11, 2023. The FDA has also granted marketing authorization for the Sofia 2 SARS Antigen+ FIA, a test for detecting COVID-19 virus within 6 days of symptom onset. The agency has established criteria for special controls to ensure safety and effectiveness for tests of this type. Additionally, the FDA has provided updates on reports of squamous cell carcinoma in the capsule around breast implants, and will host a webinar about its Critical Path for Rare Neurodegenerative Diseases public-private partnership on March 15.

title: FDA Seeks $7.2 Billion to Protect and Advance Public Health by Enhancing Food Safety and Advancing Medical Product Availability
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is requesting a $7.2 billion budget for fiscal year 2024 to leverage new technologies, recruit a skilled workforce, and adapt oversight to new production and business models. The request includes an increase of $372 million and a $150 million boost in user fees. Key highlights include $128.2 million for food safety modernization, $23 million for opioid crisis efforts, and $50 million to advance the president's Cancer Moonshot goals. The FDA also proposes changes to improve regulatory clarity and enforcement, such as removing uncertainty for pesticide regulation, expanding drug shortage notification requirements, and broadening inspection authority.

title: FDA Updates Mammography Regulations to Require Reporting of Breast Density Information and Enhance Facility Oversight
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration published updates to the mammography regulations to require facilities to notify patients about the density of their breasts, strengthen oversight and enforcement, and improve interpretation of mammograms. The updates aim to improve breast cancer detection and patient access to information about breast density and its impact on cancer risk. The final rule amends the Mammography Quality Standards Act of 1992, which authorizes FDA oversight over mammography facilities. The updates are intended to enhance patient communication, enforcement, and modernize regulations to incorporate current science and mammography best practices.

title: FDA Proposes New Requirements for Tobacco Product Manufacturing Practices
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is proposing new requirements for tobacco product manufacturers to minimize or prevent contamination and limit additional risks by ensuring product consistency. The proposed requirements, which would be finalized if approved, would establish standards for tobacco product design and development, manufacturing, and distribution. These requirements aim to prevent the manufacture and distribution of tobacco products contaminated with foreign substances, such as metal and glass, and address inconsistencies between e-liquid product labeling and actual concentrations. The requirements would also establish a framework for manufacturers to take corrective actions, including recalls, in the event of a contamination issue. The FDA plans to hold a public oral hearing on April 12 and will review comments for 180 days. A meeting of the Tobacco Products Scientific Advisory Committee will be held on May 18 to seek recommendations on the requirements.

title: FDA Roundup: March 7, 2023
body_summary:
The FDA has issued a letter to healthcare providers about expanded work to evaluate the potential risk of exposure to toxic compounds in hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis systems made with chlorinated peroxide cured silicone. The FDA is working with manufacturers to collect and evaluate data to determine the risk and develop strategies if needed.

The FDA has also unveiled a new Dietary Supplement Ingredient Directory, a webpage where the public can find information on ingredients used in dietary supplements. The directory includes links to the agency's actions and communications for each ingredient.

The FDA revised and reissued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for disposable, single-use surgical masks for healthcare professionals during the COVID-19 pandemic. The revision authorizes emergency use of only those masks listed in the EUA's Appendix A.

The FDA cleared the first device authorized under its Safer Technologies Program, a device for fluorescence-guided visualization during gastric and bariatric surgical procedures.

As of today, 444 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under EUAs, including 299 molecular tests and 84 antibody and other immune response tests.

title: FDA Roundup: March 3, 2023
body_summary:
The US FDA has published several news items, including:
A discussion paper on artificial intelligence in drug manufacturing to gather input on AI's impact on the agency's regulatory framework.
A final guidance on continuous manufacturing (CM) of drug substances and drug products.
A letter to healthcare providers about potential issues with a disposable part of the Getinge/Maquet Cardiohelp system.
Pre-registration for the annual training course, Achieving Data Quality and Integrity in Maximum Containment Laboratories, has opened, with virtual and in-person options available.
The FDA has approved Skyclarys (omaveloxolone) as the first treatment for Friedreich’s ataxia, a rare degenerative disease.
As of today, 444 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs).

title: FDA Roundup: February 28, 2023
body_summary: The FDA is withdrawing a 2005 proposed rule on food standards due to comments received in 2005 and 2020. The FDA has also issued letters to healthcare providers about the potential risk of early structural valve deterioration with Abbott Trifecta valves. The FDA has issued an emergency use authorization for an at-home diagnostic test that can identify and differentiate between influenza A and B and SARS-CoV-2. The Lucira COVID-19 & Flu Home Test is a single-use test that can be purchased without a prescription and performed at home. The FDA has updated the Breakthrough Devices Program online metrics to add more device designations and marketing authorizations. The FDA has authorized the EnteraSense Ltd. PillSense System, a device for detecting blood in the upper gastrointestinal tract in adults. The FDA will host a virtual public meeting on Patient-Focused Drug Development for Long COVID on April 25, 2023. The agency has also announced the next presentation in the FDA Grand Rounds lecture series on March 9, 2023, on the topic of Microphysiological Systems as Novel Disease Models and Drug Development Tools.

title: FDA Provides Update on Proposed Human Foods Program and Office of Regulatory Affairs Restructuring
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has begun a national search for a new Deputy Commissioner for Human Foods. The agency is updating its proposed restructuring of the Human Foods Program and Office of Regulatory Affairs (ORA) to enhance coordination, prevention, and response activities. The proposed structure includes an empowered Deputy Commissioner for Human Foods who will report directly to the FDA Commissioner. The ideal candidate will have executive-level and real-world experience in leading the Human Foods Program. The agency is also working on an agency-wide transformation effort to integrate ORA's enterprise-wide expertise with product subject matter experts. Key initiatives include assessing ORA functions, analyzing inspection and compliance functions, and empowering the Deputy Commissioner for Human Foods to oversee program and field resource allocation. The FDA aims to finalize its proposal this Fall, with a 30-day notification period to Congress, and will continue to engage with stakeholders throughout the process.

title: FDA Takes Action to Restrict Unlawful Import of Xylazine
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has taken action to restrict the unlawful entry of xylazine into the country, addressing growing public health concerns. Xylazine, a chemical found in illicit drugs and overdose deaths, will be restricted to prevent its entry into the US market for illicit purposes, while maintaining availability for its legitimate uses in animals. Veterinarians use xylazine to sedate large animals, but it is not safe for human use and can cause serious side effects. The agency aims to prevent xylazine from being mixed with opioids and other illicit products, and will scrutinize imports of xylazine-containing drugs to ensure they are properly labeled and for legitimate veterinary use. The FDA is collaborating with federal, state, and local partners to investigate xylazine-related activities and ensure availability of xylazine-containing drugs for veterinarians.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Economic Analysis Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index Report for January
body_summary: The document states that progress has been made on inflation, with annual inflation in January down from the summer and unemployment at a 50-year low. Take-home pay has also increased. Gas prices have dropped, with prices more than $1.60 since last summer's peak. The speaker emphasizes that the country faces global economic challenges from a position of strength and will not be undermined by Republican efforts to repeal the Inflation Reduction Act or cut critical programs. The speaker's vision is to finish the job in transitioning to stable and steady growth that benefits all Americans.

title: FDA Outlines Steps to Strengthen Tobacco Program
body_summary: The US FDA has announced plans to strengthen tobacco regulation. CTP Director Brian King plans to release a 5-year strategic plan by the end of the year, aiming to optimize review processes, increase the use of the Tobacco Products Scientific Advisory Committee, and post scientific policy memos. The agency plans to convene a summit with senior officials from HHS and DOJ to explore new compliance and enforcement approaches. The FDA aims to reduce addictiveness by establishing a maximum nicotine level and characterizing flavors in cigars, with a goal of cutting cancer death rates in half over 25 years. The agency has also authorized 23 tobacco-flavored e-cigarette products and issued marketing denial orders for over 1 million flavored e-cigarette products deemed harmful to youth.

title: FDA Roundup: February 24, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration published a series of news updates. In a two-part series, Commissioner Robert M. Califf reflects on his one-year anniversary and shares his vision for the future of the agency. The FDA's Foods Program made strides in 2022 to protect the safety of human foods and expand access to safe and nutritious foods. The agency also continues work to advance medical products for patients with rare diseases. Rare Disease Week is observed in February, and the FDA will host a virtual Rare Disease Day. The FDA issued a letter to healthcare providers about potential exposure to airborne chemicals from neonatal incubators. The agency is working with manufacturers to collect data on the products. On March 22, the FDA will co-host a virtual public meeting with the Environmental Protection Agency's Office of Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention. The FDA issued emergency use authorizations for two COVID-19 tests and has authorized over 443 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations.

title: FDA Authorizes First Over-the-Counter At-Home Test to Detect Both Influenza and COVID-19 Viruses
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued an emergency use authorization for the first over-the-counter at-home diagnostic test that can differentiate and detect influenza A and B, commonly known as the flu, and SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19. The Lucira COVID-19 & Flu Home Test is a single-use at-home test kit that provides results from self-collected nasal swab samples in roughly 30 minutes. The test can be purchased without a prescription and is intended for individuals with signs and symptoms consistent with a respiratory tract infection. The test works by swirling the sample swab in a vial and displays results in 30 minutes or less. The test has been validated to correctly identify 99.3% of negative and 90% of positive Influenza A samples, 100% of negative and 88.3% of positive COVID-19 samples, and 99.9% of negative Influenza B samples.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee and Board of Governors held a joint meeting on January 31-February 1, 2023. Jerome H. Powell was re-elected as chair, John C. Williams as vice chair, and Joshua Gallin as secretary. The committee selected the Federal Reserve Bank of New York to execute transactions for the System Open Market Account and appointed Patricia Zobel, Roberto Perli, and Julie Ann Remache as deputy manager and managers of SOMA. They approved a new governance document for open market operations and reaffirmed policies on information security, external communications, investment, and trading. The committee reviewed financial markets, expecting moderate economic growth and potential slowdown in inflation risks. Members agreed to raise the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 4-1/2 to 4-3/4 percent to achieve maximum employment and inflation at 2 percent over time.

title: FDA Provides Draft Labeling Recommendations for Plant-based Milk Alternatives to Inform Consumers
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced draft recommendations for industry on the naming of plant-based foods marketed as milk alternatives. The draft guidance also recommends voluntary nutrient statements for labeling some plant-based milk alternatives. 

The FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf developed the draft guidance to provide clear labeling for consumers to make informed nutrition and purchasing decisions. The guidance aims to address the increased availability and consumption of plant-based milk alternative products, which have expanded to include various types such as cashew, coconut, flaxseed, and walnut-based beverages.

The draft guidance recommends that plant-based milk alternative products with the term "milk" in their name include a voluntary nutrient statement comparing their nutrient composition to that of milk. The FDA encourages consumers to use the Nutrition Facts label to compare the nutrient content of different products.

The FDA is accepting comments on the draft guidance, which does not apply to other plant-based dairy alternatives. A manufacturer may choose to implement the recommendations in a draft guidance before the guidance becomes final.

title: FDA Files Civil Money Penalty Complaints Against Four E-Cigarette Product Manufacturers
body_summary: The US FDA has filed civil money penalty (CMP) complaints against four tobacco product manufacturers for manufacturing and selling e-liquids without marketing authorization. This is the first time the FDA has taken such action to enforce the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act's premarket review requirements for new tobacco products. The FDA previously warned the companies about the violations, but they continued to make and sell unauthorized e-liquids. The FDA is seeking the maximum allowed penalty of $19,192 for each violation. The companies can pay the penalty, settle, or request an extension to respond to the complaint. The FDA has issued over 550 warning letters to firms for violating the law, and most have complied and removed their products from the market.

title: FDA Roundup: February 21, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration published a news summary on Friday. The Commissioner of Food and Drugs, Robert M. Califf, M.D., reflected on his one-year anniversary and shared his vision for the future of the agency.
