Tracey Forfa, J.D., a 30-year veteran of the agency, has been selected as the next Director of the FDA's Center for Veterinary Medicine, effective February 26, 2023. The FDA authorized the Medasense Biometrics Ltd. PMD-200 with the Nociception Level (NOL) Index monitoring system for healthcare specialists to assess physiological response to painful stimuli in anesthetized patients. As of today, 442 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 299 molecular tests and 84 antibody tests.

title: FDA Roundup: February 17, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Lamzede (velmanase alfa), the first enzyme replacement therapy for the treatment of non-central nervous system manifestations of alpha-mannosidosis, a rare genetic condition. Lamzede restores normal cellular activity in patients with alpha-mannosidosis, which affects about 1 in every 500,000 people worldwide. The most common adverse reactions are hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis. The FDA has also published updates on its Medical Countermeasures Initiative and highlighted the new 2022 Food Code, which clarifies food donations from retail food establishments. As of today, 444 tests and sample collection devices are authorized for COVID-19 testing, including 300 molecular tests and 85 antibody tests.

title: Executive Order 14091—Further Advancing Racial Equity and Support for Underserved Communities Through the Federal Government
body_summary: The US Government has ordered the Federal Government to advance equity for all Americans, including underserved communities. By 30 days, agencies must establish Agency Equity Teams led by senior officials, coordinated by the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy's White House Steering Committee on Equity. Each agency must submit an Equity Action Plan by 2025, prioritizing strategies to engage with and invest in underserved communities. The government aims to award 15% of Federal procurement dollars to small business concerns owned by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals by 2025.

title: FDA Advances Additional Activities to Prevent Drug Overdoses and Reduce Death
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has declared a public health emergency due to the opioid crisis. In response, the agency plans to increase transparency regarding opioid analgesics, aiming to improve advisory committee decision-making and public understanding. The FDA will also explore new regulatory tools, including requiring drug developers to demonstrate material safety advantages over existing opioids. The agency aims to improve the pipeline of non-addictive treatments for pain and restore public trust through more effective use of advisory committees, with key recommendations from the 2017 National Academies and potential additional authorities from Congress.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index Report for January
body_summary: Inflation in America is decreasing, with annual inflation falling for 7 consecutive months. Food prices at grocery stores have also decreased. Gas prices are down about $1.60 from their peak last year. Real wages for working Americans have increased over the last 7 months. The administration is continuing to lower costs for families through the Inflation Reduction Act, which has lowered prescription drug costs, health care costs, and home energy costs for tens of millions of Americans. The administration is also eliminating junk fees and creating manufacturing jobs to rebuild supply chains. However, the Republican-led Congress has proposed repealing the Inflation Reduction Act, which would make inflation worse, increase the deficit, and threaten Medicare and Social Security. The administration will stand firm against any efforts to make inflation worse.

title: FDA Roundup: February 10, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued an emergency use authorization for the Cepheid Xpert Mpox test for use in a point-of-care setting, following validation data gathered through the National Institutes of Health Independent Test Assessment Program. The FDA also issued draft guidance to manufacturers of infant formula and laboratories conducting testing on infant formula, and updated information about medical device reports associated with the breakdown of polyester-based polyurethane foam used in Philips Respironics ventilators and machines. The FDA revised its guidance on compounding certain ibuprofen products, and authorized 443 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody and immune response tests, and antigen tests.

title: FDA Roundup: February 7, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is updating its easystep-by-step guide to include information about reporting at-home COVID-19 test results to MakeMyTestCount.org. The FDA encourages voluntary and anonymous reporting of positive or negative test results to help public health departments assess and modify their response to COVID-19. As of today, 440 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 296 molecular tests, 85 antibody tests, and 58 antigen tests.

title: FDA Roundup: February 3, 2023
body_summary: The US FDA announced it does not intend to object to the use of certain qualified health claims regarding the consumption of cocoa flavanols in high flavanol cocoa powder and a reduced risk of cardiovascular disease, provided the claim is worded correctly. The FDA also alerted consumers and healthcare practitioners not to purchase and immediately stop using EzriCare Artificial Tears and Delsam Pharma’s Artificial Tears due to potential bacterial contamination. The manufacturer initiated a voluntary recall and the FDA placed the manufacturer on import alert for inadequate response to records request and current good manufacturing practice violations. The FDA authorized the RefleXion Medical Radiotherapy System, which combines emission computed tomography detection and a linear accelerator, for marketing. The agency also revised the Letters of Authorization for Paxlovid and Lagevrio to remove the requirement for positive test results to prescribe these products. As of today, 443 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 298 molecular tests and 79 molecular authorizations.

title: FDA Approves First Oral Treatment for Anemia Caused by Chronic Kidney Disease for Adults on Dialysis
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Jesduvroq tablets as the first oral treatment for anemia caused by chronic kidney disease in adults receiving dialysis for at least four months. The approval allows patients who have been on dialysis for at least four months to have an additional oral treatment option. The effectiveness of Jesduvroq was established in a study of 2,964 adults, which showed that it raised and maintained hemoglobin levels within a target range. Jesduvroq has a boxed warning for an increased risk of thrombotic vascular events and has warnings and precautions for heart failure, high blood pressure, stomach erosions, and gastrointestinal bleeding. The FDA granted approval to GlaxoSmithKline LLC.

title: Implementation Note issued February 1, 2023
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on February 1, 2023: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 4.65 percent, effective February 2, 2023. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective February 2, 2023, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 4-1/2 to 4-3/4 percent. Conduct overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 4.75 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion; the aggregate operation limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 4.55 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $60 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest into agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve a 1/4 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate to 4.75 percent, effective February 2, 2023. In taking this action, the Board approved requests to establish that rate submitted by the Boards of Directors of the Federal Reserve Banks of Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Richmond, Atlanta, Chicago, Kansas City, Dallas, and San Francisco. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators point to modest growth in spending and production. Job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation has eased somewhat but remains elevated. Russia's war against Ukraine is causing tremendous human and economic hardship and is contributing to elevated global uncertainty. The Committee is highly attentive to inflation risks. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 4-1/2 to 4-3/4 percent. The Committee anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate in order to attain a stance of monetary policy that is sufficiently restrictive to return inflation to 2 percent over time. In determining the extent of future increases in the target range, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in its previously announced plans. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Lisa D. Cook; Austan D. Goolsbee; Patrick Harker; Philip N. Jefferson; Neel Kashkari; Lorie K. Logan; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: FDA Proposes Redesign of Human Foods Program to Enhance Coordinated Prevention and Response Activities
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has announced a new, transformative vision for its Human Foods Program and the Office of Regulatory Affairs (ORA). The proposed structures will have clear priorities focused on protecting and promoting a safe and nutritious U.S. food supply. A single leader, the Deputy Commissioner for Human Foods, will oversee the unified Human Foods Program, reporting directly to the Commissioner. The Program will unify functions from the Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition, Office of Food Policy and Response, and certain ORA functions. Key elements of the proposal include a Center for Excellence in Nutrition, an Office of Critical Foods, and an Office of Integrated Food Safety System Partnerships. The FDA plans to establish a Human Foods Advisory Committee to provide independent expert advice and strengthen enterprise information technology and analytical capabilities. The ORA operating structure will be transformed into an enterprise-wide organization supporting the Human Foods Program and other FDA regulatory programs.

title: FDA Roundup: January 31, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) published a perspective on tobacco regulation in 2022, highlighting progress and looking ahead to 2023. The agency also announced a virtual public meeting on fatal overdoses, issued warning letters to companies selling monkeypox products without FDA approval, and authorized marketing of three new tobacco-flavored heated tobacco products. In 2022, the FDA released its Annual Report, which highlighted achievements in device safety and introduced a new plasmid classification method for antimicrobial resistance. The FDA has authorized 443 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 298 molecular tests, 85 antibody and immune response tests, 59 antigen tests, and one diagnostic breath test.

title: Federal Court Enters Consent Decree Against Florida-based Drug Importer and Distributor
body_summary: The U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida entered a consent decree of permanent injunction against LGM Pharma LLC, an importer and distributor of active pharmaceutical ingredients (API), and two of its executives, Prasad Raje and Shailesh Vengurlekar. The consent decree requires the firm to ensure compliance with current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) requirements under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetics Act (FD&C Act). The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) will conduct ongoing compliance auditing and reporting, and the agency may take action, including ordering the company to cease receiving and distributing drug substances, if further violations occur. The FDA inspected the company's facilities in 2022 and identified significant departures from CGMP requirements, including inadequate quality control measures. A consent decree is in place to require the company to implement and adhere to rigorous quality standards under FDA supervision.

title: FDA Proposes Individual Risk Assessment for Blood Donations, While Continuing to Safeguard U.S. Blood Supply
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is proposing a change in blood donor eligibility assessment, moving from time-based deferrals to individual risk-based questions to reduce the risk of transfusion-transmitted HIV. This approach is similar to policies in the UK and Canada. The proposal is based on a review of available data, including information from countries with similar HIV epidemiology and ongoing surveillance of the US blood supply. The FDA believes the new approach will not compromise safety or availability of the blood supply. The proposed changes include:

* Eliminating time-based deferrals for men who have sex with men (MSM) and women who have sex with MSM
* Revising the donor history questionnaire to ask about new or multiple sexual partners in the past three months
* Deferring donors who report new or multiple sexual partners and had anal sex in the past three months
* Allowing donors who do not report new or multiple sexual partners and anal sex to donate, provided all other eligibility criteria are met

Other considerations include:

* No change in deferral time periods for other HIV risk factors
* Deferring individuals with a positive HIV test or those taking HIV medication
* Blood establishments will continue to test for transfusion-transmitted infections
* Proposing deferral policies for PrEP and PEP users

The agency will review comments for 60 days before finalizing the guidance, which will then be implemented by the nation's blood collection establishments.

title: FDA Concludes that Existing Regulatory Frameworks for Foods and Supplements are Not Appropriate for Cannabidiol, Will Work with Congress on a New Way Forward
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has concluded that a new regulatory pathway for cannabidiol (CBD) products is needed to balance access with oversight and manage risks. The agency is prepared to work with Congress on this matter. The FDA is denying three citizen petitions to allow the marketing of CBD products as dietary supplements due to safety concerns, including potential harm to the liver, interactions with medications, and risks to vulnerable populations such as children and pregnant individuals. A new pathway could provide safeguards and oversight for CBD products, including clear labels, prevention of contaminants, and measures to mitigate risks of ingestion by children. The FDA will not pursue rulemaking allowing CBD in dietary supplements or conventional foods, but will consider a new regulatory pathway for CBD-containing products for animals. The agency will continue to monitor the marketplace and take action against products that pose risks, in coordination with state regulatory partners.

title: Statement on Health Insurance Enrollment Under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: President's efforts to lower healthcare costs and ensure affordable access to quality healthcare have delivered record-breaking results. Over 16.3 million Americans signed up for health insurance through healthcare.gov and state-based marketplaces from November 1 to January 15. This is more than double the number of Americans who signed up during the first Affordable Care Act open enrollment in 2014. Since taking office in January 2021, there has been a 50-percent increase in enrollment in the 30 States using healthcare.gov. Four out of five consumers found health care coverage for $10 a month or less, with millions of families saving $800 per person per year on premiums thanks to the extension of lower rates through the Inflation Reduction Act.

title: FDA Denies Marketing of Two Vuse Menthol E-Cigarette Products Following Determination They Do Not Meet Public Health Standard
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued marketing denial orders for two menthol e-cigarette products currently marketed by R.J. Reynolds Vapor Company. The products, Vuse Vibe Tank Menthol 3.0% and Vuse Ciro Cartridge Menthol 1.5%, cannot be marketed or distributed in the U.S. without risking FDA enforcement. The FDA director, Brian King, stated that the applications for these products did not present sufficient scientific evidence to show that the potential benefit to adult smokers outweighs the risks of youth initiation and use. The FDA evaluated the company's premarket tobacco product applications and determined that the applications lacked sufficient evidence to demonstrate that permitting the marketing of the products would be appropriate for the protection of the public health.

title: FDA Announces Action Levels for Lead in Categories of Processed Baby Foods
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is announcing draft guidance for industry on action levels for lead in processed foods intended for babies and children under two years of age. The proposed action levels aim to reduce potential health effects from dietary exposure to lead. The FDA considers these levels achievable when measures are taken to minimize lead presence and expects industry to strive for continual reduction. The draft guidance outlines action levels of 10 parts per billion (ppb) for certain foods and 20 ppb for others, with varying levels for baby foods to account for consumption differences. The FDA evaluates contaminant levels and exposure based on consumption to determine potential health risks. The action levels are not binding, but the FDA will consider them when determining enforcement actions. The agency expects these levels to result in a 24-27% reduction in lead exposure from foods.

title: Statement on State Unemployment Rates and Efforts To Lower Insulin Costs
body_summary: The US has reached record low unemployment rates nationwide, with 38 states at or below 4% unemployment, including 15 at or below 3%. The Inflation Reduction Act caps seniors' insulin costs at $35 for a month's supply. New data shows 1.5 million seniors could have saved $500 per year on insulin if the provision had been in effect in 2020. The US economy is strong, with Americans seeing neighbors back to work, higher wages, lower pharmacy prices, and new businesses opening.

title: FDA Roundup: January 24, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a final guidance on quality considerations for clinical research related to cannabis and cannabis-derived compounds. The agency reopened the comment period for the proposed rule on color additive certification for 45 days. The FDA has also cleared for marketing the Tidepool Loop, a mobile application for automated insulin dosing to help manage type 1 diabetes. Additionally, the FDA has authorized over 443 COVID-19 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including molecular, antibody, antigen, and diagnostic breath tests.

title: Memorandum on Further Efforts To Protect Access to Reproductive Healthcare Services
body_summary:
The President has ordered further efforts to protect access to reproductive healthcare services, including medication abortion. Since 2000, the medication mifepristone has been approved by the FDA for use in the United States as a safe and effective method to end early pregnancy. On January 3, 2023, the FDA modified the Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS) for mifepristone, allowing healthcare providers and patients to use telehealth to prescribe and receive the medication by mail. The changes aim to reduce the burden on the healthcare delivery system while ensuring access to the medication.

Despite these efforts, some State officials have announced plans to impose restrictions to limit access to mifepristone. The Secretary of Health and Human Services, the Attorney General, and the Secretary of Homeland Security have directed the Interagency Task Force on Reproductive Healthcare Access to consider actions to protect access to reproductive healthcare services. The President remains committed to supporting safe access to mifepristone and defending women's fundamental freedoms.

Within 60 days of the date of this memorandum, the Secretary of HHS, the Attorney General, and the Secretary of Homeland Security shall consider issuing guidance for patients and providers on accessing mifepristone and any further actions to educate individuals on their ability to seek legal reproductive care.

title: FDA Roundup: January 20, 2023
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued guidance on compounding certain ibuprofen products to bolster supply amid record high demand. The FDA has also announced the availability of a draft guidance for mpox drug development programs and published a final rule on radiological health regulations. The agency has authorized 443 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 298 molecular tests and 85 antibody tests, with the purpose of protecting public health and safety against harmful exposure to radiation emitting products and medical devices.

title: FDA Roundup: January 13, 2023
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has released various updates and announcements. The FDA will end the intended enforcement discretion period for harvest and post-harvest agricultural water requirements in the Produce Safety Rule on January 26, 2023, for large covered farms. During this transition, the FDA will work with state and industry partners to advance training and technical assistance.

The FDA has signed a Mutual Recognition Agreement with Swissmedic, allowing for shared GMP inspectional findings to reduce unnecessary costs. The FDA has also published a new informational video about over-the-counter hearing aids and published a Consumer Update about sesame labeling requirements.

The FDA has announced two meetings to identify the scientific research base for action levels for contaminants in foods eaten by babies and young children. The agency has also announced a two-day virtual workshop on February 9-10, 2023, and will webcast the first meeting of the NASEM Committee on the Role of Seafood Consumption in Child Growth and Development on January 19, 2023.

The FDA has approved Airsupra (albuterol and budesonide) inhalation aerosol for the treatment of bronchoconstriction and asthma attacks in patients 18 years of age and older. The FDA has also approved DectoGard, a generic doramectin topical solution for the treatment of gastrointestinal roundworms and other parasites in cattle.

As of January 1, 2023, sesame must be labeled as an allergen on packaged foods, including dietary supplements. The FDA has authorized various COVID-19 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody and other immune response tests, and antigen tests.

title: Statement on the Announcement of Hanwha Q CELLS' Plans To Expand and Build Manufacturing Facilities in Dalton and Bartow County, Georgia
body_summary: The US government has announced a record-breaking solar investment by Hanwha Q CELLS, a direct result of the President's economic plan and the Inflation Reduction Act. This investment is expected to create thousands of good-paying jobs in Georgia, many of which do not require a 4-year degree. The investment will bring back supply chains, lower clean energy costs, and help combat the climate crisis. It will also ensure the production of cutting-edge solar technology in the US.

title: FDA Roundup: January 10, 2023
body_summary: The US FDA has issued guidance on the Foreign Supplier Verification Programs for Importers of Food for Humans and Animals. The agency has also approved 37 new drugs in 2022, known as "novel" drugs, which target various disease areas. The FDA has issued warning letters to Olympus Medical Systems Corporation and its subsidiary Aizu Olympus Co, Ltd. for violations related to medical device reporting and quality system regulations. The FDA has announced a webinar on food safety culture on January 25, 2023, and is testing a single eSTAR for both US and Canadian agencies. The agency has also launched a joint pilot with Health Canada to test the use of eSTAR. Additionally, the FDA has announced new ads for its "The Real Cost" Youth Cigarette Prevention Campaign, and has licensed Adacel for immunization during pregnancy to prevent pertussis. As of today, there are 442 tests and sample collection devices authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations.

title: FDA Roundup: January 06, 2023
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is closely monitoring the emergence of the XBB.1.5 subvariant, a SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant estimated to account for 28% of circulating variants in the US. Due to its similarity to variants not neutralized by Evusheld, the FDA does not anticipate that Evusheld will neutralize XBB.1.5, potentially leaving individuals who have received Evusheld vulnerable to COVID-19. The FDA has issued a warning letter to globalpharmacyplus.com for selling unapproved and misbranded COVID-19 drugs. As of today, 442 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 297 molecular tests and 59 antigen tests. The FDA has also proposed product standards to prohibit menthol as a characterizing flavor in cigarettes and all characterizing flavors in cigars.

title: FDA Grants Accelerated Approval for Alzheimer’s Disease Treatment
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Leqembi (lecanemab-irmb) for the treatment of Alzheimer's disease using the Accelerated Approval pathway. Leqembi is the second of a new category of medications approved for Alzheimer's disease that target the fundamental pathophysiology of the disease. The approval was granted based on a Phase 3 randomized clinical trial that showed significant reduction of amyloid beta plaque in patients with Alzheimer's disease. The drug was studied in a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 856 patients, and treatment was initiated in patients with mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia stage of disease. Leqembi was approved with warnings for amyloid-related imaging abnormalities and infusion-related reactions. The FDA granted Fast Track, Priority Review, and Breakthrough Therapy designations to Eisai R&D Management Co., Ltd. for Leqembi.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee selected Richard Ostrander as deputy general counsel, effective December 13, 2022. The committee discussed financial market developments, including eased conditions, improved sentiment, and declining Treasury yields. Equity markets rose, but growth risks remained. In foreign exchange markets, the dollar depreciated due to moderating US interest rate concerns. The collapse of a crypto lender did not pose broader market risks. Inflation expectations moderated, with survey-based measures pointing to a decline in inflation risk premiums. The Federal Reserve maintained elevated policy rates through 2023, with some respondents shifting their expected path higher. Treasury yields and inflation compensation measures declined modestly. Stock market indexes rose due to reduced concerns about inflation outlook. Borrowing costs decreased, credit flows moderated, and credit quality remained solid. The expected federal funds rate path ended lower, driven by larger-than-expected moderation in inflation. The US economic activity prepared for the December FOMC meeting showed stronger real GDP growth in H2 2022 than previously projected. Labor supply and demand imbalance persisted, with labor force participation rate little changed since January. The Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent to restore price stability, driven by concerns about inflation risks, supply and demand imbalances, and Russia's war against Ukraine.

title: FDA Roundup: December 30, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced that January 1, 2026, will be the uniform compliance date for final food regulations issued in calendar years 2023 and 2024. The FDA approved Briumvi (ublituximab-xiiy) injection for treating patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis. The agency also issued the 2022 edition of the FDA Food Code, providing guidance on food donations and retail food safety. On December 23, the FDA approved a supplemental application for Plan B One-Step. Additionally, the FDA has authorized over 443 tests and sample collection devices for COVID-19 testing, including 298 molecular tests and 79 molecular authorizations.

title: Statement on Health Insurance Enrollment Under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: The US government has announced that nearly 11.5 million Americans signed up for health insurance on healthcare.gov from November 1 to December 15, representing an 18% increase over the same period last year. This marks an all-time record for enrollment. The uninsured rate has fallen to 8%, its lowest level in history. As a result of the Inflation Reduction Act, lower rates on health insurance set to expire will be extended, saving millions of Americans an average of $800 a year. Starting January 1, seniors will see a month's supply of insulin capped at $35, Medicare beneficiaries will pay $0 out of pocket for recommended adult vaccines, and prescription drug companies will pay Medicare a rebate if they raise prices faster than inflation for drugs administered at a doctor's office.

title: FDA Roundup: December 23, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced several updates. The VQIP Application Portal will open on January 1, 2023, for benefits during fiscal year 2024. The FDA has approved a new indication for Actemra (tocilizumab) injection for treating hospitalized adult patients with COVID-19. Two new OTC at-home COVID-19 tests have been issued emergency use authorizations, including the Advin COVID-19 Antigen Test @Home and the ASSURE-100 Rapid COVID-19 Home Test. As of today, 440 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under emergency use authorizations.

title: FDA Approves New HIV Drug for Adults with Limited Treatment Options
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Sunlenca (lenacapavir), a new antiretroviral medication, for adult patients with HIV-1 infections resistant to other treatments. Sunlenca is administered as subcutaneous injections once every six months and is given in combination with other antiretroviral drugs. The safety and efficacy of Sunlenca were established in a multicenter clinical trial involving 72 patients. In the trial, 87.5% of patients who received Sunlenca achieved a certain level of virus reduction within 14 days, and 81% continued to have low HIV RNA levels after 26 weeks. The most common adverse reactions were injection site reactions and nausea. The FDA granted Sunlenca Priority Review, Fast Track, and Breakthrough Therapy designations and approved it for use by Gilead Sciences.

title: FDA Roundup: December 20, 2022
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has published news on various agency initiatives. The Office of Digital Transformation has released a technology-focused Leadership Modernization Action Plan (LMAP), aiming to strengthen technology leadership capabilities. 

The FDA has approved Zycosan (pentosan polysulfate sodium injection) for controlling clinical signs associated with osteoarthritis in horses. 

The agency has issued emergency use authorizations for the ImmuView COVID-19 Antigen Home Test, an OTC COVID-19 antigen diagnostic test that provides results in 15 minutes. 

The FDA has issued a final guidance on Best Practices for Convening a GRAS Panel. 

The White House Office of Science and Technology Policy has announced a request for information related to the Coordinated Framework for the Regulation of Biotechnology.

As of today, 441 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations.

title: FDA Provides Update on External Evaluation to Strengthen Agency’s Tobacco Program
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration's Tobacco Program has released its findings and recommendations following an external evaluation. The evaluation was conducted by a panel led by former FDA Chief of Staff Lauren Silvis. The panel assessed the program's regulatory processes and operations, and provided recommendations for improvement. The FDA leadership, including Director Brian King, Ph.D., M.P.H., will review the report's findings and recommendations over the next several weeks. The FDA aims to prevent initiation and help people quit tobacco use, particularly combustible tobacco products. Despite declines in cigarette use, nearly 500,000 Americans still die from cigarette smoking each year. The FDA will ensure clear communication of any changes to its operations and processes, and will provide support to its workforce to fulfill its commitment to public health.

title: Federal Court Enters Consent Decree Against Oklahoma Drug Compounder
body_summary: The U.S. District Court for the Western District of Oklahoma entered a consent decree against Qualgen LLC, prohibiting the company from distributing adulterated drugs in interstate commerce. The decree follows a complaint filed by the U.S. Department of Justice on behalf of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, which asserts that Qualgen introduced adulterated drugs into interstate commerce. The FDA has previously cited Qualgen for CGMP violations since 2015, including a safety alert in 2015 and a warning letter in 2016. Qualgen is registered as an outsourcing facility and is allowed to exempt compounded drugs from FDA approval requirements, but must comply with CGMP requirements. The agency's most recent inspection ended in September 2022.

title: FDA Roundup: December 16, 2022
body_summary: The FDA has released several updates and announcements. A draft guidance on antimicrobial resistance is open for public comment until March 20, 2023. Manufacturers must comply with new regulations on sesame labeling, effective January 1, 2023. The FDA has provided guidance on COVID-19 testing and has authorized over-the-counter tests. The agency has also updated labeling for capecitabine tablets (Xeloda) and authorized over 440 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 298 molecular tests, 86 antibody tests, and 55 antigen tests. The FDA has warned about fraudulent over-the-counter flu products and posted warnings for companies selling CBD-containing products without FDA approval.

title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapy for the Treatment of High-Risk, Non-Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Adstiladrin (nadofaragene firadenovec-vncg), a gene therapy for adult patients with high-risk Bacillus Calmette-Guérin-unresponsive non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer, on Today. The approval provides an innovative treatment option for patients with high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer that is unresponsive to BCG therapy. Director of the FDA's Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, Peter Marks, stated that this approval addresses an area of critical need. Bladder cancer is a common disease where malignant cells form a tumor in the bladder, and most newly diagnosed bladder cancers (75-80%) are classified as non-muscle invasive bladder cancer. The safety and effectiveness of Adstiladrin was evaluated in a multicenter clinical study involving 157 patients, 98 of whom achieved a complete response (51%) after receiving Adstiladrin therapy once every three months for up to 12 months. Adstiladrin is administered into the bladder via a urinary catheter and is associated with common adverse reactions such as bladder discharge, fatigue, and hematuria. The FDA granted approval to Ferring Pharmaceuticals A/S.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA to Hold Advisory Committee Meeting to Discuss Future Vaccination Regimens Addressing COVID-19
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) will hold a meeting of its Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee (VRBPAC) on January 26, 2023, to discuss modifying the composition of primary doses and booster doses of COVID-19 vaccines. The committee, along with representatives from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the National Institutes of Health, will examine the state of the pandemic, variant evolution, and available data on the current monovalent and bivalent vaccines. The FDA will consider recommendations from the VRBPAC and, if necessary, adjust the current authorizations and approvals. The agency is also planning to discuss the optimal composition of COVID-19 vaccines for primary and booster immunization. This meeting follows a similar VRBPAC meeting in June 2022, which advised the FDA to develop modified COVID-19 vaccines with an omicron BA.4/5 spike protein component for booster doses.

title: Statement on Senator Joseph A. Manchin III's Energy Permitting Reform Proposal
body_summary: The US Congress passed the Inflation Reduction Act to reduce everyday costs, including energy costs. Inflation has already started to come down, but work is not yet done. Senator Manchin supports a permitting reform proposal to cut Americans' energy bills, promote US energy security, and boost energy projects. Many projects face delays, impeding economic growth, job creation, and reducing reliance on foreign imports. Senator Manchin's legislation is a step toward unlocking new energy projects to cut consumer costs and spur jobs. Congress promised a reliable, affordable, and sustainable US energy future with the Inflation Reduction Act. Passing Senator Manchin's permitting reform legislation can help keep that promise and advance the energy future.

title: Implementation Note issued December 14, 2022
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on December 14, 2022: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 4.4 percent, effective December 15, 2022. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective December 15, 2022, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent. Conduct overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 4.5 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion; the aggregate operation limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 4.3 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $60 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest into agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve a 1/2 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate to 4.5 percent, effective December 15, 2022. In taking this action, the Board approved requests to establish that rate submitted by the Boards of Directors of the Federal Reserve Banks of Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Chicago, St. Louis, Minneapolis, Kansas City, Dallas, and San Francisco. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators point to modest growth in spending and production. Job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation remains elevated, reflecting supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic, higher food and energy prices, and broader price pressures. Russia's war against Ukraine is causing tremendous human and economic hardship. The war and related events are contributing to upward pressure on inflation and are weighing on global economic activity. The Committee is highly attentive to inflation risks. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent. The Committee anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate in order to attain a stance of monetary policy that is sufficiently restrictive to return inflation to 2 percent over time. In determining the pace of future increases in the target range, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in the Plans for Reducing the Size of the Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet that were issued in May. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; James Bullard; Susan M. Collins; Lisa D. Cook; Esther L. George; Philip N. Jefferson; Loretta J. Mester; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: FDA Roundup: December 13, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has updated its device shortage list to remove medical gloves (product codes LYY, LYZ, LZA, and LZC). The FDA will continue to monitor the supply chain and update the list as new information becomes available. The agency also released a systematic literature review on advancing food safety culture, aiming to improve the beliefs, attitudes, and behaviors of people and organizations. As of today, 440 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 298 molecular tests and 86 antibody and other immune response tests.

title: Executive Order 14089—Establishing the President's Advisory Council on African Diaspora Engagement in the United States
body_summary: The President of the United States has ordered the establishment of the President's Advisory Council on African Diaspora Engagement in the United States to strengthen dialogue and collaboration with the African Diaspora. The council, composed of 12 members appointed by the Secretary of State, will provide advice on strengthening connections between the US Government and the African Diaspora in the US. The council's functions include providing information, analysis, and recommendations on strategies to advance equity and opportunity for African Diaspora communities, supporting the UN's Permanent Forum on People of African Descent, and promoting cultural, social, political, and economic ties between African communities, the global African Diaspora, and the US. The Advisory Council will meet quarterly and is funded by the Department of State.

title: FDA Roundup: December 9, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is releasing an at-a-glance summary of news from around the agency. On Thursday, the FDA approved the first oral new animal drug to improve glycemic control in otherwise healthy cats with diabetes mellitus not previously treated with insulin, Bexacat (bexagliflozin tablets). The FDA also provided information and resources for consumers about non-invasive body contouring technologies, and warned about the risks associated with these devices. On Wednesday, the FDA released the results of its 2022 sampling assignment, testing talc-containing cosmetic products for the presence of asbestos, with no detections found. The FDA also approved an expansion of the indications for use for the Endomagnetics Ltd. Magtrace and Sentimag Magnetic Localization System for patients with breast cancer. On Tuesday, the FDA issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for the Diazyme SARS-CoV-2 Neutralizing Antibody CLIA Kit. As of today, there are 440 tests and sample collection devices authorized by the FDA under EUAs, including 298 molecular tests and 86 antibody and other immune response tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Updated (Bivalent) COVID-19 Vaccines for Children Down to 6 Months of Age
body_summary: The US FDA has amended emergency use authorizations to include use of updated COVID-19 vaccines in children as young as 6 months. The Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech vaccines have been updated to provide better protection against the omicron variant. Children 6 months through 5 years old can receive a single booster dose of the updated Moderna vaccine, while children 6 months through 4 years old who have not completed their primary series can receive the updated Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine as a third dose. The updated Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine is also authorized as a third dose for children 6 months through 4 years old who have not received the third dose with the monovalent Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine, and as a single booster dose for individuals 5 years and older.

title: Joint Statement—United States-United Kingdom Energy Security and Affordability Partnership
body_summary: The US and UK commit to intensifying their collaboration to support international energy security, affordability, and sustainability in the face of Russia's illegal invasion of Ukraine. Their immediate goal is to stabilise energy markets, reduce demand, and ensure short-term security of supply. To achieve this, they are establishing a Joint Action Group for Energy Security and Affordability, which will focus on three priority areas: energy efficiency, gas supply, and nuclear cooperation. The UK aims to reduce its energy consumption by 15% by 2030, while the US invests over $30 billion in energy efficiency and renewable energy solutions for low-income communities. The US also aims to enhance its LNG supply to the UK and wider European market, while prioritising low-carbon LNG infrastructure. The Joint Action Group will be convened by a representative from the offices of the President and the Prime Minister, and will complement the existing Strategic Energy Dialogue.

title: FDA Provides Update on External Evaluation to Strengthen Agency’s Human Foods Program
body_summary: The FDA Commissioner has commissioned an external evaluation of the Human Foods Program, including the Office of Food Policy and Response, Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition, and relevant parts of the Office of Regulatory Affairs. The evaluation panel, facilitated by the Reagan-Udall Foundation, has released its findings and recommendations to the agency. The Commissioner is committed to providing a public update on the new vision for the FDA Human Foods Program by the end of January 2023, and will form a group of agency leaders to advise on implementing the findings. The Human Foods Program aims to provide a safe and nutritious food supply, and the Commissioner is committed to building a world-class program that works best for the public, stakeholders, and employees. The evaluation has identified the need for evolution of the program leadership and structure, and the agency will prioritize maintaining upgraded digital technology systems.

title: FDA Roundup: December 6, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a final guidance on prioritizing enforcement and regulatory actions for homeopathic products marketed in the US without FDA approval. The agency will prioritize products intended for populations at greater risk, such as infants and children, the elderly, and pregnant women, and ophthalmic and injectable products. The FDA has warned about certain homeopathic products, including those containing atoxic substances, and previously recalled products due to contamination. The agency has also updated safety communications for the Endologix AFX endovascular grafts and recommended alternative treatment options for patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm. The FDA is hosting a Rare Disease Day virtual event on February 27, 2023, and has issued updates to the labeling for the Impella RP System manufactured by Abiomed. The FDA has authorized over 441 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody tests, and antigen tests.

title: The President's News Conference With President Emmanuel Macron of France
body_summary: US President Joe Biden reaffirmed the US's commitment to cooperation with France on issues like terrorism and peace. He discussed the Inflation Reduction Act, which aims to create jobs and boost manufacturing, but acknowledged potential differences in subsidies with European countries. Biden expressed willingness to work with Europe to address these differences and ensure fair competition. France's President Emmanuel Macron emphasized the need for resynchronization of economic policies, including addressing issues like semiconductors and hydrogen batteries. The two leaders agreed on a collaborative approach and pledged to stand together against Russia's brutal war against Ukraine, reaffirming their commitment to Ukrainian sovereignty. President Biden stated that for a sustainable peace, Russia's President Putin must pull out of Ukraine, but has no immediate plans to contact him, considering speaking with Putin if he's interested in ending the war.

title: Joint Statement by President Biden and President Emmanuel Macron of France
body_summary: US President Joe Biden and French President Emmanuel Macron reaffirmed their relationship during a State Visit in Washington, emphasizing a shared vision to strengthen security, increase prosperity, and combat climate change. They committed to increasing defense cooperation, addressing global issues, and promoting democratic values. The leaders condemned Russia's invasion of Ukraine, reaffirming support for Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity. The US and France plan to deepen their cooperation on defense space activities, energy, climate change, biodiversity, and global health. They also aim to intensify cooperation on global health security, pandemic prevention, and response, promote an open and transparent agricultural market, strengthen democracy, and combat disinformation.

title: FDA Approves First Fecal Microbiota Product
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Rebyota, the first fecal microbiota product, for the prevention of recurrence of Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) in individuals 18 years and older. Rebyota is administered rectally as a single dose and is prepared from stool donated by qualified individuals. The FDA assessed the safety of Rebyota in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical studies and found that 978 individuals received at least one dose of Rebyota. The most common side effects after receiving Rebyota were abdominal pain, diarrhea, and nausea. The effectiveness of Rebyota was evaluated in a multicenter study, which found that the overall estimated rate of success in preventing recurrent CDI through 8 weeks was significantly higher in the Rebyota group (70.6%) than in the placebo group (57.5%). The FDA granted approval of Rebyota to Ferring Pharmaceuticals Inc.

title: FDA Roundup: November 29, 2022
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued two guidance documents related to food allergen labeling. One document provides guidance on listing major food allergens on labels, and the other document offers recommendations for the effectiveness of anthelmintics in preventing heartworm disease in dogs. The FDA is seeking public comment on both documents, with a 60-day deadline for submissions.

The FDA has also extended the comment period for a proposed rule on food labeling, increasing the deadline from January 30, 2023, to February 16, 2023. 

Additionally, the FDA has issued a safety alert advising consumers not to eat Dai One Food Co. frozen half shell oysters with a specific harvest date from the Republic of Korea.

The FDA is collaborating with the National Institute of Standards and Technology to standardize the description of temperature sensitivity and stability of monoclonal antibodies and other large molecules used in vaccines and therapeutics. 

The agency has also authorized various tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 443 tests and devices for COVID-19 testing.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A Federal Open Market Committee meeting was held November 1-2, 2022, where the Chair discussed ethical standards and accountability. The committee discussed financial market developments in the US, including tightened conditions and higher-than-expected core inflation. They viewed an expected policy rate increase as likely, with some expecting a slower pace of future increases. The federal funds rate increased, passing through to overnight money market rates. Money market fund net yields rose, retail bank deposit rates increased modestly, and foreign asset prices were volatile. Sovereign bond yields in most advanced economies rose moderately, and the US dollar appreciated against major currencies. The committee raised the target range for the federal funds rate by 75 basis points to bring inflation back to 2% over time, and decided to continue reducing Treasury securities and agency debt holdings.

title: FDA Roundup: November 22, 2022
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is issuing an at-a-glance summary of news from around the agency. 

The FDA issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the Lucira COVID-19 and Flu Test, a single-use molecular test for detection of COVID-19 and flu. 

The FDA has received over 90,000 medical device reports associated with the breakdown of PE-PUR foam in ventilators and machines included in a recall announced in June 2021. 

The FDA posted warning letters to five companies for illegally selling products containing cannabidiol (CBD). 

The FDA authorized the Fastep COVID-19 Antigen Home Test and the CorDx COVID-19 Antigen Test, both over-the-counter (OTC) COVID-19 antigen diagnostic tests. 

The FDA will hold a public meeting on Dec. 7, 2022, to offer opportunity for comment on the proposed recommendations for reauthorization of the Animal Drug User Fee Act (ADUFA). 

The FDA issued an immediately in-effect guidance on the preparation of beta-lactam oral antibiotic suspension products. 

As of today, 439 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 300 molecular tests and 53 antigen tests.

title: FDA Approves First Gene Therapy to Treat Adults with Hemophilia B
body_summary: The US FDA has approved Hemgenix, an adeno-associated virus vector-based gene therapy, for the treatment of adults with Hemophilia B. This condition is caused by missing or insufficient levels of blood clotting Factor IX. The approval provides a new treatment option for patients with Hemophilia B, who often experience a high burden of disease. Hemgenix is a one-time gene therapy given as a single dose, which consists of a viral vector carrying a gene for clotting Factor IX. The safety and effectiveness of Hemgenix were established in two studies of 57 adult men with severe or moderately severe Hemophilia B. The most common adverse reactions associated with Hemgenix include liver enzyme elevations, headache, and mild infusion-related reactions. The FDA granted approval of Hemgenix to CSL Behring LLC.

title: FDA Roundup: November 18, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) recently issued updates on several topics. The FDA issued emergency use authorizations for the Hotgen COVID-19 Antigen Home Test and the NIDS COVID-19 Antigen Home Test, allowing for the sale of these tests as over-the-counter diagnostic tools. The agency also updated its Automated External Defibrillators (AED) webpage with information on FDA-approved AEDs and AED accessories. Furthermore, the FDA published reports on cybersecurity modernization, infant formula safety, and online medicine safety. Additionally, the FDA completed its first pre-market consultation for a human food made from cultured animal cells and announced the availability of a draft amended Environmental Assessment (EA) for Atlantic salmon with an intentionally altered genome.

title: FDA Approves First Drug That Can Delay Onset of Type 1 Diabetes
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Tzield (teplizumab-mzwv) injection to delay the onset of stage 3 type 1 diabetes in adults and pediatric patients 8 years and older with stage 2 type 1 diabetes. The drug, administered by intravenous infusion once daily for 14 consecutive days, has been shown to delay the development of stage 3 type 1 diabetes in a randomized, double-blind, event-driven, placebo-controlled trial with 76 patients. The trial results, published after a median follow-up of 51 months, showed that 45% of patients who received Tzield were later diagnosed with stage 3 type 1 diabetes, compared to 72% of those who received a placebo. The FDA granted Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy designations to Provention Bio, which will receive the approval.

title: Joint Statement—G-20 Bali Leaders' Declaration
body_summary: G20 leaders met in Bali, Indonesia on November 15-16, 2022, to address global economic challenges. They reaffirmed their commitment to cooperation and adopted policies to promote strong, inclusive, and sustainable growth. Countries agreed to support the most affected by the food crisis, based on assessed needs, and promote innovative practices in agriculture and digital innovation. The G20 also strengthened global efforts to combat climate change, biodiversity loss, and environmental degradation. A $1.4 billion Pandemic Fund was established to address PPR financing gaps and improve global health governance. The group aimed to enhance digital transformation, promote cross-border data flows, and improve digital literacy skills. Global financial stability was under threat, requiring reinforced resilience measures. The IMF, FSB, and IAG presented a new Data Gaps Initiative to fill identified gaps in economic and financial statistics. G20 leaders also reaffirmed their commitment to inclusive and sustainable economic recovery through concrete actions, including MSMEs, social protection, and green economy initiatives, with a focus on women's empowerment and education.

title: National Security Memorandum on Strengthening the Security and Resilience of United States Food and Agriculture
body_summary: The US Government has established a policy to ensure the food and agriculture sector's security and resilience in the face of high-consequence and catastrophic incidents. This involves identifying and assessing threats, vulnerabilities, and impacts, and prioritizing resources to prevent, protect, mitigate, respond to, and recover from the greatest risks. Security agencies must submit an interim review of critical risks to the sector within 120 days, which will inform the Federal Risk Mitigation Strategy. The US government is strengthening its food and agriculture sector through enhanced information sharing, research and development, and cybersecurity efforts to prevent and respond to threats. Key terms related to biosecurity, including agriculture and risk management, have been defined to support this effort.

title: The President's News Conference
body_summary: The President expressed optimism about the country's prospects after the recent election, where Democrats lost fewer seats in the House of Representatives than expected. Despite predictions, the President announced plans to invite Republican leaders to the White House to discuss economic and national security priorities. He vowed not to support proposals making inflation worse and reaffirmed his commitment to Social Security and Medicare. The President also stated his intention to run for re-election and discussed key issues, including a potential prisoner exchange with Russia, the Supreme Court's affirmative action decision, and economic policies to address inflation and cost of living. The President highlighted empathy in the face of adversity, referencing his personal experiences, and emphasized the need for help and support. He also addressed bipartisan cooperation, Ukraine aid, and China-U.S. relations, reaffirming his commitment to democratic values and ensuring continued funding for Ukraine.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Report on the Employment Situation in October
body_summary: The US economy has added 261,000 jobs, with an unemployment rate of 3.7 percent, a historically low rate. Since the start of the current Presidency, there has been a record 10 million job increase, including a record 700,000 manufacturing jobs added, resulting in 137,000 more manufacturing jobs than before the pandemic. Inflation remains the top economic challenge, with gas prices continuing to come down. The President's plan aims to bring costs down, particularly for healthcare, energy, and everyday expenses. The Republican plan, on the other hand, seeks to increase prescription drug costs, health insurance costs, and energy costs, while providing more tax breaks to big corporations and the wealthy.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators point to modest growth in spending and production. Job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation remains elevated, reflecting supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic, higher food and energy prices, and broader price pressures. Russia's war against Ukraine is causing tremendous human and economic hardship. The war and related events are creating additional upward pressure on inflation and are weighing on global economic activity. The Committee is highly attentive to inflation risks. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 3-3/4 to 4 percent. The Committee anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate in order to attain a stance of monetary policy that is sufficiently restrictive to return inflation to 2 percent over time. In determining the pace of future increases in the target range, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation, and economic and financial developments. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in the Plans for Reducing the Size of the Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet that were issued in May. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; James Bullard; Susan M. Collins; Lisa D. Cook; Esther L. George; Philip N. Jefferson; Loretta J. Mester; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: Implementation Note issued November 2, 2022
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on November 2, 2022: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 3.9 percent, effective November 3, 2022. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective November 3, 2022, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 3-3/4 to 4 percent. Conduct overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 4 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion; the aggregate operation limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 3.8 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $60 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest into agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve a 3/4 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate to 4 percent, effective November 3, 2022. In taking this action, the Board approved requests to establish that rate submitted by the Boards of Directors of the Federal Reserve Banks of Boston, Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Chicago, St. Louis, Minneapolis, Dallas, and San Francisco. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Economic Analysis Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index Report for September
body_summary: The economic reports show progress on the economic plan, with lower inflation and higher incomes. Inflation slowed in the third quarter, with energy prices coming down. Gas prices have declined over $1.20 since the summer's peak. Starting next year, the plan aims to lower prescription drug prices and energy costs. In January, seniors will see their Social Security checks increase by an average of $140 a month. Billion-dollar companies will also face a new tax requirement starting in January.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Economic Analysis Advance Estimate of Gross Domestic Product for the Third Quarter of 2022
body_summary: The U.S. economy is continuing to recover, with Americans' incomes up in the third quarter and price increases coming down. The economy has created 10 million jobs and unemployment is at a 50-year low, with U.S. manufacturing booming. Gas prices have fallen by $1.26 since the summer, with the most common price at $3.39 a gallon. The administration has passed laws to bring down prescription drug prices and health insurance premiums starting next year. Congressional Republicans propose a different agenda, which would increase inflation and add to the deficit, and raise costs for prescription drugs, healthcare, and energy for American families.

title: FDA Denies Marketing of Logic’s Menthol E-Cigarette Products Following Determination They Do Not Meet Public Health Standard
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued marketing denial orders (MDOs) for several e-cigarette products currently marketed by Logic Technology Development LLC (Logic). The affected products include the Logic Pro Menthol e-Liquid Package and Logic Power Menthol e-Liquid Package. These products must not be marketed or distributed in the US, or the company may face enforcement action. The FDA based its decision on a full scientific review of Logic's premarket tobacco product applications (PMTAs), which found insufficient evidence to demonstrate that the products would be appropriate for public health. The applications lacked evidence that the menthol-flavored e-cigarettes would promote complete switching or significant cigarette use reduction relative to tobacco-flavored e-cigarettes among adult smokers. The FDA will allow Logic to resubmit applications or submit new ones to address deficiencies.

title: FDA Roundup: October 25, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued a warning to consumers, caregivers, and healthcare providers not to use recalled Mighty Bliss electric heating pads distributed by Whele LLC due to risks of injury, including electric shocks, skin burns, rashes, or irritation. Whele LLC has recalled over 500,000 products sold through Amazon.com and Walmart.com. The FDA is not aware of any deaths associated with the use of these products, but has received reports of user injuries and device malfunctions. The FDA also issued a warning letter jointly with the Federal Trade Commission to Lakpura LLC for selling unapproved and misbranded products as drugs for COVID-19 treatment. Additionally, the FDA announced a public meeting to discuss adding a work charge for Cronobacter spp. in powdered infant formula. The FDA has authorized 435 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 298 molecular tests and 85 antibody tests.

title: FDA Roundup: October 21, 2022
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued a draft guidance on the Breakthrough Devices Program, which aims to reduce disparities in health and healthcare. The draft guidance proposes updates to clarify how the program may be applicable to certain medical devices that promote health equity. 

The FDA also issued final guidance on the refusal of inspection by a foreign food establishment or foreign government, as well as guidance on Good Manufacturing Practice for Animal Cells, Tissues, and Cell- and Tissue-Based Products. 

The FDA extended the public comment period for the reauthorization of the Animal Generic Drug User Fee Act (AGDUFA IV). 

The FDA authorized the Novavax COVID-19 Vaccine, Adjuvanted, for use as a first booster dose for individuals 18 years and older. 

The FDA announced the Advancing Real-World Evidence (RWE) Program, which provides sponsors the opportunity to meet with Agency staff to discuss the use of RWE in medical product development. 

The FDA authorized the marketing of the ScanNav Anatomy Peripheral Nerve Block, a software as a medical device that can identify anatomical structures within ultrasound images. 

As of October 21, 2022, there are 437 tests and sample collection devices authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 300 molecular tests and 79 molecular authorizations.

title: FDA, DOJ Seek Permanent Injunctions Against Six E-cigarette Manufacturers
body_summary: The US Department of Justice has filed complaints for permanent injunctions in federal district courts against six e-cigarette manufacturers, representing the first time the FDA has initiated such proceedings. The defendants, including Morin Enterprises Inc., Soul Vapor LLC, and others, failed to submit premarket applications for their e-cigarettes and continued to manufacture, sell, and distribute them despite previous warnings from the FDA. The injunctions would require the companies and individuals to stop manufacturing, selling, and distributing their e-cigarettes, as well as obtain marketing authorization from the FDA. The FDA had previously warned each company that they were in violation of the law, but continued to manufacture and sell unauthorized e-cigarettes. The injunctions would also require the defendants to obtain marketing authorization before marketing their products.

title: FDA Roundup: October 18, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued emergency use authorizations (EUAs) for various tests and devices, including a molecular test for COVID-19, a test for influenza, and a device to cool the inside of the mouth during chemotherapy. The FDA has also provided updates on postmarket surveillance studies, including one on transvaginal mesh for pelvic organ prolapse, which showed similar outcomes to native tissue repair but with potential additional risks. Additionally, the FDA has processed and reviewed non-tobacco nicotine product applications, issued Refuse to Accept letters for non-compliant products, and accepted over 1,600 applications.
