The FDA has also authorized over 60 warning letters to manufacturers, including brands popular among youth, and has issued a Breakthrough Device designation for a device intended to cool the inside of the mouth during chemotherapy.

title: FDA Awards 19 Grants and Two Contracts Related to Rare Diseases, including ALS
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has awarded 19 new grants and two new contracts totaling over $38 million to support clinical trials, natural history studies, and regulatory science tools for rare diseases. The grants and contracts, funded by the FDA's Orphan Products Grants Program, aim to advance the development of medical products for rare diseases, including Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS). The awards support the Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Act, established in December 2021, which requires the FDA to award grants and contracts for research on ALS and other rare neurodegenerative diseases. The FDA has funded clinical trials and natural history studies totaling over $36 million, including studies on rare cancers, ALS, Myotonic Dystrophy Type 1, and Ataxia-Telangiectasia. The grants also support the development of physical assessment tools for ALS patients and the review of patient preference information for brain-computer interface devices. The FDA's Office of Orphan Products Development will continue to invest in progressive studies to advance medical product development for rare diseases.

title: Executive Order 14087—Lowering Prescription Drug Costs for Americans
body_summary:
President Joe Biden, by the authority vested in him, orders the following:

Section 1. Policy. The administration aims to reduce the cost of prescription drugs for Americans. On average, Americans pay two to three times as much as people in other countries for prescription drugs, and one in four Americans who take prescription drugs struggle to afford their medications.

In July 2021, President Biden signed Executive Order 14036, which directed various actions to improve competition, increase wages, and reduce prices for prescription drugs. In August 2022, he signed Public Law 117-169, the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022, which will lower the cost of prescription drugs and save millions of Americans hundreds or thousands of dollars per year.

The IRA will protect Medicare beneficiaries from catastrophic drug costs by phasing in a cap for out-of-pocket costs at the pharmacy and establishing a $35 monthly cap per prescription for insulin. The Secretary of HHS will be able to negotiate prices for selected high-cost prescription drugs for Medicare beneficiaries for the first time ever.

Section 2. HHS Actions. The Secretary of HHS shall consider selecting new health care payment and delivery models to lower drug costs and promote access to innovative drug therapies. The Secretary must submit a report to the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy within 90 days, describing any selected models and their plan and timeline.

Section 3. General Provisions. This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.

title: FDA Roundup: October 14, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has published several news articles and announcements. The FDA is seeking feedback on distributed and point-of-care drug manufacturing technologies, which could enable rapid and localized responses to changing demand and improve access to quality drugs. The agency has also released new prevention strategies to enhance food safety, building on its extensive research into foodborne illnesses and outbreaks. Additionally, the FDA is holding a public meeting on October 26, 2022, to discuss the reauthorization of the Animal Generic Drug User Fee Act (AGDUFA), which provides funding for generic new animal drug reviews. As of today, the FDA has authorized over 436 emergency use authorizations (EUAs) for COVID-19 tests and sample collection devices, including 35 antigen tests and 8 molecular tests for serial screening programs.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index Report for September
body_summary: Americans are facing high costs of living. The President aims to give middle-class families breathing room in dealing with costs. A report shows some progress in fighting higher prices, with inflation averaging 2% over the last 3 months. Prices are still too high, and the President's top priority is addressing global inflation. The economic plan strengthens the US position to tackle the challenge. The Inflation Reduction Act has already helped, including locking in lower health care premiums for 13 million people, lowering seniors' prescription drug prices, and capping out-of-pocket expenses. Republicans' priority is repealing the Inflation Reduction Act, which would increase everyday costs, not reduce them.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech Bivalent COVID-19 Vaccines for Use as a Booster Dose in Younger Age Groups
body_summary: The US FDA has authorized a single booster dose of the Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccines for children aged 6 to 11 and 5 to 11 years, respectively. The Moderna vaccine is also authorized for administration to children as young as 6 years old at least two months after primary or booster vaccination. The Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine has been authorized for children aged 5 through 11 based on safety and effectiveness data from adults over 55 who received a bivalent booster dose and children 5-11 who received a monovalent booster dose.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary:
Here is the final summary:

The Federal Open Market Committee met on September 20-21, 2022, discussing financial market developments and open market operations. The meeting led to a decision to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 3-3.25% and anticipate ongoing increases to be appropriate, aiming to address elevated inflation and maintain price stability. Treasury yields climbed, while equity prices initially rose before retracting gains, and the U.S. dollar appreciated against major currencies. The Committee also decided to continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency MBS.

title: Statement on Family Health Coverage Under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: The US administration is finalizing a rule to fix the "family glitch" in employer-based health insurance, making it easier for family members to access Affordable Care Act subsidies. The change, starting next month, will affect about 1 million Americans, potentially gaining them coverage or reducing their insurance costs. This marks the most significant administrative action to implement the Affordable Care Act since its inception. The rule aims to address a regulatory flaw that previously made family members ineligible for subsidies even if their employers' coverage was affordable for them. The administration has made progress in lowering the uninsured rate, which is now at a record-low 8 percent, and encourages Americans to sign up for a plan starting November 1.

title: FDA Roundup: October 11, 2022
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is launching two new initiatives. The National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine is conducting an independent study on the role of seafood consumption in child growth and development, partnering with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, US Department of Agriculture, and US Environmental Protection Agency. The FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health is launching the Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program (TAP) Pilot to demonstrate earlier interactions with stakeholders and provide proactive advice on medical device development.

The FDA has authorized 436 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including molecular tests, antibody tests, antigen tests, and diagnostic breath tests. The FDA has also authorized 1127 revisions to EUA authorizations, and 35 antigen tests and 8 molecular tests for serial screening programs.

title: FDA Roundup: October 7, 2022
body_summary: The US FDA has issued several updates and authorizations for various medical products and tests. The agency has authorized the Alinity m MPXV test for detecting monkeypox DNA using lesion swab specimens. The test is the first commercial kit to be authorized for detection of monkeypox. The FDA has also partnered with the Critical Path Institute to develop clinical development tools for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, a rare disease. Additionally, the agency has published two proposed rules to harmonize clinical research regulations with the HHS Common Rule. The FDA has also issued final guidances to enhance patient safety in post-approval studies and postmarket surveillance. Furthermore, the agency has provided updates on its postmarket evaluation of the Essure device and released activities for the safety of imported produce. The FDA has also authorized 436 tests and sample collection devices for COVID-19 under emergency use authorizations, including 299 molecular tests, 85 antibody tests, and 51 antigen tests.

title: FDA Approves Vaccine for Use During Third Trimester of Pregnancy to Prevent Whooping Cough in Infants Younger Than Two Months of Age
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Boostrix, a vaccine for pertussis, for use during the third trimester of pregnancy to prevent the disease in infants under two months old. The vaccine, developed by GlaxoSmithKline Biologicals, boosts antibodies in the mother, which are transferred to the developing baby. According to the FDA, the vaccine is 78% effective in preventing pertussis in infants under two months old when administered during the third trimester of pregnancy. The approval is based on a re-analysis of observational data from 108 cases of pertussis and 183 control infants. The safety of Boostrix was assessed in a randomized, placebo-controlled study, which found no vaccine-related adverse effects on pregnancy or the fetus/newborn.

title: New Data Show More Than 2.5 Million U.S. Youth Currently Use E-Cigarettes
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has released federal data on e-cigarette use among US youth from the 2022 National Youth Tobacco Survey. The data shows that 2.5 million (9.4%) of middle and high school students reported current e-cigarette use, with nearly 85% using flavored e-cigarettes and 27.6% using e-cigarettes daily. The FDA has announced additional steps to address brands popular among youth, including a warning letter to Puff Bar and Hyde, LLC, and marketing denial orders for 32 Hyde e-cigarettes. The FDA has also clarified its authority to regulate tobacco products containing nicotine from any source, including non-tobacco nicotine products. The agency is committed to using its authorities to address youth e-cigarette use and protect public health.

title: FDA Roundup: October 4, 2022
body_summary: The US FDA has announced several updates and news items. The FDA and CDC signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) in September to strengthen food safety in retail environments. The FDA also issued a Safety Alert about raw Canadian oysters potentially contaminated with salmonella. Additionally, the FDA has introduced an electronic submission portal, called the CDRH Customer Collaboration Portal, which allows manufacturers to submit premarket submissions online. Starting October 1, 2023, all 510(k) submissions must be submitted as electronic submissions using eSTAR. The FDA has also released information about the risk of COVID-19 due to certain variants not neutralized by Evusheld. The FDA continues to recommend Evusheld as an option for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to prevent COVID-19.

title: FDA Roundup: September 30, 2022
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) published several updates on its website, including a report from the National Academies of Science, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM) on pain management and the opioid epidemic. The FDA is considering the report's recommendations and will continue to prioritize substance use and overdose prevention efforts. The agency also issued a warning letter to Bespoke Apothecary LLC for selling unapproved and misbranded COVID-19 products. 

The FDA approved two generic animal drug products: SpectoGard for bovine respiratory disease and Simplera Otic Solution for otitis externa in dogs. The agency announced updates to its COVID-19 test policy to encourage traditional premarket review pathways and prioritize review of tests with significant public health benefits. As of today, 437 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under emergency use authorizations (EUAs).

title: FDA Pathway Supports Long-Term Stability, Diversity of Safe and Nutritious Infant Formula Supply in the U.S.
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has published guidance to help infant formulas operating under enforcement discretion remain on the market. The FDA aims to ensure stable, longer-term access to safe and nutritious infant formula across the country. 

In July 2022, the agency committed to developing a new framework for continued and expanded access to infant formula products. 

The FDA has issued 16 enforcement discretion letters to eight companies across nine countries, which helped ease the temporary supply shortage and replenish store shelves. 

Manufacturers must send a letter to the FDA by December 5, 2022, outlining their intent to pursue completion of all regulatory requirements. 

The FDA intends to extend enforcement discretion for covered infant formulas until January 6, 2023, or longer, and will evaluate requests to determine whether to extend the period. 

The agency expects some manufacturers to meet all requirements quickly, while others may need the full timeframe. 

All companies, including those with enforcement discretion, must ultimately comply with all regulatory requirements.

title: FDA Approves New Treatment Option for Patients with ALS
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Relyvrio to treat patients with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), a life-threatening disease. The approval was granted after a 24-week, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study, where 137 adult patients with ALS showed improved clinical outcomes with Relyvrio. The recommended dosage is one packet (3 grams sodium phenylbutyrate and 1-gram taurursodiol) daily, with a potential increase to twice a day after three weeks. Relyvrio may cause adverse reactions such as diarrhea, abdominal pain, and nausea. The FDA granted Priority Review designation and orphan drug designation to Amylyx Pharmaceuticals Inc., which developed the medication.

title: FDA Proposes Updated Definition of ‘Healthy’ Claim on Food Packages to Help Improve Diet, Reduce Chronic Disease
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) proposed updated criteria for the "healthy" nutrient content claim on food packaging. The proposed rule aims to align the definition of the "healthy" claim with current nutrition science, the updated Nutrition Facts label, and the Dietary Guidelines for Americans. 

The proposed rule would update the "healthy" claim definition to better account for the nutrients in various food groups, making more foods eligible for the claim. The updated definition would require products to contain a meaningful amount of food from at least one of the food groups or subgroups recommended by the Dietary Guidelines and adhere to specific limits for certain nutrients, such as saturated fat, sodium, and added sugars.

The proposed rule is part of the FDA's commitment to helping consumers improve nutrition and dietary patterns, and is also related to the White House Conference on Hunger, Nutrition, and Health and the national strategy to end hunger, improve nutrition, and reduce diet-related diseases by 2030.

title: FDA, Veterans Health Administration Collaborate to Help Accelerate Medical Device Innovation and Advancement of Care
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration and the Veterans Health Administration are announcing a collaboration to accelerate American medical device innovation. The VA Ventures Innovation Institute in Seattle will host up to 12 FDA staff to foster collaborations between the two agencies. The FDA staff will focus on regulatory science, while VA staff will provide clinical context and hands-on training for innovators. The organizations will work together to develop and disseminate new tools for testing the safety and effectiveness of medical devices and emerging technologies. This effort aims to streamline the regulatory evaluation process, providing standardized tests that can help reduce risks for early innovators. The collaboration will initially focus on interoperable systems and autonomous medical devices, and future areas of work will include developing test methods for devices that can be used remotely through 5G networks.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Updates COVID-19 Test Policy, Encourages Developers to Seek Traditional Premarket Review for Most Test Types
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration updated its COVID-19 test policy to encourage the transition of tests to traditional premarket review pathways while ensuring continued access to tests. The FDA will review only a small subset of new emergency use authorization requests for diagnostic tests and encourages developers to pursue authorization through the de novo classification or 510(k) clearance pre-market review pathways. Director Jeff Shuren stated that shifting to traditional premarket review would best meet public health needs at the current stage of the COVID-19 public health emergency. The FDA has adapted its approach to address public's testing needs and has worked closely with test developers to increase testing capacity and public access to rapid tests.

title: FDA Roundup: September 27, 2022
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration is providing an overview of its activities to enhance the safety of imported produce. This follows the 2019 release of the Strategy for the Safety of Imported Food (Import Strategy), which describes the agency's approach to enhancing the safety of imported food.

The FDA has reopened the comment period for a request for information seeking available use and safety information on phthalates, with a new deadline of December 27, 2022. Comments should be submitted to Regulations.gov with the docket number FDA-2022-N-0571.

The FDA has completed the Software Precertification (Pre-Cert) Pilot Program, which explored innovative approaches to regulatory oversight of medical device software. The agency has found that rapidly evolving technologies require a new regulatory paradigm, which would require a legislative change.

The FDA is taking further action to prevent outbreaks of foodborne illnesses through the development of food safety prevention strategies. The agency will host a virtual town hall series on test development and validation during public health emergencies, including sessions on SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19) and monkeypox.

As of today, 437 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 300 molecular tests and 85 antibody tests.

title: New FDA Draft Guidance Aims to Protect Children who Participate in Clinical Trials
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a draft guidance on ethical considerations for including and protecting children in clinical trials. The guidance aims to assist industry, sponsors, and institutional review boards in considering the enrollment of children in clinical investigations of drugs, biological products, and medical devices. According to Dionna Green, M.D., director of the FDA's Office of Pediatric Therapeutics, children need access to safe and effective medical products and healthcare professionals need data to make evidence-based decisions when treating children. The draft guidance outlines the ethical framework for protecting children in clinical research, including risk and benefit considerations, and provides guidance on fundamental concepts for IRBs, sponsors, and industry to consider when reviewing or conducting clinical trials involving children.

title: FDA Roundup: September 23, 2022
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued several key guidance documents and made important announcements. The FDA has issued new guidance to help facilitate the availability of naloxone to prevent opioid overdoses and reduce death. This guidance supports the agency's effort to expand the availability and access to this life-saving medication, particularly for harm reduction programs and manufacturers.

Additionally, the FDA has granted accelerated approval to Retevmo (selpercatinib) for adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic solid tumors with a rearranged during transfection (RET) gene fusion. The recommended dose is 120 mg orally twice daily for patients under 50 kg and 160 mg orally twice daily for patients 50 kg or greater.

The FDA has also granted regular approval for adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with a RET gene fusion. The agency approved the Oncomine Dx Target (ODxT) Test as a companion diagnostic for selpercatinib.

Furthermore, the FDA has updated its Public Health Alert on Mother's Touch Formula, advising consumers to discontinue use and throw away the product due to non-conformity to the FDA's infant formula standards.

The FDA has also published an interview with John Skerritt, the head of Australia's Therapeutic Goods Administration, discussing Australia's robust strategy for regional and global medical product engagement.

Currently, the FDA has authorized 438 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including molecular tests, antibody and immune response tests, antigen tests, and diagnostic breath tests.

title: Implementation Note issued September 21, 2022
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on September 21, 2022: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 3.15 percent, effective September 22, 2022. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective September 22, 2022, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 3 to 3-1/4 percent. Conduct overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 3.25 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion; the aggregate operation limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 3.05 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $60 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest into agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve a 3/4 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate to 3.25 percent, effective September 22, 2022. In taking this action, the Board approved requests to establish that rate submitted by the Boards of Directors of the Federal Reserve Banks of Boston, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Chicago, St. Louis, Kansas City, and Dallas. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators point to modest growth in spending and production. Job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation remains elevated, reflecting supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic, higher food and energy prices, and broader price pressures. Russia's war against Ukraine is causing tremendous human and economic hardship. The war and related events are creating additional upward pressure on inflation and are weighing on global economic activity. The Committee is highly attentive to inflation risks. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 3 to 3-1/4 percent and anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in the Plans for Reducing the Size of the Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet that were issued in May. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; James Bullard; Susan M. Collins; Lisa D. Cook; Esther L. George; Philip N. Jefferson; Loretta J. Mester; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: FDA Roundup: September 20, 2022
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has alerted medical device users about a potential cybersecurity risk for the Medtronic MiniMed 600 Series Insulin Pump System. The risk allows unauthorized access to the pump system, which could lead to the pump delivering too much or too little insulin. 

The FDA has granted accelerated approval to Skysona (elivaldogene autotemcel), the first cell-based gene therapy to slow the progression of neurologic dysfunction in boys 4-17 years old with early, active cerebral adrenoleukodystrophy. 

The FDA has authorized the marketing of the Phagenyx System, which delivers electrical stimulation to the oropharynx, part of the throat at the back of the mouth behind the oral cavity, used in treating stroke patients with dysphagia. 

The FDA issued a voluntary recall for the NIM CONTACT Reinforced EMG Endotracheal Tube and NIM Standard Reinforced EMG Endotracheal Tube due to the risk of airway obstruction. 

As of today, 438 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 301 molecular tests, 85 antibody tests, and 51 antigen tests.

title: FDA Committed to Strengthening U.S. Infant Formula Supply; Review Provides Roadmap to Support Ongoing Efforts
body_summary: The US FDA has been working with government partners to expand consumer access to infant formula while ensuring safety, nutrition, and quality standards. In response to the 2022 Abbott Sturgis facility closure, Dr. Steven Solomon conducted a top-down review of FDA activities, which was released in a 10-page report. The report highlights findings and recommendations to support the agency's efforts to ensure access to infant formula, including the need for additional resources and authorities. The report also identifies the need for greater diversification of manufacturers, investment in new facilities, and commitment to quality and safety standards. The FDA has already implemented some changes, including updating processes and procedures, and a data system to track production and distribution. The agency is committed to implementing necessary changes to avoid future supply shortages and ensure access to safe and nutritious infant formula.

title: FDA Concludes Internal Review of Agency Actions Related to the U.S. Infant Formula Supply
body_summary: FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf, M.D., asked for an internal review of the agency's actions related to Cronobacter illness, infant formula manufacturing, and the shortage of infant formulas in 2022. The report, based on over 40 interviews with FDA staff and leadership, focuses on the agency's response and identifies five major areas of need. These areas include modern information technology, sufficient staffing and resources, updated emergency response systems, increased scientific understanding of Cronobacter, and assessment of the infant formula industry. The report highlights systemic vulnerabilities that require continued modernization and investment in expertise and tools to address future public health challenges. The FDA lacks specific authorities and resources to address these issues, and the agency recommends utilizing the appropriations process to secure necessary authorities and resources.

title: FDA Roundup: September 16, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is taking steps to increase the availability of novel treatments for rare diseases and conditions in dogs and cats. The FDA has launched the ORA News and Stories platform on FDA.gov, featuring news, conversations, media coverage, and stories of ORA's work. ORA News and Stories will showcase the latest ORA innovations and enterprising ideas. The FDA has also warned consumers about social media trends encouraging misuse of nonprescription medications, which can harm people and cause death. The FDA has authorized 438 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 301 molecular tests and 85 antibody tests. A virtual meeting of the CDRH Anesthesiology and Respiratory Therapy Devices Panel will be held on November 1, 2022, to discuss concerns about pulse oximeter accuracy.

title: FDA and NIH Launch Public-Private Partnership for Rare Neurodegenerative Diseases
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the National Institutes of Health have launched the Critical Path for Rare Neurodegenerative Diseases (CP-RND), a public-private partnership aimed at advancing the understanding of neurodegenerative diseases and developing treatments for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and other rare neurodegenerative diseases. The FDA and NIH have selected the Critical Path Institute (C-Path) as the convener of this partnership. 

The partnership will leverage the expertise of public and private sectors to create new breakthroughs in treating these diseases. Hilary Marston, FDA Chief Medical Officer, and Walter Koroshetz, director of the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, have expressed the need for new treatments for rare neurodegenerative diseases.

The CP-RND will focus on patient-focused drug development, utilizing the FDA-funded Rare Disease Cures Accelerator-Data and Analytics Platform (RDCA-DAP) to facilitate the characterization of neurodegenerative diseases and identify molecular targets for these diseases.

This partnership is a key component of the FDA’s Action Plan for Rare Neurodegenerative Diseases, including ALS, which was announced in June.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Report on the Consumer Price Index for August
body_summary: The U.S. economy has seen more progress in bringing global inflation down, with prices remaining flat for two consecutive months. Gas prices have decreased by an average of $1.30 per gallon since the summer began. Real wages have also increased for the second month in a row, providing hard-working families with a bit of relief. The Inflation Reduction Act was passed to lower healthcare, prescription drug, and energy costs. The economic plan aims to bring prices down while creating good-paying jobs and bringing manufacturing back to America.

title: FDA Roundup: September 13, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has reissued the Aug. 19, 2022, letter of authorization for the Novavax COVID-19 Vaccine, Adjuvanted, to revise the conditions of authorization related to the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System (VAERS) reporting requirements. The FDA has also issued a draft guidance on Computer Software Assurance for Production and Quality System Software. As of today, 438 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 301 molecular tests and sample collection devices, 85 antibody and other immune response tests, 51 antigen tests, and 1 diagnostic breath test.

title: Executive Order 14082—Implementation of the Energy and Infrastructure Provisions of the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022
body_summary: President Joseph R. Biden Jr. ordered the effective implementation of the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 on September 12, 2022. The order, part of Executive Order 14052, aimed to accelerate clean energy innovation, reduce consumer energy costs, and address the climate crisis. As part of this, an Interagency Working Group on Coal and Power Plant Communities and Economic Revitalization was established, with the National Climate Advisor, Assistant to the President for Economic Policy, and Senior Advisor for Clean Energy Innovation and Implementation serving as Co-Chairs. The revised Executive Order 12898 was also implemented to enhance climate action and energy implementation.

title: FDA Issues Safety Alert for Squamous Cell Carcinoma and Various Lymphomas in Scar Tissue around Breast Implants
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued a safety communication informing patients and providers about reports of squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) and various lymphomas in the capsule or scar tissue around breast implants. The FDA currently believes that the risk of SCC and other lymphomas occurring in the tissue around breast implants is rare. The agency is providing clear and understandable information to the public as quickly as possible after an initial extensive review. The FDA is convening stakeholders, consulting with cancer experts, and closely monitoring data sources to ensure a coordinated approach. The agency encourages patients to report any cases of SCC, lymphoma, or other cancer in the scar tissue around breast implants to the FDA. If a patient with breast implants experiences a problem, the FDA strongly encourages reporting through MedWatch. The safety communication underscores the FDA's commitment to sharing information to help patients consider and discuss implant risks with their doctors.

title: Monkeypox Update: FDA Takes Significant Action to Help Expand Access to Testing
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is announcing steps to further increase monkeypox testing capacity and accessibility nationwide. The agency will continue to engage federal public health partners to facilitate the availability of monkeypox tests. Since the first case of monkeypox was detected in the US, the FDA has been working to increase production and distribution of the FDA-cleared test, clearing the use of additional reagents and automation to increase testing capacity. The FDA also issued guidance to facilitate the development of additional tests, outlining enforcement policies, recommendations for emergency use authorization, and plans to prioritize review of EUA requests. This guidance follows a declaration by the Secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services justifying the emergency use of in vitro diagnostics. The FDA also authorized the Quest Diagnostics Monkeypox Virus Real-Time PCR test, which is intended to detect monkeypox and other non-variola orthopoxvirus DNA using lesion swab specimens.

title: Certain Philips Respironics Masks for BiPAP, CPAP Machines Recalled Due to Safety Issue with Magnets That May Affect Certain Medical Devices
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has recalled over 17 million Philips Respironics masks due to a serious safety concern. The recalled masks have magnets that can potentially affect or cause movement of certain implanted metallic medical devices, such as brain stents, pacemakers, and implantable cardioverter defibrillators. This could result in injury or death to the mask user or people near the patient. Five mask types are affected: DreamWisp, DreamWear, Amara View, Wisp, and Wisp Youth. To date, Philips has reported 14 serious injuries. The FDA is providing recommendations for patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers to reduce the potential for harm from these products.

title: FDA Roundup: September 6, 2022
body_summary: The US FDA published the 2022 "Advancing Regulatory Science at FDA: Focus Areas of Regulatory Science" report, outlining topics requiring targeted investment in regulatory science research. The report aims to facilitate product development, inform regulatory decision-making, and improve guidance. The agency also provided updates on COVID-19 testing, with 438 tests and sample collection devices authorized under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 301 molecular tests, 85 antibody tests, 51 antigen tests, and 1 diagnostic breath test.

title: FDA Roundup: September 2, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is publishing a summary of news from around the agency. The FDA has warned consumers to beware of Ultraviolet (UV) wands that give off unsafe levels of radiation, citing potential risk of injury. The agency is also encouraging a whole-of-governments approach to combating illicit health products, collaborating with nearly 20 countries and hosting a workshop in Paris on September 15-16. The FDA has announced a virtual meeting on October 20 to discuss a De Novo request for a prescription diagnostic genetic test. A virtual meeting is also scheduled for September 7 to discuss a new drug application for a treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). As of today, 438 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Acid Sphingomyelinase Deficiency, a Rare Genetic Disease
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Xenpozyme (Olipudase alfa) for treatment in pediatric and adult patients with Acid Sphingomyelinase Deficiency (ASMD), a rare genetic disease. ASMD causes premature death and has a debilitating effect on patients' lives. Xenpozyme, an enzyme replacement therapy, was shown to improve lung function and reduce liver and spleen size in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of 31 patients. The most common side effects include headache, cough, and fever. Xenpozyme carries a boxed warning for severe hypersensitivity reactions. The FDA awarded the sponsor, Genzyme, a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher. Over 7,000 rare diseases affect more than 30 million people in the United States, with many being life-threatening and without treatments.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Moderna, Pfizer-BioNTech Bivalent COVID-19 Vaccines for Use as a Booster Dose
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) amended emergency use authorizations for the Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccines to authorize bivalent formulations as a single booster dose. The bivalent vaccines contain two mRNA components, one from the original SARS-CoV-2 strain and one from the BA.4 and BA.5 lineages of the omicron variant. Individuals 18 years and older can receive a single booster dose of the Moderna bivalent vaccine, while those 12 years and older can receive the Pfizer-BioNTech bivalent vaccine. Clinical studies found improved immune responses to the omicron BA.1 variant in individuals who received the bivalent vaccines, with better results seen in individuals 18 years and older for the Moderna vaccine and those 12 years and older for the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine.

title: FDA Roundup: August 30, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced several developments. The FDA's Overdose Prevention Framework aims to prevent drug overdoses and reduce deaths, with priorities including primary prevention, harm reduction, evidence-based treatments, and protecting the public from unapproved or counterfeit drugs. The Center for Veterinary Medicine is holding a virtual public listening session on October 18, 2022, to gather public comments on updating its policy on regulating animal foods with certain types of claims. The FDA has also issued safety communications, including a recall of Philips Respironics bi-level positive airway pressure machines due to potential contamination and a marketing authorization for the Vibrant System, a device for treating chronic idiopathic constipation.

title: FDA Removes N95 Respirators from Medical Device Shortage List, Signaling Sufficient Supply
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has removed N95 respirators from its medical device shortage list due to increased domestic manufacturing and updates to the agency's supply chain assessment. This action is the result of collaboration with industry and federal stakeholders, as well as the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health's approval of new disposable N95s and reusable respirators. The removal is a result of demand no longer exceeding supply. The FDA has worked closely with partners to stabilize and rebuild healthcare access to high-quality respirators, including those made in the US. The agency has taken actions to provide flexible policies and ensure timely access to medical devices during the COVID-19 public health emergency.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Economic Analysis Report on Personal Consumption Expenditures for July
body_summary: The American people are starting to get relief from high prices. The Inflation Reduction Act signed last month will also help bring prices down. Gas prices decreased every day this summer, the fastest decline in over a decade. Personal income was up last month, according to a recent measure of inflation. The economic plan is building the economy from the bottom up and the middle out, and progress is being made.

title: FDA Roundup: August 26, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has provided additional guidance for prescribers to evaluate potential drug interactions when using Paxlovid therapy for COVID-19. The agency has also approved a single-dose vial presentation of COMIRNATY (COVID-19 Vaccine, mRNA) and posted additional FAQs for stakeholders on the FDA Food Safety Modernization Act final rule on Laboratory Accreditation for Analyses of Foods. The FDA has also issued the 2022 edition of the Voluntary National Retail Food Regulatory Program Standards and a final guidance on designing and conducting tobacco product perception and intention studies. As of today, there are 439 authorized tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 302 molecular tests and 78 molecular authorizations.

title: FDA and Mexican Counterparts Report Progress in Food Safety at Second Annual Partnership Meeting
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and its Mexican counterparts, COFEPRIS and SENASICA, held their second annual Food Safety Partnership Meeting to strengthen their collaboration on food safety and consumer protection. Frank Yiannas, FDA's deputy commissioner for food policy and response, emphasized the importance of this partnership as the US and Mexico approach the 200th anniversary of their relations. The meeting aimed to enhance food safety in both countries through the exchange of best practices, training, and data sharing. Key outcomes included the collaboration on Salmonella outbreak response, Cyclospora detection, and Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) data sharing. The three agencies also reviewed Produce Safety Rule trainings and worked on a new model for conducting inspections involving all three agencies.

title: FDA Roundup: August 23, 2022
body_summary: The US FDA is providing an update on its news and initiatives. The FDA's Office of Global Policy and Strategy is partnering with the Inter-American Institute for Cooperation in Agriculture (IICA) to facilitate the implementation of the Food Safety Modernization Act in Latin America. The FDA and the Duke-Margolis Center for Health Policy are hosting a virtual public workshop on October 11 to gather feedback on a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS) integration prototype. The workshop will involve key stakeholders, including patients, prescribers, pharmacists, and health system representatives. The FDA has also authorized 439 emergency use authorizations (EUAs) for COVID-19 tests and sample collection devices, including 302 molecular tests, 85 antibody tests, and 51 antigen tests.

title: FDA Roundup: August 19, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the emergency use of Novavax COVID-19 Vaccine for individuals 12 through 17 years of age, following a rigorous analysis of safety and effectiveness data. The agency has also announced the publication of a new test method standard for detection of nitric oxide production in vitro. The FDA has warned patients, caregivers, and healthcare professionals about autoinjector devices that may not be compatible with glatiramer acetate injection drug products, and issued a report outlining its work to combat the COVID-19 pandemic. The agency has also signed a confidentiality commitment with Ecuador's Vice Ministry of Aquaculture and Fisheries to establish a shrimp safety pilot program, and issued a warning letter to VPR Brands LP for marketing illegal flavored nicotine gummies. The FDA has updated its safety communication regarding medical device reports related to Philips Respironics ventilators, and authorized over 400 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody tests, and antigen tests.

title: FDA Warns Manufacturer for Marketing Illegal Flavored Nicotine Gummies
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued a warning letter to VPR Brands LP (doing business as "Krave Nic") for marketing illegal flavored nicotine gummies. The gummies have 1 milligram of nicotine each and are available in three flavors. The FDA has not received a premarket tobacco product application from the manufacturer, and the products are not authorized to be sold or distributed in the US. The warning letter requests a response from the manufacturer on how they intend to address any violations and bring their products into compliance with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. The FDA is taking action to curb the unlawful marketing of tobacco products, particularly those that youth could easily confuse with regular products.

title: FDA Approves First Cell-Based Gene Therapy to Treat Adult and Pediatric Patients with Beta-thalassemia Who Require Regular Blood Transfusions
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Zynteglo, a cell-based gene therapy, for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients with beta-thalassemia who require regular red blood cell transfusions. The approval was granted after two multicenter clinical studies established the safety and effectiveness of the treatment, which is administered as a single dose and aims to achieve transfusion independence. 89% of 41 patients receiving Zynteglo achieved transfusion independence. Common adverse reactions included reduced platelet and blood cell levels, mucositis, and fever. The FDA granted approval to bluebird bio, Inc., in addition to Priority Review, Fast Track, Breakthrough Therapy, and Orphan Designations.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A Federal Open Market Committee meeting was held on July 26-27, 2022, with Jerome H. Powell as Chair. The meeting discussed financial market developments, including elevated uncertainty about the outlook and potential for shocks from abroad. Financial conditions eased modestly, but remained tighter than at the start of the year. Treasury yields fell, and respondents marked down their growth forecasts for 2022-2023. The Committee projected a weaker US economic outlook, with GDP above potential this year but closing the gap by 2023. Unemployment rate was expected to rise and reach its natural rate by end of 2024. Total PCE price inflation was 4.8% in 2022, declining to 2.2% in 2023 and 1.9% in 2024. The Committee agreed to raise the federal funds rate 75 basis points at this meeting to bring inflation back down to 2 percent. The Committee also directed the Desk to undertake open market operations to maintain the federal funds rate, approved raising interest rates on reserve balances and primary credit rate, both effective July 28, 2022.

title: Statement on the Food and Drug Administration Rule Regarding Over-the-Counter Purchase of Hearing Aids
body_summary: The FDA is making hearing aids available over the counter starting mid-October, as part of an executive order to increase competition and lower costs. This move aims to deliver nearly $3,000 in savings to American families for a pair of hearing aids, and is the latest action to make the economy more competitive.

title: FDA Roundup: August 16, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a final rule to improve access to hearing aids, establishing a new category of over-the-counter hearing aids that can be purchased directly from stores or online retailers without a medical exam or prescription. The FDA has also warned the public about certain spray sunscreens that have been recalled due to benzene contamination. Additionally, the FDA has launched a new external webpage to highlight the Operation Lascar Initiative, a bilateral effort with the UK to combat the movement of illicit FDA-regulated products. The FDA has also cleared a web-based software application to aid in the evaluation of visual acuity, and has authorized over 400 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations for COVID-19 testing.

title: FDA Finalizes Historic Rule Enabling Access to Over-the-Counter Hearing Aids for Millions of Americans
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a final rule to improve access to hearing aids, which may lower costs for millions of Americans. The rule establishes a new category of over-the-counter (OTC) hearing aids, enabling consumers with mild to moderate hearing impairment to purchase hearing aids directly without a medical exam, prescription, or fitting adjustment. The rule aims to lower healthcare costs and make hearing aids more accessible. The FDA finalized the rule after receiving over 1,000 public comments and incorporated changes to ensure safety and effectiveness. The rule will take effect on mid-October, and consumers can expect to see OTC hearing aids available in stores and online.

title: FDA Roundup: August 12, 2022
body_summary:
The US FDA posted safety communications about monkeypox virus and blood donations, stating that worldwide, there have been no reports of transmission of monkeypox virus through blood transfusion and the risk remains theoretical. The FDA will continue to monitor cases and provide additional information. Additionally, the FDA issued a safety communication advising people to perform repeat testing following a negative result on any at-home COVID-19 antigen test to increase the chances of detecting an infection. 

The FDA granted accelerated approval to fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki (Enhertu) for adult patients with unresectable or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have activating human epidermal growth factor receptor2 (ERBB2) mutations. The FDA also approved Oncomine Dx Target Test and Guardant360 CDx as companion diagnostics for Enhertu.

The FDA issued final guidance for shell egg producers on complying with provisions in the egg rule to prevent Salmonella Enteritidis in shell eggs during production, storage, and transportation. 

The FDA made its annual Pesticide Residue Monitoring Program Report for Fiscal Year 2020 (FY 2020) available, summarizing findings from monitoring human and animal foods in FY 2020. As of today, 439 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs) for COVID-19 testing.

title: FDA Infant Formula Update: August 10, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has taken additional steps to increase the availability of infant formula in the U.S. Reckitt Nutrition/Mead Johnson Nutrition (Mexico) will ship an initial 331,000 pounds of base powder for PurAmino Hypoallergenic Infant Formula in August, which will be used to produce about 469,000 cans or 6 million full-size bottles. The FDA is exercising enforcement discretion for the importation of this product, and it will be distributed primarily through hospitals and healthcare settings, with select retail stores also available. This shipment is part of the FDA's efforts to bolster the supply of infant formula, which serves as the sole source of nutrition for many infants. The agency has posted a webpage with information about additional products headed to the U.S. and is working to increase the quantity of domestically-produced infant formula. The FDA also advises against making infant formulas at home or diluting formula and encourages parents and caregivers to work with their child's health care provider for recommendations on changing feeding practices.

title: FDA Issues Warning Letters to Three Companies for Selling Unapproved New Drugs for Mole and Skin Tag Removal
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued three warning letters to companies for introducing unapproved mole and skin tag removal products into interstate commerce, violating the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. The products, sold by Amazon.com, Ariella Naturals, and Justified Laboratories, have not been evaluated by the FDA for safety, effectiveness, or quality. The FDA's director of the Office of Compliance stated that it is the agency's duty to protect public health from harmful products. The FDA has noted that self-diagnosis and treatment of moles could lead to delayed cancer diagnosis and treatment, and has issued a consumer warning about the risks of these products. The companies have 15 days to respond to the warning letters, and failure to address the violations may result in legal action.

title: FDA Roundup: August 9, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a warning letter to FluxxLab LLC for selling unapproved and misbranded tincture products as drugs for use in treating or preventing COVID-19. The agency's bioresearch monitoring program has been impacted by the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation. The FDA has authorized 439 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 302 molecular tests, 85 antibody tests, 51 antigen tests, and 1 diagnostic breath test. Dr. Janet Woodcock will deliver a keynote address on regulatory best practices for global access to medicines, including anti-TB medicines.

title: Monkeypox Update: FDA Authorizes Emergency Use of JYNNEOS Vaccine to Increase Vaccine Supply
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the JYNNEOS vaccine, allowing healthcare providers to use the vaccine by intradermal injection for individuals 18 years of age and older who are at high risk for monkeypox infection. This will increase the total number of doses available by up to five-fold. The EUA also allows for use in individuals younger than 18 years of age who are at high risk of monkeypox infection, administered subcutaneously. The vaccine, modified from the Modified Vaccinia Ankara (MVA) vaccine, was approved in 2019 for prevention of smallpox and monkeypox disease in adults 18 years of age and older. The EUA was granted based on the determination of a public health emergency by the Secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services on August 9, 2022.

title: Statement on Senate Passage of Legislation To Combat Inflation, Promote Clean Energy Production, and Reduce Prescription Drug Costs
body_summary: Senate Democrats voted to lower prescription drug costs, health insurance, and energy costs, while reducing the deficit and making corporations pay their fair share. The bill caps seniors' out-of-pocket spending for prescription drugs at $2000 per year and reduces health insurance premiums for 13 million Americans by $800. The bill also invests in combating climate change, strengthens energy security, and creates jobs in the renewable energy sector. It pays for these investments through a minimum corporate tax, which does not raise taxes on individuals making under $400,000 per year. The bill has been supported by Leader Schumer and the Senate Democratic caucus.

title: Statement on the 25th Anniversary of the Children's Health Insurance Program
body_summary: President Clinton signed the Children's Health Insurance Program into law twenty-five years ago, making it possible for parents to worry less about their children's health. In 1997, 15% of the nation's children lacked health insurance, but thanks to CHIP, Medicaid, and the Affordable Care Act (ACA), only 4% are uninsured today. My administration has expanded access to affordable health care, with 1 million children gaining coverage since I became President. The Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) will build on this progress, locking in average $800 a year savings in health insurance premiums for 13 million Americans and preventing 3 million from becoming uninsured.

title: FDA Infant Formula Update: August 5, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is providing an update on additional steps taken to increase the availability of infant formula in the US. Nestlé Health Science's Nestlé SMA Nutrition Althéra is expected to be available in August 2022. The product is a specialty, hypoallergenic formula for infants with cow's milk protein allergy and/or multiple food allergies. The FDA is exercising enforcement discretion for the importation of this product and others, leveraging flexibilities to bolster supply. The agency is also working with manufacturers and suppliers to increase domestic production to ensure adequate infant formula availability. The FDA has issued guidance to facilitate the importation of infant formula products intended for foreign markets and is monitoring online marketplaces for fraudulent products.

title: FDA Approves First Targeted Therapy for HER2-Low Breast Cancer
body_summary: The US FDA approved Enhertu, an IV infusion for treating patients with unresectable or metastatic HER2-low breast cancer. This is the first approved therapy for this subtype, which is estimated to affect 287,850 new female breast cancer diagnoses in the US in 2022. The approval is based on the DESTINY-Breast04 clinical trial, which showed improvement in progression-free and overall survival for patients with unresectable or metastatic HER2-low breast cancer. Enhertu's approval aligns with the Cancer Moonshot program's goals of targeting right treatments to the right patients and speeding progress against rare cancers. The trial included 557 adult patients, mostly females (99.6%) with a median age of 57, and showed common adverse reactions such as nausea, fatigue, and diarrhea. Enhertu received priority review and breakthrough therapy designations, and was granted approval four months ahead of the PDUFA deadline.

title: FDA Roundup: August 5, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has cautioned pet owners not to feed their pets certain lots of Darwin’s Natural Pet Products raw cat food due to Salmonella contamination. Whole genome sequencing revealed Salmonella Typhimurium in the turkey product and Salmonella Typhimurium and Kentucky in the chicken product. The FDA has released new educational materials on genetically modified organisms (GMOs) to help consumers understand GMOs. The FDA has also recognized National Immunization Awareness Month and updated its list of Breakthrough Devices, now including over 50 authorized devices. The FDA has authorized 439 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including molecular tests, antibody tests, antigen tests, and diagnostic breath tests.

title: Executive Order 14079—Securing Access to Reproductive and Other Healthcare Services
body_summary:
President Biden has issued an executive order to protect access to reproductive healthcare services. On July 8, 2022, following the Supreme Court's decision to overrule Roe v. Wade, President Biden signed Executive Order 14076. The order aims to address the devastating implications of eliminating the right recognized in Roe v. Wade on women's health and public health. 

The order directs the Department of Health and Human Services to clarify hospitals and providers' obligations under the Emergency Medical Treatment and Labor Act to provide stabilizing care, including abortion, if necessary to stabilize a patient's emergency medical condition. It also issues guidance to retail pharmacies on their obligations under Federal civil rights laws to ensure equal access to comprehensive reproductive and other healthcare services.

The order is intended to address the crisis facing women's health and public health, including reports of women being denied health- and life-saving emergency care due to fears of legal reprisal. The order also aims to promote compliance with non-discrimination laws in obtaining medical care and to advance research on the effect of access to reproductive healthcare on maternal health outcomes.

The order is part of President Biden's policy to support women's access to reproductive healthcare services, including their ability to travel to seek abortion care in States where it is legal.

title: FDA Continues Efforts to Support Innovation in Medical Device Sterilization
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) oversees sterilization methods for medical devices to ensure effectiveness and safety. Ethylene oxide is the most commonly used method, widely used by manufacturers and contract sterilizers, sterilizing over 20 billion devices annually. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) plans to propose an air pollution rule to address ethylene oxide emissions from commercial sterilizers. The FDA is working with sterilizers to reduce ethylene oxide use and has launched initiatives to develop novel sterilization methods. The FDA's EtO Sterilization Master File Pilot Program and 510(k) master file pilot program aim to reduce ethylene oxide emissions, while the Innovation Challenges encourage new strategies to reduce emissions and explore alternative sterilization methods. The FDA is also focused on preventing shortages of sterilized medical devices due to reduced supply.

title: Statement on Efforts To Reduce Health Care Costs and Expand Insurance Coverage
body_summary: The US has made significant progress in reducing the number of uninsured Americans, with 8% of the population currently uninsured, the lowest in history. Over 35 million Americans are enrolled in Affordable Care Act (ACA) related coverage, including 21 million in Medicaid expansion coverage denied to nearly 4 million in states that refused to expand it. Since the administration's start, 5 million more people have gained health insurance coverage. The Inflation Reduction Act aims to lock in an average $800 annual savings in health insurance premiums for 13 million Americans and prevent 3 million from becoming uninsured. The administration urges Congress to pass the legislation swiftly to lower healthcare costs and make coverage more accessible.

title: FDA Roundup: August 2, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced the approval of generic firocoxib tablets for osteoarthritis in horses. The FDA has also issued a final guidance on dietary supplements containing N-acetyl-L-cysteine (NAC), exercising enforcement discretion for compliant products. As of today, 438 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 301 molecular tests, 85 antibody tests, and 51 antigen tests, with 78 molecular and 1 antibody authorization for home-collected samples.

title: Statement on the 57th Anniversary of Medicare and Medicaid
body_summary: The 57th anniversary of Medicare and Medicaid is today, marking nearly 140 million Americans' access to affordable health care coverage. Republicans propose to put these programs on the chopping block every 5 years, threatening 140 million Americans' access. Congressional Democrats, including the author, fight to strengthen these programs, ensuring no American faces a choice between health care and food. The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 will keep Affordable Care Act improvements, protect 3 million from becoming uninsured, allow Medicare to negotiate prescription drug costs, and cap out-of-pocket drug costs at $2,000 per year. This legislation aims to strengthen health and financial security for millions of Americans.

title: FDA Provides Update on Agency Response to Monkeypox Outbreak
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration is providing an update on its response to monkeypox in the US. The agency has made diagnostics, vaccines, and therapeutics more available to consumers. 

The FDA has established a dedicated website to provide information on its regulatory activities related to monkeypox. Commissioner Robert M. Califf has stated that the agency is using its full authorities to make additional diagnostics and treatments available. 

A vaccine, JYNNEOS, is FDA-approved for prevention of monkeypox disease in adults 18 years and older. The FDA has expedited the submission of a manufacturing change to allow for the distribution of approximately 800,000 doses. 

A test, cleared by the FDA, can detect monkeypox virus by swab from a lesion. The test is available through commercial laboratories and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. 

There is currently no FDA-approved medicine for the treatment of monkeypox disease; however, TPOXX (tecovirimat) is being made available through the CDC's Expanded Access Program.

title: FDA Roundup: July 29, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration updated its FAQs on Testing for SARS-CoV-2 to note that no tests remain on the commercial manufacturer serology test notification list. All tests previously on the list have either been issued an Emergency Use Authorization or should no longer be distributed, marketed, or offered. The FDA also announced fiscal year 2023 fee rates and payment procedures under the Animal Drug User Fee Amendments of 2018 and Animal Generic Drug User Fee Amendments of 2018. User fee rates for importers and accreditation bodies participating in the Voluntary Qualified Importer Program and Accredited Third-Party Certification Program were also announced. The FDA posted a Consumer Update on gene therapy, noting that it has approved multiple gene therapy products for cancer and rare diseases. As of today, 439 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 302 molecular tests, 85 antibody tests, and 51 antigen tests.

title: Statement on Legislation To Combat Inflation, Promote Clean Energy Production, and Reduce Prescription Drug Costs
body_summary: The President spoke with Senators Schumer and Manchin, offering support for their agreement on a bill to fight inflation and lower costs for American families. The agreement aims to make prescription drugs cheaper by allowing Medicare to negotiate lower prices, reducing health insurance costs for 13 million Americans by an average of $800 a year. The bill also aims to improve energy security and tackle the climate crisis by providing tax credits and investments for energy projects. This will create thousands of new jobs and lower energy costs. The bill will reduce the deficit beyond $1.7 trillion, paid for by requiring big corporations to pay their fair share of taxes, with no tax increases for families making under $400,000 a year.

title: FDA Seeks to Improve Patient Communication on LASIK Benefits and Risks Through Issuance of Draft Guidance
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued a draft guidance to improve labeling for LASIK devices. The goal is to provide clear information about the benefits and risks of LASIK surgery, including potential adverse effects such as dry eye, pain, and visual symptoms. The FDA collaborated with external experts and conducted research, including the LASIK Quality of Life Collaboration Project, to inform the recommendations. The draft guidance proposes patient labeling information, including a patient decision checklist, that includes details on who is a good candidate for LASIK, what to expect after surgery, and long-term risks. The FDA encourages public feedback on the proposed labeling recommendations.

title: Implementation Note issued July 27, 2022
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on July 27, 2022: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 2.4 percent, effective July 28, 2022. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective July 28, 2022, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent. Conduct overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 2.5 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion; the aggregate operation limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 2.3 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in the calendar months of July and August that exceeds a cap of $30 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Starting in the calendar month of September, roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $60 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest into agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in the calendar months of July and August that exceeds a cap of $17.5 billion per month. Starting in the calendar month of September, reinvest into agency MBS the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in each calendar month that exceeds a cap of $35 billion per month. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve a 3/4 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate to 2.5 percent, effective July 28, 2022. In taking this action, the Board approved requests to establish that rate submitted by the Boards of Directors of the Federal Reserve Banks of Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Chicago, Dallas, and San Francisco. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Recent indicators of spending and production have softened. Nonetheless, job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation remains elevated, reflecting supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic, higher food and energy prices, and broader price pressures. Russia's war against Ukraine is causing tremendous human and economic hardship. The war and related events are creating additional upward pressure on inflation and are weighing on global economic activity. The Committee is highly attentive to inflation risks. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent and anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in the Plans for Reducing the Size of the Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet that were issued in May. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michael S. Barr; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; James Bullard; Susan M. Collins; Lisa D. Cook; Esther L. George; Philip N. Jefferson; Loretta J. Mester; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: FDA Roundup: July 26, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced several updates and actions. On August 11, 2022, the FDA will present a webinar for stakeholders to discuss Food Facility Registration, Biennial Renewal, and obtaining an acceptable Unique Facility Identifier. U.S. and foreign human and animal food facilities must register with the FDA and renew their registration between October 1 and December 31, 2022. The FDA is developing a food safety prevention strategy for fresh and frozen berries in response to hepatitis A and norovirus outbreaks. The FDA has authorized extended expiration dates for Paxlovid lots manufactured prior to the EUA issuance. There are 439 authorized tests and sample collection devices for COVID-19 testing, including 302 molecular tests and 85 antibody tests. The FDA has also authorized revisions to 1046 EUA authorizations.

title: FDA Roundup: July 22, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration published several guidance documents and issued new regulations. The FDA published a guidance on "Failure to Respond to an ANDA Complete Response Letter Within the Regulatory Timeframe" and "Orange Book Questions and Answers" to assist applicants and approved application holders. The agency also published a proposed rule to revise the National Drug Code Format and Drug Label Barcode Requirements to adopt a single, uniform 12-digit format. Additionally, the FDA posted a final guidance on "Unique Device Identification: Policy Regarding Compliance Dates for Class I and Unclassified Devices, Direct Marking, and Global Unique Device Identification Database Requirements for Certain Devices." The agency also warned consumers about potential risks associated with the use of certain ultraviolet (UV) wands and issued import alerts for enoki mushrooms and hydrogen-infused water beverages. Furthermore, the FDA issued a supplemental notice of proposed rulemaking for pre-harvest agricultural requirements and authorized new tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations.

title: FDA Details Optimized Approach for Regulatory Oversight Tools to Better Protect Public Health
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is releasing a draft guidance on the expanded use of remote regulatory assessments (RRAs) to enhance oversight of FDA-regulated products. RRAs are an additional tool that complements inspections and other means of obtaining information, and their use is intended to be consistent across all FDA-regulated products. Over the last two years, the FDA has performed over 1,470 domestic and 600 foreign entity establishment RRAs, identifying unreported adverse events and helping the agency make regulatory decisions. The draft guidance aims to provide transparency to stakeholders on how RRAs may be used and promote consistency in their conduct. The FDA intends to continue using RRAs according to a risk-based approach that protects public health.
