title: FDA Conducting Evaluation of Key Agency Activities to Strengthen Operations
body_summary: I rejoined the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as Commissioner of Food and Drugs in February 2022, having previously served in the role five years earlier. The agency has taken significant actions benefiting public health since my return, but also faces challenges testing regulatory frameworks and operations. I have commissioned external experts to evaluate two key programs: the Human Foods Program and the Center for Tobacco Products. The Human Foods Program, which includes the Office of Food Response and Policy, faces challenges related to the increasing diversity and complexity of the nation's food systems and supply chain. The Center for Tobacco Products, established 13 years ago, will continue its work during the evaluation. An independent partner organization, the Reagan-Udall Foundation, will report its findings on the evaluation within 60 business days. I am committed to addressing the findings and implementing recommended changes, which will strengthen the FDA and prepare it for future scientific challenges and opportunities.

title: FDA Roundup: July 19, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has updated its device shortage lists and provided information on devices removed from the list due to increased availability of semiconductor chips. The FDA has also issued a request for information on the food contact uses of fluorinated polyethylene, seeking scientific data and information on its current uses, consumer dietary exposure, and safety information. The FDA is reopening the comment period for a request seeking available use and safety information on remaining phthalates authorized for use as plasticizers in food contact applications. As of today, 441 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 304 molecular tests, 85 antibody and other immune response tests, and 51 antigen tests.

title: Statement on the Food and Drug Administration and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Authorization of the Novavax COVID-19 Vaccine for Adults
body_summary: The Food and Drug Administration has authorized Novavax's protein-based COVID-19 vaccine for adults. The vaccine is now one of four safe and effective COVID-19 vaccines available to protect Americans against serious illness, hospitalizations, and death. This comes after the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention also conducted an independent scientific review. The vaccine has been used to protect over 260 million Americans at least with their first shot and nearly 110 million people with a booster shot. The administration has saved over 2 million American lives. With BA.5 increasing infections, the president encourages everyone to get vaccinated, particularly those over 50 or immunocompromised, to stay up to date on their COVID-19 vaccinations.

title: Statement on Climate Change, Clean Energy, and Health Care Legislation
body_summary: The President will take strong Executive action if the Senate does not tackle the climate crisis and strengthen the domestic clean energy industry. This will create jobs, improve energy security, and protect against oil and gas price hikes. The President also supports a bill to negotiate lower drug prices for Medicare and prevent health insurance premium increases for millions of families. The Senate should pass the bill before the August recess and send it to the President's desk for signing. The President thanks Leader Schumer and Speaker Pelosi for their efforts to produce a strong bill.

title: FDA Roundup: July 15, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has announced various news and updates. The agency's Total Diet Study (TDS) Report for Fiscal Years 2018-2020 is now available, providing data on nutrients and toxic elements from the US Food Supply. The FDA has also issued a safety communication advising people to use swab samples taken directly from a lesion for testing the monkeypox virus. The agency has updated educational resources for parents and caregivers regarding imported infant formula and provided information on genotyping tests for SARS-CoV-2 mutations. The FDA has issued warning letters to manufacturers and retailers for unlawfully marketing non-tobacco nicotine products. The agency has recognized six accreditation bodies under the Laboratory Accreditation for Analyses of Foods (LAAF) program and authorized over-the-counter at-home COVID-19 antigen tests.

title: FDA Provides Educational Resources for Parents and Caregivers to Support Confidence for Imported Infant Formula Products
body_summary: The US FDA has announced the availability of educational resources for parents and caregivers on using imported infant formula. The agency's "Names to Know" graphics and infographic highlight the amounts of imported formula. Resources include infographics, a Consumer Update, and short consumer videos addressing frequently asked questions. The FDA has also created a conversion chart to help consumers safely prepare imported infant formula. Parents and caregivers are encouraged to talk to their baby's healthcare provider for recommendations on changing feeding practices and formulas. Tips are available for finding safe substitutes and reporting counterfeit formula.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Report on the Consumer Price Index for June
body_summary: Today's headline inflation reading is out of date, with energy comprising nearly half of the monthly increase in inflation. The price at the pump has fallen by about 40 cents since mid-June, providing important breathing room for American families. Annual "core inflation" has come down for the third month in a row, with the rate below 6 percent for the first time since last year. The U.S. is producing 12.1 million barrels of oil per day, and the president plans to continue releasing oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, working with European allies to put a price cap on Russian oil, and urging Congress to pass legislation to reduce everyday expenses. The president will also oppose efforts to raise taxes on working people or threaten Social Security and Medicare.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Emergency Use of Novavax COVID-19 Vaccine, Adjuvanted
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the Novavax COVID-19 Vaccine, Adjuvanted, to prevent COVID-19 caused by SARS-CoV-2 in individuals 18 years of age and older. The vaccine has been authorized after a thorough analysis and evaluation of the available safety and effectiveness data, and meets the FDA's rigorous standards for safety, effectiveness, and manufacturing quality. The vaccine is administered as a two-dose primary series, three weeks apart, and contains the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and Matrix-M adjuvant. The vaccine was assessed in an ongoing randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled study, which showed a 90.4% effectiveness in preventing mild, moderate or severe COVID-19. The most commonly reported side effects included pain/tenderness, redness and swelling at the injection site, fatigue, muscle pain, headache, joint pain, nausea/vomiting and fever. The authorization will be effective until the circumstances justify its termination and may be revised or revoked if it no longer meets the statutory criteria.

title: FDA Warns Four Companies for Selling Tainted Honey-based Products with Hidden Active Drug Ingredients
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) posted warning letters to four companies for selling honey-based products containing active drug ingredients not listed on the product labels, including Cialis and Viagra. These products may pose a significant health risk to consumers due to interactions with nitrates and potential lowering of blood pressure. The FDA has requested responses from the companies within 15 working days to address these issues. The agency previously warned consumers about over 10 honey-based products containing hidden drug ingredients and encourages stores, websites, and online marketplaces to stop selling these products. Consumers are advised to talk to a health care professional before using any over-the-counter product marketed for sexual enhancement.

title: Executive Order 14076—Protecting Access to Reproductive Health Care Services
body_summary: The President has ordered to protect access to reproductive healthcare services, including abortion, by issuing a policy to support women's right to choose and to protect and defend reproductive rights. The Federal Government will take action to promote access to critical reproductive healthcare services, including abortion, and to ensure the safety and security of patients, providers, and third parties. The order includes definitions of key terms, potential actions to protect and expand access to reproductive healthcare services, and steps to ensure patient safety and security. An Interagency Task Force on Reproductive Healthcare Access will be established to coordinate Federal interagency policymaking, program development, and outreach efforts. The order also encourages private pro bono attorneys, bar associations, and public interest organizations to assist patients, providers, and third parties seeking reproductive healthcare services.

title: FDA Roundup: July 8, 2022
body_summary: The US FDA approved COMIRNATY (COVID-19 Vaccine, mRNA) for individuals 12-15 years old to prevent COVID-19. The approval follows a rigorous analysis and evaluation of safety and effectiveness data. COMIRNATY has been authorized for individuals 16 years and older since August 2021. The FDA finalized Guidance for Industry #245 to help animal food facilities develop food safety plans. The FDA will host virtual town halls on July 27 and August 24 to share information on SARS-CoV-2 test development and answer questions. As of today, 438 tests and sample collection devices are authorized for COVID-19 testing, including 303 molecular tests, 85 antibody tests, 49 antigen tests, and 1 diagnostic breath test.

title: FDA Infant Formula Update: July 8, 2022
body_summary:
The US FDA is providing an update on steps taken to increase infant formula availability in the US. Additional steps will lead to more infant formula products becoming available. 

A recent US FDA decision has led to the approval of Care A2+ 0-12 Months Infant Formula from Australia. 

The initial product shipment is scheduled for the first week of August. The product will be distributed to approximately 20,000 retail locations nationwide, covering about 91% of the population. 

The FDA is exercising enforcement discretion for the importation of certain infant formula products listed above. 

The agency is leveraging flexibilities to increase the supply of products while ensuring safe use and adequate nutrition. 

The FDA issued guidance on May 16 that outlined a process for importing infant formula products intended for foreign markets or export to foreign countries. 

The agency has posted a webpage with information on additional products headed to the US. 

The FDA expects that measures and resumption of production at the Abbott Nutrition's Sturgis, Mich. facility will increase supply. 

The FDA advises against making infant formulas at home or diluting formula. Parents and caregivers are encouraged to work with their child's healthcare provider for recommendations on changing feeding practices. 

The US Department of Health and Human Services also provides information on infant formula at HHS.gov/formula. 

The FDA monitors online marketplaces for fraudulent products and works with major online retailers to remove violative products.

title: FDA Infant Formula Update: July 6, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken additional steps to increase the availability of infant formula in the US. Vitaflo USA LLC, a company from The Netherlands, will make its specialty formula PKU Start available within two weeks through direct purchase and medical distribution channels. The FDA has exercised enforcement discretion for the importation of this formula, following nutritional adequacy and safety reviews. The agency is leveraging flexibilities to bolster supply, and ongoing efforts include monitoring online marketplaces for fraudulent products and collaborating with major retailers to remove violative products. The FDA will continue to dedicate resources to ensure safe and nutritious infant formula remains available, and parents are advised to work with their child's healthcare provider for recommendations on changing feeding practices.

title: FDA Developing New Framework for Continued, Expanded Access to Infant Formula Options for U.S. Parents and Caregivers
body_summary: The US infant formula supply needs to be diversified and strengthened due to the recent shutdown of a major plant and natural weather events. The FDA has issued guidance to temporarily exercise enforcement discretion for certain requirements on infant formula to address the shortage. The agency has prioritized review of requests from firms that can demonstrate product safety, produce large volumes, and get products onto shelves quickly. The FDA has increased infant formula supplies, including over 400 million 8-ounce bottles from nine countries, and has set enforcement discretion to remain in effect until November 14, 2022. The agency plans to provide a single technical assistance contact for new entrants, host meetings with existing companies, and issue further guidance for companies that have received temporary enforcement discretion.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Pharmacists to Prescribe Paxlovid with Certain Limitations
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration revised the Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for Paxlovid to allow state-licensed pharmacists to prescribe the drug to eligible patients. This change aims to expand access to timely treatment for some patients who are eligible for Paxlovid. Patients who test positive for COVID-19 should first seek care from their regular healthcare provider or a Test-to-Treat site. State-licensed pharmacists can prescribe Paxlovid with certain limitations, including requiring patients to bring specific information, such as electronic or printed health records, a list of medications, and results of laboratory blood work. Under the revised authorization, patients may need to be referred to a clinical evaluation with a licensed healthcare professional if certain conditions apply.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A joint meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee and the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System was held on June 14-15, 2022. The meeting discussed financial developments, including significant swings in asset prices and tightening financial conditions. Near-term policy rate expectations shifted after the release of the May consumer price index report. The effective federal funds rate remained steady at 83 basis points, while the Secured Overnight Financing Rate softened due to high liquidity and declining Treasury bill supply. Participation in the overnight reverse repurchase agreement facility increased, with a manager noting potential for further lifting of the per-counterparty limit. Prime credit scores inched up from low levels, while household borrowing increased slightly. The staff economic outlook projected GDP growth rebounding in Q2 and remaining solid over 2023, but with less accommodative monetary policy and tightening financial conditions leading to reduced forecasts for 2022-2024. PCE price inflation was expected to be 5.0% in 2022, slowing to 2.4% in 2023 and 2.0% in 2024. The labor market remained tight, with employment growth moderating but still robust. The Committee anticipated raising interest rates 75 basis points to address imbalances in the labor market and reduce inflation pressures. The Federal Reserve Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent and anticipated ongoing increases to reduce inflation pressures by restraining aggregate demand.

title: FDA Roundup: July 5, 2022
body_summary: The US FDA has opened registration for the 2022 Public Meeting of the National Antimicrobial Resistance Monitoring System (NARMS) to be held virtually on September 21 and 22, 2022. The meeting is open to all stakeholders at no cost. On June 30, the FDA issued warning letters to four companies selling unapproved kratom products and one company selling essential oils for opioid treatment, due to concerns over kratom's safety. The FDA advises consumers not to use kratom or essential oils for opioid treatment and is actively evaluating available scientific information on the issue. As of today, 438 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 303 molecular tests, 85 antibody tests, and 49 antigen tests.

title: FDA Roundup: July 1, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration announced a request for nominations for consumer representatives to serve on advisory committees and panels. The agency seeks to include diverse perspectives, regardless of gender identification, religious affiliation, racial and ethnic identification, or disability status. Nominations must be submitted by August 15, 2022. The FDA also released updates on its action plan for Supporting Antimicrobial Stewardship in Veterinary Settings and revised the Evusheld Fact Sheet for Healthcare Providers. Additionally, the FDA approved the Beyond Air, Inc. LungFit PH device to treat pulmonary hypertension in newborn infants. As of today, 438 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Recommends Inclusion of Omicron BA.4/5 Component for COVID-19 Vaccine Booster Doses
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration's Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee met on June 28, 2022, to discuss whether a change to COVID-19 vaccine strain composition for booster doses is necessary for the 2022 fall and winter seasons. The committee voted in favor of including an SARS-CoV-2 omicron component in COVID-19 vaccines for boosters in the U.S. beginning in fall 2022. The FDA has advised manufacturers to develop modified vaccines with an omicron BA.4/5 spike protein component to create a two-component (bivalent) booster vaccine, which may be introduced in early to mid-fall 2022. The FDA will evaluate data from clinical trials with modified vaccines containing an omicron BA.4/5 component and assess their safety, effectiveness, and manufacturing quality.

title: FDA Infant Formula Update: June 30, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing an update on steps taken to increase infant formula availability. Danone's Aptamil Gold Plus will be available in the U.S. in August, with approximately 555,000 cans (1.1 million pounds) expected. The FDA is leveraging flexibilities to boost supply, exercising enforcement discretion for importation of certain products. Guidance issued on May 16 outlined a process for importing infant formula products for foreign markets. The agency continues to work with manufacturers and suppliers to increase domestically-produced product. Parents are advised against making infant formulas at home or diluting formula, and caregivers are encouraged to work with healthcare providers for recommendations.

title: FDA Infant Formula Update: June 28, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is increasing the availability of infant formula in the US. Abbott Nutrition's Similac Advance 2'-FL Stage 1 formula will be available in mid-July, with an estimated 18,677 cans (about 35,000 pounds) being made available. The FDA is exercising enforcement discretion for the importation of this product, and Abbott Nutrition will reserve some inventory for free distribution to Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) agencies. The FDA is also leveraging flexibilities to increase the supply of infant formula, and is in discussions with manufacturers and suppliers to ensure adequate supply. The agency has issued guidance on May 16 to facilitate the importation of infant formula products for foreign markets, and will continue to monitor online marketplaces and consumer complaints to prevent counterfeit and fraudulent products.

title: FDA Roundup: June 28, 2022
body_summary:
The US FDA has authorized an extension to the shelf-life of specific lots of the refrigerated AstraZeneca monoclonal antibody Evusheld from 18 months to 24 months. This extension applies to unopened vials of Evusheld stored under refrigerated conditions. The FDA has also granted an extension to the shelf-life of specific lots of the Regeneron monoclonal antibodies casirivimab and imdevimab from 24 months to 30 months.

The agency has authorized 438 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody tests, antigen tests, and diagnostic breath tests. The FDA has also authorized 27 antigen tests and 8 molecular tests for serial screening programs.

title: FDA Introduces Innovative Proposal to Advance Consumer Access to Nonprescription Drugs
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a proposed rule to broaden the range of marketed nonprescription drugs available to consumers, enabling them to self-treat certain common conditions. FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf stated that nonprescription drug products play a vital role in America's healthcare system. The proposed rule aims to increase the availability of drugs that would otherwise only be available by prescription. If finalized, the rule would establish requirements for drug companies to submit new applications for nonprescription drug products with additional conditions for nonprescription use. The rule would require an additional condition for nonprescription use to be approved by the FDA if it ensures safe and effective self-use by consumers without healthcare professional supervision. The comment period for the proposed rule ends 120 days after publication in the Federal Register, and the FDA will review and consider comments to develop the final rule.

title: FDA Infant Formula Update: June 27, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing an update on increased flexibilities to lead to more infant formula available in the U.S. Bellamy's Organic has agreed to provide 696,000 cans (about 1.4 million pounds or about 21 million full-size, 8-ounce bottles) of its products, Bellamy's Organic Organic Infant Formula Step 1 (0-6 months) and Bellamy's Organic Organic Follow-On Formula Step 2 (6-12 months), starting early July and over the next several months. The FDA is exercising enforcement discretion for the importation of these products, leveraging flexibilities to ensure safe and adequate nutrition. The agency remains in discussions with manufacturers and suppliers to increase supply.

title: FDA Roundup: June 24, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced the recognition of JANAAC as an Accreditation Body Under FSMA- Accredited Third Party Certification Program for a period of five years. The FDA will convene a public meeting of the Medical Devices Advisory Committee later this year to discuss the accuracy of pulse oximeters. As of today, 438 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 303 molecular tests, 85 antibody and other immune response tests, and 49 antigen tests. The FDA has also authorized 1011 revisions to EUA authorizations.

title: FDA Releases Action Plan for Rare Neurodegenerative Diseases, Including ALS
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has unveiled an Action Plan for Rare Neurodegenerative Diseases, including Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), to improve and extend the lives of people with these diseases. The plan, developed in accordance with the Accelerating Access to Critical Therapies for ALS Act, aims to advance the development of safe and effective medical products and facilitate patient access to novel treatments. The plan includes regulatory science initiatives, enhancements to existing programs, and new policy initiatives, such as establishing a public-private partnership and engaging in targeted activities to bolster scientific advancement and promote innovation. The plan focuses on specific areas, including improving characterization of disease pathogenesis and natural history, facilitating patient access to new drugs, enhancing clinical trial infrastructure and agility, and leveraging ongoing FDA regulatory science efforts.

title: FDA Denies Authorization to Market JUUL Products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued marketing denial orders (MDOs) to JUUL Labs Inc. for all their products currently marketed in the US. The company must stop selling and distributing these products, and retailers must remove them from the market. The FDA determined that JUUL's premarket tobacco product applications lacked sufficient evidence regarding the toxicological profile of the products, citing insufficient and conflicting data. The MDOs only pertain to commercial distribution and retail sales, not individual consumer possession or use. The FDA recommends against modifying or adding substances to tobacco products and encourages users to report any unexpected health problems. The agency will take enforcement action against distributors and retailers who fail to comply with the order.

title: FDA Provides Update on Efforts to Increase Supply and Availability of Safe and Nutritious Infant Formula
body_summary: The US FDA has taken steps to ensure access to safe infant formula following Abbott Nutrition's voluntary recall. The agency has issued enforcement discretion letters for the importation of infant formula products from six countries, covering approximately 365 million bottles. FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf has spoken with infant formula manufacturers, who have increased production efforts. Regular inspections of infant formula facilities, including annual surveillance inspections, have been conducted, with a focus on firms with high risk factors. Abbott Nutrition has released certain specialty infant formula products on a case-by-case basis for infants with medical conditions. The FDA has reviewed over 129 consumer complaints, including nine infant deaths, with two linked to the Abbott Nutrition Sturgis plant and one related to an infant death in January 2022.

title: FDA Infant Formula Update: June 22, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is providing an update on additional steps taken to increase the availability of infant formula in the US. Global Kosher's Kendamil First Infant Formula with Iron will be made available in the US, with an initial shipment of 25,000 cases (150,000 cans). The FDA is exercising enforcement discretion for the importation of this product, and the agency will continue to work with manufacturers and suppliers to increase supply. The FDA has also issued guidance on May 16 to outline a process for importing infant formula products intended for a foreign market or for domestic distribution. The agency expects that increased production and supply will be available on store shelves moving forward.

title: FDA Announces Plans for Proposed Rule to Reduce Addictiveness of Cigarettes and Other Combusted Tobacco Products
body_summary:
The Biden-Harris Administration has published plans for potential regulatory actions, including a proposed product standard by the US Food and Drug Administration to establish a maximum nicotine level in combusted tobacco products to reduce addictiveness. The goal is to reduce youth use, addiction, and death. 

Each year, 480,000 people die prematurely from smoking-attributed diseases, and tobacco use costs nearly $300 billion annually. Nicotine is not toxic, but it's the main driver of sustained use of combusted products. 

The US Surgeon General has reported that 87% of adult smokers start smoking before age 18. A 2018 FDA paper projected that a potential nicotine product standard could result in 33 million fewer regular smokers by 2100, and 8 million fewer deaths from tobacco-related illnesses. 

The Spring 2022 Unified Agenda lists several planned potential regulatory actions, including tobacco products. The FDA is also focused on its regulatory oversight of e-cigarettes and other electronic nicotine delivery systems, and has taken action on nearly 99% of submitted products.

title: FDA Roundup: June 21, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a draft guidance on Non-Clinical Performance Assessment of Tissue Containment Systems Used During Power Morcellation Procedures. Comments can be submitted within 60 days atwww.regulations.govunder docket number FDA-2022-D-0737. The FDA has also approved a second generic naloxone hydrochloride (HCI) intranasal spray. Additionally, the FDA issued the final guidance,FDA Oversight of Food Covered by Systems Recognition Arrangements: Guidance for Food and Drug Administration Staff. The FDA has authorized 438 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 303 molecular tests and 85 antibody and other immune response tests.

title: Statement on the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Authorization of the Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccines for Children Under Age Five
body_summary: The Food and Drug Administration and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention have authorized and recommended COVID-19 vaccines for children under 5. This development comes after a rigorous scientific review, allowing virtually every American now eligible for protection from the virus. The administration has been planning to secure doses and offer mRNA vaccines to children as young as 6 months old. Over 220 million Americans have been fully vaccinated, with 100 million boosted, and 2 million lives saved. Parents can start scheduling appointments at pediatricians' offices, children's hospitals, and pharmacies this week, with vaccine availability increasing on vaccines.gov.

title: FDA Roundup: June 17, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced the publication of three International Test Method Standards in Nanotechnology by the American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) International. NCTR scientists conducted research with support from the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences (NIEHS) toward the collaborative consensus-standards development for liposomes. The FDA has also sent its ninth annual Report on Drug Shortages for Calendar Year 2021 to Congress, highlighting 41 new drug shortages and 317 potential shortages that the agency helped prevent. The FDA has authorized 438 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 303 molecular tests and 49 antigen tests, with 1005 revisions to EUA authorizations.

title: FDA Infant Formula Update: June 17, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken additional steps to increase the availability of infant formula in the US market. The agency has exercised enforcement discretion for the importation of certain infant formula products, allowing them to be sold at major retailers. Aptamil First Infant Milk Stage 1, manufactured by Danone (Ireland), will be made available in the US, starting in July. The product is suitable for most infants but may not be suitable for premature or low birth weight infants. The FDA has also issued guidance to facilitate the importation of infant formula products intended for foreign markets. The agency is working to improve supply and availability, with measures expected to lead to more domestic production and increased quantity of products on store shelves. The FDA advises against making infant formulas at home or diluting formula and encourages parents to work with healthcare providers for recommendations on changing feeding practices.

title: Statement on the Food and Drug Administration's Authorization of the Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccines for Children Under Age Five
body_summary: The Food and Drug Administration has authorized COVID-19 vaccines for kids under the age of 5. Pending CDC recommendations, parents will be able to get their youngest kids vaccinated as early as next week. The US is the first country to offer COVID-19 vaccines to children under 5, with mRNA doses available for children as young as 6 months old. The administration secured vaccine doses and will begin shipping millions to trusted locations, including pediatricians' offices, hospitals, and pharmacies. Vaccinations will start as early as next week, with appointments ramping up over the coming days and weeks.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccines for Children Down to 6 Months of Age
body_summary: The US FDA authorized emergency use of the Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccines for children as young as 6 months old. The vaccines were authorized based on rigorous safety, effectiveness, and manufacturing data. A clinical trial of 1,700 children aged 6-23 months and 3,000 children aged 2-5 years found the vaccine to be effective in preventing severe COVID-19 outcomes. The most common side effects included pain, redness, swelling, fever, and lymph node swelling. The vaccine's effectiveness in infants and children was found to be comparable to those in adults. Safety data showed rare cases of myocarditis and pericarditis, which typically resolved with conservative management. The FDA and CDC monitor COVID-19 vaccine safety through systems like VAERS, requiring reporting of serious adverse events, hospitalizations, and deaths.

title: Implementation Note issued June 15, 2022
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on June 15, 2022: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 1.65 percent, effective June 16, 2022. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective June 16, 2022, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent. Conduct overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 1.75 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion; the aggregate operation limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 1.55 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in the calendar months of June and July that exceeds a cap of $30 billion per month. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap. Reinvest into agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in the calendar months of June and July that exceeds a cap of $17.5 billion per month. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve a 3/4 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate to 1.75 percent, effective June 16, 2022. In taking this action, the Board approved the request to establish that rate submitted by the Board of Directors of the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: FDA Infant Formula Update: June 15, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has taken additional steps to increase the availability of infant formula in the U.S. through increased flexibilities. Mead Johnson Nutrition/Reckitt, a Singapore-based company, will provide 4.5 million pounds of base powder for production, resulting in approximately 5.7 million cans of Enfamil Stage 1 formula. The base powder will begin shipping in June to a Minnesota facility, with follow-on shipments continuing through November. The FDA is evaluating options to get the product to the U.S. as quickly as possible. The agency is leveraging flexibilities to ensure safe and nutritious infant formula is available while meeting contractual obligations under the WIC program. The FDA has issued guidance on May 16 to allow the importation of certain infant formula products, and is monitoring online marketplaces for fraudulent products.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Overall economic activity appears to have picked up after edging down in the first quarter. Job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Inflation remains elevated, reflecting supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic, higher energy prices, and broader price pressures. The invasion of Ukraine by Russia is causing tremendous human and economic hardship. The invasion and related events are creating additional upward pressure on inflation and are weighing on global economic activity. In addition, COVID-related lockdowns in China are likely to exacerbate supply chain disruptions. The Committee is highly attentive to inflation risks. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1â1/2 to 1-3/4 percent and anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate. In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in the Plans for Reducing the Size of the Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet that were issued in May. The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; James Bullard; Lisa D. Cook; Patrick Harker; Philip N. Jefferson; Loretta J. Mester; and Christopher J. Waller. Voting against this action was Esther L. George, who preferred at this meeting to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 0.5 percentage point to 1-1/4 percent to 1-1/2 percent. Patrick Harker voted as an alternate member at this meeting.

title: FDA Roundup: June 14, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced plans to study how patients weigh the benefits and risks associated with smooth and textured breast implants, including the risk of Breast Implant Associated Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma (BIA-ALCL). The Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH) expects the survey results to help assess whether patients' perception of risks is influenced by information about potential benefits. The study will be conducted by Research Triangle Institute International. The FDA has also issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the Labcorp VirSeq SARS-CoV-2 NGS Test on the PacBio Sequel II sequencing system for the identification and differentiation of SARS-CoV-2 Phylogenetic Assignment of Named Global Outbreak (PANGO) lineages. As of today, 437 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under EUAs, including molecular tests, antibody tests, antigen tests, and diagnostic breath tests.

title: FDA Approves First Systemic Treatment for Alopecia Areata
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Olumiant (baricitinib) oral tablets to treat adult patients with severe alopecia areata, a condition affecting over 300,000 people in the US annually. This marks the first FDA approval of a systemic treatment for alopecia areata. The approval was granted based on efficacy and safety data from two randomized trials, with patients receiving Olumiant or a placebo, showing significant improvements in scalp hair coverage. Olumiant is a Janus kinase inhibitor that blocks inflammation pathways. The most common side effects include upper respiratory tract infections, headache, and fatigue. The FDA granted the approval to Eli Lilly and Company, with priority review and breakthrough therapy designations.

title: FDA Infant Formula Update: June 10, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing an update on additional steps taken to increase infant formula availability. Abbott, a Spanish company, has committed to selling some formula on Similac.com and other online retailers, while providing emergency samples to areas with low supply. The FDA is exercising enforcement discretion for the importation of infant formula products, including Abbott's Similac Total Comfort and NeoSure, following nutritional adequacy and safety reviews. The agency has also issued guidance on May 16 to facilitate the importation of infant formula products for a foreign market or domestic distribution. The FDA expects increased supply from Abbott's resumed production at its Sturgis, Mich., facility, and advises against making infant formulas at home or diluting formula.

title: FDA Roundup: June 10, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has authorized the marketing of two new tobacco products, Daily disposable e-cigarettes from NJOY LLC, through the Premarket Tobacco Product Application (PMTA) pathway. The FDA issued marketing granted orders for NJOY Daily Rich Tobacco 4.5% and NJOY Daily Extra Rich Tobacco 6%. The agency also issued marketing denial orders for multiple other Daily branded e-cigarette products. Additionally, the FDA warned consumers about the potential dangers of products treating moles, seborrheic keratoses, or skin tags, advising them to avoid these products due to their potentially harmful side effects. As of today, 437 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 302 molecular tests and 85 antibody tests.

title: FDA Launches Campaign Aimed at Preventing E-Cigarette Use Among American Indian/Alaska Native Youth
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has launched the "Next Legends" Youth E-cigarette Prevention Campaign to educate American Indian/Alaska Native youth about the harms of vaping. The campaign aims to reach approximately 400,000 Native teens, with studies showing that Native youth are more susceptible to e-cigarette use than non-Native peers. The campaign features unique branding and tailored messaging created in consultation with AI/AN community members and experts. Digital video advertisements will be placed on social media sites and streaming platforms, with additional billboard, radio, and TV ads in Alaska. The campaign's messaging focuses on the negative health consequences and addiction risks of using e-cigarettes. The FDA's media contractor partnered with a Native-owned advertising agency to ensure cultural relevancy for the target audience.

title: FDA Roundup: June 7, 2022
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is considering a master file pilot program for premarket approval holders using radiation, including gamma radiation, to sterilize approved medical devices. The pilot program aims to support sterilization supply chain resiliency and advance alternative ways to sterilize devices. The FDA is working with sterilization experts, medical device manufacturers, and government agencies to develop new sterilizing agents or alternatives while maintaining device safety and effectiveness.

The FDA has released a new online resource page for human and animal food producers affected by flooding and severe weather incidents. The page provides information on federal and state resources available to those impacted.

The FDA has also announced a live webinar on June 22, "Reporting of Veterinary Drug Supply Chain Information Using the Animal Drug Manufacturing System (ADMS) eSubmitter Tool." The webinar is intended for animal drug manufacturers, U.S. agents, and government agencies.

The FDA has cleared the AFib History Feature for use with compatible Apple Watches and Health app. Additionally, the agency has provided guidance for prescribers to evaluate potential drug interactions when using Paxlovid therapy for COVID-19.

As of today, 438 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 308 molecular tests and 49 antigen tests.

title: FDA Infant Formula Update: June 3, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing an update on steps taken to increase infant formula availability in the U.S. under recent increased flexibilities. Nestlé (Mexico) is expected to bring about 1.3 million cans (2.2 million pounds or 33 million full-size bottles) of Gerber Good Start Gentle formula to the U.S. market, with availability expected from July to October. The FDA is exercising enforcement discretion for the importation of these products, leveraging flexibilities to ensure safe and nutritious formula is available. The agency remains in discussions with manufacturers and suppliers to increase supply, and has issued guidance on May 16 to facilitate the importation of certain infant formula products. The FDA has also posted a webpage with information on additional products headed to the U.S. and continues to monitor online marketplaces and consumer complaints to ensure safe formula is available.

title: FDA Roundup: June 3, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration updated its safety communication on a new handpiece for the Renuvion/J-Plasma device system, which is cleared for treating moderate to severe wrinkles and rhytides in patients with certain skin types. The FDA also announced open periods for applications to support the development of evidence-based guidelines for managing postoperative pain in obstetric patients and safe tapering of benzodiazepines. Additionally, the FDA authorized changes to the Fact Sheet for Healthcare Providers Administering Vaccine for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine and opened a new period for grants to develop animal drugs for uncommon diseases. As of today, 437 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under emergency use authorizations for COVID-19 testing.

title: FDA Launches New Dietary Supplement Education Initiative for Consumers, Educators, and Healthcare Professionals
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration launched a new initiative called Supplement Your Knowledge to educate consumers, educators, and healthcare professionals about dietary supplements. The initiative aims to provide reliable information about the potential benefits and risks associated with dietary supplements. The FDA advises consumers to talk to their doctor or healthcare professional before using dietary supplements, as some may interact with medicines or other supplements. The agency encourages consumers and healthcare professionals to report adverse reactions to the Safety Reporting Portal. The Supplement Your Knowledge resources include public education videos and fact sheets, a curriculum for high school students, and a continuing medical education program for healthcare professionals.

title: FDA Roundup: May 31, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is hosting a free, virtual Regulatory Education for Industry (REdI) Annual Conference 2022 from June 6 to June 10, featuring Dr. Robert M. Califf as keynote speaker. The conference will cover COVID-19 milestones and future activities. The event offers 32.5 contact hours of continuing education for physicians, pharmacists, and nurses. The FDA has authorized 436 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 302 molecular tests, 84 antibody tests, 49 antigen tests, and 1 diagnostic breath test.

title: FDA Roundup: May 27, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is taking action to protect animals and the safety of the food supply by issuing warning letters to companies illegally selling CBD products intended for use in food-producing animals. The FDA has also authorized an extension of the shelf life of the Eli Lilly monoclonal antibody bebtelovimab from 12 to 18 months. Additionally, the FDA has issued warning letters to Santhigram Kerala Ayurvedic Co. of U.S., Inc. and Ayuryoga, Inc. for selling unapproved products with fraudulent claims to treat multiple diseases, including COVID-19. The FDA has also revised the scope of authorization for Evusheld’s EUA to include new information on hypersensitivity reactions and the risk of cross-hypersensitivity with COVID-19 vaccines. The FDA has authorized over 436 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 302 molecular tests and 84 antibody and other immune response tests.

title: FDA Efforts to Result in Millions of Additional Bottles of Infant Formula to Further Increase U.S. Supply
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is providing additional steps to increase infant formula availability on US store shelves in the coming weeks and months. FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf stated that the agency is working around the clock with government partners and industry to ensure adequate infant formula is available whenever parents and caregivers need it. Bubs Australia plans to provide at least 1.25 million cans of its infant formula, which will make at least 27.5 million full-size bottles available. The US Department of Health and Human Services is evaluating options to get the products to the US as quickly as possible. The FDA has notified Bubs Australia that it is exercising enforcement discretion for the importation of certain infant formula products.

title: Statement on the Bureau of Economic Analysis Report on Inflation for April
body_summary: The report shows annual inflation declining to around 4 percent at an annual rate, down from 6 percent in the previous 3 months. This is a sign of progress, but inflation remains too high. The current inflation rate is impacting food and energy prices, mainly due to Putin's price hike. The speaker's top economic priority is tackling inflation, and their plan involves giving the Federal Reserve independence to lower families' costs and reduce the Federal deficit. Congressional Republicans have a different plan, which would increase taxes on working families and potentially affect programs like Social Security and Medicare every 5 years.

title: FDA Flexibilities, Collaboration to Yield Millions of Bottles of Specialized Medical Infant Formula in Coming Months to Increase U.S. Supply
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has taken steps to address the shortage of specialized medical infant formula, which is currently in short supply in the US. The FDA has made progress in just the past week, including announcing that it has informed Kendal Nutricare that it will exercise enforcement discretion for the importation of certain infant formula under the Kendamil brand. This allows for the importation of about 2 million cans of infant formula, expected to be released in June. The FDA has also announced that it will not object to the release of about 300,000 cans of EleCare amino acid-based infant formula to individuals needing urgent, life-sustaining supplies. The agency is working closely with Danone's Nutricia business to boost production of specialized medical formula products and has posted a webpage with information about additional products headed to the US. The FDA has also taken steps to improve supply and availability, including increasing flexibility for manufacturers to produce infant formula products domestically.

title: Executive Order 14074—Advancing Effective, Accountable Policing and Criminal Justice Practices To Enhance Public Trust and Public Safety
body_summary:
The US Attorney General is tasked with implementing various reforms aimed at improving the criminal justice system, including increasing public trust and community-oriented policing. The Attorney General will issue guidance on best practices for independent investigations of deaths in custody, improve training for investigations into deprivation of rights under color of law, and strengthen officer recruitment and retention practices. The Attorney General must also develop and publish a report on law enforcement officer wellness within 180 days, assess Federal officer wellness practices, and implement changes as necessary.

Additionally, the Attorney General will work with law enforcement agencies to identify obstacles to participating in a use-of-force database, reduce administrative burdens, and provide training and technical assistance. The Attorney General will issue guidance on notifying family members of deaths in custody and revising policies, and publish a report on law enforcement officer review of Body Worn Camera footage with the Secretary of HHS.

The Attorney General will submit a strategic plan to advance criminal justice reform goals within 150 days, consulting with relevant agencies and safeguarding independence. The Attorney General will also review State, Tribal, local, and territorial LEAs' transition to the FBI's Uniform Crime Reporting Program and submit a report to the President within 120 days. Federal agencies with law enforcement-related grants must also submit a report to the Assistant Attorney General for the Civil Rights Division within 180 days.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A joint Federal Open Market Committee and Board of Governors meeting was held on May 3-4, 2022, discussing monetary policy expectations in the United States. The Federal Reserve raised its target federal funds rate to 3/4 to 1 percent and decided to begin reducing its balance sheet on June 1. Monetary policy tightening is expected over coming months, with sovereign yields increasing and domestic equity prices declining since the March FOMC meeting. The debt-to-GDP ratio remains low, business debt is elevated but interest coverage ratios are high, and banks are well capitalized with strong liquidity. PCE price inflation was revised up slightly due to supply constraints and is expected to be 4.3% in 2022, stepping down to 2.5% in 2023 and 2.1% in 2024. The Federal Reserve Committee aims to achieve maximum employment and a 2 percent inflation objective through this stance.

title: FDA Flexibilities to Yield Millions of Cans of Additional Infant Formula in Coming Months to Increase Supply Available to U.S. Consumers
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken steps to increase the availability of infant formula, including importing safe and nutritious products from overseas. FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf announced that Kendal Nutricare will send about 2 million cans of infant formula to the U.S. in June, following increased flexibilities regarding importation. The FDA also announced that it will not object to the release of about 300,000 cans of EleCare specialty formula by Abbott Nutrition on a case-by-case basis. The agency is working closely with manufacturers and suppliers to increase supply and availability, particularly for specialty products. The FDA has also held a webinar to review recent guidance for the infant formula industry and has taken steps to improve supply and availability.

title: FDA Roundup: May 24, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced the availability of one final guidance and two draft guidances for blood establishments. The final guidance removes recommendations to defer blood donors based on geographic risk or receipt of a blood transfusion in certain countries. The draft guidance describes circumstances under which the FDA will not take regulatory action for non-compliance with regulations for blood donors with blood pressure or pulse outside specified limits. The FDA also announced the availability of a report on the feasibility of establishing a voluntary public-private partnership to collect and analyze antimicrobial use data from food-producing animals. Additionally, the FDA authorized the marketing of BONESUPPORT AB Cerament G, a device-drug combination product for the treatment of osteomyelitis. As of today, 435 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under emergency use authorizations (EUAs).

title: FDA Roundup: May 20, 2022
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued a response to two food additive petitions and a citizen petition on May 19, amending its food additive regulation to no longer allow most phthalates to be used in food contact applications. The FDA also requested information on safety data and current use of certain phthalates. 

The agency published an article by Janet Woodcock, M.D., and Meredith Chuk, M.D., detailing the FDA's Enterprise Modernization Action Plan to improve business processes and IT systems. The plan aims to strengthen alignment between agency-wide strategic objectives and investments.

The FDA updated its safety communications and FAQs on the Philips Respironics ventilator, BiPAP machine, and CPAP machine recalls, providing the latest information on medical device reports. 

The agency authorized marketing of BONESUPPORT AB Cerament G, the first device-drug combination product of its kind, for the treatment of osteomyelitis. 

The FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health, Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, and Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research are hosting the 2022 Regulatory Education for Industry Annual Conference from June 6 through June 10, 2022.

As of today, 433 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations. This includes 300 molecular tests and sample collection devices, 83 antibody and other immune response tests, 49 antigen tests, and 1 diagnostic breath test.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Eosinophilic Esophagitis, a Chronic Immune Disorder
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Dupixent to treat eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) in adults and pediatric patients 12 years and older weighing at least 40 kilograms. This marks the first FDA approval of a treatment for EoE. The approval was granted based on the results of a randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, multicenter, placebo-controlled trial, which included two 24-week treatment periods. In the trial, 60% of patients who received Dupixent achieved reduced eosinophils in the esophagus, and 22 points improved in the Dysphagia Symptom Questionnaire score. The FDA previously approved Dupixent in 2017 for the treatment of moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis and certain types of asthma.

title: New FDA Draft Guidance Aims to Increase Safety Information About Dietary Supplement Marketplace
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced a draft guidance aimed at increasing safety information about the dietary supplement marketplace. The guidance allows manufacturers and distributors to submit late new dietary ingredient (NDI) notifications, which will help the agency gain more safety information and better protect public health. This draft guidance proposes enforcement discretion for a limited time and in limited circumstances to encourage manufacturers and distributors to correct past failures to submit required NDI notifications. The agency intends to exercise enforcement discretion for 180 days after the guidance is published. The draft guidance is part of the FDA's effort to strengthen the regulation of dietary supplements through modernization and reform, and it includes a new submission type for stakeholders to electronically submit their late notifications.

title: FDA Urges Drug Manufacturers to Develop Risk Management Plans to Promote a Stronger, Resilient Drug Supply Chain
body_summary: The US FDA is issuing draft guidance to help manufacturers develop, maintain, and implement risk management plans to mitigate the potential for drug shortages. This guidance aligns with principles from the International Council for Harmonisation guidance for industry, Q9 Quality Risk Management. The guidance provides a framework for stakeholders to consider when developing risk management plans, including identifying risk factors to consider. The goal is to reduce the risks of a disruption in the drug supply chain, ensuring an uninterrupted supply of safe, effective, and high-quality drugs to Americans.

title: FDA Roundup: May 17, 2022
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued an at-a-glance summary of recent news. On May 24-25, a two-day workshop will be held for stakeholders to learn about a quality management program and engage with the agency. 

The FDA has issued Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for the Labcorp Pixel by Labcorp COVID-19+Flu+RSV Test Home Collection Kit. This test detects COVID-19, influenza A and B, and Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) and can be used without a prescription for people 18 years and older with a self-collected nasal swab sample. 

A Class I recall notification has been issued for the Avanos Medical Cortrak*2 Enteral Access System due to reports of injuries and patient deaths after using the device. 

The FDA and the Department of Health and Human Services' Office of the Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response have issued a statement about the shelf-life of sotrovimab, which continues to be evaluated. 

As of today, 433 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations.

title: FDA Encourages Importation of Safe Infant Formula and Other Flexibilities to Further Increase Availability
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is announcing a guidance to increase the availability of infant formula across the country while protecting infant health. The agency is encouraging infant formula manufacturers worldwide to take advantage of these flexibilities. Commissioner Robert M. Califf has stated that the agency is leaving no stone unturned to increase availability and has implemented a streamlined process to facilitate importation of infant formula at U.S. ports of entry. The FDA has already seen a 300% increase in infant formula imports year-to-date and expects that the measures taken will continue to improve supply and availability. The agency is prioritizing submissions for products that demonstrate safety and nutritional adequacy and is working closely with manufacturers and suppliers to expedite entry for products made abroad.

title: FDA Provides New Updates on Activities to Mitigate Infant Formula Supply Challenges, Abbott Nutrition Agrees to Take Corrective Actions at Facility to Produce Safe Infant Formula
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has announced updates on its efforts to increase infant formula availability in the US. On May 16, the US District Court for the Western District of Michigan entered a consent decree requiring Abbott Nutrition to address safety concerns at its Sturgis, Michigan infant formula production facility. The proposed consent decree obliges Abbott to take corrective actions, including testing products, ceasing production, and promptly notifying the FDA in case of contamination. The FDA is also taking steps to improve supply, including working with other infant formula manufacturers to increase production and importation of comparable products. The agency recognizes variation in availability throughout the country and is exploring ways to alleviate supply challenges through better distribution. The FDA expects supply to continue improving over the next couple of months, with national infant formula sales by volume increasing by over 13% in April and in-stock rates reaching nearly 80% at the week ending May 8.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes First  COVID-19 Test Available without a Prescription That Also Detects Flu and RSV
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) authorized the Labcorp Seasonal Respiratory Virus RT-PCR DTC Test for use without a prescription by individuals with symptoms of respiratory viral infection consistent with COVID-19. The test can identify and differentiate multiple respiratory viruses, including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A and B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Results are delivered online, with follow-up from a healthcare provider for positive or invalid test results. The test can be purchased online or in a store without a prescription, and its use is allowed for individuals 18 years and older, 14 years and older with adult supervision, or 2 years and older with adult assistance.

title: FDA Approves Novel, Dual-Targeted Treatment for Type 2 Diabetes
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Mounjaro (tirzepatide) injection to improve blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes as an addition to diet and exercise. Mounjaro was found to be effective in improving blood sugar control and was more effective than other diabetes therapies in clinical studies. Type 2 diabetes affects over 30 million Americans and is a chronic and progressive condition. Mounjaro is administered once weekly and activates both GLP-1 and GIP receptors, leading to improved blood sugar control. In clinical trials, patients receiving the maximum recommended dose of Mounjaro had a 1.6% lowering of hemoglobin A1c levels, compared to 1.5% with placebo and 0.5% more than semaglutide. Obesity was common among study participants, and the maximum recommended dose of Mounjaro resulted in an average weight loss of 15-23 pounds. Mounjaro has been associated with nausea, vomiting, and decreased appetite, and may cause thyroid C-cell tumors in rats, but its safety and efficacy in humans are unknown.

title: FDA Roundup: May 13, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing an update on recent news. The FDA advised consumers about the risk of accidental ingestion of edible products containing THC, which may cause serious adverse events, especially in children. The FDA issued a final guidance to reduce microbial food safety hazards in seed for sprouting. Six new tobacco products were authorized through the Premarket Tobacco Product Application pathway, including e-cigarette devices. The FDA approved Radicava ORS for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). The FDA launched the Accelerating Rare Disease Cures (ARC) Program to speed up the development of treatments for rare diseases. There are 432 authorized COVID-19 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations.

title: Joint Statement by President Biden and President Ursula von der Leyen of the European Commission on the Second Global COVID-19 Summit
body_summary: The United States and the European Union are implementing the U.S.-EU Agenda for Beating the Global Pandemic, Vaccinating the World, Saving Lives Now and Building Back Better Health Security of September 22, 2021. Presidents Biden and von der Leyen reaffirmed milestones in their strong cooperation towards the five headline goals of the Agenda. The EU and U.S. have shared over one billion COVID-19 vaccine doses and aim to deliver 1.9 billion doses worldwide. They seek to ensure vaccine deliveries based on country demand, focusing on sub-Saharan Africa. The partnership will focus on vaccine readiness, strengthening logistics, combating hesitancy, and building health systems capacity. The U.S. and EU will consult with partners such as AVATT, CoVDP, and COVAX to accelerate vaccine absorption. They will strengthen dialogues with multilateral development banks and global partners to improve vaccine uptake and sustainable financing. The joint EU-U.S. COVID-19 manufacturing and supply chain task force was launched in September 2021 to provide early warning of supply chain bottlenecks and coordinate efforts to sustain vaccine production capabilities. The U.S. and EU are committed to cooperating on the establishment of a new Financial Intermediary Fund for pandemic preparedness and global health security at the World Bank. They will cooperate on strengthening the global health architecture, including the WHO, and conclude a convention or international instrument on pandemic prevention, preparedness, and response.

title: FDA Roundup: May 10, 2022
body_summary: The FDA approved Olumiant (baricitinib) for the treatment of COVID-19 in hospitalized adults requiring supplemental oxygen, non-invasive or invasive mechanical ventilation, or ECMO. This is the first immunomodulatory treatment for COVID-19 to receive FDA approval. Olumiant was first issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) in 2020 and later revised to authorize it as a standalone treatment in 2021. The FDA has revised the EUA to remove the population covered under the approved indication. The FDA continues to work on its Coronavirus Treatment Acceleration Program to expedite the development and availability of therapeutic drugs and biological products for COVID-19. The FDA also issued a safety communication warning against using the Skippack Medical Lab SARS-CoV-2 Antigen Rapid Test due to concerns over false results. The FDA has identified this issue as a Class I recall and has recalled the test. The FDA posted a consumer update about the agency's role in protecting public health and issued warning letters to companies selling adulterated dietary supplements. The FDA also issued draft guidance for industry on preventing contamination of animal feed and will accept public comment until August 8, 2022.

title: FDA Takes Important Steps to Improve Supply of Infant and Specialty Formula Products
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is working to increase the availability of infant and specialty formula products. On February 17, the agency warned consumers not to use certain powdered infant formula products from Abbott Nutrition's Sturgis, Michigan facility, and Abbott initiated a voluntary recall. The FDA has been working with Abbott and other manufacturers to bring safe products to the U.S. market. 

FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf stated that the agency is doing everything in its power to ensure there is adequate product available where and when needed. The FDA continues to take significant actions to help increase the current supply of infant formula in the U.S. Other infant formula manufacturers are meeting or exceeding capacity levels to meet current demand. 

The agency is meeting with major infant formula manufacturers, optimizing production schedules, and expediting review of notifications of manufacturing changes to increase supply. The FDA is also monitoring the status of the infant formula supply using the 21 Forward food supply chain continuity system and compiling data on trends for in-stock rates.

title: FDA Roundup: May 6, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared the Spectrum Medical Quantum Heater-Cooler and compatible Qura Quantum PureFlow Heat Exchangers for use in cardiopulmonary bypass procedures. The devices regulate temperature using a glycol-based heat transfer fluid, which mitigates the risk of contamination. The FDA has also issued a warning to healthcare providers about the potential risk of exposure to non-dioxin-like polychlorinated biphenyl acids (PCBAs) and polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) with certain hemodialysis machines manufactured by Fresenius Medical Care. The FDA has also published a public dashboard tracking its sequencing efforts to analyze SARS-CoV-2 RNA from wastewater samples. Additionally, the FDA has issued final guidance on feasibility and early feasibility clinical studies for certain medical devices intended to improve glycemic control in patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Limits Use of Janssen COVID-19 Vaccine to Certain Individuals
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has limited the authorized use of the Janssen COVID-19 Vaccine to individuals 18 years of age and older who have access to or are not suitable for other COVID-19 vaccines, and who elect to receive the Janssen vaccine due to concerns about mRNA vaccines. This decision follows an updated analysis of reported cases of thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS), a rare but potentially life-threatening blood clotting condition. The FDA determined that the known and potential benefits of the vaccine outweigh the risks for these individuals. The revised authorized use of the vaccine includes a warning statement about the risk of TTS and updated information for healthcare providers and recipients.

title: FDA Permits Marketing for New Test to Improve Diagnosis of Alzheimer’s Disease
body_summary: The US FDA has permitted marketing for the first in vitro diagnostic test for early detection of amyloid plaques associated with Alzheimer's disease. The Lumipulse G β-Amyloid Ratio (1-42/1-40) test is intended for adult patients aged 55 and older with cognitive impairment. The test measures the ratio of β-amyloid 1-42 and 1-40 concentrations in human cerebral spinal fluid. A positive test result is consistent with the presence of amyloid plaques, while a negative result reduces the likelihood of Alzheimer's disease. The test is not a screening or stand-alone diagnostic assay. The FDA evaluated the test's safety and effectiveness in a clinical study of 292 CSF samples and granted Breakthrough Device designation. The test is now available for marketing to Fujirebio Diagnostics, Inc.

title: FDA Issues Warning Letters to Companies Illegally Selling CBD and Delta-8 THC Products
body_summary: The US FDA has issued warning letters to five companies for selling products labeled as containing delta-8 tetrahydrocannabinol (delta-8 THC) in ways that violate the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act). This is the first time the FDA has taken such action. Delta-8 THC has psychoactive and intoxicating effects and may be dangerous to consumers. The FDA has received reports of adverse events experienced by patients who have consumed these products. The agency is concerned about the growing popularity of delta-8 THC products being sold online and in stores nationwide, often with claims that they treat or alleviate the side effects of diseases or medical disorders. The FDA has not evaluated the effectiveness or safety of these products, and has issued warning letters to companies that have violated the FD&C Act, including those that have marketed CBD products as dietary supplements or added CBD to human and animal foods. The FDA has requested written responses from the companies within 15 working days stating how they will address these violations.

title: Memorandum on Promoting United States Leadership in Quantum Computing While Mitigating Risks to Vulnerable Cryptographic Systems
body_summary: The US government has outlined its policies and initiatives related to quantum computing through the National Security Memorandum 10. The policy aims to maintain the country's competitive advantage in quantum information science while mitigating the risks of quantum computers to national security. Key actions include maintaining US leadership in quantum computing, mitigating the threat of CRQCs through timely transition to quantum-resistant cryptography, and fostering the next generation of scientists and engineers. The US Secretary of Commerce will establish a project to work with the private sector on post-quantum cryptography, while the Secretary of Homeland Security will engage with critical infrastructure and SLTT partners. By December 31, 2022, federal agencies must develop comprehensive technology protection plans to safeguard quantum computing R&D, acquisition, and user access.

title: Implementation Note issued May 4, 2022
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on May 4, 2022: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 0.9 percent, effective May 5, 2022. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective May 5, 2022, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 3/4 to 1 percent. Conduct overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 1.0 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion; the aggregate operation limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 0.8 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities maturing in the calendar month of June that exceeds a monthly cap of $30 billion. Redeem Treasury coupon securities up to this monthly cap and Treasury bills to the extent that coupon principal payments are less than the monthly cap.
