Reinvest into agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) the amount of principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS received in the calendar month of June that exceeds a monthly cap of $17.5 billion. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve a 1/2 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate to 1 percent, effective May 5, 2022. In taking this action, the Board approved requests to establish that rate submitted by the Boards of Directors of the Federal Reserve Banks of Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Chicago, St. Louis, Minneapolis, Kansas City, Dallas, and San Francisco. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Although overall economic activity edged down in the first quarter, household spending and business fixed investment remained strong. Job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has declined substantially. Inflation remains elevated, reflecting supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic, higher energy prices, and broader price pressures. The invasion of Ukraine by Russia is causing tremendous human and economic hardship. The implications for the U.S. economy are highly uncertain. The invasion and related events are creating additional upward pressure on inflation and are likely to weigh on economic activity. In addition, COVID-related lockdowns in China are likely to exacerbate supply chain disruptions. The Committee is highly attentive to inflation risks. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. With appropriate firming in the stance of monetary policy, the Committee expects inflation to return to its 2 percent objective and the labor market to remain strong. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 3/4 to 1 percent and anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate. In addition, the Committee decided to begin reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities on June 1, as described in the Plans for Reducing the Size of the Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet that were issued in conjunction with this statement. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committeeâs goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; James Bullard; Esther L. George; Patrick Harker; Loretta J. Mester; and Christopher J. Waller. Patrick Harker voted as an alternate member at this meeting.

title: FDA Roundup: May 3, 2022
body_summary: The US FDA has proposed an order for Philips to repair, replace, or refund recalled CPAP, BiPAP, and ventilator devices manufactured after November 2015. The FDA also announced organizational changes within the Center for Devices and Radiological Health, including the creation of new offices and the realignment of work within the Office of Clinical Evidence and Analysis. Abbott Nutrition is allowed to release certain specialty and metabolic formulas on a case-by-case basis despite a voluntary recall and FDA warning about potential bacterial infection risks. The FDA warned about counterfeit at-home COVID-19 diagnostic tests being distributed or used in the US, which may lead to false results, spreading the virus, and delaying medical treatment. As of today, 433 tests and sample collection devices are authorized for use under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 298 molecular tests, 84 antibody tests, and 50 antigen tests.

title: FDA Roundup: April 29, 2022
body_summary: The FDA has announced several actions related to egg safety during HPAI outbreaks, including publishing a Q&A webpage and issuing draft guidance on the Accredited Third-Party Certification Program. The FDA also notified healthcare providers about Medtronic Heartware Ventricular Assist Devices, updated COVID-19 diagnostic test expiration dates, and approved an expanded indication for the TransMedics Organ Care System. Additionally, the FDA established action levels for lead in juice, authorized a shelf-life extension for Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine, and updated COVID-19 testing authorizations. Under emergency use authorizations, the FDA has approved 433 tests and sample collection devices, including 298 molecular tests, 84 antibody and other immune response tests, 50 antigen tests, and 1 diagnostic breath test.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Announces Tentative Advisory Committee Meeting Schedule Regarding COVID- 19 Vaccines
body_summary:
The FDA has revised the dates of its upcoming Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee meetings. The new meeting dates are as follows: 
June 14 for Moderna's EUA request for 6 years through 17 years of age 
June 15 for Moderna's EUA request for 6 months through 5 years of age and Pfizer-BioNTech's EUA request for 6 months through 4 years of age. The FDA plans to convene VRBPAC meetings on June 7 to discuss an EUA request for a COVID-19 vaccine by Novavax, and on June 28 to discuss whether the SARS-CoV-2 strain composition of COVID-19 vaccines should be modified.

title: FDA Proposes Rules Prohibiting Menthol Cigarettes and Flavored Cigars to Prevent Youth Initiation, Significantly Reduce Tobacco-Related Disease and Death
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is announcing proposed product standards to prohibit menthol as a characterizing flavor in cigarettes and all characterizing flavors (other than tobacco) in cigars. These proposed rules aim to significantly reduce disease and death from combusted tobacco product use, particularly among youth and young adults. The rules are based on clear science and evidence establishing the addictiveness and harm of these products. The proposed product standards have the potential to reduce youth experimentation and addiction, and increase the number of smokers that quit. The rules build on the Family Smoking Prevention and Tobacco Control Act, which prohibited all characterizing flavors (other than tobacco and menthol) in cigarettes in 2009. The proposed rules are part of the Administration's reignited Cancer Moonshot to reduce the death rate from cancer by at least 50 percent over the next 25 years.

title: FDA Takes Steps to Limit Lead in Juice to Further Reduce Exposure to Toxic Elements in Foods
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued draft action levels for lead in single-strength apple juice and other single-strength juices and juice blends. The action levels aim to reduce potential health effects from dietary exposure to lead. Draft action levels are recommended limits of lead in juice, with 10 parts per billion (ppb) for single-strength apple juice and 20 ppb for other single-strength juice types. The FDA estimates that establishing a 10 ppb action level for apple juice could result in a 46% reduction in exposure to lead in children. The agency is accepting comments on the draft guidance and will work with manufacturers to encourage the adoption of best practices to lower levels of lead in juice.

title: FDA Roundup: April 26, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of four new tobacco products through the Premarket Tobacco Product Application (PMTA) pathway. The FDA issued marketing granted orders to NJOY LLC for its Ace closed e-cigarette device and three tobacco-flavored e-liquid pods. In addition, the FDA announced the May and June dates for the Virtual Town Hall Series for Test Developers on Coronavirus (COVID-19) and authorized 431 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 296 molecular tests, 84 antibody and other immune response tests, and 50 antigen tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Approves First COVID-19 Treatment for Young Children
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) expanded the approval of the COVID-19 treatment Veklury (remdesivir) to include pediatric patients 28 days of age and older weighing at least 3 kilograms. The agency approved Veklury for patients hospitalized or not hospitalized with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 and at high risk for progression to severe COVID-19. This action makes Veklury the first approved COVID-19 treatment for children less than 12 years of age. The FDA revoked the emergency use authorization for Veklury previously covering this pediatric population. The agency's approval is supported by efficacy results from phase 3 clinical trials in adults and a phase 2/3 clinical study in pediatric patients. Possible side effects of Veklury include increased levels of liver enzymes and allergic reactions. The FDA approved Gilead Sciences Inc. for the treatment.

title: FDA Roundup: April 22, 2022
body_summary: The US FDA announced the availability of draft guidance on products labeled as dietary supplements containing N-acetyl-L-cysteine, which will explain the agency's intent to exercise enforcement discretion on certain NAC-containing products. On Tuesday, the FDA issued warning letters to Kleinhart, LLC for selling unapproved products with unproven COVID-19 claims. The FDA also warned patients and healthcare providers about the risk of false results with non-invasive prenatal screening (NIPS) tests, as well as COVID-19 testing updates, with 432 authorized tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs).

title: FDA Considers New Approach to Improve Safe Disposal of Prescription Opioid Analgesics, Decrease Unnecessary Exposure to Unused Medication
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is seeking public comment on a potential change requiring opioid analgesics used in outpatient settings to be dispensed with prepaid mail-back envelopes and pharmacists to provide patient education on safe disposal of opioids. This modification aims to provide a convenient disposal option for patients. FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf stated that the mail-back envelope requirement would complement current disposal programs and provide meaningful steps to improve safe use and disposal. Patients commonly report having unused opioid analgesics, and educating them about disposal options can increase disposal rates. Mail-back envelopes have favorable characteristics, such as not requiring patients to mix medications with substances or chemicals. The FDA is accepting public comments until June 21, 2022.

title: FDA Warns of Risks Associated with Non-Invasive Prenatal Screening Tests
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration is warning the public about the risks of false results, inappropriate use, and inappropriate interpretation of non-invasive prenatal screening (NIPS) tests. NIPS tests, also known as cell-free DNA tests or NIPT, look for signs of genetic abnormalities in a fetus by testing a sample of blood from the pregnant person. Director Jeff Shuren, M.D., J.D., stated that these tests have not been reviewed by the FDA and may be making claims about their performance that are not based on sound science.

NIPS tests can provide information about the possibility of a child being born with a serious health condition, but they are screening tests, not diagnostic tests. They only provide information about the risk that a fetus may have a genetic abnormality, and additional testing may be needed to confirm whether or not a fetus is affected.

The FDA recommends that patients and health care providers discuss the benefits and risks of all prenatal genetic testing, including NIPS tests, with a genetic counselor or other health care provider before considering such testing or making any decisions about their pregnancy.

title: FDA Roundup: April 19, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration issued a final rule amending the allowable level for fluoride in bottled water to 0.7 milligrams per liter (mg/L). The FDA also announced a draft revision of a guidance on the use of published literature in animal drug approvals, open for public comment on April 20. The FDA released the NARMS Integrated Summary 2019, a national public health surveillance system that monitors antimicrobial resistance data. On Monday, the FDA released a Constituent Update on research linked to E. coli outbreaks in bagged romaine lettuce. As of today, 431 emergency use authorizations (EUAs) for COVID-19 testing are authorized, including molecular tests, antibody tests, antigen tests, and diagnostic breath tests.

title: FDA Takes New Steps Regarding Evaluating Public Health Importance of Additional Food Allergens
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a draft guidance on evaluating the public health importance of food allergens not listed as major allergens in the U.S. The major food allergens currently identified are milk, eggs, fish, crustacean shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, and soybeans, but more than 160 foods cause food allergic reactions. The guidance focuses on immunoglobulin E antibody-mediated food allergies, which can trigger severe reactions. The FDA aims to evaluate the public health importance of non-listed food allergens, including those with low prevalence rates. The guidance outlines the approach the FDA will take, including considering evidence of causation, prevalence, and severity. The agency is seeking comments on the draft guidance, which can be submitted at www.regulations.gov until 120 days after publication in the Federal Register.

title: FDA Roundup: April 15, 2022
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) to InspectIR Systems for theirInspectIR COVID-19 Breathalyzer test on April 14. The test detects chemical compounds in breath samples associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection. The authorization allows the test to be performed in environments where the patient specimen is collected and analyzed, using an instrument about the size of a carry-on luggage, and provides results in less than three minutes.

Additionally, the FDA announced that new legislation clarifying the agency's ability to regulate tobacco products containing nicotine will take effect on April 14, 2022. 

The FDA also issued a statement about the shelf-life of bamlanivimab and/or etesevimab, recommending that all unopened vials of these medications be retained until the shelf-life extension evaluation is complete.

The agency authorized a shelf-life extension for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine, supplied in multiple dose vials, to be stored in an ultra-low temperature freezer for up to 12 months.

As of April 14, 431 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 297 molecular tests and 50 antigen tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes First COVID-19 Diagnostic Test Using Breath Samples
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the first COVID-19 diagnostic test that detects chemical compounds in breath samples associated with a SARS-CoV-2 infection. The test, called the InspectIR COVID-19 Breathalyzer, can be performed in various environments and provides results in under three minutes. The test was validated in a study of 2,409 individuals, showing 91.2% sensitivity and 99.3% specificity. The test uses gas chromatography gas mass-spectrometry to detect five Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection. The FDA Director, Jeff Shuren, stated that the test is an example of rapid innovation in COVID-19 diagnostic tests. The InspectIR COVID-19 Breathalyzer will be produced at a rate of approximately 100 instruments per week, increasing testing capacity by approximately 64,000 samples per month.

title: FDA Takes Important Steps to Increase Racial and Ethnic Diversity in Clinical Trials
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a new draft guidance for industry to develop plans to enroll more participants from underrepresented racial and ethnic populations in clinical trials. The guidance aims to expand on previous guidances to improve clinical trial diversity. FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf stated that ensuring meaningful representation of racial and ethnic minorities in clinical trials is fundamental to public health. The guidance recommends that sponsors develop a Race and Ethnicity Diversity Plan early in clinical development. Barriers to participation include mistrust, inadequate recruitment and retention efforts, language and cultural differences, health literacy, and limited access to healthcare. The FDA will continue to engage with federal partners, medical product manufacturers, and healthcare professionals to increase enrollment of diverse populations.

title: FDA Issues Final Guidance on Animal Drug Compounding from Bulk Drug Substances
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a final guidance, "Compounding Animal Drugs from Bulk Drug Substances," to protect animal health by recognizing the need for access to certain compounded animal drugs. The guidance aims to balance access to these drugs with ensuring their safety and quality. The FDA recognizes the need for veterinarians to have access to compounded animal drugs that aren't available as approved products, and the guidance outlines flexibilities for pharmacists and veterinarians to compound animal drugs from bulk drug substances. The agency will prioritize enforcement actions on products that pose the greatest risk to human and animal health, and will provide education and outreach to stakeholders during implementation. The guidance affects over 1,600 FDA-approved animal drugs and approximately 20,000 FDA-approved human drugs that could be prescribed for animal use.

title: FDA and DEA Warn Online Pharmacies Illegally Selling Adderall to Consumers
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) have issued joint warning letters to operators of two websites that illegally sell Schedule II stimulants, including amphetamine drug products marketed as Adderall, without a prescription. The FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf stated that the joint action demonstrates the federal government's commitment to reducing the public health danger posed by drugs sold online. The warning letters warn consumers to dispose of unused medicine from these websites and not purchase or use prescription drugs without a prescription. The FDA urges consumers to obtain prescription drugs from state-licensed US pharmacies or physicians in the US, where the quality of drug manufacturing, packaging, distribution, and labeling can be assured. The DEA Administrator Anne Milgram warned that consumers cannot trust the safety or legitimacy of pills sold on unaccredited sites, and strongly urges anyone seeking controlled medications to obtain a prescription from a trusted medical professional and have it dispensed by a licensed pharmacy.

title: Joint Statement from CMS Administrator Chiquita Brooks-LaSure and FDA Commissioner Robert M. Califf, M.D., on Ensuring Access to Safe and Effective Treatments
body_summary: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) share a priority to ensure innovative interventions for people. Both agencies recognize the importance of reliable data to make effective treatments available to patients. The FDA's approval process is based on a careful evaluation of data, determining the product's safety and effectiveness. CMS conducts its own review to determine if an item or service should be covered nationally by Medicare, including assessing its reasonableness and necessity for the Medicare population. The agencies work together to advance the development and availability of innovative medical products, with a shared goal of caring for the people they serve.

title: FDA Roundup: April 8, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized several COVID-19-related products and issued guidance on cybersecurity in medical devices. On April 7, the FDA extended the shelf life of the Janssen COVID-19 Vaccine to 11 months, allowing storage at 2-8 degrees Celsius. The agency also authorized two over-the-counter (OTC) at-home COVID-19 antigen tests that show results in 15 minutes. These tests can be used by people aged 14 and older, or 2 and older with adult assistance. The FDA has authorized 428 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 294 molecular tests, 84 antibody tests, and 50 antigen tests.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on March 15-16, 2022, reviewing global financial market developments following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The committee discussed reducing policy accommodation due to elevated inflation, leading to a review of its balance sheet runoff and considering agency MBS sales. Global financial conditions tightened due to equity price declines, increased sovereign yields and credit spreads, and an appreciated US dollar. The Committee decided not to make any decisions regarding the plan but made substantial progress on it. The staff's economic outlook projected slower real GDP growth in 2022 before picking up slightly in 2023, with inflation expected to remain elevated due to supply and demand imbalances, higher energy prices, and broader price pressures. The Federal Open Market Committee raised the target range for the federal funds rate to 1/4 to 1/2 percent and anticipated ongoing increases, voting members including Jerome H. Powell, John C. Williams, Michelle W. Bowman, Lael Brainard, Esther L. George, Patrick Harker, Loretta J. Mester, and Christopher J. Waller, with James Bullard voting against.

title: Executive Order 14070—Continuing To Strengthen Americans' Access to Affordable, Quality Health Coverage
body_summary: The President of the United States has issued an executive order to protect and strengthen Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act (ACA). The policy, signed on January 28, 2021, aims to make high-quality healthcare accessible and affordable for every American. Agencies have taken numerous actions, including expanding Medicaid in Missouri and Oklahoma, extending Medicaid eligibility to pregnant individuals, and operating a Special Enrollment Period that allowed 2.8 million Americans to enroll in coverage under the ACA. The President has also signed the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, which further strengthens Medicaid and the ACA, making ACA coverage more affordable for 9 million Americans. Despite progress, nearly 4 million Americans remain locked out of Medicaid expansion, and millions struggle to obtain necessary care.

title: FDA Roundup: April 5, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration announced that sotrovimab is no longer authorized to treat COVID-19 in any US region due to increases in cases caused by the Omicron BA.2 sub-variant, with more than 50% of cases attributed to this variant. The FDA issued a Safety Communication supporting the transition to fully disposable duodenoscopes and provided results from postmarket surveillance studies showing high concern organisms in 6.6% of samples tested after contamination. A public health alert was issued to avoid potentially contaminated raw oysters from Canada, linked to an orovirus outbreak. The FDA also updated reprocessing instructions for certain urological endoscopes manufactured by Karl Storz and authorized tests and sample collection devices for COVID-19 testing, including 425 authorized EUAs.

title: FDA Roundup: April 1, 2022
body_summary: The FDA issued updates on the COVID-19 pandemic, revised guidance for emergency use authorization for vaccines, and approved new products like Zenalpha. The FDA also addressed citizen petitions and extended the public comment period for a public hearing on scientific data for a new animal drug. On March 29, the FDA authorized medical devices and tests, including Agili-C for cartilage defects, the BrainTemp Neonate System for measuring neonate brain temperature, and Evusheld with updated dosing information. Additionally, the FDA granted emergency use authorizations for 425 tests and sample collection devices, including molecular, antibody, and antigen tests.

title: FDA Roundup: March 29, 2022
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has authorized a manufacturing change for the Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine to include an additional presentation for booster vaccination doses only. The new presentation is in multiple dose vials with dark blue caps and labels with a purple border. The Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine is now authorized for individuals 18 years and older in two presentations: multiple dose vials with red caps and light blue labels for primary vaccination and booster vaccination, and multiple dose vials with dark blue caps and purple labels for booster vaccination only.

The FDA has also issued warning letters to two companies, Iodine Products Inc and Applied Biological Laboratories Inc, for selling unapproved products with unproven COVID-19 claims. Additionally, the agency has added information about leveraging validation data from a study on pediatric self-swabbing for COVID-19 diagnostic testing.

A federal judge has entered a consent decree of permanent injunction against Bravo Packing, Inc, prohibiting the company from selling, manufacturing and distributing adulterated pet food until they take corrective measures. The FDA has also warned seven companies for selling CBD products using research studies to claim or imply misleadingly that their products will cure, mitigate, treat or prevent COVID-19.

As of today, 425 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 293 molecular tests, 84 antibody and other immune response tests, and 48 antigen tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Second Booster Dose of Two COVID-19 Vaccines for Older and Immunocompromised Individuals
body_summary: The US FDA has authorized a second booster dose of Pfizer-BioNTech or Moderna COVID-19 vaccines for individuals 50 years and older, as well as certain immunocompromised individuals, at least 4 months after their first booster dose. Emerging evidence suggests a second booster dose improves protection against severe COVID-19 and is not associated with new safety concerns. The FDA amended the emergency use authorizations to allow a second booster dose for individuals 12 years and older with immunocompromise, and 18 years and older with certain immunocompromise conditions. The agency evaluated data from Israel, the US, and other sources, including a study of healthcare workers, which showed increases in neutralizing antibody levels against SARS-CoV-2 virus after a second booster dose.

title: Federal judge enters consent decree against New Jersey raw animal food manufacturer
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced that Bravo Packing, Inc., an animal food manufacturing company, has agreed to stop selling, manufacturing, and distributing raw pet food. The FDA has entered a consent decree of permanent injunction against the company for violating public safety standards under the Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA). The decree requires the company to complete corrective actions and prohibits them from receiving, preparing, processing, packing, holding, labeling, and/or distributing pet food unless they comply. The FDA had previously issued warning letters and conducted inspections in 2019 and 2021, finding significant food safety violations, including grossly insanitary conditions and contamination with Salmonella and Listeria monocytogenes. The decree also allows the FDA to order a shutdown, recall, or other corrective action in the event of future violations.

title: FDA Roundup: March 25, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is issuing a 30-day procedural notice on planned preliminary quantitative consumer research on voluntary symbols for the "healthy" nutrient content claim. The notice responds to comments received on a 60-day procedural notice issued in May 2021. Sotrovimab, a COVID-19 treatment, is no longer authorized for use in HHS Regions 1 and 2 due to the high frequency of the Omicron BA.2 sub-variant. The FDA has also published "Improving Nutrition to Turn the Tide on Diet-Related Chronic Disease" by Susan Mayne, Ph.D. As of today, 425 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 293 molecular tests, 84 antibody tests, and 48 antigen tests.

title: FDA Issues Decisions on Additional E-Cigarette Products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized several tobacco-flavored electronic nicotine delivery system (ENDS) products from Logic Technology Development LLC under the Logic Vapeleaf, Logic Power, and Logic Pro brands, including devices. The agency's review concluded that the likely benefit for adult smokers who significantly reduce their cigarette use outweighs the risk to youth, provided that the company follows postmarketing requirements to reduce youth access and exposure. These products are not safe and do not imply FDA approval. The agency has issued marketing denial orders to Logic for multiple other ENDS products, and applications for Logic's additional products, including menthol, remain under review. The FDA has taken action on approximately 99% of the nearly 6.7 million ENDS products submitted for premarket authorization. Commissioner Robert M. Califf and director Mitch Zeller have emphasized the agency's commitment to reducing tobacco-related disease and death, particularly among youth. The authorization imposes strict marketing restrictions, including restrictions on youth exposure to tobacco advertising, and the FDA will closely monitor compliance.

title: Statement on the 12th Anniversary of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: The main action is that the author's administration has protected and built on the Affordable Care Act (ACA), also known as Obamacare. The author stood beside President Barack Obama when he signed the law into effect 12 years ago, and the administration has since taken steps to lower health care costs and make coverage more accessible. The ACA has delivered quality, affordable health coverage to over 30 million Americans, including protections for preexisting conditions, reduced prescription drug costs for seniors, and increased enrollment to a record high of 14.5 million Americans. Despite Republican efforts to repeal the ACA, the author's administration will continue to protect and build on its landmark achievements.

title: FDA Statement on Medical Device User Fee Amendments (MDUFA)
body_summary: The FDA and medical device industry representatives have reached an agreement on proposed recommendations for the fifth reauthorization of the medical device user fee program. Under the agreement, the FDA would collect at least $1.78 billion in user fees over five years, with a total potential funding of up to $1.9 billion, if specified goals are met. The proposed recommendations have been posted on the FDA's website and will be published in the Federal Register for public comment. A virtual public meeting will be held on April 19, 2022, to provide public input on the proposed recommendations. The final recommendations are scheduled to be delivered to Congress in April 2022, after public input is considered and the recommendations are revised as necessary.

title: FDA Roundup: March 22, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has published an at-a-glance summary of news from around the agency. On March 22, the FDA clarified that the effectiveness of certain provisions of the yogurt standard of identity final rule have been stayed. The FDA has also added prefilled 0.9% sodium chloride IV lock/flush syringes to the device shortage list and the device discontinuance list. On March 21, the FDA issued a recall notice for Philips Respironics ventilators due to expired adhesive parts. The FDA released a new online Agricultural Water Assessment Builder to help farms understand the proposed requirements for an agricultural water assessment. The FDA also released a new quarterly podcast series, TechTalk, and approved Ztalmy (ganaxolone) to treat seizures associated with cyclin-dependent kinase-like 5 deficiency disorder. As of today, 425 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs).

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA to Hold Advisory Committee Meeting on COVID-19 Vaccines to Discuss Future Boosters
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is hosting a virtual meeting of its Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee (VRBPAC) on April 6 to discuss COVID-19 vaccine booster doses and addressing current and emerging variants. Representatives from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the National Institutes of Health will participate. Peter Marks, director of the FDA's Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, stated that preparing for future COVID-19 needs requires vaccines as the best defense against the disease. The April 6 meeting aims to inform the agency's regulatory strategy for addressing COVID-19 and virus variants.

title: FDA Roundup: March 18, 2022
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has issued several updates regarding COVID-19 testing and safety. On March 18, the FDA added frequently asked questions to its COVID-19 Test FAQs, warning people about the potential for harm if FDA-authorized at-home COVID-19 tests are not used according to the manufacturer's instructions. The FDA is also reminding people to keep the tests out of reach from children and pets.

The agency has received reports of injuries caused by incorrect test use, such as people putting test chemicals in their eyes or swallowing test solution. The FDA has issued safety communications and warning letters to several websites and companies selling unapproved products with unproven COVID-19 claims.

As of March 16, the FDA has authorized 422 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 290 molecular tests, 84 antibody and other immune response tests, and 48 antigen tests. The agency has also authorized 882 revisions to EUA authorizations.

title: FDA, Reagan-Udall Foundation to Hold Important Public Workshop to Discuss Naloxone Access
body_summary: The US FDA will host a virtual public workshop on March 29 to discuss access to naloxone, a drug used to reverse opioid overdoses. The workshop is a collaboration with the Reagan-Udall Foundation for the FDA. Director Patrizia Cavazzoni stated that making naloxone more accessible is a crucial part of combating opioid-related overdose. The workshop aims to review naloxone availability, address perceived barriers, and explore innovative approaches to place naloxone in the hands of those who need it most. The FDA has taken several steps to support naloxone availability, including encouraging over-the-counter products and adding recommendations to opioid medication prescribing information.

title: Implementation Note issued March 16, 2022
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on March 16, 2022: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to raise the interest rate paid on reserve balances to 0.4 percent, effective March 17, 2022. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective March 17, 2022, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 1/4 to 1/2 percent. Conduct overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 0.5 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion; the aggregate operation limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 0.3 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities and reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) in agency MBS. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve a 1/4 percentage point increase in the primary credit rate to 0.5 percent, effective March 17, 2022. In taking this action, the Board approved requests to establish that rate submitted by the Boards of Directors of the Federal Reserve Banks of Boston, Philadelphia, Cleveland, Richmond, Atlanta, Chicago, St. Louis, Minneapolis, Kansas City, and San Francisco. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Indicators of economic activity and employment have continued to strengthen. Job gains have been strong in recent months, and the unemployment rate has declined substantially. Inflation remains elevated, reflecting supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic, higher energy prices, and broader price pressures. The invasion of Ukraine by Russia is causing tremendous human and economic hardship. The implications for the U.S. economy are highly uncertain, but in the near term the invasion and related events are likely to create additional upward pressure on inflation and weigh on economic activity. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. With appropriate firming in the stance of monetary policy, the Committee expects inflation to return to its 2 percent objective and the labor market to remain strong. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1/4 to 1/2 percent and anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate. In addition, the Committee expects to begin reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities at a coming meeting. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Esther L. George; Patrick Harker; Loretta J. Mester; and Christopher J. Waller. Voting against this action was James Bullard, who preferred at this meeting to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 0.5 percentage point to 1/2 to 3/4 percent. Patrick Harker voted as an alternate member at this meeting.

title: FDA Roundup: March 15, 2022
body_summary: The FDA is announcing the availability of two draft guidance documents. The first draft guidance, "Human Gene Therapy Products Incorporating Human Genome Editing," provides recommendations for sponsors developing human gene therapy products, including product design, product manufacturing, and clinical trial design. The second draft guidance, "Considerations for the Development of Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T Cell Products," provides CAR T cell-specific recommendations regarding chemistry, manufacturing, and control, pharmacology and toxicology, and clinical study design. The FDA has reopened the comment period for the draft Compliance Policy Guide (CPG) entitled "Compliance Policy Guide Sec. 540.525 Scombrotoxin (Histamine)-forming Fish and Fishery Products – Decomposition and Histamine." The FDA has also updated its frequently asked questions about the Philips Respironics CPAP, BiPAP, and ventilator recall. Additionally, the FDA has provided updates on Essure, a permanently implanted birth control device, and warned consumers against using the Renuvion/J-Plasma device for certain aesthetic procedures. The FDA has authorized 422 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody tests, and antigen tests.

title: FDA Approves First Generic of Symbicort to Treat Asthma and COPD
body_summary: The US FDA approved the first generic version of Symbicort (budesonide and formoterol fumarate dihydrate) Inhalation Aerosol for treating asthma in patients six years old and older, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in patients with chronic bronchitis and/or emphysema. The generic product is a metered-dose inhaler containing both budesonide and formoterol, and is approved for two strengths. The FDA's director, Sally Choe, stated that the approval is part of the agency's efforts to increase competition and access to quality medicines. The approval is the first of its kind for a complex drug-device combination product, and reflects the FDA's commitment to bringing generic copies of complex drugs to the market. The generic version is now available from Mylan Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

title: FDA Roundup: March 11, 2022
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued an Enforcement Policy Regarding Certain Provisions Guidance for Industry, outlining specific enforcement discretion policies for provisions in the Current Good Manufacturing Practice and Hazard Analysis and Risk-Based Preventive Controls for Human Food and Animal Food, Foreign Supplier Verification Program, Produce Safety, and Intentional Adulteration regulations. 

The FDA also issued a warning letter to Viraldine, LLC on March 7, for selling unapproved products with fraudulent COVID-19 claims. On March 4, the FDA authorized an extension for the shelf life of the refrigerated Janssen COVID-19 Vaccine from six to nine months, allowing the product to be stored at 2-8 degrees Celsius. 

As of today, 421 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 291 molecular tests and sample collection devices, 85 antibody and other immune response tests, and 45 antigen tests. The FDA has authorized 25 antigen tests and 9 molecular tests for serial screening programs.

title: FDA Orders Philips Respironics to Notify Patients Regarding the Recall of Certain Breathing Assistance Machines
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued an order to Philips Respironics requiring the company to notify patients and others about the June 14, 2021, recall of certain ventilators, CPAP, and BiPAP machines due to the unreasonable risk of substantial harm to public health posed by the degradation of PE-PUR sound abatement foam. The FDA has determined the order is necessary due to inadequate notification efforts by Philips. The order mandates Philips to improve communication about the recall and the risk posed by the foam with patients and the public. Philips must notify all device users, suppliers, distributors, retailers, and healthcare providers within 45 days and provide monthly updates to registered device users on the Philips website.

title: FDA Roundup: March 8, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced several key developments. The FDA has signed a domestic mutual reliance partnership agreement with the Minnesota Department of Agriculture, focusing on establishing key metrics, data sharing, and inventory reconciliation. On March 7, a consent decree was signed requiring Salud Natural Entrepreneur, Inc. of Illinois to complete corrective actions to ensure compliance with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. The FDA has also announced a low-risk determination for the marketing of genome-edited beef cattle and their offspring, and authorized over 420 emergency use authorizations (EUAs) for COVID-19 testing, including molecular and antigen tests, as well as sample collection devices.

title: FDA Makes Low-Risk Determination for Marketing of Products from Genome-Edited Beef Cattle After Safety Review
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has made a low-risk determination for the marketing of products, including food, from two genome-edited beef cattle and their offspring. The intentional genomic alteration (IGA) does not raise any safety concerns. The IGA results in the equivalent genotype and short-hair coat trait seen in conventionally bred cattle. This is the FDA's first low-risk determination for enforcement discretion for an IGA in an animal for food use. The product developer plans to use the genetic products from these two animals with select customers in the global market soon, with meat products expected to be available for purchase by general consumers as early as two years.

title: FDA Roundup: March 4, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has published news updates. CDER approved four new drugs for rare diseases in oncology and hematology in the first two months of 2022. In 2022, 26 of CDER's 50 novel drug approvals were for orphan diseases. A multi-agency collaboration, including NASA, NIH, HHS BARDA, and FDA, announced an award to extend the viability of complex human models for at least six months. The FDA authorized 419 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 290 molecular tests, 85 antibody tests, and 44 antigen tests.

title: FDA Urges Companies to be ’Recall Ready’ to Protect Public Health as Part of Final Guidance for Voluntary Recalls
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration finalized guidance to help companies prepare to quickly and effectively remove violative products from the market. The guidance describes steps companies should take to develop recall policies and procedures, including training, planning, and record-keeping. Associate Commissioner of Regulatory Affairs Judith McMeekin stated that voluntary recalls are the fastest and most effective way to correct or remove violative products, with the aim of protecting public health and the integrity of the supply chain. The final guidance explains how companies should maintain distribution records and use electronic communications to facilitate faster recall actions. The FDA recommends that companies develop recall procedures to quickly inform their entire distribution chain, and will continue to work with companies to improve their recall procedures.

title: Memorandum on Maximizing Assistance To Respond to COVID-19
body_summary:
The President of the United States orders the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency to maximize assistance to respond to the COVID-19 pandemic. The policy aims to protect and support families, schools, and businesses, and assist State, local, Tribal, and territorial governments.

FEMA will provide a 100 percent Federal cost share for work eligible for assistance under Public Assistance Category B, including work described in a Presidential Memorandum dated January 21, 2021. The assistance is for projects performed from January 20, 2020, through July 1, 2022. The memorandum is implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.

title: FDA Roundup: March 1, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration issued safety communications warning people not to use certain COVID-19 tests, including the Celltrion DiaTrust COVID-19 Ag Rapid Test and the SD Biosensor STANDARD Q COVID-19 Ag Home Test, due to the risk of false results. The FDA also posted a Consumer Update regarding an infant formula recall and announced the availability of a resource on the responsible use of anthelmintic chemicals to control anthelmintic resistance in grazing livestock species. As of today, 420 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 290 molecular tests and 85 antibody tests.

title: FDA Clinical Trial Guidances Share Biden Administration’s Goals for Advancing Development of Cancer Treatments
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued three final guidances on cancer clinical trials, aligning with President Biden's 2016 Cancer Moonshot initiative. The goal is to reduce cancer death rates by 50% over the next 25 years and improve patient care. The guidances include:

Inclusion of Older Adults in Cancer Clinical Trials: recommends enrolling older adults (65+) in early phase studies and including discrete age groups to encourage enrollment.

Expansion Cohorts: Use in First-in-Human Clinical Trials to Expedite Development of Oncology Drugs and Biologics: provides advice on designing trials with multiple expansion cohorts to assess safety, pharmacokinetics, and anti-tumor activity.

Master Protocols: Efficient Clinical Trial Design Strategies to Expedite Development of Oncology Drugs and Biologics: addresses master protocol design, including information on trial design approaches and interactions with the FDA.

These guidances aim to address inequities, target the right treatments to the right patients, and expedite progress against deadly and rare cancers. The FDA's Director for the Oncology Center for Excellence, Richard Pazdur, stated that these principles align with the Cancer Moonshot's mission.

title: FDA Roundup: February 25, 2022
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued updates on various news and actions from the agency. On February 24, the FDA made new PFAS test results available, showing detectable levels in three food samples, but no scientific evidence to avoid these foods. The FDA also posted updates on PFAS in food contact applications and revised the emergency use authorization for Evusheld (tixagevimab co-packaged with cilgavimab) due to reduced effectiveness against certain Omicron subvariants.

Additionally, the FDA updated information on COVID-19 antibody testing and added new question and answer resources. A proposed rule to harmonize the Quality System regulation with the international ISO 13485:2016 standard is also available for public comments.

The FDA approved the first generic of Farxiga (dapagliflozin) tablets, used to treat type 2 diabetes, and issued a warning letter to My Natural Treatment for selling unapproved products with fraudulent COVID-19 claims. As of February 24, 419 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody tests, and antigen tests.

title: FDA Approves Treatment for Wider Range of Patients with Heart Failure
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Jardiance (empagliflozin) to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in adults. Jardiance was originally approved in 2014 for type 2 diabetes patients, but now also approved for patients with heart failure and established cardiovascular disease. The approval is based on a randomized, double-blind, international trial involving 2,997 participants who received Jardiance or a placebo. In this trial, Jardiance was shown to reduce the risk of death from cardiovascular causes or hospitalization for heart failure by 14%, mainly due to fewer hospitalizations for heart failure. The FDA also noted that side effects were generally consistent with diabetes patients.

title: FDA Permits Marketing of First Condom Specifically Indicated for Anal Intercourse
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of the first condoms specifically indicated to reduce transmission of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) during anal intercourse. The One Male Condom, developed by Global Protection Corp., is a natural rubber latex sheath that covers the penis and has three versions: standard, thin, and fitted. The fitted condoms have a paper template to aid in finding the best size for each user. The FDA's De Novo authorization allows for faster market access and enables subsequent devices of the same type to be cleared through the 510(k) pathway. The safety and efficacy of the One Male Condom were studied in a clinical trial involving 504 men, which found a total condom failure rate of 0.68% for anal intercourse and 1.89% for vaginal intercourse. The study also reported a 1.92% overall adverse event rate, with most adverse events related to STIs, discomfort, or lubricant use.

title: FDA Roundup: February 22, 2022
body_summary: The US FDA has posted a new resource, At-Home COVID-19 Diagnostic Tests, listing all FDA-authorized at-home over-the-counter tests. The agency has also expanded an FDA approval for a cardiac cryoablation catheter to include children aged 2 and older, and issued alerts for several FDA-regulated products purchased from Family Dollar stores in Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Missouri, and Tennessee due to insanitary conditions. On February 15, the FDA issued warning letters to two websites for marketing unapproved and misbranded drugs, including COVID-19. The agency has authorized 420 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 290 molecular tests, 85 antibody tests, and 45 antigen tests.

title: FDA Alerts the Public to Potentially Contaminated Products from Family Dollar Stores in Six States
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is alerting the public that FDA-regulated products from Family Dollar stores in Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Missouri, and Tennessee, purchased between Jan. 1, 2021, and the present, may be unsafe due to insanitary conditions at the company's West Memphis, Arkansas distribution facility. The FDA inspected the facility in January 2022 and found rodent infestation, insanitary conditions, and products stored without protection against contamination. The agency is working with the company to initiate a voluntary recall of affected products. Consumers are advised not to use and to contact the company regarding impacted products, and to discard all drugs, medical devices, cosmetics, and dietary supplements, regardless of packaging.

title: FDA Roundup: February 18, 2022
body_summary: The FDA has found four additional lots of AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine drug substance manufactured at the Emergent facility in Baltimore, Maryland, to be acceptable for export. These lots may now be exported for use. The agency conducted a thorough review of facility records and quality testing results, taking into consideration the current worldwide COVID-19 public health emergency. The FDA previously warned consumers not to use certain powdered infant formula produced in Abbott Nutrition's facility in Sturgis, Michigan, due to Cronobacter sakazakii and Salmonella Newport infections. The agency has initiated a voluntary recall of the potentially affected product, including Similac, Alimentum, and EleCare powdered formulas. The FDA also published 43 new product-specific guidances to support generic drug product development, including recommendations for COVID-19 testing updates.

title: FDA Warns Consumers Not to Use Certain Powdered Infant Formula Produced in Abbott Nutrition’s Facility in Sturgis, Michigan
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is investigating consumer complaints of Cronobacter sakazakii and Salmonella Newport infections related to powdered infant formula produced at Abbott Nutrition's Sturgis, Michigan facility. Four reports of Cronobacter sakazakii infections and one complaint of a Salmonella Newport infection have been received, resulting in hospitalization and potential death in two cases. The FDA has initiated a voluntary recall of Similac PM 60/40 powdered infant formula with the lot code 27032K800. This recall affects specialty formula for certain infants who would benefit from lowered mineral intake. The recall includes products manufactured at the Sturgis facility and was likely exported to other countries. Parents and caregivers are advised to check their product lot code on the company's website to see if it is part of the recall.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; and James A. Clouse, Secretary, were selected for the Federal Open Market Committee. The committee reaffirmed Authorization for Domestic Open Market Operations and Foreign Currency Operations. The FOMC authorizes purchases and sales of foreign currencies, including swap transactions with US Treasury, foreign monetary authorities, and other entities. The Committee will commence a formal framework review in 2024, concluding in 2025. Private employment gains slowed, while average hourly earnings rose at an annual rate of 6.2%. Inflation remained high, with total PCE price inflation at 5.7% and core PCE inflation at 4.7%. The economy's path depends on the virus' course. Participants expect continued gains in economic activity and employment with reduced inflation.

title: FDA Roundup: February 15, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration released a request for public comments on antimicrobial use in companion animals and its potential impact on antimicrobial resistance. The FDA intends to use the information collected to promote antimicrobial stewardship in companion animals. The agency also published updates on interim results from two postmarket studies on Essure, a permanently implanted birth control device for women, and provided warnings to unapproved online pharmacies that sell unregulated medicines, including COVID-19 treatments. As of today, the FDA has authorized 421 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 291 molecular tests and 85 antibody and other immune response tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes New Monoclonal Antibody for Treatment of COVID-19 that Retains Activity Against Omicron Variant
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for bebtelovimab, a monoclonal antibody, to treat mild to moderate COVID-19 in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older weighing at least 40 kilograms. The EUA is for high-risk patients who are at risk of progression to severe COVID-19, including hospitalization or death, and for whom alternative treatment options are not accessible or clinically appropriate. The authorization is based on clinical and nonclinical data, including a phase 2 clinical trial that showed bebtelovimab reduced time to sustained symptom resolution and viral load. The FDA has carefully monitored circulating viral variants and found that bebtelovimab retains activity against the omicron variant and its subvariant BA.2. Possible side effects include itching, rash, infusion-related reactions, nausea, and vomiting.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Postpones Advisory Committee Meeting to Discuss Request for Authorization of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine for Children 6 Months Through 4 Years of Age
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has been notified by Pfizer of new data regarding its emergency use authorization request for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine in children 6 months through 4 years of age. Due to the recent omicron surge and high hospitalizations in this age group, the agency is postponing a meeting to consider additional data on a third dose. The decision is made to allow more time to evaluate the new data, ensuring the data supports effectiveness and safety before authorization. The agency will provide an update on timing once they receive additional data and have completed an updated evaluation.

title: FDA Takes Steps Aimed at Fostering Development of Non-Addictive Alternatives to Opioids for Acute Pain Management
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued draft guidance to support the development of non-addictive alternatives to opioids for managing acute pain lasting up to 30 days. The guidance aims to foster the development of non-opioid analgesics to reduce opioid exposure and prevent new addiction. This initiative aligns with the HHS Overdose Prevention Strategy, focusing on four priority areas. The guidance is intended to help companies develop non-opioid analgesics for acute pain, with the ultimate goal of providing improved treatment alternatives to alleviate patient suffering and mitigate the risks associated with opioid use. The guidance is part of the Substance Use-Disorder Prevention that Promotes Opioid Recovery and Treatment for Patients and Communities Act, and the FDA is accepting public comments until April 11, 2022.

title: FDA Roundup: February 8, 2022
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is warning healthcare providers, parents, and caregivers of pediatric patients about a risk of strangulation from using certain enteral feeding delivery sets. The FDA has received reports of two toddler deaths due to this risk. The agency has announced a virtual workshop on March 23-24 to develop multi-component biomarker concepts and terminology.

The FDA has issued guidance discouraging the development or use of sanitation tunnels that spray humans with disinfectant, due to concerns over COVID-19 prevention and treatment. The agency has also warned people not to use the E25Bio COVID-19 Direct Antigen Rapid Test (DART) due to concerns over false labeling and potential injury from improper use.

As of today, 421 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA for COVID-19 testing, including 291 molecular tests, 85 antibody tests, and 45 antigen tests. The agency has authorized 812 revisions to emergency use authorizations, and 26 antigen tests and nine molecular tests for serial screening programs.

title: FDA Roundup: February 4, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a revised draft guidance for industry on assessing pressor effects of drugs, advising sponsors on premarketing assessment of a drug's effect on blood pressure. The FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health has announced its 2022-2025 Strategic Priorities, focusing on three priority areas. The center established clear goals and measures of success for its device program and strategic priorities. The FDA has also proposed a rule on National Standards for the Licensure of Wholesale Drug Distributors and Third-Party Logistics Providers to improve the security of the drug supply chain. A new website was launched by the Center for Veterinary Medicine's Office of Research to showcase its innovative research on protecting human and animal health. The FDA has resumed conducting domestic surveillance inspections, starting February 7, and will continue to conduct foreign and domestic mission-critical inspections. As of February 2, 421 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations.

title: FDA Sodium Reduction Efforts Underscored in USDA’s Transitional Nutrition Standards for School Meals
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a final rule on transitional nutrition standards for school-based meals, supporting whole-of-government efforts to improve nutrition and reduce chronic disease. The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food and Nutrition Service has issued this rule, aligning with the FDA's voluntary sodium reduction targets. The rule sets standards for school meals to move towards lower-sodium options, supporting a gradual sodium reduction strategy for the National School Lunch Program and the School Breakfast Program. This initiative, combined with the FDA's recent guidance on sodium reduction, may encourage industry to lower sodium levels in products found in schools and at home. The goal of these efforts is to improve dietary patterns, reduce average sodium intake, and improve the health and well-being of children, one of the most vulnerable populations.

title: FDA Approves First Generic of Restasis
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved the first generic version of Restasis (cyclosporine ophthalmic emulsion) 0.05% single-use vials to increase tear production in patients with keratoconjunctivitis sicca. The approval is the first generic version of the drug, which was initially approved for use in the US nearly 20 years ago. The drug's developer, Mylan Pharmaceuticals Inc., submitted data to demonstrate that the generic product meets the FDA's rigorous approval standards. The FDA's approval reflects its commitment to advancing patient access to lower-cost, high-quality generic drug products. The generic version of Restasis will help address the millions of Americans suffering from dry eyes, a condition that affects millions each year.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Advisory Committee Meeting to Discuss Request for Authorization of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine for Children 6 Months Through 4 Years of Age
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is announcing a virtual meeting of its Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee on February 15 to discuss the request for emergency use authorization of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine for use in children 6 months through 4 years of age. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that the agency is committed to a timely review of the data. The FDA has previously authorized the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine for use in children 5 through 11 years of age and recently authorized a single booster dose for individuals 12 through 15 years of age and older. As of December 19, 2021, 8.7 million COVID-19 vaccinations have been given to kids 5 through 11 years of age. The meeting will provide a clear understanding of the data and information the FDA will evaluate, and the agency intends to make background material available to the public.

title: FDA Roundup: February 1, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has released several updates. On January 31, a video provides an overview of the 2021 Food Allergy Safety, Treatment, Education, and Research (FASTER) Act, which adds sesame to the list of major food allergens effective January 1, 2023. The FDA has also released a list of draft and final guidance topics for the next 12 months. On the same day, the FDA published its 2021 Annual Report for the Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH), which includes information on the COVID-19 response and medical device innovation. Additionally, on January 28, the FDA issued a safety communication warning people to stop using the Empowered Diagnostics CovClear COVID-19 Rapid Antigen Test and ImmunoPass COVID-19 Neutralizing Antibody Rapid Test due to false results. The FDA has identified this issue as a class I recall, the most serious type of recall.

title: FDA Roundup: January 28, 2022
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has added four bulk drug substances to the list of substances that may be used in compounding by outsourcing facilities. The substances include diphenylcyclopropenone (DPCP) for topical use, glycolic acid for topical use, squaric acid dibutyl ester (SADBE) for topical use, and trichloroacetic acid (TCA) for topical use. The FDA has also determined that eight other bulk drug substances will not be added to the list at this time. The agency is continuing to balance patient protection and access to compounded drugs. 

The FDA has published guidances on generic drug application submissions, labeling, and review to bring greater efficiency and transparency to the generic drug review process. The guidances support the agency's Drug Competition Action Plan, which encourages robust and timely market competition for generic drugs. 

The FDA has issued updates related to agricultural water compliance dates and the recall of certain Philips Respironics ventilators. The agency has authorized tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody tests, and antigen tests.

title: Statement on Health Insurance Enrollment Under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: The administration aims to make health care a right, not a privilege, for all Americans. Since November 1, 14.5 million Americans have signed up for quality, affordable health coverage, with 10 million enrolling through healthcare.gov. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reports that one in seven uninsured Americans gained coverage between the end of 2020 and September 2021. The American Rescue Plan has lower costs and expanded access to health care. Families are saving an average of $2,400 on their annual premiums, with four out of five consumers finding quality coverage for under $10 a month. The administration will continue to lower costs and expand health coverage, including through the Build Back Better agenda, to ensure millions of Americans have dependable health insurance.

title: Implementation Note issued January 26, 2022
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on January 26, 2022: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 0.15 percent, effective January 27, 2022. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective January 27, 2022, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 0 to 1/4 percent. Complete the increase in System Open Market Account (SOMA) holdings of Treasury securities by $40 billion and of agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) by $20 billion, as indicated in the monthly purchase plans released in mid-January. Increase the SOMA holdings of Treasury securities by $20 billion and of agency MBS by $10 billion, during the monthly purchase period beginning in mid-February. Increase holdings of Treasury securities and agency MBS by additional amounts as needed to sustain smooth functioning of markets for these securities. Conduct overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 0.25 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion; the aggregate operation limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 0.05 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities and reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS in agency MBS. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for purchases and reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 0.25 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Indicators of economic activity and employment have continued to strengthen. The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic have improved in recent months but are being affected by the recent sharp rise in COVID-19 cases. Job gains have been solid in recent months, and the unemployment rate has declined substantially. Supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic and the reopening of the economy have continued to contribute to elevated levels of inflation. Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses. The path of the economy continues to depend on the course of the virus. Progress on vaccinations and an easing of supply constraints are expected to support continued gains in economic activity and employment as well as a reduction in inflation. Risks to the economic outlook remain, including from new variants of the virus. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent. With inflation well above 2 percent and a strong labor market, the Committee expects it will soon be appropriate to raise the target range for the federal funds rate. The Committee decided to continue to reduce the monthly pace of its net asset purchases, bringing them to an end in early March. Beginning in February, the Committee will increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $20 billion per month and of agency mortgageâbacked securities by at least $10 billion per month. The Federal Reserve's ongoing purchases and holdings of securities will continue to foster smooth market functioning and accommodative financial conditions, thereby supporting the flow of credit to households and businesses. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; James Bullard; Esther L. George; Patrick Harker; Loretta J. Mester; and Christopher J. Waller. Patrick Harker voted as an alternate member at this meeting.

title: FDA Roundup: January 25, 2022
body_summary: The FDA has issued final guidances on patient engagement in medical device clinical studies and principles for selecting patient-reported outcome instruments, as well as proposed a new rule to amend its regulation on pre-market notifications for food contact substances. Additionally, the agency has authorized 423 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 291 molecular tests, 87 antibody tests, and 45 antigen tests. The FDA also added 783 revisions to EUA authorizations for serial screening programs.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Limits Use of Certain Monoclonal Antibodies to Treat COVID-19 Due to the Omicron Variant
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has revised the authorizations for two monoclonal antibody treatments, bamlanivimab and etesevimab, and REGEN-COV, to limit their use to only when the patient is likely to have been infected with or exposed to a variant susceptible to these treatments. Due to the high frequency of the omicron variant in the US, these treatments are not authorized for use. The omicron variant is estimated to account for over 99% of cases as of Jan. 15, making it highly unlikely that COVID-19 patients are infected with a variant other than omicron. The NIH COVID-19 Treatment Guidelines Panel recently recommended against the use of these treatments due to reduced activity against the omicron variant. Alternative therapies such as Paxlovid, sotrovimab, Veklury, and molnupiravir are authorized to treat patients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 who are at high risk for progression to severe disease.

title: FDA Takes Actions to Expand Use of Treatment for Outpatients with Mild-to-Moderate COVID-19
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken two actions to expand the use of the antiviral drug Veklury (remdesivir) to certain non-hospitalized adults and pediatric patients for the treatment of mild-to-moderate COVID-19 disease.
