The FDA has authorized Veklury for adults and pediatric patients (12 years of age and older who weigh at least 40 kilograms) with positive results of direct SARS-CoV-2 viral testing, and who are not hospitalized and have mild-to-moderate COVID-19, and are at high risk for progression to severe COVID-19. The agency has also revised the Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for Veklury to additionally authorize the drug for treatment of pediatric patients weighing 3.5 kilograms to less than 40 kilograms or pediatric patients less than 12 years of age weighing at least 3.5 kilograms. The approval is supported by a randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial that included 562 non-hospitalized patients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19. The main outcome measured in the trial was whether a patient was hospitalized for any COVID-19 related reason or died within 28 days of treatment.

title: FDA Roundup: January 21, 2022
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration announced two FY 2022 funding opportunities totaling up to $800,000 for antimicrobial stewardship in veterinary settings and reducing antimicrobial resistance in animal agriculture. The FDA released its 2021 report, "FDA Voices: What FDA's Foods Program Achieved in 2021 to Protect Consumers and the Food Supply," byline Frank Yiannas. The agency approved the first transdermal buprenorphine animal drug, Zorbium, for controlling pain in cats after surgery. The FDA updated its device shortage list to include all blood specimen collection tubes and continued to conduct inspections, including temporary changes to ensure employee and regulated firm safety amid the COVID-19 pandemic. The agency extended the pause on domestic surveillance inspections through February 4, with the goal of restarting them in April. As of today, 422 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under emergency use authorizations.

title: The President's News Conference
body_summary: President Biden marks his first year in office, citing significant progress on COVID-19, inflation, and job creation, including 210 million Americans fully vaccinated, 6 million new jobs created, and child poverty dropping by nearly 40%. He outlines his Build Back Better plan to cut childcare costs in half, but faces Republican obstruction. The administration has provided $10 billion for testing to ensure US schools remain operational, with 95% still open, despite funding inefficiencies. The President remains confident in passing key parts of the Build Back Better law and notes that 16 Senate members voted to extend the Voting Rights Act. He also expresses skepticism about Russia's potential invasion of Ukraine and confirms the US will defend NATO member countries. The administration is working to reduce access costs, increase computer chip production, and release more oil to mitigate inflation.

title: FDA Roundup: January 18, 2022
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing an at-a-glance summary of news from around the agency. The CDRH Health of Women Program Strategic Plan is now available. CDRH initially issued a proposed strategic plan in September 2019 and considered public feedback. The plan outlines three priorities to protect and promote the health of women. 

On January 14, the FDA released a report on its investigation of the Salmonella Typhimurium outbreak that caused 31 reported illnesses and four hospitalizations in the U.S. between June and August 2021. The outbreak was linked to packaged salad greens during the summer of 2021. The FDA worked with the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and state partners to investigate the outbreak. 

As of today, 420 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs). These include 290 molecular tests and sample collection devices, 87 antibody and other immune response tests, and 44 antigen tests. The FDA has authorized 766 revisions to EUA authorizations.

title: FDA Releases CDRH Health of Women Strategic Plan to Better Inform Medical Device Research and Regulation for All Women
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration's Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH) has released its Health of Women Program Strategic Plan, building on previous proposals and public feedback. The plan aims to protect and promote women's health, strengthen regulatory science, and address sex- and gender-specific issues in medical device research and regulation. The program was created in 2016 and has been working to improve understanding of medical devices' performance in women. The strategic plan outlines three priorities: Sex- and Gender-Specific Analysis & Reporting, Integrated Approach for Current & Emerging Issues Related to the Health of Women, and Research Roadmap. The plan aims to ensure all women have access to innovative, safe, and effective medical devices, with a focus on patient-centered care and partnerships across CDRH. The FDA's Office of Women's Health will support the implementation of these priorities.

title: FDA Roundup: January 14, 2022
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has published its priorities for calendar years 2022-2023 through the Interagency Food Safety Analytics Collaboration, a collaboration between the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the FDA, and the Food Safety and Inspection Service. The FDA has also announced a new program for state egg and egg product regulators, the Egg Regulatory Program Standards, to integrate regulatory activities into an efficient and effective process for improving egg and egg product safety. 

The FDA has issued its report, Advancing Health Through Innovation: New Drug Therapy Approvals 2021, which highlights the agency's role in bringing innovative drug therapies to patients in need. The agency has published an FDA Voices on this report, Many Important Drugs Approved in 2021 as COVID-19 Pandemic Continues. 

The FDA has made available its 2021 Year in Review: Working for You report, which offers highlights of the agency's work in 2021. The agency has also announced the approval of the new animal drug, Solensia, for the control of pain associated with osteoarthritis in cats. 

The FDA will hold a public hearing on Scientific Data and Information Related to the Residue of Carcinogenic Concern for the New Animal Drug Carbadox, a carcinogenic new animal drug used in swine feed, on March 10, 2022. The FDA has also issued a warning to patients and prescribers about the potential for dental problems associated with buprenorphine medicines. 

The FDA has revoked the standard of identity for French dressing in response to a citizen petition from the Association for Dressings and Sauces. As of today, 420 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations.

title: FDA Releases Federal Interagency Working Group Scientific Opinions on Testing Methods for Asbestos in Talc-Containing Cosmetic Products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) released a white paper developed by the Interagency Working Group on Asbestos in Consumer Products (IWGACP) that contains scientific opinions for testing talc-containing cosmetics and talc for the possible presence of asbestos. The FDA has been sampling and testing talc-containing cosmetics for asbestos, but has found that methods may not always detect the presence of asbestos. The IWGACP's scientific opinions recommend using both Polarized Light Microscopy (PLM) and Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) to identify and report the presence of asbestos, as well as establishing policies and procedures for training, quality assurance, and quality control. The FDA plans to peer-review the white paper and consider its recommendations for regulatory policy developments on a definition of particles of interest and standardized testing methods for asbestos.

title: FDA Approves Novel Treatment to Control Pain in Cats with Osteoarthritis, First Monoclonal Antibody Drug for Use in Any Animal Species
body_summary: The US FDA approved Solensia, the first treatment for pain associated with osteoarthritis in cats, and the first monoclonal antibody approved by the FDA for use in any animal species. The treatment works by blocking a protein called nerve growth factor (NGF) involved in pain regulation. The FDA approved Solensia after evaluating two clinical studies showing it to be effective in controlling pain associated with osteoarthritis in cats. The treatment is available by prescription only and is given by subcutaneous injection once a month based on the cat's weight. Common side effects include vomiting, diarrhea, injection site pain, and skin reactions, which are generally mild and do not require treatment cessation.

title: FDA Roundup: January 11, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced that it does not intend to object to the use of certain qualified health claims regarding the consumption of magnesium and a reduced risk of high blood pressure, provided that the claims are appropriately worded. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock testified before the U.S. Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions. The FDA also announced revisions to the Janssen COVID-19 Vaccine Fact Sheets for health care providers and recipients, following new safety information regarding the risk of Immune Thrombocytopenia. As of today, 420 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 290 molecular tests and 43 antigen tests.

title: FDA Roundup: January 7, 2022
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing an update on news from around the agency. On January 5, the FDA published an interactive public data dashboard for the Reportable Food Registry, which allows anyone to view historical data. The FDA issued an outbreak advisory on January 6 regarding a multistate outbreak of E. coli O157:H7, which has been reported from four states, with 10 cases and seven associated consumer purchases. The FDA will hold virtual public meetings on the proposed rule for agricultural water standards. The agency also added organ preservation solutions to the device shortage list and authorized various COVID-19 tests and sample collection devices.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Shortens Interval for Booster Dose of Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine to Five Months
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) amended the emergency use authorization for the Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine to shorten the time between completing a primary series and a booster dose to at least five months for individuals 18 years of age and older. This change aims to reduce waning immunity, particularly against the highly contagious omicron variant. The FDA's director, Peter Marks, noted that vaccination is the best defense against COVID-19. The amendment brings consistency in booster dose timing among mRNA vaccines and encourages everyone to get vaccinated. Common side effects reported after booster doses include pain, redness, swelling, fatigue, headache, muscle or joint pain, and chills.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a meeting via videoconference from December 14-15, 2021, discussing financial market developments and open market operations. They discussed normalization of monetary policy, considering lessons learned from previous experiences and alternative approaches. The main topics included the timing and sequencing of policy rate changes and balance sheet actions. Participants agreed that the federal funds rate should be the primary means for adjusting monetary policy, but noted differences between current economic conditions and those in the past. The Committee projected a higher inflation rate driven by supply chain bottlenecks and energy prices, with real GDP growth expected to slow in 2023 as the economy reopens and supply constraints ease. They decided to reduce the monthly pace of net asset purchases for Treasury securities and agency MBS by $20 billion and $10 billion respectively, effective January, maintaining the federal funds rate at 0-1/4% until labor market conditions reach maximum employment levels.

title: FDA Roundup: January 4, 2022
body_summary: The US FDA announced several updates and approvals on December 21-29, 2021. On December 21, it published its wastewater surveillance for SARS-CoV-2 variants. On December 28, the FDA approved an abbreviated new drug application for Albuterol Sulfate Inhalation Solution. On December 29, it implemented temporary changes to its inspectional activities to ensure employee and firm safety, postponing certain foreign inspections. The FDA also announced additional approvals for at-home COVID-19 antigen tests, including the SD Biosensor and Siemens' CLINITEST Rapid COVID-19 Antigen Self-Test. On December 22, it reissued the Tide Laboratories DTPM COVID-19 RT-PCR Test emergency use authorization to detect the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron Variant. As of December 29, the FDA authorized two over-the-counter COVID-19 antigen tests, including the SD Biosensor, Inc. COVID-19 At-Home Test, and an additional OTC test.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Takes Multiple Actions to Expand Use of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) amended the emergency use authorization (EUA) for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine. 

A single booster dose is now authorized for individuals 12 years of age and older. The FDA shortened the time between the completion of primary vaccination and a booster dose to at least five months. Additionally, a third primary series dose is authorized for certain immunocompromised children 5 through 11 years of age. 

The FDA reviewed real-world data from Israel, including safety data from over 6,300 individuals 12 through 15 years of age who received a booster dose at least five months following completion of the primary vaccination series. The data shows no new safety concerns following a booster in this population. 

Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that the need to quickly adapt to the evolving virus requires using the best available science to make informed decisions with the health and safety of the American public in mind. 

The FDA is also authorizing the use of a single booster dose five months after completion of the primary vaccination series, which may provide better protection sooner against the highly transmissible omicron variant.

title: Statement on the Death of Former Senate Majority Leader Harry M. Reid
body_summary: Harry Reid and the author grew up on different sides of the country, sharing values like loyalty, faith, and resolve. During their 20 years in the US Senate, and 8 years as Vice President, Reid demonstrated his commitment to his word and actions. He passed the Recovery Act, rescued the American auto industry, and passed the Affordable Care Act and Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform. As Senate Majority Leader, Reid led battles over budgets and fought for troops' needs. He also championed Social Security reform and created Nevada's Great Basin National Park. Reid's leadership was driven by a desire to do right for the people, rather than seeking power. He was a devoted husband to Landra and father to six children and many grandchildren. The author sends love and prayers to Landra and the Reid family, honoring Reid as a dear friend and giant of their history.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 28, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has taken several actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey has entered a consent decree of permanent injunction against Natural Solutions Foundation, a New Jersey-based company, requiring it to comply with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. The company's two principals, Rima Laibow and Ralph Fucetola, were accused of selling unapproved and misbranded drugs. The FDA has also updated the emergency use authorization for COVID-19 convalescent plasma to limit its use to patients with immunosuppressive disease or those receiving immunosuppressive treatment. Additionally, the FDA has updated its SARS-CoV-2 Viral Mutations: Impact on COVID-19 Tests web page to share new information regarding the impact of the SARS-CoV-2 omicron variant on antigen diagnostic tests. The FDA has authorized 419 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 290 molecular tests and 42 antigen tests.

title: FDA Authorizes Marketing of Tobacco Products that Help Reduce Exposure to and Consumption of Nicotine for Smokers Who Use Them
body_summary: The US FDA has authorized the marketing of 22nd Century Group Inc.'s "VLN King" and "VLN Menthol King" combusted, filtered cigarettes as modified risk tobacco products (MRTPs), which aim to reduce nicotine exposure for smokers. The products contain less nicotine, with 96% lower levels than most conventional cigarette brands, and are expected to help adult smokers transition away from highly addictive combusted cigarettes. The authorization includes specific claims about reduced nicotine consumption, such as "95% less nicotine" and "helps reduce your nicotine consumption." The manufacturer must also label the products with warnings about the dangers of smoking and include certain warnings statements. The FDA requires the company to conduct postmarket surveillance and studies to determine if the authorization criteria continue to be met. The products are subject to postmarket requirements and restrictions, including limiting youth access and advertising.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Additional Oral Antiviral for Treatment of COVID-19 in Certain Adults
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for Merck's molnupiravir to treat mild-to-moderate coronavirus disease (COVID-19) in adults with positive SARS-CoV-2 viral testing and at high risk for severe COVID-19. Molnupiravir is authorized for adults 18 years and older, not for pre-exposure or post-exposure prevention, and not for initiation of treatment in hospitalized patients. The EUA is based on data from a clinical trial showing that molnupiravir reduces the risk of hospitalization or death from COVID-19 by 51% compared to a placebo. Molnupiravir is administered as four 200mg capsules taken orally every 12 hours for five days and is not recommended for use during pregnancy or in patients younger than 18 years. The FDA has also emphasized the importance of vaccination in preventing COVID-19.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 23, 2021
body_summary:
The US FDA has announced updates regarding the SARS-CoV-2 omicron variant and COVID-19 tests. On Wednesday, the FDA updated its website with new information on the impact of the omicron variant on antigen diagnostic tests and molecular diagnostic tests. The FDA also released a joint statement with ASPR on the circulating SARS-CoV-2 viral variants, including Omicron, and how they may be associated with resistance to monoclonal antibodies.

Data show that bamlanivimab and etesevimab administered together or REGEN-COV may not retain activity against the Omicron variant, while sotrovimab appears to retain activity. The FDA has paused further allocations of bamlanivimab and etesevimab together and etesevimab alone pending updated data from the CDC.

The FDA has also authorized two oral antivirals, Pfizer's Paxlovid and Merck's molnupiravir, for the treatment of mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in certain patients. As of today, 418 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 290 molecular tests and sample collection devices, 87 antibody tests, and 41 antigen tests.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Announces Outbreak Investigation of Listeria monocytogenes Found in Dole Packaged Salad
body_summary: The FDA, CDC, and state partners are investigating a multistate outbreak of Listeria monocytogenes infections potentially linked to Dole packaged salad. Dole has voluntarily recalled packaged salads produced at two facilities. To date, 16 illnesses have been reported from 13 states, with two product samples matching the outbreak strain. Dole initiated a recall of prepackaged garden salad mixes from a facility in North Carolina in October 2021. Subsequent testing found the same Listeria strain in products from a facility in Arizona. As a result, Dole is ceasing production and initiating a new recall of various products and brands produced at both facilities.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes First Oral Antiviral for Treatment of COVID-19
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for Pfizer's Paxlovid for the treatment of mild-to-moderate coronavirus disease (COVID-19) in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older weighing at least 40 kilograms. The EUA allows for the use of Paxlovid for patients with positive SARS-CoV-2 testing and high risk for progression to severe COVID-19. Paxlovid is a pill taken orally twice daily for five days, and its administration is not authorized for longer than five consecutive days. The FDA approved one vaccine and authorized others to prevent COVID-19, and the public is urged to get vaccinated and receive a booster if eligible. The primary data supporting the EUA for Paxlovid come from a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial. Paxlovid significantly reduced the proportion of people with COVID-19-related hospitalization or death from any cause by 88% compared to placebo among patients treated within five days of symptom onset. Possible side effects of Paxlovid include impaired sense of taste, diarrhea, high blood pressure, and muscle aches.

title: Statement on Health Insurance Enrollment Under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: The main action is the promise to ensure access to quality, affordable health care for all Americans. Since taking office, more than 4.6 million Americans have gained health coverage through the Affordable Care Act. From November 1 to December 15, 13.6 million Americans signed up for coverage, with 1.8 million new enrollees. Americans can still sign up through January 15. The administration has made quality coverage more affordable, with families saving an average of $2,400, and four out of five consumers finding coverage for under $10 a month. The Build Back Better Act would reduce premiums for 9 million Americans, cover 4 million in states that failed to expand Medicaid, expand Medicare for hearing coverage, lower prescription drug costs, and cap insulin at $35 a month. This Act represents the single most consequential expansion of affordable health care since the Affordable Care Act.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 21, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On December 20, the FDA's Center for Veterinary Medicine announced an update to its eSubmitter system to collect more facility information from animal drug manufacturers. This enhancement aims to improve the Agency's ability to access supply chain data and identify potential animal drug shortages. The update is part of the Animal Drug and Manufacturing System, funded by the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act. Additionally, a new project funded by the FDA, Australia's CSIRO, and global partners will use systems biology and machine learning to enhance the understanding of nonclinical model responses to SARS-CoV-2. The FDA has also authorized 418 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 290 molecular tests, 87 antibody tests, and 41 antigen tests.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Announces Outbreak Investigation of Listeria monocytogenes Found in Fresh Express Packaged Salad
body_summary: The FDA, along with the CDC and state partners, is investigating a multistate outbreak of Listeria monocytogenes infections associated with packaged salad. A positive sample of Fresh Express Sweet Hearts salad mix has been reported to match the outbreak strain. Ten people infected with the outbreak strain have been reported from eight states. Fresh Express has voluntarily recalled products and consumers are advised not to eat, sell or serve any recalled products. The recall includes all Use-By Dates of fresh salad items with product codes Z324 through Z350. Consumers should use extra vigilance in cleaning and sanitizing any surfaces and containers that may have come in contact with recalled products to reduce the risk of cross-contamination. The investigation is ongoing, and additional information will be provided as it becomes available.

title: FDA Conditionally Approves First Oral Tablet to Treat Chemotherapy-Induced Diarrhea in Dogs
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) conditionally approved Canalevia-CA1 (crofelemer delayed-release tablets) for the treatment of chemotherapy-induced diarrhea in dogs, the first treatment to be approved for this condition. Canalevia-CA1 is available only by prescription due to the need for professional veterinary expertise. The active ingredient, crofelemer, functions by inhibiting chloride ion and water secretion in intestinal epithelial cells, similar to its use in humans with HIV/AIDS. The drug received conditional approval through the Minor Use/Minor Species pathway, as it is expected to affect fewer than 70,000 dogs in the US annually. Canalevia-CA1 was granted conditional approval to Jaguar Animal Health, with the initial approval valid for one year and potential for four annual renewals.

title: FDA Grants Marketing Authorization for Inferior Vena Cava Filter Removal Device
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of the Philips CavaClear Laser Sheath, a laser-based device for removing Inferior Vena Cava (IVC) filters. The device is designed to facilitate detachment of firmly adherent IVC filters from the IVC wall using ultraviolet laser energy. The FDA assessed the safety and effectiveness of the device through a retrospective clinical study in 265 patients, which demonstrated a procedural technical success rate of 96%. The device is intended for use in conjunction with conventional snare devices and is contraindicated in certain situations, including the presence of a blood clot within the filter or surrounding veins. The FDA granted marketing authorization to Philips, marking the first laser-based device for IVC filter removal.

title: FDA Approves New Treatment for Myasthenia Gravis
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Vyvgart (efgartigimod) for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis in adults who test positive for anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibodies. Myasthenia gravis is a chronic autoimmune, neuromuscular disease causing weakness in skeletal muscles that worsens after activity and improves after rest. Vyvgart is an antibody fragment that binds to the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn), reducing overall levels of IgG, including abnormal AChR antibodies. The safety and efficacy of Vyvgart were evaluated in a 26-week clinical study of 167 patients. The study showed that more patients with myasthenia gravis responded to treatment with Vyvgart compared to those who received placebo. Common side effects include respiratory tract infections, headache, and urinary tract infections. Patients should monitor for signs and symptoms of infections during treatment. The FDA granted Fast Track and Orphan Drug designations to argenx BV.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 17, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved an abbreviated new drug application for Vasopressin Injection, 20 Units/mL Multiple Dose Vials, to increase blood pressure in adults with vasodilatory shock on December 15, 2021. The FDA also approved a manufacturing change for Comirnaty (COVID-19 Vaccine, mRNA) to include a new buffer formulation, which makes the vaccine more stable at refrigerated temperatures. The FDA previously authorized this vaccine formulation for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine in October. The FDA has authorized 422 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 292 molecular tests, 89 antibody tests, and 41 antigen tests.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The Federal Reserve is committed to using its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals. With progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have continued to strengthen. The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic have improved in recent months but continue to be affected by COVID-19. Job gains have been solid in recent months, and the unemployment rate has declined substantially. Supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic and the reopening of the economy have continued to contribute to elevated levels of inflation. Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses. The path of the economy continues to depend on the course of the virus. Progress on vaccinations and an easing of supply constraints are expected to support continued gains in economic activity and employment as well as a reduction in inflation. Risks to the economic outlook remain, including from new variants of the virus. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent. With inflation having exceeded 2 percent for some time, the Committee expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment. In light of inflation developments and the further improvement in the labor market, the Committee decided to reduce the monthly pace of its net asset purchases by $20 billion for Treasury securities and $10 billion for agency mortgage-backed securities. Beginning in January, the Committee will increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $40 billion per month and of agency mortgageâbacked securities by at least $20 billion per month. The Committee judges that similar reductions in the pace of net asset purchases will likely be appropriate each month, but it is prepared to adjust the pace of purchases if warranted by changes in the economic outlook. The Federal Reserve's ongoing purchases and holdings of securities will continue to foster smooth market functioning and accommodative financial conditions, thereby supporting the flow of credit to households and businesses. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Mary C. Daly; Charles L. Evans; Randal K. Quarles; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: FDA Approves First Drug to Prevent Graft Versus Host Disease
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Orencia (abatacept) for the prevention of acute graft versus host disease (aGVHD) in adults and pediatric patients two years of age or older undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. This approval incorporates real-world evidence as one component of clinical effectiveness. 

The drug was evaluated in two separate studies, GVHD-1 and GVHD-2, which showed that Orencia improved overall survival rates in patients undergoing stem cell transplantation, with 97% and 98% survival rates, respectively. However, severe aGVHD-free survival was not significantly improved. 

Common side effects of Orencia for aGVHD prevention include anemia, hypertension, and cytomegalovirus reactivation. Patients should be monitored for Epstein-Barr virus reactivation and CMV infection. 

Orencia received Breakthrough, Orphan Drug, and Priority Review designations for this indication. The FDA granted approval to Bristol Myers Squibb, and development of this product was partially supported by the FDA's Orphan Products Grants Program.

title: Implementation Note issued December 15, 2021
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on December 15, 2021: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 0.15 percent, effective December 16, 2021. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective December 16, 2021, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 0 to 1/4 percent. Complete the increase in System Open Market Account (SOMA) holdings of Treasury securities by $60 billion and of agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) by $30 billion, as indicated in the monthly purchase plans released in mid- December. Increase the SOMA holdings of Treasury securities by $40 billion and of agency MBS by $20 billion, during the monthly purchase period beginning in mid-January. Increase holdings of Treasury securities and agency MBS by additional amounts as needed to sustain smooth functioning of markets for these securities. Conduct overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 0.25 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion; the aggregate operation limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 0.05 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities and reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS in agency MBS. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for purchases and reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 0.25 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Statement on the Pfizer Incorporated COVID-19 Antiviral Treatment
body_summary: The President's administration is encouraged by promising data from Pfizer on its antiviral pill, showing effectiveness in reducing severe illness risk in COVID-19 patients. The pill is one of several tools in the fight against the virus, including Omicron. Several steps remain, including FDA authorization, before availability. The administration has ordered enough pills to treat 10 million Americans. Vaccination and booster shots remain crucial in saving lives. If authorized, the pill will mark a significant step forward in the pandemic's path out. Widespread vaccinations, boosters, testing, and effective treatment for ill patients will further reduce COVID-19's impact on lives and the economy.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 14, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced revisions to the Janssen COVID-19 Vaccine Fact Sheets for Healthcare Providers and Recipients. The fact sheets now include a Contraindication to the administration of the vaccine to individuals with a history of thrombosis with thrombocytopenia. The FDA continues to investigate the level of potential excess risk and finds that the known and potential benefits outweigh the risks in individuals 18 years of age and older. There are 421 authorized tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 291 molecular tests and 89 antibody and immune response tests.

title: Executive Order 14058—Transforming Federal Customer Experience and Service Delivery To Rebuild Trust in Government
body_summary: The US government aims to improve customer experience by redesigning online services for various departments. The Secretary of each department is tasked with designing and delivering new online experiences, simplifying processes, and reducing physical document requirements. The Administrator of USAID reviews and revises grant and cooperative agreement regulations to reduce administrative burdens. Joint Agency Actions include integrating Login.gov accounts and streamlining the Public Service Loan Forgiveness process. The Director of OMB leads a team to coordinate customer experience initiatives across agencies, urging all departments to apply guidance to improve service delivery, modernize digital experiences, and streamline processes.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Publishes Discussion Paper and Seeks Public Input on 3D Printing of Medical Devices at the Point of Care
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has published a discussion paper on 3D printing of medical devices at the point of care (PoC), such as hospitals and doctor's offices. The paper, attributed to CDRH's William Maisel and Ed Margerrison, provides insight into the benefits and challenges of 3D printing at hospitals and presents a potential approach for regulatory oversight. The discussion paper is intended to foster discussion and solicit feedback from the public to inform future policy development. It will be open for public comments for 60 days at https://www.regulations.gov/docket/FDA-2021-N-1272.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 10, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On December 9, 2021, the FDA updated its web page on SARS-CoV-2 Viral Mutations: Impact on COVID-19 Tests to share the latest information. The update included new information about the Meridian Bioscience, Inc. Revogene SARS-CoV-2 test, which is expected to fail to detect the SARS-CoV-2 omicron variant. As of today, 422 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 291 molecular tests and sample collection devices, 90 antibody and other immune response tests, and 41 antigen tests. The FDA has also authorized 703 revisions to EUA authorizations.

title: FDA Issues Improvement Plan Focused on Modernizing Foodborne Illness Outbreak Responses
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is releasing a Foodborne Outbreak Response Improvement Plan to strengthen food safety and protect consumers. The plan focuses on four priority areas: tech-enabled product traceback, root-cause investigations, analysis and dissemination of outbreak data, and operational improvements. The plan aims to enhance the speed, effectiveness, coordination, and communication of foodborne outbreak investigations, ultimately translating into enhanced prevention of outbreaks. The plan was developed with input from experts in the public and private sectors, including the US Department of Agriculture's Food Safety Inspection Service, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, and state health officials. The FDA has also contracted with the University of Minnesota's School of Public Health to assess its capacity to support multistate outbreak investigations.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Expands Eligibility for Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Booster Dose to 16- and 17-Year-Olds
body_summary: The US FDA amended the emergency use authorization (EUA) for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine to authorize a single booster dose for individuals 16 and 17 years of age at least six months after completion of primary vaccination. The amendment expands the use of the vaccine for this age group, allowing them to receive a booster dose with either the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine or Comirnaty. The decision is based on data showing that vaccine effectiveness against COVID-19 is waning after the second dose for all adults and for those in the 16-17 age group. The FDA evaluated the benefits and risks of the booster dose and concluded that the benefits outweigh the risks of myocarditis and pericronitis. The FDA will publicly post documents regarding the decision on its website.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes New Long-Acting Monoclonal Antibodies for Pre-exposure Prevention of COVID-19 in Certain Individuals
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for AstraZeneca's Evusheld for pre-exposure prophylaxis (prevention) of COVID-19 in certain adults and pediatric individuals 12 years of age and older weighing at least 40 kilograms. The authorization requires individuals to have compromised immune systems or a history of severe adverse reactions to a COVID-19 vaccine. One dose of Evusheld, administered as two separate injections, may be effective for six months. The product is not authorized for treatment or post-exposure prevention of COVID-19. The FDA has approved one vaccine and authorized others to prevent COVID-19, and vaccination is still recommended. The EUA is based on the totality of available scientific evidence, which shows that Evusheld may be effective for pre-exposure prevention and that its known benefits outweigh its known risks.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Takes New Steps Aimed at Advancing Development of Individualized Medicines to Treat Genetic Diseases
body_summary: The FDA is issuing draft guidance to provide recommendations for managing the administration of individualized investigational Antisense Oligonucleotide (ASO) drugs in a clinical trial. The guidance is specifically tailored to the unique circumstances involving relatively few individuals and includes information regarding drug quality, manufacturing guidelines, and clinical considerations. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock, M.D. hopes that these draft guidances will help promising drugs reach patients in a timely manner and is optimistic that the development of individualized drug products may continue to change the landscape for treating rare diseases.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 7, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has updated its webpage to share the latest information on SARS-CoV-2 viral mutations and their impact on COVID-19 tests. The FDA has added new information about tests whose performance could be impacted by SARS-CoV-2 genetic mutations, specifically those found in the omicron variant. The list includes tests where viral mutations cause a specific detection pattern that may help signal the presence of the omicron variant. The FDA has also added the Tide Laboratories, LLC, DTPM COVID-19 RT-PCR Test to the list of impacted tests. As of today, 425 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 294 molecular tests and 90 antibody and other immune response tests.

title: FDA Expands Authorization of Two Monoclonal Antibodies for Treatment and Post-Exposure Prevention of COVID-19 to Younger Pediatric Patients, Including Newborns
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has revised the emergency use authorization (EUA) of bamlanivimab and etesevimab, previously authorized for children 12 years old and older weighing at least 88 pounds, to additionally authorize the treatment of mild to moderate COVID-19 in all younger pediatric patients, including newborns, who have a positive COVID-19 test and are at high risk for progression to severe COVID-19. The EUA also authorizes post-exposure prophylaxis for prevention of COVID-19 in all pediatric patients, including newborns, at high risk of progression to severe COVID-19. Pediatric patients under one year of age who are exposed to COVID-19 are at high risk for severe COVID-19. The authorization is based on safety and efficacy data in adolescents and adults, as well as pharmacokinetic and safety data from a clinical trial in pediatric patients.

title: FDA Proposes Changes to Food Safety Modernization Act Rule to Enhance Safety of Agricultural Water Used on Produce
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a proposed rule to enhance the safety of produce by requiring farms to conduct comprehensive assessments of their agricultural water quality. The proposal aims to identify and mitigate hazards in water used to grow produce, following several recent outbreak investigations that revealed potential routes of contamination. The proposed rule would replace some existing requirements for agricultural water in the Produce Safety Rule (PSR) and is part of the FDA's implementation of the Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA). If finalized, the proposal would result in fewer outbreaks in the US related to produce, protecting public health and saving lives. The proposed rule includes requirements for farms to manage their agricultural water quality based on comprehensive assessments, annual assessments of pre-harvest agricultural water, and expedited mitigation measures for hazards related to certain activities. The FDA plans to engage with stakeholders, hold virtual public meetings, and develop an online tool to assist growers in understanding agricultural water assessments.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: November 30, 2021
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has announced actions to address the impact of the new omicron variant on the fight against the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA is actively working with partners to evaluate the potential impact on diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccines. The agency is also conducting bioinformatic research and system development, funded by the FDA, to expand the FDA-ARGOS database. The database contains curated genomic sequence data to support research and regulatory decisions.

As of today, 423 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 293 molecular tests, 90 antibody tests, and 40 antigen tests. The FDA has also authorized 696 revisions to test EUA authorizations. The agency is committed to communicating with the public as it learns more about the variant.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Actively Working to Investigate, Address Potential Impacts of Omicron Variant; Urges Vaccination and Boosters
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is actively working with federal partners, international regulators, and medical product companies to address the potential impact of the new omicron variant on diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccines. The agency is quickly evaluating the potential impact of this variant and expects to complete most of the work in the coming weeks. The FDA has been monitoring for the emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants since early in the pandemic and has worked with companies to evaluate and address the impact of variants on products. The agency has taken steps to adapt to emerging variants, including requiring companies to monitor for variants and taking action. The FDA believes that high-volume PCR and antigen tests show low likelihood of being impacted and will continue to review and adjust course as needed. The current vaccines remain highly effective, and additional booster shots provide further protection against COVID-19 infection.

title: FDA Approves New Imaging Drug to Help  Identify Ovarian Cancer Lesions
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Cytalux, an imaging drug, to assist surgeons in identifying ovarian cancer lesions. Cytalux is administered as an intravenous injection prior to surgery and binds to folate receptors, illuminating under fluorescent light to enhance surgeons' ability to detect cancerous tissue. The FDA's approval aims to help identify deadly ovarian tumors that may otherwise go undetected. The drug was approved for adult patients with ovarian cancer, and its safety and effectiveness were evaluated in a randomized, multi-center study. The most common side effects were infusion-related reactions, and the drug may cause fetal harm when administered to pregnant women. Cytalux is indicated for use with a Near-Infrared fluorescence imaging system, and its use carries a risk of image interpretation errors. The American Cancer Society estimates over 21,000 new cases and 13,000 deaths from ovarian cancer in 2021.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on November 2-3, 2021, discussing global financial markets, sovereign yields, and policy-sensitive rates. The median forecast for headline PCE inflation in 2021 was revised up, while the Reserve Bank of Australia ended its yield target and signaled a potential rate hike in 2023. The Federal Reserve's Desk issued a monthly purchase schedule on November 12 reflecting a potential reduction in net asset purchases, with the System Open Market Account portfolio peaking around next June at about $8.5 trillion. Maximum production was weighed down by public health restrictions and electricity rationing in emerging markets, while advanced economies generally recovered at a solid pace. Inflation rates abroad rose due to energy price increases and supply bottlenecks. Businesses' leverage fell in Q2 and returned to pre-pandemic levels, with corporate debt becoming more sustainable due to increased earnings and low rates. The Federal Reserve announced a reduction in the pace of net asset purchases, maintaining an accommodative stance until maximum employment and price stability goals were achieved.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Common Type of Post-Transplant Infection that is Resistant to Other Drugs
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Livtencity (maribavir) as the first drug for treating adults and pediatric patients with post-transplant cytomegalovirus infection/disease that does not respond to available antiviral treatment. Livtencity works by preventing human cytomegalovirus enzyme pUL97, blocking virus replication. The drug was evaluated in a Phase 3 study involving 352 transplant recipients with CMV infections, with 56% of those treated with Livtencity showing a reduction in CMV DNA levels. The most common side effects include taste disturbance, nausea, and fatigue. Livtencity received Breakthrough Therapy and Priority Review designations. The approval was granted to Takeda Pharmaceuticals Company Limited.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: November 23, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized three over-the-counter COVID-19 antigen diagnostic tests. These tests, from InBios, Access Bio, and Becton, Dickinson and Company, can be used for self-testing or with adult assistance. The InBios SCoV-2 Ag Detect Rapid Self-Test delivers results in 20 minutes and can be used as a single test or serial test. The Access Bio CareStart COVID-19 Antigen Home Test gives results in 10 minutes and can be used as a single test or serial test. The Becton, Dickinson and Company BD Veritor At-Home COVID-19 Test gives results in 15 minutes and can be used as a single test or serial test. The FDA has also reissued EUAs for these tests, allowing them to be used without a prescription for people with COVID-19 symptoms. Additionally, the FDA has authorized 423 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 293 molecular tests, 90 antibody tests, and 40 antigen tests.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Issues Final Orders Reclassifying Certain Hepatitis C Diagnostic Tests from Class III to Class II
body_summary: The FDA has issued two final orders reclassifying certain Hepatitis C virus diagnostic tests from class III to class II, allowing them to use the less burdensome premarket notification (510(k)) pathway. This decision was made by Timothy Stenzel, M.D., Ph.D., director of the Office of In Vitro Diagnostics and Radiological Health. The reclassification will support increased competition and access to these tests, benefiting the National Viral Hepatitis Action Plan.

title: FDA Approves First Drug to Improve Growth in Children with Most Common Form of Dwarfism
body_summary: The US FDA approved Voxzogo (vosoritide) injection to improve growth in children aged five and older with achondroplasia, a genetic condition causing short stature and disproportionate growth. The approval fulfills an unmet medical need for over 10,000 children in the US. Voxzogo was evaluated in a year-long phase 3 study, where 121 participants showed an average growth velocity of 1.57 centimeters taller compared to those receiving a placebo. The most common side effects include injection site reactions, vomiting, and decreased blood pressure. Voxzogo's labeling lists decreased blood pressure as a serious side effect. The approval was granted to BioMarin under an accelerated approval pathway, with a post-marketing study required to assess final adult height.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Expands Eligibility for COVID-19 Vaccine Boosters
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) amended emergency use authorizations (EUA) for the Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccines, allowing a single booster dose for all individuals 18 years of age and older after completing primary vaccination. The amendments expand the use of booster doses to include individuals who completed their primary vaccination series with any FDA-authorized or approved COVID-19 vaccine. The FDA based its decision on analysis of immune response data from clinical studies, which demonstrated a booster response in antibody levels against the SARS-CoV-2 virus. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that authorizing a single booster dose helps provide continued protection against COVID-19. The FDA determined that the benefits of the booster dose outweigh the risks of myocarditis and pericarditis in individuals 18 years of age and older.

title: FDA Approves First Drug to Improve Growth in Children with Most Common Form of Dwarfism
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Voxzogo injection to improve growth in children five years of age and older with achondroplasia, a genetic condition causing severely short stature. The approval fulfills an unmet medical need for over 10,000 children in the US. Therese Kehoe, director of the Division of General Endocrinology, stated that the approval underscores the FDA's commitment to making new therapies available for rare diseases. Voxzogo works by reducing the activity of a growth regulation gene and stimulating bone growth. In a year-long phase 3 study, 121 participants showed an average growth increase of 1.57 centimeters compared to those receiving a placebo. The most common side effects include injection site reactions, vomiting, and decreased blood pressure. The FDA approved Voxzogo under accelerated approval, which includes a post-marketing study to assess final adult height, and granted approval to BioMarin.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Expands Eligibility for COVID-19 Vaccine Boosters
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) amended the emergency use authorizations (EUA) for the Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccines, authorizing a single booster dose for all individuals 18 years of age and older after completion of primary vaccination with any FDA-authorized or approved COVID-19 vaccine. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock said this helps provide continued protection against COVID-19. The FDA evaluated the benefits and risks of the use of these vaccines in the general adult population, determining that the benefits outweigh the risks of myocarditis and pericarditis. The FDA analyzed immune response data from participants who received a booster dose, which demonstrated a booster response. The amendments were granted to ModernaTX Inc. and Pfizer Inc.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Announces Investigation of E. coli O157:H7 Outbreak Linked to Spinach
body_summary: The FDA, CDC, and state partners are investigating a multistate outbreak of E. coli O157:H7 infections associated with spinach consumption. As of Nov. 15, 10 people infected with the outbreak strain have been reported from seven states, including Iowa, Indiana, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Ohio, and South Dakota. The outbreak started on dates ranging from Oct. 15 to Oct. 27, with five people reporting eating spinach in the week before becoming sick. A sample of Josie's Organics Baby Spinach, with a "Best If Used By" date of Oct. 23, 2021, tested positive for E. coli O157:H7. Consumers, restaurants, and retailers are advised not to eat, sell, or serve this product. The FDA is tracing back the supply of the baby spinach and deploying investigators along the supply chain. Consumers who have symptoms of E. coli infection should contact their healthcare provider.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: November 16, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced several actions on November 15, 2021, to support nationwide COVID-19 testing efforts. The FDA reissued the Policy for Coronavirus Disease-2019 Tests During the Public Health Emergency, issued a new Umbrella EUA for SARS-CoV-2 Molecular Diagnostic Tests for serial testing, and reissued the EUA for Molecular Diagnostic Tests for SARS-CoV-2 Developed and Performed by Laboratories Certified Under CLIA to Perform High Complexity Tests. The FDA also updated the FAQs on Testing for SARS-CoV-2 and revised the Enforcement Policy for Viral Transport Media During the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) Public Health Emergency. As of today, 422 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 293 molecular tests and 90 antibody and other immune response tests.

title: FDA Authorizes Marketing of Virtual Reality System for Chronic Pain Reduction
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of EaseVRx, a prescription-use immersive virtual reality system, to help patients with chronic lower back pain reduce pain through cognitive behavioral therapy and other behavioral methods. EaseVRx consists of a VR headset and controller with a "Breathing Amplifier" that directs a patient's breath toward the headset's microphone for deep breathing exercises. The device's VR program uses established principles of behavioral therapy to address physiological symptoms of pain and aid in pain relief. The FDA evaluated EaseVRx in a randomized, double-blinded clinical study of 179 participants, finding that 66% of EaseVRx participants reported a greater than 30% reduction in pain, compared to 41% of control participants. EaseVRx was granted Breakthrough Device designation and is manufactured by AppliedVR.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Updates Test Policies to Help to Ensure Accuracy and Reliability of Tests and Increase Access to At-Home Tests
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is taking several actions to increase access to accurate and reliable COVID-19 tests, particularly at-home and point-of-care diagnostic tests. The FDA has authorized over 420 tests and sample collection devices, and its recent authorizations may result in up to 400 million more over-the-counter (OTC) tests available monthly by early 2022. The FDA has also withdrawn a policy that directed not to enforce premarket review requirements for laboratory developed tests (LDTs), which will help ensure test accuracy. The agency now generally intends to focus its review on emergency use authorization (EUA) requests for at-home and point-of-care diagnostic tests, high-volume lab-based molecular diagnostic tests, and tests for which the request is from a US government stakeholder. The FDA expects newly offered COVID-19 tests, including LDTs, to have an EUA or traditional marketing authorization prior to clinical use.

title: FDA Approves Treatment for Rare Blood Disease
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Besremi (ropeginterferon alfa-2b-njft) injection to treat adults with polycythemia vera, a blood disease that causes the overproduction of red blood cells. Over 7,000 rare diseases affect more than 30 million people in the United States, with polycythemia vera affecting approximately 6,200 Americans each year. Besremi is the first FDA-approved medication for polycythemia vera that patients can take regardless of their treatment history. It is a long-acting drug taken by injection under the skin once every two weeks, and its effectiveness was evaluated in a 7.5-year trial that showed 61% of patients achieved a complete hematological response. Besremi can cause side effects such as liver enzyme elevations, low white blood cell counts, and flu-like illness. The FDA granted approval to PharmaEssentia Corporation, and Besremi received orphan drug designation, providing incentives for drug development for rare diseases.

title: FDA Provides Update on Recall of Certain Philips Respironics Breathing Assistance Machines
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is providing an update on the June 14, 2021, recall of certain Philips Respironics ventilators, CPAP, and BiPAP machines due to potential health risks related to polyester-based polyurethane foam used in the devices. The recall was initiated by Philips Respironics, which has since developed a plan to repair the foam with a different, silicone-based foam. The FDA initially approved this plan, but additional information regarding the silicone-based foam has raised concerns. The FDA has requested Philips Respironics to perform independent testing to determine potential safety risks. Until the results are available, the FDA does not recommend that patients discontinue use of their repaired devices.

title: Statement on the Intention To Nominate Dr. Robert M. Califf To Be Commissioner of Food and Drugs
body_summary: The main action is the nomination of Dr. Robert Califf to lead the Food and Drug Administration. Dr. Califf, one of the most experienced clinical trialists in the country, has strong bipartisan support, having received it in 2016. He is expected to ensure the FDA continues its science and data-driven decision-making. The nomination comes after the leadership of Dr. Janet Woodcock, who has led the agency during a busy and challenging time. The Senate is urged to swiftly confirm Dr. Califf's nomination to continue the important work at this critical moment.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: November 12, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On November 9, 2021, an updated Molecular and Antigen Home Use Test Template was posted to assist test developers. As of today, 422 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 293 molecular tests, 90 antibody tests, and 39 antigen tests. The FDA has also authorized 18 antigen tests and nine molecular tests for serial screening programs.

title: Memorandum on Maximizing Assistance To Respond to COVID-19
body_summary: The President of the United States, by authority vested in him, has ordered the following: The policy of the Administration is to combat and respond to the COVID-19 pandemic with the full capacity and capability of the Federal Government. The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) is authorized to provide a 100 percent Federal cost share for all work eligible for assistance under Public Assistance Category B, pursuant to the Stafford Act, including work related to the Governors' use of the National Guard from January 20, 2020, through April 1, 2022.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: November 5, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) authorized an over-the-counter (OTC) COVID-19 test, theiHealth COVID-19 Antigen Rapid Test, on November 5, 2021, for people 15 years and older or 2 years and older with an adult's assistance. The test delivers results in 15 minutes and can be used for serial testing over three days. The FDA also authorized the use of two additional batches of the Janssen COVID-19 Vaccine manufactured at the Emergent facility on November 5, 2021. Additionally, the FDA cleared the first 510(k) for the BioFire COVID-19 Test 2, a molecular diagnostic test, on November 1, 2021, which has been offered under an EUA since March 2020.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Provides New Draft Guidance on Premarket Submissions for Device Software Functions
body_summary: The FDA is publishing a draft guidance on regulatory considerations for device software functions. Director Bakul Patel states that the guidance aims to provide clarity, simplicity, and harmonization with current best practices. The draft guidance, titled "Content of Premarket Submissions for Device Software Functions," pertains to device software functions, including software in medical devices and software as a medical device. It describes recommended documentation for premarket submissions, intended to provide information on documentation to be included in submissions for the FDA's evaluation of safety and effectiveness. The draft guidance will replace an existing guidance issued in 2005 and will be published as part of the FDA's commitment to publish a revised version as part of the MDUFA IV Digital Health commitments.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The Federal Reserve is committed to using its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals. With progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have continued to strengthen. The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic have improved in recent months, but the summer's rise in COVID-19 cases has slowed their recovery. Inflation is elevated, largely reflecting factors that are expected to be transitory. Supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic and the reopening of the economy have contributed to sizable price increases in some sectors. Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses. The path of the economy continues to depend on the course of the virus. Progress on vaccinations and an easing of supply constraints are expected to support continued gains in economic activity and employment as well as a reduction in inflation. Risks to the economic outlook remain. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. With inflation having run persistently below this longer-run goal, the Committee will aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time so that inflation averages 2 percent over time and longerâterm inflation expectations remain well anchored at 2 percent. The Committee expects to maintain an accommodative stance of monetary policy until these outcomes are achieved. The Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time. In light of the substantial further progress the economy has made toward the Committee's goals since last December, the Committee decided to begin reducing the monthly pace of its net asset purchases by $10 billion for Treasury securities and $5 billion for agency mortgage-backed securities. Beginning later this month, the Committee will increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $70 billion per month and of agency mortgageâbacked securities by at least $35 billion per month. Beginning in December, the Committee will increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $60 billion per month and of agency mortgage-backed securities by at least $30 billion per month. The Committee judges that similar reductions in the pace of net asset purchases will likely be appropriate each month, but it is prepared to adjust the pace of purchases if warranted by changes in the economic outlook. The Federal Reserve's ongoing purchases and holdings of securities will continue to foster smooth market functioning and accommodative financial conditions, thereby supporting the flow of credit to households and businesses. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Mary C. Daly; Charles L. Evans; Randal K. Quarles; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: Implementation Note issued November 3, 2021
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on November 3, 2021: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 0.15 percent, effective November 4, 2021. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective November 4, 2021, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 0 to 1/4 percent. Complete the increase in System Open Market Account (SOMA) holdings of Treasury securities by $80 billion and of agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) by $40 billion, as indicated in the monthly purchase plans released in mid-October. Increase the SOMA holdings of Treasury securities by $70 billion and of agency MBS by $35 billion, during the monthly purchase period beginning in mid-November. Increase the SOMA holdings of Treasury securities by $60 billion and of agency MBS by $30 billion, during the monthly purchase period beginning in mid-December. Increase holdings of Treasury securities and agency MBS by additional amounts as needed to sustain smooth functioning of markets for these securities. Conduct overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 0.25 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion; the aggregate operation limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 0.05 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities and reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS in agency MBS. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for purchases and reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 0.25 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: November 2, 2021
body_summary: The US FDA announced several actions in its ongoing response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On October 22, it deemed two lots of AstraZeneca vaccine drug substance manufactured at the Emergent facility in Baltimore, Maryland, acceptable for potential export. The FDA also reissued an emergency use authorization for the OraSure Technologies InteliSwab COVID-19 Rapid Test, allowing its use without a prescription for people with COVID-19 symptoms, serial testing for people without symptoms, and self-collected nasal swab samples. The FDA has authorized 421 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 293 molecular tests, 90 antibody tests, and 38 antigen tests.

title: Statement on the 2022 Open Enrollment Period for Health Insurance Marketplace
body_summary: Health care should be a right, not a privilege, for all Americans. With the open enrollment period starting on healthcare.gov, Americans can gain quality, affordable health coverage from January 15, 2022. Signing up is easy, with options available through the Affordable Care Act, and a range of plans for those not receiving coverage through their employer. Since taking office, nearly 3 million more Americans gained access to health coverage during the special enrollment period. The Department of Health and Human Services is quadrupling staff to help families navigate their options, reaching more people in additional languages. The Build Back Better framework will expand affordable health care, reducing premiums for over 9 million Americans, delivering coverage to 4 million uninsured people, and expanding Medicare for affordable hearing care. Americans are urged to visit healthcare.gov to renew or shop for a plan, and Congress is urged to send the framework to the President's desk as soon as possible.

title: FDA Authorizes Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine for Emergency Use in Children 5 through 11 Years of Age
body_summary: The US FDA has authorized the emergency use of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine for children aged 5-11, based on data from independent advisory committee experts. The vaccine was found to be 90.7% effective in preventing COVID-19 in this age group, with comparable immune responses to those of individuals 16-25 years of age. The vaccine's safety was studied in approximately 3,100 children, showing no serious side effects. The FDA also authorized a manufacturing change for Pfizer's COVID-19 vaccine to include a new formulation with Tris buffer, maintaining stability and pH levels at refrigerated temperatures.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: October 29, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On October 22, 2021, Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock and Director Peter Marks discussed expanding the use of single booster doses for COVID-19 vaccines, including Moderna and Janssen vaccines. The FDA also clarified the use of Pfizer-BioNTech's single booster dose and authorized mixed-and-matched booster doses for eligible individuals. The agency is investigating imported medical gloves and recommends avoiding them. The FDA authorized its 11th over-the-counter COVID-19 test and issued an emergency use authorization for a new diagnostic test. As of today, 421 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under emergency use authorizations, including 293 molecular tests, 90 antibody tests, and 38 antigen tests.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Collaborates with Health Canada and UK’s MHRA to Foster Good Machine Learning Practice
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration, Health Canada, and the UK's Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency jointly issued guiding principles for Good Machine Learning Practice (GMLP) in medical device development. The principles aim to advance high-quality artificial intelligence/machine learning enabled medical device development. The guiding principles were developed by the International Medical Device Regulators Forum, international standards organizations, and other collaborative bodies. The FDA's Digital Health Center of Excellence collaborated with international public health partners, including Health Canada and the MHRA, to inform the development of these principles. The guidance aims to support the development and maturation of GMLP, with the potential to significantly improve patient care and transform healthcare.

title: FDA Strengthens Safety Requirements and Updates Study Results for Breast Implants
body_summary: The US FDA has taken new actions to strengthen breast implant risk communication and help patients make informed decisions. The agency issued orders restricting the sale and distribution of breast implants to ensure patients receive adequate risk information. New labeling for all legally marketed breast implants has been approved, including a boxed warning, patient decision checklist, and updated silicone gel-filled breast implant rupture screening recommendations. The FDA has also released updated information on the status of breast implant manufacturer post-approval studies. The agency will continue to use its full authorities to ensure the post-market safety of medical products.
