title: FDA, NIH, and 15 private organizations join forces to increase effective gene therapies for rare diseases
body_summary: The US FDA, NIH, 10 pharmaceutical companies, and 5 non-profit organizations have partnered to develop gene therapies for the 30 million Americans suffering from rare diseases through the Bespoke Gene Therapy Consortium (BGTC). The initiative aims to optimize gene therapy development and support 4-6 clinical trials for rare diseases, employing different types of AAV vectors. The BGTC is part-managed by the Foundation for the National Institutes of Health and will receive $76 million in funding over five years. The NIH and private partners will contribute to supporting BGTC-funded projects.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: October 26, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA has authorized the 10th over-the-counter (OTC) COVID-19 test, reissued the emergency use authorization (EUA) for another OTC COVID-19 test, and updated the EUA templates for test developers. The FDA has issued an EUA for the Celltrion DiaTrust COVID-19 Ag Home Test and reissued the EUA for the Quidel QuickVue At-Home OTC COVID-19 Test. The test for the Celltrion DiaTrust COVID-19 Ag Home Test can be used without a healthcare provider prescription, while the Quidel QuickVue At-Home OTC COVID-19 Test can be used with or without symptoms. As of today, 420 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Makes Progress on Efforts to Understand Presence of Asbestos in Cosmetic Products
body_summary: The FDA has conducted a year-long sampling assignment to test talc-containing cosmetic products for the presence of asbestos. The results show that all 50 samples assessed were negative for asbestos. The agency will conduct another sampling assignment in 2022, selecting 50 additional samples for testing, and will communicate any results indicating the presence of asbestos. The next survey results will be released next year. The FDA is committed to protecting consumers from contaminated cosmetic products and will take prompt action to inform the public and work with companies to remove products containing asbestos from the market.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Makes Progress on Efforts to Understand Presence of Asbestos in Cosmetic Products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has tested 50 talc-containing cosmetic products for the presence of asbestos, with all samples found negative. This follows a year-long sampling assignment and the development of standardized testing methods for asbestos in talc by an interagency working group. The FDA will conduct another sampling assignment in 2022 and communicate any results indicating asbestos presence. The results of the next survey will be released next year.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: October 22, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA began posting materials for the next Vaccine and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee meeting on October 26. The committee will discuss amending Pfizer-BioNTech's Emergency Use Authorization for their COVID-19 vaccine to children 5 through 11 years of age. On October 19, the FDA approved an abbreviated new drug application for succinylcholine chloride injection, indicated to facilitate tracheal intubation and skeletal muscle relaxation during surgery or mechanical ventilation. The FDA has authorized 419 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 292 molecular tests, 89 antibody and immune response tests, and 38 antigen tests.

title: Federal Judge Enters Consent Decree with Utah-based Dietary Supplement Manufacturer
body_summary: A federal court has ordered a dietary supplement manufacturer, Grandma's Herbs, Inc., and its two owners, Kevin R. Parr and Tracey Parr, to stop selling products until they come into compliance with federal regulations. The U.S. District Court for the District of Utah has entered a consent decree of permanent injunction. The FDA has not approved Grandma's Herbs' products for any use, despite claims that they can diagnose, cure, or treat serious illnesses. The consent decree prohibits the defendants from manufacturing or distributing products with such claims until requirements are met. The FDA had previously warned the company in 2017, stating that many products are not dietary supplements but unapproved new and misbranded drugs. The consent decree requires Grandma's Herbs, Inc. to hire a labeling expert, remove violative labeling, and receive FDA permission to resume operations. The U.S. Department of Justice filed the complaint on behalf of the FDA.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Takes Additional Actions on the Use of a Booster Dose for COVID-19 Vaccines
body_summary: The US FDA has expanded the use of a booster dose for COVID-19 vaccines, allowing a single booster dose for eligible populations. This includes a single booster dose of the Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine for individuals 65 years and older, as well as those at high risk of severe COVID-19, and a single booster dose of the Janssen (Johnson and Johnson) COVID-19 Vaccine for individuals 18 years and older. Additionally, "mix and match" booster doses can be administered for any available COVID-19 vaccine, with the same dosing intervals as the primary vaccine.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Announces Investigation of Salmonella Outbreak Linked to Whole, Fresh Onions
body_summary: The FDA, CDC, and state partners are investigating a multistate outbreak of Salmonella Oranienburg infections linked to whole, fresh onions. The FDA's traceback investigation has identified ProSource Inc. as a source of potentially contaminated onions imported from Mexico, which has resulted in 652 illnesses. The FDA advises restaurants, retailers, and consumers not to eat, sell, or serve red, yellow, and white onions supplied by ProSource Inc. from July 1 through August 27, or products containing these onions. ProSource Inc. has agreed to a voluntary recall. An additional supplier, Keeler Family Farms, has also been identified, and both companies have agreed to voluntary recalls. Consumers should ask if the onions being served or sold were recalled or supplied by these companies.

title: FDA Permits Marketing of New Oral Tobacco Products through Premarket Tobacco Product Application Pathway
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of four new oral tobacco products by U.S. Smokeless Tobacco Company LLC under the brand name Verve. The FDA determined that marketing these products would be consistent with the statutory standard for public health protection, based on data showing they are unlikely to initiate or reinitiate tobacco use among youth, nonsmokers, and former smokers. The approved products are Verve Discs Blue Mint, Verve Discs Green Mint, Verve Chews Blue Mint, and Verve Chews Green Mint. Mitch Zeller, FDA director of the Center for Tobacco Products, stated that the products are intended for adult tobacco users and may help addicted smokers switch to products with potentially fewer harmful chemicals. The FDA is placing stringent marketing restrictions on Verve products and requires the company to report on consumer research studies, advertising, and sales data.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: October 19, 2021
body_summary: The US FDA has announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On Oct. 12, the FDA approved propofol injectable emulsion for single patient-use vials as an intravenous general anesthetic and sedation drug. The agency has also updated recall classifications for the Alinity m SARS-CoV-2 AMP Kit and Alinity m Resp-4-Plex AMP Kits to correct software issues. As of today, the FDA has authorized 418 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 292 molecular tests, 89 antibody tests, and 37 antigen tests.

title: FDA Approves Cyltezo, the First Interchangeable Biosimilar to Humira
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Cyltezo (adalimumab-adbm), the first interchangeable biosimilar product for certain inflammatory diseases. Cyltezo is both biosimilar to and interchangeable with Humira (adalimumab) for its approved uses. The approval of Cyltezo facilitates access to treatments for serious health conditions. It is approved for treating moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis, active psoriatic arthritis, and other conditions. The FDA approved Cyltezo on October 15, 2021, and it is offered in a single-dose, pre-filled glass syringe.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: 10/15/21
body_summary: The US FDA continued its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On October 12, the FDA posted an assessment of the Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) process, conducted by Booz Allen Hamilton. The assessment focused on EUA request processing, review times, test accuracy, and reliability. The Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition published a constituent update encouraging vaccination against influenza and COVID-19. As of today, 418 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under EUAs, including 292 molecular tests, 89 antibody tests, and 37 antigen tests.

title: FDA to Hold Advisory Committee Meeting to Discuss Merck and Ridgeback’s EUA Application for COVID-19 Oral Treatment
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is announcing an upcoming meeting of its Antimicrobial Drugs Advisory Committee (AMDAC) to discuss Merck and Ridgeback's request for an emergency use authorization (EUA) for molnupiravir, an investigational antiviral drug to treat COVID-19. The committee will meet on November 30 to discuss the available data supporting the use of molnupiravir to treat mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in adults who have tested positive for COVID-19 and are at high risk for progression to severe COVID-19. The FDA is evaluating the safety and effectiveness data submitted by Merck and Ridgeback, and director Patrizia Cavazzoni stated that a public discussion with the advisory committee will help ensure clear understanding of the scientific data. The meeting will include presentations from the company, the FDA's perspective, and an open public hearing where the public can provide comments.

title: FDA Awards 11 Grants to Clinical Trials to Develop New Medical Products for Rare Disease Treatments
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has awarded 11 new clinical trial research grants totaling over $25 million for the next four years. The grants support the development of medical products for patients with rare diseases. The grants will fund studies of products addressing unmet needs in rare diseases or providing significant improvements in treatment or diagnosis. The studies include those for children, such as one evaluating the treatment of a rare inherited skin disease, and another evaluating early treatment for infants with tuberous sclerosis complex. The grants also include an innovative demonstration project to evaluate a tool improving data accuracy for clinical trials. The grants will be awarded to institutions including Armgo Pharma, Boston Children's Hospital, Castle Creek Biosciences, Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center, Duke University, Massachusetts General Hospital, Mayo Clinic Rochester, Reveragen Biopharma, and University of Florida.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary:
A Federal Open Market Committee meeting was held by videoconference on September 21-22, 2021. The committee discussed financial market developments, including domestic conditions remaining highly accommodative despite concerns about COVID-19's Delta variant. Median respondents marked down GDP growth and revised up inflation projections this year.

The staff's economic outlook for the US was broadly similar to the July projection, with real GDP expected to post a sizable gain in the second half of 2021 and over the year as a whole. The unemployment rate was projected to decline to historically low levels. The staff continued to expect that this year's rise in inflation would be transitory, but supply constraints were putting upward pressure on prices, leading to a projected increase in PCE price inflation.

The labor market is expected to continue improving, with some participants noting that the labor force participation rate may lag behind other indicators. Firms are experiencing difficulty hiring workers, leading to reduced hours and production, as well as incentives like wage increases and bonuses.

Participants discussed slowing down asset purchases, with an illustrative path featuring monthly reductions by $10 billion in Treasury securities and $5 billion in agency mortgage-backed securities. The Committee decided to characterize inflation as "elevated" instead of stating it had "risened". They also agreed that if progress toward maximum-employment and price-stability goals continued, a moderation in asset purchases may soon be warranted.

title: To Improve Nutrition and Reduce the Burden of Disease, FDA Issues Food Industry Guidance for Voluntarily Reducing Sodium in Processed and Packaged Foods
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is issuing a final guidance to provide voluntary short-term sodium reduction targets for food manufacturers, chain restaurants, and food service operators. The targets aim to decrease average sodium intake from approximately 3,400 milligrams to 3,000 milligrams per day, a 12% reduction, over the next 2.5 years. This guidance is part of the agency's whole-of-government approach to nutrition and health, aiming to address preventable diet-related chronic diseases and advance health equity.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: October 12, 2021
body_summary: The US FDA has announced that it intends to withdraw guidance documents on temporary policies for manufacturers to produce alcohol-based hand sanitizers and alcohol. Effective December 31, 2021, companies must cease production of these products. Hand sanitizers manufactured before or on December 31, 2021, must no longer be sold to wholesalers or retailers by March 31, 2022. The FDA has authorized 416 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 291 molecular tests, 88 antibody tests, and 35 antigen tests.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Withdrawing Temporary Guidances for Alcohol-Based Hand Sanitizers
body_summary: The FDA has announced its intention to withdraw temporary guidances for manufacturers producing certain alcohol-based hand sanitizers, effective December 31, 2021. The agency has determined that the supply of hand sanitizers from traditional suppliers has increased, making the temporary policies no longer necessary. Manufacturers who were eligible for these temporary policies must cease production of these products after December 31, 2021. Those who wish to continue producing hand sanitizer must comply with applicable requirements, including the FDA's Current Good Manufacturing Practice requirements. Manufacturers who no longer plan to produce these products can deregister by following the Electronic Drug Registration and Listing Instructionspage.

title: FDA Permits Marketing of E-Cigarette Products, Marking First Authorization of Its Kind by the Agency
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of three new tobacco products, including Vuse Solo closed ENDS devices and tobacco-flavored e-liquid pods, through the Premarket Tobacco Product Application (PMTA) pathway. The authorization allows these products to be legally sold in the US, but also imposes strict marketing restrictions, including digital and radio advertising restrictions, to reduce youth exposure. The FDA determined that the products meet the standard for the protection of public health, as they are less toxic than combusted cigarettes and may benefit adult smokers who switch to these products. The agency is still evaluating applications for other flavored products, including menthol-flavored products, and will continue to monitor the marketing of these products.

title: FDA Approves Innovative Treatment for Pediatric Patients with Congenital Athymia
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Rethymic for the treatment of pediatric patients with congenital athymia, a rare immune disorder. Rethymic is the first thymus tissue product approved in the US, composed of human allogeneic thymus tissue that is processed and cultured, and then implanted to help reconstitute immunity. The approval was granted to Enzyvant Therapeutics, Inc. The safety and efficacy of Rethymic were established in clinical studies involving 105 patients, aged one month to 16 years, who received a single administration of Rethymic from 1993 to 2020. Rethymic improved survival rates, reduced infection frequency and severity, and is not indicated for patients with severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID).

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: October 8, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued a safety communication on October 5, alerting users of the potential for false positive results from certain lots of the Ellume COVID-19 Home Test due to a manufacturing issue. The FDA is working with Ellume to address the issue and ensure it is resolved. The FDA has authorized over 415 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 290 molecular tests, 89 antibody tests, and 36 antigen tests, as of October 5.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Warns Public and Health Care Professionals Not to Use Needle-free Devices for Injection of Dermal Fillers
body_summary: The FDA is warning the public and healthcare professionals not to use needle-free devices for injection of hyaluronic acid or other lip and facial fillers. The devices, marketed as Hyaluron Pens, Hyla-Pen, microinjectors, and others, have not been approved by the FDA. The FDA's priority is protecting patients from serious adverse events, including permanent damage to the skin, lips, and eyes. Binita Ashar, M.D., director of the Office of Surgical and Infection Control Devices, stated that these devices are often sold online, bypassing consultation with a licensed healthcare provider. The FDA is monitoring online platforms and alerting the public to the dangers of using unapproved products, some of which may be irreversible.

title: FDA Issues Final Order and Guidance on Surgical Staplers and Staples for Internal Use
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced several actions related to surgical staplers and staples, aiming to increase their safe use. According to William Maisel, M.D., M.P.H., chief medical officer, the agency is regulating these devices to ensure they are safe to use. The FDA has reclassified surgical staplers for internal use from Class I to Class II, requiring premarket review and special controls to mitigate known risks. This change will subject these devices to more stringent regulatory requirements, including premarket notification and special controls. The agency has also issued final guidance on labeling recommendations for manufacturers of surgical staplers and staples for internal use. An updated letter to health care providers was issued to alert professionals to the safe and effective use of these devices. The FDA's actions follow an analysis of medical device reports, which found that improper use and function of the staplers were the primary causes of adverse effects.

title: FDA Announces Signing of Domestic Mutual Reliance Agreements with California, Florida, Utah and Wisconsin
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced that California, Florida, Utah, and Wisconsin have entered into domestic mutual reliance agreements with the agency. These agreements aim to reduce human foodborne illness outbreaks, reduce duplication of regulatory oversight, and increase public health protection by focusing on areas of higher risk. According to Erik Mettler, assistant commissioner for partnerships and policy in the FDA's Office of Regulatory Affairs, foodborne illness outbreaks are largely preventable but can have devastating consequences. The FDA is committed to keeping Americans safe through these partnerships, which will strengthen the agency's relationship with state regulatory partners and improve industry compliance with applicable food safety requirements. The agreements will facilitate data sharing, risk prioritization, inspections, and outbreak investigations among other key focus areas. The FDA will also leverage work from other regulatory programs to identify needs and build quality management systems.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Warns Firms for Continuing to Market E-cigarette Products After Agency Denied Authorizations
body_summary: The FDA has issued warning letters to 20 companies for continuing to unlawfully market electronic nicotine delivery system (ENDS) products that are subject to Marketing Denial Orders. The FDA has also issued warning letters for one company that received a Refuse to File determination and six companies that did not submit any premarket applications. These 28 companies have listed over 600,000 products with the FDA. As of September 23, the FDA has issued 323 MDOs, accounting for over 1,167,000 flavored ENDS products. The FDA will prioritize enforcement against companies marketing ENDS products without authorization, especially those with a likelihood of youth use or initiation.

title: FDA Revises Hospital and Health System Compounding Guidance to Help Preserve Patient Access to Compounded Drugs
body_summary: The FDA is revising its draft guidance to preserve access to compounded drugs for patients whose medical needs cannot be met by an FDA-approved drug. The revised policy removes the one-mile radius provision and proposes a two-part compliance policy. The policy describes circumstances under which the agency generally does not intend to take action against hospital or health system pharmacies that compound and distribute drugs without a valid patient-specific prescription. These circumstances include administering compounded drugs only to patients within the hospital or health system and using or discarding the drugs within 24 hours of leaving the pharmacy. The revised draft guidance outlines the FDA's intention to take a risk-based approach to enforcement, considering factors such as poor compounding practices, lack of sterility assurance, and interstate distribution of non-patient-specific compounded drugs. The agency encourages hospitals and health systems to have procedures in place to obtain non-patient-specific compounded drugs from outsourcing facilities and to consider registering their pharmacies as outsourcing facilities.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: October 5, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On September 28, the FDA issued a warning letter to Strategia Project Management, Inc. for selling an unapproved product with unproven COVID-19 claims. The FDA has authorized 414 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 289 molecular tests, 89 antibody tests, and 36 antigen tests. These include 65 molecular authorizations and one antibody authorization for use with home-collected samples. The FDA has also authorized revisions to EUA authorizations and specified that consumers concerned about COVID-19 should consult with their healthcare provider.

title: FDA Finalizes Two Foundational Rules for Companies Seeking to Market New Tobacco Products
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued two final rules for the premarket review of new tobacco products. The PMTA final rule provides additional information on the requirements for the content, format, and review of Premarket Tobacco Product Applications (PMTAs) and Substantial Equivalence (SE) Reports. The final rule describes the information an applicant must include in a PMTA for the FDA to complete a substantive review of an application, including requirements for submitting application amendments, the time for review, and withdrawal of applications.

The SE final rule provides additional information on the requirements for the content and format of SE reports, allowing for greater predictability and efficiency for all stakeholders. It addresses the FDA's communications with the applicant, the retention of records that support the SE report, confidentiality of an SE report, and how an applicant can amend or withdraw an SE report.

The rules are effective on November 4, and applications submitted through these pathways must meet the requirements described in these final rules. The PMTA final rule was finalized after receiving and reviewing comments during the public comment period, and the SE final rule provides additional information on the requirements for SE reports.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Additional OTC Home Test to Increase Access to Rapid Testing for Consumers
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued an emergency use authorization for the ACON Laboratories FlowflexCOVID-19 Home Test, an over-the-counter COVID-19 antigen test. This authorization is part of the FDA's efforts to increase the availability of accurately reliable OTC tests to meet public health needs. The test, which does not require serial testing, is expected to double rapid at-home testing capacity in the U.S. over the next several weeks, with the manufacturer planning to produce more than 100 million tests per month by year-end and 200 million by February 2022. The FDA has authorized over 400 COVID-19 tests and sample collection devices, prioritizing at-home diagnostic tests due to their public health importance.

title: FDA to Hold Advisory Committee Meetings to Discuss Emergency Use Authorization for Booster Doses and COVID-19 Vaccines for Younger Children
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is announcing two upcoming meetings of its Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee to discuss newly available data for the currently available COVID-19 vaccines. On October 14 and 15, the advisory committee will meet to discuss the use of booster doses of the Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine and the Janssen COVID-19 Vaccine, both authorized for emergency use to prevent COVID-19 in individuals 18 years of age and older. The committee will also hear presentations and discuss the use of a booster of a different vaccine than the one used for the primary series. Peter Marks, director of the FDA's Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, stated that it's critical to evaluate the information on the use of booster doses in various populations. The FDA anticipates receiving a request from Pfizer to amend its emergency use authorization to allow the use of its COVID-19 vaccine in children 5 through 11 years of age, and will schedule an advisory committee meeting on October 26 to inform the agency's decision-making.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: October 1, 2021
body_summary: The FDA announced authorization of a single booster dose of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine for certain populations. On Sep. 29, the FDA authorized an emergency use authorization for one additional batch of the Janssen COVID-19 vaccine manufactured at the Emergent facility, bringing the total number of authorized batches to nine. The FDA conducted a thorough review of facility records and quality testing and concluded that these batches are suitable for use. Testing updates include 412 authorized tests and sample collection devices, including 289 molecular tests, 88 antibody tests, and 35 antigen tests. The FDA has authorized 16 antigen tests and eight molecular tests for serial screening programs and 641 revisions to EUA authorizations.

title: Federal officials seize spices and food additive products held under insanitary conditions from a Florida warehouse
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced a mass seizure of FDA-regulated spices and food additive products held for sale under insanitary conditions at Lyden Spice Corporation in Miami, Florida. The seizure was completed today, resulting in over 25,000 boxes/bags of bulk ready-to-eat spices and food additives, including monosodium glutamate, crushed red chili, and sesame seeds, being seized. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that the FDA will continue to take action against those who threaten the safety and quality of regulated products. An inspection conducted by the FDA between June 8 and June 28, 2021, revealed insanitary conditions, including rodent feces, rodent gnawing, and live and dead insects, leading to the complaint being filed with the U.S. Department of Justice.

title: FDA Clears First Major Imaging Device Advancement for Computed Tomography in Nearly a Decade
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has cleared the Siemens NAEOTOM Alpha, a new technological improvement for Computed Tomography (CT) imaging. The device uses photon-counting detectors, which measure individual X-ray photons, allowing for more detailed information and improved image quality. This marks the first major new technology for CT imaging in nearly a decade. The FDA granted clearance through the 510(k) premarket clearance pathway, demonstrating the device's substantial equivalence to a legally marketed predicate device. The device is designed to transform X-ray photons into 3-dimensional images, aiding in diagnosis, treatment preparation, and radiation therapy planning.

title: Youth E-cigarette Use Remains Serious Public Health Concern Amid COVID-19 Pandemic
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention have released a study estimating that over 2 million U.S. middle and high school students reported using e-cigarettes in 2021. The 2021 National Youth Tobacco Survey found that 11.3% of high school students and 2.8% of middle school students reported current e-cigarette use. Flavored e-cigarettes were used by 84.7% of e-cigarette users, with fruit, candy, and mint flavors being the most common. The study also found that 43.6% of high school students and 17.2% of middle school students reported using e-cigarettes on 20 or more days in the past 30 days. The FDA has taken action against companies selling flavored e-cigarette products to youth, with over 1 million premarket applications denied since 2020.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Warns Consumers of Risk of Exposure to Unsafe Levels of Radiation with Safe-T-Lite UV WAND
body_summary: The FDA is warning consumers that using the Safe-T-Lite UV WAND, a handheld ultraviolet-C (UV-C) germicidal wand, may put users at risk of exposure to unsafe levels of UV-C radiation and cause injury to the skin, eyes, or both after a few seconds of exposure. The product emits a level of radiation more than 3,000 times faster than the international ultraviolet exposure limit and is intended to be held in the hand for 30 to 60 seconds. The FDA advises consumers to use alternative disinfectant methods and will continue to monitor the issue.

title: FDA Takes Steps Aimed at Improving Quality, Safety and Efficacy of Sunscreens
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has proposed revisions to the requirements for over-the-counter (OTC) sunscreens, aiming to improve their quality, safety, and efficacy. The proposed updates include maximum SPF values, active ingredients, broad spectrum requirements, and product labeling. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that sun safety is important for everyone, regardless of skin tone, and that Americans can reduce risks from sun exposure with continued use of broad spectrum sunscreen with SPF values of at least 15.

The proposed order builds upon the 2020 Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security (CARES) Act, which reformed and modernized the regulation of sunscreens marketed without approved applications. The deemed final order for sunscreens, established by the CARES Act, sets requirements for active ingredients, labeling, and effectiveness.

The proposed order proposes to update the GRASE status for 16 active ingredients, expands GRASE status to include oils, lotions, creams, gels, butters, pastes, ointments, and sticks, and introduces GRASE status for spray sunscreens, subject to testing and labeling requirements. The order also aims to ensure consumers have access to sunscreens with adequate UVA protection and proposes updates to labeling to make key product information easier to identify.

The FDA will consider comments on the proposed order during a 45-day public comment period before issuing a revised final order. The effective date for the revised final order cannot be earlier than one year after its issuance.

title: Implementation Note issued September 22, 2021
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on September 22, 2021: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 0.15 percent, effective September 23, 2021. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective September 23, 2021, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 0 to 1/4 percent. Increase the System Open Market Account holdings of Treasury securities by $80 billion per month and of agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) by $40 billion per month. Increase holdings of Treasury securities and agency MBS by additional amounts and purchase agency commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) as needed to sustain smooth functioning of markets for these securities. Conduct overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 0.25 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion; the aggregate operation limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 0.05 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $160 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities and reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS in agency MBS. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for purchases and reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 0.25 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The Federal Reserve is committed to using its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals. With progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have continued to strengthen. The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic have improved in recent months, but the rise in COVID-19 cases has slowed their recovery. Inflation is elevated, largely reflecting transitory factors. Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses. The path of the economy continues to depend on the course of the virus. Progress on vaccinations will likely continue to reduce the effects of the public health crisis on the economy, but risks to the economic outlook remain. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. With inflation having run persistently below this longer-run goal, the Committee will aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time so that inflation averages 2 percent over time and longerâterm inflation expectations remain well anchored at 2 percent. The Committee expects to maintain an accommodative stance of monetary policy until these outcomes are achieved. The Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time. Last December, the Committee indicated that it would continue to increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $80 billion per month and of agency mortgageâbacked securities by at least $40 billion per month until substantial further progress has been made toward its maximum employment and price stability goals. Since then, the economy has made progress toward these goals. If progress continues broadly as expected, the Committee judges that a moderation in the pace of asset purchases may soon be warranted. These asset purchases help foster smooth market functioning and accommodative financial conditions, thereby supporting the flow of credit to households and businesses. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Mary C. Daly; Charles L. Evans; Randal K. Quarles; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Publishes Material Safety Data to Promote Safer, More Effective Medical Devices
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) partnered with ECRI to study and publish safety profiles for materials commonly used in implantable medical devices. The goal is to improve the safety of medical devices through the use of safer materials and preventing patients from receiving devices that contain materials that could cause an adverse response. The FDA and ECRI conducted a comprehensive literature search and systematic review to identify the current state of knowledge about medical device material performance after implantation. The first four reports on magnesium, polypropylene, polyurethanes, and siloxanes are available now on the FDA website. This is an ongoing effort, and the FDA will release new reports as they become available.

title: FDA Issues Draft Guidance on Donor Eligibility and Manufacturing of Cellular Therapies for Animals
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has issued two draft guidance documents for public comment on good manufacturing practice requirements for animal cells, tissues, and cell- and tissue-based products. These documents aim to support the development of promising products that can benefit animal health. Dr. Janet Woodcock, Acting Commissioner of the FDA, stated that the goal is to help manufacturers be successful in their efforts to develop innovative products.

The draft guidance documents cover two topics: Good Manufacturing Practices for Animal Cells, Tissues, and Cell- and Tissue-Based Products (#253) and Donor Eligibility for Animal Cells, Tissues, and Cell- and Tissue-Based Products (#254). The documents provide recommendations for manufacturers to meet requirements for good manufacturing practice, including methods for preventing contamination and ensuring quality.

The FDA is accepting public comments on both draft guidance documents until November 22, 2021, and will host a webinar later this year to discuss the documents with all interested stakeholders.

title: FDA Authorizes Booster Dose of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine for Certain Populations
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) amended the emergency use authorization (EUA) for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine to allow for use of a single booster dose, to be administered at least six months after completion of the primary series, in individuals 65 years of age and older, individuals 18 through 64 years of age at high risk of severe COVID-19, and individuals 18 through 64 years of age whose frequent institutional or occupational exposure to SARS-CoV-2 puts them at high risk of serious complications of COVID-19. 

The FDA considered the totality of the available scientific evidence and analyzed safety and immune response data from a subset of participants from the original clinical trial of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine. The agency also evaluated real-world data on the vaccine's efficacy over a sustained period of time provided by U.S. and international sources.

The booster dose is authorized for administration to these individuals at least six months following completion of their primary series and may be given at any point after that time. The FDA-authorized Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine is the same formulation as the FDA-approved Comirnaty and the vaccines may be used interchangeably.

The amendment to the EUA to include a single booster dose was granted to Pfizer Inc. on August 23, following a public meeting of the FDA's Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee (VRBPAC) on September 17, and consideration of the data submitted by the vaccine manufacturer.

title: FDA Authorizes Software that Can Help Identify Prostate Cancer
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has authorized the marketing of Paige Prostate, an artificial intelligence-based software designed to assist pathologists in detecting areas of concern on prostate biopsy images that may harbor cancer. The software, developed by Paige.AI, is intended to be used as an adjunct to the review of digitally-scanned slide images. According to the FDA, Paige Prostate improved detection of cancer on individual slide images by 7.3% on average when compared to pathologists' unassisted reads. The software is compatible with digitized slide images and can be used with a slide image viewer. The FDA evaluated data from a clinical study where 16 pathologists examined 527 slide images of prostate biopsies, including 171 cancer and 356 benign samples. The software has been authorized under the De Novo premarket review pathway, a regulatory pathway for low- to moderate-risk devices of a new type.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Posts an Initial Batch of Four Deemed Final Administrative Orders for Over-the-Counter Drugs
body_summary: The FDA, under the direction of Theresa M. Michele, will post deemed final administrative orders for OTC drugs as part of the OTC Monograph Reform under the CARES Act. These orders, established by the CARES Act, took effect on its enactment date. The first four deemed final orders include products for nighttime sleep-aid, antiflatulent, topical otic, and corn and callus removers. The orders will be publicly posted on the FDA's new web portal, OTC Monographs@FDA, allowing public search and updates on proposed and final rules. The FDA is committed to promoting innovation in the OTC marketplace and ensuring the safety and effectiveness of OTC monograph drugs.

title: Federal Court Enters Consent Decree Against Florida Compounder, Prohibiting Manufacture and Distribution of Drugs Due to Insanitary Conditions
body_summary: The U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida has entered a consent decree of permanent injunction against Premier Pharmacy Labs Inc., prohibiting the company from producing or distributing any drugs until it complies with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) and other requirements. The U.S. Department of Justice, on behalf of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), filed a complaint alleging that Premier Pharmacy manufactured and distributed drugs made under insanitary conditions at its facility, despite multiple warnings from the FDA. The FDA's Office of Compliance director, Donald D. Ashley, stated that Premier Pharmacy and its owner, Vern A. Allen, placed patients at significant risk. The consent decree requires Premier Pharmacy to not engage in compounding operations or distribution until it completes corrective actions and establishes a comprehensive quality control system, subject to FDA authorization.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: September 17, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On September 17, the FDA issued a letter to healthcare providers warning about potential false positive results with Abbott Alinity m SARS-CoV-2 AMP and Alinity m Resp-4-Plex AMP Kits. The FDA revised the Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for bamlanivimab and etesevimab administered together to include post-exposure prophylaxis for adults and pediatric patients at high risk of severe COVID-19. The FDA has approved one vaccine and authorized others to prevent COVID-19 and serious clinical outcomes. On September 15, the FDA issued a revised guidance for the enforcement of face masks and barrier face coverings during the public health emergency. The FDA also authorized the use of two additional batches of the Janssen COVID-19 vaccine manufactured at the Emergent facility.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Hosts Third Summit Focused on Reducing the Availability of Opioids Online
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) hosted its thirdOnline Opioid Summit, "Reducing the Availability of Opioids Online," on September 9, 2021. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock emphasized the ongoing national public health emergency of the opioid crisis, which continues to affect nearly every community. The summit aimed to include stakeholders from various sectors in the conversation to find innovative solutions to prevent the illegal sale of opioids through internet platforms and services. Attendees discussed topics such as the evolving landscape of online opioid purchasing, enhancing cross-industry collaboration, and preventing the illegal sale of opioids online. The FDA remains committed to addressing the opioid crisis, focusing on decreasing exposure to opioids, supporting treatment, and taking action against those involved in the illegal importation and sale of unapproved and misbranded opioids.

title: FDA Advances Data, IT Modernization Efforts  with New Office of Digital Transformation
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced the reorganization of its information technology, data management, and cybersecurity functions into the new Office of Digital Transformation (ODT). The office will report directly to the FDA commissioner and elevate its functions to agency-level. This reorganization aims to advance the agency's information technology transformation with improved data and IT competencies, enhancing agency operations to support the public health mission. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that good data management is crucial for the agency's mission to ensure safe and effective products for American families. The FDA has been undertaking a modernization effort since September 2019, with plans to prioritize data and information stewardship throughout its operations. The agency has also announced the appointment of Vid Desai as its new Chief Information Officer.

title: Statement on the Progress of the Health Insurance Marketplace Special Enrollment Period in Response to the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency
body_summary: The administration opened healthcare.gov for a special enrollment period on February 15 to allow Americans to find quality, affordable health plans. Six months later, 2.8 million more Americans have gained access to reliable health coverage. This brings the total to 12.2 million Americans actively enrolled in coverage under the Affordable Care Act, an all-time high. Premiums have decreased by an average of $67 a month, and out-of-pocket spending has declined dramatically. The administration aims to lower prescription drug costs, provide health care premium tax cuts, and deliver quality, affordable care to millions more through its Build Back Better agenda.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Announces Winners of Food Traceability Challenge
body_summary: The FDA launched the New Era of Smarter Food Safety Low- or No-Cost Tech-enabled Traceability Challenge in June to encourage the development of cost-effective traceability solutions. The challenge received 90 submissions from around the world and has chosen 12 winning teams from the US, Canada, and New Zealand. The winning teams are FarmTabs, Freshly, HeavyConnect, ItemChain, Kezzler, Mojix, OpsSmart, Precise, Roambee/GSM/Wiliot's, Rfider, TagOne, and Wholechain. The FDA will host a webinar on September 28 at 11 a.m. ET for the winning teams to present their solutions and take questions.

title: FDA Will Follow The Science On COVID-19 Vaccines For Young Children
body_summary: The FDA is eager to see COVID-19 vaccines available for children under 12 years of age, following concerns from parents and grandparents. The agency is undertaking a meticulous review process to ensure safety and efficacy, requiring thorough clinical trials of adequate size. Manufacturers are currently enrolling participants in clinical trials, and the FDA will work closely with them to analyze data and make a decision. The agency expects to review submissions rapidly, likely in weeks, but will not cut corners on the evaluation process. Once a vaccine is authorized or approved, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices will discuss clinical recommendations. Parents can currently ask their healthcare providers about vaccinating their kids using one of the available vaccines, but must remember that the vaccine doses being studied are different from those authorized for older populations. The FDA is working to meet the public health need and hopes to have pediatric COVID-19 vaccines available in the coming months.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: September 10, 2021
body_summary: The FDA has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock announced the FDA's approach to COVID-19 vaccines for young children. The FDA approved an abbreviated new drug application for dexmedetomidine injection on September 3, indicating it for sedation in intensive-care settings and surgical procedures. The agency has prioritized the review of generic drug applications for potential treatments and supportive therapies for patients with COVID-19. The FDA authorized one additional batch of Janssen COVID-19 vaccine drug substance manufactured at the Emergent facility on September 8, bringing the total to six authorized batches. The FDA revised its guidance on the development of abbreviated new drug applications during the COVID-19 pandemic on September 9. The agency has authorized over 400 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody tests, and antigen tests, for COVID-19 testing and screening.

title: FDA, FTC Warn 10 Companies Illegally Selling Dietary Supplements Claiming to Treat Diabetes
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration and the Federal Trade Commission have issued warning letters to 10 companies for illegally selling dietary supplements that claim to cure, treat, or prevent diabetes, in violation of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. The FDA urges consumers not to use these products, as they have not been evaluated by the agency to be safe or effective. More than 34 million Americans live with diabetes. The FDA is committed to protecting consumers from products that make unlawful claims to treat or prevent diabetes. The agency has not evaluated the effectiveness of these unapproved products and advises consumers to consult their doctor or pharmacist before purchasing or using any dietary supplement or drug.

title: FDA In Brief: As Consumers Order More Meals and Groceries  Online, FDA Plans Public Meeting to Address Food Safety Risks
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) will hold a virtual public meeting on Oct. 19-21 to address the safety of foods ordered online and delivered directly to consumers. The meeting, entitled "The FDA New Era of Smarter Food Safety Summit on E-Commerce: Ensuring the Safety of Foods Ordered Online and Delivered Directly to Consumers," will be held to enhance understanding of e-commerce business models and identify ways to control potential food safety risks. The meeting is part of the FDA's New Era of Smarter Food Safety initiative, which aims to build on the Food Safety Modernization Act through technology and digital tools. The summit is one of four core elements outlined in the 2020 blueprint, focusing on New Business Models and Retail Modernization.

title: Executive Order 14043—Requiring Coronavirus Disease 2019 Vaccination for Federal Employees
body_summary: The President orders the halt of COVID-19 spread in the United States by relying on data and science-based public health measures. The nationwide public health emergency remains in effect, and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends vaccination to slow the spread of COVID-19. As of September 9, 2021, one of the COVID-19 vaccines, Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine, has received FDA approval, and two others, Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine and Janssen COVID-19 Vaccine, have been authorized for emergency use. The President determines that requiring COVID-19 vaccination for all Federal employees is necessary to promote health and safety. Each agency must implement a program to require COVID-19 vaccination for all Federal employees, with exceptions as required by law.

title: FDA Makes Significant Progress in Science-Based Public Health Application Review, Taking Action on Over 90% of More Than 6.5 Million ‘Deemed’ New Tobacco Products Submitted
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has reviewed applications for over 6.5 million deemed new tobacco products, mostly electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS) products. As of today, the agency has taken action on about 93% of the total timely-submitted applications, including issuing Marketing Denial Orders (MDO) for more than 946,000 flavored ENDS products due to insufficient evidence of benefit to adult smokers. The agency has also issued 132 MDOs for flavored ENDS products and refused to file applications for approximately 4.5 million products due to missing required contents. The FDA continues to work on the remaining applications and is committed to completing the review as quickly as possible to provide regulatory certainty.

title: FDA In Brief: As Consumers Order More Meals and Groceries  Online, FDA Plans Public Meeting to Address Food Safety Risks
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) will hold a virtual public meeting on Oct. 19-21, entitled The FDA New Era of Smarter Food Safety Summit on E-Commerce: Ensuring the Safety of Foods Ordered Online and Delivered Directly to Consumers. The summit aims to address the potential safety vulnerabilities of online-delivered foods, particularly during the "last mile" of delivery. The meeting will be attended by members of the food industry, regulatory counterparts, consumers, and others. The FDA previously announced the New Era of Smarter Food Safety initiative in April 2019, which represents a new approach to food safety leveraging technology and other tools to create a safer food system. The summit is a critical step in this effort, following the release of the New Era of Smarter Food Safety blueprint in July 2020.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Announces Public Workshop to Reconsider Mandatory Prescriber Education for Opioids
body_summary: The FDA is reconsidering mandatory opioid prescriber education as part of its Opioid Analgesic Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS). A two-day public workshop will be held to gather input from stakeholders on whether mandatory prescriber education can mitigate the opioid crisis. The workshop aims to explore the value of a single source for education on the appropriate use of opioids, risks of abuse and misuse, and treatment of opioid use disorder. The number of opioid prescriptions has decreased, but overdose deaths and opioid-involved deaths remain high. The FDA recognizes that mandatory prescriber education may help address the issue and minimize the burden on the healthcare delivery system.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Announces Public Workshop to Reconsider Mandatory Prescriber Education for Opioids
body_summary: The FDA is reconsidering the need for mandatory opioid prescriber education through the Opioid Analgesic Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS). A two-day public workshop will be held to gather input on aspects of the current opioid crisis that could be mitigated by requiring mandatory prescriber education as part of a REMS. The workshop aims to explore the value of a single source for education on the appropriate use of opioids, risks of opioid abuse and misuse, and treatment of opioid use disorder. The number of dispensed opioid analgesic prescriptions has declined from 84 per 100 residents in 2012 to 43 per 100 residents in 2020, but opioid overdoses and opioid-involved deaths are higher than ever. The FDA recognizes that mandatory prescriber education may minimize the burden on the healthcare delivery system. The workshop is being convened by the Duke-Margolis Center for Health Policy and supported by a cooperative agreement between the FDA and Duke-Margolis.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: September 7, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has taken actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The agency issued a warning letter to Kaleido Biosciences, Inc., for not complying with federal laws and regulations during a clinical trial of an investigational drug to mitigate and treat COVID-19. The FDA has authorized 409 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 287 molecular tests, 88 antibody and other immune response tests, and 34 antigen tests. This includes 62 molecular authorizations for home-collected samples, one molecular prescription at-home test, and 14 antigen tests for serial screening programs.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Reaches Milestone in Competitive Generic Therapy Drug Approvals
body_summary: The FDA has approved more than 100 generic drug applications with a Competitive Generic Therapy (CGT) designation, reaching a milestone in the program's success since its inception in 2017. Sally Choe, Ph.D., director of the Office of Generic Drugs, attributes this achievement to the program's encouragement of generic drug development and marketing. The first CGT-designated abbreviated new drug application was approved on August 8, 2018, and the related guidance was finalized in March 2020. More than 80% of first-approved applicants started marketing their drugs within 75 days after FDA approval. The CGT program aims to foster generic competition and help address high drug costs, as part of the FDADrug Competition Action Plan.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA to Hold Advisory Committee Meeting to Discuss Pfizer-BioNTech’s Application for COVID-19 Booster
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration plans to evaluate and determine the safety and effectiveness of additional COVID-19 vaccine doses, or "boosters," this fall. The process involves vaccine manufacturers submitting data to the agency, which will then be reviewed by the FDA. The FDA is evaluating data submitted by Pfizer-BioNTech in a supplemental Biologics License Application for its COVID-19 vaccine. A virtual meeting of the Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee will be held on September 17, 2021, to discuss the matter. The meeting will be livestreamed on the FDA's YouTube channel and webcast from the FDA website.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: August 27, 2021
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On August 25, the FDA issued a letter to health care providers, warning them to stop using certain N95 respirators manufactured by Shanghai Dasheng Health Products Manufacture Co., Ltd. due to a lack of quality management system. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) also revoked all respirator approvals previously issued to Shanghai Dasheng.

The FDA has also warned Invisi Smart Technologies for offering for sale adulterated and misbranded Invisi Smart Masks. The agency has authorized over 400 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody tests, and antigen tests. These authorized tests include 60 molecular authorizations, one antibody authorization, and 14 antigen tests for serial screening programs.

title: FDA Approves First-of-Its-Kind Stroke Rehabilitation System
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the MicroTransponder Vivistim Paired VNS System, a drug-free rehabilitation system, to treat moderate to severe upper extremity motor deficits associated with chronic ischemic stroke. The system uses vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) to reduce deficiencies in upper limb and extremity motor function and to improve patients' ability to move their arms and hands. The FDA evaluated the safety and effectiveness of the system in a clinical study of 108 patients, which showed that the treatment group had a higher average score increase on the Upper Extremity Fugl-Meyer Assessment (FMA-UE) than the control group. The system is intended for use in both clinical and at-home settings, and patients are trained on how to use the device safely. The FDA granted the Vivistim System Breakthrough Device designation due to its potential to treat a life-threatening or irreversibly debilitating disease or condition.

title: FDA Denies Marketing Applications for About 55,000 Flavored E-Cigarette Products for Failing to Provide Evidence They Appropriately Protect Public Health
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued the first marketing denial orders for electronic nicotine delivery system products. The FDA received applications from three applicants, JD Nova Group LLC, Great American Vapes, and Vapor Salon, for about 55,000 flavored ENDS products. The products were denied due to a lack of sufficient evidence showing a benefit to adult smokers to overcome the public health threat posed by youth use. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that the FDA aims to reduce tobacco-related disease and death. The agency has received applications from over 500 companies covering more than 6.5 million tobacco products and plans to continue reviewing premarket tobacco applications to ensure products meet the standard for protection of public health.

title: FDA Releases PFAS Testing Results from First Survey of Nationally Distributed Processed Foods
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration released the results of its first survey on per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in nationally distributed processed foods. 164 of 167 tested foods had no detectable levels of PFAS, while three samples - fish sticks, canned tuna, and protein powder - had detectable levels. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that the results do not suggest avoiding particular foods due to PFAS contamination. The survey included foods commonly eaten by babies and young children, such as baby foods and frozen foods. The FDA will continue its work to better understand PFAS levels in the food supply.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: August 24, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has announced actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On August 22, the FDA updated the Pfizer-BioNTech emergency use authorization to extend the shelf-life of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine from 6 months to 9 months. This extension applies to products stored at -90 degrees Celsius and can be applied to batches that may have expired prior. The FDA has also authorized 403 tests and sample collection devices, including molecular, antibody, and antigen tests, as well as prescription and over-the-counter at-home tests, for emergency use.

title: FDA and Mexican Counterparts Report Progress and Next Steps for Food Safety Partnership
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and its Mexican counterparts, the Federal Commission for the Protection from Sanitary Risks (Cofepris) and the National Service of Agro-Alimentary Health, Safety and Quality (SENASICA), held the first Food Safety Partnership Annual Meeting on August 20. This meeting marks an important milestone in food safety and builds upon the Statement of Intent signed in September 2020 to enhance the partnership between the three agencies.

The partnership, which broadened the scope of products to include all human foods under the FDA's jurisdiction traded between the two countries, reflected on accomplishments from the past year and set goals for the coming year. The FDA plans to work closely with SENASICA and Cofepris on activities that will enhance communication and oversight.

About one-third of all imported food into the U.S. is from Mexico, including 60% of all imported produce. The partnership aligns with the FDA's New Era of Smarter Food Safety Blueprint, which includes tech-enabled traceability, smarter tools and approaches for prevention and outbreak response, new business models, and food safety culture.

The partnership is utilizing smarter tools and approaches, exchanging analytical methods to detect foodborne illness pathogens, increasing data sharing, and updating the Binational Protocol for outbreak response. The agencies are also focusing on ways to leverage SENASICA's risk reduction standards and fostering industry best practices to further the safety of exported Mexican produce.

The partnership has trained more than 300 growers on the Produce Safety Alliance's grower-training curricula, and about 90% of the Mexican papaya industry has been trained on papaya best practices. The partnership will continue to strengthen work with industry on Foreign Supplier Verification Programs trainings for importers and the verification of papaya best practice implementation.

title: FDA Approves First COVID-19 Vaccine
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine, now marketed as Comirnaty, for the prevention of COVID-19 disease in individuals 16 years of age and older. The vaccine also remains available under emergency use authorization (EUA) for individuals 12 through 15 years of age and certain immunocompromised individuals. The FDA's approval was based on safety and effectiveness data from a randomized, controlled, blinded clinical trial of thousands of individuals, with the vaccine showing 91% effectiveness in preventing COVID-19 disease. The vaccine contains messenger RNA and is administered as a series of two doses, three weeks apart. The FDA has required the company to conduct postmarketing studies to further assess the risks of myocarditis and pericarditis following vaccination with Comirnaty.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: August 20, 2021
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration announced actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On August 19, the agency issued a warning letter to Mahita, LLC dba PushMyCart for selling unapproved products with unproven COVID-19 claims. On August 13, the FDA held a stakeholder call to discuss vaccines for younger children and adolescents. Assistant Secretary for Health Rachel Levine and Director of FDA's Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research Peter Marks were featured speakers.

The FDA has authorized 402 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 282 molecular tests, 87 antibody tests, and 33 antigen tests. The agency has also authorized revisions to these authorizations, totaling 610.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A joint meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee and the Board of Governors was held on July 27-28, 2021. The economy made progress towards maximum employment and price-stability goals since December, with most participants judging substantial further progress not met on employment but achieved on price-stability. Implied rates on interest rate futures initially rose but subsequently retraced, while longer-term yields fell due to changes in term premiums. Market participants expected gradual tapering of net asset purchases, with the first reduction possibly coming in January. The establishment of Standing Repurchase Agreement Facilities was also approved, with broad support from participants. Real PCE rose in Q2 at a pace similar to Q1, supported by federal stimulus and reduced social distancing. Consumer spending was held back as producers struggled to meet demand. Business fixed investment slowed sharply due to motor vehicle production disruptions. The US international trade deficit remained high, with real goods imports still at a second-highest level and real goods exports below pre-COVID-19 levels. Banks reported easing lending standards for commercial and industrial loans in June, with demand improving. Financing conditions remained accommodative for corporate bonds, leveraged loans, and municipal debt. The staff assessed financial vulnerabilities as notable, citing elevated asset valuation pressures, nonfinancial leverage, and funding risks. The Federal Reserve reaffirmed its commitment to using tools to support the economy, promoting maximum employment and price stability. The FOMC decided to maintain an accommodative monetary policy stance until its desired outcomes are achieved.

title: Joint Statement from HHS Public Health and Medical Experts on COVID-19 Booster Shots
body_summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services has released a statement outlining the Administration's plan for COVID-19 booster shots. The statement is attributable to several public health experts, including Dr. Rochelle Walensky, Dr. Janet Woodcock, Dr. Vivek Murthy, and Dr. Anthony Fauci. According to the statement, COVID-19 vaccines continue to be effective in reducing risk of severe disease, hospitalization, and death, but protection begins to decrease over time. Based on this, a booster shot is recommended to maximize vaccine-induced protection and prolong its durability. The plan is to begin offering booster shots this fall, with the first dose to be administered 8 months after an individual's second dose. The plan also includes booster shots for people who received the Johnson & Johnson vaccine and for residents of long-term care facilities. The Administration's top priority remains protecting the American people from COVID-19 with safe, effective, and long-lasting vaccines.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Issues a Corporate-Wide Warning Letter to Company Associated with Contaminated Pet Food, Hundreds of Adverse Events
body_summary: The FDA has issued a corporate-wide warning letter to Midwestern Pet Foods, Inc. following inspections that revealed apparent violations of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act shared across multiple plants. The violations were associated with the illness or death of hundreds of pets who had eaten the company's dry dog food, particularly SPORTMiX brand. Samples of SPORTMiX were found to contain high levels of aflatoxin, with some samples having levels as high as 558 parts per billion. Midwestern has voluntarily recalled these products, as well as all corn-containing pet foods manufactured at its Chickasha plant. The company has also recalled several brands of pet food manufactured at its Monmouth, Illinois plant after samples tested positive for Salmonella. The FDA has found that Midwestern's food safety program appears inadequate to significantly minimize or prevent Salmonella in its pet food. As of August 9, the FDA is aware of more than 130 pet deaths and over 220 pet illnesses linked to eating Midwestern's pet food.

title: Memorandum on Maximizing Assistance To Respond to COVID-19
body_summary: The President of the United States has ordered as follows: Consistent with the nationwide emergency declaration of March 13, 2020, the policy is to combat and respond to COVID-19 with the full capacity and capability of the Federal Government to protect and support families, schools, and businesses, and to assist State, local, Tribal, and territorial governments with emergency and disaster assistance available from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). FEMA shall provide a 100 percent Federal cost share for all work eligible for assistance under Public Assistance Category B, including work described in the Presidential Memorandum of January 21, 2021. The memorandum shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations. The Administrator of FEMA is authorized and directed to publish this memorandum in the Federal Register.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: August 13, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken action against companies selling unapproved products with COVID-19 claims, including Secret of the Islands. The FDA has authorized the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine for emergency use in people 12 and older, and the CDC recommends vaccination for everyone 12 and older. The FDA has amended emergency use authorizations for the Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna COVID-19 Vaccines to allow for an additional dose in certain immunocompromised individuals. As of today, the FDA has authorized 402 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 282 molecular tests, 87 antibody tests, and 33 antigen tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Additional Vaccine Dose for Certain Immunocompromised Individuals
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) amended emergency use authorizations (EUAs) for the Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna COVID-19 Vaccines to allow an additional dose for immunocompromised individuals, specifically solid organ transplant recipients or those with conditions equivalent to immunocompromise. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices will discuss further clinical recommendations. The FDA determined that immunocompromised individuals, particularly those at risk of severe disease, may benefit from a third dose of the Pfizer-BioNTech or Moderna Vaccines. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that the action allows doctors to boost immunity in this vulnerable group. Immunocompromised individuals should be counseled on physical precautions and close contacts should get vaccinated.

title: FDA Grants First of its Kind Indication for Chronic Sleep Disorder Treatment
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved a new indication for Xywav for idiopathic hypersomnia in adults. Xywav is already approved for treating cataplexy or excessive daytime sleepiness in patients with narcolepsy. A double-blind placebo-controlled study in 154 adult patients with IH found that patients who switched from Xywav to placebo experienced worsening symptoms. Common adverse events included nausea, headache, dizziness, anxiety, and vomiting. Xywav has a boxed warning for central nervous system depression and abuse, and its active moiety is oxybate, a Schedule I controlled substance. The FDA granted this application Fast Track and Priority Review designations, and Xywav will be subject to strict safety controls under a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy. The FDA approved Xywav for use in adults with IH and granted it to Jazz Pharmaceuticals plc.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: August 6, 2021
body_summary: The FDA has found certain lots of AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine drug substance manufactured at the Emergent facility in Baltimore, Maryland, to be acceptable for export. The AstraZeneca vaccine is not authorized for use in the U.S. The agency conducted a thorough review of facility records and quality testing results, considering the current worldwide COVID-19 public health emergency. The FDA has also approved an abbreviated new drug application for dexamethasone sodium phosphate injection, a treatment for various conditions. Additionally, the FDA has authorized 399 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including molecular and antigen tests, as well as prescription and over-the-counter at-home tests.

title: FDA Approves New Treatment for Pompe Disease
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Nexviazyme (avalglucosidase alfa-ngpt) for intravenous infusion to treat patients 1 year of age and older with late-onset Pompe disease. This approval brings patients another enzyme replacement therapy option for this rare disease. The effectiveness of Nexviazyme was demonstrated in a study of 100 patients who showed improved lung function similar to the other therapy. Common side effects included headache, fatigue, and joint pain, while serious reactions included hypersensitivity reactions and infusion-associated reactions. Genzyme Corporation is granted the approval of Nexviazyme.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Reminds Industry of Specific Regulations for the Use of Fluorinated Polyethylene in Food Contact Containers
body_summary: The FDA has issued a letter to the industry reminding manufacturers that only certain fluorinated polyethylene containers are authorized for food contact use. The letter is intended for food packaging manufacturers and food manufacturers that use these containers. The agency is taking this step to ensure compliance with regulations and prevent the formation of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), some of which are associated with adverse health effects.
