The FDA has become aware that certain PFAS can form and migrate from some fluorinated high-density polyethylene containers, as tested by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

title: FDA Participates in New ‘Collaborative Communities’ to Address Emerging Challenges in Medical Devices
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced participation in several new collaborative communities aimed at addressing challenges in patient health care. These communities are a forum where private and public sector representatives work together to achieve common objectives and outcomes. The FDA currently participates in 12 established and managed communities, which focus on topics such as medical device development and product quality, valvular heart disease, digital pathology, and reducing rates of self-injury among people with diabetes. The FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health director, Jeff Shuren, and deputy director, Michelle Tarver, have welcomed the growth of collaborative communities, which have led to significant progress in addressing public health challenges. The FDA participates in these communities to contribute its knowledge and perspective, and the number of communities has continued to grow since the goal of 10 was set in 2018-2020.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: August 3, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock and Director Peter Marks discussed COVID-19 vaccines, including reports of Guillain-Barré Syndrome following Janssen (Johnson & Johnson) vaccination. The FDA has authorized 398 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs). This includes 279 molecular tests, 87 antibody tests, and 32 antigen tests. There are 53 molecular authorizations and one antibody authorization for home-collected samples. The FDA has also authorized 595 revisions to EUA authorizations and 13 antigen tests for serial screening programs.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: July 30, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA revised the Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for REGEN-COV to add an authorization for post-exposure prophylaxis in adults and pediatric individuals at high risk of severe COVID-19. REGEN-COV is only authorized for post-exposure use and not for pre-exposure prophylaxis. The FDA has also revised the EUA for baricitinib, allowing it to be used alone for treating COVID-19 in hospitalized adults and pediatric patients requiring oxygen or mechanical ventilation. Additionally, the FDA authorized an extension for the shelf life of the Janssen COVID-19 Vaccine, allowing it to be stored at 2-8 degrees Celsius for six months. The FDA has authorized over 400 tests and sample collection devices, including 279 molecular tests and 53 molecular authorizations.

title: Implementation Note issued July 28, 2021
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on July 28, 2021: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to establish the interest rate paid on reserve balances at 0.15 percent, effective July 29, 2021. 1 As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective July 29, 2021, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 0 to 1/4 percent. Increase the System Open Market Account holdings of Treasury securities by $80 billion per month and of agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) by $40 billion per month. Increase holdings of Treasury securities and agency MBS by additional amounts and purchase agency commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) as needed to sustain smooth functioning of markets for these securities. Conduct overnight repurchase agreement operations with a minimum bid rate of 0.25 percent and with an aggregate operation limit of $500 billion; the aggregate operation limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 0.05 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $80 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities and reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS in agency MBS. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for purchases and reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 0.25 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website . 1. As announced on June 2, 2021 , the Federal Reserve Board approved a final rule, effective July 29, amending Regulation D to eliminate references to an interest on required reserves (IORR) rate and to an interest on excess reserves (IOER) rate and replace them with a single interest on reserve balances (IORB) rate. Therefore, the Board voted on one rate, the IORB rate, at this meeting and will continue to do so going forward. Return to text

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The Federal Reserve is committed to using its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals. With progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have continued to strengthen. The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic have shown improvement but have not fully recovered. Inflation has risen, largely reflecting transitory factors. Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses. The path of the economy continues to depend on the course of the virus. Progress on vaccinations will likely continue to reduce the effects of the public health crisis on the economy, but risks to the economic outlook remain. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. With inflation having run persistently below this longer-run goal, the Committee will aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time so that inflation averages 2 percent over time and longerâterm inflation expectations remain well anchored at 2 percent. The Committee expects to maintain an accommodative stance of monetary policy until these outcomes are achieved. The Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time. Last December, the Committee indicated that it would continue to increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $80 billion per month and of agency mortgageâbacked securities by at least $40 billion per month until substantial further progress has been made toward its maximum employment and price stability goals. Since then, the economy has made progress toward these goals, and the Committee will continue to assess progress in coming meetings. These asset purchases help foster smooth market functioning and accommodative financial conditions, thereby supporting the flow of credit to households and businesses. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Mary C. Daly; Charles L. Evans; Randal K. Quarles; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: FDA Approves First Interchangeable Biosimilar Insulin Product for Treatment of Diabetes
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Semglee (insulin glargine-yfgn), the first interchangeable biosimilar insulin product, for the treatment of Type 1 and 2 diabetes mellitus. Semglee is biosimilar to and interchangeable with Lantus (insulin glargine), a long-acting insulin analog. This approval allows patients to have additional safe, high-quality, and potentially cost-effective options for treating diabetes. The FDA's approval is based on evidence showing that Semglee is highly similar to Lantus in terms of safety, purity, and potency. The product is available in 10 mL vials and 3 mL prefilled pens and should be administered subcutaneously once daily.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: July 23, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced updates to its COVID-19 response efforts. On July 22, the FDA issued an Emergency Use Authorization to Becton, Dickinson and Company for its BD Vacutainer Plus Citrate Plasma Tubes for coagulation testing. The agency also posted FAQs about sodium citrate blood specimen collection tubes. On July 20, the FDA issued a warning letter to Jordan's Crossing Herbal Connections for selling an unapproved product with unproven COVID-19 claims. As of today, 395 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under emergency use authorizations, including 279 molecular tests, 86 antibody tests, and 30 antigen tests. The FDA has also authorized 586 revisions to EUA authorizations.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: July 20, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced several actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock testified before the U.S. Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions. FDA leaders reflected on the use of Emergency Use Authorizations and other resources in making drug, device, and biological products available. The FDA held a stakeholder call to discuss COVID-19 vaccines, including reports of Guillain-Barré Syndrome following Janssen COVID-19 vaccination. An FDA Consumer Update on COVID-19 vaccines is available in five additional languages. As of today, 396 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under emergency use authorizations, including 281 molecular tests, 85 antibody tests, and 30 antigen tests. The FDA has also authorized 576 revisions to these authorizations.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: July 16, 2021
body_summary: The US FDA has formally accepted Pfizer's Biologics License Application for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine, granting priority review and paving the way for licensure for individuals 16 years of age and older. The vaccine is currently authorized for emergency use in individuals ages 12 and older, with a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) Goal Date of January 2022. The FDA has also authorized over 396 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 281 molecular tests, 85 antibody tests, and 30 antigen tests.

title: Statement on Two Million Americans Signing Up for Health Coverage and Launching the "Summer Sprint to Coverage" Campaign
body_summary: The Administration has opened a special enrollment period through HealthCare.gov, providing Americans the opportunity to sign up for health insurance. Five months later, two million Americans have signed up, gaining access to quality, affordable health care. This milestone builds on progress expanding access to health insurance through vital programs like Medicaid and the Children's Health Insurance Program. The Administration lowered health care costs with the American Rescue Plan, saving nine million Americans an average of $2,400 per year. The Build Back Better agenda will expand on these efforts, adding dental, vision, and hearing coverage to Medicare, closing the Medicaid coverage gap, and making premium reductions permanent. The Administration is launching a 30-day "Summer Sprint to Coverage" campaign to help people sign up for health coverage by August 15.

title: FDA Grants First Full Approval for Treatment of Lymphoma in Dogs
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) fully approved Tanovea (rabacfosadine injection) to treat lymphoma in dogs. Tanovea is the first conditionally approved new animal drug for dogs to achieve full approval. The drug was initially approved under the Minor Use and Minor Species (MUMS) program in December 2016. 

The FDA's MUMS program aims to make more medications available to veterinarians and animal owners for the treatment of minor animal species and uncommon diseases. Tanovea's active ingredient, rabacfosadine, kills rapidly growing cancer cells and is administered via injection over 30 minutes, repeated every three weeks for up to five administrations.

Studies have shown that Tanovea extended the median survival rate by 61 days and median progression-free survival by 168 days in dogs with complete response to the drug. Common side effects include diarrhea, decreased appetite, and weight loss, while serious adverse events include pulmonary fibrosis and skin issues.

Tanovea was developed by VetDC Inc. and is now available for use by licensed veterinarians to treat canine lymphoma. The FDA encourages dog owners to work with their veterinary team to report any adverse events or side effects related to the use of Tanovea.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: July 13, 2021
body_summary: The FDA is announcing revisions to the vaccine recipient and vaccination provider fact sheets for the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 Vaccine to include information about Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS), a neurological disorder. There have been 100 preliminary reports of GBS following vaccination with the Janssen vaccine, 95 of which were serious and required hospitalization. The FDA continues to work with the CDC to monitor reports of GBS and has found that the known and potential benefits of the vaccine outweigh the known and potential risks. The FDA has authorized an additional batch of vaccine drug substance manufactured at the Emergent facility and has revised the fact sheets to include warnings about GBS. The agency has also authorized 396 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations.

title: Executive Order 14036—Promoting Competition in the American Economy
body_summary: The US President, Joe Biden, issued an executive order on July 9, 2021, to promote competition in the US economy. The order aims to address market concentration, monopolization, and unfair competition, particularly in industries affecting workers, farmers, small businesses, and consumers. The White House Competition Council, led by the Assistant to the President for Economic Policy, coordinates efforts with heads of major agencies, including the FTC, Commerce, Labor, Health, and Transportation, to address these issues. The government has initiated rulemakings in various industries, such as meat, agriculture, retail, and telecommunications, to promote competition, lower prices, and innovation. Key actions include updating FDA regulations for biosimilar products, reducing costs of covered products for consumers, and improving competition in contract procurement.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Issues Systems Recognition Draft Guidance
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a draft guidance on FDA oversight of food products covered by Systems Recognition Arrangements. This draft guidance addresses the agency's oversight of foods imported from countries participating in Systems Recognition Arrangements, such as Australia, Canada, and New Zealand. The guidance aims to take a risk-based approach to food safety, leveraging regulatory partners' food safety systems to ensure safe food imports. The FDA plans to adjust its regulatory oversight activities to focus on the ability of food safety authorities to identify and address issues, rather than solely on the ability of food safety systems to prevent them. The guidance is part of the FDA's New Era of Smarter Food Safety initiative, which aims to bend the curve of foodborne illness through the use of new technologies and modernized approaches.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: July 9, 2021
body_summary:
The US FDA has taken actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA funded a study on the impact of 3D printing on the COVID-19 response in September 2020. The study, conducted by America Makes, shows successes, challenges, and key lessons learned. The FDA has reviewed the report to assess gaps in the response and potential mitigations for future public health emergencies. 

The FDA issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for the VITROS Immunodiagnostic Products Anti-SARS-CoV-2 IgG Quantitative Test to measure IgG antibodies to SARS-CoV-2. The FDA also issued warning letters to 12 firms for offering adulterated and misbranded tests, face masks, respirators, and surgical masks. 

As of today, 395 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations. The FDA has authorized 561 revisions to EUA authorizations.

title: Joint CDC and FDA Statement on Vaccine Boosters
body_summary: The United States has highly effective vaccines widely available for those aged 12 and up, providing protection from severe disease and death from COVID-19 variants like Delta. Americans who are not vaccinated remain at risk, with virtually all hospitalizations and deaths occurring among the unvaccinated. The FDA, CDC, and NIH are conducting a science-based process to consider booster shots, taking into account laboratory, clinical trial, and cohort data. Americans who have been fully vaccinated do not need a booster shot at this time, but the process will be reviewed as new data becomes available.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on June 15-16, 2021, discussing repurchase agreement arrangements, including the establishment of domestic and foreign international monetary authorities (FIMA) repo facilities. The FOMC discussed the design of a standing repo facility and FIMA repo facility, focusing on restricting eligible collateral to US Treasury securities or accepting agency securities and agency mortgage-backed securities. The Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) remained at 1 basis point, while the effective federal funds rate decreased 1 basis point to 6 basis points. Business equipment spending increased solidly in the second quarter, driven by rising orders for nondefense capital goods. Consumer price inflation continued to rise globally, driven by rebounding energy prices and fading effects of steep price declines. The credit quality of large nonfinancial corporations remained stable, with no reported corporate defaults in April. Economic activity expanded rapidly, led by consumer spending, with most participants revising up real GDP growth projections compared to March.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: July 6, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has taken actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On June 29, 2021, Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock and Director Peter Marks discussed updates on myocarditis and pericarditis following vaccination with Pfizer-BioNTech or Moderna COVID-19 Vaccines. The FDA has authorized 393 tests and sample collection devices, including 281 molecular tests, 84 antibody tests, and 28 antigen tests. The FDA has also authorized 560 revisions to emergency use authorizations, including 11 antigen tests and 3 molecular tests for serial screening programs.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: July 2, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) authorized the use of an additional batch of the Janssen COVID-19 vaccine under emergency use authorization. This is the fourth batch of vaccine drug substance manufactured at the Emergent facility to be authorized. The FDA conducted a thorough review of facility records and quality testing results, concluding that the batches are suitable for use. The agency continues to work with Janssen and Emergent BioSolutions to address issues with the Emergent facility. The FDA revoked EUAs for non-NIOSH-approved disposable respirators on June 30 and July 6, 2021, and for decontamination and bioburden reduction systems on June 30, 2021. The FDA has authorized 393 tests and sample collection devices, including molecular, antibody, and antigen tests, for emergency use.

title: FDA Provides Update on Ongoing Efforts to Better Understand the Occurrence of PFAS in the Food Supply
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has updated its sampling and testing efforts to better understand the occurrence of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in the food supply. The FDA analyzed 94 samples of various food products collected in FY2020 and found only one sample of cod with detectable levels of two types of PFAS – perfluorooctane sulfonate (PFOS) and perfluorononanoic acid (PFNA). The FDA has determined that the PFAS levels do not present a human health concern. The agency conducts a safety assessment to evaluate the potential health concern, considering factors such as action levels, food consumption, contaminant levels, and toxicity. The FDA's approach considers the available scientific literature and toxicological reference values. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that the U.S. food supply is among the safest in the world, and the available scientific evidence does not support avoiding particular foods due to PFAS exposure.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Revokes Emergency Use Authorizations for Certain Respirators and Decontamination Systems as Access to N95s Increases Nationwide
body_summary: The FDA is revoking EUAs for imported, non-NIOSH-approved respirators and decontamination and bioburden reduction systems due to an increase in domestically-manufactured NIOSH-approved N95s. As a result, healthcare organizations should transition away from crisis capacity conservation strategies implemented at the onset of the pandemic. The revocation follows the CDC's updated recommendations and OSHA's Emergency Temporary Standard requiring NIOSH-approved or FDA-authorized respirators for healthcare workers. Over 875 respirator models have been approved by NIOSH, with more than 6,400 on the NIOSH-certified equipment list. The FDA has also withdrawn guidance documents related to decontamination and bioburden reduction systems.

title: FDA Approves Component of Treatment Regimen for Most Common Childhood Cancer
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Rylaze as a component of a chemotherapy regimen to treat acute lymphoblastic leukemia and lymphoblastic lymphoma in adult and pediatric patients who are allergic to E. coli-derived asparaginase products. The approval provides a consistently sourced alternative to a pivotal component of potentially curative therapy for children and adults with this type of leukemia. Rylaze was evaluated in a study of 102 patients and found that the recommended dosage would provide the target level of asparaginase activity in 94% of patients. The study also identified common side effects of Rylaze, including hypersensitivity reactions, pancreatic toxicity, and liver toxicity. The FDA granted approval of Rylaze to Jazz Pharmaceuticals.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: June 29, 2021
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken action in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA has sent its Report on Drug Shortages for Calendar Year 2020 to Congress, including a section on the agency's efforts to address COVID-19-related drug shortages. The FDA has leveraged various tools to increase patient access to medications in shortage, such as expediting reviews and publishing guidances. The agency is also working to implement drug shortage-related provisions of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act.

As of today, 389 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 278 molecular tests, 83 antibody and other immune response tests, and 28 antigen tests. The FDA has authorized 553 revisions to EUA authorizations, including 11 antigen tests and three molecular tests for serial screening programs.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: June 25, 2021
body_summary: The US FDA is revising patient and provider fact sheets for the Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccines to include warnings about increased risks of myocarditis and pericarditis following vaccination. The Fact Sheets for Healthcare Providers and Recipients and Caregivers have been revised to include this information. The FDA is also reminding healthcare facilities to follow manufacturer instructions for reprocessing flexible bronchoscopes and providing new recommendations for single-use bronchoscopes to reduce potential infection transmission. The FDA has approved 1,000 original and supplemental generic drug applications for COVID-19 treatment and has issued a warning letter to Pacific Center of Health for selling unapproved products with unproven COVID-19 claims. As of today, 389 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Drug for Treatment of COVID-19
body_summary: The US FDA issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for Actemra (tocilizumab) to treat hospitalized adults and pediatric patients over 2 years old who require supplemental oxygen, non-invasive or invasive mechanical ventilation, or ECMO. This action is based on clinical trials that showed Actemra reduces the risk of death and time spent in hospital for these patients. The trials, including RECOVERY and EMPACTA, demonstrated a statistically significant reduction in mortality and hospital discharge time. The FDA is authorizing the EUA for hospitalized patients with COVID-19 who are receiving corticosteroid therapy. Actemra is not approved as a treatment for COVID-19, but its known benefits outweigh potential risks. The EUA applies to four clinical trials, including EMPACTA, COVACTA, and REMDACTA, which also assessed the safety of Actemra when used for COVID-19 treatment. Fact sheets with dosing instructions and potential side effects will be made available to healthcare providers and patients.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Encourages Inclusion of Patients with Incurable Cancers in Oncology Clinical Trials Regardless of Prior Therapies
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued a draft guidance document, "Cancer Clinical Trial Eligibility Criteria: Available Therapy in Non-Curative Settings," which encourages the inclusion of patients with incurable cancers in clinical trials, regardless of receiving alternative treatment options. The draft guidance, led by Richard Pazdur, director of the FDA's Oncology Center of Excellence, aims to broaden patient eligibility criteria for oncology clinical trials. The FDA believes patients with incurable cancers should be eligible to participate if provided with adequate information to make an informed decision. The guidance is part of the FDA's broader initiative to encourage rational expanded patient eligibility for oncology clinical trials.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: June 22, 2021
body_summary: The US FDA issued a Drug Safety Communication warning that symptoms like headache, nausea, and dizziness can occur after applying alcohol-based hand sanitizers to the skin and inhaling the vapors. The FDA reviewed case reports and found most cases had minor or minimal effects, but some required treatment. The agency warned consumers to use hand sanitizer in well-ventilated areas. On May 18, 2021, the FDA issued a warning letter to Umbrella for selling an unapproved product with unproven COVID-19 claims. Consumers should consult their healthcare provider for COVID-19 concerns. As of today, the FDA has authorized 388 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations.

title: FDA Approves First Oral Blood Thinning Medication for Children
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Pradaxa oral pellets to treat children 3 months to less than 12 years old with venous thromboembolism after injection treatment, and to prevent recurrent clots among these patients. Pradaxa was also approved in capsule form for children eight years and older with venous thromboembolism. This approval makes Pradaxa the first FDA-approved blood thinning medication for children that can be taken by mouth. The safety and efficacy of Pradaxa were evaluated in studies involving 267 pediatric patients, which showed that it was comparable to standard of care in preventing blood clots. Important side effects of Pradaxa include digestive system symptoms and bleeding, and it is not recommended for patients with certain medical conditions.

title: FDA Approves a Nasal Antihistamine for Nonprescription Use
body_summary: The US FDA approved Astepro (azelastine hydrochloride nasal spray, 0.15%) for nonprescription use through a partial prescription switch for seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis in adults and children six years of age and older. The approval allows individuals to use the nasal antihistamine safely and effectively without a healthcare provider's assistance. To qualify for this switch, the data must demonstrate the drug's safety and effectiveness for self-medication as directed in proposed labeling. The approval is considered a first-in-class switch for a nasal antihistamine, with the 0.1% strength remaining prescription-based for children 6 months to 6 years old and seasonal allergy indication for children 2 to 6 years old. The FDA granted the approval to Bayer Healthcare LLC.

title: Statement on the U.S. Supreme Court Decision Upholding the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: The U.S. Supreme Court decision reaffirms the Affordable Care Act as the law of the land, a victory for 130 million Americans with preexisting conditions and millions more who were at risk of losing their health care during the pandemic. The law has protected people from being denied coverage due to preexisting conditions, allowed free preventive screenings, and enabled young people to stay on their parents' insurance until age 26. After over a decade of challenges, the court has rejected the third major challenge, paving the way to move forward and build on the landmark law. The American Rescue Plan has expanded coverage and lowered health care costs, with over 1.2 million Americans signing up for coverage. The decision affirms the law's strength, delivering for the American people, and advances the goal of making health care a right, not a privilege.

title: Implementation Note issued June 16, 2021
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on June 16, 2021: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to set the interest rate paid on required and excess reserve balances at 0.15 percent, effective June 17, 2021. Setting the interest rate paid on required and excess reserve balances 15 basis points above the bottom of the target range for the federal funds rate is intended to foster trading in the federal funds market at rates well within the Federal Open Market Committee's target range and to support the smooth functioning of short-term funding markets. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective June 17, 2021, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 0 to 1/4 percent. Increase the System Open Market Account holdings of Treasury securities by $80 billion per month and of agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) by $40 billion per month. Increase holdings of Treasury securities and agency MBS by additional amounts and purchase agency commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) as needed to sustain smooth functioning of markets for these securities. Conduct repurchase agreement operations to support effective policy implementation and the smooth functioning of short-term U.S. dollar funding markets. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 0.05 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $80 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities and reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS in agency MBS. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for purchases and reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 0.25 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The Federal Reserve is committed to using its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals. Progress on vaccinations has reduced the spread of COVID-19 in the United States. Amid this progress and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have strengthened. The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic remain weak but have shown improvement. Inflation has risen, largely reflecting transitory factors. Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses. The path of the economy will depend significantly on the course of the virus. Progress on vaccinations will likely continue to reduce the effects of the public health crisis on the economy, but risks to the economic outlook remain. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. With inflation having run persistently below this longer-run goal, the Committee will aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time so that inflation averages 2 percent over time and longerâterm inflation expectations remain well anchored at 2 percent. The Committee expects to maintain an accommodative stance of monetary policy until these outcomes are achieved. The Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time. In addition, the Federal Reserve will continue to increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $80 billion per month and of agency mortgageâbacked securities by at least $40 billion per month until substantial further progress has been made toward the Committee's maximum employment and price stability goals. These asset purchases help foster smooth market functioning and accommodative financial conditions, thereby supporting the flow of credit to households and businesses. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Mary C. Daly; Charles L. Evans; Randal K. Quarles; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: June 15, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) authorized the use of an additional batch of the Janssen COVID-19 vaccine drug substance manufactured at the Emergent BioSolutions facility under the emergency use authorization (EUA). This is the third batch of Janssen drug substance authorized, following a thorough review of facility records and quality testing. The FDA has not yet included the Emergent BioSolutions plant in the Janssen EUA as an authorized manufacturing facility, but is working on the issue with Janssen and Emergent BioSolutions management. The FDA has also updated translations of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine Fact Sheet for Recipients and Caregivers and its COVID-19 Response At-A-Glance Summary.

title: FDA Approves StrataGraft for the Treatment of Adults with Thermal Burns
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved StrataGraft for the treatment of adult patients with thermal burns containing intact dermal elements, where surgical intervention is clinically indicated. StrataGraft is a bi-layered construct produced from human skin cells grown together, applied topically to the burn wound. The approval is based on two randomized clinical studies involving 101 adult patients with deep partial thickness thermal burns. The treatment has demonstrated effectiveness in achieving complete wound closure and reducing the need for autografts. Common side effects reported were pruritus, blisters, and impaired healing. The safety profile was similar to that of autografting, with no reports of rejection. StrataGraft was granted regenerative medicine advanced therapy, Priority Review, and Orphan Drug designations. It was developed in conjunction with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services’ Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority.

title: Joint Statement—Carbis Bay Group of Seven (G-7) Summit Communiqué
body_summary: On June 11-13, 2021, G7 leaders met in Cornwall to agree on a shared agenda for global action to build back better. They committed to vaccinating the world by 2022, reinvigorating economies with $12 trillion in support, securing future prosperity through freer, fairer trade, and protecting the planet. G7 countries pledged $870 million in vaccine doses and $2 billion in total funding for the ACT-Accelerator to accelerate vaccine distribution to poorest countries. Leaders also acknowledged the Independent Panel's recommendations on global health, committed to improving global resilience, and prioritized a green transition, aiming to cut greenhouse gas emissions and keep the 1.5°C global warming threshold within reach by 2050. The G7 aims to conserve at least 30% of global land, eradicate forced labor in global supply chains by October 2021, and phase out unabated coal power generation by end of 2021. They also support mandatory climate-related financial disclosures and pledged $100 billion annual public and private finance commitment by 2025.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: June 11, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On June 10, the FDA issued a safety communication warning the public to stop using the Innova SARS-CoV-2 Antigen Rapid Qualitative Test for diagnostic use due to concerns over the test's performance. The test has not been authorized, cleared, or approved by the FDA for commercial distribution or use in the United States. The FDA has added sodium citrate tubes to the device shortage list, providing conservation strategies. As of today, 384 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under emergency use authorizations, including 275 molecular tests and 81 antibody and other immune response tests.

title: FDA Takes Steps to Increase Availability of COVID-19 Vaccine
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is authorizing for use, under the emergency use authorization (EUA), two batches of the Janssen COVID-19 Vaccine manufactured at the Emergent BioSolutions facility in Baltimore. The FDA conducted a thorough review of facility records and quality testing results, concluding that these batches are suitable for use. The decision allows the Janssen vaccine made with this drug substance to be used in the U.S. or exported to other countries, subject to certain conditions. The FDA has also revised the letter of authorization to facilitate potential export and will keep the public informed as batches under review are completed. The agency has extended the expiration dating for the refrigerated Janssen COVID-19 Vaccine to 4.5 months, giving jurisdictions with doses on hand additional time to administer vaccine.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Provides Guidance on Measuring Patient-Reported Outcomes in Cancer Clinical Trials
body_summary: The FDA's Oncology Center of Excellence has released a draft guidance document to improve the quality and consistency of patient-reported outcomes in cancer clinical trials. The document, "Core Patient-Reported Outcomes in Cancer Clinical Trials," aims to provide recommendations to sponsors on which patient-reported outcomes to measure and how often to assess them. The draft guidance addresses the administration schedule of products, frequency of PRO assessments, and labeling considerations for PROs submitted with oncology product applications. The FDA's efforts are part of a sustained effort to engage patients and outcomes research experts in identifying methods to rigorously collect patient-reported outcomes in cancer clinical trials.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: June 8, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The White House, HHS Office of the Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response, and FDA released policy recommendations to address vulnerabilities in the US pharmaceutical supply chain. The recommendations have been accepted by President Biden. FDA Acting Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that pharmaceutical supply chains are essential for national and health security, and it is the right time to take action to keep the supply chain secure and resilient. The FDA has also issued warning letters to companies selling unapproved products with unproven COVID-19 claims, and a Wisconsin man was sentenced to three years in prison for tampering with and attempting to spoil COVID vaccine doses. As of today, 384 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 275 molecular tests and 28 antigen tests.

title: FDA Grants Accelerated Approval for Alzheimer’s Drug
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Aduhelm for the treatment of Alzheimer’s disease. Aduhelm was approved using the accelerated approval pathway for a serious and life-threatening illness that provides a meaningful therapeutic advantage over existing treatments. The approval is based on the drug's effect on a surrogate endpoint, reduction of amyloid beta plaque, which is reasonably likely to predict a clinical benefit to patients.

Alzheimer’s disease affects 6.2 million Americans and is an irreversible, progressive brain disorder that slowly destroys memory and thinking skills. Researchers evaluated Aduhelm's efficacy in three studies representing 3,482 patients, showing a significant dose-and time-dependent reduction of amyloid beta plaque.

The FDA requires Biogen, the company behind Aduhelm, to conduct a new randomized, controlled clinical trial to verify the drug's clinical benefit. Aduhelm was granted Fast Track designation to expedite its development and review.

title: Statement on Federal Government Benefits for Residents of Puerto Rico
body_summary: The Department of Justice will file a brief in the Supreme Court case United States v. Vaello-Madero, addressing the constitutionality of a provision in the Social Security Act that denies Puerto Rico residents Supplemental Security Income (SSI). This provision is inconsistent with the administration's policies and values. The Department of Justice has a longstanding practice of defending the constitutionality of Federal statutes, regardless of policy preferences. The administration calls on Congress to amend the Social Security Act to extend SSI benefits to Puerto Rico residents, and supports eliminating Medicaid funding caps and aligning the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program with states.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Patients with Plasminogen Deficiency, a Rare Genetic Disorder
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Ryplazim (plasminogen, human-tvmh) for treating patients with plasminogen deficiency type 1, also known as hypoplasminogenemia. This rare genetic disease impairs tissue and organ function and may lead to blindness. The approval helps address an unmet medical need for individuals affected by this disease. The active ingredient in Ryplazim is plasminogen, purified from human plasma, which increases plasma levels to temporarily correct the deficiency and reduce lesions. A single-arm, open-label clinical trial of 15 patients showed at least 50% improvement in lesions and no new lesions in 48 weeks. Common side effects include abdominal pain, bleeding, and fatigue. The FDA granted Ryplazim Orphan Drug Designation, Fast Track designation, and Priority Review, and also offered a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher.

title: FDA Approves New Drug Treatment for Chronic Weight Management, First Since 2014
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Wegovy (semaglutide) injection for chronic weight management in adults with obesity or overweight, in addition to a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity. The drug is indicated for adults with a BMI of 27 kg/m2 or greater with at least one weight-related condition, or those with a BMI of 30 kg/m2 or greater. The approval was granted to Novo Nordisk. The drug works by mimicking a hormone that targets appetite and food intake. In clinical trials, over 2,600 patients received Wegovy for up to 68 weeks, with an average weight loss of 12.4%. Common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, and vomiting. The FDA has warned about the potential risk of thyroid C-cell tumors and pancreatitis.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: June 4, 2021
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On June 1, the FDA approved an abbreviated new drug application for albuterol sulfate inhalation aerosol 90 mcg (base)/actuation, a treatment for bronchospasm in patients four years of age and older. The FDA has also prioritized the review of generic drug applications for potential treatments and supportive therapies for patients with COVID-19.

The FDA has updated information on the SARS-CoV-2 Viral Mutations: Impact on COVID-19 Tests webpage, including a potential impact on the performance of the Mesa Biotech Inc. Accula SARS-CoV-2 Test due to a genetic mutation. The FDA has also reissued the Letter of Authorization for REGEN-COV (Casirivimab and Imdevimab) treatment for COVID-19, updating the dosage and coformulation presentation.

Additionally, the FDA has authorized 380 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 275 molecular tests and 25 antigen tests. This includes 52 molecular authorizations that can be used with home-collected samples.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA provides new guidance to further enhance the security of prescription drugs in the U.S. supply chain
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is finalizing two guidance documents to help ensure that prescription drugs are identified and traced properly as they move through the supply chain. The FDA is issuing these guidance documents to help stakeholders comply with the Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) requirements. The DSCSA, enacted in 2013, aims to build an electronic, interoperable system to identify and trace certain prescription drugs as they are distributed in the US. The FDA is also soliciting feedback to further improve the drug supply chain under DSCSA. The guidance documents cover various aspects of DSCSA, including enhanced drug distribution security at the package level, which goes into effect on November 27, 2023. The FDA is providing recommendations on system attributes necessary for secure tracing of products at the package level.

title: FDA Alerts Health Care Providers to Stop New Implants of Certain Ventricular Assist Device System
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is advising healthcare providers to stop implanting end-stage heart failure patients with Medtronic's Heartware Ventricular Assist Device (HVAD) System due to a higher frequency of neurological adverse events and mortality associated with the system. Medtronic has stopped the distribution and sale of the HVAD System and issued a notification requesting physicians to stop new implants. The FDA advises using alternative devices, such as the Abbott Heartmate 3 Left Ventricular Assist System (LVAS), and informing patients to continue normal use of device components. The FDA has received over 100 complaints, including reports of 14 patient deaths, and will continue to monitor adverse events associated with the device.

title: FDA Authorizes Marketing of Diagnostic Aid for Autism Spectrum Disorder
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of the Cognoa ASD Diagnosis Aid, a machine learning-based software to help diagnose autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in children 18 months to 5 years old. The device uses input from parents, caregivers, and health care providers to assist physicians in evaluating patients at risk of ASD. The FDA assessed the device's safety and effectiveness in a study of 425 patients and found it to provide a positive or negative diagnosis in 32% of patients, with 81% of those with a positive diagnosis matching the panel's conclusions. The device is intended as an aid in the diagnosis of ASD, not a stand-alone diagnostic device. The FDA has established special controls for devices of this type, including requirements related to labeling and performance testing.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: June 1, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has announced several actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA has issued a safety communication warning the public to stop using the Lepu Medical Technology SARS-CoV-2 Antigen Rapid Test Kit and the Leccurate SARS-CoV-2 Antibody Rapid Test Kit due to concerns over their performance. These tests were not authorized, cleared, or approved by the FDA and have been identified as a Class I recall, the most serious type of recall. The FDA has authorized 380 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 275 molecular tests, 80 antibody tests, and 25 antigen tests.

title: FDA Launches Challenge to Spur Development of Affordable Traceability Tools as Part of Broader Food Safety Efforts
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) launched a challenge to develop affordable, tech-enabled traceability tools to improve food safety. The goal is to encourage the development of low- to no-cost traceability solutions that can be used by food producers of all sizes. The challenge aims to advance the FDA's New Era of Smarter Food Safety initiative, which was released in July 2020. The FDA is seeking innovative solutions from food technology solution providers, public health advocates, and entrepreneurs. The challenge invites submissions from June 1 through July 30, and up to 12 winners will be selected based on their solutions' ability to meet specific traceability challenges and demonstrate innovation, usability, affordability, scalability, and interoperability.

title: Nevada-Based Bottled Water Manufacturer Agrees to Stop Production for Failure to Comply with Manufacturing Requirements
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced that Real Water Inc. has agreed to cease operations until it complies with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and other requirements. A consent decree of permanent injunction was entered on June 1 between the U.S. and Real Water Inc., along with its majority shareholder, AffinityLifestyles.com Inc. and its executives. The FDA alleges that Real Water Inc. violated the FD&C Act by failing to meet preventive controls requirements and follow current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) requirements for bottled water. The company's products were linked to cases of acute liver failure and non-viral hepatitis in adults, resulting in one death. Real Water Inc. issued a precautionary recall of all sizes of its products on March 24. As part of the consent decree, the company must hire a qualified independent expert to inspect its facilities and establish procedures to ensure compliance with the FD&C Act and its implementing regulations.

title: FDA Seeks $6.5 Billion to Further Investments in Critical Public Health Infrastructure, Core Food Safety and Medical Product Safety Programs
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has requested a total budget of $6.5 billion for FY 2022, an 8% increase over FY 2021, to invest in critical public health infrastructure, core food safety and medical product safety programs, and other vital public health programs. The request includes $3.6 billion in budget authority and $2.9 billion in user fees. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that the funding will support immediate priorities and address complex challenges, such as the opioid crisis and promoting health equity among underserved communities. The budget request includes increases for critical public health infrastructure, core safety programs, and public health issues.

title: Executive Order 14031—Advancing Equity, Justice, and Opportunity for Asian Americans, Native Hawaiians, and Pacific Islanders
body_summary: The President establishes the President's Advisory Commission on Asian Americans, Native Hawaiians, and Pacific Islanders and the White House Initiative on Asian Americans, Native Hawaiians, and Pacific Islanders to advance equity, justice, and opportunity for these communities. The Commission provides advice on executive branch efforts to address systemic barriers and promote inclusion. The White House Initiative is led by two Co-Chairs and the Commission's Executive Director, and requires agencies to prepare plans outlining measurable actions to advance equity for American Indian and Alaska Native communities. The Initiative coordinates with the Regional Network to support these communities and will develop a government-wide interagency plan annually, building on four previous executive orders.

title: FDA Approves First Targeted Therapy for Lung Cancer Mutation Previously Considered Resistant to Drug Therapy
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Lumakras (sotorasib) as the first treatment for adult patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) whose tumors have a specific type of genetic mutation called KRAS G12C and who have received at least one prior systemic therapy. This approval represents a significant step towards personalized treatment approaches for patients with certain types of cancer. The FDA approved the 960 milligram dose of Lumakras based on available clinical data and pharmacokinetic modeling. The approved treatment showed an objective response rate of 36% and a duration of response of six months or longer in a study of 124 patients. Common side effects include diarrhea, musculoskeletal pain, nausea, fatigue, liver damage, and cough. Lumakras was approved under the Accelerated Approval pathway and received Fast Track, Priority Review, and Breakthrough Therapy designations. The FDA also approved companion diagnostics, the QIAGEN therascreen KRAS RGQ PCR kit and the Guardant360 CDx, to determine if Lumakras is an appropriate treatment for patients.

title: FDA Seeks $6.5 Billion to Further Investments in Critical Public Health Infrastructure, Core Food Safety and Medical Product Safety Programs
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is requesting a total budget of $6.5 billion for fiscal year (FY) 2022, an 8% increase over FY 2021. This includes $3.6 billion in budget authority and $2.9 billion in user fees. The budget will be used to invest in critical public health infrastructure, core food safety and medical product safety programs, and other vital public health programs. The agency's priorities include funding for data modernization, inspection and surveillance work, and initiatives to improve maternal and infant health. The budget also seeks to address complex challenges such as the opioid crisis and promote health equity among underserved communities. The FDA's budget includes funding for increased inspections, strengthening the supply chain, and improving animal drug safety and predictive technologies. The agency's proposal also includes legislative measures to bolster its authorities and further its mission to protect and promote public health.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: May 28, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced several actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On May 27, the agency issued a warning letter to Oclo Nanotechnology for selling unapproved chlorine dioxide products with unproven COVID-19 claims. The FDA also recommended that healthcare personnel and facilities transition away from using non-NIOSH-approved disposable respirators. As of today, 379 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations.

title: FDA Approves First Targeted Therapy for Lung Cancer Mutation Previously Considered Resistant to Drug Therapy
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Lumakras (sotorasib) as the first treatment for adult patients with non-small cell lung cancer whose tumors have a specific type of genetic mutation called KRAS G12C and who have received at least one prior systemic therapy. The approval is based on a study of 124 patients with locally advanced or metastatic KRAS G12C-mutated non-small cell lung cancer. The objective response rate was 36%, and 58% of those patients had a duration of response of six months or longer. The approved dose is 960 milligrams, and the agency is requiring a postmarketing trial to investigate a lower dose. Common side effects include diarrhea, musculoskeletal pain, and liver damage. The FDA approved Lumakras using the Accelerated Approval pathway, and it also received Fast Track, Priority Review, Breakthrough Therapy, and Orphan Drug designations.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: May 28, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On May 27, 2020, a warning letter was issued to Oclo Nanotechnology for selling unapproved chlorine dioxide products with unproven COVID-19 claims. The FDA also warned consumers not to drink chlorine dioxide products, which can cause nausea, vomiting, and severe dehydration. On May 27, 2021, the FDA recommended that healthcare personnel and facilities transition away from non-NIOSH-approved disposable respirators. As of today, the FDA has authorized 379 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 274 molecular tests, 80 antibody tests, and 25 antigen tests.

title: FDA, FTC Warn Five Companies Illegally Selling Dietary Supplements Claiming to Treat Infertility
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the Federal Trade Commission issued warning letters to five companies for selling dietary supplements that claim to cure, treat, or prevent infertility and other reproductive health disorders. The companies are LeRoche Benicoeur/ConceiveEasy, EU Natural Inc., Fertility Nutraceuticals LLC, SAL NATURE LLC/FertilHerb, and NS Products, Inc. The FDA's Associate Commissioner, Judy McMeekin, stated that such products can harm consumers and said protecting Americans' health is the FDA's highest priority. The FTC's Acting Director, Daniel Kaufman, said women and families facing fertility issues deserve evidence-based solutions. Consumers should be cautious of products with unproven claims and consult their doctor before purchasing or using any dietary supplement or drug.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Additional Monoclonal Antibody for Treatment of COVID-19
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the monoclonal antibody therapy sotrovimab to treat mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older weighing at least 40 kilograms. The authorization is for patients with positive SARS-CoV-2 viral testing and who are at high risk for progression to severe COVID-19. The EUA was granted based on an interim analysis from a clinical trial showing an 85% reduction in hospitalization or death among patients treated with sotrovimab. The treatment is not authorized for hospitalized patients or those requiring oxygen therapy due to COVID-19. Sotrovimab is a laboratory-made protein designed to block the virus' attachment and entry into human cells. The FDA requires fact sheets with dosing instructions, potential side effects, and drug interactions to be made available to healthcare providers and patients.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Additional Monoclonal Antibody for Treatment of COVID-19
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the investigational monoclonal antibody therapy sotrovimab to treat mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in adults and pediatric patients 12 years old and older weighing at least 40 kilograms. The EUA is for individuals at high risk of progression to severe COVID-19, including those 65 years old or older, or those with certain medical conditions. Sotrovimab is not authorized for hospitalized patients or those requiring oxygen therapy due to COVID-19. The FDA has evaluated the totality of available evidence and determined that sotrovimab may be effective in treating adults and certain pediatric patients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19. The known and potential benefits of sotrovimab outweigh the known and potential risks for the drug. The EUA was issued to GlaxoSmithKline, and the treatment has shown an 85% reduction in hospitalization or death in patients treated with sotrovimab compared to those receiving a placebo.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Announces Draft Guidances to Help Increase Transparency, Assist Reporting and Timely Completion for Certain Medical Device Studies after FDA Approval or Clearance
body_summary: The FDA issued two draft guidance documents on continuous surveillance of certain devices. The documents aim to increase transparency and assist in reporting and timely completion of studies on the safety and effectiveness of moderate and high-risk devices. The guidance documents describe postmarket surveillance of moderate and high-risk devices and post-approval study procedures. The FDA will reinforce to device sponsors the importance of engaging early and often with the agency to ensure data collection and implementation of required postmarket studies. The FDA's review of post-approval studies and postmarket surveillance data is part of its commitment to protect public health by ensuring devices on the market are safe and effective.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: May 25, 2021
body_summary: The US FDA has updated its guidance on Emergency Use Authorization for Vaccines to Prevent COVID-19, clarifying its approach to reviewing EUA requests for the remainder of the pandemic. The agency may decline to review requests for vaccines not developed with prior engagement. The FDA also issued a report on South Korea's COVID-19 response strategy, which has been deemed successful in "flattening the curve" of the pandemic. As of today, the FDA has authorized 378 tests and sample collection devices under EUAs, including 273 molecular tests and 80 antibody tests.

title: FDA Approves First Targeted Therapy for Subset of Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Rybrevant (amivantamab-vmjw) as the first treatment for adult patients with non-small cell lung cancer whose tumors have specific types of genetic mutations: epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) exon 20 insertion mutations. The FDA also approved the Guardant360 CDx (Guardant Health Inc.) as a companion diagnostic for Rybrevant. This approval marks the first time patients with non-small cell lung cancer with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations will have a targeted treatment option. The approval was granted to Janssen Pharmaceutical Companies of Johnson & Johnson. The study evaluated Rybrevant's efficacy in 81 patients and showed an overall response rate of 40%. Common side effects include rash, infusion-related reactions, and shortness of breath. Patients taking Rybrevant should limit sun exposure and have their pregnancy status confirmed before treatment.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: May 21, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) continued its response to the COVID-19 pandemic by issuing reminders to healthcare providers to ensure accurate SARS-CoV-2 testing samples. The FDA also updated its FAQs and fact sheets on SARS-CoV-2 antibody tests and COVID-19. The agency revised its definition of high-risk COVID-19 patients, including additional medical conditions. Additionally, the FDA authorized 376 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including molecular, antibody, and antigen tests. The FDA received a $9.2 million grant to expand the CURE ID platform for automated data collection from electronic health records. The agency issued a warning letter to BGP, LLC, for selling an unapproved product with unproven COVID-19 claims.

title: FDA Announces Seizure of Adulterated Dietary Supplements Containing Kratom
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration announced the seizure of over 207,000 units of dietary supplements and bulk ingredients containing kratom, including 34,000 kilograms of bulk kratom. The products, manufactured by Atofil, LLC, a subsidiary of Premier Manufacturing Products, are worth approximately $1.3 million. The FDA expressed substantial concern over kratom's safety, citing potential for abuse and risks to public health. The agency stated that kratom has been indicated to have both narcotic and stimulant-like effects, and withdrawal symptoms may include hostility, aggression, and muscle aches. The FDA issued an import alert in February 2014 and filed a complaint alleging that kratom is a new dietary ingredient with inadequate information to ensure its safety. The agency continues to warn consumers not to use products containing kratom and encourages reporting of adverse events to the MedWatch program.

title: Joint Statement by President Biden and President Moon Jae-in of South Korea
body_summary: The United States and the Republic of Korea reaffirmed their ironclad alliance, committing to peace, prosperity, and democratic norms. In a new era, they seek a partnership that provides regional stability, human rights, and the rule of law. The US committed to extended deterrence, joint military readiness, and a conditions-based transition of wartime operational control. President Biden and President Moon reiterate their shared commitment to complete denuclearization and address the Democratic People's Republic of Korea's nuclear programs. The two sides agreed to strengthen their alliance on various fronts, including climate change, vaccine cooperation, and democracy, aiming to align official international financing with net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. They also pledged to combat abuse of women, corruption, and ensure freedoms, with President Biden invited to visit the ROK.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Alerts Patients and Health Care Providers About Possible Problems with Mammograms Performed at Capitol Radiology LLC
body_summary: The FDA is alerting patients and healthcare providers that there may be problems with the quality of mammograms performed on or after June 26, 2018, at Capitol Radiology LLC in Laurel, Maryland. The facility failed to meet several requirements of the Mammography Quality Standards Act and had its accreditation revoked by the ACR on March 24, 2021. The FDA recommends that patients contact Capitol Radiology to gain access to their medical records and, in some cases, they may require follow-up imaging with another facility. The annual MQSA inspection revealed that the facility failed to perform a required weekly quality control test for at least 12 consecutive weeks between June 16, 2020, and September 12, 2020. The FDA requires all mammography facilities to meet certain baseline quality standards and be certified to legally operate in the United States.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Solicits Public Feedback on Discussion Paper as Part of its Ongoing Commitment to Patient Safety
body_summary: The FDA is announcing the release of a discussion paper on Conveying Materials Information about Medical Devices to Patients and Healthcare Providers: Considerations for a Framework. This follows an Immunology Devices Panel Advisory Committee meeting held in November 2019, which evaluated the safety of specific materials used in medical devices and discussed the current state of scientific evidence. The discussion paper aims to foster discussion and solicit feedback from stakeholders, including patients, on how to ensure patients and healthcare providers have access to more comprehensive information about medical device materials. The FDA is seeking stakeholder feedback until July 19, 2021, on including more specific materials information on user or tissue-contacting materials in labeling for devices, particularly those that are implanted or intended for repeated use.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on April 27-28, 2021, to discuss economic developments and monetary policy. Financial markets showed modest easing over the intermeeting period, with equity prices rising and Treasury yields declining. The Committee reaffirmed its commitment to achieving maximum employment and price stability. It maintained its target range until labor market conditions reached maximum employment and inflation rose to 2% and moderately exceeded it for some time. The Federal Reserve also agreed to continue increasing Treasury securities and agency mortgage-backed securities by at least $80 billion and $40 billion per month, respectively, while assessing the stance of monetary policy based on incoming information and adjusting as necessary.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Issues Draft Guidance on Early Clinical Studies for Certain Medical Devices to Improve Glycemic Control for Type 2 Diabetes
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a draft guidance providing recommendations for feasibility and early feasibility clinical studies for certain medical devices intended to therapeutically improve glycemic control in patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, independent of medication delivery. This follows a growing interest among medical device manufacturers and researchers, as well as the diabetes community, to develop therapeutic devices for improved glycemic control. The FDA is seeking feedback from manufacturers and the diabetes community, with comments due by July 20, 2021.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Authorizes Longer Time for Refrigerator Storage of Thawed Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine Prior to Dilution, Making Vaccine More Widely Available
body_summary: Pfizer Inc. submitted data to the FDA to support storage of undiluted, thawed vials of its COVID-19 vaccine for up to one month at refrigerator temperatures. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is authorizing undiluted, thawed Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine vials to be stored in the refrigerator at 2°C to 8°C (35°F to 46°F) for up to 1 month. This change should make the vaccine more widely available to the American public. The revised storage time was demonstrated through data submitted to the FDA.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Advises Against Use of SARS-CoV-2 Antibody Test Results to Evaluate Immunity or Protection From COVID-19, Including After Vaccination
body_summary: The FDA is reminding the public of the limitations of COVID-19 antibody testing, particularly after vaccination. Antibody tests can identify individuals who may have been exposed to the virus, but they should not be used to determine immunity or protection. The FDA will continue to monitor the use of authorized antibody tests for other purposes. The FDA's safety communication states that results from SARS-CoV-2 antibody tests should not be used to evaluate immunity or protection from COVID-19 after vaccination. The authorized vaccines induce antibodies to specific viral protein targets, making post-vaccination antibody test results negative in individuals without a history of previous natural infection.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: May 18, 2021
body_summary: The FDA announced actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On May 17, FDA provided information on CytoDyn's leronlimab development program, stating that recent clinical trials data do not support clinical benefit for treating COVID-19. The Janssen COVID-19 Vaccine Fact Sheet has been updated in multiple languages. The FDA authorized 374 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 272 molecular tests, 78 antibody tests, and 24 antigen tests, as well as nine antigen tests and four molecular tests for serial screening programs.

title: FDA In Brief: Science Forum Highlights Regulatory Science Advancements in Protecting and Promoting Public Health
body_summary: The FDA is hosting its 2021 Science Forum, Science as the Foundation for Protecting and Promoting Public Health, on May 26-27. The event will showcase the work of over 11,000 FDA scientists and invited nationally renowned scientists, including Anthony Fauci, M.D. The forum will cover various topics, including improving clinical and postmarket evaluation, using big data, empowering patients and consumers, and advancing products based on novel technologies, as well as medical countermeasures, food and cosmetic safety, and substance use and misuse. The event is hosted by the FDA's Office of the Chief Scientist and will take place virtually.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Provides Guidance on Master Protocols for Evaluating Prevention, Treatment Options for COVID-19
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a final guidance on master protocols for evaluating drugs and biological products for the treatment or prevention of COVID-19. According to Janet Woodcock, M.D., Acting FDA Commissioner, the agency used every tool at its disposal to quickly review and act on new therapies for COVID-19. Master protocols have been used to evaluate multiple drugs simultaneously, such as the Accelerating COVID-19 Therapeutics Interventions and Vaccines (ACTIV) public-private initiative. The FDA expects master protocols to continue playing an important role in addressing public health needs created by the pandemic. The guidance describes FDA's current recommendations for sponsors of master protocols, focusing on design, conduct, and statistical considerations.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: May 14, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a warning letter to Crown Wellness, Inc. on April 29, 2021, for selling an unapproved product with COVID-19 claims. The FDA has authorized 372 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 270 molecular tests, 78 antibody tests, and 24 antigen tests. These tests can be used for various purposes, such as testing and serial screening programs. The FDA has also authorized 498 revisions to EUA authorizations.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Releases Investigation Report Following 2020 Salmonella Outbreak Linked to Red Onions
body_summary: The FDA has released a report on the 2020 Salmonella Newport outbreak, which was linked to red onions and caused over 1,600 reported illnesses in the US and Canada between June and October 2020. The outbreak was investigated by the FDA, CDC, and Canadian officials, and was found to be linked to whole red onions supplied by Thomson International, Inc. The FDA identified several factors that may have contributed to the contamination, including potentially contaminated irrigation water and animal intrusion.
