The FDA's leading hypothesis is that contaminated irrigation water used in a growing field in Holtville, California may have led to contamination of the onions. The FDA encourages all produce growers to assess risks that may be posed by adjacent and nearby land uses, especially as it relates to the presence of livestock and the interface between farmland, rangeland, irrigation water, and other agricultural areas.

title: Statement on the Progress of the Health Insurance Marketplace Special Enrollment Period in Response to the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency
body_summary: The US administration has opened healthcare.gov to provide a special enrollment period for Americans to sign up for health insurance. Since February 15, 1 million Americans have signed up, gaining access to quality, affordable health care. The administration has also made progress in expanding access to health insurance and lowering health costs. Americans with existing coverage can now help family members and friends get covered. The median deductible for new coverage has dropped by 90%, and the administration plans to make premium reductions permanent with the American Families Plan.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Finalizes Guidance with Internationally Harmonized Recommendations to Further Support Safe, High-Quality Human Drug Products
body_summary: The FDA is announcing a final guidance for industry on managing postapproval changes to pharmaceutical products. The guidance, known as "Q12 Technical and Regulatory Considerations for Pharmaceutical Product Lifecycle Management," provides a framework for predicting and efficiently managing changes to product quality. The guidance will help manufacturers identify necessary elements to assure product quality and reduce the likelihood of quality-related supply disruptions and drug shortages. The FDA aims to promote international harmonization of regulatory requirements under the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) and is committed to seeking scientifically-based harmonized technical procedures for the development and manufacture of drugs.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: May 11, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) took action against Covalon Technologies Inc. for selling unapproved COVID-19 products with fraudulent claims. The FDA also expanded the emergency use authorization for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine to include individuals 12 through 15 years of age. The agency updated its COVID-19 ResponseAt-A-Glance Summary and issued a press release on May 10. The FDA authorized 370 tests and sample collection devices, including 270 molecular tests, 76 antibody tests, and 24 antigen tests, for emergency use authorizations. These include 9 antigen tests and 3 molecular tests for serial screening programs. The FDA also authorized 488 revisions to EUA authorizations.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA to Hold Meeting of its Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee to Discuss Pediatric Use of COVID-19 Vaccines
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration's Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research will convene a virtual meeting of the Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee on June 10, 2021, to discuss emergency use authorization for COVID-19 vaccines in individuals 12 through 17 years of age. The committee will consider the data needed to support an emergency use authorization and a biologics license application for a COVID-19 vaccine in children under 12 years of age. The meeting will be webcast and livestreamed on the FDA's YouTube, Facebook, and Twitter channels, and a public docket for comments will be available.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine for Emergency Use in Adolescents in Another Important Action in Fight Against Pandemic
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has expanded the emergency use authorization (EUA) for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine to include adolescents 12 through 15 years of age. The EUA was originally issued for individuals 16 years of age and older in December 2020. The FDA has determined that the vaccine has met the statutory criteria to amend the EUA and that its known and potential benefits outweigh its known and potential risks in this population. The vaccine is administered as a series of two doses, three weeks apart, and has been shown to be non-inferior to the immune response in older participants. The vaccine has also been shown to be 100% effective in preventing COVID-19 among vaccinated participants without prior infection.

title: Statement on the Food and Drug Administration's Expanded Emergency Use Authorization of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine To Include Adolescents
body_summary: The Food and Drug Administration has expanded the emergency use authorization for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine to include individuals 12 to 15 years old, in addition to those 16 years and older. This decision is a promising development in the fight against the virus. Millions of 16- and 17-year-olds have been safely vaccinated, leading to a decline in COVID-19 cases, hospitalizations, and deaths. The safe and effective vaccines are curbing the spread of the virus, saving thousands of lives, and allowing millions of Americans to return to a closer to normal life.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: May 7, 2021
body_summary: The US FDA has taken actions to protect consumers in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On May 6, 2021, the agency issued a warning letter to Disinfect & Shield for selling an unapproved product with fraudulent COVID-19 claims. Consumers should consult with their healthcare provider. The FDA has authorized 370 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 270 molecular tests, 76 antibody tests, and 24 antigen tests. The agency has also authorized 9 antigen tests and 3 molecular tests for serial screening programs and made 483 revisions to EUA authorizations.

title: FDA In Brief: FDA Issues Procedural Notice on Potential Plans to Conduct Research About Use of ‘Healthy’ Symbols on Food Products
body_summary: The FDA is issuing a procedural notice on preliminary consumer research planned on the use of symbols on food product labels to convey the nutrient content claim 'healthy.' The agency is seeking input on ways to enhance the quality, usefulness, and clarity of the information to be collected. This research is part of the FDA's Nutrition Innovation Strategy (NIS) to modernize claims and address health inequities associated with nutrition-related chronic diseases. The FDA plans to publish a proposed rule to update the definition of the 'healthy' nutrient content claim and intends to conduct quantitative consumer research on the proposed symbol. The public has 60 days to comment on the proposed information collection.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Outlines Inspection and Assessment Activities During Pandemic, Roadmap for Future State of Operations
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a new report, "Resiliency Roadmap for FDA Inspectional Oversight," detailing the agency's inspectional activities during the COVID-19 pandemic and its plan to move toward a more consistent state of operations. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that the FDA experienced unprecedented challenges during the pandemic and is committed to getting back to a more consistent state of inspectional capacity.

Between March 2020 and March 2021, the FDA conducted 821 mission-critical inspections, including 29 in foreign countries. The agency also conducted 777 prioritized domestic inspections since resuming work in July 2020. Over 1,300 record requests were made, leading to high levels of regulatory decision actions.

The FDA plans to prioritize domestic and foreign inspections based on risk, with a longer interval between inspections for lower-risk facilities. The agency will also modernize its data enterprise platforms and cross-program interoperability infrastructure to support innovation in regulatory oversight.

The FDA will leverage available tools and resources to meet its inspectional responsibilities while achieving optimal public health outcomes. An agency-wide Inspectional Affairs Council will plan and coordinate inspectional activities.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: May 4, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration announced its actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. As of today, 369 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 270 molecular tests and 76 antibody tests. The FDA has also authorized 8 antigen tests and 3 molecular tests for serial screening programs. Additionally, the agency has authorized 481 revisions to EUA authorizations.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: April 30, 2021
body_summary: The US FDA approved ANDA for 23.4% Sodium Chloride Injection USP and Morphine Sulfate Injection USP. The FDA updated the EUA Authorized Serology Test Performance page and revoked the emergency use authorization for the Battelle CCDS Critical Care Decontamination System. As of March 31, 2021, Battelle ceased all decontamination site operations. The FDA authorized 369 tests and sample collection devices, including 270 molecular tests, 76 antibody and other immune response tests, and 23 antigen tests.

title: FDA Approves Treatment for Chronic Kidney Disease
body_summary: The US FDA has approved Farxiga (dapagliflozin) oral tablets to reduce the risk of kidney function decline, kidney failure, cardiovascular death, and hospitalization for heart failure in adults with chronic kidney disease at risk of disease progression. The approval is based on a multicenter, double-blind study involving 4,304 patients. The study found that Farxiga significantly reduced the risk of disease progression and cardiovascular death compared to a placebo. Patients with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions, dialysis treatment, or specific kidney diseases should not use Farxiga. The medication can cause dehydration, urinary tract infections, and metabolic acidosis, and patients should be assessed for their volume status and kidney function before starting treatment.

title: FDA Commits to Evidence-Based Actions  Aimed at Saving Lives and Preventing Future Generations of Smokers
body_summary: The US FDA has announced plans to issue proposed product standards to significantly reduce disease and death from using combusted tobacco products. The agency will work towards banning menthol as a characterizing flavor in cigarettes and all characterizing flavors in cigars. The decision is based on clear science and evidence establishing the addictiveness and harm of these products. The proposed standards aim to reduce youth initiation, increase smoking cessation among current smokers, and address health disparities. The FDA is taking urgent action to reduce tobacco addiction and curb deaths. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that banning menthol will help people quit and save lives, particularly among communities disproportionately affected by these deadly products.

title: Implementation Note issued April 28, 2021
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on April 28, 2021: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on required and excess reserve balances at 0.10 percent, effective April 29, 2021. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective April 29, 2021, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 0 to 1/4 percent. Increase the System Open Market Account holdings of Treasury securities by $80 billion per month and of agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) by $40 billion per month. Increase holdings of Treasury securities and agency MBS by additional amounts and purchase agency commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) as needed to sustain smooth functioning of markets for these securities. Conduct repurchase agreement operations to support effective policy implementation and the smooth functioning of short-term U.S. dollar funding markets. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 0.00 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $80 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities and reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS in agency MBS. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for purchases and reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 0.25 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The Federal Reserve is committed to using its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals. The COVID-19 pandemic is causing tremendous human and economic hardship across the United States and around the world. Amid progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have strengthened. The sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic remain weak but have shown improvement. Inflation has risen, largely reflecting transitory factors. Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses. The path of the economy will depend significantly on the course of the virus, including progress on vaccinations. The ongoing public health crisis continues to weigh on the economy, and risks to the economic outlook remain. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. With inflation running persistently below this longer-run goal, the Committee will aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time so that inflation averages 2 percent over time and longerâterm inflation expectations remain well anchored at 2 percent. The Committee expects to maintain an accommodative stance of monetary policy until these outcomes are achieved. The Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time. In addition, the Federal Reserve will continue to increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $80 billion per month and of agency mortgageâbacked securities by at least $40 billion per month until substantial further progress has been made toward the Committee's maximum employment and price stability goals. These asset purchases help foster smooth market functioning and accommodative financial conditions, thereby supporting the flow of credit to households and businesses. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Mary C. Daly; Charles L. Evans; Randal K. Quarles; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: FDA Takes Action For Failure to Submit Required Clinical Trial Results Information to ClinicalTrials.Gov
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) requires clinical trial sponsors to register and submit summary results information to ClinicalTrials.gov within 21 days after the first human subject is enrolled. The FDA has issued its first Notice of Noncompliance to Acceleron Pharma, Inc. for failing to submit required summary results information for a clinical trial evaluating the safety and effectiveness of the drug dalantercept in combination with axitinib in patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma. The notice gives Acceleron 30 days to submit the required information, and the FDA authorizes civil money penalties for noncompliance. The FDA takes compliance with these requirements seriously and will continue to encourage voluntary compliance, taking action when necessary to ensure required information is available on ClinicalTrials.gov.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: April 27, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued warning letters to two companies: pharmacygeoff.md for marketing unapproved drugs for multiple diseases, including COVID-19, and Group Cyrenne Inc. dba HomeoAnimal for selling a "Virus Defense Kit" containing products that claim to mitigate, prevent, treat, diagnose, or cure COVID-19 in pets. The FDA has also authorized over 369 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs) for COVID-19 testing, including 270 molecular tests and 76 antibody and other immune response tests. The FDA recommends that consumers consult with their healthcare provider and veterinarians about COVID-19 and that consumers concerned about COVID-19 should consult with their healthcare provider.

title: FDA Authorizes Marketing of Device to Facilitate Muscle Rehabilitation in Stroke Patients
body_summary: The US FDA has authorized the marketing of the Neurolutions IpsiHand Upper Extremity Rehabilitation System, a Brain-Computer-Interface device, for stroke rehabilitation patients 18 and older. The device, which assists in muscle re-education and range of motion, was found safe and effective in a 12-week trial involving 40 patients. The FDA granted Breakthrough Device designation, expedited review, and special controls for devices of this type. The device is prescription-only, may not be used by patients with severe spasticity or skull defects, and was reviewed through the De Novo classification request. The FDA protects the public health by ensuring safety and effectiveness of medical devices, including this new authorization for the IpsiHand System.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: April 23, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has taken actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA recently inspected Emergent BioSolutions, a proposed manufacturing facility for the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 Vaccine, and cited observations that did not meet FDA requirements. Emergent BioSolutions has agreed to pause new production while working with the FDA to resolve quality issues. Vaccines already manufactured will undergo additional testing and evaluation before potential distribution. The FDA has authorized 369 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 270 molecular tests, 76 antibody tests, and 23 antigen tests.

title: FDA and CDC Lift Recommended Pause on Johnson & Johnson (Janssen) COVID-19 Vaccine Use Following Thorough Safety Review
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration and the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention have determined that the recommended pause on the use of the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 Vaccine in the US should be lifted. The pause was recommended after reports of six cases of a rare and severe type of blood clot. Medical and scientific teams reviewed available data, including reports submitted to the Vaccine Adverse Event Reporting System, and concluded that the vaccine's known and potential benefits outweigh its known and potential risks in individuals 18 years of age and older. The FDA and CDC will continue to monitor the safety of the vaccine and have confidence that it is safe and effective in preventing COVID-19.

title: FDA Approves Immunotherapy for Endometrial Cancer with Specific Biomarker
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted accelerated approval to Jemperli (dostarlimab) for treating patients with recurrent or advanced endometrial cancer that has progressed on or following prior treatment with a platinum-containing chemotherapy and whose cancers have a specific genetic feature known as dMMR. The approval was given after a single-arm, multi-cohort clinical trial showed that 42.3% of patients with dMMR recurrent or advanced endometrial cancer who received Jemperli had a complete or partial response to treatment. Common side effects include fatigue, nausea, and diarrhea, and serious conditions such as inflammation of healthy organs may occur. Jemperli is approved for use by women with dMMR endometrial cancer, and the FDA designated the treatment as a Breakthrough Therapy. The approval was granted to GlaxoSmithKline, and the agency has protected the public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of the treatment.

title: FDA Continues Important Steps to Ensure Quality, Safety and Effectiveness of Authorized COVID-19 Vaccines
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has completed an inspection of Emergent BioSolutions, a proposed manufacturing facility for the Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 Vaccine. The FDA has not authorized this facility to manufacture or distribute any of Johnson & Johnson's COVID-19 Vaccine or components. The inspection cited several observations, which are outlined in the FDA Form 483. The FDA is working with Emergent BioSolutions to address these conditions, including pausing new production and conducting additional testing of existing vaccines.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: April 20, 2021
body_summary: The FDA has taken steps to facilitate the authorization of tests for pooling specimens from asymptomatic individuals in serial testing programs. The agency issued an amendment for many molecular diagnostic COVID-19 tests that had received an emergency use authorization for testing individual samples. The amendment requires test developers to submit a notification to the FDA with information required by the amendment. As of today, 367 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations. This includes 269 molecular tests and sample collection devices, 75 antibody and other immune response tests, and 23 antigen tests. The FDA has authorized 8 antigen tests and 2 molecular tests for serial screening programs.

title: FDA Announces New Streamlined Approach to Add Pooled Serial Screening Claims to Certain Authorized Tests for Use in Serial Testing Programs
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an amendment to many molecular diagnostic COVID-19 tests that had received an emergency use authorization (EUA), allowing for the use of pooled nasal specimens in serial testing programs. The amendment enables test developers to self-certify their tests for pooling, and the FDA will add those tests to a list of authorized tests for pooling nasal specimens. This move aims to increase testing accessibility and capacity. The FDA has established requirements for test developers to submit notifications with validation data and pooling procedures to utilize this approach. The public can access the full list of authorized tests on the FDA website.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Revokes Emergency Use Authorization for Monoclonal Antibody Bamlanivimab
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) revoked the emergency use authorization (EUA) for bamlanivimab, a monoclonal antibody therapy, to treat mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in adults and certain pediatric patients. The decision was made based on the increasing risk of treatment failure due to the emergence of SARS-CoV-2 viral variants resistant to bamlanivimab alone. The FDA issued the EUA on November 9, 2020, and determined that the known and potential benefits no longer outweigh the risks. Alternative monoclonal antibody therapies, such as REGEN-COV and bamlanivimab and etesevimab, remain available under EUA for the same uses.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: April 16, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The agency issued a warning letter to Trinity Natural Health & Pain Management, Inc. for selling an unapproved product with fraudulent COVID-19 claims. The FDA requested the company to cease the sale of any unapproved products for COVID-19 treatment or prevention. On Tuesday, the FDA and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommended a pause in the use of the Janssen (Johnson & Johnson) COVID-19 Vaccine due to six reported cases of a rare and severe type of blood clot in people who received the vaccine. The FDA added questions to its website about the recommended pause. The agency also authorized over 363 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 266 molecular tests and 75 antibody tests.

title: FDA Approves First Immunotherapy for Initial Treatment of Gastric Cancer
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Opdivo (nivolumab) in combination with certain types of chemotherapy for the initial treatment of patients with advanced or metastatic gastric cancer, gastroesophageal junction cancer, and esophageal adenocarcinoma. This is the first FDA-approved immunotherapy for the first-line treatment of gastric cancer. Richard Pazdur, M.D., director of the FDA's Oncology Center of Excellence, stated that the approval shows a survival benefit for patients with advanced or metastatic gastric cancer. Opdivo was evaluated in a randomized, multicenter trial of 1,581 patients, where those receiving Opdivo in combination with chemotherapy lived longer than those receiving chemotherapy alone. Median survival was 13.8 months for patients receiving Opdivo plus chemotherapy, compared to 11.6 months for those receiving chemotherapy alone. Common side effects include peripheral neuropathy, nausea, fatigue, and musculoskeletal pain. Serious conditions such as immune-mediated side effects, including pneumonitis, colitis, and nephritis, can also occur. Opdivo was granted Priority Review and Orphan Drug designations, and approval was given to Bristol-Myers Squibb Company. The review was conducted under Project Orbis, which includes collaboration with international regulatory agencies.

title: FDA Provides Guidance on Remote Interactive Evaluations for Oversight of Drug Facilities During COVID-19
body_summary: The FDA has used various tools to oversee facilities that manufacture FDA-regulated products during the COVID-19 public health emergency, including record requests, reliance on trusted regulatory partners, and remote interactive evaluations. These evaluations have informed the FDA's regulatory decision-making, ensured drug quality, and helped determine the scope, depth, and timing of future inspections. The FDA is expanding the use of remote interactive evaluations as part of its strategy to evaluate medical product facilities. A new guidance document, "Remote Interactive Evaluations of Drug Manufacturing and Bioresearch Monitoring Facilities During the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency," provides clarity on how the FDA will request and conduct these evaluations. The agency will use various interactive tools, including remote livestreaming, teleconferences, and screen sharing, to evaluate facilities at pharmaceutical companies, bioresearch monitoring facilities, and outsourcing facilities registered under section 503B of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. The FDA will use risk management methods and related tools to determine when to request a facility's participation in a remote interactive evaluation.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: April 13, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced actions to address COVID-19 health disparities among racial and ethnic minority communities. The FDA has authorized 358 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 262 molecular tests, 75 antibody tests, and 21 antigen tests. The agency has also authorized tests for serial screening programs. As part of National Minority Health Month, the FDA is focusing on strategies to address health disparities and protect the health of diverse populations.

title: Joint CDC and FDA Statement on Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 Vaccine
body_summary: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) are reviewing six reported cases of a rare and severe type of blood clot in individuals after receiving the Johnson & Johnson (J&J) vaccine. These cases, which occurred among women aged 18-48, resulted in cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) and thrombocytopenia. The CDC will convene an Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) meeting to assess the potential significance of these cases. The FDA is also investigating the cases. As a precaution, the CDC recommends a pause in the use of the J&J vaccine until the process is complete. The CDC and FDA will provide additional information and answer questions at a media briefing later today.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: April 9, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA recommends that healthcare personnel and facilities transition away from using decontaminated disposable respirators for reuse, due to an adequate domestic supply of new respirators approved by the CDC's NIOSH. The FDA also issued warning letters to two companies, Allure Imports and About Mineral, for selling unapproved products with fraudulent COVID-19 claims. The FDA requested these companies to immediately cease the sale of such products. As of today, 354 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 258 molecular tests and 75 antibody tests.

title: FDA Authorizes Marketing of First Device that Uses Artificial Intelligence to Help Detect Potential Signs of Colon Cancer
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized marketing of the GI Genius, the first device that uses artificial intelligence (AI) to assist clinicians in detecting lesions in the colon during colonoscopies. Courtney H. Lias, Ph.D., acting director of the GastroRenal, ObGyn, General Hospital and Urology Devices Office, stated that AI has the potential to transform healthcare and improve patient care. A study involving 700 subjects found that the GI Genius was able to identify lab-confirmed adenomas or carcinomas in 55.1% of patients, compared to 42.0% with standard colonoscopy, an observed difference of 13%. The device is designed to highlight regions of the colon where a potential lesion is detected, allowing for a more extended examination in real time during colonoscopy. The FDA reviewed the GI Genius through the De Novo premarket review pathway and granted marketing authorization to Cosmo Artificial Intelligence, Ltd.

title: FDA Releases Action Plan for Reducing Exposure to Toxic Elements from Foods for Babies, Young Children
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced a new action plan, Closer to Zero, to reduce exposure to toxic elements in foods commonly eaten by babies and young children. The plan sets forth the FDA's approach to achieving the lowest possible levels of toxic elements, such as arsenic, lead, cadmium, and mercury, in these foods.

The FDA's goal is to reduce the levels of these toxic elements to the greatest extent possible, while also considering the feasibility and achievability of action levels. The plan outlines a multi-phase approach, with the first phase focusing on setting action levels for lead in categories of foods consumed by babies and young children.

The FDA will use a four-pronged approach to set action levels, including evaluating the scientific basis, proposing action levels, consulting with stakeholders, and finalizing action levels. The agency will prioritize its work on elements for which it has the most data and information, starting with arsenic and lead.

The Closer to Zero plan aims to push the levels of toxic elements in these foods closer and closer to zero over time, while also ensuring that limiting exposure to toxic elements does not have unintended consequences. The FDA will continue its research and collaborations on this topic, and plans to combine its efforts with other initiatives to improve maternal and infant nutrition and health.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting on March 16-17, 2021, and approved a final rule revising Rules Regarding Availability of Information. The committee's policy framework and forward guidance remained consistent, with expectations from Desk surveys little changed. The labor market showed signs of recovery, with average hourly earnings and compensation per hour increasing due to changes in workforce composition. Treasury yield curve steepened, with 5- and 10-year yields rising, attributed to increased investor optimism about the economic outlook. Broad equity price indexes rose on net, consistent with the stronger outlook. Spreads on high-yield corporate bonds narrowed, and financing conditions for businesses and households with access to capital markets remained accommodative. The staff expected real GDP growth to slow down in 2022 and 2023 but still outpace potential, leading to a decline in the unemployment rate. Participants expected annual inflation to edge down next year, with supply constraints and strong aggregate demand supporting the economy's reopening. The Committee reaffirmed its commitment to using its full range of tools to support the US economy during the pandemic, aiming for maximum employment and inflation averaging 2 percent over time.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Issues Emergency Use Authorization for the Symbiotica COVID-19 Self-Collected Antibody Test System
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued an emergency use authorization for the Symbiotica COVID-19 Self-Collected Antibody Test System, allowing for the first antibody test authorized for use with home-collected dried blood spot samples. This test is intended for individuals 18 years or older or 5 years or older, collected by an adult, to aid in identifying those with an adaptive immune response to SARS-CoV-2. The test should not be used to diagnose acute infection and its effectiveness and duration in conferring immunity are currently unknown.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: April 6, 2021
body_summary: The FDA announced actions to aid in responding to the COVID-19 pandemic. It issued an Emergency Use Authorization to Symbiotica, Inc. for the COVID-19 Self-Collected Antibody Test System, allowing for at-home blood sample collection. The test system requires a prescription and aims to identify recent or previous COVID-19 infections. The FDA also issued a new guidance on developing generic drugs during the pandemic, providing general recommendations to applicants. As of today, 355 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under emergency use authorizations, including 258 molecular tests, 75 antibody tests, and 22 antigen tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Makes Two Revisions to Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine Emergency Use Authorization to Help Increase the Number of Vaccine Doses Available
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced two revisions to the Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine. The first revision clarifies the number of doses per vial, allowing for a maximum of 11 doses with a range of 10-11 doses. The second revision authorizes the availability of an additional multi-dose vial with a maximum of 15 doses, ranging from 13-15 doses. The revisions aim to increase vaccine supply, allowing more doses to be administered quickly. Director Peter Marks stated that these changes will help end the pandemic more rapidly. The FDA evaluated data showing the number of doses that can be extracted from the vials, which will be reflected in the updated Fact Sheet for Healthcare Providers. The dosing regimen remains unchanged, and the vaccine is administered as a two-dose series.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: April 2, 2021
body_summary: The US FDA has taken swift action to get more tests for screening asymptomatic individuals on the market. On March 31, the FDA authorized several COVID-19 tests for over-the-counter use without a prescription for serial screening, such as testing twice a week in schools or other settings. The FDA also authorized serial screening tests for use in a point-of-care setting, such as a doctor's office. The agency has authorized 354 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 258 molecular tests, 74 antibody tests, and 22 antigen tests. The FDA has also posted new information on viral mutations and impact on COVID-19 tests, including translations in five additional languages.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Continues to Advance Over-the Counter and Other Screening Test Development
body_summary: The US FDA took swift action to authorize several tests for screening asymptomatic individuals on the market. The agency authorized several over-the-counter (OTC) tests for serial screening, as well as one serial screening test for use in a point-of-care (POC) setting without a prescription. These authorizations follow the FDA's recent actions to advance OTC and other screening test development. The tests authorized include Quidel QuickVue, Abbott BinaxNOW, and BD Veritor System, among others. The authorizations are part of the FDA's efforts to support test development and increase consumer access to testing, particularly for serial screening of asymptomatic individuals.

title: FDA is Investigating Reports of Infections Associated with Reprocessed Urological Endoscopes
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is investigating medical device reports describing patient infections and contamination issues associated with reprocessing urological endoscopes, including cystoscopes, ureteroscopes, and cystourethroscopes. The FDA is concerned about three reported deaths outside the United States and is reminding healthcare providers to follow labeling and reprocessing instructions to properly clean and reprocess the devices. Since January 1, 2017, through February 20, 2021, the FDA received over 450 medical device reports describing post-procedure patient infections or other possible contamination issues associated with reprocessing these devices. Olympus Corporation and Karl Storz were cited as device manufacturers in some reports. The FDA is continuing to investigate these reports and has issued recommendations for reprocessing and using these devices.

title: FDA Allows for First Point-of-Care  Chlamydia and Gonorrhea Test to be Used in More Near-Patient Care Settings
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has allowed the use of the Binx Health IO CT/NG Assay at point-of-care settings, including physician offices and urgent care centers, under a Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA) Certificate of Waiver. The waiver was granted due to the test's performance being comparable to those performed in a CLIA certified laboratory. The test can detect the presence of bacteria causing chlamydia and gonorrhea in approximately 30 minutes. Tim Stenzel, director of the Office of In Vitro Diagnostics and Radiological Health, stated that this allows for quicker and more appropriate treatment of sexually-transmitted infections, which affect one in five Americans annually.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: March 30, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has updated its COVID-19 response efforts, including approving an abbreviated new drug application for succinylcholine chloride injection USP 200 mg/10 mL. This approval, effective March 29, allows the injection to facilitate tracheal intubation and provide skeletal muscle relaxation during surgery or mechanical ventilation. The FDA has also authorized 349 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 258 molecular tests and 74 antibody and other immune response tests. The agency continues to facilitate access to safe and effective medical products to address critical needs during the pandemic.

title: FDA Approves First Cell-Based Gene Therapy for Adult Patients with Multiple Myeloma
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Abecma, a cell-based gene therapy, for treating adult patients with multiple myeloma who have not responded to or whose disease has returned after at least four prior lines of therapy. The therapy, developed by Celgene Corporation, a Bristol Myers Squibb company, is the first cell-based gene therapy approved by the FDA for multiple myeloma. According to the National Cancer Institute, multiple myeloma accounted for approximately 1.8% (32,000) of all new cancer cases in the US in 2020.

Abecma is a B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-directed genetically modified autologous chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, where patients' own T-cells are collected, genetically modified, and infused back into the patient. The therapy has shown promising results, with 72% of patients partially or completely responding to treatment, and 65% remaining in complete response for at least 12 months.

However, treatment with Abecma can cause severe side effects, including cytokine release syndrome, hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis/macrophage activation syndrome, neurologic toxicity, and prolonged cytopenia. The FDA is requiring hospitals and clinics that dispense Abecma to be specially certified and staff to be trained to recognize and manage these side effects.

title: FDA Authorizes Marketing of Device to Improve Gait in Multiple Sclerosis Patients
body_summary: The US FDA has authorized the marketing of the Portable Neuromodulation Stimulator (PoNS), a device intended for treating gait deficit in patients with mild to moderate multiple sclerosis (MS) symptoms. The device is a neuromuscular tongue stimulator that generates electrical pulses to stimulate the trigeminal and facial nerves. The device is for use by patients aged 22 and older as an adjunct to supervised therapeutic exercise programs. The device was assessed through two clinical studies and a retrospective analysis of real-world data, showing significant improvement in gait function in patients with MS. The PoNS device is not approved for use in patients with certain medical conditions, such as penetrating brain injuries or pacemakers. The device was granted Breakthrough Device designation and reviewed through the De Novo premarket review pathway.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: March 26, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration announced several actions in its ongoing response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On March 23, 2021, an emergency use authorization was issued to Twist Bioscience Corporation for their SARS-CoV-2 NGS Assay, a next-generation sequencing test for identifying SARS-CoV-2 RNA. The FDA has authorized 348 tests and sample collection devices, including 258 molecular tests, 74 antibody and immune response tests, and 16 antigen tests, which can be used with home-collected samples. The agency is also publicly sharing information about the evidence behind emergency use authorizations for COVID-19 vaccines.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: March 23, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On March 22, the FDA provided an update on simple steps to slow the spread of the disease. The FDA and the National Institutes of Health (NIH) have also made updates to the CURE ID app to improve its effectiveness. The agency issued a warning letter to PYRLess Group, LLC dba Dr. Fitt, for selling unapproved products with fraudulent COVID-19 claims. As of today, 343 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including molecular tests, antibody tests, and antigen tests. The FDA is responsible for protecting the public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: FDA Warns Companies Illegally Selling Over-the-Counter CBD Products for Pain Relief
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued warning letters to Honest Globe Inc. and Biolyte Laboratories LLC for selling products labeled as containing cannabidiol (CBD) in ways that violate the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act). The FDA has not approved any over-the-counter (OTC) drugs containing CBD, and none of these products meet the requirements to be legally marketed without an approved new drug application. The letters cite substandard manufacturing practices and explain that CBD has known pharmacological effects on humans, with demonstrated risks. FDA Principal Deputy Commissioner Amy Abernethy stated that unapproved CBD products may have dangerous health impacts and side effects. The FDA will continue to monitor and take action against companies that unlawfully market their products, prioritizing those that pose a risk to public health. The FDA has previously sent warning letters to other companies for illegal selling of unapproved CBD products, and has not approved any CBD-containing drug products other than one prescription drug for treating seizures.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes First Machine Learning-Based Screening Device to Identify Certain Biomarkers That May Indicate COVID-19 Infection
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the Tiger Tech COVID Plus Monitor, a machine learning-based screening device for COVID-19. The device is intended for use by trained personnel to identify certain biomarkers indicative of hypercoagulation, sepsis, cancer, and severe allergic reactions in asymptomatic individuals over 5. The device is designed for use after a temperature reading that does not meet fever criteria in settings following CDC guidelines. The FDA director, Jeff Shuren, stated that the device could help identify infected individuals and reduce COVID-19 spread in various public settings. The device's clinical performance was studied in hospital and school settings, demonstrating a 98.6% positive percent agreement and 94.5% negative percent agreement. The FDA issued the EUA to Tiger Tech Solutions, Inc.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: March 19, 2021
body_summary:
The FDA announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic: 
On March 16, a new web page was posted to help establish testing programs for screening people without symptoms and with no known or suspected exposure to COVID-19. 
The FDA also posted templates for test developers to facilitate submission of an EUA request for certain COVID-19 tests. 
On March 17, the FDA granted marketing authorization for BioFire Diagnostics' BioFire Respiratory Panel 2.1 diagnostic test, which can be marketed beyond the public health emergency. 
The FDA approved an abbreviated new drug application for azithromycin tablets, indicated for specified mild to moderate infections caused by designated, susceptible bacteria. 
The FDA authorized revised fact sheets for health care providers to include additional information on susceptibility of SARS-CoV-2 variants to each monoclonal antibody therapy. 
As of March 18, 341 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 254 molecular tests and sample collection devices, 72 antibody and other immune response tests, and 15 antigen tests.

title: FDA Permits Marketing of First SARS-CoV-2 Diagnostic Test Using Traditional Premarket Review Process
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted marketing authorization to the BioFire Respiratory Panel 2.1, a diagnostic test for simultaneous qualitative detection and identification of multiple respiratory viral and bacterial nucleic acids in nasopharyngeal swabs. The test, which had an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA), was granted marketing authorization using the De Novo premarket review pathway. The grant marks an important step in the FDA's response to the COVID-19 pandemic, as it is the first SARS-CoV-2 diagnostic test permitted to be marketed beyond the public health emergency. The FDA reviewed data from over 500 test samples and demonstrated a reasonable assurance that the test was safe and effective. The test is for use in individuals suspected of respiratory tract infections, including COVID-19. The FDA has revoked the EUA for this device and established special controls to define labeling and performance testing requirements. The marketing authorization was granted to BioFire Diagnostics LLC.

title: Implementation Note issued March 17, 2021
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on March 17, 2021: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on required and excess reserve balances at 0.10 percent, effective March 18, 2021. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective March 18, 2021, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 0 to 1/4 percent. Increase the System Open Market Account holdings of Treasury securities by $80 billion per month and of agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) by $40 billion per month. Increase holdings of Treasury securities and agency MBS by additional amounts and purchase agency commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) as needed to sustain smooth functioning of markets for these securities. Conduct repurchase agreement operations to support effective policy implementation and the smooth functioning of short-term U.S. dollar funding markets. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 0.00 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $80 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities and reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS in agency MBS. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for purchases and reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 0.25 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The Federal Reserve is committed to using its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals. The COVID-19 pandemic is causing tremendous human and economic hardship across the United States and around the world. Following a moderation in the pace of the recovery, indicators of economic activity and employment have turned up recently, although the sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic remain weak. Inflation continues to run below 2 percent. Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses. The path of the economy will depend significantly on the course of the virus, including progress on vaccinations. The ongoing public health crisis continues to weigh on economic activity, employment, and inflation, and poses considerable risks to the economic outlook. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. With inflation running persistently below this longer-run goal, the Committee will aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time so that inflation averages 2 percent over time and longerâterm inflation expectations remain well anchored at 2 percent. The Committee expects to maintain an accommodative stance of monetary policy until these outcomes are achieved. The Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time. In addition, the Federal Reserve will continue to increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $80 billion per month and of agency mortgageâbacked securities by at least $40 billion per month until substantial further progress has been made toward the Committee's maximum employment and price stability goals. These asset purchases help foster smooth market functioning and accommodative financial conditions, thereby supporting the flow of credit to households and businesses. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Mary C. Daly; Charles L. Evans; Randal K. Quarles; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA takes steps to streamline path for COVID-19 screening tools, provides information to help groups establishing testing programs
body_summary: The FDA provides information to test developers about a streamlined path to emergency use authorization for screening tools to screen asymptomatic individuals. This includes a new supplemental template for test developers seeking EUA of certain tests for serial testing. Serial testing involves testing the same individual multiple times within a few days to detect asymptomatic infection. The template applies to molecular and antigen tests, as well as at-home tests, and includes recommendations to streamline the authorization of screening tests with serial testing. The FDA believes that evidence of a test's strong performance in symptomatic patients combined with serial testing can mitigate the risk of false results when testing asymptomatic individuals. A fact sheet outlining considerations for selecting a test for use in a screening testing program has also been issued, providing helpful information to groups setting up testing programs.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: March 16, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On March 15, 2021, the FDA launched the COVID-19 EUA FDA Adverse Events Reporting System (FAERS) Public Dashboard to provide weekly updates on adverse event reports for drugs and therapeutic biological products used under an EUA during the public health emergency. The FDA also issued a warning letter jointly with the Federal Trade Commission to Ravenscroft Apothecary, Inc. for selling unapproved products with fraudulent COVID-19 claims. The company was requested to immediately cease the sale of any unapproved and unauthorized products for the treatment or prevention of COVID-19. As of today, 341 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: March 12, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA issued a warning letter to Cannafyl for selling unapproved products with fraudulent COVID-19 claims. The agency also issued a letter to clinical laboratory staff, point-of-care facility staff, and healthcare providers to alert them about potential false positive results with the Roche Molecular Systems cobas SARS-CoV-2 & Influenza A/B Nucleic Acid Test. Additionally, the FDA issued an Emergency Use Authorization for Propofol-Lipuro1% injectable emulsion for use in intensive care units. As of today, 341 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA, including 254 molecular tests, 72 antibody and other immune response tests, and 15 antigen tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: March 9, 2021
body_summary: The US FDA announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On Friday, the FDA issued Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) to Cue Health Inc. for its over-the-counter at-home diagnostic test for COVID-19, which can be used without a prescription. The FDA also issued EUA to Adaptive Biotechnologies for its T-Detect COVID Test, which analyzes DNA to identify recent or previous SARS-CoV-2 infection. Additionally, the FDA warned CAMA Wellness Center/IodoRios Company, LLC for selling an unapproved product with fraudulent COVID-19 claims. As of today, 340 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under EUAs.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Adaptive Biotechnologies T-Detect COVID Test
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the T-Detect COVID Test, a next-generation sequencing-based test that analyzes DNA sequences from T cells to identify individuals with an adaptive T cell immune response to SARS-CoV-2. The test is indicated for use by qualified healthcare professionals on samples from individuals who are 15 days or more post-symptom onset. A positive test result indicates recent or prior infection with SARS-CoV-2, while a negative result indicates that a patient is unlikely to have been infected. The test will be used to help determine if a person previously had COVID-19, especially for individuals who have exhibited symptoms but not tested positive for COVID-19 using a molecular or antigen diagnostic test. The test is currently limited to laboratories designated by Adaptive Biotechnologies Corporation that are certified under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA).

title: Statement on the Progress of the Health Insurance Marketplace Special Enrollment Period in Response to the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency
body_summary: The main action is that the President's administration opened healthcare.gov for a special enrollment period to provide affordable health care to Americans. Since February 15, over 200,000 Americans have gotten covered. The President encourages everyone who needs health insurance to sign up before May 15. The House of Representatives passed the American Rescue Plan, which includes steps to lower health costs and increase Federal subsidies to ensure no one pays more than 8.5% of their income on health coverage. The plan aims to expand coverage to an additional 4 million people with low incomes and extend coverage for low-income women who have recently given birth. The American Rescue Plan is essential to defeating the pandemic and lays a foundation for better health, a stronger economy, and peace of mind for Americans.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: March 2, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has updated its COVID-19 response efforts and announced several actions. The agency issued an Emergency Use Authorization for Quidel's QuickVue At-Home COVID-19 Test, allowing for at-home use with a prescription. The test detects SARS-CoV-2 proteins from a nasal swab sample and provides results in 10-15 minutes. The FDA has also issued warning letters to Ageless Global, LLC, and KDunn and Associates, P.A., for selling unapproved products with fraudulent COVID-19 claims. The agency has authorized over 335 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 249 molecular tests and 71 antibody tests. The FDA protects the public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Issues Authorization for Quidel QuickVue At-Home COVID-19 Test
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the Quidel QuickVue At-Home COVID-19 Test, allowing individuals aged 14 and older or 8 and older with adult assistance to collect and test their samples at home. The test is authorized for individuals suspected of COVID-19 by their healthcare provider within the first six days of symptom onset. The FDA also issued an EUA for Quidel's QuickVue SARS Antigen Test in December 2020. The FDA prioritizes the availability of at-home testing options in response to the pandemic, working with test developers to bring important diagnostics to the public. The FDA is an agency within the US Department of Health and Human Services, responsible for protecting the public health and safety of human products, medical devices, and food supply.

title: FDA Authorizes First Robotically-Assisted Surgical Device for Performing Transvaginal Hysterectomy
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has authorized the marketing of the Hominis Surgical System, a robotically-assisted surgical device, for benign hysterectomy with salpingo-oophorectomy. The device was evaluated in a clinical study of 30 patients, showing no conversions to open or other laparoscopic surgical approaches. Observed adverse events included minor blood loss, urinary tract infection, and delayed healing of the vaginal cuff. The FDA reviewed the device through the De Novo premarket review pathway and established special controls, including labeling and performance testing requirements, to ensure safety and effectiveness. The device is intended for use in patients aged 37-79, with varying body mass indexes and comorbidities. The FDA granted marketing authorization to Memic Innovative Surgery Ltd.

title: FDA Issues Emergency Use Authorization for Third COVID-19 Vaccine
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the Janssen COVID-19 Vaccine, allowing its distribution in the US for individuals 18 years and older. The EUA is based on data showing the vaccine's effectiveness in preventing COVID-19, with an overall effectiveness of approximately 67% in preventing moderate to severe/critical cases. The vaccine was administered as a single dose and had a safety profile with mild to moderate side effects. FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that the vaccine's benefits outweigh its risks. The EUA requires Janssen Biotech Inc. to submit a pharmacovigilance plan, including monitoring safety and completing longer-term safety follow-up for participants in ongoing clinical trials. The authorization will remain in effect until circumstances justify its termination.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: February 26, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA held a meeting to discuss the Emergency Use Authorization request from Janssen Biotech Inc. for its COVID-19 Vaccine. The agency added new devices to the device discontinuance list, including sterilization products and oxygen conservers, and warned consumers about alcohol-based hand sanitizers packaged in containers that may resemble food or drinks. The FDA also added 332 tests and sample collection devices to the emergency use authorization list, including molecular tests, antibody tests, and antigen tests. The agency protects the public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices, as well as regulating tobacco products.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Molybdenum Cofactor Deficiency Type A
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Nulibry (fosdenopterin) for injection to treat Molybdenum Cofactor Deficiency Type A, a rare genetic disorder. The FDA action marks the first approval for a therapy to treat this disease. Hylton V. Joffe, M.D., M.M.Sc, director of the Office of Rare Diseases, Pediatrics, Urologic and Reproductive Medicine, stated that the FDA remains committed to facilitating the development and approval of safe and effective therapies for patients affected by rare diseases. Nulibry replaces the missing substance cyclic pyranopterin monophosphate (cPMP) and has shown an 84% survival rate at three years for treated patients, compared to 55% for untreated patients. Side effects include complications related to the intravenous line and phototoxicity. The FDA granted Priority Review, Breakthrough Therapy, and Orphan Drug designations, as well as a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher. The approval was granted to Origin Biosciences, Inc. The FDA protects the public health by assuring the safety and effectiveness of drugs and other products.

title: FDA Authorizes Marketing of Novel Device to Help Protect Athletes’ Brains During Head Impacts
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has authorized the marketing of the Q-Collar, a non-invasive device worn around the neck to protect the brain from the effects of repetitive sub-concussive head impacts during sports activities. The device, a C-shaped collar, applies compressive force to the neck to increase blood volume and reduce brain movement. The FDA assessed the safety and effectiveness of the Q-Collar through a study involving 284 athletes aged 13 and older, finding significant changes in the brain of participants who did not wear the device. The Q-Collar may reduce the occurrence of specific changes in the brain associated with brain injury. The device is intended for over-the-counter use and should be worn with other protective sports equipment.

title: FDA Statement on Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee Meeting
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) will rapidly work toward finalization and issuance of an emergency use authorization for the Janssen Biotech Inc. COVID-19 Vaccine following a positive advisory committee meeting outcome. The FDA has notified federal partners involved in vaccine allocation and distribution to execute their plans for timely vaccine distribution. The FDA is an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, responsible for protecting the public health and ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: FDA Approves Targeted Treatment for Rare Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy Mutation
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Amondys 45 (casimersen) injection for treating Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients with a confirmed mutation of the DMD gene that is amenable to exon 45 skipping. The approval is based on an increase in dystrophin production in skeletal muscle observed in patients treated with the therapy. Approximately 8% of DMD patients have a mutation amenable to exon 45 skipping. Eric Bastings, M.D., deputy director of the Office of Neuroscience in the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, stated that developing targeted treatments is crucial for personalized medicine. Amondys 45 was evaluated in a double-blind, placebo-controlled study with 43 patients, showing a significant increase in dystrophin protein levels. The FDA concluded that the data demonstrated an increase in dystrophin production that is reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit. Side effects observed include upper respiratory tract infections, cough, fever, and joint pain. Amondys 45 was approved using the Accelerated Approval pathway, with the FDA granting Fast Track and Priority Review designations, as well as Orphan Drug designation. The approval is granted to Sarepta Therapeutics, Inc.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Allows More Flexible Storage, Transportation Conditions for Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has allowed undiluted frozen vials of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine to be transported and stored at conventional temperatures for up to two weeks. This change, approved after Pfizer submitted data to the FDA, allows for more flexible storage conditions, easing the burden of ultra-low cold storage equipment procurement. The alternative temperature is not applicable to thawed vials before or after dilution. The updated Fact Sheets for Healthcare Providers are available on the FDA website, intended to help frontline workers understand the new storage temperatures.

title: Executive Order 14017—America's Supply Chains
body_summary:
The US President has ordered the strengthening of America's supply chains to ensure economic prosperity and national security. This order requires a 100-day review of supply chain risks, with reports submitted to the President on semiconductor manufacturing, high-capacity batteries, critical minerals, and pharmaceuticals. Sectoral supply chain assessments will be conducted for various industries, including defense, public health, ICT, energy, transportation, and agriculture, to identify critical goods and materials, manufacturing capabilities, and risks.

The US government will require each report to include a review of critical goods and materials, manufacturing capabilities, defense and intelligence risks, and contingency assessments for supply chain disruptions. The reports must also prioritize critical goods and materials, identify policy recommendations, and propose executive and legislative changes to strengthen supply chains.

The Executive Order defines key terms related to critical goods and materials, and it is subject to applicable law and available appropriations. The Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs and the Assistant to the President for Economic Policy will coordinate efforts to implement this order.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: February 23, 2021
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced actions in its ongoing response to the COVID-19 pandemic. Yesterday, the FDA issued guidances for medical product developers to address SARS-CoV-2 variants. The FDA also issued a safety communication about pulse oximeters, providing recommendations for patients and healthcare providers on using them accurately. 

The FDA has authorized 331 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 247 molecular tests and 70 antibody tests. There are 37 molecular authorizations for home-collected samples and one molecular prescription at-home test. 

The FDA protects the public health by assuring the safety and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices, as well as regulating tobacco products.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Issues Policies to Guide Medical Product Developers Addressing Virus Variants
body_summary:
The US FDA issued guidances for medical product developers to address the emergence of variants of SARS-CoV-2. The FDA is committed to identifying efficient ways to modify medical products to address these variants. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that the agency is using every tool to fight the pandemic, including pivoting as the virus adapts.

The FDA has updated its guidance on vaccines to provide recommendations to vaccine developers, including those who have received emergency use authorization. The guidance outlines the FDA's scientific recommendations for modifications to authorized vaccines. Manufacturers are encouraged to study modified vaccines in both naïve and previously vaccinated individuals.

The FDA has also issued a guidance for test developers to evaluate the impact of emerging and future viral genetic mutations on COVID-19 tests. The guidance provides information on evaluating the potential impact of viral genetic mutations on test performance, including design considerations and ongoing monitoring.

Additionally, the FDA has issued a new guidance for the development of monoclonal antibody products targeting SARS-CoV-2, including addressing the impact of emerging variants. The agency is aware that some monoclonal antibodies are less active against emerging variants and provides recommendations for the generation of non-clinical, clinical, and chemistry, manufacturing and controls data.

The FDA is committed to continuously monitoring genomic databases for emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants and evaluating phenotypically any specific variants in the product target that are becoming prevalent.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: February 19, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced the approval of two abbreviated new drug applications for piperacillin and tazobactam for injection, which can treat various infections in adult and pediatric patients. The FDA also issued a warning letter to Dr. Paul's Lab for selling an unapproved product with fraudulent COVID-19 claims. The agency has authorized 331 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody tests, and antigen tests. The FDA protects the public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices, as well as regulating food, cosmetics, and tobacco products.

title: FDA Warns 10 Companies for Illegally Selling Dietary Supplements Claiming to Treat Depression and Other Mental Health Disorders
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued warning letters to 10 companies for selling dietary supplements that claim to cure, treat, or prevent depression and other mental health disorders. The affected companies include Enlifta LLC, Lifted Naturals, Mountain Peak Nutritionals, and eight others. The FDA warns that these products are unapproved new drugs that could harm consumers who use them instead of seeking proven treatments from qualified health care providers. The agency is committed to protecting the public from unlawful dietary supplements and has requested responses from the companies within 15 working days stating how they will address these issues.

title: COVID-19 Update: USDA, FDA Underscore Current Epidemiologic and Scientific Information Indicating No Transmission of COVID-19 Through Food or Food Packaging
body_summary: The U.S. Department of Agriculture, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, and the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention continue to state that there is no credible evidence of food or food packaging being associated with or as a likely source of viral transmission of SARS-CoV-2, the virus causing COVID-19. Despite reports of viral detection on food and packaging, scientific consensus and studies suggest that the risk of transmission is extremely low. The FDA shares this update based on the best available information from scientific bodies across the globe, including the International Commission on Microbiological Specifications for Foods, which states that to date, there has been no evidence that food, food packaging, or food handling is a source of SARS-CoV-2 transmission.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on January 26-27, 2021. Jerome H. Powell was selected as Chair, John C. Williams as Vice Chair, and James A. Clouse as Secretary. The Committee authorized open market transactions, including buying and selling securities, lending Eligible Securities, and conducting operational readiness testing. The Chair may instruct the Selected Bank to adjust monetary policy or address temporary disruptions in U.S. dollar funding markets. Foreign currency operations were authorized up to $2.5 billion per calendar year. The Committee reaffirmed its Program for Security of FOMC Information and Statement on Longer-Run Goals and Monetary Policy Strategy. It reviewed employment and inflation objectives, planning annual reviews and a public review every 5 years. The Federal Reserve's tools provided effective control over the federal funds rate and other overnight money market rates. The staff projected GDP growth would slow down in 2021 before gradually rising to 2% by the end of the medium term.

title: FDA Approves First in the World, First-of-Its-Kind Implant for the Treatment of Rare Bone Disease as a Humanitarian Use Device
