body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the Patient Specific Talus Spacer 3D-printed talus implant for humanitarian use to treat avascular necrosis (AVN) of the ankle joint. The implant, developed by Additive Orthopaedics, LLC, is the first of its kind and provides a joint-sparing alternative to other surgical interventions. The FDA reviewed data from 31 patients and 32 talus replacement surgeries, showing that the implant reduced pain and improved range of motion in the ankle joint. The most common adverse events reported were pain and scar tissue at the surgery site. The approval is for humanitarian use, intended to benefit patients with this rare and potentially debilitating condition.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: February 16, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA issued a warning letter to Evolved Ayurvedic Discoveries, Inc./BioCBDPlus for selling unapproved products with fraudulent COVID-19 claims. The agency has also authorized 331 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations (EUAs), including 247 molecular tests, 70 antibody tests, and 14 antigen tests. These tests can be used for home-collected samples with 37 molecular authorizations. The FDA protects the public health by assuring the safety and effectiveness of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: Statement on the Start of the Health Insurance Marketplace Special Enrollment Period in Response to the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency
body_summary: The US President is announcing an effort to ensure all Americans have access to quality, affordable health care. Starting today and ending May 15, 2021, the government is opening healthcare.gov for Americans to sign up for health insurance using a special enrollment period. The American Rescue Plan aims to lower health costs, expand access to care, and increase Federal subsidies. The plan will reduce premiums to no more than 8.5% of income and incentivize states to cover an additional 4 million low-income individuals. The President encourages everyone to sign up for health insurance through healthcare.gov, and for those with existing coverage, to help their family and friends enroll.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: February 12, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. This week, the FDA posted a webpage on COVID-19 Vaccine Safety Surveillance and issued an emergency use authorization for a monoclonal antibody combination for treating mild to moderate COVID-19. The FDA also revised its guidance on Investigational COVID-19 Convalescent Plasma. As of today, 327 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 243 molecular tests, 70 antibody tests, and 14 antigen tests. The FDA is an agency within the US Department of Health and Human Services, protecting public health by ensuring the safety and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: FDA Approves Drug to Reduce Bone Marrow Suppression Caused by Chemotherapy
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Cosela (trilaciclib) as the first therapy to reduce chemotherapy-induced bone marrow suppression in adults with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. Cosela inhibits cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6, protecting bone marrow cells from damage caused by chemotherapy. This approval will give patients a treatment option to reduce the occurrence of severe neutropenia and allow them to complete chemotherapy on time. The effectiveness of Cosela was evaluated in three randomized studies, which found that patients who received Cosela had a lower chance of severe neutropenia and shorter duration of severe neutropenia compared to those who received a placebo.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Monoclonal Antibodies for Treatment of COVID-19
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the treatment of mild to moderate COVID-19 in adults and pediatric patients 12 years old or older weighing at least 40 kilograms. This EUA includes treatment for patients 65 years old or older or those with certain chronic medical conditions. In a clinical trial, bamlanivimab and etesevimab administered together significantly reduced COVID-19-related hospitalization and death during 29 days of follow-up compared to placebo. The authorized use does not include patients hospitalized due to COVID-19 or requiring oxygen therapy. The data supporting this EUA are based on a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial in 1,035 non-hospitalized adults with mild to moderate COVID-19 symptoms. The primary endpoint was COVID-19 related hospitalizations or death by any cause during 29 days of follow-up, with a 70% reduction in hospitalizations or death in patients treated with bamlanivimab and etesevimab administered together.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Monoclonal Antibodies for Treatment of COVID-19
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for bamlanivimab and etesevimab administered together for the treatment of mild to moderate COVID-19 in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 40 kilograms who test positive for SARS-CoV-2 and are at high risk for progressing to severe COVID-19. The EUA includes treatment for those who are 65 years of age or older or have certain chronic medical conditions. A clinical trial showed that a single intravenous infusion of bamlanivimab and etesevimab administered together significantly reduced COVID-19-related hospitalization and death during 29 days of follow-up compared to placebo. The authorized use does not include patients who are hospitalized due to COVID-19 or require oxygen therapy due to COVID-19. The data supporting this EUA are based on a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial in 1,035 non-hospitalized adults. The primary endpoint was COVID-19 related hospitalizations or death by any cause during 29 days of follow-up, with a 70% reduction in hospitalization or death in the bamlanivimab and etesevimab group compared to the placebo group.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: February 9, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a Letter to Health Care Providers on using ventilator splitters during the COVID-19 pandemic, providing information on their use, risks, and reporting requirements. As of today, the FDA has authorized 323 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody tests, and antigen tests. The FDA is an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, responsible for protecting public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: FDA Announces New Resource for Veterinarians and Pet Owners Interested in Clinical Field Studies of Animal Cells, Tissues, and Cell- and Tissue-Based Products
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is announcing a listing of clinical field studies investigating Animal Cells, Tissues, and Cell- and Tissue-Based Products (ACTPs) in veterinary patients. The webpage provides information on clinical field studies for the use of ACTPs in veterinary patients, including study name, species, condition, product type, and recruitment/phone number. Participation in these studies is voluntary, and sponsors must consent to having their study information listed on the webpage. The studies listed are investigational, and the safety and effectiveness of the ACTPs have not yet been determined. The webpage will be updated quarterly, and the FDA encourages sponsors to develop data for potential FDA approval.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: February 5, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA scheduled a meeting of its Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee for February 26, 2021, to discuss a request for emergency use authorization for a COVID-19 vaccine from Janssen Biotech Inc. The agency also cautioned health care professionals and compounders about potential risks associated with compounding remdesivir drug products and advised against compounding them. On February 4, the FDA revised the Letter of Authorization for COVID-19 convalescent plasma to limit its use to high titer plasma for treating hospitalized patients with COVID-19. The FDA has authorized 322 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody tests, and antigen tests.

title: FDA Approves New Treatment For Adults With Relapsed Or Refractory Large-B-Cell Lymphoma
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Breyanzi (lisocabtagene maraleucel), a cell-based gene therapy, for adult patients with certain types of large B-cell lymphoma who have not responded to or relapsed after at least two other systemic treatments. The therapy, a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy, is the third gene therapy approved by the FDA for certain types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma, including diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL). 

Breyanzi is not indicated for primary central nervous system lymphoma. The therapy has a complete remission rate of 54% in a multicenter clinical trial of over 250 adults. However, treatment with Breyanzi can cause severe side effects, including cytokine release syndrome (CRS), which is a life-threatening systemic response. To address this risk, the FDA is requiring healthcare facilities to be specially certified and staff to be trained to recognize and manage the risks of CRS.

The FDA granted Breyanzi Orphan Drug, Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy, and Breakthrough Therapy designations. The approval was granted to Juno Therapeutics Inc., a Bristol-Myers Squibb Company.

title: FDA Authorizes Marketing of Novel Device to Reduce Snoring and Mild Obstructive Sleep Apnea in Patients 18 Years and Older
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of a new prescription-only device, eXciteOSA, to reduce snoring and mild obstructive sleep apnea. The device, which is intended for patients 18 years or older, works by delivering electrical muscle stimulation to the tongue to improve tongue muscle function and prevent airway obstruction during sleep. The FDA assessed the device in 115 patients with snoring and found a reduction of more than 20% in snoring time. For patients with snoring and mild sleep apnea, the device reduced the Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) by 48% in 41 out of 48 patients. The most common adverse events were excessive salivation and tongue discomfort. The device is contraindicated for patients with certain medical conditions and should be used under the guidance of a healthcare professional. The FDA granted marketing authorization to Signifier Medical Technologies, LLC.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Announces Advisory Committee Meeting to Discuss Janssen Biotech Inc.’s COVID-19 Vaccine Candidate
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has scheduled a VRBPAC meeting on Feb. 26, 2021, to discuss the request for emergency use authorization for a COVID-19 vaccine from Janssen Biotech Inc. The meeting will provide a public discussion of the data submitted in support of safety and effectiveness. Acting FDA Commissioner Janet Woodcock stated that this discussion will help ensure the public has a clear understanding of the scientific data and information to be evaluated by the FDA. The FDA intends to make background materials available to the public and will livestream the meeting on its YouTube, Facebook, and Twitter channels.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Continues Important Work to Support Medical Product Development to Address New Virus Variants
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is adapting to new coronavirus variants to ensure healthcare providers have the most up-to-date diagnostics, treatments, and vaccines. Since the pandemic began, the FDA has been monitoring identified and emerging variants, assessing their impact on authorized products, and working with medical product sponsors and international partners. The agency has experience with evolving infectious diseases, such as influenza, and is utilizing its expertise to inform a path forward for COVID-19 variants. The FDA is developing guidances for diagnostic, therapeutic, and vaccine developers to guide ongoing medical product development, including expedited drug development for therapeutics and diagnostics. Currently, available information suggests that authorized vaccines remain effective in protecting against COVID-19, but the agency is considering expanding in silico monitoring and labeling authorized products to be transparent about their performance.

title: Memorandum on Maximizing Assistance From the Federal Emergency Management Agency To Respond to COVID-19
body_summary: By the authority vested in me as President, I hereby order the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to provide a 100 percent Federal cost share for all work eligible for assistance under Public Assistance Category B, pursuant to sections 403 and 502 of the Stafford Act, from January 20, 2020, through January 20, 2021, and then from January 21, 2021, through September 30, 2021. This policy is consistent with the nationwide emergency declaration concerning the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic on March 13, 2020. The memorandum is to be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: January 29, 2021
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA added a new frequently asked question (FAQ) regarding COVID-19 vaccine distribution, stating that the agency is not responsible for vaccine distribution. The FDA has also updated its guidance on clinical trials of medical products during the public health emergency, clarifying that receipt of certain medical products, such as vaccines, may be considered "investigational" products.

The FDA has approved an abbreviated new drug application for furosemide injection, indicated for treating edema associated with congestive heart failure, cirrhosis of the liver, and renal disease. The agency has also issued warning letters to Allimax Usand and AusarHerbs for selling unapproved products with fraudulent COVID-19 claims.

The FDA has placed all alcohol-based hand sanitizers from Mexico on a country-wide import alert to prevent entry of potentially dangerous products. The agency has authorized over 320 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody tests, and antigen tests. The FDA continues to work with regulatory counterparts in Mexico to ensure compliance with regulations.

The FDA protects the public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of medical products, vaccines, and medical devices, as well as regulating tobacco products and ensuring the safety of the nation's food supply.

title: Executive Order 14009—Strengthening Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act
body_summary:
By the authority vested in me as President, it is hereby ordered: Section 1. Policy. The Affordable Care Act has reduced the number of uninsured Americans by over 20 million, extended consumer protections to over 100 million people, and strengthened the Nation's healthcare system. The policy of my Administration is to protect and strengthen Medicaid and the ACA, and to make high-quality healthcare accessible and affordable for every American.

Section 2. Special Enrollment Period. The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic has triggered a public health and economic crisis. To address this, the Secretary of Health and Human Services shall consider establishing a Special Enrollment Period for uninsured and under-insured Americans to seek coverage through the Federally Facilitated Marketplace.

Section 3. Immediate Review of Agency Actions. The heads of agencies shall review existing regulations, orders, guidance documents, policies, and agency actions to determine their consistency with the policy set forth in section 1. They shall examine policies or practices that may undermine protections for people with pre-existing conditions, reduce coverage under Medicaid or the ACA, or present unnecessary barriers to accessing coverage.

Section 4. Revocation of Certain Presidential Actions. Executive Orders 13765 and 13813 are revoked. Heads of agencies shall consider suspending, revising, or rescinding agency actions related to these executive orders, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law and the policy set forth in section 1.

Section 5. General Provisions. Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.

title: Executive Order 14008—Tackling the Climate Crisis at Home and Abroad
body_summary: The US government has taken comprehensive action to address the climate crisis, with a series of key actions aimed at reducing greenhouse gas emissions and increasing global climate ambition. The President ordered domestic and international action, establishing the White House Office of Domestic Climate Policy and a National Climate Task Force to coordinate policy. The federal government aims to lead the nation's effort by example, with actions including expanding climate forecast capabilities, improving infrastructure investment, and conserving at least 30% of lands and waters by 2030. A Civilian Climate Corps Initiative will conserve public lands and waters, while an Interagency Working Group on Coal and Power Plant Communities and Economic Revitalization aims to revitalize the economies of affected communities. The White House also established the White House Environmental Justice Advisory Council and the Office of Management and Budget must publish an annual Environmental Justice Scorecard by February 2022.

title: Implementation Note issued January 27, 2021
body_summary: Decisions Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation The Federal Reserve has made the following decisions to implement the monetary policy stance announced by the Federal Open Market Committee in its statement on January 27, 2021: The Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to maintain the interest rate paid on required and excess reserve balances at 0.10 percent, effective January 28, 2021. As part of its policy decision, the Federal Open Market Committee voted to authorize and direct the Open Market Desk at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective January 28, 2021, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to: Undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 0 to 1/4 percent. Increase the System Open Market Account holdings of Treasury securities by $80 billion per month and of agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) by $40 billion per month. Increase holdings of Treasury securities and agency MBS by additional amounts and purchase agency commercial mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) as needed to sustain smooth functioning of markets for these securities. Conduct repurchase agreement operations to support effective policy implementation and the smooth functioning of short-term U.S. dollar funding markets. Conduct overnight reverse repurchase agreement operations at an offering rate of 0.00 percent and with a per-counterparty limit of $30 billion per day; the per-counterparty limit can be temporarily increased at the discretion of the Chair. Roll over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities and reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency MBS in agency MBS. Allow modest deviations from stated amounts for purchases and reinvestments, if needed for operational reasons. Engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency MBS transactions." In a related action, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System voted unanimously to approve the establishment of the primary credit rate at the existing level of 0.25 percent. This information will be updated as appropriate to reflect decisions of the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors regarding details of the Federal Reserve's operational tools and approach used to implement monetary policy. More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The Federal Reserve is committed to using its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals. The COVID-19 pandemic is causing tremendous human and economic hardship across the United States and around the world. The pace of the recovery in economic activity and employment has moderated in recent months, with weakness concentrated in the sectors most adversely affected by the pandemic. Weaker demand and earlier declines in oil prices have been holding down consumer price inflation. Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses. The path of the economy will depend significantly on the course of the virus, including progress on vaccinations. The ongoing public health crisis continues to weigh on economic activity, employment, and inflation, and poses considerable risks to the economic outlook. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. With inflation running persistently below this longer-run goal, the Committee will aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time so that inflation averages 2 percent over time and longerâterm inflation expectations remain well anchored at 2 percent. The Committee expects to maintain an accommodative stance of monetary policy until these outcomes are achieved. The Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time. In addition, the Federal Reserve will continue to increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $80 billion per month and of agency mortgageâbacked securities by at least $40 billion per month until substantial further progress has been made toward the Committee's maximum employment and price stability goals. These asset purchases help foster smooth market functioning and accommodative financial conditions, thereby supporting the flow of credit to households and businesses. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Mary C. Daly; Charles L. Evans; Randal K. Quarles; and Christopher J. Waller.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: January 26, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has updated its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The agency has posted a CDER Conversation with Katie Gray, Pharm.D., acting director of CDER's Office of Prescription Drug Promotion, discussing their COVID-19 response. This response has focused on compliance actions regarding prescription drug promotional materials making false or misleading claims about COVID-19 prevention or treatment. As of today, 320 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including 238 molecular tests, 69 antibody tests, and 13 antigen tests. The FDA protects the public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of drugs, vaccines, and medical devices, as well as regulating the nation's food supply and other products.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: January 22, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. A criminal investigation led to the arrest of Johnny T. Stine, who was found to have claimed to have a COVID-19 vaccine and offered to sell it to customers for $400-$1000 each. Stine's company, North Coast Biologics, had previously received a warning letter from the FDA. The FDA has reissued Emergency Use Authorizations (EUAs) for decontamination systems to limit the number of decontamination cycles and respirator reuses permitted. The FDA has also added two new devices to the device discontinuance list, including 3M's 3M Triple Layer Molded Face Mask and BioFire Diagnostics' FilmArray Instrument. As of today, 319 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations, including molecular tests, antibody tests, and antigen tests. The FDA will continue to investigate fraudulent COVID-19 treatments and bring to justice those who try to profit from the pandemic.

title: Executive Order 13997—Improving and Expanding Access to Care and Treatments for COVID-19
body_summary:
President Joe Biden orders the following policy actions:

Section 1: Policy - Improve the Nation's healthcare systems to address COVID-19, accelerate the development of novel therapies, and improve access to quality and affordable healthcare.

Section 2: Accelerating the Development of Novel Therapies - The Secretary of Health and Human Services, in consultation with the National Institutes of Health Director, will develop plans to support large-scale randomized trials and research on COVID-19 treatments, particularly for underrepresented populations.

Section 3: Improving the Capacity of the Nation's Healthcare Systems to Address COVID-19 - The Secretary of Defense, HHS, and other agencies will provide surge assistance to critical care facilities and develop recommendations for supporting healthcare workers and patients.

Section 4: Improving Access to Quality and Affordable Healthcare - The Secretary of Defense, HHS, and Veterans Affairs will establish targets for the production, allocation, and distribution of COVID-19 treatments and provide support to overcome barriers to using existing treatments.

Section 5: General Provisions - The order does not impair the authority granted by law to executive departments, nor affects the functions of the Office of Management and Budget.

title: Executive Order 13995—Ensuring an Equitable Pandemic Response and Recovery
body_summary: The President orders a government-wide effort to address health inequities resulting from COVID-19, focusing on communities of color and underserved populations. The COVID-19 Health Equity Task Force, led by the Secretary of HHS, is established to provide recommendations to the President on mitigating health inequities and preventing future disparities. The Task Force will include experts and individuals with lived experience. By June 2023, the Task Force must submit a final report to the President addressing ongoing health inequities and recommending actions to combat them. The Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency and agency heads must consult with the Task Force to strengthen COVID-19 equity data collection and reporting, and ensure equitable allocation of resources. The Secretary of HHS must provide recommendations on contact tracer placement and outreach to promote vaccine trust among underserved populations.

title: Executive Order 13996—Establishing the COVID-19 Pandemic Testing Board and Ensuring a Sustainable Public Health Workforce for COVID-19 and Other Biological Threats
body_summary:
By the authority vested in me as President, it is hereby ordered as follows:

Section 1. Policy. The policy of my Administration is to control coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) by using a Government-wide, unified approach that includes establishing a national COVID-19 testing and public health workforce strategy, working to expand the supply of tests, and enhancing laboratory testing capacity.

Section 2. COVID-19 Pandemic Testing Board. The COVID-19 Pandemic Testing Board is established, chaired by the Coordinator of the COVID-19 Response and Counselor to the President, to coordinate Federal Government efforts to promote COVID-19 diagnostic, screening, and surveillance testing.

Section 3. Actions to Address the Cost of COVID-19 Testing. The Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of HHS, and the Secretary of Labor, in coordination with the COVID-19 Response Coordinator, shall facilitate the provision of COVID-19 testing free of charge to those who lack comprehensive health insurance.

Section 4. Establishing a Public Health Workforce Program. The Secretary of HHS and the Secretary of Labor shall consult with State, local, Tribal, and territorial leaders to understand the challenges they face in pandemic response efforts, including challenges recruiting and training sufficient personnel.

Section 5. General Provisions. Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget.

JOSEPH R. BIDEN, JR.

title: Memorandum To Extend Federal Support to Governors' Use of the National Guard To Respond to COVID-19 and To Increase Reimbursement and Other Assistance Provided to States
body_summary: President Biden orders the Secretary of Defense and Secretary of Homeland Security to extend federal support to governors' use of the National Guard to respond to COVID-19, increasing reimbursement and other assistance provided to states. The policy aims to combat and respond to COVID-19 with the full capacity and capability of the Federal Government. The Secretary of Defense is required to request governors to order National Guard forces to perform duty on a fully reimbursable basis. FEMA will fund 100% of the cost of activities associated with National Guard use to respond to COVID-19. The memorandum also provides assistance for Category B emergency protective measures, including funding for personal protective equipment and disinfecting services, and expedites reimbursement for eligible emergency work projects.

title: FDA Approves First Extended-Release, Injectable Drug Regimen for Adults Living with HIV
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Cabenuva, a complete regimen for treating HIV-1 infection, as a monthly injectable treatment for adults who are virologically suppressed. This is the first FDA-approved injectable regimen for HIV-infected adults. The approval allows patients to switch from daily oral treatment to a once-monthly injection. The safety and efficacy of Cabenuva were established through two clinical trials in 1,182 adults, with no clinically relevant change in CD4+ cell counts. The most common adverse reactions were injection site reactions, fever, and fatigue. The approval was granted to ViiV Healthcare, and the FDA designated Cabenuva and its companion drug Vocabria as Fast Track and Priority Review.

title: Executive Order 13987—Organizing and Mobilizing the United States Government to Provide a Unified and Effective Response To Combat COVID-19 and To Provide United States Leadership on Global Health and Security
body_summary:
The President has ordered the Federal Government to act swiftly and aggressively to combat coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). This order creates the position of Coordinator of the COVID-19 Response and Counselor to the President, and takes steps to organize the White House and activities of the Federal Government to combat COVID-19 and prepare for future biological and pandemic threats.

The COVID-19 Response Coordinator will report directly to the President and advise and assist in responding to the COVID-19 pandemic. The Coordinator will coordinate efforts to produce, supply, and distribute personal protective equipment, vaccines, tests, and other supplies, and will also coordinate efforts to expand COVID-19 testing and vaccine distribution.

The order also establishes an NSC Directorate on Global Health Security and Biodefense, which will be headed by a Senior Director for Global Health Security and Biodefense. The Senior Director will oversee the Global Health Security Agenda Interagency Review Council, which will review and recommend actions to the President concerning emerging domestic and global biological risks and national biopreparedness policies.

The heads of agencies are required to bring any procedural, departmental, legal, or funding obstacle to the COVID-19 response to the attention of the COVID-19 Response Coordinator, and the Coordinator will immediately bring to the President's attention any issues that require Presidential guidance or decision-making.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: January 19, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued new guidance to notify drug manufacturers and compounders of its policy on testing procedures for alcohol and isopropyl alcohol to prevent methanol contamination. The FDA has also created a collaboration with the National Institute of Standards and Technology to adopt advanced manufacturing technologies and strengthen the nation's public health infrastructure. The FDA has updated its guidance on investigational COVID-19 convalescent plasma and posted updated information on its website regarding blood donation. As of today, 319 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations. The agency protects the public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: FDA Marks Historic Public Health Milestone with Finalization of Two Key Rules for Companies Seeking to Market New Tobacco Products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) finalized two foundational rules for the premarket review of new tobacco products. The rules, which went into effect, provide additional information on minimum requirements for content, format, and review of premarket tobacco product applications (PMTAs) and substantial equivalence (SE) reports, aiming to increase transparency and efficiency in the review process. The rules will apply to all premarket applications for electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS) products and require manufacturers to demonstrate that marketing of new tobacco products would be appropriate for the protection of public health. Manufacturers of deemed new tobacco products, including e-cigarettes, that were on the market as of Aug. 8, 2016, were required to submit a premarket application to the FDA by Sept. 9, 2020. The FDA is responsible for protecting the public health and regulating tobacco products, as well as other products such as food, cosmetics, and medical devices.

title: Executive Order 13980—Protecting Americans From Overcriminalization Through Regulatory Reform
body_summary: President Donald J. Trump issued an executive order on January 18, 2021, to improve transparency and fairness in regulatory enforcement. The order aims to reduce regulatory burdens on Americans by providing notice of potential criminal liability for violating regulations. Key provisions include requiring agencies to clearly state conduct subject to criminal penalties, disfavoring strict liability offenses, focusing criminal prosecutions on individuals with actual or constructive knowledge of prohibited conduct causing substantial public harm, publishing guidance on addressing regulatory offenses, and protecting against certain actions by the Department of Justice.

title: Federal judge enters consent decree against Washington state juice processor
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) entered a consent decree with Valley Processing, Inc. and its owner, Mary Ann Bliesner, to stop distributing adulterated juice products. The FDA alleged that Valley Processing's products contained inorganic arsenic and patulin toxins, posing health risks to consumers. The company was found to process juice under grossly insanitary conditions and failed to adhere to food safety standards. A consent decree prohibits Valley Processing from distributing FDA-regulated products unless it completes corrective actions. The company must destroy any remaining juice, notify the FDA in advance, and comply with specific remedial measures before processing or distributing any future products.

title: FDA Warns Firms to Remove Unauthorized E-liquid Products from Market in First Letters Issued to Manufacturers that Did Not Submit Premarket Applications by Deadline
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued warning letters to 10 firms manufacturing and operating websites selling electronic nicotine delivery system (ENDS) products, specifically e-liquids, advising them that selling these products without premarket authorization is illegal. The firms did not submit premarket tobacco product applications by the Sept. 9, 2020 deadline. The FDA plans to post a list of products for which the agency has received applications, but is verifying certain information first.

The warning letters were issued to Little House Vapes LLC; Castle Rock Vapor LLC; Dropsmoke Inc.; Perfection Vapes Inc.; CLS Trading LLC d/b/a Vape Dudes HQ; Session Supply Co.; Coastal E-Liquid Laboratory/GC Vapors LLC; Dr. Crimmy LLC d/b/a Dr. Crimmy’s V-Liquid; CMM Capital LLC d/b/a ETX Vape; and E-Cig Barn LLC.

These companies have listed over 100,000 products with the FDA, and the agency will continue to prioritize enforcement against companies that market ENDS products without authorization. The FDA has requested responses from each firm within 15 working days detailing how they intend to address the agency's concerns.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: January 15, 2021
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued three new guidelines in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On January 14, the FDA issued guidance on protecting participants in bioequivalence studies for abbreviated new drug applications. On January 13, the FDA issued guidance on potency assay considerations for monoclonal antibodies and other therapeutic proteins targeting SARS-CoV-2 infectivity. On January 13, the FDA also issued guidance on coagulation systems for measurement of viscoelastic properties during the COVID-19 public health emergency. The agency has also authorized 317 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 236 molecular tests, 68 antibody tests, and 13 antigen tests.

title: FDA Grants First Conditional Approval Under Expanded Authority to Control Seizures in Dogs with Idiopathic Epilepsy
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted conditional approval for KBroVet-CA1, a potassium bromide chewable tablet, to control seizures in dogs with idiopathic epilepsy. This is the first conditional approval under the FDA's expanded authority for certain new animal drugs. The drug works by stabilizing neurons to reduce seizure likelihood. Prior to this, the FDA's conditional approval was limited to minor species or rare diseases. KBroVet-CA1 meets the criteria, as there is no approved treatment for idiopathic epilepsy in dogs, affecting approximately 5% of the canine population. The initial approval is valid for one year with potential for four annual renewals, requiring the sponsor to collect remaining effectiveness data. The sponsor, Pegasus Laboratories Inc., used safety data from a Public Master File created by the FDA, avoiding animal testing.

title: CBP, FDA Seize Counterfeit, Unauthorized E-Cigarettes
body_summary: U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers, along with FDA agents, have seized 33,681 units of e-cigarettes with a manufacturer's suggested retail price of $719,453. In December 2020, they previously seized 42 shipments from China, including counterfeit e-cigarettes from the Puff Bar brand. The seizure is part of a joint operation to intercept counterfeit or violative e-cigarettes that don't meet U.S. laws. CBP Port Director Timothy Lemaux stated that counterfeit products pose a serious health risk to consumers, particularly children. The FDA's Mitch Zeller emphasized the agency's priority on enforcement against e-cigarette products, especially those appealing to youth. In fiscal year 2020, CBP seized 93,590 units of e-cigarettes that didn't meet U.S. regulations. The FDA has issued warnings to companies, including Cool Clouds Distribution Inc. (doing business as Puff Bar), to remove flavored disposable e-cigarettes and youth-appealing products from the market.

title: FDA Releases Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning Action Plan
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has released its first Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning (AI/ML)-Based Software as a Medical Device Action Plan. This plan outlines a multi-pronged approach to advance the Agency's oversight of AI/ML-based medical software. The plan's director, Bakul Patel, stated that the plan will further the enormous potential of these technologies to improve patient care while ensuring safe and effective software functionality.

The plan includes five actions: developing a regulatory framework, supporting good machine learning practices, fostering a patient-centered approach, advancing real-world performance monitoring pilots, and continuing to collaborate with stakeholders. The plan is a response to stakeholder feedback received from a 2019 discussion paper and aims to advance the development of digital health technologies within the FDA's regulatory role.

title: FDA Releases Artificial Intelligence/Machine Learning Action Plan
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration released its first AI/ML-Based Software as a Medical Device Action Plan, outlining a multi-pronged approach to advance the Agency's oversight of AI/ML-based medical software. The plan, announced by Bakul Patel, director of the Digital Health Center of Excellence, aims to improve patient care while ensuring safe and effective software functionality. The five actions outlined in the plan include developing a regulatory framework, supporting good machine learning practices, fostering a patient-centered approach, and advancing real-world performance monitoring pilots. This action plan responds to stakeholder feedback received since the April 2019 discussion paper and welcomes continued feedback.

title: FDA Conditionally Approves First Oral Tablet to Treat Lymphoma in Dogs
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration conditionally approved Laverdia-CA1 (verdinexor tablets) to treat dogs with lymphoma, a type of cancer. Laverdia-CA1 prevents certain proteins from leaving the nucleus of cancer cells, thereby controlling cancer growth. The treatment is given orally twice a week, with a 72-hour gap between doses. The FDA approved this treatment for dogs with B- or T-cell lymphoma, with 58 client-owned dogs showing progression of lymphoma for at least 56 days after taking verdinexor. The most common adverse reactions were anorexia, vomiting, and weight loss. Steven M. Solomon, D.V.M., M.P.H., director of the FDA's Center for Veterinary Medicine, stated that this approval provides a much-needed option for treating dogs with lymphoma.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: January 8, 2021
body_summary:
The US FDA took action in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. 

The FDA alerted clinical laboratory staff and health care providers that genetic variants of SARS-CoV-2 may lead to false negative results with molecular tests for SARS-CoV-2. 

A U.S. District Court in Georgia granted a consent decree of permanent injunction against Fusion Health and Vitality LLC, Fusion Ionz LLC, and Matthew Ryncarz for violating federal law by distributing products containing vitamin D and hordenine HCl as preventions or treatments for COVID-19. 

The order of permanent injunction prohibits the defendants from selling or distributing unapproved new drugs or misbranded drugs with claims that the products can cure, mitigate, treat, or prevent diseases in people, including COVID-19. 

The FDA also posted a new webpage with frequently asked questions about the Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine. 

As of today, 311 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations. 

The FDA protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and other biological products for human use, and medical devices.

title: FDA Issues Alert Regarding SARS-CoV-2 Viral Mutation to Health Care Providers and Clinical Laboratory Staff
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is monitoring the potential impact of viral mutations, including the B.1.1.7 variant, on authorized SARS-CoV-2 molecular tests. The FDA is taking additional actions to ensure accurate tests, believing the risk of mutations impacting overall testing accuracy is low. The agency will continue to monitor SARS-CoV-2 genetic viral variants to ensure authorized tests provide accurate results. The FDA has been monitoring SARS-CoV-2 viral mutations throughout the pandemic and is working with test developers to review incoming data. Three currently authorized molecular tests may be impacted by genetic variants, but the impact does not appear to be significant. Laboratories should expect some false results to occur even with very accurate SARS-CoV-2 tests. The FDA encourages stakeholders to report adverse events or suspected adverse events experienced with molecular tests for detection of SARS-CoV-2.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A joint meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee and the Board of Governors was held on December 15-16, 2020. The meeting discussed financial market developments, including improved sentiment due to reduced uncertainty and positive vaccine news. In December 2023, the Federal Reserve's balance sheet increased to $7.3 trillion due to growth in securities holdings. The drilling and mining sector declined further in October, while industrial production rose strongly over October and November. Small business loan originations increased in October, while financing conditions remained accommodative for borrowers accessing government-backed loans. Participants noted that low-income households were hard hit by the resurgent virus, with looming expiration of unemployment benefits and loan forbearance programs worsening their situations. The Federal Open Market Committee agreed to maintain an accommodative monetary policy stance to foster economic recovery and achieve average inflation rate of 2 percent over time. They voted to continue buying Treasury securities of at least $80 billion per month and agency MBS of at least $40 billion per month until substantial further progress is made toward the Committee's maximum employment and price stability goals. The Federal Reserve decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 0-1/4 percent and continue increasing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency mortgage-backed securities until substantial progress is made toward maximum employment and price stability goals.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: January 5, 2021
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA posted a new webpage on the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act (CARES Act), highlighting authorities to enhance the FDA's ability to identify and prevent drug shortages. The CARES Act amended the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require manufacturers of certain drugs to provide information on permanent discontinuances and interruptions in manufacturing. The FDA also expanded the requirement for manufacturers to report the amount of each drug manufactured for commercial distribution. Additionally, the FDA issued a warning letter to Coco's Holistic Specialties & Apothecary for selling unapproved drug products with fraudulent COVID-19 claims. The FDA has authorized 310 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 235 molecular tests and 64 antibody tests.

title: FDA Statement on Following the Authorized Dosing Schedules for COVID-19 Vaccines
body_summary: Two mRNA vaccines have shown 95% effectiveness in preventing COVID-19 disease in adults. The FDA-authorized dosing schedule for these vaccines is recommended to be followed for safe protection. The interval between doses is 21 days for Pfizer-BioNTech and 28 days for Moderna. The data in firms' submissions regarding the first dose is often misinterpreted, and using a single dose regimen or administering less than the dose studied in clinical trials without understanding the depth and duration of protection can be concerning. Some discussions about changing the dosing schedule or dose aim to increase vaccine availability, but such changes are not supported by adequate scientific evidence. The FDA recommends sticking to the authorized dosing schedule for COVID-19 vaccines.

title: FDA Takes Steps to Provide Clarity on Developing New Drug Products in the Age of Individualized Medicine
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved over twice as many drugs for rare diseases, also known as orphan drugs, in the past eight years as in the previous eight years. Recent advances in scientific knowledge and drug development technology have enabled the development of drugs tailored to specific genetic variants of patients with rare genetic diseases. These drugs, referred to as "n of 1" therapies, bring unique challenges due to the rapid progression of the disease and the need for prompt medical intervention. The FDA is releasing new draft guidance on investigational new drug (IND) submissions for individualized antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) drug products to provide clarity on the regulatory process for these emerging products. The guidance addresses issues such as obtaining feedback from the FDA, regulatory submissions, Institutional Review Board (IRB) review, and informed consent. The FDA recognizes the need to address ethical and societal issues raised by this new drug-discovery paradigm and is willing to work with developers to bring these products safely to patients.

title: FDA Takes Steps to Provide Clarity on Developing New Drug Products in the Age of Individualized Medicine
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is releasing a new draft guidance on investigational new drug (IND) submissions for individualized antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) drug products. This guidance aims to provide clarity on interacting with and making regulatory submissions to the FDA for these emerging drug products. The FDA has seen an increase in development and approval of drugs for rare diseases, including genetic diseases, in recent years. With advances in testing and molecular diagnosis, it is now possible to pinpoint the exact cause of a patient's disease, leading to potential development of tailored drug products. However, developing these products poses challenges, including rapidly progressing diseases requiring prompt medical intervention, and the need for clarification on regulatory submissions and data requirements. The guidance addresses key points, including feedback from the FDA, regulatory submissions, Institutional Review Board (IRB) review, informed consent, and effectiveness measurement. The FDA is working to address ethical and societal issues associated with this new drug-discovery paradigm and is committed to ensuring the safe development of these individualized drug products.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 30, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced several actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA published a new toolkit to help stakeholders communicate in English and Spanish about hand sanitizer safety and use. A new COVID-19 Communication Toolkits webpage was also launched, providing links to all FDA toolkits on COVID-19 topics. The agency's achievements in 2020 were highlighted in an FDA Voices article, including the publication of an infographic on authorized COVID-19 tests and collection kits. Warning letters were issued to Sparrow & Health Performance LLC and Riverstone LLC for unapproved and misbranded products related to COVID-19. The FDA approved two abbreviated new drug applications for heparin sodium injection on December 29. As of December 28, 309 tests and sample collection devices are authorized under emergency use authorizations, including 235 molecular tests, 63 antibody tests, and 11 antigen tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 28, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has announced updates to its response efforts to the COVID-19 pandemic. On December 23, the FDA added pipette tips and micro pipettes to the Device Shortage List, and also updated the list with clarifying notes and links to more resources. The FDA has also posted a new web page, "Supplies of Medical Devices for COVID-19: Frequently Asked Questions". Additionally, the FDA has authorized 309 tests and sample collection devices under emergency use authorizations, including 235 molecular tests, 63 antibody tests, and 11 antigen tests.

title: FDA Approves First Generic of Drug Used to Treat Severe Hypoglycemia
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the first generic version of glucagon for injection, 1 mg/vial, for treating severe hypoglycemia and as a diagnostic aid. The drug is a synthetic version of human glucagon, which helps increase blood sugar levels and slow down gastrointestinal movement. The approval was granted to Amphastar Pharmaceuticals, Inc. and reflects the FDA's commitment to advancing patient access to lower-cost, high-quality generic drug products.

title: FDA Takes Further Steps to Confront Opioid Crisis Through Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy Programs
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has taken steps to strengthen the Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategies (REMS) program for transmucosal immediate-release fentanyl (TIRF) products to ensure safe use. This program aims to mitigate the risks associated with TIRF medicines, which contain fentanyl and are used to manage breakthrough pain in adults with cancer. The FDA has finalized modifications to the program, including requirements for prescribers to document a patient's opioid tolerance with each prescription, outpatient pharmacies to verify tolerance, and inpatient pharmacies to develop internal policies. The FDA also continues to evaluate the opioid analgesic (OA) REMS, hosting a public workshop to discuss methods to evaluate its impact on prescriber behavior and patient outcomes. The goal of the OA REMS is to educate prescribers and healthcare providers on treating and monitoring patients with pain.

title: FDA authorizes marketing of new device designed to remove dead pancreatic tissue
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized marketing of the EndoRotor System to treat walled-off pancreatic necrosis (WOPN), a potentially deadly condition that can occur after severe acute pancreatitis. The device, developed by Interscope, Incorporated, enables the removal of necrotic tissue through a minimally invasive procedure. In a clinical trial, 30 patients with WOPN underwent the EndoRotor System procedure, with an average of 85% reduction in necrotic tissue and 98.5% clearance in half of the subjects. However, three patients experienced serious adverse events, including two cases of gastrointestinal bleeding and one case of pneumoperitoneum leading to death. The FDA requires a boxed warning to emphasize the device should not be used in patients with known or suspected pancreatic cancer or those with specific contraindications.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 22, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has posted translations of the Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine fact sheet for recipients and caregivers, and for healthcare providers, in multiple languages including Arabic, Chinese, French, Spanish, Tagalog, and Vietnamese. The FDA has also approved three abbreviated new drug applications (ANDAs): for etomidate injection, furosemide injection, and succinylcholine chloride injection. The FDA recognizes the increased demand for certain products during the COVID-19 public health emergency and remains committed to facilitating access to safe and effective medical products. As of Dec. 22, 306 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under emergency use authorizations (EUAs).

title: FDA Warns Companies Illegally Selling CBD Products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued five warning letters to companies selling CBD products in ways that violate the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. The letters address illegal marketing of unapproved CBD products claiming to treat medical conditions, including nasal, ophthalmic, and inhalation products, as well as those added to food and marketed as dietary supplements. The FDA's priority is to protect public health and has previously sent warning letters to other companies illegally selling unapproved CBD products. The companies that received the letters are Bee Delightful G&L Wellness, New Leaf Pharmaceuticals, NextL3vel Services Group, LLC, and two others. The FDA requests responses from the companies within 15 working days to address the issues.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 21, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has posted translations of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine fact sheet for recipients and caregivers in multiple languages, including Arabic, Burmese, and Vietnamese. The agency has also updated its COVID-19 Response At-A-Glance Summary and issued a temporary guidance on review timelines for applicant responses to complete response letters when a facility assessment is needed. title: FDA Takes Additional Action in Fight Against COVID-19 By Issuing Emergency Use Authorization for Second COVID-19 Vaccine
body_summary: The US FDA has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine, allowing its distribution in the US for individuals 18 years and older. The vaccine has been authorized based on evidence showing it may be effective in preventing COVID-19, with benefits outweighing risks. The vaccine's safety will be monitored, including longer-term safety follow-up for ongoing clinical trials participants. ModernaTX, Inc. received the EUA, which is effective until circumstances justifying the authorization are terminated.

title: FDA Takes Additional Action in Fight Against COVID-19 By Issuing Emergency Use Authorization for Second COVID-19 Vaccine
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine, allowing its distribution in the US for individuals 18 years and older. The vaccine has been shown to be effective in preventing COVID-19, with a safety profile that outweighs its known and potential risks. The Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine contains messenger RNA (mRNA) that instructs cells to produce a "spike" protein, triggering an immune response. A pharmacovigilance plan has been approved, which includes longer-term safety follow-up for ongoing clinical trial participants. This plan aims to monitor the vaccine's safety profile and evaluate any safety concerns.

title: FDA Statement on Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee Meeting
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has informed the sponsor that it will rapidly work toward finalization and issuance of an emergency use authorization for the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine. The agency has also notified the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and Operation Warp Speed to execute their plans for timely vaccine distribution. The FDA is an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, responsible for protecting the public health and ensuring the safety and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: FDA Approves First Oral Hormone Therapy for Treating Advanced Prostate Cancer
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Orgovyx (relugolix) for the treatment of adult patients with advanced prostate cancer. Orgovyx is the first oral drug in this class, which may eliminate the need for clinic visits for treatments that require healthcare provider administration. The approval was granted to Myovant Sciences, with a safety and efficacy evaluation conducted in a randomized, open-label trial of 622 patients. The trial showed a castration rate of 96.7% in patients receiving Orgovyx. Common side effects include hot flush, increased glucose, and musculoskeletal pain. The FDA advises healthcare providers to monitor electrocardiograms and electrolytes due to potential effects on the heart and electrolyte levels. The drug may cause fetal harm and loss of pregnancy when administered to pregnant females.

title: FDA Approves Prosthetic Implant for Above-the-Knee Amputations
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved the Osseoanchored Prostheses for the Rehabilitation of Amputees (OPRA) Implant System, the first implant system marketed in the US for adults with transfemoral amputations. The device is surgically anchored into the patient's remaining thigh bone, allowing connection to an external prosthetic limb. The FDA approved the OPRA Implant System after a clinical study of 65 participants, which showed an average improvement in prosthetic use score of 35.1 points at two years and 39.6 points at five years compared to conventional socket prostheses. The device has been available under humanitarian device exemptions since 2015 and has been installed with two surgical procedures, requiring six months of training and rehabilitation after the second surgery.

title: Statement by President-elect Joe Biden on FDA Emergency Use Authorization for Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine
body_summary: The Food and Drug Administration has authorized the emergency use of the Moderna COVID-19 vaccine, bringing the total number of authorized vaccines to two, including Pfizer-BioNTech. This move is seen as a milestone in the fight against COVID-19. The administration of the vaccine has begun, with health care workers and residents of long-term care facilities receiving the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine this week, and bipartisan leaders including Vice President Pence, Speaker Pelosi, and Senator McConnell publicly receiving the vaccine today. The speaker looks forward to publicly receiving the vaccine on Monday and aims to administer 100 million vaccine shots in the first 100 days of their administration, which will focus on science and containing the virus.

title: FDA Approves First Adjuvant Therapy for Most Common Type of Lung Cancer
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Tagrisso (osimertinib) as the first adjuvant treatment for patients with non-small cell lung cancer whose tumors have a specific type of genetic mutation. This approval was granted for patients with epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations. Approximately 20% of patients with non-small cell lung cancer have EGFR mutations, and 30% have resectable disease, making them candidates for Tagrisso as adjuvant therapy after tumor removal. Tagrisso was previously approved in 2018 for first-line treatment of patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. The approval was based on a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 682 patients with early stage non-small cell lung cancer and EGFR exon 19 deletions or exon 21 L858R mutation-positive. In the overall trial population, patients who received Tagrisso had an 80% decrease in chance of disease recurrence compared with patients who received a placebo. Tagrisso was granted Orphan Drug designation and Breakthrough Therapy designation for the treatment of EGFR mutation-positive non-small cell lung cancer, and its approval was granted to AstraZeneca by the FDA.
