title: Trump Administration Sets the Pace for Food Loss and Waste Reduction Efforts to Continue
body_summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), FDA, and USDA renewed a three-year joint agency formal agreement to improve coordination and communication on reducing food loss and waste. The agreement reaffirms the agencies' commitment to reducing food loss and waste by 50 percent by 2030. Since the Trump Administration launched the Winning on Reducing Food Waste Initiative, the collaborative effort has achieved great success through public-private partnerships and education efforts. The agreement will continue to build on these successful partnerships. EPA Administrator Andrew Wheeler, U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Sonny Perdue, and FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn stated their commitment to achieving the goal. The agencies will focus on six priority areas: enhancing interagency coordination, increasing consumer education, improving food loss and waste measurement, clarifying food safety information, collaborating with private industry, and encouraging federal agencies to reduce food waste.

title: FDA Warns Consumers to Avoid Certain Male Enhancement and Weight Loss Products Sold Through Amazon, eBay and Other Retailers Due to Hidden, Potentially Dangerous Drug Ingredients
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is warning consumers not to use nearly 50 male enhancement and weight loss products that have been found to contain hidden ingredients and may pose a significant health risk. The FDA purchased these products on Amazon and eBay and found that they contain active pharmaceutical ingredients not listed on their labels, including some with ingredients found in prescription drugs. 

These products may cause potentially serious side effects and interact with medications or dietary supplements a consumer is taking. The FDA urges consumers to beware of purchasing or taking these products. All 26 of the products purchased on Amazon and 20 of 25 products purchased on eBay contained undeclared active pharmaceutical ingredients. 

The FDA has found that many of the products have names that are the same as or similar to tainted products that have been the subject of previous warnings. These products are unapproved new drugs, adulterated dietary supplements, and misbranded due to inaccurate labels. The FDA encourages consumers to report any adverse events and to be cautious about using certain products, especially those promoted for sexual enhancement, weight loss, or pain relief.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 16, 2020
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued two new Emergency Use Authorizations (EUA) in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. 

The FDA authorized the BinaxNOW COVID-19 Ag Card Home Test for at-home use with a prescription, allowing individuals 15 years or older to collect and test nasal swab samples suspected of COVID-19. 

The FDA also authorized the Ellume COVID-19 Home Test for at-home use without a prescription, allowing individuals 2 years old and older to detect proteins of the SARS-CoV-2 virus from a nasal swab sample. 

The agency has also posted online materials for an upcoming Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee meeting on December 17.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The Federal Reserve is committed to using its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals. The COVID-19 pandemic is causing tremendous human and economic hardship across the United States and around the world. Economic activity and employment have continued to recover but remain well below their levels at the beginning of the year. Weaker demand and earlier declines in oil prices have been holding down consumer price inflation. Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses. The path of the economy will depend significantly on the course of the virus. The ongoing public health crisis will continue to weigh on economic activity, employment, and inflation in the near term, and poses considerable risks to the economic outlook over the medium term. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. With inflation running persistently below this longer-run goal, the Committee will aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time so that inflation averages 2 percent over time and longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored at 2 percent. The Committee expects to maintain an accommodative stance of monetary policy until these outcomes are achieved. The Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time. In addition, the Federal Reserve will continue to increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $80 billion per month and of agency mortgage-backed securities by at least $40 billion per month until substantial further progress has been made toward the Committee's maximum employment and price stability goals. These asset purchases help foster smooth market functioning and accommodative financial conditions, thereby supporting the flow of credit to households and businesses. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Patrick Harker; Robert S. Kaplan; Neel Kashkari; Loretta J. Mester; and Randal K. Quarles.

title: Actualización sobre el coronavirus (COVID-19): La FDA emite  una nueva autorización para la prueba en el hogar  BinaxNOW COVID-19 Ag Card
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for the BinaxNOW COVID-19 Ag Card test, which can be used by patients at home with a prescription. The test is authorized for use with at-home nasal swab samples collected by patients 15 years or older if their healthcare provider suspects COVID-19 within the first seven days of symptoms. It is also authorized for use with at-home nasal swab samples collected by adults of 4 years or older if their healthcare provider suspects COVID-19 within the first seven days of symptoms. The test will be offered in conjunction with a telehealth service that guides users through the sample collection process and provides assistance with reading and understanding results. The telehealth provider will also report all test results to relevant health authorities, in compliance with local, state, and federal requirements. According to FDA Commissioner Dr. Stephen M. Hahn, "The FDA continues to authorize COVID-19 tests that will give more Americans greater flexibility and options for testing". The test is expected to have a significant impact on manufacturing processes and support testing for millions of people.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Antigen Test as First Over-the-Counter Fully At-Home Diagnostic Test for COVID-19
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the first over-the-counter (OTC) fully at-home diagnostic test for COVID-19, the Ellume COVID-19 Home Test. This test, a rapid lateral flow antigen test, can be used by individuals 2 years of age or older and detects fragments of proteins from the SARS-CoV-2 virus from a nasal swab sample. The test was authorized on [date], following the approval of two other COVID-19 tests for home use last month and last week. The FDA has authorized over 225 diagnostic tests for COVID-19, including more than 25 tests that allow for home collection of samples. The Ellume COVID-19 Home Test can return results in as little as 20 minutes and is expected to produce over three million tests in January 2021. Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn and Jeff Shuren, director of FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health, emphasized the importance of expanding access to testing and innovation in test development.

title: FDA Approves First-of-its-Kind Intentional Genomic Alteration in Line of Domestic Pigs for Both Human Food, Potential Therapeutic Uses
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the first intentional genomic alteration (IGA) in an animal, GalSafe pigs, for both human food consumption and as a source for potential therapeutic uses. The IGA aims to eliminate alpha-gal sugar on the surface of the pigs' cells, which can cause allergic reactions in people with Alpha-gal syndrome (AGS). The FDA Commissioner, Stephen M. Hahn, praised the approval as a "tremendous milestone for scientific innovation". The approval is the result of a risk-based approach and ensures that the product is safe for animals, people, and achieves its intended results. The FDA has determined that food from GalSafe pigs is safe for the general population to eat, and the product developer, Revivicor Inc., intends to sell meat from these pigs by mail order.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 14, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. Yesterday, the FDA posted a review memorandum outlining its decision to authorize the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine. The agency has made efforts to ensure transparency in the vaccine review process. Warning letters have been issued to three firms selling unapproved products with fraudulent COVID-19 claims, and another firm promoting such products. The FDA has also approved an abbreviated new drug application for midazolam injection, a medication for preoperative sedation. As of December 14, 299 tests and sample collection devices are authorized by the FDA under EUAs. The FDA has also posted a video on safely using hand sanitizer.

title: FDA Statement on Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee Meeting
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) will rapidly work toward finalization and issuance of an emergency use authorization for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine. The agency has notified the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and Operation Warp Speed to execute their plans for timely vaccine distribution. The FDA is an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, responsible for protecting public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of various products, including vaccines and medical devices.

title: Statement by President-elect Biden on FDA Advisory Committee Recommended Emergency Use Authorization of Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine
body_summary: Yesterday marked another tragic milestone in the fight against COVID-19. The FDA's Advisory Committee recommended an Emergency Use Authorization for the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine. This vaccine's development and evaluation were free from political influence. The administration will scale up manufacturing and distribution to distribute 100 million shots in the first 100 days. To achieve this, the Trump Administration must purchase the negotiated doses, and Congress must fund the distribution efforts. The administration plans to manage a robust plan to contain the virus starting on day one, with measures including mask wearing, social distancing, and limiting travel over the holidays.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Holds Advisory Committee Meeting to Discuss Authorization of COVID-19 Vaccine Candidate as Part of Agency’s Review of Safety and Effectiveness Data
body_summary: The FDA's Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee is meeting to discuss Pfizer Inc.'s request for emergency use authorization for a COVID-19 vaccine. The FDA has been working to facilitate the rapid development and availability of COVID-19 vaccines while maintaining rigorous scientific standards for safety and effectiveness. The committee's discussion will provide transparency and public input, ensuring clear public understanding of the scientific data. The FDA's career staff has reviewed thousands of pages of technical information, including clinical trial data, and will consider the committee's input before making a final decision on authorization. The decision will be made by FDA's career officials in the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 10, 2020
body_summary: The FDA announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee met to discuss the first request for emergency use authorization for a COVID-19 vaccine, submitted by Pfizer Inc. in partnership with BioNTech Manufacturing GmbH. The FDA has issued emergency use authorizations for 298 tests and sample collection devices, including 229 molecular tests and sample collection devices, 61 antibody tests, and 8 antigen tests. The agency has also issued a warning letter to Paradigm RE, LLC for selling unapproved and misbranded products with fraudulent COVID-19 claims. The FDA protects the public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of various products.

title: Memorandum on the National Space Policy
body_summary: The US National Space Policy supersedes previous directives, promoting responsible space operations, a robust commercial space sector, and international cooperation. It aims to strengthen US leadership in space, industrial base, and capabilities, while safeguarding critical infrastructure and Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) systems. The policy requires periodic reporting to the National Space Council and establishes standards for space professional development. The US government seeks to improve space system development and procurement, strengthen interagency and commercial partnerships, and promote international cooperation. Key initiatives include improving timely acquisition and deployment, reducing programmatic risk, and promoting innovation. The policy also addresses regulatory oversight, orbital debris research, and the development of space nuclear power systems. The US will maintain a timely and responsive regulatory environment for licensing space activities and promote the commercial space sector to lead in the global space market. NASA continues to lead the civil space sector using commercial capabilities, while the United States Space Force develops forces to project power in space and defend US national interests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes First  Direct-to-Consumer COVID-19 Test System
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized LabCorp's Pixel COVID-19 Test Home Collection Kit for use by individuals 18 years and older without a prescription. This kit allows individuals to self-collect a nasal swab sample at home and send it to LabCorp for testing. Positive or invalid test results are delivered by phone, while negative results are delivered via email or online portal. The kit can be purchased online or in stores without a prescription, enabling users to determine if self-isolation is appropriate and assist with healthcare decisions.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 8, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. Today, the FDA posted background material for the upcoming Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee public meeting to discuss Emergency Use Authorization of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 Vaccine for individuals 16 years of age and older. On December 7, the FDA approved an abbreviated new drug application for dexmedetomidine hydrochloride injection, indicated for sedation of patients. The FDA has also issued safety communications, including a warning about the risks of metal face masks during MRI exams. Additionally, the FDA has authorized the first diagnostic test for COVID-19 and influenza A and B, and as of December 8, there are 297 authorized tests and sample collection devices under EUAs.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes First COVID-19 and Flu Combination Test for use with home-collected samples
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has authorized the first diagnostic test for at-home collection of patient samples to detect COVID-19 and flu. The Quest Diagnostics RC COVID-19 +Flu RT-PCR Test is allowed for prescription use with the Quest Diagnostics Self-Collection Kit, enabling individuals to collect a sample at home and ship it to a laboratory for analysis. This authorization is seen as a step to address the ongoing COVID-19 fight, particularly during the flu season. FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn said this test can provide timely answers to patients faster and in the comfort of their own homes, allowing them to continue quarantining while awaiting results.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes First COVID-19 and Flu Combination Test for use with home-collected samples
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the first diagnostic test for at-home collection of patient samples to detect COVID-19 and influenza A and B (flu). The Quest Diagnostics RC COVID-19 +Flu RT-PCR Test can be used with the Quest Diagnostics Self-Collection Kit for individuals suspected of respiratory viral infection consistent with COVID-19. The test allows patients to collect a sample at home, ship it to a Quest Diagnostics laboratory for analysis, and receive results while continuing to quarantine. This authorization is a step in the FDA's nationwide response to COVID-19 and aims to provide timely information to patients with unknown respiratory ailments.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 4, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a guidance on the enforcement policy for the Quality Standards of the Mammography Quality Standards Act during the COVID-19 public health emergency. The agency has also issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for the Lumin LM3000 Bioburden Reduction UV System, the first ultraviolet-C (UV-C) light-based bioburden reduction system for emergency use in bioburden reduction of certain N95 respirators. The FDA has added content to the question-and-answer appendix in its guidance titled, "Conduct of Clinical Trials of Medical Products During COVID-19 Public Health Emergency." PrecisionFDA has launched the COVID-19 Precision Immunology App-a-thon, which encourages the scientific and analytics community to develop innovative applications to explore the relationship between personalized immune repertoires and COVID-19 disease variables. As of December 1, 295 tests are authorized by FDA under EUAs, including 227 molecular tests, 61 antibody tests, and 7 antigen tests.

title: Statement by President-elect Joe Biden on the November Jobs Report and Continuing Economic Crisis
body_summary: The US economy is stalling, with millions of people losing jobs or facing reduced hours, health insurance, or risk of losing it. One in six renters are behind on rent, and one in four small businesses are struggling to stay open. The unemployment gap between Black and Latino workers remains large. A recent jobs report showed 2.3 million more people in long-term unemployment, the largest increase on record. If Congress fails to act, 12 million Americans will lose unemployment benefits by the end of December. Emergency paid leave and eviction moratoriums will expire, causing vital funding for testing, public health workers, and small business assistance to be lost. Bipartisan efforts in the Senate have led to a proposed $900 billion relief package, but it is not enough. Congress must pass a deal for the American people, and will need to act again in January.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 3, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has taken actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA issued a warning letter jointly with the Federal Trade Commission to Rat's Army for selling unapproved products with fraudulent COVID-19 claims. The agency updated the SARS CoV-2 reference panel comparative data on its website to reflect the latest information. As of December 1, 295 tests are authorized by the FDA under EUAs, including 227 molecular tests, 61 antibody tests, and 7 antigen tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: December 1, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has reissued the August 23, 2020, emergency use authorization for COVID-19 convalescent plasma for the treatment of hospitalized patients with COVID-19. The FDA has also issued warning letters to Avazo-Healthcare, LLC, for selling adulterated and misbranded COVID-19 test kits and unapproved drug products with fraudulent claims. The agency has posted warning letters for other companies, including ChromaDex, Innovative Medicine LLC, Red Moon Herbs, and Sage Woman Herbs, Ltd. dba Sage Consulting & Apothecary. The FDA has updated guidance on notifying the FDA of permanent discontinuance or interruption in manufacturing of medical devices under Section 506J of the FD&C Act. As of December 1, 295 tests are authorized by the FDA under EUAs, including 227 molecular tests, 61 antibody tests, and 7 antigen tests.

title: FDA Approves First PSMA-Targeted PET Imaging Drug for Men with Prostate Cancer
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Ga 68 PSMA-11, a radioactive diagnostic agent, for positron emission tomography (PET) imaging of prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) positive lesions in men with prostate cancer. Ga 68 PSMA-11 is indicated for patients with suspected prostate cancer metastasis or recurrence based on elevated serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels. The approval is expected to aid healthcare providers in assessing prostate cancer and detecting cancer spread. Ga 68 PSMA-11 binds to PSMA, which is an important target for prostate cancer imaging. The safety and efficacy of Ga 68 PSMA-11 were evaluated in two clinical trials involving 960 men with prostate cancer. The trials demonstrated the effectiveness of Ga 68 PSMA-11 in detecting sites of disease in patients with biochemical evidence of recurrent prostate cancer. The FDA approved the use of Ga 68 PSMA-11 for imaging patients with prostate cancer, and its approval is expected to have important implications for patient care.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) held a meeting via videoconference on November 4-5, 2020, with Jerome H. Powell, Chair, and John C. Williams, Vice Chair, present. Markets saw little change over the intermeeting period, remaining accommodative. Financial markets were influenced by rising COVID-19 cases in Europe and the US, as well as election and fiscal policy uncertainties. The FOMC discussed asset purchases, considering their role in supporting maximum employment and price stability goals. Participants agreed that ongoing careful consideration of potential next steps is appropriate, but no immediate adjustments were necessary. The Federal Reserve's balance sheet increased to $7.2 trillion due to growth in securities holdings and offsetting decline in US dollar liquidity swaps. Real GDP rebounded rapidly in Q3 but remained below pre-pandemic levels, while labor market conditions improved. Consumer price inflation returned to its year-earlier pace, and total PCE rose strongly. The FOMC aims to achieve maximum employment and price stability, with a target inflation rate of 2 percent over the longer run, and decided to maintain an accommodative stance until these goals are achieved.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Issues New Policy on Dry Heat for Reuse of Certain Respirators
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued guidance on using dry heat to support single-user reuse of certain particulate filtering facepiece respirators (FFRs) during the COVID-19 public health emergency. The guidance provides recommendations for bioburden reduction systems that use dry heat to reduce microorganisms on FFRs for reuse by a single user. The FDA does not object to the use of certain dry heat systems for reducing bioburden and supporting single-user reuse of otherwise disposable FFRs. The guidance applies to FFRs that have been FDA-cleared, authorized under existing EUAs, or are imported and not manufactured in China. Manufacturers should follow recommended system settings and labeling, and also follow existing CDC reuse recommendations.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: November 24, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA published a new page on FDA.gov with answers to frequently asked questions about face masks, surgical masks, and respirators. The FDA has also posted two templates for serology tests, which provide recommendations for validation data and other information to support EUA requests for SARS-CoV-2 antibody tests. On November 23, the FDA approved an abbreviated new drug application for dexmedetomidine hydrochloride injection, indicated for sedation in intensive-care settings. As of November 24, 291 tests are authorized by the FDA under EUAs, including 225 molecular tests, 59 antibody tests, and 7 antigen tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: November 23, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved an abbreviated new drug application for succinylcholine chloride injection on Nov. 20, and issued an EUA for casirivimab and imdevimab on Nov. 21. The FDA also authorized 289 tests under EUAs, including 224 molecular tests, 58 antibody tests, and 7 antigen tests, as of Nov. 18. Casirivimab and imdevimab were shown to reduce COVID-19-related hospitalization or emergency room visits in patients at high risk for disease progression within 28 days after treatment when compared to placebo. The FDA recently posted a new infographic on a potential pathway for vaccines. The FDA protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices, as well as regulating food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, electronic radiation products, and tobacco products.

title: FDA Expands Approval of Influenza Treatment to Post-Exposure Prevention
body_summary: The US FDA has expanded the approved indication for Xofluza (baloxavir marboxil) to include post-exposure prevention of influenza in patients 12 years of age and older after contact with someone who has the flu. Xofluza is now available as granules for mixing in water, in addition to its previous tablet form. The expanded indication will provide an option to help prevent influenza, particularly during a flu season that will coincide with the coronavirus pandemic. Xofluza's safety and efficacy for post-flu exposure prevention are supported by a randomized, double-blind, controlled trial involving 607 subjects who received either a single dose of Xofluza or a placebo. The trial found that Xofluza reduced the risk of infection by 99% compared to the placebo. Common side effects include diarrhea, bronchitis, and nausea. Patients should not take Xofluza with certain products or have a known hypersensitivity reaction to the medication. The FDA granted approval to Genentech USA, Inc. The agency protects public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs.

title: FDA Approves First Drug to Treat Rare Metabolic Disorder
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Oxlumo (lumasiran) as the first treatment for primary hyperoxaluria type 1 (PH1), a rare genetic disorder. This approval results from the work of experts and community members coordinated by the Oxalosis & Hyperoxaluria Foundation and the Kidney Health Initiative. PH1 affects an estimated one to three individuals per million in North America and Europe, causing kidney stones and progressive kidney damage. Oxlumo decreases oxalate production, with a 65% reduction in urine oxalate levels in patients treated with the medication, compared to 12% in the placebo group. The medication was evaluated in two studies, one in patients six years and older and an open-label study in patients younger than six years. Oxlumo received orphan drug designation and breakthrough therapy designation, and the manufacturer, Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, Inc., received a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher. The FDA granted the approval of Oxlumo on behalf of the agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Monoclonal Antibodies for Treatment of COVID-19
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for casirivimab and imdevimab, administered together, to treat mild to moderate COVID-19 in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age or older weighing at least 40 kilograms. The EUA is based on a clinical trial showing reduced hospitalization or emergency room visits in patients at high risk for disease progression within 28 days after treatment. The therapy must be administered together by intravenous infusion and is not authorized for patients hospitalized due to COVID-19. The FDA has determined that the known and potential benefits of casirivimab and imdevimab outweigh the known and potential risks.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: November 20, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued an EUA for the drug baricitinib (Olumiant), in combination with remdesivir (Veklury), for the treatment of suspected or laboratory confirmed COVID-19 in hospitalized adults and pediatric patients two years of age or older requiring supplemental oxygen, invasive mechanical ventilation, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). The safety and effectiveness of baricitinib continues to be evaluated. The FDA has also issued warnings to Pro Breath MD, LLC dba Dentist Select and OraCare, and Vibrant Health Care, Inc., for selling unapproved products with fraudulent COVID-19 claims. The agency is scheduled to discuss the request for emergency use authorization of a COVID-19 vaccine from Pfizer-BioNTech on December 10.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Hutchinson-Gilford Progeria Syndrome and Some Progeroid Laminopathies
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Zokinvy (lonafarnib) capsules to reduce the risk of death due to Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome and certain processing-deficient progeroid laminopathies in patients one year of age and older. This is the first FDA-approved medication for these diseases, which cause premature aging and death. Zokinvy, a farnesyltransferase inhibitor, helps prevent the buildup of defective progerin or progerin-like protein in cells. The effectiveness of Zokinvy was demonstrated in trials involving 62 patients, with a significant increase in lifespan compared to untreated patients. Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and fatigue. The FDA granted Priority Review designation and Orphan Drug Designation, and the approval was given to Eiger BioPharmaceuticals, Inc.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Announces Advisory Committee Meeting to Discuss COVID-19 Vaccine Candidate
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has scheduled a meeting of its Vaccines and Related Biological Products Advisory Committee (VRBPAC) on Dec. 10 to discuss a COVID-19 vaccine request from Pfizer, Inc. in partnership with BioNTech Manufacturing GmbH. FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn has assured the American people that the FDA's process will be transparent. The VRBPAC meeting will discuss the safety and effectiveness of Pfizer and BioNTech's vaccine. The FDA will review the request as expeditiously as possible, while maintaining a thorough and science-based process. Background materials, including the meeting agenda and committee roster, will be made available to the public two business days prior to the meeting.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Drug Combination for Treatment of COVID-19
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the drug baricitinib, in combination with remdesivir, for the treatment of suspected or laboratory confirmed COVID-19 in hospitalized adults and pediatric patients two years of age or older requiring supplemental oxygen, invasive mechanical ventilation, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). The authorization is based on a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial (ACTT-2) that showed baricitinib, in combination with remdesivir, reduced time to recovery within 29 days after initiating treatment compared to patients who received a placebo with remdesivir. The safety and effectiveness of this investigational therapy continues to be evaluated. The EUA was issued by the FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn, M.D. Baricitinib is a janus kinase inhibitor and is approved for the treatment of moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis. Remdesivir is an FDA-approved intravenous antiviral drug for use in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older and weighing at least 40 kilograms. The FDA authorized the emergency use of baricitinib, in combination with remdesivir, for the treatment of certain hospitalized patients with suspected or laboratory-confirmed COVID-19.

title: FDA Releases New Outbreak Investigation Table
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is releasing a new tool to provide timely information on foodborne illness outbreak investigations. The tool, part of the Coordinated Outbreak Response and Evaluation (CORE) Network, will be updated weekly and include information on all foodborne outbreaks initiated by the FDA. The information will be shared with the public before a public health advisory or recall is issued. The FDA will continue to share updates during the early stages of an investigation, but not before all information is available. This new tool demonstrates the FDA's commitment to transparent communication with stakeholders and consumers. The FDA has already taken steps to release information early in some cases and will continue to work towards sharing information at the earliest stages of an investigation.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes First COVID-19 Test for Self-Testing at Home
body_summary: The US FDA has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the first at-home COVID-19 diagnostic test, the Lucira COVID-19 All-In-One Test Kit. The test is a molecular test that can be self-administered at home and provides rapid results. The test is authorized for individuals 14 years old and older who are suspected of COVID-19, and for use in point-of-care settings for all ages. The test works by swirling a self-collected nasal swab sample in a vial, and results can be read in 30 minutes or less. The FDA Commissioner, Stephen M. Hahn, and Jeff Shuren, director of the Center for Devices and Radiological Health, have praised the test as an important diagnostic advancement to address the pandemic. The test must be prescribed by a healthcare provider, and results must be reported to public health authorities.

title: COVID-19 Update: FDA’s Ongoing Commitment to Transparency for COVID-19 EUAs
body_summary: The FDA is announcing its plan to provide more transparency around its emergency use authorization (EUA) process for drugs and biological products, including vaccines. The agency has launched the COVID-19 Pandemic Recovery and Preparedness Plan (PREPP) to optimize the ongoing COVID-19 response and strengthen its resilience. As part of PREPP, the FDA intends to publicly post its reviews of the scientific data and information supporting EUA issuance, revision, or revocation for all drug and biological products, including vaccines. The agency will disclose information from EUA review documents as appropriate, with potential redactions to protect sensitive data. This step aims to increase public confidence in the EUA review process. The FDA has already posted some scientific review documents and will continue to do so. The agency is committed to transparency and science-driven decision-making in its fight against COVID-19.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: November 17, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has reaffirmed its commitment to transparency regarding emergency use authorization (EUA) decisions, including updates on its plan to share scientific reviews for EUAs issued, revised, or revoked for drugs and biological products. The FDA is taking steps to promote transparency and public confidence in its scientific review process by posting scientific reviews, to the extent permitted by law, on its website. This includes reorganizing FAQs on testing for SARS-CoV-2 and updating answers to certain questions. As of today, 288 tests are authorized by the FDA under EUAs, including 223 molecular tests, 58 antibody tests, and 7 antigen tests. The FDA is also publishing a new podcast titled "Personal Protective Equipment and COVID-19" featuring discussions on PPE and its role in reducing COVID-19 spread.

title: FDA Approves First Intratumoral Injection to Treat Non-Metastatic Mast Cell Tumors in Dogs
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Stelfonta (tigilanol tiglate injection) to treat dogs with non-metastatic, skin-based (cutaneous) mast cell tumors (MCTs). Stelfonta is injected directly into the MCT and works by activating a protein that spreads throughout the treated tumor, causing it to disintegrate. The FDA approved Stelfonta for use in dogs with non-metastatic MCTs located on or under the skin, particularly in the leg area. The approval provides an additional treatment option for local mast cell tumors. The safety and effectiveness of Stelfonta were established in a study involving 118 dogs, with a complete remission rate of 75% after treatment. Stelfonta carries a boxed warning for human safety due to the risk of severe wound formation from accidental self-injection or needle stick injuries. The drug is available only by prescription due to the professional expertise required for its administration.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: November 16, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has updated its guidance on investigational COVID-19 convalescent plasma, extending the period of enforcement discretion through February 2021. This will allow continued access to convalescent plasma for hospitalized COVID-19 patients while blood establishments develop necessary operating procedures. The agency has also published a new webpage providing technical information and resources on COVID-19 diagnostic testing, including a companion webpage with plain language information on testing for patients and consumers. As of today, 288 tests are authorized by the FDA under EUAs, including 223 molecular tests, 58 antibody tests, and 7 antigen tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: November 13, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken actions against Natural Solutions Foundation and two individuals, Dr. Rima Laibow and Ralph Fucetola, for allegedly distributing a misbranded and unapproved new drug, Dr. Rima RecommendsTMNano Silver 10PPM, as a prevention or treatment for COVID-19 and other diseases. The FDA, along with the Federal Trade Commission, had previously issued a warning letter to the defendants. The agency is concerned that such products may cause consumers to delay or stop appropriate medical treatment, leading to serious harm. As of today, 288 tests are authorized by the FDA under EUAs, including 223 molecular tests, 58 antibody tests, and 7 antigen tests.

title: Joint Statement by the United States and the Heads of State of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) on Human Capital Development at the 8th ASEAN-U.S. Summit
body_summary: The Heads of State/Government of ASEAN and the US met via videoconference on November 14, 2020, to strengthen the ASEAN-US Strategic Partnership. They reaffirmed their commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific region, focusing on human capital development, health, and economic growth. Key decisions included education for a resilient population, promoting women's economic participation, and enhancing digital literacy education. The ASEAN community also committed to preventing re-victimization, protecting victims of human trafficking, and promoting the rights of persons with disabilities, while strengthening democracy, supporting anti-corruption efforts, and adhering to the rule of law.

title: Statement by the President-elect on COVID-19
body_summary: I met with the co-chairs of the transition COVID-19 Advisory Board, including Dr. Vivek Murthy, Dr. David Kessler, and Dr. Marcella Nunez-Smith, who briefed me on the accelerating public health crisis. The crisis is marked by surges in reported infections, hospitalizations, and fatalities nationwide. The president-elect demands a robust and immediate federal response, including resources for frontline healthcare workers, surge capacity for hospitals, clear guidance, and effective distribution of testing kits and supplies. I renew my call for every American to step up and take action on social distancing, hand washing, and mask wearing to protect themselves and others.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: November 12, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA has issued a new Consumer Update warning consumers to avoid fraudulent flu products and offering tips on how to spot them. The agency has sent warning letters to companies offering for sale medical products with fraudulent claims. As of October 31, more than 560 drug development programs were in planning stages, over 370 trials had been reviewed by the FDA, and 6 COVID-19 treatments were authorized for emergency use. The FDA has also authorized 288 tests under EUAs, including 223 molecular tests, 58 antibody tests, and 7 antigen tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: November 10, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On November 12, the FDA will host a virtual presentation on the effectiveness of facial coverings in reducing the spread of infection. The presentation will provide an overview of the FDA's research on this topic and discuss the development of a comprehensive risk-assessment tool. Currently, 288 tests are authorized by the FDA under EUAs, including 223 molecular tests, 58 antibody tests, and 7 antigen tests. The FDA is an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, responsible for protecting public health and regulating various products such as drugs, vaccines, medical devices, and food supply.

title: FDA Encourages Manufacturers to Clearly Declare All Uses of Sesame in Ingredient List on Food Labels
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a draft guidance encouraging food manufacturers to voluntarily declare sesame as an ingredient on food labels. This move aims to help Americans with sesame allergies identify products that may contain the ingredient. According to Dr. Susan Mayne, director of the FDA's Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition, sesame is often not declared by name on labels, even when it is used as a flavor or spice. The FDA has received data on the occurrence and severity of sesame allergies in the U.S., which indicates that some allergic reactions may be caused by products with undeclared sesame or ingredients like tahini. The agency is encouraging manufacturers to label their products if they contain sesame, even when not required to do so.

title: FDA Encourages Manufacturers to Clearly Declare All Uses of Sesame in Ingredient List on Food Labels
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a draft guidance encouraging food manufacturers to voluntarily declare sesame in the ingredient list on food labels. This move aims to help Americans identify products that might contain sesame, a common allergen. According to Susan Mayne, Ph.D., director of the FDA's Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition, sesame is often used as a 'flavor' or 'spice' without being declared on the label. The FDA has received data on sesame allergies and has found that reactions, such as hives and anaphylaxis, may occur from products with undeclared sesame or tahini. The agency is encouraging food manufacturers to label their products with sesame, even when not required by law. The FDA also continues to assess allergens of public health importance and protects the public health by regulating the nation's food supply, cosmetics, and other products.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: November 9, 2020
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the monoclonal antibody therapy bamlanivimab for the treatment of mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in adult and pediatric patients. Bamlanivimab is authorized for patients 12 years of age and older weighing at least 40 kilograms, at high risk for severe COVID-19, and certain chronic medical conditions.

The FDA also issued final guidance on designing and executing clinical trials to include diverse populations. This guidance provides recommendations for broadening eligibility criteria in clinical trials and increasing enrollment of underrepresented populations. 

Additionally, the FDA approved an abbreviated new drug application for cisatracurium besylate USP 10 mg/5mL and 200 mg/20 mL, an adjunct to general anesthesia to facilitate tracheal intubation. The FDA issued an EUA for GenScript USA Inc.'scPass SARS-CoV-2 Neutralization Antibody Detection Kit, the first serology test authorized to detect neutralizing antibodies from recent or prior COVID-19 infection.

As of today, 288 tests are authorized by FDA under EUAs, including 223 molecular tests, 58 antibody tests, and 7 antigen tests.

title: FDA Offers Guidance to Enhance Diversity in Clinical Trials, Encourage Inclusivity in Medical Product Development
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued final guidance to promote diverse populations in clinical trials for medical products. The guidance aims to increase enrollment of underrepresented populations in clinical trials by providing recommendations on designing and executing trials. The FDA recommends broadening clinical trial eligibility criteria, considering logistical and participant-related factors, and engaging with patient advocacy groups and patients to design trials that participants would be willing to enroll in. The guidance also includes recommendations for improving enrollment and retention of participants with rare diseases. The FDA is committed to increasing enrollment of diverse populations in medical product development and will continue to engage with federal partners, medical product manufacturers, medical professionals, and health advocates to achieve this goal.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Monoclonal Antibody for Treatment of COVID-19
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for the monoclonal antibody therapy bamlanivimab to treat mild-to-moderate COVID-19 in adult and pediatric patients. Bamlanivimab is authorized for patients 12 years of age and older weighing at least 40 kilograms, and at high risk for severe COVID-19. The therapy was shown to reduce hospitalization or emergency room visits in patients at high risk for disease progression within 28 days after treatment. The EUA was based on an interim analysis from a phase two randomized clinical trial involving 465 non-hospitalized adults. The trial found that bamlanivimab reduced COVID-19-related hospitalizations and emergency room visits by 67%. Bamlanivimab is not authorized for patients hospitalized due to COVID-19.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes First Test that Detects Neutralizing Antibodies from Recent or Prior SARS-CoV-2 Infection
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration authorized the first serology test that detects neutralizing antibodies from recent or prior SARS-CoV-2 infection, which are antibodies that bind to a specific part of a pathogen and have been observed to decrease SARS-CoV-2 viral infection of cells. The FDA issued an emergency use authorization for the thecPass SARS-CoV-2 Neutralization Antibody Detection Kit, which specifically detects this type of antibody. This authorization marks the first time a test has been authorized to detect neutralizing antibodies, which are different from binding antibodies that only detect the presence of a virus. The FDA notes that the effect of neutralizing antibodies for SARS-CoV-2 in humans is still being researched, and patients should not interpret results as telling them they are immune. The authorization was issued to GenScript USA Inc. for its thecPass SARS-CoV-2 Neutralization Antibody Detection Kit.

title: FDA Takes Efforts to Protect Patients from Potentially Harmful Compounded Drugs Through Finalizing Insanitary Conditions Guidance
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is releasing a final guidance to help compounders identify and prevent insanitary conditions at their facilities. The FDA aims to protect patients from exposure to poor quality compounded drugs. Insanitary conditions include dirt, mold, insects, trash, peeling paint, and unclean exhaust vents. The FDA has taken regulatory and enforcement actions against compounders with such conditions. The guidance also recommends using risk management tools to develop controls to prevent insanitary conditions. The FDA will continue to address insanitary conditions and work with states and the Department of Justice to protect patients. Both traditional compounders and outsourcing facilities should take measures to avoid such conditions.

title: FDA Permits Marketing of New Device Designed to Reduce Sleep Disturbance Related to Nightmares in Certain Adults
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has permitted the marketing of a new device called Nightware, which is intended to temporarily reduce sleep disturbance related to nightmares in adults 22 years or older with nightmare disorder or PTSD. The device provides gentle vibration through touch based on an analysis of heart rate and motion during sleep. The device was studied in a 30-day randomized, sham-controlled trial of 70 patients, who showed improvement on sleep scales, with the active group showing greater improvement than the sham group. The evidence demonstrated the probable benefits outweighed the probable risks. Nightware is intended to be used under the supervision of a healthcare provider and is not a standalone therapy for PTSD. It is available by prescription only and is intended for home use.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The Federal Reserve is committed to using its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals. The COVID-19 pandemic is causing tremendous human and economic hardship across the United States and around the world. Economic activity and employment have continued to recover but remain well below their levels at the beginning of the year. Weaker demand and earlier declines in oil prices have been holding down consumer price inflation. Overall financial conditions remain accommodative, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses. The path of the economy will depend significantly on the course of the virus. The ongoing public health crisis will continue to weigh on economic activity, employment, and inflation in the near term, and poses considerable risks to the economic outlook over the medium term. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. With inflation running persistently below this longer-run goal, the Committee will aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time so that inflation averages 2 percent over time and longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored at 2 percent. The Committee expects to maintain an accommodative stance of monetary policy until these outcomes are achieved. The Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time. In addition, over coming months the Federal Reserve will increase its holdings of Treasury securities and agency mortgage-backed securities at least at the current pace to sustain smooth market functioning and help foster accommodative financial conditions, thereby supporting the flow of credit to households and businesses. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Mary C. Daly; Patrick Harker; Robert S. Kaplan; Loretta J. Mester; and Randal K. Quarles. Ms. Daly voted as an alternate member at this meeting.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: November 3, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has taken actions against companies selling fraudulent COVID-19-related products. title: FDA, Homeland Security Agencies Take Additional Action to Prevent Import of Illegal and Harmful Medical Products Through International Mail Facilities
body_summary: Leadership from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Homeland Security Investigations, signed a Memorandum of Understanding to stop harmful products posing a threat to public health and entering the U.S. through International Mail Facilities. The MOU will maximize inspection and detection capabilities to prevent this activity. CBP and ICE-HSI will partner with the FDA in joint operations at IMFs to target illicit opioids, including fentanyl, medical devices, and dietary supplements regulated under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. The partnership aims to intercept fraudulent COVID-19 products and coordinate ongoing activities through information sharing, shared facilities, and future operations. FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn and CBP Acting Commissioner Mark A. Morgan emphasized the importance of the partnership in preventing illegal and potentially harmful products from entering the country.

title: FDA Publishes List of Essential Medicines, Medical Countermeasures, Critical Inputs Required by Executive Order
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued an executive order to identify essential medicines, medical countermeasures, and critical inputs that are medically necessary to be available at all times to protect against public health emergencies. The goal is to ensure the American public is protected against outbreaks of emerging infectious diseases and chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats. The FDA has developed a list of 223 drug and biological product essential medicines and medical countermeasures, including 96 device medical countermeasures. These essential medicines and medical countermeasures are primarily needed for patients in U.S. acute care medical facilities. The FDA is working with federal partners to acquire these products, accelerate domestic manufacturing, and address supply chain vulnerabilities.

title: FDA Approves Lotion for Nonprescription Use to Treat Head Lice
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Sklice, an ivermectin lotion, for over-the-counter use to treat head lice in patients 6 months of age and older. This is the result of a prescription-to-over-the-counter (Rx-to-OTC) switch process, which aims to promote public health by increasing consumer access to drugs that would otherwise be available only by prescription. The FDA granted approval to Arbor Pharmaceuticals LLC, and Sklice will be marketed as a nonprescription drug. The approval is based on data demonstrating the safety and effectiveness of the lotion when used as directed. Sklice is a single-use lotion with ivermectin 0.5% as the active ingredient, and its use is limited to external treatment of the scalp and dry hair.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for COVID-19
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has approved the antiviral drug Veklury (remdesivir) for the treatment of COVID-19 requiring hospitalization in adult and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older weighing at least 40 kilograms. Veklury can only be administered in a hospital or healthcare setting. The approval is the first for a COVID-19 treatment and does not include the entire population previously authorized to use Veklury under an Emergency Use Authorization. Clinical trials assessing the safety and efficacy of Veklury in pediatric patients are ongoing. 

The FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn said the agency is committed to expediting the development and availability of COVID-19 treatments. The approval was supported by data from three randomized, controlled clinical trials assessing the safety and efficacy of Veklury. The trials included 1,062 hospitalized subjects with mild, moderate, and severe COVID-19 who received Veklury or a placebo. 

Veklury has been shown to improve recovery from COVID-19 within 10 days compared to 15 days for the placebo group. The odds of clinical improvement at Day 15 were also statistically significantly higher in the Veklury group. 

Important information about using Veklury is available in the prescribing information, including dosing instructions, potential side effects, and drug interactions. Possible side effects include liver enzyme increases and allergic reactions.

title: FDA Reissues Emergency Use Authorization for Certain Non-NIOSH-Approved Filtering Face-Piece Respirators Manufactured in China
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) reissued the Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for certain filtering face-piece respirators (FFRs) manufactured in China. The reissued EUA no longer includes eligibility criteria, and the FDA will no longer review requests or add respirator models to the list of authorized respirators. The FDA recognizes a shortage of FFRs and will continue to authorize respirator models already included in the reissued EUA. The decision was made to address current U.S. demand for these products. A respirator shortage assessment was completed to understand product availability and assess the demand for respirators. The assessment showed that KN95 respirator models authorized by this EUA meet current demand. The assessment also highlighted limited adoption of KN95 design in healthcare settings and unused imported non-NIOSH-approved products. Suzanne Schwartz, M.D. M.B.A., Director of the FDA's Office of Strategic Partnerships and Technology Innovation, stated that reissuing the EUA was appropriate to support healthcare personnel's personal protective equipment needs.

title: FDA awards six grants to fund new clinical trials to advance the development of medical products for the treatment of rare diseases
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has awarded six new clinical trial research grants totaling over $16 million to support the development of medical products for patients with rare diseases. The grants, awarded through the Congressionally-funded Orphan Products Grants Program, will enhance the development of potentially life-changing treatments for patients with rare diseases over the next four years. The grants support clinical studies of products addressing unmet needs in rare diseases or providing significant improvements in treatment or diagnosis. The grant recipients include institutions such as Acucela, Inc., Fred Hutchinson Cancer Research Center, Seattle Children’s Hospital, and the University of Cincinnati. The grants were evaluated by over 90 rare disease and clinical trial experts and will provide additional resources to support rare disease research during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: FDA Reaffirms Commitment to Safety, Security of its Public Health Laboratories

The group will explore best practices in industry and leverage expertise from existing safety councils to strengthen existing safety measures. The FDA is committed to ensuring laboratory safety to protect personnel and research, and will continue to work collaboratively with the Office of Laboratory Safety to safeguard laboratory safety and security. The agency has over 2,500 researchers and analysts working to develop new approaches and standards for evaluating the safety and efficacy of regulated products.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A joint meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee and the Board of Governors was held on September 15-16, 2020. Chair Jerome Powell, Vice Chair John Williams, and Governor Richard Clarida opened the meeting with remarks in memory of Thomas Laubach, a world-class economist who passed away last week. US real GDP rebounded rapidly in Q3, with labor market conditions improving and employment below pre-pandemic levels. Consumer price inflation remained low, while total nonfarm payroll employment expanded strongly in July and August. The Committee decided to maintain the federal funds rate at 0-1/4% until labor market conditions reach maximum employment and inflation rises to 2%.

title: FDA Issues Final Guidance for Certain Labeling Recommendations for Breast Implants
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued the final guidance "Breast Implants - Certain Labeling Recommendations to Improve Patient Communication" to help improve information about breast implant risks. The draft guidance was issued in 2019. Director of the Office of Surgical and Infection Control Devices, Binita Ashar, stated that women need access to information to make informed decisions about breast implants. The FDA has received new information on risks, including breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma and breast implant illness, and has taken steps to address these risks. The agency convened the General and Plastic Surgery Devices Advisory Panel in 2019 to discuss breast implant safety. The Panel recommended requiring a boxed warning and a standardized checklist in breast implant labeling. The final guidance recommends manufacturers incorporate a boxed warning and a patient decision checklist into labeling, with updates to silicone gel-filled breast implant rupture screening recommendations and provision of patient device cards. The FDA will continue to work with stakeholders to disseminate risk information about breast implants.

title: FDA Approves First Drug to Treat Group of Rare Blood Disorders in Nearly 14 Years
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Nucala (mepolizumab) for adults and children aged 12 years and older with hypereosinophilic syndrome (HES) for six months or longer without another identifiable non-blood related cause of the disease. The new indication for Nucala is the first approval for HES patients in nearly 14 years. This approval marks the first time in over a decade that there is a new FDA-approved treatment option for patients with HES. Nucala was evaluated in a randomized, double-blind, multicenter, placebo-controlled trial in 108 patients with HES, showing a 50% relative reduction in HES flares compared to the placebo group. The most common side effects of Nucala in patients with HES include upper respiratory tract infection and pain in extremities. Nucala has been granted orphan drug designation and fast track designation for the treatment of HES, and is also approved for patients aged 6 years and older with severe asthma and for adult patients with eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.

title: Executive Order 13951—An America-First Healthcare Plan
body_summary: The US President has ordered to improve healthcare efficiency and quality, focusing on patient choice and control. In 2017, the administration expanded coverage options, increased health reimbursement arrangements, and issued rules to boost association health plans. To direct certain agencies, Executive Order 13877 was signed on June 24, 2019, requiring patients to access meaningful price and quality information prior to care delivery. The administration also took steps to lower healthcare costs, such as approving generic drugs, capping insulin prices, and reducing government payments to overcharging hospitals. In 2016-2017, the administration transformed healthcare in rural America by supporting small hospitals and clinics, and transitioning to value-based payment mechanisms. The US President issued another executive order on September 24, 2020, aiming to improve American healthcare by reducing dependence on foreign manufacturers, expanding access to affordable healthcare, and lowering costs, with a focus on giving Americans more choice, lower costs, and better care.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes First Point-of-Care Antibody Test for COVID-19
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued an emergency use authorization for the Assure COVID-19 IgG/IgM Rapid Test Device, a serology point-of-care test. The test, which was first authorized in July 2020, is now authorized for use with fingerstick blood samples. This allows for more convenient testing in doctor’s offices, hospitals, urgent care centers, and emergency rooms. The test will help conserve resources and reduce processing time for other COVID-19 tests. The FDA has granted nearly 50 serology tests an emergency use authorization since the start of the pandemic. The test uses a lateral flow assay with venous whole blood, serum, plasma, and fingerstick whole blood. Patients should not interpret results as telling them they are immune, as the presence of antibodies is unknown and may not confer protective immunity. The FDA cautions against using serology test results to stop taking steps to protect themselves and others.

title: FDA Issues Recommendations for Certain High-Risk Groups Regarding Mercury-Containing Dental Amalgam
body_summary: The FDA is issuing updated recommendations regarding dental amalgam and potential risks to certain high-risk individuals associated with mercury-containing fillings. The agency has found that pregnant women, women planning to become pregnant, nursing women, and children under six years of age may be at greater risk for potential harmful health effects from mercury vapor released from the device. The FDA is recommending that these groups use non-mercuryalternatives to dental amalgam, such as composite resins and glass ionomer cement fillings. The agency is not recommending removal or replacement of existing amalgam fillings in good condition unless medically necessary. The FDA has been reviewing scientific literature and public comments for over 20 years, but uncertainties remain about the effects of long-term exposure to dental amalgam on high-risk groups and potential health outcomes.

title: FDA Takes Actions to Help Lower U.S. Prescription Drug Prices
body_summary: The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration have taken actions to allow states to import certain prescription drugs from Canada as part of the Safe Importation Action Plan. The final rule implements a provision of federal law that enables FDA-authorized programs to import prescription drugs from Canada under specific conditions. The rule allows states, Indian tribes, and pharmacists to submit importation program proposals to the FDA for review and authorization. The programs must demonstrate significant cost reductions and ensure the drugs meet established specifications and standards. The final guidance describes procedures for drug manufacturers to obtain a National Drug Code for FDA-approved prescription drugs. Prescription drugs imported under the pathway can be available to patients in various settings, including hospitals, pharmacies, and healthcare providers' offices, with FDA-approved labeling.

title: The President's News Conference
body_summary: The President announced that Johnson and Johnson's vaccine candidate has reached the final stage of clinical trials, a record time, as part of Operation Warp Speed. The administration awarded $200 million in CARES Act funding to states to prepare for vaccine distribution. The President reported a 99.98% survival rate for individuals under 50 and a significant decrease in hospitalizations and emergency room visits. Additionally, the administration reported a 10.6 million job creation, a nearly 50% increase in flu vaccine enrollment, and a rise in retail sales and manufacturing. The President discussed the Supreme Court nomination process, stating his nominee is "highly qualified" and will be announced on Saturday. The President expressed urgency in vaccine development, stating that delays could result in more lives lost and emphasized the pandemic's urgency over politics.

title: FDA Requiring Labeling Changes for Benzodiazepines
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration requires an update to the Boxed Warning for benzodiazepines and class-wide labeling changes to include the risks of abuse, misuse, addiction, physical dependence, and withdrawal reactions. In 2019, an estimated 92 million benzodiazepine prescriptions were dispensed, with alprazolam being the most common. The FDA aims to promote public health by minimizing risks associated with controlled substances while enabling appropriate medical use. The agency is requiring revisions to patient Medication Guides and other labeling changes to educate patients and caregivers about the risks.

title: FDA Achieves Key Milestone, Finalizes Framework That Will Resume Shellfish Trade with Europe for the First Time in 10 Years
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has finalized an equivalence determination for two European Union (EU) Member States, Spain and the Netherlands, allowing for the resumption of trade in molluscan shellfish between the US and EU for the first time since 2010. The FDA Deputy Commissioner for Policy, Legislation and International Affairs, Anna Abram, stated that this action reflects key strategic international engagement and will unlock economic opportunity for US exporters. The determination is a result of a multi-year review of EU shellfish safety controls implemented in Spain and the Netherlands. The FDA Deputy Commissioner for Food Policy and Response, Frank Yiannas, noted that this will make a wider selection of healthy and safe seafood options available to American consumers. The FDA will recognize other EU Member States in the future, as appropriate, in separate determinations.

title: FDA Launches the Digital Health Center of Excellence
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is launching the Digital Health Center of Excellence within the Center for Devices and Radiological Health. The launch aims to further the agency's dedication to advancing digital health technology, including mobile health devices, Software as a Medical Device, and technologies used to study medical products. FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn announced the move, stating it will enable the agency to rapidly develop and review cutting-edge digital health technologies. The Digital Health Center of Excellence will provide centralized expertise and serve as a resource for digital health innovators, the public, and FDA staff. Bakul Patel has been appointed as the first director, and the agency plans to build a coordinating structure and operation to modernize digital health policies and regulatory approaches.

title: FDA Clarifies Types of Evidence Relevant to Determining the “Intended Use” of FDA-Regulated Products
body_summary: The FDA proposed updates to its regulations to clarify the types of evidence considered when determining a product's intended use, which determines whether it falls within the agency's jurisdiction. The proposed rule, "Amendments to Regulations Regarding 'Intended Uses,' aims to provide better clarity to regulated industry and stakeholders. The FDA's longstanding approach is that any relevant source of evidence may be considered when evaluating a product's intended use. However, the proposed revisions clarify that a firm's knowledge of a healthcare provider's prescription or use of an approved product for an unapproved use is not sufficient to establish the product's intended use. The update is expected to provide greater certainty and predictability for regulated parties, with examples of relevant and irrelevant evidence outlined in the preamble. The FDA has previously revised language in its intended use regulations and has considered public comments, including those received on its 2017 final rule, which will be repealed and replaced by this proposed rule.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The Federal Reserve is committed to using its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals. The COVID-19 pandemic is causing tremendous human and economic hardship across the United States and around the world. Economic activity and employment have picked up in recent months but remain well below their levels at the beginning of the year. Weaker demand and significantly lower oil prices are holding down consumer price inflation. Overall financial conditions have improved in recent months, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses. The path of the economy will depend significantly on the course of the virus. The ongoing public health crisis will continue to weigh on economic activity, employment, and inflation in the near term, and poses considerable risks to the economic outlook over the medium term. The Committee seeks to achieve maximum employment and inflation at the rate of 2 percent over the longer run. With inflation running persistently below this longer-run goal, the Committee will aim to achieve inflation moderately above 2 percent for some time so that inflation averages 2 percent over time and longer-term inflation expectations remain well anchored at 2 percent. The Committee expects to maintain an accommodative stance of monetary policy until these outcomes are achieved. The Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and expects it will be appropriate to maintain this target range until labor market conditions have reached levels consistent with the Committee's assessments of maximum employment and inflation has risen to 2 percent and is on track to moderately exceed 2 percent for some time. In addition, over coming months the Federal Reserve will increase its holdings of Treasury securities and agency mortgage-backed securities at least at the current pace to sustain smooth market functioning and help foster accommodative financial conditions, thereby supporting the flow of credit to households and businesses. In assessing the appropriate stance of monetary policy, the Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook. The Committee would be prepared to adjust the stance of monetary policy as appropriate if risks emerge that could impede the attainment of the Committee's goals. The Committee's assessments will take into account a wide range of information, including readings on public health, labor market conditions, inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Patrick Harker; Loretta J. Mester; and Randal K. Quarles. Voting against the action were Robert S. Kaplan, who expects that it will be appropriate to maintain the current target range until the Committee is confident that the economy has weathered recent events and is on track to achieve its maximum employment and price stability goals as articulated in its new policy strategy statement, but prefers that the Committee retain greater policy rate flexibility beyond that point; and Neel Kashkari, who prefers that the Committee indicate that it expects to maintain the current target range until core inflation has reached 2 percent on a sustained basis.

title: FDA issues first injunction under Produce Safety Rule to Illinois-based food manufacturer for repeated food safety violations
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced that Fortune Food Product, Inc., an Illinois-based processor of sprouts and soy products, has agreed to stop production until it complies with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.
