title: Executive Order 13948—Lowering Drug Prices by Putting America First
body_summary:
The President orders the following:

Section 1 states that Americans pay more for prescription drugs than residents of any other developed country, and it is unacceptable that they subsidize innovation and lower-cost drugs for the rest of the world. The Council of Economic Advisers has found that Americans finance much of the biopharmaceutical innovation that the world depends on.

The President orders the following policies:

Section 2 states that the Medicare program should not pay more for costly prescription drugs or biological products than the most-favored-nation price. The "most-favored-nation price" is the lowest price, after adjusting for volume and differences in national gross domestic product, for a pharmaceutical product sold in a member country of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).

Section 3 requires the Secretary of Health and Human Services to implement a rulemaking plan to test a payment model in which Medicare would pay no more than the most-favored-nation price for certain high-cost prescription drugs and biological products covered by Medicare Part B.

Section 4 requires the Secretary to develop and implement a rulemaking plan to test a payment model in which Medicare would pay no more than the most-favored-nation price for Part D prescription drugs or biological products where insufficient competition exists.

Section 5 revokes the Executive Order of July 24, 2020, "Lowering Drug Prices by Putting America First."

Section 6 states that nothing in the order shall be construed to impair or affect the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget.

Hahn has expressed concern about hand sanitizers being packaged to appear consumable products, which could confuse consumers into accidentally ingesting a potentially deadly product.

Drinking hand sanitizer can be lethal to young children, and the agency is seeing an increasing number of adverse events, including cardiac effects, central nervous system effects, hospitalizations, and death.

The FDA encourages consumers to report adverse events or quality problems with hand sanitizers and is urging retailers to remove potentially dangerous products from store shelves and online marketplaces. title: FDA Updates Analysis of Medical Device Reports of Breast Implant Illness and Breast Implant-Associated Lymphoma

The US Food and Drug Administration is providing an update on adverse events reported related to breast implants, including breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL) and systemic signs and symptoms referred to as breast implant illness (BII). The FDA has analyzed global medical device reports for BIA-ALCL, covering reports received through January 5, 2020, and found 733 unique cases and 36 patient deaths globally. 

The FDA has also qualified the BREAST-Q Reconstruction Module as a medical device development tool (MDDT) to aid in the assessment of certain medical devices like breast implants. This tool was used to assess quality of life and satisfaction with breast reconstruction surgery.

The FDA remains committed to thoughtful, scientific, and transparent public dialogue concerning breast implant safety and effectiveness, and will continue to analyze all available information regarding risks associated with breast implants.

title: FDA Approves Treatment for Rare Disease Affecting Optic Nerves, Spinal Cord
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Enspryng (satralizumab-mwge) for the treatment of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) in adults with anti-aquaporin-4 (AQP4) antibody-positive patients. NMOSD is a rare autoimmune disease affecting the optic nerves and spinal cord, with approximately 4,000 to 8,000 Americans impacted. Enspryng reduced NMOSD relapses by 74% in patients who were anti-AQP4 positive in a 96-week clinical study. The drug was approved with warnings for increased risk of infection, elevated liver enzymes, and other side effects. Vaccination with live-attenuated or live vaccines is not recommended during treatment. The FDA granted approval to Genentech Inc., with Enspryng being the third approved treatment for NMOSD.

Yale intends to provide the SalivaDirect protocol as an "open source" protocol, allowing designated laboratories to perform the test in their labs using commercially available components. This is the fifth test authorized by the FDA that uses saliva as a sample for testing, eliminating the need for nasopharyngeal swabs and potentially lowering the risk to healthcare workers.

title: FDA Approves New Opioid for Intravenous Use in Hospitals, Other Controlled Clinical Settings
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Olinvyk, an opioid agonist, for the management of moderate to severe acute pain in adults, specifically for short-term intravenous use in hospitals or controlled clinical settings. Olinvyk is indicated for patients whose pain is severe enough to require an intravenous opioid and for whom alternative treatments are inadequate. The medication is not indicated for at-home use. The FDA approved Olinvyk after rigorous review of its risks and benefits, with 1,535 patients treated in controlled and open-label trials. The safety and efficacy of Olinvyk were established in randomized, controlled studies, with patients administered Olinvyk reporting decreased pain compared to placebo. The most common side effects are nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, and constipation. Olinvyk carries a boxed warning about addiction, abuse, and misuse, as well as life-threatening respiratory depression and neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome. The FDA granted approval to Trevena Inc. and set a maximum recommended daily dose limit of 27 milligrams.

title: FDA Approves Oral Treatment for Spinal Muscular Atrophy
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Evrysdi (risdiplam) to treat patients two months of age and older with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), a rare genetic disease. Evrysdi is the first oral drug approved to treat SMA. The efficacy of Evrysdi was evaluated in two clinical studies, including one with 21 patients with infantile-onset SMA, where 41% could sit independently after 12 months of treatment, and 81% were alive without permanent ventilation after 23 months. A second study with 180 patients with later-onset SMA showed a significant increase in motor function score at the one-year mark. Common side effects include fever, diarrhea, and joint pain. The FDA granted fast track designation, priority review, orphan drug designation, and a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher to Genentech, Inc.

title: FDA Approves First Liquid Biopsy Next-Generation Sequencing Companion Diagnostic Test
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved the first liquid biopsy companion diagnostic that uses next-generation sequencing technology to identify patients with specific EGFR gene mutations in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The Guardant360 CDx assay combines liquid biopsy and NGS to guide treatment decisions. The approval was granted to Guardant Health and marks a new era for mutation testing. The test uses two technologies: liquid biopsy and NGS. Liquid biopsy provides genetic information about the tumor from a blood sample, while NGS allows for simultaneous detection of mutations in 55 tumor genes. The approval is specific to identifying EGFR mutations in patients who will benefit from treatment with TAGRISSO.

title: Executive Order 13941—Improving Rural Health and Telehealth Access
body_summary:
By the authority vested in me as President, it is hereby ordered that the Administration is committed to improving the health of all Americans, including those in rural communities. The Administration recognizes that rural Americans face unique challenges, such as limited transportation opportunities and shortages of healthcare workers, which contribute to financial insecurity and impaired health outcomes. Since 2010, 129 rural hospitals have closed, and the average occupancy rate of a hospital that closed was only 22 percent.

To help patients better access healthcare providers, my Administration implemented new flexibility regarding telehealth services, and internal analysis shows a dramatic increase in virtual visits for CMS beneficiaries. The report also finds that telehealth visits continued to be frequent even after in-person primary care visits resumed.

Within 30 days, the Secretary of HHS will announce a new model to test innovative payment mechanisms, and within 30 days, the Secretary and the Secretary of Agriculture will develop and implement a strategy to improve rural health infrastructure. Additionally, the Secretary will submit a report to the President within 30 days regarding existing and upcoming policy initiatives to increase rural access to healthcare and improve health outcomes.

The order also proposes to extend temporary telehealth services and services offered to Medicare providers in rural areas beyond the duration of the PHE.

title: La FDA les recomienda a los consumidores que eviten las cebollas rojas de un proveedor en California; la investigación continúa para encontrar la fuente
body_summary: The FDA, along with CDC and state and local partners, is conducting a rapid investigation into a Salmonella Newport outbreak, likely linked to red onions. Canadian health officials investigated a similar outbreak and determined that US red onions are the probable source. The FDA's investigation of the outbreak's traceback identified Thomson International, Inc. of Bakersfield, CA, as a probable source of contaminated red onions. Consumers, restaurants, and retailers are advised not to consume, sell, or serve red, white, yellow, or sweet onions from Thomson International, Inc. The FDA will provide updates as the investigation unfolds, particularly if there are critical updates to public health.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes First Tests that Estimate a Patient’s Antibodies from Past SARS-CoV-2 Infection
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized two COVID-19 serology tests, the ADVIA Centaur COV2G and Atellica IM COV2G from Siemens, which estimate the quantity of antibodies present in an individual's blood. These tests are considered "semi-quantitative" and do not provide a precise measurement. The FDA's director, Tim Stenzel, believes these tests can help evaluate antibodies in response to SARS-CoV-2 infection, but patients should not interpret results as indicative of immunity. The FDA cautions against using these tests to stop taking precautions to protect themselves and others, and reminds patients that serology tests do not diagnose active infections.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 31, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued a warning letter to Vapore, LLC, dba Mypurmist, for selling fraudulent COVID-19 related products with misleading claims. The FDA requested that the company immediately cease selling the unapproved and unauthorized product. The FDA has authorized 194 tests under EUAs, including 159 molecular tests, 33 antibody tests, and 2 antigen tests. The FDA is responsible for protecting the public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of various products, including drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: The President's News Conference
body_summary:
US President expressed sadness over the passing of Herman Cain, a dear friend and a wonderful person. He mourned the loss of 150,000 Americans who died from the China virus, and the resurgence of cases in countries such as Japan, China, and Australia. The President emphasized the need for vaccination and treatment. He announced strong measures to protect vulnerable populations.

The administration has taken aggressive action to rescue American workers, including a $3 trillion economic relief package, saving over 50 million jobs through the Paycheck Protection Program. The administration aims to add 7 million more jobs in the next 2 months. The administration is asking Congress to pass legislation to extend unemployment benefits, stop evictions, and provide additional economic relief payments.

The President is frustrated with the process of mail-in ballots, citing concerns about voter fraud and lack of transparency. He wants an election with clear results. The President also discusses the COVID-19 pandemic, referencing a Wall Street Journal editorial that highlights countries where the virus has surged despite being hailed as models.

The President also mentioned the city of Portland, Oregon, stating that it is a mess, and Homeland Security has done a great job. The Governor and Mayor are not doing it right, and the President will deploy the National Guard if necessary. The administration is working on a strategy to develop a powerful coronavirus vaccine, which is almost ready and will be delivered quickly.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 29, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) updated the Molecular Diagnostic templates on July 28, addressing diagnostic tests for COVID-19 and other respiratory pathogens. The FDA has authorized 193 tests under Emergency Use Authorizations (EUAs), including 158 molecular tests, 33 antibody tests, and 2 antigen tests. The agency is responsible for ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices, as well as regulating food, cosmetics, dietary supplements, and tobacco products.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Posts New Template for At-Home and Over-the-Counter Diagnostic Tests for Use in Non-Lab Settings, Such as Homes, Offices or Schools
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has posted a new template for commercial developers to help them develop and submit emergency use authorization requests for COVID-19 diagnostic tests that can be performed at home or in non-lab settings. The template provides recommendations for validation, sensitivity, and specificity of these tests, which are intended to be made available over-the-counter without a prescription. FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn stated that the goal is to facilitate innovation and enhance Americans' access to COVID-19 tests. The FDA aims to make these tests available in pharmacies, allowing individuals to collect samples, run tests, and receive results quickly at home. The recommended sensitivity is lower than lab-based tests, but the benefits of broader access outweigh the risk.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The Federal Reserve is committed to using its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals. The coronavirus outbreak is causing tremendous human and economic hardship across the United States and around the world. Following sharp declines, economic activity and employment have picked up somewhat in recent months but remain well below their levels at the beginning of the year. Weaker demand and significantly lower oil prices are holding down consumer price inflation. Overall financial conditions have improved in recent months, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses. The path of the economy will depend significantly on the course of the virus. The ongoing public health crisis will weigh heavily on economic activity, employment, and inflation in the near term, and poses considerable risks to the economic outlook over the medium term. In light of these developments, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent. The Committee expects to maintain this target range until it is confident that the economy has weathered recent events and is on track to achieve its maximum employment and price stability goals. The Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook, including information related to public health, as well as global developments and muted inflation pressures, and will use its tools and act as appropriate to support the economy. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the stance of monetary policy, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. To support the flow of credit to households and businesses, over coming months the Federal Reserve will increase its holdings of Treasury securities and agency residential and commercial mortgage-backed securities at least at the current pace to sustain smooth market functioning, thereby fostering effective transmission of monetary policy to broader financial conditions. In addition, the Open Market Desk will continue to offer large-scale overnight and term repurchase agreement operations. The Committee will closely monitor developments and is prepared to adjust its plans as appropriate. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Patrick Harker; Robert S. Kaplan; Neel Kashkari; Loretta J. Mester; and Randal K. Quarles.

title: FDA Warns Companies Illegally Selling Hangover Remedies
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued warning letters to seven companies for illegally selling unapproved dietary supplements that claim to cure, treat, or prevent hangovers. The companies include Double Wood LLC, Ebnsol Inc., Vita Heaven LLC, Happy Hour Vitamins, LES Labs, Mind, Body & Coal LLC, and Purple Biosciences LLC. Director Steven Tave stated that these products could harm consumers, especially young adults, and that they should not be used as a substitute for responsible alcohol consumption. The FDA advises consumers to consult with their doctor or pharmacist before purchasing or using any dietary supplement or drug. The companies have 15 working days to respond with a plan to correct the violations, or they may face legal action, including product seizure and/or injunction.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 28, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. Today, the agency posted audio and transcript versions of its podcast series FDA Insight, featuring Dr. Peter Marks, Director of the FDA Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, in a discussion on COVID-19 vaccines. The FDA has issued emergency use authorizations (EUAs) for two molecular diagnostic tests, the Lilly SARS-CoV-2 Assay and the SNL-NM 2019 nCoV Real-Time RT-PCR Diagnostic Assay, for Eli Lilly and Company and Sandia National Laboratories, respectively. The FDA has authorized a total of 193 tests under EUAs, including 158 molecular tests, 33 antibody tests, and 2 antigen tests.

title: The President's News Conference
body_summary: The President has announced a historic agreement with Kodak to begin producing critical pharmaceutical ingredients in the US, aiming to create 360 new jobs and produce 25% of all active ingredients needed for generic drugs. The administration has invested $3 billion in the nation's industrial base and provided a $765 million loan through the Defense Production Act to support the launch of Kodak Pharmaceuticals. The US is ramping up domestic production of rapid point-of-care tests, aiming to produce 8 million test kits per month, and over 100 million swabs per month by January. The President is set to announce a new relief measure, exploring immigration reform, including a path to citizenship for DACA recipients, and negotiating lower drug prices with pharmaceutical representatives.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Reiterates Warning About Dangerous Alcohol-Based Hand Sanitizers Containing Methanol, Takes Additional Action to Address Concerning Products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) warns consumers and healthcare professionals not to use certain alcohol-based hand sanitizers due to the presence of methanol, a toxic substance. The agency has placed products containing methanol on an import alert and is working with manufacturers to recall affected products. Eskbiochem S.A. de C.V. has issued a warning letter to its distributors regarding the distribution of products with undeclared methanol and misleading claims. The FDA first warned about methanol-containing hand sanitizers in June and issued a further warning in recent days about increasing adverse events, including blindness, cardiac effects, and hospitalizations. Consumers must stop using hand sanitizers on the FDA's list of dangerous products and immediately report any adverse events to the agency's MedWatch program. The FDA urges consumers, healthcare professionals, and manufacturers to take action to prevent further harm.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 27, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic on July 24. The FDA reissued the LabCorp COVID-19 RT-PCR Test EUA to expand its use to anyone after scientific data showed its ability to detect SARS-CoV-2 in a general, asymptomatic population. The FDA also authorized pooled sample testing, allowing for fewer tests to be conducted overall. The agency continues to warn consumers and healthcare professionals about certain alcohol-based hand sanitizers due to the presence of methanol. An import alert has been placed on products containing methanol, and a warning letter has been issued to Eskbiochem S.A. de C.V. regarding the distribution of products with undeclared methanol. The FDA approved an abbreviated new drug application for heparin sodium on July 24. Additionally, emergency use authorizations were issued to two companies for serology-based tests for the detection and differentiation of IgG and IgM antibodies to SARS-CoV-2. As of July 24, the FDA has authorized 191 tests under EUAs, including 156 molecular tests, 33 antibody tests, and 2 antigen tests.

title: The President's News Conference on COVID-19 Vaccine Development at the Fujifilm Diosynth Biotechnologies Bioprocess Innovation Center in Morrisville, North Carolina
body_summary: The President announced progress in Operation Warp Speed, a record-breaking vaccine development initiative. The Moderna vaccine has entered phase three clinical trials, with a second vaccine expected to begin phase three trials soon. The initiative has accelerated therapeutics development, with over 140 clinical trials underway. The US has distributed nearly 100 million N95 masks and is building thousands of ventilators monthly. The country has a sufficient stockpile of personal protective equipment and is sending aid to 15,000 nursing homes in need. The administration aims to develop a vaccine with a goal of announcing progress within the next 2 weeks. President Trump believes the US will defeat the virus, citing the administration's efforts, which have led to record job numbers and a predicted "V" recovery.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes First Diagnostic Test for Screening of People Without Known or Suspected COVID-19 Infection
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) reissued the LabCorp COVID-19 RT-PCR Test emergency use authorization (EUA) to include testing for asymptomatic individuals and pooled sample testing. The authorization allows for the test to be used on anyone, regardless of symptoms, and for pooled samples containing up to five individual swab specimens. The FDA Commissioner, Stephen M. Hahn, stated that this authorization is a step towards broad screening that may help enable the reopening of schools and workplaces. The test is available for prescription-only use, either at home or by a healthcare provider, and the data demonstrated its accuracy in asymptomatic populations. The reissuance eliminates the need for healthcare providers to consider risk factors when prescribing the test.

title: Executive Order 13947—Lowering Drug Prices by Putting America First
body_summary:
The President of the United States orders that Americans should not bear extra burdens to compensate for the shortfalls that result from the nationalized public healthcare systems of wealthy countries abroad. The Council of Economic Advisers has found that Americans finance much of the biopharmaceutical innovation that the world depends on. The Federal Government is the largest payer for prescription drugs in the world, but it pays more than many smaller buyers, including other developed nations.

The President orders that the Medicare program should not pay more for costly Part B prescription drugs or biological products than the most-favored-nation price. The most-favored-nation price is the lowest price, after adjusting for volume and differences in national gross domestic product, for a pharmaceutical product that the drug manufacturer sells in a member country of the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development that has a comparable per-capita gross domestic product.

The Secretary of Health and Human Services shall immediately take appropriate steps to implement a rulemaking plan to test a payment model pursuant to which Medicare would pay, for certain high-cost prescription drugs and biological products covered by Medicare Part B, no more than the most-favored-nation price.

This order is not intended to create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States.

title: FDA Approves First Cell-Based Gene Therapy For Adult Patients with Relapsed or Refractory MCL
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Tecartus, a cell-based gene therapy, for the treatment of adult patients with mantle cell lymphoma who have not responded to or relapsed following other treatments. Tecartus, a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy, is the first cell-based gene therapy approved by the FDA for this condition. The therapy was approved under the Accelerated Approval pathway and received Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy designations. The safety and efficacy of Tecartus was established in a multicenter clinical trial of 60 adults, with a complete remission rate of 62% and an objective response rate of 87%. Tecartus carries a boxed warning for cytokine release syndrome and neurologic toxicities, which can be fatal or life-threatening. The FDA requires a post-marketing observational study to further evaluate the long-term safety of Tecartus.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 24, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA has issued an updated summary of its response efforts, providing a quick look at facts and highlights. The agency has authorized 188 tests under Emergency Use Authorization (EUA), including 155 molecular tests, 31 antibody tests, and 2 antigen tests. The FDA is part of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and is responsible for ensuring the safety and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, medical devices, and the nation's food supply.

title: Executive Order 13939—Lowering Prices for Patients by Eliminating Kickbacks to Middlemen
body_summary:
President Donald J. Trump orders the following:

The high prices of pharmaceutical drugs in the United States are partly due to the complex mix of payers and negotiators that separate consumers from manufacturers. To fix this, the President directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to complete rulemaking to exclude certain discounts from safe harbor protections under the anti-kickback statute and establish new safe harbors for discounts that can be applied at the patient's point-of-sale. The rulemaking must confirm that the action will not increase Federal spending, Medicare beneficiary premiums, or patients' total out-of-pocket costs.

title: Executive Order 13937—Access to Affordable Life-Saving Medications
body_summary: President Donald J. Trump has ordered that Americans without access to affordable insulin and injectable epinephrine through commercial insurance or Federal programs such as Medicare and Medicaid can purchase these pharmaceuticals from a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) at a price that aligns with the cost at which the FQHC acquired the medication. The Secretary of Health and Human Services is required to take action to ensure future grants are conditioned upon FQHCs' established practices to make insulin and injectable epinephrine available at the discounted price paid by the FQHC grantee or sub-grantee. The order aims to address the steep increases in list prices for these medications in recent years, which can lead to "penny pricing" at FQHCs, resulting in high prices for low-income Americans at the point of sale.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 23, 2020
body_summary: The US FDA announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA updated its Testing Supply Substitution Strategy slide show, providing validated supply alternatives for labs to continue testing when there is a supply issue. The FDA and Federal Trade Commission jointly issued a warning letter to 21st Century LaserMed Pain & Regenerative Medicine Institute for offering unapproved products for COVID-19 prevention, treatment, or diagnosis. The FDA has authorized 187 tests under EUAs, including 154 molecular tests, 31 antibody tests, and 2 antigen tests. The FDA is responsible for protecting public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: The President's News Conference
body_summary: The US President announces a historic agreement with Pfizer to produce and deliver 100 million vaccine doses, as part of Operation Warp Speed, with an additional 500 million doses to follow. The President also takes steps to combat the coronavirus pandemic, including increased testing, rapid diagnostic devices, and $5 billion in funding. The President prioritizes shielding high-risk Americans while allowing younger citizens to return to work or school, and advocates for mask-wearing, social distancing, and hand-washing. The President also discusses economic recovery, addressing short-term unemployment insurance and deploying Federal law enforcement officers to cities with high crime rates. The President responds to criticisms from Democrats, including former President Barack Obama and Joe Biden, by highlighting the administration's achievements on criminal justice reform and employment numbers.

title: The President's News Conference
body_summary: The US President updates the nation on the response to the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on controlling the outbreak in the Sun Belt, advancing an economic relief package, and developing a vaccine. The administration has made significant progress, with a 75% decline in fatalities nationwide since mid-April. The President highlights the importance of protecting vulnerable populations and notes that young adults may be asymptomatic or experience mild symptoms. The US has conducted over 50 million COVID-19 tests, second only to India, and plans to expand testing capabilities. The administration aims to manage the pandemic and ultimately end it, with vaccine development nearing completion and the military ready to distribute vaccines.

title: FDA Extends Enforcement Discretion Policy for Certain Regenerative Medicine Products
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is extending its enforcement discretion policy for certain human cell, tissue, and cellular and tissue-based products (HCT/Ps). As a result, manufacturers and potential sponsors have an additional six months to determine if they need to submit an Investigational New Drug (IND) or marketing application. The FDA's November 2017 regenerative medicine policy framework was developed to facilitate innovation. The agency has outlined its intent to exercise enforcement discretion until May 2021, but notes that this policy only applies to products without significant safety concerns. Director Peter Marks stated that the policy does not provide a cover for bad actors and that the agency will take action against manufacturers and health care providers offering unapproved regenerative medicine products. The FDA has stepped up its oversight of cellular and related products and has issued compliance actions and pursued litigation for serious violations.

title: FDA Notifies Companies, Including Puff Bar, to Remove Flavored Disposable E-Cigarettes and Youth-Appealing E-Liquids from Market for Not Having Required Authorization
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued warning letters to 17 companies, including Cool Clouds Distribution Inc. (doing business as Puff Bar), to remove flavored disposable e-cigarettes and youth-appealing e-liquid products from the market. The FDA is concerned about the appeal of these products to youth and is taking action to enforce compliance with premarket authorization requirements. The warning letters were issued due to ongoing internet monitoring for violations of tobacco laws and regulations, and the companies are required to respond within 15 working days detailing their plans for addressing the agency's concerns. The FDA has also issued other warning letters and actions, including refusing admission of at least 74 entries of disposable e-cigarettes products and issuing letters to seven tobacco product manufacturers requesting information on their compliance with premarket requirements.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 20, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced several actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA reissued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for Quest Diagnostics' SARS-CoV-2 rRT-PCR test, allowing it to be used with pooled samples containing up to four individual upper-respiratory swab specimens. The FDA also extended its enforcement discretion policy for human cell, tissue, and cellular and tissue-based products (HCT/Ps) for an additional six months, through May 2021. The agency issued guidance to expand the availability of transport media for clinical specimens and posted answers to frequently asked questions about transport media. To date, the FDA has authorized 186 tests under EUAs, including 153 molecular tests, 31 antibody tests, and 2 antigen tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Issues First Emergency Authorization for Sample Pooling in Diagnostic Testing
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration reissued an emergency use authorization for Quest Diagnostics' SARS-CoV-2 rRT-PCR test to allow for the use of pooled samples containing up to four individual swab specimens collected under observation. The test, initially authorized on March 17, 2020, remains authorized to test individual samples and self-collected nasal swab specimens. The FDA Commissioner, Stephen M. Hahn, stated that this EUA is an important step forward in getting more COVID-19 tests to more Americans quickly while preserving testing supplies. The testing strategy is most efficient in areas with low prevalence.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 17, 2020

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 16, 2020

The agency is providing support through a directory for industry and laboratory questions about COVID-19 and medical devices. To date, the FDA has authorized 182 tests under EUAs, including 151 molecular tests, 29 antibody tests, and 2 antigen tests. The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 15, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has updated its Frequently Asked Questions on Testing for SARS-CoV-2. The revised FAQs include a list of laboratories removed from the list of laboratories that had developed and validated diagnostic tests. The FDA has determined that there are significant problems with these tests that cannot be addressed in a timely manner and should no longer be used. The agency is responsible for protecting public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 14, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA has posted an updated Coronavirus Treatment Acceleration Program (CTAP) webpage, providing information on CTAP's purpose, strategy, and operations, including a dashboard showing crucial statistics related to COVID-19 therapeutics. The agency has also released a new FDA Voices article discussing efforts to leverage cross-agency scientific resources and expertise on COVID-19 therapeutic development and review. As of today, there are over 510 drug development programs in planning stages for potential therapies for COVID-19, and the agency has reviewed more than 230 trials of potential therapies. The FDA has issued warning letters to two firms, Health Beauty Love and Kegan Wellness, for selling unapproved products with false or misleading claims. The agency has also added dexamethasone sodium phosphate to the list of drugs for temporary compounding by outsourcing facilities and pharmacy compounders during the COVID-19 public health emergency.

title: FDA Launches New Era of Smarter Food Safety Initiative, Releases Blueprint and Pilot Study
body_summary: The FDA's New Era of Smarter Food Safety Blueprint outlines a path to ensure the safety of the American public, building on the Food Safety Modernization Act. The blueprint incorporates new technologies to create a digital, transparent, and safer food system, aiming to promote integrity, advance innovation, and foster a growth in food safety culture. The FDA is exploring new approaches to food safety, including engaging the retail food industry and state governments to change practices, educating consumers, and implementing new strategies to address foodborne disease. The blueprint was developed with input from hundreds of people and seeks to be implemented over the next decade.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 13, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. FDA scientists have identified areas of the COVID-19 virus that trigger strong protective antibody responses in rabbits. The virus uses two parts of the spike protein to attach to cells and fuse with the cell membrane. The FDA has released a blueprint for implementing the New Era of Smarter Food Safety, which aims to create a more digital and safer food system. The blueprint includes tech-enabled traceability, smarter tools for preventing and responding to food-borne illness outbreaks, and modernized product recalls. The FDA has issued emergency use authorizations (EUA) for two devices: the GammaCore Sapphire Non-invasive Vagus Nerve Stimulator and the SleepWeaver Prevent CPAP Mask. To date, the FDA has authorized 175 tests under EUAs. The FDA protects the public health by ensuring the safety and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices, as well as regulating the nation's food supply, cosmetics, and tobacco products.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA prepares for resumption of domestic inspections with new risk assessment system
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is resuming prioritized domestic inspections of FDA-regulated facilities, with plans to restart on-site inspections during the week of July 20. The decision is based on the COVID-19 Advisory Rating system, which uses real-time data to assess the number of COVID-19 cases in a local area. The FDA will consider three metrics: Phase of the State, statistics measured at the county level, and the virus' trajectory. Prioritized domestic inspections will depend on downward trends in new cases and hospitalizations, as well as the availability of public transportation. The FDA will pre-announce inspections to ensure the safety of investigators and firms' employees, except for undercover retail tobacco inspections. The agency is committed to the health, safety, and well-being of its investigators and the public.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 10, 2020
body_summary:
The US FDA has announced actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The agency is preparing to resume domestic inspections, guided by a new risk-assessment system, with the first inspections scheduled for July 20. The FDA developed a COVID-19 Advisory Rating system to assess the safety of inspections based on real-time data from state and national sources. This system will be made available to state partners who conduct inspections on the agency's behalf.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 8, 2020

The agency issued a warning letter to Ionogen, LLC, for selling fraudulent COVID-19-related products, and federal prosecutors charged four Florida residents for marketing a toxic bleach as a cure for COVID-19. Additionally, the FDA has added several hand sanitizer products to its list of products with confirmed and potential methanol contamination. The agency has authorized 169 tests under EUAs, including 141 molecular tests, 26 antibody tests, and 2 antigen tests.

title: FDA Approves New Therapy for Myelodysplastic Syndromes (MDS) That Can Be Taken at Home
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Inqovi tablets for treatment of adult patients with myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML). The approval represents an advance in treatment options for patients with MDS, who previously required intravenous therapy. Inqovi is taken once daily for five consecutive days of each 28-day cycle. The approval was based on clinical trial results showing similar drug concentrations between intravenous decitabine and Inqovi, with about half of patients no longer requiring transfusions. The safety profile of Inqovi was similar to intravenous decitabine, with common side effects including fatigue, constipation, and fever. The FDA granted Priority Review, and the approval was made to Astex Pharmaceuticals, Inc., a subsidiary of Otsuka Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd.

title: FDA Authorizes Marketing of IQOS Tobacco Heating System with ‘Reduced Exposure’ Information
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has authorized Philip Morris Products S.A.'s "IQOS Tobacco Heating System" as modified risk tobacco products (MRTPs). This marks the second set of products to be authorized as MRTPs and the first tobacco products to receive "exposure modification" orders. These orders permit the marketing of a product as containing a reduced level of or presenting a reduced exposure to a substance. The authorization requires Philip Morris Products S.A. to conduct postmarket surveillance and studies to determine whether the MRTP orders continue to be appropriate. Mitch Zeller, J.D., director of the FDA's Center for Tobacco Products, stated that the company's data shows that marketing these products could help addicted adult smokers transition away from combusted cigarettes and reduce their exposure to harmful chemicals. The IQOS Tobacco Heating System includes an electronic device that generates a nicotine-containing aerosol by heating tobacco-filled sticks. The FDA previously authorized the marketing of these products in April 2019 via the premarket tobacco application (PMTA) pathway. The authorization includes requirements for the company to monitor youth awareness and use of the products and to keep the FDA apprised of efforts to prevent youth access and exposure. The company must also request and receive authorization from the FDA to continue marketing the products with the same modified exposure information after the initial orders expire in 4 years.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 7, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has taken actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. Yesterday, the FDA issued a letter to clinical laboratory staff and health care providers warning of a false positive result with BD SARS-CoV-2 Reagents for the BD Max System test, with 3% of results found to be false positives. The FDA is working with Becton, Dickinson and Company to resolve this issue. The agency has also updated Molecular Diagnostic templates on its website to provide recommendations for the validation of assays intended for pooling patient samples. Additionally, the FDA has issued warning letters to five companies selling fraudulent COVID-19 products, including SinoTradition.com, Butterfly Expressions, LLC, Lotus Herbal Supplements, Lianhuaqingwencaps.com, and Shen Clinic, LLC. The FDA has authorized 166 tests under EUAs, including 138 molecular tests, 26 antibody tests, and 2 antigen tests. The agency protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Issued Emergency Use Authorization for Point of Care Antigen Test
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for the BD Veritor System for Rapid Detection of SARS-CoV-2, a COVID-19 antigen diagnostic test. This is the second antigen test authorized by the FDA for SARS-CoV-2 detection. The test can be used in laboratories certified under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA) for high, moderate, or waived complexity testing. FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn authorized the test, noting its importance in expanding America's testing capabilities and its potential to scale up testing for millions of Americans. The FDA is responsible for protecting the public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of various products, including medical devices, food, and cosmetics.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 6, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration added content to its guidance on conducting clinical trials during the COVID-19 pandemic, clarifying methods for obtaining informed consent from hospitalized patients and those in isolation. The FDA also issued an emergency use authorization for the third diagnostic test for detecting viruses that cause flu and COVID-19, expanding its previous authorizations to BioFire Diagnostics, LLC and QIAGEN GmbH. Additionally, the FDA issued an EUA for a COVID-19 antigen test to Becton, Dickinson and Company, and authorized 164 tests under EUAs, including 137 molecular tests, 25 antibody tests, and 2 antigen tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 2, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced actions to protect the American public from COVID-19. The FDA warned consumers and healthcare professionals about hand sanitizer products containing methanol, which can be toxic and life-threatening. The agency has authorized 162 tests under Emergency Use Authorization, including 136 molecular tests, 25 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test. The FDA is responsible for protecting public health, safety, and security, including the nation's food supply, cosmetics, and tobacco products.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup July 1, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced the distribution of the first round of SARS-CoV-2 reference panel materials to support the evaluation of diagnostic tests for COVID-19. The panel is an independent performance validation step for clinical purposes. The FDA issued Emergency Use Authorizations (EUAs) to TNS Co., Ltd, The Kroger Co., and Psomagen, Inc., for their COVID-19 diagnostic tests. The FDA authorized a total of 161 tests under EUAs, including 135 molecular tests, 25 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test. The agency also issued a warning letter to the Center for Wellness and Integrative Medicine for selling unapproved products to mitigate, prevent, treat, diagnose, or cure COVID-19.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A Federal Open Market Committee meeting was held by videoconference on June 9-10, 2020, where the Chair reaffirmed the Federal Reserve's commitment to fostering diversity, inclusion, and racial equality. The Committee discussed various policy tools, including outcome-based forward guidance, large-scale asset purchases, and yield curve control policies. They considered potential effects on financial markets, central bank independence, and private-sector balance sheets. Participants noted challenges with implementing these policies, especially on longer-term yields, and emphasized the importance of clear communications. The staff assessed the impact of the coronavirus outbreak on the economy and projected a gradual recovery in real GDP and unemployment rate by the second half of 2020. The Committee maintained the target range for the federal funds rate at 0-1/4 percent, decided to continue monitoring developments, and use its tools as necessary to support the economy.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 30, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced several actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA provided guidance titled "Development and Licensure of Vaccines to Prevent COVID-19" to facilitate the development of safe and effective vaccines. The guidance outlines the agency's recommendations for COVID-19 vaccine development, including the data needed for manufacturing, clinical development, and approval. The FDA will evaluate any potential vaccine candidate, regardless of technology. The guidance aims to support traditional FDA approval by directly evaluating the vaccine's ability to protect humans from SARS-CoV-2 infection and disease. The FDA also considers the Accelerated Approval pathway for vaccine licensure. Additionally, the agency issued an Emergency Use Authorization to LifeHope Labs for its molecular-based diagnostic panel. The FDA has authorized 157 tests under EUAs, including 132 molecular tests, 24 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test. The agency protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of various products, including drugs, vaccines, medical devices, and food.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Takes Action to Help Facilitate Timely Development of Safe, Effective COVID-19 Vaccines
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has provided guidance to companies, researchers, and others developing COVID-19 vaccines. The guidance outlines the agency's recommendations for data needed to facilitate the manufacturing, clinical development, and approval of COVID-19 vaccines. 

The FDA Commissioner, Stephen M. Hahn, M.D., emphasizes the need for a safe and effective vaccine to prevent COVID-19. He also stresses the agency's commitment to maintaining its regulatory independence and ensuring decisions are based on science and available data.

The guidance encourages the inclusion of diverse populations in clinical trials and includes studies to support vaccine use during pregnancy and pediatric assessments. The FDA expects that a COVID-19 vaccine would prevent disease or decrease its severity in at least 50% of people who are vaccinated.

The agency also addresses the consideration of an accelerated approval pathway and Emergency Use Authorization for COVID-19 vaccines. The FDA will thoroughly evaluate data from vaccine clinical trials and only approve or make available a COVID-19 vaccine if it meets high standards.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 29, 2020
body_summary: The US FDA has taken actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. A warning letter was jointly issued to Hong Kong-based companies SuperHealthGuard and Loyal Great International, Ltd., advising them to cease selling unapproved products online with misleading claims about mitigating, preventing, or curing COVID-19. The FDA is protecting public health and enforcing the FTC Act, 15 U.S.C. 41, prohibiting unsupported drug advertising claims. The FDA has authorized 155 SARS-CoV-2 molecular diagnostic tests, including Inform Diagnostics and DSL COVID-19 Assay, and added several ventilator products to the list of authorized devices. The FDA also advises consumers not to purchase or use unapproved products, and warns that failure to correct violations could result in legal action, including seizure and injunction.

title: FDA Approves First-Line Immunotherapy for Patients with MSI-H/dMMR Metastatic Colorectal Cancer
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Keytruda for the first-line treatment of patients with unresectable or metastatic microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) or mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) colorectal cancer. This approval marks the first immunotherapy for this patient population as a first-line treatment without chemotherapy. Keytruda targets PD-1/PD-L1, helping the immune system fight cancer cells. The FDA approved Keytruda based on a multicenter, international, open-label, active-controlled, randomized trial comparing Keytruda with chemotherapy in 307 patients. The study demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in progression-free survival, with a median of 16.5 months in the Keytruda group. Common side effects include fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, and immune-mediated conditions such as pneumonitis and colitis. The FDA granted Priority Review, and this approval was given to Merck & Co.

title: FDA Approves Breast Cancer Treatment That Can Be Administered At Home By Health Care Professional
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Phesgo, a combination of pertuzumab, trastuzumab, and hyaluronidase, for the treatment of adult patients with HER2-positive breast cancer that has spread to other parts of the body and for treatment of adult patients with early HER2-positive breast cancer. Phesgo is administered under the skin and is initially used in combination with chemotherapy. The approval was granted four months ahead of the FDA's goal date. The therapeutic components of Phesgo are the same as those in FDA-approved intravenous pertuzumab and trastuzumab. Patients should be selected based on an FDA-approved companion diagnostic test. The FDA has warned about the risk of potential heart failure, fetal harm, and lung toxicity, and patients should be monitored for these conditions.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 26, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The agency issued a warning letter to Curativa Bay Corporation for selling fraudulent COVID-19 products with misleading claims. The FDA has updated templates for laboratories and commercial manufacturers to facilitate submission of Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) requests for serology tests. There are currently 153 authorized tests under EUAs, including 129 molecular tests, 23 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test. The FDA protects the public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of various products, including drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: FDA Approves New Therapy for Dravet Syndrome
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Fintepla, a Schedule IV controlled substance, for the treatment of seizures associated with Dravet syndrome in patients aged 2 and older. Dravet syndrome is a life-threatening, rare, and chronic form of epilepsy. Fintepla offers an additional effective treatment option for patients with this disease. The effectiveness of Fintepla was demonstrated in two clinical studies involving 202 subjects between ages 2 and 18. Subjects treated with Fintepla had significantly greater reductions in the frequency of convulsive seizures compared to those who received placebo. The studies showed reductions in seizure frequency within 3-4 weeks and remained consistent over 14- to 15-week treatment periods. Fintepla is associated with valvular heart disease and pulmonary arterial hypertension, and requires cardiac monitoring. The drug is available only through a restricted distribution program due to these risks.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 25, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. A new report, Partnering with the European Union and Global Regulators on COVID-19, highlights the FDA's long-standing collaboration with the European Union and its European Medicines Agency to promote the safety and effectiveness of medical products. The FDA has updated its list of Emergency Use Authorizations (EUAs) for ventilators and ventilator accessories, adding the AustinP51 resuscitator to the list. The AustinP51 is a portable emergency-use resuscitator designed to provide ventilatory support for patients requiring mechanical ventilation. The FDA has also authorized 150 tests under EUAs, including 126 molecular tests, 23 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test. The FDA is responsible for protecting the public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of medical products and the nation's food supply.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 24, 2020
body_summary: The US FDA launched its first "FDA Insight" podcast featuring Commissioner Stephen Hahn and Deputy Commissioner Anand Shah discussing COVID-19 efforts. Future podcasts will feature Hahn and other FDA leaders on various topics. Commissioner Hahn spoke at the Brussels Forum2020, and he and US Secretary of Agriculture Sonny Perdue issued a joint statement on food export restrictions related to COVID-19. The statement clarified that there is no evidence that people can contract COVID-19 from food or food packaging. The FDA has authorized 149 tests under EUAs, including molecular tests, antibody tests, and antigen tests. The FDA protects the public health by ensuring the safety and security of food, drugs, and medical devices.

title: Executive Order 13930—Strengthening the Child Welfare System for America's Children
body_summary: The US Administration has ordered that every child deserves a family. The Administration has focused on prevention strategies to keep children safe and strengthen families, with the goal of improving the child welfare system. This includes reducing the need for foster care and increasing adoption rates, particularly for children with disabilities and those who have aged out of foster care. The US Secretary will provide a web-based training platform for child welfare and mental health practitioners, make funds available for guardianship, and establish a plan to support kinship care and youth exiting foster care.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 23, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has taken actions to address the COVID-19 pandemic. FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn explains that the agency is working to ensure timely reviews of medical product applications despite increased volume and constraints. The FDA has maintained its goal of meeting application reviews at the same pace as recent years. The agency is partnering with the Critical Path Institute and National Institutes of Health on the CURE Drug Repurposing Collaboratory (CDRC) to exchange clinical practice data and identify potential new uses for existing drugs. CDRC will focus on capturing global clinician treatment experiences to identify drugs with possible treatment approaches. The FDA will unveil the blueprint for the New Era of Smarter Food Safety in the coming weeks, which will outline how the agency will use technology to strengthen food safety over the next decade. The FDA has authorized 145 tests under EUAs, including 122 molecular tests, 22 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test.

title: FDA Announces First of Its Kind Pilot Program to Communicate Patient Reported Outcomes from Cancer Clinical Trials
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has launched Project Patient Voice, an initiative to provide patient-reported symptom data from cancer trials for marketed treatments. The data will be available on a new website, where patients and healthcare professionals can access information on symptomatic side effects. The data is collected through questionnaires completed by patients during clinical trials. 

The pilot website will include a list of cancer clinical trials with available patient-reported symptom data, along with visualizations and data provided by the drug companies. The first phase of the pilot will include only one trial, and the FDA will seek public feedback to improve the website. AstraZeneca is collaborating with the FDA to provide patient-reported outcome data for one of their FDA-approved drugs.

The Project Patient Voice initiative aims to provide standardized methods for displaying patient-reported symptomatic adverse events. The data should be used as a complement to FDA patient labeling and patient information, not as a sole source of information for medical care decisions. The FDA will host a virtual public workshop on July 17 to gather feedback from various stakeholders on the project.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 22, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has taken actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA issued a guidance document addressing formal meetings and user-fee applications for medical devices during the public health emergency. The agency also issued a warning letter to North Isle Wellness Center, which sells unapproved COVID-19 products with misleading claims. The FDA protects the public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of various products, including drugs, vaccines, biological products, medical devices, and food.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 19, 2020
body_summary: The US FDA has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The agency is working in partnership with the NIH, VA, and America Makes to support non-traditional manufacturing approaches to address device shortages, including PPE. The FDA has provided information on labeling and testing for face shields and face masks, and has issued temporary policies for face masks and respirators. The agency has also issued guidance on device manufacturing interruptions and discontinuances, and has recommended actions for pharmaceutical manufacturers to take when an employee has a confirmed COVID-19 infection. The FDA has authorized 144 tests under EUAs, including molecular tests, antibody tests, and antigen tests. Additionally, the agency has issued warning letters to companies selling fraudulent COVID-19 products, and is reminding clinical laboratory staff and health care providers to stop using certain COVID-19 antibody tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Takes Additional Action to Harness Real-World Data to Inform COVID-19 Response Efforts
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is participating in the COVID-19 Diagnostics Evidence Accelerator, a collaborative project to advance diagnostic testing. The project, organized by the Reagan-Udall Foundation and Friends of Cancer Research, aims to analyze real-time diagnostic and clinical data to inform the scientific evaluation of diagnostic tools and medical interventions for COVID-19. FDA Principal Deputy Commissioner Amy Abernethy said the project will contribute to the agency's response to the public health emergency. The Diagnostics Evidence Accelerator is the companion project to the previously announced Therapeutic Evidence Accelerator. Ellen V. Sigal, Chair of both organizations, stated that the collaboration is meeting the urgency of the moment to speed the pace of diagnostic testing. Key research questions will include evaluating real-world performance of SARS-CoV-2 diagnostic tests and antibody tests. The FDA will focus on using real-world data to understand antibody immunity, disease prevalence, and individual risk factors. The evidence generated will be complementary to other studies and address questions not yet answered.

title: FDA Approves First Therapy for Rare Disease that Causes Low Phosphate Blood Levels, Bone Softening
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Crysvita injection to treat patients age two and older with tumor-induced osteomalacia, a rare disease that causes weakened and softened bones. The tumors associated with TIO release a hormone-like substance that lowers phosphate levels. Crysvita helps increase phosphate levels in the blood. The safety and efficacy of Crysvita were evaluated in two studies, enrolling 27 adults with TIO. In these studies, patients received Crysvita every four weeks, with half achieving normal phosphate levels through week 24 and maintaining them through week 144. Crysvita has been linked to hypersensitivity reactions and may increase the risk of nephrocalcinosis. The most common side effects reported were tooth abscess, muscle spasms, and dizziness. Crysvita is approved to treat adults and children six months and older with X-linked hypophosphatemia, a condition that causes low phosphate levels and impaired bone growth.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 18, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. Today, the FDA participated in a virtual meeting with the International Society for Neglected Tropical Diseases to discuss the use of the CURE ID app for capturing case reports on treatments for neglected tropical diseases and COVID-19. The FDA has also published FAQs on its Temporary Policy Regarding Certain Food Labeling Requirements During the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency. As of today, the FDA has authorized 141 tests under Emergency Use Authorizations, including 120 molecular tests, 20 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test. The FDA is an agency within the US Department of Health and Human Services, responsible for protecting public health and ensuring the safety and security of food, cosmetics, and medical devices.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 17, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has taken actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On June 16, 2020, the FDA approved an abbreviated new drug application for succinylcholine chloride injection 200 mg/10 mL, indicated for tracheal intubation and skeletal muscle relaxation. The FDA has also published guidance on statistical considerations for clinical trials during the COVID-19 public health emergency. The agency has issued warning letters to three companies for marketing adulterated and misbranded COVID-19 products, including tests and antibody tests. title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Issues Warning Letters to Companies Inappropriately Marketing Antibody Tests, Potentially Placing Public Health at Risk
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued warning letters to three companies for marketing adulterated and misbranded COVID-19 antibody tests. The agencies involved are Medakit Ltd., Antibodiescheck.com and Yama Group, and Dr. Jason Korkus, DDS. In the warning letters, the FDA outlined violations, including offering test kits for sale in the US without approval, misbranding products with false labeling, and using the FDA logo without permission. The FDA reminds consumers that there are no authorized at-home COVID-19 test kits, and warns against fraudulent products claiming to prevent, diagnose, or cure the virus.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 16, 2020
body_summary: The FDA has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA posted a new web page to answer questions about adverse event reporting for medical devices distributed under Emergency Use Authorizations or related to COVID-19 guidance documents. The FDA also revoked the EUA of the Chembio Diagnostic System's DPP COVID-19 IgM/IgG System test due to performance concerns. Additionally, the FDA updated template guidelines for the validation of molecular diagnostic tests for developers. To date, the FDA has authorized 140 tests under EUAs, including 118 molecular tests, 21 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 16, 2020
body_summary: The US FDA has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA posted a new web page addressing adverse event reporting for medical devices under emergency use authorization or discussed in COVID-19-related guidance documents. The FDA also revoked the emergency use authorization for Chembio Diagnostic System's DPP COVID-19 IgM/IgG System, a SARS-CoV-2 antibody test, due to performance concerns. The FDA has authorized 140 tests under EUAs, including 118 molecular tests, 21 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Facilitating Diagnostic Test Availability for Asymptomatic Testing and Sample Pooling
body_summary: The FDA has taken steps to facilitate the development and authorization of molecular diagnostic tests for broad screening of asymptomatic individuals. The FDA has outlined the steps for a test to be validated for screening of asymptomatic individuals by providing updated templates for test developers. This will make it easier for developers to get their tests authorized for this use. The FDA has also made available FAQs with information regarding tests for screening asymptomatic individuals. The agency recognizes that organizations may want to conduct screening of asymptomatic individuals to ensure the safety of their employees, patients, and others. The FDA has encouraged test developers to reach out to discuss appropriate validation approaches for novel testing ideas, such as asymptomatic screening and specimen pooling. The agency is proactively working with diagnostic test developers to facilitate new approaches and get more tests to more Americans more quickly.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Revokes Emergency Use Authorization for Chembio Antibody Test
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) revoked the emergency use authorization of the Chembio Diagnostic System, Inc. (Chembio) DPP COVID-19 IgM/IgG System, a SARS-CoV-2 antibody test, due to performance concerns with the test's accuracy. The test was one of the first antibody tests authorized by the FDA during the COVID-19 public health emergency. The FDA concluded that the test's known and potential benefits did not outweigh its known and potential risks, including a higher than expected rate of false results. The test's manufacturer, Chembio, had submitted data showing the test generated a higher rate of false results than authorized. The FDA decision was made to protect public health and safety. The FDA will continue to monitor test performance and take actions as appropriate.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Adult Onset Still’s Disease, a Severe and Rare Disease
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Ilaris (canakinumab) injection for the treatment of Active Still’s disease, including Adult-Onset Still’s Disease (AOSD). The approval provides patients with a treatment option. Prior to this approval, patients had no FDA-approved treatments for their disease. Ilaris was previously approved for Systemic Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (SJIA) in patients aged 2 years and older. The safety and efficacy of Ilaris for the treatment of patients with AOSD was established using comparable pharmacokinetic exposure and extrapolation of established efficacy of canakinumab in patients with SJIA. Common side effects reported by patients treated with Ilaris include infections, abdominal pain, and injection-site reactions.

title: FDA Warns Four Manufacturers of Unapproved Injectable Drugs Labeled as Homeopathic
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued warning letters to four companies, Hervert Pharmaceuticals, LLC; MediNatura, Inc.; 8046255 Canada, Inc., doing business as Viatrexx; and World Health Advanced Technologies, Ltd., for selling unapproved injectable drug products labeled as homeopathic, which pose serious risks to patient health and violate federal law. The FDA is concerned about the risks associated with unapproved injectable drug products labeled as homeopathic due to their direct administration into the body, bypassing natural defenses. The agency has issued warning letters to these companies, and the products have been placed on import alert 66-41 to stop them from entering the U.S. The FDA encourages consumers and healthcare professionals to report adverse events or quality problems experienced with these products to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 15, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA has revoked the emergency use authorization for chloroquine phosphate and hydroxychloroquine sulfate, citing that the known and potential benefits of these medications no longer outweigh the known and potential risks for the authorized use. The FDA has also warned health care providers about a potential drug interaction related to remdesivir, which is now advising against co-administration with chloroquine phosphate or hydroxychloroquine sulfate. Additionally, the FDA has approved an abbreviated new drug application for succinylcholine chloride injection, which is indicated for facilitating tracheal intubation and providing skeletal muscle relaxation during surgery or mechanical ventilation. The FDA has authorized 138 tests under EUAs, including 117 molecular tests, 20 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test. The agency is committed to facilitating access to safe and effective medical products to address critical needs during the pandemic.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Warns of Newly Discovered Potential Drug Interaction That May Reduce Effectiveness of a COVID-19 Treatment Authorized for Emergency Use
body_summary: The US FDA is warning healthcare providers about a potential drug interaction between remdesivir and chloroquine phosphate or hydroxychloroquine sulfate. The agency is revising the fact sheet for healthcare providers to state that co-administration of these medications is not recommended due to reduced antiviral activity of remdesivir. The FDA is continuing to evaluate all data related to remdesivir and has revised the fact sheet to include additional safety data and dosing recommendations. The agency has also updated the fact sheet for patients and caregivers to alert them to possible allergic reactions. The FDA issued an emergency use authorization for remdesivir in May 2020 to treat COVID-19 patients with severe disease, and the safety and efficacy of the drug continue to be evaluated.

title: FDA Permits Marketing of First Game-Based Digital Therapeutic to Improve Attention Function in Children with ADHD
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) permitted marketing of the first game-based digital therapeutic device to improve attention function in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). The prescription-only device, EndeavorRx, is for pediatric patients ages 8-12 with primarily inattentive or combined-type ADHD. EndeavorRx improves attention function as measured by computer-based testing and is the first digital therapeutic to improve ADHD symptoms. The device is intended for use as part of a therapeutic program that may include clinician-directed therapy, medication, and/or educational programs. Jeffrey Shuren, M.D., J.D., director of the FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health, stated that the EndeavorRx device offers a non-drug option for improving ADHD symptoms. The FDA reviewed data from multiple studies involving over 600 children and found no serious adverse events. Common adverse events observed with EndeavorRx include frustration, headache, dizziness, and emotional reaction. The FDA granted marketing authorization for EndeavorRx to Akili Interactive through the De Novo premarket review pathway.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Revokes Emergency Use Authorization for Chloroquine and Hydroxychloroquine
body_summary: The US FDA has revoked the emergency use authorization for chloroquine phosphate and hydroxychloroquine sulfate to treat COVID-19 in hospitalized patients. The agency determined that the legal criteria for issuing the authorization are no longer met, citing emerging scientific data that shows the drugs are unlikely to be effective in treating COVID-19. The decision was made after a rigorous assessment by scientists, and the FDA will continue to review emerging information associated with the emergency uses for authorized products. The FDA granted the initial EUA on March 28, 2020, based on the science and data available at the time.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 12, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration announced several actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for Cue Health Inc.'s Cue COVID-19 Test, allowing its use at the Point of Care in patient care settings. Additionally, the FDA issued a warning letter to EUCYT Laboratories, LLC for marketing an unapproved exosome product for COVID-19 treatment or prevention. The FDA has authorized 135 tests under EUAs, including molecular, antibody, and antigen tests.

title: FDA Approves New Therapy for Rare Disease Affecting Optic Nerve, Spinal Cord
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Uplizna (inebilizumab-cdon) injection for intravenous use to treat neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) in adult patients with a specific antibody. This is the second approved treatment for NMOSD in the past year. The approval follows a clinical study of 230 adult patients, where 77% of patients treated with Uplizna had a reduced risk of NMOSD relapse compared to the placebo group. Uplizna has been shown to cause infusion reactions, depletion of certain proteins, and increased risk of infection. The FDA has warned that pregnant women should not take Uplizna, and health professionals are advised to inform females of reproductive age to use effective contraception during treatment.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 10, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA and NIH have updated the CURE ID crowd-sourcing app to allow healthcare providers to share their COVID-19 treatment experiences.
