The FDA issued an emergency use authorization to Illumina, Inc. for the first COVID-19 diagnostic test using next-generation sequence technology. The Illumina COVIDSeq Test is authorized for the qualitative detection of SARS-CoV-2 RNA from respiratory specimens. The FDA has authorized 131 tests under EUAs, including 111 molecular tests, 19 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes First Next Generation Sequence Test for Diagnosing COVID-19
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) to Illumina, Inc. for the first COVID-19 diagnostic test utilizing next generation sequence technology. The FDA authorized the Illumina COVIDSeq Test for qualitative detection of SARS-CoV-2 RNA from respiratory specimens. Dr. Stephen Hahn, FDA Commissioner, stated that this tool will expand testing capabilities and aid in monitoring virus mutations. The FDA, part of the US Department of Health and Human Services, regulates various products, including drugs, vaccines, biological products, medical devices, food, cosmetics, and tobacco products.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The Federal Reserve is committed to using its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals. The coronavirus outbreak is causing tremendous human and economic hardship across the United States and around the world. The virus and the measures taken to protect public health have induced sharp declines in economic activity and a surge in job losses. Weaker demand and significantly lower oil prices are holding down consumer price inflation. Financial conditions have improved, in part reflecting policy measures to support the economy and the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses. The ongoing public health crisis will weigh heavily on economic activity, employment, and inflation in the near term, and poses considerable risks to the economic outlook over the medium term. In light of these developments, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent. The Committee expects to maintain this target range until it is confident that the economy has weathered recent events and is on track to achieve its maximum employment and price stability goals. The Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook, including information related to public health, as well as global developments and muted inflation pressures, and will use its tools and act as appropriate to support the economy. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the stance of monetary policy, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. To support the flow of credit to households and businesses, over coming months the Federal Reserve will increase its holdings of Treasury securities and agency residential and commercial mortgage-backed securities at least at the current pace to sustain smooth market functioning, thereby fostering effective transmission of monetary policy to broader financial conditions. In addition, the Open Market Desk will continue to offer large-scale overnight and term repurchase agreement operations. The Committee will closely monitor developments and is prepared to adjust its plans as appropriate. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Patrick Harker; Robert S. Kaplan; Neel Kashkari; Loretta J. Mester; and Randal K. Quarles.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 9, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved an abbreviated new drug application for succinylcholine chloride injection, indicated to facilitate tracheal intubation and provide skeletal muscle relaxation during surgery or mechanical ventilation, on June 8, 2020. The FDA warned a company, organic-beauty-recipes.com, for selling a fraudulent COVID-19 product, which was promoted with misleading claims. The agency authorized 128 tests under EUAs, including 108 molecular tests, 19 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test. The FDA is responsible for protecting public health through the safety and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 8, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued certain Emergency Use Authorizations (EUAs) to revise respirator decontamination systems, reissued EUAs covering imported respirators, and issued a guidance on prescription drug sample distribution during the COVID-19 public health emergency. The FDA added the BioMedInnovations SuppleVent Ventilator to the list of ventilators authorized under a previous EUA. The agency has authorized 125 tests under EUAs, including 107 molecular tests, 17 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test.

title: Federal Government Announces New Pilot Program to Help Stop Illegal Availability of Unapproved Opioids Online
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the National Telecommunications and Information Administration are launching a 120-day pilot to reduce the availability of unapproved opioids sold online. The FDA will notify participating internet registries, including Neustar, Verisign, and Public Interest Registry, when it sends a warning letter to website operators who fail to respond adequately. The internet registries will review the notifications and assess whether to take action, such as domain name suspensions or blocks. The NTIA will work with the internet registries and the FDA to assess the pilot's impact. The pilot is part of President Trump's effort to combat the opioid crisis, which has been a top health priority. The pilot's effectiveness will be analyzed after its completion.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Reissues Emergency Use Authorizations Revising Which Types of Respirators Can Be Decontaminated for Reuse
body_summary:
The FDA is reissuing emergency use authorizations (EUAs) for respirators to specify which ones are suitable for decontamination. The FDA has decided that certain respirators, including those manufactured in China, should not be decontaminated for reuse by healthcare personnel. 

The FDA has revised the relevant EUAs to no longer authorize decontamination or reuse of respirators with exhalation valves. The agency has reissued the EUAs for non-NIOSH-approved disposable filtering facepiece respirators manufactured in China, revising the scope of authorization to exclude respirators that have been decontaminated. 

The FDA is also revising the EUAs for imported respirators, including those manufactured in China, to include new language related to decontamination and revise the scope of authorization with respect to jurisdictions eligible for eligibility. 

Anand Shah, M.D., FDA Deputy Commissioner for Medical and Scientific Affairs, stated that the FDA continues to provide flexibility and adapt to evolving needs based on data and science, while ensuring public health protection.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 5, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced several actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA has updated its COVID-19 Response At-A-Glance Summary to provide facts and figures on the agency's response efforts. The agency has also changed the hours for the COVID-19 Industry Hotline to 8:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time, Monday through Friday. For urgent inquiries, the FDA Emergency Line (1-866-300-4374) remains available after-hours. The FDA has published new guidance expanding the availability and capability of non-invasive monitoring devices, which facilitates patient monitoring while reducing contact and exposure. The guidance replaces a previous March 20, 2020, guidance and expands the scope to include additional device types. The FDA has authorized 124 tests under EUAs, including 106 molecular tests, 17 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test. The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 4, 2020
body_summary:
The FDA has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, including:
Issuing a new video resource explaining diagnostic and antibody tests.
Issuing warning letters to operators of four websites marketing unapproved COVID-19 products.
Launching a webinar series on June 9, 12:00 pm – 1:00 pm ET, to provide information on respirators and answer questions.
Issuing a letter to clinical laboratory staff and health care providers about a safety risk with using transport media and SARS-CoV-2 testing platforms.
Publicly posting test performance data from four antibody test kits.
Authorizing 120 tests under EUAs, including 104 molecular tests, 15 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test.
The FDA recognizes the increased demand for certain products during the pandemic and is committed to facilitating access to medical products to address critical needs.
The agency is responsible for protecting the public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices, as well as regulating food, cosmetics, and tobacco products.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Publicly Shares Antibody Test Performance Data From Kits as Part of Validation Study
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has publicly posted test performance data from four additional antibody test kits on open.fda.gov, as part of its independent performance validation study effort with the National Institutes of Health's National Cancer Institute. The data, which are the result of an important cross-government effort, were first posted on May 4, 2020, and include results from tests not previously subject to an EUA or pre-EUA. Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn, M.D. and NCI Director Norman E. "Ned" Sharpless, M.D., praised the collaboration between the FDA, NIH, CDC, and BARDA, which provided laboratory capacity and expertise to support the testing. The testing was performed at the Frederick National Laboratory for Cancer Research, and the data will continue to support FDA's decision-making.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 3, 2020
body_summary: The US FDA announced actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA introduced a new web-based resource, titled Testing Supply Substitution Strategies, to support labs performing authorized COVID-19 tests. This 22-slide PowerPoint file provides detailed information on validated supply alternatives to address supply issues with some test components. The FDA updated its guidance on Conduct of Clinical Trials of Medical Products during COVID-19 Public Health Emergency, adding a new question-and-answer on 21 CFR Part 11 compliance for electronic systems used to generate electronic signatures on clinical trial records. The FDA also issued an alert to healthcare professionals regarding the temporary absence of the "paralyzing agent" warning statement on the vial caps of two neuromuscular blocking agents. The FDA has authorized 120 tests under EUAs, including 104 molecular tests, 15 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test, and works with over 400 test developers who have submitted or will submit EUA requests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 2, 2020
body_summary: The FDA today announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The agency has published a new guidance titled Institutional Review Board (IRB) Review of Individual Patient Expanded Access Requests for Investigational Drugs and Biological Products During the COVID-19 Public Health Emergency. The FDA has also added two ventilators, one developed by NASA, to the list of authorized ventilators under the ventilator emergency use authorization (EUA). Additionally, the agency has authorized an emergency resuscitator for the Fitbit Flow, a continuous respiratory support system, and provided procedural assistance to sponsors and applicants for pediatric product development plans for the treatment and prevention of COVID-19. The FDA has also created a new web page, titled Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) Resources for Health Professionals, to help health professionals quickly access FDA resources. To date, the FDA has authorized 119 tests under EUAs, which include 103 molecular tests, 15 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Takes Action to Protect Public Health; Increase Supply of Alcohol-Based Hand Sanitizer
body_summary: The FDA has updated its guidances to ensure the manufacturing and compounding of certain alcohol-based hand sanitizer products, providing clarity on tolerable levels of impurities, particularly gasoline and benzene, in ethanol used in hand sanitizers. This action aims to prevent harm and ensure widespread access to hand sanitizers during the COVID-19 public health emergency. The FDA appreciates the industry's willingness to meet increasing demand for alcohol-based hand sanitizers and continues to assess and update its policies as necessary. The agency recommends the use of hand sanitizers containing at least 60% alcohol, and consumers should keep hand sanitizers out of reach of children and seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center if ingested.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup June 1, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration announced actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On May 29, the FDA issued a new report, FDA Voices, and a Consumer Update to explain regulatory terminology and the agency's role in evaluating new medical products. The FDA is working with over 400 test developers to authorise 117 EUA requests for tests detecting the virus or its antibodies. The agency authorises tests for safety, effectiveness, and security, including 101 molecular tests, 15 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test. The FDA protects the public health by regulating human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, biological products, medical devices, and the nation's food supply.

title: Federal judge enters order of permanent injunction against New York company for distributing unapproved drugs
body_summary: A federal judge has ordered Sundial Herbal Products to stop distributing unapproved new drugs and misbranded drugs until they comply with federal law. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration had previously warned Sundial about violating the law, but they continued to distribute unapproved products despite promises to correct the issues. The court concluded that Sundial's products lack published studies to support their claims, and the FDA had not approved any application for their drugs. The FDA is concerned that these products may cause consumers to delay or stop appropriate medical treatment. As a result, U.S District Judge Edgardo Ramos entered a permanent injunction against Rahsan Hakim and Adoniiah Rahsan, individuals doing business as Sundial Herbal Products, on May 27, 2020. The FDA had issued warning letters to Sundial in 2013 and 2017, but follow-up inspections revealed that the defendants did not make the necessary corrections.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 29, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The agency is making its FDA MyStudies app available for free to investigators to obtain patients' informed consent for clinical trials that cannot be conducted in person due to COVID-19 measures. FDA has also issued warning letters to two companies, Quadrant Sales & Marketing, Inc. and StayWell Copper Products, for selling fraudulent COVID-19 products with false or misleading claims. The FDA has authorized 114 COVID-19 tests under Emergency Use Authorization (EUA), including 101 molecular tests, 12 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test. The agency is also providing a template on its website to facilitate the submission of EUA requests for at-home sample collection kits.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Takes Steps to Streamline Development of Tests With At-Home Sample Collection
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has included a voluntary EUA template for at-home sample collection kits on its website to support the development of COVID-19 tests for at-home self-collection. This template reflects the FDA's current thinking on the data and information required for developers to submit to facilitate the EUA process. The FDA has been supportive of making accurate and reliable tests widely available, especially for at-home self-collection, which raises concerns about safety and accuracy. The director of the FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health stated that the agency will continue to support streamlined review processes while protecting patients and public health. The FDA has authorized several COVID-19 tests for use with at-home collection of samples, but no tests are currently authorized for complete at-home use.

title: FDA Approves New Option to Treat Heavy Menstrual Bleeding Associated with Fibroids in Women
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Oriahnn, a medication consisting of elagolix, estradiol, and norethindrone acetate, for managing heavy menstrual bleeding associated with uterine leiomyomas (fibroids) in premenopausal women. The approval was based on clinical trials showing that 68.5% and 76.5% of patients who received Oriahnn achieved a significant reduction in menstrual blood loss. The medication is available as capsules for oral use and has been shown to be effective in reducing symptoms of heavy menstrual bleeding. However, Oriahnn may cause bone loss over time, and women should not take it for more than 24 months. The FDA has also warned about the risk of vascular events and thrombotic disorders associated with Oriahnn, and has contraindications for certain women, including those with a history of blood clots and uncontrolled hypertension.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 27, 2020
body_summary: The US FDA issued guidance for reporting temporary closures and requesting assistance during the COVID-19 pandemic. The agency warned four companies, including CBD Gaze, Alternavita, Musthavemom.com, and Careful Cents, for promoting fraudulent COVID-19 products. A judge issued a preliminary injunction against Xephyr LLC, requiring them to stop distributing colloidal silver products. The FDA authorized 113 tests under EUAs for COVID-19 detection, including 100 molecular tests, 12 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test, working with over 400 test developers to submit EUA requests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 28, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued an Emergency Use Authorization for the Stryker Sustainability Solutions VHP N95 Respirator Decontamination System to decontaminate compatible N95 respirators, which can be reused by healthcare personnel to prevent exposure to pathogenic microorganisms. The FDA has also provided a SARS-CoV-2 reference panel to support the evaluation of diagnostic tests for COVID-19. To date, the FDA has authorized 113 tests under EUAs, including 100 molecular tests, 12 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test, for developers who have submitted EUA requests for tests that detect the virus or antibodies to the virus.

title: FDA Alerts Patients and Health Care Professionals to Nitrosamine Impurity Findings in Certain Metformin Extended-Release Products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has found elevated levels of the nitrosamine impurity N-Nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) above its acceptable intake limit in several lots of the extended-release (ER) formulation of metformin, a prescription drug used to control high blood sugar in patients with type 2 diabetes. The agency is in contact with five firms to recommend they voluntarily recall their products. Metformin ER formulations from other manufacturers that supply a significant portion of the US market are not being recalled. The FDA is continuing to work closely with manufacturers to ensure appropriate testing. Assessments are underway to determine whether metformin ER recalls will result in shortages. The FDA recommends that healthcare professionals continue to prescribe metformin when clinically appropriate, as testing has not shown NDMA in immediate-release (IR) metformin products.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Provides New Tool to Aid Development and Evaluation of Diagnostic Tests That Detect SARS-CoV-2 Infection
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has provided a SARS-CoV-2 reference panel to support the evaluation of diagnostic tests for COVID-19. This panel, which includes nucleic acid tests that identify the presence of the virus' genetic material (RNA), is an additional step to ensure the quality and performance of the tests. The FDA's reference panel is available to commercial and laboratory developers who are interacting with the agency through the pre-emergency use authorization (EUA) process. The panel provides developers with well-characterized reagents to compare the performance of different molecular diagnostic tests under the same conditions. The FDA has taken this step to ensure Americans have access to trustworthy diagnostic tests and to address poorly performing tests. This effort is part of the FDA's ongoing evaluation of diagnostic tests and its commitment to protecting and promoting public health.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 26, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for gowns and other personal protective equipment (PPE) to protect healthcare personnel and patients. The agency also provided flexibility to farms regarding the qualified exemption under the Produce Safety Rule. The FDA approved an abbreviated new drug application for succinylcholine chloride injection to facilitate tracheal intubation and provide skeletal muscle relaxation during surgery or mechanical ventilation. The FDA has authorized 113 tests under EUAs, including 100 molecular tests, 12 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test. The FDA protects the public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: FDA Approves Only Drug in U.S. to Treat Severe Malaria
body_summary: The US FDA has approved artesunate for injection to treat severe malaria in adult and pediatric patients. The treatment should be followed by an oral antimalarial regimen. This approval comes after a randomized controlled trial and a published randomized controlled trial showed the safety and efficacy of IV artesunate. The FDA granted Priority Review and Orphan Drug Designation to Amivas, the manufacturer. Artesunate is a lifesaving drug that can help prevent severe malaria complications. The FDA protects the public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of drugs and medical devices.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for a Form of Bladder Dysfunction in Pediatric Patients as Young as 2 Years of Age
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved VESIcare LS (solifenacin succinate) oral suspension for the treatment of neurogenic detrusor overactivity (NDO) in children ages two years and older. This is the first FDA-approved treatment for NDO patients as young as two years of age. The treatment requires only once a day dosing, which is a significant improvement over the current standard of care, which required up to three times a day dosing. VESIcare LS was initially approved in 2004 for the treatment of overactive bladder in adults 18 years and older. The FDA's approval was based on two clinical trials involving 95 pediatric NDO patients, which showed significant improvements in bladder function and reductions in symptoms. The most common side effects of VESIcare LS include constipation, dry mouth, and urinary tract infection.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 22, 2020
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has announced several actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA and US Department of Agriculture released recommendations to address shortages of PPE, cloth face coverings, disinfectants, and sanitation supplies in the food and agriculture industry. The FDA issued a guidance document providing temporary flexibility in food labeling requirements for manufacturers and vending machine operators. The agency is also providing flexibility to the vending machine industry and will not object if covered operators do not meet labeling requirements to provide calorie information.

The FDA issued a warning letter to two companies, Apollo Holding LLC and North Coast Biologics LLC, for selling fraudulent COVID-19 products. These products, including cannabidiol and unapproved vaccines, claim to be safe and effective for the prevention and treatment of COVID-19, but have not been approved by the FDA.

The FDA updated its FAQs on testing for SARS-CoV-2, clarifying information on at-home self-collection and authorized tests. The agency has authorized 109 tests under EUAs, including 96 molecular tests, 12 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test.

The FDA is responsible for protecting the public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices, as well as regulating the nation's food supply and other products.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 21, 2020
body_summary: The FDA announced that it has removed a list of antibody tests from the "notification list" of tests being offered under the Policy for Coronavirus Disease-2019 Tests During the Public Health Emergency. The tests on this new removal list include those voluntarily withdrawn by their commercial manufacturer and those without a pending EUA request. The FDA expects these tests not to be marketed or distributed. Antibody tests offered by commercial manufacturers under the policy remain on the notification list pending review of their EUA request. The FDA issued guidance to help continue the availability of medical devices during the public health emergency, allowing limited modifications to approved devices without prior submission. The FDA approved two new drug applications for dexmedetomidine hydrochloride injection and succinylcholine chloride injection. The FDA recognizes the increased demand for certain products during the COVID-19 public health emergency and remains committed to facilitating access to medical products. The agency also announced that the effective date of the "Required Warnings for Cigarette Packages and Advertisements" final rule has been postponed to October 16, 2021.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Provides Promised Transparency for Antibody Tests
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has posted a list of antibody tests that are being removed from the notification list of tests being offered under the Policy for Coronavirus Disease-2019 Tests During the Public Health Emergency. These tests were voluntarily withdrawn by their commercial manufacturers or do not have a pending EUA request. The FDA expects the tests on this list to not be marketed or distributed. The agency's revised guidance, announced on May 4, 2020, recommends that commercial manufacturers of antibody tests submit an EUA request within 10 business days. The list is expected to be updated, and the FDA will continue to work with industry to develop accurate tests.

title: FDA Releases Report on Investigation into Fall 2019 Outbreaks of Illnesses Tied to Romaine Lettuce
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is committed to protecting the safety of workers and consumers from foodborne illness as the nation navigates the COVID-19 public health emergency. As part of its efforts, the FDA released an investigation report on three outbreaks of E. coli O157:H7 illnesses tied to romaine lettuce in Fall 2019. The report found that proximity to cattle to produce fields may have been a contributing factor to the contamination. The FDA is calling on leafy greens growers to assess and mitigate risks associated with adjacent and nearby land uses, including grazing lands and animal operations. The agency is also urging growers to implement prevention strategies, such as increasing buffer zones and adding physical barriers, to prevent contamination from uphill adjacent cattle grazing lands. The FDA is also working on a 2020 Leafy Green STEC Action Plan to prevent foodborne outbreaks linked to fresh leafy greens, which includes advancing safety of agricultural water, enhancing inspection programs, and improving traceability.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on April 28-29, 2020, discussing financial market developments and economic outlook. Swift Fed actions and strong fiscal measures improved markets, but uncertainty remained regarding corporate credit, emerging markets, and mortgage markets. The global economy experienced a sharp contraction in activity due to the coronavirus outbreak, with foreign governments announcing large fiscal packages and central banks taking accommodative measures. The Federal Reserve maintained its accommodative stance, kept the federal funds rate target range unchanged at 0 to 1/4 percent, and continued purchasing Treasury securities and agency MBS to support market functioning.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 20, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA and U.S. Department of Agriculture signed a Memorandum of Understanding to support the U.S. food and agriculture sector, aiming to maintain access to a safe food supply. The FDA issued an Emergency Use Authorization for the COVID-19 Airway Management Isolation Chamber at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center. The FDA and Federal Trade Commission warned two companies, Life Unlearned, LLC, and SpiceTac, for promoting and selling fraudulent COVID-19 products. The FDA has authorized 105 tests under EUAs, including molecular, antibody, and antigen tests. The agency protects the public health by ensuring the safety and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices, as well as the nation's food supply.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Collaborations Promote Rigorous Analyses of Real-World Data to Inform Pandemic Response
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has entered into an agreement with Aetion to collaborate on advanced analytical techniques to answer urgent COVID-19 research questions. The FDA and Aetion aim to answer questions about diagnostics and medications, and risk factors for COVID-19-related complications. The agency recognizes the potential of diverse real-world data sources to inform its response to the pandemic. The FDA has worked with public and private partners to collect and analyze real-world data, including data from Sentinel, and is expanding its work to identify new datasets. This effort is part of the COVID-19 Evidence Accelerator, a collaborative initiative between the FDA, academia, and industry. The FDA is regularly engaging with stakeholders to harness the power of data and facilitate medical countermeasures, mitigate shortages, and ensure product safety and quality. The FDA is an agency within the US Department of Health and Human Services, responsible for protecting public health and ensuring the safety and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 18, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken actions to protect consumers from fraudulent COVID-19 products. The agency issued warning letters to two companies, Noetic Nutraceuticals and The Golden Road Kratom, for making misleading claims about their CBD and kratom products, respectively. The FDA also issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for an at-home COVID-19 test kit from Everlywell, Inc. The agency has authorized 103 tests under EUAs, including molecular, antibody, and antigen tests. The FDA has also approved an Abbreviated New Drug Application for hydroxychloroquine sulfate tablets for the treatment of malaria, lupus, and rheumatoid arthritis.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update:  FDA Authorizes First Standalone At-Home Sample Collection Kit That Can Be Used With Certain Authorized Tests
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the Everlywell COVID-19 Test Home Collection Kit for at-home collection of nasal swab specimens for analysis by COVID-19 diagnostic tests. The kit is specifically authorized for use by individuals who have been screened using an online questionnaire reviewed by a healthcare provider. The FDA has authorized two diagnostic tests for use with the Everlywell kit, and additional tests may be authorized in the future if data demonstrate accuracy. The kit allows patients to self-collect a nasal sample at home and ship it overnight to a CLIA-certified lab for testing. The labs authorized to test specimens collected using the kit are Fulgent Therapeutics and Assurance Scientific Laboratories. The kit is available by prescription only and is currently the only authorized at-home sample collection kit for use with multiple authorized COVID-19 diagnostic tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 15, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA has issued an updated report on its response efforts, providing facts, figures, and highlights. The agency has also issued a consumer update on coronavirus testing basics and warned two companies, Benjamin McEvoy and White Eagle Native Herbs, for selling fraudulent COVID-19 products. The FDA has authorized 100 tests under Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) and is working with over 400 test developers. The agency has also changed the hours for its COVID-19 Industry Hotline and published contact information for medical devices during the pandemic.

title: FDA Approves First Drug for Fourth-Line Treatment of Advanced Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Qinlock (ripretinib) tablets as a fourth-line treatment for advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST). Qinlock is indicated for adult patients who have received prior treatment with three or more kinase inhibitor therapies, including imatinib. The approval was based on the results of a clinical trial that enrolled 129 patients with advanced GIST, which showed a 6.3-month progression-free survival (PFS) rate in the Qinlock group, compared to one month in the placebo group. Qinlock's side effects include alopecia, fatigue, nausea, and serious side effects such as skin cancer, hypertension, and cardiac dysfunction. The FDA granted Priority Review and Fast Track designation, as well as Breakthrough Therapy and Orphan Drug designation, to Deciphera Pharmaceuticals, Inc. for Qinlock, which was approved three months ahead of schedule.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 14, 2020
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for infusion pumps and accessories to address concerns over their availability, particularly for healthcare providers to safely administer medications and fluids to patients. The EUA also clarifies that drugs can be compounded under a specific policy when standard personal protective equipment (PPE) are not available.

The FDA has authorized 98 EUA requests for tests detecting the virus or antibodies, including 85 molecular tests, 12 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test. The agency has worked with over 390 test developers to submit EUA requests.

The FDA, an agency within the US Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by ensuring the safety and security of various products, including human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, medical devices, and food.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Federal judge enters temporary injunction against Xephyr LLC doing business as N-Ergetics, preventing sale of Colloidal Silver Products for COVID-19
body_summary: A federal court has entered a temporary restraining order against Xephyr LLC, doing business as N-Ergetics, and three individuals associated with the entity, requiring them to immediately stop distributing colloidal silver products. The court found that Xephyr and the associated individuals are violating the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act by unlawfully distributing unapproved new drugs and misbranded drugs. The FDA had previously issued a warning letter to Xephyr about its colloidal silver products, and the company had resumed marketing its products as a treatment for COVID-19 after removing their COVID-19-related webpages. The temporary restraining order expires on June 4, 2020, and there will be a hearing on May 21, 2020, to extend the injunction.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Informs Public About Possible Accuracy Concerns with Abbott ID NOW Point-of-Care Test
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is alerting the public to early data suggesting potential inaccurate results from using the Abbott ID NOW point-of-care test for COVID-19 diagnosis. The test may return false negative results. The FDA is in direct communications with Abbott to study the data and create additional mechanisms for testing. Director Tim Stenzel notes that the test can still identify positive cases in minutes, but negative results may need to be confirmed with a high-sensitivity authorized molecular test.

The FDA has received 15 adverse event reports about the Abbott ID NOW device, suggesting users are receiving inaccurate negative results. Abbott has agreed to conduct post-market studies, including at least 150 COVID-19 positive patients in various clinical settings. The FDA will review interim data and publicly communicate any updates. Consumers or healthcare providers can reach Abbott directly for more information.

title: FDA issues warning letters to two breast implant manufacturers as part of ongoing efforts to protect patients
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued warning letters to two breast implant manufacturers, Allergan and Ideal Implant Incorporated, for failing to comply with regulatory requirements. 

Allergan received a warning letter for failing to conduct post-approval studies to assess the long-term safety and risks of two models of breast implants, which were voluntarily recalled from the market last year. 

The FDA has also issued a warning letter to Ideal Implant Incorporated for failing to comply with current good manufacturing practice requirements and adverse event reporting requirements following an inspection conducted earlier this year. 

The FDA requires manufacturers of approved silicone gel-filled breast implants to conduct post-approval studies to further evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the products. 

A manufacturer's failure to comply with post-approval requirements may result in additional action. 

The FDA has taken additional steps to ensure the agency is monitoring the safety and risks of breast implants, including the development of thePatient Registry and Outcomes for Breast Implants and Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma (ALCL) Etiology and Epidemiology (PROFILE) registry. 

The FDA monitors adverse events related to breast implants and takes appropriate action necessary to ensure the safety of medical products in the marketplace.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 13, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced a virtual Town Hall on May 15, 2020, to discuss 3D printed swabs production and use during the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA also posted a new webpage with information on the use of thermal imaging systems. The agency has authorized 95 tests under EUAs, including 82 molecular tests, 12 antibody tests, and 1 antigen test, in collaboration with over 390 test developers. The FDA protects the public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of various products, including drugs, vaccines, medical devices, and food.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 11, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA issued an Emergency Use Authorization for the Fresenius Propoven 2% Emulsion for sedation in patients older than 16 who require mechanical ventilation in an ICU. The agency also issued warning letters to two companies selling fraudulent COVID-19 products, including Seanjari Preeti Womb Healing, L.L.C. and Plum Dragon Herbs, Inc. The FDA has posted 46 COVID-19 related warning letters and added content to its guidance on conducting clinical trials during the public health emergency. The agency approved two Abbreviated New Drug Applications, including cisatracurium besylate injection and azithromycin tablets. The FDA has issued 92 EUAs for COVID-19 tests, including one for a new antigen test from Quidel Corporation. The agency continues to work with test developers and has notified over 245 laboratories that have begun testing under its COVID-19 policy. The FDA also updated its policy for coronavirus disease-2019 tests during the public health emergency.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA updates on surveillance inspections during COVID-19
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration will continue to utilize alternative inspection tools and approaches during the COVID-19 pandemic, postponing domestic and foreign routine surveillance inspections. This will be done on a case-by-case basis, with mission-critical inspections conducted with safety measures in place. The FDA is collaborating with the CDC to develop a process for returning to on-site facility surveillance inspections, following the gating criteria outlined in the White House Guidelines for Opening Up America Again. The FDA's priority is to protect the health and well-being of its workforce, state contract inspectors, and the health of workers in regulated industries. The agency believes that most FDA-regulated firms understand their responsibility to ensure product safety and quality. The FDA is in steady communication with industry partners and regulatory counterparts to assist during this time. The agency is confident in its ability to maintain oversight during the pandemic, leveraging all available authorities and alternative tools.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Takes New Actions to Accelerate Development of Novel Prevention, Treatment Options for COVID-19
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has provided new guidance to help accelerate the development of prevention and treatment options for COVID-19. The guidance documents aim to make the process for submitting applications to initiate studies for new drugs and biological products more efficient. FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn, M.D., stated that accelerating the development of safe and effective therapies is one of the FDA's highest priorities.

The FDA has been working directly with federal health partners, academia, and industry to advance medical countermeasures against COVID-19. The agency has launched the Coronavirus Treatment Acceleration Program to help move new medical products to patients as soon as possible. Over 130 clinical trials of potential COVID-19 related drugs and biological products are currently underway, and additional development programs are in the planning stages.

The guidances issued today outline recommendations for ways to design clinical trials to evaluate safety and effectiveness of these medical products. The guidance documents are supplemented by a variety of ongoing activities and broad agency guidance to support innovative study designs. The FDA is engaged in a public-private partnership with the National Institutes of Health and others to speed the development of COVID-19 vaccine and treatment options.

title: The President's News Conference
body_summary: The US President announces an update on the country's coronavirus testing capacity, stating that the US has developed the most advanced and robust testing system in the world. The President announces new steps to make tests more widely available, including sending $1 billion to states and territories. He credits doctors, nurses, workers, and the American people for their efforts, predicting a strong third quarter, excellent fourth quarter, and a record-breaking year for the US. The President also discusses COVID-19 testing, highlighting the White House's great testing capability and warning against China's attempts to steal vaccine technology. He assures parents that most children recover from a rare syndrome affecting 85 children, with 3 deaths, and credits early action for saving hundreds of thousands of lives. The President claims that 20,000 new cases and 1,000 deaths occur daily despite plateauing cases.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes First Antigen Test to Help in the Rapid Detection of the Virus that Causes COVID-19 in Patients
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued the first emergency use authorization (EUA) for a COVID-19 antigen test, a new category of tests for use in the ongoing pandemic. The EUA was issued late Friday to Quidel Corporation for the Sofia 2 SARS Antigen FIA test, authorized for use in high and moderate complexity laboratories certified by Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments (CLIA), as well as for point-of-care testing by facilities operating under a CLIA Certificate of Waiver. This is the second EUA issued by the FDA for COVID-19 diagnostic tests, following the issuance of EUAs for polymerase chain reaction (PCR) tests and serological tests. Antigen tests, which detect fragments of proteins found on or within the virus, can provide rapid results in minutes, but may not detect all active infections and have a higher chance of false negatives. The FDA anticipates issuing an EUA template for antigen tests to help manufacturers streamline submissions and expedite review and issuance of additional EUAs.

title: FDA Approves First Therapy for Patients with Lung and Thyroid Cancers with a Certain Genetic Mutation or Fusion
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Retevmo (selpercatinib) capsules to treat three types of tumors: non-small cell lung cancer, medullary thyroid cancer, and other types of thyroid cancers. The FDA approved Retevmo specifically for patients with RET gene alterations. The cancer types that Retevmo is approved to treat include non-small cell lung cancer, advanced medullary thyroid cancer, and advanced RET fusion-positive thyroid cancer. The medication is a kinase inhibitor that blocks a type of enzyme and helps prevent cancer cells from growing. The FDA approved Retevmo based on the results of a clinical trial involving patients with each of the three types of tumors. The approval was granted under the Accelerated Approval pathway, Priority Review, and Breakthrough Therapy designation. Retevmo was approved for patients 12 years of age and older who require systemic therapy.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 8, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration authorized the first diagnostic test with the option of using home-collected saliva samples for COVID-19 testing. Specifically, the FDA issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) to Rutgers Clinical Genomics Laboratory for their COVID-19 laboratory-developed test (LDT), which had been previously authorized under the high complexity molecular-based LDT "umbrella" EUA, to permit testing of samples self-collected by patients at home using the Spectrum Solutions LLC SDNA-1000 Saliva Collection Device. The FDA issued two documents to assist retail food establishments that might have been closed or partially closed during the COVID-19 pandemic in preparing to reopen. The agency also issued warning letters to four companies for selling fraudulent COVID-19 products, including non-alcohol-based hand sanitizer products and CBD products with misleading claims. The FDA approved an abbreviated new drug application for lidocaine hydrochloride injection USP, 1%, and issued EUAs for the Duke Decontamination System and other diagnostic tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes First Diagnostic Test Using At-Home Collection of Saliva Specimens
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has authorized the first diagnostic test that allows for home-collected saliva samples for COVID-19 testing. The test, developed by Rutgers Clinical Genomics Laboratory, uses the Spectrum Solutions LLC SDNA-1000 Saliva Collection Device. This authorization builds on a previous EUA for a nasal swab test with a home-collection option. FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn stated that authorizing more at-home test options increases patient access to testing without traveling to a doctor's office. The Rutgers test is the only authorized COVID-19 diagnostic test using saliva samples to test for SARS-CoV-2. This authorization is limited to testing performed at the Rutgers Clinical Genomics Laboratory.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Continues to Combat Fraudulent COVID-19 Medical Products
body_summary: The US FDA is taking steps to combat companies and individuals selling unproven medical products claiming to mitigate, prevent, treat, diagnose or cure COVID-19. The agency has issued 42 warning letters to companies making bogus claims and has taken action against sellers of fraudulent products, including chlorine dioxide products and "Miracle Mineral Solution". The FDA has also discovered hundreds of such products sold online with unproven claims as part of Operation Quack Hack. The agency is working with online marketplaces, domain name registrars, and social media websites to remove these products from their platforms. The FDA has sent hundreds of abuse complaints to domain name registrars and internet marketplaces, who have voluntarily removed the identified postings. The agency encourages anyone aware of suspected fraudulent medical products for COVID-19 to report them. The FDA has also intercepted and investigated cases of mislabeled COVID-19 "treatment kits" and brought a criminal complaint against a British man who sought to profit from the pandemic and jeopardize public health.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 7, 2020
body_summary: The FDA has taken actions to combat scams selling unproven COVID-19 products. Two companies, Alive By Nature, Inc. and GlutaGenic, have been warned for selling fraudulent products claiming to prevent or treat COVID-19. The FDA issued Emergency Use Authorizations (EUA) to Sherlock BioSciences, Inc.'s CRISPR SARS-CoV-2 Kit and reissued EUA for non-NIOSH-approved respirators manufactured in China. The agency has issued 63 individual EUAs for test kit manufacturers and laboratories, adding 25 authorized tests for high complexity molecular-based laboratory developed tests. The FDA has worked with over 385 test developers and over 245 laboratories to implement their COVID-19 Policy, enabling the use of authorized tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 6, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA issued an immediately in effect guidance to notify the Center for Devices and Radiological Health of a permanent discontinuance or interruption in manufacturing of a device under Section 506J of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. The guidance is intended to help the Agency prevent or mitigate shortages of certain medical devices. On May 11, 2020, the FDA will host a webinar for medical device manufacturers and others to learn more about the guidance. To date, the FDA has issued 60 individual EUAs for test kit manufacturers and laboratories, and 25 authorized tests have been added to the EUA letter of authorization for high complexity molecular-based laboratory developed tests. The FDA has also notified more than 240 laboratories that have begun testing under the agency's COVID-19 policy for diagnostic tests.

title: FDA approves new treatment for a type of heart failure
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Farxiga (dapagliflozin) oral tablets for adults with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization. The approval, given Priority Review designation, aims to significantly improve the safety or effectiveness of treating heart failure. Farxiga, the first SGLT2 inhibitor to be approved for this condition, was shown to improve survival and reduce hospitalization in a clinical trial involving 4,744 participants. The drug's effectiveness was evaluated in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study. Farxiga can cause dehydration, urinary tract infections, and genital yeast infections, and its use requires careful assessment of patients' volume status and kidney function. The approval was granted to AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals LP.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 4, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA has issued a revised policy on antibody tests for COVID-19, which prioritizes access and accuracy. The agency has also issued warning letters to operators of two websites that market unapproved COVID-19 products. The FDA has authorized the first serology test with scientific evidence from a new independent validation effort. The testing was performed at the Frederick National Laboratory for Cancer Research, and the results were validated by a collaborative effort with the NIH, CDC, and Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority. The FDA has issued 58 individual Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) requests for test kit manufacturers and laboratories, and has added 25 authorized tests to the EUA letter of authorization for high complexity molecular-based laboratory developed tests. The agency continues to work with over 380 test developers and has issued a COVID-19 Diagnostics FAQ. The FDA is part of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and is responsible for protecting the public health and safety of the nation's food supply and other products.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup May 1, 2020
body_summary: The FDA has issued several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. An Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) has been granted for remdesivir, an investigational antiviral drug, to treat severe COVID-19 in adults and children hospitalized with low blood oxygen levels or requiring oxygen therapy. The FDA has also updated its guidance on convalescent plasma and added a new webpage for investigators. In addition, the FDA has issued EUAs for several diagnostic tests, including tests from more than 380 test developers, and has updated its COVID-19 Diagnostics FAQ. The FDA has also issued an EUA for the Fresenius Medical Care multiFiltrate PRO System and multiBic/multiPlus Solutions to treat continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) shortages.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Issues Emergency Use Authorization for Potential COVID-19 Treatment
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued an emergency use authorization for the investigational antiviral drug remdesivir to treat suspected or laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 in adults and children hospitalized with severe disease. The authorization was granted based on a clinical trial showing promising results, two days after the National Institutes of Health's trial. The FDA allowed for remdesivir to be distributed and administered intravenously to treat severe COVID-19 cases. The EUA requires fact sheets with important information about using remdesivir, including dosing instructions and potential side effects. The drug may have increased liver enzyme levels and infusion-related reactions as possible side effects. The EUA was issued to Gilead Sciences Inc. and is effective until terminated or revised.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 30, 2020
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, including:

The FDA has added a ventilator developed by NASA to the list of authorized ventilators for treating patients with COVID-19. The ventilator, known as VITAL, is designed to last three to four months and provides respiratory support for patients experiencing respiratory failure or insufficiency.

The FDA has also issued a guidance on flexibility under the Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA) to facilitate the distribution of prescription drug products needed to respond to COVID-19.

The FDA has issued 53 emergency use authorizations for test kit manufacturers and laboratories, and 23 authorized tests have been added to the EUA letter of authorization for high complexity molecular-based laboratory developed tests (LDTs).

The agency has been working with over 380 test developers to submit emergency use authorizations for tests that detect the virus.

The FDA continues to monitor and update its COVID-19 Diagnostics FAQ and COVID-19 Policy for Diagnostic Tests for Coronavirus Disease-2019 during the Public Health Emergency Guidance.

The FDA is responsible for protecting the public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices, as well as regulating the nation's food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, and tobacco products.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Includes Ventilator Developed by NASA in Ventilator Emergency Use Authorization
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) added a ventilator developed by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) to the list of authorized ventilators under the ventilator emergency use authorization (EUA) issued in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The ventilator, called VITAL, is tailored to treat patients with COVID-19 and is intended to last three to four months. It provides respiratory support for patients experiencing respiratory failure or insufficiency and can be built with components outside the current medical device supply chain. The FDA Commissioner, Stephen M. Hahn, and NASA Administrator, Jim Bridenstine, praised the initiative, which demonstrates the potential for innovation and collaboration during a crisis. The FDA continues to engage with stakeholders to facilitate the ramping up of production of ventilators. The EUA allows for the emergency use of certain ventilators, anesthesia gas machines, and other devices in healthcare settings.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The Federal Reserve is committed to using its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time, thereby promoting its maximum employment and price stability goals. The coronavirus outbreak is causing tremendous human and economic hardship across the United States and around the world. The virus and the measures taken to protect public health are inducing sharp declines in economic activity and a surge in job losses. Weaker demand and significantly lower oil prices are holding down consumer price inflation. The disruptions to economic activity here and abroad have significantly affected financial conditions and have impaired the flow of credit to U.S. households and businesses. The ongoing public health crisis will weigh heavily on economic activity, employment, and inflation in the near term, and poses considerable risks to the economic outlook over the medium term. In light of these developments, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent. The Committee expects to maintain this target range until it is confident that the economy has weathered recent events and is on track to achieve its maximum employment and price stability goals. The Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook, including information related to public health, as well as global developments and muted inflation pressures, and will use its tools and act as appropriate to support the economy. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the stance of monetary policy, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. To support the flow of credit to households and businesses, the Federal Reserve will continue to purchase Treasury securities and agency residential and commercial mortgage-backed securities in the amounts needed to support smooth market functioning, thereby fostering effective transmission of monetary policy to broader financial conditions. In addition, the Open Market Desk will continue to offer large-scale overnight and term repurchase agreement operations. The Committee will closely monitor market conditions and is prepared to adjust its plans as appropriate. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Patrick Harker; Robert S. Kaplan; Neel Kashkari; Loretta J. Mester; and Randal K. Quarles.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 29, 2020
body_summary: The FDA issued a Consumer Update with tips on good nutrition and using the updated Nutrition Facts label during the pandemic. The agency also issued an injunction halting the sale of various silver products promoted as COVID-19 treatments. The FDA granted accelerated approval for a new cancer therapy regimen, allowing patients to visit cancer centers less often. Additionally, the FDA issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for SARS-CoV-2 Antibody Tests, which have been validated by the National Institutes of Health's National Cancer Institute. The FDA has issued 50 EUAs for test kit manufacturers and laboratories, and 23 authorized tests have been added to the EUA letter of authorization. The agency has worked with over 380 test developers to submit EUA requests and has notified more than 235 laboratories that have begun testing under the COVID-19 Policy for Diagnostic Tests.

title: FDA Grants Marketing of New Device for Continuous Dialysis Therapy for use in Pediatric Patients with Certain Kidney Conditions
body_summary:
The US FDA has granted marketing authorization for the CARPEDIEM System, a new device for continuous hemodialysis or hemofiltration therapy in pediatric patients weighing 2.5 to 10 kilograms. This therapy is indicated for critically ill pediatric patients with acute kidney injury or fluid overload. The device was designed to address the unmet need for pediatric patients with smaller weights. 

Data from an independent registry showed a 97% survival rate to discontinuation of CRRT in patients treated with the CARPEDIEM System, compared to a 48% survival rate in patients treated with currently cleared devices. The survival rate at discharge from the ICU was 55% in patients treated with the CARPEDIEM System. 

Potential complications include weight scale alarm, low blood pressure, air in the dialysis circuit, and high pressure in the blood filter. A post-approval study will document real-world treatments of the device in the US. The FDA granted marketing authorization to Medtronic Inc.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 28, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA issued a new video resource explaining Emergency Use Authorizations (EUAs), which provide timely access to critical medical products. The agency also warned two companies, Hopewell Essential Oils and Santiste Labs LLC, for selling fraudulent COVID-19 products with misleading claims. The FDA has issued 50 emergency use authorizations for test kit manufacturers and laboratories, and has authorized 22 high complexity molecular-based laboratory developed tests. The agency has worked with over 380 test developers to submit EUA requests, and has updated its COVID-19 Diagnostics FAQ. The FDA protects the public health by ensuring the safety and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, medical devices, and other products.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 27, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA has issued a statement to increase the availability of alcohol-based hand sanitizer and to warn consumers about hand sanitizer with fraudulent claims. Calls to the National Poison Data System related to hand sanitizer have increased by 79 percent compared to March 2019. The FDA has also developed fact sheets to help answer questions from the food and agriculture sector about respirators and cloth face coverings. The agency has updated its Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) for face masks and posted FAQs on the EUA for face masks. To date, the FDA has issued 49 individual EUAs for test kit manufacturers and laboratories, and 21 authorized tests have been added to the EUA letter of authorization for high complexity molecular-based laboratory developed tests. The FDA has also notified over 225 laboratories that they can begin testing under its COVID-19 Policy for Diagnostic Tests for Coronavirus Disease-2019.

title: FDA Provides Updates on Adverse Event Reports and Postmarket Activities Associated with Essure
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a letter to Bayer outlining conditions for submitting additional postmarket information about Essure, a permanent birth control device. Bayer must start providing reportable adverse events to the FDA in July 2020 and submit monthly updates. The FDA will make these events publicly available on its Problems Reported with Essure webpage. Bayer must also submit summaries of reportable events, including patient demographics, to the FDA's MAUDE database. This variance will expire after one year, unless extended, and Bayer will be required to follow regular adverse event reporting requirements for all Essure-associated reportable events. The FDA is committed to ensuring public health safety and will make all submitted events publicly available.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Reiterates Importance of Close Patient Supervision for ‘Off-Label’ Use of Antimalarial Drugs to Mitigate Known Risks, Including Heart Rhythm Problems
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a Drug Safety Communication regarding known side effects of hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine, including serious and potentially life-threatening heart rhythm problems, when used for treating or preventing COVID-19. The risks may be mitigated when health care professionals closely screen and supervise patients. 

FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn stated that the agency is providing appropriate information for health care professionals to make medical decisions. The FDA has issued an Emergency Use Authorization to allow hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine products donated to the Strategic National Stockpile to be distributed in limited circumstances. 

These drugs are FDA-approved to treat malaria and certain autoimmune diseases, but not for COVID-19. Clinical trials are ongoing to determine their safety and effectiveness for COVID-19. The FDA requires that fact sheets with important information about using these drugs in treating COVID-19 be made available to health care providers and patients.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 24, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA issued an immediately in effect guidance to expand the availability of remote digital pathology devices, which may help facilitate continuity of patient care. The agency also issued a Drug Safety Communication regarding known side effects of hydroxychloroquine and chloroquine, warning of serious heart rhythm problems. The FDA warned a seller of fraudulent COVID-19 products, Prefense LLC, which offered unapproved and misbranded hand sanitizer products. The agency has issued 44 emergency use authorizations for test kits and added 19 authorized tests to its list. The FDA has worked with over 380 test developers and notified more than 225 laboratories that they are testing under its COVID-19 policy. The agency protects the public health by ensuring the safety and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices, as well as regulating tobacco products.

title: FDA Warns Companies Illegally Selling CBD Products to Treat Medical Conditions, Opioid Addiction
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued warning letters to two companies, BIOTA Biosciences, LLC and Homero Corp DBA Natures CBD Oil Distribution, for illegally selling unapproved products containing cannabidiol (CBD) that claim to treat medical conditions, including opioid addiction. The FDA is cracking down on companies that make unfounded treatment claims, with FDA Principal Deputy Commissioner Amy Abernethy stating that CBD has not been shown to treat opioid addiction. The two companies were found to market products as a treatment for serious diseases and as an alternative to opioids. The FDA has not approved any CBD products other than one prescription human drug product to treat rare, severe forms of epilepsy. The companies have been warned to correct their violations within 15 working days, or face legal action, including product seizure and/or injunction.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 23, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued guidelines to increase the availability and capability of non-invasive fetal and maternal monitoring devices, fetal dopplers, and imaging systems needed for lung disease diagnosis and treatment during the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA has also issued temporary policy flexibility for foreign food entities and their products, and has updated its Best Practices for Retail Food Stores, Restaurants, and Food Pick-Up/Delivery Services During the COVID-19 Pandemic. To date, the FDA has issued 44 emergency use authorizations for test kit manufacturers and laboratories, and has authorized 18 high complexity molecular-based laboratory developed tests. The agency has worked with over 360 test developers to submit emergency use authorization requests for COVID-19 tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Court Grants FDA’s Request for Extension of Premarket Review Submission Deadline for Certain Tobacco Products Because of Impacts from COVID-19
body_summary: The United States District Court for the District of Maryland ordered the FDA to require manufacturers of e-cigarettes, cigars, and other deemed new tobacco products to submit applications for premarket review by May 12, 2020. Due to the coronavirus pandemic, the FDA requested a 120-day extension of the deadline, which was granted. The new deadline for applications is now September 9, 2020. This extension allows manufacturers to prepare for the premarket review process without compromising employee health or risking the spread of COVID-19. The FDA also stated that they will continue to monitor and take action against e-cigarette products on the market, including those subject to enforcement actions, while also prioritizing enforcement against certain products widely used by youth.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 22, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has taken several actions in its response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA issued emergency use authorization for the Philips IntelliVue Patient Monitors MX750/MX850, IntelliVue 4-Slot Module Rack FMX-4 and IntelliVue Active Displays AD75/AD85 to be used in hospitals for remote monitoring of COVID-19 patients. The agency also issued a warning letter to Copper Touch, LLC, for selling unapproved and misbranded COVID-19 products. Additionally, the FDA issued guidance on the repackaging of propofol injectable emulsion for hospitalized patients during the pandemic. The FDA has issued 43 emergency use authorizations for test kit manufacturers and laboratories, and has notified over 215 laboratories of their COVID-19 diagnostic testing policies. The FDA continues to protect the public health by regulating food, cosmetics, dietary supplements, electronic radiation products, and tobacco products.

title: FDA Approves New Therapy for Triple Negative Breast Cancer That Has Spread, Not Responded to Other Treatments
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted accelerated approval to Trodelvy (sacituzumab govitecan-hziy) for the treatment of adult patients with triple-negative breast cancer that has spread to other parts of the body. This approval represents a new targeted therapy for patients living with this aggressive malignancy. The approval was based on the results of a clinical trial involving 108 patients with metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. The overall response rate was 33.3%, with 55.6% of patients maintaining their response for 6 or more months. Trodelvy targets the Trop-2 receptor and is linked to a topoisomerase inhibitor. The FDA approved Trodelvy based on its potential to provide a new treatment option for patients who have received at least two prior therapies.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 21, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA authorized the first diagnostic test with an at-home sample collection option for COVID-19, allowing patients to collect and mail their own nasal samples for testing. Additionally, the FDA issued an emergency use authorization for the Sterilucent HC 80TT Hydrogen Peroxide Sterilizer to decontaminate compatible N95 respirators for single-user reuse. The agency has also provided flexibility to the food industry to support the food supply chain and meet consumer demand, and approved an Abbreviated New Drug Application for Albuterol Sulfate Inhalation Solution. To date, the FDA has issued 42 emergency use authorizations for test kit manufacturers and laboratories, and over 210 laboratories have begun testing under the FDA's COVID-19 policy.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes First Test for Patient At-Home Sample Collection
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has authorized the first diagnostic test with a home collection option for COVID-19. The FDA has re-issued the emergency use authorization for LabCorp's COVID-19 RT-PCR Test, allowing patients to collect and mail their own nasal swab samples using the Pixel by LabCorp COVID-19 Test home collection kit. The authorization enables patients to collect their own samples at home and mail them to a LabCorp lab for testing. The test is available to consumers in most states with a doctor's order, and LabCorp plans to distribute the kits in the coming weeks. The FDA worked with LabCorp to ensure the test is safe and accurate for at-home collection.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Serological Test Validation and Education Efforts
body_summary: The FDA is working to make serological tests for COVID-19 widely available while ensuring accuracy and reliability. The agency has issued four emergency use authorizations (EUA) for serological tests and is streamlining the review process. The FDA is collaborating with the National Institutes of Health and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to evaluate serological tests, with performance assessments expected to begin soon. The agency has provided regulatory flexibility for serological tests, allowing developers to market and use them without prior review. The FDA is also taking action against firms making or distributing unvalidated COVID-19 tests, issuing Warning Letters and detaining fraudulent test kits, and sharing educational materials with state governments and healthcare professionals.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Federal judge enters temporary injunction against Genesis II Church of Health and Healing, preventing sale of Chlorine Dioxide Products Equivalent to Industrial Bleach to Treat COVID-19
body_summary: A federal court has entered a temporary injunction against the Genesis II Church of Health and Healing and four individuals associated with the entity, requiring them to immediately stop distributing its "Miracle Mineral Solution" (MMS), an unproven treatment for Coronavirus, COVID-19, and other diseases. The court found that the defendants are violating the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act by unlawfully distributing MMS, which has a chlorine dioxide content equivalent to industrial bleach. The FDA has warned consumers numerous times not to purchase or drink chlorine dioxide products, and the agency has received reports of serious adverse events after consuming such products. The temporary restraining order is in effect until May 1st, 2020, and there will be a hearing on the government's request to extend the injunction on that date.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 17, 2020
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. A public-private partnership, the Accelerating COVID-19 Therapeutic Interventions and Vaccines (ACTIV) partnership, has been formed with the National Institutes of Health, the European Medicines Agency, and over a dozen biopharmaceutical companies to speed the development of COVID-19 vaccine and treatment options. The partnership aims to develop a collaborative framework for prioritizing vaccine and drug candidates, streamlining clinical trials, and coordinating regulatory processes.
