The FDA has issued temporary injunctions against the Genesis II Church of Health and Healing and four individuals associated with the entity, requiring them to stop distributing the "Miracle Mineral Solution" (MMS), an unproven and potentially harmful treatment. The FDA has warned consumers numerous times not to purchase or drink chlorine dioxide products, such as MMS, sold as medical treatments.

The FDA has also issued warnings against a seller of fraudulent COVID-19 products, Nova Botanix LTD DBA CanaBD, which sells unapproved and misbranded cannabidiol (CBD) products with misleading claims. The FDA has expanded COVID-19 testing options, including the use of spun synthetic swabs, and issued an emergency use authorization for an extracorporeal blood purification device to treat patients with confirmed COVID-19. The FDA has issued emergency use authorizations for over 39 test kit manufacturers and laboratories and added 16 high complexity molecular-based laboratory developed tests to its authorization list.

title: FDA Approves First Targeted Treatment for Patients with Cholangiocarcinoma, a Cancer of Bile Ducts
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted accelerated approval to Pemazyre (pemigatinib), the first treatment approved for adults with certain types of previously treated, advanced cholangiocarcinoma. 

Pemazyre was approved for patients with locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma with an FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement who had received prior treatment. The approval was based on a clinical trial with 107 patients, who received Pemazyre once a day for 14 consecutive days, followed by 7 days off, in 21-day cycles until the disease progressed or the patient experienced an unreasonable level of side effects. 

The overall response rate was 36%, with 2.8% of patients having a complete response and 33% having a partial response. The most common adverse reactions were hyperphosphatemia, alopecia, diarrhea, and nausea. The FDA granted this application Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy designation, and approved it to Incyte Corporation.

title: FDA Approves First New Drug Under International Collaboration, A Treatment Option for Patients with HER2-Positive Metastatic Breast Cancer
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Tukysa (tucatinib) for the treatment of adult patients with advanced forms of HER2-positive breast cancer that cannot be removed with surgery or has spread to other parts of the body, including the brain, in combination with chemotherapy (trastuzumab and capecitabine). The approval is part of Project Orbis, a collaboration between the FDA and international regulators, including the Australian Therapeutic Goods Administration, Health Canada, Health Sciences Authority, Singapore, and Swissmedic. The approval was granted four months prior to the FDA's goal date, demonstrating the agency's commitment to expedite oncology product development. Tukysa is a kinase inhibitor that blocks a type of enzyme and helps prevent cancer cells from growing. The clinical trial supporting this approval enrolled 612 patients and showed a median progression-free survival of 7.8 months, compared to 5.6 months in patients who received placebo. Common side effects of Tukysa include diarrhea, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, nausea, fatigue, and hepatotoxicity.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA, Gates Foundation, UnitedHealth Group, Quantigen, and U.S. Cotton Collaborate to Address Testing Supply Needs
body_summary: The US FDA has expanded COVID-19 testing options by recognizing spun synthetic swabs, similar to Q-tips, for nasal testing. US Cotton, a subsidiary of Parkdale-Mills, has developed a fully synthetic polyester-based Q-tip-type swab for compatibility with COVID-19 testing. The FDA, in partnership with industry partners including UnitedHealth Group, Quantigen, and the Gates Foundation, has conducted clinical studies that support the use of these swabs. The swabs allow for self-collection, limiting healthcare provider exposure, and are more comfortable for patients. The FDA plans to produce these swabs in large quantities to meet diagnostic testing needs.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Continues User-Fee Related Reviews Through COVID-19
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) continues to execute its user fee review activities while responding to the public health needs of the COVID-19 pandemic. The agency's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research and Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research staff are working diligently to address challenges and carry out their duty to safeguard public health. The New Drug Program, Generic Drug Program, and Biologics and Biosimilars Programs are meeting key review program user fee performance goals, approving applications, and communicating with applicants. The agency is taking steps to minimize disruptions, including extending response due dates for certain applications. The FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health is also meeting its Medical Device User Fee Amendments review goals, but may face challenges in sustaining its current level of performance due to increased workload. The agency's staff are working at full capacity, and if shortages and supply disruptions increase, they will be ready to reprioritize work as necessary.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 16, 2020
body_summary: The US FDA has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The agency has encouraged recovered patients to donate convalescent plasma to help others fight the disease. A new webpage has been launched to guide patients to local blood or plasma collection centers. The FDA has issued warning letters to companies distributing unapproved chloroquine phosphate products, which are intended for aquarium fish, and warned consumers not to take these products without a prescription. The agency has also issued a warning letter to a seller of fraudulent COVID-19 products. The FDA has posted tips for shopping for food during the pandemic and has updated guidance on outsourcing facilities to compound certain human drugs. Additionally, the agency has issued guidance on conducting clinical trials during the pandemic and has updated its COVID-19 Diagnostics FAQ. The FDA has also issued temporary policies for outsourcing facilities and has added content to its guidance on clinical trials.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Encourages Recovered Patients to Donate Plasma for Development of Blood-Related Therapies
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is working with partners to expedite the development and availability of convalescent plasma, a potential treatment for COVID-19, made from blood donated by recovered individuals. Convalescent plasma has the potential to lessen the severity of COVID-19. The FDA has expanded access to convalescent plasma through a protocol led by the Mayo Clinic, and numerous clinical trials are underway to evaluate its safety and efficacy. The FDA has launched a new webpage to guide recovered COVID-19 patients to local plasma collection centers, and the American Red Cross has set up a website for interested donors. Recovered COVID-19 patients can donate plasma, which can help up to four patients, and people who have fully recovered for at least two weeks can contact local collection centers to schedule an appointment.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 15, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued two new emergency use authorizations for serology tests to detect coronavirus antibodies to Ortho-Clinical Diagnostics, Inc. and Chembio Diagnostic Systems, Inc. The FDA has also issued an emergency use authorization for the decontamination cycle of Stryker Instrument's Sterizone VP4 Sterilizer for reusing N95 respirators. The agency has posted a new "At-a-Glance Summary" capturing its major activities in the fight against COVID-19. The FDA has issued guidance on digital health devices for treating psychiatric disorders and warned a company, Earth Angel Oils, for selling unapproved and misbranded COVID-19 products. To date, 36 emergency use authorizations have been issued for COVID-19 tests, and over 190 laboratories have begun testing under the agency's COVID-19 Policy for Diagnostic Tests.

title: The President's News Conference
body_summary: US President instructs his administration to halt funding for the World Health Organization (WHO) while reviewing its role in the coronavirus pandemic, citing mismanagement and opposition to travel restrictions from China. The US has successfully ramped up ventilator production, with 150,000 units manufactured and a stockpile of 10,000 ventilators ready for emergency use. The President announces a Dynamic Ventilator Reserve to lend unused ventilators to areas of need. He also thanks hospital leaders for their help and announces a list of industries and companies to be contacted over the next 24 hours. The President discusses the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act, saying it's helped small businesses stay open, with hundreds of thousands of loan applications approved. An investigation is underway regarding the World Health Organization's handling of the coronavirus, and the President vows to enforce a "Slow the Spread" policy, citing progress in testing and a goal to open up to 100,000 fewer deaths than projected.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 13, 2020
body_summary:
The US FDA has announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA is taking steps to ensure a stable supply of chloroquine phosphate and hydroxychloroquine sulfate, releasing product-specific guidances to support generic drug development. The FDA is prioritizing review of Abbreviated New Drug Applications for these drugs under MAPP 5240.3.

The FDA has also issued a Consumer Update on how to make a difference during the pandemic, and added new questions and answers to its webpage on hand sanitizers and COVID-19. The agency has issued emergency use authorizations for various medical devices, including the Perfusor Space Syringe Infusion Pump System and the ASP STERRAD Sterilization Systems, to help increase the availability of respirators and diagnostic tests.

To date, the FDA has issued 34 emergency use authorizations for diagnostic tests, and over 300 test developers have said they will submit EUA requests. The FDA has also notified over 180 laboratories that they are allowed to test under its COVID-19 Policy for Diagnostic Tests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Issues Emergency Use Authorization to Decontaminate Millions of N95 Respirators
body_summary: The US FDA issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for Advanced Sterilization Products (ASP) to decontaminate 4 million N95 respirators per day in hospital settings. FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn granted the EUA for ASP's STERRAD Sterilization Cycles, which use vaporized hydrogen peroxide gas plasma sterilization. The authorization will provide access to millions of respirators for healthcare workers, increasing their protection against COVID-19. There are approximately 9,930 STERRAD systems in 6,300 hospitals across the US, with each system capable of reprocessing 480 respirators per day.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Authorizes Blood Purification Device to Treat COVID-19
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued an emergency use authorization for a blood purification system to treat patients 18 years of age or older with confirmed COVID-19 admitted to the ICU with respiratory failure. The authorized product works by reducing cytokines and other inflammatory mediators. The FDA has authorized the use of the Spectra Optia Apheresis System and Depuro D2000 Adsorption Cartridge devices, developed by Terumo BCT Inc. and Marker Therapeutics AG. Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn stated that the FDA will continue to expedite the development and availability of treatments for COVID-19. The FDA has also noted its responsibility for protecting the public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of medical devices.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Issues Second Emergency Use Authorization to Decontaminate N95 Respirators
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued its second emergency use authorization to decontaminate compatible N95 respirators for reuse by health care workers in hospital settings. This EUA supports decontamination of approximately 750,000 N95 respirators per day in the U.S. HHS Secretary Alex Azar stated that authorizing this sterilization system will provide hospitals with the protection they need for healthcare workers on the frontlines. FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn granted an emergency use authorization to STERIS Corporation for its N95 Decontamination Cycle, a low-temperature sterilization process using vaporized hydrogen peroxide. The STERIS V-PRO Decontamination Cycle can process 10 respirators at one time, taking approximately 28 minutes to complete. The FDA will continue to work to mitigate the COVID-19 pandemic and help increase the supply of essential medical devices.

title: FDA Approves First Therapy for Children with Debilitating and Disfiguring Rare Disease
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Koselugo (selumetinib) for the treatment of pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), a genetic disorder causing tumors on nerves. Koselugo is the first FDA-approved drug to treat this rare disease, which typically begins early in life. The approval is based on a clinical trial showing a 66% overall response rate, with all patients experiencing a partial response. The FDA granted this application Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy designation, and awarded a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher. Koselugo is approved for patients with symptomatic, inoperable plexiform neurofibromas, and can cause serious side effects including heart failure and ocular toxicity. The FDA advises healthcare professionals to use effective contraception during treatment with Koselugo, particularly for females of reproductive age.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 10, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA recently issued emergency use authorizations (EUA) for a blood purification system and decontamination methods to treat patients with confirmed or imminent respiratory failure, and for decontaminating compatible N95 respirators for reuse. The FDA also issued guidance for pharmacy compounders experiencing shortages of personal protective equipment (PPE) and provided limited regulatory flexibility to adopt risk mitigation strategies. The agency has issued warning letters to companies selling fraudulent COVID-19 products, and has taken steps to protect consumers. The FDA has issued several EUAs for diagnostic tests, and continues to work with test developers and laboratories to ensure the availability of tests. The agency is responsible for protecting the public health by assuring the safety and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, medical devices, and other products.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 9, 2020
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA has outlined a temporary policy to expand the availability of portable cryogenic oxygen and nitrogen containers, allowing firms that fill and distribute these containers to take certain safeguards to prevent gas mix-ups. This guidance will be in effect until the end of the public health emergency.

The FDA has also issued information and best practices for retail food stores, restaurants, and pick-up and delivery services to protect workers and customers. Additionally, the FDA has updated its information on safety protections regarding the use of Fecal Microbiota for Transplantation (FMT) due to the risk of transmission of SARS-CoV-2 through FMT.

The FDA has issued a warning letter to one company, Free Speech Systems LLC, for selling fraudulent COVID-19 products. The FDA has issued emergency use authorizations for 32 diagnostic tests and has notified over 150 laboratories to begin testing under its COVID-19 Policy for Diagnostic Tests.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held meetings in March 2020 to address financial market volatility amid the global coronavirus spread. Markets remained volatile, with the S&P 500 index declining 18% and Treasury yields moving lower. The committee expected to reduce the federal funds rate by 1 percentage point at its next meeting and potentially announce additional Treasury and agency mortgage-backed securities purchases. Trading conditions were strained across markets. The Federal Reserve lowered its target range for the federal funds rate by 100 basis points to 0-1/4 percent, increased its holdings of Treasury securities by $500 billion and agency MBS by $200 billion, and decided to reinvest all principal payments from agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities in agency mortgage-backed securities. The committee voted to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 50 basis points to 1-1/4 percent due to concerns about the coronavirus's potential impact on economic activity, employment, and price stability.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 8, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has taken actions to protect consumers and animals from fraudulent COVID-19 products. Three sellers, Genesis II Church of Health and Healing, Savvy Holistic Health dba Holistic Healthy Pet, and CBD Online Store, have been warned for selling products with false or misleading claims. The FDA has issued guidance on the administration and study of convalescent plasma to patients seriously ill with COVID-19. The agency has also issued emergency use authorizations for 31 diagnostic tests and notified over 150 laboratories that they can begin testing under its COVID-19 policy.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Warns Seller Marketing Dangerous Chlorine Dioxide Products that Claim to Treat or Prevent COVID-19
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a warning letter to a seller marketing fraudulent chlorine dioxide products known as "Miracle Mineral Solution" for the prevention and treatment of COVID-19. The FDA has previously warned consumers not to purchase or drink chlorine dioxide products sold online as medical treatments due to the lack of scientific evidence supporting their safety and effectiveness. The agency is taking action to protect Americans and has issued a joint warning letter with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to the Genesis II Church of Health and Healing for selling chlorine dioxide products that fraudulently claim to treat or prevent COVID-19. The FDA has received reports of serious adverse events, including respiratory failure, life-threatening low blood pressure, and acute liver failure, after consuming these products. The agency is urging consumers to seek medical help from their healthcare providers and to report any adverse events or quality problems experienced with COVID-19 products to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program.

title: FDA Approves First Generic of a Commonly Used Albuterol Inhaler to Treat and Prevent Bronchospasm
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the first generic version of Proventil HFA (albuterol sulfate) Metered Dose Inhaler, 90 mcg/Inhalation, for the treatment or prevention of bronchospasm in patients four years of age and older with reversible obstructive airway disease, as well as the prevention of exercise-induced bronchospasm in this age group. The approval was granted to Cipla Limited. The FDA Commissioner, Stephen M. Hahn, M.D., stated that the agency recognizes the increased demand for albuterol products during the novel coronavirus pandemic and remains committed to facilitating access to medical products to address critical needs. The generic product is intended for use in patients with asthma and other conditions that cause bronchospasm, with common side effects including upper respiratory tract infection, rhinitis, and rapid heart rate. The FDA regularly guides industry through the development process for generic products, including metered dose inhalers, and requires applicants to submit data and information to demonstrate that these products meet the agency's rigorous approval standards.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Serological Tests
body_summary: Serological tests measure the body's immune response to COVID-19 by detecting antibodies or proteins in the blood. These tests are not effective for diagnosing COVID-19, especially in the early stages of an infection. However, they can help identify individuals who have overcome an infection and have developed an immune response. In the future, these tests may be used to determine if individuals are no longer susceptible to infection and can return to work. The tests can also aid in determining who can donate convalescent plasma, which may serve as a treatment for those seriously ill from COVID-19. The FDA has issued a policy allowing developers to market or use their tests once they have performed evaluation to determine accuracy and reliability. Over 70 test developers have notified the FDA of available tests, but some firms falsely claim their tests are FDA approved or authorized. The FDA will take action against firms making false claims or marketing tests that are not accurate and reliable.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 7, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. Last night, the FDA issued guidelines for remote ophthalmic assessment and monitoring devices, as well as extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) and cardiopulmonary bypass devices, to facilitate patient care while reducing contact and exposure. The FDA also released a temporary policy regarding enforcement of the Egg Safety Rule to allow shell egg producers to sell their eggs to retail locations. Additionally, the FDA approved an Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) for Hydroxychloroquine Sulfate Tablets USP, 200 mg, to treat malaria, lupus, and rheumatoid arthritis. The agency has issued 30 emergency use authorizations for diagnostic tests and is working with manufacturers to assess supplies and evaluate market demand.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 6, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On April 4, 2020, the FDA issued guidance on clinical electronic thermometers, and on April 5, 2020, the FDA issued guidance on infusion pumps and accessories. These policies aim to expand the availability of these tools to address the public health emergency. To date, 28 emergency use authorizations have been issued for diagnostic tests, and over 145 laboratories have begun testing under the FDA's COVID-19 Policy. The FDA continues to update its COVID-19 Diagnostics FAQ and works with over 270 test developers to submit emergency use authorization requests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 3, 2020
body_summary: The US FDA announced several actions in its ongoing response to the COVID-19 pandemic, including leading a collaboration to develop and implement a protocol for convalescent plasma distribution, revising guidelines for respirator use and emergency use authorization for KN95 respirators, and issuing guidance for new animal drug development. The FDA also extended the comment period for a proposed rule on laboratory accreditation for food analysis and released a temporary policy for shell egg packaging and labeling during the pandemic. To date, 28 emergency use authorizations for diagnostic tests have been issued, and over 240 test developers have committed to submitting EUA requests.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Coordinates National Effort to Develop Blood-Related Therapies for COVID-19
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is accelerating the development of medical countermeasures to treat and prevent COVID-19. The agency is facilitating the development of convalescent plasma and hyperimmune globulin, antibody-rich blood products made from blood donated by people who have recovered from the virus. These products can be administered to individuals diagnosed with COVID-19, and limited data suggests they may have benefits. The FDA is launching a new national effort to bring these therapies to market as fast as possible, with the goal of facilitating emergency access for patients. The agency has partnered with the American Red Cross, the Mayo Clinic, and other organizations to expedite the development and availability of these products. The FDA anticipates that this collaborative effort will be able to move thousands of units of plasma to patients in need in the coming weeks. The agency is also working to accelerate the development and availability of hyperimmune globulin for potential treatment of COVID-19.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 2, 2020
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA is revising recommendations in several guidances regarding blood donor eligibility based on recent studies and epidemiological data. The changes will be implemented immediately and may remain in place after the pandemic ends. The FDA is also publishing a fourth guidance providing notice of alternatives to certain requirements regarding blood donor eligibility for the duration of the pandemic.

Additionally, the FDA has issued warning letters to three companies for selling fraudulent COVID-19 products, including unapproved and misbranded colloidal silver products, homeopathic drug products, and essential oils. The FDA has issued emergency use authorizations (EUA) for 25 diagnostic tests, including a serology test that detects the presence of coronavirus antibodies.

The FDA has deployed almost 400 Commissioned Corps officers to aid in the response to the pandemic, with over 1,100 officers serving nationwide. The agency continues to work tirelessly to protect the public health and ensure the safety of the food supply, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Provides Updated Guidance to Address the Urgent Need for Blood During the Pandemic
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued guidance for immediate implementation to address the urgent need for blood and blood components during the COVID-19 pandemic. Donor centers have experienced a significant reduction in donations due to social distancing measures. The FDA is revising recommendations in several guidances regarding blood donor eligibility, including:

- For male donors who had sex with another man, the recommended deferral period is being changed from 12 months to 3 months.
- For female donors who had sex with a man who had sex with another man, the recommended deferral period is being changed from 12 months to 3 months.
- For those with recent tattoos and piercings, the recommended deferral period is being changed from 12 months to 3 months.
- For individuals who have traveled to malaria-endemic areas, the recommended deferral period is being changed from 12 months to 3 months.
- An alternate procedure is being provided for blood components from such donors, allowing for pathogen-reduced blood collection without a deferral period.

These changes are being implemented immediately and are expected to remain in place after the pandemic ends. The FDA aims to increase blood donations while protecting donor health and maintaining a safe blood supply.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup April 1, 2020
body_summary: The FDA announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, including the availability of quality-controlled SARS-CoV-2 reference sequence data to help test developers and vaccine developers. The data will enable expedited development of medical countermeasures, identify new targets for future tests, and support development of synthetic reference material. The FDA also issued a constituent update to provide temporary flexibility to chain restaurants, and continued to issue warning letters to companies selling fraudulent COVID-19 products. To date, 23 emergency use authorizations have been issued for diagnostic tests, including an EUA for Yale New Haven Hospital's SARS-CoV-2 PCR test. The FDA works with over 220 test developers to submit EUA requests, and has authorized more than 110 laboratories to test under the agency's COVID-19 Policy for Diagnostic Tests.

title: FDA Approves Additional Treatment for Adults and Adolescents with Hemophilia A or B and Inhibitors
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Sevenfact, a coagulation factor VIIa (recombinant)-jncw, for treating and controlling bleeding episodes in adults and adolescents 12 years of age and older with hemophilia A or B and inhibitors. The active ingredient is expressed in genetically engineered rabbits. Dr. Peter Marks, director of the FDA's Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, stated that this approval provides another treatment option for patients with hemophilia who have developed inhibitors. The FDA approved Sevenfact after a comprehensive analysis of scientific evidence and determined it to be safe and effective. The safety and efficacy of Sevenfact were evaluated in clinical studies, which showed a proportion of 86% of mild or moderate bleeding episodes treated successfully. The product is contraindicated in patients with known allergy or hypersensitivity to rabbits or rabbit proteins.

title: FDA Requests Removal of All Ranitidine Products (Zantac) from the Market
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is requesting manufacturers to immediately withdraw all prescription and over-the-counter ranitidine drugs from the market due to the presence of a contaminant known as N-Nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA). The FDA has determined that the impurity in some ranitidine products increases over time and at higher temperatures, posing a risk to consumer exposure. The agency will send letters to manufacturers requesting withdrawal and advising consumers to stop taking ranitidine products, dispose of them properly, and consider alternative treatments. The FDA has found NDMA in some ranitidine products, which is a probable human carcinogen, but the agency notes that low levels of NDMA are commonly ingested through diet and are unlikely to lead to cancer.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA expedites review of diagnostic tests to combat COVID-19
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has provided unprecedented flexibility to labs and manufacturers to develop and offer COVID-19 tests, balancing urgent need with oversight. The FDA has been proactive and supportive of test development, offering expertise and quick authorization for tests with scientific backing. 

Typically, the CDC develops diagnostic tests first, with access to viral samples. However, in this pandemic, the FDA assisted CDC in resolving manufacturing issues and utilizing commercial manufacturers. Laboratories can always develop their own tests; the COVID-19 outbreak did not change this. With a viral sample, tests can be confirmed in two to three days. Early availability of viral samples is crucial for quick deployment.

Since January, the FDA has worked with over 230 test developers, granting 20 emergency authorizations, and over 110 laboratories have notified the FDA of using their own tests. The FDA provided recommendations for test accuracy and a short form for EUA submissions. 

The FDA implemented policy updates to increase testing availability, allowing labs to test prior to FDA review and empowering states to take responsibility for tests without review. The agency plays a pivotal role in the emergency response, protecting public health and ensuring the safety and security of various products.

title: FDA on Signing of the COVID-19 Emergency Relief Bill, Including Landmark Over-the-Counter Drug Reform and User Fee Legislation
body_summary: The President signed a $2 trillion emergency relief bill into law, continuing COVID-19 response efforts and easing economic impact. The legislation provides $80 million in funding for the FDA's COVID-19 response, including medical countermeasures and vaccine development. The bill also reforms and modernizes OTC drug regulation, granting the FDA new authorities to advance innovative, safe, and effective options. The FDA will use these new tools to promote innovation and improve OTC monograph drug safety and effectiveness.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup March 30, 2020
body_summary:
The FDA announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. On March 28, 2020, an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) was issued for hydroxychloroquine sulfate and chloroquine phosphate to treat hospitalized patients with COVID-19. The EUA requires fact sheets on using these drugs to be made available to healthcare providers and patients.

On March 29, 2020, an enforcement policy was issued to expand the availability and capability of sterilizers, disinfectant devices, and air purifiers. This policy aims to ease burdens on healthcare providers and facilities.

The FDA also amended the EUA for the Battelle Decontamination System to allow for the reuse of compatible N95 respirators during the pandemic.

On March 30, 2020, an enforcement policy was issued to expand the availability of surgical apparel, including gowns and gloves.

The FDA warned two companies, Corona-cure.com and Carahealth, for selling unapproved products claiming to mitigate, prevent, treat, diagnose, or cure COVID-19. The agencies are monitoring social media and online marketplaces for fraudulent COVID-19 products.

The FDA has issued an updated guidance on conducting clinical trials of medical products during the pandemic and has issued emergency use authorizations for diagnostic tests, including Abbott Diagnostics Scarborough, Inc.'s test.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA takes further steps to help mitigate supply interruptions of food and medical products
body_summary: The FDA is working around the clock to ensure Americans have access to safe food and medical products during the COVID-19 pandemic. The agency is partnering with FEMA to address supply chain issues, including importing needed medical products. FDA has issued Emergency Use Authorizations (EUA) for respirators, ventilators, and other devices to increase their availability. The agency is also facilitating importation of PPE and other devices, providing guidance to manufacturers and healthcare facilities to mitigate shortages. Additionally, the FDA is monitoring blood supplies, which have been reduced due to social distancing measures, and is encouraging individuals to donate blood. Despite this, the agency reports no widespread disruptions in the human and animal food supply chain, and is supporting veterinary professionals by encouraging PPE conservation and postponing non-urgent medical procedures.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup March 27, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA is working closely with manufacturers to ensure timely notification of any permanent discontinuance or interruption of drug and biological product manufacturing. The agency published guidance on the importance of these notifications and requested additional details from applicants and manufacturers. The FDA also issued a Consumer Update and a letter to stakeholders warning about the dangers of using chloroquine phosphate products meant for aquarium fish, which can be mistaken for FDA-approved human medications. To date, 19 emergency use authorizations have been issued for diagnostic tests, and over 220 test developers have submitted EUA requests to the FDA. The agency continues to work with laboratories and updates its COVID-19 Diagnostics FAQ.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA takes action to help increase U.S. supply of ventilators and respirators for protection of health care workers, patients
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration issued an Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) to allow for the emergency use in health care settings of certain ventilators, anesthesia gas machines, positive pressure breathing devices, and respirators due to shortages during COVID-19. The EUA applies to devices that meet specified criteria for safety, performance, and labeling, and are not currently marketed in the US or require a modification that would trigger a new premarket notification. The FDA also issued an EUA for certain imported non-NIOSH-approved respirators that meet performance standards and have a marketing authorization in specified jurisdictions, subject to conditions of authorization. This EUA does not affect previous authorizations and does not permit use by the general public.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup March 26, 2020
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA issued guidance on a temporary policy regarding nutrition labeling of certain packaged food during the pandemic, providing flexibility for restaurants and food manufacturers. The agency also posted questions and answers related to consumer use of hand sanitizer, discussing steps being taken to increase supply. Additionally, the FDA issued an enforcement policy for face masks and respirators, aiming to expand availability for the general public and healthcare professionals. The FDA entered into a Memorandum of Understanding with the Department of Veterans Affairs, National Institutes of Health, and America Makes to facilitate connections between patients, healthcare providers, and local manufacturers for 3D printing of medical devices. To date, the FDA has issued 17 emergency use authorizations for diagnostic tests, including the AvellinoCoV2 test, and over 100 laboratories have begun testing under the agency's COVID-19 Policy for Diagnostic Tests.

title: FDA Continues to Support Transparency and Collaboration in Drug Approval Process as the Clinical Data Summary Pilot Concludes
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) needs to take a more collaborative approach to its drug approval process. In 2019, 60% of the participants in the clinical trials supporting the 48 novel drugs approved by the FDA were located outside the US. The FDA is working to improve collaboration efforts with other regulatory agencies and increase transparency related to drug approval decisions.

The FDA implemented the Clinical Data Summary Pilot Program in 2018, which aimed to evaluate whether disclosing certain information from clinical study reports improves public access to drug approval information. The pilot found inefficiencies in having multiregional disclosure requirements and identified a potential approach to facilitate a harmonized system for disclosing study reports.

The FDA has decided to conclude the pilot and will apply the lessons learned to future efforts, including implementing a centralized international library, on-demand system, and standardized anonymization and disclosure standards. The agency will continue to invest in international harmonization efforts and keep stakeholders informed of any future projects.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup, March 25, 2020
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken several actions in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA issued guidance for industry on the manufacture of alcohol for use in hand sanitizers, adding hydroxychloroquine sulfate to category 1 for compounding using bulk drug substances. The agency has also issued an emergency use authorization for ventilators, anesthesia gas machines, and other medical devices, as well as added updates to its COVID-19 Diagnostics FAQ. The FDA has worked with over 190 test developers to issue 16 emergency use authorizations for nationwide use, and has notified over 100 laboratories under its COVID-19 laboratory developed test policy.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Daily Roundup, March 24, 2020
body_summary: The FDA has facilitated access to convalescent plasma to help shorten the length or lessen the severity of COVID-19 illness. The agency is also engaging with researchers to develop a master protocol for convalescent plasma use. In response to FFR shortages, the FDA has authorized certain imported disposable FFRs that are not NIOSH-approved for use in healthcare settings. The agency has issued a Letter of Authorization for non-NIOSH approved respirators and is advising consumers to beware of fraudulent coronavirus tests, vaccines, and treatments. The FDA has issued emergency use authorizations for diagnostic tests and is working to facilitate the entry of personal protective equipment into the US. The agency has also provided updates on food safety and supply, reassuring that the US food supply remains safe for people and animals.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The Federal Reserve is committed to use its full range of tools to support the U.S. economy in this challenging time and thereby promote its maximum employment and price stability goals. The Federal Open Market Committee is taking further actions to support the flow of credit to households and businesses by addressing strains in the markets for Treasury securities and agency mortgage-backed securities. The Federal Reserve will continue to purchase Treasury securities and agency mortgage-backed securities in the amounts needed to support smooth market functioning and effective transmission of monetary policy to broader financial conditions. The Committee will include purchases of agency commercial mortgage-backed securities in its agency mortgage-backed security purchases. In addition, the Open Market Desk will continue to offer large-scale overnight and term repurchase agreement operations. The Committee will continue to closely monitor market conditions, and will assess the appropriate pace of its securities purchases at future meetings. Voting (by notation) for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Patrick Harker; Robert S. Kaplan; Neel Kashkari; Loretta J. Mester; and Randal K. Quarles. In a related set of actions, the Federal Reserve announced additional measures to support the flow of credit to households and businesses. More information can be found on the Federal Reserve Board's website . In connection with these plans, the Committee voted unanimously to authorize and direct the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective March 23, 2020, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 0 to 1/4 percent. The Committee directs the Desk to increase the System Open Market Account holdings of Treasury securities and agency mortgage-backed securities (MBS) in the amounts needed to support the smooth functioning of markets for Treasury securities and agency MBS. The Committee also directs the Desk to include purchases of agency commercial mortgage-backed securities in its agency mortgage-backed security purchases. The Committee also directs the Desk to continue conducting term and overnight repurchase agreement operations to ensure that the supply of reserves remains ample and to support the smooth functioning of short-term U.S. dollar funding markets. In addition, the Committee directs the Desk to conduct overnight reverse repurchase operations (and reverse repurchase operations with maturities of more than one day when necessary to accommodate weekend, holiday, or similar trading conventions) at an offering rate of 0.00 percent, in amounts limited only by the value of Treasury securities held outright in the System Open Market Account that are available for such operations and by a per-counterparty limit of $30 billion per day. The Committee directs the Desk to continue rolling over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities and to reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities received during each calendar month in agency mortgage-backed securities. Small deviations from these amounts for operational reasons are acceptable. The Committee also directs the Desk to engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency mortgage-backed securities transactions." More information regarding open market operations and reinvestments may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website .

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Issues first Emergency Use Authorization for Point of Care Diagnostic
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued an emergency use authorization for the Cepheid Xpert Xpress SARS-CoV-2 test, a point-of-care COVID-19 diagnostic. The test is expected to provide results within hours, rather than days. HHS Secretary Alex Azar stated that this new tool will make testing more accessible to Americans. FDA Commissioner Stephen Hahn said that the authorization marks an important step in expanding testing and rapid results. The test will be available in high- and moderate-complexity laboratories and certain patient care settings. The company plans to roll out availability by March 30.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Alerts Consumers About Unauthorized Fraudulent COVID-19 Test Kits
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is monitoring the market for fraudulent COVID-19 diagnostic, prevention, and treatment claims. As a result, unauthorized test kits are being marketed to test for COVID-19 at home, and the FDA has not authorized any test for home purchase. The agency is working with test developers to expand safe and accurate testing, including home collection. The FDA warns consumers to follow CDC guidelines and consult their medical provider if symptoms occur. The agency will take action to protect consumers from bad actors, including issuing warning letters, seizures, and injunctions. If aware of fraudulent test kits, consumers should report them to the FDA.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA allows expanded use of devices to monitor patients’ vital signs remotely
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a new policy allowing manufacturers of certain FDA-cleared non-invasive vital sign-measuring devices to expand their use for remote patient monitoring. The devices, which include body temperature, respiratory rate, heart rate, and blood pressure measures, can help healthcare providers access information about a patient's vital signs while the patient is at home, reducing hospital visits and exposure to coronavirus. FDA Principal Deputy Commissioner Amy Abernethy stated that this policy reflects the FDA's commitment to ease burdens on healthcare providers during the public health emergency. The policy applies to modifications to the indications, claims, functionality, or hardware or software of FDA-cleared remote monitoring devices used to support patient monitoring, and is limited to the duration of the emergency.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA provides guidance on production of alcohol-based hand sanitizer to help boost supply, protect public health
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued two guidance documents to communicate its policy for the temporary manufacture of certain alcohol-based hand sanitizer products during the COVID-19 pandemic. The agency's policy allows for the temporary manufacture of these products by manufacturers and compounders, with the goal of increasing supply and meeting demand. The guidance documents outline the requirements for product labeling, manufacturing methods, and reporting requirements, including the submission of adverse event reports to the FDA. The policy is in effect for the duration of the public health emergency declared by the Secretary of Health and Human Services on January 31, 2020. The FDA Commissioner, Stephen M. Hahn, stated that the agency will work with manufacturers and compounders to increase the supply of alcohol-based hand sanitizer available to Americans.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: Blood Donations
body_summary: The nation's blood supply is in need of a steady supply of donors due to reduced blood donations since the COVID-19 pandemic. Every two seconds, a patient needs a blood transfusion. The FDA is responsible for ensuring the safety and security of the nation's blood supply. To address this, the nation encourages healthy individuals to donate blood, recognizing it as a critical public health contribution. Donating blood is safe and takes only a short time. Appointments can be made at blood donation centers, which take social distancing precautions to prevent the spread of infections. The nation's blood supply can be found at AABB, America's Blood Centers, American Red Cross, Armed Services Blood Program, and Blood Centers of America, among others.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Continues to Facilitate Development of Treatments
body_summary: The US FDA continues to play a critical role in the response to the COVID-19 pandemic, facilitating the development and availability of life-saving medical countermeasures. President Trump has directed the agency to work with the public and private sector to ensure access to critical drugs, including chloroquine, being studied for its potential to treat mild-to-moderate COVID-19. The FDA is working with other agencies, academic centers, and industry partners to expedite the development and availability of medical products, including repurposing existing therapies and pursuing new therapeutics. The agency is also addressing the COVID-19 crisis by protecting Americans from fraudulent products and safeguarding public health, while regulating various products, including human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, medical devices, food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, and tobacco products.

title: FDA Approves New Treatment for Pediatric Patients with Any Strain of Hepatitis C
body_summary: The US FDA approved a supplemental application for Epclusa (sofosbuvir and velpatasvir) to treat hepatitis C virus (HCV) in children aged 6 years and older or weighing at least 37 pounds. The approval expands treatment options for children and adolescents with HCV, particularly in settings with limited access to HCV genotype testing. The FDA previously approved Epclusa for adults. The approval is based on a clinical trial of 173 pediatric patients who received Epclusa orally for 12 weeks and showed comparable safety and efficacy to adults. The trial demonstrated high cure rates for patients with HCV genotypes 1, 2, 3, 4, and 6. The FDA granted Priority Review to Gilead Sciences Inc.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Focuses on Safety of Regulated Products While Scaling Back Domestic Inspections
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has directed all eligible employees to begin teleworking in line with White House Coronavirus Task Force guidance. This decision aims to help slow the spread of the COVID-19 pandemic and keep the workforce healthy to carry out the FDA's critical public health mission. The FDA has postponed most foreign facility inspections through April, except for mission-critical inspections. Domestic routine surveillance facility inspections have been temporarily postponed due to industry concerns about visitors, but for-cause inspection assignments will be evaluated and proceed if mission-critical. The FDA remains committed to ensuring the safety and quality of FDA-regulated products, leveraging available authorities to protect public safety.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Issues Guidance for Conducting Clinical Trials
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued guidance for industry, investigators, and institutional review boards conducting clinical trials during the COVID-19 pandemic. The FDA recognizes challenges that may arise due to quarantines, site closures, and other considerations, and outlines considerations to assist sponsors in ensuring the safety of trial participants, maintaining compliance with good clinical practice, and minimizing risks to trial integrity. The guidance emphasizes patients' safety and aims to support the continuation of clinical trials while safeguarding the health and well-being of study participants. The FDA released this guidance to help industry and investigators navigate the pandemic and move forward with critical clinical trials.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Issues Temporary Policy for FSMA Onsite Audit Requirements
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a temporary policy to help prevent disruptions in the food supply chain during the coronavirus (COVID-19) public health emergency. The policy allows receiving facilities and importers to temporarily waive onsite audits required under the FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) if alternative methods are used instead. The policy is intended to minimize disruptions while ensuring food safety and will be revisited as travel restrictions and advisories are lifted. The FDA is closely monitoring the food supply chain and is in regular contact with food manufacturers and grocery stores, with no nationwide shortages reported.

title: Joint Statement by Group of Seven Leaders on the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID–19) Pandemic
body_summary:
The Leaders of the Group of Seven acknowledge the COVID-19 pandemic as a human tragedy and global health crisis, posing risks to the world economy. They commit to a strongly coordinated international approach based on science and evidence, utilizing the strengths of private enterprise. The goal is to resolve health and economic risks caused by the pandemic and set the stage for strong, sustainable economic growth and prosperity.

To protect people at risk, they will coordinate public health measures, restore confidence, growth, and protect jobs. The G7 will support global trade and investment, encourage science, research, and technology cooperation. They will also pool epidemiologic data to better understand and fight the virus.

The G7 will increase coordinated research efforts, including through the global alliance Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness and Innovation. They will support the launch of joint research projects and the sharing of facilities for rapid development, manufacture, and distribution of treatments and a vaccine.

To implement these objectives, the G7 will coordinate efforts across all parts of their governments, with a focus on protecting the health and safety of everyone. They will also address the economic impact of the outbreak, mobilizing policy tools to achieve strong growth in G7 economies and safeguard against downside risks.

The G7 will coordinate monetary and fiscal measures, targeted actions, and international financial assistance to support workers, companies, and sectors most affected. They will reinforce the importance of coordination among international organizations and call on the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group to further support countries worldwide.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The coronavirus outbreak has harmed communities and disrupted economic activity in many countries, including the United States. Global financial conditions have also been significantly affected. Available economic data show that the U.S. economy came into this challenging period on a strong footing. Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January indicates that the labor market remained strong through February and economic activity rose at a moderate rate. Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Although household spending rose at a moderate pace, business fixed investment and exports remained weak. More recently, the energy sector has come under stress. On a 12âmonth basis, overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy are running below 2 percent. Market-based measures of inflation compensation have declined; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. The effects of the coronavirus will weigh on economic activity in the near term and pose risks to the economic outlook. In light of these developments, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 0 to 1/4 percent. The Committee expects to maintain this target range until it is confident that the economy has weathered recent events and is on track to achieve its maximum employment and price stability goals. This action will help support economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation returning to the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective. The Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook, including information related to public health, as well as global developments and muted inflation pressures, and will use its tools and act as appropriate to support the economy. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the stance of monetary policy, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. The Federal Reserve is prepared to use its full range of tools to support the flow of credit to households and businesses and thereby promote its maximum employment and price stability goals. To support the smooth functioning of markets for Treasury securities and agency mortgage-backed securities that are central to the flow of credit to households and businesses, over coming months the Committee will increase its holdings of Treasury securities by at least $500 billion and its holdings of agency mortgage-backed securities by at least $200 billion. The Committee will also reinvest all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities in agency mortgage-backed securities. In addition, the Open Market Desk has recently expanded its overnight and term repurchase agreement operations. The Committee will continue to closely monitor market conditions and is prepared to adjust its plans as appropriate. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Patrick Harker; Robert S. Kaplan; Neel Kashkari; and Randal K. Quarles. Voting against this action was Loretta J. Mester, who was fully supportive of all of the actions taken to promote the smooth functioning of markets and the flow of credit to households and businesses but preferred to reduce the target range for the federal funds rate to 1/2 to 3/4 percent at this meeting. In a related set of actions to support the credit needs of households and businesses, the Federal Reserve announced measures related to the discount window, intraday credit, bank capital and liquidity buffers, reserve requirements, andâin coordination with other central banksâthe U.S. dollar liquidity swap line arrangements. More information can be found on the Federal Reserve Board's website .

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA gives flexibility to New York State Department of Health, FDA issues Emergency Use Authorization diagnostic
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration took two actions to address the coronavirus outbreak. The agency issued enforcement discretion, allowing the New York State Department of Health to authorize certain laboratories in New York to begin patient testing after validating their tests and notifying the NYSDOH. Laboratories will provide validation data to NYSDOH within 15 days instead of pursuing an Emergency Use Authorization with FDA. The FDA also authorized the Roche cobas SARS-CoV-2 Test, the third Emergency Use Authorization granted for a diagnostic test during the COVID-19 outbreak. The FDA Commissioner, Stephen M. Hahn, stated that the agency's actions demonstrate its commitment to expedite test availability. The FDA granted flexibility to NYSDOH based on the urgent public health need for additional testing capacity.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Issues Emergency Use Authorization to Thermo Fisher
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued its fourth COVID-19 diagnostic Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) to Thermo Fisher for its TaqPath COVID-19 Combo Kit. The FDA Commissioner, Stephen M. Hahn, stated that the agency's dedication to reviewing and authorizing diagnostics during the public health emergency. Since the outbreak began, over 80 test developers have sought the FDA's assistance, and more than 30 laboratories have notified the agency of their intention to test or begin testing soon. The FDA issued the EUA to Thermo Fisher within 24 hours of receiving the request, making it the second commercially distributed test to receive an EUA during the outbreak. The FDA is responsible for protecting public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of various products, including diagnostic tests, medical devices, and food supplies.

title: The President's News Conference
body_summary: The US President announces a series of decisive actions to combat the coronavirus, including suspending entry of foreign nationals who have been to Europe and declaring a national emergency to provide up to $50 billion for states and territories. Deborah Birx, White House Coronavirus Response Coordinator, announces a new testing approach using high-throughput automated machines to deliver results in 24-36 hours. The President also waives interest on student loans, purchases large quantities of crude oil for the Strategic Reserve, and outlines a plan to protect Americans from the virus. The US has developed a strong testing system, allowing for millions of tests, and has shared data with China, which has shown a decrease in cases. The administration is working with the cruise line industry and other countries to ensure safety and prosperity. The President claims emergency powers and coordination with countries like Italy and China to combat the pandemic, and states he will likely get tested for COVID-19 "fairly soon".

title: Memorandum on Expanding State-Approved Diagnostic Tests
body_summary: By the authority vested in me as President, it is hereby ordered: The policy of the United States is to take proactive measures to prepare for and respond to public health threats, including the public health emergency involving Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19), declared by the Secretary of Health and Human Services on January 31, 2020. The Food and Drug Administration, in coordination with the State of New York, allowed flexibility in expediting State-approved COVID-19 testing. If additional States request flexibility to authorize laboratories to develop and perform tests, the Secretary shall take appropriate action. This memorandum is authorized and directed to be published in the Federal Register.

title: FDA Launches New Campaign to Help Consumers Use the New Nutrition Facts Label
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has launched an initiative to help consumers use the new Nutrition Facts label to maintain healthy dietary practices. The campaign, "What's In It For You?", aims to reach the general public and focus on consumers at increased risk of nutrition-related chronic diseases. The new label was finalized in May 2016 and became mandatory for most manufacturers in January 2020. The label features bold listings for serving sizes and calorie counts, as well as new required listings for added sugars, vitamin D, and potassium. The campaign includes videos and educational materials to educate consumers, healthcare professionals, teachers, dietitians, and community leaders about the new label.

title: Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) Update: Foreign Inspections
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is postponing most foreign inspections through April due to the COVID-19 outbreak. Inspections deemed mission-critical will be considered on a case-by-case basis. The decision was made based on factors such as State Department Level 4 travel advisories, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention travel recommendations, and access restrictions imposed by certain countries. The FDA will continue to monitor the situation closely and employ alternative tools to ensure the safety of imported products, including denying entry of unsafe products, physical examinations, and product sampling. The FDA will also work with US Customs and Border Protection to target products that violate applicable laws and regulations. The agency has the ability to adjust its risk-based import screening tool, PREDICT, to focus on specific products being entered into US commerce.

title: FDA Warns Retailers, Manufacturers to Remove Unauthorized E-Cigarette Products from Market
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued 22 warning letters to online and brick-and-mortar e-cigarette retailers and manufacturers for selling flavored, cartridge-based electronic nicotine delivery system (ENDS) products, which lack marketing authorization, as these products are illegal. The warning letters were sent to establishments like 7-Eleven and Shell, and are the first of ongoing actions consistent with the FDA's recently issued policy of enforcement priorities for e-cigarettes. The FDA is prioritizing enforcement against products targeted at youth, flavored products other than tobacco or menthol, and products with inadequate measures to prevent underage access. Companies that do not cease manufacture, distribution, and sale of these unauthorized tobacco products risk FDA regulatory actions.

title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Group of Progressive Interstitial Lung Diseases
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Ofev (nintedanib) oral capsules to treat patients with chronic fibrosing interstitial lung diseases (ILD) with a progressive phenotype. This is the first FDA-approved treatment for this group of fibrosing lung diseases. Ofev's safety and effectiveness were evaluated in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of 663 adults, with patients receiving 150 milligrams of Ofev twice a day or a placebo for 52 weeks. After 52 weeks, patients who received Ofev had less lung function decline compared to those on the placebo. The most common side effects were diarrhea, nausea, and stomach pain. Banu Karimi-Shah, M.D., acting deputy director of the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, said the approval helps to fulfill an unmet treatment need for patients with limited or no treatment options.

title: FDA Proposes Broad Approach for Conducting Safety Trials for Type 2 Diabetes Medications
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued a new draft guidance for evaluating the safety of new drugs for type 2 diabetes mellitus. The guidance proposes broad safety evaluations before drug approval, looking beyond ischemic cardiovascular disease, and includes a broader scope of human subjects, such as older subjects and those with chronic kidney disease. The guidance aims to provide valuable safety information for medications used to improve glycemic control. The 2020 draft guidance was developed based on recommendations from the FDA's Endocrinologic and Metabolic Drugs Advisory Committee and stems from the ongoing evaluation of cardiovascular outcomes trials.

title: Coronavirus Update: FDA and FTC Warn Seven Companies Selling Fraudulent Products that Claim to Treat or Prevent COVID-19
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) issued warning letters to seven companies for selling unapproved COVID-19 products. These products pose significant risks to patient health and violate federal law. The FDA and FTC are taking action to protect Americans during the global COVID-19 outbreak.

The warning letters were issued in response to the sale and promotion of fraudulent COVID-19 products. The FDA considers these products a threat to public health. Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn stated that the agency will aggressively pursue those that place the public health at risk and hold bad actors accountable.

The FTC Chairman Joe Simons added that the warning letters are just the first step, and the agency is prepared to take enforcement actions against companies that continue to market this type of scam. The FDA and FTC have jointly warned companies that claim to cure, treat or prevent serious diseases like COVID-19 may cause consumers to delay or stop appropriate medical treatment, leading to serious and life-threatening harm.

The warning letters were issued to companies that sell teas, essential oils, tinctures, and colloidal silver products that make fraudulent claims about preventing, treating, or curing COVID-19. The FDA has previously warned that colloidal silver is not safe or effective for treating any disease or condition. Companies that fail to make adequate corrections may be subject to legal action, including seizure or injunction.

title: FDA Approves New Treatment for Adults with Cushing’s Disease
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Isturisa (osilodrostat) oral tablets for adults with Cushing's disease, a rare condition where excessive cortisol production occurs. The FDA supports the development of safe and effective treatments for rare diseases, and Isturisa is the first FDA-approved drug to directly address cortisol overproduction. Isturisa was evaluated in a study of 137 adult patients, mostly women, and showed significant benefits in reducing cortisol levels. The majority of patients achieved normal cortisol levels within 24 weeks, and 86% maintained normal levels after a 12-week withdrawal study. Common side effects included adrenal insufficiency, headache, and edema. Isturisa is taken twice daily and received Orphan Drug Designation, granted to a drug intended to treat a rare disease.

title: FDA Advances Work Related to Cannabidiol Products with Focus on Protecting Public Health, Providing Market Clarity
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is evaluating cannabidiol (CBD) products to educate the public about their risks and gather science on their safety and potential benefits. The FDA is concerned that some people think CBD products are safe and can't hurt, but no products have been evaluated or approved by the agency. Americans are encouraged to consult with healthcare providers before using CBD products, and the agency is working to expand educational efforts, gather data, and monitor the marketplace for products that pose a risk to public harm. The FDA is also re-opening a public docket to allow stakeholders to provide data and information on CBD products. Additionally, the agency is evaluating a risk-based enforcement policy to address concerns about other drug claims and products, including those with potential risks from contaminants, false claims, and products marketed for vulnerable populations.

title: New ‘Feed Your Mind’ Initiative Launches to Increase Consumer Understanding of Genetically Engineered Foods
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, in collaboration with the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the U.S. Department of Agriculture, launched the "Feed Your Mind" initiative to help consumers better understand genetically modified organisms (GMOs). The initiative aims to answer common questions about GMOs, including what they are, how and why they are made, and how they are regulated. The FDA Commissioner, Stephen M. Hahn, stated that there are misconceptions about GMOs, while Under Secretary Greg Ibach emphasized the importance of producing foods in ways that meet consumer expectations. The EPA Assistant Administrator, Alexandra Dapolito Dunn, highlighted the agency's commitment to pushing agricultural innovation forward. The initiative is launching in phases, with a new website and fact sheets being released today, followed by additional materials in 2020 and 2021. Funding for the initiative was provided by Congress in 2017.

title: FDA Requires Stronger Warning About Risk of Neuropsychiatric Events Associated with Asthma and Allergy Medication Singulair and Generic Montelukast
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is requiring a boxed warning for montelukast, a medication used to treat asthma and allergic rhinitis, due to the risk of neuropsychiatric events. The warning advises healthcare providers to avoid prescribing montelukast for patients with mild symptoms, particularly those with allergic rhinitis. The decision follows the FDA's review of available data on continued reports of neuropsychiatric events, including agitation, depression, and suicidal thoughts and actions. The FDA aims to make informed treatment decisions and notes that there are many other safe and effective medications available. The warning was updated in 2008, and the FDA re-evaluated the benefits and risks of montelukast in 2019, concluding that the risks may outweigh the benefits in some patients, especially when symptoms are mild and can be treated with alternative therapies.

title: FDA Takes Rare Step to Ban Electrical Stimulation Devices for Self-Injurious or Aggressive Behavior
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has published a final rule to ban electrical stimulation devices (ESDs) used for self-injurious or aggressive behavior due to their unreasonable and substantial risk of illness or injury. The devices, which administer electrical shocks to interrupt behavior, have been linked to psychological and physical risks, including depression, anxiety, and pain. The FDA considered evidence from clinical and scientific data, expert input, and comments from stakeholders, including parents, state agencies, and disability rights groups, to determine that the risks outweigh the benefits. The ban is effective 30 days after publication in the Federal Register, with a gradual transition period for devices in use as of publication. The FDA has only banned two other medical devices since gaining the authority to do so.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: The fundamentals of the U.S. economy remain strong. However, the coronavirus poses evolving risks to economic activity. In light of these risks and in support of achieving its maximum employment and price stability goals, the Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/2 percentage point, to 1 to 1â1/4 percent. The Committee is closely monitoring developments and their implications for the economic outlook and will use its tools and act as appropriate to support the economy. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Patrick Harker; Robert S. Kaplan; Neel Kashkari; Loretta J. Mester; and Randal K. Quarles.

title: FDA Informs Patients, Providers and Manufacturers About Potential Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities in Certain Medical Devices with Bluetooth Low Energy
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has informed patients, healthcare providers, and manufacturers about cybersecurity vulnerabilities in medical devices, referred to as "SweynTooth," which affect Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) technology. The vulnerabilities may allow unauthorized users to crash or access device functions, posing risks to medical devices such as pacemakers, glucose monitors, and ultrasound devices. The FDA is recommending that medical device manufacturers stay alert for these vulnerabilities and proactively address them.

Affected microchip manufacturers include Texas Instruments, NXP, Cypress, Dialog Semiconductors, Microchip, STMicroelectronics, and Telink Semiconductor. The FDA is asking medical device manufacturers to communicate to healthcare providers and patients which devices may be affected by SweynTooth and ways to reduce associated risks.

Patients should consult their healthcare providers to determine if their medical device could be affected and seek help immediately if they think their device is not working as expected. The FDA will continue to assess new information and keep the public informed if significant new information becomes available.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA and CDC take action to increase access to respirators, including N95s, for health care personnel
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention took action to make more respirators, including certain N95s, available to health care personnel. The FDA granted the CDC's request for an emergency use authorization to allow health care personnel to use certain industrial respirators during the COVID-19 outbreak in health care settings. This action aims to maximize the number of respirators available to meet the needs of the U.S. health care system, thereby protecting the American people. The FDA and CDC are aware of reports of increased ordering and shortages of personal protective equipment, but they are taking steps to address these issues by expanding the use of respirators that are NIOSH approved but do not currently meet FDA regulatory requirements.

title: FDA Approves New Therapy for Patients with Previously Treated Multiple Myeloma
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Sarclisa (isatuximab-irfc) for the treatment of adult patients with multiple myeloma who have received at least two prior therapies including lenalidomide and a proteasome inhibitor. Sarclisa, a CD38-directed cytolytic antibody, has been shown to reduce the risk of disease progression or death by 40% in a clinical trial involving 307 patients. The FDA approved the treatment based on the results of a clinical trial involving patients with relapsed and refractory multiple myeloma. The treatment is administered through intravenous infusion and has been associated with common side effects such as neutropenia and infusion-related reactions.
