title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Update: FDA Issues New Policy to Help Expedite Availability of Diagnostics
body_summary: The US FDA has issued a new policy to enable certain laboratories to develop and use validated COVID-19 diagnostics before the agency completes review of their Emergency Use Authorization (EUA) requests. The policy aims to rapidly expand testing capacity in the US and address the critical public health need of detecting COVID-19 cases. Laboratories must be certified to perform high-complexity testing and follow specific guidelines, including test validation, FDA notification, and interim confirmatory clinical testing. The policy allows laboratories to begin using their tests immediately, but they must submit an EUA request within 15 business days. The FDA is expediting the review of medical products, including diagnostics, to support laboratories working on this urgent public health situation.

title: The President's News Conference
body_summary: The US President announced plans to withdraw 8,000 troops from Afghanistan following successful reconciliation efforts, thanking President Ghani, NATO, the UN, and US military personnel for their work. The President also authorized additional travel restrictions on Iran, increased travel advisories for Italy and South Korea, and discussed public health measures to contain the spread of the coronavirus. The administration has taken steps to reduce travel to and from impacted areas and implemented health measures. The President assured Americans that they could go about their normal lives, but emphasized the importance of taking precautions.

title: FDA Approves First Generic of Daraprim
body_summary: The US FDA has approved the first generic version of Daraprim tablets for treating toxoplasmosis, a parasitic infection caused by Toxoplasma gondii. The approval is part of the FDA's Drug Competition Action Plan, aimed at increasing competition in markets with limited or no generic alternatives. The generic version, sponsored by Cerovene Inc., will provide more treatment options for populations vulnerable to toxoplasmosis, such as pregnant women and individuals with HIV/AIDS. Toxoplasmosis can be caused by eating undercooked meat, contaminated water, or accidental contact with cat feces. The FDA has taken steps to improve the efficiency of generic drug development and review, and to close loopholes that allowed brand-name companies to delay generic competition. The approved generic version of Daraprim will have the same safety and efficacy as the brand-name drug, and will be subject to the same quality standards. Common side effects of pyrimethamine, the active ingredient in Daraprim, include hypersensitivity reactions and anorexia.

title: Coronavirus (COVID-19) Supply Chain Update
body_summary: The FDA has been closely monitoring the supply chain due to the COVID-19 outbreak, anticipating potential disruptions to medical product supplies. In response, the agency is working with manufacturers to mitigate shortages, including those of critical medical products and personal protective equipment. The FDA has identified 63 essential medical device facilities in China and is in touch with 180 manufacturers, 20 of which source their active pharmaceutical ingredients solely from China. To address supply challenges, the FDA proposes requiring firms to notify the agency of anticipated supply interruptions and manufacturers to report their manufacturing capacity. The agency aims to promote the continued availability of essential devices through measures such as temporary importation and enforcement of compliance with the law.

title: FDA Reminds Patients that Devices Claiming to Clean, Disinfect or Sanitize CPAP Machines Using Ozone Gas or UV Light Have Not Been FDA Authorized
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is issuing a safety communication to inform patients and healthcare providers that devices claiming to clean, disinfect or sanitize CPAP devices or accessories using ozone gas or UV light are not legally marketed for this use in the US. The FDA recommends following the manufacturer's cleaning instructions, which typically include regular cleaning with soap and water. Exposure to ozone gas can worsen chronic respiratory diseases, while UV light-based products can cause burns, eye damage, or increase the risk of skin cancer. The FDA has received reports of adverse events, including cough, difficult breathing, and asthma attacks, from patients using ozone gas-based products. Ozone gas must be present at a safe concentration to be effective, and leaks can occur in CPAP systems, leading to unsafe ozone levels.

title: The President's News Conference
body_summary: US President Donald Trump extended condolences to victims and families in Milwaukee after a shooting at a Molson Coors Brewing Company plant took five lives. He also discussed the global coronavirus outbreak, citing successful early decisions to close US borders. The President announced Vice President Mike Pence as head of the Corona Task Force to oversee the nation's response. He handed over to Dr. Anne Schuchat to discuss the US response. Trump mentioned potential travel restrictions to China, South Korea, and Italy, citing the country's strong economy and consumer sector as a factor. The President defended the tourism industry, claiming travel-related stocks will recover, and criticized politicians for politicizing the response. He stated that 26,000 to 69,000 people die from the flu annually and believes the current situation is unusual. Trump denied the CDC exaggerating the threat, saying he trusts his instincts over health officials' advice. The US is taking steps to restrict travel from Brazil and China, and the President wants to get back to business as usual with Dr. Fauci's efforts to contain the spread.

title: FDA Takes New Steps to Increase the Safety of Laparoscopic Power Morcellators when used in Gynecologic Surgeries
body_summary: The FDA is taking steps to make laparoscopic power morcellators (LPMs) safer in gynecologic surgeries. The agency is granting marketing authorization for updated labeling of the PneumoLiner containment system, releasing draft guidance recommending the addition of specific safety information to product labeling for LPMs, and issuing a Safety Communication. The updated labeling will define the appropriate patient population for the safe and effective use of the PneumoLiner containment system, stating that it should only be used in pre-menopausal women under 50 years old. The FDA is also recommending that labeling include contraindications and warnings highlighting the risks of using LPMs in gynecologic surgeries, particularly for women over 50 years old. The agency is taking these actions based on available scientific information and will continue to review information on LPMs to ensure public safety.

title: Coronavirus Update: FDA steps to ensure quality of foreign products
body_summary: The FDA is continuing its multi-pronged approach to addressing the novel coronavirus outbreak, including facilitating diagnostic, treatment, and prevention efforts, and monitoring the medical product supply chain. While inspections in China are currently suspended due to the US Department of State's Travel Advisory, the FDA is using alternative tools to monitor safety, including import screening, examinations, and sampling. The agency is utilizing its risk-based approach to ensure quality and compliance with applicable requirements. The FDA is also focusing on verifying the quality of imported products, with over 60% of FDA-regulated products from China being medical devices. The agency is exploring the use of record requests to facilitate inspections in China when travel restrictions are lifted. Additionally, the FDA is working with US Customs and Border Protection to target products that violate FDA regulations, and is utilizing its PREDICT screening tool to prioritize examinations and sample collections.

title: FDA approves first generic of ProAir HFA
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the first generic version of ProAir HFA (albuterol sulfate) Inhalation Aerosol for the treatment or prevention of bronchospasm in patients four years of age and older, and the prevention of exercise-induced bronchospasm in patients four years of age and older. The generic drug product was developed by Perrigo Pharmaceutical Co.

The FDA has a longstanding commitment to advance patient access to lower-cost, high-quality generic drug products, and to expand opportunities to bring generic copies of complex drugs to the market. The agency has issued guidance documents and implemented policies to promote generic competition for complex generic drug products, including metered dose inhalers.

According to the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, bronchospasms occur when the muscles surrounding the airways swell and tighten, squeezing the airways and making them smaller. The most common side effects associated with Albuterol Sulfate Inhalation Aerosol are headache, rapid heart rate, pain, dizziness, and chest pain.

The FDA regularly takes steps to guide industry through the development process for generic drug products, including combination products. The agency requires sponsors to submit appropriate data and information to demonstrate that complex generic drug-device combination products meet the agency's rigorous approval standards.

title: FDA Authorizes Marketing of the First Genetic Test to Aid in the Diagnosis of Fragile X Syndrome
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of the AmplideX Fragile X Dx and Carrier Screen Kit, the first FDA-authorized genetic test for Fragile X Syndrome (FXS), a genetic condition causing inherited developmental delay and intellectual disability. The test is intended to aid in diagnosing FXS and identifying individuals who may be carriers of the associated genetic alteration, the FMR1 gene. The test uses blood specimens to measure CGG trinucleotide repeats in the FMR1 gene and can determine whether a patient has a normal, intermediate, premutation, or full mutation. The FDA reviewed data demonstrating the test's accuracy greater than 95% and established special controls for test developers. The authorization was granted to Asuragen Inc., and the test is intended for use in adults, with women having a higher risk of passing the premutation to their daughters.

title: FDA Announces Collaborative Review of Scientific Evidence to Support Associations Between Genetic Information and Specific Medications
body_summary: The FDA is concerned with the safe use of medications based on pharmacogenetic test reports that are not supported by sound science. The agency has warned firms offering genetic tests making claims not adequately supported by science, and some manufacturers have continued marketing their tests despite this warning. The FDA has not enforced regulatory requirements for laboratory-developed tests (LDTs), but is committed to modernizing regulation. To address safety issues, the FDA is introducing a new web-based resource providing information on gene-drug interactions supported by scientific evidence. This resource includes a table of established and additional gene-drug interactions with sufficient scientific evidence. The FDA is also seeking public comment on specific pharmacogenetic associations and plans to update the table periodically.

title: FDA Works to Ensure Smooth Regulatory Transition of Insulin and Other Biological Products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken steps to ensure a smooth regulatory transition for insulin products and other biological products. On March 23, 2020, an application for a biological product will be deemed a license, enabling submission of applications for biosimilar and interchangeable products. This transition is expected to increase patient access, adding more choices and potentially reducing costs of insulin products. The FDA Commissioner, Stephen M. Hahn, stated that this change will bring down prices and help patients have access to more choices for life-saving drugs. The agency has issued a final rule and frequently asked questions documents to provide information to stakeholders. The rule defines the term "biological product" and clarifies the FDA's interpretation of the statutory term "protein." The transition is expected to open up new pathways for manufacturers to bring biosimilar and interchangeable versions of insulin and other transitioning products to market.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on January 28-29, 2020, to discuss various matters related to monetary policy and financial stability. The committee reaffirmed its Authorization for Domestic Open Market Operations and selected the Federal Reserve Bank of New York to execute transactions for the System Open Market Account. Lorie K. Logan was appointed as manager subject to approval from the same bank. Jerome H. Powell was re-elected as Chairman, John C. Williams as Vice Chairman, and James A. Clouse as Secretary. The committee also authorized the Federal Reserve Bank to conduct open market transactions in foreign currencies, including purchases and sales. Participants discussed financial stability risks, noting that low policy rates may contribute to a buildup of vulnerabilities, but agreed that supervisory, regulatory, and macroprudential tools should be used to address these risks. The FOMC maintained the federal funds rate at 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent, citing solid job gains and low unemployment rate.

title: FDA Takes Action with Indian Government to Protect Consumers From Illicit Medical Products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced its first bilateral enforcement operation with the Government of India, targeting approximately 500 shipments of illicit, unapproved prescription drugs and combination medical devices. The operation, called Operation Broadsword, took place from January 28 to 30 and was a collaboration between the FDA's Office of Regulatory Affairs, Office of Criminal Investigations, and the Government of India's Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs. Investigators examined over 800 shipments, identifying around 50 different FDA-regulated products, including medications for serious diseases such as cancer and HIV. The operation aims to stop illicit products from entering the country that may pose health risks to patients. This is part of the FDA's mission to inspect, detect, and intercept illegal products, including those that are unapproved, counterfeit, and potentially dangerous. The FDA and the Government of India have been strengthening bilateral engagement since September 2019, and this operation is a result of that cooperation.

title: FDA’s Actions in Response to 2019 Novel Coronavirus at Home and Abroad
body_summary: The FDA is proactively identifying and addressing potential disruptions to the medical product supply chain during the COVID-19 pandemic. The agency has dedicated additional resources to review and coordinate data to better identify potential vulnerabilities to the U.S. medical product sector. The FDA is closely monitoring reports of increased ordering of essential medical devices and conducting regular inspections of FDA-regulated products manufactured overseas. The agency has not seen increased risks for American consumers from imported products from China and continues to review products from China using its routine process. The FDA is also working to detect and prevent the spread of misinformation about COVID-19 treatments and vaccines.

title: FDA Approves Three Drugs for Nonprescription Use Through Rx-to-OTC Switch Process
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved three drugs for over-the-counter (OTC) use: Voltaren Arthritis Pain (diclofenac sodium topical gel, 1%), Pataday Twice Daily Relief (olopatadine HCl ophthalmic solution/drops, 0.1%), and Pataday Once Daily Relief (olopatadine HCl ophthalmic solution/drops, 0.2%). The approval process, called an Rx-to-OTC switch, allows the FDA to assess safety and effectiveness for self-medication. The drugs are intended for temporary relief of arthritis pain and itchy eyes due to pollen, ragweed, or animal hair. Approval was granted to GlaxoSmithKline plc for Voltaren Arthritis Pain, and to Alcon for Pataday Twice Daily Relief and Pataday Once Daily Relief.

title: FDA Authorizes Marketing of First Cardiac Ultrasound Software That Uses Artificial Intelligence to Guide User
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of Caption Guidance software, which uses artificial intelligence to assist medical professionals in acquiring high-quality cardiac ultrasound images. The software, developed by Caption Health Inc., is indicated for use in adult patients undergoing two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography (2D-TTE). The FDA evaluated two independent studies, which showed that the software enabled registered nurses to acquire echocardiography images and videos of diagnostic quality. The FDA reviewed the device through the De Novo premarket review pathway and is establishing special controls to ensure safety and effectiveness. The agency granted marketing authorization to Caption Health Inc. and plans to host a public workshop to discuss emerging applications of AI in radiological imaging.

title: FDA Expertise Advancing the Understanding of Intentional Genomic Alterations in Animals
body_summary: The FDA is overseeing intentional genomic alterations in animals developed using novel techniques, such as genome editing, through a risk-based approach. The agency is committed to fostering innovation, promoting consumer confidence, and protecting public health. The FDA's Center for Veterinary Medicine is leveraging its scientific and technical expertise to develop a timely and efficient process for overseeing genome editing in animals. A public education campaign will soon be undertaken to help consumers learn about the safety and benefits of agricultural biotechnology products. The FDA's Veterinary Innovation Program facilitates advancements in the development of innovative animal products. The agency is partnering with America's farmers, innovators, biotechnology companies, and research universities to oversee this space. An analysis published in Nature Biotechnology highlights the FDA's expertise in detecting unintended alterations in genome-edited animals.

title: FDA Authorizes Marketing of First Cardiac Ultrasound Software That Uses Artificial Intelligence to Guide User
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) authorized the marketing of Caption Guidance, a software that assists medical professionals in capturing cardiac ultrasound images. The software uses artificial intelligence to help users capture high-quality images of a patient's heart, specifically for two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography. The FDA's deputy director, Robert Ochs, Ph.D., stated that this authorization enables medical professionals to use this tool, increasing access to safe and effective cardiac diagnostics. The software was developed using machine learning to differentiate between acceptable and unacceptable image quality. The FDA evaluated data from two independent studies, showing that the software enabled registered nurses to capture echocardiography images of diagnostic quality. The FDA reviewed the device through the De Novo premarket review pathway and established special controls to ensure safety and effectiveness. The authorization was granted to Caption Health Inc.

title: FDA Takes Significant Step in Coronavirus Response Efforts, Issues Emergency Use Authorization for the First 2019 Novel Coronavirus Diagnostic
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) to enable the emergency use of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's (CDC) 2019-nCoV Real-Time RT-PCR Diagnostic Panel. The test was previously limited to use at CDC laboratories, but the EUA allows its use at any CDC-qualified lab across the country. This move comes after a public health emergency declaration by the Health and Human Services Secretary, Alex Azar, on January 31, which recognized the potential threat of the 2019-nCoV virus.

The 2019-nCoV virus, identified in Wuhan, China in December 2019, can cause severe respiratory illness in humans. The FDA Commissioner, Stephen M. Hahn, stated that the collaboration with the CDC has been vital in rapidly developing and facilitating access to the diagnostic test. The test provides presumptive detection of 2019-nCoV from respiratory secretions and is authorized for patients who meet the CDC criteria for 2019-nCoV testing.

The EUA is based on scientific data and recognizes the public health emergency posed by the 2019-nCoV virus. The FDA is committed to working with developers, international partners, and the US government to help support the public health response to the outbreak.

title: FDA and FTC Announce New Efforts to Further Deter Anti-Competitive Business Practices, Support Competitive Market for Biological Products to Help Americans
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) have signed a joint statement to enhance collaboration on a robust marketplace for biological products, including biosimilars and interchangeable products. The agencies will take steps to address false or misleading promotion about biosimilars and deter anti-competitive behavior. FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn stated that competition is key for affordable medicines, while FTC Chairman Joseph Simons emphasized the importance of enforcing antitrust laws in healthcare markets.

Biosimilars are highly similar to existing FDA-approved products, with the potential to reduce healthcare costs. The FDA and FTC have concerns about false or misleading statements comparing biological reference products and biosimilars, which may be slowing progress and hampering uptake. The agencies will collaborate on public outreach efforts, including a workshop on March 9, to address competition in the biologics market.

The FDA will publish draft guidance on presenting data and information about biosimilars and reference products in a truthful and non-misleading manner. The draft guidance is part of the FDA's Biosimilars Action Plan, which outlines four key strategies to accelerate biosimilar competition. The FDA is accepting comments on the draft guidance from February 4 to April 6.

title: FDA approves first drug for treatment of peanut allergy for children
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Palforzia, a peanut allergen powder, to mitigate allergic reactions in children with peanut allergy. Treatment with Palforzia can start in individuals aged 4-17 years with a confirmed diagnosis of peanut allergy. Patients who take Palforzia must continue to avoid peanuts in their diets. The treatment consists of three phases: Initial Dose Escalation, Up-Dosing, and Maintenance. Palforzia was assessed in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study involving approximately 500 peanut-allergic individuals, showing that 67.2% of recipients tolerated a 600 mg dose of peanut protein with no more than mild allergic symptoms after 6 months of maintenance treatment. The safety of Palforzia was also evaluated in two double-blind, placebo-controlled studies, with the most commonly reported side effects including abdominal pain and anaphylaxis. The FDA is requiring a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) with this approval, which includes elements to assure safe use, and will only be available through specially certified healthcare providers, health care settings, and pharmacies to patients who are enrolled in the REMS program.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in December indicates that the labor market remains strong and that economic activity has been rising at a moderate rate. Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Although household spending has been rising at a moderate pace, business fixed investment and exports remain weak. On a 12âmonth basis, overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy are running below 2 percent. Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1â1/2 to 1-3/4 percent. The Committee judges that the current stance of monetary policy is appropriate to support sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation returning to the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective. The Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook, including global developments and muted inflation pressures, as it assesses the appropriate path of the target range for the federal funds rate. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Patrick Harker; Robert S. Kaplan; Neel Kashkari; Loretta J. Mester; and Randal K. Quarles.

title: FDA launches mobile-friendly database with information on life-saving HIV drugs as part of ongoing mission to empower the public through increased access to information and data
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has launched an interactive database offering critical information about antiretroviral drugs (ARVs) eligible for purchase under the President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) program. The database aims to improve access to life-saving treatments for HIV patients worldwide. PEPFAR was created in 2003 to address the global HIV crisis, and since its launch, low-cost, quality-assured ARVs have been provided to over 15 million people globally. The FDA plays a critical role in ensuring safe and effective ARVs are available worldwide, including those eligible for purchase through PEPFAR. The database will provide essential information, including prescribing details, manufacturing information, and storage requirements, making it valuable to public health stakeholders.

title: FDA Continues Strong Support of Innovation in Development of Gene Therapy Products
body_summary: The FDA is announcing the release of six final guidances and a draft guidance on gene therapy manufacturing and clinical development. The agency aims to provide product developers with meaningful guidance to answer critical questions as they research and design their gene therapy products. The six final guidances cover manufacturing issues and provide recommendations for those focusing on gene therapy products in specific disease areas. The draft guidance on interpreting sameness of gene therapy products under the orphan drug regulations outlines the FDA's proposed current thinking on an interpretation of sameness between gene therapy products. The FDA Commissioner, Stephen M. Hahn, and the director of the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, Peter Marks, expressed their support for the growth of innovative research and product development in the field of gene therapy. The agency plans to continue working with stakeholders to make the development and review of gene therapy products more efficient while ensuring their safety and effectiveness.

title: FDA Announces Key Actions to Advance Development of Novel Coronavirus Medical Countermeasures
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced critical actions to advance development of novel coronavirus medical countermeasures. The FDA will collaborate with interagency partners, product developers, international partners, and global regulators to expedite the development and availability of medical products. FDA Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn said the agency is working closely with public health partners to mitigate the impact of the novel coronavirus. The FDA is sharing updates on processes in place to help developers understand the pathways for Emergency Use Authorization and is launching a webpage with key information for the public. Deputy Commissioner Anna Abram said the agency is committed to ensuring safe and effective medical countermeasures are available as quickly as possible. The FDA is working to facilitate the development and availability of diagnostics and therapeutics for the novel coronavirus. Sponsors can request information and templates for diagnostic tests and therapeutics via the FDA's Pre-IND Consultation program.

title: FDA informs health care providers, facilities and patients about potential cybersecurity vulnerabilities for certain GE Healthcare Clinical Information Central Stations and Telemetry Servers
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is issuing a safety communication to inform health care providers, facilities, and patients about cybersecurity vulnerabilities identified in certain GE Healthcare Clinical Information Central Stations and Telemetry Servers. These vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to remotely take control of the device, potentially silencing alarms or interfering with patient monitors. Suzanne Schwartz, M.D., MBA, acting director of the Office of Strategic Partnerships and Technology Innovation, stated that the agency is committed to addressing cybersecurity issues to keep patients safe. The FDA recommends that health care facilities segregate the network connecting patient monitors with the affected devices and use firewalls, segregated networks, and other technologies to minimize the risk of remote or local network attacks. This is the FDA's ninth safety communication on medical device cybersecurity vulnerabilities since 2013.

title: FDA approves first treatment option specifically for patients with epithelioid sarcoma, a rare soft tissue cancer
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted accelerated approval to Tazverik (tazemetostat) for the treatment of adults and pediatric patients aged 16 years and older with metastatic or locally advanced epithelioid sarcoma. Epithelioid sarcoma is a rare sub-type of soft tissue sarcoma with less than one percent of all soft tissue sarcomas. Tazverik blocks the activity of the EZH2 methyltransferase, which may help keep cancer cells from growing. A clinical trial enrolling 62 patients with metastatic or locally advanced epithelioid sarcoma showed an overall response rate of 15%, with 1.6% of patients having a complete response and 13% having a partial response. The most common side effects were pain, fatigue, nausea, and vomiting. Patients are at increased risk of developing secondary malignancies. The FDA advises healthcare professionals to use effective contraception during treatment and for a certain period after the final dose. Tazverik was granted accelerated approval and received Orphan Drug designation, with the FDA granting approval to Epizyme Inc.

title: FDA approves first treatment for thyroid eye disease
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Tepezza (teprotumumab-trbw) for the treatment of adults with thyroid eye disease, a rare condition that causes eye inflammation and bulging. The approval represents the first drug for this condition and has the potential to alter the course of the disease, potentially sparing patients from multiple invasive surgeries. Thyroid eye disease impacts a small percentage of the population, particularly women, and can be incapacitating. Tepezza was approved based on results from two studies involving 170 patients, who showed significant reductions in eye protrusion after treatment. Common adverse reactions include muscle spasm, nausea, and hair loss. The FDA granted Priority Review, Fast Track, and Breakthrough Therapy Designation, as well as Orphan Drug designation, to support the development of this product.

title: Statement on quality issues with certain Cardinal Health surgical gowns and packs
body_summary: Cardinal Health alerted its customers on Jan. 11 and Jan. 15, 2020, to potential quality issues affecting some of its Level 3 surgical gowns and PreSource procedural packs due to the potential for contamination. The FDA recommends that customers discontinue use of these products immediately. The FDA is working to assess the cause and full impact of the concerns. Specific product lots are impacted, and the FDA is concerned about possible contamination. Cardinal Health will soon issue a recall, and the FDA is engaged in activities to mitigate supply chain disruption, including identifying alternative Level 3 gowns. The FDA has a device shortages mailbox for reporting potential or actual supply issues.

title: Statement on the Salinas-linked romaine lettuce E. coli O157:H7 outbreak and status update on investigation
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is providing an update on the status of E. coli O157:H7 illnesses linked to romaine lettuce. Two multi-state romaine lettuce outbreaks, affecting 167 and 10 people in 27 and 5 states respectively, have been declared over. A third outbreak in Washington state, sickening 11 people, has also been declared over. The last reported illness onset date was December 21. The FDA's traceback investigation identified a common grower in Salinas, California, but the cause of the contamination remains unknown. Soil samples found a strain of E. coli unrelated to the outbreaks, but it does not explain the illnesses. The FDA is planning to conduct an in-depth root-cause investigation to inform preventive controls and prevent future outbreaks. The agency is committed to preventing foodborne illness and working with the industry to identify and address causes. The FDA is also launching a New Era of Smarter Food Safety initiative to improve its ability to track and trace products through the supply chain.

title: Michigan-based food manufacturer agrees to stop production after repeated food safety violations
body_summary: U.S. District Judge Sean F. Cox entered a consent decree of permanent injunction between the U.S. and Home Style Foods, Inc., owned by Michael J. Kowalski and quality manager Juan Valesquez. Home Style Foods, Inc. has agreed to discontinue selling food products until it complies with federal regulations. The decision follows multiple FDA inspections that found Listeria monocytogenes in the company's food preparation area and violations of seafood safety regulations. The FDA, led by Chief Counsel Stacy Cline Amin, obtained the injunction to prevent potentially contaminated food from reaching consumers. The consent decree prohibits the defendants from selling food until they meet certain requirements, including making corrective actions and notifying the FDA before operations can resume. The FDA had inspected the facility seven times between May 2009 and June 2018, finding significant objectionable conditions and Listeria monocytogenes in two of the inspections.

title: FDA approves the first targeted therapy to treat a rare mutation in patients with gastrointestinal stromal tumors
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Ayvakit (avapritinib) for the treatment of adults with unresectable or metastatic gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) harboring a PDGFRA exon 18 mutation. This approval includes the PDGFRA D842V mutation, the most common exon 18 mutation. Ayvakit is a kinase inhibitor that blocks a type of enzyme called a kinase and helps keep cancer cells from growing. The FDA based its approval on the results of a clinical trial involving 43 patients, including 38 patients with PDGFRA D842V mutation. The overall response rate for patients with PDGFRA exon 18 mutation was 84%, with 7% having a complete response. The recommended dose was 300 mg once daily. Common side effects included edema, nausea, fatigue, and vomiting. The FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track Designation to Ayvakit, as well as Orphan Drug Designation, and approved it for Blueprint Medicines Corporation.

title: FDA, USDA and EPA announce joint platform to streamline information about agricultural biotechnology products
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, the Department of Agriculture, and the Environmental Protection Agency launched a Unified Website for Biotechnology Regulation in recognition of January 2020 as National Biotechnology Month. The website streamlines information about agricultural biotechnology products and is part of President Donald J. Trump's Executive Order on Modernizing the Regulatory Framework for Agricultural Biotechnology Products. 

FDA Commissioner Stephen Hahn stated that the agency aims to foster flexible, risk-based approaches in biotechnology while protecting human and animal health. The Unified Website for Biotechnology Regulation describes the federal review process for certain biotechnology products and allows users to submit questions to the three agencies. 

The FDA's Plant and Animal Biotechnology Innovation Action Plan, announced in October 2018, focuses on the agency's risk-based regulatory approach. This approach aims to secure confidence in the reliability and performance of plant and animal-based innovative products.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: Federal Reserve staff revised up their forecast for real GDP growth in the second half of 2019 due to stronger household spending and business investment data. Despite this revision, GDP growth was still expected to slow in the coming years, mostly due to soft business investment and slower government spending increases. The unemployment rate was projected to remain flat around its current level through 2022, while total PCE price inflation was revised down a bit for 2019 and expected to rise above its pace this year beyond 2019. Participants reviewed monetary policy strategy, tools, and communication practices, emphasizing the importance of sustaining economic expansion to reach more people who had experienced difficulty finding employment. The Federal Reserve maintained the target range for the federal funds rate at 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent, judging it appropriate to support economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near 2 percent.

title: FDA finalizes enforcement policy on unauthorized flavored cartridge-based e-cigarettes that appeal to children, including fruit and mint
body_summary: The US FDA is prioritizing enforcement against unauthorized flavored e-cigarette products, particularly those appealing to kids, due to the 2019 National Youth Tobacco Survey showing over 5 million US middle and high school students are current e-cigarette users. Companies must cease manufacture, distribution, and sale of unauthorized flavored cartridge-based e-cigarettes within 30 days or face enforcement actions. The FDA will focus on products with labeling or advertising resembling kid-friendly foods and drinks, or products marketed directly to minors. The agency has accepted premarket applications for flavored ENDS products and will prioritize enforcement against products sold after May 12, 2020, without a submitted application.

title: FDA approves new treatment for adults with migraine
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Ubrelvy (ubrogepant) tablets for the acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults. Migraine affects an estimated 37 million people in the US, with Ubrelvy representing an important new option for its acute treatment. The FDA approved Ubrelvy after demonstrating its effectiveness in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials involving 1,439 adult patients with a history of migraine. The patients who received Ubrelvy experienced significantly greater pain freedom and symptom reduction compared to those receiving placebo. Common side effects reported were nausea, tiredness, and dry mouth. Ubrelvy is contraindicated for co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors.

title: FDA approves first generics of Eliquis
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved two applications for the first generics of Eliquis (apixaban) tablets to reduce the risk of stroke and systemic embolism in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation. Apixaban is also indicated for the prophylaxis of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and for the treatment of DVT and pulmonary embolism (PE) following initial therapy. The first generic approvals of a direct oral anticoagulant, apixaban does not require repeated blood testing. The approvals mark a key part of the FDA's Drug Competition Action Plan and aim to increase patient access to more affordable medicines. Atrial fibrillation affects an estimated 2.7-6.1 million people in the US, and apixaban will be dispensed with a Medication Guide for patients. Health care professionals should counsel patients on signs and symptoms of possible bleeding, and consider risks when scheduling patients for spinal procedures. The FDA granted approval to Micro Labs Limited and Mylan Pharmaceuticals Inc., and the medicine is available from the manufacturers.

title: FDA approves new treatment option for patients with HER2-positive breast cancer who have progressed on available therapies
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted accelerated approval to Enhertu (fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki) for the treatment of adults with unresectable or metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer who have received two or more prior anti-HER2-based regimens. Enhertu is a human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-directed antibody and topoisomerase inhibitor conjugate. The approval was based on the results of a clinical trial enrolling 184 female patients with HER2-positive, unresectable and/or metastatic breast cancer.

The overall response rate was 60.3%, with a median duration of response of 14.8 months. The prescribing information includes a Boxed Warning for the risk of interstitial lung disease and embryo-fetal toxicity. The FDA also granted Breakthrough Therapy and Fast Track designations to Enhertu, which expedites the development and review of drugs for serious conditions.

The approval was granted four months prior to the FDA's goal date, and Enhertu was approved by the FDA for Daiichi Sankyo.

title: FDA, DEA seize 44 websites advertising sale of illicit THC vaping cartridges to US consumers as part of Operation Vapor Lock
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) have seized 44 websites advertising the sale of illicit vaping cartridges containing tetrahydrocannabinol (THC). This action is part of Operation Vapor Lock, which aims to investigate the supply chain of vaping products linked to recent lung injuries. The FDA and DEA took action after identifying online networks advertising THC vaping cartridges in clear violation of federal law. Commissioner Stephen M. Hahn stated that the agency needs to fully understand the causes of vaping-related lung injuries and will continue to take action against online and in-person sources of illicit vaping products. Acting DEA Administrator Uttam Dhillon emphasized that these seizures send a message to anyone seeking to capitalize on the trend. The FDA encourages consumers to report suspected criminal activity, and the agency is analyzing samples from 31 states and one territory for the presence of various chemicals, including THC and nicotine.

title: First FDA-approved vaccine for the prevention of Ebola virus disease, marking a critical milestone in public health preparedness and response
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Ervebo, the first FDA-approved vaccine for the prevention of Ebola virus disease (EVD) in individuals 18 years of age and older. The vaccine was approved after a study conducted in Guinea during the 2014-2016 outbreak, which showed that Ervebo was 100% effective in preventing Ebola cases with symptom onset greater than 10 days after vaccination. The vaccine is administered as a single-dose injection and is a live, attenuated vaccine that has been genetically engineered to contain a protein from the Zaire ebolavirus. The FDA granted Priority Review and a Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher to Merck & Co., Inc. for the approval of Ervebo. The vaccine is critical in preventing the spread of EVD and is expected to help protect against the Zaire ebolavirus. The FDA approval is part of the agency's efforts to fight Ebola in close coordination with international partners, including the World Health Organization.

title: Statement on National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine report on framing opioid prescribing guidelines for acute pain
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) contracted the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM) to develop evidence-based guidelines for opioid analgesic prescribing for acute pain. NASEM provided a framework to evaluate current and future opioid prescribing, identifying gaps in evidence and outlining needed research. The FDA will consider NASEM's recommendations as part of implementing the Substance Use-Disorder Prevention that Promotes Opioid Recovery and Treatment for Patients and Communities Act (SUPPORT Act) provision. The FDA aims to reduce opioid exposure, prevent new addiction, and support treatment for opioid use disorder.

title: FDA takes efforts to improve quality of compounded drugs from outsourcing facilities through collaboration and education as part of new Center of Excellence
body_summary:
The FDA is announcing the Compounding Quality Center of Excellence to enhance collaboration among outsourcing facilities and improve the quality of compounded medicines. The initiative aims to provide educational programs and support outsourcing facilities in reliably producing high-quality products. The Center of Excellence will have three main areas of focus: in-person and online education and trainings, a conference to exchange ideas and best practices, and market research.

Registration is now open for the March courses, and participants will have the opportunity to earn continuing education credits while enhancing their understanding of necessary procedures and guidelines. The in-person trainings will target registered outsourcing facilities and will focus on key aspects of current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) and FDA policies.

The FDA will also host a Center of Excellence conference in September 2020 in Dallas, Texas, to provide a forum for outsourcing facilities and related stakeholders to offer their feedback on policies and regulatory issues. Market research will be conducted to better understand the possible barriers and opportunities outsourcing facilities may encounter, including business growth and viability, adhering to CGMP regulations, and interactions with the FDA.

The goal of the Center of Excellence is to help support outsourcing facilities' efforts to meet quality standards, which will hopefully reduce risks these products may pose to the public health.

title: FDA approves new type of therapy to treat advanced urothelial cancer
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has granted accelerated approval to Padcev, an antibody-drug conjugate targeting Nectin-4, a cell surface protein expressed on bladder cancer cells. The drug is indicated for adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer who have previously received a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor and platinum-containing chemotherapy. A clinical trial of 125 patients showed an overall response rate of 44%, with 12% having a complete response and 32% having a partial response. Common side effects include fatigue, peripheral neuropathy, and dry eye. The FDA granted accelerated approval to Astellas Pharma US Inc. and requires a further clinical trial to verify the clinical benefit of Padcev.

title: Trump Administration takes historic steps to lower U.S. prescription drug prices
body_summary: President Trump, along with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, issued a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) that would allow for the importation of certain prescription drugs from Canada. The NPRM is the first step in implementing a provision of federal law that would reduce the cost of covered products to the American consumer. Health and Human Services Secretary Alex Azar stated that the announcement outlines two pathways for the safe importation of certain prescription drugs. The FDA is accepting comments on the NPRM for 75 days and on a draft guidance for 60 days. The draft guidance describes procedures for drug manufacturers to follow to facilitate importation of prescription drugs, including biological products, that are FDA-approved and manufactured abroad. Eligible prescription drugs would have to be relabeled with the required U.S. labeling prior to importation and undergo testing for authenticity, degradation, and to ensure that the drugs meet established specifications and standards.

title: Statement on the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth District Ruling Regarding the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act
body_summary: The US Supreme Court's decision in Texas v. Azar confirms that the individual mandate, a key component of Obamacare, is unconstitutional. This ruling does not alter the current healthcare system. The administration continues to work on providing access to high-quality healthcare at an affordable price, while protecting those with preexisting conditions. The proposed radical healthcare changes by the far left would strip Americans of their current coverage, which the administration vows to prevent. The president prioritizes providing affordable, high-quality healthcare to the American people.

title: Statement on low-cost biosimilar and interchangeable protein products
body_summary: The FDA plans to remove the exclusion of "chemically synthesized polypeptides" from the biosimilar and interchangeable transition, allowing more efficient market entry for these products. This change will help expand access to lower-cost biosimilar and interchangeable protein products, such as insulin, and promote innovation in manufacturing methods. The change will enable chemically synthesized products to come to market through abbreviated pathways, reducing resource-intensity. The FDA is responsible for ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices, as well as regulating other products. The change is set to take effect in March 2020.

title: FDA authorizes first interoperable, automated insulin dosing controller designed to allow more choices for patients looking to customize their individual diabetes management device system
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of the Tandem Diabetes Care Control-IQ Technology, an interoperable automated glycemic controller device. The device connects to an alternate controller-enabled insulin pump (ACE pump) and integrated continuous glucose monitor (iCGM) to automatically adjust insulin delivery. This is the first such controller that can be used with other diabetes devices in a customizable diabetes management system for automated insulin delivery. The FDA's action continues its efforts to ensure the safety and efficacy of innovative diabetes management systems.

title: FDA clears first fully disposable duodenoscope, eliminating the potential for infections caused by ineffective reprocessing
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared for marketing the first fully disposable duodenoscope, the EXALT Model D Single-Use Duodenoscope, to treat bile duct disorders and other upper GI problems. The device eliminates the risk of potential infection due to ineffective reprocessing. The FDA has set safety risks, including potential injuries, to using the device. The FDA previously issued communications and granted Breakthrough Device designation to expedite the development of the device. The device was reviewed through the premarket clearance (510(k)) pathway and was cleared to Boston Scientific Corporation.

title: FDA approves use of drug to reduce risk of cardiovascular events in certain adult patient groups
body_summary: The US FDA has approved Vascepa (icosapent ethyl) as an adjunctive therapy to reduce cardiovascular risk among adults with elevated triglyceride levels of 150 mg/dL or higher, who also have established cardiovascular disease or diabetes and two or more additional risk factors. The FDA approved Vascepa for patients who continue physical activity and maintain a healthy diet. Vascepa is the first FDA-approved drug to reduce cardiovascular risk in patients with elevated triglyceride levels as an add-on to maximally tolerated statin therapy. The approval was granted to Amarin Pharma Inc. after a study involving 8,179 patients showed that Vascepa significantly reduced the risk of cardiovascular events. The active ingredient is eicosapentaenoic acid, derived from fish oil. Common side effects include musculoskeletal pain, peripheral edema, and atrial fibrillation.

title: FDA authorizes first test to aid in newborn screening for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of a newborn screening test for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD), a rare genetic disorder. The test, GSP Neonatal Creatine Kinase-MM kit, will help identify potential treatment options for newborns before symptoms appear. The test measures the concentration of a protein called CK-MM, which increases in the blood when there is muscle damage. Elevated levels may indicate DMD. The FDA reviewed the test through a de novo premarket review pathway and found it to be accurate in identifying DMD-causing genetic mutations. The kit is intended for newborn screening and not for diagnosis or screening of other forms of muscular dystrophy. The FDA is establishing special controls for tests of this type, which provide a reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness.

title: FDA grants accelerated approval to first targeted treatment for rare Duchenne muscular dystrophy mutation
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted accelerated approval to Vyondys 53 (golodirsen) injection to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) patients with a confirmed mutation of the dystrophin gene amenable to exon 53 skipping. The FDA recognized the urgent need for new treatments for serious neurological disorders and has a long-standing commitment to working with researchers, drug companies, and patients to develop and approve treatments for rare diseases. Vyondys 53 was approved under the accelerated approval pathway, which provides earlier patient access to promising new drugs while clinical trials are conducted to verify predicted clinical benefit. The drug was evaluated in a two-part clinical study, showing an increase in dystrophin production in skeletal muscle. The FDA is requiring the company to conduct a clinical trial to confirm the drug's clinical benefit. The most common side effects reported were headache, fever, and nausea. Approval was granted to Sarepta Therapeutics, and the FDA also granted Fast Track and Priority Review designations, as well as an Orphan Drug designation and a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher.

title: Statement on new findings and current status of the romaine lettuce E. coli O157:H7 outbreak investigation
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is updating its investigation into the E. coli O157:H7 outbreak linked to romaine lettuce. The initial investigation pointed to farms in Salinas, California, as potential sources of contaminated romaine lettuce. The FDA, in partnership with the California Department of Public Health and the California Department of Food and Agriculture, deployed inspection teams to these farms in November. While most samples tested negative, the Wisconsin Department of Health Services recently reported isolating E. coli O157:H7 from a bag of pre-washed, chopped romaine lettuce.

The FDA has also been tracking two separate outbreaks of E. coli O157:H7, including one linked to Fresh Express Sunflower Crisp Chopped Salad Kits, with eight confirmed cases in the US and 24 cases in Canada. The agency is working with health officials in Washington State regarding an outbreak associated with romaine consumption at a local restaurant chain, with 10 confirmed and three probable cases.

The FDA has identified a common grower between each of the outbreaks, reinforcing earlier traceback results. However, it's too early to determine if other sources may have been involved. The agency is actively investigating other traceback leads to triangulate a more precise location of the contamination. The FDA is using DNA-fingerprinting capabilities, such as Whole Genome Sequencing, to detect and link cases of foodborne illness, saving lives.

The agency is working with state partners, the industry, and technology-enabled traceability to target consumer advice to a defined growing region. The FDA is also conducting traceback investigations into the produce industry, which involves digging into past records to work backward from case-patients to the source of contaminated foods.

title: FDA issues warning letter for not including the most serious risks in advertisement for medication-assisted treatment drug
body_summary:
The FDA posted a warning letter to Alkermes, Inc. for misbranding the drug Vivitrol, an extended-release injection formulation of naltrexone, by omitting warnings about the most serious risks associated with the drug from promotional materials. Vivitrol is approved for the prevention of relapse to opioid dependence following opioid detoxification and should be part of a comprehensive management program that includes psychosocial support. The FDA is requesting Alkermes, Inc. to immediately cease advertising practices that misbrand Vivitrol and provide a written response to the warning letter by December 16.

The FDA is concerned because the print advertisement about Vivitrol fails to adequately communicate important warnings and precautions listed in the product labeling, including the risk of opioid overdose, a potentially fatal risk. The FDA is also requesting Alkermes, Inc. to include a comprehensive plan of action to disseminate truthful, non-misleading, and complete corrective messages about the issues discussed in the warning letter.

The FDA has issued this warning letter as part of its commitment to protect the public health by ensuring that prescription drug information is truthful, balanced, and accurately communicated. The FDA is also focusing on addressing the opioid crisis, which remains one of the FDA's top public health priorities.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in October indicates that the labor market remains strong and that economic activity has been rising at a moderate rate. Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Although household spending has been rising at a strong pace, business fixed investment and exports remain weak. On a 12âmonth basis, overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy are running below 2 percent. Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1â1/2 to 1-3/4 percent. The Committee judges that the current stance of monetary policy is appropriate to support sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective. The Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook, including global developments and muted inflation pressures, as it assesses the appropriate path of the target range for the federal funds rate. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; James Bullard; Richard H. Clarida; Charles L. Evans; Esther L. George; Randal K. Quarles; and Eric S. Rosengren.

title: FDA underscores that consumers should not use drugs, dietary supplements and devices recalled from Basic Reset and Biogenyx following consent decree for federal violations
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is alerting consumers of a recall of 25 drug, dietary supplement, and medical device product lines distributed by Basic Reset and Biogenyx of Hendersonville, Tennessee. A federal court entered a consent decree of permanent injunction between the United States and the two companies and their owner, Fred R. Kaufman III, in September. Basic Reset and Biogenyx must recall and stop distributing products until they comply with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and other requirements. Products to be recalled include drugs like Earth Wash and Ionyte, dietary supplements Mello-Tonin and Body Mass Reset, and devices Energy FX. The FDA issued recall notices on September 23 and October 18, requesting disposal or return to the place of purchase for products sold, purchased, or distributed after November 7, 2017. The FDA is reminding consumers not to use these products and distributors not to sell them, as they do not meet FDA regulations. Melinda K. Plaisier, FDA Associate Commissioner for Regulatory Affairs, stated that the FDA's laws are designed to protect public health by ensuring products are safe and effective. Basic Reset and Biogenyx have not received FDA approval for the sale of certain drugs and devices, despite claims they can diagnose, cure, or treat various conditions.

title: FDA sends warning to companies for offering unapproved umbilical cord blood products that may put patients at risk
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has warned Liveyon Labs Inc. and Liveyon LLC for processing and distributing unapproved products derived from umbilical cord blood, including PURE and PURE PRO. The FDA has also issued warning letters to RichSource Stem Cells, Inc., and Chara Biologics, Inc., for offering unapproved stem cell products to patients.

The warning letter issued to Liveyon Labs and Liveyon LLC notes significant deviations from current good tissue practice (CGTP) and current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) requirements, including deficient donor eligibility practices, inadequate aseptic practices, and deficient environmental monitoring.

The FDA has inspected the Liveyon Labs and Liveyon LLC facility and found evidence of significant deviations from CGTP and CGMP requirements, including deficient donor eligibility practices, inadequate aseptic practices, and deficient environmental monitoring.

The FDA is taking this action because Liveyon Labs and Liveyon LLC failed to take appropriate measures to protect patient safety. The agency is aware that there are establishments that prey upon vulnerable populations by commercially marketing stem cell products with false and misleading claims about their effectiveness for treating serious diseases.

The FDA has issued a safety alert about exosome products, and there have been reports of serious adverse events experienced by patients in Nebraska who were treated with unapproved products marketed as containing exosomes.

title: Statement from Janet Woodcock, M.D., director of FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, on impurities found in diabetes drugs outside the U.S.
body_summary: The US FDA is investigating the presence of genotoxic impurities, called nitrosamines, in some drug products, including metformin. Over the past year and a half, several drug products, including angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) and ranitidine, have been found to contain small amounts of nitrosamines. The FDA is aware that some metformin medicines in other countries were reported to have low levels of NDMA. The agency is investigating whether metformin in the US market contains NDMA and is above the acceptable daily intake limit of 96 nanograms. The FDA will work with companies to test samples of metformin sold in the US and will recommend recalls if high levels of NDMA are found. The FDA recommends that patients with type 2 diabetes continue taking metformin, but patients should consult their healthcare professional before stopping the medication.

title: FDA orders Puerto Rico fertility clinic to cease manufacturing immediately for significant violations that pose a danger to health
body_summary: The US FDA has ordered Gynecology, Reproductive Endocrinology and Fertility Institute in Puerto Rico to immediately cease manufacturing due to significant violations of FDA regulations. Dr. Rosa I. Cruz, the Medical Director and Owner, is also required to cease operations. The clinic's failure to test donor specimens for communicable diseases and determine donor eligibility put patients at risk. The FDA inspection found significant violations, including failure to test for HIV-1/2, hepatitis B virus, and other diseases. The clinic must immediately cease all manufacturing and resume operations only when it achieves compliance with FDA regulations. The FDA has asked patients who received reproductive tissues from the clinic to notify them of their concerns.

title: California-based food manufacturer agrees to stop production after repeated food safety violations
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced that Golden Gate Soy Products, a California-based food manufacturer, has agreed to discontinue selling food products until the company complies with federal regulations. The FDA found Listeria monocytogenes in the company's food preparation area and held food for distribution in insanitary conditions during several inspections since 2017. A consent decree was entered on November 22, 2019, between the US and Golden Gate Soy Products Inc., requiring the company to notify the FDA and take corrective actions before resuming operations. The FDA Associate Commissioner for Regulatory Affairs, Melinda K. Plaisier, stated that the FDA takes its role to protect the food supply seriously and that the company's practices are unacceptable. The consent decree prohibits the company from introducing contaminated or potentially contaminated food products into the marketplace.

title: FDA approves system for the delivery of ear tubes under local anesthesia to treat ear infection
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved a new system for delivering tympanostomy tubes (ear tubes) that can be inserted into the eardrum to treat recurrent ear infections. The Tubes Under Local Anesthesia (Tula) System, developed by Tusker Medical, is the first ear tube delivery system that can be performed in young children using local anesthesia in a physician's office setting. The system consists of anesthetic Tymbion, Tusker Medical tympanostomy tubes, and devices for delivery and anesthesia. The FDA evaluated data from 222 pediatric patients and found an 86% and 89% procedural success rate in children under 5 and 5-12 years old, respectively. The system is approved for use in children as young as six months old, but not for patients under six months or those with certain allergies. The Tula System was granted Breakthrough Device designation, which allows for expedited review and development. The FDA approved the system for patients suffering from recurrent ear infections, offering a safe and effective treatment option that can be administered with minimal discomfort.

title: FDA warns 15 companies for illegally selling various products containing cannabidiol as agency details safety concerns
body_summary: The US FDA has issued warning letters to 15 companies for violating the FD&C Act by selling CBD products as dietary supplements or adding CBD to human and animal foods. This action aims to address concerns about the safety of CBD products, including potential liver injury, interactions with other drugs, and unknown risks, particularly for vulnerable populations like children and pregnant women. The FDA has not approved any CBD products other than one prescription human drug product for rare epilepsy disorders. Companies must respond within 15 working days with a plan to correct violations, or face legal action, including product seizure and injunction. The FDA encourages reporting of adverse reactions through its MedWatch program to ensure public health and safety.

title: FDA approves novel treatment to target abnormality in sickle cell disease
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted accelerated approval to Oxbryta (voxelotor) for the treatment of sickle cell disease in adults and pediatric patients 12 years of age and older. The approval provides hope to approximately 100,000 people in the U.S. and over 20 million globally living with the condition. The FDA Commissioner, Adm. Brett P. Giroir, stated that the approval is a significant step in the battle against sickle cell disease. Oxbryta is an inhibitor of deoxygenated sickle hemoglobin polymerization, which can help reduce the severity of the condition. The therapy has shown a 51.1% increase in hemoglobin response rate in patients taking 1500 mg of Oxbryta, compared to 6.5% in the placebo group. Common side effects include headache, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and nausea. Accelerated Approval and Orphan Drug Designation were granted to Global Blood Therapeutics, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.

title: Statement on efforts to help make development of biosimilar and interchangeable insulin products more efficient
body_summary: The FDA is announcing new draft guidance to facilitate the development of and improve patient access to life-saving insulin products. The guidance aims to increase market competition among insulin products, which may lower costs for patients and payors and increase access and product choice. The draft guidance clarifies what data and information may be needed to support a demonstration of biosimilarity or interchangeability for a proposed insulin product. The FDA recommends that under certain circumstances, a comparative clinical immunogenicity study may not be necessary for approval of certain proposed biosimilar and interchangeable insulin products. The guidance reflects the FDA's decades of experience with insulin products and consideration of stakeholder feedback. The FDA recommends a more efficient development program that could ultimately bring biosimilar or interchangeable insulin products to the market more quickly.

title: Statement on new steps to advance innovation in medical device sterilization with ethylene oxide
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is closely monitoring the impact of ethylene oxide sterilization facility closures on the availability of sterile medical devices. To address this concern, the FDA has announced two new Innovation Challenges to accelerate the development and review of sterilization technology innovations. The FDA has selected 12 applications from 46 submissions, which will be accelerated for development and review. Additionally, the FDA is launching a new pilot program, the Ethylene Oxide Sterilization Master File Pilot Program, to expedite approvals of changes to ethylene oxide sterilization processes and facilities. This program aims to reduce ethylene oxide use and minimize supply interruptions, ensuring patient access to safe medical devices.

title: FDA approves new treatment for adults with partial-onset seizures
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved XCOPRI (cenobamate tablets) to treat partial-onset seizures in adults, providing an additional treatment option for patients with this difficult-to-control condition. The safety and efficacy of XCOPRI were established in two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies that enrolled 655 adults. The recommended maintenance dose is 200 mg daily, with some patients requiring additional titration to 400 mg daily. XCOPRI has been associated with Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS) and a shortening of the QT interval, and patients with hypersensitivity to cenobamate or Familial Short QT syndrome should not use the drug. Common side effects reported in clinical trials include somnolence, dizziness, fatigue, diplopia, and headaches.

title: FDA takes second action under international collaboration, approves new treatment option for patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted supplemental approval to Calquence (acalabrutinib) for the treatment of adults with chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL), as part of a collaboration with the Australian Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) and Health Canada through Project Orbis. This new approved indication provides a new treatment option for patients with CLL or SLL. The approval was based on two randomized clinical trials that compared Calquence to other standard treatments. The FDA also granted Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy designation, and approved AstraZeneca's application. The approval was made four months prior to the FDA's goal date, and utilized the Real-Time Oncology Review (RTOR) pilot program.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on October 29-30, 2019, where they discussed monetary policy strategy, tools, and communication practices. Staff briefings covered various topics, including negative interest rates, large-scale asset purchase programs, balance sheet policy tools, and forward guidance. The committee considered ways to enhance public confidence and support its monetary policy framework, evaluating tools for different economic scenarios and reviewing financial market developments. Participants discussed repo operations, with some advocating for a standing facility to support control of the federal funds rate. The FOMC reported accommodative financing conditions, with mortgage rates near their lowest level since mid-2016. Residential home-purchase originations remained high, while refinancing originations jumped to their highest level since late 2012. The committee voted to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent due to persistent inflation shortfalls and concerns about a decline in longer-run inflation expectations. Additionally, the FOMC approved a statement outlining steps to ensure an ample supply of reserves, allowing control over short-term interest rates through setting administered rates.

title: FDA approves first treatment for inherited rare disease
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has granted approval to Givlaari (givosiran) for the treatment of adult patients with acute hepatic porphyria. The drug, developed by Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, was approved based on a clinical trial of 94 patients, showing a 70% reduction in porphyria attacks compared to patients receiving a placebo. Givlaari can treat this disease by reducing the number of attacks that disrupt patients' lives. Common side effects include nausea and injection site reactions. The FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy, Priority Review, and Orphan Drug designations for Givlaari. Patients should be monitored for anaphylactic reactions and renal function, and have their liver function tested before and during treatment.

title: Statement from Sarah Yim, M.D., acting director of the Office of Therapeutic Biologics and Biosimilars in the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, on FDA’s continued progress facilitating competition in the biologic marketplace with approval of 25th biosimilar product
body_summary: The FDA has approved Abrilada, a biosimilar to Humira, allowing for increased competition in the market. This approval is one of nine new biosimilar products the FDA has taken action on in 2019, bringing the total to 25. The approval of biosimilar products offers more access to treatments and lower costs for patients. The FDA has also enrolled 74 programs for 38 reference products in the Biosimilar Product Development Program, laying the foundation for ongoing competition. Biosimilar products approved by the FDA undergo rigorous evaluation to meet licensure requirements and are manufactured under the same quality standards as brand-name medicines.

title: FDA approves first contact lens indicated to slow the progression of nearsightedness in children
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved the first contact lens to slow the progression of myopia in children between 8 and 12 years old. The MiSight contact lens, a single-use, disposable soft lens, was approved for use daily to correct nearsightedness and slow myopia progression. Myopia is a common cause of correctable visual impairment worldwide and can lead to other eye problems if severe. The approval was based on data from a three-year clinical trial of 135 children and real-world evidence. The trial showed that MiSight lenses reduced myopia progression and axial eye length changes compared to conventional soft contact lenses. The FDA granted approval to CooperVision Inc. using the Premarket Approval pathway, which requires sufficient valid scientific evidence to ensure the device is safe and effective.

title: FDA approves first targeted therapy to treat patients with painful complication of sickle cell disease
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Adakveo (crizanlizumab-tmca), a treatment to reduce vaso-occlusive crisis in patients with sickle cell disease, for those 16 years and older.
