The approval was based on a randomized clinical trial of 198 patients, who experienced fewer vaso-occlusive crisis visits annually and had a delayed time to first experience crisis. Common side effects included back pain, nausea, and joint pain. The FDA granted Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy designation, and Novartis is the manufacturer.

title: FDA clears first duodenoscope with disposable elevator piece, reducing the number of parts needing disinfection
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has cleared for marketing the first duodenoscope with a sterile, disposable elevator component, the Pentax Medical Video ED34-i10T2 model. This device reduces the number of parts that need to be cleaned and disinfected between uses, aiming to lower the risk of infection among patients. The FDA's director, Jeff Shuren, M.D., J.D., stated that improving duodenoscope safety is a top priority. Duodenoscopes, used in over 500,000 procedures annually, are less invasive than traditional surgery to treat various gastrointestinal conditions. The FDA has previously recommended transitioning to duodenoscopes with disposable components to reduce contamination. The Pentax Medical Video ED34-i10T2 was reviewed through the 510(k) pathway and received clearance from the FDA, which protects the public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of medical devices.

title: FDA approves new antibacterial drug to treat complicated urinary tract infections as part of ongoing efforts to address antimicrobial resistance
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Fetroja, an antibacterial drug, for treatment of patients 18 years old or older with complicated urinary tract infections, including kidney infections caused by susceptible Gram-negative microorganisms, who have limited or no alternative treatment options. The approval was based on a study of 448 patients with cUTIs, where 72.6% of Fetroja-treated patients showed resolution of symptoms and eradication of bacteria within seven days. However, labeling for Fetroja includes a warning about a higher all-cause mortality rate compared to other antibiotics, particularly in critically ill patients. The most common adverse reactions observed were diarrhea, constipation, and nausea. Fetroja should not be used in individuals with a history of severe hypersensitivity to beta-lactam antibacterial drugs. The FDA granted Priority Review and Qualified Infectious Disease Product designation to Shionogi & Co., Ltd.

title: FDA issues warning letter to Dollar Tree stores for receiving potentially unsafe drugs
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a warning letter to Greenbrier International, Inc., doing business as Dollar Tree, for receiving over-the-counter drugs produced by foreign manufacturers with serious violations of federal law. The warning letter outlines multiple violations of current good manufacturing practices at contract manufacturers used to produce Dollar Tree's Assured Brand OTC drugs, as well as other drug products sold at Dollar Tree and Family Dollar stores. The FDA is investigating and taking action against companies that place US patients at risk, and Dollar Tree has the ultimate responsibility to ensure that it does not sell potentially unsafe drugs. The warning letter details Dollar Tree's receipt of adulterated drugs from manufacturers that received FDA warning letters in 2018, and the FDA has requested the company implement a system to ensure that it does not import adulterated drugs. The agency encourages health care professionals and consumers to report any adverse events to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program.

title: FDA approves therapy to treat patients with relapsed and refractory mantle cell lymphoma supported by clinical trial results showing high response rate of tumor shrinkage
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted accelerated approval to Brukinsa (zanubrutinib) capsules for the treatment of adult patients with mantle cell lymphoma who have received at least one prior therapy. This approval provides another treatment option for patients with a life-threatening condition. Mantle cell lymphoma typically spreads to lymph nodes, bone marrow, and other organs by the time it is diagnosed. A single-arm clinical trial of Brukinsa showed that 84% of patients experienced tumor shrinkage, with a median duration of response of 19.5 months. Common side effects include decreased blood cell counts and upper respiratory tract infections. The FDA granted Accelerated Approval, Breakthrough Therapy Designation, and Orphan Drug Designation to BeiGene USA Inc., a company that will manufacture and distribute the drug.

title: FDA approves first therapy to treat patients with rare blood disorder
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Reblozyl (luspatercept–aamt) for the treatment of anemia in adult patients with beta thalassemia who require regular red blood cell transfusions. This approval, granted on an FDA Fast Track designation and Orphan Drug designation, is expected to help decrease the number of blood transfusions for patients with this inherited blood disorder. The approval is based on a clinical trial of 336 patients, where 21% of those who received Reblozyl achieved a 33% reduction in transfusions compared to 4.5% of those who received a placebo. Common side effects include headache, bone pain, and hypertension, which requires monitoring by healthcare professionals.

title: Statement on the agency’s efforts to protect patients through postmarket drug safety surveillance practices
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration prioritizes public health and safety. The FDA's postmarket surveillance and risk evaluation programs identify new adverse events and learn about known adverse events from over two million reports submitted annually through the MedWatch Program and VAERS. Staff use this information to identify safety concerns and recommend actions to improve product safety.

The 21st Century Cures Act (2016) amended the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, eliminating the requirement for the FDA to prepare a summary analysis of adverse drug reaction reports within 18 months or when 10,000 individuals use the drug, whichever occurs later. The Cures Act also required the FDA to make its best practices for drug safety surveillance publicly available.

The FDA has posted a draft document outlining its approach for timely postmarket analyses of drugs and biologics. The document includes risk-based principles, tools, methods, and signal detection and evaluation activities. The FDA monitors the safety of products with complex characteristics, such as new molecular entities, biological license applications, and products with complex pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic characteristics.

The FDA will investigate and consider appropriate actions if information changes the benefit-risk profile of a product, including labeling changes and requiring postmarketing studies. The agency will continue to provide guidance and oversight to ensure product sponsors complete postmarketing studies in a timely manner.

title: FDA authorizes marketing of first next-generation sequencing test for detecting HIV-1 drug resistance mutations
body_summary: The US FDA has authorized the marketing of a test to detect HIV Type-1 drug resistance mutations using next-generation sequencing (NGS) technology, known as the Sentosa SQ HIV Genotyping Assay. This test is the first to use NGS technology approved by the FDA for marketing in the US. The test will help healthcare providers select effective treatment options for patients with HIV by identifying mutations in the virus that can impact the effectiveness of certain drugs. The FDA reviewed data demonstrating the test's sensitivity and specificity and established special controls to ensure its accuracy and reliability. The authorization is expected to provide an additional tool in the fight against HIV, with the potential to help patients with HIV live longer and healthier lives.

title: FDA authorizes marketing of first next-generation sequencing test for detecting HIV-1 drug resistance mutations
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of the Sentosa SQ HIV Genotyping Assay, a test to detect human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) Type-1 drug resistance mutations using next generation sequencing (NGS) technology. This is the first HIV drug resistance assay to use NGS technology authorized for marketing in the U.S. The assay detects mutations in genes of the HIV-1 virus from a sample of a patient's blood, helping healthcare providers select an effective combination of drugs in an antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimen. The FDA reviewed data demonstrating a greater than 95% sensitivity and specificity in detecting 342 HIV drug-resistant mutations. The test is intended for use in patients with HIV-1 who are about to start or already taking antiviral therapy.

title: Statement on new testing results, including low levels of impurities in ranitidine drugs
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is investigating the detection of a contaminant called N-Nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) in ranitidine medications, commonly known by the brand name Zantac. The agency has found levels of NDMA in ranitidine that are similar to those expected from eating common foods like grilled or smoked meats. However, some levels exceed the FDA's acceptable limits. The agency is asking companies to voluntarily recall ranitidine products with NDMA levels above the acceptable limits. Additionally, the FDA is requesting that manufacturers test their drugs and send samples to the agency for testing. The agency has not found NDMA in other H2 blockers and proton pump inhibitors. Patients taking prescription ranitidine or nizatidine are advised to speak with their healthcare professional about other treatment options.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September indicates that the labor market remains strong and that economic activity has been rising at a moderate rate. Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Although household spending has been rising at a strong pace, business fixed investment and exports remain weak. On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy are running below 2 percent. Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. In light of the implications of global developments for the economic outlook as well as muted inflation pressures, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent. This action supports the Committee's view that sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective are the most likely outcomes, but uncertainties about this outlook remain. The Committee will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook as it assesses the appropriate path of the target range for the federal funds rate. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; James Bullard; Richard H. Clarida; Charles L. Evans; and Randal K. Quarles. Voting against this action were: Esther L. George and Eric S. Rosengren, who preferred at this meeting to maintain the target range at 1-3/4 percent to 2 percent.

title: USDA, EPA and FDA announce partnership with the Food Waste Reduction Alliance
body_summary: The U.S. Department of Agriculture, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced a partnership with the Food Waste Reduction Alliance to formalize industry education and outreach efforts with the Grocery Manufacturers Association, the Food Marketing Institute, and the National Restaurant Association. The partnership aims to reduce food waste generated, increase safe and nutritious food donations, and divert food waste from landfills. Acting FDA Commissioner Ned Sharpless and U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Sonny Perdue expressed support for the shared goal of reducing food waste, while EPA Administrator Andrew Wheeler highlighted the environmental and social benefits of reducing food loss and waste. The agreement builds upon the Winning on Reducing Food Waste Initiative launched in 2018, which aims to reduce food loss and waste by 50 percent by 2030.

title: Digital submission of adverse event reports for investigational new drug applications reflects FDA’s ongoing modernization efforts
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is requiring electronic submission of certain safety reports for products being evaluated under an Investigational New Drug (IND) application into the FDA's Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS). The FDA is making available a draft guidance outlining the process, which will allow the agency to access and review both pre- and post-market safety information in the same system and with the same data standard. The guidance aims to implement a standard digital framework for the electronic submission, review, and tracking of IND safety reports in FAERS, using a data standard known as ICH E2B. The submission process will be voluntary until two years after the finalization of the guidance, at which point it will be mandatory for sponsors of commercial INDs. The FDA encourages all sponsors to begin submitting IND safety reports to FAERS voluntarily as soon as the new process is available.

title: Statement on FDA’s new report regarding root causes and potential solutions to drug shortages
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is prioritizing access to safe and effective medicines for Americans. In response to Congress' request, the FDA formed an inter-agency task force to study drug shortages, determine root causes, and make recommendations for enduring solutions. The task force analyzed 163 drugs that went into shortage from 2013 to 2017 and found that shortages often occurred due to disruption in supply, with prices rarely rising after shortages began. The task force recommends increasing understanding of the impacts of drug shortages and companies' contracting practices, developing a system to measure and rate a facility's quality management maturity, and considering new contracting approaches to ensure a reliable supply of drugs. The report also describes legislative proposals and planned FDA initiatives to prevent supply disruptions and emphasizes the need for international action.

title: Statement on concerns with medical device availability due to certain sterilization facility closures
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is closely monitoring the closure of certain large-scale sterilization facilities that use ethylene oxide, which could affect the availability of some sterile medical devices. The FDA is working with impacted device manufacturers and healthcare delivery organizations to minimize adverse effects on patients. A public advisory committee meeting is scheduled for November 6 and 7, 2019, to develop new strategies to reduce ethylene oxide emissions from medical device sterilization. The FDA collaborates with the U.S. EPA to review and enforce Clean Air Act regulations, ensuring public safety and mitigating the impact of sterilization facility closures on patients.

title: Statement on agency’s first year accomplishments implementing SUPPORT Act authorities to address the opioids crisis
body_summary: The FDA has implemented actions under the SUPPORT Act to address the opioid crisis, including clarifying regulation of non-addictive pain products and developing evidence-based opioid analgesic prescribing guidelines. The agency has also restricted the entrance of illicit drugs, improved packaging and disposal, and clarified postmarket authorities. Additionally, the FDA is working to promote the development of non-opioid pain treatments. The FDA remains committed to addressing the opioid crisis, decreasing exposure to opioids, and preventing new addiction, utilizing its regulatory authority to address the crisis.

title: Statement on the agency’s efforts to protect patients from potentially harmful drugs sold as homeopathic products
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) recognizes the use of unapproved drugs, including homeopathic products, to treat diseases and conditions. Homeopathic products are marketed as natural alternatives but may not meet modern standards for safety and effectiveness. The FDA uses a risk-based approach to monitor these products and evaluate reports of adverse effects.

Homeopathy is an alternative medical practice that originated in the late 1700s and is based on the principle of "like cures like." Homeopathic drug products are made from various substances, including plants, animals, minerals, and chemicals, and have the potential to cause harm if poorly manufactured or marketed as substitute treatments for serious diseases.

In 2017, the FDA issued a draft guidance discussing its risk-based enforcement approach to homeopathic products. The agency has revised the draft guidance and is seeking public input. The revised guidance prioritizes categories of homeopathic products that pose a higher risk to public health, including products with certain ingredients and routes of administration.

The FDA is withdrawing the Compliance Policy Guide (CPG) 400.400, which was issued in 1988 and is inconsistent with the agency's risk-based approach. The agency has issued warning letters to companies that produce homeopathic products for significant violations of current good manufacturing practice regulations.

The FDA is committed to a risk-based approach to homeopathic products and will continue to take regulatory and enforcement actions when patients are at risk. The agency encourages healthcare professionals and consumers to report adverse events or quality problems with homeopathic products to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program.

title: Statement on the agency’s continued efforts to protect women’s health and enhance safety information available to patients considering breast implants
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is issuing a draft guidance to help ensure patients have complete information about the benefits and risks of breast implants. The draft guidance recommends that manufacturers incorporate a boxed warning and patient decision checklist in the device's labeling. The boxed warning should include risks such as the chance of developing complications, additional surgery, and breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL). A patient decision checklist can guide discussion during a patient's consultation with a surgeon. The guidance also proposes revising rupture screening recommendations for patients with silicone gel-filled breast implants, recommending ultrasound or MRI screening at five to six years following implantation and then every two years thereafter. Additionally, the FDA recommends that breast implant manufacturers include product ingredient information in the device's labeling and provide updated information on the manufacturer's website.

title: Statement on the agency’s continued efforts to protect women’s health and enhance safety information available to patients considering breast implants
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a draft guidance to help ensure patients have complete information about the benefits and risks of breast implants. The draft guidance recommends that manufacturers incorporate a boxed warning and patient decision checklist in the device's labeling, update recommendations for patient screening for device rupture, and include product ingredient information in a way that is easy for patients to understand. The guidance also recommends revising screening recommendations for patients with silicone gel-filled breast implants, including increased screening intervals and easier access to information. The FDA aims to improve patient safety and informed decision-making for women considering breast implants.

title: FDA grants first-ever modified risk orders to eight smokeless tobacco products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of eight Swedish Match USA, Inc. snus smokeless tobacco products through the modified risk tobacco product (MRTP) pathway. The products, sold under the "General" brand name, had previously been authorized for U.S. sale without modified risk claims in 2015. The FDA made this authorization after reviewing scientific evidence submitted by the company, which supports the claim that using General Snus instead of cigarettes reduces the risk of mouth cancer, heart disease, lung cancer, stroke, emphysema, and chronic bronchitis. The agency has also placed stringent advertising and promotion restrictions on the products, including a requirement to restrict advertising to adults. The products' packaging and advertising must bear warning statements required for all smokeless tobacco products. The MRTP orders are product-specific and limited to five years.

title: FDA grants first-ever modified risk orders to eight smokeless tobacco products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has authorized the marketing of eight Swedish Match USA, Inc. snus smokeless tobacco products under the "General" brand name, marking the first time the agency has used the modified risk tobacco product (MRTP) pathway. The products, previously authorized for US sale without modified risk claims in 2015, can now be marketed with the claim "Using General Snus instead of cigarettes puts you at a lower risk of mouth cancer, heart disease, lung cancer, stroke, emphysema, and chronic bronchitis." The FDA reviewed scientific evidence supporting this claim and found it to be supported. The agency has placed stringent restrictions on advertising and promotion to prevent youth access and exposure. The products' packaging and advertising must bear required warning statements. The authorization is product-specific and limited to five years, during which time the manufacturer must conduct postmarket studies.

title: FDA, FTC warn company marketing unapproved cannabidiol products with unsubstantiated claims to treat teething and ear pain in infants, autism, ADHD, Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s disease
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) posted a joint warning letter to Rooted Apothecary LLC, alleging it illegally sells unapproved products containing cannabidiol (CBD) online with unsubstantiated claims about treating various diseases and conditions. The FDA and FTC are concerned that Rooted Apothecary's claims are not supported by scientific evidence and may harm vulnerable populations, such as infants and children. The agency has determined that CBD products cannot be marketed as dietary supplements and has requested the company correct the violations within 15 working days, warning of potential legal action, including product seizure and injunctions.

title: FDA approves new breakthrough therapy for cystic fibrosis
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Trikafta, the first triple combination therapy, for patients 12 years and older with cystic fibrosis who have at least one F508del mutation. The FDA used Priority Review, Fast Track, Breakthrough Therapy, and orphan drug designation programs to advance the approval in the most efficient manner possible. Trikafta is approved for patients with 90% of the cystic fibrosis population, affecting 27,000 people in the US. Two trials demonstrated the efficacy of Trikafta in increasing forced expiratory volume in one second, improving sweat chloride, and reducing pulmonary exacerbations. The safety profile of Trikafta was generally similar across all subgroups of patients, with serious adverse reactions including rash and influenza events. The FDA approved Trikafta to Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated, which will receive a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher.

title: Baby powder manufacturer voluntarily recalls products for asbestos
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a voluntary recall of Johnson's Baby Powder after testing found chrysotile fibers, a type of asbestos, in a sample from one lot of the product. Consumers who have the affected lot (#22318RB) should stop using it immediately and contact Johnson & Johnson for a refund. The FDA has been conducting testing of talc-containing cosmetic products for asbestos since 2018, testing approximately 50 products. Two samples of Johnson's Baby Powder, one positive and one negative, were tested. The FDA expects to issue full results by the end of the year. The agency will continue to update its safety alert with new information. Johnson & Johnson has previously warned consumers about products tested positive for asbestos. The FDA is calling on industry to register and list products via the Voluntary Cosmetics Registration Program.

title: Statement on continued progress enhancing patient access to high-quality, low-cost generic drugs
body_summary: The FDA's generic drug program is having a strong year, with 1,171 generic drug approvals in fiscal year 2019, breaking the all-time record of 971 for fiscal year 2018. This includes 935 full approvals and 236 tentative approvals, with 125 applications for first generics of medicines with no generic competition. The FDA approved first generics for emergency opioid overdose treatment and drugs to treat conditions such as pulmonary arterial hypertension, breast cancer, seizures, depression, and various infections. The FDA's scientific review and assessment process ensures that generic medications meet the same standards as name-brand medications. The agency will continue to publish guidances and take policy steps to facilitate a stable and competitive market, increasing access to medicines.

title: Statement Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation
body_summary: Consistent with its January 2019 Statement Regarding Monetary Policy Implementation and Balance Sheet Normalization, the Committee reaffirms its intention to implement monetary policy in a regime in which an ample supply of reserves ensures that control over the level of the federal funds rate and other short-term interest rates is exercised primarily through the setting of the Federal Reserve's administered rates, and in which active management of the supply of reserves is not required. To ensure that the supply of reserves remains ample, the Committee approved by notation vote completed on October 11, 2019 the following steps: In light of recent and expected increases in the Federal Reserve's non-reserve liabilities, the Federal Reserve will purchase Treasury bills at least into the second quarter of next year in order to maintain over time ample reserve balances at or above the level that prevailed in early September 2019. In addition, the Federal Reserve will conduct term and overnight repurchase agreement operations at least through January of next year to ensure that the supply of reserves remains ample even during periods of sharp increases in non-reserve liabilities, and to mitigate the risk of money market pressures that could adversely affect policy implementation. These actions are purely technical measures to support the effective implementation of the FOMC's monetary policy, and do not represent a change in the stance of monetary policy. The Committee will continue to monitor money market developments as it assesses the level of reserves most consistent with efficient and effective policy implementation. The Committee stands ready to adjust the details of these plans as necessary to foster efficient and effective implementation of monetary policy. In connection with these plans, the Federal Open Market Committee voted unanimously to authorize and direct the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, until instructed otherwise, to execute transactions in the System Open Market Account in accordance with the following domestic policy directive: "Effective October 15, 2019, the Federal Open Market Committee directs the Desk to undertake open market operations as necessary to maintain the federal funds rate in a target range of 1-3/4 to 2 percent. In light of recent and expected increases in the Federal Reserve's non-reserve liabilities, the Committee directs the Desk to purchase Treasury bills at least into the second quarter of next year to maintain over time ample reserve balances at or above the level that prevailed in early September 2019. The Committee also directs the Desk to conduct term and overnight repurchase agreement operations at least through January of next year to ensure that the supply of reserves remains ample even during periods of sharp increases in non-reserve liabilities, and to mitigate the risk of money market pressures that could adversely affect policy implementation. In addition, the Committee directs the Desk to conduct overnight reverse repurchase operations (and reverse repurchase operations with maturities of more than one day when necessary to accommodate weekend, holiday, or similar trading conventions) at an offering rate of 1.70 percent, in amounts limited only by the value of Treasury securities held outright in the System Open Market Account that are available for such operations and by a per-counterparty limit of $30 billion per day. The Committee directs the Desk to continue rolling over at auction all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of Treasury securities and to continue reinvesting all principal payments from the Federal Reserve's holdings of agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities received during each calendar month. Principal payments from agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities up to $20 billion per month will continue to be reinvested in Treasury securities to roughly match the maturity composition of Treasury securities outstanding; principal payments in excess of $20 billion per month will continue to be reinvested in agency mortgage-backed securities. Small deviations from these amounts for operational reasons are acceptable. The Committee also directs the Desk to engage in dollar roll and coupon swap transactions as necessary to facilitate settlement of the Federal Reserve's agency mortgage-backed securities transactions." More information about these plans may be found on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's website . title: FDA approves new treatment for patients with migraine
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Reyvow tablets for the acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults. Reyvow is not indicated for preventive treatment. The approval was based on two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials involving 3,177 adult patients with a history of migraine. In these studies, patients receiving Reyvow experienced significantly greater pain resolution and symptom relief compared to those receiving placebo. The FDA granted approval to Eli Lilly and Company. Migraine affects over 10% of people worldwide, with women being three times more likely to experience it. The effectiveness of Reyvow was demonstrated two hours after treatment, but patients were advised not to drive or operate machinery for at least eight hours after taking the drug due to the risk of driving impairment.

title: FDA allows marketing of first rapid diagnostic test for detecting Ebola virus antigens
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has allowed the marketing of the first rapid diagnostic test, the OraQuick Ebola Rapid Antigen Test, to detect Ebola virus antigens in human blood and cadaveric oral fluid. The test provides a rapid, presumptive diagnosis that must be confirmed. The test was granted Breakthrough Device designation, which allows the company to expedite evidence generation and the agency's review of the device. The FDA has established special controls to ensure the safety and effectiveness of the test. The test is intended for use in patients suspected of and with signs or symptoms consistent with Ebola Virus Disease (EVD), and is not intended for general Ebola infection screening or testing of individuals at risk of exposure without observable signs of infection.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on September 17-18, 2019, discussing monetary policy strategy, tools, and communication practices amid concerns about the effective lower bound (ELB) constraining future interest rates. The committee reviewed potential challenges in achieving employment and inflation objectives due to low neutral interest rates, uncertainty about the neutral rate, and long-lasting ELB spells. FOMC participants discussed strengthening the monetary policy framework to avoid such scenarios. The FOMC lowered the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-3/4 to 2 percent in response to strong labor market conditions and moderate economic activity.

title: FDA awards two grants for natural history studies in rare diseases
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has awarded two new research grants for natural history studies in rare diseases. The grants, totaling $6.5 million over four years, are intended to facilitate the design of efficient clinical trials to test future treatments. The studies will focus on rare diseases such as medullary thyroid carcinoma and cardiac disease in Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The grants were awarded to the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center and Vanderbilt University Medical Center, respectively. Funding for these grants comes from the FDA's Orphan Products Grants Program, which is funded by Congress.

title: FDA approves first treatment to increase pain-free light exposure in patients with a rare disorder
body_summary: The US FDA has approved Scenesse (afamelanotide), an implant, to increase pain-free light exposure in adult patients with a history of phototoxic reactions from erythropoietic protoporphyria. This rare disorder causes skin pain and changes when exposed to light due to accumulated protoporphyrin IX. Scenesse, a melanocortin-1 receptor agonist, increases eumelanin production in the skin. Clinical trials showed that patients who received Scenesse spent more time outdoors without pain than those who received a placebo, with median hours of 64 and 0.75, respectively. Side effects include implant site reactions, nausea, and skin hyperpigmentation. Scenesse is administered by healthcare professionals and patients are encouraged to maintain sun protection measures. The FDA granted this application Priority Review designation and Orphan Drug designation to Clinuvel.

title: FDA awards two grants for natural history studies in rare diseases
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has awarded two new research grants for natural history studies in rare diseases, providing over $4.1 million over the next four years. The grants will fund studies on medullary thyroid carcinoma and cardiac disease in Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center and Vanderbilt University Medical Center will receive approximately $1.7 million and $2.4 million, respectively, for their prospective studies. The grants aim to provide critical knowledge on how rare diseases progress over time, inform decision-making for treatment, and improve clinical trial efficiency.

title: FDA awards 12 grants to fund new clinical trials to advance the development of medical products for the treatment of rare diseases
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has awarded 12 new clinical trial research grants totaling more than $15 million over the next four years to enhance the development of medical products for patients with rare diseases. The grants were awarded to principal investigators from academia and industry across the country through theOrphan Products Clinical Trials Grants Program, funded by Congress to encourage clinical development of drugs, biologics, medical devices, and medical foods for the treatment of rare diseases.

The grants aim to substantially contribute to marketing approval of products to treat rare diseases or provide essential data needed for development of such products. The recipients include institutions such as Chemocentryx, Inc., Cincinnati Children’s Hospital Medical Center, Columbia University Health Sciences, Cumberland Pharmaceuticals, Inc., and others.

The FDA received 89 clinical trial grant applications that were reviewed and evaluated for scientific and technical merit by over 100 rare disease experts. The grants are focused on supporting product development to meet the needs of patients impacted by a variety of rare diseases, mainly those affecting children and cancers.

The recipients will conduct phase 1 and 2 studies, as well as other types of studies, to advance treatments for rare diseases such as Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy, sickle cell disease, and Fanconi Anemia. The grants are part of the FDA's efforts to foster product development in areas of unmet need and to support research for rare diseases that have little or no treatment options for patients.

Since its creation in 1983, the Orphan Products Grants Program has provided over $400 million to fund more than 600 new clinical studies. The program aims to speed the development of products for rare diseases and ultimately make needed treatments available to those patients who need them most.

title: Statement on consumer warning to stop using THC vaping products amid ongoing investigation into lung illnesses
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) are investigating severe lung injuries and deaths associated with vaping products. The latest data shows that vaping products containing tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the primary psychoactive component of cannabis, are the primary cause of these illnesses. The FDA urges consumers to stop using THC vaping products and not to modify or add substances to purchased products. The agency is collecting and analyzing samples, conducting criminal and civil investigations, and working with federal, state, and local partners to identify the cause or causes of the illnesses. The FDA has collected over 440 samples from 18 states and is prioritizing those associated with patient illnesses. The agency is committed to working to answer critical questions and protect the public health.

title: Executive Order 13890—Protecting and Improving Medicare for Our Nation's Seniors
body_summary:
President Donald J. Trump signed an executive order on October 3, 2019, titled "Maximizing Freedom for Medicare Patients and Providers." The order aims to improve the Medicare program by encouraging competition, reducing waste and fraud, and promoting better quality care. Key actions include:

- Proposing regulations to provide seniors with better quality care and cost data within 1 year.
- Using Medicare claims data to inform health providers about practice patterns that are outliers or outside recommended standards of care within 1 year.
- Proposing changes to the Medicare program to combat fraud, waste, and abuse, including through the use of artificial intelligence, by January 1, 2021, and annually thereafter.
- Studying approaches to transition toward true market-based pricing in the FFS Medicare program and submitting the results to the President within 180 days.
- Proposing regulatory changes to reduce the burden on providers and eliminate inefficiencies within 1 year.

The Administration aims to enhance the program's fiscal sustainability through alternative payment methodologies, increase choice, and lower regulatory burdens. The President proposes regulations to provide beneficiaries with more diverse and affordable plan choices, improve access to providers, enable providers to spend more time with patients, encourage innovation for patients, and reward care through site neutrality.

title: FDA approves second drug to prevent HIV infection as part of ongoing efforts to end the HIV epidemic
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Descovy (emtricitabine 200 mg and tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg) for HIV-1 pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) in at-risk adults and adolescents weighing at least 35kg, excluding those with receptive vaginal sex. Descovy is not indicated for individuals at risk of HIV-1 infection from receptive vaginal sex. The FDA approval is based on a randomized, double-blind multinational trial showing that Descovy is similar to Truvada in reducing the risk of acquiring HIV-1 infection. The primary endpoint was the rate of HIV-1 infection in each group, with the trial following participants for 48 to 96 weeks. Descovy is contraindicated in individuals with unknown or positive HIV-1 status. The approval provides more prevention options for certain patients at-risk for acquiring HIV and aims to reduce new HIV infections by 75% in the next five years and by 90% in the next ten years.

title: FDA informs patients, providers and manufacturers about potential cybersecurity vulnerabilities for connected medical devices and health care networks that use certain communication software
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is informing patients and healthcare professionals about a set of cybersecurity vulnerabilities, referred to as "URGENT/11", that may introduce risks for medical devices and hospital networks. The vulnerabilities, which exist in a third-party software called IPnet, affect several operating systems and may impact certain medical devices connected to a communications network. The FDA is urging manufacturers to remain vigilant and take proactive steps to disclose vulnerabilities and mitigate them. The agency is recommending that manufacturers conduct a risk assessment and develop risk mitigation plans to address the vulnerabilities. Patients should talk to their healthcare providers to determine if their medical device could be affected and seek help immediately if they notice any changes in functionality. The FDA will continue to assess new information and keep the public informed if significant new information becomes available.

title: Statement on measuring the progress being made through implementing the FDA Food Safety Modernization Act
body_summary: Congress passed the U.S. Food and Drug Administration Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) in 2011 to shift the food safety system from response to prevention. As the seven foundational rules of FSMA reach their compliance dates, the FDA has launched a new dashboard, Food Safety Dashboard, to track implementation and progress. The dashboard publishes metrics on compliance with the FSMA rules, including preventive control rules and recall times. Initial data show that since 2016, the majority of companies inspected are in compliance with the new requirements, and industry has improved the time to initiate voluntary recalls from four days to two days in 2019. The FDA plans to update the data quarterly, with the goal of publishing metrics for all seven rules, aiming to reduce foodborne illnesses and death attributed to contaminated food.

title: FDA and DEA warn website operators illegally selling opioids
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) have issued joint warning letters to four online networks operating 10 websites that illegally market unapproved and misbranded versions of opioid medicines, including tramadol. The warning letters instruct the networks to immediately stop selling these opioids to American consumers. This joint action demonstrates the federal government's commitment to enhance interagency coordination to respond to the opioid crisis. The networks, including Divyata Euphoria Healthcare Pvt Ltd. and JCM Dropship Meds4U, have been found to violate the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and the Controlled Substances Act. The FDA has issued similar warning letters in May and August 2018 and March 2023, and will continue to take regulatory action against those who contribute to the illegal importation and sale of opioids.

title: Statement on continued efforts to evaluate materials in medical devices to address potential safety questions
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is taking next steps in evaluating the safety of specific materials used in medical devices, particularly metals and metal alloys. The agency will hold a public advisory committee meeting on November 13-14, 2019, to convene experts and the public on this issue. The meeting aims to discuss the potential for certain patients to develop immune and inflammatory reactions to metal-containing implants and to evaluate the adequacy of current approaches and standards for biocompatibility. The FDA is also working to engage the public, industry stakeholders, and scientists to determine the current state of the science and identify critical gaps. The agency has posted two scientific reviews on the current scientific knowledge regarding metal implants and dental amalgams.

title: FDA approves first treatment for children with rare diseases that cause inflammation of small blood vessels
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Rituxan injection to treat granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA) and microscopic polyangiitis (MPA) in children 2 years of age and older in combination with glucocorticoids. This is the first approved treatment for children with these rare diseases, which cause inflammation in small blood vessels. Rituxan was approved under priority review and orphan designation, with a 6-month review goal and incentives for rare disease development. The safety profile in pediatric patients was consistent with known safety profiles in adult patients with autoimmune diseases. A clinical trial of 25 patients showed that 14 were in remission at 6 months and all 25 were in remission at 18 months. Common side effects included infections, infusion-related reactions, and nausea.

title: FDA approves treatment for adults and children with all genotypes of hepatitis C and compensated cirrhosis that shortens duration of treatment to eight weeks
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Mavyret (glecaprevir and pibrentasvir) tablets for an eight-week duration to treat adults and children ages 12 and older or weighing at least 99 pounds with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) genotype 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6 infection and compensated cirrhosis. This approval extends treatment duration for all treatment-naïve adult and certain pediatric patients with HCV genotypes 1-6. Jeffrey Murray, MD, stated that this approval provides an eight-week treatment regimen for any treatment-naïve HCV patient, regardless of cirrhosis status or genotype. Mavyret is a combination of direct-acting antiviral drugs that reduce HCV levels to undetectable, and in most cases, cure HCV infection.

title: Remarks prepared for testimony before a U.S. House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on FDA Regulation of Electronic Nicotine Delivery Systems and Investigation of Vaping Illnesses
body_summary:
The FDA is discussing its regulation of electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS) and the agency's ongoing investigation into lung injuries associated with vaping products. 

The investigation, led by FDA, CDC, and state partners, has not identified a specific substance or product linked to the cases. 

FDA's Office of Emergency Operations is coordinating with CDC, and the agency's regulatory field force is collecting samples for analysis at the Forensic Chemistry Center.

The agency is also working with Customs and Border Protection to identify illicit vaping products and with the DEA to investigate cases containing THC oils.

FDA is addressing the epidemic of youth use of ENDS products, including a recent announcement about its intention to issue a policy on flavored ENDS products.

The policy would prioritize enforcement of premarket authorization requirements for non-tobacco flavors, and would not mean that flavored e-cigarettes could never be marketed.

title: FDA approves first live, non-replicating vaccine to prevent smallpox and monkeypox
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the Jynneos Smallpox and Monkeypox Vaccine, Live, Non-Replicating, for the prevention of smallpox and monkeypox disease in adults 18 years of age and older determined to be at high risk. The vaccine is the only currently FDA-approved vaccine for the prevention of monkeypox disease. 

The vaccine is made from a modified form of the vaccinia virus called Modified Vaccinia Ankara, which does not cause disease in humans and is non-replicating. It was approved based on a clinical study showing that it protected against smallpox, as well as non-human primate studies showing protection against the monkeypox virus. 

The vaccine is available for those determined to be at high risk of either smallpox or monkeypox infection, and is part of the Strategic National Stockpile, the nation’s largest supply of potentially life-saving pharmaceuticals and medical supplies.

title: FDA announces voluntary recall of Sandoz ranitidine capsules following detection of an impurity
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is recalling 14 lots of prescription ranitidine capsules distributed by Sandoz Inc. due to the presence of N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA), a probable human carcinogen. The recall is a precautionary measure to ensure patient safety. The FDA is investigating the root cause and risk of the impurity and is testing ranitidine products from multiple manufacturers. Acting FDA Commissioner Ned Sharpless stated that the agency will continue to investigate and work to ensure that patients can continue taking the medicines they need without concern. Patients taking recalled ranitidine capsules should follow the recall instructions provided by the company, while those taking non-recalled ranitidine can continue to take it. The FDA encourages patients and healthcare professionals to report any adverse reactions to the agency's MedWatch program.

title: Statement on FDA efforts to encourage patient engagement in medical device clinical investigations
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is committed to involving patients, their families, and caregivers in the review of medical device applications. The FDA values patient experience and insights to understand the benefits and risks of medical devices. To improve this process, the FDA is releasing a draft guidance on patient engagement in medical device clinical investigations. The draft guidance provides recommendations for manufacturers to engage patients in various aspects of clinical investigation design. The FDA has established a Patient Engagement Advisory Committee (PEAC) to encourage patient involvement in medical product regulatory processes. The committee's recommendations include approaches for sponsors to engage with patient advisors, improving informed consent documents, and weighing in on outcomes that matter most to patients. The FDA has also created the Patient and Caregiver Connection program to provide timely input from patients on medical device submissions. This program builds on the FDA's commitment to patients, aiming to advance the development and evaluation of innovative medical devices and improve the efficiency and quality of clinical investigations.

title: Statement on final guidance to help advance development of novel treatments for ALS
body_summary: The FDA has issued a final guidance for industry on developing drugs for the treatment of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). The guidance aims to facilitate the development and approval of new products for ALS patients, who have been frustrated by the lack of new treatments for the disease. The FDA has recognized the strength and resilience of the ALS community and has committed to working with researchers, drug companies, and patients to advance the development of effective treatments. The final guidance provides recommendations on clinical trial design and ways to measure effectiveness, and emphasizes the importance of early interaction with the FDA to facilitate clinical development programs. The guidance also outlines strategies to minimize unnecessary exposure to placebo and expedite trials, such as master protocols and adaptive designs. The FDA remains committed to supporting the ALS community and is open to considering alternative approaches to meeting its requirements for approval.

title: FDA issues proposed rule for premarket tobacco product applications as part of commitment to continuing strong oversight of e-cigarettes and other tobacco products
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a proposed rule related to premarket tobacco product applications (PMTAs). The proposed rule aims to ensure that PMTAs contain sufficient information for evaluation, including details on physical aspects and potential public health benefits and harms. The FDA will review PMTAs to evaluate the public health benefits and harms of tobacco products, including understanding the likelihood of users stopping and non-users starting to use products. The proposed rule also codifies procedures for review and communications, as well as requirements for manufacturers to maintain records related to legal marketing status. The rule will be open for public comments through November 25, 2019.

title: FDA approves first oral GLP-1 treatment for type 2 diabetes
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Rybelsus (semaglutide) oral tablets to improve blood sugar control in adult patients with type 2 diabetes, along with diet and exercise. Rybelsus is the first glucagon-like peptide receptor protein treatment approved for use in the US that does not require injection. The FDA approval was granted to Novo Nordisk. Patients with type 2 diabetes can now have a new option for treating the condition without injections. The efficacy and safety of Rybelsus were studied in several clinical trials, which showed a significant reduction in blood sugar levels compared to placebo. Rybelsus carries warnings about potential increased risk of thyroid c-cell tumors and pancreatitis, and patients with certain medical conditions or a family history of these conditions should not use the medication.

title: Statement on continued efforts to increase availability of all forms of naloxone to help reduce opioid overdose deaths
body_summary: The U.S. government is working to address the opioid crisis by making naloxone, an emergency opioid overdose reversal treatment, more widely available. Naloxone is available in three FDA-approved forms: injectable, auto-injector, and nasal spray, all of which require a prescription. However, many states have passed laws allowing pharmacists to dispense naloxone under a standing order, which can help increase access. The FDA has approved the first generic naloxone hydrochloride nasal spray and is working to make naloxone more accessible through various efforts. These include granting priority review to generic applications, developing a model Drug Facts label for over-the-counter (OTC) approval, and conducting research on naloxone. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services has also launched a 5-Point Strategy to Combat the Opioids Crisis, which includes targeting overdose reversing drugs. The FDA is committed to expanding the availability of all forms of naloxone to individuals at risk of an overdose.

title: Executive Order 13887—Modernizing Influenza Vaccines in the United States To Promote National Security and Public Health
body_summary: The US President has ordered a modernization of the domestic influenza vaccine enterprise to improve response to emerging influenza viruses. A National Influenza Vaccine Task Force, co-chaired by the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Health and Human Services, has been created to identify actions and monitor progress. The Task Force aims to develop more effective and longer-lasting vaccines, expand domestic manufacturing capacity, and increase influenza vaccination rates. It also calls for developing new vaccine technologies, including cell-based and recombinant vaccine manufacturing, and providing incentives for private manufacturers to develop pandemic vaccines. The Task Force will estimate costs, evaluate incentives, and support clinical studies to develop and produce effective influenza vaccines for pandemic response.

title: FDA continues to take steps to fulfill its commitment to strengthen and modernize the 510(k) medical device program
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has announced the issuance of draft guidances outlining premarket performance criteria and testing methodologies for four types of medical devices: conventional foley catheters, cutaneous electrodes for reporting purposes, orthopedic non-spinal metallic bone screws and washers, and spinal plating systems. These devices are expected to be the first to be eligible for the new, voluntary premarket notification pathway. The goal of this pathway is to advance safer and more effective devices. The FDA is seeking public feedback on these guidances, which will aid in the finalization of the initial device-specific guidances and expansion of the pathway to other types of medical devices. The pathway aims to benchmark modern technology against modern standards, promoting efficient review and driving market competition to develop safer devices.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in July indicates that the labor market remains strong and that economic activity has been rising at a moderate rate. Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Although household spending has been rising at a strong pace, business fixed investment and exports have weakened. On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy are running below 2 percent. Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. In light of the implications of global developments for the economic outlook as well as muted inflation pressures, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-3/4 to 2 percent. This action supports the Committee's view that sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective are the most likely outcomes, but uncertainties about this outlook remain. As the Committee contemplates the future path of the target range for the federal funds rate, it will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook and will act as appropriate to sustain the expansion, with a strong labor market and inflation near its symmetric 2 percent objective. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair, John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Charles L. Evans; and Randal K. Quarles. Voting against the action were James Bullard, who preferred at this meeting to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent; and Esther L. George and Eric S. Rosengren, who preferred to maintain the target range at 2 percent to 2-1/4 percent.

title: FDA takes first action under new international collaboration with Australia and Canada designed to provide a framework for concurrent review of cancer therapies, approving treatment for patients with endometrial carcinoma
body_summary:
The US FDA is announcing Project Orbis, a collaboration with the Australian Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) and Health Canada to review oncology drugs concurrently. The project aims to facilitate simultaneous decisions in all three countries, potentially reducing delays in regulatory submissions.

The FDA, TGA, and Health Canada collaborated on the review of applications for two oncology drugs, Lenvima (lenvatinib) and Keytruda (pembrolizumab), for the treatment of advanced endometrial carcinoma. The project used the Real-Time Oncology Review (RTOR) pilot program and Assessment Aid to expedite the approval.

Lenvima was initially approved by the FDA in 2015, and Keytruda was approved in 2014. The FDA granted accelerated approval to Lenvima in combination with Keytruda for the treatment of patients with advanced endometrial carcinoma. The approval was based on the results of a clinical trial involving 94 patients.

The FDA approved Lenvima in combination with Keytruda, which was developed by Eisai Inc. and Merck Sharp & Dohme Corp. The FDA also committed the sponsor to provide additional data to the agency. This review was conducted under the Oncology Center of Excellence's RTOR pilot program and Assessment Aid.

title: Statement alerting patients and health care professionals of NDMA found in samples of ranitidine
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has found that some ranitidine medicines, including Zantac, contain the nitrosamine impurity N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA) at low levels. NDMA is classified as a probable human carcinogen. The FDA has been investigating NDMA in blood pressure and heart failure medicines since last year and has recommended numerous recalls of Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers (ARBs) due to unacceptable levels of nitrosamines. The agency is evaluating whether the low levels of NDMA in ranitidine pose a risk to patients. The FDA is working with international regulators and industry partners to determine the source of the impurity. Patients taking prescription ranitidine should talk to their healthcare professional about alternative treatment options, and consumers can report any adverse reactions to the FDA's MedWatch program.

title: Trump Administration Combating Epidemic of Youth E-Cigarette Use with Plan to Clear Market of Unauthorized, Non-Tobacco-Flavored E-Cigarette Products
body_summary:
The Trump Administration announced plans to finalize a compliance policy prioritizing enforcement of premarket authorization requirements for non-tobacco-flavored e-cigarettes, including mint and menthol flavors. The policy aims to clear the market of unauthorized products and reverse the youth e-cigarette use epidemic. Health and Human Services Secretary Alex Azar stated that the administration will not stand idly by as youth e-cigarette use becomes an on-ramp to combustible cigarettes or nicotine addiction.

Acting FDA Commissioner Ned Sharpless emphasized the need to act swiftly against flavored e-cigarette products attractive to children. The policy will serve as a powerful tool to combat the troubling trend of youth e-cigarette use. The FDA plans to share more details soon and has been holding retailers and manufacturers accountable for marketing and sales practices that increase youth accessibility and appeal of e-cigarettes.

The Trump Administration has demonstrated a deep commitment to preventing youth from using all tobacco products, including e-cigarettes. The FDA has issued warning letters and civil money penalties to retailers for sales to minors, and has also removed dozens of e-liquid products resembling kid-friendly products from the market. The agency has also launched campaigns to educate youth about the dangers of e-cigarette use, including "The Real Cost" Youth E-Cigarette Prevention Campaign.

title: Statement on improving adverse event reporting of compounded drugs to protect patients
body_summary: The FDA is taking steps to protect patients from poor-quality compounded drugs, which are not evaluated by the FDA for safety, effectiveness, and quality. The agency is working to ensure that patients have access to lawfully-marketed compounded drugs while minimizing the risks associated with these products. Recently, an inspection of BioTE Medical uncovered 4,202 adverse events associated with compounded hormone pellets, which suggested a possible link to endometrial cancer, prostate cancer, and other health issues. The FDA is continuing to investigate and take action against outsourcing facilities that do not comply with adverse event reporting requirements. The agency is also working with states to finalize a memorandum of understanding to investigate complaints of adverse events associated with compounded drugs and report serious adverse events to the agency. Additionally, the FDA has contracted with the National Academy of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine to conduct a study on the risks associated with compounded hormone products.

title: FDA warns JUUL Labs for marketing unauthorized modified risk tobacco products, including in outreach to youth
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a warning letter to JUUL Labs Inc. for marketing unauthorized modified risk tobacco products, including a presentation given to youth at a school. The agency expresses concern about several issues raised in a recent Congressional hearing, including JUUL's outreach and marketing practices targeted at students, tribes, health insurers, and employers. Acting FDA Commissioner Ned Sharpless stated that JUUL has ignored the law and made false statements about its products. The FDA has determined that JUUL has marketed its products as modified risk tobacco products without an appropriate FDA order in effect. The agency has requested that JUUL provide a written response within 15 working days describing its corrective actions and plan for maintaining compliance with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.

title: FDA approves first treatment for patients with rare type of lung disease
body_summary: The US FDA approved Ofev (nintedanib) capsules to slow the rate of decline in pulmonary function in adults with interstitial lung disease associated with systemic sclerosis or scleroderma. The approval is the first for this rare lung condition. The treatment was studied in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 576 patients aged 20-79, who received treatment for 52 weeks. Patients who took Ofev had less lung function decline compared to those on placebo. The most frequent serious adverse event reported was pneumonia (2.8% Ofev vs. 0.3% placebo). The FDA granted the approval to Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals Inc., an agency within the US Department of Health and Human Services, which protects the public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: FDA sends warning to company for selling unapproved umbilical cord blood and umbilical cord products that may put patients at risk; continues to warn patients of the risk of unapproved stem cell therapy
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has warned Stemell, Inc., and its president Peyman Taeidi, for manufacturing and distributing unapproved products derived from umbilical cord blood and umbilical cord, posing potential safety concerns. The FDA has found significant deviations from current good tissue practice (CGTP) and current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) requirements, including deficient donor eligibility practices and environmental monitoring. Stemell's unapproved products are StemL UCB-Plus and StemL UCT-Plus. The FDA will increase oversight related to cell-based regenerative medicine and will take action to protect patients. The company was inspected in March, and the FDA has issued a warning letter, requiring Stemell to correct the deviations. The FDA has also sent letters to 20 other manufacturers and healthcare providers offering unapproved stem cell products, reiterating the agency's compliance and enforcement policy.

title: Federal judge enters consent decree against Tennessee drug, dietary supplement and device distributors, Basic Reset and Biogenyx, for drug, device and dietary supplement violations
body_summary: A federal court has ordered two Tennessee-based companies, Basic Reset and Biogenyx, and their owner, Fred R. Kaufman III, to stop distributing drugs, dietary supplements, and devices until they comply with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. The companies were found to have unlawfully distributed unapproved new drugs, adulterated and misbranded dietary supplements, and an adulterated and misbranded device. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has not approved any of these products for use, despite the companies' claims that they could be used to diagnose or treat various conditions. The FDA has issued warnings to the companies in the past, but they failed to correct the violations. A consent decree was entered, prohibiting the companies from directly or indirectly receiving, labeling, or distributing these products until they take steps to ensure compliance, including recalling products, hiring qualified experts, and receiving FDA permission to resume operations.

title: Statement on federal and state collaboration to investigate respiratory illnesses reported after use of e-cigarette products
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) are investigating severe respiratory disease cases linked to e-cigarette products. An adult in Illinois died after using an e-cigarette product, and the agencies are working closely with state and local health officials to investigate. As of August 27, 2019, 215 possible cases have been reported from 25 states, with more cases under investigation. Patients reported symptoms such as breathing difficulty, shortness of breath, and chest pain before hospitalization, and some also experienced gastrointestinal issues. The CDC and FDA are standardizing information collection and consulting with states to gather information on products and substances used. The FDA has received 80 samples for analysis, and more information is needed to determine the cause of the illnesses. The agencies recommend that people avoid using e-cigarette products, especially youth, young adults, pregnant women, and non-tobacco users. CDC and FDA will continue to advise and alert the public as more information becomes available.

title: FDA recommends health care facilities and manufacturers begin transitioning to duodenoscopes with disposable components to reduce risk of patient infection
body_summary: The US FDA recommends transitioning from reusable to disposable or fully disposable duodenoscopes due to persistent contamination issues. This decision follows challenges with cleaning and reprocessing reusable devices, posing patient safety risks. To address this, the FDA is working with manufacturers to develop new designs, increase supply of disposable duodenoscopes, and conduct postmarket surveillance studies. The agency also plans to update duodenoscope labels with contamination rate data and convene a panel in 2019 to discuss contamination rates and reprocessing methods.

title: Statement on the agency’s ongoing efforts to resolve safety issue with ARB medications
body_summary: The FDA is investigating and addressing the impact of recent ARB recalls due to nitrosamine impurities, which raised concerns about patient safety. The agency is working to provide transparent information about the risk of exposure and has already identified 43 ARB medications with no nitrosamine impurities. The FDA aims to quickly address any issue to prevent harm to patients and is enhancing oversight of manufacturing data, collaborating with global regulatory partners, and improving industry's tracking and detection of potentially dangerous drugs. The agency will continue to monitor and regulate drugs, vaccines, and medical devices to ensure public health and safety.

title: FDA requests recall of sterile compounded drug products produced by Pacifico National Inc., dba AmEx Pharmacy, reminds patients and health care professionals to stop using due to potential risks
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is warning patients and healthcare professionals not to use drug products made by Pacifico National Inc., doing business as AmEx Pharmacy, in Melbourne, Florida, due to significant quality and sterility concerns. The FDA has found conditions at the facility that could cause contamination or pose risks to patients. The agency initially recommended a voluntary recall of all unexpired sterile drugs but AmEx Pharmacy declined. As a result, the FDA has issued a formal request for a recall of all non-expired lots of sterile drugs. The agency is also urging consumers to stop using these drugs and dispose of them immediately. The FDA is requesting the outsourcing facility to cease production of sterile drugs until adequate remediation actions have been taken. There have been reports of adverse events associated with the use of AmEx Pharmacy's drugs.

title: Statement calling on all sectors of the papaya industry to improve practices to better protect consumers
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is urging the papaya industry to take actions to prevent future outbreaks of foodborne illness, particularly after the recent outbreak of Salmonella Uganda linked to imported, fresh papayas. The FDA is calling on growers, importers, and retailers to review their operations and implement procedures to minimize contamination, including assessing water use, pesticide and fungicide use, and enhancing traceability. The agency is also increasing sampling and screening of papayas at the border and collaborating with the Mexican government to determine ways to further prevention efforts. The FDA has issued a warning letter to a papaya importer, Agroson's LLC, following an investigation that uncovered significant violations of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: Federal Reserve's monetary policy actions since the financial crisis included lowering the federal funds rate to its effective lower bound and providing additional accommodation through forward guidance and balance sheet policy. The committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on July 30-31, 2019, discussing the ongoing review of monetary policy strategy, tools, and communication practices. Staff briefings provided insights into the Federal Reserve's actions since the financial crisis. Policymakers face challenges in influencing inflation and inflation expectations, considering possible modifications to policy strategy, tools, and communication practices would take time, be careful, deliberate, and patient. The committee lowered its target range for the federal funds rate to 2-2.25% due to strong labor markets and solid growth, with inflation gradually moving towards its 2% objective.

title: FDA warns company for putting consumers at risk with drug manufacturing data integrity violations
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) posted a warning letter to Ningbo Huize Commodity Co., an over-the-counter drug manufacturer, for significant current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) violations, including data integrity issues. The FDA has focused on preventing, uncovering, and combating data integrity lapses and has updated guidance for industry on ensuring data integrity and compliance with CGMP.

The warning letter details a failure by Ningbo Huize to have adequate quality control mechanisms in place, including falsified documents. The company's adulterated products must be removed from the market, and the FDA considers them misbranded due to incomplete product labels. The FDA has previously placed the company on import alert in 2019 and has requested that the company address the agency's concerns.

 Failure to correct violations may result in the FDA refusing admission of products manufactured at the company's facility. The FDA emphasizes the importance of preventing data integrity lapses to ensure product quality and safety. The agency will continue to ensure that drug manufacturers meet the required standards for drug quality and will take action against manufacturers who fail to comply.

title: Statement on new results demonstrating continued success of the agency’s youth smoking prevention efforts and significant public health cost savings
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has successfully deployed anti-tobacco campaigns to educate youth about the dangers of tobacco and e-cigarette use, yielding significant results. The "The Real Cost" campaign, launched in 2014, has prevented up to 587,000 youth from initiating smoking between 2014 and 2016. The campaign's success has been demonstrated through its ability to reach 95% of its target audience aged 12-17 and engage over 31.6 million youth on social media. The campaign's impact is estimated to have saved over $53 billion by preventing hundreds of thousands of youth from becoming established adult smokers. The FDA plans to continue its efforts to educate youth about the dangers of tobacco and e-cigarette use, including expanding the campaign to address e-cigarette use and launching new campaigns targeting youth and young adults.

title: FDA approves new antibiotic to treat community-acquired bacterial pneumonia
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Xenleta (lefamulin) to treat adults with community-acquired bacterial pneumonia. Ed Cox, M.D., M.P.H., director of FDA's Office of Antimicrobial Products, stated that the new drug provides another option for treating this serious disease. The safety and efficacy of Xenleta were evaluated in two clinical trials with 1,289 patients, showing that treatment with Xenleta was comparable to another antibiotic, moxifloxacin with or without linezolid.
