Xenleta has the potential to cause a prolonged QT interval and should not be used in patients with known hypersensitivity to lefamulin or other pleuromutilin antibiotics. The FDA granted Priority Review and Qualified Infectious Disease Product designation to Xenleta, which was developed by Nabriva Therapeutics. This approval reinforces the FDA's commitment to addressing the threat of antimicrobial-resistant infections and provides patients with more treatment options for serious infections.

title: FDA approves new device to improve symptoms in patients with advanced heart failure
body_summary: The US FDA approved the Barostim Neo System for patients with advanced heart failure who are not suited for other treatments. The device treats symptoms of heart failure, including fatigue, palpitations, and shortness of breath, and is designed to address an unmet medical need in patients who fail to benefit from standard treatments. The FDA gave the device a Breakthrough Device designation due to its potential to provide a clinical improvement in patients with this debilitating condition. The device includes a pulse generator and electrical impulses that relax blood vessels and inhibit stress-related hormones to reduce heart failure symptoms. A clinical trial with 408 patients showed improvements in symptoms and quality of life. Potential complications include infection, nerve damage, and exacerbation of heart failure. The device is indicated for patients with a regular heart rhythm and a left ventricular ejection fraction of less than or equal to 35%.

title: FDA expands indication for several transcatheter heart valves to patients at low risk for death or major complications associated with open-heart surgery
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved an expanded indication for several transcatheter heart valves to include patients with severe aortic valve stenosis at low risk for death or major complications associated with open-heart surgery. The approved devices include Sapien 3, Sapien 3 Ultra, CoreValve Evolut R, and CoreValve Evolut PRO. This expansion follows a thorough review of data demonstrating these devices are safe and effective for this larger population. The approval is the first of its kind for the FDA, which assesses new medical technologies and expanded uses for previously approved products.

A clinical study found that patients with severe aortic stenosis who received aortic valve replacement with the Sapien 3 transcatheter heart valve had comparable outcomes to those receiving traditional open-heart surgery. Another study showed similar results for the CoreValve Evolut R and CoreValve Evolut PRO devices. However, the FDA notes that treatment with these devices is associated with a potential risk of serious complications, including death, stroke, and bleeding.

The FDA requires manufacturers to continue to follow patients enrolled in their randomized studies for 10 years to monitor transcatheter aortic valve safety and effectiveness. The approval also includes participation in the Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry.

title: FDA approves treatment for patients with rare bone marrow disorder
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Inrebic (fedratinib) capsules to treat adult patients with certain types of myelofibrosis. The approval was based on a clinical trial where 289 patients were randomized to receive two different doses of fedratinib or placebo. The trial showed that 35 patients treated with the 400mg daily dose experienced a significant therapeutic effect, and 36 patients experienced a 50% reduction in myelofibrosis-related symptoms. Inrebic was approved for intermediate-2 or high-risk primary or secondary myelofibrosis. The prescribing information includes a Boxed Warning for the risk of serious and fatal encephalopathy, and health care professionals are advised to assess thiamine levels in patients prior to starting Inrebic. Common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fatigue, and muscle spasms. The FDA granted Priority Review designation and Orphan Drug designation to Impact Biomedicines, Inc., a subsidiary of Celgene Corporation.

title: FDA expands indication for several transcatheter heart valves to patients at low risk for death or major complications associated with open-heart surgery
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved an expanded indication for several transcatheter heart valves to include patients with severe aortic valve stenosis at low risk for death or major complications associated with open-heart surgery. The devices, including Sapien 3, Sapien 3 Ultra, CoreValve Evolut R, and CoreValve Evolut PRO, were previously indicated for patients at intermediate or higher risk. A clinical study with 503 patients and another study with 734 patients showed that the transcatheter heart valves achieved comparable results to open-heart surgery, demonstrating safety and effectiveness. The FDA requires manufacturers to continue to follow patients for 10 years to monitor safety and effectiveness, including long-term valve durability. The approvals were granted to Edwards Lifesciences LLC for Sapien 3 and Sapien 3 Ultra, and Medtronic CoreValve LLC for CoreValve Evolut R and CoreValve Evolut PRO.

title: FDA approves first of its kind device to treat pediatric patients with progressive idiopathic scoliosis
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the first spinal tether device, The Tether – Vertebral Body Tethering System, to treat idiopathic scoliosis in children and adolescents. The device aims to correct spinal curves in growing patients whose conditions have not responded to conservative treatment. The FDA reviewed data from 57 patients who received the device, showing 43 patients with sufficient improvement of their spinal curvature without needing spinal fusion surgery. The device is designed to maintain a fuller range of motion compared to spinal fusion procedures. The FDA granted approval to Zimmer Biomet Spine, the device's manufacturer.

title: FDA approves treatment for patients with rare bone marrow disorder
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Inrebic (fedratinib) capsules to treat adult patients with certain types of myelofibrosis. This decision provides an additional treatment option for patients with the rare bone marrow disorder. The approval is based on the results of a clinical trial involving 289 patients, which showed that 35 patients experienced a significant therapeutic effect and 36 patients experienced greater than or equal to a 50% reduction in myelofibrosis-related symptoms. The FDA approved Inrebic for patients with intermediate-2 or high-risk primary or secondary myelofibrosis. The prescribing information for Inrebic includes a Boxed Warning about the risk of serious and fatal encephalopathy. Common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, fatigue, and muscle spasms. The FDA granted this application Priority Review designation and Orphan Drug designation, and approved the application to Impact Biomedicines, Inc., a subsidiary of Celgene Corporation.

title: FDA approves first of its kind device to treat pediatric patients with progressive idiopathic scoliosis
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration approved the first spinal tether device, The Tether – Vertebral Body Tethering System, to correct idiopathic scoliosis in children and adolescents who have not responded to conservative treatment options. The device is intended for growing children and adolescents whose spinal curves are approaching or have reached the range where surgical treatment is an option. 

Idiopathic scoliosis is a sideways curvature of the spine whose cause is unknown, affecting approximately 6,800 patients in the US each year. The standard treatment is external bracing, but for patients who do not respond, spinal fusion surgery may be used. The Tether – Vertebral Body Tethering System provides an alternative, designed to continue to correct the curvature while maintaining a fuller range of motion. 

The FDA reviewed data from 57 patients, showing that 43 patients had sufficient improvement of the curvature of their spines at two years. Serious adverse events included overcorrection of the curvature, tether breakage, and pneumothorax. Zimmer Biomet Spine will partner with the Harms Study Group to develop a patient data registry to gather and track real-world evidence. The FDA granted the approval of The Tether - Vertebral Body Tethering System to Zimmer Biomet Spine.

title: FDA approves third oncology drug that targets a key genetic driver of cancer, rather than a specific type of tumor
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted accelerated approval to Rozlytrek (entrectinib), a treatment for adult and adolescent patients with NTRK gene fusion tumors. This is the third time the agency has approved a cancer treatment based on a common biomarker across different types of tumors. The approval marks a new paradigm in the development of tissue agnostic cancer drugs. The FDA approved Rozlytrek for patients 12 years of age and older with NTRK-fusion-positive tumors, using efficacy information from adults. The treatment was shown to shrink tumors in 57% of patients with substantial response rates, with 61% of patients experiencing persistent tumor shrinkage for nine months or longer. Rozlytrek was also approved for the treatment of adults with non-small cell lung cancer whose tumors are ROS1-positive and have spread. The most common side effects were fatigue, constipation, and dysgeusia, while the most serious side effects included congestive heart failure and cognitive impairment.

title: FDA approves third oncology drug that targets a key genetic driver of cancer, rather than a specific type of tumor
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted accelerated approval to Rozlytrek (entrectinib) for adult and adolescent patients with NTRK gene fusion and no effective treatments. The approval marks the third time the agency has approved a cancer treatment based on a common biomarker across different tumor types. The treatment was evaluated in four clinical trials studying 54 adults with NTRK fusion-positive tumors, with a 57% overall response rate. The FDA Acting Commissioner Ned Sharpless said the approval is part of a new paradigm in cancer drug development. The treatment was also approved for pediatric patients 12 years and older with NTRK-fusion-positive tumors, and for adults with non-small cell lung cancer whose tumors are ROS1-positive and have spread to other parts of the body. Rozlytrek's common side effects include fatigue, constipation, and dizziness, while serious side effects include congestive heart failure and cognitive impairment.

title: FDA proposes new required health warnings with color images for cigarette packages and advertisements to promote greater public understanding of negative health consequences of smoking
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has proposed a rule requiring new health warnings on cigarette packages and in advertisements to promote public understanding of the negative health consequences of smoking. The proposed warnings, featuring photo-realistic color images, focus on lesser-known health risks such as bladder cancer, diabetes, and conditions that can cause blindness. The rule aims to increase public awareness of tobacco's risks and fulfill a requirement in the Family Smoking Prevention and Tobacco Control Act. The US District Court for the District of Massachusetts ordered the FDA to publish a proposed rule by August 2019 and issue a final rule by March 2020.

title: FDA approves new drug for treatment-resistant forms of tuberculosis that affects the lungs
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Pretomanid Tablets in combination with bedaquiline and linezolid for treating a specific type of highly treatment-resistant tuberculosis (TB) of the lungs. FDA Principal Deputy Commissioner Amy Abernethy stated that the threat of antimicrobial-resistant infections is a key challenge. The approval marks the second time a drug is being approved under the Limited Population Pathway for Antibacterial and Antifungal Drugs. Pretomanid is approved for treating a limited population of adult patients with extensively drug-resistant, treatment-intolerant, or nonresponsive multidrug-resistant pulmonary TB. The safety and effectiveness of Pretomanid were demonstrated in a study of 109 patients, with 95 (89%) being successes. Adverse reactions included peripheral neuropathy, acne, anemia, nausea, and visual impairment. Pretomanid is the second drug to be approved under the LPAD pathway, established by Congress, to advance development and approval of antibacterial and antifungal drugs. The FDA granted Pretomanid Tablets Priority Review and Orphan Drug designation. The Global Alliance for TB Drug Development is awarded a Tropical Disease Priority Review Voucher with this approval.

title: FDA warns consumers about the dangerous and potentially life threating side effects of Miracle Mineral Solution
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is warning consumers not to purchase or drink a product called Miracle Mineral Solution (MMS) due to reported health issues. The FDA has warned about the dangers of MMS since 2010, as it has not been approved for any use and can cause serious side effects when mixed. The product is being promoted as a remedy for various conditions, but it contains a bleach-like substance that can cause severe vomiting, diarrhea, and life-threatening conditions. The FDA encourages consumers to seek immediate medical attention if they have experienced adverse health effects and to report them through MedWatch.

title: FDA notifies four companies to remove 44 flavored e-liquid and hookah tobacco products from the market for not having required marketing authorization
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued warning letters to four companies, notifying them that 44 flavored e-liquid and hookah tobacco products do not have required marketing authorization and cannot be legally sold in the US. This action is part of the FDA's effort to investigate and take action against illegally marketed tobacco products amid the youth e-cigarette use epidemic.

The FDA is committed to tackling the trend of youth e-cigarette use and nicotine addiction in children, which threatens to erase years of progress in combating tobacco use among kids. The agency has issued warning letters to nearly 90 companies seeking information about 130 Electronic Nicotine Delivery System (ENDS) products, and some companies have removed products from the market as a result.

The products subject to the warning letters were introduced or modified after August 8, 2016, and the FDA has requested responses from each of the four companies within 15 working days on how they intend to address the agency's concerns. Failure to correct violations may result in further action such as seizure or injunction.

The FDA has several tools to enforce the requirements of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, including pursuing administrative actions and pursuing judicial actions such as seizures or injunctions. The agency protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and other biological products for human use, and medical devices.

title: FDA notifies four companies to remove 44 flavored e-liquid and hookah tobacco products from the market for not having required marketing authorization
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued warning letters to four companies for selling 44 flavored e-liquid and hookah tobacco products without the required marketing authorization. The action is part of the FDA's effort to combat the epidemic of youth e-cigarette use in America. Acting FDA Commissioner Ned Sharpless stated that the agency will continue to monitor companies and take swift action against violations. The products were introduced or modified after August 8, 2016, and are subject to the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act's premarket requirements. The companies receiving warning letters are Mighty Vapors LLC, Liquid Labs USA LLC, V8P Juice International LLC, and Hookah Imports Inc. The FDA has requested responses from the companies within 15 working days on how they intend to address the agency's concerns. Failure to correct violations may result in further action such as seizure or injunction.

title: FDA statement on court ruling related to compounded bulk drug substances and the agency’s ongoing efforts to implement its compounding authorities
body_summary: A U.S. District Court judge in Washington, D.C. has upheld FDA's interpretation of clinical need regarding bulk substances for outsourcing facilities in drug compounding. The FDA is pleased with the decision, which is a victory for public health. The agency had previously determined that vasopressin is not a bulk drug substance with clinical need, and the court agreed, finding that the agency's method of determining clinical need is consistent with the law. The FDA will continue to evaluate bulk drug substances in accordance with its interpretation of clinical need. The agency recognizes the importance of compounded drugs for patients whose medical needs cannot be met by an FDA-approved product, but also notes that compounded drugs pose ongoing risks if not manufactured properly. The FDA has taken steps to modernize and clarify its policies on compounding, including research efforts and inspections to ensure quality and safety.

title: Statement on data accuracy issues with recently approved gene therapy
body_summary: The FDA approved Zolgensma, a gene therapy product, to treat children under two years old with spinal muscular atrophy, on May 24. Following approval, the agency became aware of a data manipulation issue related to product testing in animals submitted by AveXis Inc., the product's manufacturer. The FDA is carefully assessing the situation and remains confident that Zolgensma should remain on the market, but is taking the issue seriously. The agency is evaluating the impact of the data manipulation on the product's development process and will use its full authorities to take action, including civil or criminal penalties, if necessary.

title: FDA statement on court ruling related to compounded bulk drug substances and the agency’s ongoing efforts to implement its compounding authorities
body_summary: A US District Court judge in Washington, D.C. upheld FDA's interpretation of clinical need for bulk substances used by outsourcing facilities in drug compounding. The FDA had previously determined that vasopressin is not a bulk drug substance with clinical need due to an existing FDA-approved product. The court agreed, finding the agency's method of determining clinical need consistent with the law. The FDA will continue to evaluate bulk drug substances in accordance with its interpretation. The agency prioritizes compounding work, recognizing its role in providing essential drugs for patients with unmet medical needs. However, compounded drugs pose risks if not manufactured properly, and the FDA's oversight is essential to ensure patient safety. The agency has taken steps to modernize policies on compounding quality and will finalize a Memorandum of Understanding with states to coordinate safety actions.

title: Statement on data accuracy issues with recently approved gene therapy
body_summary: The FDA approved Zolgensma, a gene therapy product, for treating children under two with spinal muscular atrophy, despite a data manipulation issue in animal testing data. The agency is carefully assessing the situation and remains confident that Zolgensma should remain on the market. Concerns are limited to a small portion of the product testing data, and the totality of human clinical trial data supports an overall favorable benefit-risk profile. The FDA will take action, including civil or criminal penalties, if necessary.

title: FDA approves first therapy for rare joint tumor
body_summary: The US FDA has approved Turalio (pexidartinib) capsules for treating adult patients with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT) associated with severe morbidity or functional limitations and not responsive to surgery. The tumor causes debilitating symptoms and can significantly affect quality of life. The approval was based on the results of a multi-center international clinical trial involving 120 patients, with 59 receiving placebo. The clinical trial demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in overall response rate in patients who received Turalio, with an overall response rate of 38% compared to no responses in patients who received placebo. The prescribing information includes a Boxed Warning about the risk of serious and potentially fatal liver injury. Turalio is available only through the Turalio Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy Program. Common side effects include increased lactate dehydrogenase, aspartate aminotransferase, and other enzymes.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in June indicates that the labor market remains strong and that economic activity has been rising at a moderate rate. Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Although growth of household spending has picked up from earlier in the year, growth of business fixed investment has been soft. On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy are running below 2 percent. Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. In light of the implications of global developments for the economic outlook as well as muted inflation pressures, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 2 to 2-1/4 percent. This action supports the Committee's view that sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective are the most likely outcomes, but uncertainties about this outlook remain. As the Committee contemplates the future path of the target range for the federal funds rate, it will continue to monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook and will act as appropriate to sustain the expansion, with a strong labor market and inflation near its symmetric 2 percent objective. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. The Committee will conclude the reduction of its aggregate securities holdings in the System Open Market Account in August, two months earlier than previously indicated. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; James Bullard; Richard H. Clarida; Charles L. Evans; and Randal K. Quarles. Voting against the action were Esther L. George and Eric S. Rosengren, who preferred at this meeting to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent.

title: FDA clears new indications for existing Lyme disease tests that may help streamline diagnoses
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared four enzyme immunoassay (EIA) tests for marketing with new indications to aid in the diagnosis of Lyme disease. The tests, developed by ZEUS Scientific, use a modified two-tier test approach that combines two EIA tests concurrently or sequentially, rather than the current two-step process. This new method is as accurate as current methods for detecting antibodies against Borrelia burgdorferi, the causative agent of Lyme disease. The tests were reviewed through the premarket notification (510(k)) pathway and were granted clearance by the FDA. The agency cited the importance of early diagnosis to ensure the best outcome for patients, particularly those with a condition that can have a devastating impact if left untreated.

title: FDA takes action to protect patients from risk of certain textured breast implants; requests Allergan voluntarily recall certain breast implants and tissue expanders from market
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has requested Allergan to recall specific models of its textured breast implants due to the risk of breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL). The recall includes models such as Natrelle Saline-Filled and Natrelle Silicone-Filled breast implants, as well as tissue expanders. The FDA has received 573 unique cases of BIA-ALCL, including 33 patient deaths, with 481 cases attributed to Allergan implants. The risk of BIA-ALCL with Allergan BIOCELL textured implants is approximately six times higher than with textured implants from other manufacturers. The FDA will continue to monitor the situation and take additional actions if necessary.

title: FDA approves first treatment for severe hypoglycemia that can be administered without an injection
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Baqsimi nasal powder, the first glucagon therapy for emergency treatment of severe hypoglycemia, without an injection. Severe hypoglycemia occurs when blood sugar levels fall below a normal range, typically in people with diabetes using insulin treatment. Baqsimi is approved for patients with diabetes ages four and older. The therapy increases blood sugar levels by stimulating the liver to release stored glucose into the bloodstream. The efficacy and safety of Baqsimi were evaluated in two studies of adults with diabetes, showing adequate blood sugar response. Baqsimi should not be taken by patients with certain conditions, such as pheochromocytoma or insulinoma, or those with known hypersensitivity to glucagon. The most common adverse reactions associated with Baqsimi are nausea, vomiting, and eye-related symptoms. The FDA granted approval to Eli Lilly and Company.

title: FDA warns company marketing unapproved cannabidiol products with unsubstantiated claims to treat cancer, Alzheimer’s disease, opioid withdrawal, pain and pet anxiety
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a warning letter to Curaleaf Inc. for illegally selling unapproved products containing cannabidiol (CBD) online with unsubstantiated claims that the products treat various conditions, including cancer, Alzheimer's disease, and opioid withdrawal. The FDA is concerned that these products put patients and consumers at risk by leading them to delay important medical care.

Acting FDA Commissioner Ned Sharpless stated that the agency is taking action to protect public health and to ensure that companies do not deceive consumers by illegally selling products marketed for therapeutic uses for which they are not approved.

The FDA has established a high-level internal working group to explore potential pathways for lawfully marketing CBD products and has opened a public hearing to obtain scientific data and information about the safety and manufacturing of these products.

Curaleaf has 15 working days to respond to the warning letter and correct its violations. Failure to do so may result in legal action, including product seizure and injunction.

The FDA is also concerned about the proliferation of products claiming to contain CBD marketed for therapeutic or medical uses without FDA approval.

title: FDA suspends facility registration of Texas-based seafood producer after significant, repeated food safety violations
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has suspended the food facility registration of Topway Enterprises Inc. (Kazy's Gourmet), citing serious sanitation issues and the presence of Listeria and pathogenic Listeria monocytogenes (L. monocytogenes) in their facility. The company was previously inspected by the FDA and Texas Department of State Health Services in February and again in June, where serious violations were observed, including poor employee sanitation, uncleaned utensils, and cracked floors. The FDA issued a safety alert on July 18, advising restaurants and food retailers to stop selling and discarding Topway's ready-to-eat (RTE) seafood products due to possible Listeria contamination. The company has not implemented adequate corrective actions and will not be allowed to resume operations until a corrective plan is established and implemented.

title: FDA approves first generics of Lyrica
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved multiple applications for first generics of Lyrica (pregabalin) on July 19. This approval allows for the management of neuropathic pain associated with diabetic peripheral neuropathy, postherpetic neuralgia, partial onset seizures, fibromyalgia, and neuropathic pain associated with spinal cord injury. Janet Woodcock, M.D., director of the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, stated that the approval demonstrates the FDA's commitment to advancing patient access to lower-cost, high-quality generic medicines. The FDA requires that generic drugs meet rigorous scientific and quality standards. Pregabalin must be dispensed with a patient Medication Guide containing important information about its uses and risks. The FDA granted approvals to eight companies, including Alembic Pharmaceuticals, Alkem Laboratories, Amneal Pharmaceuticals, and Teva Pharmaceuticals.

title: FDA approves new treatment for complicated urinary tract and complicated intra-abdominal infections
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Recarbrio, an antibacterial drug product, to treat adults with complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI) and complicated intra-abdominal infections (cIAI). The FDA approved Recarbrio, a three-drug combination injection containing imipenem-cilastatin and relebactam, after assessing its efficacy and safety in clinical trials. The drug is reserved for situations where there are limited or no alternative antibacterial drugs. The FDA's Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation and Priority Review were granted to Recarbrio, which was developed by Merck & Co., Inc. The FDA's goal is to address the threat of antimicrobial-resistant infections, a key challenge facing the agency.

title: Statement on the agency’s actions to tackle the epidemic of youth vaping and court ruling on application submission deadlines for certain tobacco products, including e-cigarettes
body_summary: A US District Court judge in Maryland has issued a decision requiring e-cigarette and other electronic nicotine delivery system (ENDS) makers and importers to submit applications for their currently marketed products to the agency within 10 months. The FDA is committed to accelerating the review of e-cigarettes and other new tobacco products. The agency will use this decision to evaluate the public health benefits and harms of products and ensure their safety for public health. The FDA has outlined its recommendations for e-cigarette premarket applications and encourages industry to use these resources. The agency will continue to take action to address the epidemic of youth e-cigarette use through compliance, education, and enforcement.

title: Executive Order 13880—Collecting Information About Citizenship Status in Connection With the Decennial Census
body_summary: President Donald Trump issued an executive order on July 11, 2019, requiring the Department of Commerce to collect accurate data on the total number of citizens, non-citizens, and illegal aliens in the country. The order aims to improve data on immigration and asylum issues, particularly at the southern border, and seeks cooperation from various federal agencies, including Homeland Security, State, and Social Security Administration, to gather citizenship data.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A joint meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee and Board of Governors was held on June 18-19, 2019. A proposal for a standing fixed-rate repurchase agreement (repo) facility to provide temporary liquidity at a fixed rate was presented. Participants discussed trade-offs in setting the fixed rate and considerations for eligible counterparties. The Consumer Price Index rose 1.8% over the 12 months ending in May, while core CPI inflation was 2%. Core PCE price inflation decreased to 1.6%, with consumer food price inflation remaining low and energy prices slowing. Real consumer expenditures picked up in Q2, driven by a solid pace of growth. Nominal retail sales increased in May, with light motor vehicle sales rising sharply. Firms with high China exposure and those in cyclical sectors experienced significant losses due to trade tensions. The labor market remained strong with low unemployment, but job gains were weaker than expected. Economy-wide wage growth was consistent with productivity growth, but there were limited signs of upward pressure on wages. Inflation expectations were at historically low levels. The Federal Open Market Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent.

title: Executive Order 13879—Advancing American Kidney Health
body_summary:
President Donald J. Trump has ordered to advance American kidney health, citing the unacceptable state of care for patients with chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease. The order aims to:

Prevent kidney failure by promoting better diagnosis, treatment, and preventive care.

Increase patient choice through affordable alternative treatments for end-stage renal disease.

Increase access to kidney transplants by modernizing the organ recovery and transplantation systems.

An awareness initiative on kidney and related diseases will be launched within 120 days, focusing on research, education, and patient support.

A payment model will be selected to test innovations in compensating providers for kidney care services based on patient cost and quality outcomes.

Another payment model will be selected to evaluate the effects of creating payment incentives for greater use of home dialysis and kidney transplants.

The development of an artificial kidney will be encouraged through the Kidney Innovation Accelerator.

Efforts will be made to increase the utilization of available organs through revised Organ Procurement Organization rules and evaluation metrics.

Financial barriers to living organ donation will be removed.

The order will be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.

title: FDA approves new treatment for refractory multiple myeloma
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted accelerated approval to Xpovio (selinexor) tablets in combination with dexamethasone for treating adult patients with relapsed refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) who have received at least four prior therapies. Efficacy was evaluated in 83 patients, resulting in a 25.3% overall response rate. The median time to first response was four weeks, and the median duration of response was 3.8 months. Xpovio must be dispensed with a patient Medication Guide and is approved for use in patients with no available therapy. The FDA granted this application Fast Track designation and Orphan Drug designation to Karyopharm Therapeutics.

title: FDA warns repackers distributing pharmaceutical ingredients, including opioids, for putting consumers at risk with significant violations of manufacturing quality standards
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued warning letters to three repackers of active pharmaceutical ingredients (API), B&B Pharmaceuticals, Inc., Asclemed USA, Inc. doing business as Enovachem, and Spectrum Laboratory Products, Inc., for significant violations of current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) requirements. 

The FDA is vigilant in inspecting API repackers to identify and prevent weaknesses in the legitimate supply chain, particularly in the context of the opioid crisis. The agency has found significant supply chain issues in the API repacking industry, posing a real threat to public health.

The FDA requires API repackers to follow quality standards, including clearly identifying the original manufacturer of the drugs, such as opioids. This information is crucial to ensure drugs meet high quality standards.

The warning letters issued to the three companies describe various failures to conform to CGMPs, including inadequate investigation of complaints and failure to provide certificates of analysis with critical information. The FDA has also issued separate warning letters to other API repackers for similar violations.

title: Statement on steps to make health care professional and patient labeling information for prescription medications consistent and clear
body_summary: The FDA is committed to providing health care professionals and patients with accurate and actionable information about prescription medications to make informed treatment decisions. The FDA continually works to ensure that medication and biological product labeling provides clear information to facilitate safe and effective use. One key area of focus is the potential for abuse and physical dependence, particularly with prescription opioids. The FDA has taken steps to provide clear information on a drug's abuse and dependence potential, and this is part of the agency's ongoing evaluation of a drug's benefits and risks. The FDA has issued new draft guidance on the Drug Abuse and Dependence Section of Labeling for Human Prescription Drug and Biological Products, which aims to ensure that information in product labeling is clear, concise, and informative. The guidance recommends defining key terms, presenting abuse-deterrent properties, and presenting information in a consistent manner. The FDA also issued a second draft guidance on Instructions for Use — Patient Labeling for Human Prescription Drug and Biological Products and Drug-Device and Biologic-Device Combination Products — Content and Format, which aims to promote development of consistent content and format across patient labels to facilitate safe and effective use.

title: FDA issues third status report on investigation into potential connection between certain diets and cases of canine heart disease
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is providing an update on its investigation into reports of dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) in dogs eating certain types of pet food. The FDA is sharing adverse event reports, an updated case count, and new testing results, including the pet food brands most frequently identified. The agency acknowledges that it does not yet know how certain diets may be associated with DCM in some dogs. Director Steven M. Solomon stated that the FDA is committed to continuing its scientific investigation into the possible link between DCM and certain pet foods. Between Jan. 1, 2014, and April 30, 2019, the FDA received 524 reports of DCM, including 515 canine reports and 9 feline reports. The agency first alerted the public in July 2018 and has since consulted with stakeholders to inform its investigation.

title: FDA approves first treatment for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, a rare autoimmune disease of the central nervous system
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Soliris (eculizumab) injection for the treatment of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) in adult patients who are anti-aquaporin-4 (AQP4) antibody positive. The approval was granted after a clinical study showed that Soliris reduced the number of NMOSD relapses by 94 percent over a 48-week course. The drug was developed by Alexion Pharmaceuticals and is available only through a restricted program under a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS). The FDA has also granted Orphan Drug Designation for this use, which provides incentives for the development of drugs for rare diseases.

title: FDA warns patients and health care providers about potential cybersecurity concerns with certain Medtronic insulin pumps
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is warning patients and healthcare providers about potential cybersecurity risks in certain Medtronic MiniMed insulin pumps. The FDA recommends that patients using these models switch to insulin pumps with enhanced cybersecurity capabilities. The recalled pumps are Medtronic's MiniMed 508 and Paradigm series insulin pumps, and Medtronic is providing alternative pumps to affected patients. As of now, the FDA is not aware of any confirmed reports of patient harm related to these risks. The risks are due to vulnerabilities in the wireless communication between the insulin pumps and other devices.

title: FDA approves first treatment for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder, a rare autoimmune disease of the central nervous system
body_summary: The US FDA approved Soliris (eculizumab) injection for the treatment of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (NMOSD) in adult patients who are anti-aquaporin-4 (AQP4) antibody positive. The drug provides the first FDA-approved treatment for NMOSD, a debilitating disease that affects the central nervous system. The approval was based on a clinical study of 143 patients with NMOSD, which showed that Soliris reduced the number of NMOSD relapses by 94 percent over a 48-week course. Soliris is available only through a restricted program under a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS), and it carries a boxed warning for the risk of life-threatening and fatal meningococcal infections. The drug was previously approved for the treatment of paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria and atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome.

title: FDA issues third status report on investigation into potential connection between certain diets and cases of canine heart disease
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is providing an update on its investigation into reports of dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) in dogs eating certain pet foods. The FDA is sharing adverse event reports, an updated case count, and new testing results. The agency has identified the most frequently occurring pet food brands in these reports. The FDA does not yet know how certain diets may be associated with DCM in some dogs, but it is taking steps to protect human and animal health. The investigation is ongoing, and the FDA will provide updates as information becomes available. Between January 1, 2014, and April 30, 2019, the FDA received 524 reports of DCM, including 515 canine reports and 9 feline reports. The agency first alerted the public about a possible link between DCM and pet foods in July 2018 and has consulted with stakeholders to inform its investigation.

title: FDA warns patients and health care providers about potential cybersecurity concerns with certain Medtronic insulin pumps
body_summary: The US FDA is warning patients and healthcare providers about potential cybersecurity risks in certain Medtronic MiniMed insulin pumps. The agency recommends that patients using these models switch to newer models with enhanced cybersecurity capabilities. The potential risks are related to wireless communication between the pumps and other devices. The FDA is concerned that unauthorized users could access a nearby pump and change settings, leading to hypoglycemia or high blood sugar. Medtronic is providing alternative pumps to patients and has identified 4,000 patients in the US who may be using vulnerable devices. The FDA is working to ensure Medtronic addresses the issue and will keep the public informed if new information becomes available.

title: FDA approves first treatment for chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Dupixent to treat adults with nasal polyps accompanied by chronic rhinosinusitis. The treatment is the first for inadequately controlled chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps. Dupixent reduces nasal polyp size and congestion, and improves smell and reduces the need for surgery and oral steroids. The efficacy was established in two studies with 724 patients. Serious allergic reactions and eye problems may occur, including conjunctivitis and keratitis. Common side effects include injection site reactions and eye inflammation. Dupixent was originally approved in 2017 for eczema and in 2018 for asthma. The approval was granted to Regeneron Pharmaceuticals.

title: FDA approves first treatment for chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Dupixent to treat adults with nasal polyps and chronic rhinosinusitis. Dupixent was first approved in 2017 for eczema and later in 2018 for asthma. The new approval makes Dupixent the first treatment for inadequately controlled chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps. Patients receiving Dupixent showed significant reductions in nasal polyp size and congestion, as well as improved ability to smell and reduced need for surgery. However, Dupixent may cause serious allergic reactions and eye problems. The most common side effects include injection site reactions and eye inflammation. Patients should avoid live vaccines and consult their healthcare professional if experiencing new or worsening eye symptoms.

title: FDA issues warnings to companies selling illegal, unapproved kratom drug products marketed for opioid cessation, pain treatment and other medical uses
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued warning letters to two kratom marketers, Cali Botanicals of Folsom, California, and Kratom NC of Wilmington, North Carolina, for illegally selling unapproved, misbranded kratom-containing drug products with unproven claims about treating or curing opioid addiction and withdrawal symptoms. The FDA has warned consumers not to use kratom, a plant that grows naturally in Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Papua New Guinea, due to its potential for addiction, abuse, and dependence. The companies are directed to address the FDA's concerns and failure to correct violations may result in law enforcement action.

title: Statement on stem cell clinic permanent injunction and FDA’s ongoing efforts to protect patients from risks of unapproved products
body_summary: US District Judge Ursula Ungaro issued an order stopping US Stem Cell Clinic LLC and US Stem Cell Inc. from manufacturing or distributing adipose tissue-derived stem cell products until they come into compliance with the law. The US Department of Justice, on FDA's behalf, initiated this action in May 2018, seeking a permanent injunction after the companies failed to comply with FDA regulations. The court granted the government's motion for summary judgment in 2019, concluding the companies adulterated and misbranded their cellular products. The FDA will continue to take enforcement actions against clinics that endanger patients' health with inadequate manufacturing conditions or unapproved products. The agency is nearly halfway through its period of exercising enforcement discretion for regenerative medicine products, but will continue to regulate products that pose safety concerns.

title: Statement on stem cell clinic permanent injunction and FDA’s ongoing efforts to protect patients from risks of unapproved products
body_summary: US District Judge Ursula Ungaro has issued an order stopping US Stem Cell Clinic LLC, US Stem Cell Inc., and Chief Scientific Officer Kristin Comella from manufacturing or distributing adipose (fat) tissue-derived stem cell products, known as stromal vascular fraction (SVF) products, until they comply with the law. The US Department of Justice initiated this action in May 2018, seeking a permanent injunction after the companies failed to comply with FDA regulations. The court granted the government's motion for summary judgment in June 2019, concluding the defendants adulterated and misbranded their cellular products. The FDA will continue to take enforcement action against those who endanger patients' health with inadequate manufacturing conditions or unapproved products. The agency is committed to advancing the safe development of regenerative medicine products, particularly those for serious diseases, and will prioritize resources on clinics and products that pose the greatest risk to patients.

title: Executive Order 13877—Improving Price and Quality Transparency in American Healthcare To Put Patients First
body_summary: President Donald J. Trump announced several executive orders aimed at enhancing patient choice and transparency in healthcare. The actions include requiring hospitals to publicly post standard charge information within 60 days, issuing an advance notice of proposed rulemaking on providing expected out-of-pocket costs to patients within 90 days, and issuing reports on impediments to healthcare price and quality transparency within 180 days. Additionally, a Health Quality Roadmap will be developed to align data and quality measures across various healthcare programs within 180 days. The president also signed an executive order on June 24, 2019, requiring the Secretary of the Treasury to propose regulations and the Secretary of Health and Human Services to submit a report on surprise medical billing within 180 days.

title: FDA expands approval of treatment for cystic fibrosis to include patients ages 6 and older
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has expanded the indication for Symdeko (tezacaftor/ivacaftor) tablets to treat pediatric patients ages 6 years and older with cystic fibrosis who have certain genetic mutations. This expansion is based on improved treatments and life expectancy for patients with cystic fibrosis. The FDA approved Symdeko initially for patients ages 12 and older with the same specific genetic mutations. The new approval provides an important treatment option for younger patients and includes safety and dosing information specific to this population. Symdeko is used for patients with two copies of the most common type of mutation – F508del mutation – or at least one of the responsive mutations. The efficacy of Symdeko was evaluated in three Phase 3 trials for patients ages 12 and older, with extrapolation to younger patients. The safety of Symdeko for patients ages 6 to less than 12 was supported by a study with 70 patients. The FDA granted this application Priority Review, and approval was granted to Vertex Pharmaceuticals Incorporated.

title: FDA approves new treatment for hypoactive sexual desire disorder in premenopausal women
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Vyleesi (bremelanotide) to treat acquired, generalized hypoactive sexual desire disorder (HSDD) in premenopausal women. Hylton V. Joffe, M.D., M.M.Sc., director of the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research’s Division of Bone, Reproductive and Urologic Products, stated that Vyleesi provides women with another treatment option for this condition. HSDD is characterized by low sexual desire that causes marked distress or interpersonal difficulty and is not due to a co-existing medical or psychiatric condition.

The effectiveness and safety of Vyleesi were studied in two 24-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in 1,247 premenopausal women with acquired, generalized HSDD. In these trials, about 25% of patients treated with Vyleesi had an increase of 1.2 or more in their sexual desire score compared to about 17% of those who took placebo. The most common side effects of Vyleesi are nausea, vomiting, flushing, injection site reactions, and headache.

Vyleesi is not recommended for patients with high blood pressure that is uncontrolled or those with known cardiovascular disease. The FDA also warned that Vyleesi may significantly decrease the levels of naltrexone in the blood when taken with naltrexone-containing medications. The FDA granted approval of Vyleesi to AMAG Pharmaceuticals.

title: Statement on agency’s efforts to increase transparency in medical device reporting
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration's Center for Devices and Radiological Health has formally ended the Alternative Summary Reporting (ASR) Program, which allowed manufacturers of certain devices to submit quarterly summary reports instead of individual reports for well-known events. The ASR Program has been closed due to the sunset of the program and the implementation of the Voluntary Malfunction Summary Reporting (VMSR) Program, which enables the FDA to detect potential safety signals and free up resources to focus on addressing the highest risks. The agency has also posted ASR data from 1999 to 2019 and plans to make MAUDE more user-friendly in the next few years. The FDA will continue to rely on medical device reports as a source of information, but emphasizes the need for modernized, active surveillance that utilizes real-world data to detect safety signals.

title: Statement on the FDA’s benefit-risk framework for evaluating opioid analgesics
body_summary: The FDA is taking steps to address the crisis of opioid addiction by issuing a new draft guidance to evaluate the benefit-risk of opioid pain medications. The agency will consider the benefits and risks of proposed new opioid analgesics relative to other already approved opioid and non-opioid analgesics. The draft guidance recommends that companies provide information on whether their drug has any characteristics that would mitigate the risks of overdose, abuse, or addiction. The FDA is also announcing a public meeting on September 17 to further discuss the agency's benefit-risk assessment of opioid analgesics. Additionally, the agency plans to issue guidance on appropriate clinical endpoints and clinical trial approaches for the development of non-opioid drugs for use in the treatment of acute and chronic pain. The FDA will continue to apply an evidence-based decision-making approach to evaluate the safety of approved opioid products based on post-market data and additional sources of information.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in May indicates that the labor market remains strong and that economic activity is rising at a moderate rate. Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Although growth of household spending appears to have picked up from earlier in the year, indicators of business fixed investment have been soft. On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy are running below 2 percent. Market-based measures of inflation compensation have declined; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent. The Committee continues to view sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective as the most likely outcomes, but uncertainties about this outlook have increased. In light of these uncertainties and muted inflation pressures, the Committee will closely monitor the implications of incoming information for the economic outlook and will act as appropriate to sustain the expansion, with a strong labor market and inflation near its symmetric 2 percent objective. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Charles L. Evans; Esther L. George; Randal K. Quarles; and Eric S. Rosengren. Voting against the action was James Bullard, who preferred at this meeting to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points.

title: Statement on a new effort to improve transparency and predictability for generic drug applicants to help increase timely access to high-quality, lower cost generic drugs
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is committed to enhancing and streamlining the development and approval process of high-quality generic drugs to facilitate American patients' access to lower-cost medicines. The FDA has taken steps to support complex generic drug development and application review, prioritize review of certain generics, and publish a list of off-patent, off-exclusivity brand drugs. To improve efficiency, the agency is enhancing the Paragraph IV Patent Certifications List, which provides information about exclusivity related to generic challenges of patents on "brand" drug products. The updated list will include additional data points, such as the status of 180-day exclusivity decisions, dates of first approval, marketing status, and expiration dates of blocking patents. This update aims to provide greater transparency and certainty for industry, enabling more informed decisions on resource allocation. The FDA also plans to publish additional guidances and policy steps to assist generic drug applicants.

title: Statement on new guidance for the declaration of added sugars on food labels for single-ingredient sugars and syrups and certain cranberry products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a final guidance on the declaration of Added Sugars on single-ingredient products such as powdered sugar, pure maple syrup, and honey. The new guidance aims to help consumers better understand the amount of sugar in these products and how it contributes to their daily sugar intake. The FDA is exercising enforcement discretion to allow manufacturers to include a "†" symbol next to the Added Sugars declaration, which leads consumers to a statement explaining the gram amount of Added Sugars and how it contributes to the Daily Value. The guidance also clarifies the labeling of Added Sugars on certain cranberry products, allowing manufacturers to include a symbol that leads to a statement indicating that the product has natural sugars and meets the recommended limit for Added Sugars. The FDA has given manufacturers until July 1, 2021, to comply with the new labeling requirements.

title: FDA approves new treatment for pediatric patients with type 2 diabetes
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Victoza (liraglutide) injection for treating pediatric patients 10 years or older with type 2 diabetes. This is the first non-insulin drug approved for this age group since metformin was approved in 2000. Victoza has been approved for adult patients with type 2 diabetes since 2010. The approval is based on evidence of safety and efficacy, and it provides an additional treatment option for children with type 2 diabetes, which is becoming increasingly common. The drug improves blood sugar levels by mimicking the effects of a natural hormone in the body.

title: Federal officials seize adulterated dietary supplements from Life Rising Corporation due to poor manufacturing practices
body_summary: U.S. Marshals seized over 300,000 containers of dietary supplements from Life Rising Corporation at the request of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. The FDA determined there was probable cause that the company prepared, packed, and/or held dietary supplements under conditions that do not conform to the dietary supplement current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) requirements. The company's dietary supplements were valued at approximately $3.5 million. The FDA issued an Administrative Detention Order to prevent these products from reaching consumers until they could be seized. The agency also issued a safety alert for three Life Rising products due to potential lead contamination. Life Rising previously recalled products in 2016 and 2017 for elevated lead levels. The FDA discourages consumers from purchasing or using dietary supplement products bearing brand names Life Rising, Holicare, or HopeStream.

title: Statement on FDA’s scientific work to understand per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in food, and findings from recent FDA surveys
body_summary: The US FDA has tested dairy products from a farm in New Mexico and produce from North Carolina, finding no health concern from per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) at the levels detected. The FDA partners with states to advance PFAS detection, sharing scientific information and supporting response to contamination events. The agency aims to test more foods, develop state testing capacities, and continue to support public health protection, collaborating with federal and state agencies.

title: Executive Order 13874—Modernizing the Regulatory Framework for Agricultural Biotechnology Products
body_summary: US President establishes a science-based regulatory system for agricultural biotechnology products to protect public health and the environment while fostering innovation and competitiveness. The system consists of 10 sections. The President instructs the Secretaries to develop an international communications strategy to increase acceptance of agricultural biotechnology products abroad, aiming to open and maintain markets for US agricultural exports. The US Trade Representative must develop an international strategy to remove unjustified trade barriers within 120 days.

title: FDA finalizes guidance for premarket tobacco product applications for electronic nicotine delivery systems as part of commitment to continuing a strong oversight of e-cigarettes
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) finalized its guidance for manufacturers submitting new tobacco product applications through the premarket tobacco product application (PMTA) pathway for electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS), such as e-cigarettes. The guidance aims to provide companies with recommendations to consider as they prepare a PMTA to help the FDA evaluate the public health benefits and harms of a product. Acting FDA Commissioner Ned Sharpless emphasized the importance of protecting public health and children from the dangers of nicotine and tobacco-related disease and death.

The guidance clarifies the PMTA process for ENDS products and recommends information for applicants to include in a PMTA submission, such as packaging design to mitigate accidental nicotine exposure and information on battery safety. The FDA is also exploring product standards to prevent injuries from known tobacco product risks.

The PMTA pathway requires manufacturers to demonstrate that marketing of the new tobacco product would be appropriate for the protection of the public health. The agency's evaluation includes reviewing a tobacco product's components, ingredients, additives, and health risks, as well as how the product is manufactured, packaged, and labeled.

The FDA is committed to providing a solid, science-based regulatory foundation to ensure that ENDS products authorized for marketing are appropriate for the protection of public health. The agency will continue to assist industry in complying with federal tobacco regulations through online information, meetings, webinars, and guidance documents.

title: FDA approves first chemoimmunotherapy regimen for patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has granted accelerated approval to Polivy (polatuzumab vedotin-piiq) in combination with bendamustine and a rituximab product, to treat adult patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) that has progressed or returned after at least two prior therapies. This approval provides an alternative option for patients in whom multiple treatments have not worked. Polivy binds to a specific protein on B cells, releasing a chemotherapy drug, and has shown efficacy in a study of 80 patients. The complete response rate was 40% with Polivy plus BR compared to 18% with BR alone. Common side effects include low blood counts, nerve damage, and fatigue. The FDA advises close monitoring for infusion-related reactions, infections, and tumor lysis syndrome. Further clinical trials are required to verify Polivy's clinical benefit. Polivy is an antibody-drug conjugate, and its approval was granted to Genentech.

title: FDA permits marketing of first medical device for relief of pain associated with irritable bowel syndrome in patients 11-18 years of age
body_summary: The US FDA has approved the marketing of the IB-Stim, a medical device that aids in reducing functional abdominal pain in patients 11-18 years old with irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), when combined with other therapies. The device, a small single-use electrical nerve stimulator, is placed behind the patient's ear and emits low-frequency electrical pulses to stimulate certain cranial nerves. According to a published clinical study, the device showed significant improvement in abdominal pain and Pain Frequency Severity Duration (PFSD) scores in treated patients. The study included 50 patients and found that 52% of treated patients experienced at least a 30% decrease in usual pain, and 59% experienced a 30% decrease in worst pain. The device is contraindicated for patients with hemophilia, cardiac pacemakers, or psoriasis vulgaris.

title: Remarks on World Food Safety Day: ‘Food Safety Is Everyone’s Business’
body_summary: The first World Food Safety Day recognizes that food safety affects everyone worldwide. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) supports this global effort to improve food safety. The FDA has implemented several initiatives to prevent foodborne illnesses, including the FDA Food Safety Modernization Act, a New Era of Smarter Food Safety, and the Nutrition Innovation Strategy. These efforts aim to strengthen food safety cultures, promote public health, and empower consumers to make informed choices. The FDA believes that food safety equals behavior and that promoting a culture of food safety is crucial for effective food safety management. The agency encourages everyone to get involved in spreading the word about food safety and taking steps to avoid foodborne illnesses.

title: FDA, FTC take action to protect kids by citing four firms that make, sell flavored e-liquids for violations related to online posts by social media influencers on their behalf
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) have issued warning letters to four firms that manufacture, advertise, and sell flavored e-liquid products due to violations related to online posts by social media influencers. The FDA's Youth Tobacco Prevention Plan aims to limit youth access to all tobacco products, with a focus on e-cigarette use. Acting FDA Commissioner Ned Sharpless stated that the FDA will continue to tackle the e-cigarette epidemic among kids, including limiting youth access to flavored products and taking action against manufacturers and retailers who illegally market these products. Social media influencers posted content touting the flavored e-liquid products without including the required nicotine warning statement. The products subject to the warning letters include those from Solace Technologies, Hype City Vapors, Humble Juice Co., and Artist Liquids Laboratories. The FDA and FTC have requested responses from each company within 15 working days, with potential further action including seizure or injunction.

title: Statement on FDA’s request for information on requiring fixed-quantity blister packaging for certain opioid pain medicines to help decrease unnecessary exposure to opioids
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is implementing new authorities to reduce unnecessary exposure to prescription opioids and potentially lower the rate of new addiction. The SUPPORT Act allows the FDA to require special packaging for opioids and other drugs that pose a risk of abuse or overdose. The FDA is opening a public docket to solicit feedback on the potential use of this authority to require certain immediate-release opioid analgesics to be made available in fixed-quantity, unit-of-use blister packaging. Studies suggest that patients typically use significantly fewer pills than they are prescribed for common surgical procedures and acute pain conditions, and that excess pills can be misused or abused. The FDA seeks feedback on the potential public health impact of making fixed-quantity unit-of-use blister packages available, including which opioid products and number of pills to include.

title: FDA puts company on notice for marketing unapproved stem cell products for treating serious conditions
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has sent an untitled letter to R3 Stem Cell, LLC, a company offering unapproved stem cell products for various diseases and conditions, including Lyme disease, diabetes, and Parkinson's disease. The FDA has notified over 50 affiliate centers or clinics of this action. Acting Commissioner Ned Sharpless stated that the agency will prioritize regulatory actions against those promoting unapproved products, which may place people's health at risk. The company's website promotes stem cell therapies for numerous diseases, including dementia and Parkinson's disease, and directs patients to "R3 Stem Cell Centers of Excellence" for treatment. The products would be regulated as drugs and biological products, requiring demonstration of safety and effectiveness. The FDA has sent 46 regulatory correspondences, including warning letters, and has two court cases pending. Health care professionals and consumers are encouraged to report adverse events related to R3 Stem Cell, LLC products to the FDA's MedWatch program.

title: FDA approves first PI3K inhibitor for breast cancer
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Piqray (alpelisib) tablets for treating postmenopausal women and men with hormone receptor-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative, PIK3CA-mutated, advanced or metastatic breast cancer. The FDA also approved a companion diagnostic test, therascreen PIK3CA RGQ PCR Kit, to detect the PIK3CA mutation. The approval was made under the Real-Time Oncology Review pilot program, which allowed the FDA to begin analyzing key efficacy and safety datasets prior to official submission. The drug's efficacy was studied in the SOLAR-1 trial, which showed significant prolonged progression-free survival in patients with tumors that had a PIK3CA mutation. Common side effects include high blood sugar levels, diarrhea, and nausea. The FDA granted approval to Novartis and QIAGEN Manchester, Ltd. for the companion diagnostic test.

title: FDA approves innovative gene therapy to treat pediatric patients with spinal muscular atrophy, a rare disease and leading genetic cause of infant mortality
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Zolgensma, a gene therapy, to treat children under two years old with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA). Acting FDA Commissioner Ned Sharpless approved the treatment, which targets the cause of SMA, the most severe form of the disease. SMA is caused by a mutation in the SMN1 gene, leading to motor neuron death and muscle weakness. The treatment, an adeno-associated virus vector-based gene therapy, aims to deliver a functional copy of the human SMN gene into motor neuron cells. The FDA based its approval on an ongoing clinical trial involving 36 pediatric patients and a completed trial with 21 patients treated with Zolgensma. The treatment has shown significant improvement in developmental motor milestones and reduced the risk of death in patients with SMA. The FDA granted Fast Track, Breakthrough Therapy, and Priority Review designations to AveXis Inc., the manufacturer of Zolgensma.

title: FDA permits marketing of first diagnostic test to aid in detecting prosthetic joint infections
body_summary: The US FDA has permitted the marketing of the Synovasure Lateral Flow Test Kit as an aid for detecting periprosthetic joint infection in synovial fluid of patients undergoing revision surgery. The test detects human alpha defensins, which are antimicrobial proteins released by white blood cells in response to infection. The FDA reviewed a clinical study of 305 samples and found that 89.5% of subjects with an infection diagnosis were also identified as positive by the test kit. The test is intended to aid in a patient's diagnosis of prosthetic joint infection and should be used in conjunction with other clinical and diagnostic findings. The FDA has also established special controls for the test to ensure safety and effectiveness. The marketing authorization has been granted to CD Diagnostics Inc.

title: FDA authorizes marketing of first diagnostic test for detecting Zika virus antibodies
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has authorized the marketing of a diagnostic test to detect Zika virus immunoglobulin (IgM) antibodies in human blood. The ZIKV Detect 2.0 IgM Capture ELISA is the first Zika diagnostic test to be marketed in the U.S. under traditional premarket authorities. The test is designed to identify proteins produced by the body's immune system when it tests for Zika virus infection in the blood. The FDA reviewed data from a clinical study of 807 test samples and demonstrated that the test was safe and effective. The test is for use in patients with clinical signs and symptoms consistent with Zika virus infection, or those who meet the CDC's Zika virus epidemiological criteria. The FDA has also revoked the EUA for this device, which was initially authorized for emergency use in 2016. The agency is now considering whether the test is an adequate, approved, and available alternative to other currently available Zika virus antibody diagnostic tests.

title: FDA alerts hospitals, laboratories and health care professionals about recall of Beckman Coulter blood test analyzers due to risk of inaccurate platelet analyzing results
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is issuing a Class 1 recall of Beckman Coulter DxH 800, DxH 600, and DxH 900 hematology analyzers due to inaccurate blood platelet counts. The devices were used to diagnose diseases and conditions such as anemia and blood cancers. The recall was initiated in 2018 after complaints of erroneously elevated platelet results. The FDA is urging healthcare professionals to use alternative diagnostic testing or confirm analyzer results with manual scanning or estimate of platelets. The agency has worked with the manufacturer to correct the issue, but has not evaluated the effectiveness of a software update alone. The FDA recommends laboratories use backup analyzers, if available, and follow recommended actions to ensure accurate patient assessments. The recall affects over 2,000 laboratories in the U.S. and the FDA encourages healthcare professionals to report any adverse events or quality problems experienced with the use of Beckman Coulter products.

title: FDA clears first diagnostic tests for extragenital testing for chlamydia and gonorrhea
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared for marketing two diagnostic tests: the Aptima Combo 2 Assay and the Xpert CT/NG. These tests can detect the presence of Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae, causing chlamydia and gonorrhea, through throat and rectal specimens. The tests were previously only cleared for urine, vaginal, and endocervical samples. The FDA granted clearance to Hologic, Inc. for the Aptima Combo 2 Assay and to Cepheid for the Xpert CT/NG. The tests will fill an unmet public health need by allowing for more screening of these infections. Tim Stenzel, director of the Office of In Vitro Diagnostics and Radiological Health, stated that early diagnosis is crucial to prevent complications. The rate of sexually transmitted infections is increasing, with 1.7 million cases of chlamydia and over 500,000 cases of gonorrhea in the U.S. in 2017.

title: Memorandum on Enforcing the Legal Responsibilities of Sponsors of Aliens
body_summary: The President has ordered enforcement of immigration laws, requiring sponsors of aliens to fulfill their commitment under law when an alien applies for or receives means-tested public benefits. The Department of Agriculture and Health and Human Services must issue updated procedures and guidance within 90 days to ensure compliance. The Secretaries of Agriculture and Health and Human Services will advise sponsors, aliens, and others about the enforcement of reimbursement and deeming requirements. The Secretary of the Treasury and Homeland Security will refer cases to the Attorney General for enforcement.

title: Federal judge enters consent decree against compounder PharMedium Services for violations at multiple facilities
body_summary: U.S. District Judge Virginia M. Kendall entered a consent decree of permanent injunction between the U.S. and PharMedium Services, LLC, in partnership with its president Scott Aladeen and vice president Warren Horton, today. The decree prohibits PharMedium from manufacturing, holding, or distributing drugs at its Tennessee facility until it completes corrective actions and receives authorization from the FDA. The company has ceased operations at its Mississippi facility, and its Texas and New Jersey facilities must hire an independent expert to review their operations to ensure compliance with the law. The government alleges that PharMedium manufactured and distributed adulterated drugs, distributed unapproved new drugs, and misbranded drugs. The FDA had previously issued warning letters for similar violations in 2007 and between 2013 and 2018.

title: Federal court enters consent decree against Texas compounder, Pharm D Solutions, LLC to cease the manufacturing of drugs intended to be sterile due to insanitary conditions
body_summary: U.S. District Judge Keith P. Ellison signed a consent decree ordering Texas-based company Pharm D Solutions, LLC, and its owners Luis R. De Leon and Juan C. De Leon, to stop producing compounded drugs intended to be sterile until they comply with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. The FDA previously warned the company about violating the law, and despite this, Pharm D Solutions continued to put patients at risk.
