The consent decree requires the company to cease all sterile compounding operations and distribution until it completes corrective actions.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee voted to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent due to global economic and financial developments and muted inflation pressures. The committee views sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near its symmetric 2 percent objective as the most likely outcomes. Effective April 30, 2019, Anna Paulson was selected as Associate Economist until her successor is chosen in 2020. The committee also voted to reduce the Treasury redemptions cap from $30 billion to $15 billion monthly and reinvest principal payments received on agency MBS in uniform MBS rather than Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac securities.

title: FDA Warns Against the Use of Unauthorized Devices for Diabetes Management
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is warning patients and healthcare professionals about the risks associated with using unapproved or unauthorized devices for diabetes management, including continuous glucose monitoring systems, insulin pumps, and automated insulin dosing systems. The FDA notes that these devices can result in inaccurate blood glucose measurements or unsafe insulin dosing, leading to serious injury or death.

According to Jeff Shuren, M.D., J.D., director of the FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health, "millions of Americans use continuous glucose monitors and insulin delivery devices to monitor and treat their diabetes." However, the agency is concerned that patients may not be aware of the risks associated with using unapproved or unauthorized devices.

The FDA has received reports of serious adverse events, including insulin overdose requiring medical attention, and recommends that patients talk to their doctor about appropriate diabetes management devices for their needs. The agency encourages patients and healthcare professionals to report adverse events to MedWatch, the FDA Safety Information and Adverse Event Reporting program.

The FDA is committed to monitoring the safety of medical devices throughout a product's total lifecycle and alerting the public when safety issues are identified. The agency is also working to streamline regulatory pathways to promote innovation and patient access to approved diabetes management devices.

title: FDA approves first anticoagulant (blood thinner) for pediatric patients to treat potentially life-threatening blood clots
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Fragmin (dalteparin sodium) injection for subcutaneous use to reduce the recurrence of symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE) in pediatric patients one month of age and older. VTE can lead to death and is often associated with underlying conditions such as cancer or congenital heart disease. The approval is based on a single trial with 38 pediatric patients, where 21 achieved resolution of VTE, seven showed regression, and one experienced recurrence. Common side effects of Fragmin include bleeding, thrombocytopenia, and pain at the injection site. The FDA granted this application Priority Review designation, and Pfizer holds the application. Fragmin is a type of heparin that works as an anticoagulant, and its efficacy in children was based on the trial.

title: FDA warns manufacturers of products labeled as homeopathic for putting consumers at risk with significant violations of manufacturing quality standards
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has posted warning letters to five companies that produce products labeled as homeopathic for significant violations of current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) regulations. Four of the companies jointly produce a product labeled as homeopathic that poses a significant safety risk to consumers due to improper sterility testing. The FDA has also warned another company, Newton Laboratories, for human drug CGMP and misbranding violations, as well as unapproved new animal drug violations. The FDA encourages consumers to report adverse events or quality problems experienced with these products to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program.

title: Statement from Acting FDA Commissioner Ned Sharpless, M.D., on policy advancements to help bring interchangeable biosimilars to market
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is issuing final guidance on the pathway for "interchangeable" biologics, which can be substituted without a prescriber's involvement. This guidance aims to promote competition in the biologic market and improve patient access to safe and effective, lower-cost generic drugs, biosimilars, and interchangeable biologics. The guidance provides clarity for developers seeking to demonstrate their proposed biological product meets the statutory interchangeability standard under the Public Health Service Act. The FDA's goal is to increase access to life-saving medications and potentially lower healthcare costs through competition. The guidance also addresses the development of biosimilar and interchangeable insulin products, which may be substituted at the pharmacy level. The FDA will consider stakeholder feedback and input from patients when evaluating data for biosimilar and interchangeable insulin products.

title: Statement from Principal Deputy Commissioner Amy Abernethy, M.D., Ph.D., and Janet Woodcock, M.D., director of FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, on policies designed to capture more data to better understand effects of prescription drugs in pregnant and nursing women
body_summary: The FDA is issuing two draft guidances to increase the availability of high-quality safety information for drugs used during pregnancy or lactation. The first draft guidance, Clinical Lactation Studies: Considerations for Study Design, will provide recommendations for sponsors conducting clinical lactation studies, including when to conduct such studies and how to handle ethical considerations. The second draft guidance, Postapproval Pregnancy Safety Studies, will outline recommendations on how to design studies and leverage data, including real-world data, to assess the outcomes of pregnancies in women taking FDA-regulated drugs during pregnancy. The draft guidances build on previous guidance and are consistent with the recommendations made by the Task Force on Research Specific to Pregnant Women and Lactating Women. The FDA aims to provide women with important safety information to make informed decisions about their health and the health of their babies.

title: FDA approves first treatment for children with Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome, a rare autoimmune disorder
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Ruzurgi (amifampridine) tablets for the treatment of Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS) in patients aged 6 to less than 17 years. This is the first FDA approval specifically for pediatric patients with LEMS. Billy Dunn, M.D., director of the Division of Neurology Products, said the approval will provide a treatment option for pediatric patients with significant weakness and fatigue. LEMS is a rare autoimmune disorder that affects the connection between nerves and muscles, causing weakness and other symptoms. The drug's effectiveness was established in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of 32 adult patients, showing patients on Ruzurgi experienced less impairment. Common side effects reported with Ruzurgi include burning sensation, abdominal pain, and dizziness. The FDA granted Priority Review and Fast Track designations, as well as Orphan Drug designation, and approved the drug to Jacobus Pharmaceutical Company, Inc.

title: FDA approves new treatments for heart disease caused by a serious rare disease, transthyretin mediated amyloidosis
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Vyndaqel (tafamidis meglumine) and Vyndamax (tafamidis) capsules on May 3 for the treatment of transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) in adults. These are the first FDA-approved treatments for this disease. Vyndaqel and Vyndamax have the same active moiety, tafamidis, but differ in dosage. The FDA's Director of Cardiovascular and Renal Drugs, Norman Stockbridge, stated that these treatments are an important advancement in treating ATTR-CM. A clinical trial of 441 patients showed that Vyndaqel improved survival rates and reduced hospitalizations for cardiovascular problems. The drugs received Fast Track, Priority Review, and Breakthrough Therapy designations, as well as Orphan Drug designation. Approval was granted to FoldRx, a subsidiary of Pfizer.

title: Statement from FDA Principal Deputy Commissioner Amy Abernethy, M.D., Ph.D., and Jeff Shuren, M.D., J.D., director of the FDA’s Center for Devices and Radiological Health on FDA’s new efforts to protect women’s health and help to ensure the safety of breast implants
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has been investigating the safety of breast implants since 2011, focusing on textured implants and the risk of breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL). The FDA is taking steps to better characterize the condition, including improving information available to women and healthcare professionals, incorporating product ingredient information into labeling, and making medical device reports publicly available. The agency partners with registries such as the Patient Registry for Breast Implant-Associated Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma (PROFILE) and the National Breast Implant Registry (NBIR) to collect real-world data on breast implant safety and performance. The FDA aims to strengthen evidence generation to inform regulatory actions and provide better information for women considering breast implants.

title: First FDA-approved vaccine for the prevention of dengue disease in endemic regions
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Dengvaxia, the first vaccine approved for preventing dengue disease caused by all four dengue virus serotypes, for individuals ages 9 through 16 who have laboratory-confirmed previous dengue infection and live in endemic areas. Dengue is endemic in US territories and affects over one-third of the world's population. The vaccine was determined to be approximately 76% effective in preventing symptomatic dengue disease in previously infected individuals. Dengvaxia has already been approved in 19 countries and the European Union, and is not approved for use in individuals not previously infected by any dengue virus serotype.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in March indicates that the labor market remains strong and that economic activity rose at a solid rate. Job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Growth of household spending and business fixed investment slowed in the first quarter. On a 12-month basis, overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy have declined and are running below 2 percent. On balance, market-based measures of inflation compensation have remained low in recent months, and survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent. The Committee continues to view sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective as the most likely outcomes. In light of global economic and financial developments and muted inflation pressures, the Committee will be patient as it determines what future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate may be appropriate to support these outcomes. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were: Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; James Bullard; Richard H. Clarida; Charles L. Evans; Esther L. George; Randal K. Quarles; and Eric S. Rosengren.

title: FDA permits sale of IQOS Tobacco Heating System through premarket tobacco product application pathway
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of new tobacco products, including the IQOS "Tobacco Heating System" and Marlboro Heatsticks, manufactured by Philip Morris Products S.A. The agency determined that authorizing these products is appropriate for public health protection due to their lower levels of toxins compared to combustible cigarettes. The products were evaluated through the premarket tobacco product application (PMTA) pathway, which requires manufacturers to demonstrate that marketing is appropriate for public health protection. The FDA placed stringent marketing restrictions on the products to prevent youth access and exposure, including requirements for targeted advertising to adults, notification of labeling and advertising plans, and warning labels about nicotine addiction. The agency will continue to monitor market dynamics and take action as necessary to ensure the sale of these products remains appropriate.

title: FDA approves device to help increase access to more lungs for transplant
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the Xvivo Perfusion System with Steen Solution Perfusate, a device that can temporarily ventilate, oxygenate, and pump preservation solution through lungs deemed unsuitable for transplant. This approval allows for an increased number of lungs to be available for transplant, potentially benefiting more patients. The device was originally granted marketing authorization in 2014 under a humanitarian device exemption and is now approved through the more stringent premarket approval pathway. The FDA evaluated data from a study involving 332 sets of donor lungs, showing a one-year survival rate of 94% for lungs deemed suitable and 86.4% for lungs perfused with the device. The most common adverse events include acute rejection, bronchial complications, respiratory failure, and infections. The approval was granted to Xvivo Perfusion Inc. and supports the development of innovative technologies to increase the donor organ pool for transplant patients.

title: FDA approves first treatment for pediatric patients with lupus
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Benlysta (belimumab) intravenous infusion for treatment of children with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), the first FDA-approved treatment for pediatric patients with the disease. This approval fulfills an unmet need for therapies in pediatric patients with SLE. The approval is based on a 52-week study of 93 pediatric patients with SLE, which showed a higher proportion of patients achieving the composite primary endpoint and a lower risk of severe flares when receiving Benlysta IV plus standard therapy. The drug's safety and pharmacokinetic profiles in pediatric patients were consistent with those in adults. The FDA granted this application a Priority Review designation. The approval is effective for GlaxoSmithKline, and the FDA will require the manufacturer to provide a Medication Guide to inform patients of the risks associated with Benlysta. The drug's common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, and fever, and patients may experience infusion reactions.

title: FDA launches public education campaign to encourage safe removal of unused opioid pain medicines from homes
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) launched a new education campaign called "Remove the Risk" to help Americans understand the importance of removing and properly disposing of unused prescription opioids from their homes. The campaign targets women aged 35-64, who are most likely to oversee household health care decisions. The FDA aims to decrease unnecessary exposure to opioids and prevent new addiction.

Prescription opioids are powerful pain-reducing medicines that can help patients manage pain when prescribed for the right condition and used properly. Misuse or abuse can cause serious harm, including addiction, overdose, and death. In 2017, retail pharmacies dispensed over 191 million opioid prescriptions, with 90% of patients not finishing their prescribed medication.

The FDA launched a toolkit of materials, including PSAs, fact sheets, social media graphics, and website badges, to educate individuals, healthcare providers, and organizations about safe disposal of unused prescription opioids. The agency also updated information on safe disposal on its webpage.

The "Remove the Risk" campaign aims to educate Americans on the issue and provide easy-to-follow steps to remove prescription opioids from their homes. Medicine take-back options are the preferred way to dispose of most types of unneeded medicines safely, including opioids. The next National Prescription Drug Take-Back Day is on April 27, 2019.

title: Statement from FDA Associate Commissioner for Regulatory Affairs Melinda K. Plaisier, on agency’s new steps to strengthen the process of initiating voluntary recalls
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is issuing a new draft guidance on initiating voluntary recalls for FDA-regulated products. The guidance aims to provide industry with clear information on preparing for and executing recalls. Key recommendations include:

Training: Companies should identify and train personnel on recall responsibilities, establish recall communications plans, and identify FDA reporting requirements.

Record Keeping: Companies should properly code products, maintain distribution records, and use modern approaches like blockchain technology for product traceability.

Procedures: Companies should prepare and maintain written recall initiation procedures to swiftly ensure recalled products are removed from the market.

The FDA has been working to improve recalls over the past 18 months, including adopting new policies for rapidly posting recalls and issuing guidance on public warnings and notifications. The agency remains committed to learning from recalls and seeking opportunities for improvement to ensure public safety.

title: Statement from Jeffrey Shuren, M.D., J.D., Director of the FDA’s Center for Devices and Radiological Health, on new steps to help reduce risks associated with surgical staplers for internal use and implantable staples
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is strengthening its efforts to address device safety issues in the post-market, as outlined in its Medical Device Safety Action Plan. The agency has alerted the public to concerns regarding surgical staplers for internal use and implantable surgical staples, which are widely used in various surgical applications. The alert was prompted by a large number of medical device reports associated with the use of these devices, including over 41,000 individual adverse event reports from January 1, 2011 to March 31, 2018. The most commonly reported problems include staple line openings, malformations, and misfiring.

To better protect patients, the FDA is proposing to increase the regulatory requirements of surgical staplers for internal use by reclassifying them into a higher-risk category that requires premarket notification review and clearance prior to marketing. The agency is also issuing a draft guidance, "Surgical Staplers and Staples for Internal Use - Labeling Recommendations," to help manufacturers ensure their labeling provides adequate information for safe use. Furthermore, the FDA intends to hold a public meeting of the General and Plastic Surgery Devices Panel in May 2019 to discuss the proposed reclassification and draft guidance.

title: Statement from Peter Marks, M.D., Ph.D., director of FDA’s Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, on FDA’s continued confidence in the safety and effectiveness of the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine
body_summary: The FDA strongly emphasizes the importance of vaccines in preventing preventable diseases such as measles, mumps, and rubella. The MMR vaccine has been approved for nearly 50 years and has been shown to be highly effective in preventing these diseases. Measles has been completely eradicated in the US since 2000, and mumps cases have decreased by 99%. The vaccine has been proven safe and effective, with two doses being 97% effective against measles, 88% effective against mumps, and 97% effective for rubella. The FDA will continue to monitor outbreaks and provide information on vaccine safety and effectiveness.

title: FDA permits marketing of first medical device for treatment of ADHD
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has permitted the marketing of the Monarch external Trigeminal Nerve Stimulation (eTNS) System, the first medical device to treat attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). The device is approved for patients aged 7 to 12 years old who are not taking prescription ADHD medication and is the first non-drug treatment for ADHD granted marketing authorization by the FDA. The device, developed by NeuroSigma, uses mild nerve stimulation to treat ADHD symptoms. Clinical trials show that subjects using the eTNS device had statistically significant improvement in their ADHD symptoms compared to a placebo group. The most common side effects observed with eTNS use are drowsiness, increased appetite, and fatigue. The FDA granted marketing authorization to NeuroSigma and will review subsequent devices of the same type through the 510(k) premarket process.

title: FDA approves first generic naloxone nasal spray to treat opioid overdose
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted final approval of the first generic naloxone hydrochloride nasal spray, commonly known as Narcan. The agency plans to prioritize the review of additional generic drug applications for products intended to treat opioid overdose. FDA Deputy Center Director Douglas Throckmorton stated that these efforts aim to make naloxone more readily available and accessible. The FDA will also help facilitate the approval of an over-the-counter naloxone product. The agency has already taken steps to increase naloxone product availability, including granting priority review to generic drug applications and exploring ways to increase naloxone product availability in the community.

title: FDA Statement from Deputy Commissioner for Food Policy and Response Frank Yiannas on new steps to protect consumers from unlawful ingredients in dietary supplements
body_summary:
The FDA is launching a new tool to alert the public about potentially unlawful dietary supplements. The Dietary Supplement Ingredient Advisory List will be housed on the FDA website, listing ingredients that appear to be unlawfully marketed in dietary supplements. The list will be updated regularly and will not be exhaustive. Consumers can sign up to receive updates and stakeholders can submit feedback to support or refute the FDA's preliminary assessment.

The FDA has warned eight companies for marketing dietary supplements containing DMHA, which is considered adulterated. Three companies have been warned for marketing dietary supplements containing phenibut, which is misbranded. These companies have 15 business days to respond and comply with the law. The FDA will continue to use enforcement tools to protect consumers and will take action without notice if necessary. The agency is committed to ensuring that products sold as dietary supplements meet the law's requirements and do not put consumers at risk.

title: FDA takes action to protect women’s health, orders manufacturers of surgical mesh intended for transvaginal repair of pelvic organ prolapse to stop selling all devices
body_summary: The US FDA has ordered manufacturers Boston Scientific and Coloplast to immediately stop selling and distributing surgical mesh products for transvaginal repair of pelvic organ prolapse (POP) in the US due to lack of evidence on their safety and effectiveness. This decision follows a series of escalating safety actions to protect the health of thousands of women undergoing transvaginal surgery for POP. The FDA prioritizes providing patients with access to safe medical devices, and has partnered with medical organizations to develop a Women's Health Technologies CRN to address unique device therapies.

title: Statement from Jeff Shuren, M.D., director of the Center for Devices and Radiological Health, on agency efforts to mitigate temporary shortage of pediatric breathing tubes due to recent closure of Illinois sterilization facility
body_summary: The FDA has alerted the public to a temporary shortage of tracheostomy tubes manufactured by Smiths Medical due to the closure of a sterilization facility in Michigan. The shortage affects pediatric patients, as alternative tubes with similar functionality are limited. The FDA is working with Smiths Medical to quickly resolve the sterilization challenges and bring the critical devices to patients. The shortage is expected to be resolved by the week of April 22. Healthcare professionals, parents, and caregivers are advised to contact Smiths Medical for updates and to explore alternative options, such as reusing and cleaning tubes or using other FDA-cleared tracheostomy tubes. The FDA is closely monitoring the situation and updating its website with the latest information.

title: FDA issues final rule on safety and effectiveness of consumer hand sanitizers
body_summary: The US FDA has issued a final rule to ensure that over-the-counter hand sanitizers are safe and effective. The rule establishes that certain active ingredients, including triclosan and benzethonium chloride, are not allowed in OTC hand sanitizers. The FDA has finalized its previous determination that 28 active ingredients are not eligible for evaluation under the OTC Drug Review. The rule also seeks to ensure consistency and accuracy in the agency's safety and effectiveness evaluations. Director Janet Woodcock stated that the rule aims to provide consumers with confidence in the safety and effectiveness of hand sanitizers. The rule will not affect most hand sanitizers, which use ethyl alcohol as the active ingredient.

title: FDA warns public not to use unapproved or uncleared medical devices to help assess or diagnose a concussion
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is warning the public not to use medical devices marketed to consumers that claim to help assess, diagnose, or manage head injury, including concussion or traumatic brain injury. The FDA has not reviewed these tools for safety and efficacy, which could result in an incorrect diagnosis and potentially lead to a person with a serious head injury returning to normal activities instead of getting medical care. The FDA has cleared only a limited number of medical devices to aid in concussion diagnosis, treatment, or management, and they require evaluation by a healthcare professional. The FDA director, Jeffrey Shuren, states that there are currently no devices to aid in assessing concussion that should be used by consumers on their own. The FDA is monitoring the medical device market and will take further action if necessary.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a meeting on March 19-20, 2019, discussing options for transitioning to the longer-run size of the balance sheet. The staff presented two options: ending the reduction in securities holdings at the end of September 2019 or potentially reducing the pace of redemptions before that date. The Committee intended to slow balance sheet runoff, reduce uncertainty about its securities holdings, and resume growth of the balance sheet when necessary. Consumer spending is expected to remain solid in the near term, supported by elevated household net worth and upbeat consumer sentiment. Economic growth in foreign economies slowed further, with weakness in many emerging markets. The Federal Reserve reported that foreign risky assets tracked similar US asset movements over the intermeeting period. Participants viewed a sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near 2 percent objective as likely outcomes over the next few years. The Committee voted unanimously to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent, citing strong labor market conditions and muted inflation pressures despite slower economic growth in early 2019.

title: Statement by Douglas Throckmorton, M.D., Deputy Center Director for Regulatory Programs in FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, on new opioid analgesic labeling changes to give providers better information for how to properly taper patients who are physically dependent on opioids
body_summary: The FDA is requiring changes to the prescribing information for all opioid analgesic medicines used in the outpatient setting to provide expanded information on safely decreasing the dose in patients who are physically dependent on opioids. This includes considering factors such as the dose of the drug, the duration of treatment, the type of pain being treated, and the physical and psychological attributes of the patient. The FDA is also issuing a Drug Safety Communication for health care providers and patients on the importance of having informed discussions between patient and clinician and ensuring follow-up and support for patients managing pain and changes to their medication regimens.

title: FDA approves new treatment for osteoporosis in postmenopausal women at high risk of fracture
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Evenity (romosozumab-aqqg) to treat osteoporosis in postmenopausal women at high risk of breaking a bone (fracture). These women have a history of osteoporotic fracture or multiple risk factors for fracture, or have failed or are intolerant to other osteoporosis therapies. The approval was based on two clinical trials involving over 11,000 women, which showed that Evenity reduced the risk of a new fracture in the spine (vertebral fracture) by 73% compared to placebo. Evenity is a monoclonal antibody that blocks the effects of the protein sclerostin and works mainly by increasing new bone formation. The medication should not be used in patients who have had a heart attack or stroke within the previous year due to an increased risk of cardiovascular death, heart attack, and stroke. Common side effects include joint pain and headache. The FDA granted the approval to Amgen.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on continued efforts to advance safe biotechnology innovations, and the deactivation of an import alert on genetically engineered salmon
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has advanced a comprehensive framework for the efficient development of safe biotechnology products, including a newPlant and Animal Biotechnology Innovation Action Plan. The FDA recently deactivates a 2016 import alert that prevented GE salmon from entering the U.S. The FDA's approval of AquAdvantage Salmon, a genetically engineered Atlantic salmon, followed a comprehensive analysis of scientific evidence, which determined that the salmon met statutory requirements for safety and effectiveness. The FDA no longer has the authority to issue labeling guidance on GE content in human foods, as this authority has been divested to the USDA. The FDA believes this authority has been satisfied by the USDA's issuance of final regulations implementing the National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard.

title: FDA approves first two-drug complete regimen for HIV-infected patients who have never received antiretroviral treatment
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Dovato, a two-drug regimen consisting of dolutegravir and lamivudine, for treating HIV-1 infection in adults with no antiretroviral treatment history. This is the first FDA-approved two-drug regimen for HIV-infected adults who have never received treatment. The approval allows patients to take a single tablet while reducing toxicity and potential drug interactions from a third drug. Dovato was demonstrated to be effective in reducing HIV levels in two clinical trials involving 1,433 adults. The treatment was associated with common adverse reactions, and patients with HIV and hepatitis B are advised to monitor closely. The FDA granted approval to ViiV Healthcare, and the approval aims to increase access to effective HIV treatment.

title: FDA warns about risks of using home use test strips that are pre-owned or not authorized for sale in U.S., including those for glucose, warfarin
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has warned against using test strips from a previous owner or those not authorized for sale in the US due to the risk of infection or inaccurate test results, which can cause serious harm, including death. The FDA issued a safety alert to patients and healthcare professionals about the risks. Tim Stenzel, director of the Office of In Vitro Diagnostics and Radiological Health, stated that purchasing pre-owned or unauthorized test strips may put users at risk. The FDA recommends inspecting the package for opened or altered status and checking expiration dates to determine if a test strip is pre-owned or unauthorized. Patients should purchase test strips from trusted sources, such as local pharmacies or manufacturers, and consider patient assistance programs or coupons to reduce costs. The FDA is committed to alerting the public about safety issues with medical devices and encourages reporting of adverse events through MedWatch.

title: FDA issues warning letter to genomics lab for illegally marketing genetic test that claims to predict patients’ responses to specific medications
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued a warning letter to Inova Genomics Laboratory for illegally marketing certain genetic tests that claim to predict patients' responses to specific medications based on genetic variants. The tests have not been reviewed by the FDA for safety and effectiveness. The FDA is concerned that selecting or changing drug treatment in response to the test results could lead to potentially serious health consequences for patients. The agency is taking action to protect the public from the significant risk these tests pose. Inova is required to respond within 15 working days with details of how the violations will be corrected. The FDA has also issued safety communications to warn consumers and healthcare professionals about the risks of pharmacogenetic tests that make unsubstantiated claims.

title: FDA and CBP bolster collaboration to protect public health and safety
body_summary: U.S. Food and Drug Administration and U.S. Customs and Border Protection leaders signed an agreement to enhance inspection and detection capabilities to prevent harmful products from entering the U.S. through International Mail Facilities and Ports of Entry. The agreement aims to increase efficiency, reduce duplication of efforts, and facilitate mission responsibilities through knowledge-transfer, collaboration on laboratory space and equipment, and sharing of resources. FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb and U.S. Customs and Border Protection Commissioner Kevin K. McAleenan emphasized the importance of this joint effort, citing the need to protect the public from illicit and dangerous products, such as unapproved fentanyl products and counterfeit prescription drugs. The agreement will focus on identifying trends, coordinating shared space, and developing new targeting and enforcement strategies. In Fiscal Year 2018, the FDA examined packages from over 180 countries, with approximately 90% containing products that should not have entered the country.

title: FDA Statement on the agency’s list of known nitrosamine-free valsartan and ARB class medicines, as part of agency’s ongoing efforts to resolve ongoing safety issue
body_summary: The FDA has announced that it has identified 40 ARB medications with no known nitrosamine impurities, and an estimated 200-400 ARB medications are still under evaluation. The agency has been working to thoroughly understand the issue, address exposure to unnecessary risk, and prevent future impurities from reoccurring. The FDA has established an internal working group and collaborated with global regulators to minimize risks to patients. The agency has also identified factors that contribute to the formation of nitrosamine impurities during manufacturing, including the use of recycled raw materials. Patients are advised to continue taking their medicine until a safe replacement or alternative treatment option is provided. The FDA expects many companies to manufacture nitrosamine-free ARB medications in approximately six months, and the agency will prioritize its investigation into this ongoing issue to ensure patient safety.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., and Biologics Center Director Peter Marks, M.D., Ph.D. on FDA’s continued efforts to stop stem cell clinics and manufacturers from marketing unapproved products that put patients at risk
body_summary: The FDA emphasizes the importance of voluntary compliance with regulations, particularly for products that pose significant health risks, as stem cell therapies are developed and marketed. The agency aims to advance safe and effective stem cell therapies through scientific work and clinical investigation, collaborating with stakeholders to bring safe products to market. Companies manufacturing unapproved stem cell therapies have been issued warnings by the FDA, which will take steps to address those putting patients at risk. The FDA requires careful development requirements for stem cell therapies due to the unique risks they pose, and has a responsibility to regulate various products, including human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, medical devices, and food supply, to protect public health.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., and Principal Deputy Commissioner Amy Abernethy, M.D., Ph.D., on FDA’s ongoing scientific investigation of potential safety issue related to seizures reported following e-cigarette use, particularly in youth and young adults
body_summary: The FDA is informing the public of a potential emerging safety issue related to e-cigarettes. Reports have identified 35 cases of seizures following e-cigarette use between 2010 and early 2019. While the FDA is concerned by these cases, it cannot yet determine if there is a direct relationship between e-cigarette use and seizure risk. The FDA is urging the public to voluntarily report additional adverse events, particularly among youth and young adults, to help inform their work. Reports should include information about the specific product used, product use preceding the adverse event, and other relevant details. The FDA will continue to investigate this issue and take additional steps to protect the public, especially youth, from the dangers of e-cigarettes and other tobacco products.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. and Deputy Commissioner Anna Abram on new 2019 efforts to improve the quality of compounded drugs
body_summary: The FDA plans to modernize its compounding policies in 2019 to balance access to compounded drugs with safety. The agency will use funds to establish a "Center of Excellence" and update compound drug quality. The FDA aims to regulate compounding from bulk substances and finalize guidance on ensuring drugs are not prepared under insanitary conditions. To achieve this, the agency will finalize a Memorandum of Understanding with states to secure public health goals, building on lessons from the 2012 fungal meningitis outbreak. The FDA will also issue revised draft guidance for hospital and health system compounding, hold public meetings, and continue working with stakeholders to develop policies ensuring safe access.

title: FDA takes new steps to increase access to adverse event report data for medical products used in animals
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has made available online adverse event reports related to animal drugs and medical devices used in animals, dating back 30 years. These reports are now accessible electronically on openFDA.gov, an agency-run digital platform. The reports include information from the FDA's Center for Veterinary Medicine's Adverse Event Reporting (AER) system and will be uploaded to openFDA.gov on a quarterly basis. Approximately 865,075 adverse event reports were submitted between January 1, 1987, and April 3, 2019. The reports are associated with approved animal drugs, unapproved/compounded drugs, and medical devices used in animals. The FDA aims to enhance transparency and sharing of adverse event report data to benefit human and animal health.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the agency’s continued efforts to bring competition to the insulin market to lower prices and expand access
body_summary: The FDA aims to promote competition in the insulin market to address the $330 billion annual healthcare expenditure for Americans with diabetes. The Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act of 2010 introduced a pathway for biosimilar and interchangeable products, which the FDA plans to transition for insulin products. Under the FDA's Biosimilars Action Plan, newly approved biological products will have a suffix in their name, while older products will be exempt. The agency will announce guidance on interchangeability and address barriers to biosimilar competition to ensure patients have access to affordable insulin.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new steps to advance agency’s continued evaluation of potential regulatory pathways for cannabis-containing and cannabis-derived products
body_summary: The FDA is announcing new steps to advance its consideration of a framework for the lawful marketing of cannabis and cannabis-derived products, including CBD. A public hearing on May 31 and a written public comment period are scheduled. The agency will form a high-level internal working group to explore potential pathways for dietary supplements and conventional foods containing CBD. The goal is to address safety and functionality concerns and potential impact on the drug approval process. The FDA has already issued warning letters to three companies making unsubstantiated claims about their products' ability to treat serious diseases. The agency aims to explore lawful marketing pathways for CBD products, including dietary supplements and conventional foods, and will share information with the public.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. on steps toward a new, tailored review framework for artificial intelligence-based medical devices
body_summary: The US FDA is considering a new regulatory framework to promote the development of safe and effective medical devices that use advanced artificial intelligence algorithms. The agency aims to keep up with the rapid pace of innovation in these technologies. A discussion paper outlines information specific to devices with AI algorithms that make real-world modifications, including the algorithm's performance, manufacturer's plan for modifications, and risk management. The framework would allow for modifications to be made from real-world learning and adaptation while ensuring safety and effectiveness. The FDA expects to issue draft guidance informed by comments and feedback from experts and stakeholders. The goal is to enable beneficial and innovative AI software to come to market while maintaining a gold standard of safety and effectiveness.

title: FDA takes new enforcement actions as part of the agency’s ongoing effort to combat the illegal online sales of opioids
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued two warning letters to website operators that illegally market potentially dangerous, unapproved, and misbranded opioid medications, including tramadol. The warning letters, sent to azmedicinalshop.com and thedonrx.net, request immediate cessation of sales of violative drugs to U.S. consumers. The FDA is hosting an Online Opioid Summit to advance innovative solutions to protecting Americans from opioids sold online. Commissioner Scott Gottlieb stated that combating the opioid epidemic requires a broad collaboration across the internet community. The agency has already taken action against 23 other websites, and plans to continue targeting and ending illegal opioid sales. Opioid addiction is a critical public health concern, with 47,600 opioid-related deaths in the U.S. in 2017. The FDA is committed to reducing opioid exposure, promoting non-addictive alternatives, and addressing the illicit sale of opioids online.

title: FDA warns homeopathic firms for putting patients at risk with significant violations of manufacturing quality standards
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has posted warning letters to four companies producing homeopathic drug products for significant violations of current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) regulations. King Bio Inc. of Asheville, N.C. is one of the companies, which has continued to concern the FDA due to low quality operations and potential harm to consumers. The FDA has also posted warning letters to Red Mountain Incorporated, Tec Laboratories Incorporated, and B. Jain Pharmaceuticals Pvt. Ltd. for various quality and misbranding violations. The warning letters highlight issues such as contamination, toxic substances, and lack of quality oversight. The FDA is committed to addressing these concerns to protect patients and the public.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new efforts to advance treatment strategies for helping youth addicted to nicotine as a result of the epidemic rise in teen use of e-cigarettes
body_summary: The FDA is committed to addressing the growing issue of youth e-cigarette use, which has more than tripled in the past year. The agency has launched a series of enforcement actions, public education campaigns, and new policies to prevent youth access to flavored tobacco products. However, given the rise in youth e-cigarette use, the need to prevent youth from using tobacco in any form and to explore evidence-based approaches to address existing youth tobacco use and nicotine addiction is clear. The FDA is holding a public scientific workshop on May 15 to discuss scientific understanding and treatment options for youth tobacco addiction and cessation, with a focus on e-cigarette cessation. The workshop aims to gather scientific information, stimulate discussion, and inform the development of new therapies to support youth tobacco cessation.

title: FDA approves new oral treatment for multiple sclerosis
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Mavenclad tablets to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis in adults. Mavenclad is recommended for patients who have had an inadequate response to or are unable to tolerate an alternate drug. The approval is based on a clinical trial of 1,326 patients with relapsing forms of MS, which showed significant reductions in relapses and disability progression. Mavenclad must be dispensed with a Medication Guide and has warnings about increased risk of malignancy, fetal harm, and other potential side effects. The FDA approved the drug for EMD Serono, Inc. and protects the public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of human drugs.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., Director of FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research Janet Woodcock, M.D. and Director of FDA’s Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research Peter Marks, M.D. on Expanded Access –Looking Forward
body_summary: The FDA remains committed to facilitating access to investigational medical products for patients with serious or immediately life-threatening diseases or conditions when no comparable or satisfactory alternative therapy options are available. Since 2010, drug sponsors have provided access to over 13,000 patients. The FDA encourages sponsors to offer expanded access (EA) in circumstances where continued access to a promising medicine after a clinical trial would be appropriate. EA can be considered as a mechanism for patients who have participated in a trial to continue receiving a drug that may have provided benefit. The FDA supports sponsors in providing EA, particularly after patients show promise on an experimental drug. An analysis of over 10,000 EA applications shows that the incidence of a clinical hold due to an adverse event on an EA IND was 0.2 percent.

title: FDA approves treatment for patients with a type of inflammatory arthritis
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Cimzia (certolizumab pegol) injection for treating adults with non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis (nr-axSpA), a type of inflammatory arthritis. The FDA has granted approval to UCB. The approval follows a randomized clinical trial involving 317 adult patients with nr-axSpA, which showed greater responses in patients treated with Cimzia compared to those treated with placebo. The efficacy and safety profile of Cimzia have been studied, with a Boxed Warning advising health care professionals and patients about the increased risk of serious infections and lymphoma.

title: Remarks from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., as prepared for testimony before a U.S. Senate Subcommittee on Appropriations on FDA’s Fiscal Year 2020 budget
body_summary: The FDA Director testified before a subcommittee, discussing the agency's efforts to combat the opioid crisis and requesting $55 million in funding for FY 2020. The crisis, driven by the growing use of illicit drugs like fentanyl, requires a comprehensive approach. The FDA proposes a new approach to opioid drug approvals, considering opioids as a class differently from other drug classes. The goal is to incentivize the development of safer and more effective opioid products, including abuse-deterrent formulations. A premarket demonstration would be required to show superiority to an already-approved opioid. The FDA aims to encourage the development of novel treatments with significant advantages over existing options, ultimately reducing the crisis of opioid addiction.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on actions to advance our comprehensive plan to reduce tobacco-related disease and death, through new efforts to improve the tobacco product application review process, including a newly proposed rule
body_summary: The FDA has issued a proposed rule to establish requirements for the content and format of reports manufacturers must send to demonstrate the substantial equivalence of a new tobacco product. The proposed rule will provide information on how the agency intends to evaluate these submissions. The rule aims to improve the efficiency and predictability of the review process, particularly for new tobacco products that could allow currently addicted adult smokers to access nicotine without the risks associated with combustible tobacco products.

title: FDA advances landmark policy changes to modernize mammography services and improve their quality
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is proposing amendments to key regulations governing mammography facilities to improve the quality of breast cancer screening services. The proposed amendments aim to enhance the information provided to patients and healthcare professionals, allowing for more informed medical decision-making. The FDA is modernizing mammography quality standards and enhancing enforcement efforts to ensure the safety and quality of mammography services. The proposed rule would require facilities to provide breast density information to patients and healthcare professionals, and would modernize the way mammography facilities communicate with patients and healthcare professionals. The FDA is committed to supporting new innovations and methods to prevent, detect, and treat cancer, and the proposed amendments are part of the agency's broader commitment to protecting the health of women. The proposed rule is available online for public comment for 90 days from publication.

title: FDA approves new oral testosterone capsule for treatment of men with certain forms of hypogonadism
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Jatenzo, an oral testosterone capsule, to treat men with certain forms of hypogonadism. Jatenzo is not recommended for men with "age-related hypogonadism" due to its potential risks. The drug's benefits do not outweigh its risks for this use. Jatenzo was demonstrated to be effective in a four-month clinical trial involving 166 men, with 87% achieving normal testosterone levels. The drug contains a boxed warning for increased risk of heart attack, stroke, and cardiovascular death. The FDA requires all testosterone product manufacturers to conduct blood pressure postmarketing trials. Common side effects include headache, high blood pressure, and nausea. The FDA granted approval to Clarus Therapeutics.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new steps to strengthen agency’s safety requirements aimed at mitigating risks associated with transmucosal immediate-release fentanyl products
body_summary: The FDA is strengthening its Opioid Analgesics Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program to improve the safe use of transmucosal immediate-release fentanyl (TIRF) medicines. The REMS program aims to ensure that these medicines are prescribed only to opioid-tolerant patients. To achieve this, the FDA is issuing new requirements to manufacturers, including verifying patient opioid tolerance with each prescription and creating a patient registry to monitor for serious adverse events. These changes will drive more judicious prescribing and better patient awareness of the serious risks of these medications. The FDA plans to finalize updates to the TIRF REMS program over the next year, with the goal of ensuring patients with breakthrough cancer pain have access to necessary treatments.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., and Director of FDA’s Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research Peter Marks, M.D., Ph.D., on efforts to promote and foster blood pathogen reduction technologies
body_summary: Blood products are critical to public health, offering life-saving benefits for various conditions and surgical procedures. Ensuring their safety is a top priority due to unique risks, including contamination by pathogens. To mitigate these risks, pathogen reduction technologies are being explored, which use nucleic acid binding compounds and/or ultraviolet light to inactivate pathogens. These technologies can address over 95% of existing and emerging pathogens, but have limitations, including not inactivating all viruses and addressing prions. The ideal technology would be inexpensive, simple to implement, and provide robust pathogen inactivation, potentially enabling reduced or eliminated screening requirements for travel to malaria-endemic areas and reducing the cost of screening blood. The Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research at the FDA is pursuing research to advance pathogen reduction technology, with the goal of perfecting these approaches.

title: FDA approves new oral drug to treat multiple sclerosis
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Mayzent tablets to treat adults with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS), including clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease. The approval was based on a clinical trial of 1,651 patients who showed a statistically significant reduction in disability progression and fewer relapses. Mayzent must be dispensed with a patient Medication Guide and may increase the risk of infections, cause changes in vision, and affect liver and lung function.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on steps the Agency is taking to prevent potential medical device shortages and ensure safe and effective sterilization amid shutdown of a large contract sterilization facility
body_summary: The FDA is addressing potential medical device shortages due to the closure of a sterilization facility in Illinois, which was shut down by the state EPA over high levels of ethylene oxide. The FDA has been working to secure alternative locations and methods for sterilization, actively monitoring the situation and encouraging medical device manufacturers to assess potential impacts on device distribution and consider alternative contract sterilizers. The agency plans to discuss innovative sterilization methods, including reducing environmental exposure risks, with the infection control community and host a public advisory committee meeting. The FDA will work with manufacturers, contract sterilizers, and government agencies to evaluate potential impacts and take steps to avert device shortages, particularly following facility closures.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January indicates that the labor market remains strong but that growth of economic activity has slowed from its solid rate in the fourth quarter. Payroll employment was little changed in February, but job gains have been solid, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Recent indicators point to slower growth of household spending and business fixed investment in the first quarter. On a 12-month basis, overall inflation has declined, largely as a result of lower energy prices; inflation for items other than food and energy remains near 2 percent. On balance, market-based measures of inflation compensation have remained low in recent months, and survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent. The Committee continues to view sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective as the most likely outcomes. In light of global economic and financial developments and muted inflation pressures, the Committee will be patient as it determines what future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate may be appropriate to support these outcomes. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were: Jerome H. Powell, Chairman; John C. Williams, Vice Chairman; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; James Bullard; Richard H. Clarida; Charles L. Evans; Esther L. George; Randal K. Quarles; and Eric S. Rosengren.

title: FDA takes action against marketer of unapproved products claiming to treat addiction, chronic pain and other serious conditions
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has posted a warning letter to Nutra Pharma Corp for illegally marketing unapproved products labeled as homeopathic with claims about treating addiction and chronic pain. FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb has stated that the agency is dedicated to protecting consumers from bogus claims and fraudulent products, particularly those that exploit Americans harmed by the opioid crisis. The FDA has issued a warning letter to Nutra Pharma for their products "Nyloxin Oral Spray" and others, which have been shown to have unsubstantiated claims and may pose serious health risks. The agency has requested responses from Nutra Pharma within 15 working days and may take legal action without further notice if violations are not corrected.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., and Deputy Commissioner Frank Yiannas on new steps to strengthen FDA’s food safety program for 2020 and beyond
body_summary: The US FDA is proposing new funding for its food safety system, building on the Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA). The proposed budget will invest in new technologies such as Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) and blockchain to detect and respond to food contamination, as well as support state partnerships to create a prevention-based food safety system. The agency aims to improve timeliness and efficiency of premarket safety reviews for food ingredients, including genome-edited animals and plants. The FDA requests additional resources to advance innovative food products while ensuring their safety, and has announced a new policy plan to clarify its approach and avoid unnecessary barriers to innovation in biotechnology.

title: FDA issues warning letters to two breast implant manufacturers for failure to comply with post-approval study requirements
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued warning letters to two breast implant manufacturers, Mentor Worldwide LLC and Sientra, Inc., for failing to comply with their premarket approval orders to conduct post-approval studies on the long-term safety and risks of their silicone gel-filled breast implants. The FDA requires all manufacturers of approved silicone gel-filled breast implants to conduct post-approval studies to further evaluate safety and effectiveness. The warning letters noted serious deficiencies in Mentor's post-approval study for its MemoryShape breast implant and Sientra's post-approval study for its Silicone Gel Breast Implants, including poor patient enrollment and follow-up rates, and significant data inconsistencies. The FDA requests responses from both manufacturers within 15 working days to address the noted violations and may take action, including pursuing criminal and civil penalties, if compliance is not achieved.

title: FDA approves new device for treating moderate to severe chronic heart failure in patients
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the Optimizer Smart system for treating patients with chronic, moderate-to-severe heart failure who are not suited for other treatments. The device received a Breakthrough Device designation due to its treatment of a life-threatening disease. About 5.7 million people in the US have heart failure, a condition caused by diseases that damage the heart. The Optimizer Smart system consists of an implantable pulse generator, battery charger, programmer, and software. It delivered electrical impulses to the heart to improve its squeezing capability. The FDA evaluated data from two clinical trials with 389 patients, showing improvements in walking distance and quality of life. The device is indicated for patients with limited physical activity and symptomatic heart failure.

title: FDA approves first treatment for post-partum depression
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Zulresso (brexanolone) injection for the treatment of postpartum depression (PPD) in adult women. This is the first drug specifically approved for PPD. Zulresso has a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) and is only available through a restricted distribution program at certified healthcare facilities. The drug requires administration by a healthcare provider and continuous monitoring for excessive sedation and sudden loss of consciousness. Zulresso was shown to be effective in improving depressive symptoms in two clinical studies, and its approval was granted Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy designation.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., and Deputy Commissioner Frank Yiannas on advancing new tools and science for implementing agricultural water requirements for produce safety
body_summary: The FDA is extending compliance dates for agricultural water requirements under the Produce Safety Rule. The rule, part of the Food Safety Modernization Act, sets science-based standards for growing, harvesting, packing, and holding fruits and vegetables. The extension will allow farmers to implement measures to mitigate potential risks, particularly for large farms (January 2022), small farms (January 2023), and very small farms (January 2024). The FDA aims to ensure safe produce and water go hand in hand, applying lessons learned from recent outbreaks, including those linked to romaine lettuce in 2018 and last fall. The agency will incorporate expert input and scientific developments to solidify standards and protect public health.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. and Jeff Shuren, M.D., Director of the Center for Devices and Radiological Health, on efforts to evaluate materials in medical devices to address potential safety questions
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulates medical devices to ensure benefits outweigh risks, focusing on biocompatibility and clinical studies on device materials. Recent advances in materials science have led to innovations like 3D printing and miniaturized implants. However, a growing body of evidence suggests biological responses to certain materials, such as inflammation and tissue changes, leading to pain and other symptoms. The FDA is working to better understand device materials and improve patient safety through initiatives like the National Evaluation System for Health Technology (NEST) and research on breast implants. The agency is conducting assessments of various materials' long-term health effects, including breast implants and metal devices, and revising protocols for postmarket surveillance of devices like the Essure system. The FDA is also exploring the link between immune and inflammatory reactions to metal implants, gathering input from experts, patients, and manufacturers to inform its evaluation of materials used in implantable devices.

title: FDA allows marketing of new device to help treat carbon monoxide poisoning
body_summary: The US FDA has allowed the marketing of ClearMate, a new device intended to treat patients with carbon monoxide poisoning in emergency rooms. The device works by increasing a patient's breathing rate, allowing a normal amount of oxygen to attach to hemoglobin. The FDA reviewed data from clinical studies on 100 patients, which showed the device was effective at eliminating carbon monoxide. The device was reviewed under the FDA's De Novo premarket review pathway and was granted marketing authorization to Thornhill Research, Inc. This action creates a new regulatory classification, allowing subsequent devices of the same type with the same intended use to go through the 510(k) premarket process.

title: FDA approves new indication for valve repair device to treat certain heart failure patients with mitral regurgitation
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved a new indication for the MitraClip device, a heart valve repair device, to treat moderate-to-severe or severe mitral regurgitation in patients with normal mitral valves who develop heart failure symptoms due to diminished left heart function. The approval expands the device's indication to patients who have failed to get symptom relief from other therapies. The MitraClip device is inserted through a minimally invasive procedure to grasp the mitral valve leaflets and reduce blood backflow. A study of 614 patients with heart failure showed that the risk of re-hospitalization for heart failure symptoms was reduced by 47 percent and the risk of death within two years was decreased by 37 percent in patients who received the MitraClip device. The device is contraindicated in patients who cannot tolerate blood thinners or have certain heart conditions.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new strategies to modernize clinical trials to advance precision medicine, patient protections and more efficient product development
body_summary: The FDA is modernizing clinical trials to accommodate novel precision medicine approaches, aiming to streamline product development, testing, and diagnostics. The agency promotes innovative trial designs, such as master protocol trials, and encourages decentralized clinical trials and mobile technologies. To support this, the FDA releases guidance on a Risk-Based Approach to monitoring of Clinical Investigations, which helps expand efficient monitoring approaches and advances precision medicine. The agency aims to protect human subjects and ensure data quality through risk-based monitoring, leveraging computerized algorithms and advanced analytics to improve the safety and effectiveness of medical products.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on advancing new policies aimed at preventing youth access to, and appeal of, flavored tobacco products, including e-cigarettes and cigars
body_summary: The FDA is proposing to end compliance policy for flavored electronic nicotine delivery system (ENDS) products, except for tobacco-, mint-, and menthol-flavored products, to prioritize enforcement and prevent youth access. Manufacturers must submit premarket applications by August 8, 2021. The agency aims to regulate nicotine levels in combustible cigarettes to make them minimally or non-addictive. The FDA will monitor and enforce tobacco product regulations, including e-cigarettes and flavored cigars, and unveil a television advertisement to educate children about e-cigarette risks. The agency will reconsider mint- and menthol-flavored ENDS product policies and consider measures to curb youth e-cigarette use, including a proposed rule to ban characterizing flavors in cigars.

title: FDA approves a new generic valsartan
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved a new generic of Diovan (valsartan), an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) that treats high blood pressure and heart failure. The FDA prioritized the review of this drug application to address the recent shortage of valsartan products due to multiple recalls caused by nitrosamine impurities. The FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb said the approval aims to help relieve the shortage and provide patients with a new medicine. The FDA has conducted a major investigation to address the presence of nitrosamine impurities in generic ARB products, working with companies to remove affected products from the market and implementing new testing methods. The FDA has also engaged with manufacturers to facilitate manufacturing process changes to ensure ARBs are free of detectable levels of nitrosamine impurities. The agency will continue to evaluate ARB medicines and update the list of recalled products on its website.

title: Federal judge enters consent decree against Texas compounder, Guardian Pharmacy Services
body_summary: A federal court ordered JMA Partners, Inc., doing business as Guardian Pharmacy Services, to stop producing compounded drug products intended to be sterile until the company complies with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and other requirements. The consent decree requires Guardian to cease sterile operations until it completes corrective actions, including hiring a qualified independent expert to inspect its facility. The FDA had previously issued warnings and conducted inspections, including a 2016 warning letter for insanitary conditions and a 2018 risk alert following adverse event reports involving patients who received compounded triamcinolone-moxifloxacin products. The FDA alleges that Guardian manufactured and distributed drugs under insanitary conditions and in violation of current good manufacturing practice requirements. The company's owner, Jack R. Munn, is also subject to the consent decree.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on Administration’s request for new FDA funding to continue to advance robust regulatory framework for oversight of e-cigarettes, prevent youth access and initiation; and harness innovation to advance the safety of food, compounded drugs, U.S. bl
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is seeking a $6.1 billion budget for FY 2020 to protect public health. The agency aims to address the opioid epidemic, regulate e-cigarettes, and improve food safety. Key initiatives include reducing unnecessary opioid exposure, developing non-opioid alternatives for pain management, and modernizing oversight of dietary supplements. The FDA plans to invest in pathogen reduction technology, strengthen compound drug oversight, and enhance medical product safety and innovation initiatives. The agency is also modernizing its policies and processes to improve medical device reviews, post-market surveillance, and cybersecurity.

title: FDA takes steps to help reduce risks associated with surgical staplers and implantable staples
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a letter to healthcare providers to alert them about an increasing number of medical device reports associated with the use of surgical staplers for internal use and implantable surgical staples. The agency is aware of more than 41,000 individual reports, including 366 deaths, over 9,000 serious injuries, and 32,000 malfunctions, from January 1, 2011 to March 31, 2018. The letter provides updated recommendations to reduce risks associated with the use of these devices, including reviewing labeling instructions and indications for use, and considering alternative options if the patient's tissues are swollen, prone to bleeding, or dead. The FDA plans to issue a new draft guidance for public comment and hold a public meeting to discuss reclassifying surgical staplers for internal use.

title: USDA and FDA Announce a Formal Agreement to Regulate Cell-Cultured Food Products from Cell Lines of Livestock and Poultry
body_summary: The U.S. Department of Agriculture's (USDA) Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) and the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services' Food and Drug Administration (FDA) have jointly announced a formal agreement to oversee the production of human food products derived from the cells of livestock and poultry. The agreement describes the oversight roles and responsibilities for both agencies and how they will collaborate to regulate the development and entry of these products into commerce. Under the agreement, FDA oversees cell collection, cell banks, and cell growth and differentiation, while FSIS will oversee the production and labeling of human food products derived from the cells of livestock and poultry. The agencies have agreed upon a joint regulatory framework, with a transition from FDA to FSIS oversight during the cell harvest stage.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA’s steps on naming of biological medicines to balance competition and safety for patients receiving these products
body_summary: The FDA is updating its naming convention for biosimilars and originator products to promote pharmacovigilance and ensure patient safety. Starting in 2017, the FDA applied a four-letter suffix to approved biosimilars and originator products. The updated policy, released today, indicates that the FDA will no longer modify the names of already licensed products without a suffix. Instead, the agency will designate a new name for interchangeable biosimilars, combining the core name with a four-letter suffix. This framework aims to secure pharmacovigilance and promote patient safety. The FDA also plans to apply the naming convention to vaccines to determine if existing information is sufficient for ensuring pharmacovigilance.

title: FDA approves new nasal spray medication for treatment-resistant depression; available only at a certified doctor’s office or clinic
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Spravato, a nasal spray containing esketamine, for the treatment of depression in adults who have tried other antidepressants but have not benefited from them. The drug is available only through a restricted distribution system due to its risk of serious adverse outcomes, including sedation and dissociation, and potential for abuse and misuse. Patients must be monitored by a healthcare provider for at least two hours after receiving the drug, and the patient must sign a Patient Enrollment Form to acknowledge the risks. Spravato was evaluated in four clinical trials, with one showing statistically significant effect on depression severity within two days. The most common side effects were dissociation, dizziness, and sedation. The FDA approved the application of Janssen Pharmaceuticals, Inc. and granted Fast Track and Breakthrough Therapy designations to the drug.

title: Executive Order 13861—National Roadmap To Empower Veterans and End Suicide
body_summary: The US President, Donald J. Trump, has ordered a national call to action to improve the quality of life of veterans, who on average die by suicide every 20 minutes. A comprehensive national public health roadmap will be developed within 365 days to prevent suicide, focusing on holistic care and collaboration across sectors. The roadmap will be accompanied by a legislative proposal for grants to local communities and a national research strategy to improve coordination and monitoring of research efforts. A task force, led by an Executive Director designated by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, will facilitate public-private partnerships and monitor implementation of the roadmap, set to terminate two years after submitting a roadmap to the President.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., and Susan Mayne, Ph.D., director of the Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition, on tests confirming a 2017 finding of asbestos contamination in certain cosmetic products and new steps that FDA is pursuing to improve cosmetics safety
body_summary: The FDA is calling on the cosmetic industry to improve safety oversight, particularly for products containing talc. In 2017, reports of asbestos contamination in products sold to children under 18 prompted an investigation, leading to a safety alert and confirmed asbestos presence in 4 product samples.
