The agency is now requesting information from manufacturers about talc sourcing and testing procedures, investigating sourcing and testing practices, and encouraging voluntary registration of products. The FDA aims to report adverse events and modernize its approach to cosmetics regulation to better protect consumers.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on forceful new actions focused on retailers, manufacturers to combat youth access to e-cigarettes as part of FDA’s Youth Tobacco Prevention Plan
body_summary: The FDA is cracking down on e-cigarette sales to youth, targeting retailers and manufacturers that violate laws. The agency has sent letters to corporate management of Walgreens, the top violator among pharmacies, and is seeking information from over 40 companies about illegally marketed e-cigarette products. The FDA plans to hold retailers accountable and explore additional enforcement avenues to target violative sales and marketing practices. The agency is also partnering with state attorneys general and enforcing regulations on tobacco product sales and marketing to combat youth e-cigarette use. Studies are underway to investigate the potential health effects of e-cigarettes, including the risk of cancer. The FDA emphasizes the importance of retailers and manufacturers taking steps to prevent tobacco products from reaching minors.

title: FDA provides update on its ongoing investigation into ARB drug products; reports on finding of a new nitrosamine impurity in certain lots of losartan and product recall
body_summary:
The FDA is updating the public on its ongoing investigation into the recent voluntary recalls of generic angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) drug products. Hetero Labs Ltd. in India has announced the recall of 87 lots of losartan potassium tablets due to the presence of the impurity N-Nitroso-N-methyl-4-aminobutyric acid (NMBA). The FDA's interim acceptable intake limits for NMBA are higher than the levels found in the recalled losartan potassium tablets.

The FDA's evaluation suggests that the risk of cancer to patients with NMBA exposure is less than the risk from NDEA exposure, but any presence of impurities in drug products is not acceptable. The agency has developed novel testing methods to detect and measure nitrosamine impurities and is conducting an extensive organic chemistry analysis to develop methods to detect additional nitrosamine impurities.

The FDA has identified NMBA in lots of losartan potassium, but it has not been found in previously recalled ARB products. The agency is continuing its investigation and will work with companies to swiftly remove affected products from the market if nitrosamine impurities are found at levels above the interim acceptable intake limits.

Patients taking ARB drug products from recalled lots should check the list periodically for updates and continue taking their medicine until a replacement or different treatment option is provided. The FDA will provide updates on the list of products included in the recalls as more information becomes available.

title: FDA warns CanaRx for selling unapproved, misbranded and unsafe imported drugs to unsuspecting Americans
body_summary: The US FDA posted a warning letter to CanaRx, a company that facilitates the distribution of unapproved new drugs and misbranded drugs to US consumers. The FDA is concerned that these drugs pose serious health risks to consumers. CanaRx's scheme involves foreign physicians rewriting US prescriptions and supplying unapproved, potentially counterfeit, or expired drugs to US consumers. The FDA is troubled by CanaRx's marketing tactics and the lack of safeguards for these drugs. The company is requested to respond within 10 working days with details on how it will correct its violations. The FDA is committed to promoting safe and effective generic alternatives and will take enforcement action if necessary. Consumers who have concerns about CanaRx-supplied medications should consult their healthcare provider.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. as prepared for oral testimony before the U.S. House Subcommittee on Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies, Committee on Appropriations
body_summary:
Chairman Bishop and members of the subcommittee, the FDA is witnessing a historic period of scientific advancement, with unparalleled opportunities to improve health and wellbeing. The FDA's Fiscal Year 2019 budget includes a substantial increase, which will help uncover new treatment options, improve competition to lower drug costs, and advance development of treatments for rare diseases. The new funding will also improve consumer safety by modernizing food product oversight and medical product safety and manufacturing.

The FDA is undertaking a significant modernization effort for its Office of New Drugs, updating its approach to drug review across every stage of the life cycle. This includes adopting new standard templates for Investigational New Drug Applications, launching a "safety signal tracker" to consolidate information on safety concerns, and conducting meetings early in the drug review cycle to scope out potential safety issues.

The agency is also updating its guidance on how to assess clinical effectiveness for drugs, incorporating real-world evidence and real-world data, and launching a new effort to analyze safety data more efficiently across the entire drug lifecycle. The FDA's Adverse Event Reporting System for drugs will be expanded to cover more types of safety data, including pre-market drug safety data.

The support of this Committee is key to these efforts, which aim to leverage the tools of science and innovation to advance public health. The FDA has new and better opportunities to improve patient safety and confirm clinical evidence of benefit for drugs targeted to unmet medical needs, potentially reducing the cost of drug development and making medicines more affordable.

title: FDA statement on FDA’s modern approach to advanced pharmaceutical manufacturing
body_summary: The US FDA is taking steps to advance the adoption of continuous manufacturing (CM) in the pharmaceutical industry. CM transforms traditional manufacturing processes into a single system based on modern process monitoring and controls. This approach enables steady output of finished drug products and reduces complexity and uncertainty. The FDA has charged an Emerging Technology Team to help early adopters of CM surface and resolve implementation challenges. The agency is also providing guidance and information to interested companies and has issued draft guidance to support the development and implementation of CM. There are now four companies manufacturing five approved products using CM processes, and over 20 additional companies have engaged with the FDA. The FDA aims to promote drug quality and improve manufacturing efficiency through CM.

title: FDA, CDC, and CMS launch task force to help facilitate rapid availability of diagnostic tests during public health emergencies
body_summary: The US FDA, CDC, and CMS have launched the Tri-Agency Task Force for Emergency Diagnostics to improve collaboration and accelerate the development and deployment of diagnostic tests in clinical and public health laboratories during public health emergencies. The task force aims to leverage the expertise of each agency to address issues related to implementing diagnostic tests authorized for emergency use under EUA and other unmet needs in public health preparedness. The task force will provide a forum for coordination, consultation, and improvement of diagnostic test availability during public health emergencies.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. on the agency’s 2019 policy and regulatory agenda for continued action to forcefully address the tragic epidemic of opioid abuse
body_summary: The FDA is addressing the opioid crisis by taking a more aggressive approach to regulatory action, expanding risk evaluation and mitigation strategies, updating labeling, and training healthcare providers on safe use and addiction medicine. The agency has also considered the risks of illicit use and taken action to limit access to certain drugs, including rationalizing prescribing practices and pursuing evidence-based guidelines. To reduce exposure to opioids, the FDA is cutting off illicit internet traffic, increasing interdiction efforts, and expanding enforcement against illicit opioids. The agency is reviewing the effectiveness of the REMS program for transmucosal immediate-release fentanyl medicines and plans to modify it to strengthen its ability to mitigate risks. The FDA has also been assessing the development and use of safe and effective Medication-Assisted Treatment for opioid use disorder.

title: FDA issues warning letter to clinic illegally marketing unapproved thermography device, warns consumers to avoid using thermography devices to detect breast cancer
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a warning letter to Total Thermal Imaging Inc., a California-based company, and its president Linda Hayes for illegally marketing and distributing an unapproved thermography device as a sole screening device for breast cancer and other diseases. The FDA also issued a safety communication to warn patients that thermography is not cleared by the FDA as an alternative to mammography and should not replace mammography for breast cancer screening or diagnosis. 

The FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb stated that the agency will not tolerate individuals or companies marketing unapproved devices that deceive patients and put them at risk. The FDA is concerned that patients may rely on unapproved claims that thermography may be used as a sole screening device for breast cancer and miss the chance to detect cancer in its earliest stages. 

Thermography is a noninvasive tool that uses an infrared camera to produce images showing heat and blood flow patterns on or near the surface of the body. It has been cleared by the FDA only as an adjunctive tool, not as a standalone screening or diagnostic tool. 

Total Thermal Imaging Inc. markets the Thermography Business Package, an unapproved device that includes a FLIR Systems Inc. thermographic camera and proprietary software, as a sole screening tool for breast cancer and other diseases. The device requires premarket approval by the agency. 

The warning letter requests that Total Thermal Imaging Inc. immediately cease distributing the Thermography Business Package and respond within 15 working days with details of how the violations will be corrected. Any violations not corrected could lead to enforcement action such as seizure, injunction or civil money penalties.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., and Deputy Commissioner Frank Yiannas on a new strategy to advance FDA’s food safety mission and modernize oversight of imported food
body_summary: The US FDA has implemented a comprehensive imported food safety strategy to address concerns. The strategy aims to prevent food safety problems, detect and refuse unsafe products, and respond quickly to safety issues. Key components include onsite inspections, risk-informed prioritization, foreign supplier verification programs, and systems recognition programs. The FDA also optimizes import screening and review processes, enhances response to safety issues, and adopts modern tools for efficiency and effectiveness. The agency assesses its performance, publishes performance measures, and commits to keeping its food safety mission robust and effective.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on efforts to spur development of innovative devices, including new advancements in novel brain implants, that can help patients with paralysis or amputation gain mobility
body_summary: The FDA is issuing draft guidance to promote the development of brain-computer interface (BCI) devices, which can directly control a limb prosthesis by a patient's thought processes. The goal is to enhance mobility and independence for people with severe disabilities, including those with paralysis or amputation. The draft guidance aims to bridge the gap between current regulatory considerations and emerging technologies. The agency is encouraging public comments to consider all viewpoints before finalization.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., and Director of FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research Janet Woodcock, M.D., on the FDA’s continuing efforts to maintain its strong oversight of generic drug quality issues domestically and abroad
body_summary: The FDA prioritizes patient and consumer health by assessing and mitigating risks through rigorous data analysis and science-based activities. The agency refutes reports that generic drugs are of lesser quality than brand-name drugs, stating they use the same active ingredients and have the same risks and benefits. The FDA conducts premarket reviews, inspections, and monitoring of manufacturing plants to ensure compliance with good manufacturing practices. A multidisciplinary team analyzes data from various sources, including spontaneous reports, controlled clinical trials, and electronic healthcare databases, to identify potential safety signals. The agency takes regulatory action to improve product safety, such as updating labeling or removing a product from the market. The FDA ensures generic manufacturers meet the same standards as domestic manufacturers, with testing and inspections to affirm quality and consistency.

title: FDA advances new proposed regulation to make sure that sunscreens are safe and effective
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a proposed rule to update regulatory requirements for most sunscreen products in the United States. The rule aims to ensure consumers have access to safe and effective preventative sun care options. The proposal addresses sunscreen active ingredient safety, dosage forms, and sun protection factor (SPF) and broad-spectrum requirements.

The FDA proposes that zinc oxide and titanium dioxide are Generally Recognized as Safe (GRASE) for use in sunscreens, while PABA and trolamine salicylate are not. The agency is seeking additional data on 12 ingredients and proposes updates to labeling, including the addition of active ingredients on the front of the package.

The proposal also includes new labeling requirements, such as a notification for consumers to read the skin cancer/skin aging alert, and revised formats for SPF, broad spectrum, and water resistance statements. The FDA is seeking public comment on the proposed rule and will consider comments as it works towards developing a final rule.

The rule is part of the FDA's ongoing efforts to take into account modern science to ensure the safety and effectiveness of sunscreens. The agency is working towards comprehensive OTC reform to facilitate changes necessary for the FDA to keep pace with evolving science and new safety data.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on additional steps by the agency to support the development of safe and effective novel nicotine replacement therapies to help smokers quit cigarettes
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is releasing a second draft guidance on developing novel nicotine replacement therapy (NRT) products to help smokers quit combustible cigarettes. These products could potentially offer an opportunity to save lives by empowering adults to safely and effectively quit smoking. The guidance aims to describe new endpoints that are meaningful to helping currently addicted adult smokers, outlining a broader set of criteria for new approvals. The FDA established the Nicotine Steering Committee in 2017 to create a flexible framework for product innovations that have the potential to help smokers quit combustible cigarettes. The guidance recognizes that nicotine replacement therapy products have been effective in providing adults with tools to help quit smoking, and novel products may offer additional opportunities for health-concerned smokers.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: Jerome H. Powell chaired a joint meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee and Board of Governors on January 29-30, 2019, electing John C. Williams as Vice Chairman. The Committee authorized the Federal Reserve Bank to execute open market transactions for the System Open Market Account, including purchasing and selling foreign currencies. The Committee reaffirmed principles and adjusted as needed at its annual meeting amid volatile financial markets. Consumer price inflation remained below 2% in November, with strong job growth and industrial production increases in December. The Committee maintained the target range for the federal funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent, citing global economic and financial developments and muted inflation pressures.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., and Director of FDA’s Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research Peter Marks, M.D., Ph.D., cautioning consumers against receiving young donor plasma infusions that are promoted as unproven treatment for varying conditions
body_summary: The FDA has warned consumers and healthcare providers about establishments offering infusions of plasma from young donors to treat various conditions, including normal aging, memory loss, and serious diseases like dementia, Parkinson's disease, and Alzheimer's disease. The FDA has no proven clinical benefit for plasma infusion from young donors for these conditions, and there are associated risks. These treatments have not gone through rigorous testing and should not be assumed safe or effective. The FDA strongly discourages consumers from pursuing this therapy outside of clinical trials.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new policy to improve access and foster price competition for drugs that face inadequate generic competition
body_summary:
The FDA is taking new steps to support downward pressure on drug prices by clearing a path for more efficient generic development. The agency is working to reduce barriers to generic development and lower the cost of generic entry. In the next year, the FDA will advance additional policies to promote generic competition, including for complex drugs. This includes issuing guidance documents on developing specific complex generic medicines and addressing regulatory and scientific challenges.

The FDA will also issue a draft guidance on establishing active ingredient sameness and develop new analytical tools and in vitro tests to support approval of complex generic drugs. A new pathway for Competitive Generic Therapies (CGTs) will provide incentives for developing generic versions of drugs with inadequate generic competition. The pathway allows companies to submit requests to designate a drug as a CGT at the time of submitting an abbreviated new drug application (ANDA) or at any time before.

The FDA has already granted over 100 CGT designation requests and approved the first five ANDAs for generic drugs designated as CGTs, providing 180-day marketing exclusivity to the applicants. The agency aims to encourage development of safe and effective generic competition for drugs with sole source status. The FDA is also working to make generic drug development more efficient and predictable, reducing approval times and providing greater transparency to generic industry stakeholders.

title: FDA issues warning letter to doctor for illegally marketing unapproved device with claims to prevent and treat tightening of scar tissue around breast implants
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration issued a warning letter to Dr. Mark Berman, M.D. of Beverly Hills, California for illegally marketing an unapproved implantable device, the Pocket Protector, which claims to prevent and treat capsular contracture in breast implants. Dr. Berman is also accused of significant deviations from the FDA's quality system requirements and current good manufacturing practices. The warning letter reflects the agency's commitment to advancing policies that enhance device safety, particularly for women. The FDA has warned the public about safety issues related to breast implants and unsafe silicone injections. Dr. Berman's marketing of other FDA-regulated products without approval is currently the subject of a federal enforcement case filed in May 2018.

title: FDA authorizes first interoperable insulin pump intended to allow patients to customize treatment through their individual diabetes management devices
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has permitted the marketing of the Tandem Diabetes Care t:Slim X2 insulin pump with interoperable technology for children and adults with diabetes. The pump, an alternate controller enabled (ACE) infusion pump, is the first interoperable pump that can be used with different diabetes therapy systems, allowing patients to customize their treatment. The FDA Commissioner, Scott Gottlieb, stated that this innovation has the potential to aid patients seeking individualized diabetes therapy systems. The pump delivers insulin under the skin at set or variable rates and can be digitally connected to communicate with other diabetes management devices. The FDA granted marketing authorization to Tandem Diabetes Care Inc. and established criteria for the accuracy, reliability, cybersecurity, and clinical relevance of ACE infusion pumps.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. and Deputy Commissioner Frank Yiannas on findings from the agency’s investigation of the November 2018 outbreak of E. coli O157:H7 in California-linked romaine lettuce
body_summary: In November 2018, the US FDA and CDC issued a public warning about an E. coli O157:H7 outbreak linked to romaine lettuce. The outbreak strain was detected in an on-farm water reservoir in California, and the FDA believes contaminated lettuce became contaminated through this water. A farm had a procedure to test reservoir water for generic E. coli but failed to ensure sufficient sanitizer was present. The investigation identified multiple farms in California that may have been implicated. To prevent future outbreaks, the FDA has recommended that leafy green growers, buyers, and retailers improve tracing and sourcing practices. The FDA will work with industry to adopt technologies for real-time product tracing and conduct microbiological surveillance sampling assignments for romaine lettuce.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. on new programs to promote the adoption of innovations in drug manufacturing that can improve quality and lower drug costs
body_summary: The FDA is announcing a new draft guidance to recognize voluntary consensus standards related to pharmaceutical quality. This program aims to promote development and use of consensus standards to expedite pharmaceutical development and streamline the review of drug product applications. The program will allow stakeholders and FDA staff to propose pharmaceutical quality standards for potential recognition by the FDA, providing industry with additional options for pharmaceutical development and manufacturing. The goal is to reduce regulatory uncertainty, allowing manufacturers to utilize new or innovative approaches within their development programs. Informally recognized standards will also be publicly available. The program does not change existing law requirements and is intended to facilitate recognition of other standards concerning pharmaceutical quality to make the adoption of advances in drug manufacturing and application review more efficient.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on ongoing efforts to stop the spread of illicit opioids, further secure the U.S. drug supply chain and forcefully confront opioid epidemic
body_summary: The FDA has been taking steps to combat the opioid crisis by increasing enforcement and interdiction efforts, particularly at international mail facilities. In 2017, the USPS processed nearly half a billion international parcels, with 80% of websites providing guidance on mailing illicit drugs instructing traffickers to use the Postal Service. The FDA has identified and referred suspect shipments, leading to hundreds of arrests and prosecutions. In addition, the agency has taken action against online networks selling opioids, sending warning letters to 70 websites operating illegally. The FDA has also warned McKesson Corp. for violations related to the Drug Supply Chain Security Act, including failing to quarantine and investigate suspect products. To address the crisis, the FDA is developing new guidance on opioids, modernizing the development pathway for non-opioid analgesics, and advancing guidelines for opioid prescribing and packaging to limit abuse and misuse. The agency is also utilizing new authorities to ensure the integrity of supply chains.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the agency’s new efforts to strengthen regulation of dietary supplements by modernizing and reforming FDA’s oversight
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is announcing a new plan to modernize dietary supplement regulation and oversight, aiming to balance innovation and efficiency with increased consumer protection. The goal is to implement significant changes over the next 25 years. The agency is committed to ensuring safety, maintaining product integrity, and fostering informed decision-making. Key initiatives include developing a rapid-response tool to alert the public about potentially dangerous ingredients, improving NDI notification submissions, and updating the compliance policy for dietary supplements. The FDA plans to engage in public dialogue about modernizing the Dietary Supplement Health and Education Act (DSHEA), exploring options for exclusivity, product listing requirements, and enhanced enforcement strategies.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new data demonstrating rising youth use of tobacco products and the agency’s ongoing actions to confront the epidemic of youth e-cigarette use
body_summary: The US FDA has released new data from the 2018 National Youth Tobacco Survey, showing a significant increase in e-cigarette use among middle and high school students, from 3.6 million to 3.6 million in 2018, with over 1.5 million more students using e-cigarettes in the past year. The study suggests that JUUL and flavored products are driving the trend, with youth using e-cigarettes more frequently and with flavored products more often. In response, the FDA is revising its compliance policy to restrict the sale of flavored e-cigarette products in physical locations where people under 18 are permitted, and will curtail online sales without heightened age verification processes. The agency has also launched a new campaign, "The Real Cost," to prevent youth e-cigarette use, and has received positive feedback from teachers on the helpfulness of resources to engage with students about e-cigarette use.

title: FDA takes action against 17 companies for illegally selling products claiming to treat Alzheimer’s disease
body_summary: The US FDA has posted 12 warning letters and 5 online advisory letters to foreign and domestic companies selling 58 unapproved products claiming to prevent, treat, or cure serious diseases such as Alzheimer's disease. These products, including dietary supplements, have not been reviewed by the FDA and are not proven safe and effective. The FDA warns that these products may be ineffective, unsafe, and delay proper medical care. FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb has announced new actions to strengthen the regulatory framework overseeing dietary supplements, including efforts to promote innovation while upholding safety. The FDA has issued over 40 warning letters in the past five years to companies making similar claims, and consumers are advised to remain vigilant when purchasing products claiming to prevent, treat, or cure diseases without proof.

title: FDA takes new steps to adopt more modern technologies for improving the security of the drug supply chain through innovations that improve tracking and tracing of medicines
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is launching a pilot project to enhance tracing and verification of prescription drugs in the supply chain. The program aims to test innovative technologies to improve the security of the drug supply and reduce diversion. Eligible entities can apply to participate. The pilot will inform the development of an enhanced electronic track-and-trace system set to go into effect in 2023. The system will help prevent counterfeit drugs from entering the supply chain and improve the ability to detect and respond to illegitimate products. FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb and expert Frank Yiannas will work together to leverage technologies like blockchain to strengthen the US food supply. The goal is to fully secure electronic product tracing, establish robust product verification, and ensure that all parties involved in handling drugs can spot and quarantine suspect products.

title: FDA pursues order barring specific retailers from selling tobacco products as part of its continuing efforts to target youth tobacco use
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) initiated enforcement action against certain retail locations of Walgreen Co. and Circle K Stores Inc. for repeated violations of restrictions on the sale and distribution of tobacco products, including sales of cigars and menthol cigarettes to minors. The agency filed complaints seeking No-Tobacco-Sale Orders (NTSO), which would bar the two specific retail locations from selling tobacco products for 30 days. The affected locations are a Walgreens store in Miami, Florida, and a Circle K store in Charleston, South Carolina. Walgreens has 22% of its stores inspected having illegally sold tobacco products to minors, with over 1,550 warning letters and 240 civil money penalty actions against its stores nationwide for unlawful tobacco product sales to minors. Circle K has also had high rates of repeat violations, with over 1,045 warning letters and 205 civil money penalty actions issued against its stores. The FDA Commissioner, Scott Gottlieb, M.D., expressed concern over the pharmacy setting's influence on consumer and retailer perceptions around tobacco products, and the agency will continue to hold retailers accountable by vigorously enforcing the law.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new steps to strengthen the agency’s process for issuing public warnings and notifications of recalls
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is issuing new guidance to strengthen and modernize the process for issuing public warnings about voluntary recalls and notifications of recalls. The final guidance outlines circumstances when a company should issue a public warning, describes the general timeframe for companies to issue such a warning, and explains when the FDA may take action to issue its own public warning. The FDA has already begun implementing the recommendations outlined in the final guidance and has issued consumer warnings related to several products, including Kellogg's Honey Smacks, recalled vegetables, and angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) drugs. The agency has also seen a five-year low in recalls, with 7,420 recalls in fiscal year 2018, but increased publicizing of these events has led to more recalls being reported. The FDA is committed to improving processes, education, and awareness to protect public health and continue to seek opportunities for improvement.

title: Federal court enters consent decree against Ranier’s Rx Laboratory and owner for manufacturing purportedly sterile drug products in insanitary conditions
body_summary: The U.S. District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania entered a consent decree of permanent injunction between the United States and Ranier's Rx Laboratory Inc., owned by pharmacist Francis H. Ranier, today. The FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb stated that the agency is committed to ensuring compounded drugs are made under appropriate production standards. Despite warnings, Ranier's and its owner placed patients at risk by compounding drugs under insanitary conditions. The consent decree prohibits Ranier's from manufacturing, holding, or distributing human or animal sterile drugs compounded at their facility until they comply with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and FDA regulations. On July 10, 2018, the FDA warned the public against using Ranier's products due to concerns about their sterility.

title: Statement from Binita Ashar, M.D., of the FDA’s Center for Devices and Radiological Health on agency’s continuing efforts to educate patients on known risk of lymphoma from breast implants
body_summary: The FDA is updating information on breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL), a known risk of breast implants. As of September 2018, the agency has received 660 medical device reports (MDRs) regarding BIA-ALCL cases since 2010, with 457 unique cases, including 9 patient deaths. The number of MDRs has increased by 246 since last year. The FDA is committed to educating patients and healthcare providers about the benefits and risks of breast implants and is encouraging patients to review their device labeling and file MDRs with the agency. The agency is also participating in the Patient Registry and Outcomes for Breast Implants and Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma Etiology and Epidemiology (PROFILE) and will discuss breast implant safety at its upcoming public meeting.

title: FDA approves first therapy for the treatment of adult patients with a rare blood clotting disorder
body_summary: The US FDA has approved Cablivi injection, the first therapy specifically indicated, for the treatment of adult patients with acquired thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (aTTP). This rare and life-threatening disorder causes blood clotting. The therapy, combined with plasma exchange and immunosuppressive therapy, is a targeted treatment that inhibits the formation of blood clots. The efficacy of Cablivi was studied in a clinical trial involving 145 patients, with improved platelet counts and lower rates of aTTP-related death and recurrence of aTTP. The FDA granted Priority Review designation and Orphan Drug designation to Ablynx, the manufacturer. Common side effects reported were bleeding of the nose or gums and headache.

title: FDA warns patients and doctors about recall of home-use test strips used with device to monitor blood thinner warfarin, not authorized for sale in U.S.
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is warning patients and doctors about certain test strips used with CoaguChek test meter devices to monitor warfarin levels, which may provide inaccurate results and pose serious health risks. Terrific Care/Medex Supply LLC issued a voluntary recall of certain Roche Diagnostics test strip lots due to a Class I recall, the most serious type of recall. This recall is related to the November 2018 Roche Diagnostics Recall, which involved over 1.1 million packages of CoaguChek XS PT Test Strips. The recalled test strips were distributed by Terrific Care/Medex Supply and include catalog numbers not included in the previous Roche recall. The FDA is advising patients and healthcare providers to stop using these test strips and instead rely on alternative methods, such as blood draws from a vein and laboratory tests, to monitor warfarin levels.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the agency’s efforts to enhance the utility of the Orange Book to foster drug competition
body_summary:
The FDA aims to enhance transparency and clarity in the generic drug development process. To achieve this, they will issue new draft guidance on marketing status notifications under Section 506I of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. The guidance provides clarity on the required categories and descriptions of information to be shared with FDA on marketing status for brand and generic drugs.

The FDA will also evaluate therapeutic equivalence and assign therapeutic equivalence codes, which are published in the Orange Book. This guidance aims to increase transparency around the FDA's policies and procedures related to evaluation and assignment of TE codes.

Additionally, the FDA plans to issue draft guidance to assist drug product applicants and approved application holders in using the Orange Book, providing answers to commonly asked questions regarding the Orange Book.

The agency will also solicit public comment on Orange Book use and potential enhancements, including re-examining what pharmaceutical patents should be listed in the Orange Book.

The FDA's goals include enhancing generic competition, reducing regulatory burdens, and providing transparency to enable more informed decisions on resource allocation.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on 2019 efforts to advance the development of complex generics to improve patient access to medicines
body_summary: The FDA is advancing policies to promote generic competition and patient access for complex drugs, which are harder to "genericize" under traditional approaches. Complex drugs, such as inhaled drugs, topical patches, and eye drops, often face no generic competition due to their complex formulation or delivery systems. The agency has advanced new policies to help promote generic competition for these medicines. In 2019, the FDA plans to issue additional guidance documents, address regulatory and scientific challenges, and develop new analytical tools to support approval of complex generic drugs. The goal is to provide scientific and regulatory clarity on complex generic drugs, promoting access to these important therapies and the economic stability of the generic drug industry.

title: FDA approves first generic Advair Diskus
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the first generic version of Advair Diskus, a medication for asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), for twice-daily treatment in patients aged four years and older. Mylan obtained approval to market its generic inhaler in three strengths: 100mcg/50mcg, 250mcg/50mcg, and 500mcg/50mcg. The approval brings more competition to the market, benefiting patients who rely on the drug. The FDA has made efforts to advance the development of generic versions of complex products, including drug-device combination products, with guidance documents and public consultations.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in December indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a solid rate. Job gains have been strong, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Household spending has continued to grow strongly, while growth of business fixed investment has moderated from its rapid pace earlier last year. On a 12-month basis, both overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy remain near 2 percent. Although market-based measures of inflation compensation have moved lower in recent months, survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. In support of these goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent. The Committee continues to view sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective as the most likely outcomes. In light of global economic and financial developments and muted inflation pressures, the Committee will be patient as it determines what future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate may be appropriate to support these outcomes. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were: Jerome H. Powell, Chairman; John C. Williams, Vice Chairman; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; James Bullard; Richard H. Clarida; Charles L. Evans; Esther L. George; Randal K. Quarles; and Eric S. Rosengren.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., and Jeff Shuren, M.D., Director of the Center for Devices and Radiological Health, on a record year for device innovation
body_summary: The FDA is committed to protecting and promoting public health by ensuring medical devices on the US market are high-quality, safe, and effective. The agency's focus on both safety and innovation is key to improving patient safety. In 2018, the FDA issued several statements and reports to inform the public about additional actions the agency was taking to continue modernizing its approach to device safety. The agency has also granted 112 Breakthrough Device Designation requests since 2015, and approved or cleared nine breakthrough devices in 2018. Examples of innovative devices approved in 2018 include an automated insulin dosing system, a smallest heart valve for newborns, and a mobile medical app to treat substance abuse disorders. The FDA plans to implement the National Evaluation System for Health Technology (NEST) in 2019 and establish premarket pathways to foster innovation while prioritizing patient safety. The agency will also consider actions that might require new authority, such as making older devices ineligible as predicates.

title: FDA Statement on the FDA’s ongoing investigation into valsartan and ARB class impurities and the agency’s steps to address the root causes of the safety issues
body_summary: The FDA investigated the presence of nitrosamine impurities, including NDMA and NDEA, in generic angiotensin II receptor blocker medicines manufactured by Zhejiang Huahai Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd. The impurities posed a potential safety concern and led to the facility being placed on import alert, a warning letter being issued, and affected products being recalled. In response, the FDA developed and shared new testing methods to detect and quantify the impurities, and will continue to work with manufacturers to prevent similar incidents. The agency has evaluated safety data to determine acceptable intake levels for NDMA and NDEA, and is working with manufacturers to fix processes and mitigate shortages.

title: FDA statement from Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. announcing efforts to improve the quality of the information used to assess the effectiveness of REMS programs in supporting the safe use of medications
body_summary:
The FDA is announcing the availability of two draft guidances to improve the risk management of certain drugs and biologics. The guidances aim to enhance the effectiveness of risk mitigation programs, which can help ensure that the benefits of these products outweigh their risks. The FDA's primary risk management tool is communicating through FDA-approved product labeling, but in some cases, a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) may be required.

A REMS is a drug safety program designed to reinforce medication use behaviors and actions that support the safe use of a medication. Most REMS include requirements for communication between healthcare providers and patients, as well as limitations on access to the medication until certain conditions are met. The FDA works closely with companies to determine the best way to assess the effectiveness of a REMS and ensure that it is meeting its goals.

The FDA is advancing new guidance on the assessment of REMS programs, which provide a framework for companies to develop a REMS Assessment Plan. This plan should consider how the REMS program goals, objectives, and design may impact the types of metrics and data sources that can be used to assess the program's effectiveness. The draft guidance recommends incorporating process indicators and outcome measures in the REMS Assessment Plan.

Additionally, the FDA is issuing a second draft guidance on conducting REMS assessment surveys to evaluate patient or healthcare provider knowledge of REMS-related information. The draft guidance discusses general principles and recommendations related to conducting REMS assessment knowledge surveys, including study design, survey data collection and processing, and data analysis.

The FDA will continue to update the public on its work, including its approach to reviewing existing medical product applications and associated policy development. The goal is to ensure that REMS are achieving their public health goals and are designed and

title: FDA permits marketing of first test to aid in the diagnosis of a sexually-transmitted infection known as Mycoplasma genitalium
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has permitted the marketing of a new test to aid in the diagnosis of Mycoplasma genitalium (M. gen.), a sexually-transmitted infection. M. gen. is associated with inflammation of the urethra and cervix, and is difficult to detect with traditional laboratory methods. The Aptima Mycoplasma genitalium Assay, a nucleic acid amplification test, has been granted marketing authorization by the FDA. The test, developed by Hologic Inc., detects M. gen. in urine, urethral, penile meatal, endocervical or vaginal swab samples. According to the FDA, the test correctly identified M. gen. in approximately 90% of vaginal, male urethral, and male urine samples, and in 77.8% and 81.5% of female urine and endocervical samples, respectively. The FDA reviewed data from a clinical study involving 11,774 samples, and established special controls to ensure the accuracy and reliability of tests of this type.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. and Jeff Shuren, M.D., Director of the Center for Devices and Radiological Health, on latest steps to strengthen FDA’s 510(k) program for premarket review of medical devices
body_summary: The FDA has announced two developments to advance its policy effort on the 510(k) program. The agency has posted final guidance establishing the framework for the Safety and Performance Based Pathway, which aims to modernize the approach to moderate risk devices by allowing manufacturers to use objective performance criteria. The pathway will benchmark modern technology against modern standards, potentially driving greater market competition to develop safer devices. The FDA is also soliciting public comment on steps to encourage medical device manufacturers to develop innovations that enhance the safety of 510(k) devices, including the potential to post a list of FDA-cleared devices that demonstrated substantial equivalence to older predicate devices.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on unprecedented new efforts to support development of over-the-counter naloxone to help reduce opioid overdose deaths
body_summary: The FDA has developed model labeling for over-the-counter (OTC) naloxone products, making it easier for consumers to understand how to use the drug in emergency situations. The model labeling is designed to be consumer-friendly and contains the key information needed for an untrained bystander to administer naloxone. The FDA conducted label comprehension testing, which showed that consumers can understand the model labeling. The FDA will now provide a model labeling for sponsors to use in their OTC naloxone product applications, making it easier for companies to develop OTC naloxone products. This move aims to increase access to naloxone and help combat the opioid crisis.

title: FDA approves first generic version of Sabril to help treat seizures in adults and pediatric patients with epilepsy
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the first generic version of Sabril (vigabatrin) 500 mg tablets for treating complex partial seizures in patients 10 years and older who have responded inadequately to several alternative treatments. The approval is part of the FDA's efforts to support access and reduce drug costs, particularly for critically important medicines. The generic version, approved by Teva Pharmaceuticals USA, will be available to patients as an adjunctive therapy to other primary treatments. The FDA emphasizes the importance of ensuring generic drugs meet rigorous approval standards to guarantee quality products. Vigabatrin tablets carry a boxed warning for permanent vision loss, and the FDA requires manufacturers to develop a shared-system Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program to ensure safe use.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. and Peter Marks, M.D., Ph.D., Director of the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research on new policies to advance development of safe and effective cell and gene therapies
body_summary: The FDA expects to see a surge in cell and gene therapy products entering early development, with over 200 INDs expected by 2020. By 2025, the agency predicts approving 10-20 cell and gene therapy products per year. In 2019, the FDA plans to introduce new policy guidance and an advanced drug development framework to support the growing field. Key areas of focus include expedited review programs, clinical guidance documents, and regulations for manufacturing and delivery of cell-based therapies. The agency also plans to address cell therapy safety and enforcement issues, including enforcement actions in 2019 for products posing significant safety risks to patients. The FDA intends to issue guidance on a proposed innovative trial design to facilitate individual researchers pooling clinical data.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on December 18-19, 2018, focusing on potential long-run frameworks for monetary policy implementation. The committee reviewed options to maintain control of interest rates during the transition to a long-run operating regime and discussed reducing reserves to promote efficient implementation of monetary policy. Labor market conditions strengthened, and real GDP growth was strong, with consumer price inflation at 2% in October. The FOMC ratified the Desk's domestic transactions over the intermeeting period and raised the target range for the federal funds rate to 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent, emphasizing a data-dependent approach to future policy decisions.

title: FDA approves first treatment for rare blood disease
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Elzonris (tagraxofusp-erzt) infusion for the treatment of blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) in adults and pediatric patients aged two years and older. This is the first FDA-approved therapy for BPDCN, which is an aggressive and rare disease affecting the bone marrow and blood. The efficacy of Elzonris was studied in two clinical trials, with 28 patients showing an overall response. Common side effects include capillary leak syndrome, nausea, and fatigue. The FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy and Priority Review designation, as well as Orphan Drug designation, to Stemline Therapeutics, the company developing Elzonris. The labeling contains a Boxed Warning for capillary leak syndrome, which can be life-threatening or fatal.

title: FDA approves first treatment for rare blood disease
body_summary: The US FDA approved Elzonris (tagraxofusp-erz) infusion for treating blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) in adults and pediatric patients aged 2 years and older. There was no FDA-approved therapy for BPDCN prior to this approval. The disease is more common in men over 60 years old. The efficacy of Elzonris was studied in two single-arm clinical trials, with 13 patients achieving complete remission and 15 patients achieving a partial response. Common side effects included capillary leak syndrome, nausea, and fever. The FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy and Priority Review designations, as well as Orphan Drug designation. Approval was granted to Stemline Therapeutics.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on signing of the Agriculture Improvement Act and the agency’s regulation of products containing cannabis and cannabis-derived compounds
body_summary: The Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018 was signed into law, removing hemp from the Controlled Substances Act and making it no longer an illegal substance under federal law. The FDA's authority to regulate cannabis and cannabis-derived compounds under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act is preserved. The FDA plans to hold a public meeting to gather input on the lawful marketing of hemp products containing cannabis or cannabis-derived compounds, aiming to create a more predictable and efficient regulatory framework.

title: FDA sends warning to company for marketing dangerous unapproved stem cell products that put patients at risk and puts other stem cell firms, providers on notice
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has warned Genetech, Inc. of San Diego, California, and its president Edwin N. Pinos for marketing unapproved stem cell products without FDA approval and violating current good tissue practice and good manufacturing practice requirements. Genetech processed umbilical cord blood into unapproved human cellular products, which were distributed by Liveyon, LLC. The FDA found significant deviations from current good tissue practice and good manufacturing practice requirements, including deficient donor eligibility practices, unvalidated manufacturing processes, and a lack of control over components used in production. This may have led to microbial contamination, potentially causing serious blood infections in patients. The FDA is sending letters to other manufacturers and healthcare providers to reiterate its compliance and enforcement policy.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new steps to strengthen the long-term safety oversight of the Essure device following discontinuation of its U.S. sales
body_summary: The FDA has extended the post-market surveillance study of the Essure permanent birth control device from three to five years, requiring additional blood tests and more frequent reports on its safety and effectiveness. The agency is reviewing medical literature, clinical trial data, and medical device reports to improve its monitoring systems. This includes the implementation of an active surveillance system to detect device safety signals faster. The FDA plans to use the HT-CRN to gather evidence and detect safety issues with medical devices, prioritizing patients' health and informing the public of new risks.

title: FDA warns about safety risks of teething necklaces, bracelets to relieve teething pain or to provide sensory stimulation
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has warned parents, caregivers, and healthcare providers about the safety risks associated with jewelry used to relieve teething pain in children. The agency has received reports of death and serious injuries, including strangulation and choking, caused by teething jewelry such as amber teething necklaces.

The FDA has advised against using teething jewelry, citing risks including choking, strangulation, and injury to the mouth and infection. The agency has also warned against using teething creams, benzocaine products, and other local anesthetics for mouth and gum pain, as they can cause serious conditions like methemoglobinemia.

The FDA has issued a safety communication and encourages consumers to report any injuries or adverse events related to teething jewelry. Parents are advised to consider alternative ways of treating teething pain, such as rubbing inflamed gums with a clean finger or using a teething ring made of firm rubber.

The agency has received reports of two recent incidents, one involving a 7-month-old child who choked on a wooden teething bracelet and another involving an 18-month-old child who was strangled to death by an amber teething necklace.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in November indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a strong rate. Job gains have been strong, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low. Household spending has continued to grow strongly, while growth of business fixed investment has moderated from its rapid pace earlier in the year. On a 12-month basis, both overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy remain near 2 percent. Indicators of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. The Committee judges that some further gradual increases in the target range for the federal funds rate will be consistent with sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective over the medium term. The Committee judges that risks to the economic outlook are roughly balanced, but will continue to monitor global economic and financial developments and assess their implications for the economic outlook. In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 2-1/4 to 2â1/2 percent. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were: Jerome H. Powell, Chairman; John C. Williams, Vice Chairman; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Mary C. Daly; Loretta J. Mester; and Randal K. Quarles.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., and Jeff Shuren, M.D., Director of the Center for Devices and Radiological Health, on new steps to promote innovations in medical devices that help advance patient safety
body_summary: The FDA is taking steps to enhance medical device safety and innovation. The agency has finalized guidance on its Breakthrough Devices Program, which aims to encourage the development of innovative devices that improve patient outcomes. The FDA also announced plans for a new Safer Technologies Program (STeP), which will support the development of devices with significant safety advantages. STeP will provide an additional pathway for device manufacturers to bring innovative safety advancements to market. The FDA plans to apply principles and features of the Breakthrough Devices Program to devices with potential for significant safety improvements, regardless of their intended use.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. on the FDA’s 2017 report on declining sales/distribution of antimicrobial drugs for food animals, a reflection of improved antimicrobial stewardship
body_summary: The FDA reports a 33% decline in domestic sales and distribution of medically important antimicrobials intended for use in food-producing animals between 2016 and 2017. This decline is part of the FDA's efforts to support antimicrobial stewardship in animals. The 2017 Summary Report on Antimicrobials Sold or Distributed for Use in Food-Producing Animals highlights a 43% decline since 2015 and a 28% decline since 2009. The decline is attributed to the implementation of the FDA's Guidance for Industry (GFI) #213, which recommended eliminating production uses of medically important antimicrobials in animal feed and drinking water. The FDA's Center for Veterinary Medicine (CVM) and industry partners have made significant strides in addressing antimicrobial resistance in animals. The FDA has a five-year action plan to combat antimicrobial resistance and preserve the effectiveness of antimicrobial drugs.

title: Michigan-based food manufacturer agrees to stop operations after repeated food safety violations
body_summary: A federal court ordered Saranac Brand Foods to discontinue selling food products until the company complies with federal regulations. The order follows inspections by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and Michigan Department of Agriculture and Rural Development, which found Listeria monocytogenes in the company's food preparation area. U.S. District Judge Paul L. Maloney entered a consent decree of permanent injunction on November 30, 2018, between the U.S. and Saranac Brand Foods, and its co-owners, Dennis M. Nowak and Daniel R. Nowak. The consent decree prohibits the defendants from receiving, preparing, processing, packing, holding, labeling, and/or distributing foods at or from their facility until certain requirements are met. The FDA has documented a pattern of food safety violations at the facility, which has put consumers in harm's way. The FDA issued a Warning Letter to the company in August 2016, and followed up with a list of inspectional observations in November 2017.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. and Director of FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research Janet Woodcock, M.D., on efforts to modernize generic drug labels while maintaining the efficiency of generic development
body_summary: The FDA is revising labeling for brand and generic drugs to ensure consistency and provide up-to-date safety and efficacy information. This effort aims to improve access to accurate information for healthcare providers and patients. The FDA will update labels on certain generic cancer drugs, working with brand companies to ensure timely updates. The agency is balancing the need for efficient and low-cost generic drug development with the need to provide prescribers and patients with the most up-to-date information to guide treatment decisions.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. and FDA Deputy Commissioner Frank Yiannas on new findings and updated consumer recommendations related to the romaine lettuce E. coli O157:H7 outbreak investigation
body_summary: The US FDA and CDC warned of a multi-state E. coli O157:H7 outbreak linked to romaine lettuce on Nov. 20, advising against eating romaine lettuce. The FDA worked with romaine producers and distributors to withdraw the product from the market and launched a traceback investigation, identifying a specific farm as the source of contamination. As of Dec. 13, the investigation identified 11 different distributors, nine different growers, and eight different farms as potential sources of contaminated romaine lettuce. The outbreak resulted in 59 people becoming ill in 15 states. The FDA now allows consumers to safely eat romaine lettuce from certain counties in California, provided it was harvested after Nov. 23. To improve tracing, the FDA will begin labeling romaine lettuce with its harvest origin and date, and will launch a comprehensive tracing effort in early 2019 to track and trace products through the supply chain.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the agency’s efforts to improve drug quality through vigilant oversight of data integrity and good manufacturing practice
body_summary: The FDA is updating its guidance on ensuring data integrity in pharmaceutical manufacturing to protect patient safety and prevent drug shortages of critical medicines. The goal is to maintain clear guidelines for companies to prevent product quality issues and address inadequate processes and systems. The FDA has focused on preventing, uncovering, and combating data integrity lapses, and is now updating its guidance to provide industry with clear guidance on ensuring data integrity and compliance with current good manufacturing practice (CGMP). The new guidance aims to help manufacturers create a quality culture where employees understand the seriousness of data integrity and promote data integrity as a core value. The FDA will use inspections, pre-approval inspections, and assessments of applications to ensure data integrity, and is expanding its partnerships with international regulatory counterparts to advance best practices on data security.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new actions advancing the agency’s biosimilars policy framework
body_summary: The FDA aims to balance innovation and access by promoting competition in the pharmaceutical market. The agency sets record-breaking numbers of generic approvals and encourages biosimilar products to lower costs and increase access to new medical breakthroughs. To address challenges, the FDA has improved its biosimilar approval process and will issue new guidance documents to clarify scientific and regulatory considerations. The agency is also transitioning certain biological products from the drug pathway to the biologics pathway, including insulin, to promote competition and reduce costs. This move aims to bring affordable insulin access to millions of Americans affected by diabetes, where annual healthcare spending is $330 billion and diabetes deaths could soon surpass the third leading cause of death. The FDA plans to introduce a new pathway to market for biosimilar insulins, potentially leading to lower prices and better access.

title: FDA warns API manufacturer involved in valsartan recall, provides information for patients taking these medications
body_summary: The FDA has issued a warning letter to Zhejiang Huahai Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd., a manufacturer of valsartan, a heart medication, due to manufacturing violations at its Chuannan facility. The facility has been linked to impurities found in valsartan and other products in the angiotensin II receptor blocker class. The FDA has also put the facility on import alert, stopping all API made there and finished drug products from entering the US. The agency has announced recalls of valsartan and other products containing NDMA and NDEA, both known animal and suspected human carcinogens. The FDA Commissioner, Scott Gottlieb, has stated that the investigation is ongoing and the agency is taking action to protect patient health and safety.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. and Deputy Commissioner Anna Abram on new efforts to assure the quality of compounded drugs
body_summary: The FDA is updating its policies related to outsourcing facilities, which are compounding pharmacies that can provide hospitals, physicians' offices, and other healthcare facilities with supplies of compounded drugs for "office stock" without receiving patient-specific prescriptions. The goal is to make it more feasible for compounding pharmacies to become outsourcing facilities while maintaining patient safety. The FDA is concerned that some compounding pharmacies that are not registered as outsourcing facilities continue to engage in activities that put patient safety at risk. To address this, the FDA is releasing a revised draft guidance that outlines practices for drugs produced under current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) requirements by outsourcing facilities. The guidance aims to provide clarity on quality assurance, maintaining suitable facilities, sterility, stability testing, and beyond-use dates for products that do not go through the FDA drug approval process. The FDA will also hold a public meeting in May to solicit comments on the draft guidance revisions and will take action against facilities with deficient practices to stop issues before they lead to patient harm.

title: FDA clears mobile medical app to help those with opioid use disorder stay in recovery programs
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared a mobile medical application called reSET-O to help increase retention in outpatient treatment programs for individuals with opioid use disorder (OUD). The app is a prescription cognitive behavioral therapy intended to be used in addition to outpatient treatment under the care of a health care professional. The FDA reviewed a 12-week clinical trial of 170 patients, which showed a statistically significant increase in retention for patients who used the desktop version of the reSET-O program compared to those who did not. The app was developed by Pear Therapeutics and cleared through the premarket notification (510(k)) pathway. The FDA granted clearance of the reSET-O device, which is intended to be used while participating in an outpatient OUD treatment program.

title: Statement from Jeff Shuren, M.D., J.D., Director of the Center for Devices and Radiological Health, on updated safety communication about rates of duodenoscope contamination from preliminary postmarket data
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is committed to advancing medical device safety, particularly for duodenoscopes, which are used for minimally invasive procedures to diagnose and treat problems in the pancreas and bile duct. The FDA has ordered device manufacturers Olympus, Fujifilm, and Pentax to conduct postmarket surveillance studies to determine if healthcare facilities can properly clean and disinfect the devices. Preliminary results from these studies indicate higher-than-expected contamination rates, with up to 3% of properly collected samples testing positive for more than 100 colony forming units of low concern organisms. The FDA is issuing safety communication recommendations to hospitals and healthcare providers to enhance duodenoscope reprocessing, including following manufacturer instructions, implementing supplemental reprocessing measures, and carefully inspecting the elevator recess. The FDA is also encouraging manufacturers to develop new product designs, including disposable components, to reduce the risk of contamination. The agency is working to reduce patient exposure to infections in healthcare settings and is committed to protecting patient safety.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the FDA’s new effort for developing and class labeling of in vitro companion diagnostics for classes of oncology therapeutic products
body_summary: The FDA has issued a new draft guidance to make it easier for providers to use the same diagnostic test to guide the use of a class of oncology therapeutic products, rather than one specific oncology therapeutic product. The guidance aims to promote better patient care and address the challenge of narrow labeling that ties a drug to a specific diagnostic test. The policy reflects that in some cases, if evidence is sufficient, the companion diagnostic's intended use should name the specific group or class of therapeutic products, rather than specific products. The guidance will help test developers to extrapolate the use of an approved or cleared diagnostic test to the entire oncology therapeutic product class. The FDA aims to advance patient care and recognition that companion diagnostics inform both the development and approved use of therapeutic products.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA’s new strategic framework to advance use of real-world evidence to support development of drugs and biologics
body_summary: The FDA is announcing a new 2019 strategic Framework to advance the use of real-world data (RWD) and real-world evidence (RWE) in regulatory decisions. The Framework aims to leverage RWD and RWE to improve regulatory decisions, particularly in post-market safety evaluation, and includes initiatives to incorporate RWE into drug and biologic review programs. The goal is to provide information that can better inform regulatory decisions, particularly in areas where existing electronic health records (EHRs) and medical claims data may not capture all necessary data elements. The framework will explore strategies for filling gaps in data collection, including the use of mobile technologies, electronic patient reported outcome tools, and wearables, while ensuring patient privacy.

title: FDA takes new action to advance the development of reliable and beneficial genetic tests that can improve patient care
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has recognized the Clinical Genome Resource (ClinGen) consortium's ClinGen Expert Curated Human Genetic Data as a source of valid scientific evidence for supporting clinical validity in premarket submissions. This recognition facilitates test developers to rely on the information available in the database to support the validity of their tests. The ClinGen database contains information about genes, genetic variants, and their relationship to disease. The FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb stated that the recognition will advance the development of novel technologies that provide critical, potentially life-saving information. The database has been collected and studied by researchers worldwide.

title: FDA and DoD formalize collaboration to advance medical products in support of American military personnel
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration and the Department of Defense's Office of Health Affairs signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) regarding medical product development and assessment. The MOU builds upon the work of both agencies to prioritize the efficient development of safe and effective medical products for American service members.

The MOU formalizes the framework under which the DoD and FDA will implement the 2017 law for enhanced engagement between the two agencies. The FDA will work closely with the DoD to evaluate medical product access, expedite review of priority products, and provide technical advice for rapid development and manufacturing.

The 2017 law expanded the FDA's authority to authorize emergency uses of medical products to reduce deaths and severity of injuries caused by CBRN agents. The MOU furthers the partnership between the DoD and FDA to equip military personnel with innovative medical support.

The FDA has already been working closely with the DoD to expedite availability of medical products, particularly those used to treat injuries in battlefield settings. Examples include the Emergency Use Authorization for French freeze-dried plasma issued earlier this year.

The MOU sets forth a framework to implement the 2017 law, including provisions to expedite the development of medical products and streamline review. The FDA and DoD are committed to ongoing partnership and confidence that the MOU will enhance their efforts to serve the health care needs of American military personnel.

title: FDA authorizes first test to aid in detecting a type of herpes virus in newborns called cytomegalovirus
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has permitted the marketing of a new diagnostic test to aid in detecting cytomegalovirus (CMV) in newborns less than 21 days of age. The test, Alethia CMV Assay Test System, uses a saliva swab to detect CMV DNA and may help healthcare providers quickly identify the virus in newborns. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, more than half of adults by age 40 have been infected with CMV. The FDA evaluated the analytical and clinical performance of the device, showing that 99% of samples were correctly identified as negative, and 5 out of 34 archived specimens were correctly identified as positive. The FDA granted marketing authorization to Meridian Bioscience, Inc., and established special controls to ensure the accuracy and effectiveness of the test.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: A joint meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee and the Board of Governors was held on November 7-8, 2018, discussing long-run monetary policy implementation frameworks. The committee discussed alternative policy rates, including targeting overnight unsecured rates or secured funding rates. Some participants saw advantages in a regime of abundant excess reserves, which could provide good control of short-term money market rates. Foreign economic growth picked up in Q3, with Mexico's economy growing briskly and China's GDP growth slowing down. The Federal Reserve staff forecasted moderate stability for the US economy, with real GDP growth projected to slow down in 2021 after rising above potential growth from 2018-2020. The committee maintained the target range for the federal funds rate at 2-2.25% due to balanced risks to the economic outlook.

title: FDA warns company for selling e-liquids that resemble kid-friendly foods as part of the agency’s ongoing Youth Tobacco Prevention Plan
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued a warning letter to Electric Lotus LLC for selling nicotine-containing e-liquids in packaging resembling kid-friendly food products, such as cereal and candy. The company was also cited for illegally selling products to a minor, failing to list its products with the FDA, and selling e-liquids without required FDA premarket authorization. The warning letter follows actions taken by the FDA against 17 other makers and sellers of similar e-liquids. FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb warned that such marketing can lead to accidental ingestion of potentially lethal doses of nicotine by young kids. The products in the warning letter include "Cereal Treats" products that resemble popular cereal brands, and the FDA has requested that Electric Lotus respond within 15 working days to describe how it intends to address the agency's concerns.

title: FDA approves first biosimilar for treatment of adult patients with non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Truxima (rituximab-abbs) as the first biosimilar to Rituxan (rituximab) for treating adult patients with CD20-positive, B-cell non-Hodgkin's lymphoma. This approval is part of the FDA's Biosimilars Action Plan to advance policies and enable more opportunities for biosimilar manufacturers to make these products commercially successful.

Truxima is indicated for treating relapsed or refractory, low-grade, and CD20-positive B-cell NHL as a single agent, and for previously untreated follicular, CD20-positive, B-cell NHL in combination with first-line chemotherapy.

The FDA's approval of Truxima is based on data showing it is highly similar to Rituxan, with no clinically meaningful differences in terms of safety, purity, and potency. Truxima has been approved as a biosimilar, not as an interchangeable product, and has a boxed warning for potential side effects.
