The FDA granted approval of Truxima to Celltrion, and this approval brings the total number of approved biosimilars to 15. The FDA has also approved several other biosimilars, including Hyrimoz and Udenyca, in recent years.

title: FDA approves treatment for adult patients who have relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with a certain genetic mutation
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Xospata (gilteritinib) tablets for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who have a FLT3 mutation. The FDA also approved a companion diagnostic test, the LeukoStrat CDx FLT3 Mutation Assay, developed by Invivoscribe Technologies, Inc. Xospata targets the FLT3 gene and is the first drug to be approved for treating patients with AML having a FLT3 mutation who have relapsed or who don't respond to initial treatment. The efficiency of Xospata was studied in a clinical trial of 138 patients, where 21% achieved complete remission. Common side effects reported were muscle and joint pain, fatigue, and elevated liver enzymes. The FDA granted Fast Track and Priority Review designation and Orphan Drug designation to Astellas Pharma, the agency responsible for protecting the public health by assuring the safety and effectiveness of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and medical devices.

title: FDA approves first treatment for Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome, a rare autoimmune disorder
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Firdapse tablets for the treatment of Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (LEMS) in adults, marking the first FDA approval for a treatment of this rare autoimmune disorder. LEMS causes weakness and other symptoms due to the body's immune system attacking the connection between nerves and muscles. The approval was based on clinical trials that showed Firdapse to be more effective than placebo in patients with LEMS. The most common side effects were paresthesia, upper respiratory tract infections, and other gastrointestinal issues. The FDA granted Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy designations, as well as Orphan Drug designation, to Catalyst Pharmaceuticals, Inc. The approval was granted to the FDA agency responsible for protecting the public health and ensuring the safety and security of human and veterinary drugs.

title: FDA warns consumers to avoid Rhino male enhancement products found at retailers because of undeclared and potentially dangerous drug ingredients
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is warning consumers not to purchase or use Rhino male enhancement products due to a recent rise in reported health issues. Since 2007, the FDA has identified over 25 products marketed with variations of the name "Rhino" that contained hidden drug ingredients. These products, including Platinum Rhino 25000, Krazzy Rhino 25000, and Gold Rhino 25000, have been sold at gas stations, convenience stores, and online platforms like eBay and Amazon. Reports of people experiencing chest pain, severe headaches, and prolonged erections have led to surgical intervention and hospitalization due to extreme drops in blood pressure. The FDA has received reports of people experiencing adverse effects after taking these products. The agency is investigating a South Korean national for smuggling raw materials, producing Rhino capsules, and distributing the misbranded drug products throughout the US. The FDA has posted warnings that these products contain undeclared ingredients similar to active ingredients in FDA-approved prescription drugs.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on risk of heavy metals, including nickel and lead, found in some kratom products
body_summary: The FDA has issued warnings about the serious risks associated with the use of kratom, including novel risks due to contamination, salmonella, and heavy metals. The agency has found disturbingly high levels of heavy metals, including lead and nickel, in 26 tested kratom products. These levels are not considered safe for human consumption and may cause heavy metal poisoning with chronic use. The FDA is contacting companies marketing kratom products to make them aware of the results and issuing an advisory to warn consumers about the risks. Kratom is not legally marketed in the US as a drug or dietary supplement, and its use can be associated with opioid properties and abuse. The FDA encourages individuals seeking treatment for opioid use disorder to seek help from a healthcare provider instead of kratom.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on how modern predicates can promote innovation and advance safety and effectiveness of medical devices that use 510(k) pathway
body_summary: The FDA announced new steps to modernize its 510(k) clearance pathway for low- to moderate-risk devices substantially equivalent to existing devices. The changes aim to push for the use of more modern predicate devices, reflecting the latest advances in technology. The FDA plans to make public information about cleared devices using outdated predicates, focusing on those older than 10 years. The agency will seek public feedback and evaluate the benefits of relying on newer predicates in device submissions. The goal is to promote innovation, improve device safety and performance, and enhance global standards for medical device safety and effectiveness.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. and Jeff Shuren, M.D., Director of the Center for Devices and Radiological Health, on transformative new steps to modernize FDA’s 510(k) program to advance the review of the safety and effectiveness of medical devices
body_summary: The FDA is modernizing the 510(k) clearance pathway for medical devices to keep pace with rapidly evolving technology. The goal is to efficiently advance beneficial devices while solidifying safety standards. The agency aims to update the framework to reflect advances in technology, safety, and capabilities of new medical devices. To drive innovation, the FDA plans to make outdated predicates publicly available, promoting the use of modern devices with the latest improvements and advances. The agency also plans to finalize guidance on an alternative 510(k) pathway for devices meeting objective safety and performance criteria. This approach aims to improve safety, promote competition, and enhance patient care. The FDA plans to enhance post-market surveillance and ensure consistent action on safety signals. The current regulatory process is challenging due to its time-consuming nature.

title: FDA approves an oncology drug that targets a key genetic driver of cancer, rather than a specific type of tumor
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted accelerated approval to Vitrakvi (larotrectinib), a treatment for adult and pediatric patients with solid tumors that have a neurotrophic receptor tyrosine kinase (NTRK) gene fusion. This is the second time the agency has approved a cancer treatment based on a common biomarker. The approval marks a new paradigm in cancer drug development that is "tissue agnostic." Vitrakvi was studied in three clinical trials that included 55 patients with metastatic or unresectable tumors and no satisfactory alternative treatments. It demonstrated a 75% overall response rate, with responses lasting at least six months in 73% of patients. The FDA granted accelerated approval, Priority Review, and Breakthrough Therapy designation. Vitrakvi received Orphan Drug designation, and its approval was granted to Loxo Oncology.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the current romaine lettuce E. coli O157:H7 outbreak investigation
body_summary:
The FDA, CDC, and state authorities continue to investigate a multistate outbreak of E. coli O157:H7 infections linked to romaine lettuce in the US. As of Nov. 26, 2018, 43 people were ill in 12 states, with the last reported illness onset date being Oct. 31, 2018. An additional 22 people in Canada became ill. The FDA announced new steps to help consumers identify where their romaine is grown through voluntary labeling. 

On Nov. 20, 2018, the CDC advised the public not to consume romaine lettuce and to destroy any romaine lettuce in their homes. The FDA requested that all romaine lettuce on the market be withdrawn and destroyed. 

The investigation suggests that romaine lettuce associated with the outbreak comes from areas of California that grow romaine lettuce over the summer months, specifically the Central Coast growing regions of central and northern California. The FDA is continuing tracebacks of romaine lettuce to identify specific locations that are the likely source of the outbreak. 

The E. coli O157:H7 strain causing the outbreak is similar to one that produced an outbreak in the fall of 2017. The FDA believes that a "clean break" in the romaine supply was critical in removing potentially contaminated product from the market. 

The FDA has issued updated advice, recommending that romaine lettuce entering the market be labeled with a harvest location and a harvest date. If consumers cannot identify the romaine lettuce products are not affected, they should not eat or use them. The FDA also recommends that retailers and food service facilities not purchase romaine lettuce if they cannot identify it as not being from the implicated California regions.

title: FDA approves new treatment for patients with acute myeloid leukemia
body_summary: The US FDA has approved Daurismo (glasdegib) tablets for the treatment of newly-diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) in adults 75 years or older, or those with chronic health conditions. Clinical trials showed improved overall survival with Daurismo in combination with low-dose cytarabine compared to LDAC alone. The efficacy of Daurismo was studied in a randomized clinical trial involving 111 adult patients. Results demonstrated a significant improvement in overall survival, with a median of 8.3 months for patients treated with Daurismo plus LDAC, compared to 4.3 months for patients treated with LDAC alone. Common side effects include anemia, fatigue, and bleeding. Daurismo carries a Boxed Warning for embryo-fetal death or severe birth defects, and its use is advised against during pregnancy or breastfeeding.

title: FDA warns marketers of products labeled as dietary supplements that contain tianeptine for making unproven claims to treat serious conditions, including opioid use disorder
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued warning letters to two companies, Jack B Goods Outlet Store and MA Labs, for illegally marketing products labeled as dietary supplements that contain tianeptine, a chemical compound claimed to treat opioid use disorder, pain, and anxiety. The FDA has received reports of serious adverse events associated with tianeptine and has warned against the sale of products with unsubstantiated claims. Tianeptine is an unsafe food additive and should not be present in dietary supplements, and the FDA has not approved it for any use. The companies have been accused of preying on vulnerable patients and selling products with known safety issues. The FDA has requested responses from the companies within 15 working days and warns of potential legal action, including seizure and injunction, if violations are not corrected.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. and Jeff Shuren, M.D., Director of the Center for Devices and Radiological Health, on FDA’s updates to Medical Device Safety Action Plan to enhance post-market safety
body_summary: The FDA has released a Medical Device Safety Action Plan to enhance device safety and announce new initiatives. The agency aims to be the first to identify and act on medical device safety signals, focusing on better data and real-world evidence. The FDA will allocate $3 million to the NESTcc to support demonstration projects for building out active surveillance capabilities. The agency has initiated pilot studies for the National Evaluation System for health Technology (NEST) and a women's health coordinated registry network. The FDA regulates over 190,000 devices, approving 12 new or modified devices daily, and will convene an advisory committee meeting to discuss the safety and effectiveness of surgical mesh for transvaginal pelvic organ prolapse repair.

title: FDA approves first treatment specifically for patients with rare and life-threatening type of immune disease
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Gamifant (emapalumab-lzsg) for treating pediatric and adult patients with primary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) who have refractory, recurrent, or progressive disease or intolerance with conventional HLH therapy. This is the first FDA approval for a drug specifically for HLH. The approval is due to the efficacy of Gamifant in a clinical trial of 27 pediatric patients, with 63% experiencing a response and 70% able to proceed to stem cell transplant. Common side effects include infections, hypertension, and fever. The FDA granted Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy designation, as well as Orphan Drug designation, to Novimmune SA.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on a new qualified health claim for consuming oils with high levels of oleic acid to reduce coronary heart disease risk
body_summary: The FDA has approved a new qualified health claim for edible oils containing high levels of oleic acid, a monounsaturated fat that may reduce the risk of coronary heart disease. The claim states that consuming 1.5 tablespoons (20 grams) of these oils daily may reduce risk, but notes that they should replace higher saturated fat oils and not increase calorie intake. Edible oils meeting this criteria include high oleic sunflower oil, high oleic safflower oil, and high oleic canola oil. The FDA evaluated seven small clinical studies, finding six modest improvements in cholesterol levels when replacing saturated fats with oleic acid-containing oils. The agency's goal is to encourage industry to reformulate products using these oils.

title: FDA approves new drug to treat travelers’ diarrhea
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Aemcolo, an antibacterial drug, for the treatment of adult patients with travelers' diarrhea caused by noninvasive strains of Escherichia coli (E. coli), not complicated by fever or blood in the stool. The approval was based on a randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial in 264 adults with travelers' diarrhea in Guatemala and Mexico, which showed that Aemcolo significantly reduced symptoms. The safety of Aemcolo was evaluated in two controlled clinical trials involving 619 adults, with the most common adverse reactions being headache and constipation. Aemcolo is not recommended for use in patients with diarrhea complicated by fever and/or bloody stool or diarrhea due to pathogens other than noninvasive strains of E. coli. The FDA granted Aemcolo a Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation, which allows for expedited review and approval. The approval was granted to Cosmo Technologies, Ltd.

title: Statement from USDA Secretary Perdue and FDA Commissioner Gottlieb on the regulation of cell-cultured food products from cell lines of livestock and poultry
body_summary: The US Department of Agriculture and the US Food and Drug Administration have agreed to jointly oversee the production of cell-cultured food products derived from livestock and poultry. After a public meeting, the agencies have concluded that FDA will oversee cell collection, cell banks, and cell growth and differentiation, while USDA will oversee the production and labeling of food products. A transition from FDA to USDA oversight will occur during the cell harvest stage. The Agencies are refining the technical details of the framework, leveraging both agencies' expertise, and are confident that the regulatory framework can be successfully implemented and ensure the safety of these products.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the FDA’s efforts to hold industry accountable for fulfilling critical post-marketing studies of the benefits, safety of new drugs
body_summary: The FDA continues to require premarket clinical trials for approved drugs to ensure safety and effectiveness. The agency conducts post-marketing studies to enhance patient safety and public health. To facilitate real-world data collection, the FDA has developed tools such as the MyStudies app. The agency is modernizing its post-market process, utilizing new tools and techniques to efficiently conduct post-approval studies. The FDA aims to provide robust evidence for medical care, aiming to close the backlog of post-marketing requirements. The agency emphasizes the importance of post-marketing studies for regulatory responsibility, utilizing real-world data and trials at patient care sites. The FDA remains committed to protecting public health by regulating various products, including human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and food, through the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.

title: FDA approves first-line treatment for peripheral T-cell lymphoma under new review pilot
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the use of Adcetris (brentuximab vedotin) injection in combination with chemotherapy for adult patients with certain types of peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL). This is the first FDA approval for treatment of newly diagnosed PTCL. The approval was based on a clinical trial of 452 patients who received either Adcetris plus chemotherapy or standard chemotherapy as first-line treatment. The FDA used the Real-Time Oncology Review program to complete the approval more quickly. Adcetris is a monoclonal antibody that binds to a protein found on some cancer cells, and it is now approved to treat previously untreated systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma and other CD30-expressing PTCLs. The new approval was granted to Seattle Genetics. The FDA also granted this application Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy designation.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on efforts to reduce animal testing through a study aimed at eliminating the use of dogs in certain trials
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is proposing a study to help animal drug developers conduct certain types of research without using dogs. The aim is to reduce or eliminate the need for dogs in future trials by establishing a non-animal based model. The proposed study would involve a small number of dogs, with minimal invasive blood sampling, and would be adopted as pets at the end of the trial. The study would compare the bioequivalence of tablets containing locally and systemically acting antiparasitic drugs in dogs. The goal is to develop informatics tools that can model the absorption of drugs in the future, without requiring live dog testing. The study would be part of the FDA's efforts to reduce reliance on animals used for research and would be open for public comment for 60 days.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on proposed new steps to protect youth by preventing access to flavored tobacco products and banning menthol in cigarettes
body_summary: The FDA Commissioner is announcing proposals to address the epidemic of youth nicotine use in e-cigarettes, with a 78% increase in e-cigarette use among high school students and a 48% increase among middle school students between 2017 and 2018. The FDA aims to strike a balance between enabling adults to transition to non-combustible products and preventing nicotine products from becoming less accessible and appealing to children. The proposed policy framework includes: banning flavors in cigars to help prevent youth initiation, curtailed sales of flavored e-cigarette products sold online without age verification, and removing flavored e-cigarette products marketed to children from the market. The FDA also plans to ban menthol in combustible tobacco products, including cigarettes and cigars, while maintaining access to mint- and menthol-flavored e-cigarette products sold in age-restricted locations. The changes aim to protect kids and address the nicotine epidemic.

title: Results from 2018 National Youth Tobacco Survey show dramatic increase in e-cigarette use among youth over past year
body_summary: The US FDA and CDC released new findings from the National Youth Tobacco Survey, showing that 3.6 million middle and high school students used e-cigarettes in 2018, a 1.5 million increase from the previous year. The data suggests that youth e-cigarette users are using them more frequently and flavored products more often. The FDA plans to curb youth use trends with new policies and enforcement actions, aiming to prevent youth use while allowing e-cigarettes to serve as an off-ramp for adult smokers. The agency has launched a sustained campaign to monitor and prevent e-cigarette sales to minors, issued letters to five major manufacturers, and announced a public hearing on December 5 to discuss youth e-cigarette prevention and cessation.

title: FDA alerts doctors, patients about risk of complications when certain implanted pumps are used to deliver pain medications not approved for use with the devices
body_summary:
The FDA has alerted healthcare providers and patients about the serious complications that can occur when using medications not approved for use with implanted pumps that deliver medication into the spinal fluid to treat or manage pain. Complications may include dosing errors, pump failure, opioid withdrawal, infection, and other issues. The FDA Commissioner, Scott Gottlieb, M.D., stated that the treatment of pain has become increasingly complex and that the use of these devices must be judicious and their instructions carefully followed.

Implanted pumps are surgically inserted under the skin and connected to an implanted catheter to deliver medicines. The FDA-approved pump labeling identifies pain medicines that have been evaluated by the FDA for compatibility with the pump. However, some patients are being treated with medications that are not approved for use with these pumps, which may lead to serious risks due to pump failure or dosage errors.

The FDA recommends that healthcare providers review the implanted pump labeling to identify the medicines and medicine concentrations approved for use with the specific pump. Patients and providers who experience an adverse event due to an implanted pump or suspect an infusion pump is having problems are encouraged to file a voluntary report through MedWatch.

title: FDA warns StemGenex Biologic Laboratories LLC of illegally marketing an unapproved cellular product manufactured in a facility with significant manufacturing violations, putting patients at risk
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has warned StemGenex Biologic Laboratories LLC about marketing a purported stem cell product without FDA approval and for significant deviations from current good manufacturing practice requirements. The FDA has also stated its support for sound, scientific research and regulation of cell-based regenerative medicine. The agency recently inspected StemGenex's facility and found significant deviations from current good manufacturing practice requirements, including unvalidated manufacturing processes, an uncontrolled environment, and lack of control over components used in production. The FDA has requested StemGenex to correct these deviations within 15 working days. Health care professionals and consumers are advised to report any adverse events related to the StemGenex product to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program.

title: FDA authorizes emergency use of first Ebola fingerstick test with portable reader
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued an emergency use authorization (EUA) for a rapid, single-use test for the detection of Ebola virus. The test, called the DPP Ebola Antigen System, can be used with blood specimens from individuals with signs and symptoms of Ebola virus disease. The test is portable and uses a battery-operated reader, making it suitable for use outside of laboratories. The EUA allows for the use of an unapproved medical product to help mitigate potential threats from infectious diseases. The FDA has authorized the test for use in areas where patients are likely to be treated and in laboratories that are adequately equipped. The EUA is part of the FDA's ongoing efforts to make medical products available quickly to address potential threats. The test has been authorized for use by Chembio Diagnostic Systems Inc. and is the second Ebola rapid antigen fingerstick test available under EUA.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new steps to strengthen and modernize agency’s oversight and reporting of inspections for sterile injectable drugs
body_summary: The FDA is modernizing its inspections program to more efficiently collect and analyze data from inspections to improve the quality of pharmaceutical products. The New Inspection Protocol Project (NIPP) uses standardized electronic inspection protocols to assess and record data from surveillance and pre-approval inspections for sterile drug products. The first phase of NIPP aimed to develop a protocol for aseptic processing surveillance and pre-approval inspections, focusing on facilities that manufacture sterile injectable drugs. The goal is to spot problems earlier, implement mitigation steps to avoid drug shortages, and improve oversight. The new protocols will not change the role of investigators but aim to make their work more thorough and efficient. The FDA conducted multiple pilots to refine the protocols, incorporating feedback from investigators, compliance officers, and reviewers. The updated protocols promote consistent coverage, comprehensive reporting, and flexibility for investigators. The modern tools are part of the FDA's efforts to protect U.S. patients' health and safety.

title: FDA seizes food and medical products held under insanitary conditions at an Arkansas grocery warehouse
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced that the U.S. Marshals Service conducted a mass seizure of FDA-regulated products held under insanitary conditions at J and L Grocery, LLC in Alma, Arkansas on Nov. 7 and 8. The company, which receives and distributes various products, had insanitary conditions including rodents, insects, and live animals. The FDA had previously inspected the site in September and October 2018 and issued Administrative Detention Orders. A complaint was filed with the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Arkansas alleging the products are adulterated under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. Commissioner Scott Gottlieb stated that the agency is committed to protecting the public health and will take action against adulterated products.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a strong rate. Job gains have been strong, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has declined. Household spending has continued to grow strongly, while growth of business fixed investment has moderated from its rapid pace earlier in the year. On a 12-month basis, both overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy remain near 2 percent. Indicators of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. The Committee expects that further gradual increases in the target range for the federal funds rate will be consistent with sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective over the medium term. Risks to the economic outlook appear roughly balanced. In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 2 to 2-1/4 percent. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were: Jerome H. Powell, Chairman; John C. Williams, Vice Chairman; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Mary C. Daly; Loretta J. Mester; and Randal K. Quarles.

title: FDA statement on approval of OTC Primatene Mist to treat mild asthma
body_summary: The FDA has approved a new version of Primatene Mist, the only over-the-counter (OTC) metered-dose inhaler, for temporary relief from mild, intermittent asthma symptoms. The product is approved only for those diagnosed with asthma by a healthcare provider and is not a replacement for prescription asthma treatments. The new version contains hydrofluoroalkane (HFA) propellants, which are permitted under current international and U.S. law. The FDA considered concerns from practitioners and patients, including the risk of self-medicating and the importance of regular care and supervised care by a healthcare provider. The scientific review shows that the product is only beneficial for a narrow population of diagnosed asthma patients who may benefit from OTC use. The product has certain cautions, including the risk of overuse and the importance of following instructions for use. Patients with more severe asthma should not rely on the product and should work with their healthcare provider to ensure an appropriate treatment plan.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new efforts to strengthen FDA’s expanded access program
body_summary:
The FDA's Expanded Access (EA) program provides a pathway for patients to access investigational drugs, biologics, and medical devices for serious diseases and immediately life-threatening conditions outside of clinical trials when no comparable or satisfactory approved alternative therapy options are available.

The program has authorized over 9,000 applications across drugs, biologics, and devices over the last five years, with approximately 99% of requests being granted. The FDA staff is committed to ensuring the program works quickly and effectively for patients and their physicians.

To improve the program, the FDA has streamlined the required supporting documentation for expanded access requests, reducing the administrative burden for physicians. The assessment of the program found that confusion with program navigation, multi-stakeholder coordination, and administrative burden were the most frequently-cited challenges.

The FDA has taken steps to address these challenges, including updating its public website content and investing in resources to support patient/physician program navigation. The agency also intends to formally establish an agency-wide Patient Affairs Staff and Health Care Provider Affairs Program to enhance its engagement with external stakeholder groups.

The FDA is deeply committed to its Expanded Access program and facilitating access to medical products outside of clinical trials when no alternative therapy options are available to patients. The agency is also exploring the implementation of the Right to Try Act of 2017, which represents a separate and distinct pathway for patients to access unapproved, investigational treatments.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA’s effort to make more robust use of mandatory recall authority to quickly remove unsafe foods from the market
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is taking additional steps to ensure the safety of Americans by issuing a final guidance on the implementation of its mandatory recall authority. The goal is to expand the use of this authority in cases where swift intervention is needed to protect consumers from unsafe products. The guidance outlines how the FDA will give companies an opportunity to conduct a voluntary recall before ordering a mandatory recall, as required by law. This move aims to provide clarity on situations where a food product poses a serious health risk and enable the FDA to make more robust use of its recall authority. The FDA has gained this authority under the 2011 Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) and has only issued one mandatory recall order since its inception. The agency remains committed to working with companies to facilitate the orderly and prompt voluntary removal of potentially dangerous products from the food supply.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the agency’s continued efforts to address growing epidemic of youth e-cigarette use, including potential new therapies to support cessation
body_summary:
The FDA is announcing a public hearing on December 5 to discuss efforts to eliminate youth e-cigarette use, with a focus on the potential role of drug therapies to support cessation among youth. The hearing will also explore the need for drug therapies to support youth cessation of other tobacco products. The FDA has found that a public hearing is necessary to discuss ways to use drug therapies to treat teen addiction to nicotine.

The public hearing will provide an opportunity for input from across the medical and research fields, the pharmaceutical and tobacco industries, and public health stakeholders regarding approaches to eliminate youth e-cigarette use. The hearing will explore potential drug therapies to support youth e-cigarette cessation, as part of broader treatment strategies, including behavioral interventions.

The rapid growth in e-cigarette use among youth is a concern, with 1.73 million high school students and 390,000 middle school students using e-cigarettes in 2017. New preliminary data from the 2018 National Youth Tobacco Survey shows a sharp increase in the number of high school and middle school-age children reporting e-cigarette use.

The FDA is expanding its scientific priority areas to include research on youth tobacco-product cessation, including the development of data or methods to quantify the factors driving initiation and continuation of tobacco use among youth, and the understanding of youth attitudes toward e-cigarette and tobacco cessation.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on agency’s approval of Dsuvia and the FDA’s future consideration of new opioids
body_summary: The FDA is addressing the opioid crisis by taking steps to prioritize patient needs. A public debate led to a regulatory decision on Dsuvia, a sublingual opioid formulation of sufentanil. Dsuvia is restricted to certified medically-supervised health care settings and has a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) to control its distribution and use. The FDA approves Dsuvia, making it available for use in certified settings with strong limitations, including no home use and a 72-hour administration limit. The product carries a boxed warning about serious risks of addiction, overdose, and death.

title: FDA permits marketing of two devices that detect parathyroid tissue in real-time during surgery
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has permitted the marketing of two devices to help locate parathyroid tissue during surgeries such as thyroidectomy and parathyroidectomy. The Fluobeam 800 Clinic Imaging Device and the Parathyroid Detection PTeye System use fluorescent light to aid surgeons in locating parathyroid tissue, which can be difficult to distinguish from nearby tissues. The devices were previously cleared as an imaging system for capturing fluorescent images. The FDA reviewed data from studies that showed the devices to be effective in assisting surgeons, with the Fluobeam 800 reducing the rate of postoperative hypocalcemia by 76% compared to 21% without the device, and the PTeye System correctly identifying parathyroid tissue 93% of the time. The FDA granted marketing authorization to Fluoptics for the Fluobeam 800 and to AiBiomed for the PTeye System.

title: Statement on the Reimposition of Nuclear-Related Sanctions Against Iran
body_summary: The United States will complete the termination of its participation in the Iran nuclear deal on November 5. The last set of sanctions lifted under the deal will come back into force, targeting Iran's energy, shipping, and shipbuilding sectors, as well as transactions with the Central Bank of Iran and sanctioned Iranian banks. The objective is to force the regime to choose between abandoning its destructive behavior or continuing down the path toward economic disaster. The sanctions will target revenues used to fund the nuclear program and fuel regional conflict, terrorism, and enrich leaders. The measures, including 19 rounds of sanctions designations since January 2017, represent the toughest sanctions ever levied against Iran, with devastating effects on the Iranian economy. The Iranian rial has lost 70% of its value, and the economy is sliding into recession. More than 100 companies have ceased doing business with Iran, and governments and businesses should consider whether continuing to deal with Iran is worth the risk. The United States is open to reaching a new, more comprehensive deal that forever blocks Iran's path to a nuclear weapon.

title: Statement from Jeffrey Shuren, M.D., J.D., Director of the FDA’s Center for Devices and Radiological Health on the National Toxicology Program’s report on radiofrequency energy exposure
body_summary: The FDA reviews and ensures the safety of cell phones and radiation-emitting electronic products. The FDA uses decades of research and hundreds of studies to set safety limits for radiofrequency energy exposure. Recent research from the National Toxicology Program (NTP) found high levels of radiofrequency energy exposure in rodents but the FDA disagrees with the conclusions of "clear evidence" of carcinogenic activity. The FDA agrees that the findings should not be directly extrapolated to human cell phone usage. A three-day peer review of the study found upgraded conclusions for some cancers in male rats, but the FDA notes that the vote does not mean new data or findings were reported. The FDA will continue to review scientific evidence and believes the existing safety limits for cell phones remain acceptable for protecting the public health.

title: Jeffrey Shuren, M.D., J.D., director of the FDA’s Center for Devices and Radiological Health and Janet Woodcock, M.D., director of the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research on agency’s warning to consumers about genetic tests that claim to predict patients’ responses to specific medications
body_summary: The FDA is warning the public about unapproved genetic tests that claim to predict how a patient will respond to specific medications, which may not be supported by scientific and clinical evidence. These tests are being marketed directly to consumers or offered through healthcare providers, which could lead to potentially serious health consequences for patients. The FDA is concerned that healthcare providers and patients are inappropriately selecting or changing drug treatment based on the results from insufficiently substantiated genetic tests. The FDA has evaluated and authorized some genetic tests, such as those related to warfarin sensitivity and a direct-to-consumer genetic variant test, but these tests have specific indications and are subject to special controls. The agency will continue to closely monitor this area and take enforcement action as necessary.

title: FDA warns patients and doctors about risk of inaccurate results from home-use device to monitor blood thinner warfarin
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is warning patients and doctors about the potential inaccuracies of certain test strips used with the CoaguChek test meter devices to monitor warfarin levels. Roche Diagnostics has issued a Class I recall for more than 1.1 million packages of CoaguChek XS PT Test Strips, which may provide incorrect results and should not be relied upon to adjust the drug dosage. The recall affects test strips distributed nationwide from January 12, 2018, to October 29, 2018. The FDA advises patients and healthcare professionals to use alternative methods, such as laboratory tests or INR test meters, to monitor warfarin levels. Jeffrey Shuren, M.D., director of the FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health, stated that using faulty strips can lead to serious errors in medication dosage that may cause harm or death. Roche Diagnostics plans to provide new batches of corrected test strips by the end of November.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on findings from the romaine lettuce E. coli O157:H7 outbreak investigation and FDA’s efforts to prevent future outbreaks
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has released an environmental assessment detailing the final findings of an investigation into the largest E. coli O157:H7 outbreak in the country in the last decade. The outbreak, linked to contaminated romaine lettuce, resulted in five deaths and hundreds of illnesses. The FDA, CDC, and Arizona Department of Agriculture collaborated to identify factors contributing to the outbreak, which was found to be caused by the use of contaminated irrigation canal water. The FDA recommends several steps to prevent future outbreaks, including fully implementing the Food Safety Modernization Act, advancing the Produce Safety Rule, and improving traceability. The agency plans to collect and analyze romaine lettuce samples to determine product safety and will take enforcement actions against companies and farms that grow, pack, or process fresh lettuce under insanitary conditions.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on meetings with industry related to the agency’s ongoing policy commitment to firmly address rising epidemic rates in youth e-cigarette use
body_summary: The FDA has issued a call to action to stem the alarming increase in youth use of e-cigarettes, and is considering a new action plan to firmly confront and reverse the youth addiction trends. The FDA has met with the leadership of five e-cigarette companies, including Altria Group Inc., JUUL Labs Inc., and Japan Tobacco International USA Inc., to discuss steps to address the issue. The companies have presented proposals to restrict youth access to and appeal of e-cigarette products, and to address the role of flavored e-cigarettes in appealing to kids. The FDA is re-examining its regulatory approach to address the epidemic of e-cigarette use among youth, and is considering new and updated policies to its initial comprehensive plan for tobacco and nicotine regulation. The agency is committed to taking the necessary steps to fully confront the epidemic and will continue to seek public input from a diverse set of stakeholders.

title: FDA takes action to stop the use of lead acetate in hair dyes
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken action to remove lead acetate from hair coloring products due to potential safety concerns about lead exposure. The agency issued a final rule in response to a color additive petition, which repeals the regulation allowing for the use of lead acetate as a color additive. The rule removes the only authorization for the use of lead as an ingredient in cosmetic products. FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb stated that the action is part of the agency's commitment to protect Americans by reducing exposure to toxic elements. The decision is based on new scientific data showing that there is no longer a reasonable certainty that there is no harm from the use of lead acetate as a color additive. The FDA has granted a 12-month enforcement discretion period for firms to reformulate products containing lead acetate, allowing consumers to identify and avoid these products.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the FDA’s new consideration of labeling for sesame allergies
body_summary: The FDA is committed to ensuring Americans have access to information about common allergens in packaged foods. The Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act of 2004 requires foods containing eight major allergens – milk, eggs, fish, shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, and soybeans – to declare the food source on labels. However, sesame allergies are not yet required to be declared, despite a growing concern. The FDA is advancing a new effort to consider labeling for sesame to protect people with sesame allergies. The agency has issued a request for information to learn more about the prevalence and severity of sesame allergies and the impact of labeling.

title: FDA permits marketing of a diagnostic test to aid in the determination of menopausal status
body_summary: The US FDA has permitted the marketing of the PicoAMH Elisa diagnostic test as an aid in determining a patient's menopausal status. This test measures Anti-Müllerian Hormone (AMH) levels in the blood to assess a woman's approach to or entry into menopause. The test's accuracy was evaluated in a study involving 690 women aged 42 to 62, which showed it performed reasonably well in determining AMH levels and identifying women with completed or impending menopause. The test should be used in conjunction with other clinical assessments and laboratory findings to ensure safe and effective use. The FDA has also established special controls to ensure the test's accuracy, clinical performance, and labeling meet agency expectations. The test is authorized for marketing by Ansh Labs, a company within the US Department of Health and Human Services.

title: FDA approves new drug to treat influenza
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Xofluza (baloxavir marboxil) for treating acute uncomplicated influenza in patients 12 years of age and older who have been symptomatic for no more than 48 hours. The approval was granted under Priority Review, which aims to expedite action on applications deemed to significantly improve treatment, diagnosis, or prevention of serious conditions. Xofluza provides an additional treatment option for patients with flu, and its safety and efficacy were demonstrated in two randomized controlled clinical trials involving 1,832 patients. The most common adverse reactions included diarrhea and bronchitis. The FDA granted approval to Shionogi & Co., Ltd. and emphasized the importance of yearly vaccination as the primary means of preventing and controlling flu outbreaks.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on how new regulatory authorities will assist the agency in more forcefully addressing opioid crisis; included as part of the newly enacted Substance Use-Disorder Prevention that Promotes Opioid Recovery and Treatment (SUPPORT) for Patients and C
body_summary: The President signed the Substance Use-Disorder Prevention that Promotes Opioid Recovery and Treatment (SUPPORT) Act into law, granting the FDA additional authorities to combat the opioid crisis. The new law aims to decrease opioid exposure, advance innovation in pain medicines, and increase enforcement and interdiction work to stop illicit drugs from entering the US. Key provisions include expanding the FDA's authority to inspect packages, debar entities that import adulterated or misbranded drugs, and issue mandatory recall orders for controlled substances. The law supports the development of evidence-based opioid prescribing guidelines for acute pain treatment and grants the FDA new authority to require post-market studies on the efficacy of opioid pain medicines.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on agency’s efforts to advance new ways to increase the availability of naloxone as one means for reducing opioid overdose deaths
body_summary: The FDA is announcing a two-day advisory committee meeting in December to solicit input and advice on strategies to increase the availability of naloxone products for community use. The meeting will consider options for increasing access to naloxone, including co-prescribing with opioid prescriptions, and will weigh logistical, economic, and harm reduction aspects of different strategies. The committee will also discuss naloxone's potential development as an over-the-counter (OTC) product and gather insights from community programs that have made naloxone available in the community. The FDA has been working to improve naloxone availability, including the approval of injectable naloxone, auto-injector, and nasal spray formulations, and has created a model DFL and simple pictogram to encourage OTC development.

title: FDA launches global operation to crack down on websites selling illegal, potentially dangerous drugs; including opioids
body_summary:
The US FDA, in partnership with international regulatory and law enforcement agencies, targeted 465 websites selling unapproved opioid, oncology, and antiviral prescription drugs to US consumers as part of Operation Pangea XI, the eleventh annual International Internet Week of Action. The operation, led by Interpol, aimed to combat the unlawful sale and distribution of counterfeit medical products on the internet. FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb stated that consumers are being put at risk by individuals prioritizing financial gains over patient safety.

As part of the operation, FDA's Office of Criminal Investigations initiated criminal investigations into illegal online pharmacies, resulting in the arrest and indictment of a San Diego resident known as "The Drug Llama". The FDA sent warning letters to seven networks operating 465 websites, and over 450 domain names were brought to the attention of search engines and domain name registries.

This year's Operation Pangea also took place at three international mail facilities in the US, where FDA investigators found products attempting to enter the country from India, the UK, China, and El Salvador. The operation targeted the infrastructure supporting illegal online sales of drugs, including credit card processors involved in transaction laundering.

The FDA is working with other government agencies, internet stakeholders, social media platforms, and advocacy groups to curb the illegal sale of prescription opioids online. Consumers are encouraged to report suspected criminal activity to the FDA's Office of Criminal Investigations and report any unlawful sale of medical products online to the FDA.

title: Federal judge enters consent decree against Tennessee over-the-counter drug manufacturer
body_summary: A federal court ordered Keystone Laboratories, Inc. to stop selling over-the-counter drug products until the company complies with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and other requirements. The consent decree was entered by U.S. District Judge John T. Fowlkes, Jr. for the Western District of Tennessee. The company's owner, Melinda Menke, and president, Elizabeth Jumet, were also included in the decree. Keystone failed to manufacture and distribute OTC products according to current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) requirements, and some products were misbranded due to inadequate directions for use on the product labels. The consent decree requires Keystone to cease operations until it completes corrective actions, including hiring an independent expert to inspect its facility and establishing a comprehensive quality control system. This is not the first warning issued to Keystone; the FDA previously warned the company in March 2013 for similar violations, and subsequent inspections in 2016 and 2017 observed repeat violations. The U.S. Department of Justice filed the complaint on behalf of the FDA.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on agency’s ongoing commitment to improving efficiency, transparency of tobacco product application review process as part of FDA’s comprehensive framework to reduce tobacco-related disease and death
body_summary: The FDA is holding a public meeting to discuss the policies and processes for tobacco product application review. The goal is to evaluate the risks and benefits of novel products like e-cigarettes and ensure they are marketed in a way that protects public health. The FDA has committed to developing new guidance and regulations, including product standards, to improve the efficiency and transparency of the review process. The meeting aims to gather information on scientific principles and gather suggestions for further process improvements. The FDA also plans to announce additional improvements to the product application and review processes to provide industry with more predictability on timelines.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA’s new steps to help produce farmers, processors more effectively comply with food safety requirements
body_summary: Congress passed the FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) to charge the FDA with establishing science-based standards for the safe production and harvesting of produce. The Produce Safety Rule requires domestic and foreign farms to implement preventive measures during growing, harvesting, packing, and holding of produce. The Preventive Controls rule requires food facilities, such as fresh-cut produce processing plants, to have a food safety plan in place. The FDA is releasing two new draft guidance documents to assist farmers and processors in achieving compliance with FSMA's preventive controls. The draft guidance for farmers provides examples of possible approaches to comply with the Produce Safety Rule, while the draft guidance for processors discusses how to comply with recent modernized requirements for current good manufacturing practices and hazard analysis and risk-based preventive controls. The FDA will hold four public meetings to introduce and get feedback on the draft Produce Safety Rule guidance.

title: Trump Administration Launches “Winning on Reducing Food Waste” Initiative
body_summary: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), and Food and Drug Administration (FDA) signed a joint agency formal agreement under the Winning on Reducing Food Waste initiative. The agreement aims to improve coordination and communication across federal agencies to better educate Americans on reducing food loss and waste. The signing ceremony was attended by U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Sonny Perdue, Acting EPA Administrator Andrew Wheeler, and FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. Food waste in the United States is estimated to be between 30-40% of the food supply, corresponding to approximately 133 billion pounds and $161 billion worth of food in 2010. The joint effort aims to reduce food waste by 50% by 2030, with the Trump Administration commending 23 organizations and businesses for joining the U.S. Food Loss and Waste 2030 Champions initiative.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary:
Here is a summary of the source document:

The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on September 25-26, 2018. The committee discussed macroeconomic vulnerabilities, trade tensions, and market sentiment. Domestic economic data was stronger than expected, boosting Treasury yields. Nominal Treasury yields increased, with the 10-year yield above 3%. Stock prices rose 4%, driven by positive corporate earnings and domestic economy news. Financing conditions for large nonfinancial firms remained accommodative, while small businesses saw favorable conditions. The committee judged that the economy was evolving as expected, with strong labor market conditions and inflation near 2%. Members anticipated further gradual increases in the target range would be consistent with a sustained economic expansion, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near 2% over the medium term. The FOMC raised the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 2-2.25 percent.

title: FDA and DHS increase coordination of responses to medical device cybersecurity threats under new partnership; a part of the two agencies’ broader effort to protect patient safety
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) have announced a memorandum of agreement to strengthen coordination and cooperation on addressing cybersecurity in medical devices. The FDA Commissioner, Scott Gottlieb, and DHS Undersecretary, Christopher Krebs, emphasize the importance of this partnership to protect patients and stay ahead of evolving medical device cybersecurity vulnerabilities. The agreement aims to enhance mutual awareness of potential threats, share information, and coordinate responses to identified vulnerabilities. Under the agreement, DHS will serve as the central medical device vulnerability coordination center, while the FDA will continue to provide technical and clinical expertise. The goal is to create an environment of shared responsibility for identifying and addressing cybersecurity risks, ultimately protecting patients who rely on lifesaving medical devices.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA’s new steps to modernize drug development, improve efficiency and promote innovation of targeted therapies
body_summary: The FDA is modernizing its regulatory framework to advance targeted therapies and improve the development of innovative treatments. This year, the agency has approved 45 novel drugs and biologics, close to its total of 46 in 2017. New treatments are offering hope for improved quality of life and survival for patients with rare and common diseases. The FDA is issuing guidance documents to provide clarity and direction for drug developers, including one on minimal residual disease as a biomarker and another on targeted therapies for low-frequency molecular subsets.

title: FDA advances investigation into whether more than 40 e-cigarette products are being illegally marketed and outside agency's compliance policy
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) sent letters to 21 e-cigarette companies, including Vuse Alto and myblu, seeking information about potentially illegal marketing of flavored products to youth. The FDA aims to stem the youth e-cigarette use epidemic and enforce its compliance policy. In March, the agency issued an advance notice of proposed rulemaking to seek public comment on the role of flavors in tobacco products. The FDA plans to expedite the review of comments and explore additional restrictions on electronic nicotine delivery systems to reduce youth exposure. The agency also launched "The Real Cost" Youth E-Cigarette Prevention Campaign, targeting 10.7 million youth aged 12-17, and considers revising its policy on flavored products, which may lead to their removal from the market.

title: FDA approves new DNA-based test to determine blood compatibility
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved ID CORE XT, a molecular-based assay for blood transfusion medicine. This assay helps determine blood compatibility by identifying non-ABO red blood cell types. ID CORE XT is the second molecular assay approved for use in transfusion medicine and reports genotypes as final results. The assay can help streamline blood compatibility testing and provide an alternative to traditional serological methods. The FDA approval was granted to Progenika Biopharma S.A., a Grifols company. The assay was compared to licensed serological reagents and DNA sequencing tests, demonstrating comparable performance. The FDA protects the public health by ensuring the safety and effectiveness of medical products and devices.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new efforts to advance the development of generic copies of complex drugs to improve patient access to medicines
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is announcing a series of guidance documents to advance the development of generic transdermal and topical delivery systems (TDS). The FDA aims to provide increased transparency and predictability for applicants seeking to develop generic copies of complex drugs, which often face less competition due to their formulation and delivery systems. Two new draft guidance documents will be released, focusing on assessing adhesion and irritation/sensitization potential of proposed generic TDS. Additionally, 23 revised product-specific guidance documents will be issued to support industry in identifying appropriate methodologies and evidence for developing generic TDS products. The FDA is committed to developing product-specific guidance documents to promote more efficient and effective frameworks for developing generic copies of complex drugs, with the goal of advancing patient access and more affordable medicines.

title: FDA approves expanded use of Gardasil 9 to include individuals 27 through 45 years old
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved a supplemental application for Gardasil 9, expanding its approved use to women and men aged 27 through 45 years. This approval aims to help prevent HPV-related diseases and cancers in a broader age range. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) states that HPV vaccination prior to infection can prevent over 90% of these cancers. Gardasil 9 covers nine HPV types and was previously approved for use in males and females aged 9 through 26 years. The vaccine is 88% effective in preventing persistent infection, genital warts, and cervical cancer in women aged 27 through 45. The FDA's approval is based on a study of approximately 3,200 women in this age group, followed for an average of 3.5 years. The vaccine was granted priority review status, which facilitates and expedites the review of medical products addressing serious or life-threatening conditions.

title: FDA allows marketing of first self-fitting hearing aid controlled by the user
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the marketing of the Bose Hearing Aid, a user-fitted wireless air conduction hearing aid. This is the first hearing aid to enable users to fit, program, and control the device on their own without assistance. The device is intended for individuals 18 years or older with mild to moderate hearing impairment. The FDA reviewed data from 125 patients, showing comparable outcomes to professional fitting, and found that self-fitting resulted in generally preferred settings. The device has been labeled to inform users to consult a hearing healthcare professional when needed. The FDA granted marketing authorization to Bose Corporation under the De Novo premarket review pathway.

title: La FDA aprueba el uso ampliado de Gardasil 9 para incluir a personas de 27 a 45 años de edad
body_summary:
The US FDA approved a supplemental request for Gardasil 9, a nonavalent vaccine against the human papillomavirus (HPV), to expand its approved use to include men and women aged 27-45. The Gardasil 9 vaccine protects against certain types of cancer and diseases caused by nine HPV strains. Dr. Peter Marks, director of the FDA's Center for Biological Evaluation and Research, stated that the approval represents an opportunity to help prevent HPV-related diseases and cancers in a wider age range.

According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), 14 million Americans are infected with HPV each year, and 12,000 women are diagnosed with cervical cancer caused by certain HPV strains, resulting in 4,000 deaths. The Gardasil vaccine was approved by the FDA in 2006 to prevent certain types of cancer and diseases caused by four HPV strains. The Gardasil 9 vaccine protects against the same four strains plus five additional ones. The vaccine was previously approved for use in people aged 9-26.

A study involving approximately 3,200 women aged 27-45 showed that the Gardasil vaccine was 88% effective in preventing a range of HPV-related infections, including cervical cancer. The FDA approval of the Gardasil 9 for women aged 27-45 is based on these results and new data from the study. The efficacy of the Gardasil 9 in men aged 27-45 is inferred from the data for women and additional data from a study involving 150 men aged 27-45.

The Gardasil 9 vaccine was approved for use in approximately 13,000 people after evaluating its safety and side effects. The most common side effects reported were pain, inflammation, redness, and headaches. The FDA designated the Gardasil 9 as a priority for evaluation due to its potential to treat a serious and potentially deadly disease.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new agency actions to further deter ‘gaming’ of the generic drug approval process by the use of citizen petitions
body_summary: The FDA has issued a revised draft guidance to improve the efficiency and predictability of the generic drug review process. The goal is to focus more reviewer resources on scientific reviews and reduce the burden on the FDA. The guidance aims to deter companies from improperly using citizen petitions to delay generic approvals. The FDA will consider petitions submitted with the primary purpose of delaying approval and may deny them on that basis. The agency will also refer these matters to the Federal Trade Commission. The revised guidance seeks to lessen the impact of review on pending approval actions, aiming to respond to petitions within 150 days if they are received within 150 days of the product application's goal date. This policy aims to reduce approval decision delays and provide greater regulatory certainty.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. on FDA’s efforts to strengthen the agency’s medical device cybersecurity program as part of its mission to protect patients
body_summary: The FDA is addressing medical device cybersecurity vulnerabilities by developing a cybersecurity "playbook" for healthcare delivery organizations, signing memoranda of understanding with stakeholders to increase information sharing and transparency, and partnering with the US Department of Homeland Security. The agency's Center for Devices and Radiological Health has taken a holistic approach to building its medical device cybersecurity program since 2013, and the FDA has participated in exercises such as the 2013 'Cracked Domain' exercise and the 2016 Capstone National Level Exercise. The agency has also proposed creating a Center of Excellence for Digital Health to establish more efficient regulatory paradigms and support a cybersecurity unit, and remains committed to protecting patient lives from cyber threats.

title: FDA approves first treatment for advanced form of the second most common skin cancer
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Libtayo (cemiplimab-rwlc) injection for treating patients with metastatic or locally advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) who are not candidates for curative surgery or radiation. Libtayo works by targeting the PD-1 pathway, helping the body's immune system fight cancer cells. The FDA has approved six immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting this pathway, including Libtayo. The approval was granted due to the drug's effectiveness, as shown in two open-label clinical trials with 108 patients, where 47.2% of patients experienced tumor shrinkage or disappearance. Common side effects include fatigue, rash, and diarrhea. The drug must be dispensed with a patient Medication Guide and carries serious warnings, including the risk of immune-mediated adverse reactions and harm to a developing fetus.

title: FDA approves first treatment for advanced form of the second most common skin cancer
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Libtayo (cemiplimab-rwlc) injection for the treatment of patients with metastatic or locally advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) who are not candidates for curative surgery or radiation. Libtayo works by targeting the PD-1 pathway and may help the body's immune system fight cancer cells. The drug was studied in two open-label clinical trials, involving 108 patients, and showed a 47.2% objective response rate. Common side effects include fatigue, rash, and diarrhea, while more serious reactions can include immune-mediated adverse reactions, such as lung or liver problems. The FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy and Priority Review designations to Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc. for the approval of Libtayo.

title: FDA authorizes first next generation sequencing-based test to detect very low levels of remaining cancer cells in patients with acute lymphoblastic leukemia or multiple myeloma
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has permitted the marketing of the ClonoSEQ assay, a next-generation sequencing-based test for minimal residual disease (MRD) in patients with acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) or multiple myeloma. The FDA Commissioner, Scott Gottlieb, stated that the approval is an important step forward for patients suffering from ALL and multiple myeloma. The ClonoSEQ assay measures MRD at levels below 1 in 1 million cells, which is more sensitive than current methods. The FDA evaluated data from clinical studies involving 273 patients with ALL and 706 patients with multiple myeloma, showing that the assay correlated with event-free survival and disease-free survival. The FDA reviewed the ClonoSEQ assay through the de novo premarket review pathway and established special controls to ensure the accuracy, reliability, and effectiveness of the test. The FDA granted marketing authorization of the ClonoSEQ assay to Adaptive Biotechnologies Corporation.

title: FDA approves a new antibacterial drug to treat a serious lung disease using a novel pathway to spur innovation
body_summary:
The US FDA has approved a new drug, Arikayce, for the treatment of lung disease caused by Mycobacterium avium complex (MAC) in a limited population of patients with refractory disease. MAC is a type of nontuberculous mycobacteria commonly found in water and soil, causing symptoms such as persistent cough, fatigue, and shortness of breath. 

The approval was granted under the Limited Population Pathway for Antibacterial and Antifungal Drugs (LPAD) pathway, which aims to spur development of drugs targeting infections with unmet medical needs. Arikayce is the first drug to be approved under this pathway. 

The FDA also approved Arikayce under the Accelerated Approval pathway, which allows for approval of drugs showing a surrogate endpoint that is reasonably likely to predict a clinical benefit to patients. The sponsor of Arikayce will be required to conduct an additional post-market study. 

The drug was developed by Insmed, Inc. and was granted Fast Track, Breakthrough Therapy, Priority Review, and Qualified Infectious Disease Product designations. Arikayce was shown to be effective in a randomized clinical trial, where 29% of patients treated with the drug had no growth of mycobacteria in their sputum cultures for three consecutive months.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on preparations for the upcoming flu season and vaccinations
body_summary: The FDA, along with its partners, has selected strains for the 2018-2019 flu vaccine, including two influenza A types (H1N1 and H3N2) and one or two types of influenza B. The strains were chosen based on data from the Southern hemisphere, where flu strains are currently circulating. The strains are expected to offer good protection against the flu. The FDA ensures standardization and release of influenza vaccines, which undergo quality control tests, including sterility testing. The CDC and FDA collaborate to monitor flu vaccine effectiveness and safety. The majority of flu vaccines are made using chicken eggs, but newer technologies like mammalian cells and recombinant DNA offer advantages. Preliminary data suggests cell-based vaccines may have better effectiveness than egg-based vaccines. The FDA encourages investment in advanced domestic manufacturing to meet domestic and global demand.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on modernizing standards of identity and the use of dairy names for plant-based substitutes
body_summary: The FDA aims to ensure consumers can easily identify the type of product they're purchasing for themselves and their families. As part of its Nutrition Innovation Strategy, the agency plans to modernize the outdated framework for food standards to allow industry flexibility for innovation while maintaining key characteristics and nutritional integrity. The FDA has concerns that plant-based products, such as soy-based alternatives to cheese and nut-based alternatives to milk, may lead consumers to believe they have the same nutritional attributes as dairy products, even though these products can vary widely. To address this, the FDA has issued a request for information (RFI) to solicit comments and feedback from the public on how consumers use plant-based alternatives and how they understand terms like "milk" or "cheese" when labeling products made from soy, peas, or nuts. The agency hopes to receive data submissions to learn more about the nutritional profiles of different milk and plant-based products and to inform the development of draft guidance on appropriate labeling of plant-based alternatives.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new FDA commitment to disclose retailer information for certain food recalls to improve consumer safety
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) aims to ensure food safety by providing consumers with actionable information to avoid potentially contaminated products. The FDA has issued a new draft guidance outlining situations when disclosing retail information for products undergoing recalls is appropriate, particularly in cases where the food is not easily identified as being subject to a recall and may be available for consumption. The draft guidance will be publicized for recalls involving serious health consequences or death, and will be released for certain types of recalled foods, such as rawhide chews or fresh fruits and vegetables sold individually. The FDA believes this new approach will improve recall efficiency and protect consumers. The agency has already taken steps to align with this approach, such as releasing retailer information for a recall of pre-cut melon associated with a Salmonella outbreak. The new draft guidance is part of the FDA's broader action plan to further improve its oversight of food safety and recall processes.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in August indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a strong rate. Job gains have been strong, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has stayed low. Household spending and business fixed investment have grown strongly. On a 12-month basis, both overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy remain near 2 percent. Indicators of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. The Committee expects that further gradual increases in the target range for the federal funds rate will be consistent with sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective over the medium term. Risks to the economic outlook appear roughly balanced. In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 2 to 2-1/4 percent. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were: Jerome H. Powell, Chairman; John C. Williams, Vice Chairman; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Lael Brainard; Richard H. Clarida; Esther L. George; Loretta J. Mester; and Randal K. Quarles.

title: Remarks from Anna Abram as prepared for delivery to the 2018 Intergovermental Meeting on Drug Compounding
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) held its seventh intergovernmental meeting on drug compounding, where Deputy Commissioner Anna Abram welcomed attendees. The agency has overseen over 200 recalls since the 2012 fungal meningitis outbreak. To address insanitary conditions, the FDA released a revised draft guidance and two final guidances on compounding and repackaging of radiopharmaceuticals. Additionally, the FDA issued draft guidance on evaluating bulk drug substances for compounding by outsourcing facilities. Over the next two days, the agency plans to share additional policy developments and engage with stakeholders on compounding regulation.

title: FDA awards 12 grants to fund new clinical trials to advance the development of medical products for the treatment of rare diseases
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has awarded 12 new clinical trial research grants totaling over $18 million to support the development of medical products for patients with rare diseases. The grants, awarded through theOrphan Products Clinical Trials Grants Program, aim to enhance the development of treatments for rare diseases with limited market opportunities. The program, funded by Congressional appropriations, encourages clinical development of drugs, biologics, medical devices, or medical foods for use in rare diseases. The grants are intended for clinical studies evaluating the safety and effectiveness of products that could result in or substantially contribute to FDA approval for rare disease treatments.

title: FDA takes important steps to encourage appropriate and rational prescribing of opioids through final approval of new safety measures governing the use of immediate-release opioid analgesic medications
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved a new plan to address the opioid crisis, including a final Opioid Analgesic Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) for 347 opioid analgesics. The plan includes expanded measures to communicate the risks of opioid pain medications to patients and healthcare providers, requiring training for healthcare providers involved in pain management. The FDA also approved new safety labeling changes for all opioid analgesic products intended for use in an outpatient setting.
