The agency aims to decrease unnecessary opioid exposure, support treatment, and develop novel pain therapies, and will continue to evaluate existing drugs and take regulatory action as needed.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the FDA’s ongoing efforts to prevent foodborne outbreaks of Cyclospora
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has identified Cyclospora, a parasite that causes intestinal infection, in domestically grown produce items, including cilantro. The FDA has detected Cyclospora in domestically grown cilantro, which has not been linked to any illnesses, but it represents the second time the parasite has been identified in U.S.-grown produce. This year has seen a notable increase in cyclosporiasis cases, with 2,173 cases reported as of September 12. Two large produce-associated outbreaks have been linked to Del Monte vegetable trays and McDonald's salads sold in 14 states, resulting in 250 and 511 illnesses, respectively. The FDA has worked with companies to recall implicated products and trace the source of contamination. The agency has also identified Cyclospora in imported produce and has taken action to prevent contaminated shipments from entering the U.S. market. The FDA emphasizes the importance of its surveillance activities, the need to broaden its tools to address domestic contamination events, and the significance of implementing the Produce Safety Rule to prevent microbial contamination.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on launch of ‘The Real Cost’ Youth E-Cigarette Prevention Campaign amid evidence of sharply rising use among kids
body_summary: The US FDA is taking forceful steps to address the growing use of e-cigarettes among teens, citing alarming data showing a sharp rise in teen e-cigarette use over the last year. The agency will restrict adult access to e-cigarettes, encourage manufacturers to make them less attractive, and prevent kids from becoming addicted to nicotine and transitioning to cigarettes. The FDA is expanding its Youth Tobacco Prevention Plan and launching a new "Real Cost" youth e-cigarette prevention campaign. The agency has extended the compliance date for marketing applications until 2022 and has taken previous actions, such as issuing warning letters to over 60 businesses that sold JUUL brand products to minors.

title: FDA launches new, comprehensive campaign to warn kids about the dangers of e-cigarette use as part of agency’s Youth Tobacco Prevention Plan, amid evidence of sharply rising use among kids
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) launched a youth e-cigarette prevention campaign, targeting nearly 10.7 million youth aged 12-17, to educate them about the dangers of e-cigarettes. HHS Secretary Alex Azar and FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb emphasized the need to protect America's youth from e-cigarette risks. The FDA is issuing letters to five major e-cigarette manufacturers, asking them to submit plans to address youth access and use of their products within 60 days. Failure to comply may result in revisiting the current policy and potentially removing flavored products from the market. The agency is also exploring measures to make tobacco products less toxic, appealing, and addictive.

title: FDA approves device for treatment of acute coronary artery perforations
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the PK Papyrus Covered Coronary Stent System, a device for treating acute coronary artery perforations. The device, which has not been approved for this indication in 17 years, provides a new treatment option to seal perforations and stop blood leakage during procedures. The device is a balloon-expandable covered coronary stent and delivery system that can be advanced into the perforated coronary artery vessel using a balloon catheter. The FDA reviewed data from 80 patients who received the device to treat coronary artery perforations, with 95% successful delivery and 91.3% successful sealing of perforations. The device is contraindicated for certain patients, including those unable to take anti-platelet and anticoagulation therapy, and those with known allergies to certain materials used in the device.

title: Statement from Binita Ashar, M.D., of the FDA’s Center for Devices and Radiological Health on agency’s commitment to studying breast implant safety
body_summary: The FDA is addressing concerns about breast implants and associated connective tissue diseases, including rheumatoid arthritis and scleroderma. An external assessment of data showed an increased risk, but the FDA disagrees due to methodological shortcomings. The agency urges caution in viewing the assessment's conclusions. To address safety issues, the FDA has developed a Patient Registry for Breast Implants and Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma (ALCL) registry. In 2019, the FDA's Medical Devices Advisory Committee will hold a public meeting to discuss breast implant safety and effectiveness, led by Dr. Binita Ashar.

title: FDA provides update on its ongoing investigation into valsartan products; and reports on the finding of an additional impurity identified in one firm’s already recalled products
body_summary: The US FDA is investigating an additional impurity, N-Nitrosodiethylamine (NDEA), in three lots of Torrent Pharmaceuticals' recalled valsartan drug products. The impurity, a known animal and suspected human carcinogen, was found in products made using API from Zhejiang Huahai Pharmaceuticals (ZHP). The FDA has retested all valsartan API and products, including those currently marketed in the US, and found NDEA in some ZHP products. The agency is continuing to test products for NDEA and will work with companies to remove affected products from the market. The FDA expects to complete a risk analysis in the coming days and will provide updates to the public as new information becomes available.

title: FDA approves new kind of treatment for hairy cell leukemia
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Lumoxiti injection for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory hairy cell leukemia who have received at least two prior systemic therapies. This is the first CD22-directed cytotoxin treatment for patients with HCL. The approval follows a single-arm, open-label clinical trial of 80 patients, which showed a durable complete response rate of 30% and an overall response rate of 75%. Common side effects include infusion-related reactions, edema, nausea, fatigue, and diarrhea. The prescribing information includes warnings about capillary leak syndrome and hemolytic uremic syndrome. The FDA granted Fast Track and Priority Review designations and Orphan Drug designation to AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals.

title: FDA awards five grants to advance the development of pediatric medical devices
body_summary: The US FDA has awarded five grants totaling up to $6 million per year for five years to Pediatric Device Consortia across the country. The program aims to enhance the development, production, and distribution of pediatric medical devices. The grants have awarded $37 million since 2009. Five consortia received grants, including Philadelphia Pediatric Medical Device Consortium, National Capital Consortium for Pediatric Device Innovation 2.0, and University of California San Francisco-Stanford Pediatric Device Consortium. The grants provide advice and support services to innovators of children's medical devices, covering areas such as intellectual property, prototyping, and clinical trial design. The FDA Commissioner, Scott Gottlieb, stated that the program aims to encourage the development of safe and effective medical devices for pediatric patients. The grants will also support the Real World Evidence Demonstration Project, which aims to gather data on pediatric medical devices. The program has assisted or advised over 1,000 medical device projects, and 19 pediatric medical devices are now available to patients.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., and Center for Devices and Radiological Health Director Jeff Shuren, M.D., J.D., on agency efforts to work with tech industry to spur innovation in digital health
body_summary: The FDA is working to modernize its regulatory approach to digital health, enabling innovation and improving patient outcomes. The agency has launched a Digital Health Innovation Action Plan to encourage development and greater innovation in the digital health space. With this effort, the FDA aims to reduce the time and cost of market entry while ensuring patient safeguards are in place. The agency recognizes the need for a modern, flexible, and risk-based approach to regulation, which will foster innovation and reduce barriers to market entry. The FDA has taken steps to encourage more development and innovation in digital health, including a software precertification pilot program. The agency believes that with a more modern approach, it will see an increase in the development of health products from a variety of digital software developers, including traditional medical device companies, large tech companies, and small start-ups. The FDA is committed to working with developers to bring safe, effective, and innovative products to market, and has proposed the creation of a Center of Excellence for Digital Health to advance modernizing its regulatory approach.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new steps to address epidemic of youth e-cigarette use
body_summary: The FDA has unveiled a policy to reduce tobacco-related deaths and disease by regulating nicotine levels in combustible cigarettes and non-combustible forms of nicotine delivery. The goal is to reduce smoking rates from 15% to 1.4% and prevent 33 million people from becoming smokers. The agency is re-examining its compliance policy for e-cigarettes, citing an "epidemic of use" among teens, and considering stricter enforcement, including stricter marketing regulations and investigations into manufacturers' sales and marketing practices. Five dominant e-cig manufacturers, including JUUL and Vuse, have received warning letters, with the FDA requiring them to submit plans to address widespread youth use within 60 days. The agency plans to step up enforcement actions against e-cigarette sales to minors and launch a national campaign to warn teenagers of the dangers of nicotine and e-cigarette use.

title: FDA takes new steps to address epidemic of youth e-cigarette use, including a historic action against more than 1,300 retailers and 5 major manufacturers for their roles perpetuating youth access
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has taken enforcement actions against retailers selling e-cigarettes to minors, issuing over 1,300 warning letters and fines. The agency is cracking down on retail sales of e-cigarettes to youth, revising its compliance policy for flavored e-cigarettes, and asking top-selling brands to submit plans to address youth access and use. The FDA warns that youth use of e-cigarettes is reaching epidemic proportions, citing concerns about nicotine addiction and the developing adolescent brain. The FDA is re-examining its compliance policy for premarket tobacco applications, issuing letters to manufacturers of JUUL, Vuse, MarkTen XL, blu e-cigs, and Logic, asking them to submit plans to address youth access within 60 days.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new warning letters FDA is issuing to companies marketing kratom with unproven medical claims; and the agency’s ongoing concerns about kratom
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is taking action against kratom vendors making unsubstantiated claims about their products. Kratom, a plant native to Thailand and other countries, contains opioids and has the potential for abuse. The FDA has issued warning letters to two vendors, Chillin Mix Kratom and Mitra Distributing, for marketing kratom products with claims that they can treat opioid withdrawal and other serious medical conditions. This is a violation of federal law. The FDA is concerned that these products can pose serious health risks, including delaying patients from seeking appropriate treatment and putting them at risk of overdose and death. The FDA will continue to promote innovation and access to FDA-approved treatments for opioid use disorder and work to reduce stigma around these therapies. Consumers are urged not to consume kratom and to seek medical care from their healthcare provider.

title: USDA and FDA announce joint public meeting on use of animal cell culture technology to develop products derived from livestock and poultry
body_summary: U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Sonny Perdue and FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb announced a joint public meeting on Oct. 23-24, 2018, to discuss cell culture technology for livestock and poultry products. The meeting, hosted by the USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service and FDA, will focus on potential hazards, oversight, and labeling of cell cultured food products. Representatives from industry, consumer groups, and stakeholders are invited to participate. The meeting will be held at the U.S. Department of Agriculture South Building in Washington, DC, and pre-registration is available on the FSIS website. Written comments can be submitted by Nov. 26, 2018, on regulations.gov.

title: FDA approves new dosage strength of buprenorphine and naloxone sublingual film as maintenance treatment for opioid dependence
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Cassipa, a sublingual film containing buprenorphine and naloxone, for the maintenance treatment of opioid dependence. This approval provides a new dosage strength (16mg/4mg) of buprenorphine and naloxone sublingual film, available in both brand name and generic versions. Cassipa was approved through an abbreviated approval pathway under the 505(b)(2) pathway, relying on the FDA's finding of safety and effectiveness for Suboxone sublingual film. The manufacturer submitted Cassipa-specific pharmacokinetic data to establish its safety and efficacy. The FDA Commissioner, Scott Gottlieb, M.D., stated that the introduction of new treatment options has the potential to broaden access for patients. The FDA is committed to helping those with opioid use disorder transition to lives of sobriety and encourages healthcare professionals to offer adequate treatment options.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new steps to help ensure the quality of and preserve access to compounded drugs by pursuing closer collaboration with states
body_summary: The FDA has issued a revised draft memorandum of understanding (MOU) with states to address public health concerns related to compounded drugs. The goal is to collaborate with states to maximize resources and public health impact while ensuring patient access. Key provisions include identifying compounders that distribute more than 50% of their compounded drugs interstate, reporting information to the FDA, and adopting a risk-based approach to oversight. The FDA aims to prioritize inspections of compounders based on risk. The agency also plans to issue revised draft guidance on insanitary conditions in compounding facilities and CGMP requirements for outsourcing facilities, aiming to promote voluntary compliance and protect public health.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on an updated approach for including added sugar information on the Nutrition Facts labels of pure maple syrup and honey
body_summary: The FDA is updating the Nutrition Facts label to provide consumers with accurate information on added sugars. The new label will list the total grams of sugar, distinguishing between naturally occurring sugars and added sugars. The updated label also includes a listing of "added sugars" and a new daily value for added sugars. The FDA has issued draft guidance for industry to clarify the added sugars declaration on the label of pure, single-ingredient "packaged as such" products like maple syrup and honey. The guidance aims to address concerns that these products may contain added sugars, and the FDA is currently drafting a revised approach. The FDA anticipates issuing the final guidance by early next year, with the goal of empowering consumers to make informed and healthy dietary choices.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the agency’s global efforts to help assure product quality and transparency at foreign drug manufacturing facilities
body_summary: The FDA has established a framework to ensure global drug products meet high-quality standards, prioritizing inspections based on potential risks to patients. The agency has improved transparency by publishing inspection outcomes and collaborated with other countries to recognize foreign regulatory authority inspections. The FDA participates in the Pharmaceutical Inspection Co-operation Scheme (PIC/S) and the International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) to harmonize drug inspections and standards. To enhance drug production reliability, the FDA fosters advanced manufacturing practices, including continuous manufacturing, and awards grants to research institutions to adopt these technologies. The agency aims to ensure high-quality manufacturing and confidence in U.S. products, regardless of manufacturing location.

title: Statement on National Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month
body_summary: The President of the United States joins Americans in remembering those lost to ovarian cancer, supporting those fighting the disease, and reaffirming the commitment to eradicate cancer. During National Ovarian Cancer Awareness Month, the President urges all women, especially those at increased risk, to consult their healthcare providers about their risk of ovarian cancer. The administration supports research and medical professionals, and has approved an additional therapy for ovarian cancer treatment and signed "right to try" legislation.

title: La FDA facilite les échanges commerciaux entre les partenaires commerciaux américains et étrangers grâce à un nouveau programme de certification des exportations de produits alimentaires
body_summary:
The FDA has announced a new export certification program for certain food products, regulated by the agency and charging fees for new certifications. The certification program is part of the FDA's efforts to facilitate American exports and stimulate the economy. Scott Gottlieb, FDA Commissioner, stated that the new program will help American exporters meet the requirements of importing countries. The program is in line with the FDA's previous efforts to simplify export processes. 

The FDA added a new provision to the FD & C Act in 1996, allowing exporters to request certification for food products. However, this provision did not include foods regulated by the FDA. The 2011 Food Safety Modernization Act amendment added food to the list of products subject to FDA regulation. The new export certification program implements this amendment.

The FDA has previously issued other types of certifications for exported food products. The new program is complementary to certifications issued by other government agencies. The FDA will continue to coordinate with other agencies on certification and will participate in consultations with foreign governments on certification requests. The FDA will also continue to issue the current "Sales for Compliance" certificate for dietary supplements, pharmaceuticals, and other special foods.

title: FDA announces voluntary recall of Montelukast tablets by Camber Pharmaceuticals due to incorrect drug in bottles
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is warning consumers and healthcare professionals about a voluntary recall of one lot of Montelukast Sodium Tablets due to a mix-up with Losartan Potassium Tablets. The affected product, lot number MON17384, has an expiration date of December 31, 2019, and was shipped in 30-count bottles labeled as Montelukast Sodium Tablets 10mg. This mix-up poses a safety risk, particularly for pregnant women taking Montelukast, as Losartan can harm or kill the fetus. The FDA recommends that consumers contact their healthcare provider or pharmacist immediately to report the issue. Camber Pharmaceuticals, Inc. is responsible for the recall, and to date, no adverse event reports have been received.

title: FDA helps facilitate trade between U.S. and foreign trading partners with new export certification program for food
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration announced a new export certification program for certain FDA-regulated food products. The program aims to facilitate exports to countries that import food products from the U.S. The program is based on the Federal Food, Drug & Cosmetic Act and implements the Food Safety Modernization Act amendment. The FDA will assess fees for issuing new export certifications to U.S.-based manufacturers or exporters of these products. The program will be complementary to existing export certifications for foods issued by other U.S. government agencies. The FDA will coordinate with other agencies and partner with foreign governments to ensure the needs of U.S. exporters are met. The program will begin issuing new export certificates starting October 1, 2018.

title: District Court orders permanent injunction against companies selling sexual enhancement products containing undisclosed drugs
body_summary: The U.S. District Court for the District of New Jersey entered a permanent injunction against S Hackett Marketing LLC, R Thomas Marketing LLC, Shawn Hackett, and Roger Thomas, requiring them to cease distributing drugs until they take remedial measures and comply with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. The defendants sold unapproved and misbranded drugs through over 100 websites, claiming they could treat serious conditions without FDA approval. FDA laboratory testing found undisclosed sildenafil in some products, posing serious health risks. The FDA had previously issued a warning letter to the companies and the U.S. Department of Justice filed a complaint on their behalf.

title: FDA Statement on FDA’s ongoing investigation into valsartan impurities and recalls and an update on FDA’s current findings
body_summary: The FDA found that some generic versions of valsartan, an angiotensin II receptor blocker, contain the impurity N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA), which has the potential to cause cancer. The FDA launched an investigation and identified four manufacturers using valsartan API from Zhejiang Huahai Pharmaceutical Co. for the US market. The agency took immediate steps to address the issue, issuing recalls for affected products and estimating that the risk of cancer from the impurity could be extremely low, with one additional case of cancer over the lifetimes of 8,000 people taking the highest valsartan dose daily for four years. The FDA is reviewing records, testing products, and working with global regulatory agencies to mitigate the risk and ensure safe use of valsartan and other angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs).

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA’s support for exempting coffee from California’s cancer warning law
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is concerned about a California law, Proposition 65, which requires labeling of certain products with cancer warnings, including coffee. The FDA has reviewed the science on acrylamide, a chemical found in coffee, and found that it does not support a cancer warning. In fact, the FDA believes that such a warning could mislead consumers about the benefits of moderate coffee consumption. The FDA strongly supports a proposed regulation to exempt coffee from a Proposition 65 cancer warning, as it aligns with the agency's mission to provide science-based information to consumers.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the agency’s ongoing work to forcefully address the opioid crisis
body_summary: The US FDA has made significant efforts to address the opioid crisis over the past 17 months. The agency has taken actions such as extending risk evaluation and mitigation strategy programs, updating educational content for providers, and advancing evidence-based guidelines for opioid prescribing. The FDA has also protected children from unnecessary exposure to opioids, requested the market withdrawal of a drug, and expanded its oversight of drugs shipped illegally through international mail facilities. The agency plans to issue at least four new guidance documents to streamline drug development for specific areas, reducing the number of studies required for chronic pain indications.

title: FDA alerts consumers, pet owners not to use products manufactured by King Bio, including Dr. King’s label, homeopathic drug and pet products
body_summary: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is warning consumers and pet owners not to use King Bio Inc.'s products, including homeopathic drug products, due to high levels of microbial contamination. The company has expanded its voluntary recall for the second time to include all water-based drug products marketed for humans and animals. The FDA recommends that consumers stop using and dispose of these products immediately. The recall affects products such as Dr. King’s Children’s Cough Relief, Dr. King’s Chicken Pox Symptom Relief, and pet products for urinary incontinence and digestion relief. The FDA inspected King Bio's facility and collected product samples, which revealed microbial contaminants including Burkholderia Multivorans. The company previously recalled three products in July 2018 and expanded its recall to include 32 more products in August 2018. The FDA is focusing enforcement on products with the greatest potential to cause risk to patients, including vulnerable populations like children. Consumers and pet owners are advised to report adverse events or quality problems to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program.

title: FDA takes action against 21 websites marketing unapproved opioids as part of agency’s effort to target illegal online sales
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has warned four online networks operating 21 websites to immediately stop selling potentially dangerous, unapproved, and misbranded opioid medications, including tramadol. FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb stated that cutting off illicit online sales of opioids is critical in addressing the opioid crisis. The FDA has issued 13 warning letters to over 70 websites this summer and plans to continue cracking down on these networks. Patients who buy prescription medicines from illegal online pharmacies may be putting their health at risk due to counterfeit, contaminated, or expired products. The networks receiving warning letters include CoinRX MedInc.biz, PharmacyAffiliates.org, and PharmaMedics. The FDA requests responses from each company within 10 working days and may take legal enforcement action if violations are not corrected.

title: Memorandum on Modernizing the Monetary Reimbursement Model for the Delivery of Goods Through the International Postal System and Enhancing the Security and Safety of International Mail
body_summary: The President of the United States has ordered reforms to the international postal system, aiming to modernize the monetary reimbursement model and enhance security and safety. The reforms promote fair and nondiscriminatory rates, unrestricted competition, and clear distinctions between governmental and operational responsibilities. The United States seeks to reform the Universal Postal Union (UPU) to align with these objectives, including full reimbursement of US Postal Service costs and avoidance of preferences favoring foreign mailers. Director General of the UPU will describe US policies and intentions in a memorandum. The Secretary of the UPU is tasked with seeking agreement on future Convention texts at UPU meetings, including a September 2018 Extraordinary Congress, and will submit a report to the President by November 1, 2018, on implementing the memorandum's policies.

title: Companies cease sales of e-liquids with labeling or advertising that resembled kid-friendly foods following FDA, FTC warnings
body_summary: The US FDA has announced that 17 companies have stopped selling nicotine-containing e-liquids with misleading labeling or advertising, including kid-friendly food products. The FDA warned these companies in May, and they have since taken corrective action. The agency is committed to protecting youth from the dangers of nicotine and tobacco products. FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb stated that removing these products from the market is a critical step towards protecting kids. The FDA will continue to take enforcement actions to restrict youth access, limit youth appeal, and reduce toxic exposure to youth. The agency has issued warning letters to companies that sold products to minors, and plans to explore measures to make tobacco products less toxic and appealing to youth.

title: FDA approves first drug for neurotrophic keratitis, a rare eye disease
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Oxervate (cenegermin), the first drug, for treating neurotrophic keratitis, a rare disease affecting the cornea. The approval provides a novel topical treatment offering complete corneal healing for many patients. The safety and efficacy of Oxervate were studied in 151 patients with neurotrophic keratitis in two eight-week randomized controlled studies. In these studies, complete corneal healing in eight weeks was demonstrated in 70% of patients treated with Oxervate, compared to 28% of patients treated without cenegermin. The most common adverse reactions include eye pain, ocular hyperemia, eye inflammation, and increased lacrimation. Oxervate was granted Priority Review designation and received Orphan Drug designation. The FDA approved Oxervate to Dompé farmaceutici SpA.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new steps to advance the development of evidence-based, indication-specific guidelines to help guide appropriate prescribing of opioid analgesics
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has awarded a contract to the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM) to develop evidence-based guidelines for appropriate opioid analgesic prescribing for acute pain resulting from specific medical conditions or procedures. The goal is to support rational prescribing practices and reduce the likelihood of misuse and abuse of opioids. The contract will help identify evidence needed to inform clinical practice guidelines, understand current guideline development, and outline research required to generate evidence. NASEM will conduct a consensus study and issue a report on its findings, which will include meetings and public workshops to engage stakeholders. The FDA already has an Opioid Analgesic Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) in place to educate prescribers on appropriate prescribing practices.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee maintained the target range for the federal funds rate at 1-3/4 to 2 percent due to strong labor market conditions and inflation near 2 percent. Staff analysis presented potential monetary policy options, evaluating the effectiveness of current toolkit and assessing the likelihood of returning to the effective lower bound. The committee discussed tools to address an economic downturn, acknowledging uncertainty about their effectiveness. The rate of quits increased, while initial claims for unemployment insurance benefits remained low. Labor compensation rose modestly, with industrial production and real PCE showing moderate growth.

title: FDA permits marketing of transcranial magnetic stimulation for treatment of obsessive compulsive disorder
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has permitted the marketing of the Brainsway Deep Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation System for the treatment of obsessive compulsive disorder (OCD). This follows data from a randomized, multi-center study of 100 patients, where 38% of patients responded to the device, compared to 11% when using a sham device. The study evaluated the reduction in patients' Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (YBOCS) score, a common metric for measuring OCD severity. The most frequent adverse reaction was headache, reported by 37.5% of patients who received the device. The Brainsway device is contraindicated for patients with certain medical implants and should be used with earplugs to reduce exposure to loud sounds. The FDA reviewed the device through the de novo premarket review pathway and permitted marketing to Brainway Ltd.

title: FDA approves first generic version of EpiPen
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the first generic version of the EpiPen and EpiPen Jr (epinephrine) auto-injector for emergency treatment of allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, in adults and pediatric patients weighing over 33 pounds. Teva Pharmaceuticals USA gained approval to market its generic epinephrine auto-injector in 0.3 mg and 0.15 mg strengths. The FDA Commissioner, Scott Gottlieb, M.D., said this approval will provide patients with a lower-cost option for life-saving epinephrine treatment. The FDA has published three draft or final guidances since 2009 to help guide the development of generic epinephrine auto-injectors. The approval of this generic product means patients can have another approved product to help protect against potential drug shortages.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on advancing the science and regulation of live microbiome-based products used to prevent, treat, or cure diseases in humans
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is playing a key role in sorting through the science and science fiction of probiotics, with a focus on their role in treating and preventing disease. Certain medical issues, such as bacterial infections, may disrupt the normal complement of microorganisms within the body, and research has shown that manipulating the microbiota may improve cancer treatment. There is also preliminary evidence suggesting that certain microorganisms or "good bacteria" may help prevent some diseases, including necrotizing enterocolitis in premature infants. The FDA is actively monitoring the use of probiotics in this population due to reported serious side effects. The agency has issued guidance on how researchers can study probiotics as drugs and is convening a workshop with the National Institutes of Health to discuss the regulatory framework for live microbiome-based products. The FDA aims to advance regulatory science in this field and ensure that products are properly evaluated for their safety and effectiveness.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on significant public health value and cost savings resulting from the agency’s youth smoking prevention campaign
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) aims to reduce tobacco-related disease and death by preventing youth from becoming addicted to tobacco. The agency is exploring measures to make tobacco products less toxic and appealing, enforcing federal youth access restrictions, and educating youth about the dangers of tobacco use. As part of its plan, the FDA is reducing nicotine in cigarettes to minimally- or non-addictive levels and investing in public education campaigns, including the successful "The Real Cost" campaign, which has prevented nearly 350,000 youth from smoking since its launch in 2014. The campaign has resulted in savings of over $31 billion for youth, their families, and society. The FDA will continue to invest in tobacco prevention efforts, including a new campaign on youth use of e-cigarettes, to reduce the number of kids who use tobacco products.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the FDA’s new resource guide to support responsible opioid prescribing for pain management in animals
body_summary: The FDA has issued guidance to veterinarians on the safe use of opioids in animals, as part of its efforts to address the opioid epidemic. The agency recognizes that opioids have a legitimate role in treating pain in animals, but also have potential risks, including addiction and abuse in humans. The guidance provides recommendations for veterinarians, including following state and federal regulations on prescribing opioids, properly safeguarding and storing medications, and using alternative pain management options when appropriate. The FDA is also providing resources, such as training and education, to help veterinarians identify the signs of opioid abuse and take steps to prevent diversion. The agency is committed to supporting veterinarians in their efforts to curb the diversion of opioids and promote appropriate prescribing practices.

title: FDA allows marketing of first direct-to-consumer app for contraceptive use to prevent pregnancy
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has permitted the marketing of the first mobile medical application, Natural Cycles, as a method of contraception to prevent pregnancy. The app uses an algorithm to calculate a woman's fertile days based on body temperature readings and menstrual cycle information. Natural Cycles requires daily temperature readings and tracking of the menstrual cycle, with women using the app for contraception advised to abstain from sex or use protection when the app indicates they are fertile. Clinical studies involving 15,570 women showed a "perfect use" failure rate of 1.8 percent and a "typical use" failure rate of 6.5 percent. The app is intended for use in pre-menopausal women aged 18 and older, but not for women with certain medical conditions or those using hormonal treatments. The FDA reviewed the app through the de novo premarket review pathway and is establishing special controls to ensure the app's accuracy and effectiveness.

title: FDA approves new vaginal ring for one year of birth control
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Annovera, a combined hormonal contraceptive, for women of reproductive age to prevent pregnancy. Annovera is a reusable, donut-shaped vaginal system that can be used for an entire year. The system is used for three weeks, followed by one week out of the vagina, repeating every four weeks. The FDA's approval is based on clinical trials with healthy women aged 18-40, showing a low risk of pregnancy, with about 2-4 women out of 100 getting pregnant in the first year. However, Annovera carries a boxed warning for cigarette smoking and serious cardiovascular events. The most common side effects are similar to those of other combined hormonal contraceptives. The FDA is requiring postmarketing studies to further evaluate the risks of venous thromboembolism.

title: FDA approves first-of-its kind targeted RNA-based therapy to treat a rare disease
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Onpattro (patisiran) infusion for treating peripheral nerve disease caused by hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (hATTR) in adult patients. This is the first FDA-approved treatment for patients with polyneuropathy caused by hATTR, a rare and debilitating genetic disease. Onpattro is a small interfering ribonucleic acid (siRNA) treatment that targets the root cause of the disease by altering the genetic drivers. The drug was approved based on a clinical trial involving 225 patients, who showed better outcomes in measures of polyneuropathy, including muscle strength, sensation, and reflexes. The FDA granted this application Fast Track, Priority Review, and Breakthrough Therapy designations. Approval was granted to Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, Inc. The drug is designed to interfere with RNA production of an abnormal form of the protein transthyretin (TTR), reducing the accumulation of amyloid deposits in peripheral nerves.

title: FDA approves new treatment for a rare genetic disorder, Fabry disease
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Galafold (migalastat), the first oral medication for treating adults with Fabry disease. Fabry disease is a rare genetic disorder caused by mutations in the alpha-galactosidase A (GLA) gene, affecting approximately one in 40,000 males. The drug is indicated for adults with Fabry disease who have a genetic mutation determined to be responsive to treatment. Galafold increases the activity of the body's deficient enzyme, differing from enzyme replacement therapy. The efficacy of Galafold was demonstrated in a six-month clinical trial, showing a greater reduction in globotriaosylceramide (GL-3) in blood vessels of the kidneys. The safety of Galafold was studied in four clinical trials, and the most common adverse reactions were headache, nasal and throat irritation, and urinary tract infection. Galafold was approved using the Accelerated Approval pathway and received Priority Review designation and Orphan Drug designation.

title: FDA alerts healthcare providers, women about risks associated with improper use of rupture of membranes tests
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has alerted healthcare providers and women about serious adverse events related to the improper use of tests for detecting ruptured membranes in pregnant women. The FDA reminds providers that these tests should not be used independently to diagnose a rupture of the membranes, but only in conjunction with other clinical assessments. The agency has received reports of 13 fetal deaths and multiple health complications in pregnant women due to the improper use of these tests, which may provide false negative results. The FDA is urging pregnant women to contact their healthcare providers if they are concerned about amniotic membranes that may have ruptured too early. The agency is also notifying the public of a voluntary recall for one brand of ROM test strips due to a device malfunction.

title: FDA approves first generic drug under new pathway aimed at enhancing market competition for sole source drugs
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved several strengths of potassium chloride oral solution as the first generic drugs to receive Competitive Generic Therapy (CGT) designation. The approval was made possible by the FDA's new CGT pathway, which was created to expedite the development and review of generic drugs for products with inadequate competition. The CGT pathway was implemented under the FDA Reauthorization Act of 2017, which provides review enhancements and expedited review for applicants who receive CGT designation. The approved potassium chloride oral solution products, intended for treating and preventing hypokalemia, are eligible for 180 days of CGT exclusivity. The FDA granted approval to Apotex Inc. and requires generic drug applicants to demonstrate that their products meet the agency's rigorous approval standards.

title: FDA approves treatment for two rare types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Poteligeo (mogamulizumab-kpkc) injection for intravenous use for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory mycosis fungoides (MF) or Sézary syndrome (SS) after at least one prior systemic therapy. The approval fills an unmet medical need for patients with MF and is the first FDA approval of a drug specifically for SS. 

Mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome are rare types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Poteligeo is a monoclonal antibody that binds to a protein found on some cancer cells. A clinical trial of 372 patients showed that progression-free survival was longer for patients taking Poteligeo (median 7.6 months) compared to patients taking vorinostat (median 3.1 months). Serious warnings of treatment with Poteligeo include the risk of dermatologic toxicity, infusion reactions, and autoimmune problems. The FDA granted this application Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy designation, as well as Orphan Drug designation.

title: FDA takes new steps to encourage the development of novel medicines for the treatment of opioid use disorder
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has issued new scientific recommendations to encourage innovation and development of novel medication-assisted treatment (MAT) drugs for opioid use disorder (OUD). The new draft guidance outlines ways for drug developers to measure and demonstrate the effectiveness and benefits of new or existing MAT products. 

HHS Secretary Alex Azar stated that the Trump Administration is pursuing every opportunity to address the opioid epidemic and support patients struggling with opioid use disorder. The evidence is clear that medication-assisted treatment works, and it is a key piece of defeating the drug crisis facing the country.

The FDA's new guidance identifies several additional potential clinical endpoints and outcome measures that drug developers may consider, including the impact on adverse outcomes like mortality, emergency medical interventions, and Hepatitis C seroconversion. The agency encourages sponsors to discuss their plans with the agency early in the drug development process.

The FDA is committed to providing assistance to sponsors interested in developing a validated measurement of patient-reported experiences, such as "craving" or "urge to use" opioids, which make it difficult for patients with OUD to sustain recovery.

The agency's new guidance builds on previous draft guidance issued in April and a paper with the National Institute on Drug Abuse. The FDA also held a meeting in April to hear from individuals with OUD on a wide range of topics.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new steps the agency is taking to support the development of novel nicotine replacement drug therapies to help smokers quit cigarettes
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration is developing policies to reduce tobacco-related disease and death by regulating nicotine and tobacco products. A key part of this framework is exploring the role of novel forms of nicotine delivery, such as e-cigarettes, in achieving public health goals. The FDA is working to recognize the role of these products in supporting smokers to quit combustible cigarettes. The agency has established a Nicotine Steering Committee to evaluate new, evidence-based opportunities to advance therapeutic nicotine products. 

The FDA is releasing two draft guidances aimed at supporting the development of novel, inhaled nicotine replacement therapies. The first draft guidance, "Nonclinical Testing of Orally Inhaled Nicotine-Containing Drug Products," focuses on evaluating potential toxicities associated with orally inhaled nicotine-containing drug products. The second draft guidance will address new potential clinically relevant outcomes for smoking cessation products and alternative treatment regimens.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA’s continued, careful oversight of the REMS associated with transmucosal immediate-release fentanyl products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) will host a public advisory committee meeting on August 3 to review data from the Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) with Elements to Assure Safe Use (ETASU) for transmucosal immediate-release fentanyl (TIRF) products. The FDA is seeking the advice of outside experts on the effectiveness of the REMS and whether changes to the REMS might be necessary. The TIRF products are medically important but pose serious risks. The FDA has determined that a REMS would be necessary to ensure the benefits of TIRF products outweigh their risks, and the TIRF REMS was approved in 2011 to include all members of the TIRF class. The REMS aims to limit use to opioid-tolerant patients and educate prescribers, pharmacists, and patients on potential risks. The committee will discuss the effectiveness of the REMS, including evaluating the reliability of data and assessing the impact of the REMS on prescribing patterns.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in June indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a strong rate. Job gains have been strong, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has stayed low. Household spending and business fixed investment have grown strongly. On a 12-month basis, both overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy remain near 2 percent. Indicators of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. The Committee expects that further gradual increases in the target range for the federal funds rate will be consistent with sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective over the medium term. Risks to the economic outlook appear roughly balanced. In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1-3/4 to 2 percent. The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting strong labor market conditions and a sustained return to 2 percent inflation. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were: Jerome H. Powell, Chairman; John C. Williams, Vice Chairman; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Lael Brainard; Esther L. George; Loretta J. Mester; and Randal K. Quarles.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA’s new efforts to advance antimicrobial stewardship in veterinary settings
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has identified antimicrobial resistance as a global public health challenge. The FDA will implement a new five-year blueprint to advance antimicrobial stewardship in veterinary settings, aiming to reduce the overuse of antimicrobial drugs and combat resistance. The Center for Veterinary Medicine (CVM) will focus on aligning antimicrobial drug product use with principles of stewardship, supporting better stewardship, and enhancing monitoring of antimicrobial resistance. The plan will include goals such as establishing appropriate durations of use for medically important antimicrobials, bringing all dosage forms under veterinary oversight, and advancing new strategies for promoting stewardship in companion animals. The FDA will also develop guidance with broad stakeholder input, enhance transparency, and improve data collection and sharing on antimicrobial drug use and resistance.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on efforts to safeguard women’s health from deceptive health claims and significant risks related to devices marketed for use in medical procedures for “vaginal rejuvenation”
body_summary: The FDA is warning women and their healthcare providers about the marketing of "vaginal rejuvenation" devices that claim to treat menopause, urinary incontinence, and sexual function issues, but have serious risks and no adequate evidence to support their use. These devices use lasers and other energy-based devices to destroy or reshape vaginal tissue. The FDA has cleared or approved these devices for treating serious conditions like cervical or vaginal tissue destruction and genital warts, but not for "vaginal rejuvenation." The agency has found numerous cases of vaginal burns, scarring, pain, and recurring pain, and is warning women of the potential harm from these devices. The FDA has notified seven device manufacturers of their concerns and is requiring them to address the issues within 30 days. If the concerns are not addressed, the FDA will consider enforcement actions.

title: FDA approves first treatment for rare adrenal tumors
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Azedra (iobenguane I 131) injection for the treatment of adults and adolescents aged 12 and older with unresectable, metastatic pheochromocytomas or paragangliomas. This is the first FDA-approved treatment for this condition. The drug has been shown to decrease the need for blood pressure medication and reduce tumor size in some patients. The efficacy was demonstrated in a single-arm, open-label clinical trial involving 68 patients, with 17 (25%) experiencing a 50% or greater reduction in all antihypertensive medications for at least six months. Common side effects include lymphopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, and hypertension. The FDA granted Fast Track, Breakthrough Therapy, and Priority Review designations, as well as Orphan Drug designation, to Progenics Pharmaceuticals, Inc. for the approval of Azedra.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the process FDA is undertaking for reviewing and modernizing the agency’s standards of identity for dairy products
body_summary: The FDA is committed to advancing policies that enable consumers to safely benefit from innovations in food production. To achieve this, the agency is modernizing its standards of identity for food products, including plant-based alternatives to dairy products. This effort aims to ensure that consumers have accurate information about the nutritional attributes of the foods they consume. The FDA is also taking steps to facilitate food innovations that can give consumers more choices, enable better nutrition, and improve labeling. Specifically, the agency is reviewing the labeling of plant-based beverages marketed as "milk," which can be misleading due to their varying nutritional content compared to traditional dairy products. The FDA will gather stakeholder feedback and conduct a public process to review its standards and ensure that consumers are not misled by these products. The agency will also consider the potential First Amendment issues related to the use of terms like "milk" on plant-based alternatives.

title: FDA approves magnetic device system for guiding sentinel lymph node biopsies in certain patients with breast cancer
body_summary: The US FDA approved a magnetic device system for guiding lymph node biopsies in patients with breast cancer undergoing mastectomy. The Magtrace and Sentimag Magnetic Localization System uses magnetic detection to identify specific lymph nodes for surgical removal. Dr. Binita Ashar, director of the FDA's Division of Surgical Devices, stated that sentinel lymph node biopsies are crucial for determining cancer spread and treatment. The system was compared to a control method in a trial of 147 patients, with a detection rate of 94.3% for the Sentimag System. The most common adverse events reported were breast discoloration, cardiac disorder, and potential allergic reaction. The system is contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to iron oxide or dextran compounds and is not recommended for patients with metal implants in the axilla or chest.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. on voluntary recalls of Ritz, Goldfish and other products issued out of an abundance of caution
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is working with Mondelēz International, Inc., Pepperidge Farm Inc., and Flowers Foods, Inc. to initiate voluntary recalls of certain products due to a potential Salmonella contamination risk. Recalled products include Mondelēz's Ritz cheese sandwiches and Ritz Bits cheese products, certain Pepperidge Farm's Goldfish, and Flowers Foods' Swiss Rolls. The recalls are being initiated out of an abundance of caution, with no evidence of illness or contamination at this time. The FDA believes these products may contain a common whey ingredient supplied by Associated Milk Producers Inc. that may have been contaminated with Salmonella. The agency is investigating the potential risk and closely monitoring reported cases of food-related illness.

title: FDA continues taking key actions on bulk drug substances used for compounding to advance the regulatory framework governing compounded drugs and to protect patients
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is announcing actions to protect public health related to the compounding of human drug products. The FDA is issuing an alert warning about the bulk drug substance cesium chloride, which carries significant safety risks for patients. The agency is also taking steps to implement the statutory requirements for bulk drug substances used in compounding. The FDA is collaborating with universities to gather and analyze information important for developing the list of bulk drug substances that may be used in compounding. The agency is updating the categories of substances subject to its interim policies on compounding with bulk drug substances. The FDA intends to move cesium chloride to category 2 under its interim policy, raising significant safety risks in compounding. The agency will take regulatory action, such as issuing a warning letter or seizing product, if it encounters a compounder using a substance in category 2.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on manufacturer announcement to halt Essure sales in the U.S.; agency’s continued commitment to postmarket review of Essure and keeping women informed
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) was notified by Bayer that the Essure permanent birth control device will no longer be sold or distributed after December 31, 2018. This decision follows the FDA's patient safety action in April, restricting the sale and distribution of Essure due to reports of serious adverse events associated with its use. The FDA has been investigating these reports and has taken steps to address patient safety concerns, including conducting a post-market surveillance study and requiring Bayer to add a boxed warning to the labeling and a Patient Decision Checklist. As of February 2018, there was a 70% decline in sales of Essure in the US. The FDA will continue to monitor adverse events reported to its database and will communicate publicly on any new findings or concerns. Bayer will continue to enroll new participants in the post-market study, and the FDA will work with the company to determine how to move forward.

title: FDA approves first targeted treatment for patients with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia who have a certain genetic mutation
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved Tibsovo tablets for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who have a specific genetic mutation. Tibsovo is a targeted therapy that fills an unmet need for patients with AML who have an IDH1 mutation. The approval is based on a single-arm trial of 174 adult patients, which showed a complete remission in 32.8 percent of patients. Common side effects include fatigue, increase in white blood cells, joint pain, diarrhea, and shortness of breath. Women who are breastfeeding should not take Tibsovo due to potential harm to a newborn baby. The FDA has also approved the RealTime IDH1 Assay, a companion diagnostic for detecting the IDH1 mutation. The agency granted Fast Track and Priority Review designations and Orphan Drug designation for Tibsovo.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on agency’s efforts to encourage the development of and broaden access to generic versions of opioid analgesics that are formulated to deter abuse
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is encouraging the development of opioid analgesic products with abuse-deterrent formulations (ADFs). These formulations are designed to make certain types of abuse more difficult. The FDA recognizes that ADFs are not "abuse-proof" and do not prevent addiction, overdose, or death. The agency is posting new product-specific guidances to support the development of generic ADF opioid products, which are currently only available as brand-name products due to their higher cost. The guidances recommend specific studies for abuse deterrence evaluations and are part of the FDA's efforts to encourage the development of safe and effective generic products. The FDA aims to decrease the rate of new addiction and make the misuse and abuse of these drugs more difficult.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the formation of a new work group to develop focused drug importation policy options to address access challenges related to certain sole-source medicines with limited patient availability, but no blocking patents or exclusivities
body_summary: The FDA is examining whether allowing the short-term importation of foreign versions of critical medicines can complement its efforts to support patient access during shortages. The FDA wants to explore policy frameworks that would involve importing drugs under specific circumstances, with adequate assurances of safety and effectiveness. The goal is to balance near-term access with long-term safety and competition. The agency will consider various factors, including statutory requirements, safety and effectiveness assessments, and maintaining incentives for manufacturers seeking FDA approval. The policy would be temporary and narrowly tailored to avoid risks of counterfeits and unsafe drugs. The FDA aims to advance multiple FDA-approved versions of each medically important drug and promote a stable, safe, and effective competition.

title: Statement from FDA warning about significant health risks of contaminated illegal synthetic cannabinoid products that are being encountered by FDA
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has become aware of reports of severe illnesses and deaths resulting from the use of synthetic cannabinoid products contaminated with brodifacoum, a long-acting anticoagulant. These products, sold as substitutes for marijuana under names like "K2" and "Spice," pose significant public health concerns. The FDA has previously worked with the DEA to place synthetic cannabinoids in Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act. However, despite efforts, entities continue to manufacture and distribute these products, often with added brodifacoum, which poses severe health risks due to its potential to cause severe bleeding. In recent months, hundreds of individuals have been hospitalized, and several related deaths have occurred. The FDA is warning individuals to avoid using synthetic marijuana products, especially those contaminated with brodifacoum, and is urging healthcare providers to be aware of the risks and consider synthetic cannabinoid exposure when treating patients with unexplained bleeding. The FDA also warns of potential contamination of donated blood products, given brodifacoum's long-acting vitamin K antagonist activity.

title: FDA approves first cancer drug through new oncology review pilot that enables greater development efficiency
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Kisqali (ribociclib) in combination with an aromatase inhibitor for the treatment of pre/perimenopausal or postmenopausal women with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer. This approval is part of two new pilot programs aimed at improving the efficiency and rigor of the FDA's review process for cancer drugs. The first program, Real-Time Oncology Review, allows for earlier review of clinical trial data, while the second program provides a templated Assessment Aid to facilitate a more streamlined review process. The FDA used these new approaches to approve Kisqali in combination with fulvestrant for the treatment of postmenopausal women with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer. The approval was granted less than one month after the June 28 submission date, several months ahead of the goal date.

title: Remarks from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., as prepared for delivery at the Brookings Institution on the release of the FDA’s Biosimilars Action Plan
body_summary: The US FDA is releasing a Biosimilars Action Plan to promote competition and affordability in the biologic market. The plan aims to reduce costs and enhance patient access, with the goal of reducing time, uncertainty, and cost. The FDA recognizes the need for a payment system that takes advantage of price competition. Estimates suggest that biosimilar competition could save $54 billion to $250 billion from 2017 to 2026. The plan includes four key strategies: improving development and approval processes, maximizing scientific and regulatory clarity, developing effective communications, and reducing gaming of FDA requirements. The FDA seeks to strengthen partnerships with regulatory authorities in Europe, Japan, and Canada, and update the Purple Book and FDA review tools to improve efficiency.

title: New York-based food processors agree to stop food preparation operations due to food safety violations
body_summary: Two New York-based food processing companies, Euroline Foods, LLC and Royal Seafood Baza, Inc., have agreed to stop preparing food products due to contamination with Listeria monocytogenes (L. mono) at their facility. A consent decree, entered on July 16, 2018, by U.S. District Judge Brian M. Cogan, prohibits the companies from receiving, preparing, and distributing foods that present a L. mono hazard until they meet certain requirements. The companies, co-owned by Eduard Shnayder, Syoma Shnayder, and Albert Niyazov, and their manager Oleg Polischouk, must retain an independent laboratory to collect and analyze environmental and finished food samples for L. mono, develop a program to control L. mono, and take other corrective actions. The FDA found widespread L. mono contamination at the facility and took action to protect Americans. The companies are not allowed to bring contaminated products to market, but can distribute sealed and enclosed food that is in compliance with the FD&C Act.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. on new efforts to empower consumers by advancing access to nonprescription drugs
body_summary: The FDA is launching a new effort to increase access to nonprescription drug products, aiming to empower consumers to self-treat common conditions and potentially some chronic conditions. The goal is to lower costs for the healthcare system and provide greater efficiency and empowerment for consumers. The FDA will consider innovative approaches, such as digital health technologies, to support consumers in safely self-selecting and using certain drugs. The agency will review two approaches: developing labeling in addition to the Drug Facts Labeling (DFL) and implementing additional conditions to ensure safe and effective use. The FDA will ensure that products receive a robust scientific review to maintain its gold standard for safety and effectiveness. The agency plans to continue this effort with proposed rulemaking and will provide additional information as needed.

title: FDA warns of imposters sending consumers fake warning letters
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is warning consumers about counterfeit warning letters that are linked to an international extortion scam. These fake letters claim the FDA has determined that there are drug violations based on a review of parcels and social media accounts. Consumers who receive such letters are advised to contact the FDA Internet Pharmacy Task Force for assistance. The FDA generally does not issue warning letters to individuals who purchase medicines online and urges consumers to be on alert that these letters are probably fake and part of a scam. The agency is also warning consumers about the dangers of purchasing medicines from illegal online pharmacies, which can pose health risks due to counterfeit or contaminated products, data breaches, and harassment.

title: FDA approves the first drug with an indication for treatment of smallpox
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved TPOXX (tecovirimat), the first drug with an indication for the treatment of smallpox, a contagious and sometimes fatal infectious disease. TPOXX provides an additional option in case smallpox is used as a bioweapon. The drug was approved under the FDA's Animal Rule, which allows efficacy findings from animal studies to support an FDA approval. The safety of TPOXX was evaluated in 359 healthy human volunteers without a smallpox infection, with side effects including headache, nausea, and abdominal pain. The FDA granted approval of TPOXX to SIGA Technologies Inc., in collaboration with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services' Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (BARDA).

title: FDA announces voluntary recall of several medicines containing valsartan following detection of an impurity
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is alerting health care professionals and patients of a voluntary recall of several drug products containing the active ingredient valsartan, used to treat high blood pressure and heart failure, due to an impurity called N-nitrosodimethylamine (NDMA). The recall affects products supplied by Zhejiang Huahai Pharmaceuticals, a company that has stopped distributing its valsartan active pharmaceutical ingredient (API). The FDA is working with affected companies to reduce or eliminate the valsartan API impurity from future products. Patients taking the recalled valsartan-containing medicines should continue taking their medicine until they have a replacement product. The FDA's review is ongoing and has included investigating the levels of NDMA in the recalled products, assessing the possible effect on patients who have been taking them.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on formation of a new drug shortages task force and FDA’s efforts to advance long-term solutions to prevent shortages
body_summary: The FDA is establishing a new Drug Shortages Task Force to address ongoing shortages of medically necessary products. Led by Keagan Lenihan, the task force will explore holistic solutions to underlying causes of shortages. The task force will build on existing work, including the Food and Drug Administration Safety and Innovation Act of 2012, and consider structural solutions across the pharmaceutical industry, healthcare providers, payors, and government regulators. The FDA's employees work behind-the-scenes to anticipate and mitigate drug shortages, collaborating with manufacturers to prevent 145 shortages in 2017. The agency aims to ensure patients have access to needed drugs, and the task force will report on its progress to prevent and mitigate drug shortages.

title: FDA expands its support for states to advance implementation of produce safety activities
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced new cooperative agreements with Hawaii, Kentucky, and Mississippi, and renewed agreements with 43 other states to support the implementation of the FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) Produce Safety Rule. The rule establishes science-based minimum standards for the safe growing, harvesting, packing, and holding of fruits and vegetables. The FDA is providing $32.5 million in funding to help states implement produce safety standards in their farming communities. This funding is part of the agency's mission to protect and promote public health. The cooperative agreements are a key part of implementing a modern produce safety system and will support farmers through training, guidance, and inspections.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. on agency’s efforts to advance development of gene therapies
body_summary: The FDA has issued a new framework for gene therapies, including draft guidance documents for diseases such as hemophilia, retinal disorders, and rare diseases. The framework aims to foster the development of safe and effective gene therapies while ensuring patient safety. Three new draft guidance documents have been issued: Human Gene Therapy for Hemophilia, Human Gene Therapy for Retinal Disorders, and Human Gene Therapy for Rare Diseases. The documents provide recommendations on clinical trial design, preclinical considerations, and manufacturing issues related to gene therapy products. The US FDA is updating its guidance on human gene therapy products to promote safe and effective development, with the aim of building confidence in gene therapy and advancing treatments for debilitating diseases.

title: Federal judge enters consent decree against Minnesota dairy farm for drug residue violations
body_summary: U.S. District Judge Wilhelmina M. Wright entered a consent decree of permanent injunction against Todd & Patty Meech Dairy Farm and its owners, Todd Meech and Patty Meech, for introducing adulterated meat into interstate commerce and failing to comply with federal requirements for administering drugs to food-producing animals. The consent decree prohibits the defendants from delivering animals and meat into the food supply, unless they meet certain requirements. The requirements include establishing systems to prevent the sale or distribution of animals with high levels of animal drugs and improving drug inventory and animal identification records. The FDA must inspect and certify the farm's compliance before it can resume business operations related to meat production. The permanent injunction does not prohibit the sale of milk, as there was no evidence of adulteration. The FDA has approximately 500 cattle and has a history of violations, including failing to maintain adequate treatment records.

title: FDA updates warnings for fluoroquinolone antibiotics on risks of mental health and low blood sugar adverse reactions
body_summary: The US FDA is requiring safety labeling changes for fluoroquinolone antibiotics to strengthen warnings about mental health side effects and serious blood sugar disturbances. The FDA has reviewed adverse event reports and case reports and found a range of mental health side effects, including disturbances in attention, disorientation, and delirium, which will be listed separately in the labeling. The agency also requires explicit reflection of the potential risk of coma with hypoglycemia in the Blood Glucose Disturbances subsection of the labeling. The FDA first added a Boxed Warning to fluoroquinolones in 2008 and has made similar updates in 2011 and 2013. The agency is committed to keeping risk information current and comprehensive to ensure informed decisions about fluoroquinolone use.

title: FDA takes action to support American military personnel by granting an authorization for freeze-dried plasma product to enable broader access while the agency works toward approval of the product
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted an emergency use authorization (EUA) to the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) to enable the emergency use of Pathogen-Reduced Leukocyte-Depleted Freeze-Dried Plasma manufactured by the Centre de Transfusion Sanguine des Armées. The authorization supports access to this product in emergency situations involving military combat, where plasma is not available or practical. The product can be used to treat hemorrhage or coagulopathy in military personnel. The FDA Commissioner, Scott Gottlieb, M.D., said that the agency is committed to expediting the development and availability of safe and effective medical products for the military. The authorization was granted in response to a DoD request and is part of the FDA's effort to prioritize the development of medical products for the U.S. military.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on balancing access to appropriate treatment for patients with chronic and end-of-life pain with need to take steps to stem misuse and abuse of opioids
body_summary: The US FDA is addressing the opioid epidemic by balancing access to opioids with efforts to reduce addiction. The agency is holding a Patient-Focused Drug Development meeting to gather patient perspectives on chronic pain treatment. The FDA is releasing a revised blueprint for opioid training, requiring education on non-opioid alternatives and extending it to pharmacists and nurses. The agency is also launching an innovation challenge for medical devices and creating guidance documents to promote the development of non-addictive pain medications. To combat the crisis, the FDA is taking steps to address the misuse of kratom and stem the flow of illegal opioids, particularly through the mail. The goal is to support rational prescribing practices and new treatment options without addictive opioids.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on June 12-13, 2018, ratifying by unanimous vote the Open Market Desk's domestic transactions over the intermeeting period. The Committee discussed labor market conditions, inflation expectations, and monetary policy, agreeing to raise the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 1-3/4 to 2 percent. The economy was seen as strong, with labor market conditions strengthening further, driven by a strong labor market, stimulative policies, and accommodative financial conditions.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. and FDA Deputy Commissioner for Foods and Veterinary Medicine Stephen Ostroff, M.D., on the ongoing risk of salmonella in kratom products
body_summary: The FDA has concluded its months-long investigation into a large outbreak of salmonellosis linked to kratom-containing products. In February, the CDC PulseNet identified an outbreak involving 24 people, which was later found to be linked to kratom consumption. The investigation revealed that 42 out of 81 samples of kratom collected and tested were contaminated with salmonella, a one in two chance for users. This high contamination rate shows that a significant proportion of kratom products may be contaminated with salmonella. The investigation found that kratom is grown, harvested, and processed in problematic conditions in southeast Asia, which creates an environment for widespread contamination. The FDA strongly discourages the public from consuming kratom, citing its addictive properties and lack of proven medical uses. The agency has issued mandatory recall orders for contaminated products and is taking steps to protect the public health.

title: FDA approves novel device for treating breathing difficulty from severe emphysema
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved the Zephyr Endobronchial Valve (Zephyr Valve) device to treat severe emphysema.
