This device is a less invasive treatment option for patients with severe symptoms that have not improved from taking medicines. The device was designed to prevent air from entering damaged lung areas and allow trapped air and fluids to escape, relieving pressure. In a multi-center study of 190 patients, 47.7% of those treated with Zephyr Valves experienced a 15% improvement in pulmonary function scores, compared to 16.8% of those in the control group. The device is contraindicated for patients with active lung infections, allergies, and certain medical conditions. The FDA granted Breakthrough Device designation to expedite evidence generation and review.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on developments in the romaine outbreak investigation, recent outbreaks and the use of modern tools to advance food safety
body_summary: The FDA, CDC, and Arizona state officials are investigating a romaine lettuce E. coli O157:H7 outbreak linked to the Yuma region. Genetic analysis of canal water and E. coli samples suggests the bacteria may have come from the water source. The investigation aims to determine how the bacteria entered the water and contaminated the lettuce. The FDA has improved its detection and solution capabilities through new technologies and laboratory techniques, including whole genome sequencing, which has enabled precise tracking of outbreaks. The FDA is leveraging its GenomeTrakr network to link illnesses to potential food sources and strengthen its food safety program through the Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA), a shift towards prevention and faster recall of contaminated products.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on agency’s continued efforts relating to compounded drugs for patients who cannot use an FDA-approved drug
body_summary: The US Department of Justice has announced numerous health care fraud enforcement actions targeting schemes billing reimbursors for medically unnecessary compounded drugs, including compounded pain and scar creams. The FDA is aware of pharmacies compounding topical pain creams with multiple ingredients, often including active ingredients in FDA-approved drugs. The agency intends to improve information available about compounded topical pain creams and is taking steps to ensure outsourcing facilities compound drugs for clinical need. The FDA is inspecting compounding facilities to assess whether drugs copied from FDA-approved drugs are being compounded for patients who could use an FDA-approved drug.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA’s efforts to collaborate with internet stakeholders to stop the illegal sale of opioids online
body_summary: The US government is taking steps to address the growing public health crisis of opioid addiction and abuse, which is contributing to overdose deaths. To confront this crisis, the FDA is working with internet stakeholders, including tech companies, academic researchers, and advocacy groups, to stop the illegal sale of opioids online. The FDA hosted an Online Opioid Summit to discuss the issue and explore ways to utilize big data solutions, artificial intelligence, and consumer education to tackle the problem. The summit aimed to bring together internet stakeholders and the FDA to develop shared solutions and foster a collaborative approach. The FDA has taken steps to enhance its vigilance against illicit activity on the internet, including criminal enforcement work, and will focus additional resources behind these efforts. The summit marked the beginning of an ongoing dialogue to address the problem of opioids being illegally sold online, and the FDA seeks to work with internet companies to implement solutions and share data.

title: Statement on National HIV Testing Day
body_summary: The U.S. government recognizes the progress made in fighting HIV and acknowledges the importance of getting tested. Early detection is crucial in containing the spread of the virus. Medical advances have enabled over 1 million Americans affected by HIV to live longer and healthier lives. In June 2017, the FDA approved generic medications that significantly reduce the risk of infection. Despite this progress, 40,000 people were diagnosed with HIV in the U.S. in 2016, with those aged 20-29 receiving more than a third of those diagnoses. In 2016, 44% of people living with HIV aged 13-24 were unaware they had the virus. National HIV Testing Day is a reminder that those unaware of their status are at risk of spreading the disease and missing life-saving treatments. The government encourages all Americans to invest in their health and be aware of their HIV status to lead healthier and longer lives.

title: FDA Approves First Drug Comprised of an Active Ingredient Derived from Marijuana to Treat Rare, Severe Forms of Epilepsy
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Epidiolex (cannabidiol) oral solution for the treatment of seizures associated with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and Dravet syndrome in patients two years of age and older. This is the first FDA-approved drug containing a purified drug substance derived from marijuana. Epidiolex was studied in three randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trials involving 516 patients, demonstrating effectiveness in reducing seizure frequency. Common side effects include sleepiness, sedation, and lethargy, as well as liver enzyme elevations and diarrhea. The FDA granted Priority Review, Fast-Track, and Orphan Drug designations for this application. Approval was granted to GW Research Ltd.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA’s new steps to advance health through improvements in nutrition under the agency’s Nutrition Innovation Strategy
body_summary: The FDA plans to modernize food labels as part of its Nutrition Innovation Strategy, aiming to reduce chronic disease burden through smart diet choices and improve nutrition information. A public meeting on July 26 will discuss the strategy with industry, nutrition experts, and consumers to gather feedback. The FDA seeks to update definitions of "healthy" and "standards of identity," simplify ingredient labels, and leverage nutrition to advance public health. The goal is to empower consumers with modernized labels and provide incentives for manufacturers to produce healthier options. The agency is also soliciting feedback on effective ways to educate consumers about the relationship between their dietary choices and health risks, as part of its efforts to promote healthy dietary choices through science-based initiatives.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the importance of conducting proper research to prove safe and effective medical uses for the active chemicals in marijuana and its components
body_summary: The FDA approved a purified form of cannabidiol (CBD) for the treatment of seizures associated with two rare, severe forms of epilepsy in patients two years of age and older. This approval is based on well-controlled clinical trials evaluating the use of this compound in the treatment of a specific condition. The purified form of CBD has been shown to meet rigorous standards, providing a new treatment option for patients. This approval demonstrates the importance of advancing sound scientific research to investigate ingredients derived from marijuana, leading to the development of new therapies.

title: FDA permits marketing of first catheter-based systems used to create vascular access for hemodialysis patients
body_summary:
The US FDA has permitted the marketing of two catheter-based devices to create connections for patients with chronic kidney disease who need hemodialysis. The FDA granted marketing authorization for the Ellipsys Vascular Access System and the everlinQ endoAVF System. These devices are designed to create arteriovenous (AV) fistulas percutaneously, allowing for less-invasive vascular access options. 

The Ellipsys Vascular Access System has been reviewed in a non-randomized study of 103 patients, with 92 (89.3%) meeting the criteria for a usable AV fistula within three months. Almost all patients required an additional procedure in the first 12 months to maintain the fistula. 

The everlinQ endoAVF System has also been reviewed, with 52 (86.7%) patients meeting the criteria for a usable AV fistula within three months. The FDA has a new regulatory classification for these devices, which may affect future devices with the same intended use.

title: FDA approves automated insulin delivery and monitoring system for use in younger pediatric patients
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has expanded the approval of the MiniMed 670G hybrid closed loop system, a diabetes management device, to include individuals aged 7 to 13 with type 1 diabetes. The device, originally approved for patients 14 years and older, automatically monitors glucose levels and provides basal insulin doses with minimal user input. The FDA evaluated data from a clinical trial involving 105 individuals aged 7 to 11 years old, finding no serious adverse events associated with use of the device. Risks include hypoglycemia, hyperglycemia, and skin irritation. The FDA requires a post-market study to evaluate device performance in real-world settings in children between 7 and 13 years old. The device is not approved for use in children 6 years old or younger and those requiring less than eight units of insulin per day.

title: FDA approves first continuous glucose monitoring system with a fully implantable glucose sensor and compatible mobile app for adults with diabetes
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the Eversense Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) system for people 18 years old and older with diabetes. The system, developed by Senseonics, Inc., includes a fully implantable sensor that can be worn for up to 90 days. The FDA Commissioner, Scott Gottlieb, stated that the approval of this seamless digital system is a vivid illustration of the potential for digital technologies to improve patient care. The system uses a novel light-based technology to measure glucose levels and send information to a mobile app. Clinical study data showed that the proportion of individuals experiencing serious adverse events was less than 1 percent. The FDA has granted approval to Senseonics, Inc. and is creating a new regulatory approach for software products, including mobile medical apps. The Eversense CGM system has the potential to help patients manage diabetes by providing accurate and timely glucose level information.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new guidance to help manufacturers implement protections against potential attacks on the U.S. food supply
body_summary: The FDA is taking steps to prevent intentional contamination of the US food supply, which poses a significant threat to public health. The FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) has granted the agency new authorities and resources to strengthen oversight. In 2016, the FDA released a final rule to address intentional adulteration hazards, including terrorism. The rule requires food facilities to implement risk-reducing strategies for vulnerable processes. To support compliance, the FDA is releasing draft guidance on food defense plans, vulnerability assessments, and mitigation strategies. The goal is to provide clarity and predictability for manufacturers while ensuring the new requirements are cost-effective. The FDA is committed to working with stakeholders, including Congress, other federal agencies, and state and local governments, to protect the American food supply.

title: Statement from Douglas Throckmorton, M.D., deputy center director for regulatory programs in FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, on the agency’s response to ongoing drug shortages for critical products
body_summary: The FDA is addressing shortages of medically necessary medications, including IV fluids, opioid analgesics, and EpiPen. Key shortages include an IV fluid shortage in Puerto Rico after hurricanes, which is improving as manufacturers increase production and temporarily import products. A shortage of injectable opioid analgesics is also occurring due to production delays and quality issues at a Pfizer facility, with the FDA working with other companies to increase production. Additionally, an EpiPen supply shortage is caused by regional supply disruptions and manufacturer issues, with the FDA working closely with Mylan to resolve the issue. The FDA prioritizes the resolution of these shortages and provides updates on its website. Mylan has established a customer service number to help pharmacies and patients locate EpiPens. The FDA expects the issue to be short-term, given the nearly four billion drugs ordered annually, and works to mitigate and prevent drug shortages through industry cooperation, communication, and regulatory actions.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. and FDA Deputy Commissioner Anna Abram on emerging food innovation, “cultured” food products
body_summary:
The FDA announced a public meeting to discuss the opportunities and challenges of cultured food products made from animal cell culture technology. The meeting aims to foster dialogue regarding these emerging food technologies and their regulatory considerations. The FDA has jurisdiction over products made from animal cell culture technology under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.

The development of cultured food products involves complex technical challenges, including the growth medium used to multiply cells and ensure differentiation into the correct cell types. The FDA evaluates microbial, algal, and fungal cells generated by large-scale culture and uses its existing regulatory tools and policies to ensure food safety.

The July 12 meeting will provide an opportunity for the FDA to share its initial thinking on regulating these products, discuss potential benefits and challenges, and engage with stakeholders. The FDA Science Board will also be leveraged during their October meeting to inform the agency's approach to these novel products.

The FDA is committed to ensuring the safety of the nation's food supply and looks forward to the public meeting and continued dialogue with stakeholders to gather information and exchange ideas about this new sector.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the agency’s efforts to better equip consumers with nutritional information about dietary fiber in their food
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration is taking steps to ensure consumers have access to updated, science-based information to make informed dietary choices. In March, the FDA announced a comprehensive Nutrition Innovation Strategy to reduce preventable death and disease related to poor nutrition. Part of this effort includes overhauling the Nutrition Facts label, the first change in over 20 years.

The FDA has issued decisions on citizen petitions regarding additional dietary fibers, including mixed plant cell wall fibers, arabinoxylan, alginate, inulin, and seven other fibers. These fibers can be counted as fiber on the Nutrition Facts label, and food manufacturers can declare them on the label to empower consumers to choose healthful diets.

The FDA is also working to provide clear expectations for industry to meet the new labeling requirements, while maintaining an approach grounded in rigorous science. The agency has issued new guidance allowing food manufacturers to count these fibers in their labeling, and has expressed intent to exercise enforcement discretion to permit their use pending completion of rulemaking.

The FDA's goal is to ensure consumers can trust that the latest food products offer real health benefits, and to empower consumers to make positive changes in their diets. The agency believes that access to reliable, science-based information about food and diets can help reduce chronic diseases and alleviate health disparities through improved nutrition.

title: FDA approves first generic versions of Suboxone sublingual film, which may increase access to treatment for opioid dependence
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the first generic versions of Suboxone sublingual film for the treatment of opioid dependence. Commissioner Scott Gottlieb stated that the FDA is taking steps to advance the development of improved treatments and make these medicines accessible to patients. The FDA has also taken steps to address the stigma associated with opioid replacement therapy, highlighting that medication-assisted treatment (MAT) is often the most effective approach for opioid dependence. The FDA has approved generic versions of buprenorphine and naloxone sublingual film, which will be available for use as part of a complete treatment plan.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in May indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a solid rate. Job gains have been strong, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has declined. Recent data suggest that growth of household spending has picked up, while business fixed investment has continued to grow strongly. On a 12-month basis, both overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy have moved close to 2 percent. Indicators of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. The Committee expects that further gradual increases in the target range for the federal funds rate will be consistent with sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective over the medium term. Risks to the economic outlook appear roughly balanced. In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-3/4 to 2 percent. The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting strong labor market conditions and a sustained return to 2 percent inflation. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its maximum employment objective and its symmetric 2 percent inflation objective. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chairman; William C. Dudley, Vice Chairman; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Lael Brainard; Loretta J. Mester; Randal K. Quarles; and John C. Williams.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA’s efforts to foster discovery and development of new tools to fight antimicrobial-resistant infections
body_summary: The US government is taking steps to combat antibiotic-resistant infections, which claim 23,000 lives annually. The FDA and Congress are working together to encourage the development of new antibiotics. To support this effort, the Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designation and a new licensing model for reimbursement have been established. These initiatives aim to create a predictable market for new antibiotics and advance the development of drugs for rare infections. The FDA is issuing draft guidance on the Limited Population Pathway for Antibacterial and Antifungal Drugs (LPAD) pathway, which will consider a drug's benefit-risk assessment and alternative treatments, and offers streamlined clinical development approaches for companies developing drugs under this pathway.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new efforts to advance medical product communications to support drug competition and value-based health care
body_summary: The US Department of Health and Human Services has set forth a blueprint to address rising drug prices, aiming to link payments to drug value and remove regulatory obstacles to value-based purchasing. Secretary Alex Azar announced this plan, highlighting the importance of linking payments to drug value and promoting competitive contracting based on measures of value that matter most to purchasers and patients. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is issuing updated guidance documents to provide clearer guidance on communication between pharmaceutical companies and payors, including information about drug effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness. Two guidance documents are being issued: one addressing communications with payors, and the other addressing communications that are consistent with FDA-required labeling. The goal is to advance public health benefits by facilitating access to cutting-edge medical technologies, reducing overall cost of providing benefits to patients, and promoting access.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new agency efforts to advance the patient voice in medical product development and FDA regulatory decision-making
body_summary: The FDA has issued a draft guidance to inform patients and product developers on principles for collecting comprehensive and representative patient experience data for medical product development and regulatory decision-making. The guidance addresses sampling methods for collecting representative information on patient experience and operationalizing the collection, analysis, and dissemination of patient experience data. The FDA aims to better engage the patient community in the development and regulation of medical products. The guidance is part of the FDA's Patient-Focused Drug Development (PFDD) initiative, which aims to address the need to better enable patients to provide meaningful input into drug and biologic development.

title: Federal judge enters consent decree against Delta Pharma
body_summary: U.S. District Judge Neal B. Biggers entered a consent decree of permanent injunction between the U.S. and Delta Pharma, Inc., and its president Tommy T. Simpson and vice president Charles Michael Harrison. The FDA had alleged that Delta Pharma continued to violate the law despite repeated promises to correct deficiencies. Commissioner Scott Gottlieb stated that the FDA would hold the company accountable under the law while pursuing new policy steps to make it easier for compounders to meet requirements. The consent decree prohibits Delta Pharma from manufacturing or distributing its drugs until they comply with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and FDA regulations. Delta Pharma is required to cease operations until it completes corrective actions, including hiring a qualified independent expert to inspect its facility. The company is registered as an outsourcing facility under section 503B of the FD&C Act and cannot resume operations until it receives authorization from the FDA.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on 2017 National Youth Tobacco Survey results and ongoing FDA efforts to protect youth from the dangers of nicotine and tobacco products
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is taking steps to protect youth from tobacco products, citing declines in overall youth tobacco use since 2017. The agency is examining a policy to render cigarettes minimally or non-addictive to prevent nicotine addiction in future generations. E-cigarettes remain a major concern, with 2.1 million youth using them in 2017, and the agency is conducting a nationwide blitz to prevent tobacco product sales to minors. The agency has issued warning letters to manufacturers, distributors, and retailers for selling e-liquids with false or misleading labeling and advertising. JUUL Labs Inc. and other manufacturers have been required to provide information to examine marketing practices and youth use. The FDA is also conducting focus groups with teens to inform public education efforts. The agency plans to launch a full-scale campaign to prevent youth use of e-cigarettes and is exploring measures to make tobacco products less toxic and appealing to youth.

title: FDA seeks permanent injunction against company selling unapproved hand sanitizers that claim to prevent infections from numerous pathogens
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has filed a complaint against Innovative BioDefense, Inc. and its president and CEO, Colette Cozean, to prohibit the sale of their Zylast topical antiseptics with claims that they are effective against certain pathogens. The FDA claims that these products are drug claims and are regulated as drugs, but have not been proven to be safe and effective. The agency warns that people may use these products with a false sense of safety, leading to potential health risks. The FDA is seeking a permanent injunction to halt the manufacturing, holding, and distribution of the products until they comply with FDA regulations. The complaint was filed after a warning letter in June 2015 and is being brought before the court on behalf of the FDA.

title: FDA Deputy Commissioner for Policy, Planning, Legislation, and Analysis Anna Abram, remarks prepared for testimony before a subcommittee of the U.S. House Committee on Energy and Commerce on the Pandemic and All-Hazards Preparedness Act
body_summary:
Chairman Burgess, Ranking Member Green, and committee members, the FDA is working towards making sure Americans have the medical products needed to protect them from a range of public health threats, including naturally-occurring and deliberate threats. The agency is actively engaged with federal colleagues, medical product developers, and international organizations, including the World Health Organization, to support international response efforts. 

PAHPA, passed in 2006 and reauthorized in 2013, is a key piece of legislation that has strengthened the nation's preparedness and response capabilities to respond to public health emergencies involving chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear threats, as well as emerging infectious disease threats. 

Prior to joining FDA, the speaker worked on health care policy with Senator Richard Burr, serving as Health Policy Director for many years. They collaborated with colleagues serving in the House of Representatives, including this committee. 

PAHPRA recognized the key role FDA plays in emergency preparedness and response and codified FDA's efforts to augment review processes and advance regulatory science to enable better response to public health emergencies and emerging health threats. 

As of the end of fiscal year 2017, FDA has approved, licensed, or cleared 121 medical countermeasures, including 60 Emergency Use Authorizations since 2005. 

FDA has issued final guidance on the development of animal models to support the approval and clearance of medical countermeasures under the Animal Rule, which has led to 13 medical countermeasures being approved under this rule. 

The agency has also been actively implementing new authorities within its Medical Countermeasures Initiative to prioritize the efficient development of safe and effective medical products for U.S. military personnel.

title: FDA and USDA announce key step to advance collaborative efforts to streamline produce safety requirements for farmers
body_summary: The FDA and USDA have aligned their produce safety requirements, making it easier for farmers to comply with the FDA Food Safety Modernization Act's Produce Safety Rule. The alignment, announced by Agriculture Secretary Sonny Perdue and FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, covers areas such as biological soil amendments, worker training, and equipment. The new step aims to streamline produce safety requirements for farmers. The Produce Safety Rule went into effect on January 26, 2016, and requires large farming operations to comply by January 2018. Small and very small farms have additional time to comply. The USDA Harmonized GAP Audit Program will help farmers assess their food safety practices as they prepare to comply with the Produce Safety Rule.

title: FDA takes action against 53 websites marketing unapproved opioids as part of a comprehensive effort to target illegal online sales
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has warned nine online networks operating 53 websites to stop illegally marketing potentially dangerous, unapproved, and misbranded opioid medications, including tramadol and oxycodone. The warning letters were issued to companies that fail to correct the violations may face enforcement action, including product seizure or injunction. 

FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb has stated that the illegal online marketing of unapproved opioids is contributing to the nation's opioid crisis. Patients who buy prescription medicines from illegal online pharmacies may be putting their health at risk due to counterfeit, contaminated, or expired products. 

The networks receiving warning letters include AnonShop, Eassybuyonline, Instabill, ECS-Rx, Medstore.biz, One Stop Pharma, RemedyMart, RxCash.Biz, and TramadolHub. The FDA has requested responses from each company within 10 working days and encourages consumers to report suspected criminal activity.

title: FDA warns companies to stop selling dangerous and illegal pure and highly concentrated caffeine products
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration has issued warning letters to parties responsible for liquidcaffeine.com and Dual Health Body and Mind for illegally selling highly concentrated caffeine products. The FDA considers these products a threat to public health. Commissioner Scott Gottlieb has stated that the agency will enforce the law to protect consumers from these products, which have been linked to at least two deaths.

The recommended safe serving size of highly concentrated caffeine products is 200 milligrams, equivalent to 1/16 of a teaspoon of pure powder. However, the liquidcaffeine.com product contains multiple toxic doses and its labeling incorrectly implies that a safe serving can be measured with a pump not sold with the product. The Dual Health Body and Mind product contains 8 ounces of pure powdered caffeine, which is over 1,000 servings and cannot be accurately measured with common household tools.

The FDA has previously issued guidance that dietary supplements consisting of pure or highly concentrated caffeine in powder or liquid forms are generally unlawful when sold directly to consumers in bulk packaging. The recipients of the warning letters have 15 days to address the violations and prevent them from recurring.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on proposed modernization of FDA’s drug review office
body_summary: The FDA is modernizing its drug evaluation process to address the complexity of novel drugs targeting unmet needs. Director Dr. Janet Woodcock has proposed changes to modernize the Office of New Drugs, aiming to elevate scientists' thought leadership, provide more product-specific guidance documents, and engage external stakeholders, including disease specialists, academic researchers, and regulatory partners. The goal is to improve efficiency, enhance scientific leadership, and promote patient-focused drug development. The proposed changes aim to create a more therapeutic-focused review process, promote internal collaboration, and improve workflow and workforce management.

title: FDA approves first biosimilar to Neulasta to help reduce the risk of infection during cancer treatment
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved Fulphila (pegfilgrastim-jmdb) as the first biosimilar to Neulasta (pegfilgrastim) to decrease the chance of infection in patients with non-myeloid cancer receiving myelosuppressive chemotherapy. Fulphila is approved as an abiosimilar product and has been shown to have no clinically meaningful differences in safety, purity, and potency compared to Neulasta. The FDA granted approval to Mylan GmbH. Serious side effects of Fulphila include bone pain, pain in extremities, and potential tumor growth. The agency prioritizes bringing new biosimilars to patients to promote competition and reduce drug costs.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA’s work to mitigate shortages of intravenous drugs, shorten supply disruptions and better predict vulnerabilities
body_summary: The FDA is addressing drug shortages caused by manufacturing and quality issues, supply chain disruptions, and clinical demand surges. To mitigate shortages, the FDA collaborates with sponsors, explores information sharing, and develops manufacturing reliability technologies. The agency evaluates its authorities to reduce shortages, including expanding risk assessments and contingency plans. The FDA works with industry to prevent shortages, supports facility and product identification, and develops plans to return to adequate production levels.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new policies to reduce the ability of brand drug makers to use REMS programs as a way to block timely generic drug entry, helping promote competition and access
body_summary: The US system for developing new drugs aims to balance access with innovation by rewarding novel innovation through market-based rewards. However, this system sometimes fails to materialize in a timely manner due to tactics by brand drug makers. The FDA requires drug makers to develop Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) for serious risk-associated drugs. REMS requirements can be used to restrict generic entry, but this is not intended to delay competition. To address this issue, the FDA is introducing new policies requiring brand and generic drug makers to develop a single shared REMS program when a generic drug seeks approval. This aims to improve efficiency and prevent brand drug makers from using REMS to block generic entry. The FDA will also issue draft guidance on Developing a Shared System REMS and Waivers of the Single, Shared System REMS Requirement to help generic drug makers navigate the process.

title: FDA approves first artificial iris
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved the first stand-alone prosthetic iris in the US, a surgically implanted device to treat adults and children with an iris completely missing or damaged due to congenital conditions. The CustomFlex Artificial Iris was approved for treating congenital aniridia, a rare genetic disorder, and other conditions such as albinism, traumatic injury, or surgical removal due to melanoma. The device is made of thin, foldable medical-grade silicone and is custom-sized and colored for each individual patient. A non-randomized clinical trial of 389 patients showed significant decreases in light sensitivity and glare, improvement in health-related quality of life, and high patient satisfaction rates. The device is contraindicated in certain conditions, and its approval was granted through a premarket approval application, which is the most stringent type of device marketing application.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on federal preparedness and FDA’s response efforts to the Ebola virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is taking steps to respond to the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The agency has built a strong team of scientists, researchers, and policy experts to prepare the nation for emerging infectious diseases. During the 2014-2015 Ebola outbreak, the FDA advanced the availability of investigational medical countermeasures, including drugs, vaccines, and diagnostic tests. The agency is now employing its experiences and resources to assist in the global response to the current outbreak. The FDA is working with global health authorities, including the World Health Organization (WHO), to provide scientific and regulatory advice to medical product developers and support international response efforts. The agency is focused on advancing the availability of an Ebola vaccine, supporting the development of investigational drugs for treatment, and facilitating the availability of diagnostic tests. The FDA is also committed to protecting consumers from fraudulent products claiming to prevent, treat, or cure Ebola.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the signing of the Right to Try Act
body_summary: The FDA remains committed to enhancing access to promising investigational medicines for patients with serious or life-threatening diseases. The agency has taken steps to improve access to these treatments, allowing patients and families to make informed decisions about their care. The President signed into law the Right to Try Act of 2017, which amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to establish a new pathway for patients diagnosed with life-threatening diseases or conditions who have exhausted approved treatment options. The FDA will implement this law to increase access to unapproved, investigational treatments, while protecting patients' autonomy and safety. The agency will carefully consider decisions about products that can serve as effective treatments for terminal illnesses, and implement the new law consistent with its longstanding values of ensuring patient safety and security.

title: FDA approves new treatment for moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has expanded the approval of Xeljanz (tofacitinib) to include adults with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis. Xeljanz is the first oral medication approved for chronic use in this indication. The approval provides an alternative therapy for a debilitating disease with limited treatment options. The efficacy of Xeljanz for the treatment of moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis was demonstrated in three controlled clinical trials, showing that 10mg of Xeljanz given twice daily induces remission in 17 to 18 percent of patients by week eight. The safety of chronic use of Xeljanz for ulcerative colitis was studied in a 52-week placebo-controlled trial. Common adverse events associated with Xeljanz treatment for ulcerative colitis include diarrhea, elevated cholesterol levels, and headache. Patients treated with Xeljanz are at increased risk for developing serious infections that may lead to hospitalization or death.

title: As part of efforts to combat opioid crisis, FDA launches innovation challenge to spur development of medical devices ‒ including digital health and diagnostics ‒ that target pain, addiction and diversion
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration launched an innovation challenge to develop medical devices, including digital health technologies and diagnostic tests, to address the opioid crisis. The goal is to accelerate the development and review of innovative products to detect, treat, and prevent addiction. The challenge is open to products in any stage of development and is intended to provide incentives for product developers to invest in products addressing addiction. The FDA will accept submissions from June 1, 2018, through September 30, 2018, and will select applicants based on the product's feasibility, potential public health impact, and novelty of the concept.

title: Executive Order 13837—Ensuring Transparency, Accountability, and Efficiency in Taxpayer-Funded Union Time Use
body_summary: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Director has ordered executive branch employees to spend at least 3/4 of their paid time performing agency business or attending training to maintain skills. This decision aims to eliminate unnecessary expenditures and ensure taxpayer-funded union time is used efficiently, in reasonable amounts, and in the public interest. By May 25, 2018, the OPM Director must publish a standardized form for agencies to report on taxpayer-funded union time. The reports must be published by June 30 each year, starting with fiscal year 2019. Agencies have 45 days to implement the order, and each agency head must designate an official to ensure compliance.

title: FDA approves a new treatment for PKU, a rare and serious genetic disease
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Palynziq (pegvaliase-pqpz) for adults with phenylketonuria (PKU), a rare genetic disease affecting about 1 in 10,000 to 15,000 people in the US. The approval comes after two clinical trials showed that Palynziq, a novel enzyme therapy, helps address a significant unmet need in PKU patients with uncontrolled blood phenylalanine concentrations. The safety and efficacy of Palynziq were demonstrated in trials involving patients with blood phenylalanine concentrations greater than 600 µmol/L. The FDA approved Palynziq to BioMarin Pharmaceutical Inc. and requires prescribers, pharmacies, and patients to enroll in a restricted program under a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) due to the risk of anaphylaxis.

title: FDA permits marketing of artificial intelligence algorithm for aiding providers in detecting wrist fractures
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has permitted the marketing of Imagen OsteoDetect, a computer-aided detection and diagnosis software designed to detect wrist fractures in adult patients. The software uses artificial intelligence algorithms to analyze X-ray images and mark the location of fractures. The company submitted studies demonstrating improved detection accuracy and sensitivity when using the software. The FDA reviewed the device through the De Novo premarket review pathway and granted marketing authorization to Imagen.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary:
A joint meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee and the Board of Governors was held on May 1-2, 2018. The manager of the System Open Market Account discussed financial market developments, including a decline in U.S. equity prices, a rise in nominal Treasury yields, and no significant change in expected federal funds rate. The deputy manager briefed on recent federal funds market developments, noting an increase in the effective federal funds rate and discussion of adjusting the interest on excess reserves (IOER) rate to 5 basis points below the top of the target range for the federal funds rate.

The spread of the IOER rate over the effective federal funds rate narrowed to 5 basis points. The Committee discussed making a small technical adjustment to set the IOER rate modestly below the top of the target range, which could be made when the FOMC increases the target range, simplifying communications and emphasizing the IOER rate's role in implementing policy decisions.

The PCE price index increased 2% over 12 months ending March, and core PCE inflation was 1.9%. Consumer price index rose 2.4%, and core CPI inflation was 2.1%. Longer-run inflation expectations were little changed. Real GDP growth picked up in some emerging market economies, but slowed in some advanced foreign economies due to weather factors.

The FOMC raised the federal funds rate by 25 basis points at the March meeting, and market participants expected a further increase at the June meeting. Equity prices declined initially due to trade tensions and technology sector news, but recovered later. Banks reported weaker loan demand across residential real estate categories and consumer credit growth moderated.

Participants viewed recent firming in inflation as providing reassurance it would reach symmetric 2% objective on a sustained basis. Most saw tight labor markets drawing individuals into workforce and supporting their projections of near-2% inflation over medium term. The Federal Open Market Committee maintained the target range for the federal funds rate at 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent, judging that labor market conditions had strengthened and economic activity had been rising at a moderate rate.

Members expected inflation on a 12-month basis to run near the Committee's symmetric 2% objective over the medium term. The next meeting is scheduled for June 12-13, 2018.

title: FDA takes action against the use of OTC benzocaine teething products due to serious safety risk, lack of benefit
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration is warning consumers that over-the-counter teething products containing benzocaine pose a serious risk to infants and children. The agency has announced that OTC oral health products containing benzocaine should no longer be marketed and is asking companies to stop selling these products for teething pain. If companies do not comply, the FDA will initiate a regulatory action to remove these products from the market. The FDA is also requesting that companies add new warnings to all other benzocaine oral health products to describe certain serious risks. 

Benzocaine is marketed to help relieve pain from a variety of conditions such as teething, sore throat, canker sores and irritation of the mouth and gums. The products are sold under the OTC brand names Anbesol, Baby Orajel, Cepacol, Chloraseptic, Hurricaine, Orabase, Orajel and Topex, as well as store brands and generics. 

The agency made specific recommendations to manufacturers in order to protect patients and make sure the most up-to-date drug safety information will appear on drug labels. The FDA is requiring manufacturers of all FDA-approved prescription local anesthetics to standardize warning information about the risk of methemoglobinemia in product labeling across this class of products. 

The FDA recommends parents and caregivers to follow the American Academy of Pediatrics' recommendations for treating teething pain, which include using a teething ring made of firm rubber or gently rubbing or massaging the child's gums. The FDA also previously cautioned parents and caregivers not to give certain homeopathic teething tablets to children and to seek advice from their health care professional for safe alternatives.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new FDA actions to keep consumers safe from the harmful effects of sun exposure, and ensure the long-term safety and benefits of sunscreens
body_summary: The US FDA is updating regulations on nonprescription sunscreens to ensure safe and effective products. The agency aims to balance innovation with consumer protection, following the latest scientific evidence. The FDA is urging industry to conduct research on additional sunscreen active ingredients and is encouraging consumers to be watchful for unscrupulous companies making false claims. Stricter product testing and warning letters have been sent to companies making unproven claims about dietary supplements that claim to protect against sun exposure. A proposed rule will address dosage forms and SPF values, with the aim of bringing safe and effective sunscreen products to the public.

title: FDA warns companies selling illegal, unapproved kratom products marketed for opioid cessation, pain treatment and other medical uses
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued warning letters to three kratom marketers and distributors, Front Range Kratom of Colorado, Kratom Spot of California, and Revibe of Missouri, for selling unapproved kratom products with unproven claims about treating opioid addiction and other medical conditions. The FDA has also warned consumers not to use kratom, which is believed to have properties that expose users to the risks of addiction, abuse, and dependence. The agency has received concerning reports about the safety of kratom and has confirmed salmonella contamination in kratom products distributed by Revibe. The FDA is taking enforcement actions against unscrupulous products to protect public health and has promised to make the approval process more efficient for novel, safe, and effective medical treatments.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new agency efforts to shine light on situations where drug makers may be pursuing gaming tactics to delay generic competition
body_summary: The FDA is making public a list of companies that have potentially blocked access to samples of their branded products, in an effort to improve generic drug development and approval. This list includes companies that have imposed restrictions on distribution or refused to sell samples, citing elements to assure safe use (ETASU) or other reasons. The FDA will take steps to determine the factors at play and provide guidance to generic drug developers. The agency will also notify the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) about these inquiries. The FDA has issued 21 Safety Determination Letters to brand companies, clarifying that there are no REMS-related reasons why samples of their product cannot be provided to generic drug developers. The agency aims to promote access to needed medicines by enhancing generic competition and addressing anticompetitive business practices.

title: FDA approves novel preventive treatment for migraine
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Aimovig (erenumab-aooe) for the preventive treatment of migraine in adults. Aimovig is administered via once-monthly self-injections and works by blocking calcitonin gene-related peptide. The treatment was evaluated in three clinical trials involving 1,897 participants, with results showing a significant reduction in migraine days. The most common side effects reported were injection site reactions and constipation. Aimovig was granted approval to Amgen Inc. by the FDA.

title: FDA requires additional e-cigarette makers to provide critical information so the agency can better examine youth use and product appeal, amid continued concerns around youth access to products
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) sent official requests for information to four e-cigarette manufacturers, requiring them to submit important documents to better understand the youth appeal of these products. The action is part of the FDA's Youth Tobacco Prevention Plan, which aims to protect youth from the dangers of nicotine and tobacco products. The plan includes taking aggressive steps to address youth use of e-cigarettes and other electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS). The FDA has selected these companies based on product attributes that overlap with those of JUUL, including the use of e-liquids with high nicotine concentration and product design features that are intuitive for novice users. The companies have until July 12, 2018, to respond to the agency. The FDA has also expanded its efforts to prevent youth use of e-cigarettes, including a nationwide blitz of brick-and-mortar and online retailers, warning letters to businesses that sold JUUL brand products to minors, and a public education campaign focusing on preventing youth use of e-cigarettes.

title: FDA approves the first non-opioid treatment for management of opioid withdrawal symptoms in adults
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Lucemyra (lofexidine hydrochloride) for the mitigation of withdrawal symptoms to facilitate abrupt discontinuation of opioids in adults. Lucemyra is not a treatment for opioid use disorder (OUD), but can be used as part of a broader, long-term treatment plan for managing OUD. The approval represents the first FDA-approved non-opioid treatment for the management of opioid withdrawal symptoms. The safety and efficacy of Lucemyra was supported by two randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trials of 866 adults meeting Diagnostic and Statistical Manual-IV criteria for opioid dependence.

Lucemyra is an oral, selective alpha 2-adrenergic receptor agonist that reduces the release of norepinephrine. The most common side effects from treatment with Lucemyra include hypotension (low blood pressure), bradycardia (slow heart rate), somnolence (sleepiness), sedation and dizziness. The FDA is requiring 15 postmarketing studies, including both animal and human studies, to support longer-term use and use in children.

The FDA granted this application Priority Review and Fast Track designations, and an independent FDA advisory committee supported the approval of Lucemyra. The approval is part of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services' Five-Point Strategy to Combat the Opioid Crisis.

title: FDA approves first epoetin alfa biosimilar for the treatment of anemia
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Retacrit (epoetin alfa-epbx) as a biosimilar to Epogen/Procrit (epoetin alfa) for treating anemia caused by chronic kidney disease, chemotherapy, or HIV infection. Retacrit is also approved for reducing blood transfusions before and after surgery. The approval is based on data showing Retacrit is highly similar to Epogen/Procrit, with no clinically meaningful differences in safety, purity, and potency. Biosimilar Retacrit has been approved as an abiosimilar, not interchangeable product. The FDA granted approval to Hospira Inc., a Pfizer company.

title: FDA expands approval of Gilenya to treat multiple sclerosis in pediatric patients
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Gilenya (fingolimod) to treat relapsing multiple sclerosis (MS) in children and adolescents aged 10 years and older. This is the first FDA approval of a drug to treat MS in pediatric patients. The drug was first approved in 2010 to treat adults with relapsing MS. The clinical trial evaluating Gilenya in pediatric patients included 214 patients aged 10-17 and showed that 86% remained relapse-free after 24 months of treatment. Serious risks of Gilenya include slowing of heart rate, serious infections, and vision problems. The FDA granted Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy designation for this indication and approved the drug to Novartis.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the Trump Administration’s plan to lower drug prices
body_summary: The Administration is taking a collaborative effort to address the rising cost of drugs. President Trump's bold plan puts patients first in advancing actions to lower list prices. The FDA shares the goal of ensuring quality and affordable care, prioritizing the timely development and approval of generics and biosimilars. The FDA has taken steps as part of the Drug Competition Action Plan, including removing barriers to generic drug development and market entry. In 2017, the FDA approved over 1,000 generic drug applications, and it expects to beat that goal this year. The agency is committed to adopting strong policies to reduce gaming of statutory and regulatory requirements and to address abuses that impede competition. The FDA will continue to work on addressing significant health challenges and implementing new measures as part of a forthcoming Biosimilar Action Plan to promote drug competition and access for patients.

title: La FDA advierte a más empresas que dejen de engañar a los niños con líquidos electrónicos que asemejan alimentos inocuos para los niños, como parte del Plan de Prevención del Tabaquismo Juvenil
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has extended warnings to manufacturers and retailers of electronic liquids used in e-cigarettes that resemble food products, such as cereals, drinks, and pancakes, to prevent them from being sold to children. Dr. Scott Gottlieb, MD, said, "If you're targeting kids, we're going to target you." The FDA has also taken steps to prevent the sale of other 13 manufacturers and retailers of electronic liquids that contain nicotine and resemble food products. The FDA has sent letters to companies requesting answers to how they plan to address the addiction issue. Failure to comply may result in additional penalties, such as seizure or judicial action. The FDA has also expanded its efforts to prevent youth access to e-cigarettes, including a new campaign called "The Real Cost" and a plan to restrict the sale and promotion of e-cigarettes.

title: FDA warns more companies to stop misleading kids with e-liquids that resemble kid-friendly foods as part of Youth Tobacco Prevention Plan
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued four new warning letters to manufacturers and retailers selling e-liquids used in e-cigarettes with labeling and/or advertising that resemble kid-friendly food products. The warning letters follow actions taken last week against 13 other makers and sellers of nicotine-containing e-liquids. The FDA Commissioner, Scott Gottlieb, stated that companies targeting children with these products will be targeted. The products include "Frank 'N Vape," "Chill Purple Grape," and "Unicorn Cakes," which are considered misbranded due to their misleading labeling and advertising. The FDA has requested responses from the companies within 15 working days. The FDA's Youth Tobacco Prevention Plan aims to address all aspects of youth access and appeal of tobacco products, particularly e-cigarettes. The plan includes measures to make tobacco products less toxic and appealing to youth.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the public health benefits from enactment of menu labeling
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) implemented a uniform standard for restaurant menus and takeout foods, providing consistent access to calorie and nutrition information nationwide. This legislation, enacted by Congress, aims to reduce the burden of chronic disease and encourage healthier eating habits. The FDA completed a final guidance document, clarifying how businesses can comply with the new regulation, including flexible options for displaying calories on menus and menu boards. The agency plans to work collaboratively with covered establishments to help them meet the requirements, focusing on educational outreach and providing reasonable opportunities for adjustments. The menu labeling rule is part of the FDA's broader Nutrition Innovation Strategy, which aims to provide consumers with easier access to nutritious foods and encourage the food industry to innovate in producing healthier products.

title: FDA permits marketing of new endoscopic device for treating gastrointestinal bleeding
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has permitted marketing of Hemospray, a new device used to control certain types of bleeding in the gastrointestinal (GI) tract. The device, developed by Wilson-Cook Medical Inc., is intended to treat most types of upper or lower GI bleeding and has stopped bleeding in 95 percent of patients within five minutes. However, re-bleeding was observed in 20 percent of patients and one serious side effect, bowel perforation, was observed in approximately 1 percent of patients. The FDA approved the device through the De Novo remarket review pathway and permits its marketing to treat upper and lower GI bleeding in certain patients.

title: FDA approves new uses for two drugs administered together for the treatment of BRAF-positive anaplastic thyroid cancer
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Tafinlar (dabrafenib) and Mekinist (trametinib), administered together, for the treatment of anaplastic thyroid cancer (ATC) that cannot be removed by surgery or has spread to other parts of the body (metastatic), and has a type of abnormal gene, BRAF V600E (BRAF V600E mutation-positive). This is the first FDA-approved treatment for patients with this aggressive form of thyroid cancer, and the third cancer with this specific gene mutation that this drug combination has been approved to treat. The approval demonstrates that targeting the same molecular pathway in diverse diseases is an effective way to expedite the development of treatments that may help more patients.

Tafinlar and Mekinist are also approved for use, alone or in combination, to treat BRAF V600 mutation-positive metastatic melanoma and BRAF V600E mutation-positive, metastatic non-small cell lung cancer. The efficacy of Tafinlar and Mekinist in treating ATC was shown in an open-label clinical trial, where 57% of patients experienced a partial response and 4% experienced a complete response. The side effects of Tafinlar and Mekinist in patients with ATC are consistent with those seen in other cancers when the two drugs are used together.

Common side effects include fever, rash, chills, headache, joint pain, cough, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and dry skin. Severe side effects include the development of new cancers, growth of tumors, serious bleeding problems, heart problems, severe eye problems, and serious anemia. The FDA granted Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy designation for this indication, and also granted Orphan Drug designation to assist and encourage the development of drugs for rare diseases.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in March indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a moderate rate. Job gains have been strong, on average, in recent months, and the unemployment rate has stayed low. Recent data suggest that growth of household spending moderated from its strong fourth-quarter pace, while business fixed investment continued to grow strongly. On a 12-month basis, both overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy have moved close to 2 percent. Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. The Committee expects that, with further gradual adjustments in the stance of monetary policy, economic activity will expand at a moderate pace in the medium term and labor market conditions will remain strong. Inflation on a 12-month basis is expected to run near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective over the medium term. Risks to the economic outlook appear roughly balanced. In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent. The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting strong labor market conditions and a sustained return to 2 percent inflation. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its objectives of maximum employment and 2 percent inflation. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. The Committee will carefully monitor actual and expected inflation developments relative to its symmetric inflation goal. The Committee expects that economic conditions will evolve in a manner that will warrant further gradual increases in the federal funds rate; the federal funds rate is likely to remain, for some time, below levels that are expected to prevail in the longer run. However, the actual path of the federal funds rate will depend on the economic outlook as informed by incoming data. Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chairman; William C. Dudley, Vice Chairman; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Lael Brainard; Loretta J. Mester; Randal K. Quarles; and John C. Williams.

title: FDA, FTC take action against companies misleading kids with e-liquids that resemble children’s juice boxes, candies and cookies
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) have issued 13 warning letters to manufacturers, distributors, and retailers for selling e-liquids used in e-cigarettes with labeling and/or advertising that resembles kid-friendly food products, such as juice boxes, candy, or cookies. The warning letters also cite companies for illegally selling these products to minors.

FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb stated that no child should be using any tobacco product, and that companies have a responsibility to ensure they aren't putting children in harm's way. The FDA will continue to take action against those who sell tobacco products to youth and market products in this way.

The warning letters include products with names such as "One Mad Hit Juice Box" and "Vape Heads Sour Smurf Sauce", which resemble children's food products. The FTC joined the FDA in issuing the warning letters under Section 5 of the Federal Trade Commission Act.

The FDA has also announced a nationwide blitz of brick-and-mortar and online retailers, and issued warning letters to businesses that sold JUUL brand products to minors. The agency is exploring clear and meaningful measures to make tobacco products less toxic, appealing, and addictive with an intense focus on youth.

title: La FDA y la FTC actúan contra las empresas que engañan a los niños con ‘líquidos electrónicos’ que semejan cartones de jugo, dulces y galletas infantiles
body_summary: The US FDA and FTC issued 13 warning letters to manufacturers, distributors, and retailers selling "e-liquids" in packaging that resembles food, especially to children. Dr. Scott Gottlieb, FDA Commissioner, warned that these products pose a serious risk to children. The FDA and FTC will take measures to prevent the sale of e-liquids to minors and reduce exposure to toxic substances. In 2016, over 2 million middle and high school students used e-cigarettes and flavored tobacco products. The FDA has launched a nationwide advertising campaign and issued warnings to companies selling JUUL products to minors, with proposed regulations including restrictions on flavored products, child-resistant packaging, and labeling to prevent accidental exposure to nicotine.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new enforcement actions and a Youth Tobacco Prevention Plan to stop youth use of, and access to, JUUL and other e-cigarettes
body_summary: The FDA has cited 40 retailers for selling JUUL e-cigarettes to minors as part of a nationwide effort to crack down on youth sales. The agency is taking steps to prevent future generations from becoming addicted to tobacco products, including requiring JUUL Labs to submit documents on product marketing and youth appeal. The FDA plans to invest in science-based campaigns to educate youth about the dangers of tobacco products, with a full-scale e-cigarette prevention effort set to launch in September under the "The Real Cost" brand umbrella. The agency also intends to pursue product standards and regulations for electronic nicotine delivery systems to address known hazards and concerns, with the goal of achieving the greatest public health benefit.

title: Remarks from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., as prepared for testimony before a U.S. Senate Committee on Appropriations on FDA’s Fiscal Year 2019 budget
body_summary:
Chairman Hoeven, Ranking Member Merkley, and Subcommittee members, the President's FY 2019 Budget request for the FDA includes $5.8 billion in total resources, with a $473 million increase in budget authority and $190 million in user fees. The Budget requests new resources to advance critical areas of science, domestic technology, and public health. 

The proposal modernizes generic drug development and review to increase competition, promote generic substitution, and lower drug costs. The Budget also seeks to update generic drug labels and expand real-world evidence for medical products. This includes $100 million to advance the use of real-world experience to inform patient care and expedite medical product development. The proposal aims to enhance patient safety, improve the use of real-world evidence, and make the FDA's oversight more efficient and cost-effective.

title: FDA takes new steps to advance the development of innovative products for treating opioid use disorder
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has released the first of two new draft guidances to support the development of treatment options for people with opioid use disorder (OUD). The first guidance explains the FDA's thinking on drug development and clinical trial design issues for sustained-release "depot" buprenorphine products. HHS Secretary Alex Azar and FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb have emphasized the importance of medication-assisted treatment in treating opioid dependence. The agency's draft guidance focuses on ways drug companies can efficiently explore innovations in depot buprenorphine products. The FDA recommends studies for these products, including efficacy studies and novel endpoints. The agency also intends to issue additional guidance on novel clinical endpoints to support the development of new treatments.

title: FDA authorizes new use of test, first to identify the emerging pathogen Candida auris
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has authorized the first test to identify the emerging pathogen Candida auris (C. auris), which can cause serious infections in hospitalized patients. The FDA permitted marketing for a new use of the BRUKER MALDI Biotyper CA system, which can reliably identify C. auris 100 percent of the time. This system uses matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization (MALDI-TOF) mass spectrometry in combination with a reference organism database. The authorization was granted through the De Novo premarket review pathway, and the FDA plans to propose to exempt certain mass spectrometry microorganism identification system processes from additional premarket review.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new steps to encourage more widespread innovation and development of new treatments for opioid use disorder
body_summary: The FDA is working to address the opioid crisis by prioritizing treatment options for addiction and overdose. The agency aims to improve access to medication-assisted treatments (MAT), such as buprenorphine, to stabilize brain chemistry and reduce cravings. A new draft guidance outlines steps for developing depot buprenorphine products, including streamlined development pathways and novel clinical endpoints. The FDA plans to develop a framework for assessing the effectiveness of MAT treatments, including craving as a relevant endpoint. To support these efforts, the agency is revising a training program for physicians on opioid use disorder treatment, including information on pain management and safe opioid use. The goal is to change the culture of medicine to better prevent new cases of addiction and reduce stigma around MAT use.

title: Federal judge enters consent decree against Cantrell Drug Company
body_summary: U.S. District Judge Kristine G. Baker entered a consent decree of permanent injunction against Cantrell Drug Company of Little Rock, Arkansas, and its CEO James L. McCarley, Jr. The decree prohibits Cantrell and McCarley from manufacturing or distributing drugs until they comply with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) and FDA regulations. The FDA alleges that Cantrell manufactured and distributed adulterated drugs due to insanitary conditions and non-compliance with current good manufacturing practice (CGMP) requirements. The consent decree requires Cantrell to cease operations until it completes corrective actions, including hiring an independent expert to inspect its facility. Cantrell must also receive authorization from the FDA before resuming operations. The company is registered as an outsourcing facility under section 503B of the FD&C Act.

title: Remarks from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. on Fiscal Year 2019 budget request for FDA
body_summary: The FDA has received bipartisan support from the Committee. Last year saw a record-breaking number of medical product approvals, with significant increases in generic drug, novel drug, and medical device approvals. The 2019 budget request includes $5.8 billion in total resources, a 13% increase from FY 2018, to invest in advanced manufacturing, compounding pharmacies, and generic drug review. The budget also funds a knowledge management platform to improve decision-making and scientific rigor. The FDA aims to improve drug development efficiency by lowering costs and increasing predictive accuracy, requiring better regulatory tools, management, and science. With the Committee's continued support, the FDA will protect public health and advance opportunities for Americans to improve their health.

title: FDA approves first therapy for rare inherited form of rickets, x-linked hypophosphatemia
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Crysvita (burosumab-twza), the first drug to treat adults and children ages 1 year and older with x-linked hypophosphatemia (XLH), a rare, inherited form of rickets. XLH causes low levels of phosphorus in the blood, leading to impaired bone growth and development in children and adolescents, and problems with bone mineralization throughout a patient's life. The safety and efficacy of Crysvita were studied in four clinical trials, with 94 percent of adults receiving Crysvita achieving normal phosphorus levels, and 94-100 percent of children achieving normal phosphorus levels with treatment every two weeks. Crysvita was granted Breakthrough Therapy and Orphan Drug designations, and is being developed to treat approximately 3,000 children and 12,000 adults in the United States, who experience symptoms such as bowed legs, short stature, and joint pain.

title: Statement by Dr. Susan Mayne on FDA efforts to reduce consumer exposure to arsenic in rice
body_summary: The US Food and Administration has taken steps to reduce exposure to inorganic arsenic in infant rice cereal. In 2016, the FDA developed a method to distinguish organic from inorganic arsenic in rice and published a risk assessment on the potential health impacts associated with exposure to arsenic from rice and rice products. The agency identified an "action level" of 100 parts per billion for inorganic arsenic in infant rice cereal and asked food manufacturers to take this measure, which is largely achievable. The FDA continues to recommend a variety of grains for pregnant women and infants and notes that non-rice infant cereal options are available. The agency is part of a broader initiative to reduce exposure to toxic elements in food and has created a Toxic Elements Working Group to identify and prioritize efforts to achieve the public health goal of reducing exposure to toxic elements.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new efforts to enhance and modernize the FDA’s approach to medical device safety and innovation
body_summary: The FDA has released the Medical Device Safety Action Plan to enhance device safety and reduce risks. Led by Dr. Jeffrey Shuren, the plan focuses on five key areas: establishing a patient safety net, streamlining postmarket mitigations, spurring innovation towards safer devices, advancing cybersecurity, and integrating pre- and postmarket offices. The plan aims to balance innovation and risk, with initiatives such as a reorganized device safety approach, new regulatory options, and a focus on comparative safety claims. To support this, the FDA seeks authorities and funding, including a proposed CyberMed Safety Expert Analysis Board, to improve data gathering, particularly in women's health, and address cybersecurity vulnerabilities. The FDA prioritizes medical device safety to protect American patients by minimizing risks and advancing device technologies.

title: FDA takes step to protect consumers against dietary supplements containing dangerously high levels of extremely concentrated or pure caffeine
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a new guidance to clarify that dietary supplements containing pure or highly concentrated caffeine in powder or liquid forms are considered unlawful when sold in bulk quantities directly to consumers. The guidance is immediately in effect, and the FDA will take steps to remove illegal products from the market. Highly concentrated and pure caffeine products have been linked to at least two deaths and pose a significant public health threat due to the risk of excessive and potentially dangerous use. The recommended safe serving size of such products is 200 mg of caffeine, but they are often sold in bulk quantities with small serving sizes, leading to a high risk of overuse and misuse.

title: FDA finalizes guidances to accelerate the development of reliable, beneficial next generation sequencing-based tests
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has finalized two guidances for the efficient development of novel DNA scanning technology to diagnose genetic diseases. The guidances provide recommendations for designing, developing, and validating tests that use next-generation sequencing (NGS). Commissioner Scott Gottlieb has stated that these guidances provide a modern and flexible framework to generate data needed to support FDA reviews of NGS-based tests.

The first guidance, "Use of Public Human Genetic Variant Databases," describes an approach where test developers may rely on clinical evidence from FDA-recognized public databases to support clinical claims for their tests. The second guidance, "Considerations for Design, Development, and Analytical Validation of NGS-Based IVDs," provides recommendations for designing, developing, and validating NGS-based tests used to diagnose individuals with suspected genetic diseases.

These guidances aim to facilitate the development and validation of NGS-based tests, which can help identify genetic diseases and guide medical treatments. The FDA has received extensive feedback from stakeholders and has established criteria for genetic health risk tests. The guidances serve as a continuation of the FDA's work creating regulatory efficiencies in the development and review of NGS tests.

title: FDA permits marketing of artificial intelligence-based device to detect certain diabetes-related eye problems
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has permitted the marketing of the first medical device using artificial intelligence to detect diabetic retinopathy in adults with diabetes. Diabetic retinopathy is a leading cause of vision loss among working-age adults. The device, IDx-DR, is a software program that analyzes images of the eye to provide a screening decision, and it was evaluated in a clinical study of 900 patients. The FDA evaluated data from the study, which showed that IDx-DR could accurately detect more than mild diabetic retinopathy 87.4% of the time. The device is designed for use in primary care doctor's offices and does not require a clinician to interpret the images or results. The FDA has granted Breakthrough Device designation to IDx LLC, the company behind the device, to expedite its review and development.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on March 20-21, 2018.
