The committee discussed recent labor indicators showing modest gains, with private-sector job openings and quits increasing slightly. Total industrial production expanded in January and February, while consumer expenditures appeared to rise at a modest pace driven by employment and real disposable personal income growth. Real PCE edged down in January but is expected to increase due to tax refund delivery and lower withholding resulting from tax cuts. The FOMC's balance sheet continued to shrink as scheduled without notable market effects, and financing conditions for non-financial corporations and households remained accommodative. Most participants expected inflation to rise due to arithmetic effect and agreed on raising the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to support strong labor market conditions. The FOMC directed the Desk to roll over at auction principal payments from Treasury securities maturing exceeding $12 billion, and reinvest in agency mortgage-backed securities received exceeding $8 billion, with effective changes starting in April.

title: FDA clears first contact lens with light-adaptive technology
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has cleared the first contact lens to incorporate a technology that darkens the lens in bright light, the Acuvue Oasys Contact Lenses with Transitions Light Intelligent Technology. The lenses are indicated for daily use to correct nearsightedness (myopia) or farsightedness (hyperopia) in people with certain degrees of astigmatism. The lenses contain a photochromic additive that adapts to visible light filtered to the eye based on UV light exposure. The FDA reviewed a clinical study of 24 patients and found no concerns with driving performance or vision while wearing the lenses. The lenses should not be used by patients with certain conditions, such as inflammation or infection, or by those who have previously experienced discomfort from contact lenses. The lenses are intended for daily wear for up to 14 days and should not be used as substitutes for UV protective eyewear. Johnson & Johnson Vision Care, Inc. submitted the product for FDA clearance through the 510(k) pathway, which granted clearance to the FDA.

title: FDA restricts sale and distribution of Essure to protect women and to require that patients receive risk information
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has ordered the restriction of the sale and distribution of the Essure device to ensure that women considering its use are provided with adequate risk information to make informed decisions. The FDA found that some women were not being adequately informed of Essure's risks before getting the device implanted, despite previous efforts to educate patients and doctors about the risks. The FDA is requiring a unique type of restriction, using its authority to restrict the sale and distribution of a device to impose additional requirements needed to provide a reasonable assurance of its safety and effectiveness. The restriction includes a boxed warning and a patient decision checklist to be added to the labeling, which will be legally required when the product is offered to a patient. The device manufacturer, Bayer, is required to implement the restrictions immediately and ensure compliance with the sales restriction. The FDA plans to enforce these requirements and will take appropriate action for a failure to comply, including applicable criminal and civil penalties.

title: FDA orders mandatory recall for kratom products due to risk of salmonella
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has issued a mandatory recall of all food products containing powdered kratom manufactured, processed, packed, or held by Triangle Pharmanaturals LLC due to contamination with salmonella. The recall affects products from various brands, including Raw Form Organics, Molecule Kratom, Chameleon Kratom, Naturally Kratom, Lifted Kratom, Live Well Kratom, and Third Eye Kratom. The FDA advises consumers to discard the products and avoid kratom and its psychoactive compounds, mitragynine and 7-hydroxymitragynine, in any form and from any manufacturer. The recall was issued due to a multi-state outbreak of salmonellosis, which is associated with high hospitalization rates among kratom product users. The FDA is working with the CDC to investigate the outbreak.

title: New York raw milk cheese company ordered to stop sales for food safety violations
body_summary: A federal court has ordered Vulto Creamery LLC to stop manufacturing its ready-to-eat aged soft, semi-soft and hard cheeses until it complies with food safety regulations. On March 30, 2018, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of New York entered a consent decree of permanent injunction against Vulto Creamery LLC and its owner Johannes "Jos" H. Vulto. The FDA moved quickly to get the company to recall and destroy all its cheese products and cease production to prevent further tainted food from harming consumers. FDA Associate Commissioner for Regulatory Affairs Melinda K. Plaisier said the company must demonstrate to the FDA that its products are safe. The consent decree requires Vulto Creamery to retain an independent laboratory, retain an independent expert, and develop a program to control L. mono and eliminate unsanitary conditions at its facility. The FDA, in collaboration with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, investigated a multi-state outbreak of listeriosis linked to Vulto Creamery's soft cheese, resulting in eight infected people from four states and two deaths.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA’s efforts to enhance the patient perspective and experience in drug development and review
body_summary: The FDA is enhancing its benefit-risk assessment and communication in the human drug review process. The agency began this work in 2013 as part of the Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) V, with continued efforts in 2017 and further expanded under 21st Century Cures. An update to the implementation plan, titled "Benefit-Risk Assessment in Drug Regulatory Decision-Making," has been issued, providing an overview of the steps taken and a roadmap for enhancing the Benefit-Risk Framework. The goal is to provide guidance by June 2020 that articulates the FDA's decision-making context and framework for benefit-risk assessment, including how patient experience data can be used to inform benefit-risk assessment. The FDA's Benefit-Risk Framework improves clarity and consistency in communicating drug regulatory decisions, and ensures that patient experience data is integrated into drug development and regulatory decision-making.

title: FDA expands approval of Blincyto for treatment of a type of leukemia in patients who have a certain risk factor for relapse
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted accelerated approval to Blincyto to treat adults and children with B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) who are in remission but still have minimal residual disease (MRD). This is the first FDA-approved treatment for patients with MRD-positive ALL. The approval was granted under the accelerated approval pathway for serious conditions with unmet medical need. A single-arm clinical trial showed that 70 patients achieved undetectable MRD, and over half of the patients remained alive and in remission for at least 22.3 months. The side effects of Blincyto are consistent with those seen in other uses of the drug, including infections, fever, headache, and low levels of certain blood cells. Serious risks of Blincyto include infections, pancreatitis, and cytokine release syndrome. The FDA granted this application Priority Review and Orphan Drug designation, and approved the drug for Amgen Inc.

title: Federal judge approves consent decree with New York dietary supplement manufacturer Riddhi USA
body_summary: A federal court has ordered Riddhi USA, Inc. to stop selling its dietary supplements until the company comes into compliance with FDA regulations. The U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York entered a consent decree of permanent injunction with Riddhi USA, Inc. and its president and owner Mohd M. Alam. The decree requires the defendants to cease manufacturing or distributing dietary supplements due to repeated violations of good manufacturing practice regulations and failure to provide required information on product labels. The FDA issued a warning letter to Riddhi USA in 2016 after a facility inspection identified violations. The consent decree also prohibits Riddhi USA from resuming operations unless it hires an expert to ensure compliance with regulations and receives FDA approval.

title: Federal judge approves consent decree with Florida company that sold unapproved new drugs and misbranded drugs
body_summary: A federal court ordered MyNicNaxs, LLC, the company owned by Chevonne Torres, to stop selling drugs and dietary supplements until they comply with the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act) and other requirements. The U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Florida entered a consent decree of permanent injunction between the US and MyNicNaxs, LLC, Chevonne Torres, and Michael Banner, an officer at the company. The company marketed weight loss and sexual enhancement products, some of which tested positive for undeclared active pharmaceutical ingredients. The FDA's Office of Compliance director, Donald D. Ashley, stated that marketing such products poses serious safety risks to consumers. FDA tests showed the products contained ingredients like Sildenafil, Sibutramine, and Phenolphthalein, which are subject to the FD&C Act. The complaint alleges that these products are drugs because they are intended to cure or treat disease, and are misbranded due to false and misleading labeling. The permanent injunction requires the defendants to cease distributing unapproved new drugs or misbranded drugs, and prohibits them from receiving, manufacturing, or distributing drugs until they receive a written notification from the FDA. In 2015, the FDA issued a warning letter to MyNicNaxs after discovering they continued to sell unapproved new drugs.

title: FDA authorizes first fully interoperable continuous glucose monitoring system, streamlines review pathway for similar devices
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has permitted the marketing of the Dexcom G6 integrated continuous glucose monitoring system for children aged two and older and adults with diabetes. This is the first type of continuous glucose monitoring system permitted by the agency to be used as part of an integrated system with other compatible medical devices and electronic interfaces. The Dexcom G6 system is classified as a class II device and is subject to certain criteria called special controls. This authorization enables developers of future iCGM systems to bring their products to market in the least burdensome manner possible. The FDA evaluated data from two clinical studies of the Dexcom G6, which included 324 adults and children with diabetes, and found no serious adverse events during the studies. The risks associated with use of the system include hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia, skin irritation, and redness around the device's adhesive patch.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on a key step in advancing FDA’s oversight of drug compounding and implementing new laws governing outsourcing facilities
body_summary: The FDA is issuing a draft guidance on how to formulate the list of bulk drug substances for compounding under the Drug Quality and Security Act. This list, also known as the 503B bulks list, will be used by outsourcing facilities to determine which bulk drug substances can be used to compound drugs. The FDA is proposing to interpret the statutory language "bulk drug substances for which there is a clinical need" to mean that there is a clinical need, or reason, for an outsourcing facility to compound a drug product using a bulk drug substance. The agency will evaluate bulk drug substances using a two-part analysis, considering whether the attributes of the approved drug make it unsuitable for certain patients, and whether the compounded drug is intended to address that attribute. The draft guidance also outlines a balancing test that will be used to weigh factors such as physical and chemical characterization, safety issues, effectiveness, and historical use. The FDA will engage with stakeholders through the public comment process and will finalize the guidance based on the law established by Congress to meet patient medical needs.

title: Statement from FDA’s Donald St. Pierre on findings from ongoing investigation into lead testing issues
body_summary: The US FDA warned Americans in May 2017 that lead tests from Magellan Diagnostics may provide inaccurate results for some children and adults. In response, the FDA investigated the issue with Becton Dickinson (BD) Company, the manufacturer of certain blood sample collection tubes used with lead tests. BD conducted studies that showed a significant chance of false results when using whole blood collected from the vein with Magellan's LeadCare tests in certain tubes. The affected tubes contain a chemical called thiuram that can release sulfur-containing gases that bind to lead particles, making it difficult to detect the correct amount of lead. The FDA recommends not using Magellan lead tests with blood samples taken from the vein, but they can still be used with capillary blood samples. BD has identified specific tubes with thiuram that can be used with Magellan lead tests. The FDA is investigating if this issue may impact other blood collection tube manufacturers and evaluating other factors that may have contributed to inaccurate results. The FDA is also conducting testing to determine if other clinical laboratory tests are affected by the thiuram chemical interference.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a moderate rate. Job gains have been strong in recent months, and the unemployment rate has stayed low. Recent data suggest that growth rates of household spending and business fixed investment have moderated from their strong fourth-quarter readings. On a 12-month basis, both overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy have continued to run below 2 percent. Market-based measures of inflation compensation have increased in recent months but remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. The economic outlook has strengthened in recent months. The Committee expects that, with further gradual adjustments in the stance of monetary policy, economic activity will expand at a moderate pace in the medium term and labor market conditions will remain strong. Inflation on a 12-month basis is expected to move up in coming months and to stabilize around the Committee's 2 percent objective over the medium term. Near-term risks to the economic outlook appear roughly balanced, but the Committee is monitoring inflation developments closely. In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent. The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting strong labor market conditions and a sustained return to 2 percent inflation. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its objectives of maximum employment and 2 percent inflation. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. The Committee will carefully monitor actual and expected inflation developments relative to its symmetric inflation goal. The Committee expects that economic conditions will evolve in a manner that will warrant further gradual increases in the federal funds rate; the federal funds rate is likely to remain, for some time, below levels that are expected to prevail in the longer run. However, the actual path of the federal funds rate will depend on the economic outlook as informed by incoming data. Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chairman; William C. Dudley, Vice Chairman; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Lael Brainard; Loretta J. Mester; Randal K. Quarles; and John C. Williams.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on efforts to reduce tobacco use, especially among youth, by exploring options to address the role of flavors ‒ including menthol ‒ in tobacco products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is issuing an advance notice of proposed rulemaking (ANPRM) to examine the role of flavors in tobacco products, aiming to prevent youth initiation and promote adult smoking cessation. The agency seeks data and research on flavors in tobacco initiation, use, and cessation, as well as consumer perceptions and potential health effects. The FDA aims to protect public health and reduce tobacco-related deaths, with a plan to lower nicotine levels in cigarettes to minimally or non-addictive levels. The proposal is part of a comprehensive plan to reduce tobacco-related deaths and is being developed under the FDA's regulation of tobacco products, under the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services.

title: FDA expands approval of Adcetris for first-line treatment of Stage III or IV classical Hodgkin lymphoma in combination with chemotherapy
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved Adcetris (brentuximab vedotin) to treat adult patients with previously untreated stage III or IV classical Hodgkin lymphoma (cHL) in combination with chemotherapy. The approval was based on a clinical trial comparing Adcetris plus chemotherapy to a chemotherapy-only regimen. The trial found that patients treated with Adcetris plus chemotherapy were 23% less likely to experience progression, death, or initiation of new therapy. The FDA approved Adcetris for this indication based on a Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy designation. Common side effects of Adcetris include neutropenia, peripheral neuropathy, and fever. The FDA granted this approval to Seattle Genetics, Inc. and has a boxed warning for the risk of John Cunningham virus infection, a rare but serious brain infection.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on pivotal public health step to dramatically reduce smoking rates by lowering nicotine in combustible cigarettes to minimally or non-addictive levels
body_summary: The US FDA is issuing an advance notice of proposed rulemaking to explore a product standard to lower nicotine in cigarettes to minimally or non-addictive levels, aiming to reduce nicotine-related deaths and disease. The goal is to save millions of lives, with estimates suggesting 5 million additional adult smokers could quit within one year and 33 million people avoiding regular smoking by 2100. The FDA plans to regulate both novel nicotine delivery products and traditional tobacco products, ensuring innovation of less harmful products while maximizing public health benefits. The FDA invites public feedback on policies to guide a healthier future, with the aim of achieving significant public health gain and placing the US on the path to one of the biggest public health victories.

title: FDA warns duodenoscope manufacturers about failure to comply with required postmarket surveillance studies to assess contamination risk
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued warning letters to Olympus, Fujifilm, and Pentax, three duodenoscope manufacturers, for failing to comply with federal law requirements. The FDA ordered these manufacturers to conduct postmarket surveillance studies to assess the effectiveness of reprocessing duodenoscopes in 2015. Olympus has failed to start data collection, while Pentax and Fujifilm have failed to provide sufficient data. The FDA expects these companies to submit a plan by March 24, 2018, outlining how study milestones will be achieved. The FDA also requires 50% of samples collected in the study to be processed by August 31, 2018, and 100% by the end of 2018. The FDA may take additional action, including seizure, injunction, and civil money penalties, if the companies fail to adequately respond to the warning letter.

title: Remarks from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., as prepared for oral testimony before the U.S. House Committee on Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations hearing “Examining U.S. Public Health Preparedness for and Response Efforts to Seasonal Influenza.”
body_summary: The chairman of the subcommittee has invited the witness to testify on the response to the 2017-2018 seasonal flu, acknowledging that this flu season has been particularly hard. The witness agrees that investing in the universal flu vaccine is crucial, but notes that this process is still many years off. Instead, the witness suggests focusing on enhancing the production of existing licensed vaccines and investing in advanced domestic manufacturing to ensure new and existing technologies are scalable. The witness highlights the work of BARDA in developing alternatives to egg-based vaccines, such as cell-based and recombinant technologies, but notes that most manufacturers continue to produce egg-based vaccines. The witness suggests studying the effectiveness of cell-based and recombinant vaccines, particularly in comparison to egg-based vaccines, and is using CMS data to compare patients who received cell-based and egg-based vaccines. The witness also notes the challenges with newer cell-based approaches and is working with the FDA to develop more effective cell lines and a robust recombinant vaccine manufacturing process.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on effort to help bolster U.S. shellfish market by taking mutually beneficial steps to resume shellfish trade with the EU
body_summary: The U.S. and EU have taken steps to allow molluscan shellfish trade between the two countries for the first time in years. The FDA has published a proposed determination that the EU's safety controls are equivalent to those of the U.S., while the EC is completing administrative procedures for its own proposed determination. This follows a multi-year review of shellfish safety systems in both countries, with technical experts concluding that many safety controls are equivalent. The proposed equivalence determination will create new market access and make healthier and safer shellfish options available to consumers. If finalized, it will allow Massachusetts and Washington state to send bivalve molluscan shellfish to the European market again, and shellfish exporters from Spain and the Netherlands to sell raw bivalve shellfish in the U.S. market.

title: Declaración del Dr. Scott Gottlieb, comisionado de la FDA, sobre las actividades de la dependencia en relación con la actual evaluación posterior a la comercialización del Essure y su compromiso de mantener a las mujeres informadas
body_summary: The FDA takes seriously concerns about the Essure device, which is used as a permanent birth control method. Since its approval in 2002, the FDA has been monitoring its safety and effectiveness. In 2015, the agency convened a panel of medical experts to address concerns about the device, including reports of abdominal pain, irregular menstrual bleeding and device displacement. The FDA also required the device's manufacturer, Bayer, to conduct a post-marketing study to evaluate its safety profile. As part of its ongoing monitoring, the FDA continues to evaluate reports of adverse effects from Essure users and will make public any new findings or concerns. The agency is also working to balance the benefits and risks of the device, considering new information as it becomes available. The FDA will continue to communicate publicly about this issue, sharing its findings and helping women make informed decisions about the device.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA activities related to the ongoing post-market review of Essure and FDA’s commitment to keep women informed
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has taken steps to address concerns about the medical device Essure, which is used as a method of permanent birth control. The agency has convened a panel of medical experts, ordered a post-marketing study, and required a boxed warning and patient decision checklist to be added to the product labeling. As part of its ongoing efforts, the FDA continues to review medical device reports and provide updates on its website. In 2017, the agency received nearly 12,000 reports of adverse events, with most mentioning potential device removal. The FDA is actively investigating these reports and will continue to monitor the device's safety profile, relying on peer-reviewed studies and other data sources to inform its assessment.

title: FDA expands approval of replacement heart valve, smallest mechanical valve size approved in the world
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved the Masters Series Mechanical Heart Valve with Hemodynamic Plus (HP) Sewing Cuff for use in newborn pediatric patients to treat heart defects. The 15-mm valve size is the smallest mechanical heart valve approved, making it suitable for young patients with congenital valve defects. This approval expands treatment options for over 35,000 babies born with congenital heart defects in the US each year. The Masters Series Mechanical Heart Valve was first approved in 1995 and was granted approval by the FDA to St. Jude Medical.

title: FDA authorizes, with special controls, direct-to-consumer test that reports three mutations in the BRCA breast cancer genes
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has authorized the Personal Genome Service Genetic Health Risk (GHR) Report for BRCA1/BRCA2 (Selected Variants) test, which analyzes DNA from a self-collected saliva sample to identify increased risk of breast and ovarian cancer in women and breast cancer or prostate cancer in men. The test detects three specific BRCA1/BRCA2 mutations that are most common in Ashkenazi (Eastern European) Jewish descent, but not in the general population. A negative result does not rule out the possibility of carrying other BRCA mutations that increase cancer risk. The test was developed by 23andMe and has been granted marketing authorization by the FDA. The agency has established special controls to ensure the test's accuracy, reproducibility, and safety. The test should not be used as a substitute for medical screenings or counseling, and individuals should consult a physician or genetic counselor before using the test results for treatment decisions.

title: FDA approves first tests to screen for tickborne parasite in whole blood and plasma to protect the U.S. blood supply
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has approved two tests for detecting antibodies to Babesia microti and DNA in human plasma and whole blood samples, respectively. The tests, ImugenBabesia microtiArrayed Fluorescent Immunoassay (AFIA) and ImugenBabesia microtiNucleic Acid Test (NAT), will be used to screen donors of whole blood and blood components, as well as living organ and tissue donors. This move aims to identify and respond to potential threats to the nation's blood supply, as babesiosis is a preventable and treatable disease. The tests are the first approvals of Babesia detection tests for use in screening donors, with the majority of reported cases in the US coming from states in the Northeast and upper Midwest.

title: FDA approves new HIV treatment for patients who have limited treatment options
body_summary: The US FDA has approved Trogarzo, a new antiretroviral medication, for adult patients with HIV who have tried multiple treatments and are multidrug resistant. Trogarzo is administered once every 14 days and used in combination with other medications. The approval was based on a clinical trial of 40 heavily treatment-experienced patients, who showed significant decreases in HIV RNA levels after adding Trogarzo to their treatment regimens. The trial demonstrated the benefit of Trogarzo in reducing HIV RNA suppression. The FDA granted Fast Track, Priority Review, and Breakthrough Therapy designations, as well as Orphan Drug designation. Trogarzo is administered by a trained medical professional and has been used by 292 patients with HIV-1 infection, with common adverse reactions including diarrhea, dizziness, and nausea.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA’s commitment to modernizing food and nutrition programs
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is working to modernize its food safety system and advance nutrition initiatives. The agency is responsible for overseeing about 80% of the nation's food supply. The Government Accountability Office (GAO) has reviewed the FDA's food and nutrition programs since 2011 and made two recommendations, including developing performance standards and a plan to implement the strategic plan. The FDA has made significant progress in implementing new programs aimed at protecting the food supply and promoting healthier food choices. The agency is taking additional steps, including reviewing recall processes and issuing new guidance on public warnings. The FDA plans to continue pursuing ways to streamline policies, increase transparency, and promote public health through a prevention-oriented food safety system.

title: FDA warns of fraudulent and unapproved flu products
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is warning consumers to be wary of unapproved products claiming to prevent, treat, or cure influenza. This year's severe flu season raises concerns about the potential for consumers to be lured into buying unproven flu treatments, particularly counterfeit antivirals sold online. FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb has stated that the flu has been widespread, leading to a record number of flu-related hospitalizations. The FDA advises consumers to look for telltale signs of fraudulent flu products, such as products claiming to reduce severity and length of the flu, boost immunity, or offer a safe alternative to the flu vaccine. Consumers should be aware that there are no legally marketed over-the-counter drugs to prevent or cure the flu. The FDA recommends buying prescription drugs from licensed pharmacies and reporting adverse reactions to the agency's MedWatch program.

title: Statement on National Colorectal Cancer Awareness Month
body_summary: President Trump joins Americans in recognizing those battling colon and rectal cancer during National Colorectal Cancer Awareness Month. The National Cancer Institute estimates over 135,000 new diagnoses in 2017, with about 50,000 fatalities. The President's administration works with Congress to advance immunotherapy approaches, precision medicine, and new treatments under the 21st Century Cures Act. Gene therapies recently approved by the FDA will quickly reach the market while ensuring patient safety. With over 1 million US survivors, improved treatment and prevention measures have helped. The President encourages Americans to learn about risk factors, prevention methods, and screening guidelines to reduce their risk of developing colorectal cancer.

title: FDA alerts health care professionals and patients not to use compounded drugs from Cantrell Drug Company; agency seeks action to stop production and distribution
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration has alerted healthcare professionals and patients not to use drug products produced by Cantrell Drug Company due to serious deficiencies in its compounding operations. The agency has concerns about quality and sterility assurance, which put patient safety at risk. The FDA has taken action, including a preliminary injunction, to prevent the company from further producing and distributing drugs. The company is required to stop manufacturing and distributing drugs until it complies with federal regulations and recall all non-expired products. Healthcare professionals are advised to check their medical supplies, quarantine products from Cantrell, and not administer them to patients. Examples of affected drugs include opioids and antibiotics.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA’s new efforts to advance implementation of the new consumer Nutrition Facts label for foods
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is updating the Nutrition Facts label to provide more accurate information about food choices and their impact on health. The new label will include changes to help consumers understand the quantity of added sugars. The FDA is launching an educational campaign to help Americans learn about and use the new label. In addition, the agency is issuing guidance documents to food manufacturers to help them implement the new label, including guidelines for labeling honey, maple syrup, and certain cranberry products. The FDA is responsible for protecting public health by ensuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of various products, including human and veterinary drugs, vaccines, and food.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA’s ongoing efforts to help improve effectiveness of influenza vaccines
body_summary: US healthcare officials are investigating the lower effectiveness of this year's flu vaccines against the H3N2 strain, which caused widespread illness in 50 US states. The preliminary vaccine effectiveness for H3N2 was 25% in certain age groups. The FDA, CDC, and other agencies are working together to determine the root cause and improve vaccine efficacy for future flu seasons. The FDA aims to reduce flu severity by treating those with flu-like symptoms and high risk of complications with antiviral drugs.

title: Statement from Stephen Ostroff M.D., Deputy Commissioner for Foods and Veterinary Medicine, on National Toxicology Program draft report on Bisphenol A
body_summary: The US FDA has concluded that Bisphenol A (BPA) is safe for its currently authorized uses in food containers and packaging, based on the available scientific evidence. The FDA has been evaluating BPA safety and has conducted its own research on its use in food packaging. The National Toxicology Program (NTP) has released a draft report on a comprehensive two-year rodent study examining the potential effects of BPA on health, conducted by FDA scientists. The study found "minimal effects" on BPA-dosed groups of rodents, but identified some areas that may merit further research. The FDA supports its current determination that BPA is safe for consumers, and looks forward to the external peer review of the study in April.

title: FDA oversees destruction and recall of kratom products; and reiterates its concerns on risks associated with this opioid
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has announced the voluntary destruction and recall of a large volume of kratom-containing dietary supplements nationwide. The company, Divinity by Divinity Products Distribution, has agreed to stop selling all products containing kratom. The FDA encourages all companies selling kratom-containing products to remove them from the market and submit evidence to the agency.

According to the FDA, kratom contains compounds similar to opioids and poses serious risks of abuse, overdose, and death. There is no evidence of its safety or effectiveness for medical use. The FDA has identified 44 reported deaths associated with kratom use and is monitoring a nationwide outbreak of salmonella associated with kratom products.

The agency has advised consumers not to use kratom products and to dispose of any products in their possession. The FDA recommends reporting adverse events or quality problems associated with kratom products to the agency's online Safety Reporting Portal. The FDA Commissioner, Scott Gottlieb, has stated that the agency will take aggressive enforcement action against kratom-containing products and will continue to warn consumers against its use.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary:
The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on January 30-31, 2018. The committee selected Janet L. Yellen as Chairman until February 2, 2018, and Jerome H. Powell as Chairman effective February 3, 2018, until the selection of his successor in 2019. William C. Dudley was selected as Vice Chairman. The Federal Reserve Bank of New York was authorized to execute transactions for the System Open Market Account (SOMA), with Simon Potter and Lorie K. Logan serving as manager and deputy manager, respectively.

The Committee authorizes foreign currency transactions up to $2.5 billion per calendar year, requiring prior notice. The Chairman may act on behalf of the Committee if consultation is not feasible. Total nonfarm payroll employment increased solidly in December, with national unemployment rate remaining at 4.1%. Labor force participation rate held steady, and total industrial production rose over two months.

The S&P 500 index rose significantly due to a stronger global economic outlook and supportive tax legislation. The FOMC raised its target federal funds rate in December, with no disruptions in money markets. The dollar weakened against most currencies, especially emerging market currencies. Market-based measures of policy expectations and longer-term sovereign yields increased in many countries.

The Federal Open Market Committee met, discussing economic growth, inflation, and labor market conditions. They agreed that information received since December indicated the labor market continued to strengthen and economic activity expanded at a solid rate. Inflation was expected to move up this year and stabilize around the Committee's 2% objective over the medium term.

The Committee maintained the target range for the federal funds rate at 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 percent, with a vote of 10 in favor and none against. The committee also approved a statement stating that economic activity has been rising at a solid rate, labor market conditions are strong, and inflation is expected to move up this year and stabilize around the Committee's 2% objective over the medium term.

title: FDA expands approval of Imfinzi to reduce the risk of non-small cell lung cancer progressing
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration approved Imfinzi (durvalumab) for the treatment of stage III non-small cell lung cancer patients whose tumors are unresectable and have not progressed after chemoradiation. The approval was based on a randomized trial of 713 patients, which showed a median progression-free survival of 16.8 months for Imfinzi patients compared to 5.6 months for placebo patients. Imfinzi targets the PD-1/PD-L1 pathway and has been shown to reduce the risk of cancer progression in patients with stage III unresectable NSCLC. The approval was granted by AstraZeneca, and the FDA also granted Priority Review and Breakthrough Therapy designations. Common side effects of Imfinzi include cough, fatigue, and serious risks include immune-mediated side effects and infection. The FDA approved Imfinzi for patients with an estimated 222,500 new diagnoses and 155,870 deaths from lung cancer in 2017.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. on the efficacy of the 2017-2018 influenza vaccine
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is working to better protect the public against the flu by applying lessons learned from this year's outbreak to next season's flu vaccines. The agency is collaborating with the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), National Institutes of Health (NIH), and other federal partners to select the most appropriate flu strains for inclusion in seasonal influenza vaccines. 

The FDA convenes an advisory panel of experts in just two weeks to help select strains for next season's flu vaccines. The panel reviews data on circulating strains of influenza from around the world and assesses the safety and effectiveness of the vaccine. The FDA also ensures the quality of manufacturing processes, providing seed viruses and quality control reagents to manufacturers. 

This year's flu vaccine has shown lower-than-expected efficacy, raising questions about its effectiveness. However, preliminary analysis of CMS data suggests the cell-based influenza vaccine may have better effectiveness in preventing influenza than the egg-based vaccine. Scientists are working to understand the basis for this finding and its potential to improve the production of a more effective H3N2 vaccine for next season.

title: FDA expands treatment window for use of clot retrieval devices in certain stroke patients
body_summary: The US FDA has cleared the Trevo clot retrieval device to treat certain stroke patients up to 24 hours after symptom onset, expanding the device's indication to a broader group of patients. The device is cleared for use as an initial therapy for strokes due to blood clots to reduce paralysis, speech difficulties, and other stroke disabilities, and as an addition to treatment with medication that dissolves blood blots. The device was previously cleared for use in patients six hours after symptom onset. Carlos Peña, director of the division of neurological and physical medicine devices, stated that expanding the treatment window will significantly increase the number of stroke patients who may benefit from treatment. The Trevo device was first cleared in 2012 and has undergone an expanded marketing for certain patients since 2016. The device is inserted through a catheter to remove a blood clot and restore blood flow. The FDA evaluated data from a clinical trial comparing patients treated with the Trevo device to those who had only medical management, and found that 48% of patients treated with the Trevo device were functionally independent three months after their stroke.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. on advancing the development of novel treatments for neurological conditions; part of broader effort on modernizing FDA’s new drug review programs
body_summary: The FDA is modernizing its drug regulatory programs to expand access to safe and effective treatments for serious neurological conditions. The agency is adopting a team-based approach, integrating experts from different disciplines and stages of a product's life cycle. To support this effort, the FDA has issued five guidance documents for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, migraine, epilepsy, Alzheimer's disease, and ALS. The guidance documents provide clear scientific advice for product developers to save time and resources, ultimately bringing new medicines to patients more efficiently. The FDA aims to improve its review process to foster innovation, engaging with sponsors, patients, and researchers while maintaining its gold standard for product review and protecting consumers.

title: FDA approves new treatment for a certain type of prostate cancer using novel clinical trial endpoint
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Erleada (apalutamide) for the treatment of patients with non-metastatic, castration-resistant prostate cancer. This is the first FDA-approved treatment for non-metastatic, castration-resistant prostate cancer. The approval was based on a randomized clinical trial of 1,207 patients, where Erleada showed a robust effect on metastasis-free survival. The median metastasis-free survival for patients taking Erleada was 40.5 months compared to 16.2 months for patients taking a placebo. The FDA granted the approval to Janssen Pharmaceutical Companies, and the treatment has common side effects, including fatigue, hypertension, and joint pain, with severe side effects including falls, fractures, and seizures.

title: FDA authorizes marketing of first blood test to aid in the evaluation of concussion in adults
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has permitted marketing of the first blood test to evaluate mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI), also known as concussion, in adults. The test, called the Banyan Brain Trauma Indicator, was reviewed and authorized for marketing in under 6 months as part of the FDA's Breakthrough Devices Program. The test works by measuring levels of proteins released from the brain into blood within 12 hours of head injury. According to the FDA, the test was able to predict the presence of intracranial lesions on a CT scan 97.5 percent of the time. The FDA's review team worked closely with the test developer and the U.S. Department of Defense to expedite the test. Availability of the test will help healthcare professionals determine the need for a CT scan in patients suspected of having mTBI and reduce unnecessary radiation exposure.

title: FDA permits marketing of clinical decision support software for alerting providers of a potential stroke in patients
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has permitted the marketing of the Viz.AI Contact application, a clinical decision support software designed to analyze computed tomography (CT) results for potential stroke notifications. A stroke is a serious medical condition requiring emergency care and can cause lasting damage. The software uses artificial intelligence algorithms to analyze images for stroke indicators and can notify a neurovascular specialist sooner, potentially decreasing treatment time and limiting damage. The Viz.AI Contact application is intended for use by neurovascular specialists and is limited to analysis of imaging data, not replacing a full patient evaluation. The FDA reviewed the application through the De Novo premarket review pathway and created a new regulatory classification for computer-aided triage software devices with the same medical imaging intended use.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on Administration’s request for new FDA funding to promote innovation and broaden patient access through competition
body_summary: The US FDA is modernizing its regulatory paradigm to support digital health technologies, aiming to reduce the time and cost of market entry, improve patient safeguards, and enhance cybersecurity. The agency plans to implement new information technology systems and create a Center of Excellence on Digital Health to leverage real-world evidence and support breakthrough device innovations. Additionally, the FDA aims to advance public health by investing in regulatory science, manufacturing, and innovation, including funding programs for investment in new industries and establishing a "Center of Excellence on Compounding for Outsourcing Facilities" to support the growth of the industry and improve product quality.

title: FDA and NRC pave way for the first domestic supply of the most commonly used medical isotope in diagnostic imaging
body_summary: The US FDA and NRC have taken steps to ensure a stable and secure supply of a critical radioactive imaging product. The FDA approved the RadioGenix System, a unique system for producing Technetium-99m (Tc-99m), which is used in medical imaging to detect potentially life-threatening diseases. The NRC is issuing guidance and will license the RadioGenix System to enable the production of Tc-99m for its medical purpose. This marks the first domestic supply of Mo-99, the source of Tc-99m, in 30 years. The RadioGenix System is a result of years of coordination across the FDA and US government organizations, and it will help ensure more reliable, clean, and secure access to this important imaging agent. The system is owned by NorthStar Medical Radioisotopes, and its approval was granted based on safety and efficacy information already approved by the FDA.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on groundbreaking approval and interagency approach to bring stable supply of critical medical imaging isotope to the U.S.
body_summary: The FDA has approved the RadioGenix System, a novel manufacturing system for producing radioisotope Technetium-99m (Tc-99m), which has the potential to benefit many patients and restore the US ability to domestically supply a critical medical diagnostic tool for the first time in 30 years. The system will not only help save and improve lives but also reduce the risk of drug shortages and strengthen national security. Prior to this, the production process for Tc-99m involved shipping enriched uranium out of the US, creating a complicated and potentially risky supply chain. The FDA has been working closely with industry and other US government colleagues to bring a secure and stable supply of Tc-99m to the medical community. The approval was made possible by the American Medical Isotopes Production Act of 2012, which aimed to eliminate the export of highly enriched uranium from the US for medical isotope production and ensure a reliable domestic supply.

title: Memorandum on Optimizing the Use of Federal Government Information in Support of the National Vetting Enterprise
body_summary: The US Government aims to improve coordination and use of intelligence and information to identify individuals posing a threat to national security. A National Vetting Center will be established to coordinate national vetting enterprise management, protecting the US from terrorist attacks and public safety threats. The Director of National Intelligence will head a support element, providing daily direction and guidance to the Center, while the Secretary of Homeland Security will establish a Board to oversee the Center and its support element, comprising senior executives that will guide agencies supporting the Center.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on the agency’s scientific evidence on the presence of opioid compounds in kratom, underscoring its potential for abuse
body_summary: The FDA is providing details on its concerns about kratom's potential for abuse, addiction, and serious health consequences, including death. Recent scientific analysis has provided evidence of kratom compounds' opioid properties, including activation of mu-opioid receptors. The agency has placed kratom products on import alert, conducted product seizures, and concluded it has no medical benefits. In June 2016, the FDA warned about the serious heart problems caused by high doses of loperamide. The FDA urges individuals seeking treatment for opioid addiction to seek help from a healthcare provider, noting that safe and effective treatments, including FDA-approved medications, are available.

title: Statement from Jeffrey Shuren, M.D., J.D., director of the FDA’s Center for Devices and Radiological Health on the recent National Toxicology Program draft report on radiofrequency energy exposure
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) emphasizes its commitment to protecting consumers from the potential health risks of radiofrequency energy emissions from electronic products like televisions and cell phones. The FDA has relied on the National Toxicology Program (NTP) research, which was conducted to investigate the effects of high exposure to radiofrequency energy in rodents. The study found mostly equivocal evidence that whole body radiofrequency energy exposures caused cancer in rats, but also uncovered unusual findings such as exposed rats living longer than control group rats. The FDA will participate in the peer review of the study in March and will review the full set of data from the NTP draft final report. Based on its ongoing evaluation of this issue, the FDA has not found sufficient evidence that there are adverse health effects in humans caused by exposures at or under the current radiofrequency energy exposure limits.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on ongoing efforts to mitigate impact of saline shortages during this flu season
body_summary: The FDA continues to monitor the flu season closely, taking steps to ensure people with the flu have access to critical medical products. This year's flu season has been particularly challenging, with thousands of hospitalizations and a shortage of IV saline bags. The shortage, worsened by Hurricane Maria's impact on Puerto Rico's medical products manufacturing sector, has led to increased demand for saline and other products. The FDA is working to improve the shortage and track potential shortages of critical medical products, including empty IV containers. They are also monitoring influenza vaccine supplies and encouraging people to get a flu shot. The FDA is using various tools and resources to address the shortage, including extending expiration dates of certain products and importing products from foreign facilities. They are working with partners to identify and address issues impacting other products and using aggregated information to identify supply gaps.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in December indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a solid rate. Gains in employment, household spending, and business fixed investment have been solid, and the unemployment rate has stayed low. On a 12-month basis, both overall inflation and inflation for items other than food and energy have continued to run below 2 percent. Market-based measures of inflation compensation have increased in recent months but remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed, on balance. Consistent with its statutory mandate, the Committee seeks to foster maximum employment and price stability. The Committee expects that, with further gradual adjustments in the stance of monetary policy, economic activity will expand at a moderate pace and labor market conditions will remain strong. Inflation on a 12âmonth basis is expected to move up this year and to stabilize around the Committee's 2 percent objective over the medium term. Near-term risks to the economic outlook appear roughly balanced, but the Committee is monitoring inflation developments closely. In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1-1/4 to 1â1/2 percent. The stance of monetary policy remains accommodative, thereby supporting strong labor market conditions and a sustained return to 2 percent inflation. In determining the timing and size of future adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will assess realized and expected economic conditions relative to its objectives of maximum employment and 2 percent inflation. This assessment will take into account a wide range of information, including measures of labor market conditions, indicators of inflation pressures and inflation expectations, and readings on financial and international developments. The Committee will carefully monitor actual and expected inflation developments relative to its symmetric inflation goal. The Committee expects that economic conditions will evolve in a manner that will warrant further gradual increases in the federal funds rate; the federal funds rate is likely to remain, for some time, below levels that are expected to prevail in the longer run. However, the actual path of the federal funds rate will depend on the economic outlook as informed by incoming data. Voting for the FOMC monetary policy action were Janet L. Yellen, Chair; William C. Dudley, Vice Chairman; Thomas I. Barkin; Raphael W. Bostic; Lael Brainard; Loretta J. Mester; Jerome H. Powell; Randal K. Quarles; and John C. Williams.

title: FDA, USDA announce formal agreement to bolster coordination and collaboration
body_summary: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Sonny Perdue and FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. announced a formal agreement to improve the oversight of food by enhancing coordination between the two agencies. The agreement aims to increase interagency collaboration, efficiency, and effectiveness on produce safety and biotechnology activities, providing clarity to manufacturers. The USDA and FDA will work together to streamline capacities and obligations on shared concerns and jurisdiction, with a focus on supporting the FDA's work related to farming. The partnership will help move the nation's food supply system closer to the goal of "Do Right, and Feed Everyone." The agreement formalizes ongoing coordination and presents an opportunity to expand efforts through better integration and increased clarity for the agriculture and food processing sectors.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new steps to help prevent new addiction, curb abuse and overdose related to opioid products
body_summary: The FDA is taking steps to combat the opioid crisis, which has affected 11.5 million Americans in the past year. The agency is exploring ways to reduce exposure to opioids, including changing packaging and prescriber influence. In 2018, the FDA released an updated Blueprint for opioid analgesic REMS education for healthcare providers and will welcome public comments until March 16. The FDA will also discuss strategies for safe opioid prescribing with the Duke Margolis Center for Health Policy on February 15, 2018. The agency aims to reduce harm while providing effective pain management through appropriate prescribing practices, better packaging, and education.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. on FDA’s strengthened commitments to humane and judicious animal research and the termination of a nicotine study
body_summary:
The FDA is ending a study using squirrel monkeys to investigate nicotine addiction, after four monkeys died. The agency's Principal Deputy Commissioner immediately placed the study on hold and formed a team to assess the study's safety and well-being. The team found concerns about inadequate oversight and repeated reported deficiencies. Based on these findings, the FDA has permanently ended the study and will place the monkeys in a permanent sanctuary home.

To strengthen its animal research programs, the FDA is directing an independent investigation of its animal research programs, starting with those conducted at the National Center for Toxicological Research. The agency is also establishing a new Animal Welfare Council to provide centralized oversight of all animal research activities. Additionally, the FDA is working to strengthen its commitment to replacing, reducing, and refining animal studies, and has formed working groups to accelerate the adoption of modeling and simulation tools and new technologies.

title: FDA approves new treatment for certain digestive tract cancers
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Lutathera (lutetium Lu 177 dotatate) for the treatment of gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NETs) in adult patients with somatostatin receptor-positive GEP-NETs. This is the first time a radioactive drug has been approved for GEP-NETs treatment. The approval was supported by two studies, including a randomized clinical trial with 229 patients and data from 1,214 patients. Lutathera works by binding to somatostatin receptors, causing radiation damage to tumor cells. The FDA granted Priority Review and Orphan Drug designation to Lutathera, which provides incentives for developing drugs for rare diseases. Common side effects include lymphopenia, vomiting, nausea, and hyperglycemia, while serious side effects include myelosuppression, kidney damage, and infertility.

title: FDA, FTC warn companies for selling illegal, unapproved opioid cessation products using deceptive claims
body_summary:
The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) have jointly issued warning letters to 12 companies marketing unapproved opioid cessation products with unsubstantiated claims about treating opioid addiction and withdrawal. The FDA is concerned about these products, which may pose serious health risks and prevent patients from seeking approved treatments. The FTC and FDA will work together to address this issue and ensure that companies comply with federal laws regulating food, drug, and cosmetic products.

The FDA Commissioner, Scott Gottlieb, and the Acting FTC Chairman, Maureen K. Ohlhausen, have emphasized the importance of providing safe and effective treatments for opioid addiction. The Administration aims to reduce the number of Americans addicted to opioids and cut the rate of new addiction.

The FDA and FTC have issued warning letters to 11 companies, including Opiate Freedom Center, U4Life, LLC, and King Bio, Inc., which use online platforms to make false claims about their products' ability to cure or treat diseases. The agencies have requested responses from each company within 15 working days and may take law enforcement action if violations are not corrected.

The FDA and FTC have also issued a fact sheet to help consumers avoid products that promise but do not deliver help for opioid addiction or withdrawal. Healthcare professionals and consumers can report adverse events related to these products to the FDA's MedWatch program.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new policy steps for strengthening public warning and notification of recalls
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has committed to improving its recall processes to provide consumers with actionable information about potentially unsafe products. The agency has published a draft guidance that outlines its policy on public warning and notification of recalled products, including drugs, medical devices, and cosmetics. The draft guidance describes circumstances when a company should issue a public warning, the general timeline for such a warning, and what information should be included. The FDA is also developing a new policy on what information will be made available to help consumers identify hazardous recalled food. The agency plans to announce a new approach to the release of recall information this year and will publicize additional information if necessary to effectuate a recall. The FDA takes immediate action to address unsafe products and prioritizes effective recall practices as part of its consumer protection mission.

title: FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on new steps FDA is taking to enhance transparency of clinical trial information to support innovation and scientific inquiry related to new drugs
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is launching a pilot program to evaluate the effectiveness of making certain information from clinical study reports (CSRs) publicly available. The program aims to improve patient care and inform providers about the products they prescribe by releasing portions of CSRs following approval of a new drug application (NDA). The CSRs will include detailed summaries of pivotal trials, such as the study report body, protocol and amendments, and statistical analysis plan. The pilot will include up to nine recently-approved NDAs and will be launched this month. The FDA also plans to add the ClinicalTrials.gov identifier number (NCT #) to FDA materials for future drug approvals to facilitate tracking of clinical research and improve transparency.

title: FDA and DoD launch program to expedite availability of medical products for the emergency care of American military personnel
body_summary:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Department of Defense's Office of Health Affairs have launched a joint program to expedite the development and availability of safe and effective medical products for American military personnel. The program, authorized by H.R.4374, aims to address the immediate medical product priorities of the DoD and ensure these products are developed and made available in the most expeditious manner possible.

The FDA will work closely with Health Affairs to better understand the military's medical needs, expedite review of priority DoD medical products, and provide technical advice to aid in the rapid development and manufacturing of medical products for the military.

The initial phase of the program will be conducted among the FDA's Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER) and Health Affairs, with regular meetings between leadership from CBER and Health Affairs to prioritize and expedite availability of biological products essential to the urgent care of military personnel.

The program is part of an ongoing partnership between the FDA and DoD, which will lead to a robust program that can better serve the health care needs of American military personnel. The FDA and DoD are confident that this program will deliver critical battlefield medicine to U.S. troops on the battlefield.

title: FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., updates on some ongoing shortages related to IV fluids
body_summary:
The FDA has updated its efforts to address the ongoing IV saline shortages caused by Hurricane Maria in Puerto Rico. The agency continues to work with manufacturers to ensure their facilities can operate at full capacity and has imported product into the US from foreign facilities, including Brazil. Additional import sites are being explored. The FDA expects the shortage to improve in the coming weeks and months.

The agency has approved IV saline products from additional companies, including Fresenius Kabi and Laboratorios Grifols, which is expected to increase product supply in the US market. The demand for saline products has been exacerbated by a worse-than-typical flu season.

The FDA is asking companies to submit data to extend expiration dates for these products, which would allow near-expiry products to be used. Updates on new supply sources and expiration date extensions will be posted on the FDA's drug shortage website.

The agency is closely monitoring the impact of mitigation strategies and is paying attention to the demand for empty IV containers as an alternative to filled bags. The FDA is assessing existing product supply, demand trends, and manufacturer capacity to ramp up production of empty bags.

The agency is identifying steps to mitigate the issue of empty container shortages and is exploring ways to ensure that these shortages do not occur. The FDA is also aware of the impact of the severe flu season on the IV saline shortage and is encouraging health care organizations and hospitals to contact the agency directly if they are not receiving the products they need.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. responding to report from GAO and updating on FDA’s ongoing efforts to increase access to complex generic drugs
body_summary: The U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) published a report titled "Generic Drugs: FDA Should Make Public Its Plans to Issue and Revise Guidance on Nonbiological Complex Drugs." The report recommended that the FDA publicly announce its plans to issue or revise guidance for nonbiological complex drugs. The FDA agrees with the GAO's recommendation and is actively working to accomplish this goal. The FDA has been developing new policies to promote competition and access, particularly in pharmaceutical categories with limited competition. The agency has published 1,541 product-specific guidances since 2007, including 47 specific to complex generic drug products. The FDA is undertaking an economic analysis to evaluate the impacts of its policies and will release the results as soon as available. The agency is also developing new guidance for industry, including specific guidance on "sameness" requirements for ANDAs, to clarify regulatory expectations for complex generics. The FDA aims to make sure its policies and regulations keep pace with the nature of complex products and the challenges faced in protecting consumers and promoting drug competition and access.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., in response to GAO report regarding FDA’s ongoing commitment to employing a least burdensome approach to device review
body_summary: The FDA is working to make the device development and regulatory review process more modern, science-based, and efficient. As FDA commissioner, the goal is to implement the "least burdensome" approach, which aims to evaluate novel devices and accommodate iterative improvements to existing devices in a consistent and effective manner. The FDA has taken steps to apply this approach since 1997, resulting in benefits to public health. Recent efforts include expanding the use of real-world data, providing new draft guidance for the Breakthrough Device Program, and qualifying a medical device development tool. The agency plans to complete an audit of its training on least burdensome requirements by June and will periodically audit its application of this approach. The FDA is also considering new draft guidance on assessing minimal information necessary for assuring the safety and effectiveness of new devices.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., on FDA decision to seek additional time to reassess rule that would have changed longstanding practices for how the agency determined the ‛intended use’ of medical products
body_summary: The FDA is revising its intended use regulations to provide clearer rules for medical product manufacturers. The agency heard concerns about its 2017 final rule, which was deemed unclear, and is committed to addressing this issue. A new final rule notice, which includes new language on intended use, was included in a largely non-controversial final rule that primarily addressed tobacco product regulation. The new language relates to evidence considered to determine a product's intended use and may have implications for product promotion. The FDA proposes to delay the effective date of certain portions of the final rule, reverting to existing regulations and interpretations on determining intended use, which have been in effect for decades. The tobacco-related portions of the rule will go into effect. The agency has opened a comment period on the proposal to delay until February 5, 2018, and remains committed to rulemaking on intended use.

title: FDA approves first treatment for breast cancer with a certain inherited genetic mutation
body_summary: The US FDA has approved the use of Lynparza (olaparib tablets) to treat patients with certain types of breast cancer that have spread and a specific inherited genetic mutation. This is the first drug in its class (PARP inhibitor) approved to treat breast cancer. The approval is based on a randomized clinical trial of 302 patients with HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer and a germline BRCA mutation, which showed a median progression-free survival of 7 months. Lynparza is now indicated for the treatment of patients with germline breast cancer susceptibility gene (BRCA) mutated, human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-negative metastatic breast cancer, who have been previously treated with chemotherapy. The FDA has also expanded the approval of the BRACAnalysis CDx, an approved companion diagnostic to Lynparza, to include the detection of BRCA mutations in blood samples from patients with breast cancer.

title: FDA acts to protect kids from serious risks of opioid ingredients contained in some prescription cough and cold products by revising labeling to limit pediatric use
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration is requiring safety labeling changes to limit the use of prescription opioid cough and cold medicines containing codeine or hydrocodone in children under 18 years old due to the serious risks outweighing potential benefits. After changes, these products will no longer be indicated for pediatric use and will be labeled for adults 18 years and older. The FDA is updating labeling with additional safety information, including an expanded Boxed Warning, to notify about risks of misuse, abuse, addiction, overdose, and death. The changes follow a comprehensive assessment of risks and benefits and are based on available data and expert advice. The FDA is also making the required safety labeling changes available to parents and healthcare professionals through a Drug Safety Communication.

title: FDA warns Becton Dickinson & Company of significant violations of the law as part of ongoing investigation into lead testing issues
body_summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has issued a warning letter to Becton Dickinson (BD) & Company, citing several violations of federal law. The violations include marketing significantly modified versions of certain BD Vacutainer blood collection tubes without required FDA clearance or approval and failing to submit medical device reports to the FDA within the required timeframe. The inspection of BD's New Jersey facility also revealed that the company failed to evaluate and investigate a complaint involving variability in test results observed when certain BD Vacutainer blood collection tubes were used with Magellan Diagnostics' LeadCare test systems. The FDA has advised laboratories and health care professionals to follow retesting recommendations for Magellan's LeadCare test systems. BD has until February 1, 2018, to notify the FDA about specific steps taken to address the violations.

title: Statement by FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D., update on recovery efforts in Puerto Rico, and continued efforts to mitigate IV saline and amino acid drug shortages
body_summary: The FDA is providing an update on the recovery efforts in Puerto Rico, particularly addressing the IV saline shortage resulting from Hurricane Maria. The shortage is expected to improve in early 2018, with continuing improvements in the weeks ahead. Baxter, a leading producer of IV saline fluids, has returned to commercial power at all its facilities on the island. Other companies manufacturing critical drugs have also resumed production. The FDA remains committed to addressing the shortage and encourages hospitals to follow clinical recommendations for managing the shortage. The agency is pursuing efforts to increase supplies of IV saline, including approving additional products from companies like Fresenius Kabi and Laboratorios Grifols. The shortage situation is expected to improve in the coming weeks, with some product nearing expiry and potentially being used safely.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. on FDA Food Safety Modernization Act enforcement discretion guidance
body_summary: The FDA is committed to ensuring the US food supply remains among the safest in the world. The Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) represents a fundamental change in the approach to food safety, shifting from being reactive to preventive. The law was enacted in response to widespread concern about outbreaks of foodborne illnesses that kill thousands each year. To address challenges in implementing FSMA, the FDA released guidance outlining key areas where enforcement discretion will be exercised in four of the rules that implement aspects of FSMA. This action aims to reduce burdens on industry and government and provide the agency with the ability to consider the most effective and efficient way forward. The FDA is committed to taking a comprehensive approach to implementing FSMA, including training, technical assistance, and guidance documents to ensure industry and regulatory partners have the tools they need to implement the law.

title: FDA warns American CryoStem Corporation of significant deviations related to its unapproved stem cell product, Atcell
body_summary: The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued a warning letter to American CryoStem Corporation, its Chairman/CEO John S. Arnone, for marketing an unapproved adipose-derived stem cell product, Atcell, without FDA approval. The product was found to have significant deviations from current good manufacturing practice requirements, posing potential safety concerns. The FDA has also inspected the company and found that the product is intended for autologous use but involves more than minimal manipulation, which requires FDA review. The FDA plans to apply a risk-based approach to enforcement, considering the product's administration and intended use. The company has been directed to correct the violations within 15 working days, or face enforcement action.

title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee
body_summary: The Federal Open Market Committee held a joint meeting with the Board of Governors on December 12-13, 2017. Wage gains remained modest, with compensation per hour increasing 1% over four quarters and average hourly earnings rising 2.5% over 12 months. Industrial production increased briskly in October, while real personal consumption expenditures (PCE) grew modestly. Consumer sentiment was high, and housing activity edged up in the fourth quarter. Nominal government purchases rose, but real federal government purchases were flat. The US international trade deficit widened, with exports picking up in September and imports growing significantly. The Committee ratified the Desk's domestic transactions and raised the target federal funds rate to 1-1/4 to 1-1/2 percent, citing strong labor market conditions and inflation below 2 percent.

title: Statement from FDA Commissioner Scott Gottlieb, M.D. on new steps to facilitate efficient generic drug review to enhance competition, promote access and lower drug prices
body_summary: The FDA announced additional steps to promote generic competition as part of its Drug Competition Action Plan. The plan aims to reduce gaming by branded companies, resolve scientific and regulatory obstacles, and improve the efficiency of the FDA's generic review process. The FDA is releasing two documents to streamline and improve the submission and review of generic drug applications. The first document, "Good ANDA Submission Practices," highlights common deficiencies in generic drug applications that may lead to delays. The second document, "Good ANDA Assessment Practices," outlines a streamlined generic review process and introduces new templates to make each cycle more efficient and complete. The goal is to reduce the number of review cycles and improve access to generic medicines. The FDA expects to take additional steps this year to promote competition and reduce drug prices. The plan is part of the FDA's efforts to ensure safe, effective, and quality medicines are available to patients, and the agency will continue to be the gold standard for approval of all drug applications.

title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
body_summary: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in November indicates that the labor market has continued to strengthen and that economic activity has been rising at a solid rate. Averaging through hurricane-related fluctuations, job gains have been solid, and the unemployment rate declined further.
